english: How do I know if the early rains are steady enough for me to plant my maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nugbɔ lɛ nɛɔ shiŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ ŋmãa?

english: Wait until the rain has soaked deep into the soil—at least hand-depth—two or three times in a week. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout and then die if dry weather returns.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. (Kɛ hoo lɛ, eshɛɔ nine mli) shii enyɔ loo etɛ yɛ otsi mli. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Saramɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why does my young oil palm tree produce flowers but no fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi shi amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Young oil palms produce mostly male flowers during their first few years to build up strong trunks and roots. As the tree matures, it will produce female flowers that grow into full palm bunches.
ga: Palm dumɔwui woɔ fɔfɔi hii babaoo yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Koni ama tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni wa Kɛ́ tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ, ebaawo fɔfɔi yei ni baatsɔ ŋmei tsei akui.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop growing when grass starts growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ kpaɔ kwɛ̃mɔ beni jwɛi jeɔ shishi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Weeds and grass have aggressive roots that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your pepper plants. Clearing weeds around the base allows the pepper roots to get the food they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni boteɔ mli ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha o-pepper tsei lɛ mli lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Konus lɛ yeɔ ebuaa pepper shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I start applying fertilizer to my crops as early as one or two weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabɔi miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ŋmɔmɔ kɛji midu nii otsi kome loo enyɔ pɛ?

english: Just like a young child needs good food early in life to grow into a strong adult, a young crop needs early nutrients right after planting so it can establish strong roots and grow healthy.
ga: Taakɛ niyenii kpakpa he hiaa gbekɛbii bibii kɛjɛ amɛgbekɛbiiashi tɔ̃ɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Bɔni afee ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ onukpa ni he wa lɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ he miihia oblahii kɛ oblayei hu mra. amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni adu lɛ Bɔni afee ni ekɛ shishifãi ni wa aba ni eda waa

english: Do my young crop seedlings really need food right away, or can I wait until they start flowering?
ga: Ani niyenii he miihia midumɔwui bibii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ aloo manyɛ mamɛ ni amɛje fɔfɔii ashishi?

english: Seedlings need nourishment immediately during their first two weeks to build a healthy body. Waiting until flowering is like starving a child and trying to feed them only when they reach adulthood.
ga: Niyenii he miihia dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii enyɔ lɛ mli koni amɛná gbɔmɔtso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ mɔ ko mɛ kɛyashi fɔfɔi lɛ baafɔ̃ lɛ, etamɔ gbekɛ ko ni hɔmɔ miiye lɛ, ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni oha amɛ niyenii beni amɛdara pɛ.

english: How much fertilizer should I measure out for a young plant during its first feeding?
ga: Esa akɛ masusu ŋmɔshi nibii enyiɛ he aha tsei bibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ niyenii hamɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Young plants only need a small, measured portion—such as a specific small scoop or 5 grams—because their small root systems need gentle, balanced feeding without overloading them.
ga: Akɛni tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daraaa hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛsusu fã bibioo ko pɛ he, tamɔ spun bibioo ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe loo gram 5. Ebiɔ niyenii ni mli jɔ ni ja ni niyenii ni fa fe nine bɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops seem to grow slowly if I don't feed them within the first two weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo kɛji mikɛ niyenii haaa lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: A seed quickly uses up its stored energy after sprouting. Without early fertilizer by the second week, the young plant starves and stops growing actively.
ga: Dumɔwui kɛ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii oya beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ oya yɛ otsi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tso bibioo lɛ baaye hɔmɔ ni ekpa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it better to give fertilizer immediately on planting day or wait a week or two?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ dumɔ gbi lɛ nɔ loo ooomɛ otsi kome loo enyɔ?

english: Waiting until the first or second week allows the plant to settle into the soil after planting so its new roots are ready to take up the food effectively.
ga: Mɛɛ otsi klɛŋklɛŋ loo otsi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli ni tso lɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi heei lɛ afee klalo koni amɛŋɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is early feeding so important for the final harvest yield of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niyenii ni akɛhaa mra lɛ ji No hewɔ lɛ ehe hiaa waa kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaagbee yibiiwoo lɛ.

english: Proper food during the seedling stage sets the foundation for crop health. A plant that is well-fed as a 'child' grows larger and produces far more fruit or grain as an 'adult'.
ga: Niyenii ni sa yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ ji shishitoo nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahewalɛ. Tsei ni ayeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ akɛ ‘gbekɛbii’ lɛ baadara ni amɛwo yibii loo dumɔwui babaoo beni amɛdara’.

english: Will applying fertilizer to very young crops harm their delicate early roots?
ga: Ani tsei bibii waa ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ baaye amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo mra lɛ awui?

english: If you apply the correct small amount around the first or second week, it provides essential food for root growth rather than harming the plant.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ shika bibioo ni sa tsu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ loo otsi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Ebaaha niyenii ni he hiaa koni shishifãi lɛ adara yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeye tso lɛ awui.

english: Why do some of my crops die off shortly after sprouting in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi gboiɔ beni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Sprouts often fail because the soil lacks enough nutrients to support their rapid growth phase. Giving them food around the second week helps them survive and thrive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ aya nɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua ni ekwɛ̃ oya lɛ. Kɛ́ aha amɛ niyenii yɛ otsi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛshwereɔ.

english: Can I make up for missed fertilizer applications later when the crop is already full-grown?
ga: Ani manyɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ he nyɔmɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli beni tsei lɛ eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: No, late feeding cannot fix stunted early growth. Just like childhood growth cannot be redone, a plant needs food in its first two weeks to build the frame required for high yields.
ga: Dabi, niyenii ni akɛhaa sɛɛ mli lɛ nyɛŋ asaa mra be mli dalɛ ni efite lɛ. Taakɛ anyɛɛɛ afee gbekɛbiiashi dalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ. Niyenii he miihia tsei lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii enyɔ lɛ mli koni amɛma gbɛjianɔtoo ni he hiaa kɛha nibii babaoo ni anáa lɛ.

english: How do I know the right stage to begin feeding my newly planted crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male he ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi mitsei ni midu ehee lɛ niyenii hamɔ?

english: The ideal stage is around the first or second week after planting, which matches the moment the young crop transitions from seed energy to actively seeking food from the soil.
ga: Be ni sa fe fɛɛ ji aaafee otsi klɛŋklɛŋ loo otsi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli beni adu nii lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ kɛ be ni tsei bibii tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui ahewalɛ mli kɛyaa niyenii taomɔ ni yɔɔ ekãa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kpãa gbee.

english: Why should I switch from planting traditional crops like maize to growing plantains on my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake kɛjɛ blema nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ni miduɔ lɛ nɔ kɛya plantains ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Plantains generally offer higher financial returns over time because once the plant is established, it continues to produce food and income for several years, whereas maize must be cleared, tilled, and replanted every single season.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantains haa shika babaoo yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ. Ejaakɛ kɛ́ abɔ tsei lɛ Ebaaya nɔ ekɛ niyenii kɛ shika aba afii babaoo ni baa lɛ amli. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ ajie ŋmãa, atsu nii, ni adu ekoŋŋ daa be.

english: Is it true that plantain crops yield more food per acre than traditional rice or maize?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ plantain ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ acre kome mli fe blema ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Yes, a healthy plantain farm produces a much heavier weight of food per acre compared to grain crops like maize or rice, giving you more bulk product to harvest and sell in the market.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantain ŋmɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha niyenii ni tsii babaoo aba yɛ acre kome mli kɛ akɛto ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa he. Enɛ haa onáa nibii babaoo ni obaakpa ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ.

english: How does growing plantains compare to growing rice in terms of how quickly I can make money?
ga: Te plantains ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ egbɔ ehaa tɛŋŋ yɛ shika ni anáa kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ mli?

english: Rice gives you a quick return within three to four months of planting, while plantains take about 12 to 15 months for the first harvest. However, plantains keep bearing fruit continuously after that without needing to be replanted.
ga: Omɔ haa onáa sɛɛnamɔ oya yɛ nyɔji etɛ loo ejwɛ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni odu lɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, yɛ be mli ni eheɔ aaafee nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 15 dani plantains lɛ woɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii lɛ, amɛyaa nɔ amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ no sɛɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni adu amɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Do plantain crops require as much daily labor and weeding as my traditional maize field?
ga: Ani plantain ŋmɔshi nibii biɔ daa gbi nitsumɔ kɛ jwɛi babaoo tamɔ mi kusum ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: No, plantains require less weeding once they mature because their broad, heavy leaves create shade that stops weeds from growing, unlike maize which needs constant weeding throughout its life.
ga: Dabi, plantains biɔ jwɛi babaoo beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsii lɛ haa hulutsoo baa koni jwɛi akakwɛ̃. Etamɔɔɔ ŋmãa, ni biɔ ni ajie jwɛi be fɛɛ be yɛ eshihilɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Can I harvest from a plantain crop more than once, or do I have to clear the field like I do with rice?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa plantain ni fa fe ekome yɛ be kome mli loo esa akɛ makpa ŋmɔ lɛ mli tamɔ bɔ ni makpa ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Unlike rice which dies after one harvest and requires full field clearing, a plantain plant produces shoots called suckers at its base, allowing a single root stem to produce fresh plants and harvests for many years.
ga: Enɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ ŋmãa ni gboɔ yɛ kpamɔ kome sɛɛ ni ebiɔ ni ajie jɛmɛ fɛɛ lɛ he. Dumɔwui lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii yɛ amɛshishigbɛ. Enɛ haa shishifã kome woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii heei kɛ ŋmaakpamɔi afii babaoo.

english: Why do I have to buy new seeds every year for maize, but I do not need to buy seeds for plantains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmãa dumɔwui heei daa afi lɛ? Shi ani ehe ehiaaa ni ahe dumɔwui kɛha plantains?

english: Maize grows from seeds that lose quality if saved from your harvest, but plantains grow from vegetative shoots called suckers that you can simply dig up from your existing plants to expand your farm for free.
ga: Abɛi kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui ni ehiii kwraa kɛji akɛ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ okpamɔ lɛ mli. Mohu ɔ, plantains daa kɛ jeɔ tsohi nɛ a tsɛɛ ke shoots ɔ mi, nɛ o ma nyɛ maa ngɔ tsohi nɛ a ngɛ momo ɔ kɛ je o ngmɔ ɔ mi kɛ bli o ngmɔ ɔ mi yaka.

english: Does growing plantain affect my soil differently than growing traditional crops like maize?
ga: Ani plantains ni aduɔ lɛ saa mishikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe blema nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, plantains feed heavily on potassium to build their large fruits, whereas maize uses mostly nitrogen. Plantains also shade the soil and return organic matter through their large fallen leaves, helping retain soil moisture better than maize.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains yeɔ potassium babaoo koni ekɛwo aduawai wuji. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa kɛ nitrogen tsuɔ nii babaoo lɛ. Plantains hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛtsɔɔ baai agboi ni egbee shi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmãa.

english: Which crop handles dry weather better, my traditional maize plants or plantains?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei nyɛɔ amɛtsuɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he nii jogbaŋŋ? Mimaŋ ŋmãa tso loo plantain.

english: Plantains store a large amount of water inside their soft, fleshy trunks, which helps them endure short dry spells better than maize plants, which quickly wither and die if rains fail during flowering.
ga: Plantains toɔ nu babaoo yɛ amɛtso ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛŋmɛɔ amɛtsui shi yɛ be kukuoo mli ni hɔmɔ baa lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmãa tsei, ni kɛji nugbɔ nɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, amɛgboiɔ oya ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Do plantain fruits spoil faster after harvest compared to traditional grains like maize and rice?
ga: Ani plantain yibii lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ kɛ akɛto blema ŋmaa tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa he?

english: Yes, plantains are fresh, perishable fruits that ripen and soften within one to two weeks after cutting, whereas properly dried grains like maize and rice can be stored in sacks for many months without spoiling.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains ji aduawai heei ni fiteɔ oya. Amɛbaakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaafee blɛoo yɛ otsi kome loo enyɔ mli beni afolɔ amɛ sɛɛ. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni egbi jogbaŋŋ tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa Abaanyɛ akɛto kotokui amli nyɔji babaoo ni amɛfiteee.

english: Can I plant my traditional maize or rice on the same land with plantains at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu blema ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ plantains yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, during the first few months after planting young plantains, there is plenty of open space and sunlight to plant short-season crops like maize or vegetables between the rows before the plantain canopy closes.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli yɛ dumɔwui bibii ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. He ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu be kukuoo mli nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai. yɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai lɛ ateŋ dani plantain ŋtayaa lɛ ŋmɛɔ

english: Why are my maize plants growing very tall and thin without producing big corn cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miida ni amɛmiifee mlɛo ni ŋmeii wuji bɛ mli lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. The stalks stretch tall and thin to reach light, leaving the plant without enough energy to form large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tso lɛ yitso lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni eyɛ mlɛo koni emɔ la. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ náaa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmei agbo ni mli wa.

english: Why do I need to drive wooden stakes into the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔ tso nɔ mawo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that require maximum sunlight on their leaves to produce food for the growing tuber underground. Staking keeps the leaves lifted off the damp soil, exposing them to sunlight and protecting them from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Ha hulu la lɛ akpɛ ni otsi helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli baa lɛ anaa

english: Why do agricultural officers advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land where I grow my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. This enriches the soil with natural fertilizer, which helps heavy-feeding crops like maize grow much better in the next season.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kwraa yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I apply dry chemical fertilizer onto my farm when the ground is completely dry during a drought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer requires soil moisture to dissolve so that the roots can absorb the nutrients. Applying dry fertilizer to dry soil leaves concentrated salts near the roots, which can burn and damage the crop instead of helping it.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi fata shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni baanyɛ ashã ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeye ebua amɛ.

english: During the Harmattan, dry winds and low humidity cause trees to lose water quickly. Cocoa trees drop some of their leaves as a natural defense mechanism to reduce water loss and protect the trunk and roots until rain returns.
ga: Yɛ harmattan beaŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ hulutsoo be ni baa shi lɛ haa tsei lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ekomɛi amɛshwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛbuɔ amɛshishi kɛ amɛshishifãi ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and turn brown even though I water them every single day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ egbo ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Overwatering or watering late in the evening creates soggy soil where roots cannot breathe. Excessive water causes root rot and encourages fungal diseases in the soil, which prevents the roots from taking up water and leads to wilting.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli fe nine loo okɛ nu wo mli gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ aahu akɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu. Nu babaoo haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he hewalɛ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ nu ni ehaaa amɛgbi.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids, mites, or whiteflies sucking sap from the underside of leaves. It can also be a sign of a plant virus spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids, mites, loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Ebaanyɛ efee tso mli hela ko ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi hu.

english: Why do weeds in my field cause my crops to produce a small harvest even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔji amli lɛ haaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná yibii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ babaoo ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than standard crops and aggressively steal soil nutrients, light, and water. Even with good rainfall, the weeds drink up the nutrients before your crop's roots can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ daa lɛ ni amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, la kɛ nu waa. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ moŋ, shi ehi. Jwɛi lɛ hu nuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi shɛɔ amɛhe.

english: Can I leave my mature cassava roots unharvested in the ground if I am not ready to sell them yet?
ga: Can I leave unharvested mature cassava roots in the ground? Ni kɛji akɛ mifeee klalo akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ hu?

english: Yes, cassava acts as its own underground storage. Healthy mature roots can remain safely in the soil for several months without spoiling, allowing you to harvest gradually as you find buyers.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei tsuɔ nii akɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eshikpɔŋ shishi nutoohe. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eda lɛ baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo ni amɛgbooo. Ye obua bo fiofio ni Okpa nii kɛji ona mɔ ko ni baahe.

english: Why should I cut off the small side branches and extra leaves growing at the base of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? Jiemɔ fãi kɛ baai ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tomato tso lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Pruning lower side branches, often called suckers, directs the plant's food and energy away from unnecessary leaves and straight into growing bigger, healthier fruits while improving air flow to prevent disease.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ suckers lɛ ni afolɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni etsɔɔ tso lɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ ahe kɛyaa aduawai ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ koni helai akamɔ mɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings burning and turning brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ shã ni efee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants do not tolerate direct, harsh sunlight well. They need shade crops like plantains or tree canopies above them to block the intense sun while their roots establish.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ashishi koni amɛha hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ aná amɛhe hulutsoo yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ ema shi lɛ.

english: If I plant my maize seeds closer together, will I get a larger harvest from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe Ani maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too close forces the maize plants to fight each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight, which leads to weak stems and tiny or empty corn cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa tsei lɛ abɔi nu he akaŋ. Niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la, ni haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do people say I should plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the plot where I grew maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu ŋmã yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which naturally restores the nutrients that heavy-feeding crops like maize took away.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ jieɔ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: My maize plants are very green and tall, but the corn ears are small. What is happening in my soil?
ga: Mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ yɛ eŋɔli ni amɛkwɔ waa. Shi ŋmãa toi lɛ daraaa. Mɛni miiya nɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: This usually means the soil has too much nitrogen, which makes leaves grow quickly, but lacks phosphorus and potassium, which are needed to grow big grains and fruits.
ga: Nɔ titri ni enɛ tsɔɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni atsɛɔ lɛ nitrogen lɛ fa tsɔ. ni haa baai lɛ daa oya Shi ebɛ phosphorus kɛ potassium, ni he hiaa koni dumɔwui kɛ aduawai wuji akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off before any fruits appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of calcium in the soil, preventing the flower from setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ wooo yibii.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies feeding on the sap under the leaf, which can also spread a virus to the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni baanyɛ agbɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ashwã tsei hu amli

english: Why should I cut down some of the small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi plantain shishifãi titri lɛ.

english: Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, ensuring the mother plant puts all its energy and water into producing a single large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ kɛ enu fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii akuu agbo kome ni tsii.

english: Does my yam crop really need tall wooden stakes to climb, or can I leave the vines on the ground?
ga: Mi sweet potato dumɔ lɛ biɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko koni manyɛ makwɔ diɛŋtsɛ. Aloo manyɛ mashi weintsei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Staking gets the yam leaves off the wet ground so they don't rot, and lifts them up to catch maximum sunlight, which builds large, healthy tubers underground.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛkafite. ni owó nɔ koni enine ashɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii wuji ni he wa baa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why is it helpful to cover the soil around my crops with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi baawo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil, known as mulching, stops the sun from drying out the earth, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulu la lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akakwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, the plant reaches its mature height for its variety, and the ground around the base begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ bɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ naa. ni he ni ebɔle shishitoo lɛ he lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my young cocoa plants turn brown and crisp when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily in direct sun. They need fast-growing shade plants like plantains grown beside them to act as living umbrellas, shielding them from heat and keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Amɛmiisumɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ. Koni etsu nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Buu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do my maize leaves wilt and curl up during the afternoon even when there is moisture in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ lɛ?

english: In the hot afternoon sun, water evaporates from leaves faster than roots can drink it up. The plant curls its leaves to reduce its surface area exposed to the sun and trap moisture inside until the air cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Nu lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi, ni amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Yellowing of lower leaves is a sign of nitrogen hunger. When food in the soil is low, the plant starves its older bottom leaves to feed the new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji nitrogen hɔmɔ he okadi. Kɛ niyenii fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ hɔmɔ yeɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing tall and dark green but refusing to produce any flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miida ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ shi efɔɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes plants focus all their energy on leaf growth instead of flowering. Adding nutrients like phosphorus encourages the plant to start setting flowers and peppers.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo fɔfɔi. Nibii ni haa mɔ he waa tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛjeɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii shishi.

english: Cassava plants drop leaves during dry periods to save water and protect themselves from drying out completely. The plant enters a dormant resting state and will produce fresh leaves when rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛtsi amɛhe gbɛ koni amɛkagbi kwraa. Tso lɛ baabote shihilɛ ni mli wa mli ni ebaaná baai heei kɛji nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cocoa trees produce far more flowers than they can feed. If the tree lacks water or nutrients, it drops excess flowers to protect itself, keeping only the flowers that tiny beneficial insects have pollinated.
ga: Kookoo tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ ekwɛ nɔ. Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii Ebaafɔ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine lɛ nɔ koni ekɛbu ehe he. Tsɔɔmɔ fɔfɔi ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ pɛ. pollination pɛ

english: Why does my yam vine need to climb a wooden stake instead of growing along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ tsei anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to capture maximum sunlight for leaf growth. Spreading on the ground exposes leaves to dirt, diseases, and shade, resulting in smaller underground tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni enyɛ emɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni baai lɛ adara. Shikpɔŋ nɔ shweremɔ haa baai lɛ naa muji, helai kɛ hulutsoo, ni no haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: Why does planting cowpea in my field make the soil better for my next crop of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpea roots work with natural soil bacteria to trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground. When the cowpea plant dies, that stored nitrogen becomes natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Cowpea shishifãi kɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tsina tso lɛ gbo Nitrogen ni ato lɛ bafeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha sɛɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants shrinking and twisting upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Leaf twisting is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading viral sicknesses to the plant, or by extreme heat stress disrupting normal leaf expansion.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni tsɛŋeɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni tsiɔ baa lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ ni sa lɛ naa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during light winds right before the fruit ripens?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli wa waa mli lɛ? Dani aduawai lɛ baakwɛ̃?

english: Microscopic worms (nematodes) or stem borer insects chew away the roots and inner stem, destroying the plant's anchor in the soil. As the heavy bunch matures, the weakened trunk snaps or pulls free from the ground.
ga: Microscope borer (Nematodes) loo kooloi ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ tsei lɛ amli. Efiteɔ tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji kuu lɛ eda kwraa lɛ, tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ baagbee shi loo amɛbaajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei fɛɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are like human babies and burn easily under strong sunlight. They need shade from surrounding trees or plantains to protect their tender leaves and retain soil moisture while their roots develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei loo plantains ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli. Koni abu baai bibii lɛ ahe ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow instead of staying rich green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahi shi ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually signal that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil, which it needs to produce green leaf matter, or that excessive water in the soil is suffocating the roots and preventing nutrient uptake.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni he hiaa koni akɛfee baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ Aloo nu babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nyɛɔ eshɛɔ mli.

english: Why does my cassava plant have plenty of big leaves but very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ dara waa shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or fertilizer, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and branches above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ niji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato tuber ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli lɛ

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat stress or irregular watering, causing it to shed flowers to conserve water and energy for its own survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Enɛ haa efɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛto nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: Why do insects attack my cowpea crop mostly when the plants start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-cowpea tsei lɛ babaoo kɛ́ amɛbɔi fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers and young pods produce sweet nectar and soft tissue, which attract pests like thrips and pod borers looking for high-energy food during that specific growth stage.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ jieɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo. Enɛ gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ thrips kɛ pod borers ni taoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo yɛ nakai dalɛ be lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall, thin, and weak when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Why are my crops tall, thin, and weak when I plant multiple seeds? Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crowded plants compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, forcing them to stretch upward for light rather than growing strong stems.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ hulu la lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ koni amɛná la yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why does my plantain shoot produce smaller bunches when I leave all the suckers growing around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ mli gbalaa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii beni mishiɔ ŋmeii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Multiple suckers growing from the same parent plantain root compete for the same food and water in the soil, which reduces the energy available to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni jɛɔ dumɔwu shishifã kome mli lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb tall sticks to produce bigger tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ tsei niji ni kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ koni ekɛ bulbs wuji aba lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food through photosynthesis. Staking lifts the leaves off the shaded ground, allowing the plant to generate maximum energy to send down into the tuber.
ga: Sweet potato baai biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛtsɔ fotosintɛsis nɔ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni fa fe fɛɛ ni ekɛbaa shi kɛyaa bulb lɛ mli.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking leaf sap, or by viruses transmitted by these pests as they feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa beni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my garden eggs and vegetable leaves droop in the afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ amɛmli leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: In the hot afternoon sun, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can drink it from the soil. The plant droops temporarily to reduce heat exposure, then recovers as the air cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei baagbee shi be kukuoo ko koni hulutsoo ni baa lɛ aba shi. Kɛkɛ lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ.

english: When maize leaves turn yellow from the center outward, it usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to build green leaves and grow big. It can also happen if heavy rains flood the soil and drown the roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ teŋgbɛ kɛtee kponɔgbɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni eha shishifãi lɛ shwie nu.

english: How do crops like cowpeas and groundnuts make my soil better for future crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmei haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts belong to the legume family. They have tiny nodules on their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil, leaving behind natural food for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii yɛ legume weku lɛ mli. Amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ eshishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ Shi adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need maximum sunlight to produce food. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they can catch full sunlight, which sends energy down to grow large tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la lɛ fɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Enɛ tsuɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛ bulb agboi akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cassava plants have lots of leaves but produce very small, thin tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: This usually happens when cassava is planted too close together or when the soil has too much nitrogen. The plant uses all its energy to grow leaves on top instead of feeding the roots below.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaaha shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my vegetables with dry grass or palm leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmei baai aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle aduawai ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground, which is called mulching, shields the soil from the hot sun so water does not evaporate quickly. It keeps the roots cool, prevents weeds from growing, and turns into good soil food as it rots.
ga: Mulching, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Bɔni afee ni nu akatsɔ oya Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ebafeɔ niyenii kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji egbo.

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering during hot spells.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the top funnels of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that lays eggs on maize leaves. The hatched caterpillars crawl into the central leaves where it is moist and tender to feed, destroying the plant's growing point if not treated.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmãa baa nɔ lɛ. Kplukai ni efɔ lɛ shwieɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ he ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ blɛoo ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ lɛ. Enɛ baafite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ.

english: Wrinkled or curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap under the leaves, or spreading a plant virus that deforms new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni egbɔjɔ loo ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo tsei amli helai ni haa baai heei ni daraa lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ehiii lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the exact same nutrients from the dirt every year and allows pests and diseases that target maize to build up in the soil. Rotating crops keeps the soil healthy and balanced.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ He kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees drop their flowers before turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani amɛbatsɔmɔɔ cacao ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they experience stress, such as severe dry weather during the Harmattan season or a lack of water and nutrients needed to support growing pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi, tamɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi waa yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli. aloo nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ ni bɛ

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and delicate roots that burn easily under intense sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains nearby creates a living umbrella that protects the young cocoa and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Shade tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa hulutsoo baa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ.

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots and leaves crowd each other out. They end up fighting over the same small amount of sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving no plant with enough energy to make big cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Akɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ miimɔ amɛhe. Amɛwuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii fioo ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni amɛshiii tso ko ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient found in healthy soil or fertilizer that helps plants build strong, green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni anaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji.

english: Why is it a mistake for me to apply fertilizer right before a heavy rain storm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ejaaa akɛ mawo fɔmɔ kotoku dani ahum ni naa wa aba lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes the top layer of soil away, carrying your expensive fertilizer into rivers and ditches before your crop's roots ever get a chance to drink it in.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ o-fertilizer ni jara wa lɛ aya faai kɛ ŋmeii amli. Dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baaná hegbɛ ni amɛnu lɛ,

english: Animal manure acts like food for the soil. It slowly releases nutrients over time and improves the soil structure so it can hold water longer during dry spells.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ fiofio. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground when the rainy season gets too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Excess water fills up all the air spaces in the soil, effectively suffocating the roots. Without oxygen, harmless soil fungi turn destructive and cause the cassava tubers to decay.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ he fɛɛ he ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛji oxygen bɛ Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni bɛ awui lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Extreme heat causes stress to tomato plants, making pollen sticky so it cannot fertilize the flower. When flowers are not fertilized, the plant drops them to save energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ he waa aahu akɛ enyɛŋ ekɛ fɔfɔi lɛ abɔ. Kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ fɔfɔi ko Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and gives crop-specific pests a permanent home to multiply in your field.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. Ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ naa shia ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfɔ yɛ oŋmɔji amli daa.

english: Weeds are wild native plants that naturally adapted to survive harsh local conditions, allowing them to absorb soil moisture and fertilizers much faster than domesticated farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛheɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ shia lɛ amli lɛ.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat holes in the centers of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars, often called Fall Armyworms, hatch from eggs laid on the leaves by adult moths and feed on the softest, newest leaves growing in the center of the corn stalk.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ amɛ Fall Armyworms lɛ, fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii kɛwoɔ baai anɔ lɛ amli. ni oye baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo fe fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my maize farm turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This is usually a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the essential food plants need to grow green and strong. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted animal manure will help restore the green color and boost plant growth.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests if I plant maize on the same field every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows specific crop pests to build up. Rotating your crops with legumes like cowpea or groundnut puts vital nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsake onibii lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Which direction should the buds point when I am planting cassava stems?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu ŋmei tso lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ?

english: The small buds on the stem where leaves sprout must point upwards toward the sky. Planting cassava stems upside down forces the new shoots to waste energy growing downward before turning up, leading to weak plants and poor root yield.
ga: Esa akɛ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ tsei ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ anɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ haa ŋmeii heei lɛ ahewalɛ babaoo fiteɔ dani amɛdaraa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu ehiii.

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves off the ground to catch as much sunlight as possible, which helps the plant produce food to grow large tubers underground. Staking also keeps leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ niyenii ni ekɛbaakwɛ bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu buɔ tsei ahe tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures every single plant gets enough food and space to develop big, healthy fruits or grains.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ náa niyenii kɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo aduawai loo ŋmaa wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping their flowers before pod development?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani amɛmiifee pods lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often drop when the tree suffers from water stress or when sap-sucking pests like mirids attack them. Maintaining proper shade trees, keeping the soil moist, and managing pests early will help the flowers stay on and grow into pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu he haomɔ miigba tso lɛ naa. aloo kɛ́ kooloi ni yeɔ nu, tamɔ pollen lɛ tutua amɛ. Kwɛmɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ jogbaŋŋ Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni akwɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking leaf sap, or by a plant virus transmitted by insects. Controlling these pests early using neem water or recommended sprays prevents further curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni kooloi kɛbaa lɛ amli Kudɔmɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra Neem nu loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant or uneven watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist through regular watering and mulching helps the plant move calcium into the fruit properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ tsei amli loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ calcium lɛ yaa aduawai lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly and produce poor yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo ni amɛmiiwo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops by stealing the water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients from the soil. Clearing weeds early in the season makes sure your crops get all the nutrients they need to grow fast.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛjuɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya.

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, protects the soil from hot sun, keeps moisture in the ground longer, prevents weeds from sprouting, and gradually breaks down into rich organic food for your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ niyenii ni jara wa kɛha onibii.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them acts as a protective shield, keeping the soil moist and preventing the tender leaves from burning.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baatsu nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ mɔ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni otsi baai bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkashã.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my maize seeds when the rains are no longer regular?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ dɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the ground has received a few steady, soaking rains rather than planting after the very first light shower. This ensures the soil holds enough moisture for the seeds to germinate without drying out during short dry spells.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ anɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni edɔ fioo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ahum lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ yɛ be kukuoo ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and showing yellow patterns?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting improved, disease-resistant cassava stem cuttings protects your farm from this infection.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni helai nyɛɔ eyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hela nɛɛ he.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans together with my maize on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans naturally absorb nitrogen from the air and put it into the ground. This enriches the soil, giving your maize the nutrients it needs to grow strong without relying entirely on expensive fertilizers.
ga: Agbɛnɛ hu, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ baa nii. Enɛ haa oŋmei lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa nɔ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat or a lack of water. Keeping the soil covered with organic mulch and watering regularly helps the plant retain its flowers to form healthy fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ he. Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ organic mulch kwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to weak stalks and small ears. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to produce a full harvest.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ toi bibii. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛkpaa ekpamɔ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds away from my yam mounds as soon as they appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mijieɔ jwɛi kakadaji kɛjɛɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji amɛje kpo pɛ?

english: Weeds steal water and plant food from the soil much faster than yams can. Removing them early ensures that all the nutrients in the soil go directly into making your yam tubers grow big and heavy.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya kwraa fe ŋmeii. Ni ajieɔ lɛ mra Enɛ baaha niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aha o-sweet potato tubers lɛ adara ni amɛhe afee mlɛo tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do I need to make high soil mounds or ridges when planting my yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋmeii beni miduɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yams require loose, soft soil so their roots can expand easily into long, thick tubers. High mounds also allow excess rain to drain away so the yams do not sit in standing water and rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia sweet potato. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ alɛɛ mli oya ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii kakadaji ni mli tse. Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ hu haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Enɛ ji koni ŋmeii lɛ akatara nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli ni amɛkafite.

english: Why do my tomato leaves roll up tightly into tubes during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the plant's natural way of saving water and protecting itself from intense heat. Adding compost around the root zone helps the soil hold moisture longer so the plant stays cool.
ga: Baai ni atsiɔ lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ nu he ni ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kompost ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ hiɔ shi ni eyɛ fɛ̃i.

english: Why do my harvested grains get full of small holes and turn to powder after sitting in my store room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni etsɔ powda beni mita mi nitoohe lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Insects called weevils attack grain that still contains moisture. Thoroughly drying your harvested grain in the sun until it is completely hard before sealing it in airtight bags stops these pests from destroying your stored food.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ tutuaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lolo lɛ. Dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ ni agbiɔ yɛ hulu la mli kɛyashi ebaawa kwraa dani akɛwo vacuum kotokui amli. Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akafite niyenii ni ato lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when there are no bigger plants grown next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni cacao tsei ko bɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate direct sunlight because their leaves burn easily and lose water quickly. Growing fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides a protective umbrella that keeps the microclimate humid and guards the seedlings until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya ni nu lɛ hu sɛɛ foɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsĩ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo lɛ mli lɛ naa, ni ebu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaashɛ amɛdalɛ he.

english: Tomato flowers often drop without forming fruit when air temperatures become excessively high or when the plant experiences extreme dry spells. Keeping the soil consistently moist during heat stress helps the plant retain its flowers and set healthy tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ ni naa wa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔi amli ni ehaa tomato lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize crop turning yellow starting from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ eshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tip indicates a lack of nitrogen in the soil, an essential nutrient maize needs to grow green leaves. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps restore vibrant green leaf growth and supports strong stalk development.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa haa niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ. Nitrogen ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni baa lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua tso lɛ yibii ni wa lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall with thick green leaves but producing very thin roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ miida ni eyɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli tse lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to spend all their energy building tall stems and lush foliage instead of swelling their roots. A balanced soil nutrient environment encourages energy to move downward into root enlargement.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shishifãi ni efuu lɛ najiaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ja lɛ woɔ hewalɛ hewalɛ koni eya shi koni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ alɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn completely black and dry up while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ kwraa ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This behavior is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in dark, damp, and unpruned farms. Removing affected pods immediately and pruning extra tree branches lets in sunlight and air movement, stopping the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ subaŋ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli ewo duŋ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli, ni ŋmei bɛ mli lɛ amli. Jiemɔ ŋmeii ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ofolɔ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Koni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to sprout after I sow them in dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seeds require adequate soil moisture to signal them to wake up and extend their first roots. Planting in overly dry soil keeps the seed dormant or causes it to dry out and die before it can break through the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛtsɔɔ akɛ amɛte shi ni amɛkwɛ̃ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ aya wɔɔ. aloo ni eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi dani amɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my harvested cocoa beans turn moldy after I put them into storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa yibii ni mikpa lɛ mli ewo ŋmɔtɔ beni mikɛwo kotoku mli ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fresh cocoa beans carry heavy moisture inside them after harvest. If they are bagged before proper fermentation and thorough sun-drying, trapped moisture creates ideal conditions for internal fungal mold to grow and ruin bean quality.
ga: Cocoa yibii heei lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsii yɛ mli beni akpa amɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ awo kotoku mli dani atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Fɛ̃i ni amɔmɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ adara ni amɛfite ŋmeii lɛ ahilɛ-kɛhamɔ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves roll inward and droop during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves inward is a self-defense mechanism plantains use to reduce leaf surface exposure to direct sun, minimizing the amount of water lost through evaporation until cooler evening temperatures arrive.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛyaa mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mɔ he ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ akashɛ baa lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ baa shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce smaller peppers when wild grass grows close to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ pepper bibii beni koo mli jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds actively compete with crop plants for water, sunlight, and ground nutrients. Clearing grass away early ensures your pepper plants get the full share of nutrients needed to develop larger, healthy peppers.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha o-pepper tsei lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná peppers wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do stored maize grains develop small circular holes and dusty powder inside the bag after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ yɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ? Ni sũ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: These holes are made by grain weevils that bore into kernels to feed and lay eggs. Ensuring grain is dried to safe moisture levels before sealing in airtight storage bags prevents weevil larvae from damaging the crop.
ga: Dumɔwui amli ŋmeii ni tsɔɔ dumɔwui amli koni amɛye nii ni amɛwo ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni feɔ buji nɛɛ. Kɛ́ akwɛ koni ŋmaa lɛ egbi kɛyashɛ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ dani akɛwo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii ni ji weevil larvae lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have wide leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a cry for food. It means your maize lacks nitrogen nutrient in the soil or the soil is too flooded with water, preventing the roots from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji niyenii he foomɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ bɛ nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of the maize seeds I plant fail to grow out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds usually fail to sprout if they were damaged by insects during storage, planted too deep in the soil, or if the ground was too dry or flooded right after planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji kooloi fite amɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. adu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni adu lɛ.

english: How do I know which direction to put my cassava stems when planting them in the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole he ni esa akɛ okɛ o-cassava tso lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look closely at the small buds or 'eyes' on the stem cutting; they should point upwards toward the sky so the leaves can sprout upward easily while the roots grow downward into tubers.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ‘ŋmei’ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ amɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni baai lɛ adara oya yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ adara kɛya shi ni amɛfee bulb.

english: Yam plants are crawlers that need sunlight to make food. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground to catch maximum sunlight and stops the leaves from rotting.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji tsei ni shwereɔ ni hulu la he hiaa amɛ koni amɛye niyenii. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ená hulu la babaoo ni ekɛtsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my tomatoes turning black and soft while still growing on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo yɛ be mli ni edaa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant doesn't get a steady supply of water, which stops it from moving enough calcium into the growing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa. Enɛ haaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ aya tso yibii ni miida lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I grow maize on the exact same spot on my farm every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the soil of the specific nutrients that crop loves and allows insects and diseases that feed on that crop to multiply in the ground.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tsei lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ daa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni yeɔ tsei lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm; they steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops, leaving your main plants hungry and shaded.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Shi otso titri lɛ hɔmɔ kɛ hulutsoo.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting groundnuts or beans together with my other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ mikɛ mi tsei krokomɛi lɛ adu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts are natural soil improvers. They take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, which fertilizes the soil for neighboring crops.
ga: Nuts kɛ peanuts ji adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo. Amɛheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo koni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ akwɛ̃

english: Why should I avoid spraying pest chemicals on my crops during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Hot afternoon weather causes chemical sprays to evaporate quickly before working properly, and the combination of strong heat and chemicals can scorch and damage crop leaves.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya dani amɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Ni dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite tsei ahe baai.

english: Can I plant cashew trees in the heavy forest soil where my cocoa grows well?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cashew tso yɛ koo mli shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji lɛ nɔ he ni mi-kokoo lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ lɛ?

english: No, because cashew and cocoa thrive in very different environments. Cocoa needs wet, rich forest soils with shade, while cashew prefers well-drained, drier soils in open sunlight. Planting cashew in wet forest land can cause its roots to rot and die.
ga: Dabi, ejaakɛ cashews kɛ cocoa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei srɔtoi kwraa. Cocoa he miihia koo mli shikpɔŋ ni efɔ, ni baa nii kɛ hulutsoo. Shi kɛlɛ, cashews sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ yɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu cashew ŋmeii yɛ kooi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ agbo ni amɛgboi.

english: If I plant cashew and cocoa together on the same land, will they help each other grow?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu cashew kɛ cocoa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ani amɛbaaye amɛbua amɛhe ni amɛdu?

english: No, they will fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients. Cashew trees spread wide branches that block sunlight, which will starve young cocoa trees of light and eventually kill them.
ga: Dabi, amɛbaatswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Cashew tsei lɛ gbɛɔ amɛniji lɛ amɛshwãa babaoo koni amɛtsi hulu lɛ naa. Enɛ haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ la mli, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ egbeɔ amɛ.

english: How do I know if a tree crop is suitable for the climate in my area of Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso ko sa kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Crops show clear preferences for weather: crops like cocoa and coffee require high humidity and regular rainfall found in forest zones, whereas crops like cashew and shea thrive in drier transition and savanna zones with long sunny seasons.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsɔɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he suɔmɔi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ kookoo kɛ kɔfi biɔ hulutsoo babaoo kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa ni anaa yɛ kooi amli hei lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ cashew nuts kɛ shea shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsakemɔ kɛ savannah hei ni hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do some young crop seedlings wither and die quickly when I plant them in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei bibii komɛi shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ oya kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certain young plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that cannot drink water fast enough to balance what the hot sun bakes away. Without temporary shade crops to protect them, heat stress dries them out completely.
ga: Dumɔwui komɛi yɛ baai ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ anu nu oya bɔ ni sa koni ekɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ato he. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, dumɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli koni obu amɛhe. Heat haomɔ baaha amɛgbi kwraa.

english: How are cashew trees able to survive during the long dry season without drying up?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni cashew tso ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni egbiŋ?

english: Cashew trees develop a deep taproot system that reaches far under the ground to draw up underground water, allowing them to remain green and survive dry weather better than shallow-rooted crops.
ga: Cashew tsei lɛ feɔ taproot gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni yaa shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ ato. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to leave wide spaces between tree crops instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ kɛɛ wɔ akɛ wɔshi he ko ni da yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ

english: Wide spacing ensures that as trees mature, their root systems and leaf branches have enough space to gather water, soil food, and sunlight without crowding out and choking neighboring trees.
ga: Gbɛ ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ haa be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ, Tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ eniji lɛ náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛbua nu, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ hulu la naa ni amɛtsiii tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anaa ni amɛtsiii amɛ gbɛ.

english: Why do tree seeds need to be raised in nursery bags before I plant them directly on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ awo ŋmɔ mli dumɔwui amli dani adu awo saatso lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Seedlings in nursery bags are protected from harsh weather, heavy rain, and soil pests during their early fragile weeks, giving them a strong root base so they can survive transplanting onto the main field.
ga: Abuɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe yɛ amɛ shishijee otsii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shishitoo ni wa bɔni afee ni anyɛ adu amɛ kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my young trees turn yellow and drop off shortly after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi beni adu amɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a cry for help caused by root damage, overwatering in heavy clay soil, or severe shock from being moved from a shaded nursery straight into harsh sunlight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ bolɔɔ amɛbiɔ yelikɛbuamɔ ni shishifãi ni efite lɛ kɛbaa lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa mli fe nine loo shoofeemɔ ni naa wa ni jɛɔ ŋmɔ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli ni ajieɔ kɛyaa hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli baa.

english: Can I use the exact same fertilizer for my cashew trees that I use on my cocoa farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji amli lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii yɛ cashew tsei anɔ?

english: It is not recommended because each crop uses nutrients differently. Cocoa needs nutrients tailored for fruit pod development in moist soil, while cashew needs nutrients designed to encourage strong root development and flower production in dry conditions.
ga: Akɛ enɛ haaa ejaakɛ tsei srɔtoi kɛ niyenii srɔtoi tsuɔ nii. Cocoa biɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ koni aduawai ashishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, cashews biɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni afee koni eha shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ waa ni ewo fɔfɔi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with very few leaves when they are planted under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni eyɛ baai fioo ko pɛ kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: When plants do not get enough light, they stretch upward searching for the sun instead of growing thick trunks and healthy leafy branches, which leaves them weak and low-yielding.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ tsɔɔ ehe koni eyatao hulu lɛ. Mohu ɔ, e wa nɛ e peeɔ tso nɛ mi wa kɛ tso niji nɛ a he wa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin without producing big corncobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeee ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Planting maize seeds too close together makes the stalks compete heavily for sunlight and soil nutrients, causing them to stretch tall and weak instead of putting energy into forming large cobs.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo moŋ fe ni amɛaafite hewalɛ ni amɛkɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why is my plantain tree taking so long to produce a bunch of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani mi dumɔwui lɛ woɔ aduawai akui lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers need plenty of water, rich manure, and regular removal of extra shoots around the base so the main stem gets enough energy and strength to flower.
ga: Nu babaoo he miihia plantain ni nuɔ nu lɛ. ŋmeii babaoo kɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he daa bɔni afee ni tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafɔlɔ.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my pepper plants before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot, when the plant lacks steady water, or when there are not enough insects around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ nu daa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ bɛ

english: Yellowing and curling leaves on cassava usually mean the plant is infected by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies, or it is severely lacking nutrients and water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ yucca nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ emɔ tso lɛ. loo niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu ni faaa waa

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither and die when the hot harmattan season starts?
