ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni harmattha be ni mli edɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have shallow roots and tender leaves that burn easily under intense heat; without plantain trees or shade trees around to block the harsh dry wind and sun, they dry out quickly.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ la ni naa wa waa shishi lɛ. Kɛji akɛ dumɔwui loo tsei ni baatsi hulu lɛ naa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni mli egbi lɛ bɛ lɛ, ebaagbi oya.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my crops after I weed the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mijie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds produce thousands of hardy seeds that lie hidden in the soil ready to spout with rain, and their wild roots absorb moisture and nutrients much faster than cultivated farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ woɔ dumɔwui akpei abɔ ni wa ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni efee klalo akɛ nugbɔ lɛ baashwie nɔ. Ni amɛ adebɔɔ mli shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya kwraa fe tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why does my farmland soil become hard and cracked soon after the rains stop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli waa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ?

english: Soil turns hard and cracks when it has a high clay content and lacks decomposed plant material like compost or dry leaf mulch to help hold moisture and keep the ground loose.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fa babaoo. ni tsei ahe nibii ni fiteɔ tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaye abua ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni eha sũ lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ bɛ.

english: Should I water my vegetable crops early in the morning or during the hot sun at midday?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo mitsei lɛ nu leebi loo yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ mli?

english: Watering early in the morning allows crop roots to absorb moisture before heat sets in, whereas watering at midday causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before the plant can drink it.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa ŋmɔtɔ dani hulutsoo be lɛ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu yɛ shwane mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tso lɛ anu.

english: How do I know if my yam tubers under the ground are fully ripe to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato tubers ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Yams are ready for harvest when the leaves turn yellow and the main vines start drying up naturally at the end of the rainy season.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Ni wain tso titri lɛ jeɔ shishi egbiɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee.

english: Can I save seeds from the fresh tomatoes I buy at the market to plant on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ tomato hee ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Market tomatoes are often hybrid varieties, meaning seeds saved from them will likely grow into weak plants that produce very small or low-quality fruits compared to the original.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni akɛfee nɔ ko. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛtsɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii bibii waa loo ni ehiii kwraa kɛ akɛto blema tomato he.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect them from strong direct sunlight and heat. Without shade trees or food crops like plantains nearby, the hot sun burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil before their roots are strong enough.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hɔnɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much water for a long time, especially during heavy rains. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away so the underground tubers stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo be kakadaŋŋ. Titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli Dumɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my crops after the first rain falls?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi tsei akwɛmɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the soil stays consistently moist after two or three steady rains. Planting right after the very first light rain is risky because a dry spell might follow and kill the newly sprouted seeds.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ fioo sɛɛ Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be baanyɛ anyiɛ sɛɛ ni efite dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need sunlight to make food for their growing tubers. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet soil, giving them more sunlight and protecting them from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la koni amɛha amɛ bulbs ni miida lɛ niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa hulu la babaoo baa, ni ebuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ helai ahe.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth. It can also happen if the soil is too waterlogged, making it hard for roots to breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaamu.

english: Tomato flowers often fall off when temperatures become too high or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly wet. Extreme heat prevents the flowers from pollinating properly to set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa lɛ nɔ kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ trukaa lɛ nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haaa fɔfɔii lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛwo yibii.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my maize leaves and powdery dirt inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ muji ni tamɔ powder ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that hides inside the growing point of the maize plant. Catching them early and applying organic treatments like neem extract or recommended insecticides can protect your farm.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa titri ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni kɛ ehe teeɔ hei ni ŋmei tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli tamɔ neem mli nu loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ atsu nii lɛ baanyɛ abu oŋmɔ lɛ he.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the same nutrients from the soil every year and allows crop-specific pests to multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts rebuilds soil fertility naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni etswaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ emaa shi ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly and stay small when weeds are around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo ni amɛfee bibii be mli ni jwɛi ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors—they steal the light, water, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Keeping your fields clear during the early growing stages gives your crops full access to food.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ—amɛjuɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu nii yɛ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ oha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli tse yɛ shishijee be mli ni okwɛ̃ɔ lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo.

english: Is it okay if I spread chemical fertilizer on my crops when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba mli kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Applying fertilizer to bone-dry soil can burn plant roots and waste your money, as plants need soil moisture to dissolve and absorb the nutrients. Always apply fertilizer when the soil is damp, ideally after a light rain.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wu yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni efite shika. Enɛ ji akɛ, tsei lɛ taoɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛtsɔ mli ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ fioo sɛɛ.

english: How do I know the exact amount of fertilizer to give my maize plants so I don't ruin them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ mi-abele tso lɛ mli lɛ falɛ pɔtɛɛ? koni akafite lɛ

english: Fertilizer acts like targeted medicine for crops; too little leaves them weak, while too much will burn the roots. Applying a specific measured amount, such as one bottle cap of NPK fertilizer per plant placed a few centimeters away from the stem, gives the crop just the right amount of nourishment to grow strong without damage.
ga: Fertilizer tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsofa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Nɔ fioo tsɔ baaha amɛgbɔjɔ. Yɛ be mli ni nɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ baashã shishifãi lɛ, kɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ni asusu he pɔtɛɛ atsu nii, tamɔ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso fɛɛ tso mli lɛ tsɛnsi kome, ni akɛtoɔ sɛntimitai fioo komɛi pɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ ana niyenii ni sa koni tsei lɛ adara ni amɛfiteee.

english: Maize takes up a lot of nitrogen from the soil during its growth. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have roots that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and return it to the dirt, naturally restoring fertility for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Enɛ baaye abua ni aku sɛɛ aha adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ aba kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Is it better for me to water my tomato crops early in the morning or late in the evening?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ?

english: It is best to water early in the morning so the plant roots absorb moisture before the afternoon heat sets in. Watering late in the evening leaves moisture sitting on the leaves overnight, which creates an ideal environment for fungal diseases to spread.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha tso lɛ nu leebi koni eha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani shwane mli latsaa lɛ aba.Kɛ́ oowo nu gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ahi tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ nyɔɔŋ kome. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ baa.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients during the flowering stage. Keeping the soil consistently moist and applying nutrient-rich fertilizer helps the flowers stay attached and form healthy peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ dɔlɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be ni akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ babaoo fataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava stems very close together so I can fit more on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni manyɛ madu babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the plants compete underground for nutrients, water, and sunlight. Giving each stem proper spacing allows the roots enough room to swell into large, heavy tubers instead of producing many thin, unusable ones.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha shishifãi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee yitsei babaoo ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni anyɛɛɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants turn yellow and droop when planted in the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, strong sunlight and hot winds. They need temporary shade, often provided by planting plantains nearby, to protect them until their root systems grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be kukuoo ko. ni bei pii lɛ, aduɔ kɛtsɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ nɔ Koni abu he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ ahe baawa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ adamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Why do fall armyworms seem to damage my maize leaves mostly overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni fall flukes lɛ fiteɔ mi-corn baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo nyɔɔŋ kome mli lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms avoid the hot sun during the daytime by hiding deep inside the central funnel of the plant. They come out to feed in the cool of the night, which is why inspecting crops early in the morning or applying treatments late in the afternoon works best.
ga: Autumn cutworms tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ he kɛtsɔ amɛhe ni amɛhiɛɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ faa lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbatao niyenii gbɛkɛ. Enɛ hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii amli kwɛmɔ leebi loo tsofafeemɔ shwane mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How early in the season do I need to clear weeds from my maize farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Weeds must be cleared within the first three to six weeks after planting. Young maize seedlings are weak early on, and if weeds steal their water and light during this critical growth window, the final crop yield drops significantly.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ kɛyashi enumɔ mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Abele dumɔwui bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ yɛ shishijee mli. Ni kɛji jwɛi ju nu kɛ la yɛ nɛkɛ dalɛ be ni he hiaa nɛɛ mli lɛ, Naagbee ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Why do some of my planted seeds fail to sprout out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are buried too deep in the dirt, if the soil lacks moisture, or if soil insects attack them before they sprout. Planting seeds at a shallow depth—roughly twice the seed's size—and keeping the soil damp ensures proper germination.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ. loo kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa lɛ dani enyɛɔ ekwɛ̃ɔ. Dumɔ dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ—aaafee dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ toi enyɔ—ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava is typically mature between 9 and 12 months after planting. You will know it is ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and the soil surrounding the base of the main stem begins to crack from the expanding tubers below.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaale akɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ kɛjɛɔ bulb ni miigbɛ eshwa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ he.

english: Why shouldn't I put three or four maize seeds into the exact same hole when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa etɛ loo ejwɛ woɔ bu kome mli kɛ́ midu?

english: Putting too many seeds in one hole creates heavy competition among the seedlings for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in thin, weak stalks with very small or empty maize cobs instead of strong plants with full cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ kɛ akaŋshii ni naa wa baa dumɔwui ateŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmãa bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa. Mohu ɔ, e ji tso nɛ he wa nɛ e hɛ mi hyi.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant all my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mawo oshara mli akɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often a 'false start' followed by a hot, dry spell. If seeds germinate after that initial rain and experience dry soil for weeks, the young roots will dry out and die before the real rainy season begins.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ji ‘amale shishijee’ ni be ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ ni akɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ otsii babaoo. Shishifãi bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei kakadaji ama shi lɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to sunlight to create food for the growing underground tuber. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, boosting sunlight exposure and preventing leaf diseases caused by wet soil.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ha hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ ni otsi foliar helai ni shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow while the rest of the plant is green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni baai ni eshwɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green and grow leaves. The plant is moving its limited nitrogen from older leaves to feed newer top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛbaai lɛ akwɛ̃. Tsei miitsi nitrogen fioo ko kɛmiijɛ baai momo lɛ amli koni amɛyaha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have tiny root nodules that capture nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into soil fertilizer. Planting them alongside or after maize naturally feeds the soil without buying chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi bibii. No yeɔ ebuaa ni emɔɔ nitrogen gas ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ehaa efeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa masɛi loo esɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my pepper fruits turning black and soft before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni eyɛ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition, known as blossom-end rot, happens when the plant cannot absorb enough calcium from the soil, which is frequently caused by irregular watering or sudden dry spells during fruit development.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo ŋmɔlɔ ni baa trukaa yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off the extra small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Ajie nɔ krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water, food, and energy from the main mother plant. Removing all but one or two strong suckers ensures the main plantain tree gets enough food to produce a big, heavy bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ juɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, no haa ŋmeii titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the ground if I leave them in the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ sũ mli kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ sũ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli lɛ?

english: Excessive water fills the tiny air pockets in the soil, preventing cassava roots from breathing. The trapped water invites soil fungi that quickly cause the underground tubers to rot and turn watery.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ, ni no haaa ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ amu. Nu ni amɔmɔ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nine ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ nu.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling tightly upward and causing the whole plant to stunt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho kɛmiiya ŋwɛi ni amɛmiiha tso muu lɛ fɛɛ miigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is caused by a virus usually transmitted by tiny sap-sucking insects called whiteflies. Once infected, the plant struggles to transport food internally, causing leaves to roll and growth to stop.
ga: Virus ko ni bei pii lɛ koolooi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Kɛji hela lɛ emɔ Tsei lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkɛ niyenii awo mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop most of their young flowers without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi bibii lɛ ateŋ babaoo shi ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa baaa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they suffer from water stress, extreme heat, or damage from pests like mirids (capsids). It can also happen if there are not enough tiny insects (midges) in the farm to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji nu mli haomɔ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nibii ni fiteɔ nii tamɔ mirids (capsids) lɛ yeɔ amɛ awui. Enɛ baanyɛ aba mli hu kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii (teŋgbɛ nibii) ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted alongside them to protect their leaves from sunburn and to keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni abu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he, ni koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why is my maize crop turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, or that the farm has too much standing water which stops the roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ kpaa mumɔ kɛ niyenii yeli.

english: Why do I see small holes and caterpillar waste inside the top leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ yɛ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli.

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the central growing part of the maize plant and eat the tender leaves before they can fully unfold.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ fã ni miida lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii dani amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo kwraa lɛ.

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which results in thin, weak stalks and very small corn cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibii waa baa.

english: Most cassava varieties in Ghana are ready between 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the ground around the base of the stem starts to crack.
ga: Cassava henɔi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ ateŋ babaoo efee klalo kɛha dumɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishi bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Staking holds yam leaves up toward the sunlight so they can make food for the plant, which leads to bigger and healthier yam tubers underground.
ga: Ni aaamɔ ŋmɔtɔ baai lɛ amli kɛyashi hulu la mli koni akɛfee niyenii aha ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do flowers fall off my tomato plants without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when watering is irregular, or when small insects attack the flowers before they can form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ daa Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tutuaa fɔfɔi dani amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites, or viruses spread by whiteflies that weaken the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo hela ko ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni haa tsei gbɔjɔɔ.

english: What makes animal manure good for my vegetable farm compared to planting directly without it?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɔshi nibii hi kɛha mi-vegeduary ŋmɔ lɛ? Kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni aduɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni akɛ kooloi ashishifã tsuuu nii lɛ he?

english: Dried animal manure adds essential nutrients to the soil slowly, improves the soil's ability to hold water during dry spells, and helps crops build strong root systems.
ga: Nibii ni egbi lɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fiofio. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtswaa shishifãi ni mli wa

english: The first rain of the year is often followed by a heatwave or dry spell; planting too early means seeds will sprout and then wither from lack of steady water before the rainy season fully starts.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ latsaa loo nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ mra tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaagbo yɛ nu ni bɛ daa lɛ hewɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi kwraa.

english: Do I really need to put chemical fertilizer on my farm to grow big yams, or can yam grow fine without it?
ga: Ehe miihia ni mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ afata miŋmɔ lɛ he koni manyɛ makwɛ sweet potatoes wuji diɛŋtsɛ. Aloo ani sweet potatoes baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fataaa he?

english: Yams can grow without chemical fertilizer if your soil is naturally rich or if you use good compost and animal manure. However, in poor soils, adding the right fertilizer gives the crop essential nutrients like potassium, which helps the yam produce larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fataaa he kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa loo kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai tsu nii. Shi, yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium, ni yeɔ ebuaa sweet potatoes ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to put tall sticks for yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni sɛɛkwɛlɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko akwɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need plenty of sunlight to make food for the plant. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they get maximum sun and fresh air, which prevents diseases and helps the plant build bigger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni eha tso lɛ niyenii. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ he babaoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai baaa tso lɛ nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni efeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do some of my planted seed yams rot in the soil before they even sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ lɛ ekomɛi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ po lɛ?

english: Seed yams rot mainly because of waterlogged soil, excessive heat, or fungal infections entering cut pieces. Planting in well-drained mounds and treating cut seeds with wood ash or fungicide before planting helps protect them.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ babaoo ejaakɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. la ni mli edɔ fe nine Aloo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko yɛ fãi ni afo lɛ amli. Kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ mli, ni akɛ tso sũ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii tsuɔ dumɔwui ni afo lɛ ahe nii dani adu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe.

english: What is the difference between using animal manure and store-bought chemical fertilizer on my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli kɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ teŋ?

english: Animal manure feeds the soil over a long time and improves its ability to hold water, while chemical fertilizer feeds the plant directly and quickly. Using manure builds your soil for future years, whereas chemical fertilizer only supplies quick nutrients for the current season.
ga: Manure haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaa nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu lɛ yaa hiɛ. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ niyenii tɛ̃ɛ kɛ oya lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa oya kɛha be ni wɔyɔɔ mli nɛɛ pɛ.

english: Will adding double the recommended amount of fertilizer make my crops grow faster and produce more?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ shii enyɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaha mitsei lɛ adara oya ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: No, putting too much fertilizer can burn the roots of your crops and kill them. It can also cause the plant to grow too many leaves while producing small roots or fruits.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni egbe amɛ. Ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ hu aná baai babaoo yɛ be mli ni eyɛ shishifãi bibii loo aduawai.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer to my crop so it doesn't waste?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni amɛkafite?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist and the plant already has roots to absorb it, usually a few weeks after germination. Applying it in dry soil or right before a heavy downpour will either burn the plant or wash the nutrients away.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tso lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni baanyɛ aŋɔ lɛ momo lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii fioo komɛi beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ loo dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ebaashã tso lɛ loo ebaafɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or the soil has too much standing water which chokes the roots and stops them from taking up food.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo, ni miigba shishifãi lɛ anaa ni etsĩ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛye niyenii.

english: Why do my yam tubers end up small and bent instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers become bent and small when the soil in your mounds is too hard, stony, or shallow. Yams need loose, deep, soft soil so the tuber can expand downward without obstruction.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ bibii kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa tsɔ, tɛi yɔɔ mli, loo ekɔɔɔ tsɔ. Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛya shi ni nɔ ko akatsi amɛ gbɛ.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every year if I keep planting the same crop on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ feɔ bibioo daa afi kɛji mitee nɔ midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil repeatedly and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating your crops gives the soil time to replenish its nutrients.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ daa be lɛ baajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shii abɔ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ woɔ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it possible for me to farm completely organically without chemical inputs and still get a profitable harvest?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ mafee okwaayeli yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni mikɛ tsofai tsuuu nii, ni maná nibii ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he lolo?

english: Yes, organic farming can produce high yields, but it requires rich soil preparation using compost, green manure, crop rotation, and good weed control to match the crop yields of chemical farming.
ga: Hɛɛ, okwaayeli ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo. Shi esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ asaa shikpɔŋ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. kɛ jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛɔ tsofafeemɔ mli okwaayeli mli lɛ akpã gbee.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as shade umbrellas, keeping the cocoa seedlings cool and moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha kookoo dumɔwui lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I plant beans or groundnuts together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa adu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Beans and groundnuts naturally pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer for maize, helping it grow stronger without using up all the soil's nutrients.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmãa lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni edaa waa ni ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ efooo.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow and curl when the crop is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen or when it is suffering from drought. Adding fertilizer or animal manure restores the nutrients needed for green leaf growth.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo kɛji tso lɛ na hɔmɔ. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my groundnut leaves fold together in the afternoon when the weather gets hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants fold their leaves to reduce water loss through evaporation during the hottest part of the day. It is a natural defense mechanism to conserve moisture until the weather cools down.
ga: Peanut tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni nu ni fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ lɛ aba shi. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow bent and small instead of long and thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow deformed when the soil is too hard, stony, or compacted. Building tall, soft soil mounds allows the root tubers to expand easily straight downward into heavy, nutrient-rich soil.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ, eyɛ tɛi, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Gɔŋ ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni afee lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli oya.

english: Why do I need to plant cassava stem cuttings at an angle instead of straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmei niji yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni adu amɛ shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a 45-degree angle helps roots spread out properly at an optimal depth for absorbing moisture and nutrients, while making the tubers easier to harvest later.
ga: Kasava ni afo lɛ ni aduɔ yɛ 45-degree angle mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni sa jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛjie ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaakpa ŋmeii lɛ yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without fruiting when daytime temperatures become too high, when the soil dries out completely, or when bees are absent to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni yibii bɛ mli kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni ŋmeii bɛ ni baawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii

english: Why are my pepper plants producing small green leaves but no flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi fɔfɔi bɛ he lɛ?

english: Pepper plants produce lush leaves instead of flowers when they receive too much nitrogen fertilizer. High nitrogen encourages leaf growth at the expense of flower and fruit development.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ woɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ kɛ́ amɛná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo lɛ haa baai lɛ daraa ni ehaa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai lɛ daraa.

english: Why is it harmful to plant maize on the same piece of land season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously in the same spot drains the same nutrients from the soil every year and allows pests like fall armyworms to build up in the soil, leading to weaker harvests over time.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ daa yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ armyworms ni egbee shi lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why are there small green bugs on the undersides of my cabbage leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yɔɔ lɛ? Yɛ kaabeji baai lɛ ashishi?

english: Those tiny insects are aphids, which gather under leaves to feed on plant sap and hide from direct sunlight. Spraying them early with a light neem tree oil solution keeps them from ruining the leaves.
ga: Nakai kooloi bibii lɛ ji aphids. Amɛbuaa amɛhe naa yɛ baai ashishi koni amɛye tsei amli nu ni amɛtee amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Neem tso mli fɔ ni ashwieɔ nɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ebaatsi baa lɛ naa koni ekafite.

english: How can I tell if my coconut is ready to harvest for drinking water versus harvesting for dried flesh?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa kɛha nu ni anuɔ loo kɛha loo ni egbi ni akpa?

english: Coconut trees produce fruit with different uses at different stages. When the nut is smooth and bright green, it is filled with sweet drinking water. If you leave it on the tree until it turns brown and dry, the water inside shrinks and thickens into hard white coconut meat used for oil or food.
ga: Kokoo tsei woɔ yibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ fãi srɔtoi amli. Kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, akɛ nu ni anuɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔlɔ ewo mli lɛ woɔ mli. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ kɛyashi ebaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi lɛ, Nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ni wa ni yɔɔ futafuta ni akɛtsuɔ nii akɛ fɔ loo niyenii.

english: How long can harvested whole coconuts stay fresh before they spoil?
ga: Be enyiɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani amɛfite?

english: Mature brown coconuts with intact husks can stay good for several months if kept in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Fresh green drinking coconuts, however, lose their sweet water quality within a week or two after harvest.
ga: Kokoo ni eda ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi nyɔji babaoo kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi. Shi kɛlɛ, yɛ he ni hulu la kpɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ŋmeii ni anuɔ ehee lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ otsi kome loo enyɔ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Can I use empty coconut husks around my crops to help them grow better during dry seasons?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ abɔle he. Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Yes, placing dry coconut husks around the base of your crops acts as mulch. The husks act like natural sponges that soak up water, hold moisture in the soil, cool the crop roots, and slow down water evaporation under strong heat.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii ni egbi wo otsei lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaatsu nii akɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli. Omɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli sponji, ni ekɛ nu shwieɔ shi. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fɛ̃i ahi tse lɛ shishifãi amli ni ehaa nu lɛ mli latsaa baa shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi

english: How often should I water my coconut seedlings during the dry season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ afɔ ŋmei tsei anɔ nu yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Young coconut seedlings need steady moisture to establish strong roots. Water them two to three times a week during dry months, giving each plant enough water to soak deep into the soil around the base rather than just wetting the surface.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ hia nu ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. Nu shii 2-3 yɛ otsi mli yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle eshishi lɛ he lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, moŋ fe ni eeeha eshishigbɛ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛkɛ.

english: Why do some of my young coconut trees take much longer to produce fruit than others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ekomɛi heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Different coconut varieties grow at different speeds. Dwarf coconut varieties can start producing fruit in three to four years, while Tall varieties take six to ten years. Fruit production also slows down if trees are planted too close together and have to fight for light and soil nutrients.
ga: Kokooi srɔtoi baakwɛ̃ yɛ oyaiyeli srɔtoi amli Kokooi ni kɛlɛ lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3-4 mli, yɛ be mli ni kookoi ni kɛlɛ lɛ heɔ afii 6-10. Yibii ni anáa lɛ hu baa shi kɛji akɛ adu tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛná la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Can I plant vegetables or food crops between my young coconut trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu aduawai loo niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ mi ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, you can intercrop food crops like cassava, maize, or beans between young coconut trees while they are small. This makes good use of space and sunshine, and legumes like beans can even add beneficial nutrients back into the soil to help the coconut trees grow.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii ateŋ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ. Gbɛ nɛɛ kɛ ŋwɛi kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛyeɔ ebuaa bo. Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii baanyɛ amɛkɛ niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ aku sɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eye ebua ŋmei tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why are the leaves on my coconut palm turning yellow and the young fruits falling off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni aduawai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves and falling fruit are often signs of diseases like Lethal Yellowing or a lack of key soil nutrients like potassium. Strong heat and dry spells can also cause the tree to drop young nuts early to save its own strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ aduawai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji hela he okadi, tamɔ baa ŋmɔŋ hela loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ potassium. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulutsoo be baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ ajie ŋmeii bibii mra. koni ehiɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehewalɛ mli

english: What kind of fertilizer should I give my crops to make them produce more fruit?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ maha koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: Crops need balanced plant food. Nitrogen helps leaves grow green and strong, Phosphorus builds healthy roots, and Potassium helps trees produce bigger, sweeter fruits. Adding animal manure or well-rotted compost around the base also improves soil health naturally.
ga: Tsei he miihia tsei niyenii ni ja. Nitrogen haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Fosforo haa shishifãi ni mli wa baa. Ni potassium yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii wuji ni ŋɔɔ. Kooloo ŋmei loo ŋmei ni egbo ni akɛwoɔ shishitoo lɛ he lɛ hu haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ yaa hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my crops drop many of their flowers before any fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho fɔfɔi babaoo dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Crops naturally produce more flowers than they can support as full fruit. However, dropping too many flowers usually happens when the plant experiences water stress, extreme heat, or damage from small insects feeding on the soft blossoms.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua kɛji amɛwo fɔfɔi babaoo. Shi kɛlɛ, bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi babaoo ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na nu mli haomɔ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo kooloi bibii ni yeɔ fɔfɔi bibii lɛ efite amɛ.

english: How do I sprout a mature coconut nut to grow a new tree on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ madu ŋmei tso ni eda koni makwɛ tsei heei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Choose a fully mature, brown coconut that still has water sloshing inside. Lay it partially buried on its side in moist, shaded soil, and within a few weeks, a fresh green shoot will break through the husk and root into the ground.
ga: Halamɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ shi nu yɛ mli lolo lɛ. Fuu ekomɛi yɛ amɛsɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Ni yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli lɛ, tsei eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains to block the intense heat, the sun scorches the leaves, turning them yellow and stopping the plant from growing.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo loo dumɔwui ni baatsi dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ naa lɛ bɛ lɛ Hulu lɛ baashã baai lɛ. Etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa tso lɛ dalɛ

english: During the Harmattan, dry winds and hot weather dry out the soil quickly. Cocoa trees drop their leaves naturally to save water and protect themselves from dying of drought until the rains come back.
ga: Yɛ harmattan beaŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hɔmɔ he kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why should I cut off the small extra branches growing on the main stem of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kookoo tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: These extra shoots, often called water sprouts or chupons, steal water and plant food away from the rest of the tree. Removing them helps the tree direct its energy into producing big, healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi nɛɛ akɛ nu ŋmeii loo chupon ŋmeii. Ejuɔ nu ni eduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: When trees are planted too close, their roots compete for plant food in the soil and their branches block air and light from each other. This results in weak trees that produce very few pods.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tso shishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni jɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ he akaŋ. ni tsei aniji tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds around my young cocoa seedlings slow down their growth?
ga: No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle Mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ miiba shi lɛ.

english: Weeds grow quickly and steal the water, sunlight, and natural soil food that your young seedlings need. Clearing weeds around the base of the cocoa plant lets it feed properly and grow faster.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he hiaa otsei bibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ajiemɔ Cacao shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enáa niyenii ni sa ni edaa oya.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads in wet, damp weather. Too much shade and low airflow keep moisture on the pods, creating the perfect conditions for the disease to spread.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Hulu la ni fa babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni eyaaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ baamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni yeɔ emuu baa kɛha helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: What causes the branches of my cocoa tree to swell up and stop bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-kookoo niji lɛ miifu ni amɛmiikpa yibiiwoo?

english: Swollen branches are a sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, which is carried from tree to tree by tiny insects called mealybugs. The virus weakens the tree from the inside, reducing yield and eventually killing the plant.
ga: Niji ni efuu lɛ ji Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus lɛ he okadi, ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ mealybugs lɛ kɛbaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ. Virus lɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ kɛjɛɔ emli. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ egbeɔ tso lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers drop off without forming any small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Flowers often drop if insects like tiny midge flies are not present to pollinate them, or if the tree is under stress from a lack of water or nutrients in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii, tamɔ midges, bɛ ni baaha amɛwo fɔfɔii lɛ, loo kɛji akɛ nu loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil lacks the food my cocoa trees need?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa mi-cacao tsei lɛ?

english: If your soil lacks nutrients, cocoa trees will grow very slowly, their leaves will look pale instead of deep green, and the pods will remain small or drop early. Adding fertilizer or compost can rebuild the soil's strength.
ga: Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai Cocoa tsei lɛ daa blɛoo waa. Baai lɛ baafee tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe eŋɔli ni mli edɔ. Ni ŋmeii lɛ baakã he afee bibii loo amɛbaagbee shi oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ ewaje shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: How do I know when a cocoa pod on my tree is ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ eshɛ he koni akpa?

english: A cocoa pod is ready when its skin color changes completely, usually from green to bright yellow, or from dark red to orange. Tapping the pod gently will also produce a hollow sound when the beans inside separate from the shell.
ga: Cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ hewolo lɛ su tsake kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse mli. aloo kɛjɛ tsuru ni mli edɔ mli kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ mli Otswaa pod lɛ blɛoo Ehaa gbee ni mli ewo muji baa kɛ́ kɔfi yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli gbala kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants keep dying when I clear all the big trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive and burn easily in direct sunshine. Leaving mature shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains provides shelter and protects the soil moisture that young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ he waa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ ni ashiɔ loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa mɔ náa he ko ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni ehi shi lɛ he.

english: Why is it important to plant plantains on the same field as my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantains lɛ yɛ saatso kome nɔ kɛ mi-cocoa dumɔwui heei lɛ?

english: Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, shading young cocoa seedlings from harsh sunlight while providing shade for the farmer and an early source of food and income.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa okwaafoi lɛ náa hulutsoo, ni eji niyenii kɛ shika jɛɛhe yɛ shishijee bei amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow while the plants are still short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ yɛ kuku lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients away from the roots. Adding poultry manure or fertilizer helps restore their healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ he. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi ŋmɔshi nibii fataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hewalɛ, eŋɔli dalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant groundnuts on the exact same plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously allows pests and diseases specific to that plant to build up in the soil, while continuously draining the exact same soil nutrients without giving the land a break.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni ayaa nɔ akwɛ̃ɔ lɛ haa tso pɔtɛɛ ko mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be ni ehaaaa jɛmɛ akumɔ.

english: What causes the leaves of my cassava plants to curl up and show yellowish patches?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies that feed on plant sap. Planting disease-resistant cassava stem varieties is the best way to prevent this.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ baa ni ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ tsei amli nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ enɛ naa.

english: Why do my stored cowpea grains get filled with tiny holes and turn into dust after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui stash lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni etsɔɔ sũ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: Those holes are caused by tiny insects called weevils that hatch inside the stored seeds and eat them from the inside. Drying seeds thoroughly and storing them in airtight bags prevents these insects from surviving.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils ni fɔɔ dumɔwui ni ato mli ni amɛyeɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji lɛ baa. Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛto kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkahi shi.

english: When plantains are planted too closely, their broad leaves block sunlight from reaching each other and their roots fight for food and water in the soil, resulting in weak plants and small bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantains ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaai ni mli kwɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ kui bibii.

english: Can I save seeds from my harvested maize to plant again during the next farming season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mahere dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ ato ni madu ekoŋŋ yɛ okwaayeli be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: Seeds saved from high-yielding hybrid crops usually produce weaker plants with lower yields in the second generation. Buying fresh, certified seeds every season ensures strong growth and full harvests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ahereɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ amli lɛ woɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni woɔ yibii fioo yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli ni aheɔ daa be lɛ baaha amɛdara waa ni amɛkpa nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the stem without turning into fruits when the sunshine is very bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and dries out flower pollen, causing the plant to drop its blossoms to save energy. Providing light shade and watering early in the morning helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Okɛ tomato tsei lɛ ashwie shi koni okɛ hewalɛ akafite. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo kɛ nu shwie nɔ leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Yam plants signal maturity above ground when their vines and leaves begin to dry up and turn yellow naturally, showing that the tuber underground has finished growing and storing food.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ tsɔɔ amɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ dalɛ beni wain tso lɛ kɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ egbe amɛkwɛ̃mɔ kɛ niyenii ni amɛbua naa lɛ naa.

english: Why do banana plants keep growing back even after I cut them down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ banana tso lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ be mli ni mifo lɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Bananas store food and water deep inside an underground stem called a corm. Even if you chop down the top leaves and trunk, the corm below the ground stays alive and quickly pushes up new shoots.
ga: Banana kɛ niyenii kɛ nu toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni atsɛɔ amɛ rhizomes lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji ofo ŋwɛi baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ po, Shi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baahi shi ni amɛtsi ŋmeii heei kɛya ŋwɛi oya.

english: Why are plantains able to survive tough conditions better than crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli fe ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Plantains have thick, fleshy stems that hold a large amount of water and broad leaf structures that make them much tougher and more resilient during short dry spells compared to soft crops like maize.
ga: Plantains yɛ fɔ, ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛ nu babaoo toɔ. Ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa amɛhe wa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo yɛ hulutsoo be kukuoo mli. kɛ akɛto tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo tamɔ ŋmãa he.

english: Can I grow plantains deep inside the forest under big shade trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu plantains yɛ koo lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi?

english: While plantain trees are tough and can survive in shaded forest areas, they need plenty of sunlight to make energy and produce big, healthy bunches of fruit. Heavy shade will slow down their growth.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ dumɔwui lɛ wa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ kooi ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli moŋ, shi dumɔwui lɛ hu he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛwo yibii wuji ni mli wa. Shade ni tsii baaha dalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do plantains grow much faster on newly cleared forest land than on old farm soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ koo shikpɔŋ ni ajie lɛ ehee lɛ nɔ fe ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ momo nɔ lɛ?

english: Forest soil is full of rich organic matter from fallen leaves and decaying plants. Plantains need heavy feeding, so fresh forest soil gives them the rich nutrients they need to grow rapidly.
ga: Koo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo ni jɛ baai ni egbee shi kɛ tsei ni egboi amli. Niyenii babaoo he miihia plantains. No hewɔ lɛ, koo mli shikpɔŋ hee haa niyenii babaoo ni he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ oya.

english: How can I tell the difference between how a banana plant and a plantain plant behave on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ banana kɛ plantain tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ajeŋba teŋ?

english: Bananas generally produce sweeter fruit and softer leaves, while plantains grow taller, have sturdier stems, and yield firmer, starchier fruits that require cooking before eating.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, banana woɔ yibii ni ŋɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo. yɛ be mli ni plantains lɛ baakwɛ̃ Eyɛ tso ni mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ. ni ewoɔ aduawai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ starch babaoo ni esa akɛ ahoo dani aye.

english: Should I cut away the small young shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ani eji nɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tso lɛ shishi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, leaving too many small shoots, called suckers, causes them to steal food and water from the main mother plant. You should keep only one or two strong suckers so your main tree can produce big fruit.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ni eshiɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ sɛɛ. Atsɛɔ nakai akɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo tsɔ. Enɛ baaha amɛju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Esa akɛ okɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ato bɔni afee ni otso titri lɛ awo yibii wuji.

english: Why do my plantain stems split open or break easily during heavy wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ amli gbalaa loo amɛkuɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trunks are not made of hard wood; they are layers of tightly wrapped leaves filled with water. When the fruit bunch gets heavy, strong winds can easily snap or split these water-filled stems if they are not supported with bamboo poles.
ga: Akɛ tsei ni wa fee plantain tsei lɛ. Eji baai ni akɛwo mli shiŋŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ bafee nɔ ni tsii Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ akumɔ loo agbala nɛkɛ tsei ni nu eyi mli obɔ nɛɛ amli mlɛo kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei fioo ko pɛ fiɔ amɛsɛɛ.

english: What is the best way to cut down a heavy bunch of plantains without destroying the main plant or hurting myself?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ ofolɔ plantain babaoo ni ofiteee tso titri lɛ loo opilaaa ohe?

english: Make a small cut halfway up the main stem so the weight of the fruit gently bends the tree down toward you, allowing you to carefully cut the bunch off without the heavy stem crashing down suddenly.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji bibii kɛyashɛ tso lɛ fã titri lɛ nɔ koni fiofio lɛ okɛ tso yibii lɛ agbɔjɔ shi. Bɔɔ tso lɛ kɛba oŋɔɔ. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni onyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ afo tsei lɛ aniji ni ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ bɛ mli lɛ amli. egbee shi trukaa

english: Why do the leaves of my plantain plants dry up and turn brown during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baa lɛ mli egbi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains lose water quickly through their huge leaves. When rain stops, the plant intentionally lets its outer leaves dry up and die to save precious moisture for its stem and roots until the rains return.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai wuji lɛ anɔ. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ Tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛŋmɛɔ amɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ bɔni afee ni amɛto nu ni jara wa amɛha amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Can planting plantains help protect the soil on my farm from drying out?
ga: Ani plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni abu shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he koni ekagbi?

english: Yes, plantain trees have broad leaves that cast heavy shade on the ground, keeping the soil cool and reducing water evaporation, which helps protect the soil structure around them.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo waa baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ he.

english: Yellowing and dropping leaves during the dry season is often a natural defense mechanism by cocoa trees to conserve water, but it can also be caused by sap-sucking pests like mirids or severe nutrient deficiencies in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni kookoo tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ekɛbuɔ ehe koni ekɛbu nu he. Shi ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa lɛ hu baanyɛ aha eba.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop black rotten spots on the bottom before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɔɔ dani ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Black spots on the bottom of tomatoes are known as blossom-end rot. This happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium, usually caused by irregular watering rather than an insect attack or infectious disease.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tsɛŋemɔ hela ko baatutua bo loo hela ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ

english: How do I know if my soil needs chemical fertilizer or animal manure for my maize farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia tsofa loo ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: If your maize leaves turn pale yellow instead of dark green, your soil is low in nitrogen. Animal manure improves long-term soil structure and holds moisture, while chemical fertilizers provide fast nutrients, so combining both usually yields the best results.
ga: Kɛji o-corn baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koolooi ashishifã haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ enyɔ lɛ futu mli lɛ, nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ baa.

english: Why do experienced farmers say planting groundnuts or cowpeas makes the land good for future crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii wɔsɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have natural nodules on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, leaving free nutrients behind for the next crop planted on that land.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Eshiɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni aduɔ yɛ nakai he lɛ.

english: Why should I space out my seeds instead of planting many in one hole to get more crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbala dumɔwui lɛ amli moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli koni maná yibii babaoo?

english: Putting too many seeds in one hole causes the young plants to compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak, thin stems and a smaller overall harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ nyɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa, ni yibiiwoo hu baa shi yɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce very small tubers even when the stems grow very tall and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa eyɛ mli akɛ eshishifãi lɛ kɛlɛ waa ni eyɛ ŋmeii moŋ lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or is planted too close together, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of sending energy into the roots to form large tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ehe tsɔ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ amɛbaai kɛ amɛshishifãi ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, atsuɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli koni amɛfee bulb agboi.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer heat or water stress, or when given too much nitrogen fertilizer. High temperatures cause the plant to drop blossoms to survive instead of making fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo latsaa loo nu mli haomɔ mli. aloo kɛ́ onine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ haa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛhi shi yɛ yibiiwoo najiaŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants produce thin stalks and bend over easily in strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni shwieɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Weak maize stalks are often caused by planting seeds too close together, lack of potassium in the soil, or inadequate sunlight, which prevents the stem from building thick, sturdy cell walls.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmãa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. Potassium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Enɛ haaa tso lɛ ama tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe gbogboi ni mli wa ni mli wa.

english: Is it safe for me to plant my crops immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ afi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to wait until the rains are regular after two or three heavy downpours. The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell that can scorch and destroy newly sprouted seeds.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ bɔ ni sa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ ni efite lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How can I keep tiny insects from destroying my dried maize when I store it in bags?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa? Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ efiteɔ mi ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ kɛ́ akɛwo kotokui amli?

english: Insects need air and moisture to survive. You must dry your maize completely in the sun until it is hard before storing it in sealed, airtight storage bags to suffocate any pests naturally.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ fɛ̃i he miihia koolooi koni amɛhi shi. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmãa lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaawa dani okɛwo kotoku ko ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli lɛ mli koni ŋmãa lɛ ashɛre ŋmãa lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the weather is cool. Spraying in the hot afternoon sun causes the chemical to evaporate too quickly and can burn the plant leaves.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshwie tsofa lɛ nɔ leebi loo shwane mli be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsofai lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ ni ebaashã tso lɛ baai lɛ.

english: How often should I spray my crops if the disease or pest attack on my farm is very severe?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji helai loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa waa?

english: For severe cases, you should repeat the treatment about three times, leaving about two weeks between each spraying. This helps kill any new pests or disease spots that come back after the first spray.
ga: Yɛ helai ni mli wa waa amli lɛ Esa akɛ okɛ tsofafeemɔ lɛ atsu nii aaafee shii etɛ, ni oshi aaafee otsii enyɔ yɛ tsofafeemɔ fɛɛ tsofafeemɔ teŋ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ejie tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ahe hei heei fɛɛ kɛjɛ mli. ni ku esɛɛ eba yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ tsofa ni akɛshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ

english: Should I spray chemical medicine over my whole farm or only directly on the spots where plants are sick?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ loo he ni tsei lɛ hela mɔ amɛ lɛ pɛ?

english: If only a few plants show damage, putting the medicine directly on those spots saves chemical and money. However, if the pest or disease spreads quickly, spraying the surrounding healthy plants helps protect them before they get infected.
ga: Kɛji tsei fioo komɛi pɛ efite Tsofa lɛ ni akɛwoɔ nakai hei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa tsofai kɛ shika baa shi. Shi, kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ loo hela lɛ gbɛ eshwa oya lɛ, Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu amɛhe dani hela lɛ aba amɛnɔ.

english: How do I know the right amount of medicine to mix into my spray tank before taking it to the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofa ni sa ni esa akɛ afutu mli yɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛya ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Always use the exact measure recommended on the container label or by an extension agent. Using too little will not kill the pest, and using too much can damage your crops.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, kɛ gbɛjianɔtoo pɔtɛɛ ni atsɔɔ yɛ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ loo nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ tsu nii. Kɛ́ akɛ nɔ ko fioo pɛ tsu nii lɛ, egbeŋ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ. Ni kɛ akɛtsu nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How can I check my farm to know if pests are still hiding inside my crops after I spray?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mana kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lolo beni mikɛ tsofa lɛ eshwie nɔ sɛɛ?

english: Walk through your farm every few days and look closely inside the dense leaves, under the foliage, and around the stems to see if any live insects or new leaf damage remain.
ga: Nyiɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa gbii fioo ni okwɛ tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ, tsei lɛ ashishi, kɛ tsei lɛ ahe kɛkwɛ kɛji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka loo tsei heei ni efite lɛ yɛ.

english: How can I tell early on if my crop is getting sick so I can apply medicine quickly?
ga: Kulɛ mana mra. Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiye hela koni manyɛ mikɛ tsofa atsu nii oya?

english: Check your crop leaves regularly for early warning signs like yellowing, dark spots, leaf curling, or small holes chewed into the stems and leaves.
ga: Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baai lɛ amli daa kɛha kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii tamɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi, baai ni ebɔle amɛhe loo buji bibii. ŋmɔɔ tsei ashishifãi kɛ baai

english: What should I do if heavy rain falls right after I finish spraying chemical medicine on my crops?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa beni mikɛ tsofai eshwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rain can wash the medicine off the plant leaves before it has time to work. If it rains immediately after spraying, you will usually need to spray again once the leaves dry.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ tsofa kɛjɛ tsei ahe baai anɔ dani ená be ni ekɛtsu nii. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ Ehe baahia ni okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ ekoŋŋ beni baai lɛ egbi lɛ.

english: What basic things do my crops need most to survive and give a good yield?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee nibii he hiaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ waa koni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Crops need healthy soil with good nutrients, adequate water, enough sunlight, and regular protection from weeds, pests, and diseases throughout their growth.
ga: Tsei hia shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni niyenii kpakpa yɔɔ mli, nu ni fa bɔ ni sa, kɛ hulu la babaoo. kɛ hebuu daa kɛjɛ jwɛi, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, kɛ helai ahe yɛ dalɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: What should I do with leftover chemical medicine remaining in my spray tank after finishing my farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi yɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ mli lɛ beni migbe ŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Do not leave mixed chemical medicine in the spray tank because it loses its strength quickly. Spray the leftover mixture on the worst-affected farm spots or dispose of it safely away from rivers, wells, and animals.
ga: Kaashi tsofai ni efutu yɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ lɛ mli ejaakɛ enɛ baaha hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afite oya. Okɛ tsofa ni eshwɛ lɛ afɔ ŋmɔ mli hei ni efite fe fɛɛ lɛ anɔ. Aloo shɛrɛmɔ shweshweeshwe yɛ he ko ni faai, ŋshɔi, kɛ kooloi bɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Should I treat my sick crops with chemical medicine first or give them fertilizer first?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa atsa tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ loo mikɛ tsofa awo mli klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: It is best to stop the disease or pest attack with medicine first. Once the crop is no longer under attack, fertilizer will help the plant recover and grow stronger.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ okɛ tsofa baatsi hela loo tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ naa klɛŋklɛŋ. Kɛji akɛ atutuaaa ŋmɔshi nibii dɔŋŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii baaye abua ni tso lɛ aya hiɛ ni eda waa.

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana. They hide deep inside the young maize leaves to feed. You can manage them by checking your field early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or approved chemicals directly into the plant's leaves during early morning or late evening.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye niyenii. Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ nibii ni odu lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra nɔ. ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ awo tsei ahe tsei lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves twist, turn yellow, and shrink in size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? etsɔ ŋmɔŋ Ni ani egbɔjɔ yɛ elɛɛmɔ mli?

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whitefly insects or spread when you plant cuttings from sick plants. You can stop this by immediately pulling out affected plants and always using disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by extension officers.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ woɔ loo egbɛɔ eshwaa beni ofoɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ. Obaanyɛ okpa enɛ kɛtsɔ tso ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ ni ooojie amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ ŋmei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ atsu nii.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in cool, dark, and damp conditions. You can protect your trees by pruning extra branch leaves to let sunlight reach the trunk, removing infected pods early, and spraying approved fungicides.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, duŋ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛbaa. Obaanyɛ obu otso lɛ he kɛtsɔ baai krokomɛi ni ooofolɔ koni hulu la ashɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ. Jiemɔ pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ afɔ nɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my yellow corn turning yellow and drying up early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei ŋmɔŋ lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting at the lower leaves usually means your crop is hungry for nitrogen in the soil. Applying NPK or urea fertilizer early in the crop's life, or adding well-rotted compost, provides the nutrient maize needs to stay healthy and green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ onibii lɛ he miihia nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. NPK loo urea ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashihilɛ shishijee bei amli. Aloo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ afata he. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔŋ.

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, caused by a shortage of calcium in the plant or irregular watering during fruit formation. Watering your crops consistently and adding lime or wood ash to your soil before planting helps fix it.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii lɛ. Nu ni oooha ŋmɔshi nibii daa ni okɛ lime loo tso sũ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani adu lɛ baaye abua ni asaa naagba lɛ.

english: Why do my seed yam tubers refuse to sprout right after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikpa amɛ lɛ?
