english: Yam tubers go through a natural rest period called dormancy after harvest. During this time, the seed yam will not sprout regardless of soil or moisture until its natural internal clock awakens it, usually after 2 to 3 months.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ kwɛŋ ni shikpɔŋ loo hulutsoo kɔɔɔ he eko kɛyashi amɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɛlɛtswaa ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baate shi. Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 2 kɛyashi 3 sɛɛ

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and fall over easily when I sow many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, they compete heavily for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes the plants to grow tall and weak instead of thick and strong. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehe wa. He ni jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct, hot sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly and broad-leaved, acting like living umbrellas to shade the young cocoa plants and preserve soil moisture during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Covering soil with organic material like dry grass is called mulching. It keeps the soil cool under hot weather, traps water so you irrigate less often, stops weeds from taking over, and later breaks down into soil nutrients.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi. Ehiɛɔ nu mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu fioo pɛ awo mli. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni amɛkaye nɔ. ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli yɛ sɛɛ mli

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my farm help my next maize crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua mi-ŋmei srɔtoi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special root system abilities that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest them, this leaves fresh food in the soil for the next maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛ ko ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni okpaa Ebaashi niyenii hee yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Can I grow plantains and cocoa together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ plantain kɛ cocoa yɛ he kome?

english: Yes, growing plantains and cocoa together is a common practice because the large leaves of plantain plants give young cocoa seedlings essential shade and moisture while providing you with food and income before the cocoa matures.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui kɛ kookoo ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ ji nɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ. Ejaakɛ kookoo tso lɛ baai wuji lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ ni amɛnáa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika dani kookoo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why should I plant tall shade trees among my plantain crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsei kakadaji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Tall trees protect plantains from strong winds that can knock them over and provide shade that prevents harsh sunlight from drying out the soil around their roots.
ga: Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ buɔ plantain lɛ he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni baanyɛ atswa lɛ shi lɛ he, ni ehaa hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ agbi.

english: Why are my plantain fruits turning bad and rotting before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miifite ni amɛmiifite dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Plantains usually turn bad prematurely due to fungal diseases, pest attacks like weevils, or poor soil drainage, which weaken the plant and destroy the fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ ŋmeii helai, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii, loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni efiteɔ yibii lɛ.

english: What should I do with diseased or bad plantain trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee dumɔwui ni hela emɔ amɛ loo ni ehiii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: You should cut down and remove diseased plantains from the field immediately to prevent pests and fungal spores from spreading to healthy surrounding plants.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ ni ojie plantains ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ ji koni akagbɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anɔ. yɛ hewalɛ

english: Can using too many chemicals or fertilizers spoil my plantain crop?
ga: Ani tsofai loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ afite mi plantains lɛ?

english: Yes, applying excessive agrochemicals can burn the plant roots, damage the soil chemistry, and lead to poor quality or deformed plantains.
ga: Hɛɛ, okwaayeli mli tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi. efiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsofai lɛ ni ekɛ plantains ni ehiii loo ni efite baa

english: What happens if I plant too many crops and trees close together on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ mihe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Overcrowding causes crops to compete for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, which can weaken the plants and lead to smaller yields and higher chances of disease.
ga: Nibii ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ he akaŋ, ni baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa yibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi, ni helai hu baanyɛ aba.

english: How do shade trees help keep the soil moist during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ yeɔ ebuaa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Shade trees block direct sunlight from reaching the ground and drop leaves that act as mulch, slowing down water evaporation from the soil.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. ni ehaa baai ni tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nu lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ blɛoo.

english: Why is it important to separate bad harvested crops from the good ones immediately after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie ŋmaa ni ehiii kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai amli yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Separating bad produce stops rot, mold, and hidden insects from spreading to healthy crops during storage and transport to the market.
ga: Nibii gbohii ni ajieɔ lɛ mligbalamɔ tsiɔ ŋmeii, ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ kɛ be mli ni akɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do farmers combine short-term crops like plantain with long-term crops like cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kukuoo tamɔ plantains kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ kookoo feɔ ekome lɛ?

english: Plantains yield fruit within a year to give you quick food and income, while cocoa takes a few years to mature but provides steady, long-term earnings.
ga: Plantains baawo yibii yɛ afi mli koni eha bo niyenii kɛ shika oya. Yɛ be mli ni kookoo heɔ afii fioo komɛi dani ekwɛɔ lɛ, ehaa shika ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: How do I know if a tree species is suitable to grow alongside my plantains and cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso ko sa akɛ makwɛ̃ yɛ mi-plantain kɛ mi-cocoa lɛ masɛi?

english: Good companion trees have deep roots that do not compete for surface water and provide moderate shade without blocking all sunlight from your crops.
ga: Hefatalɔi tsei kpakpai yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni nyɛŋ atswa nu ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ he akaŋ ni amɛhaa hulutsoo be ni sa ni amɛtsĩii hulu lɛ naa kɛjɛɛɛ onibii amli.

english: How can I make sure I will find a buyer for my tomatoes after harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ mana mɔ ko ni baahe mi-tomato lɛ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Before planting, you can talk to local tomato traders, market queens, or processing centers to agree on supply arrangements, so you have guaranteed buyers waiting when your crop matures.
ga: Dani obaadu lɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ tomato jarayelɔ lɛ agba sane. maŋnyɛ ni yɔɔ jarayelihe lɛ loo maŋ lɛ mli nibii ahe nitsumɔhe lɛ koni amɛkpɛlɛ nibii ni amɛheɔ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, okɛ nɔmimaa haa akɛ mɛi ni baahe nii lɛ baamɛ be mli ni onibii lɛ shwere.

english: When is the best time of year to harvest tomatoes in Ghana to get the highest price?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akpa tomato yɛ Ghana koni aná jara ni hi fe fɛɛ?

english: Harvesting during the dry season using irrigation or at the end of the main rains usually gets higher prices because fewer farmers are harvesting tomatoes at that time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ nu shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ kɛ jara ni yaa hiɛ baa ejaakɛ okwaafoi lɛ kpaaa tomato fioo yɛ nakai beaŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow lots of green leaves but very few flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi fɔfɔi fioo pɛ yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to spend all its energy growing leafy stems instead of producing the flowers that turn into tomato fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, a woɔ fɔfɔi nɛ ba peeɔ tomato yiblii.

english: What causes the flowers on my tomato plants to fall off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni haa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai?

english: Extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of water causes stress to the tomato plant, making it drop its blossoms to save energy for survival.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni bɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. Ha tomato tsei lɛ agbo koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he gbɛjianɔ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my young green tomatoes turning black and rot-like?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efite lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant lacks calcium, usually caused by irregular watering that prevents the roots from absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ calcium. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni haaa shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do my tomatoes split open on the plant right when they start turning red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ trukaa yɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes crack open when they receive a sudden heavy amount of water after a dry spell, making the inside grow faster than the skin can stretch.
ga: Tomato baatswa kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo nu babaoo mli trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa tomato lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: How can I keep my harvested tomatoes fresh for longer so they do not rot before reaching the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha tomato ni mikpa lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ? Koni tomatoi lɛ akafite dani amɛyashɛ jara nɔ?

english: Pick tomatoes when they are just turning pink, transport them in hard plastic crates instead of heavy sacks, and store them in a cool, shaded area away from direct sunlight.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ tomato kɛji etsɔ pinki. Kɛkɛ ni akɛwo plastic adekai ni wa amli yɛ kotokui ni tsii najiaŋ. ni okɛto he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Ekɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ akashɛ he

english: Why do I need to leave space between my tomato plants instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishiɔ gbɛ yɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Proper spacing lets air move freely and sunlight reach the leaves, which dries up dampness and prevents fungal diseases like blight from spreading quickly.
ga: He ni jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ baai lɛ ahe Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi. ni etsi tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ late blight naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa oya.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl up and turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellowing is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading viral diseases, or by excessive heat and lack of water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine kɛ nu ni faaa yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants fall over on the ground when the tomatoes start getting heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ beni tomato lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɔjɔɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato stems are soft and flexible, so they need wooden stakes or sticks for support to keep the fruit off the soil where pests and rot can destroy them.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ tsei loo tsei atsu nii koni aduawai lɛ akajɛ shikpɔŋ, he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni fiteɔ nii baanyɛ akpata amɛhiɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I plant my maize in straight rows with proper spacing instead of just scattering the seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ni ja mli ni gbɛ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu dumɔwui kɛkɛ

english: Planting in measured rows ensures every plant gets equal access to sunlight, air, and soil nutrients without crowding each other out, making weeding and harvesting much easier.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni asusu he lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. ni amɛtsiii amɛhe gbɛ Enɛ haa jwɛi shwiemɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: How do I clear and prepare my farm ground properly before planting cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ majie he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni masaa he jogbaŋŋ dani madu ŋmei?

english: Clearing bush and making raised earth mounds or ridges loosens the soil, allowing the roots to expand freely underground and hold enough water without rotting.
ga: Tsoi bibii ni ajieɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ loo ŋmeii ni awoɔ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛhiɛɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛfiteee.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants turning yellow and dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually signal that the crop is starving of essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that the roots are suffocating from too much water in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ sũ lɛ mli, loo akɛ nu babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ efo shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops dry up so quickly even when it rained just a few days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses water fast under strong heat; covering the ground around your crops with dry grass or palm fronds traps moisture in the soil like a protective blanket.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ laajeɔ nu oya yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi. Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmei baai awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle onibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he.

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that plant needs and lets soil diseases build up; switching to beans or groundnuts restores nutrients naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ helai baa amɛhe shi. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmeii loo ŋmeii anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: How does adding dried cow dung or poultry manure help my vegetable crops grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni egbi loo kooloi ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Animal manure feeds the soil with natural plant food, helps the earth retain moisture longer, and improves soil texture so plant roots grow deeper.
ga: Koolooi ashishifãi kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight that your main plants need to develop healthy roots and fruits.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa tsei ni okɛ amɛ yeɔ sharamɔ lɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa kɛ aduawai.

english: Why do insects attack my crops more during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Dry weather stresses plants and makes their leaves weaker, which allows hungry pests searching for moisture to easily feed on and destroy them.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa baai lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa kooloi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni miitao ŋmɔtɔ lɛ akɛ amɛbaaye ni amɛkpãtã amɛhiɛ.

english: Why do farmers plant plantain trees close to young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under full sun; plantains grow fast and provide large leaves that act as living umbrellas to shade and protect young cocoa.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo kɛ hebuu kɛha kookoo bibioo lɛ.

english: Why should I trim off extra shoots and lower leaves from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ baai kɛ shishigbɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ?

english: Pruning extra stems forces the plant to send its food energy directly into developing large, juicy tomatoes rather than growing unnecessary leaves.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi fe nine lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni etsɔɔ hewalɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ gbɛ koni ekɛwo tomatoi wuji ni mli ewo nu. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookwɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight because their leaves burn easily. They need shade from larger trees or nurse crops like plantains to protect them while their roots and canopy develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo tsei ni kwɛɔ amɛ tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni ebu amɛhe be mli ni amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly when it hasn't rained for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa lɛ? Gbii babaoo nɛ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural defense mechanism to save water. By rolling up, the leaf surface area exposed to the hot sun and wind is reduced, slowing down water loss from the plant.
ga: Abɛi baai shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛtoɔ nu he. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ Ba lɛ hiɛ he ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Ha nu ni jɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ fiofio.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly very wet. Heat and moisture stress prevent the flower from pollinating properly, so the plant sheds it.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ waa nɔ. Dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo haomɔ tsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkafee pollination jogbaŋŋ. Tso lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by viral infection spread by insects, which damages the leaf tissue as it grows.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Enɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji beni edaa lɛ.

english: Why do my onion plants start flowering instead of making big bulbs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-onions lɛ miibɔi fɔmɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee bulbs wuji lɛ?

english: Onions start flowering (a process called bolting) when they experience stress from sudden temperature changes or lack of water. The plant thinks it is dying, so it shifts its energy to making seeds rather than growing a bulb.
ga: Sabalai jeɔ shishi amɛfɔ̃ɔ (nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ bolting) beni sabalai naa haomɔ kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa loo nu ni faaa yɛ emli lɛ mli. Tso lɛ susu akɛ eegbo. No hewɔ lɛ etsɔɔ hewalɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ koni ekɛfee dumɔwui yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ bulbs.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very deep in the soil, will they grow deeper roots and be stronger?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ waa Ani ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ baatsɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛhe wa?

english: Planting seeds too deep actually weakens them because the shoot runs out of stored energy trying to reach the surface. Maize seeds should be planted about 3 to 5 centimeters deep so they emerge quickly.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ mli tsɔ lɛ baaha amɛgbɔjɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hewalɛ ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii be mli ni abɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eshɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ lɛ. Esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ mli aaafee sɛntimita 3 kɛyashi 5 koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my farm make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots rot in the ground, that stored nitrogen enriches the soil for future crops.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni tsei ashishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nitrogen ni ato lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why should I remove extra suckers from my plantain mat instead of letting all of them grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛjɛ mi-plantain mat lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mahã amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ?

english: Multiple suckers compete with the main plantain tree for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Pruning to leave only one main stem and one or two suckers ensures the main plant produces large, heavy bunches.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo kɛ dumɔwui titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ yitso titri kome pɛ kɛ tso lɛ shishifã kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ feɔ kuu agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do my harvested cassava tubers start turning dark and spoiling within two days of pulling them out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni akpa lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboi yɛ gbii enyɔ mli beni ajie amɛ lɛ?

english: Unlike yams, harvested cassava roots have no natural protective outer skin layer. Once harvested, exposure to air causes rapid internal oxidation and spoilage within 48 to 72 hours unless processed or buried in wet sand.
ga: Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ sweet potato lɛ, cassava shishifãi ni akpa lɛ bɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he yɛ kponɔgbɛ. Kɛji akpa lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha oksijin aya oya ni emli fitemɔ aba yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 kɛyashi 72 mli ja atsu he nii loo afu yɛ ŋã ni mli ewo fɔ mli.

english: Why do the vines and tubers of my yam plants rot at the soil level during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ amli wain tsei kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess rain makes the soil waterlogged, starving the roots of oxygen. This creates ideal conditions for soil-borne fungi and bacteria to attack the base of the plant, causing rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ koni amɛtutua tso lɛ shishi. kɛ fitemɔ baa

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves. Applying organic manure or a nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant make food and turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji Organic ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots sometimes rot in the soil before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much water for too long, suffocating the roots and letting soil fungi attack them. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa amɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the stems without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the plant experiences water stress. Keeping the soil regularly damp and applying mulch around the roots keeps the plant cool so the flowers can set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ. Keeping the soil moist and mulching around it The roots help keep the plant cool so the flowers can set fruit.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant's juices. Spraying the leaves with neem oil or mild soapy water helps get rid of these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper leaf curl baa. Spraying the leaves with neem oil or a mild soap solution It will help get rid of these insects.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together in the same line?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-abɛi dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe yɛ sɛɛ kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing them correctly ensures every plant gets enough food to grow tall and produce large cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛto he ni sa lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow very fast with broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa the gentle shade and humidity it needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya waa kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Yam plants use their leaves to catch sunlight and make food that feeds the growing yam tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they get maximum sunshine and stay safe from fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ ebaai lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛmɔɔ hulu la ni ekɛfeɔ niyenii ni haa sweet potato tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking woɔ tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni hulu la ni fa babaoo kɛ shweshweeshwe shihilɛ kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans help make my soil better for future crops?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special crops that capture natural nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots. When you harvest them, they leave behind free plant food that helps the next crop grow better.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji okpa amɛ Amɛbaashi tsei niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko koni eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds hurt my young crops so much more than my full-grown crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ awui fe mi tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Young crops have short roots and small leaves, making them too weak to compete with fast-growing weeds for water and light. Full-grown crops have deep roots and big leaves that shade out weeds naturally.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi kukuji kɛ baai bibii. Enɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ ashi akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ la. Tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai wuji ni haa jwɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn brown and dry up during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The dry Harmattan wind pulls moisture out of plant leaves much faster than the dry soil can replace it. Covering the soil around your plantain roots with dry grass or leaves keeps the soil moist longer during dry spells.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni egbi baanyɛ atsake lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie plantain shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Officer, how do I know if my farmland is 'dead' and can no longer support healthy crops?
ga: Nitsulɔi Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ ‘egbo’ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ dɔŋŋ?

english: Exhausted or 'dead' land usually feels hard, looks pale or washed out, and produces stunted crops with yellowing leaves even when there is enough rain. You can revive it by adding organic matter, manure, or organic fertilizer to bring nutrients and beneficial soil organisms back to life.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbɔjɔ loo ‘egbo’ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ ewa. Etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbɔjɔ ni baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po. Obaanyɛ okɛwo mli ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo humus ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ koni eha niyenii kɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aba wala mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Can land that has been overused for years ever become fertile and productive again?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsu nii fe nine afii babaoo lɛ baanyɛ afee shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni ewo yibii ekoŋŋ?

english: Yes, tired land can be restored. By adding organic fertilizers, practicing crop rotation, planting leguminous cover crops like beans, and avoiding bush burning, you feed the soil organisms that rebuild rich, fertile topsoil over time.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ asaa shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ. Kɛtsɔ organic fertilizer ni akɛbaafata he lɛ Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsakeɔ nii lɛ Dumɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ jwɛi ni ashãa lɛ he. Okɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni maa shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nii ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ niyenii.

english: Is it good practice to burn my farm clearing before planting my crops?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaashã shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ dani adu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Burning might clear the land quickly, but it destroys essential organic nutrients and kills tiny organisms that keep the soil healthy. Leaving cleared plants to rot on the field naturally feeds the soil and keeps it fertile for your crops.
ga: Shãa baanyɛ ajie sũ lɛ oya. Shi efiteɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ wala mli lɛ, ni egbeɔ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa Kɛ́ oha tsei ni ajie lɛ lɛ fite yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eye ebua onibii ni oŋmɔshi nii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my crops wilt and dry up so quickly whenever the rains stop for just a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ oya be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ lɛ baakpa gbii fioo komɛi pɛ lɛ?

english: When soil lacks organic matter, it cannot hold onto water. Soil with rich organic content acts like a natural sponge, holding rainwater near the roots so your plants stay hydrated longer during dry spells.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ, enyɛŋ ehiɛ nu. Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli sponji. Kɛtsɔ nugbɔ nu ni emɔɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha otsei lɛ aná nu be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ.

english: What is the main difference between using organic fertilizer and chemical fertilizer on my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ateŋ?

english: Chemical fertilizer feeds the plant directly for a quick boost but does not improve the soil quality long term. Organic fertilizer feeds both the crop and the soil, restoring tired land and improving water retention so the soil stays rich for future seasons.
ga: Akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛyi fa oya. Shi ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Organic ŋmɔshi nibii haa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ niyenii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hei ni etɔ lɛ lɛ naa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni ehaa nu lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: How long does it take for organic fertilizer to start working after I apply it to my crops?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani organic fertilizers lɛ tsuɔ nii beni mikɛwo miŋmɔshi nibii amli sɛɛ?

english: Organic fertilizers release nutrients slowly as soil micro-organisms break them down. You will typically see crops looking greener and stronger within 2 to 3 weeks, and the soil improvement benefits continue for several seasons.
ga: Organic ŋmɔshi nibii jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii fiofio. Kɛji nibii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fite niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ obaana ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji, ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ otsii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, ni sɛɛnamɔi ni haa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛo lɛ baaya nɔ yɛ be babaoo mli.

english: Why do my maize plants have yellow leaves even when I give them plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ baa ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu babaoo moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves are a signal that your plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leaf growth. Rain alone does not supply nitrogen, so applying manure or organic fertilizer is necessary to feed the plant.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Nugbɔ pɛ haaa nitrogen. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli afata he koni akɛha tsei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are my cassava roots so small even though the leaves and stems above ground look huge?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii eyɛ mli akɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara moŋ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen but lacks phosphorus and potassium, the plant puts all its energy into growing big leaves above ground instead of developing thick, heavy tubers below ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ fa tsɔ shi fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium bɛ mli lɛ. Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ zugba a sisi tsohi nɛ a mi wa nɛ a tsiɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable plants droop in the hot afternoon sun even when the soil around them is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ mli edɔ po

english: Vegetable leaves lose moisture faster in the hot sun than damaged or weak roots can suck up from the ground. Improving root strength through balanced soil nutrients helps plants handle afternoon heat stress better.
ga: Aduawai baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Nɔ ni fe shishifãi ni efite loo ni bɛ hewalɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi ahewalɛ ni yaa hiɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛyeɔ shwane dɔlɛ he haomɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Are there special agricultural programs or banks in Ghana that help small farmers get fertilizers and inputs?
ga: Ani okwaayeli he gbɛjianɔtoo krɛdɛɛ ko loo shikatoohei komɛi yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi bibii ni amɛnáa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, institutions like the Agricultural Development Bank (ADB) and government extension programs provide financial support, flexible farm loans, and access to quality inputs like fertilizers specifically tailored for smallholder farmers.
ga: Hɛɛ, nitsumɔhei tamɔ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe (ADB) kɛ nɔyeli nitsumɔi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ haa shika. Okwaafoi ashika ni anyɛɔ atsakeɔ kɛ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ pɔtɛɛ aha okwaafoi bibii lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔtoo.

english: Why do I need to keep spraying my farm weekly even after seeing new leaves grow on my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ tsofa daa otsi eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ baai heei moŋ?

english: Tender new leaves are very attractive to pests and soft enough for diseases to enter easily. Weekly treatments during high-growth periods protect these fresh leaves until they harden and mature.
ga: Baai heei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ, ni amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni helai baanyɛ abote mli mlɛo. Otsi fɛɛ otsi mli tsofafeemɔi ni afeɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa lɛ baabu nɛkɛ baai heei nɛɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaawa ni amɛdara.

english: How many times should I apply fertilizer to my crops before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa?

english: Most crops perform best with two to three split applications of fertilizer rather than all at once. Applying it in stages ensures the plant gets food during critical growth phases like early leafing and flowering.
ga: Tsei babaoo tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli srɔtoi 2-3, moŋ fe ni akɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii shikome. Kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa niyenii yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa tamɔ baai ni jeɔ kpo kɛ fɔfɔi ni baa mra lɛ.

english: How often should I walk through my farm to check on the condition of my crops?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni makwɛ bɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ ha?

english: Checking your farm at least once a week allows you to spot early signs of leaf damage, pest activity, or water stress before the problem spreads across the whole field.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shikome yɛ otsi mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ baai lɛ efite mra. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo nu mli haomɔ Dani naagba lɛ baagbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli

english: What does it mean when my crop suddenly starts pushing out bright new leaves?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛ́ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔi baai heei ni kpɛɔ lɛ kpojiemɔ?

english: New leaf growth shows that the plant's roots are actively taking up nutrients and water from the soil. It indicates the crop is healthy and entering a stage where it needs strong protection and care.
ga: Baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ miihe niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni ebote shihilɛ ko ni biɔ hebuu kɛ kwɛmɔ ni mli wa mli.

english: Why does my crop produce many flowers or pods, but only a few actually grow into mature fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi loo ŋmeii babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔii fioo komɛi pɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ aduawai ni ekwɛ̃?

english: Plants often produce extra flowers as a backup. If the plant lacks enough water, nutrients, or suffers from heat, it will naturally drop excess flowers or pods to save energy for the remaining ones.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei woɔ fɔfɔi krokomɛi yɛ he ni ato kɛji akɛ amɛbɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. loo nine shɛɔ dɔlɛ nɔ Fɔfɔi loo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know the total time my crop needs from the day I plant to my first harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be fɛɛ ni he hiaa tso ko kɛjɛ gbi ni midu lɛ kɛyashi klɛŋklɛŋ kpamɔɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Every crop variety has a specific growth cycle ranging from a few months to over a year. Factors like rainfall, temperature, and soil health can slightly shorten or extend this maturity period.
ga: Nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ be pɔtɛɛ ko ni etsɔɔ nɔ edaa kɛjɛɔ nyɔji fioo komɛi kɛyashiɔ nɔ ni fe afi. Nibii tamɔ nugbɔshiimɔ, dɔlɛ, kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ baanyɛ aha nɛkɛ dalɛ be nɛɛ afee kuku loo esɛɛ atsɛ fioo.

english: Why are my crop fruits dropping to the ground before they are ripe enough to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ yibii lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ dani amɛshwereɔ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Premature fruit drop is usually caused by pest attacks, fungal infections, or sharp changes in water supply. Identifying the pest or fixing irrigation early helps save the remaining harvest.
ga: Premature fruit loss is usually caused by pests. Fungal hela loo tsakemɔi ni baa oya yɛ nu jɛɛhei amli Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayɔsemɔ loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ jajemɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni akwɛ nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I estimate how much harvest I will get before I even start harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mikpamɔ lɛ he akɔntaa dani mije ŋmaakpamɔ shishi?

english: You can estimate yield by sampling a few healthy plants in different parts of your farm, counting the average number of good cobs, pods, or fruits on them, and multiplying that by your total plant population.
ga: Obaanyɛ osusu yibiiwoo lɛ he kɛtsɔ tsei fioo komɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni oookwɛ mli yɛ fãi srɔtoi lɛ anɔ. ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, kanemɔ ŋmeii, ŋmeii, loo aduawai kpakpai ayibɔ ni aja mli lɛ. Then multiply by your total number of plants.

english: Why does the amount of harvested food in my barn decrease so fast even when my family hasn't eaten it all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niyenii ni akpaa yɛ mi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi oya nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ miweku lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbe naa moŋ?

english: Insects like weevils and small rodents can enter storage areas and silently destroy or consume harvested crops from the inside out. Proper drying and sealed storage bags prevent these invisible losses.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii bibii baanyɛ abote hei ni akɛ nibii toɔ lɛ ni amɛfite loo amɛye ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ dioo. Kɛjɛ mli kɛyashi kponɔgbɛ Nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotokui ni egbi ni akɛwo mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ baatsi nɛkɛ nibii ni anaaa ni laajeɔ nɛɛ anaa.

english: What should I do with the remaining crop stalks and roots left in the soil after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni eshwɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: If the previous crop was healthy, plowing the remaining plant parts back into the soil adds valuable organic matter. If the crop was diseased, those remains should be cleared out so they don't infect the next planting.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ Tso lɛ mli nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ni akuɔ sɛɛ awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ nibii ni jara wa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ fataa he. Kɛji tso lɛ hela mɔ lɛ Esa akɛ ajie Remains lɛ koni ekɛ hela akatswa tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field without any bigger plants around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni cacao tsei wuji komɛi bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because strong, direct sunlight dries out their tender leaves and damages them. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains nearby provides living shade and keeps the soil cool and moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ agbi ni efite baai bibii lɛ. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and full. Adding well-rotted animal manure, compost, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer gives the crop its green color and strength back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmei, loo ŋmei ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why do I harvest fewer bags of maize every year when I plant on the exact same piece of land each season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpaa ŋmãa fioo daa afi beni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously on the same plot drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally puts nitrogen back into the soil and restores crop yields.
ga: Abele ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ baajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake lɛ, no baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when there is heavy rainfall for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped in the soil around them for too long because the roots cannot breathe. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up tightly and stop producing good peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa pepper kpakpai lɛ feemɔ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the sap and spreading plant viruses. Spraying neem seed water or organic pesticides controls these pests and protects the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Amɛmuɔ nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwãa tsei amli. Kɛ́ akɛ neem dumɔwui amli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaakudɔ kooloi nɛɛ ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my green tomatoes get black, rotten spots on the bottom before they even turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni egbo yɛ shishi dani etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ po lɛ?

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes, known as blossom-end rot, happen when the plant cannot get enough calcium or when watering is irregular. Keeping the soil evenly moist and adding wood ash or lime to the soil helps prevent this problem.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ loo kɛ́ afɔ amɛ nu lɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa ni akɛ tso sũ loo lime fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Is it better for me to water my garden vegetables in the hot afternoon or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mibɔɔ mli aduawai lɛ anɔ nu yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli loo leebi?

english: It is best to water vegetables early in the morning because the water soaks deep into the roots before the heat causes it to evaporate. Afternoon watering can burn leaves and waste water quickly through evaporation.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha o-vegetables lɛ nu leebi ejaakɛ nu lɛ baabote shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ dani la lɛ baaho. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ ashã ni nu lɛ afite oya kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I let all the small shoots grow freely around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ? fɛɛ ni miida yɛ heyeli mli yɛ Mi plantain tso titri lɛ he

english: When too many shoots grow around one plantain stem, they steal food, water, and sunlight from the main plant, resulting in small bunches. Removing extra shoots and leaving only two or three strong ones yields bigger, heavier bunches.
ga: Beni ŋmeii babaoo ebɔle Plantain kome he lɛ Plantains juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. ni kɛ tso bibioo ko baa Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi tsei 2-3 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha niji ni dara ni tsii lɛ aba.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes to catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight allows the leaves to produce energy, which is sent down into the ground to grow large, heavy tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai ni amɛnáa hewalɛ. ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ koni efee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii

english: How does spreading dry grass around the stems of my crops help them grow better during dry weather?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he fɛɛ he Te tsei ashishifãi yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, traps moisture in the dirt so it doesn't dry out fast in the sun. It also stops weeds from growing and breaks down into natural food for the soil.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ hulu la shɛ enɔ lɛ, egbiɛɛ oya. Etsiɔ jwɛi hu naa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efite akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do many farmers plant plantains together with young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo kɛ kookoo tsei bibii feɔ ekome kɛduɔ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from harsh sunlight to survive. Plantains grow fast and develop large, wide leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving the young cocoa seedlings shade and moisture while providing you with food and income while you wait for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he koni amɛhi shi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛfeɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo dumɔwui bibii ni amɛnaa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i. Ha niyenii kɛ shika hu yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: How far apart should I space my plantain shoots when planting them?
ga: Te esa akɛ makɛ plantains lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ abɔ he tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: You should space plantains about 3 meters (10 feet) apart in every direction. Giving them enough space prevents them from competing for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, allowing each plant to yield large, heavy bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ oshi otsei lɛ aaafee mitai 3 (naji 10) yɛ he fɛɛ he. Kɛ́ aha he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaatsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋshii. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso woɔ yibii kui wuji ni tsii.

english: Look for maiden or sword suckers that have strong stems and thin, needle-like leaves. Avoid suckers with broad, wide leaves early in their life, as they tend to produce smaller, weaker bunches.
ga: Taomɔ asparagus loo swordfish ni shishifãi lɛ wa kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni tamɔ ŋmeii. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ ahe yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli mra. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛfɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ feemɔ.

english: Should I let all the tiny suckers around my main plantain tree grow, or cut some away?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maha ŋmeii bibii lɛ akwɛ̃? Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ ahe lɛ daa loo amɛfoɔ ekomɛi?

english: You should trim away extra suckers and leave only 2 or 3 healthy shoots per family (the mother plant, one medium shoot, and one small shoot). If too many suckers grow together, they fight for nutrients and produce very small plantain fingers.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei bibii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oshi tsei 2 loo 3 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ weku fɛɛ weku mli (tso nyɛ, teŋ tsei 1, kɛ tsei bibii 1). Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ he kome lɛ, Amɛyeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ plantain niji bibii waa.

english: How can I keep my plantain plants from drying out during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-plantain lɛ naa koni ekagbi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Cover the soil around the base of your plantain stems with dried grass, fallen leaves, or crop residues. This practice, called mulching, keeps the soil cool, prevents water from evaporating, and slowly breaks down into plant food.
ga: Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle plantain lɛ shishi lɛ he. baai ni egbee shi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ. Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekafee ŋmɔtɔ ni efite fiofio ni etsɔ tsei aniyenii.

english: What kind of manure is best to make my plantains grow faster and stronger?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ ni baaha mi dumɔwui lɛ adara oya ni amɛhe awa?

english: Well-rotted poultry manure or dried cow dung works very well. Apply it in a ring about a foot away from the base of the plant so the roots can absorb the nutrients like nitrogen and potassium without burning the stem.
ga: Kooloi ashishifã ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo tsina ashishifã ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa. Okɛ amɛ awo ŋwɛi ŋta ni miihe ashɛ naji kome kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen kɛ potassium. ni ehaaa tso lɛ tso lɛ ashã

english: Why are the leaves of my plantain trees turning yellow and dying early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi oya lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually signal a lack of nutrients like nitrogen, or an infection like Black Sigatoka disease. You can help the plant by clearing weeds around the base, adding organic manure, and cutting off damaged leaves so the disease doesn't spread.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen, loo hela ko, tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni ji black tick hela lɛ faaa. Obaanyɛ oye obua tso lɛ kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni ooojie kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. ni afolɔ baai ni efite lɛ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: What causes my plantain trees to fall over easily when the wind blows?
ga: Mɛni haa plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi mlɛo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa?

english: Trees often fall over because tiny worms (nematodes) or banana root weevil insects are eating the underground roots, weakening the plant's hold on the ground. Peel off damaged stem tissue and clean suckers in clean water before planting to keep these pests away.
ga: Trees often fall because of tiny worms. (Nematodes) loo banana shishifãi amli ŋmeii miiye shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi. Ehaa tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akpɛtɛɔ he lɛ baa shi. Gbalamɔ tso lɛ mli fãji ni efite lɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni he tse lɛ yɛ nu ni mli tse mli dani odu koni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ he.

english: How can I tell when my plantain bunch is ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni plantains lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Plantains are ready to harvest when the fingers look full and rounded rather than flat and angular, and when the dried flowers at the tips of the fingers easily rub off. The color will also shift from a deep dark green to a lighter green.
ga: Plantains lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji niji lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyi obɔ ni ebɔle ehe. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Ni kɛ́ fɔfɔi lɛ egbi lɛ, ewaaa akɛ okɛ oniji ashishifãi baakpa amɛhe. Su lɛ baatsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ kɛya eŋɔli ni mli tse.

english: What should I do with the big plantain stem after I cut off the fruit bunch?
ga: Kɛ́ ofo tso yibii lɛ aniji lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, mɛni esa akɛ ofee plantains wuji lɛ?

english: Cut the old stem down close to the ground after harvesting, chop it into smaller pieces, and lay them around the remaining growing suckers. The chopped stem holds a lot of water and rots into rich compost that feeds the next crop.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei momoi ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kpɔ̃ɔ bibii bibii ni okɛbɔle ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe. The chopped stems retain a lot of water. and it rots into rich compost for the next crop.

english: Young cocoa trees have shallow roots and tender leaves that burn under direct harmattan sun. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains provides a canopy that protects young cocoa from harsh heat and keeps soil moisture in.
ga: Young cacao trees have shallow roots and young leaves that burn under direct harmattan sunlight. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaha aná ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over whenever strong wind blows during the rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ baatswa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit bunches at the top. If they are planted too shallowly or infected with root pests, strong winds easily push them down. Supporting the stem with a wooden prop or fork helps hold them upright.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akuu ni tsii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. If planted too shallow or infected with root pests Strong winds easily blow them down. Kɛ́ akɛ tso loo fɔk fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Yellowing along the leaf tip and center usually shows that your maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential for healthy green leaves. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will help restore green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi kɛ amɛteŋ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eŋɔlii lɛ adara ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when the rainy season is heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long, cutting off air to the roots and encouraging fungal diseases. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ kɛha shishifãi lɛ ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela he hewalɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my yam vines grow plenty of leaves, but the tubers inside the soil remain small?
ga: Why do sweet potato vines have so many leaves? Shi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or vines are left on the ground without staking, the plant spends energy growing leaves instead of tubers. Staking vine stalks up off the ground helps leaves catch sunlight to build big tubers underneath.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo ashiɔ wain tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛ staking wooo mli. Tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai yɛ bulbs najiaŋ. Wein tso lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la ni amɛfeɔ bulbs agboi yɛ shishi.

english: Why are the leaves of my garden egg and pepper plants curling up tightly and turning small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibɔɔ mli eggplant kɛ pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa ni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on the undersides of leaves and spreading viruses. Spraying neem seed extract or soapy water helps clear these pests so new leaves can grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem dumɔwui amli nu loo nu ni akɛ samla shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni baai heei anyɛ akwɛ̃ bɔ ni sa.

english: This condition is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often when watering is irregular. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the plant pull calcium up from the soil into the developing tomatoes.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ji fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, afɔɔɔ amɛ nu be fɛɛ be Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛjieɔ calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa tomatoi ni miiya hiɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my orange trees drop small green fruits shortly after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso lɛ miiho aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Beni efɔ fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fruit drop happens when the tree lacks enough water or food to support all the fruits, or when fruit flies damage them. Giving trees compost and watering them during dry spells helps them hold onto their fruit.
ga: Yibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ yibii lɛ fɛɛ akwɛ nɔ. Aloo kɛ́ aduawai amli ŋmeii kpata amɛhiɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ mli ni awo lɛ nu yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ yibii amli.

english: Why do farmers say that planting beans or cowpeas makes the next crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in their roots. When the legume plant harvest ends, that trapped nitrogen breaks down in the soil to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa kpamɔ lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ fãa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my vegetable crops droop in the hot afternoon even when the soil is not completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? The land is not completely dry?

english: On hot days, leaves lose water to the hot air faster than roots can drink it up. Covering the soil around the plant roots with dry grass or leaves (mulching) keeps the roots cool and reduces water loss.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulching) ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa nu ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Yellow leaves at the base of maize plants are a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency. The plant moves nitrogen from older lower leaves to feed newer growth at the top, showing that the soil needs fertilizer or compost.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha dalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ niyenii. Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How do cowpea crops make the soil better for my next maize harvest?
ga: Te cowpea tsei haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with tiny organisms in the soil to pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that nitrogen stays in the soil as free natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ feɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ejie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛto shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Cassava stem cuttings have buds that point upward toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the new shoots must waste energy bending back upward, leading to weak growth and very few tubers.
ga: Cassava nine lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, esa akɛ tsei heei lɛ afite hewalɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛku amɛsɛɛ kɛya ŋwɛi. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ baa.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow tall and bushy under big trees but fail to give me fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni efeɔ ŋmɔji yɛ tso agbo ko shishi shi ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants need direct sunlight to make energy for flowering and fruiting. Under heavy shade, the plant spends all its energy stretching upward to reach the light instead of producing peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ hia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo. yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ shishi Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛgbala ehe kɛya ŋwɛi koni ená la moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by heat stress or tiny insects called whiteflies that spread the Tomato Leaf Curl Virus. The curling is the plant's way of reducing water loss or reacting to the insect infection.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo loo kooloi bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmei yɛŋ ni gbɛɔ Tomato Leaf Curl Virus lɛ eshwaa lɛ. Curling ji gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛhaa nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ baa shi loo nɔ ni amɛfeɔ kɛji kooloi tsɛŋemɔ helai emɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers drop off the tree without turning into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by severe dry weather, lack nutrients, or lack tiny pollinating insects called midges to fertilize the flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni naa wa, niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ hao amɛ. The so-called gnats fertilize the flowers.

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and heavy stems filled with water. When the soil becomes soft from rain and fruit bunches make the plant top-heavy, strong winds can easily pull the shallow roots out of the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ tso ni mli tse ni nu eyi mli obɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ efee bɔdɔɔ kɛjɛ nugbɔ lɛ mli ni aduawai lɛ ebɔle ehe lɛ haa tso lɛ náa kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ ooojɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why do young yam vines wither quickly when rain stops for just a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato tsei lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Young yam plants have soft, tender stems and shallow root systems that cannot search deep into the ground for water. They need mulching around the seed yam to keep the soil cool and moist.
ga: Young sweet potato plants have soft stems. kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ atao nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. They need to cover the ground around them. Dumɔ sweet potato dumɔwui koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Why is it bad to plant maize seeds saved from last year's hybrid harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ aaadu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa fee lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for high yields only in their first generation. Seeds saved from that harvest lose those special traits, resulting in uneven growth, smaller cobs, and much lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee. Cob lɛ ji bibioo fe no. ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi kwraa.

english: Why do my sweet potatoes start rotting quickly after I dig them out of the dry ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya beni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Digging up sweet potatoes often creates tiny cuts on their skin where soil rot organisms enter. Leaving the harvested tubers in a warm, shady spot for a few days cures the skin, making it thick enough to prevent rot.
ga: Digging sweet potatoes often causes small cuts. yɛ hewolo lɛ nɔ he ni nibii ni fiteɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ebote mli lɛ Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua hewolo lɛ ni etsa. Make it thick enough to prevent rotting.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide shade and keep the soil moist, giving the young cocoa trees the right environment to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa kookoo tso bibioo lɛ naa shihilɛ ni sa ni ekɛhiɔ shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Staking exposes yam leaves to sunlight so the plant can make more food. This energy goes down into the roots, helping the plant grow much larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Staking haa hulu la shɛɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ awo niyenii babaoo. This energy goes down to the roots. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enáa sweet potato ŋmeii ni dara kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Managing whiteflies early using neem oil sprays or sticky traps helps prevent the spread of the disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Mra be mli whitefly nɔkwɛmɔ Kɛtsɔ neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsɔnei ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni akɛtsuɔ nii. It will help prevent the spread of disease.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers from heat stress, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil evenly moist and using balanced fertilizer helps flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize is a signal that the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need for healthy green growth. Applying nitrogen fertilizers like urea or well-rotted animal manure restores soil fertility.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Groundnuts are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. When you plant maize afterward, it feeds on this left-behind nitrogen and grows stronger.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Ebaaye nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ ni ebaada waa.

english: How do I know which end of a cassava stick cutting should face up when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmei lɛ fã ni esa akɛ ekwɛ ŋwɛi beni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Always plant cassava cuttings with the small raised buds or nodes pointing upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down causes shoots to grow weakly and reduces the amount of cassava roots produced.
ga: Esa akɛ adu cassava niji kɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, ŋwɛi ni oootsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛ́ odu ohiɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ. ni ajie ŋmei shishifãi ni ajieɔ lɛ shi

english: Why should I cut away some of the extra shoots growing around the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ ekomɛi? Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: Too many shoots, or suckers, compete with the main plantain stalk for nutrients and water. Leaving only one main plant and one or two strong suckers ensures you get larger, heavier bunches of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ plantain tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ oshi tso titri kome pɛ kɛ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha ona ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why does my lowland rice field need standing water during the early stages of growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ aná nu ni damɔ shi yɛ shishijee be mli ni edara lɛ?

english: Standing water smothers weeds that would otherwise steal light and nutrients from the young rice. It also provides the constant moisture rice needs to develop strong stems and full grain heads.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni egbeɔ jwɛi ni baanyɛ aju la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa bibii amli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ hu ni enáa ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be koni ená ŋmãa ni mli wa kɛ dumɔwui ayitsei ni eyi obɔ.

english: How can I prevent small insects from eating holes in my stored cowpeas or beans?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaye mi-cowpeas loo beans ni mikɛto lɛ?

english: Insects like weevils attack stored beans if there is moisture and air. Thoroughly sun-drying your beans before storing them in sealed, airtight containers or hermetic bags suffocates insects and keeps them safe for months.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii baatutua kɔfi yibii ni ato lɛ kɛji ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ mli. Gbimɔ ŋmeii lɛ dani okɛwo tsɛnsi ko ni atsĩ naa loo vacuum kotoku mli. Ebaaha kooloi bibii lɛ agbɔjɔ ni eha amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when they get direct sun all day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and shallow roots that dry out easily under intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides a living umbrella that keeps the soil cool and moist while the trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee hulutsoo ni eha ŋmɔtɔ aba be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and soft when the rainy season gets heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛhe yɔɔ blɛoo yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in damp, humid conditions. Pruning excess branches to let sunlight reach the farm and removing infected pods quickly will help stop the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni shwereɔ yɛ fɛ̃i, fɛ̃i shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la ashɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to stay green and grow fast. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores healthy leaf color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baa lɛ su ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do the leaves on my young corn plants look like someone shot tiny holes through them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni mɔ ko efo bu bibii kɛtsɔ mli lɛ?

english: This leaf damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the central leaf funnel of the plant. Checking the central shoots early allows you to apply control measures before the worms destroy the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ faa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ oyeɔ nɔ dani ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Which part of a cassava stalk should I use as planting material for my new field?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmei tso lɛ fã esa akɛ mikɛtsu nii akɛ dumɔ nii kɛha shikpɔŋ hee?

english: You should use the firm, mature middle section of a healthy cassava stem rather than the soft green top or old root base. Cut pieces about 20 to 30 centimeters long, ensuring the growth buds point upward when placed in the soil.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmei tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eyɛ hewalɛ lɛ atsu nii. Mohu ɔ, ngɔ yi mi tomi nɛ ngɛ ŋmɔŋ loo sisi tomi momohi kɛ tsu ní. Kpɔ̃ɔ mli bibii aaafee sɛntimita 20 kɛyashi 30, ni okwɛ koni ŋmeii ni miida lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the underground tubers to grow large. Staking lifts the vines off the ground, improving air movement, preventing leaf diseases, and helping the plant capture light efficiently.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdara. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ Tsiɔ baa helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmɔɔ la jogbaŋŋ

english: How can I tell which plantain suckers are best to dig up and plant on my new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mafolɔ ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ hee lɛ mli?

english: Look for 'sword suckers', which have narrow, spear-shaped leaves and a broad, heavy bulb at the base. Avoid 'water suckers' that grow broad leaves early, as they produce weak plants and smaller bunches.
ga: Taomɔ ‘sword shoot’, ni yɔɔ baai ni mli tse ni tamɔ lance kɛ yitso ni mli kwɔ ni tsii yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ‘sucker shoot’, ni yɔɔ baai ni mli lɛɛɔ oya lɛ he ejaakɛ enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ekɛ ŋmeii bibii aba.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my green tomatoes turning dark black and soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ naagbeei lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni eyɛ blɛoo lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit, often triggered by dry soil. Keeping the soil moisture steady with regular watering helps the plant take up calcium properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni oooha ehi shi daa kɛ nu ni oooha lɛ daa lɛ baaye abua ni otso lɛ aná calcium ni sa.

english: Why are the small flowers on my pepper plants dropping off without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ji No hewɔ lɛ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsɔɔɔ pepper?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by intense heat, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen in the soil. Consistent watering and light shade during extremely hot periods help the plant retain its blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do experts advise me not to burn the cleared weeds on my farm before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nilelɔi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mikashã jwɛi ni ajie yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani midu lɛ?

english: Burning destroys valuable organic matter and kills beneficial soil organisms that feed your crops. Clearing land without burning allows dead plants to decay naturally into organic manure, improving soil fertility and water retention.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ ni ashãaa lɛ haa tsei ni egboi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ kɛ nu ni ahiɔ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ.
