english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and dry up when I remove all the surrounding trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei fɛɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are naturally understory crops that cannot handle direct harsh sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains to filter the sun, the young leaves overheat, lose moisture rapidly, and burn.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii ji tsei ni yɔɔ tsei ashishi ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo loo dumɔwui ni baatsi hulu lɛ naa bɛ lɛ, baai bibii lɛ baadɔ waa. Efiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya ni ebaanyɛ eshã.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot in the ground when we get heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain saturates poorly draining soil, water replaces the air, effectively suffocating the roots and allowing fungal rot to take over.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nu baaye kɔɔyɔɔ najiaŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ yeɔ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient it uses to produce food and maintain its green color. Applying manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps bring back the green health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii titri ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ niyenii afeemɔ mli, ni amɛhaa amɛhe su lɛ hiɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do small caterpillars hide deep inside the funnel of my maize leaves instead of sitting on top of the leaf?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaata baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm hide deep in the moist, rolled leaves at the center of the plant to protect themselves from sunlight and predators while feeding on the softest leaves.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ teɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai ni mli efɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ baai ni mli tse fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Plantain plants do not have deep, woody taproots; they rely on shallow root systems. As the bunch gets heavy, the top becomes unbalanced, making it easy for wind to pull the shallow roots right out of the soil.
ga: Seedlings do not have a deep, woody taproot. They rely on a shallow root system. Beni kuu lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɔjɔɔ lɛ Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ ejaaa. ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ aaaje shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Extreme heat and dry weather dry out the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing fertilization. When a flower is not fertilized, the plant sheds it to conserve energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ mli lɛ gĩɔ. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa Kɛji afɔɔɔ fɔfɔi Tsei lɛ jieɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into tight wrinkles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the sap from undersides of leaves, or by viruses transmitted by these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Yam vines naturally climb to lift their leaves higher off the ground into full sunlight. Spreading the leaves on a stake helps the plant capture sunlight more efficiently to feed the growing tuber under the soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛwo amɛbaa lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Kɛ́ agbɛ baai lɛ ashwã tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni emɔɔ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii.

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that work with helpful soil bacteria to pull nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food, leaving enriched soil behind for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsake lɛ amɛfee tsei aniyenii. Kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni ashiɔ ahaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and spread dark spots to other pods during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbɛɔ ŋmeii diji amɛshwaa ŋmeii krokomɛi anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in cold, wet conditions. Raindrops splash the fungal spores from infected soil or pods onto nearby healthy pods, spreading the disease rapidly.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ. This will cause the disease to spread quickly.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize crops turning yellow from the bottom up even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ moŋ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that your crop lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for lush green growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure restores healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans in my field make the soil better for growing corn in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmei dumɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants die, this nitrogen remains in the soil to naturally fertilize the next crop.
ga: Peas kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nɛkɛ nitrogen nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛwo tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn and dry out quickly in full direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains provides shelter and protects the soil from drying out while the cocoa establishes its roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa he ko ni ebuɔ he koni ekagbi yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shishifãi shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why does covering the bare soil around my vegetable plants with dry grass keep them from wilting in the heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi haa mi-vegetable tsei lɛ ahe koni amɛkagboi yɛ latsaa be mli lɛ.

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, shields the ground from the hot sun, prevents water from evaporating quickly, and keeps root zones cool during dry periods.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekaho oya ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ ahe jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ.

english: Why are the blossoms on my pepper plants falling off without turning into any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress or irregular watering. Keeping moisture levels consistent in the soil helps the plant retain flowers so they can form fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni amɛhaaa amɛ daa lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔii amli ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why should I pinch off the extra side shoots growing out of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ sɛɛ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Removing small extra shoots, called suckers, prevents the tomato plant from wasting its food energy on excess leaf growth and directs those nutrients into forming larger, healthier fruits.
ga: removing small shoots That's called sucking out. Enɛ baatsi tomato tso lɛ naa koni ekafite niyenii hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine ni miida lɛ nɔ. kɛ nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛfee aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers small and thin even though the plants grew very tall above the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe ejɔ waa lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni ŋmei tso lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ nɛkɛ?

english: When cassava stems are planted too close together, they compete heavily for underground space, sunlight, and soil nutrients, leading to lots of top foliage but tiny, underdeveloped roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi he ko, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋwɛi baai babaoo baa shi shishifãi bibii ni edako.

english: Why do my seeds fail to push out of the ground when I push them deep into the soil during planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikɛ amɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ dumɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Seeds carry limited food energy inside them to sprout and reach sunlight. Buried too deep, the young shoot exhausts its energy supply before reaching the surface and dies underground.
ga: Dumɔwui bɛ niyenii hewalɛ ni haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛ hulu la ni amɛaaná lɛ. Tsobii bibii ni afu amɛ tsɔ Ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii dani eshɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do caterpillars target the soft center leaves of my corn stalks instead of the outer leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ miikwɛ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai bibii lɛ anɔ moŋ fe kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ?

english: Pests like the fall armyworm seek out the tender, growing funnel of the maize plant because it offers young, nutrient-rich leaves and protection from predators.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ taoɔ ŋmeii tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛdaraa lɛ amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ babaoo yɛ baai bibii lɛ amli, ni ebuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my pepper crops wilt during the hottest part of the afternoon even when the soil was watered in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can draw it up from the soil. The plant temporarily wilts to conserve moisture and usually recovers when the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves often mean young cocoa trees are receiving too much direct sunlight or lack nitrogen. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects young trees from harsh sun while helping the soil retain moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiná hulu la babaoo tɛ̃ɛ loo nitrogen bɛ amɛmli. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: What causes the green cocoa pods on my trees to suddenly turn black and dry up?
ga: Mɛni ha kookoo ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ trukaa ni amɛgbi?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly during rainy and humid weather. Clearing nearby weeds and pruning extra branches lets sunlight and air dry out the farm, stopping the disease from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela ni ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ni afo tsei niji krokomɛi amli lɛ, ebaaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi aya hiɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. ni ekpa helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. Checking the leaf centers (funnels) early in the season and applying recommended extension treatments will protect your crop before the pests multiply.
ga: Fall Armyworm tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ateŋ (cones) yɛ be lɛ mli mra ni okɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ agbɛɔ ashwãa lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe dani tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How can I tell the right time to plant my maize when the rains are unreliable?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa be mli ni anyɛɛɛ akɛ he afɔ̃ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Wait until the soil receives two to three consecutive days of good rain so that moisture sinks deep. Planting in dry soil after a single light rain causes seeds to rot or sprout and die quickly.
ga: Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nugbɔ kpakpa gbii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ koni nugbɔ lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Dumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbo loo amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi oya.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall with lots of leaves, but the roots underneath remain tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil pushes cassava to put all its energy into growing stem and leaves instead of tubers. Avoiding heavy nitrogen fertilizers and choosing well-drained, potassium-rich soil encourages bigger roots.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsirɛɔ ŋmei lɛ koni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ aya ŋmeii kɛ baai ni miida lɛ anɔ. yɛ yitso najiaŋ Kɛ́ otsi ohe kɛjɛ nitrogen ni tsii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he, ni ohala shikpɔŋ ni potassium yɔɔ mli ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdara.

english: What causes my cassava leaves to curl up and display yellow and green patches?
ga: Mɛni haa cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ?

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by whiteflies and infected stem cuttings. The best solution is to plant certified disease-resistant stem varieties provided by your local agricultural office.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni yɔɔ ŋmeii yɛji kɛ niji ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ akɛ mɛi ni kɛ hela baa Ogbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni odu tso yibii sɔrɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli nitsumɔhe ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛhaa lɛ.

english: Yam rot occurs when heavy water collects around the roots in flat soil. Planting yams on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away, keeping the underground tubers healthy.
ga: Sweet potato rot baa kɛji akɛ muji bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse nɔ. Sweet potato ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni ewaje shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ

english: Why are my tomato plant blossoms falling off before any fruits start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiwo aduawai dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants experience heat stress or irregular watering. Watering consistently at the base of the plant during hot spells keeps the plant cool enough to set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi daa yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why are my pepper plants suddenly wilting and dying during the hot afternoon even when the soil is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: This is typically caused by bacterial wilt, a soil-borne disease that blocks water channels inside the stem. Rotating your crops every season prevents these bacteria from accumulating in your soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni shikpɔŋ ni tsiɔ nu gbɛi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ́ otsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa be lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkabua amɛhe naa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my cabbage plants spreading wide open instead of forming a firm, round head?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa babaoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee yitso ni ma shi shiŋŋ ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to head when planted too close together or when they lack adequate water and shade during hot periods. Proper spacing and consistent soil moisture encourage the leaves to wrap tightly into a head.
ga: Cabbage nyɛŋ atswa yitso kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ loo kɛji akɛ nu kɛ hulutsoo be ni sa bɛ mli yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ bulb lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my maize crops turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a major nutrient needed for leaf growth. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen out of the soil, so applying fertilizer like urea or adding well-rotted manure replenishes the plant food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ adara Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ niyenii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm before planting my main grain crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them first leaves natural fertilizer behind, making the soil richer for grains planted afterward.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei ni aduɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ shĩɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ kɛha sɛɛ mli ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Young cocoa plants have thin, delicate leaves that dry out quickly under full sun. Planting shade crops like plantains around them creates living shade and keeps the air humid, keeping the young seedlings alive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ mli egbiɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be tamɔ plantains yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka aba ni ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni oha tso bibioo lɛ ahi shi

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Lifting the vines on stakes exposes more leaves to sunlight and keeps them away from damp soil diseases, resulting in much larger yams.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ haa hulu la babaoo naa tsei lɛ ahe, ni ehaaa helai aba shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ bafee wuji babaoo.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting in the ground during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water prevents oxygen from reaching them. In heavy clay soil, planting cassava on top of raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the tubers stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu lɛ ehi shi, ni no haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa lɛ ayashɛ amɛhe. yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers without growing any fruit during very hot weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ shwie efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni ewooo yibii ko yɛ otsi kome ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and irregular watering stress tomato plants, making their pollen dry out. When the plant senses it cannot support fruiting due to heat or drought, it drops its blossoms to save its own life.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa pollen ni egbi lɛ baa. Beni tsei nuɔ he akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii yɛ latsaa loo hɔmɔ hewɔ lɛ. Ebaashɛ fɔfɔii ashwie shi koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala.

english: Why do my leaf vegetables look limp and soft in the middle of the afternoon even if I watered them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ amɛnɔ oya moŋ?

english: In intense afternoon heat, leaves lose water to the air faster than roots can drink it up. The plant wilts temporarily to close its pores and save moisture, usually recovering by evening as temperatures drop.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛŋa eshishifãi lɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ beni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper is often caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips or aphids that transmit plant viruses. Using natural sprays like neem oil early on stops these insects from damaging leaf tissue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. Adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi tamɔ neem fɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Koni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akafite baa lɛ mli fãji.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily right when the fruit bunches grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots to anchor them, so top-heavy fruit bunches and strong winds easily pull them up. Propping up the main stem with bamboo poles gives the plant physical support until harvest.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni baaye abua amɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, aduawai akui ni amɛyitsei ni tsii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tso ko to tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eye ebua tso lɛ kɛyashi be mli ni abaakpa.

english: Why does my mango tree drop many small green fruits long before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mangoi lɛ miiho aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Babaoo dani eda?

english: Mango trees naturally drop excess young fruit if they lack enough water, nutrients, or energy to support them all. Regular feeding and pruning allow the tree to concentrate its strength on holding onto a healthy final yield.
ga: Mango tsei lɛ baajie aduawai bibii ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛbɛ nu, niyenii mli hewalɛ, loo hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha aduawai lɛ fɛɛ aye abua. Niyenii ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa kɛ tsei ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa naagbee ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Should I soak my groundnut seeds in water over the weekend before planting them on Monday?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmei dumɔwui awo nu mli yɛ otsi lɛ naagbee dani madu yɛ Hɔɔ?

english: No, you should never soak groundnut seeds before planting. Soaking seeds in water for a couple of days causes them to rot and spoil before they even reach the soil.
ga: Dabi, esaaa akɛ okɛ ŋmei dumɔwui woɔ nu mli dani oduɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui wo nu mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ, ebaaha amɛgboi ni amɛfite dani amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po.

english: Why do groundnut seeds rot when I soak them in water before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ awo amɛ nu mli dani adu lɛ?

english: Groundnut seeds absorb water too quickly when submerged, which suffocates the living embryo inside and causes fungal rotting within two days instead of healthy growth.
ga: Peanut dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ nu oya tsɔ kɛji akɛ awo amɛ nu mli. Enɛ haa fɔmɔ kotokui ni hiɛ ka ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi. and causes the mold to decay within two days. Yɛ dalɛ kpakpa najiaŋ lɛ

english: Is preparing groundnuts for planting the same as softening them to cook for dinner?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni asaa kɛha dumɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni afee lɛ blɛoo koni akɛhoo kɛha gbɛkɛ niyenii lɛ yeɔ egbɔ?

english: No, cooking and planting require opposite methods. Soaking groundnuts softens them for cooking, but planting seeds must remain completely dry until placed in moist soil to stay alive.
ga: Dabi, nihoomɔ kɛ tsei akwɛmɔ biɔ gbɛ ni teɔ shi woɔ enɛ. Soaking peanuts softens them in cooking. Shi esa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ agbi kwraa kɛyashi be mli ni akɛ amɛ baawo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Can I buy groundnuts from the general market and soak them to help them sprout faster on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mahe ŋmei yɛ jara nɔ ni mikɛwo nu mli koni eye ebua ni ekwɛ̃ oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Market groundnuts can be used, but soaking them will kill them. Keep the seeds dry until planting day, as wet groundnuts will spoil in just a day or two.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ jara nɔ ŋmeii atsu nii. Shi kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii lɛ wo nu mli lɛ, ebaagbe amɛ. Ha dumɔwui lɛ agbi kɛyashi dumɔ gbi lɛ nɔ. Akpɔlɔi ni efɔ lɛ baafite yɛ gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ mli.

english: Why didn't my groundnuts sprout after I washed and soaked them a few days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mifɔ amɛhe ni mikɛwo nu mli gbii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are very sensitive to standing water before planting. Soaking triggers rapid spoilage instead of germination, ruining the seed.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ nuɔ he waa dani aduɔ. Nu mli ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa efiteɔ oya moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ̃. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dumɔwui lɛ afitemɔ.

english: What happens to groundnut seeds if they get wet before I put them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmei dumɔwui anɔ kɛji amɛtsɔ nu dani mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ?

english: When groundnut seeds get wet before planting, bacteria and mold break them down rapidly, causing them to spoil within two days.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei dumɔwui lɛ edɔ dani adu lɛ Bacteria kɛ fungi fiteɔ oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ mli.

english: How far in advance can I get my groundnut seeds wet before planting day?
ga: Be enyiɛ dani dumɔ gbi lɛ baashɛ ni manyɛ mafɔ mi-peanut dumɔwui lɛ anɔ?

english: You should not get groundnut seeds wet at all before planting day. Seeds should go into the moist soil completely dry so the soil controls the moisture naturally.
ga: Esaaa akɛ okɛ o-peanut dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi dani dumɔ gbi lɛ baashɛ. Esa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi kwraa nɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ akwɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What is the best way to keep my groundnut seeds healthy before planting week?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni aaatsɔ nɔ aha ŋmei dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ dani adu yɛ otsi nɛɛ mli?

english: Keep your groundnut seeds in a dry, cool place without exposing them to water. Keeping them dry prevents premature rotting and ensures high germination.
ga: Okɛ ŋmeii ato he ko ni mli ejɔ ni nu bɛ he. Kɛ́ egbi lɛ, ebaatsi fitemɔ ni baa oya lɛ naa, ni ebaaha ekwɛ̃ waa.

english: Why do my neighbours tell me not to wet my groundnut seeds before putting them in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mikaha mi-bean lɛ mli ewo nu dani mikɛ sũ afutu lɛ?

english: Your neighbours are correct because groundnuts spoil very fast when soaked in water outside the soil, destroying your crop investment before it starts.
ga: Okutsoŋnyo lɛ ja ejaakɛ ŋmeii fiteɔ oya waa kɛ́ akɛwo nu mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kponɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ onibii ni okɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ dani odumɔ jeɔ shishi.

english: How does moisture in soil treat groundnut seeds differently than moisture in a bucket of water?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛfeɔ ŋmei dumɔwui lɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ nu baagi mli lɛ he?

english: Moist soil gives groundnut seeds small amounts of water along with oxygen from air pockets, whereas soaking in a bucket cuts off air and drowns the seed in two days.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ŋmei dumɔwui lɛ náa nu fioo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ amli lɛ. Beni akɛwoɔ tanki mli lɛ, efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ nu mli yɛ gbii enyɔ mli.

english: What happens if I plant too many maize seeds in one small spot?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo yɛ he bibioo kome?

english: When seeds are planted too closely together, the plants fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow thin and weak, resulting in very small cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baawu koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛhe tsɔi ni amɛgbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if there seems to be enough space in the field?
ga: Te jwɛi baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji etamɔ nɔ ni he ko yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli bɔ ni sa?

english: Weeds have strong roots that steal water and fertilizers directly from the soil before your crops can reach them. They also block sunlight, which stunts crop growth.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ. Etsiɔ hulu la hu naa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraaa.

english: Can I keep growing cassava on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the field. Switching to a different crop helps the soil recover.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be mli, ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee tsei krokomɛi anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ehe feɔ fɛo.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have wide leaves that act like natural umbrellas, shielding young cocoa from the heat until it matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Buu kookoo bibioo lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he kɛyashi ebaagbɔ.

english: What happens to my crop roots if heavy rainwater stands on my farm for several days?
ga: Mɛni baaba mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo?

english: Standing water cuts off oxygen to the soil, suffocating the roots. Without air, the roots rot, which prevents the plant from taking up food and eventually kills it.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shishifãi lɛ baagboi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ egbeɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my vegetable plants droop during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves droop in intense heat as a defense mechanism to reduce water loss from evaporation. Once the temperature drops in the late afternoon, the leaves usually stand back up.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni ashiɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ teɔ shi ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants turning yellow instead of staying bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the plant lacks key nutrients like nitrogen, or that the ground is overwatered and preventing the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo ni eha shishifãi lɛ miigbɔjɔ.

english: Flowers drop off when the plant undergoes stress, which is often caused by sudden dry spells, extreme midday heat, or a lack of insects to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ haomɔ kpe. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmɔlɔ ni baa trukaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii ni baaha fɔfɔii lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ni bɛ

english: Why is it better to transplant my young nursery seedlings late in the afternoon instead of early morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ adu shwane mli moŋ fe leebi maŋkpa lɛ?

english: Moving seedlings shocks their delicate roots. Transplanting in the cool afternoon gives the plants the entire night to settle into the soil before facing the harsh sun.
ga: Dumɔwu lɛ ni oootsi lɛ baaha eshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ akpokpo. Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ yɛ shwane ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbɛkɛ muu lɛ fɛɛ dani hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ enɔ.

english: Why should I trim off some of the extra side shoots from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi tomato tsei lɛ ahe ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ?

english: Trimming extra shoots forces the plant to send its water and nutrients straight into developing big, healthy fruits rather than wasting energy on growing extra leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ tsɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ koni ewo yibii wuji ni mli wa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ ni okɛbaakwɛ baai krokomɛi lɛ

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to build green leaves. It can also happen when the soil stays too wet and suffocates the plant's roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small even though the stem and leaves above ground are growing very big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii nɛkɛ be mli ni shishifãi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ edara waa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or receives excessive fertilizer, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing green leaves and branches above ground instead of storing starch in the roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo enine eshɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ŋmei baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa baai eŋɔli kɛ niji ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the edges of my garden egg leaves turning brown and looking burnt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni etamɔ nɔ ni eshã lɛ?

english: Burnt brown edges on leaves often mean the plant is lacking potassium, which helps control water movement inside the crop, or that chemical fertilizer was applied too close to the main stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni shã ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ potassium bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekwɛɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. aloo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛfataa he ni bɛŋkɛɔ tso wulu lɛ he tsɔ

english: Why do my cowpea leaves fold up and close during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛŋmɛɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants naturally curl or fold their leaves during intense heat to conserve moisture. Shrinking the leaf area exposed to direct sun reduces water loss through evaporation.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ baafolɔ loo amɛbaafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. He ni baai lɛ yɔɔ ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast with large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, shielding young cocoa plants from heat while keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their blossoms before any peppers start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when temperatures get too high, when watering is inconsistent, or when the soil lacks phosphorus, which is needed to help the plant set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ daa loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ phosphorus ni he hiaa koni eye ebua tsei ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce flowers but fail to make nuts underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi shi jeee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ?

english: After pollination, groundnut flowers send down stalks called 'pegs' that must push into soft soil to form nuts. If the soil is too hard or lacks calcium, the pegs cannot penetrate or build strong shells.
ga: yɛ pollination sɛɛ Peanut fɔfɔi lɛ tsuɔ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘pegs’ ni esa akɛ ashɛre kɛya shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ nɔ koni efee nut lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo calcium bɛ mli lɛ Pin lɛ nyɛŋ abote mli loo efee ŋmei ni mli wa.

english: Why do my yam tubers split open or grow into strange shapes inside the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ amli gbalaa loo amɛmiida ni amɛmiifee nibii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams split or deform when they hit hard, rocky soil or when heavy rains suddenly follow a long dry period, causing the root tissue to expand faster than the skin can stretch.
ga: Sweet potatoes fãa loo efiteɔ kɛ́ etswa shikpɔŋ ni wa ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. aloo beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifã lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ akpã mli.

english: How can I tell if my tomato plants are dying from wilt disease or just thirsty from the sun?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-tomato tsei lɛ miigboi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli loo kumai miiye amɛ kɛkɛ kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Thirsty tomato plants recover and stand upright again in the cool evening after watering. Plants infected with bacterial or fungal wilt will stay wilted and dry up even when the soil is wet.
ga: Tomato tsei ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ baaná hewalɛ ni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be mli beni awo amɛ nu lɛ sɛɛ. Tsei ni helatsɛmɛi loo tsɛŋemɔ helai emɔ amɛ lɛ baaya nɔ agbi ni amɛgbi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Why do the leaves of my okra plants curl upward and feel sticky to the touch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji ota he lɛ?

english: Sticky, curled okra leaves are a clear sign of tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies. They feed on the plant's sap and secrete a sweet liquid that leaves the plant feeling sticky.
ga: Okra baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies lɛ yɛ. Amɛ yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛ jieɔ nu ni ŋɔɔ ni haa tso lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up under full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings lose water faster than their small roots can absorb it when exposed to direct heat. Planting them under shade crops like plantains protects them until their root systems develop fully.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nu fiteɔ oya fe shishifãi bibii. ni baaŋɔ kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo la mli tɛ̃ɛ Tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu tso lɛ he kɛyashi eshishifãi lɛ baatsɔ hiɛ kwraa.

english: Why are there small holes in my maize leaves with tiny caterpillars inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? And there's a little worm in the cone?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds on young maize leaves. Early control using recommended sprays or placing clean ash or sand in the plant whorl helps prevent severe crop loss.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. nɔkwɛmɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Kɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwie nɔ loo sũ ni he tse loo ŋã ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite waa.

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific soil nutrients and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas helps restore nitrogen naturally to the soil.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baafite shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii komɛi be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How do I know if my soil needs manure or fertilizer before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii dani madu nii?

english: If your previous crops produced pale leaves, weak stems, or small harvests despite getting enough rain, your soil lacks essential nutrients and requires organic manure or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji onibii ni odu tsutsu lɛ yɛ baai ni tsuɔ, tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, loo ŋmaa fioo ko yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ebiɔ ni akɛ humus loo humus atsu nii.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant beans alongside my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ wo ŋaa akɛ mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ adu ŋmeii?

english: Legume crops like beans capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, acting as a natural fertilizer for surrounding plants.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa tsei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water settles in the soil for too long, suffocating the roots. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away properly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from irregular watering, extreme heat, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Consistent soil moisture helps the flowers set fruit successfully.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ be fɛɛ be, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he amanehulu. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Too many suckers compete with the main plantain tree for nutrients and water, resulting in small bunches. Pruning down to one main stem and one or two young shoots keeps energy focused on large fruit production.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tso yibii bibii Afolɔ koni ashi tso lɛ yibii titri kome kɛ tso yibii bibii kome loo enyɔ haa hewalɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa yibii wuji ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yam vines need to climb toward direct sunlight so their leaves can make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking also lifts leaves off wet ground to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni akɛ ebaai lɛ atsu nii akɛ niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ tsei ahe tsei lɛ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce small yields even when it rains well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo yibii fioo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds aggressively steal sunlight, root space, water, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the resources they need to produce a full yield.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ hulu la, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛshɛ yibiiwoo ni yeɔ emuu he.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants turn brown and drop off when the sun gets too bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulu la lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct heat and burn easily under strong sunlight. The leaves dry out and fall off as a defense mechanism to keep the plant's stem from losing all its moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ, ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ naa koni ekaje emli nu fɛɛ.

english: When temperatures get too high, the heat damages the pollen inside tomato blossoms, preventing fruit from forming. The plant then sheds the useless flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Dɔlɛ kpataa pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ ahiɛ. Ehaa aduawai lɛ efeee No sɛɛ lɛ tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning pale yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate that the plant is starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient responsible for green leafy growth. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ daa lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when we have heavy rain for several weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa otsii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Excessive rain fills up all the air spaces in the soil, preventing plant roots from breathing. Without air, cassava tubers suffocate, allowing soil fungus to quickly decay the roots.
ga: Too much rain fills the air spaces in the soil. Prevents plant roots from breathing. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ Kasava shishifãi lɛ baafo. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ oya.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and wilt in the afternoon sun even when the ground is not completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbiko kwraa moŋ?

english: In intense afternoon heat, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can draw it from the soil. The plant wilts to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun to save water, and it usually recovers by evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei baagbi koni ekɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi koni ekɛbu nu he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ

english: Why do I need to stick tall wooden poles in the soil for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tso kakadaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to spread out high in the air to capture sunlight so they can manufacture food for the tuber underground. Lifting the leaves off the wet soil also prevents fungal diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni enyɛ emɔ hulu la bɔni afee ni ekɛ niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Small shoots (suckers) compete with the main plantain stem for water and nutrients. Removing the extra shoots allows all the energy to go into the mother plant so it produces a larger plantain bunch.
ga: Tso bibii (tso lɛ) kɛ plantain tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa hewalɛ fɛɛ boteɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, obaaná plantains ŋmɔshi nibii ni da fe no.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to stay small and weak even when I plant high-quality seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than main crops and steal essential sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. When weeds are left in the field, your crops starve and cannot grow to their full size.
ga: Jwɛi daa oya fe tsei ni amɛ juɔ hulu la ni he hia, nu kɛ sũ mli niyenii. Beni ashi jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaye hɔmɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛdara kɛyashɛ amɛhe.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and getting twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsake lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on the underside of leaves and sucking out plant sap, or by viruses transmitted by these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava and maize grow better when I plant them together on the same field instead of alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ fee ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ fe ni mikome too midu lɛ?

english: Planting different crops together covers the soil faster to retain moisture, prevents weeds from spreading, and confuses pests because of the mixed scents and leaf shapes.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei babaoo yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ oya koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli. Tsi jwɛi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ naa ni efutuɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ejaakɛ baai lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔ kɛ amɛhe ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ efutu.

english: How soon after harvesting my palm fruit bunches should I boil them?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee oya tɛŋŋ?

english: Boiling your palm fruits within 24 to 48 hours after harvest stops the natural oil from spoiling and becoming bitter, ensuring you produce fresh, high-quality palm oil.
ga: Palm tso yibii ni ashãa yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 24 kɛyashi 48 mli yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ Ehaa adebɔɔ mli fɔji lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa onine shɛɔ ŋmei fɔ hee ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɔ.

english: How can I tell that a palm fruit bunch on my tree is fully ripe and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: A palm fruit bunch is mature and ready for harvest when you see a few loose, bright orange or red fruits naturally dropping to the ground around the base of the tree.
ga: Palm tsei akui lɛ edara ni amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni ona yibii fioo komɛi ni kpɛɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo tsuru ni gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why is it important to separate bad or damaged palm fruits from the good ones before processing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie ŋmei yibii ni efite loo efite lɛ kɛjɛ nɔ ni hi mli dani atsu he nii lɛ?

english: Sorting removes rotten or damaged fruits that can spoil the taste, smell, and overall quality of the oil extracted from the good fruits, helping you get a better market price.
ga: Nibii ni ahalaa lɛ jieɔ aduawai ni egboi loo efite ni baanyɛ afite mu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ aduawai kpakpai amli lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ, eŋɔli, kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ fɛɛ. Helps you get better market prices.

english: What happens if I use too much fire or burn the fruits while boiling them for oil?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ la babaoo tsu nii loo mikɛ tso yibii lɛ shã be mli ni mikɛ fɔ lɛ shãa lɛ?

english: Overheating or scorching the palm fruit damages the natural oil, turning it dark, giving it a burnt taste, and significantly reducing its value.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tso yibii lɛ wo la mli fe nine loo oshã lɛ, ebaafite adebɔɔ mli fɔji lɛ. Ehaa mu lɛ feɔ duŋ. ni ekɛ shãa ŋmɔlɔ baa ni ejara baa shi waa

english: Is it better to process my harvested palm fruit myself or take it to a specialized processor?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ obaatsu ŋmei yibii ni akpa lɛ he nii loo okɛya tsɔne krɛdɛɛ ko ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ mli?

english: Taking your fruit to a local processor with proper machinery helps extract more oil faster and saves you heavy labor, though doing it yourself allows you to manage smaller harvests directly.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ aduawai lɛ tee maŋ lɛ mli nitsumɔhe ko ni tsɔne ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ojie mu babaoo oya ni ebaaha okɛ nitsumɔ ni tsii akatsu nii. Eyɛ mli akɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ obaafee lɛ haa onyɛɔ otsuɔ nibii bibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe nii tɛ̃ɛ moŋ.

english: Why do my oil palm trees produce huge fruit bunches during rainy periods but smaller ones later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mu tsei lɛ shwereɔ babaoo yɛ nugbɔ be mli shi sɛɛ mli lɛ amɛfeɔ bibii lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees need plenty of water and sunshine to feed their fruits. During the wet season, abundant water allows the tree to form large bunches, while dry periods limit the tree's energy, resulting in smaller bunches.
ga: Nu babaoo kɛ hulu la he miihia oil palm tsei koni amɛye amɛyibii lɛ. Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ beaŋ lɛ, nu ni fa babaoo lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ kui wuji. Meanwhile, dry periods limit the plant's energy. As a result, the trees become smaller.

english: How do I know when the main harvest season for my palm fruit is coming to an end?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-palm yibii lɛ akpamɔ be titri lɛ miiba naagbee?

english: You will notice fewer new fruit bunches forming on the trees, the remaining bunches ripening all at the same time, and a general slowdown in fruit production.
ga: Obaayɔse akɛ aduawai heei ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yɛ jɛmɛ. It occurs less on trees. Nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ baakwɛ̃ ekomekomei. and a general slowdown in fruit production.

english: Why do my palm trees stop producing fruits completely at certain times of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tɛŋ tsei lɛ ekpaa yibiiwoo kwraa yɛ afi lɛ mli bei komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Trees go through a natural resting period after a heavy fruiting season. They use this time to gather and store nutrients in their trunk and roots so they can produce again in the next cycle.
ga: Tsei tsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be mli yɛ yibiiwoo be ni tsii sɛɛ. Akɛ be nɛɛ buaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ anaa ni amɛkɛtoɔ koni anyɛ afee amɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ sɛɛkuu ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Visiting your farm at least once or twice a week helps you spot diseases, pest damage, and overripe fruits early before you lose money or yield.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, kɛ́ oya oŋmɔ lɛ mli shikome loo shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona helai. Pest damage Ni aduawai lɛ shwereɔ oya dani shika loo nibii ni afeɔ lɛ fiteɔ.

english: What should I do on my farm after the harvest season completely finishes?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ́ kpamɔ be lɛ eba naagbee?

english: When the harvest ends, clear weeds around the trees, prune dead leaves, and apply fertilizer so your trees can recover and build strength for the next season.
ga: Kɛ kpamɔ lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Jiemɔ jwɛi ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ ni ofolɔ baai ni egboi lɛ fɛɛ. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni otsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and tender roots that easily burn and dry out under direct heat. They require shade trees like plantains or forest trees to shield them from intense sunlight and hold moisture in the soil while they establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni shãa oya ni egbiɔ yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulu tamɔ plantains loo koo mli tsei koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli beni amɛfeɔ amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why do I need to put long sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei kakadaji ama shi lɛ? Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to reach up to catch maximum sunlight to manufacture food for the plant. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, reducing disease and directing more energy into growing large underground tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ashɛ ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛná niyenii amɛha tso lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Ha helai aba shi ni okɛ hewalɛ babaoo atsu nii ni okɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I cut away the extra shoots or suckers growing around the base of my main plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine loo ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie plantain tso lɛ tso lɛ

english: When too many suckers grow together, they compete with the main mother plant for water and soil nutrients. Removing excess suckers ensures the main tree gets enough nourishment to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ he kome lɛ Amɛkɛ tso ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and build strong stalks. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients too deep for roots to reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔŋ mli ni amɛma ŋmeii ni wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ amli shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why are my cabbage plants growing long leaves on tall stems instead of forming a tight, round head?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ baai kakadaji yɛ tsei kakadaji anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee yitsei ni mli wa ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to head when temperatures are too high or when they receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, which causes the crop to produce excessive outer leaves instead of wrapping into a firm head.
ga: Kaabaji nyɛŋ afee yitso kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ enine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa kponɔgbɛ baai babaoo tsɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni aaawo bulb ni mli wa mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots go soft and rot in the ground when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When fields stay flooded or waterlogged for too long, oxygen cannot reach the roots, causing root rot disease to set in and spoil the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ nu eyi ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli loo akɛ nu to be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ehaa shishifãi kɛ tuber fitemɔ baa.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their blossoms without forming any tomatoes during very hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and dries up the pollen inside the flowers, preventing fertilization. When a flower cannot be pollinated, the plant naturally drops it to save energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ gĩɔ. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa Beni fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee pollin Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why does swamp rice grow well in flooded soil while my maize crop dies if water sits on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ swamp ŋmãa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ shi mi ŋmãa lɛ gboɔ kɛji nu yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air passages in their stems that act like tiny straws, carrying oxygen from the leaves down to the roots underwater. Maize roots do not have this feature and quickly drown in standing water.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛmli ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔnei bibii. Ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli kɛyaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. Abele shishifãi bɛ nɛkɛ su nɛɛ ni amɛshwieɔ oya yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cowpea pods end up with tiny holes and damaged seeds inside right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea pods lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hu fiteɔ dani akpaa

english: Small insects called pod borers lay eggs on cowpea flowers and young pods. When the larvae hatch, they bore holes directly into the pods to feed on the developing seeds inside.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ pod borers lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ tsina fɔfɔi kɛ pod bibii anɔ. Beni ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ lɛ Amɛfoɔ bu yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛye dumɔwui ni miiya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and wrinkling instead of spreading out flat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites that feed on the sap beneath the leaves, or by viral diseases spread by whiteflies that distort leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii yɛŋ ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibioo lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: If I plant cassava and plantains together on the same land, will they steal nutrients from each other?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmei kɛ plantain fee ekome yɛ he kome lɛ, Ani amɛbaaju niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛ amɛhe?

english: Yes, both crops are heavy feeders and will compete for nutrients and water if planted too closely. Proper spacing ensures each crop gets enough soil nutrients and light to grow healthily without reducing your total yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ shweremɔ wa ni amɛbaaye niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ yibiiwoo fɛɛ baa shi.

english: How do I choose good plantain suckers so I do not waste money buying bad planting material?
ga: How do I choose good plantain shoots? Bɔni afee ni ehe akahi ni ofite shika kɛhe nibii ni ehiii ni akɛduɔ nii.

english: Look for maiden suckers or sword suckers with narrow, spear-shaped leaves and thick bases. Avoid broad-leaved water suckers, as they are weaker, grow slower, and yield smaller fruit bunches.
ga: Taomɔ oblayei ashishifãi loo klante ashishifãi ni baai lɛ mli tse, ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ kɛ shishigbɛ ni mli tse. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ lɛ ahe. Akɛni ebɛ hewalɛ hewɔ lɛ, edaa blɛoo ni ekɛ ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: What happens if I plant my plantain suckers at the start of the dry season instead of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ midu dumɔwui yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli moŋ fe nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers need steady soil moisture to grow roots. Planting them in the dry season will cause them to dry out, rot, or stay stunted, leading to lost money and failed crop establishment.
ga: Plantain suckers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa koni shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃. Dumɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baaha tsei lɛ agbi, amɛgboi loo amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi, ni no baaha shika ni baafite kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafee nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba.

english: How can I keep weeds away from my young plants without paying extra money for farm labor?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi jwɛi kɛjɛ mi dumɔwui lɛ ahe ni miwooo ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ he nyɔmɔ babaoo?

english: You can cover the ground around your crop roots with dry grass, leaves, or crop leftovers. This mulching blocks sunlight from weed seeds, holds soil moisture, and cuts down on the need for frequent clearing.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ ashishifãi. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ baatsi hulu la ni jɛɔ jwɛi dumɔwui amli lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa ehe ehiaaa ni ajie shii abɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli

english: How can I improve my soil fertility for plantains if I cannot afford expensive chemical fertilizers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha plantains kɛji minyɛɛɛ mahe tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: You can use well-rotted poultry manure, cow dung, or decayed cocoa pod husks around the base of the plant. These organic materials add nutrients slowly to the soil and hold water well at very low cost.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ kooloi ashishifã ni egbo, tsina ashishifãi, loo kookoo ŋmɔtɔi abɔle he. Tso shishitoo lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ. Nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ kɛ niyenii kpakpai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fiofio. ni ehiɛɔ nu jogbaŋŋ yɛ shika ni baa shi waa mli

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow during the dry season, and will the crop survive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ? Ni te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi?

english: Plantains shed older leaves and turn yellow to conserve water when soil moisture is low. As long as the central stem remains healthy and green, the plant will survive and grow new leaves once rains start.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ koni ehiɛ nu mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ faaa. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni efee eŋɔli lɛ. Tso lɛ baahi shi ni ebaakwɛ baai heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ je shishi.

english: Why are my heavy plantain plants falling over before the fruit bunches are fully ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains ni tsii lɛ miigbee shi dani aduawai akutsei lɛ efee klalo kwraa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and top-heavy stems. Strong winds or too many competing sucker shoots weaken the plant base, so you should prune extra suckers and prop up fruiting plants with sturdy wooden poles.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ tsei ni mli tse waa. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo akaŋshii babaoo ni jɛɔ ŋmeii amli baa lɛ baaha tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ agbɔjɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ ahe ni okɛ tsei ni wa fiɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ asɛɛ.

english: How long does a plantain plant take to produce a mature bunch from the day I plant it?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani plantain tsei lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eda kwraa kɛjɛɔ gbi ni adu amɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: In good weather and rich soil, a plantain plant typically takes 9 to 12 months to produce flowers and another 3 to 4 months for the bunch to mature fully for harvest.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ kpakpa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii amli lɛ, bei pii lɛ, Plantains heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi, ni ekɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 krokomɛi hu tsuɔ nii dani fɔfɔi lɛ shwereɔ kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why are the leaves at the top of my plantain plant bunching together and remaining small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ plantain lɛ yiteŋ lɛ ebɔ he ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Banana Bunchy Top Disease, which is carried by tiny insects. Infected plants cannot produce healthy fruit and should be dug up and destroyed so the disease does not spread to nearby plants.
ga: Enɛ ji Banana Bunchy Top hela, ni kooloi bibii kɛbaa lɛ he okadi. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ. ni esa akɛ atsa ni akpata hiɛ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the essential nutrient plants need to grow green and healthy. It can also happen when too much rain washes away soil nutrients or drowns the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ fite niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ loo ekɛ shishifãi lɛ shwie nu mli.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows pests and diseases that attack maize to build up in the field.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants compete heavily with each other for sunlight, soil food, and water, resulting in tall, weak stems with tiny or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli waa, ni no haa amɛfeɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni dumɔwui bibii yɔɔ mli. loo dumɔwui ni nɔ ko bɛ mli

english: Why do I need to plant cassava stem cuttings pointing upward or slanting instead of upside down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ oduɔ ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni okɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛi loo yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni oootsɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava stems have small growth buds that must face upward so the shoots can easily grow up toward the sun while the roots go deep into the ground to produce big tubers.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. Esa akɛ ekwɛ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ adara kɛbote hulu la lɛ mli oya, yɛ be mli ni eshishifãi lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under strong sunlight, so they require shade crops like plantains or shade trees to shelter them and keep the ground cool during their early stage.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei koni amɛha amɛhe nɔ ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i yɛ shishijee mli.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the inner leaves of my maize funnel, and how will it affect the yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-corn ŋmeii lɛ amli baai lɛ? Ni te ebaaná nifeemɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which feed on the growing tip of the plant, preventing proper growth and reducing your corn harvest significantly if left untreated.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ tsei ashishifãi. Etsiɔ ŋmãa ni edaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ naa, ni ebaanyɛ eha ŋmãa ni akpaa lɛ aba shi kwraa kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it necessary to clear weeds around my crops while they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and will steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops, causing your crops to become stunted early in life.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni ebaaju nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ mli. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ ogbekɛbiiashi.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and look limp during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants curl their leaves during intense heat to reduce water loss, and as long as the soil has moisture, the leaves will normally recover when the evening temperature cools down.
ga: Tsei baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Ni be fɛɛ be ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ, baai lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme atmospheric heat, poor soil nutrients, or irregular water supply, which prevents the flowers from setting fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ hao amɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli wa mli. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kpakpai loo nu ni bɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ wooo yibii

english: Why should I wait for the rainy season to fully settle before planting my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ amɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ agbe naa dani adu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: If you plant after the very first early rain, a sudden dry patch of weather can dry out the soil and kill the germinated seeds before their roots grow deep enough to survive.
ga: Kɛji odu nii yɛ leebi nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ Trukaa nugbɔshiimɔ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ dani amɛshishifãi lɛ aya shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why is it important for me to clear and prepare my land well before the major rains start in July?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni masaa he dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ July mli lɛ?

english: Preparing your land early loosens the soil so it can catch and hold the very first rains. This ensures your seeds get enough moisture right away to sprout quickly and build strong roots before the peak rains hit.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni enyɛ ená klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaha odumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa dani nugbɔ lɛ ayashɛ he ni fe fɛɛ.

english: Is it better for my crops if I leave cleared bush to rot on the farm instead of burning it?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛji miha jwɛi ni he tse lɛ fite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mashã amɛ?

english: Leaving cleared plant material to decompose protects your soil from the hot sun, keeps moisture in the ground, and gradually turns into natural manure that feeds your crops throughout the growing season.
ga: Kɛ́ oŋmɛ gbɛ ni tso nibii ni ajie lɛ lɛ fite lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu oshikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni fiofio lɛ ebafeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa onibii lɛ hewalɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if my soil is moist enough to plant seeds after land preparation?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ sɛɛ?

english: Take a handful of soil from a few inches deep and squeeze it; if it forms a ball that holds together easily without dripping water, the soil has the right moisture balance for seeds to germinate safely.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ sũ ni mli kwɔ ni ji inchi fioo ko ni okɛmiimɔ mli. Kɛji efee bɔɔlu ni ŋmɛɔ ehe mlɛo ni nu shwieee shi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ sũ lɛ yɛ nu ni sa bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when the rain stops for a few weeks in the middle of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii fioo komɛi yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves mean the plant is stressed and lacking nitrogen. Crops can only absorb food from the soil through water, so when the soil dries up, the plant starves even if nutrients are present.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao ni nitrogen bɛ ehe. Tsei baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ nu pɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lɛ Hɔmɔ baaye tso lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ moŋ.

english: How does cassava manage to survive dry periods while my other crops wither and die?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei ahi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi Mine lɛ shwieɔ ni egboɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava stores water and energy in its deep underground roots and drops its outer leaves during dry spells to save moisture, allowing it to rest until the rains return.
ga: Cassava kɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ toɔ eshishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli. ni oha kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ ahi shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni ŋmɔtɔ akahi shi. Ha ejɔɔ ehe kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their blossoms without giving me any fruit when the weather becomes extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni ewooo yibii be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, pepper plants drop their flowers as a survival mechanism to save water and protect themselves from burning out under heat stress.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ he.

english: Why shouldn't I plant the exact same crop on the same land every major season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome yɛ be fɛɛ be ni he hiaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific soil nutrients that crop needs and allows local pests and soil diseases to build up, resulting in poorer harvests each year.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ebaafee niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ. ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai baa shikpɔji ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, daa afi lɛ, nikpamɔ lɛ baafee bibioo.

english: Weeds are wild plants already native to your soil, so their seeds are tough and ready to sprout instantly, while cultivated crop seeds need extra time and care to establish their roots.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ momo. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛdumɔwui lɛ ahe wa ni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni adu lɛ biɔ be kɛ hiɛdɔɔ krɛdɛɛ dani amɛná shishifãi.

english: Why do my crops grow taller and yield better when I leave space between them instead of crowding them together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai kɛ́ mishi gbɛ yɛ amɛteŋ moŋ fe ni mikɛ amɛ baabɔ he lɛ?

english: Proper spacing gives every plant its own share of sunlight, air, and soil nutrients. When crops are crowded, they fight each other for survival and end up weak with smaller yields.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehulu, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fa babaoo lɛ Amɛbaawuu koni amɛhi shi ni amɛbaagbe naa ni amɛgbɔjɔ kɛ nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fioo.

english: Why do my seeds rot underground if a heavy rain falls immediately after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa beni midu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain can fill up all the tiny air pockets in the soil with water, effectively drowning the seeds because they need oxygen from the soil to sprout properly.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ awo kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii amli kɛ nu. fɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that scorch easily under harsh sun. Shade trees act like living umbrellas, providing cool temperatures and keeping moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
