ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ ambrela ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ daraa waa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhe hulu la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop some of their tiny young pods before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ? Dani ebaada agbo?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop excess young pods—a process called cherelle wilt—when the tree feels it does not have enough water, light, or soil nutrients to nourish every single pod to maturity.
ga: Cacao tso lɛ jieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni fa fe nine lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ ji gbɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ cherel ni shwieɔ shi. Beni tso lɛ nuɔ he akɛ nu, la loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ aná hewalɛ kɛyashi amɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do new leaves on my cocoa tree start out reddish-pink before turning green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ pinki-tsuru dani etsɔɔ eŋɔli lɛ?

english: Freshly sprouted cocoa leaves produce natural red pigments to protect their tender leaves from sun damage while they build up green chlorophyll and harden.
ga: Kookoo baai ni akwɛ̃ ehee lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli su tsuru ko ni buɔ baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he yɛ be mli ni amɛfeɔ klorofil eŋɔli ni amɛwaa lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants produce very small cobs even though the stalks grow tall and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔji moŋ lɛ?

english: Tall green leaves mean the plant got enough nitrogen for leaf growth, but small cobs happen when the soil lacks phosphorus or water at the critical time when the flowers and cobs are forming.
ga: Baai eŋɔlii ni kɛlɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miiná nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ, shi ŋmeii bibii baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ fɔsfɔs loo nu yɛ be ni he hiaa waa ni fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii miifee lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and drop off when the weather gets very dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is the cassava plant's defense mechanism to reduce water loss through its leaves during hot dry spells; once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh leaves and keep growing.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni buɔ ŋmei tsei ahe koni nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ aba shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow twisted and rough instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, loose, and deep soil to expand smoothly; hard clay, rocks, or compacted soil block the growing tuber, forcing it to bend and grow extra roots to navigate through the hard ground.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ koni egbɛ eshwa jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ, tɛi, loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ tsiɔ bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa. Enɛ nyɛɔ enɔ ni ebɔleɔ ehe ni ekwɛ̃ɔ shishifãi krokomɛi koni enyɛ etsɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing maize in the same spot every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil while allowing maize-specific pests and diseases to build up and ruin future harvests.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa ni amɛfiteɔ wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does my cowpea crop produce a lot of bushy leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea lɛ baa babaoo shi ŋmɔtɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or excessive manure, cowpea plants put all their energy into growing foliage and stem branches instead of making flowers and seed pods.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmeii babaoo yɛ Cowpea tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ niji ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui ŋmɔji

english: Leaf curling is a signal that tiny insects like aphids or thrips are sucking sap from under the leaves, or that they have infected the plant with a leaf-curl virus.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips he okadi. Nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ni amɛnuɔ Aloo etsɔɔ akɛ amɛkɛ hela ko ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ewo tso lɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without setting fruit when daytime heat is too extreme or when heavy rain washes away pollen, preventing the blossom from fertilizing.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ. Aloo beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi amli ŋmeii lɛ. Ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ afɔ.

english: Does my cocoa grow better in direct sunlight or under tree shade?
ga: Ani mi-cocoa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo yɛ tso ko shishi?

english: Cocoa grows best in partial shade. It needs protection from direct intense sunlight, but it should not be kept in total darkness, as it still needs light to grow healthy.
ga: Cocoa daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be fioo yɔɔ lɛ. Ehe miihia ni abu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Shi esaaa akɛ akɛtoɔ duŋ mli kwraa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, la he miihia amɛ lolo koni tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I plant my cocoa in a very dense forest area where sunlight hardly reaches the ground?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo yɛ kooi ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ hei ni hulu la shɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: No, cocoa should not be grown in complete darkness. While it dislikes full direct sun, it requires light filtered through partial shade to thrive and produce cocoa pods.
ga: Dabi, esaaa akɛ aduɔ kookoo yɛ duŋ mli kwraa. Eyɛ mli akɛ esumɔɔɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ. Shi ebiɔ ni atsɔ la ni tsɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃ ni ekɛ kookoo ŋmeii aba.

english: What happens to my mature cocoa if the big shade trees grow too thick and block all light?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kookoo ni eda kwraa lɛ nɔ? Kɛji tsei lɛ dara tsɔ ni amɛtsi kane lɛ fɛɛ naa lɛ,

english: If shade trees block too much sunlight and cover your mature cocoa in darkness, pod production will drop significantly because mature cocoa needs filtered light to yield well.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsiɔ hulu la babaoo naa ni amɛhaa o-cocoa momo lɛ hulutsoo yɛ duŋ mli lɛ, Pod feemɔ baa shi waa ejaakɛ cocoa ni eda lɛ biɔ la ni atsɔ mli koni enyɛ efee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant plantain on the same field with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu banana yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting plantains alongside cocoa provides temporary shade for the young cocoa trees and helps you properly space out the cocoa plants across your farm.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni akɛ kookoo duɔ lɛ baaha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ aná hulutsoo be kukuoo ko. ni ehaa okɛ kookoo tsei lɛ jaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How does adding plantains help me with the arrangement and spacing of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ plantains ni mikɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi yɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔtoo kɛ amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ mli?

english: Plantain plants serve as companion markers that help structure the farm layout, allowing you to space out your cocoa trees properly so they don't overcrowd each other.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ kadimɔi enyɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa kɛtoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni ojara cacao tsei lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ ji koni kookoo tsei lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ.

english: Will planting plantains beside my cocoa steal food from my young cocoa trees?
ga: plantains ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Ani mi cacao tso lɛ baaju niyenii kɛjɛ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ dɛŋ?

english: No, plantains actually support the young cocoa plants by creating the shade and environment they need to settle in without harming their growth.
ga: Dabi, plantains yeɔ ebuaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ kɛtsɔ hulutsoo kɛ shihilɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi ni efiteee amɛdalɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: How long should I keep my cocoa seedlings in the nursery before I transplant them to the main field?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ makɛ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahi ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛwo shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ?

english: Cocoa seedlings are generally ready to be transplanted into the main field after about 18 months, when they are mature and strong enough to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cocoa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu amɛ awo ŋmɔ titri lɛ mli yɛ aaafee nyɔji 18 sɛɛ, beni dumɔwui lɛ eda ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi lɛ.

english: When I am transplanting my 18-month-old cocoa seedling into the soil, how deep should I cover it?
ga: Kɛ́ mikɛ kookoo dumɔwu ni eye nyɔji 18 lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, te esa akɛ maha nɔ kɛyashɛ he ni eshɛ tɛŋŋ?

english: When transplanting your cocoa seedling, do not cover or bury the stem/shoot. Soil should cover the root ball, but the plant itself must remain exposed above ground.
ga: Be ni esa akɛ adu kookoo dumɔwui lɛ Kaaha nɔ loo ofu tsei lɛ ashishifãi/yiteŋ. Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ aha shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Shi esa akɛ tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know that my cocoa plant is entering its production phase to start bearing pods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi cacao tsei lɛ miibote nitsumɔ mli koni amɛje pods feemɔ shishi?

english: You will know your cocoa tree is moving into its productive stage when you observe that flowering has begun on the branches and trunk.
ga: Obaale akɛ o-cocoa tso lɛ miibote yibiiwoo be lɛ mli beni oyɔse akɛ eniji kɛ eshishifãi lɛ ebɔi fɔmɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient they need to grow strong. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer like Urea helps them regain their green color and grow well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii mli hewalɛ ko ni he hiaa ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ nitrogen tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it better to put fertilizer on my crops when the ground is completely dry or after it rains?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is always best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after rain. Roots can only drink in fertilizer when it is dissolved in water, whereas placing dry fertilizer on dry ground in hot sun can burn your crop roots.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Shishifãi baanyɛ anu ŋmɔshi nibii pɛ kɛji akɛ amɛwo nu mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso shishifãi lɛ ashã.

english: Why do the small flowers on my cocoa trees drop off before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often drop off when the tree is stressed by dry weather, lacks nutrients, or is attacked by tiny sap-sucking insects like mirids (capsids). Keeping the soil shaded and managing pests helps the flowers stay on and form pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mirids (capsids) lɛ tutua tso lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily in full sunlight. Plantains grow very fast with broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs during its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Plantains daa oya waa kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kookoo bibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How can I tell when my cassava is ready to be harvested from the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is usually mature between 9 and 12 months after planting. You will know it is getting ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the ground around the base of the stem starts to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei hiɔ shi yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaale akɛ eesaa ehe beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa

english: Staking raises the yam leaves high into the sunlight so they can capture light and make food. The more sunlight the leaves get, the bigger the yam tubers will grow under the ground.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ daraa yɛ hulu la mli bɔni afee ni amɛmɔmɔ la ni amɛhoo nii. Babaoo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, Babaoo ni sweet potato ŋmeii baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoots growing around the bottom of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: If too many shoots grow together, they steal water and food from each other. Cutting off extra shoots (pruning suckers) ensures the main plant gets enough energy to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo bua amɛhe naa lɛ Amɛbaaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ (pruning sucker) lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ dumɔwui wuji babaoo ni tsii.

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot and happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium, usually because the soil moisture keeps changing from very wet to very dry. Watering your crops regularly prevents this rot.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot ni ebaa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ nɔ ni edɔ waa kɛyaa nɔ ni egbi waa nɔ. Nu ni oooha tso lɛ daa lɛ baaye abua ni akafite nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant juices. Spraying with neem water or soap solution can help clear these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe tee baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem nu loo samla shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ.

english: Should I start planting my seeds right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui akwɛmɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to wait until two or three good rains have fallen and the rainy season is stable. The very first rain is often followed by a long dry spell that can scorch fresh seedlings.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ kpakpa baanɛ. Egbeeɔ shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baa daa. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui heei lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How do I know when my cocoa trees are getting too old and need to be cut down for new ones?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cacao tsei lɛ egbɔ tsɔ ni ehe miihia ni afolɔ amɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce best between 10 and 25 years of age. When you notice that pods are becoming very few despite proper weeding and fertilizing, or the trees show constant disease, it is time to cut them down and replant fresh seedlings.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ beni amɛye kɛjɛ afii 10 kɛyashi 25, beni oyɔseɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ faaa kwraa yɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ. Aloo tso lɛ miitsɔɔ hela be fɛɛ be. Be eshɛɛ ni ooofo ni odu dumɔwu hee.

english: Should I keep harvesting cassava from the same plants for several years, or do I need to clear them and plant fresh stems each season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maya nɔ makpa ŋmãa kɛjɛ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ afii babaoo ni baaba lɛ? Aloo esa akɛ majie mli ni madu tsei heei yɛ be fɛɛ mli?

english: Cassava roots reach their best quality within 9 to 12 months. Leaving the crop in the ground for multiple years makes the tubers woody, rotted, and low in starch, so it is best to harvest completely and plant new stem cuttings each year.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ mli afii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee tsei, ni amɛgboi, ni ŋmei fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli, no hewɔ lɛ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookpa amɛ kwraa ni odu niji heei daa afi.

english: How many years can an oil palm tree produce good fruit before I need to replace it?
ga: Afii enyiɛ mu tso baanyɛ awo yibii dani esa akɛ atsake lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees give strong yields until they are about 25 years old. Beyond this age, the palm fruits become small and the trees grow too tall to harvest safely, making it necessary to fell them and plant new palms.
ga: Mu tsei woɔ yibii babaoo aahu kɛyashi amɛwala be feɔ aaafee afii 25. Kɛji akɛ afii nɛɛ ho lɛ, Tso lɛ yibii lɛ faaa ni tsei lɛ hu kwɔ tsɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akpa shweshweeshwe. Enɛ haa ehe bahiaa ni afolɔ tɛŋ tsei heei ni adu.

english: Can I keep harvesting pepper from the same bushes for several years, or should I start fresh each year?
ga: Ani manyɛ mabua ŋmɔtɔ naa kɛjɛ jwɛi kome mli afii babaoo? Aloo esa akɛ oje dumɔ shishi ekoŋŋ daa afi?

english: While pepper bushes can live for more than one year, their fruit production drops heavily after the first harvest year, and pests build up in old bushes. Replanting fresh pepper seedlings each season gives you bigger harvests.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ pepper tsei baanyɛ ahi shi nɔ ni fe afi moŋ, Shi amɛyibiiwoo lɛ baa shi waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kpamɔ afi lɛ sɛɛ. Ni tsɛŋemɔ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ tsei momo amli. Pepper dumɔwui heei ni ooodu yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ baaha oná yibii babaoo.

english: My plantain tree has grown many small shoots around its base, so should I leave all of them to grow or cut some away?
ga: Mi dumɔwu lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni ebɔle shishigbɛ lɛ he. Ani esa akɛ mahã eda loo mafo ekomɛi?

english: You should leave only two or three strong suckers per plantain plant—one main mother plant, one medium shoot, and one small shoot. Removing the extra shoots prevents them from competing for water and nutrients, leading to larger plantain bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ oshi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ yɛ dumɔwu kome mli, tamɔ tso titri kome ni ji nyɛ. ŋmei kome ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ kɛ ŋmei bibioo kome Kɛ́ ajie ŋmei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, plantains lɛ baaná jwɛi wuji.

english: When my tomato plants start growing extra small branches on the sides, do I cut them off or leave them?
ga: Beni mi tomato tsei lɛ bɔi niji bibii akwɛ̃mɔ Titri lɛ yɛ afã lɛ Ani mifoɔ lɛ loo mishiɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning off extra side shoots—also called suckers—helps the tomato plant focus its energy on growing larger, healthier fruit instead of wasting food on excess leaves and stems.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aaafolɔ Ale lɛ hu akɛ ŋmeii Enɛ baaye abua tomato tso lɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama aduawai ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite niyenii yɛ baai kɛ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: How can I tell if my yellowing maize leaves mean the crop is sick or just getting ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmei baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hela mɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ loo eshwɛ fioo ni ebaakpa?

english: If the bottom leaves turn yellow in a V-shape while the plant is young, the maize lacks nitrogen fertilizer. However, if the entire plant turns brown and dry late in the season, the crop has simply completed its life cycle and is ready for harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli be mli ni tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Shi, kɛji akɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ, No mli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbe eshihilɛ be lɛ naa pɛŋ ni efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: How do I decide whether to treat a sick plant with chemical spray or completely pull it out of my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ baatsa amɛ loo majie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kwraa?

english: If a plant has a viral infection like swollen shoot in cocoa, chemicals will not cure it, so you must uproot and destroy it immediately to save neighboring trees. If it is only a fungal leaf spot or insect attack, spraying with the right crop chemical can save the plant.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ yɛ hela ko ni jɛɔ hela mli baa, tamɔ ŋmeii ni efu yɛ kookoo mli. Tsofai nyɛŋ atsa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ otsi amɛ ni okpãtã amɛhiɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni ohere tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ayiwala. Kɛji akɛ eji leaf spot hela loo kooloi ni tutuaa lɛ kɛkɛ Tsofai ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ahere tso lɛ yiwala.

english: How do I know if my pineapple farm can produce a second good harvest from the old plants, or if I must replant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-pineapple ŋmɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai ni ji enyɔ kɛjɛ tsei momo lɛ amli? Aloo esa akɛ madu lɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: The second harvest from old pineapple plants, called a ratoon crop, yields smaller fruits. If the parent plants look weak, stunted, or pest-damaged after the first harvest, it is better to clear the field and plant fresh suckers.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmãa ni ji enyɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmei tso momo lɛ mli lɛ akɛ Ratun tso. Ebaaha yibii bibii. Kɛji tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ, egbɔjɔ, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai efite lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ abaajie he ni eyɔɔ lɛ ni adu ŋmeii heei.

english: Why are my sweet orange trees producing very few and sour fruits even though the trees look tall and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet orange tso lɛ woɔ yibii ni mli edɔ fioo ko pɛ eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni ekɛlɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ moŋ?

english: Orange trees grown directly from seed often produce sour fruit and take many years to yield. Using grafted seedlings ensures that your citrus trees bear sweet, market-ready fruit early based on the healthy features of the parent plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, citrus tsei ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ woɔ citrus yibii ni amɛheɔ afii babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii. Kɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha o-citrus tsei lɛ afee nɔ ni ŋɔɔ ni efee klalo kɛha jarayeli mra. Edamɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ tso ni ji nyɛ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow before the crop yields fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ woɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. Without enough nitrogen in the soil, the plant cannot produce food efficiently, which leads to weak growth and small cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛji nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraaa ni egbɔjɔ, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii hu baa.

english: Why do some farmers in my community harvest more bags of grain than I do when we have the same land size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi ni yɔɔ mikutso lɛ mli lɛ kpaɔ ŋmãa kotokui babaoo fe mi, be mli ni wɔyɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Higher yields come from a combination of using certified improved seeds, planting with proper spacing, applying fertilizer at the right time, and keeping the farm free of weeds that steal crop nutrients.
ga: Yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ jɛɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛhe ni awo he odaseyeli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli. Dumɔ ni jɛkɛmɔ ni sa yɔɔ mli Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli yɛ be ni sa mli ni akwɛɔ koni jwɛi ni juɔ tsei lɛ amli niyenii lɛ akafee nɔ ko yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam plants need tall wooden sticks to climb on while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ beni eduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Yam vines use sticks to spread their leaves higher into the sunlight. Sunlight helps the leaves make food, which is then stored underground to swell and grow larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛ amɛniji lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. Akɛ enɛɛmɛi toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni tsɔnei lɛ amli alɛɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains protects young cocoa leaves from burning and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do caterpillars target the inner stem funnel of my young maize plants instead of the lower leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ miikwɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: The center funnel contains the newest, softest leaves where the plant grows. Pests like the fall armyworm hide inside this funnel to shield themselves from sunlight and predators while feeding on tender growth.
ga: Funnel ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli ji baai heei ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ yɛ he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ. Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ nɛkɛ gbɛi nɛɛ amli koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the soil when it rains continuously for weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ otsii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excess rain fills up the air pockets in heavy soil, preventing roots from breathing. Too much water combined with low oxygen causes soil fungi to attack and decay the underground tubers.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii mli lɛ amli obɔ. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkamu Nu babaoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ faaa lɛ fataa he lɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms drop off without turning into fruits when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomatoi shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: High temperatures heat up the plant and spoil the pollen inside the flowers. When pollination fails due to heat stress, the plant drops its flowers to save water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tso lɛ mli dɔɔ ni efiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛji pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii yɛ dɔlɛ hewɔ lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my maize plants stay short and produce tiny cobs if a dry spell occurs early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ yɔɔ kuku ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Kɛji hɔmɔ ba yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli

english: Water is needed for plants to stretch their stalks and absorb soil food. A early drought stunts plant growth and forces the crop to mature quickly before it can build strong, large cobs.
ga: Tsei hia nu koni amɛ tsei lɛ alɛɛ mli ni amɛ nu niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Hɔmɔ ni baa mra lɛ tsiɔ tsei adalɛ naa ni enyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛdara oya dani amɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni he wa.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for one high-yield generation. Replanting seeds harvested from hybrids causes the next crop to lose its strength, resulting in uneven plant sizes and lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee Hybrid lɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛha nɔ ni woɔ yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni akpa kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee tsofai sɔrɔtoi amli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ he awaaa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ adalɛi kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee, ni yibiiwoo hu faaa.

english: Why is it bad to plant my cassava cuttings very close together on the ridge?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii niji ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ ehiii lɛ?

english: Planting too close makes crops compete with each other for light, water, and plant nutrients. Giving each plant proper space allows the roots room to expand into bigger cassava tubers.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ tsei amli niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ehaa shishifã tsu lɛ mli lɛɛɔ kɛfeɔ ŋmei shishifãi wuji.

english: Why do my maize seedlings die so easily from small pests when they are still very young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii gbeɔ mi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ oya lɛ? Ni eji nɔ bibioo kwraa lolo?

english: Young plants get their early strength and natural defense from the seed they came from. If the mother plant was weak, diseased, or lacked nutrients while producing seeds, the offspring will lack early vigor and can easily die from minor pests or harsh conditions.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ naa hewalɛ mra. kɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ ahe. Kɛji tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, hela emɔ lɛ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ ehe yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ dumɔwui lɛ, tsinabii bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛ amɛgbekɛbiiashi tɔ̃ɔ. ni ebaanyɛ egbo oya kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii loo shihilɛi ni esaaa amli.

english: Does taking cassava stems from healthy parent plants really make a difference in my harvest?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni jɛ nyɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli lɛ ni miyeɔ lɛ haa srɔtofeemɔ baa mikpamɔ lɛ mli diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, cassava cuttings carry nutrients and health traits directly from the parent plant. Using cuttings from strong, disease-free parent plants gives the young crop the built-in protection it needs to survive early disease attacks and produce strong roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛnamɔ he sui ni jɛɔ nyɛ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ŋmei ni afo lɛ mli. Kɛ akɛ fɔlɔ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni hela bɛ mli lɛ mli ŋmeii ni afo lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa tso bibioo lɛ naa hebuu ni yɔɔ mli ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ mra lɛ amli, ni eha shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why should I give extra fertilizer and care to the crop plants I intend to save seeds from?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ni makwɛ tsei anɔ yɛ he ni mito gbɛjianɔ akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui baato lɛ afata he lɛ?

english: Parent plants pass their health and stored nutrition into their seeds. Caring for seed plants ensures the seeds are packed with nutrients and defense energy, helping the next generation survive early stresses after germination.
ga: Tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ato yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ haa. Odumɔwui lɛ akwɛmɔ haa amɛyiɔ obɔ kɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ ni buɔ mɔ he. Yelikɛbuamɔ ni akɛhaa yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ koni amɛye shishijee gbii lɛ amli haomɔi lɛ anɔ kunim. beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die shortly after I move them out of the nursery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings are fragile like newborn babies. If they are moved to the open field without shade trees like plantains to protect them from full sun, the sudden heat stress overwhelms them before their roots establish.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ waaa tamɔ abifao ni afɔ lɛ ehee lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ajie amɛ kɛtee ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni tsei tamɔ plantains bɛ mli koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he lɛ, Trukaa dɔlɛ he haomɔ baaye amɛnɔ dani shishifãi lɛ aje shishi.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my tomato plants turn yellow and drop off when flowering starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ ashishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ lɛ?

english: When crops begin to flower, they focus their energy on creating fruit. If the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen, the plant pulls strength from its older leaves to feed the young flowers, causing the leaves to die.
ga: Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔi fɔmɔ Amɛbaasusu yibiiwoo ni amɛbaawo lɛ he. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ, tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ kɛjɛ baai momoi amli koni amɛkɛha fɔfɔi bibii lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji baai lɛ agbele

english: Why do my young maize plants turn pale green and stay small after heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ bibii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain can wash away nitrogen from sandy soil. Without nitrogen, young crops lose their green color and cannot build the internal strength needed to grow tall or fight off early diseases.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen ni yɔɔ ŋã shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ nitrogen bɛ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ fiteɔ amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛtswa mligbɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛdara loo amɛwu amɛshi helai yɛ eshishijee fãi lɛ amli lɛ amɛma shi.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting so quickly inside my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ oya yɛ mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams are living plant tissues even after harvest. If they get bruised during harvest or stored in hot, unventilated rooms, small rot fungi enter the wounds and easily overcome the yam's weak natural defenses.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji tso mli fãji ni hiɔ shi yɛ kpamɔ sɛɛ po. Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ba yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli loo akɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli. Rot fungi bibii boteɔ pilamɔi amli ni amɛyeɔ sweet potato adebɔɔ mli hebuu nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ nɔ kunim oya.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers instead of turning them into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or water shortage. To preserve its own survival, the plant sheds young blossoms until conditions become safe again.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛkɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni faaa lɛ mli baa lɛ kpe. koni ehi shi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala mli Tso lɛ baawo fɔfɔi bibii kɛyashi shihilɛi baaŋmɛ lɛ gbɛ ni ewo fɔfɔi. baafee shweshweeshwe ekoŋŋ

english: Why do my plantain suckers take a very long time to sprout when I plant them in dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers need moisture and organic material to activate their underground growing points. Dry conditions keep the sucker asleep, making it weak and vulnerable to insect attacks before it can root.
ga: Plantain suckers lɛ he miihia ŋmɔtɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni baaha shikpɔŋ shishi shweremɔ hei lɛ aya hiɛ. Shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mɛi ni nuɔ nu lɛ ni amɛwɔɔ. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ ni kooloi baanyɛ atutua lɛ oya dani etswa shishifãi.

english: Using too much chemical nitrogen fertilizer causes cowpeas to put all their food energy into leaf production instead of making pods. Cowpeas produce their own nitrogen naturally, so too much extra fertilizer weakens pod development.
ga: Tsofai ni ji nitrogen ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa tsina ŋmei kɛ niyenii ni eyɔɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai yɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ. Cowpeas feɔ nitrogen yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do people tell me to plant plantain trees in my new cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi miikɛɛ mi akɛ madu plantains yɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ hee lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to harsh sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that provide living shade, keeping the cocoa cool and moisture-rich until it matures.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa.

english: Should I plant my cassava stems slanting in the soil or standing straight up?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo mafee nɔ ni ja?

english: Planting cassava stems at a slant (about 45 degrees) makes it much easier to harvest the heavy roots later, while helping the plant spread its roots well to resist dry weather.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei tsei lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ (aaafee digrii 45) lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ abaakpa shishifãi ni tsii lɛ yɛ sɛɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amɛshwaa jogbaŋŋ koni amɛnyɛ amɛte shi amɛwo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of a maize plant usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen nutrient. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK early gives the leaves back their rich green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni ji nitrogen lɛ faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK tsu nii mra lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee amɛhe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do I need to heap soil into big mounds before planting my yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ agbo ko ato dani odu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yams grow deep into the ground and need loose, soft soil to expand into large tubers. High mounds give the roots room to expand easily and prevent water from soaking and rotting them.
ga: Sweet potatoes daa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni ehe hiaa shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni ekwɛ̃ ni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Pii ni kɛlɛ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ amli shwereɔ oya ni ehaaa amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkafite.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off before any small tomatoes form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani tomato bibii feɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant gets stressed by intense heat, irregular watering, or insect attacks, preventing pollination from happening successfully.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa miigba tsei anaa. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa loo kooloi ni tutuaa lɛ Enɛ haaa pollination lɛ aye omanye.

english: Why is it a bad idea for me to grow maize on the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Growing maize in the same soil repeatedly drains specific nutrients like nitrogen and lets pests and diseases adapt to the soil, leading to smaller harvests each year.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shii abɔ lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ hoɔ, ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ nɔ. ekɛ ehe awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmaa ni abaakpa daa afi lɛ baafee nɔ ni faaa.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas make my soil better for future crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant finishes growing, that nitrogen stays in the earth, naturally feeding your next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tso lɛ gbe naa lɛ Nakai nitrogen lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ebaaha niyenii aha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do weeds steal more strength from my crops when the plants are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiju hewalɛ babaoo kɛmiijɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni tsei lɛ darako kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings have small root systems and need full sunlight and water to get established. Fast-growing weeds easily block light and steal soil food from small seedlings.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni ehe hiaa hulu la kɛ nu ni fa bɔni afee ni amɛtswa shi. Jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ tsiɔ la naa oya ni amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui bibii amli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the soil when it rains too heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: When heavy rain creates standing water around cassava roots, it cuts off air supply to the underground plant parts, causing fungi to multiply and rot the tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ehaa nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi yɛ he fɛɛ he. cassava root Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yaa tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni egboɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I pour chemical fertilizer right against the main stem of my plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ mitso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Concentrated chemical fertilizer touching the stem directly will burn and injure the tender skin of the plant. It should be applied in a ring a small distance away where the feeder roots can safely reach it.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã ni eye tso lɛ hewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ awui. Esa akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ fioo he ni shishifãi ni haa niyenii lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he shweshweeshwe lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of the plant usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, which maize needs to grow strong and stay green. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer can restore the food in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ ŋmãa lɛ adara waa ni ehi shi eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha niyenii mli hewalɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people say I should plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the land where I just harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmãa nɔ kɛkɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. Planting them after heavy-feeding crops like maize naturally refills the soil nutrients for your next planting season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ odu nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha okwɛ̃mɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long because the soil becomes waterlogged and lacks air. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, yɛ nu ni hoɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce small fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Why are my tomato plants producing small fruits? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots fight each other for water and soil nutrients, and their leaves shade each other from sunlight. Giving them enough space allows each plant to get full sunlight and nutrients to make bigger fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni baai lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ he. He ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa tso yibii wuji lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and cannot survive direct, hot sunlight for long periods. Keeping some shade trees or planting fast-growing plantains alongside them creates a canopy that protects young cocoa from heat and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbɛ be kakadaŋŋ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo plantains ni daa oya ni aduɔ yɛ ekomefeemɔ mli lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ latsaa he lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yam leaves need direct light to manufacture food for the plant. Lifting the leaves off the wet ground using stakes allows them to capture more sunlight to grow bigger tubers underground while preventing fungal diseases on the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato baai biɔ la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ niyenii aha tso lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa tsei lɛ ahe lɛ hu naa.

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and will quickly steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your seedlings. Removing weeds early gives your young crops a strong start before weeds overpower them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛbaaju nu, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya kɛha odumɔwui lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha odumɔwui lɛ aje shishi jogbaŋŋ dani jwɛi lɛ aye amɛnɔ kunim.

english: Why are there small holes appearing in the leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Small holes in maize leaves are usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm feeding on the soft leaf tissues. Catching these pests early allows you to use biological controls or pesticides before they destroy the growing point of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni yeɔ baa bibii amli fãji lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa mli lɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ mra Ehaa okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsuɔ nii dani amɛfiteɔ hei ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material, known as mulching, stops the sun from drying out the ground too quickly. It holds water in the soil longer, keeps roots cool, and prevents weed seeds from getting sunlight to grow.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ. Enɛ baatsi hulu lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ akashɛ hulu la he koni amɛdara

english: Why do crop seeds bought from an agro-dealer often yield better harvests than seeds I saved from last year's harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miheɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai be fɛɛ be fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Commercial hybrid seeds are specifically selected and bred in laboratories to resist local pests, tolerate drought, and produce uniform high yields. Saved seeds lose these strong protective traits over successive generations.
ga: Ahalaa jarayeli dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni akwɛɔ amɛ yɛ laboratorii amli pɔtɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ hebuu sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ amɛyinɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why should I dig my farm soil deep before planting instead of just making small holes on top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo miŋmɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani madu nii? Instead of making a small hole at the top?

english: Deep tilling loosens hard earth so crop roots can easily grow down deep to reach underground water and food, which helps the plants stay strong during dry hot weather.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shishifãi baanyɛ adara kɛyashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ niyenii he yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ahe wa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Why do weeds always grow faster than my main crops after I clear my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ be fɛɛ be beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit naturally in the top layer of the soil and wake up instantly when exposed to sunlight, so they grow fast and steal food from your young crop seedlings.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋgbɛ fã lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni eteɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ hulu la lɛ shɛ enɔ No hewɔ lɛ, edaa oya ni ejuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ odumɔwui bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why does it matter how deep I cover my maize seeds with dirt during planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sũ haa ŋmãa dumɔwui anɔ waa yɛ be mli ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: If you bury seeds too deep, they waste all their stored energy trying to reach sunlight and die underground. If you plant them too shallow, birds eat them or the sun dries them up.
ga: Kɛji ofu dumɔwu lɛ mli tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ amɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛto lɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshɛ hulu la he ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji odu lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ Okpoi baaye amɛ loo hulu lɛ baashã amɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and yield small harvest when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which starves all of them and lowers your harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye tsei lɛ fɛɛ ni ebaaha onibii lɛ aba shi.

english: What happens to cassava stems if I plant them shallow on top of the ground instead of slanting them into the dirt?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmei tsei anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ekɔɔɔ nɔ? Instead of throwing it into the ground?

english: Cassava planted deep in soft soil grows thick, heavy tubers underground, while cassava planted shallow near the surface grows thin, hard tubers that dry out quickly.
ga: Cassava ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli jɔ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ baaná ŋmeii ni mli wa ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni mli ekɔɔɔ he eko Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ, ŋmei bibii ni wa ni gbɛ́ɔ oya lɛ yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and fall off when there is no rain for weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ otsii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during long dry heat to stop losing water through its foliage, saving its strength underground until the rain returns.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli koni nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ akpa. Koni ehiɛ ehewalɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants turning yellow even though I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much water drowns their roots by taking away air in the soil, which hurts the roots so they cannot send food to the leaves, turning them yellow.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tso ko fe nine lɛ haa eshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ niyenii amaje baai lɛ. Ha efee ŋmɔŋ

english: Why do my tomato plants grow lots of tall green leaves but give me very few flowers and fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai kakadaŋŋ agboi babaoo shi fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Using too much leaf-boosting fertilizer makes plants put all their strength into growing big branches instead of making flowers that turn into fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ niji wuji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ fɔfɔii ewo aduawai amli lɛ

english: How can I tell that my groundnuts under the soil are fully mature and ready to be dug up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Groundnuts show they are ready when their leaves turn yellow and begin to dry up, showing that the plant has finished pushing all its energy down into filling the underground nuts.
ga: Peanuts tsɔɔ akɛ amɛfee klalo kɛji baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbɔi ŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ŋmeii ewo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting or sprouting leaves quickly after I store them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ loo ebaa shwereɔ oya beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams are alive even after harvest; if kept in warm, damp rooms with no air blowing through, the heat causes them to spoil or use up their strength sprouting leaves.
ga: Sweet potatoes hiɔ shi yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ po. Kɛ akɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli. Dɔlɛ lɛ baaha baai lɛ agbo loo amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ nii lɛ atsu nii.

english: If I pluck green leaves off my cassava plant to use as feed, will it stop the roots underground from growing big?
ga: Kɛji ogbala tso lɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ koni okɛtsu nii akɛ niyenii. Ani ebaatsi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃?

english: Yes, plucking too many leaves can reduce your harvest. Leaves act like solar panels that make food for the root, so removing too many leaves leaves the plant with less energy to expand its underground tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, baai babaoo ni ooojie lɛ baanyɛ aha onibii ni owoɔ lɛ aba shi. Baai lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo be mli nibii ni feɔ niyenii kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ajie baai babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does my cassava plant drop most of its leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is the cassava plant's way of surviving heat and drought. By losing leaves, the plant stops losing water to the hot air and protects itself until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni cassava tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ baai lɛ fite lɛ, no haaa nu lɛ afite yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli, ni ebuɔ ehe he kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Is it safe to pick fresh cassava leaves and feed them directly to livestock?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ abaabua ŋmei baai heei anaa ni akɛha kooloi tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Raw cassava leaves contain natural bitter compounds called cyanide that can hurt animals. Wilting or drying the harvested leaves in the shade for a few hours breaks down these compounds and makes them safe.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli tsofa ko ni mli wa ni atsɛɔ lɛ cyanide, ni baanyɛ aye kooloi awui yɛ cassava baa ni ahoo lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni akpa lɛ shwie shi loo egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi lɛ, efiteɔ nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ ni ehaa amɛfeɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: How do I know when my cassava crop is mature enough to dig up without ruining the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ edara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa ni mifiteee ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava is usually ready around 9 to 12 months after planting. You will notice the lower leaves turning yellow and falling naturally, and the soil around the base of the stem cracking open as the roots grow large.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha dumɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ gbáa beni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that your maize plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant nutrient needed for green leaves. This often happens when the soil is weak or after heavy rains wash nutrients away.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ loo beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ejie niyenii lɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow very tall and thin with small cob ears when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛtoi bibii yɔɔ lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When maize is planted too close, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. They stretch tall to reach light instead of using their strength to grow thick stalks and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are small ragged holes suddenly appearing in the center leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii eje kpo trukaa yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Ragged holes are a sign that caterpillars, like the fall armyworm, are eating the leaves. They hide inside the central leaf funnel of the maize plant during the day to feed on soft new leaves.
ga: Buji ni ekumɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii miiye baai lɛ tamɔ fall armyworms. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Yes, intercropping maize and cassava works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested in about three months, while cassava grows slowly at first and takes over the space after the maize is harvested.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ aaafee nyɔji etɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni eyeɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my leafy green vegetables start producing flowers and seeds so quickly instead of big green leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ miibɔi fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui oya yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: When the weather gets very hot or soil becomes dry, leafy greens get stressed and rush to make seeds before they die. Giving them light shade and keeping the soil moist helps them produce lush leaves longer.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ haoɔ ni amɛyaa oya koni amɛwo dumɔwui dani amɛgboi. Kɛ́ aha amɛ hulutsoo ni aha amɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Which stem part of a harvested cassava plant should I cut to plant a new crop, and how do I place it in the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei esa akɛ mafo kɛjɛ mi-cassava tso ni mikpa lɛ mli koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ? Ni te aaafee tɛŋŋ akɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Use the hard, woody middle section of a healthy mature stem. Cut it into finger-length pieces with several nodes, and plant them slanting or upright with the buds pointing toward the sky so shoots can sprout easily.
ga: Kɛ tso ni eda lɛ teŋgbɛ ni wa ni tamɔ tso lɛ atsu nii. Kpɔ̃ɔ mli bibii tamɔ tsɔne bibioo ko ni yɔɔ fãi srɔtoi. No sɛɛ lɛ, dumɔ amɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ loo amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ ni fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why are my crops struggling to grow on soil where sand was recently dug up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ hee ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops need topsoil because it contains organic matter and nutrients that nourish plants. When sand or topsoil is removed, the remaining hard ground cannot hold water or feed crop roots, causing plants to remain small or wither.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ he miihia tsei ejaakɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii ni haa tso lɛ hewalɛ yɛ mli. Kɛji ajieɔ ŋã loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni eshwɛ lɛ nyɛŋ ahiɛ nu loo eye ebua tsei shishifãi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ feɔ bibii loo amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why are my crops staying tiny even though I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu daa moŋ lɛ?

english: If the soil underneath is mostly coarse sand or lacks good dirt, the roots cannot spread out or absorb food. Without nutrients in the soil, extra water alone will not make crops grow big.
ga: Kɛji shishigbɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli babaoo ji ŋã ni mli edɔ loo shikpɔŋ kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã loo amɛŋɔ niyenii. Kɛji niyenii mli nibii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu kroko ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ pɛ haaa tsei lɛ adara.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow instead of healthy green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that your crop is starving for nitrogen and basic soil nutrients. This often happens when rain washes away the rich topsoil or when the soil structure has been ruined.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen kɛ niyenii krokomɛi ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ onibii amli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛɔ ni ekɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ efite lɛ

english: Why do my crops dry up so quickly when our nearby community dam is broken?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gĩ oya beni wɔ akutso lɛ mli nu ŋshɔ ni bɛŋkɛ wɔ lɛ fite lɛ?

english: Crops rely on a steady supply of moisture in the ground. When a dam breaks or dries out, the surrounding water table drops, preventing crop roots from reaching moist soil during dry periods.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa lɛ nɔ. Kɛji faa ko fite loo egbi Nu ni ebɔle ehe lɛ falɛ baa shi. Etsiɔ tsei shishifãi anaa koni amɛkashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Can I use dirty or muddy water from a disturbed stream to water my vegetables?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni mli ewo muji loo muji ni jɛ faa ko ni haoɔ lɛ mli lɛ awo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu?

english: Using water heavily mixed with mud or chemical runoff can choke crop roots and block them from taking in air. Muddy water can also leave a crust on top of the soil that stops new seeds from sprouting.
ga: Nu ni akɛ muji loo tsofai ni hoɔ efutu mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ akabote mli. Nu ni mli ewo muji hu baanyɛ ashi ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni etsĩ dumɔwui heei akwɛ̃mɔ naa.

english: Why do my plant roots rot when water sits on my field for days after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu hiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When damaged or level land causes water to flood and sit without draining, the roots drown and begin to rot underground.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ efite loo efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ekɛ nu afua kɛ nu ni anyɛɛɛ ajie lɛ baa. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛje shishi amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does sand wash over my young crop seedlings after a heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋã haa mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When nearby land or riverbanks are dug up and left bare, heavy rain washes loose sand downhill onto your farm, smothering fragile young plants and burying the good soil underneath.
ga: Kɛji akɛ atsa shikpɔŋ loo faai ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ni ashi amɛ shi lɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ ŋã ni miigbee shi baaba oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ. Efiteɔ tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ni efuɔ shikpɔŋ kpakpa yɛ amɛshishi.

english: Why do my crops wither faster when all the trees around my farm are cleared away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboɔ oya kɛ́ ajie tsei fɛɛ ni bɔle miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Trees act as natural windbreaks and shade covers that keep the surrounding soil cool and humid. Without trees, strong sun and dry winds evaporate water quickly from both the soil and crop leaves.
ga: Tsei tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ tsimɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Kɛji tsei bɛ Hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa nu shwieɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ ahe baai fɛɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up tightly like straws during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ jwɛi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants curl their leaves inward as a defense trick to save water. By making the leaves smaller under the direct sun, the plant reduces water loss until cooler evening temperatures arrive.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛyaa mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu he. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni afee lɛ bibii yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi lɛ nɔ. Tsei baaha nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my crops produce very few fruits even though I put a lot of hard work into planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ mihe woɔ mli waa moŋ?

english: When crops face constant stress from poor soil, polluted water, or dry spells, they save their energy just to stay alive instead of spending energy to produce large fruits or grains.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ haomɔi kpe be fɛɛ be kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii, nu ni mli ewo muji, loo nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli lɛ, amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛhi shi kɛkɛ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ he wami tsuɔ ní kɛ woɔ yiblii nguahi aloo ngmahi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep drying up and dying when I clear all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade from plants like plantain or banana trees because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the topsoil before their roots can grow deep enough to reach groundwater.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei tamɔ plantains loo banana tsei amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã ebaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ aya shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ he.

english: Why should I plant my maize in neat rows with measured spacing instead of scattering the seeds everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu abele yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ dumɔwui lɛ eshwa he fɛɛ he lɛ

english: Planting in spaced rows ensures each crop gets enough sunlight, air, and soil nutrients without fighting its neighbors, and it makes weeding and applying fertilizer much easier for you.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli ni gbɛ kã amɛteŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ yeee akaŋ. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants use to make food and stay green; adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer will feed the crop.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii, ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Leaf curling in cassava is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny insects called whiteflies; planting disease-resistant cassava stem cuttings prevents this from happening.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ baa ni ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ji kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ ni hiɛɔ Yucca tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ baaye abua ni enɛ akafee.

english: Why do people tell me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my land after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ midu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which naturally takes nitrogen from the air and stores it in the soil, restoring fertility for the next crop without needing expensive chemicals.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii. ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa Koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ ni ekɛ tsofai ni jara wa tsuuu nii.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat or irregular watering, as the stress causes the plant to protect itself rather than expend energy producing fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɔnyɛɛ haa tomato tso lɛ buɔ ehe he moŋ fe ni ekɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo yibii.

english: Why do some of my cut yam seeds rot in the soil after I plant them on the mounds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui ni mifo lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni midu amɛ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam pieces rot if they are planted in waterlogged soil or if the cut surfaces are not allowed to dry and heal in the shade before planting, which lets soil germs enter the flesh.
ga: Sweet potato fãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛji akɛ aŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ ni shikpɔŋ ni afo lɛ nɔ lɛ agbi ni etsa yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani adu. Enɛ baaha muawai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ abote loo lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak and thin even when plenty of rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the water, food, and light from the soil before your crop roots can catch them, so clearing weeds early gives your plants full access to nourishment.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Enɛ baaha otsei lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are ready to harvest so they do not become hard like wood?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa? No hewɔ lɛ, ewaaa tamɔ tso?

english: Most cassava varieties are ready for harvest between 9 and 12 months after planting; leaving them in the ground too long causes the roots to turn woody and fibrous as the plant gets older.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ tso kɛ ŋmeii beni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do insects eat holes through my harvested maize inside my storage crib?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-ŋma ni mikpa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Grain weevils attack maize if the cobs are put into storage while still damp or if the storage crib is not properly cleaned and treated, as moisture and darkness attract storage pests.
ga: Grain weevils lɛ tutuaa ŋmãa kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ to he ko ni akɛtoɔ be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lolo lɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ atsumɔko tsɔne ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulutsoo kɛ duŋ gbalaa kooloi kɛbaa he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the big shade trees from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie cacao tsei wuji kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from harsh, direct sunlight, which can burn their leaves and dry out the soil. Keeping or planting shade crops like plantains provides living shelter and moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand direct sun.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ baanyɛ aha baai ashã ni shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni akɛtoɔ loo aduɔ lɛ haa mɔ náa wɔɔhe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Does it matter which direction I stick my cassava cuttings into the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the raised buds pointing upward toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the plant wastes energy trying to grow downward first, leading to weak shoots and smaller tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu yucca tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ ni ŋmeii ni awó nɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji okɛ tsei shwie shi lɛ Tsei fiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛya shi klɛŋklɛŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yitsei bibii.

english: Yellowing of lower maize leaves is usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen is essential for leafy green growth, so applying a balanced fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure replenishes this food source.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he hiaa waa kɛha baa eŋɔli lɛ dalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii jɛɛhe nɛɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up to catch maximum sunlight, which the plant uses to make food for growing large tubers underground. It also keeps the foliage off damp ground, preventing fungal diseases and leaf rot.
ga: Staking Wo sweet potato baa lɛ nɔ koni onine ashɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo nɔ. Akɛ tsei lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni akɛkwɛɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaaa baai lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ naa.

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that spreads quickly in cold, wet, and humid conditions. Pruning extra branches to let in sunlight and air helps dry out the farm and slows down the spread of the fungus.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tsei amli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli gĩɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa fioo.

english: What causes the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up and become tiny?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ bibii?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaves, or transmitting a plant virus. Controlling these insects early protects the leaves so the plant can grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ aphids loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nuɔ baa mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo egbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tsei amli Mra be mli ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ Ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe koni tso lɛ anyɛ ada jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I burn the bush cleared from my land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishãa tsei bibii ni ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani miduɔ lɛ?

english: Burning destroys valuable organic matter and beneficial soil organisms that feed your crops naturally. Leaving cleared weeds to decompose creates natural mulch, which holds moisture and enriches the soil.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa kɛ sũ mli nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi ni ajie lɛ lɛ fite lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii baa. ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat or water stress, like going from very dry soil to heavy flooding. Regular watering and shielding crops from severe heat help flowers set into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu he haomɔ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa nɔ kɛtee nu afua ni mli wa nɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii daa kɛ hebuu kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why does my watermelon field produce lots of flowers but very few actual watermelons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewooo watermelon diɛŋtsɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: Watermelons have separate male and female flowers, and bees must carry pollen from male to female blossoms for fruit to grow. If bees are missing due to heavy chemical spraying, flowers will drop without making fruit.
ga: Watermelon yɛ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi. Ni esa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ aŋɔ pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi hii amli kɛya fɔfɔi yei anɔ bɔni afee ni aduawai lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛji ŋmeii lɛ laaje yɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ babaoo lɛ hewɔ lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize in the same spot repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up. Alternating with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil nitrogen and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kɔɔ ŋmãa he pɔtɛɛ aba. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsake lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni ebaaku ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and dry up when there are no bigger plants grown next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei wuji bɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct hot sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains next to young cocoa creates a canopy that provides necessary shade and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ Cocoa tso lɛ masɛi lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni he hiaa lɛ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do some farmers plant marigolds or hot pepper plants along the edges of their vegetable beds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ marigold loo hot pepper tsei yɛ amɛ aduawai aŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Certain plants produce strong scents and natural compounds that push away insect pests. Growing them alongside vegetables acts as a living barrier, keeping harmful insects away without using expensive chemicals.
ga: Tsei komɛi yɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa, ni adebɔɔ mli nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛshwieɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ aduawai ahe lɛ, ebaatsu nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni tsofai ni jara wa bɛ mli.

english: Can I put fresh droppings from my farm animals directly onto my growing crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi amli ŋmɔshi nibii heei awo miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Fresh animal manure releases strong heat and intense ammonia gas as it breaks down, which can burn plant roots. You should dry and compost animal droppings for a few weeks first so they break down safely into gentle nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ jieɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ ammonia gas ni naa wa kɛji efite. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso shishifãi ashã. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi ni okɛwo mli otsii fioo komɛi klɛŋklɛŋ koni egbɛ eshwa shweshweeshwe ni etsɔ niyenii ni mli jɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply dry chemical fertilizer around my maize when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ woɔ ŋmãa lɛ he beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need moisture to dissolve so plant roots can absorb them safely. Concentrated fertilizer placed on dry soil stays trapped next to roots and burns them, so it is best to apply it when the soil is wet after a rain.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe miihia ni nu atsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ shweshweeshwe. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpɛtɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni eshã amɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛwo nɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant cassava on the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil every season and gives plant pests a permanent place to breed. Rotating cassava with leguminous crops like groundnuts gives the soil a rest and restores nitrogen naturally.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ aná he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai fɔɔ yɛ daa Ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa ni akɛtsakeɔ ŋmãa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen baa ekoŋŋ.

english: How do weeds actually stop my maize crops from producing big cobs?
ga: Te jwɛi baafee tɛŋŋ atsĩ mi-ŋmã lɛ naa koni ekawo ŋmeii wuji?
