english: Weeds act like secret thieves on your farm, drinking up the groundwater and stealing the sunlight and soil nutrients meant for your crop. When maize has to fight weeds for survival, it lacks the energy to grow full, heavy cobs.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ amɛmiiju oŋmɔ lɛ mli teemɔŋ saji. Kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni ooonu ni oju hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Be mli ni esa akɛ ŋmãa kɛ jwɛi awui koni ehi shi lɛ ŋmãa bɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmãa ni tsii ni eyi obɔ.

english: What good does it do to pile dry grass around the base of my yam heaps during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ jwɛi ni akɛtoɔ mi sweet potato pile lɛ shishi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ he?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) acts like a blanket that blocks direct heat from the sun, trapping moisture in the dirt and keeping the yam roots cool so they can keep growing even without daily rain.
ga: Mulching ni egbi (mulching) tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket, ni tsiɔ la ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni amɛya nɔ amɛdara kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ daa gbi po.

english: Why does my soil turn into hard crust during the dry harmattan, and how can plants fix this?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa yɛ harmatta ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei baanyɛ atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii?

english: Bare soil loses its water rapidly under hot winds and bakes hard under the sun. Planting cover crops like cowpeas shields the ground from harsh weather, keeping the soil soft and rich in organic matter.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ fiteɔ nu oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi, ni ewaa yɛ hulu la shishi. Nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ cowpeas ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai ahe. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli.

english: If I cut off some of the leaves and extra shoots on my tomato plants, won't that kill the crop?
ga: Kɛ mifo baai kɛ ŋmeii ni eshwɛ yɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, No eyeŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui, aloo jeee nakai?

english: Removing unnecessary bottom leaves and extra branches (pruning) helps the plant by directing its energy into making big fruits instead of growing extra stems, while also letting wind pass through to stop leaf diseases.
ga: Ajieɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni he ehiaaa kɛ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ. (Pruning) Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛwo yibii wuji. Mohu ɔ, e daa nɛ e peeɔ tso kpa ko. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli koni ekpa baa helai.

english: Why is it better for me to start my pepper seeds in a small nursery box instead of scattering them on the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mabɔi pepper dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii amli moŋ fe ni magbɛ amɛ ashwã ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper seeds are tiny and easily washed away by heavy rain or eaten by ants on an open farm. A small nursery lets you protect and water the delicate sprouts until they develop strong roots before moving them into the big field.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui lɛ daraaa ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ amɛ oya loo ŋmeii yeɔ amɛ yɛ ŋmɔji ni agbele mli lɛ amli. He bibioo ko ni akɛkwɛɔ tsei lɛ haa onyɛɔ obuɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe ni ohaa amɛ nu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa dani okɛ amɛ yaa ŋmɔ agbo ko mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize crop lacks nitrogen, which is a vital food plant roots feed on. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or adding well-rotted manure will help the leaves turn green and photosynthesize properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei shishifãi yeɔ Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛfee fotosintɛsis jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my yam crop produce huge green leafy vines but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ miiwo wain tsei wuji ni baai eŋɔli lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Giving yams too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to spend all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of tubers below. Switching to fertilizers higher in potassium helps the plant feed the underground tuber instead.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen wo sweet potato mli fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii ni potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ moŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up into tight knots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmeii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap out of young leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Spraying your crops with neem oil solution or safe insecticides stops these pests before they ruin the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Okɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ afɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ. Ekpaa nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfiteɔ tsei lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their tiny young pods before they can grow into big cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho ŋmeii bibii bibii lɛ? dani eda ni etsɔ kookoo ŋmeii agboi

english: Young cocoa pods drop early due to a natural condition called cherelle wilt or from attacks by mirid insects. Pruning excess branches to let in air, maintaining proper shade, and controlling mirids with recommended sprays helps protect the pods.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Cherel’s wilt lɛ hewɔ. or from the attack of amazing insects. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aaafolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli Kwɛmɔ hulutsoo ni sa Ni okɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni atsɔɔ akɛ ashwieɔ nɔ lɛ akudɔ afua lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: How can I keep tiny beetles from eating up all my maize after I harvest and store it in the barn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkaye mi-ŋmãa lɛ fɛɛ beni mikpa ni mikɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Storage insects like grain weevils multiply quickly when harvested maize is still damp. You must dry your maize kernels completely under the sun until they are hard before storing them in airtight bags or treating them with approved grain protectant dust.
ga: Kplukai ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe, tamɔ ŋmaa ŋmeii lɛ, faa oya kɛji akɛ ŋmaa ni akpa lɛ mli edɔ lolo. Esa akɛ okɛ o-abele dumɔwui lɛ agbi kwraa yɛ hulu la shishi kɛyashi amɛbaafee shiŋŋ dani okɛwo vacuum kotokui amli loo okɛ sũ ni buɔ dumɔwui ahe ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu he nii.

english: Why do my cowpea plants blossom with flowers but drop them all without making any beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ fɔfɔi shi eshwieɔ fɛɛ shi ŋmeii ko kwraa shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Flower drop in cowpeas is usually caused by flower thrips insects eating the delicate parts of the blossom. Spraying your crop with a recommended protective spray just as the flower buds appear allows the flowers to mature into full bean pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ tsina ŋmei nɔ lɛ baa ji fɔfɔi thrips ni yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Spraying your crop with the recommended preventative spray as the buds appear will cause the flowers to grow into full pea pods.

english: Is it better for me to plant my cassava stems flat on the ground or on top of raised soil mounds?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmei tso yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ?

english: Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges creates loose earth that makes it easier for roots to swell into large tubers. It also prevents water from gathering around the stem during heavy rain, which stops root rot.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋmei ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji. Ehaa nu hu shwieɔ tso lɛ he yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees fall over easily during heavy rainstorms even when the trunk is strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni eda lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe wa moŋ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, and tiny worms called nematodes or banana weevil grubs often burrow into them and destroy their grip on the soil. Clearing infested roots before planting and mulching properly keeps root systems strong enough to anchor the trees.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo banana weevils lɛ shwieɔ mli ni amɛfoɔ sũ ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ he lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie shishifãi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ dani adu ni awo nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ ahe awa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop soft black rotten spots at the bottom while they are ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni mli tse beni amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: This black spot is called blossom-end rot, caused by a shortage of calcium in the plant or irregular watering during fruit formation. Watering your garden regularly and adding agricultural lime to the soil prevents this from damaging your harvest.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ he diŋ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔii anaagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli loo nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo obɔŋ lɛ mli daa ni okɛ okwaayeli mli ŋmei fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaatsi enɛ naa koni ekafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How early in the season should I start weeding my vegetable garden after planting?
ga: Beni midu nii sɛɛ lɛ, mɛɛ be esa akɛ mabɔi mi-aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ shwiemɔ?

english: You should start clearing weeds within the first two to three weeks after planting. Removing weeds while they are small prevents them from stealing water, light, and soil nutrients from your young crops during their most critical growth stage.
ga: Esa akɛ oje jwɛi lɛ ŋmɔmɔ shishi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 2-3 lɛ mli yɛ dumɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nu, la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei bibii lɛ amli yɛ amɛdalɛ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth, or that the soil is waterlogged and suffocating the roots. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help restore the green color and keep the plants healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei lɛ adalɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure will help restore the green color and make the plant healthy.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and curl up tight during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpãa shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl up as a defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun and prevent water loss through evaporation. As long as the plant bounces back in the evening when temperatures cool, it is just saving moisture to survive the dry heat.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi, ni ekɛtsi nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ he baajɔ lɛ gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ lɛ. Eji koni eye ebua ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ latsaa ni mli egbi lɛ mli kɛkɛ.

english: You should not plant immediately after the very first rain because the soil underneath is still dry and tender seeds will burn. Wait until the soil remains moist a few inches deep for two or three steady rainfalls before sowing your seeds.
ga: Esaaa akɛ oduɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi lolo ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ baashã. Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ lolo kɛyashɛ 2-3 inches mli koni eha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa 2-3 dani odu dumɔwui.

english: Why do my young tomato seedlings rot at the stem when I water them in the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui bibii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo amɛmli yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Watering during the hottest part of the day heats up the water on the soil surface, scalding tender seedling stems and creating warm, humid conditions that encourage destructive fungal diseases. It is best to water early in the morning or late in the afternoon.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli adɔ. Akɛ tso ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ shã. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ ni woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ mɔ he hewalɛ lɛ baa. Esa akɛ afɔ lɛ nu leebi loo shwane.

english: What is eating the deep center leaves of my young corn plants and leaving dark droppings?
ga: Mɛni ji baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ teŋgbɛ ni mli kwɔ lɛ ni ayeɔ ni ashiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common caterpillar that hides in the funnel of maize plants. Checking your field regularly and applying neem leaf extract or recommended insecticides early in the crop's life will protect your harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmei tsei amli ŋmeii amli lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ nibii ni odu lɛ amli daa, ni okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ atsu nii yɛ tso lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the tree before they get fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛshwereɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp, and overly shaded farms during heavy rains. Pruning extra shade branches to let in sunlight and air helps prevent the fungus from taking over your tree.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli ewo duŋ, ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji krokomɛi ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ amli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii akaye otso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I grow cassava on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Growing cassava repeatedly in the same spot drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving the earth time to recover, causing future yields to shrink. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nutrients naturally.
ga: Cassava ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nibii ni afeɔ wɔsɛɛ lɛ baa shi. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do some farmers plant cowpeas together in the same field with their maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ ŋmãa duɔ tsina ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, which acts as a free natural fertilizer for nearby maize. In return, the tall maize stalks provide light support for the cowpea vines.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ. Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, ŋmãa tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ haa tsina ŋmãa wain tsei lɛ náa la.

english: Why do seeds bought from an agro-dealer yield more harvest than seeds I saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mihe kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Commercial certified seeds are specially selected and treated to resist common local diseases and withstand dry conditions. Seeds saved from past harvests naturally lose these strong traits over time, resulting in smaller yields.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni akɛ jarayeli he odaseyeli haa lɛ krɛdɛɛ ni atsuɔ he nii koni ekɛte shi ewo maŋ lɛ mli helai ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ atsu nii. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ sui nɛɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo.

english: Why are my cassava roots staying thin and woody instead of swelling into thick tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ tsei moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need loose, soft soil and plenty of direct sunlight to feed the root and allow it to expand. Hard, compacted soil or planting under heavy shade prevents the roots from swelling into food reserves.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ. kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baahã shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni eha amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni mli edɔ loo ni aduɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baatsi shishifãi ni efuu lɛ anaa koni amɛkaha niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ.

english: Leaves turn yellow when the soil runs out of nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to build green leaves. Adding animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the plants regain their green color and grow strong.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ba shi. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Pepper plants become stunted when the soil is packed too tightly for roots to spread, or when tiny root pests attack underground. Loosening the soil before planting and adding organic compost gives the roots space and energy to grow.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ewo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ aahu akɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbɛ ashwã. Aloo kɛ́ shishifãi bibii ni fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ batutua shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ dani adu ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli awo mli lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa hegbɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛdaraa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air gets too hot and dry or when the soil lacks consistent moisture. Keeping the soil regularly watered and placing dry grass mulch around the base helps hold moisture and protects the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa Nu ni oooha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi afata he yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn under strong, direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad shade leaves to shelter the young cocoa until it becomes mature enough to tolerate full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni baanyɛ ashã yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. The rapidly growing seedlings will provide broad leaves to protect the young cocoa until they are big enough to tolerate full sun.

english: Why do my corn leaves curl up into tight tubes during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Corn plants curl their leaves to reduce the leaf surface exposed to the sun, stopping water from evaporating too fast. It is a natural self-defense mechanism the plant uses to conserve moisture during hot dry hours.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la ni baa amɛnɔ lɛ aba shi. Tsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ. Eji adebɔɔ mli he-buamɔ gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ, ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot underground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani manyɛ makpa amɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long, suffocating the roots and allowing fungi to grow. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the tubers stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. This results in the roots suffocating and allowing fungus to grow. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: How can I tell if the ground has enough rain water for my seeds to sprout safely?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha midumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe?

english: Seeds require steady moisture to germinate without drying out. You can test this by digging a hand's depth into the soil; if a squeezed handful of soil forms a soft ball without crumbling apart, there is enough water to plant.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ. You can test this by digging deep into the soil. Kɛji akɛ okɛ sũ ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ shwie shi kɛyashi efee bɔɔlu ni yɔɔ blɛoo. ni efooo mli bibii Etsɔɔ akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔwui yɛ.

english: Why do black spots on my bean leaves spread to other plants after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ mi-bean baai lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei krokomɛi anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Raindrops splash fungal spores from diseased leaves onto neighboring healthy plants. Giving your plants enough space between rows helps the leaves dry quickly in the wind, stopping the disease from spreading.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ fungal spores kɛjɛɔ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ ateŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ agbiɔ oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa amɛ. ni ekpa helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ

english: Why do weeds around my crops cause my harvested cassava to be so small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi babaoo ebɔle he lɛ? Miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ haa ŋmãa ni akpaa lɛ feɔ bibioo kwraa?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients before your crops can reach them. Clearing weeds early in the first few weeks of growth leaves all the soil nutrients available for your cassava roots to grow large.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli dani ŋmɔshi nibii shɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ agbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni amɛdaraa lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ adara.

english: How does using a mechanical planter help my seeds grow better than planting by hand?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔne ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa midumɔwui lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ fe ni mikɛ niji duɔ amɛ?

english: A planter places every seed at the exact same depth and distance apart. This ensures that every plant gets its own equal share of soil nutrients and light without being crowded by nearby plants.
ga: Okwaafonyo lɛ kɛ dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu toɔ he ni mli kwɔ kɛ bɔ ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ ha lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa sũ mli niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛtsiii tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ anaa.

english: How many years do I have to wait after planting a rubber tree before I can start harvesting latex?
ga: Kɛ́ mɔ ko du rɔbɔt tso sɛɛ lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ emɛ dani enyɛ ekpa latɛs lɛ?

english: Rubber trees usually take about 5 to 7 years to mature before the trunk is thick enough for harvesting. Tapping a tree too early will permanently stunt its growth and reduce the total latex you can harvest over its life.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, rɔbɔt tsei heɔ aaafee afii 5 kɛyashi 7 dani amɛshishifã lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa. Kɛ́ otswa tso ko mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha edalɛ aya hiɛ kwraa. ni ehaa latɛs ni obaanyɛ okpa yɛ owala be fɛɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: How long will my rubber trees continue to produce latex once they are ready for harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ mi rɔbɔt tso lɛ baaya nɔ ejie latɛs beni eshɛ he ni abaakpa lɛ?

english: If tapped correctly without damaging the tree trunk, a rubber tree can yield latex continuously for 25 to 30 years, giving you a steady income over several decades.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afolɔ tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni efiteee amɛshishifã lɛ, Rɔba tsei lɛ baanyɛ aya nɔ afee latɛs afii 25 kɛyashi 30, ni enɛ baaha oná shika ni yaa nɔ daa afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni baa lɛ amli.

english: Is harvesting rubber latex as simple as cutting any part of the tree trunk with a normal cutlass?
ga: Ani latɛs ni akpaa lɛ waaa tamɔ bɔ ni akɛ daa tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ fã ko lɛ?

english: No, rubber harvesting requires specialized skills and tools to make thin, precise cuts into the outer bark. If you cut too deep into the wood, you will permanently wound the tree, cause disease, and stop latex flow.
ga: Dabi, ŋmei lɛ mli nu lɛ akpamɔ biɔ ŋaa kɛ nibii krɛdɛɛi ni akɛfoɔ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ mli bibii ni afee lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛji akɛ afo tso lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ ebaaye tso lɛ awui kɛya naanɔ, ekɛ hela baaba ni ebaaha nu ni hoɔ lɛ akpa.

english: Why do I need to collect rubber latex early in the morning instead of during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ obua latɛs naa leebi moŋ fe shwane?

english: Rubber trees have high internal sap pressure during the cool morning hours, allowing latex to flow out easily. As the sun heats up the farm, the trees conserve water and the sap thickens and stops running.
ga: Rɔba tsei yɛ mligbɛ latɛs ni tsii waa yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be mli. Ehaa latex lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mlɛo Beni hulu lɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli dɔɔ lɛ Tsei hu yeɔ ebuaa ni akɛbuɔ nu he. Latex lɛ mli shwieɔ shi ni ekpaa shwiemɔ.

english: Why do rubber trees lose all their leaves during the dry season, and does it mean my trees are dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ rɔbɔt tsei lɛ baai fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ? Ni ani no tsɔɔ akɛ mi rɔba tso lɛ miigbo?

english: This is a natural process called 'wintering' where the tree sheds leaves to save water during dry months. The tree is not dying; it will grow fresh green leaves and resume latex production once the rainy season begins.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘fɛ̃i be’ ni tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai koni amɛkɛbu nu he yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. Tso lɛ gbooo, ewoɔ baai ni tsuɔ nii waa ni ebɔi latɛs feemɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli.

english: Why do my crops produce less yield or stop producing altogether during the heavy dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo loo amɛkpaa yibiiwoo kwraa yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli lɛ?

english: Crops need water to carry food and nutrients from the soil up into their leaves and branches. During a severe dry spell, crops slow down their internal processes to survive, causing flowers to drop and fruit or sap production to drop sharply.
ga: Tsei hia nu koni amɛkɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya amɛbai kɛ amɛniji anɔ. yɛ hɔmɔ be ni naa wa lɛ mli Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mligbɛ nifeemɔi lɛ baa shi koni amɛhi shi. Enɛ haa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni aduawai loo nu ni ajieɔ lɛ baa shi oya.

english: Can I plant short-term food crops like cassava or maize between my young rubber trees?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii ni heɔ be kuku tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Mi rɔba tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, during the first 3 to 4 years when rubber trees are still small, you can plant crops like maize or vegetables between the rows to get food and quick money while you wait for the rubber trees to mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 ni rɔba tso lɛ ji bibioo lolo lɛ mli. Obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai yɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋ koni onine ashɛ niyenii kɛ shika nɔ oya be mli ni omɛɛɔ tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so fast when my tree crops are young, but stop growing once the trees get big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛkɛ be mli ni mitsei lɛ darako lɛ? Shi ani ekpaa dalɛ kɛ́ tso lɛ da?

english: Young trees have small leaves that allow direct sunlight to hit the soil, which feeds weed seeds. As your trees grow large, their branches form a dense upper leaves layer that blocks sunlight, naturally keeping weeds from growing underneath.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni haa hulu la shɛɔ shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ. ni ji niyenii kɛha jwɛi dumɔwui Beni otso lɛ daa lɛ Amɛniji feɔ ŋwɛi baa ni mli eyi obɔ ni tsiɔ hulu la naa. Enɛ tsiɔ jwɛi anaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ yɛ shishi.

english: How do I know when it is the right time to start planting my crop seedlings at the start of the rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: It is best to wait until the rainy season settles completely and the soil stays moist after two or three heavy rains, rather than planting after the very first light rain, which can leave seedlings to dry up and die.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eba shi kwraa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa fioo komɛi asɛɛ, moŋ fe ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ fioo lɛ sɛɛ, ni baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi.

english: How do I know if my farm land is suitable for growing rubber trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ sa kɛha rɔbɔt tsei akwɛmɔ?

english: Rubber trees thrive in deep, well-drained soils in warm areas with high rainfall. Lands that stay flooded or waterlogged for weeks are not suitable because long-standing water rots the tree roots.
ga: Rɔba tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ loo ehiɔ shi otsii babaoo lɛ esaaa ejaakɛ nu ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ baaha tsei ashishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do the new improved tomato seed varieties produce so much more fruit than the seeds I save from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ mli lɛ?

english: Improved crop varieties are scientifically bred to direct more of the plant's food and energy into producing big, healthy fruits and resisting diseases, whereas seeds saved year after year gradually lose these high-yielding traits.
ga: Akɛ jeŋ nilee kwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛ tsei aniyenii kɛ hewalɛ babaoo atsu nii ni amɛkɛwo yibii ni dara, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ sui ni haa yibii babaoo nɛɛ fiofio.

english: Why can't I plant the seeds harvested from my high-yielding hybrid maize to get the same good yield next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ madu dumɔwui ni akpa kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo mli lɛ koni maná yibii kpakpai ni tamɔ nɛkɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid crops get their strength from a precise genetic mix of two parent plants. When you plant the seeds from a hybrid harvest, that special genetic combination breaks apart, leading to unpredictable growth, uneven plant heights, and much lower yields.
ga: Tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ naa amɛhewalɛ kɛjɛɔ fɔmɔ tsei enyɔ ni akɛfee ekome lɛ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛji okɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ hybrid harvest mli lɛ du lɛ Ajaraa tsɛŋemɔ helai krɛdɛɛi ni akɛtoɔ amɛhe lɛ amli. Ekɛ dalɛ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ baa Tsei lɛ agbɔjɔmɔ lɛ jeee ekome. ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi kwraa.

english: Why do some new cowpea varieties mature in just two months while my local seeds take over four months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii heei komɛi shwereɔ yɛ nyɔji enyɔ pɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mimaŋ dumɔwui lɛ heɔ nɔ ni fe nyɔji ejwɛ.

english: Newer varieties are bred to be 'short-duration' crops that trigger flowering quickly regardless of day length, allowing them to complete their life cycle fast before dry spells or late-season pests can damage them.
ga: Amɛmiifɔ tsei srɔtoi heei ni ‘Be kuku’ ni baaha amɛwo fɔfɔi oya ni gbi lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ kɔɔɔ he eko. Enɛ haa amɛgbeɔ amɛshihilɛ be lɛ naa oya dani hɔmɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ fiteɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers during hot sunny weeks instead of turning them into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwie efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ yɛ otsi kome ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: When heat becomes extreme, pepper plants enter a survival mode and drop their blossoms to preserve water and energy, waiting until temperatures cool down before trying to set fruit again.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ baaya shihilɛ mli ni amɛbaashɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Mɛɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ aba shi dani oka nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ okwɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants shed all their leaves during the dry season, and does it mean they are dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni ani no tsɔɔ akɛ eegbo?

english: Cassava drops its leaves intentionally to stop water from evaporating through them during dry weather. The plant is not dead; it is resting and conserving moisture in its roots until the rains return.
ga: Akɛ yiŋtoo shwieɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ anɔ koni nu akatsɔ mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Enɛ ji koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ.

english: Why do my garden egg plants wilt completely under the hot afternoon sun but look fresh and standing tall again by morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiho kwraa yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ? Shi kwɛmɔ akɛ ohe ejɔ bo ni odamɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ leebi.

english: During peak heat, the leaves lose water faster than the roots can drink it up, causing temporary wilting. Once the sun goes down and transpiration slows, the roots catch up and fill the stems back up with water.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli waa lɛ, baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Kɛ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baaje kpo ni amɛkɛ nu baayi tso lɛ mli.

english: Why do traditional tomato plants rot so easily during the heavy rainy season while some improved varieties stay healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ blema tomato tsei lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tomato henɔi komɛi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ lolo lɛ,.

english: Heavy rain creates damp conditions where fungal diseases bloom. Traditional varieties often lack natural defenses against wet-weather fungi, whereas improved varieties have bred-in resistance that keeps their leaves and stems healthy in high humidity.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa hulutsoo baa he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai shwereɔ yɛ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, kusum mli henɔi lɛ bɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu kɛjɛ ŋmeii ahe yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli. yɛ be mli ni henɔi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ fɔmɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahiɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ fa babaoo.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape from the tips down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛjɛ naagbee kɛba shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting at the leaf tips of older, bottom leaves is a clear sign of nitrogen starvation. The plant is pulling nitrogen out of its old leaves to feed the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Yellowing ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai momoi lɛ ashishigbɛ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Tsei miigba nitrogen kɛmiijɛ baai momoi amli koni amɛkɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: When crops are crowded, they compete intensely for sunlight. The plant spends all its energy stretching upward to reach light instead of branching out and forming the flower buds needed for fruit.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛshɛ ŋwɛi koni amɛná la. Mohu ɔ, a jeɔ nihi nɛ a peeɔ fɔfɔi nɛ he hia kɛ ha yiblii ɔ.

english: Why is my young tomato plant producing flowers when it is still tiny and has very few leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei bibii lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi yɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii waa ni amɛbaai fioo pɛ amɛyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Early flowering often happens when a seedling experiences severe stress from poor soil, root damage, or drought. The plant senses danger and tries to produce seeds immediately to reproduce before it dies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii ni baa mra lɛ baa kɛji dumɔwui kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa kpe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii, shishifãi ni efite, loo hɔmɔ mli. Tso lɛ nuɔ oshara he ni amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ewo dumɔwui koni ekɛfɔ dani egbo.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate harsh, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains protects young cocoa from heat, traps moisture in the soil, and helps the seedlings survive their first two years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ latsaa he. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Does it matter which way I point my cassava stem when planting it in the soil?
ga: Ani esa akɛ matsɔɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ gbɛ pɔtɛɛ ko beni mikɛ amɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, you must always plant cassava stems with the small buds pointing upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down forces the shoots to grow backward, which weakens the plant and leads to a tiny harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehe miihia ni odu ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, ŋwɛi ni oootsɔɔ ŋwɛi Dumɔ ni okɛ ohiɛ tsɔɔ shi lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ewo yibii fioo pɛ.

english: No, planting seeds too close together makes the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough food and light to produce large, full ears of corn.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ náa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo ŋmãa toi wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of the stalk mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is its main food for leafy growth. Applying fertilizer like NPK or urea, or adding compost, restores the green color and health.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli tamɔ NPK loo urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ hewalɛnamɔ kpakpa aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the ground, but legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas put nitrogen back into the soil naturally. Rotating these crops keeps your land fertile so your next maize crop grows better.
ga: Abele heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii Enɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nibii nɛɛ ni oootsake lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Koni o-corn ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the sunlight to make food for the growing tuber under the soil. Staking keeps the leaves away from hot, wet ground where they can easily rot.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulu lɛ mli koni ekɛha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking haa baai lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hei ni mli edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi oya lɛ.

english: What is eating ragged holes in my young corn leaves and leaving brown dust in the middle?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ bu yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii amli? Ni oshi sũ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ko yɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the center of the plant. Spraying recommended treatments early in the morning or late evening when the caterpillars come out to feed will save your crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ eje kpo kɛmiiya niyenii taomɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cold, wet, and shady conditions. Pruning excess tree branches to let in sunlight and clearing weeds helps air flow and reduces the rot.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ejɔ, fɔ́, shade shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la lɛ abote mli, ni ojie jwɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli ni ebaaha ŋmeii aba shi.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from extreme sun heat or irregular watering. Giving them steady water early in the morning and protecting the roots keeps the flowers healthy enough to form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulu ni tsoɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu daa leebi, ni abuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛwoɔ tomato.

english: How does covering the soil around my garden vegetables with dry grass help them in the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mi-aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-aduawai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) acts like an umbrella for the soil. It traps moisture in the earth so water doesn't evaporate quickly, keeps roots cool, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, nu lɛ efooo oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn under direct heat. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside your cocoa creates living shade umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting young trees until they grow stronger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Kɛ́ odu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ o-cocoa lɛ masɛi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso ni yɔɔ wala mli lɛ feɔ hulutsoo tso. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil has run out of nitrogen, which plants need to make green leaf food. Adding composted manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help your maize regain its green color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehe hiaa ni tsei kɛtsu nii yɛ niyenii ni baa eŋɔli yɔɔ mli lɛ feemɔ mli Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua o-ŋmãa lɛ ni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do small worms appear inside the funnel of my young corn plants right after they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli beni amɛkwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: These are fall armyworms. The mother moths lay eggs on young, tender leaves because the middle funnel gives the growing worms shelter and soft plant tissue to eat. Early handpicking or safe biopesticide treatment protects the crop's main leaf tip.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji fall asraafoi akuu lɛ mli ŋmeii. Nyɛmɛi ni ji ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ baai bibii anɔ ejaakɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ haa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ kɛ tsei amli fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ he ko ni amɛyeɔ. Oniji ni ooohala mra Aloo, tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ baabu tso lɛ baai titrii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the pods on my cocoa tree turn black and rot during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, dark environments. Pruning extra shade branches and clearing weeds lets air and sunlight flow through the farm, drying out the moisture that the fungus needs to spread.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ duŋ yɔɔ. Tsei ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo babaoo baa, ni ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. ni ehaa nu ni he hiaa ni ŋmei lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa.

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds very close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in tall but weak stalks with small, poorly filled corn cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni kwɔlɔ shi amɛhe waaa kɛ ŋmãa bibii ni shwieee shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: Why does my cassava root turn soft and watery if water sits on the farm for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ nu kɛji nu lɛ hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rain floods the field and water cannot drain away, root systems choke, allowing rots to break down the firm starch into liquid.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo lɛ, ŋmɔji amli nu hoɔ ni nu nyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli. The root system will suffocate. Ha ni egbo ni efolɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa lɛ mli ni etsɔ nu.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the soil dries out completely or when temperatures get too high. Mulching around the base with dry grass holds water in the soil and keeps root temperatures cool.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why is it helpful to plant groundnuts on the plot where I harvested corn last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ aaadu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmei yɛ nɔ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. Planting them refreshes soil fertility naturally after heavy-feeding crops like corn have used up the soil's strength.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ adumɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ efo shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting and becoming soft while sitting in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ miije shishi amɛmiikwɛ̃ ni amɛmiifee blɛoo beni mita shi yɛ nitoohe lɛ?

english: Yam tubers remain living plant parts after harvest. Heat and light signal to the yam that it is time to grow new shoots, using up stored food inside the tuber. Storing yams in a dark, cool, and well-ventilated structure slows down sprouting.
ga: Sweet potato tubers remain the living part of the plant after harvest. Heat and light signal to the sweet potato that it's time to plant new shoots. Kɛtsɔ niyenii fɛɛ ni ato yɛ yitso lɛ mli lɛ ni ekɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ. Storing sweet potatoes in a dark, cool, well-ventilated area will slow sprouting.

english: Can applying too much pest spray make my vegetable crops wilt or become unsafe to eat?
ga: Ani tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha mitsei lɛ agbɔjɔ loo eha amɛfee nɔ ni esaaa akɛ ayeɔ?

english: Yes, using excessive chemical spray can burn crop leaves and leave dangerous residues on vegetables that cause sickness in humans. Always measure chemical inputs carefully according to guidance to protect both plant health and consumer safety.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei ahe baai ni eshi nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ aduawai ni kɛ hela baa lɛ anɔ. Susumɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi anaa koni ebu tsei ahewalɛ kɛ mɛi ni yeɔ nii lɛ fɛɛ ahe.

english: Why shouldn't I plant many corn seeds in one hole to get more crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When you put too many seeds in one hole, the growing crops fight each other for water, light, and nutrients in the soil. This competition makes all the plants weak and results in small, poor-quality corn cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmãa bibii ni ehiii kwraa.

english: Why is it important for me to draw straight lines when planting my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo linei ni ja kɛ́ midu ŋmãa?

english: Planting along measured, straight lines ensures every crop gets equal space to grow and makes it much easier for you to weed, apply crop medicine, and harvest without stepping on your plants.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja ni asusu nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ náa he ko ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃. and help you get rid of weeds Use medicine to treat plant diseases And it's much easier to harvest without having to step on your plants.

english: How do I figure out the right amount of corn seed I need to buy for my plot of land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmãa ni sa kɛha shikpɔŋ hemɔ?

english: The required seed quantity depends on your land area and the recommended spacing between rows and holes. By measuring your field first, you can calculate the exact seed weight needed so you do not waste money buying extra.
ga: Dumɔwui abɔ ni he hiaa lɛ damɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɛ sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ afee yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta kɛ bu lɛ teŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ susumɔ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ Obaanyɛ obu dumɔwu lɛ tsiimɔ pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ he akɔntaa. Bɔni afee ni ehe akahi ni ofite shika yɛ nibii krokomɛi ni okɛbaahe lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my corn stalks growing tall and yellow instead of dark green and strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miidara ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli wa ni mli edɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Corn stalks stretch tall and turn pale when they are planted too close together or lack nutrients like nitrogen, as they struggle to reach sunlight and food.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo amɛbɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen, beni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii lɛ.

english: What causes some corn plants in my farm to stay tiny while others right next to them grow very tall?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi feɔ bibii waa yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ daraa babaoo lɛ?

english: Uneven growth usually happens when seeds are planted at different depths, when weeds steal nutrients early on, or when water accumulates unevenly across the field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dalɛ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee baa kɛji adu dumɔwui yɛ hei srɔtoi. Beni jwɛi lɛ juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ mra loo be mli ni nu lɛ buaa ehe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee

english: How do I know if the number of corn plants on my land is normal for a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ayibɔ ji nɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ kpakpa?

english: A normal plant count means your field is evenly filled without large bare spots or overcrowded clumps, allowing each plant to produce at least one full cob.
ga: Tsei ayibɔ ni baa daa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli baayi obɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni hei wuji ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko loo ŋmeii ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine bɛ mli. Enɛ haa kɛ hoo lɛ, tso fɛɛ tso woɔ ŋmei kome ni eyi obɔ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to apply crop medicine to my corn?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi tsofa baatsu nii yɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ nɔ?

english: It is best to apply medicine early in the morning or late in the evening when temperatures are cool, which keeps the liquid from drying up too fast and prevents hot sunshine from burning the leaves.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ tsofa lɛ awo mɔ he leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ akagbi oya tsɔ. ni ehaaa hulu lɛ ashã baai lɛ

english: Why do my corn leaves look burnt after I spray them with crop medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã beni mikɛ tso tsofa shwie nɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf burning occurs when the medicine is mixed too strong with water, sprayed during the heat of the day, or applied using the wrong type of chemical for that crop stage.
ga: Baai lɛ ashãa baa kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofa lɛ futu nu mli waa tsɔ. Spray yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. aloo tsofai ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli

english: Can I apply crop medicine to my field before my corn seeds start germinating?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ aje shishi amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Yes, certain pre-emergence medicines can be sprayed on bare soil immediately after planting to kill hidden weed seeds before your corn stems emerge.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ tsofai komɛi ni akɛshwieɔ shi dani ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni odu nii lɛ sɛɛ. Koni agbe jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ dani ŋmãa tsei akwɛ̃.

english: How does leaving enough space between my corn plants help me get bigger cobs?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni mashi yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ baaye abua mi ni maná ŋmãa agbo?

english: Proper spacing allows root systems to spread out freely to soak up fertilizer and ground moisture, giving the plant enough energy to fill out large, heavy ears of corn.
ga: He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛwoɔ ŋmãa toi agboi ni tsii amli.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and shallow roots that dry out quickly in direct sunlight. Providing temporary shade using fast-growing crops like plantains protects them from heat and keeps the soil moist while they establish roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains tsu nii ni akɛha hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ, ebaabu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ latsaa he, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni ewoɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil. When nitrogen is short, the plant steals it from older lower leaves to feed the young growing top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ nitrogen bɛ Tso lɛ juɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛye ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when extreme afternoon heat dries up the pollen before fertilization can happen. Giving plants consistent water and shade during peak heat can help flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shwane mli la ni naa wa lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ mli fɔfɔi lɛ gĩɔ dani fɔmɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aba. Kɛ́ akɛ nu kɛ hulutsoo ha tsei yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with bushy leaves but give me small root tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli shi ewoɔ ŋmeii ni shishifãi bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil makes cassava focus energy on leaf growth instead of roots. Applying nutrients rich in potassium helps the plant store energy underground, producing thicker cassava tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baa lɛ dalɛ nɔ moŋ fe shishifãi lɛ. Niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ potassium ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. As a result, the cassava roots become thicker.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like mites or aphids. As they suck the liquid from young leaves, the foliage puckers, curls, and stunts overall growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Be mli ni enuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ, baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛkuɔ amɛhe ni amɛtsiɔ dalɛ fɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my stored seed yams start sprouting inside the barn before the rains even arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani nugbɔ lɛ po baa lɛ?

english: Yams have a natural internal dormancy clock. Once their resting phase ends after harvest, ambient warmth and air moisture signal to the tuber that it is time to shoot vines, regardless of soil planting.
ga: Sweet potatoes yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɛlɛtswaa ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli. Beni hejɔɔmɔ be lɛ baa naagbee yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ haa bulb lɛ leɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ adu wain tso lɛ. Ekɔɔɔ he eko nɔ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my vegetable vines wilt in the afternoon sun even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miwein tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mishwieɔ amɛnɔ nu leebi moŋ?

english: In intense midday heat, plants lose water through leaf pores faster than roots can draw it from the soil. The leaves temporarily curl or wilt to conserve moisture and will recover as temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Baai lɛ baabɔle loo amɛbaagbɔjɔ be kukuoo ko koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. ni ebaahe ewa lɛ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli ba shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my maize stalks break and fall down easily during heavy rain or wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ fãa oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants fall easily if planted too shallowly or if root damage occurred from pests. Mounding soil around the base of the stems (earthing up) gives roots extra anchor support against heavy weather.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ loo kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ efite amɛshishifãi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi (shikpɔŋ nɔ) lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa waa lɛ.

english: Why do I get smaller bunches of plantain when I let many shoots grow around one mother stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miyɛ plantain tsei bibii lɛ? Beni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nyɛ kome tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Multiple shoots (suckers) sharing one root system fight with each other for water, sunlight, and food. Removing extra suckers leaves more nutrients for the main plant to yield a larger, heavier bunch.
ga: Tsoi ashishifãi babaoo ni yɔɔ shishifã kome lɛ wuɔ kɛhaa nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii babaoo koni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni da ni tsii.

english: How do I know when my oil palm fruit bunches are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-oil palm yibii lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Oil palm bunches are fully ripe when the outer fruits turn bright reddish-orange and a few loose fruits begin naturally falling to the ground around the base of the palm tree.
ga: Mu tsei akui lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa kɛ́ kponɔgbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ-tsuru ni mli tse. Ni aduawai ni egbee shi lɛ ekomɛi baaje shishi amɛgbee shikpɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛbɔle ŋmei tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and scorching in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains planted nearby to protect them, the heat dries out the leaves quickly, causing them to burn and drop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ koni akɛbu he lɛ bɛ lɛ, baai lɛ baagbi oya. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen, an essential plant nutrient. The growing maize starves and pulls nutrients out of its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei Abɛi ni miida lɛ baaye hɔmɔ ni ebaagbala niyenii kɛjɛ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Cowpeas have special beneficial bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas out of the air and put it into the soil, leaving behind natural fertilizer for the crops you plant next.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ helatsɛmɛi ahe nibii krɛdɛɛi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the ground when heavy rains stay on the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When wet soil remains flooded without proper drainage, the roots drown and fungus takes over, causing the tubers to spoil underground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nu eyi shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni ŋmeii yeɔ nɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baagboi.

english: Why does my plantain stand give small bunches if many suckers are growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo miikwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Extra suckers act like extra mouths sharing one small bowl of food. They steal water and nutrients from the main stem, leaving the mother plant with less energy to produce a large bunch.
ga: Tsoi ni fa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ daaŋ krokomɛi ni akɛjaa niyenii yɛ tsɛnsii bibii amli. Amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa tso nyɛ lɛ náaa hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do weeds make my young maize crop grow thin and weak even when rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mibi lɛ ŋmãa lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Weeds are fast growers that aggressively drink up water and fertilizer from the upper soil before your young crop's small roots can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni kɛ miishɛɛ nuɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani shishifãi bibii lɛ daa. ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ baafee nɔ ni anyɛɔ ashɛɔ he

english: Extreme heat destroys the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing them from forming fruit, so the plant sheds the useless blossoms.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. ha ewooo yibii No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa.

english: Why do yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ koni enyɛ ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants manufacture food for their underground tubers using sunlight collected by their leaves. Climbing a stake lifts the leaves higher into the sun so the plant can grow big, heavy yams.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ hulu la ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ feɔ niyenii amɛhaa amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ akwɔ ŋtayaa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaa lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni ŋtayaa tso lɛ adara ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why are my pepper plant leaves rolling up into tight curls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies, which damage the soft leaf tissue and spread plant sicknesses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni fiteɔ baai bibii lɛ amli fãji ni egbɛɔ tsei ahe helai eshwaa lɛ

english: Why does leaving dead leaves on top of my field help my crops survive dry days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mishi baai ni egboi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dead leaves forms a protective blanket called mulch. This blanket shields the dirt from direct sun so moisture cannot evaporate easily, keeping the soil damp longer.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egboi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ atade nɛɛ buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ muji kɛ muji ni jɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli baa lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, hulutsoo be lɛ sɛɛ efooo oya. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why should I cover the soil around my crops with dried grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he sũ? Akɛ jwɛi loo baai ŋmɔɔ?

english: Covering the soil, called mulching, acts like a protective blanket. It keeps the hot sun from drying out the earth too quickly, keeps crop roots cool, and slowly rots to add natural food back into your soil.
ga: Mulching, ni atsɛɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli jɔɔ ni efiteɔ fiofio koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm. They aggressively suck up the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops, leaving your main plants weak and hungry.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛmuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni onibii ni oduɔ lɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, otsei titrii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni hɔmɔ baaye amɛ.

english: Look closely at the small leaf buds on the cassava stem. These buds must always point upwards toward the sky, because that is where the green leaves and branches will sprout from. Planting them upside down makes it very hard for the crop to grow.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Kpɛtɛ ŋmei tso lɛ he Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be. Ejaakɛ jɛmɛ ji he ni baai eŋɔli kɛ tsei aniji lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ da ni etsɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ebaaha ewa aha tso lɛ akɛ ebaada.

english: Yam plants need as much sunlight as possible on their leaves to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to light and preventing leaf rot.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni eha niyenii aha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni awo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Okɛwo la mli ni otsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves in high heat to reduce water loss and protect themselves from burning. If they uncurl in the cool evening, the plant is safe, but if they stay curled, the soil needs more water.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ la ni mli wa nɔ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ akafee nɔ ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ shãa he. Kɛ amɛkoto yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ Tso lɛ baafee shweshweeshwe. Shi kɛji amɛkpãtã Shikpɔŋ lɛ hu he miihia nu babaoo.

english: Why should I cut off some of the small suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? that grows around My main plantain stem removed

english: When too many suckers grow around one stem, they fight each other for nutrients, leading to small bunches. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, ensuring your main plant produces a heavy, full bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso kome he lɛ, amɛyeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ he akaŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii. Kɛ́ ojie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi, ni no baaha otso titri lɛ afee ŋmeii ni tsii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize turning yellow starting from the tip?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ eshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting at the tip mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which gives plants their green color and energy. Feeding the soil with organic compost or nitrogen fertilizer will help the leaves turn green again.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-abele lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni ji eŋɔli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping their flowers instead of forming cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee cacao ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from water stress, sudden dry weather, or a lack of small insects to pollinate them. Keeping shade trees nearby and preserving beneficial insects helps flowers turn into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ nu he haomɔ miipiŋ amɛ. hulutsoo be ni baa trukaa loo kooloi bibii ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni bɛ, ni haa hulutsoo baa yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ni etsaa kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when temperatures are extremely high or when the soil gets too dry. Regular watering during very hot months helps the flowers stay on and grow into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu daa yɛ nyɔji ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves with small dirt-like powder inside the center leaves?
ga: Why do my baby corn leaves have rough holes and tiny dirt-like particles? Eyɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides deep inside the leaf funnel and eats young leaves. Clearing weeds early and applying recommended control measures directly into the central funnel protects your maize.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai amli shɔŋŋ ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ mra Ni akɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ lɛ baatsu nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ gbɛ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ebu o-ŋmãa lɛ he.

english: Yellow leaves mean the crop is lacking nitrogen or cannot absorb it properly. This happens if the soil is too dry, too wet, or if fertilizer was applied incorrectly, which prevents the plants from using the expensive nutrients you bought.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli loo enyɛɛɛ ejie lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baa mli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ, edɔ tsɔ, loo kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekɛ niyenii ni jara wa ni ohé lɛ akatsu nii.

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce empty shells without any seeds inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni dumɔwui bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts need calcium in the soil to form nuts inside the shells. If the soil lacks calcium, the plant still grows the outer pod, but the seeds fail to develop, leading to empty yields despite your hard work.
ga: Calcium he miihia ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ koni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium Tso lɛ baaya nɔ eda yɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli. Shi dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ɛɛ. Enɛ haa nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ feɔ yaka kɛji otsu nii waa po.

english: Why are my tomatoes small and watery, making buyers at the market offer me very low prices?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ ji bibioo ni nu yɔɔ mli lɛ? Enɛ ha mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara lɛ nɔ lɛ bawo mi jara ni baa shi kwraa.

english: Tomatoes become small and watery when they do not receive enough potassium during fruit formation or when they get too much water and insufficient sunlight. Balancing nutrients helps produce firm, sweet tomatoes that buyers pay more for.
ga: Tomato bafeɔ bibioo ni nu yɔɔ mli kɛ́ enine shɛɛɛ potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ aduawai lɛ loo kɛ́ enine shɛɛɛ nu babaoo nɔ ni hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ eshɛɛɛ enɔ. Niyenii ni ja lɛ haa tomato ni mli edɔ ni ŋɔɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ jara wa fe tsutsu lɛ baa.

english: What causes my harvested cassava to become hard and woody instead of soft when boiled?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni efeɔ tso yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee blɛoo kɛji akɛ ahoo lɛ?

english: Cassava becomes woody when left in the ground past its ideal maturity date or when it suffers severe water stress during growth. Harvesting on time prevents tubers from losing eating quality.
ga: Cassava bafeɔ tso kɛji ashi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ mli kɛho be ni sa akɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ he. aloo kɛ́ ekɛ ehe wo nu mli haomɔ ni naa wa mli yɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ. Kɛ́ akpa yɛ be naa lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite niyenii ni amɛyeɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers before growing into actual peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shi dani etsɔɔ pepper diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Peppers drop their flowers when stressed by extreme heat, drought, or poor soil nutrients like boron. The plant drops flowers to save energy to keep itself alive instead of producing fruit.
ga: Peppers shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ, hɔmɔ, loo sũ mli niyenii ni ehiii, tamɔ boron lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi, moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily before the bunches are big enough to sell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya dani ŋmeii lɛ daraa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems. If underground pests like nematodes or root borers weaken the roots, or if the soil is too soft, the heavy weight of the growing bunch makes the whole tree fall during strong winds.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ nematodes loo shishifãi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ha shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔ Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ejɔ tsɔ Tso lɛ kuu ni miida lɛ tsiimɔ ni tsii lɛ baaha tso muu lɛ fɛɛ agbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: What makes my cassava roots rot underground before I get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛná hegbɛ ni amɛkpa?

english: Underground cassava rot is usually caused by waterlogged soil that smothers the roots, combined with soil fungal diseases. Planting on raised mounds or ridges improves water drainage and keeps roots healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa. kɛ ŋmeii helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fata he Dumɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa shishifãi ni wa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing small and twisted even though I cleared the land well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni efite eyɛ mli akɛ mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Yams grow small and twisted when planted in hard, compacted soil where the tuber cannot push downward freely, or when underground insects attack the growing tip of the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes bafeɔ bibii ni efiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ nɔ. ni yitso lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛre kɛya shi yɛ heyeli mli loo beni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tutuaa ŋmei lɛ naagbee ni miida lɛ.

english: How can I know if my land is good enough before I invest my savings into planting cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ dani mikɛ shika ni mikɛto lɛ awo kookoo ŋmɔ mli?

english: Good cocoa soil is deep, dark, drains excess water easily, and holds moisture well during dry periods. An extension officer can help test your soil depth and water drainage to make sure your investment does not fail.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli kwɔ, eyɛ ediŋŋ, ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli Extension nitsulɔi baanyɛ aye abua ni amɛka shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ kɛ nu ni hoɔ lɛ amɛkwɛ koni amɛkwɛ akɛ oshika ni okɛwo mli lɛ efiteee.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout after a heavy rain falls right after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ beni adu lɛ?

english: Heavy rain can wash away small seeds, bury them too deep under heavy mud, or fill all air spaces in the soil with water, suffocating the seed before it can sprout.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo dumɔwui bibii, ni efu amɛ tsɔ yɛ muji ni mli edɔ shishi. Aloo okɛ nu awo kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the cocoa with the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: How do I know which end of a cassava stem cutting should face up when I am planting it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmei tso lɛ naagbee ni esa akɛ ekwɛ ŋwɛi beni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Look closely at the small buds or 'eyes' where the old leaves grew along the stem; these buds must point upwards toward the sky. If you plant the cutting upside down, the shoots struggle to grow properly and your root yields will be very low.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ‘ŋmei’ ni baai ni edara lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu nine lɛ hiɛ shi lɛ Ewa akɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni shishifãi ni baa lɛ baafee bibioo kwraa.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to make food for the tubers growing under the ground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp soil to get sunlight and prevents leaf diseases, which allows the yam tubers to grow much larger.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ ni ekɛtsi baai helai anaa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient in the soil, or that the field has too much standing water drowning the roots. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure will help them turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo etsɔɔ akɛ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my tomato plant leaves curling up tightly during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in the heat of the day is a protective behavior where the plant reduces its surface area to save water. If the leaves uncurl in the evening when temperatures drop, the plant is usually fine, but persistent curling can mean drought stress or a plant virus.
ga: Baai ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa be mli lɛ ji hebuu subaŋ ko ni tsei tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛji baai lɛ shwieee shi gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi lɛ Tso lɛ hi. Shi ŋmɔlɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha hɔmɔ he haomɔ loo helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ aba tso lɛ mli.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer which causes the plant to produce leaves instead of fruit. Consistent watering and balanced fertilization help keep the flowers on the plant.
