ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting groundnuts or beans in my field before I plant maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani adu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that have special root nodules that take nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the soil. When the legume crop is harvested, that trapped nitrogen remains in the soil to feed the maize crop that follows.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Weeds act like thieves in your farm because their roots take up the water and fertilizer meant for your crops, while their leaves block sunlight. When weeds surround your plants, your crops starve and cannot grow to their full size.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii lɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa Beni jwɛi ebɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ Hɔmɔ baaye oŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛdara kɛyashɛ amɛhe.

english: What is eating holes in the middle leaves of my young maize plants and leaving small brown dirt behind?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ ni eshiɔ muji bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ sɛɛ?

english: This is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central funnel of the maize plant to feed on soft leaves. You can manage them by inspecting the plants early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or putting clean ash into the funnels.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ tso lɛ ni oookwɛ mli mra lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni ajieɔ yi lɛ atsu nii. Aloo okɛ sũ ni he tse awo tsɔne lɛ mli.

english: The very first rain is often followed by a heatwave or a long dry spell before the main rainy season truly starts. If your seeds sprout after the first rain, the young seedlings will dry up and die when the rains stop for a few weeks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ loo hɔmɔ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛji odumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Tsei bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii fioo komɛi pɛ.

english: How long does it usually take from the day I plant sweet potatoes until I can harvest them?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ kɛjɛɔ gbi ni miduɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni mikpaa lɛ?

english: Sweet potatoes are quick-maturing crops, typically taking about three to four months to fully mature after planting the vine cuttings.
ga: Atomɔ ji tsei ni daa oya. Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ aaafee nyɔji 3-4 dani eshɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How can I tell from looking at my sweet potato leaves that the roots underground are ready for harvesting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛjɛ tso ni ŋɔɔ baa lɛ mli akɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ eshɛ nikpamɔ?

english: When sweet potatoes reach full maturity around three months, the leaves naturally start turning yellow and drying up, and the soil near the stem may crack as the tubers expand.
ga: Beni sweet potatoes lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa yɛ aaafee nyɔji etɛ mli. Baai lɛ baaje shishi amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ baanyɛ atse be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why do sweet potatoes mature so much faster than other root crops like cassava or yam?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii daa oya fe shishifãi krokomɛi, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Sweet potatoes grow from leafy vine cuttings that rapidly root and capture sunlight, allowing them to feed the plant and swell underground tubers in just 3 to 4 months, compared to 8 to 12 months for cassava or yam.
ga: Atomɔ ni ŋɔɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ wain tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni shwereɔ oya ni amɛmɔɔ hulu la lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛyeɔ tsei lɛ niyenii ni amɛduɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 pɛ mli, ni nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 ji nɔ ni akɛtoɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ lɛ ahe.

english: How many times in a single year can I plant and harvest sweet potatoes on my farm?
ga: Sweet potatoes enyiɛ manyɛ madu ni makpa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ afi kome mli?

english: Because sweet potatoes mature in just three months, you can easily grow and harvest two to three crops a year if you have reliable rainfall or access to irrigation.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nyɔji etɛ pɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ. Obaanyɛ odu ni okpa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ yɛ afi mli yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ. Kɛji oyɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ loo hegbɛ ni okɛ nu shwieɔ shi

english: What is happening to my sweet potato plant underground during its first month in the soil?
ga: Mɛni baa mi sweet potato tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anɔ yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ ni amɛyɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli?

english: In the first month after planting, the vine cutting focuses its energy on developing a strong root system and forming initial tubers before shifting energy to above-ground vine growth.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni adu wain tsei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Pruning vines lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa shishifãi ni mli wa lɛ afeemɔ nɔ kɛ shishijee bulbs lɛ feemɔ nɔ dani ekɛ hewalɛ tsakeɔ kɛyaa wain tso lɛ shweremɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do sweet potato vines spread out and cover the ground so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei gbɛɔ eshwaa ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Sweet potato vines naturally creep along the ground to capture maximum sunlight, create a leaf cover that stops weeds from growing, and hold moisture in the soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ nyiɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Efeɔ nɔ ko ni akɛ baai haa nɔ koni jwɛi akakwɛ̃. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli

english: Does rain in the first month after planting affect how large my sweet potatoes will grow by the third month?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ saa bɔ ni ŋmeii ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ nyɔŋ ni ji etɛ lɛ mli lɛ da ha lɛ he?

english: Yes, consistent soil moisture during the first month helps the vine establish thick roots, which directly determines how many large tubers the plant can form by the time it matures.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa wain tso lɛ ni ewoɔ shishifãi ni mli wa. Enɛ tsɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ bɔ ni tso ko baanyɛ ajie ŋmeii wuji enyiɛ beni eshɛɔ shweremɔ he lɛ.

english: Why do my sweet potato plants grow better on raised soil ridges than on flat land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mounds and ridges loosen the soil, giving sweet potato tubers room to expand easily while protecting the roots from waterlogging during heavy rains.
ga: Gɔji kɛ ŋshɔkei lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ehaa sweet potato tubers lɛ mli lɛɛɔ mlɛo Agbɛnɛ hu ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Can I use stem cuttings from my current sweet potato harvest to plant my next field?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmeii ni afolɔ kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni akpaa amrɔ nɛɛ mli lɛ atsu nii kɛdu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, sweet potatoes are grown using vine cuttings taken from mature, healthy plants, making them easy and affordable to multiply for the next planting season.
ga: Hɛɛ, akɛ ŋmeii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni eda ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ ŋmeii. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaagbɛ ashwã yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: How much labor is needed to care for a sweet potato field during its growing period?
ga: Nitsulɔi enyiɛ he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ ŋmɔ ko ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni aduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Sweet potatoes require relatively little labor after planting; main tasks involve weeding during the first month until the vines spread and naturally shade out competing weeds.
ga: Sweet potatoes biɔ nitsumɔ fioo ko pɛ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Nitsumɔ titri ji ni ajie jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi wain tsei lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛha jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and delicate roots that burn easily under full sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or cassava grown alongside them to shield them from high heat and retain soil moisture until they are established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiisumɔ ni adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ amɛhe. Enɛ ji koni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi amɛbaatswa shi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen. The maize plant moves the remaining nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to nourish the new growth at the top, which signals that the crop needs compost or fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ aya hiɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Maize consumes a large amount of nitrogen from the ground, leaving the soil tired. Groundnuts and beans are legumes that capture nitrogen from the air and return it to the soil, naturally refreshing the land for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. haa shikpɔŋ lɛ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa he ni eyɔɔ lɛ he jɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why is it better to leave cleared weeds on top of the soil rather than burning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaashi jwɛi ni ajie lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ fe ni ashã lɛ?

english: Burning grass destroys beneficial soil life and burns away organic matter. Leaving cleared weeds on top of the soil creates a protective cover that keeps the ground cool, retains rainwater, and rots into free plant food.
ga: Jwɛi ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ wala ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ni eshãa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi ni he tse yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i, ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi, ni egboɔ ni etsɔɔ tsei aniyenii.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and collapse during the daytime even when the ground is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ amɛ moŋ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ?

english: This sudden wilting is often caused by bacterial wilt, a soil disease that enters through the roots and blocks the plant's internal water tubes. Excess moisture in poorly drained soil helps these bacteria spread rapidly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni eboteɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli ni etsĩɔ tsei lɛ amli nu paipii lɛ anaa. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: What is causing ragged holes in my young corn leaves and brown dust inside the leaf whorl?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli kɛ sũ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ baa lɛ mli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the center whorl of young maize to feed on tender leaves. Spotting this early allows you to control them with natural remedies like wood ash or recommended sprays.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Enɛ ni oooyɔse mra Ehaa okɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛi tamɔ tso mli sũ loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ kudɔɔ amɛ.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to produce energy that feeds the underground tuber. Lifting the vines off the ground on stakes prevents leaf diseases and ensures the tuber grows large and healthy.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni haa ŋmeii lɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ awó wein tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extremely hot weather, prolonged dry spells, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. The plant sheds flowers to save energy and keep itself alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛna haomɔi, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ. aloo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛfataa he Tso nɛɛ woɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he ni ekɛha ehe ahi wala mli.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are fully mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ edara kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves yellow and shed, and the main stem begins to swell near the ground. You can gently dig around the base of one test plant to inspect the tuber size before harvesting the field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ fee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni tso titri lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ blɛoo abɔle kaa tso kome shishi koni okwɛ bɔ ni bulb lɛ da ha dani okpa ŋmɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know if it is safe to sow my seeds right after the first rain of the season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Planting after only one rain is risky because the soil underneath may still be dry and hot, which can scorch germinating seeds. It is safest to wait for two or three steady rains so the moisture penetrates deep into the soil.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ ekolɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi ni edɔ lolo. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ashã. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: How do I know if cocoa can grow well on my land in the Bono region?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kookoo baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ Bono kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Cocoa grows best in areas with deep, well-drained soil, good rainfall, and warm temperatures. If you see neighboring farms in your area growing healthy crops, it is a strong sign that your soil and local weather are suitable too.
ga: Cocoa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Nugbɔ nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ ni hulutsoo be lɛ hu mli edɔɔ. Kɛji ona ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ni miidu ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ. No ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ hu sa.

english: How can I get free government cocoa seedlings to start my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔyeli lɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni aheee nɔ ko koni mikɛje ŋmɔ shishi?

english: The government, through agriculture programs like COCOBOD, distributes free seedlings through registered local nurseries during the planting season. You can contact your district extension officer to register your land and request your allocation.
ga: Nɔyeli lɛ jaa dumɔwui ni aheee nɔ ko kɛtsɔɔ okwaayeli gbɛjianɔtoi tamɔ COCOBOD nɔ kɛtsɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui akwɛmɔhei ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli. Obaanyɛ oya kpokpaa nɔkwɛlɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ koni ekɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ awo wolo nɔ ni obi ni aha bo shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why are seedlings grown in nursery bags before being planted on the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduɔ dumɔwui awoɔ dumɔwui kotokui amli dani aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Nurseries protect delicate young sprouted seeds from harsh sunlight, heavy rainfall, and pests, allowing them to build strong root systems so they can survive when moved to the main field.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛkwɛɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ buɔ dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe, ni ehaa amɛtoɔ shishifãi ni mli wa koni amɛhi shi kɛ́ ajie amɛ kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if a nursery seedling is strong enough to buy or plant on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mahe loo madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Look for seedlings with dark green leaves, a sturdy stem, no visible spots or insect damage, and a soil bag that holds intact, well-watered roots.
ga: Taomɔ dumɔwui ni baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ. strong trunk He ko bɛ ni anaa loo kooloi ni efite. Ni sũ kotoku ko yɛ ni ŋmɛɔ shishifãi lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ mli.

english: How many years will it take for a new cocoa seedling to produce its first crop?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo dumɔwu hee ko woɔ eklɛŋklɛŋ yibii?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually start producing pods within 2 to 3 years after transplanting, provided they receive proper shade, water, and care.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu amɛ. Esa akɛ amɛna hɔnɔ, nu, kɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa.

english: What is the best month or season for me to transplant seedlings to my field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji nyɔŋ loo be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: It is best to plant at the beginning of the major rainy season, usually around May or June, so the roots get steady rainfall to establish themselves before any dry weather begins.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa lɛ shishijee mli. Bei pii lɛ, aaafee May loo June. Enɛ ji koni shishifãi lɛ aná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛto amɛhe shi dani hulutsoo be lɛ aje shishi.

english: Why do young cocoa trees wither and die if planted in direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji akwɛ amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have soft, tender leaves that lose water very quickly under hot sun. Direct sunlight burns the leaves and dries out the roots before the plant can mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya waa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbi dani tso lɛ adara.

english: Why do farmers plant plantain trees on the same farm with new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ?

english: Plantains grow quickly with big leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa trees the shade they need while also providing food and extra income while the cocoa grows.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛnáa hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛhaa niyenii kɛ shika kroko yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Should I clear away all big forest trees before planting cocoa on my land?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie tsei wuji ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ dani madu kookoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, you should keep some tall trees because cocoa plants naturally prefer dappled shade and humid conditions, which older forest trees provide while protecting the soil from burning.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ okɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ ahi shi ejaakɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, kookoo tsei sumɔɔ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Tsei ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ hu baaye abua ni sũ lɛ akashã.

english: How often should I water my newly transplanted cocoa seedlings if it stops raining for a few days?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo mi-cocoa dumɔwui ni midu ehee lɛ nu kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛmɔ gbii fioo komɛi?

english: During brief dry spells in the growing season, watering young seedlings every 2 to 3 days around the root base keeps the soil moist until the rains resume.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be kuku ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ mli lɛ, kɛ́ afɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ anɔ nu daa gbii 2 kɛyashi 3 yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why does plantain become so expensive and hard to find during certain months of the year in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains jara wa waa ni ewa akɛ aaana yɛ afi lɛ mli nyɔji komɛi amli yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Plantains rely heavily on rainfall to produce big bunches. During the dry season (harmattan), the lack of water slows down plantain growth and reduces fruit production, which leads to lower market supply and higher prices until the rains return.
ga: Plantains kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nugbɔshiimɔ nɔ waa koni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji. Yɛ hulutsoo be mli (harmattan) lɛ, nu ni bɛ lɛ haa plantains lɛ daalɛ baa shi, ni ehaa aduawai ni anáa lɛ hu baa shi. Enɛ haa jarayeli nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ baa shi, ni jara hu yaa hiɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do experienced farmers always advise me to plant plantains next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa be fɛɛ be akɛ madu plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive and easily burn under direct hot sunlight. Plantain plants grow very fast with broad leaves, acting as living umbrellas that provide essential shade and soil moisture for cocoa during its early years.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ tso ni haa hulutsoo, ni ehaa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa kɛha kookoo yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize crops curl up tightly into tubes during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a survival trick crops use to save water. When the sun gets too hot, the plant rolls its leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to heat, preventing moisture from escaping.
ga: Baai ni atsiɔ lɛ ji wala yiwalaheremɔ ŋaa ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛha he ni hulutsoo lɛ baa amɛnɔ lɛ aba shi. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaje mli.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping all their flowers without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni ewooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Vegetable crops drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress, extreme dry soil, or lack essential nutrients. When the plant feels stressed, it sheds flowers to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Aduawai shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo, shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa, loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli lɛ Ebaajie fɔfɔii koni ekɛto hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient for leaf growth. When nitrogen is lacking, the plant pulls whatever is left from older bottom leaves to keep the new top growth alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Beni nitrogen faaa Tsei lɛ jieɔ nɔ ni eshwɛ yɛ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli lɛ koni amɛha dalɛ hee ahi ŋwɛi.

english: Why does my farm produce smaller harvests each year even though I use the same seeds on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season without giving the earth time to replenish. Practicing crop rotation or resting the land restores missing soil nutrients.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛwo mli ekoŋŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha ejɔɔ ehe lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii ni elaaje yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why should I cut down the small plantain shoots growing around the main stem instead of letting all of them grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ plantain yitsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he, moŋ fe ni eeeŋmɛ gbɛ ni ekwɛ̃ kwraa

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water, light, and nutrients away from the main plant. Pruning excess suckers ensures the main plant gets maximum energy to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛwo tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are small green caterpillars chewing holes inside the central funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye bu yɛ mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Those caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that prefers hiding in the moist center of young maize stems. They eat the tender leaves before they unfold, which can destroy the crop if not treated early with proper pest controls.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmeii lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni sumɔɔ ni ekɛ ehe awo ŋmeii bibii ni mli edɔ lɛ ateŋ. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii dani amɛgbeleɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii mra. Kɛtsɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ ni sa nɔ

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak and stunted even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egbɔjɔ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and are stronger than cultivated crops, so they aggressively steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your crops, effectively starving them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ amɛkɛ ekãa juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ ɔ he ɔ, hwɔ maa ye mɛ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are big enough to harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ efolɔɔɔ mli?

english: You can tell cassava is mature when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to swell and crack open from the growing tubers underneath.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ yucca ko eda kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ ni efoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ eshishi lɛ he.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to intense heat and direct sun. Keeping shade trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects the young plants from sun damage and preserves moisture in the soil until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be mli lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my maize seeds once the rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: It is best to wait until the rainfall is steady for about two weeks rather than planting right after the very first shower. Planting after a single rain can cause seeds to dry out in the soil if a dry spell immediately follows.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ anɛ aaafee otsii enyɔ. Mohu ɔ, mo du mɛ ngɛ kekleekle nu ɔ se amlɔ nɔuu. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ nyiɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. You can manage this by planting disease-resistant cassava stems and removing affected plants from the farm early.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwiemɔ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu kɛ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooojie kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do experienced farmers tell me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ baakɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu tsina loo ŋmãa?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts belong to the legume family, which pulls nitrogen from the air and releases it into the soil. Maize consumes a lot of soil nutrients, so planting them together naturally fertilizes the soil and improves your overall harvest.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Abɛi kɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ni ooofee ekome kɛdu lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ebaaha okpamɔ fɛɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing plenty of flowers, but the flowers just fall off without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off without forming fruit when temperatures become too high, water supply is inconsistent, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer. Providing consistent water and balanced fertilizer helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ eyaaa nɔ daa. aloo be mli ni nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Will burning the bushes and weeds on my plot before planting hurt my soil?
ga: Ani tsei bibii kɛ jwɛi ni ashãa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani aduɔ lɛ baaye shikpɔŋ lɛ awui?

english: Burning clears the field quickly, but it destroys essential organic matter and friendly organisms in the topsoil over time. Leaving weeds to decompose or using them as mulch feeds the soil and helps retain soil water.
ga: Shãa lɛ jieɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ oya. Shi efiteɔ nibii ni he hiaa ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ naanyobɔɔ nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli. Shi jwɛi lɛ ni egbo loo okɛtsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Can I save seeds from my high-yielding hybrid maize harvest and plant them again next year?
ga: Ani manyɛ mahere dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ mli ni madu ekoŋŋ yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Seeds harvested from hybrid crops lose their special qualities in the next generation. Planting saved hybrid seed usually results in uneven crop growth, weaker resistance to pests, and much lower harvests compared to buying new certified seed.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛsui krɛdɛɛi lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ ni aduɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ adalɛ ejaaa. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahewalɛ ni baa shi Ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kwraa kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahemɔ he.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot while they are still growing on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Black pod rot is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, dark, and overcast conditions. Pruning extra canopy branches lets sunshine and airflow into the farm, which reduces moisture and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black rot ni yɔɔ pods mli lɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni duŋ ewo, ni atatu yɔɔ lɛ. Kpojiemɔ niji krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Planting too close forces crops to compete with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. This produces tall, thin plants with very small ears of corn, whereas proper spacing yields healthier plants with bigger, heavier ears.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ nɛɛ baaha tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ŋmãa toi bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ aba. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ he ni sa to he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ kɛ toi ni da ni tsii.

english: Why does my maize yield get smaller every year when I keep planting it in the exact same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mifeɔ lɛ miiba shi daa afi lɛ? Ani adu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Planting the same crop year after year drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the field. Rotating maize with legumes or tubers breaks disease cycles and restores soil balance.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsakeɔ lɛ fiteɔ hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ ni ehaa sũ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow and dying when I plant them in a clear, open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse, ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to harsh sunlight and need shade to survive. Planting shade crops like plantain or shade trees alongside cocoa protects the young plants from heat scorch and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa ni amɛtaoɔ hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What happens to my cocoa trees if I leave tall weeds to grow around them on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cocoa tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi jwɛi kakadaji yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ he?

english: Tall weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your cocoa trees, causing low yields. Overgrown weeds also trap humidity and create a home for pests and fungal diseases like Black Pod.
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɔlɔ lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei lɛ amli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yibiiwoo ni baa shi Jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ hu mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji lɛ feɔ shia.

english: Why should I cut off some of the branches from my cocoa tree when it looks healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-kookoo niji lɛ ekomɛi? Akɛ kookoo tso lɛ mli wa lolo?

english: Pruning removes dead or unnecessary branches so air can flow freely through the tree and sunlight can reach the main branches. This encourages the tree to direct its energy into producing bigger, healthier cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ tso lɛ mli oya. ni hulu la baanyɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ aniji wuji lɛ ahe Enɛ woɔ tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛfee kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, overly shady conditions. Removing infected pods immediately and clearing lower branches helps keep the air dry and stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ tsɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya ni agbala tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ agbi ni ekpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: What causes tiny insects to gather on my cocoa flowers and make the pods grow twisted?
ga: Mɛni haa kooloi bibii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ ni amɛfiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: These insects are pests like capsids (akate) that suck sap from young shoots and pods. They destroy the flowers before pods can grow, which severely reduces the amount of crop you can harvest.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids (akates) ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii amli lɛ. Amɛfiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ baa. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni obaanyɛ okpa lɛ aba shi waa.

english: How do I know the exact right time to pick a cocoa pod off the tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Cocoa pods are ready for harvest when their color changes completely—green pods turn bright yellow, and red pods turn orange-yellow. Picking them too early leads to underdeveloped beans, while leaving them too long causes beans to germinate inside.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni amɛhe su etsake kwraa lɛ. Pods eŋɔli lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Ni ŋmeii tsuru lɛ baatsake ni etsɔ ŋmeii-ŋmei. Kɛ́ ajie mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃. Yɛ be mli ni ashiɔ lɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ mli.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to ferment wet cocoa beans under plantain leaves before sun-drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkɛ cocoa ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ awo plantain baai ashishi dani wɔgbi amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Fermentation heats up the beans to kill the embryo inside and develops the sweet chocolate flavor and deep brown color. Drying raw beans without fermenting them leaves them bitter, purple, and low in market value.
ga: Fɛ̃i haa ŋmeii lɛ mli dɔɔ koni egbe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. ni afee lɛ koni ehiɛ tsokolate ni ŋɔɔ kɛ su ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ Beans ni agbi ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ, amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ni amɛhe jara waaa yɛ jara nɔ.

english: How can I tell if the soil on my farm has run out of nutrients for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa miduɔ nii?

english: When soil loses its fertility, crop leaves may look pale or yellowish, growth slows down, and fruit production drops significantly. Adding organic compost or appropriate cocoa fertilizers returns nutrients to the soil.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Tso lɛ baai lɛ baanyɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. shweremɔ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo kɛ nibii ni afeɔ lɛ eba shi waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my neighbor's small cocoa farm produce more bags than my very large farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii Mikutsoŋnyo ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ baagi babaoo fe miŋmɔ agbo lɛ.

english: Yield depends more on proper care than farm size. A smaller, well-pruned, weeded, and fertilized farm yields more high-quality pods than a large farm that is neglected or left untended.
ga: Nibii ni anáa kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ damɔ kwɛmɔ ni sa nɔ fe ŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ. Okwaafoi bibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ ajie jwɛi ni awo mli lɛ, ebaawo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmɔji wuji ni akuɔ hiɛ ashwieɔ nɔ loo ashiɔ amɛ ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How does the system work when I am ready to sell my dried cocoa beans to the government?
ga: Kɛji akɛ afee klalo akɛ abaahɔ̃ɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni egbi aha nɔyeli lɛ, te gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ tsuɔ nii ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: In Ghana, cocoa is sold through Licensed Buying Companies (LBCs) at local buying centers. The government, through Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD), sets a standard price per bag to ensure farmers receive a fair price for well-dried beans.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, ahɔ̃ɔ kookoo kɛtsɔɔ nitsumɔhei ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni amɛheɔ nii lɛ anɔ (LBCs) yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayeli hei lɛ. Nɔyeli lɛ toɔ jara ni sa kɛha kotoku kome kɛtsɔɔ Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD) lɛ nɔ koni okwaafoi lɛ aná jara ni sa kɛha amɛ ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot when there is too much water standing on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess water covers the field for too long without draining, it suffocates the roots, allowing harmful fungi and bacteria to attack and rot them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ni fa fe nine ha ŋmɔ ko nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa ni amɛgboɔ.

english: How does removing pooled water from my field help my crops survive after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni ebua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ni mijieɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Draining pooled water allows fresh air to return to the soil particles. This stops crop roots from drowning and prevents leaf yellowing and fungal diseases.
ga: Nu ni abua naa lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ mli nibii bibii lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, ni ehaa ebaa ni ji ŋmɔŋ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ hu naa.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize curling up and turning yellow when the rain stops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ?

english: Maize plants curl their leaves to trap moisture and prevent water loss through heat. When the soil becomes dry, the roots cannot collect nutrients, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛtsi nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ mli lɛ naa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ato niyenii mli hewalɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their flowers when the ground is dry for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When a tomato plant lacks water, it drops its blossoms to conserve energy and survive, sacrificing potential fruit growth to keep the main plant alive.
ga: Beni nu bɛ tomato tsei lɛ Ewoɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he ni ehi shi. Esa akɛ akɛ nyɛmɔ ni ayɔɔ akɛ aduawai akwɛ̃ lɛ ashã afɔle bɔni afee ni akwɛ tomato tsei lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my vegetables are not getting enough water from the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-vegetables lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Vegetables show water stress when their leaves wilt during the cooler morning hours, turn dull or crisp around the edges, or when their overall growth slows down significantly.
ga: Aduawai tsɔɔ nu mli haomɔ kɛji baai lɛ shwie shi yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be mli. Baai lɛ anaa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. aloo be mli ni dalɛ fɛɛ baa shi kwraa lɛ

english: How will using a machine pump to bring river water to my crops change my yield during the dry season?
ga: Te pɔmp ni mikɛbaatsu nii kɛmiikɛ faa mli nu baa miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baatsake miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Pumping water onto your farm provides your crops with a steady supply of moisture during dry months, allowing them to flower and produce healthy fruits continuously even without rainfall.
ga: Nu ni okɛwoɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tsei yaa nɔ amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ po.

english: Is it better for my crop roots if I give them a little water every day or plenty of water once a week?
ga: Ani ebaahi aha mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu fioo ha lɛ daa gbi loo nu babaoo ha lɛ shikome yɛ otsi mli?

english: Soaking the ground deeply less frequently encourages crop roots to grow deep into the soil where it stays moist, making the plants stronger against hot sun.
ga: shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu ni mli kwɔ Bei pii lɛ, enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ehaa tsei lɛ waa kɛji hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ.

english: Can I still grow vegetables if I only have a tiny stream of water near my land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu aduawai lolo kɛji miyɛ faa bibioo ko? Ebɛŋkɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yes, even small amounts of water can support crops if you direct the water straight to the plant roots using simple pipes or small pumps, preventing waste.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu fioo po baanyɛ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛji akɛ okɛ nu tee tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔ hose loo pɔmp bibioo ko nɔ lɛ, koni akafite.

english: How can I test my farm soil to know if it has enough moisture for my seeds to sprout?
ga: Maka shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ makwɛ kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ mli ni dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Squeeze a handful of soil from a few inches below the surface; if it forms a soft ball that stays together without dripping water, there is enough moisture for seeds to germinate.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ fioo ko kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi inchi fioo komɛi. Kɛji eji ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kokroo ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni akɛkpɛtɛ he ni nu shwieee shi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do crops grow faster in land that stays damp compared to land that dries out completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii daa oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ ni egbi kwraa lɛ he lɛ?

english: Roots can only absorb plant food when it is dissolved in soil water. Continuous moisture allows crops to feed and grow without interruption.
ga: Shishifãi baanyɛ aŋɔ tsei aniyenii kɛji akɛ etsɔ nu mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli pɛ. Fɛ̃i ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ yeɔ nii ni amɛdaraa ni nɔ ko nɔ ko tsiii amɛ gbɛ.

english: Why do my chickens get more strength and energy from eating corn compared to cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikooloi lɛ naa hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa ni amɛyeɔ lɛ mli fe ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Corn contains a high concentration of easily digestible carbohydrates and natural oils that provide fast energy for poultry, whereas cassava is mostly starch with lower energy density and key nutrients missing.
ga: Carbohydrates ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ oya kɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔ ni fa babaoo ni haa kooloi hewalɛ oya lɛ yɛ ŋmãa mli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei ji nɔ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ starch lɛ, eyɛ hewalɛ ni fa fioo ni niyenii mli nibii titrii bɛ mli.

english: Can I completely replace maize with cassava when making feed for my farm animals?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ato ŋmãa najiaŋ kɛ́ mikɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha niyenii?

english: No, cassava cannot completely replace maize because it lacks necessary nutrients and energy concentration, and raw cassava contains substances that can slow down an animal's growth if not heavily supplemented.
ga: Dabi, ŋmãa nyɛŋ aye ŋmãa najiaŋ kwraa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ebɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli. Ni nibii ni baanyɛ aha kooloi lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo kɛji akɛ akɛ niyenii babaoo fataaa he lɛ yɛ ŋmei ni ahoko lɛ mli.

english: Why is cassava not as effective as corn for giving farm animals quick strength?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi ahewalɛwoo mli oya lɛ?

english: Cassava contains a lot of water and fiber, meaning an animal has to consume a massive quantity to get the same amount of energy that a small portion of compact corn seeds provides.
ga: Nu kɛ fiber babaoo yɛ cassava mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ kooloo lɛ aye babaoo dani enyɛ ená hewalɛ ni ŋmei bibioo ko baaha lɛ nɔŋŋ.

english: Which crop is best to plant if my main goal is to produce high-energy feed for my animals?
ga: Mɛni ji tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ makwɛ kɛji akɛ oti titri ni ma mihiɛ ji ni mafee niyenii ni haa hewalɛ babaoo maha mikooloi lɛ?

english: Maize is the best crop to grow for feed energy because its grains pack a concentrated blend of carbohydrates and oils directly into the harvest, making it the standard energy crop for livestock.
ga: Abɛi ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ ni abaanyɛ adu kɛha niyenii hewalɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, akɛ carbohydrates kɛ fɔ ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ woɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa ŋmaa lɛ mli. ni eha efee hewalɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛhaa kooloi

english: What makes grain crops like maize store energy differently from root crops like cassava?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ni akɛtoɔ hewalɛ lɛ feɔ srɔto yɛ shishifãi ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa he?

english: Grain crops store concentrated, low-moisture energy in their seeds to nourish a new plant quickly, while root crops store energy underground mixed with a lot of water and heavy starch.
ga: Ŋmaa tsei toɔ hewalɛ ni mli ewo muji, ni mli edɔ fioo yɛ amɛdumɔwui lɛ amli koni amɛha tsei heei niyenii oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shishifãi ni aduɔ lɛ toɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi, ni amɛkɛ nu babaoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsii futuɔ mli.

english: Why do extension officers usually recommend corn over tuber crops for animal feed mix?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa he ŋaa akɛ akɛ ŋmãa awo kooloi aniyenii najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Corn grains dry easily, store longer without rotting, and mix evenly into feed while delivering consistent energy, whereas wet tubers like cassava spoil quickly and lack balanced nutrients.
ga: Abele ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Abaanyɛ akɛto be kakadaŋŋ ni efiteee. ni akɛfutuɔ kooloi aniyenii amli pɛpɛɛpɛ koni eha hewalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii ni efɔ tamɔ ŋmei fiteɔ oya ni amɛbɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni sa.

english: Is cassava suitable as a main energy crop for poultry like chickens?
ga: Ani ŋmei hi akɛ hewalɛ ŋmɔshi nibii titri kɛha kooloi tamɔ kooloi?

english: Cassava is not ideal as a primary energy crop for chickens because poultry digestive systems struggle to process heavy cassava starch efficiently compared to simple grain starches found in corn.
ga: Cassava esaaa akɛ hewalɛ ŋmɔshi nibii titri kɛha kooloi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ewaa kɛha kooloi aniyenii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ koni amɛtsu ŋmei ni tsii lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛto ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni anaa yɛ ŋmãa mli lɛ he.

english: Why does maize require so much sunlight to produce strong, energy-rich seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hulu la babaoo he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni haa hewalɛ babaoo aba lɛ?

english: Maize uses intense sunlight during photosynthesis to produce the sugars and starches that get packed tightly into the cobs, giving the final grain its high energy content.
ga: Abɛi kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa tsuɔ nii yɛ fotosintɛsis be mli ni ekɛfeɔ sugars kɛ starch ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa naagbee dumɔwu lɛ náa hewalɛ babaoo.

english: How can I tell if my harvested corn has good energy quality for feeding livestock?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ yɛ hewalɛ kpakpa kɛha kooloi ayeli?

english: Well-matured, fully dried, and bright yellow corn kernels indicate that the crop successfully transferred maximum starch and energy from the plant into the grain.
ga: Abele ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ, ni egbi kwraa, ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eye omanye ni ekɛ ŋmeii kɛ hewalɛ ni fa fe fɛɛ ejɛ tso lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmaa lɛ mli.

english: Why do alternative crops fail to give animals the same strength as maize even when animals eat a lot of them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi haaa kooloi hewalɛ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ kooloi babaoo yeɔ tsei nɛɛ moŋ, shi.

english: Even if animals eat large quantities of other crops, those crops often lack the concentrated fats and digestible starches unique to maize that the animal's body needs to generate real strength.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ kooloi yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi babaoo moŋ, shi bei pii lɛ, nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ fɔ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe. Enɛ ji ŋmãa su ni he hiaa kooloo lɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ koni ená hewalɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen or the soil is waterlogged. When heavy rain washes nutrients away or floods the root zone, the plant moves nitrogen to newer top leaves, causing the older bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ loo eha shishifã lɛ he lɛ, Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience severe heat or soil dryness. When the plant feels under stress, it sheds its blossoms to save energy and water so it can survive.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli lɛ Ebaawo fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he bɔni afee ni ehi shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa tree leaves dry up and burn when I clear all the big shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kooko tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa beni mijie tsei wuji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle strong direct sunlight because their leaves burn easily and dry out quickly. Shade trees act like umbrellas, shielding young cocoa plants from scorching heat until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ, ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Shade tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he kɛyashi tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants droop and wilt in the afternoon sun even if I watered them early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miigboi ni amɛmiigboi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: In intense midday heat, tomato leaves lose water through evaporation faster than the roots can suck up fresh water from the soil. The leaves wilt temporarily to cut down on water loss and usually perk up once the sun cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tomato baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu kpakpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ baagbee shi be kukuoo ko koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. ni amɛfɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji hulu lɛ mli jɔ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and covered in tiny white flies?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ ehà amɛhe lɛ?

english: The tiny white insects are whiteflies carrying cassava mosaic disease. They feed on leaf sap and spread a virus that twists the leaves, making it hard for the plant to produce energy and grow tubers.
ga: Kpluka bibioo ni ji ŋmei yɛŋ lɛ ji ŋmei yɛŋ ni kɛ cassava mosaic hela lɛ baa lɛ. Amɛyeɔ baa mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ baa mli hela ko ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ amɛshwãa. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei akɛ amɛbaafee hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii.

english: Why does my cassava plant grow very tall with bushy green leaves but yield very small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ miiya hiɛ waa nɛkɛ? Eyɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil encourages the plant to use its energy building tall stems and green leaves above ground rather than storing food and swelling root tubers underground.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛwo tsei lɛ ashishifãi kakadaji kɛ baai eŋɔlii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye ní kɛ toɔ, nɛ a haa nɛ shishifã ɔmɛ fuɔ ngɛ zugba a sisi.

english: Why do experienced farmers advise planting cowpeas or groundnuts alongside maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ tsina ŋmei loo ŋmei afata ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots, naturally fertilizing the neighboring maize crop without chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Okɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ awo ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsuuu nii.

english: Will removing the extra shoots around my main plantain stem help it produce a bigger bunch?
ga: Ani mi-plantain tsei titrii lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua mi ni maná tsei niji wuji?

english: Yes, removing excess suckers reduces competition for food, water, and sunlight. Pruning leaves only the primary stem allows all soil nutrients to flow directly into growing a larger fruit bunch.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ haa akaŋshii ni kɔɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la he lɛ baa shi. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ yitso lɛ pɛ he baai lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii lɛ fɛɛ hoɔ kɛyaa tsei wuji ni woɔ yibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize immediately after the very first rainy day of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ aduɔ ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry stretch that dries up the topsoil, causing freshly sprouted seeds to wither and die before steady rains arrive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni haa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ gĩɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly after I clear my farmland using a machete?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya nɛkɛ beni mikɛ machete shwieɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Clearing with a machete only cuts off weed leaves at ground level, leaving live roots and dormant seeds in the soil that rapidly sprout new shoots as soon as sunlight hits the open soil.
ga: Kɛ akɛ machete tsu nii lɛ, efoɔ jwɛi lɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ pɛ. Eshiɔ shishifãi ni hiɛ ka kɛ dumɔwui ni egboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni baakwɛ̃ oya kɛji hulu la shɛ shikpɔŋ ni agbele nɔ lɛ nɔ pɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I cut down all the big trees on my farm before planting cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mifoɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ dani miduɔ kookoo lɛ?

english: Big trees provide crucial shade for young cocoa plants, protecting them from intense sunlight, keeping the soil cool, and preventing moisture loss during dry periods.
ga: Tsei wuji lɛ haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa waa. Ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaaa ŋmɔtɔ akaje mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: How does intense sunlight affect young cocoa trees if there are no shade trees around?
ga: Te hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baaná kookoo tsei bibii anɔ hewalɛ aha tɛŋŋ kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ amɛhe?

english: Direct hot sunlight scorches young cocoa leaves, dries out the topsoil quickly, and can easily stunt or kill young cocoa plants before they mature.
ga: Hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ baashã kookoo baai lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. ni ebaanyɛ eha kookoo tsei afee blɛoo oya dani amɛdara.

english: Will cutting down shade trees make my mature cocoa trees produce more pods?
ga: Ani tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni mifoɔ lɛ baaha mi-kookoo tso ni eda lɛ awo ŋmeii babaoo?

english: While direct sunlight can temporarily boost pod yield in mature cocoa, it stresses the trees, shortens their lifespan, and increases the need for expensive fertilizers.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa kookoo ŋmeii ni eda lɛ ayibii yaa hiɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli moŋ, shi ekɛ haomɔ baa tso lɛ nɔ. Ha wala be lɛ aba shi ni aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa ni ataoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ

english: How can I tell if my cocoa farm has too much shade from big trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli tsei wuji lɛ yɛ hulutsoo babaoo tsɔ?

english: If your cocoa trees grow very tall and thin with dark green leaves but produce few flowers and pods, the tree canopy above is blocking too much light.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cacao tso lɛ da waa ni efee mlɛo ni baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ shi fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ yiteŋ miitsi la babaoo naa.

english: Why do some shade trees help cocoa while other trees harm it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi yeɔ lɛ awui lɛ?

english: Good shade trees drop nutrient-rich leaves and deep roots, while harmful trees compete with cocoa for water or attract destructive pests and diseases.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ shiɔ baa ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛ kookoo yeɔ nu he akaŋ loo amɛgbalaa kooloi kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛbaa amɛŋɔɔ.

english: Should I use a mechanical planting machine or continue planting my crops by hand?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsɔne ni akɛduɔ nii atsu nii loo maya nɔ mikɛ minine adu tsei?

english: Planting machines save time and plant seeds at uniform depths on flat, cleared land, but manual planting is better for bumpy land with tree roots and stumps.
ga: Mɔ ni duɔ nii lɛ kɛ be tsuuu nii ni eduɔ dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ tamɔ nɔ kome yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli tse nɔ. Shi dumɔwui ni aduɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tsei shishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Is a mechanical planter suitable for a newly cleared forest farm with remaining trees?
ga: Ani tsɔnei ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ sa kɛha koo mli ŋmɔji ni ajie amɛ etsɛko ni tsei eshwɛ yɛ mli lɛ?

english: Mechanical planters work best on flat, cleared land; farms with standing shade trees, underground roots, and rocks can easily damage the machine.
ga: Mɛkanika nibii ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli tse nɔ. Okwaafoi ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ, shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi, kɛ tɛi yɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ afite tsɔnei oya.

english: How do shade trees keep the soil moist during the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli?

english: Shade trees block direct sun and hot winds from reaching the ground, while their fallen leaves create a natural mulch layer that traps moisture in the soil.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, baai ni egbee shi lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: What happens to the soil on my farm if I remove all the large trees?
ga: Mɛni baaba shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ kɛji mijie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Removing all large trees exposes the bare soil to heavy rains that wash away fertile topsoil, leaving the land dry, hard, and poor for future crop growth.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ anɛ waa. ni hoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ lɛ Shiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni egbi, ni ewa ni ehiii kɛha tsei adalɛ wɔsɛɛ.

english: Can I plant temporary food crops like plantains to protect my cocoa trees from the sun?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii ni akɛyeɔ nii yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains koni mikɛbu kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he?

english: Yes, fast-growing plantains provide living umbrella shade for young cocoa trees while also giving you food and income while waiting for the cocoa to produce.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains ni shwereɔ oya lɛ haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni afee kookoo lɛ.

english: How can I tell if the water source near my land is clean enough for irrigation?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu jɛɛhe ni bɛŋkɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he tse bɔ ni sa kɛha nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Water that clears up and has no foul odor or oily chemical film is generally a good sign. Clean water allows crop roots to absorb nutrients easily without getting clogged by debris or damaged by harmful chemicals.
ga: Nu ni mli tse ni ebɛ ŋmɔlɔ loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ji okadi kpakpa. Nu ni mli tse yeɔ ebuaa tsei ashishifãi lɛ ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya ni sũ ni efiteɔ amɛ loo tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui efiteee amɛ.

english: Why do my crops look wilted even when the ground around them feels wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli egbi moŋ lɛ? Ani ebaanu he akɛ efɔ?

english: When soil stays completely flooded with standing water, the roots cannot breathe and end up suffocating. Too much trapped surface water actually prevents roots from taking up nutrients, making the plant look dry and weak.
ga: Kɛji nu ni ekã shi lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, amɛbaagbɔjɔ. Nu ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni emɔ mli tsɔ lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii kpakpai. Ehaa tso lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbi ni ebɛ hewalɛ.

english: What causes my maize plants to grow bright green and strong while my neighbor's look yellow?
ga: Mɛni haa mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe wa yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋbii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ?

english: Bright green leaves mean your crop is getting enough nitrogen from the soil. Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is hungry for nutrients or water isn't draining properly around the roots.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni kpɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛmiijɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii he miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ loo nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know if my young crops are developing healthy root systems underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midumɔwui lɛ miifee shishifãi ni mli wa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: If the stem above ground is thick, upright, and growing steady green leaves during the early weeks, it means the roots below are expanding well and finding food in the soil.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ yiteŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli tse, edamɔ shi shiŋŋ ni eyɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishigbɛ shishifãi lɛ miigbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ ni amɛmiitao niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close together to get more crops on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close forces them to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to feed and produce larger, healthier yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What should I plant on the rest of my land that is currently sitting empty?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ ni eshwɛ ni nɔ ko bɛ nɔ amrɔ nɛɛ nɔ?

english: You can plant legumes like beans or groundnuts on empty patches. They help feed the soil with nitrogen, which will nourish heavy-feeding crops like corn when you plant them in the next season.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha niyenii tsei ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ aná hewalɛ beni oduɔ amɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Is it safe to plant different types of crops together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaakwɛ tsei babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, mixing crops like maize and cassava or cowpeas can be beneficial. Different crops feed at different soil depths and protect each other from pests, helping you make the best use of your land.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ hu baanyɛ aye abua. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi yeɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hei srɔtoi ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni oná he sɛɛ babaoo.

english: What is the best way to start planting on land that I have just cleared for the first time?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ mije dumɔ shishi yɛ mishikpɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ ni ajie lɛ nɔ?

english: Start by testing or observing a small portion of the land first with a fast-growing crop like maize. This helps you understand how well the soil holds water and nutrients before investing in the whole field.
ga: Je shishi kɛtsɔ he bibioo ko ni oooka loo okwɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa. Enɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni onuɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ shishi dani okɛ shika woɔ jɛmɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do crops grow better on one side of my field than on the other side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome fe fã kroko lɛ?

english: Soil quality and water movement are rarely the same across a field. Low areas usually retain more water and nutrients washed down from higher ground, making crops grow faster there.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su kɛ nu lɛ nyiɛmɔ lɛ efɔɔɔ kaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, hei ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ hiɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni jɛɔ hei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ amli kɛbaa shi lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ nakai kpokpaa lɛ nɔ.

english: How long after planting should I expect to see my corn plants start standing tall?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ baaje shishi amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ?

english: With good rainfall and rich soil, maize sprouts within 4 to 7 days and starts growing tall and thick within 3 to 4 weeks as its root system settles.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii. Abɛi baakwɛ̃ yɛ gbii 4 kɛyashi 7 mli ni ebɔi shweremɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli be mli ni shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when exposed to full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very tender leaves and shallow roots that cannot tolerate direct, intense sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or bananas nearby to act as living umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and moist until the cocoa roots grow deeper.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ waa kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains loo banana ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi kookoo shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow starting from the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves at the base of maize plants usually show that the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the main food plant leaves need to stay dark green and make energy to grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei ahe baai koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli ni mli edɔ lɛ mli ni amɛfee hewalɛ kɛha dalɛ ni mli wa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning purple and pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ purple kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Purple leaves on cassava are often a sign that the plant cannot get enough phosphorus from the soil. Phosphorus helps the plant build strong roots and transfer energy throughout its stem and leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ yucca nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ enine shɛɛɛ fɔsfɔs ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Fosforo yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtswaa shishifãi ni wa ni ekɛ hewalɛ tsɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and skinny with very small yields when planted close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded too close together, they fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They stretch upward quickly to catch the light, using up energy on tall stems instead of building big fruits or seeds.
ga: Kɛ tsei eyi amɛhe obɔ kɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpã amɛhe oya koni amɛmɔ kane lɛ. Ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo aduawai loo dumɔwui wuji.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they face heat stress, dry winds like the Harmattan, or irregular watering. The plant sheds the flowers to protect itself from losing too much moisture.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo be mli, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi tamɔ harmattan, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ he.

english: Why are the bottoms of my developing tomatoes turning black and rotting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato shishi ni miiya hiɛ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni miifite lɛ?

english: Black rot at the bottom of tomatoes, called blossom-end rot, is caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit. This usually happens when soil moisture fluctuates between very wet and very dry, preventing the roots from taking up nutrients evenly.
ga: Rot diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ Atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni faaa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ nɔ ni efɔ waa kɛ nɔ ni egbi waa lɛ teŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná niyenii kpakpai daa.

english: Cassava roots need loose, well-tilled soil to expand. If the ground is too hard or compacted, the roots cannot push through the hard earth to store starch, leaving them thin and fibrous.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni atsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Shishifãi nyɛŋ atsɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ koni amɛhiɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Shi ni efee mlɛo ni efee fiber.

english: Why does my maize produce small, half-empty cobs if rainfall stops while it is flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Fã efolo kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa be mli ni efɔ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Maize needs steady water when it develops silks and tassels. If water is scarce during this flowering period, the pollen dries up before fertilizing the grains, resulting in cob ears with missing kernels.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmãa be fɛɛ be kɛ́ eyɛ siliki kɛ ŋmãa. Kɛji nu faaa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ Pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dumɔwui toi ni elaaje.

english: Why do black spots appear on my cocoa pods during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii diji yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black spots on cocoa pods during wet periods are caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cool, damp conditions and spreads rapidly through rainwater splashing from pod to pod.
ga: Nibii diji ni yɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔji anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli Nɔ ni kɛbaa Enɛ ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔ nu ni shwieɔ kɛjɛɔ pod kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings fall over and die at the stem right after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ beni amɛkwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seedlings falling over at the soil line suffer from damping-off, a fungal problem caused by planting in soggy soil with poor air circulation. Excess water rots the delicate stem right where it meets the dirt.
ga: Dumɔwui ni gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa sɛɛkuu. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ eyaaa nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Nu babaoo baaha tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbo yɛ hei ni muji yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to strong, direct sunlight because their roots are still small and cannot draw enough water to cool the plant. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains provides living umbrellas that shield the young cocoa leaves from scorching while keeping the soil cool and moist.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he waa. Enɛ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ daraaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛgbala nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ ajɔɔ. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden tall stakes to climb on while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam plants are naturally climbing vines that need to lift their leaves high toward the sun to produce energy. Lifting the leaves off the wet ground with stakes prevents leaves from rotting, improves air circulation around the vine, and allows the plant to send more energy downward to build larger yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni biɔ ni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu lɛ he koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni fiɔ sɛɛ wo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni efɔ lɛ, ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ wain tso lɛ he lɛ yaa hiɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo yaa shi koni ekɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning light green and yellow in a V-shape?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: When yellowing starts at the bottom leaves and moves up the stem, it is a clear sign that the soil lacks nitrogen. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left to its upper young leaves to keep growing, leaving the older lower leaves to turn yellow and starve.
ga: Beni baai ŋmɔŋ jeɔ shishi yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ ni amɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni eya nɔ eda. Enɛ haa shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ.

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have tiny beneficial nodules on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. When the crop finishes growing and its roots rot into the earth, this stored nitrogen stays behind as free fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmeii bibii. Ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ Kɛ́ tso lɛ egbe eshishifãi lɛ anaa ni eshishifãi lɛ egbo kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, Nitrogen ni ato nɛɛ baakã he ahi shi akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Does it matter which end of a cassava stem cutting points upward when I push it into the ground?
ga: Ani ŋmei tso lɛ naagbee kome baatsɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛ́ ashɛre awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, cassava stem cuttings have small growth buds or nodes along the stem that must point upward toward the sky. If you plant the cutting upside down, the shoots will struggle to bend upward, wasting the plant's energy and resulting in weak growth and smaller tuber yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei ni afo lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii bibii. Eyɛ tso lɛ shishi ni esa akɛ etsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu tso lɛ nine lɛ hiɛ shi lɛ Ebaafee nɔ ni wa waa akɛ ooobɔle tso lɛ yibii lɛ. kɛ hewalɛ ni laajeɔ baa Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ tuber yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: A single plantain root system shares its nutrients with all shoots attached to it. If you allow too many side shoots (suckers) to grow at once, they steal food from the main mother tree, causing it to bear smaller bunches of plantains; keeping only one or two healthy suckers ensures high yields.
ga: Plantain shishifã kome kɛ ŋmeii fɛɛ ni fata he lɛ jaa niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛji oŋmɛ gbɛ ni sɛɛ ŋmeii (ŋmei) babaoo shwere shikome lɛ, Ejuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ nyɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Ha ewo dumɔwui bibii. Kɛ́ ahiɛ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa yibii babaoo baa.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the branches without setting any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress or sudden water changes, such as heavy rain after a long dry spell. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save water and survival energy rather than trying to develop fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa loo nu ni yɔɔ lɛ tsake trukaa, tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni wala ahi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni oná yibii lɛ

english: Why are my maize cobs missing kernels and half-empty inside even though the plants grew tall?
