ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ bɛ ŋmeii ni fã ko efee efolo eyɛ mli akɛ tsei lɛ miida babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Maize cobs fail to fill with seeds when the crop suffers from dry weather or lack of water during the flowering stage when silks emerge. Every silk on the cob must receive pollen from the top tassel; if heat or dry conditions dry out the silks prematurely, fertilization fails and kernels do not form.
ga: Anyɛɛɛ akɛ dumɔwui awo ŋmãa ŋmãa mli kɛ́ tso lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo nu ni bɛ mli yɛ fɔfɔi be mli ni siliki jeɔ kpo lɛ hewɔ. Esa akɛ siliki fã fɛɛ fã ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ aná pollen kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ amli. Kɛji edɔ loo egbi lɛ, ebaaha kpãa lɛ agbi oya. Fɔmɔ ni akɛwoɔ fɔmɔ kotoku mli lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii ni dumɔwui lɛ efeee.

english: Curling and twisting leaves on pepper plants are caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or aphids feeding on the undersides of young leaves. The insect damage causes the leaves to grow unevenly and roll upward, which can be managed by spraying mild soap water or neem oil under the leaves.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kplukai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ haa baa lɛ daa ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee ni ebɔleɔ ehe. Abaanyɛ atsu enɛ he nii kɛtsɔ samla ni mli ejɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. loo neem fɔ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi

english: Why does my cassava spoil and rot within two days of digging it up, while my yams last for months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ fite yɛ gbii enyɔ mli beni mifo lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mi-sweet potato lɛ hiɔ shi nyɔji babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots do not have a protective outer skin layer like yams do once harvested. The moment cassava is detached from its plant stem, oxygen enters the root tissues and triggers a rapid chemical breakdown process, meaning cassava must be cooked or processed immediately after harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi bɛ kponɔgbɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he tamɔ sweet potato kɛji akpa. Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ je tso lɛ shishi pɛ kɛkɛ ni Oxygen lɛ boteɔ shishifã lɛ mli ni ekɛ tsofa ni fiteɔ oya lɛ jeɔ shishi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ ahoo ŋmãa loo atsu he nii kɛji akpa ŋmãa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen. The maize plant naturally pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young, growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛha baai bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Tomato leaf curl is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. Controlling these whiteflies early prevents the virus from spreading and stopping your plants from growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni koolooi bibii eyɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Early Whitefly Kudɔmɔ Ebaatsi helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ni ekpa tsei adalɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees drop off instead of turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ cocoa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the tree experiences stress from high heat, lack of soil moisture, or insufficient shade. Cocoa trees need surrounding shade trees to keep the air cool and humid enough for pods to form.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Cocoa tsei lɛ ahe miihia ŋmɔtɔ tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe. Enɛ ji koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔ ni edɔ bɔ ni sa koni ŋmeii lɛ afee.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting under the soil before I even dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mifolɔ amɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil retains too much water for long periods. Poor soil drainage suffocates the roots and allows fungal rot to develop underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo be kakadaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit bunches at the top. As the bunch grows, the plant becomes top-heavy, so you need to prop up the main stem using sturdy wooden poles.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋwɛi. Kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ da lɛ Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni okɛ tso ni wa atsu nii ni okɛfi tso wulu lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their small green fruits before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Peppers drop young fruit when the weather becomes too hot or when the soil dries out completely between waterings. The plant releases its fruit to conserve energy to survive the heat.
ga: Peppers baajie aduawai bibii kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ. Tsei jieɔ aduawai koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi yɛ dɔlɛ mli lɛ he.

english: Why do my stored yams start growing green shoots inside the barn before I am ready to sell them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ bɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ dani mifee klalo akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that naturally wake up from their rest period when air temperatures and moisture levels change, signaling to the yam that it is time to sprout a new vine.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ wɔɔhe mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ mli latsaa kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ tsake. Enɛ haa sweet potato lɛ leɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ ekwɛ wain tsei heei.

english: You should check if the rain wet the soil down to at least the depth of your hand. Planting after a light rain is risky because the soil can quickly dry up and kill the germinating seeds if no rain follows.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ kɛji nugbɔ efɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashɛ kɛ hoo lɛ, kɛyashɛ onine mli. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo sɛɛ Enɛ ji oshara ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ baaa.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings fall over and die at the soil line right after coming up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni amɛje kpo amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal condition called damping-off, which attacks tender stems when seedlings are kept in soil that is too wet or packed too tightly together.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dampening off, ni tutuaa tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ to shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ nɔ.

english: Why does my orange tree give a huge harvest one year and then almost no fruit the next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-citrus tso lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo afi kome shi afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ, eshwɛ fioo ni ebɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ?

english: This pattern is called alternate bearing. Producing a massive crop consumes so much of the tree's energy and nutrients that it requires a full year to recover before it can bear heavy fruit again.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ style nɛɛ akɛ bearing ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ. Ni aaawo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ biɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli aahu akɛ eheɔ afi muu fɛɛ dani enyɛɔ ewoɔ yibii ni tsii ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a canopy that shields the young plants from heat stress and keeps the soil moist while their roots grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he lɛ baa. ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: Yam plants are vines that need to lift their leaves off the ground to catch as much sunlight as possible. Staking prevents the leaves from rotting on wet soil and helps the plant produce larger, healthier tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ni esa akɛ ewó ebaa nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni enine ashɛ hulu la babaoo nɔ bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Staking haaa baai lɛ akafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I apply fertilizer to my maize crop twice instead of putting it all in the soil at planting time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ mi-ŋmã lɛ awo mli shii enyɔ moŋ fe ni mawo fɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ dumɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Maize needs nutrients at different stages of life. The first application helps roots and stems grow, while the second fuels ear and grain development. Split application also prevents heavy rains from washing all the fertilizer away before the plant can use it.
ga: Niyenii mli hewalɛ he miihia ŋmãa yɛ eshihilɛ mli fãi srɔtoi amli. Klɛŋklɛŋ nitsumɔ lɛ haa shishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ daraa. yɛ be mli ni nɔ ni ji enyɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni toi kɛ ŋmaa lɛ yaa hiɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mligbalamɔ hu haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ dani tsei lɛ kɛbaatsu nii.

english: Why is it helpful to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the same plot after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ aaadu tsina loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally restores soil fertility for the next crop, reducing the need for expensive chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: What causes tiny holes in my young maize leaves and soft droppings inside the leaves near the top?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ Yɛ baai ni bɛŋkɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ anɔ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the central leaves of young maize plants. Detecting this early allows you to apply recommended organic or chemical controls before the pest destroys the growing point.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ. mra mli ni anaa Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii dani tsɛŋemɔ helai fiteɔ he ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my plantain trees turning yellow and drying up from the edges before the fruits mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-plantain lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi kɛmiijɛ amɛshishigbɛ dani aduawai lɛ shwere lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are often a sign of Black Sigatoka disease or root damage caused by poor soil drainage. Cutting off infected leaves and ensuring water drains properly from around the base stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji Black Sigatoka hela loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ he okadi. Baai ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni aaafolɔ mli kɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ he lɛ tsiɔ hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are extremely high, when soil moisture fluctuates too much, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Consistent watering and light shade during peak hot weather help flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsakeɔ tsɔ loo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How does covering the soil around my garden crops with dry grass help them grow during dry periods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mibɔɔ mli tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Covering soil with dry grass or straw—called mulching—acts like a blanket. It prevents sunshine from drying out the earth, keeps root zones cool, and stops unwanted weeds from growing and stealing nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛ jwɛi loo jwɛi shwieɔ nɔ - ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching - tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eju niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting, signaled when the lower leaves yellow and fall off, and the ground surrounding the stem base starts to crack as the roots swell underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, ni etsɔɔ be mli ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishigbɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds instead of using seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ moŋ fe ni mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Certified seeds are specifically bred to resist local diseases, tolerate drought better, and produce uniform, high-yielding crops. Saved seeds tend to lose these beneficial traits over generations, leading to smaller harvests.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Hɔmɔ he tsuishitoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii babaoo be fɛɛ be Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ fɔɔ nɛkɛ sui ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɛɛ laajemɔ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baafee bibioo.

english: Why are my crops failing now even when I plant them at the exact same time of year I used to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efiteɔ bianɛ eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli be kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli moŋ?

english: Weather patterns have shifted due to climate change, meaning rains start later or stop earlier than in past decades. Relying strictly on traditional planting months no longer works, so farmers must monitor weather forecasts and adjust planting times accordingly.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ hewɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi miitsake. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nugbɔ lɛ baaje shishi sɛɛ mli loo ebaakpa mra fe afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni eho lɛ. Ni akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ kusum nyɔji ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ anɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ tsuuu nii dɔŋŋ, no hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ okwaafoi lɛ anyiɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he akɔntaabuu sɛɛ ni amɛtsake dumɔ bei lɛ amli yɛ nakai gbɛ nɔ.

english: Why does the strong sunshine these days scorch and dry up the leaves of my young crops so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ shãa mitsei bibii lɛ ahe baai oya ni egbiɔ lɛ?

english: Global temperatures are higher now, causing stronger heat intensity that burns delicate foliage and rapidly dries out moisture from young plants before their roots can establish deeply.
ga: Amrɔ nɛɛ jeŋ muu fɛɛ latsaa lɛ miiya hiɛ. Ekɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa baa. Enɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tso bibioo lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni mli kwɔ.

english: What is the difference between the seeds I save from my own harvest and the hybrid seeds researchers develop?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ mli lɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni niiamlitaolɔi lɛ fee lɛ ateŋ?

english: Saved seeds carry over the traits of past crops, which may not handle heat well, whereas research-developed seeds are specially bred to tolerate extreme sun, survive short dry spells, and yield more under modern changing climate conditions.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ baafee tamɔ tsutsu tsei, ni ekolɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ dɔlɛ gbɛ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, atsɔse dumɔwui ni afee yɛ niiamlitaomɔ mli lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa. Ebaanyɛ ehi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kukuoo mli. ni amɛfee nibii babaoo yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yaa nɔ amrɔ nɛɛ shishi

english: Why do some of my seeds fail to sprout in the ground even when the soil looks soft and fertile?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ blɛoo ni eyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii moŋ?

english: High soil temperatures and erratic moisture levels can stop traditional seeds from germinating. Using climate-smart certified seeds ensures higher germination rates even under intense heat.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shiŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ akpa kusum dumɔwui akwɛ̃mɔ. Dumɔwui ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he odaseyeli yɔɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ babaoo yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa po shishi.

english: Will applying chemical fertilizers guarantee a good harvest during a drought season?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baaha ŋmaa kpakpa aba yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: No, chemical fertilizers need water to dissolve and feed the crop. Without sufficient soil moisture or organic matter like manure to hold water, fertilizer cannot work properly and can actually burn the crop roots.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he miihia nu koni ekɛshwie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ ni eha amɛ niyenii. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni baaha nu ahi mli lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ ni ebaanyɛ eshã tsei shishifãi.

english: Can using chemicals on my farm harm the natural way my crops grow and survive heat?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye adebɔɔ mli bɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ awui?

english: Overusing harsh agrochemicals can damage beneficial soil life and degrade soil health, making it harder for the soil to hold moisture during dry spells, which weakens the crop's natural heat resistance.
ga: Okwaayeli mli tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ akpata shikpɔŋ nɔ wala ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ hiɛ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ lɛ fiteɔ Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ akɛ ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ ni ekɛteɔ shi ewoɔ dɔlɛ lɛ baa shi.

english: How can I protect my field crops from getting destroyed by intense heat and long periods without rain?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni hulutsoo ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ akafite amɛ?

english: You can protect your crops by applying mulch—like dry grass or leaves—around plant bases to trap soil moisture, and by planting shade trees or drought-resistant crop varieties.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe kɛtsɔ mulch, tamɔ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai, ni okɛbaabɔle otsei lɛ ashishi koni ekɛmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. kɛtsɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ adumɔ nɔ.

english: Why does the soil on my farm dry out much faster after rain than it used to years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho oya fe bɔ ni eji yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Hotter temperatures cause faster evaporation from bare soil. Adding compost or leaving crop residues on the surface helps build soil organic matter, acting like a sponge that holds water longer.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa la ni hoɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ mli baa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he loo tsei ni afolɔ ashwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ama shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni yeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are extension officers advising us to change old farming practices that worked for our parents?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔtsake okwaayeli nifeemɔi momo ni tsu nii eha wɔfɔlɔi lɛ?

english: Old practices were designed for predictable weather patterns that no longer exist. Modern methods are researched to help farmers adapt to current problems like unpredictable rains, hotter sun, and emerging pests.
ga: Afee nifeemɔi momo kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni anyɛɔ atsɔɔ hiɛ atsɔɔ ni bɛ dɔŋŋ lɛ. Amɛmiipɛi ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ gbɛi amli koni eye ebua okwaafoi ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo naagbai ni yɔɔ amrɔ nɛɛ, tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ mli. Hulu lɛ miidɔ waa. kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni miiba lɛ

english: How do researchers know that a new crop seed will actually survive in my village's specific climate?
ga: Te niiamlitaolɔi feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛleɔ akɛ dumɔwui heei baahi shi diɛŋtsɛ yɛ mi akrowa lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ pɔtɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: Researchers test new crop varieties in field trials across different climate zones, subjecting them to real heat and rainfall conditions to ensure only resilient seeds are passed on to local farmers.
ga: Nibii amlitaolɔi kaa tsei srɔtoi heei amɛkwɛɔ Yɛ ŋmɔ mli kaai amli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi srɔtoi amli Kɛtsɔ tsei nɛɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ diɛŋtsɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi pɛ ji nɔ ni akɛhaa maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily in direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees above them to protect their soft leaves and keep the soil moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo, koni amɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ baadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye hulu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I dry my harvested cocoa beans on raised bamboo tables instead of spreading them on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbi mi-kokoo yibii ni akpa lɛ yɛ ŋmei okpɔlɔ ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛshwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Drying cocoa on raised tables lets fresh air flow underneath the beans, helping them dry evenly. It also keeps them clean from dirt, chicken droppings, and mold that can spoil the crop quality.
ga: Kookoo ni agbiɔ yɛ okpɔlɔ ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ kɔfi yibii lɛ ashishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo yibii lɛ ni amɛgbiɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa ehe tseɔ kɛjɛɔ muji, wuɔ fɔmɔ nii, kɛ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Yam vines naturally climb toward sunlight to make food for the plant. When you train the vines up wooden stakes, the leaves catch more light, which helps the plant store energy and build bigger yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ otsɔse wain tso yɛ tso nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baaná la babaoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ ni ekwɛɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are my maize plants growing very tall with plenty of green leaves, but no corn cobs are forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa babaoo ni amɛyɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo lɛ? Shi ani ŋmãa ŋmeii bɛ?

english: Maize plants often produce only leaves without cobs if they get too much nitrogen but lack other nutrients like phosphorus, or if they are planted too close together and cannot get enough light.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni bɛ ŋmãa kɛji enine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ shi niyenii krokomɛi tamɔ fɔsfɔs bɛ mli, loo kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ehe tsɔ ni enine shɛɛɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ.

english: Why are the yellow flowers on my tomato plants falling off instead of turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers usually fall off when the weather gets extremely hot, when the soil becomes too dry, or when insects do not visit the flowers to pollinate them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii eyaaa fɔfɔi amli koni amɛbawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: What will happen to my crops if I plant seeds very close to each other to save space?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni mikɛha he ko akafee nɔ ko?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants fight each other for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. This results in thin, weak stalks and a smaller overall harvest.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛ fɛɛ amɛkpaa nibii bibii.

english: How can I know that my cassava tubers are big enough to harvest without digging up the whole bush?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa ni mikɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: You can check by looking at the base of the plant; when cassava tubers grow big, they push the ground up and create small cracks in the soil around the stem.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ kɛtsɔ tso lɛ shishi ni oookwɛ lɛ nɔ. Beni ŋmei shishifã lɛ daa lɛ, eshɛɔ ehe kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii bibii baa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ mli.

english: Why do people cover the ground around pepper plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi haa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛ pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket that stops the sun from drying out the dirt, keeps the plant roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa ni ehaaa sũ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: When is the best time to put fertilizer around my crops so heavy rain does not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after a light rain, but not right before a heavy downpour, so the roots can drink the food before rain washes it into deep soil.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Shi kaahã nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ miimɔ bo. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu niyenii lɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ aŋɔ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so small even when I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ?

english: Weeds have strong roots that steal the water, sunlight, and food from the soil before your crop's roots can get them, which starves your crops and slows down their growth.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aná. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ oŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni ehaa amɛdalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when I clear all the surrounding big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to protect them from direct sunlight and high temperatures. Without shade trees or plantain plants nearby, the hot sun scorches their tender leaves and dries out the topsoil before their root systems can fully develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii biɔ hulutsoo be koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa he. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ baashã ebaa bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my growing maize plants turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on maize plants usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is the key nutrient responsible for healthy leaf growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore the deep green color and boosts plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa baai lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do some of my cassava stem cuttings rot in the ground while others sprout into big bushes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ekomɛi miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu miikwɛ̃ jwɛi wuji lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings can rot if they are planted upside down, cut from old or diseased stems, or buried in heavy, waterlogged soil. Planting healthy cuttings right-side up in loose, well-drained soil ensures strong sprouting.
ga: Kasava tsei ni afo lɛ baanyɛ afite kɛji akɛ atsɔ hiɛ akwɛ nɔ. Afolɔ kɛjɛ tsei ni egbɔ loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli. loo afu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ adu tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akɛ hiɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ waa.

english: What is causing ragged holes in my maize leaves and small worms inside the central funnel of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji baa ŋmãa baa kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli? yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, a common pest in Ghana. They hide in the leaves' central shoot and feed on new growth, requiring early treatment like recommended bio-pesticides or wood ash to protect the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ ni amɛyeɔ nibii heei ni eda. Enɛ biɔ ni akɛ he awo mli mra, tamɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tso mli sũ ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa koni akɛbu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: When is the best time for me to apply chemical fertilizer to my field crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Fertilizer works best when applied to moist soil while plants are actively growing, usually a few weeks after germinating. Applying fertilizer during a dry spell can burn the roots because plants need water to absorb nutrients properly.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii fioo komɛi beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ashã ejaakɛ nu he miihia tsei lɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛná niyenii kpakpai lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do agricultural extension officers encourage me to plant groundnuts between my rows of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsumɔ he nitsulɔ lɛ wo mi hewalɛ koni madu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil, giving nearby plants like maize extra food without extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ naa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why do my pepper leaves droop in the hot afternoon even if it rained in the early morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane latsaa mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: During intense heat, leaves lose water to the air faster than the roots can suck it up from the ground. Drooping is the plant's way of conserving moisture by reducing sun exposure, and leaves usually recover in the cooler evening.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Defoliation ji gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ nu he kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛbaa shi lɛ nɔ. Ni baai lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow thin and yield smaller fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ewoɔ yibii bibii lɛ?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors, competing directly with your crops for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. When weeds grow unchecked, your crops get less nourishment, resulting in weak growth and smaller yields.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ. Ekɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli beni jwɛi lɛ daraa ni anyɛɛɛ akudɔ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaná niyenii fioo. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo fioo baa.

english: What happens if I plant my crop seeds too close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces crops to fight for light and soil space. As a result, plants become tall, thin, and weak, producing smaller cobs or fruits compared to crops spaced out properly.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi la kɛ shikpɔŋ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ baafee kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe baajɔ, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛbaawo ŋmeii bibii loo aduawai kɛ akɛto tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do dark spots appear on my tomato plants during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dark spots during rainy periods are usually fungal diseases that thrive in wet, humid air. Splashing rain bounces soil and fungus spores onto lower leaves, so removing bottom leaves and mulching the ground helps keep the plant healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni ji black spot yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yaa hiɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ ni mli edɔ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ shwieɔ sũ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ajie baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni akɛwo nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to build strong leaves. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my young cocoa pods turning black and drying up on the trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by black pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, dark shade. Pruning shade trees and weeding around the cocoa base lets sunlight and air in to keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ko ni edɔ, ni eyɛ duŋ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ afolɔ ashwie shi ni ajieɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Cocoa ŋmeii koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli koni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it helpful to cover the soil around my vegetable crop with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mikɛ jwɛi baawo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, stops the strong sun from drying out the soil water too fast. It also keeps the roots cool and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulu lɛ akatso tsɔ ni nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hu akagbi oya. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ hu mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃.

english: Why should I avoid putting chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer is strong like salt, and touching the main stem directly can burn and destroy the plant tissues. It is best to place it in a small circle a few inches away from the stem so the roots can reach for it safely.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe wa tamɔ ŋmei. Ni kɛji akɛ eshɛ tso lɛ tso lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã ni efite tso lɛ fãji. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ amɛ awo kooyigbɛ bibioo ko mli. Inchi fioo ko pɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi. kɛha root hegbɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of yellow flowers but no fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo shi ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers can drop without making fruit if the air gets too hot, if the plant lacks water, or if bees are not visiting to move pollen. Keeping the soil evenly moist and planting flowers nearby to attract bees solves this.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi baanyɛ agbo ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu Aloo kɛji ŋmeii lɛ ebaaa koni amɛbajie pollen lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ fɔfɔii ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ Koni agbala ŋmeii lɛ baaye abua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects and sits around them for too long in heavy soil. Planting your cassava cuttings on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra rainfall to drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ amɛhe. sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ Kɛ́ adu ŋmei niji yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nɛ waa.

english: What will happen if I plant my pepper seeds too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu pepper dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: When pepper plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This makes the stems thin and weak, resulting in very small peppers or few fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa ŋmeii bibii waa loo aduawai fioo pɛ baa.

english: Why should I cut off the extra small shoots growing on the sides of my tomato stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? No kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tomato tso lɛ masɛi.

english: Removing those extra side shoots, called suckers, prevents the plant from wasting energy on leafy branches. This directs all the plant's strength into growing bigger and sweeter tomatoes.
ga: Ajieɔ sɛɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmeii lɛ Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ yɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ awo tomatoi wuji ni ŋɔɔ lɛ amli.

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can get weak if tiny worms called nematodes attack them underground. Propping up heavy bunches with sturdy wooden poles prevents the trees from snapping or falling.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni ŋmeii bibii baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes lɛ tutuaa amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Tso tsei ni tsii ni wa ni akɛma shi lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ akakumɔ loo ekagbee shi.

english: Why are tiny green insects bunching up under my cabbage leaves and damaging them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ mi-cabbage baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: These insects are aphids that suck the juice directly out of the crop leaves, making them curl and wither. Spraying them with a mild liquid soap solution or neem tree leaf water washes them away safely.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji aphids ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli tɛ̃ɛ. ni haa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboiɔ Kɛ́ akɛ samla ni mli ejɔ loo neem baa nu lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni efɔ amɛhe shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die if I do not plant plantains or cassava next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛji miduuu plantains loo cassava yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot survive strong, direct sunlight when they are small. Shade plants like plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act like living umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa trees from getting scorched and keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ beni amɛdarako lɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow and stop growing when there is too much standing water on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ beni nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When rain water accumulates and stands on your field without draining, it smothers the plant roots. Roots need air to breathe; without air, they cannot absorb nutrients like nitrogen from the soil, causing the leaves to turn yellow and growth to stunt.
ga: Beni nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa ni edamɔ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ. Ebaatswa tsei ashishifãi. Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia shishifãi koni amɛmu. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Amɛnyɛŋ amɛjie niyenii tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni no haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdaraaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow very tall and thin with very few fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of putting energy into producing thick stems and heavy fruit, the plants stretch upwards competing for sunlight.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Mohu ɔ, e kɛ he wami tsuɔ ní kɛ woɔ yiblii nɛ mi wa kɛ yiblii nɛ mi wa. Mohu ɔ, tsei ɔmɛ tsɔ a he konɛ a kɛ hulu la ɔ nɛ fia a he si.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or lack of nutrients. The plant intentionally drops its flowers to conserve energy for its own survival rather than using energy to feed growing fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛjieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ he wami tsuɔ ní kɛ haa yiblii nɛ ngɛ wae ɔ niye ní.

english: Why do experienced farmers cover the soil around their vegetable crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛ jwɛi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛduɔ aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground around crops with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, blocks the sun from drying out the earth. It keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation, and prevents weeds from sprouting and stealing crop nutrients.
ga: He ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa Atsɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi duɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsĩ hulu lɛ naa ni ebaatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eju tsei amli niyenii.

english: Why should I avoid planting cassava or maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ he?

english: Planting the same crop on the same plot season after season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil over and over. It also allows specific pests and diseases that feed on that crop to build up in the soil, leading to poorer yields over time.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli be fɛɛ be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shii abɔ. Ehaa kooloi kɛ helai komɛi ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Fertilizer is best applied when the crop is actively growing and the soil is slightly moist, usually two to four weeks after planting. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn plant roots, while applying it during heavy rain washes the nutrient food away before plants can consume it.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii 2-4 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ shishifãi ashã. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe dani tsei lɛ yeɔ amɛ.

english: Why do weeds in my crop field reduce the size of my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔji amli lɛ miiba mikpamɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that grow faster than domesticated crops. They act like thieves, stealing the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops, leaving your plants weak and unable to produce big yield.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni daa oya fe shia tsei. Amɛfeɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi, amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Enɛ haa otsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do I need to cut off extra shoots growing around the base of my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: Allowing too many sucker shoots to grow from one mother plantain plant divides the soil nutrients among too many stems. Removing the extra shoots leaves all the food for one main stem, resulting in larger and heavier bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ kɛjɛ dumɔwu kome mli lɛ, ebaaja shikpɔŋ mli niyenii babaoo tsɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, niyenii pɛ eshwɛɔ kɛhaa tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantain tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my seeds rot in the ground when I push them too deep into the soil during planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ dumɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Seeds contain a limited amount of stored energy to sprout and push out of the ground. If planted too deep, the shoot runs out of energy before reaching light, and moisture deep in the ground causes the seed to rot before it breaks through the surface.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ hewalɛ fioo ko ni ato ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ, hewalɛ baaho yɛ tso lɛ mli dani eshɛ la lɛ he. Ni nu ni mli edɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ.

english: Why do my cashew fruits drop to the ground on their own when they turn red or yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew ŋmeii lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ́ amɛtsɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ loo ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Cashew fruits naturally drop from the tree once they are fully ripe. Unlike many other fruits, cashews reach their peak quality and maturity only when they fall naturally to the ground.
ga: Cashew ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ kɛji ekwɛ̃ kwraa. Esoro cashew ŋmeii yɛ aduawai krokomɛi ahe. Eyɛ su kpakpa kɛ dalɛ ni nɔ kwɔ fe fɛɛ kɛji ejɛ adebɔɔ mli egbee shikpɔŋ pɛ.

english: Should I pick my cashews directly from the tree branches or wait for them to fall?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ cashew ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo mamɛ ni amɛgbee shi?

english: It is best to wait for them to fall to the ground. Picking cashews directly from the branch often means harvesting immature nuts, which reduces the market quality and weight of the kernel.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni amɛgbee shikpɔŋ. Bei pii lɛ, cashews ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ abaakpa ŋmeii ni eshɛko lolo lɛ. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ ahilɛ kɛ amɛtsiimɔ aba shi.

english: Why are some of my cashew fruits falling to the ground while they are still small and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashews lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo ni amɛji ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Premature fruit drop is usually not normal maturity. It is caused by insect pests like the cashew bug, fungal diseases, or lack of water and nutrients, which weaken the stem before the fruit matures.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai ni shwieɔ shi oya lɛ jeee nɔ ni shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ jellyfish, fungal helai, loo nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ.

english: How often do I need to pick up the cashews that have fallen onto the ground in my farm?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ maŋɔ cashew ŋmeii ni gbeeɔ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: You should gather fallen cashews every two to three days. Leaving them on the damp ground for too long allows mold, pests, and rain to rot the apple and damage the nut inside.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ cashews ni egbee shi lɛ atsu nii daa gbii enyɔ loo etɛ. Kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ŋmeii, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, kɛ nugbɔ fiteɔ apolo lɛ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to walk around my farm regularly even when it is not harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ manyiɛ kɛbɔle he lɛ? Okɛ okwaayeli atsu nii daa kɛji jeee kpamɔɔ be po?

english: Regularly inspecting your farm helps you observe early signs of diseases, pest infestations, or nutrient shortages so you can treat them before they damage your whole harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona helai, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ he okadii mra. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ otsa lɛ dani efite onibii fɛɛ.

english: What should I do when I see a strange disease or leaf damage on my cashew trees that I don't recognize?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mikɛ hela ko ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ kpe? Aloo baa ni efite yɛ cashew tso ko nɔ ni miyɔseee lɛ?

english: Cut a sample of the affected leaf or branch, seal it in a clean plastic bag, and take it to your local agricultural extension officer so they can identify the issue and recommend the right treatment.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ tso lɛ baa loo tso nine ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ lɛ he nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ko. Akɛwo plastic kotoku ni mli tse mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛya okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ. Bɔni afee ni enyɛ ena naagba lɛ ni ekɛ tsofafeemɔ ni ja lɛ atsɔɔ.

english: How can I tell the difference between normal crop behavior and a plant disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ tsei asubaŋ ni sa kɛ tsei ahela teŋ?

english: Normal crop behavior happens uniformly across healthy plants, such as seasonal leaf shedding or natural fruit ripening. Disease usually leaves irregular spots, blackening, curling, or rotting on specific parts of the tree.
ga: Sui ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ baa yɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli, tamɔ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli loo aduawai ni shwereɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ haa tso lɛ fã fɛɛ fã feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do cashew trees on the same farm flower and drop fruit at slightly different times?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cashew tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ bei srɔtoi fioo amli lɛ?

english: Trees mature at different rates due to slight variations in soil richness, sunlight access, water availability, and the age or variety of the planting material.
ga: Tsei lɛ daa yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli tsakemɔi fioo komɛi ahewɔ. hulu la ni anáa nu ni yɔɔ kɛ afii loo nibii srɔtoi ni akɛduɔ nii.

english: Why do my cashew trees lose many of their leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ baai babaoo fite yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Losing leaves during dry weather is a natural survival trick. Trees shed leaves to conserve water and protect themselves from drying out until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni laajeɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ wala yiwalaheremɔ ŋaa. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: How does watching how my crops change over the years make me a better farmer?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ bɔ ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tsake yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ eha mifee okwaafonyo kpakpa?

english: Tracking seasonal changes helps you learn the exact timing for weeding, spraying, and harvesting on your specific land, allowing you to plan ahead and increase your yields.
ga: Be mli tsakemɔi ni oookwɛ lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni okaseɔ be pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ ajie jwɛi, ashwie nɔ, ni akpa nii yɛ oshikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa otoɔ gbɛjianɔ kɛtsɔ hiɛ ni ohaa nibii ni otsuɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow green and strong. It can also happen if heavy rains flood the soil and drown the plant's roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni eha tsei shishifãi lɛ shwie nu.

english: During dry weather, cocoa trees lose water faster than their roots can drink from the ground. Leaf curling and browning is the tree's natural reaction to save moisture until rain falls again.
ga: yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji bɔ ni tso lɛ feɔ enii ehaa koni ekɛto ŋmɔtɔ he kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants wrinkled and rolled up like small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Wrinkled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaf undersides, which damages the leaf tissue and twists its growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baa lɛ shishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni egbɔjɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji ni ehaa amɛdaraa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ.

english: What causes small holes to suddenly appear on my corn leaves?
ga: Mɛni ha buji bibii je kpo trukaa yɛ mi-abele baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Small holes in corn leaves are typically caused by pests like the fall armyworm or stem borers eating the tender leaves inside the plant while it is growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ fall armyworms loo stem borers ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai amli lɛ baa.

english: Tomatoes shed their flowers when temperatures get too hot or when the plant does not get steady water. When stressed, the plant drops flowers to save energy for itself.
ga: Tomato baawo fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni yaa nɔ daa. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛto hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ eha ehe.

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped in the soil for too long, especially in heavy soil. Too much moisture allows waterborne fungi to attack and decay the tubers underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. titri lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine lɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why do my groundnut pods turn out empty inside when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut pods lɛ efee efolo kɛ́ mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut shells happen when the soil lacks calcium during the time pods are forming, or when the ground is too dry for the plant to push food into the pods.
ga: Peanut ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ calcium bɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ miifee. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni tso lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ niyenii awo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when a little wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko pɛ tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are naturally shallow. If underground pests like nematodes or stem weevils attack the root base, the plant loses its anchor and falls under its own heavy weight.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekwɔɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ nematodes loo stem weevils tutua shishifãi lɛ. Tso lɛ sɛɛ efo ni egbee shi yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ etsiimɔ shishi.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up and turn black before the yam tubers are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ egbi ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ dani ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines turn black early when fungal diseases like leaf spot or anthracnose attack the leaves, usually spread by heavy splattering rains and hot, humid air.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ oya kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ baa mli ŋmɔtɔ loo anthracnose tutua baai lɛ. Bei pii lɛ egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ fɛ̃i.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) keeps the soil cool, prevents sunshine from drying out soil water, stops weeds from taking over, and adds food to the soil as it decays.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ. Tsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekaha nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni ekaha nɔ. ni okɛ niyenii afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he beni efiteɔ lɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning pale yellow from the tips down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ amɛshishigbɛ kɛbashi shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen. When the soil lacks enough nutrients, the plant pulls food from its older bottom leaves to feed new growth, causing the tips to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmɔshi nibii heei. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ anaabui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How does spreading dried cow manure or decayed leaves help my crops produce better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni egbi loo baai ni egboi ni mikɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Decayed plant matter and manure act like food and a water sponge in the soil. It feeds your crops natural plant food slowly and helps the soil hold onto water longer during dry heat.
ga: Tsei kɛ kooloi ashwiei ni egboi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛ sponji ni yɔɔ sũ mli. Kɛtsɔ niyenii ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ fiofio yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes through the middle leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu kɛtsɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on maize leaves. They hide deep inside the funnel of the plant, so applying treatments directly into the leaf funnel early in the day works best to control them.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai. Akɛ amɛ ewo tsei akutsei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsofa lɛ wo baai lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli mra lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ fe fɛɛ kɛha amɛhe nɔyeli.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my tomato plants get dark spots and dry up during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain splashes soil-borne fungi onto the lower leaves, causing leaf spot diseases. Removing lower leaves near the soil helps prevent splash-back and allows air to flow through, keeping leaves dry.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. cause leaf spot disease Kɛji ajieɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaaa kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. ni ehaa baai lɛ mli egbiɔ

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate strong, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa creates living umbrellas that protect young cocoa trees from heat until they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ latsaa he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ daa waa.

english: Planting too close reduces yield because the plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space allows it to grow larger and bear full fruits.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha yibiiwoo aba shi ejaakɛ tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni eda ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell. If seeds germinate and the rains stop, the delicate young sprouts will dry out and die before the main rainy season fully establishes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ ni nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ Tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ baa.

english: What causes my cassava tubers to turn soft and rot underground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔ be baashɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when heavy water remains trapped in the soil around them for too long. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away and keeps the tubers healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu afua lɛ hi shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa, ni ehaa ŋmei lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when exposed to high heat or water stress. Watering your pepper plants regularly during dry spells keeps them cool and helps the flowers stay on to become fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu he haomɔ he. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ daa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i, ni ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akakwɛ̃ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do I need to put wooden tall stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the air to spread their leaves toward sunlight. Sunlit leaves produce more plant food, which travels down to grow large, heavy yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni akwɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Baai ni hulu la babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ woɔ tsei niyenii babaoo. ni tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi koni ekwɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn under strong direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides a living canopy that keeps the soil cool and moist until the cocoa trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa.

english: Why do my yam vines need to grow up tall wooden stakes instead of spreading across the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ ada ni etsɔ tso kakadaŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves produce food for the tuber using sunlight. Lifting the vines off the ground on stakes allows all the leaves to capture maximum sunlight and airflow, resulting in much larger yams underground.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa tuber lɛ. Wein tsei lɛ ni awóɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ fɛɛ naa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ babaoo. Nɔ ni ejɛ mli eba ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ etsɔ agbo babaoo.

english: Why do my maize stalks remain short and light green even though I weed my farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ yɛ kuku lolo ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Light green, stunted maize is a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food for stem and leaf growth. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer early in the planting season helps the leaves turn dark green and grow tall.
ga: Abɛi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji tsei aniyenii titri kɛha amɛshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ amɛdalɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why do my plantain trees take so long to produce fruit when I leave all the young shoots growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii beni mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Multiple young shoots, known as suckers, compete with the main plant for water and soil nutrients. Removing extra suckers and keeping only two or three allows the main mother plant to flower and produce heavy plantain bunches faster.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii bibii babaoo akɛ suckers. Kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ aka akaŋ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni akɛ enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ to he lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo fɔfɔi ni ewo plantain tsei oya.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in my field make my maize crop grow better in the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has special root nodules that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the groundnut crop is harvested, that extra nitrogen remains in the dirt to nourish the next crop.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni eyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eya nɔ eha ŋmeii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers before any fruit begins to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani aduawai jeɔ shishi ewoɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when they experience heat stress or sudden dry soil. Spreading dry grass mulch around the base of the plants keeps the soil roots cool and holds moisture longer.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ haomɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi trukaa lɛ kpe. Kɛ́ okɛ sũ ni egbi wo otso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why does my upland rice dry out so quickly when rain stops for just two weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbɛ́ɔ oya nɛkɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa otsii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Upland rice has shallow root systems that cannot reach deep underground water. Mixing organic manure into the soil before planting improves the ground's ability to hold onto rainwater during short dry spells.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛ nɔ ŋmãa yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani adu lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ ahiɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli yɛ be kukuoo mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my green tomatoes turning black and soft before they get a chance to turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ naagbeei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani etsɔɔ etsuru lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom end rot, which happens when the plant cannot draw enough calcium from the soil due to irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture steady prevents the fruit bottoms from spoiling.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ baatsi aduawai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anaa koni ekafite.

english: Why do my cassava leaves twist up into small, pale yellow patterns and stop growing full size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf twisting in cassava is usually caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Using disease-free stem cuttings from certified extension dealers ensures the new plants grow healthy, broad leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmei mli lɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ yibii ni hela bɛ mli ni jɛ jarayelɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tsei heei lɛ aná baai ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do tiny caterpillars appear and chew holes through my cabbage leaves right when the heads are forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii jeɔ kpo ni amɛyeɔ bu yɛ mi-cabbage baai lɛ amli kɛji yitsei lɛ miifee pɛ?

english: Moths lay eggs on the undersides of green cabbage leaves, which hatch into destructive caterpillars. Spraying natural botanical solutions like neem seed extract early in the growth stage repels the insects before they destroy the cabbage head.
ga: Kpɔŋɔi woɔ amɛwui yɛ kaabii baai eŋɔli lɛ ashishi. ni baatsɔ ŋmeii ni gbeɔ mɔ. Akɛ adebɔɔ mli tso mli tsofa tamɔ neem dumɔwu mli nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shishijee be mli ni edara lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ashwie kooloi bibii lɛ dani amɛfite kaabe yitsei lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly when the sun gets hot during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ye nɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural defense to protect themselves from losing moisture in the heat. It helps the crop save water until temperatures cool down or until rain or irrigation water comes.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ loo kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ baa.

english: How can I tell if my crop is just resting from afternoon heat or actually needs water urgently?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiye shwane hejɔɔmɔ kɛkɛ loo nu he miihia amɛ oya diɛŋtsɛ?

english: If your crop wilts during the hot afternoon sun but recovers and looks firm early in the morning, it is just reacting to heat. If it remains droopy in the cool morning before the sun rises, it desperately needs water.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli Shi ehiɛ ba ehe nɔ ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni ehi shi shiŋŋ leebi maŋkpa. Eji hetoo kɛha dɔlɛ kɛkɛ. Kɛji nugbɔ miinɛ lolo yɛ leebi ni mli ejɔ dani hulu lɛ ateshi. Nu he miihia lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why do my crops stop growing well even when water is only cut off for a few hours on hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekpaa shweremɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo ko pɛ yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ po lɛ?

english: When plants lack water during hot hours, they close tiny pores on their leaves to save moisture. Closing these pores stops the plant from taking in air to produce food, which temporarily freezes its growth.
ga: Beni tsei bɛ nu yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Tso lɛ tsiɔ bu bibioo lɛ naa. yɛ baai lɛ anɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔi nɛɛ ni agbeɔ lɛ haaa tsei lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ ni amɛkɛfee niyenii. Enɛ baaha dalɛ akpa be kukuoo ko.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my crops turn yellow and fall off when water becomes scarce?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu faaa lɛ?

english: When a plant experiences water stress, it sacrifices its older lower leaves to save energy and water for the younger leaves and fresh growth at the top.
ga: Kɛ tsei kɛ nu he haomɔ kpe Ekɛ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ shaa afɔle koni ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu ato kɛha baai bibii kɛ ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee.

english: If my water source goes off for two or three hours in the afternoon, will it kill my vegetables?
ga: Kɛji mi nu lɛ gbo ŋmɛlɛtswai enyɔ loo etɛ shwane mli Ani ebaafite mi aduawai lɛ?

english: A delay of a few hours will cause temporary wilting, but most vegetables will recover once watered. However, frequent delays during the heat of the day stress the plants, which can lower your final yield.
ga: ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ baaha egbɔjɔ be kukuoo ko. Shi aduawai babaoo he waa kɛji akɛ awo amɛ nu. Shi kɛlɛ, gbi lɛ mli latsaa be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ shii abɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha naagbee yibiiwoo ni obaaná lɛ aba shi.

english: Is it better to water my crops early in the morning or during the afternoon heat?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofɔ tsei anɔ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: It is best to water early in the morning. Afternoon sun causes water to evaporate rapidly before roots can absorb it, and hot leaves can get scorched if water sits on them.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu leebi. Shwane hulu lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ nu lɛ. Ni baai ni mli edɔ fe nine lɛ baanyɛ ashã kɛji akɛ nu ha amɛhe.

english: Can flooding my field with a lot of water right after a dry spell hurt my crops?
ga: Ani nu babaoo ni mikɛbaawo miŋmɔji amli yɛ hɔmɔ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Yes, giving plants too much water suddenly after a dry delay can shock their roots and cause fruits like tomatoes to crack open due to rapid water intake.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ aha tso ko nu babaoo fe nine beni egbi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha eshishifãi lɛ akpokpo. ni ehaa aduawai tamɔ tomatoi lɛ fãa yɛ nu ni anáa oya lɛ hewɔ.

english: What can I put on my farm soil to keep it moist longer when water supply is unreliable?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mikɛwo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ koni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ be mli ni anyɛɛɛ akɛ he afɔ̃ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering bare soil around your crops with dry grass, leaves, or straw—called mulching—blocks direct sunlight, keeping the soil cool and holding moisture much longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni okɛbaabɔle ohe lɛ nɔ Okɛ jwɛi, baai, loo jwɛi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Ebaaye ebua ni etsi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be babaoo.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off when watering is inconsistent?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa lɛ?

english: Flowering requires a lot of water and energy. When water is limited, the plant drops its flowers to save its own life rather than using energy to grow fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ biɔ nu kɛ hewalɛ babaoo. Kɛ nu lɛ faaa lɛ Tso lɛ baashwie efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii kɛdu aduawai

english: Which crops can survive better if my water supply is unreliable and stops frequently?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei baanyɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ anyɛɛɛ akɛ he afɔ̃ nu ni mikɛhaa lɛ nɔ ni ekpaa shii abɔ lɛ?

english: Crops like cassava, cowpea, sorghum, and millet have deep root systems and tough structures, making them far better at handling irregular watering than delicate vegetables like lettuce or tomatoes.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei, tsina ŋmei, ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli wa. Enɛ haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛtsuɔ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ fe aduawai ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ lettuce loo tomato.

english: Young cocoa trees need partial shade to protect their tender leaves from harsh direct sunlight and heat. Planting them under shade crops like plantains or large trees keeps the soil moist and shields the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo be fioo koni amɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo tsei wuji ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhe hulu la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate that the plant is lacking nitrogen in the soil or that heavy rains have washed away nutrients. It can also happen when the ground is waterlogged, preventing the roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛye niyenii.

english: What is eating small holes in the middle leaves of my corn plants during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the growing center (whorl) of the maize plant during the day and feed on the fresh green leaves, leaving ragged holes and sawdust-like waste.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ hei (rings) lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni oye baai eŋɔli heei Shi bu ni ekumɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ sɛɛ.

english: How do I know when my cassava stems are ready for harvesting under the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is typically ready to harvest when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare stem, usually around 9 to 12 months after planting. You may also notice the ground around the base of the plant cracking as the tubers grow larger.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni eshiɔ tso ni nɔ ko bɛ mli Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Ekolɛ obaana shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ. Tso lɛ shishigbɛ fãa beni bulb lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I dump chemical fertilizer right against the main stem of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ tso titri lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly touching the stem can burn and kill the plant's delicate bark and upper roots. Fertilizer should be placed in a small ring or line a few inches away from the stem where the side roots can absorb it safely.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ashã ni amɛgboi. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmeii bibii amli. Aloo ekɛ tsɔne lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo komɛi. ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ shweshweeshwe

english: Why do my plantain suckers produce smaller bunches when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plantains are planted too close to each other, their leaves block sunlight from reaching one another and their roots compete for the same nutrients and water in the soil, resulting in smaller, weaker bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantains ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kui bibii kɛ kui ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off without setting fruit when daytime temperatures get too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly very wet. Heat stress stops the flower from pollinating properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Heat haomɔ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it bad for my soil if I burn all the cleared bushes and weeds before planting?
ga: Ani ebaana shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ gbonyo kɛji mishã tsei bibii kɛ jwɛi ni ajie lɛ fɛɛ dani midu?

english: While burning clears the land quickly, it destroys rich organic matter and kills beneficial earthworms and microbes in the soil. Over time, burning makes the soil dry out faster and lose its natural fertility.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, la ni ashãa lɛ haa jɛmɛ tseɔ oya. Shi efiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo lɛ, ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, Shãa haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.
