Kɛ́ ashi tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaabu kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi tsei lɛ baadara.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when there is too much rain during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain causes water to collect and stay flooded in the soil, the roots drown from a lack of oxygen, allowing rot-causing organisms in the wet earth to decay the crop.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu buaa ehe naa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nuɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni fiteɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Yam plants store energy in their underground tubers through sunlight caught by their leaves. Staking gets the leaves up off the ground into maximum sunlight, which allows the plant to produce much larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ hewalɛ toɔ amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛtsɔɔ hulu la ni tswaa amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Staking baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji babaoo.

english: Why does my plantain tree produce small, light bunches when I let all the young suckers grow around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miida ni amɛmiifee ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni mihaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain lɛ he lɛ.

english: All the extra shoots (suckers) growing at the base of the plantain stem compete with the mother plant for food, water, and sunlight. Pruning away weaker suckers ensures all the energy goes directly into growing one big, heavy bunch of fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei (tsei) ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain lɛ shishi lɛ fɛɛ kɛ tso nyɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa hewalɛ fɛɛ yaa tso yibii kome ni da ni tsii lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomatoes shed their flowers when temperatures get extremely high or when water supply is irregular. Extreme heat damages the pollen inside the flower, causing it to drop off before it can form a tomato fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Ha egbee shi dani etsɔ tomato.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward like cups and turning stiff?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the sap from the underside of leaves or spreading leaf-curl viruses. Controlling these pests early stops the foliage from twisting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi loo helai ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper mli. Ni aaaye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ mra Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea flowers fall off before any beans grow inside the pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Very small insects called flower thrips attack cowpeas right as they bloom to feed on the flower buds. When these pests damage the flower buds, the blossoms fall off before the bean pods have a chance to develop.
ga: Kplukai bibii waa ni atsɛɔ amɛ flower thrips lɛ tutuaa tsina ŋmeii beni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛye fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ. Kɛji nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kpata fɔfɔii ashishifãi lɛ ahiɛ lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi dani ŋmeii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Why do small caterpillars appear inside the central leaves of my maize right after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-ŋma lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ amli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Moths lay their eggs inside the tender central whorl (funnel) of young maize plants right after the rainy season begins. The hatching caterpillars, such as Fall Armyworm, feed inside the funnel where they are hidden and protected from hot sunlight.
ga: Kpɔŋɔi lɛ woɔ amɛwui lɛ yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋtayaa ni yɔɔ blɛoo (cone) lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee sɛɛ. Kplukai ni fɔɔ bii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ yeɔ nii yɛ gbɛjegbɛi ni akɛ amɛhe ewo mli ni abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food it needs to build green leaves. When there is not enough nitrogen in the soil, the plant steals food from its older bottom leaves to feed the new top leaves, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná baai eŋɔli. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Tsei juɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: What happens to my maize crop if I plant the seeds too close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight underground for soil food and water, while their leaves fight above ground for sunlight. This stress makes the plants grow tall, weak, and thin, resulting in small ears or cobs with very few grains.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛna niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la. Nɛkɛ nɔnyɛɛ nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa, amɛgbɔjɔɔ, ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa amɛfeɔ toi bibii loo ŋmeii bibii kɛ dumɔwui fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce many flowers, but the flowers fall off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant lacks water and nutrients. High temperatures dry out the pollen inside the flower so it cannot form a tomato, causing the plant to shed the flower to save its strength.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai. He ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ gĩɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, anyɛɛɛ afee tomato. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛhiɛ hewalɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce very small bunches when I leave many suckers growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa beni miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo shwereɔ yɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers act like extra mouths eating from the same bowl. They pull water, soil nutrients, and energy away from the main mother tree, leaving her with less strength to produce a heavy, full bunch of plantains.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ naabu krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ nii kɛjɛɔ tsɛnsi kome mli. Amɛgbalaa nu, niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. kɛ hewalɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ dumɔwui babaoo ni tsii.

english: Why are there ragged holes in the leaves and dirt like sawdust inside the central funnel of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe tsei kɛ muji tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni etse amɛhe lɛ? Eyɛ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which crawls into the hidden central leaves (the funnel) of the maize to eat the soft plant tissue. The sawdust-like material is the waste left behind by the worm as it feeds.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ baai (channels) ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ amli koni amɛye tsei bibii lɛ ahe fãji. Nibii ni tamɔ ŋmei ji jwɛi ni ŋmeii shiɔ yɛ amɛsɛɛ beni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why should I avoid planting pepper on the same patch of land where I harvested garden eggs last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmeii adumɔ he yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mibua abɔɔ mli ŋmeii anaa yɛ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper and garden egg are close relatives in the plant family, meaning they suffer from the exact same soil pests and diseases. Planting them in the same spot year after year gives those hidden soil diseases more time to multiply and destroy your new crop.
ga: Pepper kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋshɔŋloo ji wekumɛi ni bɛŋkɛ kpaakpa yɛ tsei aweku lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ helai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ yeɔ amɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ́ odu amɛ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ náa be babaoo ni amɛkɛshwereɔ ni amɛfiteɔ onibii heei lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and dry up during the sunny dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains planted next to them to act as living umbrellas and keep the soil moist during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Pepper leaves curl up in intense heat as a natural defense mechanism to shield themselves from the sun. By rolling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to heat, helping it trap moisture inside and stop from drying out.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni amɛkɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he. Baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ hiɛ ni hulutsoo baa lɛ baa shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ mli ni ehaaa baai lɛ agbi.

english: Cassava cuttings fail to sprout if the stems were taken from old, dry wood, if they were planted upside down, or if the soil is too dry. Healthy sprouts require mature, fresh stems planted with the leaf buds pointing upward toward the sky.
ga: Kasava tsei ni afolɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ ajie tsei ni egbɔ ni egbi lɛ amli tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Esa akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ aná ŋmeii heei ni edaa ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops stay small even after I have put fertilizer on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ bibioo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that act like sponges, stealing the fertilizer out of the soil before your main crop can absorb it. Clearing weeds before applying fertilizer ensures that your crop gets all the nutrients to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji. Amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani tso titri lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops perform worse when I plant them during the minor rainy season compared to the major season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiii kwraa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli kɛ akɛto be titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: The minor rainy season in Ghana usually brings shorter wet periods and less predictable rainfall. Crops receive less moisture and sunshine, which can slow down their growth and reduce their overall yield compared to the major rainy season.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baa shi fioo yɛ Ghana lɛ haa nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ baa. Tsei lɛ naaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulu la fioo. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shweremɔ aba shi ni eha yibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ aba shi kɛ akɛto nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa lɛ he.

english: What extra care do my crops need if I decide to plant during the minor season?
ga: Mɛɛ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ he hiaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji mikpɛ miyiŋ akɛ madu yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli?

english: During the minor season, crops need help retaining soil water. You can apply mulch around the plant bases to keep the soil cool and wet, plant drought-tolerant seeds, or provide irrigation if water is available.
ga: Yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ, yelikɛbuamɔ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ shishitoo koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Dumɔwui ni nyɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ adumɔ loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi kɛji nu yɛ

english: How do I choose the right crop variety to plant if I want to sell my harvest at the market for a good profit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tsei ni sa ni madu? Kɛji oosumɔ ni ohɔ̃ɔ onibii yɛ jara nɔ koni oná sɛɛnamɔ kpakpa.

english: To sell for profit, choose certified seed varieties that mature quickly, yield heavily, and possess qualities market buyers like—such as good size, color, longer shelf-life, and resistance to common local pests.
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ ni ohɔ̃ɔ koni onine ashɛ sɛɛnamɔ nɔ lɛ Halamɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni awo he odase akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya, ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo, ni amɛyɛ sui ni mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ sumɔɔ, tamɔ amɛdalɛ, amɛsu kpakpa, kɛ amɛshihilɛ be kakadaŋŋ. kɛ bɔ ni enyɛɔ eshiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it better to buy certified seeds from an extension worker or dealer instead of planting grain saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ ooohe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ kɛjɛ extension nitsulɔ loo nihɔɔlɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, i du duwuhi nɛ a yi wami kɛ je ye kpami nɛ i kpata be ko nɛ be ɔ mi ɔ mi.

english: Certified seeds are specifically bred and treated to resist diseases, germinate evenly, and give a higher yield, whereas saved seeds often carry pests or lose their strength over generations.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ni atsaa amɛ pɔtɛɛ koni helai akamɔ amɛ. kwɛ̃ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo amɛhewalɛ baa shi kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli.

english: What does it mean when an extension worker says a crop variety can 'handle the weather'?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛ́ sɛɛgbɛtsɔɔmɔ he nitsulɔ ko kɛɛ tso henɔ ko baanyɛ Ani obaanyɛ ‘okɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ akpee naa’?

english: It means that specific crop variety has been bred or selected to withstand harsh weather conditions, such as high heat or short dry spells, without dying or losing all its yield.
ga: Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, atsɔ tsei srɔtoi pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ loo ahala amɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni naa wa waa, tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ be kukuoo mli lɛ anaa. ni egbooo loo nibii fɛɛ ni afeɔ lɛ fiteee

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and turn yellow during hot afternoon sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves droop when the plant loses water faster through its leaves than its roots can pull from the soil. Yellowing usually means the soil is too dry or lacks nutrients required to handle hot sun stress.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ shwie nu kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo ebɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛtsu hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he haomɔi ahe nii.

english: Will applying fertilizer guarantee a good harvest even if rainfall is poor?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha ŋmaa kpakpa aba kɛji nugbɔ ni ehiii nɛ po?

english: No, fertilizer needs moisture in the soil to dissolve so plant roots can drink it up. Without enough rain or water, fertilizer stays dry and can even burn the plant roots if applied incorrectly.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu. Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, Fɛ̃i baaya nɔ agbi ni ebaanyɛ eshã tsei shishifãi kɛji akɛ akɛtsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know the right way to apply fertilizer to my crops so I do not waste money?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male bɔ ni mafee makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli jogbaŋŋ? Bɔni afee ni okafite shika?

english: Apply fertilizer close to the base of the plant roots—not touching the stem directly—when the soil is moist. Splitting the fertilizer into two applications at key growth stages ensures plants use every drop effectively.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo he ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ—ni okɛtaaa tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ—be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amlijaa yɛ nitsumɔi enyɔ mli yɛ dalɛ bei titrii amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How should I space my plants when sowing if I am farming to sell to commercial traders?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mafo mitsei lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ midu nii? Ni kɛji akɛ miitsu okwaayeli koni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ jarayelɔi hu?

english: Proper spacing gives each plant enough soil, water, and sunlight to grow uniform produce of equal size and quality, which commercial traders prefer over small or uneven harvests.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tamɔ amɛhe ni dalɛ kɛ amɛhe yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. ni jarayeli jarayelɔi sumɔɔ fe ŋmaa bibii loo ni akpaaa daa lɛ

english: What makes a harvested crop attractive to market buyers in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ feɔ nɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ sumɔɔ?

english: Market buyers look for clean, damage-free produce of uniform size that stays fresh longer. Proper fertilization, pest control, and harvesting at the right maturity stage help achieve this.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ taoɔ nibii ni he tse, ni nɔ ko nɔ ko efiteee, ni amɛdalɛ tamɔ amɛhe, ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. fɔmɔ nii ni sa ni akɛyeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ashɛɔ oti nɛɛ he.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leaf growth, or that the roots are drowning in waterlogged soil. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted compost can help them regain their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ loo shishifãi ni ebote shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua amɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛsu ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with bushy leaves, but producing tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai bibii, shi ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil contains too much nitrogen and not enough potassium, cassava plants focus all their energy on growing leaves above ground instead of feeding the tubers below. Balanced soil nutrients and potassium help encourage heavy tuber growth.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium faaa lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he nii moŋ fe ni eeeha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ niyenii. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja kɛ potassium haa ŋmeii lɛ daa.

english: What is causing small holes in my maize leaves and sawdust-like powder inside the plant tops?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmãa ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ tsei ashishifãi amli lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds on young leaves inside the center whorl of the maize plant. Early inspection and applying recommended botanical treatments or insecticides when caterpillars are small helps control them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Kwɛmɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Ni akɛ tsofai loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi lɛ baatsu nii beni ŋmeii lɛ darako lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cold, wet weather. Pruning excess canopy leaves to allow sunlight and airflow, along with picking off infected pods early, reduces the spread of the fungus.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ fɛ̃i, fɛ̃i be mli lɛ kɛbaa. Afoɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. kɛfata pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anaabuamɔ mra he. Ebaaye ebua ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ aba shi.

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is usually caused by bacterial wilt or root rot fungi that block the movement of water inside the plant stems. Rotating your fields with crops like maize or cassava breaks the disease cycle in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ji bacteria wilt loo fungal root rot ni tsiɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ naa lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa Ebaakpa helai ni yaa nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or lack of phosphorus. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch around the base helps the plant hold onto its flowers and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo fɔsfɔs ni faaa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why should I clear extra shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishitoo

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, compete with the main tree for water, sunlight, and nutrients, leading to smaller plantain bunches. Keeping only one main stem, one medium sucker, and one small sucker ensures maximum bunch weight.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei krokomɛi loo tsei lɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii. Ni aaahi tso titri kome pɛ nɔ Sucker ni dalɛ ji teŋgbɛ kɛ sucker bibioo kome Enɛ baaha aná ŋmeii ni fa fe fɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to direct heat and strong sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides living umbrellas that shield the seedlings from heat while they develop strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ cocoa masɛi lɛ haa shade ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ latsaa he yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why are my maize seeds taking so long to germinate after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize seeds delay or fail to germinate if planted too deep in the soil, planted in dry ground, or eaten by soil pests. Planting seeds about 2 to 3 centimeters deep in moist soil ensures rapid and uniform sprouting.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya loo amɛkwɛɛɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ. ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ aaafee sɛntimitai 2 kɛyashi 3 lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting early in the barn before I can take them to market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miije shishi ekwɛ̃ mra yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? dani akɛba jara nɔ?

english: Yams sprout naturally when exposed to heat and moisture in warm storage areas. Storing yams on raised, airy racks inside a cool, shaded, and well-ventilated barn slows down sprouting and keeps tubers fresh longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes baakwɛ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji akɛ amɛwo dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i mli yɛ hei ni akɛ nibii toɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ. Abaanyɛ akɛ sweet potato ato adeka ni awó nɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ fioo ni eye ebua ni bulbs lɛ ahi shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my soil is good enough to grow maize on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Doing a soil analysis allows experts to test samples of your land to check its nutrient levels and structure, showing you exactly whether maize will grow well or if you need to fix the soil first.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ niiamlipɛimɔ haa ŋaalɔi kaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii komɛi amɛkwɛɔ koni amɛna niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha. Enɛ baatsɔɔ bo faŋŋ kɛji ŋmãa lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ loo ebaakwɛ̃ŋ jogbaŋŋ. Aloo ehe miihia ni osaa shikpɔŋ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: What actually happens when an extension officer takes my soil sample for laboratory testing?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ extension nitsulɔ ko ŋɔ mi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ koni eyaka lɛ yɛ laboratorio mli?

english: The laboratory breaks down your soil to measure its pH level, organic matter, and essential nutrients, which helps create a accurate report of what your soil needs to support healthy crops.
ga: Lab lɛ gbalaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛsusu pH, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ mli lɛ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni afeɔ amaniɛbɔɔ ni ja ni kɔɔ nɔ ni he hiaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ koni eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ he.

english: If my soil is poor, does that mean I can never plant demanding crops like tomatoes on my land?
ga: Kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ minyɛɛɛ madu nibii ni asumɔɔ tamɔ tomato yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Not necessarily. Soil testing reveals specific nutrient deficiencies in your land, allowing you to treat the soil with targeted fertilizers or manure to make it suitable for crops like tomatoes.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ ko ni faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kpo. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ tsuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii koni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tomatoi lɛ akpã gbee.

english: Why does cassava grow very well in my neighbor's town, but fails when I plant it in my village?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mikutsoŋnyo maŋ lɛ mli lɛ? Shi eyeee omanye beni midu yɛ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Soil types vary across different communities and areas; soil maps show that land in one village may hold water or nutrients differently than land just a few kilometers away.
ga: Shikpɔŋ henɔi lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ akutsei kɛ hei amli. Shikpɔŋ he mfoniri tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ akrowa kome mli lɛ baanyɛ aná nu loo niyenii ni yɔɔ srɔto fe shikpɔŋ ni kɛ jɛmɛ jɛkɛmɔ ji kilomitai fioo ko pɛ lɛ.

english: How can I tell which crop is best to plant on a new piece of land I just acquired?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ madu yɛ shikpɔŋ hee ni minine eshɛ nɔ amrɔ nɛɛ nɔ?

english: You can consult local extension officers who use soil maps and tests for your area to match your land's specific soil characteristics with the crops that will grow best there.
ga: Obaanyɛ oyabi maŋ lɛ mli shweremɔ he nitsulɔ ko ni kɛ shikpɔŋ he mfoniri tsuɔ nii ni ekaa he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ekwɛɔ koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ su pɔtɛɛ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nakai kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ akpã gbee.

english: Why do agricultural extension officers sometimes recommend that our whole community plant the same type of crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akutsei muu fɛɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Researchers map out soils by area, and when a whole community shares a similar soil type that naturally favors a specific crop, planting that crop yields the best harvest for everyone.
ga: Nibii amlitaolɔi saa shikpɔŋ he mfoniri yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ naa. Ni beni akutso muu lɛ fɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ henɔ kome ni jɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ fiɔ tso pɔtɛɛ ko sɛɛ lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha mɔ fɛɛ mɔ aná ŋmaa ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my corn plants turning yellow even though I give them enough rain and water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nugbɔ kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, which a soil analysis can identify so you know exactly which fertilizer to apply.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mlipɛimɔ baanyɛ ana lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ ole ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ okɛtsu nii.

english: Should I use the exact same fertilizer that farmers in the next community are using on their crops?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okwaafoi ni yɔɔ akutso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii yɛ amɛŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii?

english: No, because soil composition changes from place to place, meaning your soil might need different nutrients than the soil in neighboring communities.
ga: Dabi, ejaakɛ nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ he fɛɛ he kɛyaa he kroko. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ baaná niyenii mli hewalɛ he hiamɔ nii sɔrɔtoi fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ akutsei ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants rot at the roots during the rainy season while pepper on nearby farms survives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli yɛ be mli ni pepper ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo lɛ?

english: Different soils absorb and drain water at different rates; heavy clay soils trap excess water around roots and cause rot, whereas looser soils drain water freely.
ga: Shikpɔji srɔtoi shwieɔ nu ni amɛjieɔ nu yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nu ni fa fe nine ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. shishifãi kɛ fitemɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni etse ehe lɛ baaho nu oya.

english: Why did my yam harvest get smaller after I planted yams on the exact same plot for three years in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ ba shi beni midu sweet potato yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously depletes specific nutrients from the soil; analyzing your soil helps you see what nutrients were lost so you can restore the soil's health.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niiamlipɛimɔ yeɔ ebua bo ni onaa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni miiho lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okɛ hewalɛ aba oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains on the same land with my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to strong sunlight and high heat. Planting plantains alongside them provides natural shade and keeps the soil cool and moist while the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand direct sun.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. plantains ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo aba ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Beni cacao tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa lɛ,

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks essential nutrients, especially nitrogen, or when flooded soil prevents roots from breathing. Applying manure or nitrogen fertilizer usually restores their healthy green color.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. titri lɛ nitrogen loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkamu. Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start to rot in the ground during heavy rain seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Excess water in heavy soil cuts off oxygen to the cassava roots, creating conditions for fungi and bacteria to cause tuber rot. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shihilɛi baa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni haa ŋmeii fiteɔ lɛ anɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do I need to guide my yam vines to climb up wooden stakes instead of letting them trail on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makudɔ sweet potato wain tso ko kɛya tso tso ko nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha enyiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves into sunlight so they can produce more food, while keeping them off hot soil and away from ground diseases, resulting in much larger tubers.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la nɔ koni amɛná niyenii babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ adɔ fe nine, ni ekɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akabɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yitso lɛ feɔ agbo kwraa.

english: Why should I cut away some of the young suckers growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ ekomɛi amli lɛ?

english: Too many suckers compete with the main plantain tree for nutrients and water. Removing extra shoots leaves only one or two strong suckers, ensuring your plantain tree produces large bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ baahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha o-plantains lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does covering the soil around my vegetables with dry grass help them survive dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mi-vegetables lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, shields the ground from direct sunlight, reducing water evaporation and keeping the crop roots cool and moist.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aba shi ni eha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do I see holes in my young maize leaves and tiny caterpillars inside the central funnels?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa bu yɛ ŋmãa bibii amli kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, which feed on the growing centers of maize plants. Identifying them early allows you to use recommended organic or chemical controls before they destroy the yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni miida lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. mra be mli ni ayɔseɔ Enɛ baaha okɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni akɛbuɔ he lɛ atsu nii dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are extremely high, when there is irregular watering, or when the soil lacks key nutrients like calcium and phosphorus required for fruit development.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa. Be mli ni nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ daa loo be mli ni niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium kɛ phosphorus ni he hiaa koni aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it beneficial to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. Planting them after nutrient-hungry crops like maize naturally restores soil fertility.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ adu nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni niyenii he hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce smaller yields even when I water the farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo yibii fioo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa moŋ?

english: Weeds compete aggressively with your crops for sunlight, soil nutrients, water, and space. Clearing weeds early ensures all the water and nutrients go directly into growing your crops.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ ŋwɛi, ni ajieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ mli mra. Enɛ haa nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ yaa onibii ni odu lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on orange trees usually mean the plant is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen or magnesium in the soil, or that the soil is holding too much water around the roots. Adding composted animal manure or a balanced fertilizer can help restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ citrus tsei anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen loo magnesium yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ nu babaoo tsɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young oranges fall off the tree before they get a chance to grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange bibii lɛ miigbee shi kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Fruit drop in orange trees happens when the tree experiences stress from dry spells, poor nutrient levels, or attacks by fruit flies and sap-sucking insects. Giving the trees extra water during dry periods and managing pests early helps the fruit stay on the branch until harvest.
ga: Yibii ni gbeeɔ citrus tsei anɔ lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli. niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ehiii Aloo aduawai amli ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ tutuaa. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei yɛ hɔmɔ be mli kɛ mra be mli ni akwɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ Enɛ baaye abua ni aduawai lɛ ahi tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ kɛyashi kpamɔ be mli.

english: Why do my crops yield better when I clear weeds regularly from around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai kɛ́ mijie jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive competitors that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Clearing them gives your crops full access to these vital resources, allowing them to grow stronger and produce a bigger harvest.
ga: Jwɛi ji akaŋshilɔi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná nibii ni he hiaa nɛɛ ahe gbɛ kwraa. Ye obua amɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛkpa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why is it bad for my crop harvest if I plant my seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiii kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants end up fighting each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with thin, weak plants that produce very small fruits or grains compared to properly spaced plants.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ baawuu koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ baaha oná tso bibioo ko ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii loo dumɔwui bibii kwraa kɛ akɛto tso ni akɛto he ni sa lɛ he.

english: How can I tell if my soil needs fertilizer before I start planting my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii dani mabɔi tsei akwɛmɔ?

english: If your previous crop grew slowly, had pale or stunted leaves, or produced a very small yield despite getting enough rain, your soil is likely low on nutrients and needs organic manure or chemical fertilizer to feed the next crop.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii ni odu tsutsu lɛ dara blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni etse loo egbɔjɔ loo ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa moŋ Etamɔ nɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ hu mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa ni ehe miihia ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: What causes small ragged holes in my maize leaves, and how does it hurt the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa mli lɛ baa, ni te eyeɔ tso lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Holes in maize leaves are typically caused by destructive pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They chew through the leaves, reducing the plant's ability to turn sunlight into food, which leaves the corn plants weak and produces smaller ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii tamɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai amli lɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ baai lɛ. Ehaa nyɛmɔ ni tsei yɔɔ ni amɛkɛtsakeɔ hulu la ni amɛfeɔ niyenii lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni ehaa toi lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: What causes white powder or dark spots to spread across the leaves of my crops?
ga: Mɛni haa powda yɛŋ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ?

english: White powder or dark spots are common signs of fungal diseases, which thrive in wet conditions or when plants are crowded together with poor air movement. Trimming overcrowded leaves and avoiding spraying water directly on the leaves helps slow the spread.
ga: Pauda yɛŋ loo ŋmɔtɔ ji ŋmɔtɔ hela he okadii ni afɔɔ namɔ. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ mli loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Kɛ́ afolɔ baai ni eyi obɔ kɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my cassava roots sometimes turn soft and rot under the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long in heavy, poorly drained soil during heavy rains. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows water to drain away quickly, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Young cocoa plants have thin leaves and delicate roots that dry out very quickly under strong, hot sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains near them creates a temporary protective canopy that shields the cocoa seedlings until they are mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni gbɛ́ɔ oya waa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa be kukuoo mli ŋtayaa ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my vegetable crops droop and wilt in the hot afternoon sun even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ miiho ni amɛmiigboi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji mikɛ nu wo nɔ leebi po.

english: During intense afternoon heat, leaves lose water faster through evaporation than roots can draw up from the ground, causing the plant to temporarily droop to protect itself. As long as the soil underground is moist, the plants will recover once the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gboɔ be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu ehe. Be abɔ ni shikpɔŋ shishi sũ lɛ mli edɔ lolo lɛ Tsei lɛ naa hewalɛ kɛji hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and have broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, shielding the cocoa seedlings from direct sun while keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋtayaai. Buu kookoo dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads easily during rainy and humid periods. Pruning trees to allow sunlight and airflow, along with removing infected pods early, helps prevent it.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Tsei ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli Agbɛnɛ hu Jiemɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu ohe.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize farm turn light yellow after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall can wash essential nitrogen nutrients out of the root zone deep into the soil. Without enough nitrogen, the plant cannot maintain its dark green color and the leaves begin to turn yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen nibii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ ahiɛ su ni ji eŋɔli ni mli edɔ mli. Ni baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔŋ tsɔmɔ.

english: Why should I rotate my maize crop with groundnuts next season instead of planting maize again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli moŋ fe ni madu ŋmãa ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the soil, while groundnuts actually take nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. Rotating them restores natural fertility to your soil without relying as heavily on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ otsake amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ ni okɛ ohe afɔ̃ɔɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ waa.

english: When cowpea soil has too much nitrogen or rich compost, the plant puts its energy into growing big leaves instead of flowers. Cowpeas naturally fix their own nitrogen, so they need balanced nutrients to produce good pods.
ga: Kɛji cowpea shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai wuji yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Cowpeas saa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni ená niyenii ni sa koni enyɛ ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa aba.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and show yellowish patches during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by the cassava mosaic virus, which is spread by small whiteflies that multiply quickly in warm weather. The virus damages the leaves and prevents the plant from growing big tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Whiteflies bibii ni fɔɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa. Virus lɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ ni etsĩɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ bulbs wuji.

english: Why do the leaves on my yam vines droop and fold during the hottest time of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ sweet potato wain tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Yam vines temporarily fold or curl their leaves in intense afternoon sun to cut down on moisture loss. It is a natural survival trick to preserve water, and the leaves will normally bounce back as the day cools down.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli loo amɛfoɔ amɛ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Eji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ ŋaa ni akɛbuɔ nu he. Ni baai lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba shi bɔ ni sa beni amɛhe jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when exposed to stress, such as very high temperatures, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients like phosphorus. Consistent watering and mulching can help keep flowers attached.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot and is caused by a shortage of calcium in the growing fruit, often triggered by irregular watering where the soil dries out completely between waterings.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kwraa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ.

english: Why do my garden eggs turn bitter even when they look ripe and healthy on the outside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ŋɔɔ waa eyɛ mli akɛ amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ yɛ kponɔgbɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Garden eggs become bitter when the plant experiences water stress or when the fruits stay on the bush too long past their peak harvest time. Picking them regularly while firm helps keep the sweet, mild flavor.
ga: Tso yibii abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ tsei lɛ na nu he haomɔ loo kɛ́ aduawai lɛ hi jwɛi lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ni eho kpamɔ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ he. Kɛ́ aŋɔ loo lɛ daa be mli ni loo lɛ mli wa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔ ni ŋɔɔ fioo lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential food for green growth. When nitrogen in the soil runs low, the plant takes food from its older bottom leaves and sends it to the younger top leaves to keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Beni nitrogen fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ ŋɔɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli ni amɛkɛyaa ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ anɔ koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my ripening tomatoes turning black and rotting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by a lack of calcium inside the fruit, often brought on by uneven watering. When soil dries out completely and then gets soaked, the plant cannot move calcium to the fruit quickly enough, causing the tissue at the bottom to collapse.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa ni edɔ. Tso lɛ nyɛŋ ajie calcium kɛya aduawai lɛ amli oya bɔ ni sa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fãji ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ akpãtãmɔ.

english: Why do I need to guide my yam vines up wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ awo tso ko nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam vines need to climb high into the sunlight so their leaves can catch maximum light to create energy. Lifted leaves make more food, which is sent down into the ground to build much larger and healthier tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi. koni ená hulu la Enɛ haa ebaai lɛ naa la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛfee hewalɛ. Baai ni awo nɔ lɛ feɔ niyenii babaoo. Akɛ enɛɛmɛi majeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni akɛfee bulbs wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants stay short and bushy without producing many branches or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɔɔ kuku ni eyɛ ŋmɔ mli ni niji loo aduawai babaoo bɛ he lɛ?

english: Pepper plants often stay stunted if the soil is too hard for their roots to spread or if microscopic worms called nematodes are attacking the roots. Giving roots loose soil and organic compost helps them branch out and grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. Aloo kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ miitutua shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ha shishifãi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ niji amli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my cabbage plants keep growing big leaves without ever forming a hard, tight ball in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? Ni afeee nɔ ko ni wa yɛ teŋgbɛ kɔkɔɔkɔ?

english: Cabbages fail to form tight heads if the weather gets too hot or if they receive too much nitrogen fertilizer late in their growth. Too much food for leaves makes the plant keep spreading open instead of wrapping inward.
ga: Kaabaji lɛ ewaŋ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛji akɛ enine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ yɛ be mli ni edaa blɛoo lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ baai lɛ ye nii fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ agbele babaoo moŋ fe ni eeefo ehe kɛya mli.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into small green tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when extreme heat or dry winds dry out the pollen inside the flower, preventing fertilization. Without pollination, the plant drops the useless flower to save its energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ latsaa ni naa wa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ ha fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa Kɛji pollination bɛ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa amɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark brown and soft on the tree before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiifee blɛoo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ po lɛ?

english: Pods turn dark and soft due to Black Pod disease, which is caused by a tiny fungus that spreads rapidly during heavy rain and high humidity. The fungus enters through small wounds or water droplets left sitting on the pod skin.
ga: Pods lɛ yɛ ediŋŋ ni eyɛ bɔdɔɔ yɛ black pod hela, ni ŋmei bibioo ko kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ. No gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Fungus boteɔ mli kɛtsɔɔ pilamɔi bibii amli. loo nu mli nu ni shwieɔ shi ni kpɛtɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahewolo he

english: Why do the leaves of my cowpea crop roll inward during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is the plant's smart way of protecting itself from hot sun and dry air. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to heat, keeping water locked inside until cooler evening hours.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji ŋaa gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ he. Tsei haa he ni hulutsoo baa amɛnɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa nu lɛ hiɔ mli kɛyashiɔ gbɛkɛ mli ni edɔɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava roots are fully grown without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni okɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava shows it is mature when its lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stem with leaves only at the top. You can also spot ground cracks around the base of the stem where thick roots are pushing up the soil.
ga: Yucca jieɔ dalɛ kpo kɛ́ eshishi baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ yitso ni bɛ nɔ ko ni baai yɔɔ nɔ lɛ pɛ eshwɛ. Obaanyɛ ona ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli lolo. Tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ shishifãi ni mli tse lɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know when a watermelon is ripe and ready to pick off the vine?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ watermelon lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ ajie lɛ?

english: Check the small curly tendril on the vine right next to where the melon stem connects. When that tendril turns brown and dry like wire, and the spot where the melon rests on the ground turns from white to pale yellow, it is ready.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli. Yɛ wain tso ni bɛŋkɛ he ni melon tso lɛ tsaa lɛ nɔ. Beni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi tamɔ waya lɛ, Ni he ni watermelon lɛ kã shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse mli. Tsɔɔmɔ akɛ ofee klalo.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize is running low on nitrogen, which is essential plant food. When the crop lacks nutrients, it pulls energy from its older bottom leaves to feed the young top leaves and growing corn cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa Kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ Ejieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli ni ekɛhaa ŋwɛi baa bibii lɛ kɛ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing tall and leafy but not producing any flowers or peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi loo ŋmeii komɛi bɛ?

english: When pepper plants get too much nitrogen fertilizer or manure, they spend all their energy growing green leaves and stems instead of producing flowers and fruit. Reducing nitrogen helps the plant switch to fruiting.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛduɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yiblii. Nitrogen ni abaaba shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtsakeɔ kɛyaa yibiiwoo nɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers split open or grow in twisted shapes under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miijara loo amɛmiidara yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers split or deform when the soil is too hard and stony, or when a heavy rain follows a long dry period, causing the inside of the tuber to expand faster than its outer skin can stretch.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baagbala loo amɛbaafite kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni tɛi babaoo yɛ mli. Aloo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa nyiɛ sɛɛ be kakadaŋŋ, ni eha egbi, ni eha yitso lɛ mligbɛ lɛ mli lɛɛ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings shrivel and die when the dry Harmattan winds start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate root systems that cannot pull water fast enough to replace what the dry Harmattan wind sucks out of their leaves. Planting shade crops like plantains protects young cocoa from direct sun and drying winds.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ agbala nu oya bɔ ni sa ni ekɛye nɔ ni harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli lɛ najiaŋ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa egbiɔ lɛ he.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high or when rainfall is irregular. Extreme heat stresses the plant, preventing proper pollination so the flower drops instead of forming fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ be fɛɛ be. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Ehaa enyɛɛɛ ekɛ fɔfɔii awo mli No sɛɛ lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ yibiiwoo najiaŋ.

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit at the top. Soft, wet soil from heavy rain loosens the roots' grip, allowing strong winds to push the top-heavy plants over.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai ni tsii yɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni jɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ haa shishifãi ni kpɛtɛɔ he lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ atswa tsei kɛ amɛ ŋwɛi tsiimɔ lɛ.

english: Curling and sticky leaves are caused by tiny insects like aphids feeding on the sap underneath the leaves. As they suck the plant juices, they leave behind a sticky liquid that attracts mold and weakens the plant.
ga: Kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ekpɛtɛɔ he lɛ baa. beni amɛmuɔ tso mli nu lɛ Amɛshiɔ nu ni mli tse ni gbalaa ŋmeii ni haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ lɛ amɛshwieɔ amɛsɛɛ.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting right in the ground before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Mature cassava roots rot in the ground when heavy rains make the soil waterlogged. Excess water starves the roots of air, allowing rot fungi in the soil to attack and destroy the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi ni edara lɛ fiteɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa, ni no haa nu shwieɔ sũ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ hɔmɔ aba shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni egboi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes turn soft and spoil so quickly before I can sell them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya dani abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes are living produce that continue to breathe and ripen rapidly after being picked. Heat speeds up this process, so keeping harvested tomatoes in cool, shaded, ventilated crates prevents heat buildup and slows down decay.
ga: Tomato ji nibii ni hiɛ ka ni yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ ni amɛshwereɔ oya kɛji ajie amɛ. Dɔlɛ baaha nifeemɔ nɛɛ aya oya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tomato ni akpa lɛ to adeka ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulutsoo akafee ekome ni ekɛ fitemɔ aba sɛɛ.

english: Why do my stored maize grains get tiny holes and turn into dust after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni etsɔ sũ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli?

english: Tiny holes and dusty grain are caused by grain weevils and borers that lay eggs inside the dried maize. Protecting stored grain in airtight containers or treating it properly prevents these insects from multiplying.
ga: Buji bibii kɛ sũ dumɔwui lɛ jɛɔ dumɔwui amli ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa ni egbi mli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ abu ŋmaa ni akɛto tsɛnsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ ahe loo akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkafa babaoo.

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade to survive because direct sunlight dries out the soil and burns their tender leaves. Leaving or planting shade trees like plantains protects young cocoa until their stems grow thick and strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ ni eshãa amɛbaai bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ oshi loo odu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi eshishifãi lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: This is usually Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet, and dark conditions. Clearing weeds and pruning extra branches helps sunlight and air flow through the farm to stop the disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, fɔ́, kɛ duŋ kɛbaa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei krokomɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛkpa hela lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are a sign that the plant is starving for nitrogen, an important food in the soil. Adding poultry manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn green again so the plant can grow big.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmɔŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ koni tsei lɛ adara.

english: How can I tell if caterpillars are attacking my maize field, and what damage do they cause?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmeii miitutua mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ? Ni mɛɛ fitemɔ amɛfiteɔ?

english: If you see ragged holes in the leaves and small sawdust-like dirt inside the center of the maize stem, your crop likely has Fall Armyworms. These caterpillars eat the leaves and growing points, which can destroy the harvest if not treated early.
ga: Kɛji ona bu ni etse ehe yɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛ muji bibii ni tamɔ ŋmei yɛ ŋmei tso lɛ teŋgbɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ asraafoi aŋmeii emɔ onibii amli. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ yeɔ baai kɛ hei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii mra.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge leafy branches but very thin roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ niji kɛ baai wuji shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are crowded too close together, cassava puts all its energy into growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers below.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo kɛ tsei lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ amɛhe tsɔ Yucca kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye ní ngɛ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot quickly inside the soil before I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani manyɛ mafo amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them without draining, especially in heavy clay soil during rainy seasons. Planting on raised soil mounds or ridges allows water to run off safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu shwie shi ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Titri lɛ, yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa waa nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Is it good to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the same land after harvesting maize?
ga: Kɛ́ akpa ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ, ani ehi akɛ aaadu tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Yes, planting legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts rebuilds the soil because these plants pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the earth, making the soil fertile again for future crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ehee. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei nɛɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why should I wait for steady rains before planting my seeds instead of planting at the very first rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa dani madu dumɔwui moŋ fe ni madu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔi fioo lɛ amli lɛ?

english: The very first rainfall of the season is often followed by a hot dry spell. If seeds germinate after one rain and then experience dry weather, the weak seedlings will dry up and die.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ latsaa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome sɛɛ ni no sɛɛ lɛ ena kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi. Dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ baagbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies. These insects drink the sap from the plant and can spread viruses that stunt leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kooloi nɛɛ nuɔ tsei amli nu lɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai ni tsiɔ baai lɛ adalɛ naa lɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers but drop them without forming tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi eshieee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer, which prevents the blossoms from turning into fruit.
ga: Tomato baashwie efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ hao lɛ. ni tsiɔ fɔfɔii anaa koni amɛkatsɔ aduawai

english: What should I do to save my crops if the rain stops unexpectedly after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ akafite kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa beni midu nii sɛɛ?

english: When the rains hold off, you can cover the soil around your crops with dry grass or leaves (mulching) to trap moisture, and water them manually early in the morning so the water does not evaporate in the sun.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa Obaanyɛ okɛha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulch) aha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ koni emɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ni okɛ nu awo ohe leebi maŋkpa koni nu lɛ akatsɔ hulutsoo be mli.

english: How can I tell if my okra plants are struggling because of a lack of water or because of a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi okra tso lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔ yɛ nu ni bɛ loo hela hewɔ?

english: Plants lacking water will wilt during the hot afternoon but recover in the cool evening, whereas diseased plants will usually show permanent leaf spots, yellowing, or curling that does not go away at night.
ga: Tsei ni nu bɛ mli lɛ baagbi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Shi ebaatsa yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ baai ni hiɔ shi daa, ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ni ebɔle amɛhe ni sɛɛ efooo gbɛkɛ mli.

english: Why do some crops survive dry weather better than others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi hiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli jogbaŋŋ fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Crops like cassava and millet have deep root systems or special leaves that store water, while shallow-rooted crops like okra and vegetables rely heavily on regular rain near the soil surface.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo baai krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tamɔ okra kɛ aduawai kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my seeds when the rainfall pattern keeps changing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui? Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ tsakeɔ be fɛɛ be

english: Instead of relying on a fixed calendar date, test the soil moisture after the first rain by digging a few inches deep; sow your seeds only when the soil stays moist and sticky below the surface.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ ohe afɔ̃ kalanda gbii pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ lɛ. Kaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ okwɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni ooofo mli kɛyashɛ inchi fioo komɛi lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ dumɔwui pɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shishigbɛ.

english: Why do my seeds fail to grow well if I plant them right after the very first light rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ sɛɛ?

english: A light rain only wets the top layer of soil, which dries out quickly under the sun and scorches fragile young roots; seeds need a deep, soaking rain to establish strong roots.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. Egbiɔ oya yɛ hulu lɛ shishi ni eshãa shishifãi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ. Nugbɔ kpakpa he miihia dumɔwui koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Does planting okra at the wrong time of the season reduce the amount of harvest I get?
ga: Ani okra ni aduɔ yɛ be ni ejaaa mli lɛ baaha ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ aba shi?

english: Yes, planting okra when water is scarce stunts its growth, causing the plant to produce fewer flowers and small, tough pods instead of abundant, tender fruits.
ga: Hɛɛ, okra ni aduɔ yɛ be mli ni nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ baaha edalɛ aya hiɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi fioo kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni wa yɛ yibii ni jara wa ni fa babaoo najiaŋ.

english: What quick-yielding crops can I plant to earn fast income while waiting for the main farming season?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii oya manyɛ madu koni maná shika oya yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ okwaayeli be titri lɛ?

english: Fast-growing crops like okra, leafy greens, and radishes mature within 60 to 90 days, allowing you to harvest and sell quickly for immediate cash while preparing for long-term crops.
ga: Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ okra, tsei ni yɔɔ baai, kɛ radishes baakwɛ̃ yɛ gbii 60 kɛyashi 90 mli, ni no baaha onyɛ okpa amɛ oya ni ohɔ̃ɔ koni onine ashɛ shika nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ be mli ni osaa ohe kɛha be kakadaŋŋ mli dumɔ.

english: Is it wise to grow okra during the dry season to get higher market prices?
ga: Ani esa akɛ adu okra yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni anyɛ ana jara ni nɔ kwɔ?

english: Dry-season okra can bring high profits because supply is low, but it requires a reliable water source like a well or river irrigation system to keep the plants alive without rain.
ga: Okra ni yɔɔ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ baanyɛ aná sɛɛnamɔ babaoo yɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ fioo lɛ hewɔ. Shi ebiɔ nu jɛɛhe ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ, tamɔ nubu loo faa mli nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi. koni tsei anyɛ ahi shi kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ

english: How does poor rainfall affect the market quality of the okra pods I harvest?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ saa okra ŋmeii ni mikpaa lɛ ahe jarayeli he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When okra plants do not get enough water, the pods become fibrous, hard, and thin, which makes buyers reject them or pay much lower prices compared to plump, soft pods.
ga: Beni gumbo tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ bafeɔ ŋmeii, amɛhe wa, ni amɛhe tseee, ni no haa mɛi ni heɔ lɛ kpooɔ amɛ loo amɛwoɔ jara ni baa shi kwraa fe ŋmeii ni mli ewo muji lɛ.

english: How do I plan my farming expenses so I do not lose money if the weather turns bad?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mato shika ni mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ okwaayeli mli lɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ lɛ mli bawo wu lɛ, mikafite shika?

english: Stagger your planting dates into smaller portions instead of planting everything at once, and purchase certified seeds early so you can replant efficiently if an early dry spell ruins the first plot.
ga: Jaa gbi ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ mli bibii bibii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu nɔ fɛɛ nɔ shikome Ni ohé dumɔwui ni awo he odase mra. Enɛ ji koni onyɛ odu ekoŋŋ jogbaŋŋ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ fite klɛŋklɛŋ shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants turn yellow when rainwater sits on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nugbɔ enɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: When rainwater pools on your field without draining, it chokes the soil and starves the roots of air. Without air, the roots cannot absorb nutrients, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nu ho kɛtee ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli ni nu bɛ mli lɛ Emɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: What can I do to stop water from standing and gathering in the middle of my farmland after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni abaanyɛ afee koni nu akadamɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ ateŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ?

english: You can dig small drainage channels or ditches across your field to guide the excess rainwater away from your crops and off the land into a safe discharge area.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nu gbɛ bibioo ko. loo ŋmeii ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔji amli koni akɛtsɔɔ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ gbɛ kɛjɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya he ko ni nu hoɔ yɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: How can I prevent heavy rainwater from washing away my topsoil and young crops on sloping land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekashwie shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni yɔɔ mi gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Planting your crop rows across the slope (contour farming) or building small soil ridges helps slow down flowing rainwater, keeping your fertile soil and young plants in place.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋji lɛ ahe (contour farming) loo shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii ni afee Ebaaye ebua ni nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ kɛ tsei bibii lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Should I apply my fertilizer right before a big rainstorm comes?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ wulu ko aba?

english: No, you should wait until after heavy rains pass or when light rain is expected. Heavy downpours will wash the fertilizer away before your crops can drink it in.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eho loo nugbɔ fioo ko baanɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nuɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because excess moisture encourages soil fungi and bacteria to attack the soft roots when they cannot get fresh air.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni mli edɔ fe nine lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua shishifãi bibii lɛ beni amɛnyɛŋ amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers drop off my pepper plants after a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain physically knocks delicate flowers off the plant, and sudden excess water stresses the plant, forcing it to drop its blossoms instead of producing fruit.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ shwieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ. Ni trukaa lɛ, nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nyɛ fɔfɔi anɔ koni amɛgbee shi moŋ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do white spots and mold appear on my tomato leaves during continuous wet weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ kɛ ŋmeii jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-tomato baai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa nɔ lɛ?

english: Continuous rain and high moisture in the air create a perfect environment for fungal diseases to multiply rapidly on damp plant leaves.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya yɛ tsei ahe baai ni mli efɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Which crops can I safely plant in low-lying areas of my farm where water naturally collects?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ makwɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni nu buaa ehe naa yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ?

english: Crops like rice and cocoyam (taro) thrive in wet, swampy soils, whereas crops like maize, cowpea, or peppers will quickly rot in flooded conditions.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ omɔ kɛ kookoo (taro) kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, tsina loo ŋmãa fiteɔ oya yɛ nu afua shihilɛi amli.

english: Why are my crops growing very slowly even though my field receives plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ lɛ? Ni miŋmɔji lɛ ná nugbɔ ni naa wa?

english: Too much rain can flush vital nutrients deep out of reach of plant roots and leave the soil cold and airless, which temporarily stops crops from growing.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ he kɛya shɔŋŋ kɛjɛ tsei shishifãi amli. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ hu bɛ mli Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa be kukuoo ko koni ekakwɛ̃.

english: What happens to my harvested maize if I leave it on the ground in the field when it rains?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ nɔ kɛji mishi yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔ mli beni nugbɔ miinɛ lɛ?

english: Rain soaked harvested maize absorbs moisture rapidly, encouraging destructive molds and toxins to grow, which ruins the grain for eating or selling.
ga: Abɛi ni akɛ nu ewo mli lɛ shwieɔ nu oya. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tsofai fɔji ni baafite dalɛ lɛ yaa hiɛ. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa lɛ afite koni aye loo ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: How many maize seeds should I plant in a single hole to get a good yield?
ga: Abele dumɔwui enyiɛ esa akɛ adu yɛ bu kome mli koni aná yibiiwoo kpakpa?

english: Planting the correct recommended number of maize seeds per hole gives each plant enough room, water, and soil nutrients to grow strong stalks and form full cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ayibɔ ni sa ni atsɔɔ akɛ adu yɛ bu kome mli lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ, nu, kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ ŋmeii ni wa akwɛ̃ ni efee ŋmãa ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why is correct seed spacing important when I am planting maize on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni ja he hiaa beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures that growing crops do not overcrowd and fight each other for sunlight and food, which directly increases your overall harvest output.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni dumɔwui lɛ eyimɔ obɔbɔ fe nine ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ kɛha hulu la kɛ niyenii. Enɛ baaha onitsumɔ lɛ fɛɛ aya hiɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds too deep into the soil?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ?

english: Seeds planted too deep struggle to push up through the soil to reach sunlight, which can cause them to rot underground or sprout into weak, slow-growing plants.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu ni mli kwɔ tsɔ lɛ baatsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya ŋwɛi koni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi loo amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛtsɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni daa blɛoo.

english: Why am I getting a much lower harvest from my maize farm than expected?
