ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ yibiiwoo ni baa shi kwraa kɛjɛɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: A low harvest usually happens when planting instructions are not followed carefully, soil nutrients are poor, weeds are left unchecked, or crops are improperly spaced.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmaa ni baa shi lɛ baa kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni kɔɔ dumɔ he lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Niyenii ni ehiii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Akwɛɛɛ jwɛi lɛ amli. aloo akɛ tsei lɛ ebɔ he yɛ gbɛ ni esaaa nɔ

english: What causes young maize crops to grow unevenly across my field?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa bibii lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Maize grows unevenly when seeds are planted at different depths, when rainfall is not absorbed equally across the land, or when parts of the soil lack good nutrients.
ga: Abɛi daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ kɛ́ adu dumɔwui yɛ hei srɔtoi ni mli kwɔ. Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ falɛ lɛ shɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ fãi komɛi bɛ niyenii kpakpai

english: How do I know if my maize plants are not getting enough food from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: When maize lacks proper soil nutrients, the leaves often turn yellow, the stalks remain thin and short, and the cobs grow small with missing grains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa bɛ niyenii ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. Tso lɛ yitso lɛ yaa nɔ ehiɔ shi ni eyɛ kuku. ni ŋmei lɛ baafee bibioo ni dumɔwui bɛ mli.

english: How can speaking with an agricultural officer help me improve my crop yields?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko ni mikɛ lɛ wieɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi koni ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Agricultural extension officers give expert guidance on proper seed spacing, correct fertilizer use, disease control, and modern techniques suited to your local soil.
ga: Okwaayeli mlilɛɛmɔ nitsulɔi haa ŋaawoo ni he esa yɛ dumɔwui ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ he. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa, helai ahe nitsumɔ kɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋaai ni sa shikpɔŋ ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Where can I get reliable advice if my crops show signs of poor growth during the season?
ga: Nɛgbɛ maná ŋaawoo ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ? Ni kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jieɔ okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ amɛdaraaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be lɛ mli hu?

english: You can visit your local government agricultural officers or community farm extension agents, who can inspect your farm and recommend practical solutions.
ga: Obaanyɛ oyasara omaŋ nɔyeli lɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ loo akutsoŋ ŋmɔ mli shweremɔ he nitsulɔ. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ gbɛi ni baaye abua bo.

english: How does having too few farm workers affect my crop harvest?
ga: Te ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi fioo pɛ ni miyɔɔ lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: If you lack enough workers to complete planting, weeding, and harvesting on time, weeds will choke your crops and unharvested food will spoil in the field.
ga: Kɛji obɛ nitsulɔi ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baadu, amɛbaakpa jwɛi, ni amɛbaakpa yɛ be naa lɛ, Jwɛi baafite onibii. ni niyenii ni akpako lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli.

english: Why do weeds lower the output of my maize farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa nibii ni anáa kɛjɛɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds grow quickly and steal water, sunlight, and plant food away from your crops, leaving the maize weak and unable to produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ewo yibii kpakpai.

english: Can I spread crop diseases to my healthy cocoa farm just by walking through an infected farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ magbɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe hela ashwã mi-kookoo ŋmɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ ŋmɔ ko ni hela lɛ emɔ mli lɛ ni miho kɛkɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, fungal spores, bacteria, and pests can stick to your clothes, boots, or cutlass. Walking directly into a healthy farm after visiting an infected one transfers these microscopic germs to your healthy trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai, helatsɛmɛi, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ akpɛtɛ otadei, o-boots, loo daggers ahe. Kɛ́ oya ŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ beni oyasara ŋmɔ ko ni hela emɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha nɛkɛ helai bibii nɛɛ aya otsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why should I clean my cutlass and tools after pruning my trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsumɔ mi-dagger kɛ nitsumɔ dadei lɛ ahe beni mifo mitsei lɛ?

english: Diseased plant sap sticks to metal blades. If you cut a healthy tree with a blade that touched a sick plant, you directly inject the disease into the fresh cut of the healthy tree.
ga: Tso mli nu ni hela emɔ lɛ kpɛtɛɔ dade ŋmei lɛ he. Kɛji okɛ ŋmei ni kɛ tso ni hela mɔ lɛ kpeɔ lɛ fo tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ Obaafee ni okɛ hela lɛ awo tso hee ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are getting sick before all the pods spoil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cacao tsei lɛ hela mɔ amɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ agboi kwraa?

english: Look out for early warning signs like leaves turning pale yellow, dark spots appearing on young green pods, white powdery spots, or wilting branches. Catching these signs early allows you to treat or isolate the tree before the whole farm gets affected.
ga: Taomɔ kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii mra, tamɔ baai ni miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Hei diji jeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ anɔ. white powder spots loo branches ni egbo Okadii nɛɛ ni ooomɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otsaa tsei loo otsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe dani ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ baaná he sɛɛ.

english: What should I do with cocoa pods that turn black and rot on the tree?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee yɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni tsɔɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ he?

english: You must pluck black pods off the tree immediately and bury them far away from the farm or burn them. Leaving rotten pods on the tree allows wind and rain to splash disease spores onto healthy pods.
ga: Esa akɛ otsi tso lɛ mli ŋmeii diji lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ofu amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he loo oshã amɛ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni egboi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ shwieɔ helai ahe ŋmeii lɛ anɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees need shade trees or plantains planted next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa ni adu tso loo tso bibioo ko ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct hot sun. Fast-growing shade plants like plantains act as living umbrellas, keeping the cocoa cool and moist until it matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa.

english: Can I plant cassava inside my young cocoa farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: It is better to avoid planting cassava too close to young cocoa trees. Cassava grows heavy root systems that aggressively draw nutrients and water away from fragile cocoa roots.
ga: Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmei dumɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ tsɔ. Cassava kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishifãi ni tsii ni gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ kookoo shishifãi ni waaa lɛ amli waa.

english: Why do crop diseases like black pod spread faster during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fungi thrive in high moisture and high humidity. Raindrops bouncing off infected leaves or soil splash disease spores onto nearby healthy pods and leaves, spreading the sickness rapidly.
ga: Mold shwereɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛjɛɔ baai ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ loo hela mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ. ni kɛ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ baa

english: Why is it important for me to prune extra or dead branches off my trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ tsei lɛ aniji ni fa fe nine loo ni egboi lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy so sunlight and air can flow through, which keeps the tree dry and prevents fungal growth. It also helps the tree direct its energy into producing fruits rather than feeding unnecessary leaves.
ga: Kpojiemɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ hu ni ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ yibii moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ tsei ahe tsei ni he ehiaaa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops yield fewer pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo ŋmɔtɔ fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds compete with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. They also create a damp shelter under the trees where harmful insects and diseases can hide and breed.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Amɛfeɔ shĩai ni mli edɔ hu yɛ tsei ashishi he ni kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui baanyɛ ahi amɛhe ni amɛfɔ bii yɛ lɛ.

english: If your plant leaves turn yellow, growth stalls, or pod production drops lower than usual despite good rain, your soil is likely low in nutrients and needs compost or fertilizer to replenish it.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ Growth panels loo pod production lɛ baa shi fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ, ni tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni ekɛwo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your soil is low on nitrogen, a key food maize needs to stay green. Adding fertilizer or well-rotted manure around the plants helps fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni niyenii ni ji ŋmãa lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ wo Ton he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans on my field after harvesting yam?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmei ni ŋɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yams take a lot of food out of the soil, while groundnuts and beans naturally trap nitrogen from the air and feed it back into the earth, making the land fertile for your next crop.
ga: Atomɔ jieɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Emɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyeɔ nii ekoŋŋ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cucumber plants grow so many leaves but very few cucumbers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi kukumba tso lɛ baa babaoo shi kukumba fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer makes the plant focus all its energy on growing leaves instead of flowers and fruit. Using a balanced fertilizer encourages fruit growth.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai anɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha aduawai lɛ adara.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct hot sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide the shade and cool moisture cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa kookoo koni ehi shi lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground when there is heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ŋmeii shishifãi jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when they sit in soaked soil for too long because wet soil starves the roots of air. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji amɛtara shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms before any fruit starts growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛyibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they suffer from sudden dry weather or extreme heat. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch helps the flowers stay on the plant.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛna trukaa kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Kɛ́ akɛ muji wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and become small and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee bibii ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Wrinkled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from under the leaves. Spraying with recommended organic or chemical insect treatments restores normal growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni egbɔjɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekwɛ bɔ ni sa lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do swarms of insects attack my cowpea crop as soon as it flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi akui tutuaa mi-cowpea tsei lɛ kɛji amɛwo fɔfɔi pɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers produce a sweet scent and nectar that attract pests like flower thrips. Inspecting your farm early and applying protection just before flowering saves the pods.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ŋɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fɔfɔi thrips lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ hebuu atsu nii dani fɔfɔi aba lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ akafite.

english: Why do small reddish-brown spots appear all over my rice leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ani su ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni jeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Brown spots on rice leaves are caused by a fungal disease that attacks plants growing in poor soil. Adding the right crop nutrients helps the rice plant resist the fungus.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni tutuaa tsei ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ omɔ baa nɔ. Tso mli niyenii ni sa ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa omɔ tsei ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and carry heavy bunches of fruit, making them top-heavy. Supporting the stems with strong wooden props prevents them from snapping or uprooting.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛwoɔ aduawai babaoo, ni no haa amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekakumɔ loo eshishijee.

english: Why is it good to plant plantain trees alongside my young cocoa plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct heat. Plantains grow quickly and have broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, shielding the young cocoa plants from the hot sun while keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: How do groundnuts help make my soil richer for the next crop I plant?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii baanyɛ aye abua ni eha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni makwɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts have tiny lumps on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. When you harvest them, they leave behind natural fertilizer that nourishes your next crop.
ga: Peanuts yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Beni okpaa lɛ Ebaashi adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from losing water. By hiding part of the leaf surface from the sun, the plant saves its internal moisture until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ shi koni nu akaje mli. Kɛtsɔ baa lɛ nɔ fã ko ni ekɛteeɔ hulu la lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi emli kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of the plant usually mean the maize is hungry for nitrogen. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to the new top leaves to keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa lɛ. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei amli koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are often caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant's juices, causing the leaves to grow out deformed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii, tamɔ mites loo thrips, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni haa baai lɛ daraa kɛjɛɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ mli

english: Why do my cassava plants have huge green tops but very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or water, the cassava plant spends all its food energy growing tall branches and green leaves instead of sending that energy down into the roots to form tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ eniyenii hewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ niji kakadaji kɛ baai eŋɔlii. Mohu ɔ, e ngɔɔ jamɛ a he wami ɔ kɛ yaa sisi ɔ mi konɛ e pee bulb.

english: Why do I need to put wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb on instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maha sweet potato wain tso lɛ tso bibioo ko ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the plant. Lifting the vines on sticks helps all the leaves catch maximum sunlight, which sends more energy down into the ground to build a big tuber.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni efee niyenii eha tso lɛ. Kɛ́ awó wain tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ lɛ, ehaa baa fɛɛ baa naa hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa hewalɛ babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛfee yitso ni da.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet. Extreme weather stresses the plant, causing it to drop its flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ haa tsei haoɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Heavy rain and thick shade create a wet, damp environment where black pod disease flourishes. The fungus thrives in excess water and spreads rapidly from pod to pod.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa haa shihilɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Biɛ ji he ni black pod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Nu ni fa fe nine mli ŋmei lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ ŋmei kome mli kɛyaa ŋmei kroko mli.

english: Why do my young oil palm trees drop their fruit bunches before they get red and ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso bibioo lɛ miiho aduawai akui dani amɛfee tɔrɔmɔɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Young oil palms often drop early fruit bunches because the tree is not mature enough to support them, or because there were not enough tiny pollinating insects around to complete the fruit setup.
ga: Mu tsei bibii lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛshwie aduawai akui yɛ shishijee mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso lɛ daaa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ nɔ. Aloo akɛni pollinators bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ awo yibii lɛ bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my plants with dry grass and leaves before the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi kɛ baai ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mitsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, acts like a protective blanket. It keeps the sun from burning the earth, stops the ground from drying out quickly, and keeps water near the roots for a longer time.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Ye obua ni hulu lɛ akashã shikpɔŋ lɛ. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi oya. ni ehaa nu hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why is it better for me to water my crops early in the morning instead of in the afternoon when it is hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo mitsei lɛ nu leebi moŋ fe shwane be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ?

english: When you water crops in the hot afternoon sun, most of the water evaporates into the air before the roots can drink it. Watering early in the morning allows the soil to absorb the water so the plant stays strong throughout the hot day.
ga: Beni okɛ nu haa onibii yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ. Nu lɛ mli babaoo shwieɔ shi kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnuɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ nu shwieɔ shi. Tso lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbi lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why does adding animal manure to my farm help my crops survive when water is scarce?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmɔ lɛ mli kooloi ashishifãi ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be mli ni nu faaa lɛ?

english: Animal manure acts like a sponge in the soil. It improves the soil's structure so that it can soak up water easily and hold onto that moisture for many days, keeping your crops hydrated longer.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ sũ mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ fɛo bɔni afee ni enyɛ eŋɔ nu oya ni ehiɛ nakai ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo. Ha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee fɛ̃i be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when there is no big tree to shade them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni tsei wuji ni baaha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under full sun. Shade trees act like living umbrellas, providing a cooler environment and protecting the young plants until their roots are deep enough to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ baa ni ebuɔ tso bibioo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ ehiɔ shi.

english: Why would a vegetable farmer build a small nursery cover or shade frame over their nursery bed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai abɔɔ mli nitsulɔ ko baama ŋmɔ bibioo ko ni akɛhaa loo hulutsoo he ko yɛ amɛ ŋmɔ mli saatsoi lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: A small covering shields tiny tender shoots from harsh sunlight and drying winds, creating a mild climate underneath so the young seedlings do not wither before they are ready to be planted out.
ga: Nɔ bibioo ko ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ buɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahe. kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ baa yɛ shishi lɛ mli Dumɔwui bibii lɛ egbooo dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaadu.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into tubes during the hot part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔji yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling up leaves is a defense mechanism. By curling its leaves, the maize plant reduces the amount of leaf area exposed to the hot sun, which prevents it from losing too much water through evaporation.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he. Baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa tso lɛ baa he ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ baa shi. Enɛ tsiɔ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers when the ground gets too dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ lɛ?

english: When a plant experiences water stress during dry spells, it saves its remaining water to keep its main stem and leaves alive by shedding its flowers, as producing fruits requires a lot of water.
ga: Kɛ tsei kɛ nu he haomɔ kpe yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ Ebaakwɛ nu ni eshwɛ lɛ nɔ koni eha tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ kɛ baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ni eeefo lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, aduawai afeemɔ biɔ nu babaoo.

english: Why does cassava stay green and alive during the dry season while my leafy vegetables dry up completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei hiɔ shi eŋɔli ni ehiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ be mli ni mi-aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava stores extra food and water in its large underground roots, allowing it to feed itself during dry times, whereas leafy vegetables have short roots and small stems that cannot store water.
ga: Cassava kɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni fa fe nine toɔ eshishifãi wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni enyɛ eye niyenii yɛ ehe yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ yɛ shishifãi kukuji kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni nyɛɛɛ ato nu.

english: Why do my tomato stems bend down and wilt when I miss watering for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ mikɛ nu shwieee nɔ gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Water gives plant stems their firmness by filling up their cells like tiny water balloons. When the soil goes dry, the plant loses this inner water pressure and wilts to conserve energy.
ga: Nu haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ damɔɔ shi kɛtsɔ wala yibii lɛ ni ewoɔ amɛmli tamɔ nu bɔɔlu bibii lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ lɛ, nu ni yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ, ni ehe miihia ni amɛkwɛ hewalɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I pour water directly at the root base of my plant instead of sprinkling it over the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafɔse nu yɛ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe ni mafɔse baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Plants take in water through their roots in the ground, not through their leaves. Wetting the leaves wastes water to evaporation and can cause fungal diseases, while watering the base feeds the plant directly.
ga: Tsei gbalaa nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ, shi jeee kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, nu lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni efiteɔ ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai aba. Yɛ be mli ni afɔɔ nu lɛ, shishitoo lɛ baaha tso lɛ niyenii tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce a heavy harvest for a few years and then suddenly give a very low yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ wo yibii babaoo afii fioo komɛi ni no sɛɛ lɛ trukaa lɛ No hewɔ lɛ yibiiwoo lɛ faaa kwraa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees go through natural yield cycles. Soil nutrients get depleted over consecutive heavy harvests, and if rainfall pattern or fertilizer application changes, the tree enters a recovery phase resulting in lower yields.
ga: Cacao tsei tsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko mli. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa babaoo ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ hewɔ. ni kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ tsake Tsei lɛ baabote sɛɛkuu mli, ni no baaha yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: How many years can I rely on the same cocoa trees to give me good harvest before they grow too old?
ga: Afii enyiɛ manyɛ mikɛ mihe afɔ̃ cacao tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ koni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai dani egbɔ tsɔ?

english: A well-maintained cocoa tree can remain productive for 25 to 30 years. After this peak period, tree productivity naturally declines, requiring systematic pruning or gradual replanting.
ga: Cacao tsei ni akwɛɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aya nɔ awo yibii afii 25 kɛyashi 30 yɛ nɛkɛ be ni fe fɛɛ nɛɛ sɛɛ. Tso lɛ yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ biɔ ni afolɔ tsei lɛ amli yɛ gbɛjianɔtoo naa loo adu ekoŋŋ fiofio.

english: What causes mature cocoa trees to suddenly dry up or break during a bad farming season?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ gbɛ́ɔ loo amɛkuɔ trukaa yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ ehiii lɛ?

english: Severe dry seasons (Harmattan), pest infestations like stem borers, and underground root diseases weaken the internal structure of the tree, making it snap easily under environmental stress.
ga: Hɔmɔ be ni naa wa (Harmattan) Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ stem borers ni baa mɔ nɔ. kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi helai Ehaa tso lɛ mligbɛ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa efoɔ oya yɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi ashishi.

english: Why does my cocoa farm suffer so much damage when weather patterns change for just one year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ efite babaoo yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ afi kome pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Perennial crops like cocoa rely on stored energy and soil moisture over long periods. A single bad weather year disrupts flower development and pod formation, affecting tree performance across the full annual cycle.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ kookoo kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ hewalɛ ni ato kɛ sũ mli nu nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Afi kome mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii lɛ gbala fɔfɔi lɛ adalɛ kɛ pod lɛ feemɔ mli. Esaa bɔ ni tso lɛ tsuɔ nii ehaa yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ he.

english: How many times in a year should I clear weeds from my cocoa farm to keep the trees healthy?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ afi mli koni tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: A cocoa farm typically needs weeding 3 to 4 times a year, especially at the start and peak of the rainy seasons, to prevent weeds from taking water and nutrients away from cocoa roots.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ Cocoa ŋmɔji amli shii 3 kɛyashi 4 yɛ afi mli, titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee kɛ eshishijee mli. Enɛ haaa jwɛi lɛ agbala nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ kookoo shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds harm my cocoa trees even after the trees have grown tall and big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miitutua mi cacao tsei lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛdara moŋ?

english: Even mature cocoa trees suffer from weeds because weed roots compete for shallow soil moisture and fertilizer, while dense bush harbors pests and fungal diseases like black pod.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ po naa jwɛi ejaakɛ jwɛi shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa shi koni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ nɔ. yɛ be mli ni tsei bibii ni eyi obɔ lɛ hiɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pods.

english: How does paying hired laborers for farm clearing help me get better cocoa yields?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mɛi ni tsuɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii ahe nii lɛ nyɔmɔwoo lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná kookoo yibii kpakpai?

english: Hiring labor ensures the entire farm is weeded quickly at the right time before weeds mature, allowing the cocoa trees to absorb all available soil nutrients without delay.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni akɛ amɛ baatsu nii lɛ haa ajieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli oya yɛ be ni sa mli dani jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ. Enɛ haa cacao tso lɛ nyɛɔ eshɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ he ni ekɛ be sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ.

english: How can I plan my money during good cocoa seasons so my farm does not fail during dry years?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mato mishika he gbɛjianɔ yɛ kookoo be kpakpa mli? Bɔni afee ni miŋmɔ lɛ akafite yɛ afii ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ amli?

english: Saving a portion of your income during main crop harvest provides essential capital to pay for farm labor, weed clearing, and spraying during lean seasons when harvests drop.
ga: Shika ni onáa lɛ fã ko ni okɛtoɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ titri lɛ mli lɛ haa anáa shika ni he hiaa koni akɛwo ŋmɔ mli nyɔmɔwoo. jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ be mli ni kpamɔ lɛ baa shi lɛ.

english: What key practices can I use on my cocoa farm to keep work moving forward when rain is low?
ga: Mɛɛ nifeemɔi titrii manyɛ mikɛtsu nii yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni nitsumɔ lɛ aya hiɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ fioo?

english: During dry cycles, leave cleared weed mulches on the ground to shade the soil and reduce water loss, prune excess secondary branches carefully, and focus on farm sanitation.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be mli Shimɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajie lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eha nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Okɛ hiɛdɔɔ afo niji ni ji enyɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ. ni amɛha hetsemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he ahia

english: Why is it important to keep weeding my cocoa farm even when cocoa yield is low and money is tight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maya nɔ mafolɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ? Enɛ ba yɛ kookoo ni afee lɛ fioo kɛ shika fioo ni yɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Neglecting farm clearance during low yield periods causes weeds to choke cocoa trees further, making recovery harder and delaying yield improvement for subsequent seasons.
ga: Ni akuɔ hiɛ ashwieɔ ŋmɔji amli ni ajieɔ yɛ be mli ni nibii ni anáa lɛ faaa lɛ eha jwɛi ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ etee hiɛ. Enɛ haa sɛɛkuu lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni ehaa yibiiwoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli bei lɛ amli.

english: When maize leaves turn pale green or yellow instead of dark green, it means the crops are hungry for nutrients like nitrogen, which fertilizer provides to help them grow tall and produce big ears.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ he miihia niyenii tamɔ nitrogen. Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii haa amɛ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛwo toi wuji.

english: Should I place fertilizer directly on top of the soil or bury it near my plants?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo mafu yɛ tsei lɛ ahe?

english: Burying fertilizer a few centimeters into the soil next to the plant roots prevents rain from washing it away and stops the hot sun from destroying its nutrient strength.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wo sũ lɛ mli sɛntimitai fioo komɛi yɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nugbɔ akashwie lɛ. ni etsĩɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafite niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ

english: Why do my maize plants dry up quickly during the sun season even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ moŋ?

english: Maize plants lose water quickly through leaves in hot weather. Watering deeply early in the morning or late in the evening allows the roots to absorb the water before the hot sun evaporates it from the soil.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ nu lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ nu dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I water two different crop fields using the same water source channel?
ga: Ani manyɛ matsɔ nu jɛɛhe kome nɔ mafɔ ŋmɔji enyɔ anɔ nu?

english: Yes, creating connected soil channels allows water to flow from one crop section, like maize, directly to another, saving time and making full use of your water.
ga: Hɛɛ, muji gbɛi ni tsa nɔ ni afee lɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ he kome, tamɔ ŋmãa, kɛyaa he kroko tɛ̃ɛ. Okɛ be ato ni okɛ onu lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my crops turning yellow and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Curling and yellow leaves are usually caused by tiny insects sucking the sap from the leaves or by crop diseases, which can be treated using appropriate agricultural sprays or natural pest solutions.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ loo tsei ahelai ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. Abaanyɛ akɛ okwaayeli mli tsofai ni sa loo adebɔɔ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe tsofai atsu enɛ he nii.

english: How can I tell if my tree crops are getting sick before they stop producing fruit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela mɔ mi tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ dani amɛkpa yibiiwoo?

english: Early signs of tree sickness include sudden leaf drop, dark spots on the bark, or small oozing holes, which show that pests or fungi are attacking the tree.
ga: Nɔ ni fata mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso hela miiye lɛ he ji baai ni shwieɔ shi trukaa. ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ he loo ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko miiho kɛmiijɛ mli Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko loo ŋmɔtɔ ko miitutua tso lɛ.

english: Is it good practice to plant maize on the same plot alongside my young tree crops?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, planting fast-growing maize alongside young tree crops gives you quick food and harvest income while the maize plants provide helpful shade to the young trees.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛfata tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ ahe lɛ baaha oná niyenii oya kɛ shika kɛjɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei haa tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Can I use the same chemical spray to treat pests on both my maize and my tree crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ agbe kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Not always. Some crop protection products work safely on tree crops but can burn soft plants like maize, so you must always check the product label or ask an expert before applying.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Nibii komɛi ni buɔ tsei ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii shweshweeshwe yɛ tsei anɔ shi ebaanyɛ eshã tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo tamɔ ŋmãa, no hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni okwɛ nɔ ni aŋma yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ loo obi ŋaalɔ ko dani okɛtsu nii.

english: Why do my maize stalks stay short and thin even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa po lɛ?

english: Rain helps plants drink, but if the soil lacks natural plant food, the maize cannot build strong stalks. Adding manure or fertilizer gives the soil the power to build tall plants.
ga: Nugbɔ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnuɔ nu. Shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tsei ahe nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ, Abɛi nyɛŋ afee ŋmeii ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni efeɔ tsei kakadaji.

english: How can I get more money when selling my harvested maize at the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná shika babaoo kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ miihɔɔ yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Drying your maize properly after harvest allows you to store it safely and sell it later during the lean season when prices go up, rather than selling immediately when the market is flooded.
ga: Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okɛtoɔ shweshweeshwe ni ohɔ̃ɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ eshɛɛɛ be mli ni jara wa lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooohɔ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ nu eyi jara lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know when my maize crop is fully mature and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Maize is ready to harvest when the outer leaves surrounding the cob turn brown and dry like paper. If you peel back the cob cover and press a fingernail into a grain, no milky liquid should come out.
ga: Abɛi efee klalo akɛ ebaakpa kɛji kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ ebɔle ehe. Cob lɛ tsɔɔ blɔfo ni egbiɔ tamɔ wolo. Kɛji otsi ŋmei lɛ he tsɔi lɛ sɛɛ ni okɛ onineshi ŋmei lɛ miimɔ mli ni efee ŋmei lɛ, Esaaa akɛ nu ko ni tamɔ mliki jeɔ kpo.

english: What happens to my cocoa pods if I leave them on the tree long after they turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ beni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ?

english: If ripe cocoa pods stay on the tree too long, the beans inside will begin to sprout or rot, and animals like squirrels will eat them, reducing your final harvest weight and quality.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ hi tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baabɔi kwɛ̃mɔ loo amɛbaafite. Ni kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii baaye amɛ, ni no baaha onaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli tsiimɔ kɛ ehilɛ aba shi.

english: Cassava plants shed their lower leaves naturally during dry spells or when soil nutrients like nitrogen are low. It is the plant's way of saving water and food for the underground tubers.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛshishi baai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hɔmɔ be mli loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ faaa. Enɛ ji gbɛ ni tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep dropping off before forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop without producing fruit when the soil gets too dry, when temperatures become extremely hot, or when tiny pests like thrips attack the base of the blossoms.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Beni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips tutuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ashishi.

english: How can I tell if my plantain leaves are drooping because of hot weather or because the plant is sick?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi plantain baai lɛ miigbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ hewɔ loo hela mɔ tso lɛ?

english: In hot sun, healthy plantain leaves fold downwards slightly to shield themselves but spring back when cooler. If the leaves turn pale yellow, dry up completely, or the main stem feels soft, the plant is lacking water or infected by root pests.
ga: hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Plantain baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe. Shi efoɔ ehe kɛji edɔ. Kɛji baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ, egbi kwraa, loo tso lɛ shishifã lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ bɔdɔɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu bɛ tso lɛ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko emɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ.

english: What will happen if I plant my tomato seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu tomato dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting tomatoes too close forces them to fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. This results in thin, weak stalks with small fruits and allows fungal diseases to spread rapidly between crowded leaves.
ga: Tomato ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ hulu la, sũ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he, ni no haa amɛshishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ aduawai bibii. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ tsei ahe tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ ateŋ.

english: Why is it good to plant cowpeas in the same farm where I plant my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu tsina ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas naturally trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the field, they feed the soil with natural nutrients that help your maize grow taller and stronger without needing as much bought fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ Amɛbaahã shikpɔŋ lɛ aná adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni baaye abua o-ŋmã lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ni ehiɛ ahi ehe nɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why does leaving thick grass around my young cocoa trees slow down their growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mli edɔ ni mishiɔ yɛ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ haa amɛdaramɔ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds and grasses have aggressive roots that steal moisture and fertilizer meant for your young cocoa trees. They also shade small plants from daylight and shelter pests that bite young shoots.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa o-cacao tsei bibii lɛ. Amɛhaa tsei bibii hu feɔ hulu la, ni amɛji kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: How are green caterpillars getting onto my cabbage leaves and eating big holes in them?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei ŋmɔŋ ko ba shi yɛ mi-cabbage baa lɛ nɔ ni eye bu agbo ko ni yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Small white butterflies lay tiny, hidden eggs on the underside of cabbage leaves. Those eggs hatch into hungry caterpillars that chew through the leaves to feed themselves.
ga: Kpɔŋɔi bibii yɛŋ fɔɔ amɛwui ni amɛkɛtee kaabeji baai ashishi. Nakai ŋmeii lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛye niyenii.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start rotting so fast after I dig them out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya beni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if cut or bruised by cutlasses during harvest, or if left under direct sun. Storing tubers on raised, shaded bamboo racks with good airflow keeps them cool and dry so they last longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛ dagger shwie nɔ loo atswa lɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. aloo kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ tsɔnei lɛ ato ŋmei shĩa ko ni nɔ kwɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔlɔ. No hewɔ lɛ abaanyɛ akɛtsu nii be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my yams grow long and thin while others grow short and thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ ekomɛi kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ be mli ni mi-sweet potatoes lɛ ekomɛi yɛ kuku ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: The shape of a yam depends on both its specific variety and how loose the soil is in your mound. Loose, soft soil allows the root to expand deep and wide easily, while hard or stony soil restricts growth and distorts the tuber shape.
ga: Bɔ ni o-sweet potato lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ damɔ o-srɔto pɔtɛɛ lɛ nɔ kɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ o-mound lɛ mli lɛ mli etse ha lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛmli kwɔ. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ dalɛ naa ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe mfoniri.

english: Why do the leaves on my yam vines turn yellow and dry up near the end of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ sweet potato wain tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni afi lɛ baa naagbee lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves at the end of the season are a natural signal that the yam plant has finished its growth cycle. The plant is transferring all its remaining energy into the underground tuber before going dormant.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ sweet potato tso lɛ eshɛ edalɛ be lɛ naagbee. Tso lɛ miitsɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ nɔ kɛmiiya ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli dani eba shi.

english: Can I cut a big seed yam into smaller pieces before planting, or will it rot in the soil?
ga: Dani madu lɛ, ani manyɛ mafolɔ dumɔwui wuji ni ji sweet potatoes lɛ bibii bibii loo amɛbaagbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, you can cut large seed yams into pieces, but you must let the cut surfaces dry and heal in the shade or rub them with wood ash before planting to prevent soil fungi and bacteria from causing rot.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ ofolɔ dumɔwui wuji amli bibii bibii, shi kwɛmɔ ni oha he ni ofo lɛ lɛ agbi ni etsa yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Aloo okɛ tso sũ ashwie nɔ dani okɛdu. Koni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ akafite.

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves up toward the sunlight. Staking maximizes sun exposure for leaf growth, keeps leaves away from damp ground diseases, and helps the plant build bigger underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ nɔ. Staking haa hulu la kroko fataa he kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ. Buu baai ahe kɛjɛ helai ahe yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji

english: Why do my yams turn out very small when I plant too many seeds on one mound?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ gɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: When too many seeds are planted on a single mound, the roots compete aggressively for water, soil nutrients, and space. Giving each seed proper spacing ensures enough resources to yield large, heavy tubers.
ga: Beni adu dumɔwui babaoo tsɔ yɛ gɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ. Shishifãi lɛ kɛ nu he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ he ni yɔɔ lɛ He ni sa ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii wuji ni tsii aba.

english: How do I know the exact time my yams are fully mature and ready to be dug out?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ mafo?

english: Yams are ready for full harvest when the above-ground vines dry up completely and die back naturally. You can also carefully dig around the top of the mound; a firm, fully formed tuber head indicates maturity.
ga: Sweet potatoes efee klalo kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ ni yeɔ emuu beni wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ egbi kwraa ni amɛgboi ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsu nii kɛbɔle gɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ hu. Yitso ni ma shi shiŋŋ, ni eyi obɔ lɛ tsɔɔ dalɛ.

english: What happens to root crops like yams if I apply too much chemical fertilizer late in the season?
ga: Mɛni baa shishifãi tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ babaoo fata he yɛ be ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa naagbee lɛ mli?

english: Excessive fertilizer late in the season causes the plant to waste energy growing green leaves and vines instead of expanding its underground tubers, which results in smaller, watery tubers that spoil quickly.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli kɛ wain tsei ni miida lɛ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ ŋmeii lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: Why do my stored yams start sprouting green shoots inside my barn after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miije shishi amɛmiikwɛ̃ yɛ mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Sprouting happens because the yam tuber's natural resting period, known as dormancy, has ended. As humidity or temperature shifts, the yam naturally wakes up to grow a new plant using the nutrients stored inside itself.
ga: Nibii ni shwereɔ lɛ baa ejaakɛ sweet potato tuber lɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be, ni ale lɛ akɛ dormancy lɛ eba naagbee. Kɛji hulutsoo be loo hulutsoo be lɛ tsake lɛ, Sweet potato lɛ baate shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛ niyenii ni akɛtoɔ sweet potato lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii ni ekɛdu tsei heei.

english: Why do my yams rot quickly if the loading boys bruise or scratch them during packing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji gbekɛ ni hiɛ lɛ shwie nɔ loo efo mli beni ekɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ?

english: A yam's skin acts as a protective shield. Cuts and bruises break this barrier, allowing rot-causing bacteria and fungi to enter the tuber, which leads to rapid decay during transport or storage.
ga: Atomɔ hewolo tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ mɔ he. Kpojiemɔi kɛ ŋmɔlɔi fiteɔ gbɛtsii nii nɛɛ. Enɛ haa helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ boteɔ bulb lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛfiteɔ oya kɛ́ akɛ amɛ tee loo akɛto he.

english: How can I prevent my yams from losing weight and shrinking while waiting in the barn to sell them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-sweet potato lɛ akagbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams lose weight because they lose water through their skin after harvest. Storing them off the bare ground in a well-ventilated, shaded barn keeps them cool and slows down moisture loss.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ nu tsɔɔ amɛhewolo nɔ kɛji akpa amɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ to shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni ŋmɔtɔ hu baaje mli fiofio.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves on cassava are usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties and removing infected plants early helps keep your crop healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Aduɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do my stored cowpea grains get full of tiny holes after a few weeks in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui stash lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Beni akɛto otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: Tiny insects called weevils lay eggs inside the seeds around harvest time. As the eggs hatch inside storage, the larvae eat their way out of the grain, leaving holes unless the grains are properly dried and stored in sealed, airtight containers.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Beni ŋmeii lɛ fɔ̃ɔ yɛ tsɛnsi lɛ mli lɛ ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ ŋmaa lɛ niyenii. kɛtsɔ bu ko ni oooshi lɛ nɔ ja dumɔwui lɛ egbi jogbaŋŋ Ni okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni atsĩ naa ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli.

english: Why does my maize crop grow tall but fail to produce big, full cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ miida shi ewooo ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Maize needs nitrogen to grow tall, but it also needs nutrients like phosphorus and potassium to form full grain cobs. If your soil lacks these balanced nutrients or if fertilizer is applied too late, the plant puts energy into leaves rather than grain.
ga: Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃. Shi niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium hu he miihia lɛ koni efee ŋmãa ŋmãa muu fɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ nɛkɛ niyenii ni ja nɛɛ bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ, Tsei kɛ hewalɛ yaa amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ amɛdumɔwui lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I burn the cleared bush on my field before planting cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishãa jwɛi ni ajie yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani miduɔ ŋmei?

english: Burning clears the land fast, but it burns away organic matter and kills beneficial soil organisms that feed your plants. Letting cleared weeds rot as mulch keeps the soil moist and naturally enriches it over time.
ga: Shãa haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tseɔ oya. Mohu ɔ, e shãa níhi nɛ ngɛ zugba a nɔ ɔ, nɛ e kpataa níhi nɛ a he hia nɛ a ngɛ zugba a mi nɛ haa o tso ɔmɛ ní ɔ a hɛ mi. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ jwɛi ni ajie lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee nɔ ni woɔ yibii yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and cool soil moisture it needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do the leaves of my yam plants start turning brown and dying off late in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ?

english: When yam vines turn brown and die back late in the season, it is a natural process where the plant shifts all its stored energy from the above-ground leaves into swelling and ripening the yam tubers underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ Eji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛto kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ amɛwoɔ sweet potato tsei ni efuu ni amɛmiikwɛ̃ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before producing any fruit during the heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme dry heat stresses tomato plants, causing them to shed their blossoms to save energy. Providing consistent watering at the roots and light shade during hot afternoons helps flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli egbi lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tomato tsei lɛ ajie amɛbai lɛ koni amɛbu hewalɛ he. Nu ni oooha shishifãi lɛ daa ni okɛ hulutsoo aha yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ tomatoi.

english: Why are my orange fruits splitting open on the tree right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-citrus yibii lɛ miiho yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: Citrus fruits split open when heavy rains come after a long dry period. The inside of the fruit fills up with water faster than the dry outer peel can stretch, causing the skin to burst.
ga: Orange yibii lɛ tswaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni nugbɔ nɛ. Nu yiɔ aduawai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni egbi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: Why do some of my corn seeds sprout quickly while others in the same row do not come up at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu kwɛɛɛ oya lɛ? Yɛ sɛɛkuu kome mli lɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko edaaa?

english: Corn seeds need uniform moisture and planting depth to germinate together. Seeds buried too deep, planted in dry spots, or eaten by soil pests will fail to sprout alongside the rest.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui he hiaa nu ni mli edɔ daa kɛ dumɔ mlibotemɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ekome. Dumɔwui ni afu amɛ tsɔ ni adu yɛ hei ni egbi loo ni kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ lɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni eshwɛ lɛ ekwɛŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my pepper plants grow so slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi-pepper tsei lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil food away from the roots of your pepper plants. Removing weeds early allows your pepper crop to absorb all available nutrients and grow much faster.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Eyeɔ ebuaa pepper tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni edaa oya kwraa.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. When nitrogen in the soil is low, the plant moves available nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the younger leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Rice plants fall over, or lodge, when they get too much nitrogen fertilizer, which makes their stems tall and weak. Heavy rains or wind can then easily push over the top-heavy plants.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi loo amɛhiɔ shi kɛ́ amɛná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni egbɔjɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ akumɔ tsei ni amɛyiteŋ wa waa lɛ oya.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil if I leave them during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays waterlogged for long periods because the roots cannot get oxygen and harmful fungi thrive in wet conditions. Excess water causes the tubers to spoil under the ground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. Nu babaoo haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my yam vines produce larger yams when I support them with wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ sweet potatoi wuji fe tsutsu lɛ beni mikɛ tsei ni akɛfee tsei fiɔ amɛsɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch maximum sunlight for growth. Staking keeps leaves off the wet ground to prevent leaf diseases and gives the plant more sunlight energy to build big tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya shɔŋŋ koni amɛna hulu la babaoo koni amɛshwere. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛtsi foliar hela naa ni eha tso lɛ hulu hewalɛ ni ekɛfee bulbs agboi.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to protect them from direct harsh sunlight and heat. Removing large trees leaves tender young cocoa plants exposed, causing them to lose water quickly and dry out.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii biɔ hulutsoo be koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Tsei wuji ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha kookoo tsei bibii ni darako lɛ aje kpo. Enɛ haa nu lɛ fiteɔ oya ni egbiɔ.

english: Why do my plantain plants produce very small bunches when many young shoots are growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii bibii babaoo miida yɛ ehe lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for soil nutrients, water, and light. Removing excess suckers ensures the main plant gets enough food to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ mli ŋmeii krokomɛi loo ŋmeii lɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, nu kɛ la mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when daytime temperatures get too high or water supply is irregular. Extreme heat damages the flower's pollen, preventing fruit from forming.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa fiteɔ fɔfɔi amli ŋmɔtɔ. Ehaa aduawai lɛ efeee

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants curling up and turning twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking sap from the leaves, or by a viral infection carried by these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ mli

english: Why does planting cowpea or groundnuts before my maize make the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ adu tsina loo ŋmeii dani adu ŋmãa lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpea and groundnut take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, naturally enriching the soil with fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why is it harmful to water my vegetable crops over their leaves during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mawo mi-vegetable tsei lɛ nu yɛ amɛbaai anɔ yɛ shwane hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Watering under hot afternoon sun causes quick water loss through evaporation, and wet leaves combined with high heat create ideal conditions for fungal diseases to break out.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ haa nu lɛ laajeɔ oya yɛ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ hewɔ. Ni baai ni efɔ ni akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa fataa he lɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ aba.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and burn when I clear all the big shade trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ mijie kookoo tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Large trees provide shade and cool temperatures, keeping the soil moist and protecting young cocoa leaves from scorching in the harsh sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni eda lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe koni amɛkashã yɛ hulu ni naa wa lɛ shishi.

english: Why do I need to support my yam vines with long wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji afi mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ asɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves into the sunlight and keeps them away from moist ground where fungal diseases can rot them.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa tso lɛ yibii lɛ shɛɔ hulu la he ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ he yɛ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ afite yɛ lɛ.

english: Why are there tiny holes in my young maize leaves with small caterpillars hiding inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni Akɛtee yɛ ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: This damage is caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm. They lay eggs on leaves, and the hatched caterpillars feed on the soft growing leaves inside the whorl, which can stunt or destroy the plant if left untreated.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm. Amɛwoɔ amɛwui lɛ yɛ baai anɔ. Ni ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ yeɔ baai bibii ni miida yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ ajie tso lɛ kpo loo efite kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper and tomato plants suddenly wilt and die within a few days even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This rapid wilting is usually caused by bacterial wilt, a disease living in the soil that enters the plant roots and blocks water from moving up the stem, causing the plant to dry out while still green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa oya nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni boteɔ tsei ashishifãi amli ni ehaaa nu aya ŋwɛi shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Gbimɔ tsei lɛ be mli ni amɛji ŋmɔji lolo lɛ.

english: Why do some of my cassava stem cuttings sprout quickly while others just rot in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ekomɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings need to come from mature, healthy stems and must be buried with the buds pointing upwards. Younger, dried-out stems or cuttings planted upside down fail to root properly and easily decay in wet soil.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmei ni afo lɛ ajɛ tsei ni eda ni wa amli. ni esa akɛ afu lɛ ni hiŋmɛii lɛ akwɛ ŋwɛi Tsoi bibii ni egbi loo tsei niji ni adu amɛyitso lɛ nyɛŋ ashishifãi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ.

english: How do I choose the best plantain suckers from an old mat to plant in my new field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ mi-mat momo lɛ mli koni mikɛdu yɛ mishikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ?

english: The best suckers are 'sword suckers', which have broad bases and narrow, spear-like leaves. Avoid 'water suckers' with wide leaves on thin bases, as they develop weak root systems and produce smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Suckers ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ‘sword suckers’, ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni mli tse ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ‘suckers’, ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ yɛ shishigbɛ bibii anɔ lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛfeɔ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ plantain tsei bibii.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my plot before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani adu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas work with beneficial soil bacteria to trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that feeds the maize crop that follows.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my vegetable harvests become smaller every year when I plant them on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai ni mikpaa lɛ faaa daa afi beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating crops breaks disease cycles and keeps the soil balanced.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ lɛ fiteɔ helai ni yaa nɔ lɛ, ni ehaa sũ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: When is the right time for me to apply chemical fertilizer to my crops so the rain does not waste it?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli? No hewɔ lɛ nugbɔ lɛ eyaaa yaka?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist but not during heavy downpours. Applying it a few weeks after germination when plants have active roots helps them absorb nutrients before rain can wash them away.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi esaaa akɛ akɛwoɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛwo tso lɛ mli otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni tso lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ beni eyɛ shishifãi ni tsuɔ nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni eŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ aho tso lɛ he.

english: Why should I spread dry grass and leaves around the stems of my vegetable crops during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai mabɔle he lɛ? Aduawai tsei yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Spreading dry grass or mulch covers the bare soil, which keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation from heat, and prevents weed seeds from getting enough light to sprout around your crops.
ga: Hay loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ Ha nu ni jɛɔ la mli lɛ mli shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. ni otsi jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the tip downward when the crop is lacking nitrogen, a vital soil nutrient. This often happens in exhausted soils that have been farmed repeatedly without adding manure or fertilizer, or after heavy rain washes nutrients away.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa kɛbaa shi kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen, ni ji shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efite ni atsu he nii shii abɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fataaa he lɛ nɔ. aloo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii laajeɔ

english: Why do my groundnut plants look bushy and healthy above the ground, but the pods underground are empty?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛji ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi pod lɛ mli efolo?

english: Empty groundnut pods, often called 'pops,' happen when the soil lacks calcium while the pods are developing. Without enough calcium, the plant forms the outer shell but fails to grow the seeds inside.
ga: Peanut ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ nɔ ko, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ ‘pea pods’ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ. Kɛji calcium faaa Tso lɛ feɔ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei shi enyɛɛɛ ekwɛ dumɔwui yɛ emli.

english: Cassava roots rot underground when water stays trapped in the soil for too long during heavy rains. Excess water stops air from reaching the roots, causing soft-rot fungi to grow and spoil the crop.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ daa ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Cocoa flowers often drop without making pods because of a lack of midges (tiny insects that pollinate the flowers), severe dry weather, or poor nutrition. Without insect pollination or enough water, the tree drops the flowers to save its strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. (kooloo bibii ni haa fɔfɔii amli fɔfɔii) kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli egbi waa loo niyenii ni ehiii Kɛji kooloi fɔji fɔji loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Tsei hu baashwie fɔfɔii anɔ koni amɛhiɛ hewalɛ mli.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their leaves and producing very small, wrinkled fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ miifite ni eewo yibii bibii ni egbɔjɔ waa lɛ?

english: Leaf dropping and small fruit in peppers are usually caused by sap-sucking pests like mites or whiteflies, or by viral diseases they spread. These insects weaken the plant and prevent proper fruit development.
ga: Baai ni gbeeɔ shi kɛ aduawai bibii Yɛ chili ŋmeii amli lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ amli. Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛtsiɔ aduawai ni sa lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my young green tomatoes develop black, sunken spots on the bottom of the fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi ni ebote shishi lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium inside the developing fruit, usually triggered by irregular watering where the soil switches between very dry and very wet.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ ehe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa teŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because their leaves burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight and high heat. Planting shade crops like plantains or leaving some forest trees creates a cooler microclimate that keeps the soil moist and protects the young cocoa.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ hia hɔɔ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ loo tsei ni ashiɔ yɛ koo lɛ mli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo baa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe.

english: Why do crops like maize grow much better when I plant them on land where I grew cowpeas last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu tsina ŋmãa yɛ nɔ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have tiny bacteria on their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the soil. When the cowpea plant dies, that stored nitrogen remains in the soil, acting as natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ helai bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi anɔ ni heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tsina tso lɛ gbo Nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting in the barn before the planting season comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani ekwɛ̃mɔ be lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Yams sprout early in storage when the storage room is too warm, humid, or well-lit. Warm temperatures signal to the tuber that it is time to wake up and grow, which reduces the weight and quality of the yam.
ga: Atomɔ ni ŋɔɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ mra. Koni akɛto be mli ni nitoohe lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ, edɔ, loo la bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. He ni mli edɔ lɛ haa bulb lɛ leɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ ete shi ni eda. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsiimɔ kɛ ehilɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily just when the bunches start getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ je shishi amɛdara lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall over because microscopic worms (nematodes) or stem borer insects weaken the root system underground. When the fruit bunch gets heavy, the weakened roots can no longer anchor the plant against wind or weight.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii bibii ahewɔ. (Nematodes) loo kooloi ni shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsii Shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ nyɛŋ amɔ tso lɛ nɔ dɔŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ loo muji ni tswaa lɛ he.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which helps them grow strong and green. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted chicken manure gives the plants the nutrients they need to recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo tsina ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it bad if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every major rainy season?
ga: Ani ejaaa kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be? Nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa?

english: Yes, planting maize continuously in the same soil drains all its nitrogen and attracts pests that feed on maize. Rotating your maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni aduɔ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ haa nitrogen lɛ fɛɛ hoɔ, ni egbalaa ŋmãa ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and stopping the plant from growing taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that spread viruses. Spraying your pepper plants with neem oil or a mild soapy water solution destroys these pests and stops leaf curl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ni akɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni mli ejɔ baashwie pepper tsei anɔ Ekpataa nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ahiɛ ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays waterlogged for long periods during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away easily so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. Koni yitso lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when soil moisture fluctuates or temperatures get too high. Mulching around the base keeps the soil cool and moist, while regular watering during flowering helps the blossoms turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomatoi shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake loo hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni oooha fɔfɔi lɛ daa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ tomato.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to eat deep holes into the central leaves of my maize?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a destructive pest that feeds heavily on young maize crops. Catching them early by checking the leaf funnels and applying recommended organic or approved chemical treatments will protect your farm.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii ni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii babaoo. Amɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ agbɛi ni oookwɛ ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ nɔ lɛ obaanyɛ oye obua ni obu oŋmɔ lɛ he.

english: Why are the green fruits on my orange tree dropping to the ground before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ mi-orange tso lɛ nɔ lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: Premature fruit drop in citrus is often caused by fruit flies piercing the young oranges to lay eggs inside. Using fruit fly bait traps and keeping the orchard floor clear of fallen fruit helps prevent this loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa citrus aduawai lɛ fiteɔ oya ji aduawai amli ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii amli koni amɛwo ŋmeii yɛ mli lɛ. Fruit fly bait ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ abɔɔ lɛ nɔ ni akwɛɔ koni aduawai ni egbee shi lɛ akafee nɔ ko lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ nɛkɛ laajemɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my yam tubers come out crooked and small instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ jeɔ kpo ni ebɔle ehe ni efee bibii moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers become misshapen if the soil beneath them is hard, compact, or stony. Digging deep, loose, stone-free mounds gives the yam tuber the soft space it needs to expand straight downwards.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baafite kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo eyɛ tɛi. Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni tɛi bɛ nɔ lɛ ni akuɔ lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ aná he ko ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shi tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my cabbage heads stay soft and loose instead of forming a tight, hard ball?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lolo ni eyɛ mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee nɔ ko ni wa ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ?
