english: Soft cabbage heads occur when plants do not get consistent water or lack balanced nutrients like phosphorus and potassium. Regular watering and applying a balanced fertilizer helps the inner leaves pack tightly together.
ga: Kaabaji yitsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa loo amɛnáaa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni sa, tamɔ fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa baaye abua ni emli baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and shallow roots that dry out quickly under direct sunlight. Leaving larger shade trees or planting plantains alongside cocoa provides a cooler shelter that protects the young crops until they are strong enough to handle full heat.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo adu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa he ko ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ latsaa lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need sunlight on as many leaves as possible to make food. Guiding the vines up wooden stakes lifts the leaves off the damp ground to catch the sun and prevents fungal rot, leading to larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni hulu la babaoo he miihia amɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛfee niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ wain tso lɛ ba tso ko nɔ lɛ, ewoɔ tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni hulu la ashɛ enɔ ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ anaa. Ekɛ mɔ yaa shikpɔŋ shishi tuber agbo ko mli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore green leaves so the plant can grow strong ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei, ŋmei, loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baa lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ koni tso lɛ anyɛ akwɛ ŋmãa toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have small nodules on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the plants decay after harvest, that extra nitrogen stays in the soil to feed whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Beni tsei fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same soil strips away the specific nutrients maize needs and allows soil-borne pests to build up year after year. Rotating maize with crops like cassava or beans gives the soil time to rebuild its nutrients and disrupts pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ abɛi lɛ mli lɛ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ feɔ ekome afi fɛɛ afi. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛsaa ehe nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ekoŋŋ. ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ lɛ

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the branch before they can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal disease called black pod, which spreads rapidly in dark, overly damp environments. Pruning excess leaves and weeds allows fresh air and sunlight into the farm, keeping the pods dry and reducing the disease.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod kɛ enɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ tsɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. Baai kɛ jwɛi ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa helai baa shi.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the inner leaves of my young maize plants right at the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ amli baai lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the soft tender leaves inside the central tube of maize plants. Catching them early by applying ash or recommended organic treatments directly into the center funnel stops them before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ anɔ. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ sũ loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛ tsofai tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa amɛkpaa dani amɛfiteɔ he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn out soft and watery when I dig them up during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ atsa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu ni mli jɔ kɛ́ atsa amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During heavy rainfall, cassava plants soak up excess water and convert their stored starch into liquid to keep growing. Waiting until the end of the rainy season allows the roots to retain their firmness and high starch content.
ga: yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ shwieɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ehaa ŋmeii ni ato lɛ feɔ nu koni eya nɔ eda. Kɛ́ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ ni amɛná starch babaoo.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms drop off the stem instead of turning into tomatoes when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ tomato kɛ́ edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, tomato plants experience heat stress and drop their flowers to save water and survival energy. Keeping the soil moist with organic mulch around the stem helps cool the roots and reduces flower loss.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Tomato tsei lɛ naa hulutsoo be mli haomɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ebɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when a strong storm hits my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ahum ni naa wa ko ba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees do not have deep taproots; their root systems spread out near the soil surface, making them top-heavy when carrying large fruit bunches. Supporting the main stem with strong bamboo poles prevents heavy winds from pulling the root ball out of the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa shɔŋŋ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ kɛ́ amɛmiiwo aduawai wuji. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tso ni wa fi tso lɛ shishi tso titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa koni ekagbala shishifã lɛ bɔɔlu lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear the weeds around the base of a big tree before cutting it down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔjie jwɛi ni yɔɔ tsei wuji ashishi dani wɔfolɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Clearing around the tree base exposes hidden hazards like snakes or stinging ants, gives workers space to cut safely without tripping, and ensures any chemical applied after cutting touches the stump cleanly.
ga: Tsei ashishi ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ osharai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ, tamɔ onufu loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ amɛ lɛ kpo, ni ehaa nitsulɔi lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛfoɔ tsei lɛ shweshweeshwe ni nɔ ko nɔ ko tsiii amɛ gbɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa koni tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ ashɛ tso lɛ he jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important to apply chemical onto a fresh tree stump immediately after cutting it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ tsofai awo tsei heei ni afo lɛ amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: A cut tree seals its surface wounds quickly. Applying chemical immediately while the wood is still fresh allows the liquid to be absorbed deep into the root system, preventing unwanted regrowth or the spread of root diseases to surrounding crops.
ga: Tso ni afo lɛ baatsi pilamɔ lɛ naa oya. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai wo tso lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ be mli ni eyɛ ehee lolo lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ abote tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. Etsiɔ tsei ni ataooo ni amɛdaraa ekoŋŋ loo shishifã hela ni gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and dry up when I clear all the shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are sensitive and burn under intense direct sunlight. Shade trees or plantain plants act like living umbrellas, protecting young cocoa from harsh heat and maintaining the moisture needed for survival.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ nuɔ la he waa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ ambrela. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. ni ekwɛ koni hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni anyɛ ahi shi lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my old cocoa trees produce fewer pods when they get very tall and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso momo lɛ miiwo ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko pɛ yɛ be mli ni cacao tso lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ waa lɛ?

english: When trees grow very tall, they spend most of their nutrients maintaining thick wood and excessive leaves rather than making flowers and pods. Overgrown upper leaves also block sunlight from lower branches where pods grow.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ da waa Amɛkɛ amɛ niyenii mli hewalɛi lɛ ateŋ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ tso ni mli tse kɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ nɔ. Yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ lɛ, ŋwɛi baai ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ hu tsiɔ hulu la ni jɛɔ shishigbɛ niji ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why should I avoid planting cassava right next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmei dumɔ he yɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Cassava roots grow aggressively and pull large amounts of water and nutrients out of the topsoil. This starves young cocoa seedlings that need those same soil nutrients to build strong roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjieɔ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha kookoo dumɔwui bibii ni he hiaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ aba koni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during heavy rains when the fruit bunch gets large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli ni aduawai akui lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems instead of deep taproots. When a heavy bunch of fruit grows at the top, soft wet soil and strong winds easily pull the shallow root network out of the ground.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ moŋ fe shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Be mli ni aduawai babaoo miida yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya.

english: Why should I cut off the small extra shoots growing at the base of my cocoa trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ he

english: These extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and food from the main trunk without producing fruit. Removing them ensures the tree directs all its energy into producing large, healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers nɛɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ mli ni amɛwooo yibii. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do some trees on my farm die suddenly from the roots up even when the top leaves look green at first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gboiɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ amɛshishifãi amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ? Kɛji akɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli yɛ shishijee mli po lɛ,.

english: Root diseases destroy the underground water channels of a plant first. The leaves stay green for a short time using remaining stored sap, but once the roots are completely dead, the entire tree collapses rapidly.
ga: Shishifãi ahe helai fiteɔ tso lɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu gbɛi lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Baai lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli be kukuoo ko. kɛtsɔ vitreous fluid ni eshwɛ lɛ nɔ Shi beni shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ gboi lɛ Tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbee shi oya.

english: Why do insects attack my cocoa trees more during the dry season than during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa mi-kokoo tsei lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Dry weather stresses trees due to water shortage, weakening their natural sap defense. Pests like Mirids (Akate) thrive in warm, dry conditions and easily feed on the weakened shoots.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa tsei haoɔ yɛ nu ni faaa lɛ hewɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, adebɔɔ mli vitreous hebuu lɛ baa shi. Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Mirids (Akate) lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ jɛmɛ. ni eyeɔ ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ mlɛo

english: Why do black spots spread so fast from one cocoa pod to another during wet weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that relies on water. Raindrops splashing off an infected pod carry microscopic spores through the air onto neighboring healthy pods, spreading the infection rapidly.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ jɛ ŋmei ko ni damɔ nu nɔ lɛ mli. Nugbɔshiimɔi ni shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni anaaa lɛ tsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: This is usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency. Maize needs nitrogen to grow strong, and when the soil lacks it, the plant moves the available nutrients from its older bottom leaves up to feed the newer leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni enyɛ eda jogbaŋŋ. ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli etse Tsei lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni etsɛ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my cowpea crop grow plenty of leaves but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ baa babaoo shi ŋmɔtɔi lɛ faaa lɛ?

english: When cowpeas receive too much nitrogen from the soil or from nitrogen-rich fertilizer, the crop puts all its energy into growing green leaves instead of producing flowers and seed pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ cowpea nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ, Crops kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni amɛaafee fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui ashishifãi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need to be planted under shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ yɛ tso ni haa hulutsoo lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight, which burns their tender leaves. Shade trees act as living umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and cool until the cocoa stems grow mature and strong.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baaha ebaa bibii lɛ ashã. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni hiɛ ka. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni edɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Do my yam vines really need wooden stakes to climb on, or can I let them spread on the ground?
ga: Mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he miihia tso tso diɛŋtsɛ koni ekɛkwɔ. Aloo manyɛ maha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ.

english: Yam vines need stakes so their leaves can spread out to catch maximum sunlight. When vines sit on the wet ground, the leaves shade each other and catch diseases, resulting in much smaller tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ni baaha amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Kɛ́ wain tsei lɛ kpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ he lɛ, baai lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni helai yeɔ amɛ. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ feɔ bibioo kwraa.

english: Why do my maize plants grow weak and thin with small cobs when I plant three or four seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ

english: Planting multiple seeds in a single hole causes overcrowding. The roots compete fiercely for the same soil food and water, leaving every plant in that hole weak and undernourished.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ haa mɛi eyiɔ obɔ fe nine. Shishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli waa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Enɛ ha tso fɛɛ tso ni yɔɔ bu lɛ mli lɛ gbɔjɔ ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ ehe.

english: What is making ragged holes in the inner leaves of my young corn plants overnight?
ga: Mɛni ha buji ba mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ amli nyɔɔŋ kome mli?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central funnel of young maize leaves during the day and eat the tender leaf tissue, creating holes as the leaf unfolds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii amli fãji Ekɛ bu baa kɛji baai lɛ gbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into little cups during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle kɔɔpoi bibii ahe lɛ? Yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Pepper leaves curl inward to reduce their surface area and save water during extreme heat, but persistent curling can also mean tiny pests like thrips or mites are sucking sap from the underside of the leaves.
ga: Akɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ mli koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi ni ekɛbu nu he yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Shi ŋmɔlɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites miinu nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the stems without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are too high or when the soil dries out completely. Severe heat or moisture stress damages the pollen inside the flower, preventing fruit formation.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Dɔlɛ loo hulutsoo ni naa wa fiteɔ pollen ŋmeii ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. ni amɛtsi aduawai ni anáa lɛ naa

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting under the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in heavy or poorly drained soil for long periods. Excess standing water starves the roots of air and allows soil fungi to rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ aye shishifãi lɛ ni eha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ afite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over on their own when the fruits start growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ aduawai lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems. As the heavy bunch of plantains develops, the top becomes heavy, causing wind or gravity to easily uproot the plant if it is not supported with wooden props.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Beni plantain lɛ mli shwieɔ shi lɛ, ŋwɛigbɛ fã lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni no haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ loo hewalɛ ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajie tso lɛ kɛji akɛ tso ko bɛ ni fiɔ esɛɛ.

english: If I acquire a large piece of land to farm maize, how far apart should I plant the seeds?
ga: Kɛji minine shɛ shikpɔŋ wulu nɔ ni madu ŋmãa lɛ Te esa akɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ mi teŋ jɛkɛ ha tɛŋŋ?

english: Plant maize seeds about 25 to 30 centimeters apart within rows that are spaced 75 centimeters apart. Giving each plant enough space ensures they do not fight for water and soil nutrients, leading to bigger cobs.
ga: Dumɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee sɛntimita 25 kɛyashi 30 yɛ ŋmãa ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimita 75 mli. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaatsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii he akaŋshii. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso lɛ yɛ ŋmei ni da fe no.

english: Why does my maize crop turn yellow and stop growing tall even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa kwɛ̃mɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize crop lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plant leaves need to stay green. Adding compost, animal manure, or NPK fertilizer will replenish the soil and help the maize bounce back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei ahe koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo NPK ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How do I store my harvested maize in a silo so insects do not eat it all?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ ato silo mli? Koni kooloi bibii lɛ akaye fɛɛ?

english: Maize must be completely dried under the sun until the grains are hard before putting them in a silo. Moisture attracts mold and insects, so keeping the grains dry and using airtight storage bags or approved storage dust keeps weevils away.
ga: Esa akɛ agbi ŋmãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee shiŋŋ dani akɛwo ŋmãa ŋmãa mli. Fɛ̃i gbalaa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii. No hewɔ lɛ, ha ŋmaa lɛ agbi ni okɛ vacuum storage bags loo sũ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akɛtoɔ mli lɛ atsu nii koni ŋmeii akabote mli.

english: Why do my maize cobs rot or grow white mold right after I harvest them from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ loo amɛnáa ŋmeii yɛŋ beni mikpa amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Maize rots after harvest if it is gathered while still wet from dew or rain, or if it was harvested too early. Drying the cobs in a well-ventilated, sunny area immediately after harvesting prevents mold from taking over.
ga: Abɛi fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ kɛji akɛ abua naa be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lolo kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ mli. aloo kɛji akɛ akpa mra tsɔ Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ yɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii ni baaye nɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Can I feed the raw maize I harvest straight from my farm to my poultry?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ni mikpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aha mikooloi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yes, chickens can eat plain maize for energy, but maize alone does not have enough protein or minerals for them to grow well or lay eggs. Crushing the maize and mixing it with fish meal or soybean meal makes a complete diet.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kooloi baanyɛ aye ŋmãa daa koni amɛná hewalɛ. Shi ŋmãa pɛ bɛ protein loo mineral ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ekwɛ̃ loo ekɛwoɔ ŋmãa. Abele ni agbɛɔ ni akɛ loo loo soybean niyenii futuɔ lɛ haa niyenii ni yeɔ emuu baa.

english: Why is it better for me to grow my own maize to feed my chickens instead of buying ready-made feed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ makwɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mi ŋmãa koni mikɛha mi kooloi lɛ niyenii moŋ fe ni mahe niyenii ni afee klalo lɛ?

english: Growing your own maize reduces your overall costs because ready-made feed includes transport fees and profit margins added by sellers. Using your own grain lowers your feed bill significantly.
ga: Bo diɛŋtsɛ o-ŋmã ni ooodu lɛ baaha shika fɛɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ aba shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɔ ni fata kooloi aniyenii ni afee klalo lɛ he ji shika ni akɛmajeɔ kɛ sɛɛnamɔ ni mɔ ni hɔ̃ɔ lɛ kɛfataa he. Kɛ́ okɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ odumɔwui tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni okɛyeɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi waa.

english: Small holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworms, which are common pests in Ghana. Checking your fields early and spraying neem leaf extract or recommended bio-pesticides will stop them from destroying the farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli mra Ni neem baa mli nu loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ amɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akpa ŋmɔ mli hiɛkpatamɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my maize crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa?

english: Maize is ready to harvest when the outer leaves turn papery and brown, and the grains become hard. If you press a grain with your thumbnail and it does not leave a soft dent, the crop is mature.
ga: Abɛi efee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ etsɔ woji kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. ni dumɔwui lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa Kɛji okɛ oshishifa lɛ nyɛ ŋmaa lɛ nɔ ni eshiii ŋmei ni yɔɔ blɛoo. Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the same field after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the earth. Crops like cowpeas and groundnuts put nitrogen back into the dirt naturally, making the soil rich again for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmei kɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Is it better to plant seeds saved from my last maize harvest or buy certified seeds from an extension agent?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli loo mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ extension agent dɛŋ?

english: Certified hybrid seeds are tested to produce much higher yields and withstand pests better than saved seeds. Saved seeds often grow weaker plants and produce smaller cobs season after season.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ mli koni ana yibiiwoo babaoo kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni hi fe dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ. Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ fɔɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ be mli.

english: How do I know if my farm soil is healthy enough to support good crop yields?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Dark, moist soil that crumbles easily in your hand and has earthworms is usually healthy and fertile. If your soil is pale, hard, or overly sandy, your crops will grow slowly because the soil lacks the organic matter needed to feed them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni edɔ ni fiteɔ oya yɛ niji amli ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yɔɔ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii baa. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ, ewa, loo eyɛ ŋã tsɔ Onibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nibii ni he hiaa ni baaha amɛye nii.

english: When is the right time to sow my seeds after the long dry season ends?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui beni hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ eho lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should wait until the rainy season brings two or three heavy rains that thoroughly wet the soil deep down. Planting after just the first light shower can trick seeds into germinating only to dry up when the sun comes back out.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli dani oná nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyiɔ obɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ alaka dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi pɛ kɛji hulu lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a signal that the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to make food and grow strong. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer early will help the leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fataa he mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my plantain trees producing small, thin bunches of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ?

english: When too many suckers (shoots) grow around one main plantain stem, they steal the food and water from the parent tree. Cut off excess suckers and leave only two or three healthy ones per stand so the main tree has enough power to produce big fruit.
ga: Beni suckers (tso) babaoo ni miida yɛ tso wulu kome he lɛ fa babaoo. Amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso nyɛ lɛ mli. Kpɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oshi ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ shidaamɔ kome mli koni eha tso titri lɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo yibii wuji.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce the food that builds large tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines toward the sun while keeping the leaves off the damp ground where fungal diseases can easily attack them.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni feɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he yɛ be mli ni ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ akashɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ atutua amɛ oya lɛ.

english: Flowers fall off when the plant gets stressed by extreme afternoon heat or dry soil. Spreading dry grass or mulch around the base of your pepper plants helps keep the root area cool and moist so the flowers stay on.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli. Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii afɔ ehe. Pepper tso lɛ shishi yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot under the ground during the wet months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ nyɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped in the soil around them for too long without draining away. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to flow away, keeping the roots safe.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni oha shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe

english: What causes small ragged holes in my young maize leaves, and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: Those holes are caused by hungry pests like armyworms hiding inside the plant leaves. Applying an approved control product directly into the center funnel of the plant early in the morning stops them before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ tamɔ asraafoi awuiyelɔi ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tsei ahe baai amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nakai bu lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛyeɔ nɔ lɛ wo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ehaa amɛkpaa dani amɛfiteɔ he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Can I plant groundnuts in the same field alongside my maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ ŋmei masɛi?

english: Yes, groundnuts are great partner crops because their roots take nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil and helps your maize grow better without competing heavily for food.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ji nanemɛi tso kpakpa ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eye ebua o-abele lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ niyenii babaoo akaŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops struggle so much even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔ mɔdɛŋ waa yɛ nugbɔ babaoo ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than main crops and steal the nutrients, sunlight, and water out of the soil before your plants can take them. Clearing weeds early in the crop's life ensures your main crops get all the food they need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ niyenii, hulu la, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani otsei lɛ baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ egbekɛbiiashi lɛ haa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important to plant my maize in straight rows with measured spacing instead of scattering the seeds across the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu mi ŋmãa lɛ yɛ ŋmãa ni ja ni asusu gbɛ ni yɔɔ teŋ lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooogbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ

english: Planting in straight lines with proper spacing ensures that every plant gets enough sunlight, soil nutrients, and water without competing with its neighbors. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much easier for you.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ ni gbɛ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ akutsoŋbii akaŋ Ehaa jwɛi ŋmɔmɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo.

english: Why do people cover the soil around young plant stems with dried grass or leaves after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei bibii ahe lɛ nɔ beni amɛdu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dried grass, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground so it does not dry out under the hot sun. It keeps the soil cool and stops weeds from growing around your tender crops.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni ekagbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃ yɛ he fɛɛ he. Oŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that scorch easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or bananas nearby creates a living canopy that protects the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains loo banana ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la fɛɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together on the same field, or will they ruin each other's growth?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ loo amɛbaafite amɛhe dalɛ?

english: You can plant them together because maize grows fast and is harvested within three to four months, while cassava grows slower and takes over the space later. This allows you to get two different food harvests from the same piece of land without them damaging each other.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu amɛ yɛ he kome ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji 3-4 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa daa blɛoo ni eŋɔ he lɛ sɛɛ mli. Enɛ haa onine shɛɔ niyenii srɔtoi enyɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ he kome ni efiteee amɛhe.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting groundnuts or beans on my land before I plant maize the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu ŋmei yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which naturally extracts nitrogen from the air and puts it into the soil. When you plant maize afterward, it uses this stored nitrogen as natural food to grow taller and yield bigger ears.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Ekɛ nitrogen ni ato nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii koni ekwɛ̃ ni ekɛ toi wuji aba.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my corn plants turning pale yellow even though they get enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ? Nɛgbɛ enáa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient for green leaf growth. When nitrogen is lacking in the soil, the plant moves what little it has to the newer top leaves, causing the older lower leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ baajie nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛya baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do weeds growing close to my young crops cause my crops to stay short and produce low yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds act like food thieves on your farm—they grow faster and aggressively suck up the water, fertilizer, and light that your crops need to thrive, leaving your crops weak and starved.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛdaraa oya ni amɛheɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la ni he hiaa bo koni onibii lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni hɔmɔ baaye bo.

english: Will removing extra suckers or shoots from my plantain trees harm them or help them produce better food?
ga: Ani ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni mijie kɛjɛ midumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ baaye amɛ awui loo ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛwo niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Removing extra suckers helps the main plantain tree because it stops the plant from sharing its energy among too many stems. Leaving only one or two healthy suckers ensures the parent plant concentrates its nutrients into producing large, heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwu titri lɛ ejaakɛ ehaa tso lɛ kɛ eshishifã lɛ jaa hewalɛ babaoo tsɔ. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ náa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa babaoo ni ekɛwoɔ plantains akui wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are there ragged holes appearing in the funnel center of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ yaafo ko jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ a-cone lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Ragged holes inside the growing center of young maize are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on the soft leaf tissues. Catching and treating this early prevents the pest from eating the growing point and destroying the entire crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahe ŋmeii lɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni miida lɛ amli lɛ baa. Mra ni ana kɛ tsamɔ Ebaatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkaye hei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ ni amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my crop seeds immediately after the very first rainfall of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry stretch before the main rainy season truly starts. If you plant too early, the seeds may germinate but will quickly dry up and die in the hot soil when the rain stops for several days.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃. Shi egbiɔ oya ni egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on some of my cocoa trees turning yellow and dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves can be a sign of diseases like Cocoa Swollen Shoot or severe nutrient loss. When trees are infected, their veins get blocked and cannot transport food and water properly, causing the leaves to dry up and fall off.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ baanyɛ afee hela okadi, tamɔ kookoo tsei ni efuu loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni elaaje waa. Kɛji tso lɛ he hela lɛ Là fãji lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ niyenii kɛ nu aya jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa baai lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: How do diseases move from a sick cocoa farm down the road into my healthy cocoa farm?
ga: Te helai gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ ni hela mɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa mi-kookoo ŋmɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Diseases like Swollen Shoot are carried by tiny insects called mealybugs. These insects can be blown by the wind, carried by ants, or moved on clothing, cutlasses, and boots when workers move between different farms.
ga: Helai tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ, ŋmeii bibii kɛbaa. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ aŋɔ kooloi bibii lɛ, ŋmeii baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ loo atadei, dadei kɛ bɔɔtui baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ be mli ni nitsulɔi lɛ nyiɛɔ ŋmɔji ateŋ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if a disease in my cocoa farm is spreading from tree to tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji helai ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ egbɛ eshwa tso kome nɔ kɛtee tso kroko nɔ?

english: If you see a sick tree and then notice that neighboring trees next to it start showing swollen branches, red leaf veins, or smaller pods, the disease is actively spreading from tree to tree.
ga: Kɛji ona tso ko ni hela mɔ lɛ ni oyɔse akɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ aniji efuu, baai lɛ ahe fãji tsuru, loo ŋmeii bibii lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hela lɛ miigbɛ eshwa tso kome nɔ kɛmiiya ekroko nɔ.

english: Why do extension officers say I must cut down my cocoa tree if it gets sick instead of just spraying it with medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ akɛ esa akɛ afo cocoa tso lɛ kɛji hela mɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni akɛ tsofa lɛ baaha lɛ kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Some cocoa diseases, like the Swollen Shoot virus, live deep inside the sap and wood of the tree where chemical sprays cannot reach. Cutting down the tree is the only way to kill the virus and save neighboring healthy trees.
ga: Kookoo helai komɛi, tamɔ Swollen Shoot virus lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ mli nu kɛ tsei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Tsei ni afoɔ lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbeɔ hela lɛ ni ahaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anáa hewalɛ.

english: If only one cocoa tree in my farm looks sick, why do officers want to cut down the healthy-looking ones next to it too?
ga: Kɛji akɛ hela mɔ kookoo tso kome pɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Mɛni hewɔ onukpai lɛ baasumɔ ni amɛfo kookoo tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Cocoa viruses spread through roots and mealybugs before symptoms appear. Nearby trees might already be infected even if they still look green, so cutting a small buffer ring around the sick tree stops hidden disease from spreading further.
ga: Cocoa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii amli dani okadii lɛ jeɔ kpo. Ekolɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ená hela momo kɛji amɛji eŋɔli lolo po, no hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ afo gbɛtsii nii bibioo ko lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua. Abɔle tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ahe koni helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ akagbɛ ashwã babaoo.

english: Will my cocoa tree grow back healthy if I just cut off the sick branches instead of removing the whole trunk?
ga: Ani mi-cacao tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ ni ehiɛ hewalɛ kɛji mifo niji ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ najiaŋ?

english: No, because viruses like Swollen Shoot live throughout the entire tree, including the trunk and roots. Trimming just the branches leaves the virus alive in the stump, allowing it to infect new shoots and nearby trees.
ga: Dabi, helai tamɔ Swollen Shoot hiɔ tso lɛ mli fɛɛ. Nɔ ni fata he ji tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Nine kome pɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaha hela lɛ ahi shi yɛ tso lɛ shishi. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã tsei heei kɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are extension workers marking my cocoa farm into blocks before cutting down diseased trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛkuu nɔkwɛlɔ lɛ kadi mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ akɛ eji blɔki lɛ? Dani abaafolɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ

english: Dividing the farm into blocks helps measure the exact area affected and ensures that workers clear every infected tree in a organized way, preventing infected pockets from being accidentally left behind.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mlijaa yɛ blɔkii amli Ebaaye ebua bo ni osusu he ni ena naagba lɛ he pɛpɛɛpɛ. kɛ nɔmimaa akɛ nitsulɔi lɛ ajie tso fɛɛ tso ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ lɛ yɛ gbɛjianɔtoo naa. Tsi baagi ni hela emɔ mli lɛ naa koni akashi yɛ sɛɛ yɛ oshara mli.

english: Is the soil where my sick cocoa trees grew poisoned by the disease?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni mi-kokoo tso ni hela mɔ lɛ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ hela nɛɛ nɔ?

english: No, cocoa viruses live inside the living plant tissues and insects, not in the dirt itself. Once the old roots die completely, the soil is safe for new crops and cocoa seedlings.
ga: Dabi, kookoo mli helai hiɔ tso ni hiɛ ka kɛ kooloi amli. Jeee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛji shishifãi momo lɛ egbo kwraa Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee shweshweeshwe kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii heei kɛ kookoo dumɔwui.

english: How long do I have to wait before I can plant new cocoa seedlings where infected trees were cut down?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani madu kookoo dumɔwui heei kɛjɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli?

english: You must wait until the old stumps and root systems are completely dead and dry, which starves out the disease-carrying insects. Planting plantains or food crops first provides shade and restores the soil before new cocoa goes in.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi tso lɛ shishifã lɛ kɛ shishifã momo lɛ baagbo kwraa ni egbi. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye kooloi ni kɛ helai baa lɛ. Kɛ́ adu plantains loo niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hulutsoo ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ dani kookoo hee abaye nɔ.

english: What should I do immediately if I spot a swollen branch or red leaf vein on one of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji mina tsei niji ni efuu loo baai tsuji ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ eko nɔ lɛ?

english: Report it right away to a local extension officer so they can inspect it. Catching disease very early allows you to deal with one tree before it infects your whole farm.
ga: Bɔɔ enɛ he amaniɛ otsɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ mli. Hela ni ooomɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otsaa tso kome dani egbɛɔ eshwaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense sunlight and can dry out quickly. Plantain trees grow fast and have large leaves that provide living shade, protecting the young cocoa trees and keeping the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbi oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why is it important for me to put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves and catch direct sunlight. When the leaves get enough sun, the plant makes more energy, which leads to larger and healthier yam tubers under the ground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã ni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa Tsei lɛ baaha hewalɛ babaoo aba. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my vegetable crops with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi aha he ni mi-vegetables lɛ yɔɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, acts as a protective blanket. It keeps the soil cool under direct sun, slows down water evaporation so you water less, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Mulch ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. koni okɛ nu akashwie nɔ fioo ni otsi jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow starting from the middle of the leaf?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing in the center of lower maize leaves is a sign that the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for green leaf growth. Applying a nitrogen-based fertilizer like Urea or NPK helps the plant regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Yellow ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei lɛ ahe baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ adalɛ Kɛ akɛ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, tamɔ urea loo NPK tsuɔ nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies, or a virus transmitted by them. Controlling these small insects early prevents leaf distortion and keeps the plant producing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ amɛmli lɛ mli kooloi bibii akudɔmɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Ebaatsi baa lɛ sɛɛkuu naa ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo yibii.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants before any tomatoes appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ dani tomato lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or uneven watering, such as long dry periods followed by heavy watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the flowers set into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli, tamɔ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ ni nu ni akɛhaa amɛ waa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni amɛwoɔ shi.

english: How do I know when my cassava crops are fully mature and ready to be dug up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Cassava is usually mature between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell it is ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the ground surrounding the stem begins to crack from the growing tubers underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baai lɛ efee klalo kɛji baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishi jeɔ shishi efoɔ kɛjɛɔ bulb ni miida yɛ shishi lɛ he.

english: Why do the leaves on my young maize field have ragged holes eaten right through them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ egbɛ eshwa amɛhe lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed inside the central leaves of the maize plant. Inspecting the field early and applying recommended control measures prevents them from destroying the plant's growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mra Ni okɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ tso lɛ atsu nii lɛ baatsi he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ fitemɔ naa.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning dark black and rotting while still on the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that spreads quickly in damp, shaded, and high-humidity conditions. Pruning excess tree branches to let in sunlight and clearing weeds around the base helps air circulate and keeps the pods dry.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ, he ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli koni hulu la aba mli, ni ajieɔ jwɛi ni bɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ ni ehaa tsei lɛ amli tsei lɛ agbiɔ.

english: Why should I leave proper spacing between my maize plants instead of planting them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ato he ko ni sa moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When maize plants are crowded together, they compete with one another for soil nutrients, sunlight, and water. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food and light to produce big, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ eyi amɛhe obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, hulu la kɛ nu. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why is it better to plant my crops in straight rows instead of just scattering the seeds everywhere on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu dumɔwui yɛ he fɛɛ he yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows gives each crop enough space to get air, light, and nutrients. It also makes it much easier for you to weed, apply fertilizer, and harvest without stepping on your crops.
ga: Ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ ená kɔɔyɔɔ, la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Agbɛnɛ hu, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo akɛ obaajie jwɛi, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, ni okpa ŋmɔshi nii ni okɛ onibii lɛ shwieee shi.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leads to weak, thin plants that produce very small yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa ni woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ baa.

english: Why do my plants need equal space around them to grow well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ he ko he hiaa mi tsei lɛ yɛ amɛhe lɛ? Ekome kɛha dalɛ kpakpa

english: Equal spacing ensures that no plant is blocked from getting full sunlight, which crops need to make food. It also gives the roots enough room to spread out and draw water and plant food from the soil.
ga: Nakai gbɛ ni kã amɛteŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ haa tsei ko bɛ ni tsiɔ hulu la ni yeɔ emuu lɛ naa. ni ji tsei ni he hiaa kɛha nihoomɔ Ehaa shishifãi lɛ hu hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni amɛjieɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why does planting in straight lines make weeding my farm easier?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni dumɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ mlɛo lɛ?

english: Straight lines create clear pathways between rows, allowing you to walk freely and move tools or weeding equipment without damaging your growing crops.
ga: Linei ni ja lɛ feɔ gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ yɛ linei lɛ ateŋ. Ehaa onyɛɔ onyiɛɔ oya ni okɛ onibii loo nibii ni okɛtsuɔ nii kɛjieɔ jwɛi lɛ yaa he kroko ni ofiteee onibii ni okwɛɔ lɛ.

english: Can I make good money and get a high harvest if I only have a small land like two acres?
ga: Ani manyɛ maná shika kpakpa ni maná yibii babaoo kɛji miyɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko ni dalɛ ji acre enyɔ pɛ?

english: Yes, you can. If you follow proper farming practices like planting in lines, controlling weeds early, and managing your soil properly, a small, well-managed plot can produce higher yields and profit than a poorly managed large farm.
ga: Hɛɛ obaanyɛ, kɛji onyiɛ okwaayeli nifeemɔi ni sa tamɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ line mli lɛ sɛɛ. Jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ mra kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ Okwaafoi bibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo ni sɛɛnamɔ aba fe ŋmɔ agbo ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do some farmers get more harvest from a small farm than others get from a huge farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi naa babaoo kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji bibii amli fe okwaafoi krokomɛi ni jɛɔ ŋmɔji wuji amli lɛ?

english: Farmers with small farms who get high yields pay close attention to proper spacing, timely weeding, and good crop care, ensuring almost every seed grows into a healthy, productive plant.
ga: Esa akɛ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji bibii ni amɛnáa yibii babaoo lɛ agbala amɛjwɛŋmɔ kɛya he ni esa akɛ amɛto amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be naa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ Enɛ haa nɔ ni miihe ashɛ dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu daa ni etsɔɔ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii.

english: How do I know the right amount of seed to buy for a two-acre farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male dumɔwui abɔ ni sa ni esa akɛ mahe kɛha ŋmɔ ni dalɛ ji acre 2 lɛ?

english: By knowing the recommended spacing between rows and plants for your crop, you can calculate the exact number of plant locations on your two acres, which prevents buying too many or too few seeds.
ga: Lemɔ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ ehi ŋwɛi ŋta kɛ tsei ateŋ kɛha odumɔ. Obaanyɛ obu he pɔtɛɛ ni obaadu nii yɛ oshikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre 2 lɛ nɔ lɛ he akɔntaa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akaheɔ dumɔwui babaoo loo fioo tsɔ.

english: At what point do I need to start using machines on my farm instead of planting by hand?
ga: Mɛɛ be ehe baahia ni mabɔi tsɔnei kɛ nitsumɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mikɛ minine baadu nii?

english: You should consider machines when your land becomes too large to plant manually on time, or when hiring human labor becomes more expensive and slower than using a planter machine.
ga: Esa akɛ osusu tsɔnei ahe beni he ni oyɔɔ lɛ da tsɔ ni onyɛŋ okɛ onine adu yɛ be naa lɛ. Aloo beni adesai anitsumɔ ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ jara wa ni ehiɛɔ shi fe tsɔnei ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ.

english: Are there simple machines I can rent to help me plant if I cannot afford to buy big tractors?
ga: Ayɛ tsɔnei ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Nɛgbɛ manyɛ maha koni maye mabua kɛkwɛ tsei? Kɛji minyɛɛɛ mahe trakta agbo ko?

english: Yes, many farming services rent out small hand-pushed seed planters or small motorized equipment that can line and plant seeds quickly without requiring you to buy expensive machinery.
ga: Hɛɛ, okwaayeli nitsumɔhei babaoo haa tsɔnei bibii ni akɛ niji tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ dumɔwui loo tsɔnei bibii ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii ni baanyɛ adu ni adu dumɔwui oya ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsɔnei ni jara wa.

english: How does using a planting machine help my farm grow better crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔne ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ ni ekwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: A planting machine drops seeds at the exact same depth and distance every time, ensuring that all your crops germinate at the same time and grow uniformly across your entire field.
ga: Mɔ ni duɔ dumɔwui lɛ duɔ dumɔwui yɛ mlibotemɔ kɛ sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ kome mli be fɛɛ be. Enɛ haa onibii fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ be kome mli. ni ekwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because their roots are not deep enough to handle harsh sunlight and dry winds. Without shade trees like plantain or forest trees to shield them, the intense sun dries out the leaves, causing them to turn yellow and drop to save the plant's life.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii biɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo kooi ni baaha hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ bɛ lɛ baaha baai lɛ agbi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi koni tso lɛ wala ahi shi.

english: Why do I see small holes in my young maize leaves and green dirt inside the center of the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ kɛ muji eŋɔli ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm attack. The caterpillars hide inside the center growing point of the maize plant during the day, eating the fresh leaves and leaving droppings behind, which stops the plant from growing healthy cobs.
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworm tutuamɔ he okadi. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe teeɔ hei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Amɛyeɔ baai heei lɛ ni amɛshiɔ ŋmeii lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi. Enɛ haaa cob tso lɛ adara waa.

english: Why does my cassava farm produce very tall bushes with lots of leaves, but tiny tubers under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi ni kwɔlɔ waa kɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or green manure, the cassava plant spends all its food energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of sending that food down into the roots to swell into large tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsɔ. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ eniyenii hewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, e haa jamɛ a niye ní ɔ yaa sisi ɔ mi konɛ e tsɔ bulb agbo ko.

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen and nutrients from the soil. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot drains the land's strength, leads to smaller harvests each year, and allows pests and diseases that feed on maize to multiply in that soil.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu nii shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, daa afi lɛ, nikpamɔ ni baa lɛ faaa. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ babaoo yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when the fruits are growing big during heavy winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai lɛ dara yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain roots grow shallow in the ground and do not anchor deep into the soil. As the heavy bunch grows at the top, the tree becomes top-heavy, so strong wind can easily pull the shallow roots out of the ground unless you support the trunk with a sturdy bamboo pole.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ nɔ, ni amɛyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji kuu lɛ da yɛ ŋwɛi Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ ooojɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ja okɛ ŋmei tso ni wa fi tso lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off before they can grow into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛdara ni amɛbatsɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they feel stressed by extreme heat or sudden changes in soil water. If the soil gets too dry or too soaked, or if the afternoon heat is too high, the plant drops its flowers to save energy.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nu tsakemɔi trukaa hao amɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo edɔ tsɔ Aloo kɛji shwane mli latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do the edges of my crop leaves turn brown and look burnt after I place fertilizer near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ashishigbɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni etamɔ nɔ ni eshã beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo amɛhe lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer is like concentrated salt. Placing high amounts directly against the plant stem or on dry soil draws water out of the roots instead of feeding them, which causes leaf tips and edges to dry up and look burnt.
ga: Fertilizer tamɔ ŋmei ni mli edɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ babaoo wo tsei lɛ ashishifãi anɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaagbala nu kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeebote mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ ashishi kɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni etamɔ nɔ ni eshã.

english: Why do my yam vines need high wood stakes to climb instead of growing along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to sunlight to manufacture food for the tuber below. When yam vines lie flat on the hot ground, the leaves get shaded, overheat, and catch diseases easily, resulting in small yam tubers.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛji akɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, baai lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛbaadɔ fe nine ni helai baamɔ amɛ oya. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, sweet potato lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ daraaa.

english: Why do my ripe tomatoes split open on the skin right after a heavy rain shower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hewolo lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: When tomato plants experience a sudden heavy rain after a dry period, the roots rapidly pump water into the fruit. The inside of the tomato expands faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the fruit skin to crack open.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tomato tsei lɛ na nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa trukaa yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa aduawai lɛ amli oya. Tomato lɛ mligbɛ lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji aduawai lɛ ahe fãi ni fãa.

english: Why do the maize seeds I dried and saved from my previous harvest fail to sprout when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni migbi ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu lɛ?

english: Saved seeds fail to sprout if they were stored with moisture inside or damaged by weevils. Moisture makes seeds spoil or lose their life energy while sitting in storage, so using clean, properly dried, insect-free seeds is critical for good germination.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ kwɛŋ kɛji akɛ akɛto ŋmɔtɔ mli loo ŋmeii efite. Fɛ̃i haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ loo amɛhe waaa beni amɛtaraa nitoohe lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, okɛ dumɔwui ni he tse atsu nii. Egbi jogbaŋŋ Ni ŋmeii ni bɛ mli lɛ he miihia koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up when the plant lacks nitrogen. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure gives the leaves their dark green color back so they can feed the growing corn cobs.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with thick leaves but produce very small roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ baai ni mli tse shi shishifãi lɛ daraaa lɛ?

english: When cassava receives too much nitrogen or water, it puts most of its energy into growing stems and leaves instead of roots. Avoiding high-nitrogen fertilizers late in the season helps the plant direct its energy underground to swell the tubers.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa nine shɛ nitrogen loo nu babaoo nɔ Ekɛ ehewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni miida lɛ ahe nii moŋ fe shishifãi. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ baaye abua tsei lɛ ni amɛkudɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ koni eha ŋmɔji lɛ amli alɛɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants drop their flowers before any bean pods appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers usually drop off when tiny insect pests like flower thrips feed on the delicate buds. Protecting the plants with natural neem leaf extracts during early flowering prevents thrips from destroying the blossoms so pods can form.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ fɔfɔi thrips lɛ ye ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Kɛ akɛ neem tso ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ bu tsei ahe yɛ fɔfɔii ni amɛwoɔ mra lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni thrips akafite fɔfɔi lɛ koni pods lɛ afee.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Spraying a mild soap-and-neem mixture helps clear these insects and stops new leaves from curling.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo mites lɛ kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni ŋmeii egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli Samla kɛ neem ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni mli ejɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ Enɛ baaye abua ni ajie ŋmeii nɛɛ ni ebaatsi baai heei ni shwieɔ shi lɛ anaa.

english: This condition is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, which often happens when watering is uneven. Keeping the soil consistently moist allows the tomato roots to continuously absorb calcium from the soil.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ji fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaha tomato shishifãi lɛ aná calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be.

english: Why are my ginger stems suddenly becoming soft and rotting at the soil level?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ginger niji lɛ yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛmiifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Soft rot in ginger is caused by soil fungi and bacteria that thrive in soggy, waterlogged soil. Planting ginger on raised beds with good drainage prevents excess water from collecting around the rhizomes and causing rot.
ga: Sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ sũ ni efɔ, ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei fitemɔ fioo baa. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ saatso ni nɔ kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi nu ni fa fe nine lɛ naa koni ekabua ehe naa. Rizom kɛ ŋmɔtɔ

english: The dry harmattan winds and hot sun evaporate water from young cocoa leaves faster than their shallow roots can absorb it. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or gliricidia around them creates shade and holds moisture in the air.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi kɛ hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa nu ni jɛɔ kookoo baai bibii amli lɛ feɔ la oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains loo glicidia ni aduɔ yɛ jɛmɛ he fɛɛ he. Ehaa hulutsoo baa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily after heavy rain even without strong winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ waaa po lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall easily when pests like root nematodes or banana weevils destroy their underground root system. Planting clean, disease-free suckers and mulching around the base keeps the root anchor strong.
ga: Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ shishifãi ni ji nematodes loo banana weevils lɛ fite shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Adumɔ tsei ni he tse ni hela bɛ mli lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Shishitoo lɛ haa shishifã lɛ he wa.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting and shrinking while stored in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ bɔi shweremɔ ni egbɔjɔ beni mikɛtoɔ mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams break dormancy and sprout when stored in warm, bright places, using up their internal water and nutrients. Storing yams on raised racks in a well-ventilated, shady yam barn slows down sprouting and keeps tubers firm.
ga: Sweet potatoes baafo shihilɛ mli ni ekwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni hulu tsoɔ ni hulu tsoɔ waa. kɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ atsu nii Akɛ sweet potatoes atoɔ ŋtayaai ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋtayaai ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why does my lowland rice yield drop if the field dries out for a few days during growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa lɛ baa shi kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi yɛ be mli ni mikwɛɔ lɛ?

english: Lowland rice relies on standing water to easily draw up soil nutrients and keep weed growth down. When the field dries out, roots get stressed, weeds sprout quickly to compete for food, and grain production drops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ nu ni damɔ shi nɔ koni ekɛjie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya ni eha jwɛi lɛ adalɛ aba shi. Kɛ́ ŋmɔji amli egbi lɛ, shishifãi lɛ haoɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya koni amɛye niyenii he akaŋ. ni ŋmaa ni anáa lɛ ba shi

english: Why do some of my maize plants survive diseases while others right next to them die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ helai nyɛɛɛ amɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ekomɛi lɛ? yɛ be mli ni tsei krokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ gboi lɛ.

english: Different plant seeds have different natural strength and immunity. Improved or hybrid seed varieties are specially bred to withstand common sicknesses, whereas older or uncertified seeds can easily catch diseases and die.
ga: Dumɔwu henɔ fɛɛ henɔ yɛ hewalɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ srɔtoi. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ loo dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni egbɔ loo ni bɛ he odaseyeli lɛ baanyɛ aná hela oya ni amɛgboi.

english: Why are the stems of my cassava plants swelling up and looking abnormal?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ fuuɔ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni jeee nɔ ni sa lɛ?

english: Stem swelling in cassava is usually a symptom of a pest infestation, like mealybugs, or a fungal infection. The plant tissue swells as a physical reaction to damage caused by the pests feeding inside it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei tsei ni efuu lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ mealybugs loo fungal helai ahe okadi. Tso mli fãji lɛ fũuɔ akɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ nifeemɔ ko ni jɛɔ nibii ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛbaa lɛ mli.

english: Can sudden cold weather or heavy rains make my pepper plants wilt and look weak?
ga: Ani fɛ̃i ni baa trukaa loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni amɛfee tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, sudden drops in temperature or excessive cold water around the roots can shock warmth-loving crops. Cold soil slows down how fast roots can absorb nutrients, making the plant droop and feel stressed.
ga: Hɛɛ, hulutsoo ni baa shi trukaa loo nu ni mli ejɔ babaoo ni ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei ni sumɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ ahe afee shoo. Shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛnuɔ haomɔ he.

english: How many hours of direct sunlight do my food crops need every day to produce well?
ga: ŋmɛlɛtswai enyiɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ he hiaa mi niyenii tsei lɛ daa gbi koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Most common crops in Ghana, such as maize, cassava, and vegetables, need about 6 to 8 hours of uninterrupted sunlight daily to convert light into energy for strong growth and good yields.
ga: Nibii ni afɔɔ feemɔ yɛ Ghana, tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ aduawai, biɔ aaafee ŋmɛlɛtswai 6 kɛyashi 8 ni hulu la ni yaa nɔ daa gbi. Koni atsake la awo hewalɛ mli kɛha dalɛ ni mli wa kɛ yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves turn pale and light green when grown under dense tree shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ akwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Plants produce a green substance called chlorophyll to catch light and make food. When big trees block necessary sunlight for too long, the leaves cannot produce enough food energy and begin losing their rich green color.
ga: Tsei feɔ nɔ ko ni ji eŋɔli ni atsɛɔ lɛ klorofil ni emɔɔ la ni efee niyenii. Kɛ tsei wuji tsi hulu la lɛ naa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ nyɛŋ afee niyenii hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa. ni ebɔi ehe su ni ji eŋɔli ni mli edɔ lɛ sɛɛ fomɔ.

english: How can I tell if a diseased crop is completely dead or if it can still recover?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso ko ni hela emɔmɔ lɛ egbo kwraa loo ebaanyɛ ehiɛ ahi ehe nɔ lolo?

english: Gently scrape a small bit of the outer skin or stem near the base with your fingernail. If the layer underneath is still moist and green, the plant is alive and can recover with proper care, water, and nutrients.
ga: Okɛ onineshi tsɔne lɛ atsɔ kponɔgbɛ loo tso ni bɛŋkɛ shishi lɛ nɔ blɛoo fioo. Kɛji shishigbɛ fã lɛ mli edɔ lolo ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni ebaanyɛ ehiɛ ahi ehe nɔ kɛji akwɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ, nu, kɛ niyenii kpakpai.

english: Can I use artificial night light in my nursery to make my young seedlings grow faster?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ kanei ni akɛfee gbɛkɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii koni mi dumɔwui lɛ adara oya?

english: Giving seedlings additional light hours can speed up growth up to a point, but plants also require a regular period of darkness every night to rest, regulate their internal functions, and grow healthy root systems.
ga: La ŋmɛlɛtswai ni yaa hiɛ ahaa dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛdara oya kɛyashɛ he ko. Shi tsei hu he miihia ni amɛná duŋ gbɛkɛ koni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe. Kudɔ mligbɛ nitsumɔ ni oha shishifã gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli awa

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and feel cold and soft during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛnuɔ he akɛ amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛhe jɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: In intense sun, plants curl their leaves to slow down water loss. The leaves feel soft because they are losing moisture faster through evaporation than the roots can pull from the dry soil.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Tsei baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni nu lɛ akafee mlɛo. Baai lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ ejaakɛ amɛfiteɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young vegetable sprouts fall over and rot at soil level right after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by a fungal disease called 'damping-off,' which thrives in cold, overly wet soil with poor airflow. It attacks fragile young stems right at ground level, killing the seedling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘damping-off’ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa, ni ehiɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ Etutuaa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ni egbeɔ dumɔwui.

english: What is the best way to help my crops recover after a long period without rain?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ maye mabua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Water them deeply during the cool early morning or late evening, cover the soil around them with dry grass mulch to hold moisture, and avoid heavy chemical fertilizers until the plants rebuild their strength.
ga: Okɛ nu awo mli jogbaŋŋ leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi, ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ nɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofai ni tsii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ahe kɛyashi tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to protect them from harsh sunlight and extreme heat. Leaving some taller trees or planting plantains alongside cocoa provides living shade, keeps the soil moist, and prevents the tender leaves from scorching until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo be koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he. tsei kakadaji loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ ni ajieɔ Cocoa lɛ baaha hulutsoo aba. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa baa bibii lɛ shãaa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen, which is a key soil nutrient needed for healthy leaf growth. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore green leaves and healthy crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ akwɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni tsei lɛ hu ada jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer to my crops when the weather is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo miŋmɔshi nibii amli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so plant roots can absorb it. Putting dry fertilizer on dry soil without moisture can scorch the roots and waste your money, as the crop cannot drink in the nutrients.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛshwie shi bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi fata shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni nu bɛ nɔ lɛ he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ ni efite shika. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei nyɛŋ anu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why is it good for me to plant beans or groundnuts on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nutrients and weakens the soil, but legumes like beans and groundnuts naturally put good nitrogen back into the dirt. Rotating maize with legumes restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaa sũ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii kɛ nitrogen kpakpa kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting seeds too closely forces the crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow strong roots and yield large, full cobs of maize.
