ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi ni wa baakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ ŋmãa toi wuji baa.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable crops early in the morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mitsei lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: It is best to water vegetables early in the morning because the moisture sinks deeply into the soil before the hot sun arrives. Watering during the hot afternoon causes quick evaporation and can burn delicate leaves.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔ aduawai anɔ nu leebi ejaakɛ ŋmɔtɔ baabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ aba. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ebaanyɛ eshã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water builds up around them because flat or heavy clay soil traps water and suffocates the roots. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu ni ekã shi ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nu ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight to make food for the tubers underground. Keeping vines off the hot ground prevents leaf diseases and results in bigger yams.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ wain tsei lɛ tsi hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ bɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ foliar helai anaa, ni ebaaha sweet potatoes lɛ afee sweet potatoi wuji.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow small and weak even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo po lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, soil nutrients, and growing space. Even with enough rain, weeds drink up the soil's fertilizer first, leaving your crops starved and weak.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po Jwɛi lɛ hu nuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii ni oduɔ nii lɛ, ni amɛhe baajɔ amɛ.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat the leaves of my young crops during the night?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ gbɛkɛ?

english: Caterpillars like fall armyworms hide under soil or leaf debris during the hot day to avoid the sun and come out at night to feed on tender leaves. Checking plants early in the morning and applying recommended treatments keeps them under control.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ cutworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi loo yɛ baai amli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli koni hulu la akashɛ amɛnɔ. ni amɛje kpo amɛbaye baai bibii gbɛkɛ Tsei lɛ amli kwɛmɔ leebi ni akɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ ahi shi yɛ kudɔmɔ shishi.

english: Why are my young coconuts splitting open on the tree before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokooi lɛ miikwɛ̃ dani amɛbaafee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Coconuts usually split or crack when there is a sudden change in water supply, such as heavy rain after a dry spell. The fruit absorbs water quickly, causing the inside to swell faster than the outer shell can expand.
ga: Kokooi sumɔɔ ni amɛgbala loo amɛgbala kɛji nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tsake trukaa, tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ shwieɔ nu oya, ni no haa emli lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ alɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my coconut trees drop their immature fruits before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei tso lɛ shwieɔ yibii bibii dani edaraa lɛ?

english: Premature fruit drop happens when the tree is stressed by a lack of water, nutrient shortages in the soil, or attacks from sap-sucking insects during early fruit development.
ga: Yibii ni shwieɔ shi oya lɛ baa kɛji nu ni bɛ lɛ hao tso lɛ. niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ tutuamɔ yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ yaa hiɛ mra lɛ.

english: How many years does a new coconut tree take before it starts producing nuts?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei tso hee ko jeɔ ŋmeii feemɔ shishi?

english: It depends on the variety. Dwarf coconut varieties usually start bearing fruit in 2 to 3 years, while traditional tall varieties take about 5 to 7 years to produce their first harvest.
ga: Edamɔ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni ji dwarf lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ blema lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 5 kɛyashi 7 dani amɛwoɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why does my coconut tree stop growing or stay at the same height for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei kpaɔ dalɛ loo amɛhiɔ shi yɛ he kome be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: A tree's growth can stall if its roots hit hard soil layers, if it lacks essential plant food like nitrogen, or if root diseases are preventing it from taking up nutrients.
ga: Tso dalɛ baanyɛ akpa kɛji eshishifãi lɛ yatswa shikpɔŋ ni wa waa. Tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen ni bɛ, loo kɛji shishifãi hela tsiɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ naa.

english: What causes the leaves of my coconut palms to turn yellow and die off?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egboɔ?

english: Yellowing leaves are often caused by nutrient shortages like potassium deficiency, prolonged dry weather, or serious palm sicknesses like Lethal Yellowing disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa, tamɔ potassium ni faaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ŋmɔŋ baa. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo tso hela ni naa wa tamɔ yellow leaf hela ni gbeɔ mɔ

english: Why does the trunk of my crop feel soft or look damaged near the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ loo amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛfite yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Soft trunks are usually a sign of fungal rot or damage from pests like palm weevils, which bore into the soft interior tissue and weaken the stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii egbo loo ŋmeii tamɔ palm weevils, ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ amli ni amɛhaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ lɛ efite.

english: Why do my small coconut seedlings look weak and tender after I transplant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akokoo tsei lɛ bibii nɛkɛ? Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ ni eyɛ blɛoo beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have soft tissue and delicate root systems that burn easily under hot sun and suffer transplant shock if they do not get enough shade and regular water during their first few months.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ fãji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni amɛnaa amanehulu yɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ mli kɛji amɛnáaa hulutsoo kɛ nu ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli.

english: Do I need to water my young coconut trees during the dry season, or can they survive on rain alone?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli? Aloo ani manyɛ mahi shi mikome too kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ?

english: While full-grown palms can survive dry spells, young trees need extra water in the dry season to build strong roots, keep their leaves green, and avoid stunted growth.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei tsei ni eda lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ, nu kroko he miihia tsei bibii yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli koni amɛma shishifãi ni wa. Ha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ dalɛ ni baa shi lɛ he.

english: Can I plant cassava or vegetables between my young coconut trees while waiting for them to fruit?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei loo aduawai yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii ateŋ be mli ni mimɛɔ aduawai?

english: Yes, intercropping with short-term food crops works well during the first 2 to 3 years because it helps shade the soil, keeps weeds down, and gives you food while the palms grow.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 lɛ mli ejaakɛ eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, egbeɔ jwɛi, ni ehaa niyenii be mli ni tso lɛ miida lɛ.

english: How do I know if my farm soil has enough nutrients for coconut trees to grow well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Healthy trees have thick stems and dark green fronds; if your young trees have thin trunks, pale green leaves, or slow growth, the soil is low in nutrients and needs organic manure or fertilizer.
ga: Tso ni wa lɛ yɛ tso ni mli wa kɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa. Kɛji akɛ odumɔwu lɛ yɛ tso bibioo ko ni baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo edaa blɛoo Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehe miihia humus loo organic fertilizer.

english: Why do my crop yields get smaller every season even though I use the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ faaa daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops remove specific nutrients from the soil every time they grow. If you plant the same crop in the same spot year after year without resting the soil or rotating with leguminous crops like beans and groundnuts, the soil loses its richness and cannot support high yields.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni adu amɛ. Kɛji akɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome afi fɛɛ afi ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ejɔɔɔ loo okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii tsakeee lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ baa shi ni enyɛɛɛ ekwɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants are lacking nitrogen, a vital nutrient needed for leaf growth, or that excessive water is suffocating the roots. Adding organic manure or a nitrogen-based fertilizer can help restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ adara Aloo nu babaoo yɛ ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungal infection that thrives in dark, overly damp conditions. Pruning excess shade trees, clearing weeds around the base, and harvesting ripe pods quickly helps air flow through and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ fe nine. Tsei ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ ni okpa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ oya koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli ni ekpa ŋmei lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants have shallow root systems and delicate leaves that quickly lose moisture under strong sun and dry winds. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to young cocoa creates shelter and keeps the surrounding soil moist during dry months.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei ahe lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why are my plantain bunches growing very small compared to other farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwereɔ fioo kɛ akɛto ŋmɔji krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Small plantain bunches often happen when too many sucker shoots grow around one main tree, stealing water and food from it. Cutting away extra suckers so that only two or three remain allows the main plant to put all its energy into growing big bunches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii baa kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ he. tso titri kome Kɛtsɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni ejuɔ kɛjɛɔ nakai tso lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ koni enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ahi shi lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ tsei wuji ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and show yellow patches on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves with yellow patches are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whitefly insects or passed down through infected stem cuttings. Planting disease-resistant cassava stem varieties is the most effective way to prevent this problem.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ woɔ loo amɛtsɔɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli ŋmeii ni afolɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Yam tubers rot underground when water sits in the soil for too long due to poor drainage, or when soil pests like nematodes create tiny wounds that let fungal rots enter. Building higher mounds allows excess water to drain away from the tubers.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli tamɔ nematodes lɛ fee pilamɔi bibii. ni haa ŋmeii boteɔ mli Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize stalks fall over easily whenever there is a strong rain or wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baa lɛ?

english: Maize plants fall over (lodging) when seeds are planted too shallow, when roots are weak, or when stem-borer pests hollow out the stalk. Planting seeds at a proper depth and mounding soil around the plant base gives the roots stronger support.
ga: Abele tsei shwieɔ shi (lodge) kɛji adu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ. Beni shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii, stem borers, tswaa shishifãi lɛ. Dumɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ni sa ni okɛ sũ lɛ ato amɛhe. Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: Tomato plants often drop their flowers when temperature levels get too high, when water is inconsistent, or when there are no bees to pollinate them. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing light cover during extreme heat helps flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. Be mli ni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni ŋmeii bɛ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants shrinking and twisting into tight balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiitsɔ bɔɔlu ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Twisted and wrinkled pepper leaves are caused by tiny pests like aphids, thrips, or mites sucking the sap out of new shoots, or by a virus transmitted by these insects. Spraying early with appropriate organic or recommended sprays controls these pests before leaves become damaged.
ga: Nibii bibii tamɔ thrips, thrips, loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei heei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Mra be mli ni akɛ tsofa ni sa loo ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ nɔ. Eyeɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ dani baai lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight scorches their delicate leaves and dries out the moisture in the soil. Planting fast-growing crops like plantain alongside young cocoa creates a living umbrella that protects the seedlings from heat while they establish deep roots.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gĩɔ. Nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains kɛ kookoo bibii adumɔ. Ehaa hulutsoo baa ni buɔ dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly when I plant the same crop on the same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the exact same crop year after year drains the soil of specific nutrients that the crop relies on, while also allowing crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the dirt. Rotating different crop types restores soil fertility naturally and breaks pest life cycles.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa niyenii ni yɔɔ srɔto ni tsei lɛ damɔɔ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi ni atsakeɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ. ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashihilɛ

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to make healthy green leaves. Adding animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer around the base of the plant helps restore green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛbaabɔle Shishitoo lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants curl up and show light yellow spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellow patches on cassava are symptoms of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by small whiteflies. Planting stem cuttings from disease-free, resistant cassava varieties prevents this virus from spreading in your farm.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ lɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ woɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ. Nibii ni afolɔ kɛjɛ ŋmei henɔi ni nyɛɔ helai kɛ helai ni bɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ hela nɛɛ akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and die suddenly during the day even when the soil has enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Sudden wilting in moist soil is often caused by bacterial wilt, a germ living in the soil that blocks the plant's internal tubes from taking up water. Removing affected plants immediately and avoiding planting tomatoes or peppers in that spot for a season stops the disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni tsiɔ tsei amli paipii lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná nu. Jiemɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tomato loo ŋmɔtɔ ni ooodu yɛ nakai he lɛ he be kome koni hela lɛ akpa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from high heat, irregular watering, or a lack of insect pollinators. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and avoiding sudden dry spells helps the flowers set healthy pepper fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛ la ni mli wa mli lɛ he. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ faaa lɛ ni akɛ mulch haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fũuɔ ni ajieɔ trukaa hulutsoo be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ pepper yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yams grow small tubers even though the vine leaves are big and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii eyɛ mli akɛ wain tso lɛ baai lɛ dara ni eyɛ ŋmeii moŋ lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes yam plants spend all their energy growing tall green leaves instead of building thick tubers under the ground. Yams need nutrients like potassium and phosphorus to encourage big, heavy tuber growth.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛbaa baai kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee yitso ni mli wa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, Sweet potatoes he miihia niyenii tamɔ potassium kɛ phosphorus koni ekɛha ŋmeii wuji ni tsii lɛ adara.

english: How can I tell under the ground if my cassava roots are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava roots are ready for harvest when the main leaves start turning yellow and dropping off, and small cracks appear in the soil around the base of the stem where the expanding tubers are pushing against the dirt.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai titrii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. ni ŋmeii bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle lɛ lɛ mli Tso lɛ shishi ji he ni bulb ni mli elɛɛ lɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do armyworms attack my maize field mostly after a short break in the rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be kukuoo ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fall armyworm moths lay eggs rapidly during hot, dry spells, and without heavy rainfall to wash away the tiny newly hatched caterpillars, their numbers explode. Inspecting the center leaves of young maize plants during dry breaks helps catch them early.
ga: Fɛ̃i be mli ŋmeii fɔɔ amɛwui oya yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Ni nugbɔ ni naa wa ko bɛ ni baaha ŋmeii ni efɔ ehee lɛ aya. Amɛyibɔ ​​lɛ tee hiɛ waa. Kɛ́ okwɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni omɔ amɛ mra.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a water-loving fungus that spreads quickly in cold, wet, and humid air. Pruning extra shade tree branches to let sunlight and wind reach the cocoa trees helps keep the pods dry and stops the fungus.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji hydrophilic fungus ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ hulutsoo be kroko mli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ kookoo tso lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni etsĩɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa.

english: How can I use all the open space on my farm so that no land goes to waste?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ he fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii koni akashi shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: You can use intercropping, which means growing shorter crops in the empty spaces between your main trees. Planting crops together allows you to harvest multiple items from the same piece of land without wasting space.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ intercropping atsu nii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ odu tsei kukuji yɛ he ni yɔɔ otsei titrii lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nibii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni ofiteee he ko.

english: Which crop should I plant first when setting up a mixed coconut and pineapple farm?
ga: Mɛɛ tso esa akɛ adu klɛŋklɛŋ kɛ́ ato ŋmei-ŋmei abɔɔ he gbɛjianɔ?

english: You should plant your main tree crop, like coconut, first so it can establish its position and root system. Once the main trees are planted, you can add short-term crops like pineapples in the surrounding space.
ga: Esa akɛ odu otso titri ni yeɔ afii babaoo, tamɔ ŋmei, dani obaanyɛ ole he ni eyɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Beni adu tso titri lɛ Obaanyɛ okɛ be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei afata he ni ebɔle he lɛ he.

english: Why should I plant pineapples beside my coconut trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ ŋmei tso masɛi lɛ?

english: Pineapples make excellent side crops for coconuts because they grow low to the ground and fit into the open spaces. They provide extra harvest while maximizing the land between your coconut trees.
ga: Pineapple ji tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfataa ŋmeii ahe ejaakɛ edaa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni eshɛɔ hei ni yɔɔ faŋŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Amɛhaa yibiiwoo babaoo yɛ be mli ni amɛhaa gbɛ ni yɔɔ o-coconut tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ yaa hiɛ babaoo.

english: How can planting shorter crops beside my main trees help me make money faster?
ga: Te tsei kukuji ni mikɛduɔ yɛ mitsei titrii lɛ ahe lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná shika oya lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Main trees like coconuts take several years to bear fruit, but fast-growing side crops like pineapples yield much sooner. Planting them together gives you food and income while you wait for your main trees to mature.
ga: Tsei wuji tamɔ ŋmeii heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii. Shi nanemɛi tso ni daa oya tamɔ ŋmei lɛ baawo yibii oya kwraa. Tsei nɛɛ ni ooodu yɛ he kome lɛ baaha oná niyenii kɛ shika yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ otso titri lɛ ni eda lɛ.

english: Can growing certain crops together help me reduce the time I spend weeding my farm?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baanyɛ aha be ni heɔ koni akɛjie jwɛi kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ aba shi?

english: Yes, planting dense living crops like pineapples between your main trees acts as a natural cover. The low foliage blocks sunlight from reaching the soil, which naturally stops weeds from taking over your field.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni hiɛ ka, tamɔ ŋmei ni adu babaoo yɛ otsei titrii lɛ ateŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni akɛhaa nɔ. Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ jwɛi naa koni ekaye oŋmɔji lɛ anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do weeds grow so fast in open field spaces, and how do I stop them naturally?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛkɛ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa jwɛi lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa?

english: Weeds grow quickly when empty soil is exposed to direct sunlight. You can stop them naturally by filling those open spaces with living crops that shade the ground and leave no room for weeds to sprout.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya kɛji shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ shɛ hulu la nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Obaanyɛ okpa amɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ tsei ni hiɛ ka ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ ni oooha nakai hei ni agbele lɛ awo mli lɛ nɔ.

english: How does keeping crop cover on the soil protect my farm during hot seasons?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ buɔ miŋmɔ lɛ he yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Growing ground cover or side crops shields the soil surface from the scorching sun. This keeps the soil cooler, retains moisture longer, and prevents the ground from drying out completely.
ga: Nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nibii ni akɛwoɔ sɛɛ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi kwraa

english: Why do coconut trees need so much space around them when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei he hiaa ni amɛná he ko ni amɛbɔle amɛhe lɛ? babaoo beni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Coconut trees grow large root systems and wide fronds over time. Giving them proper spacing ensures they get enough sunlight and nutrients, while leaving open alleys where you can plant smaller crops.
ga: Kokoo tsei feɔ shishifãi wuji kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛ́ aha amɛ gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shi gbɛjegbɛi ni agbele nɔ ni obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii bibii yɛ nɔ.

english: Do pineapples steal nutrients and water from nearby coconut trees?
ga: Ani ŋmei lɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli?

english: Pineapples have shallow roots compared to coconut trees, which feed deeper in the soil. Because they feed at different soil depths, they can grow side-by-side without stealing each other's food.
ga: Pineapple shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ fe ŋmei tsei, ni amɛyeɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛyeɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ srɔtoi anɔ. Amɛnyɛ amɛdara yɛ he kome ni amɛjuuu amɛhe niyenii.

english: How do I know when it is the right time to add secondary crops to my main tree field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ afata mi tso ŋmɔ titri lɛ he?

english: You can add secondary crops as soon as your primary trees are properly aligned and planted in the ground. Establishing your main layout first makes it easy to safely fill in the remaining spaces.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ afata he kɛji akɛ otsei titrii lɛ eto amɛhe gbɛjianɔ ni adu amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ. Ogbɛjianɔtoo titri lɛ ni ooofee klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ooowo he fɛɛ he ni eshwɛ lɛ mli shweshweeshwe.

english: How does crop sickness travel through the air from my neighbor's farm to mine?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛjɛɔ akutsoŋnyo ko ŋmɔ mli kɛyaa shika tsuru ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Many crop diseases produce tiny, invisible particles called spores that float in the air. The wind can carry these spores over long distances, causing them to land on your healthy crops and infect them even if your field was clean.
ga: Tsei ahe helai babaoo jieɔ nibii bibii bibii. nibii bibii ni anaaa ni atsɛɔ amɛ spores ni hoɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli Kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ aŋɔ nɛkɛ spores nɛɛ kɛya he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa amɛkpɛtɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa kɛji oŋmɔji lɛ amli tse po.

english: Officer, what are these airborne things called spores that people say cause plant diseases?
ga: Official Mɛni ji nibii ni hoɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni atsɛɔ amɛ spores ni gbɔmɛi kɛɔ akɛ ekɛ tsei ahelai baa?

english: Spores are like tiny, dust-like seeds produced by fungi. They float through the air, land on vulnerable crops, and start growing when conditions are right, which causes the plant to fall sick.
ga: Spores tamɔ dumɔwui bibii. tamɔ sũ ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛbaa lɛ Amɛfoɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ nɔ ni ebɔi dalɛ kɛji shihilɛi lɛ sa ni haa tso lɛ hela mɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops seem to get sick more often when the weather stays very damp and wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ hela shii abɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Damp and wet conditions create an ideal environment for plant rot and fungal diseases to thrive. High moisture allows disease spores to germinate quickly and spread across leaves and stems.
ga: Shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ haa shihilɛ ni sa kɛha tsei ni fiteɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ baa. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo lɛ haa helai amli tsɛŋemɔ helai kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa baai kɛ tsei lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: Why do crops in a clean field suddenly start rotting even when I planted healthy seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ ni mli tse mli lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ midu dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Diseases can enter a clean field through airborne spores blown by the wind, water runoff, or damp soil conditions, causing sudden infections even if the original seeds were healthy.
ga: Hela lɛ baanyɛ abote hei ni he tse kɛtsɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ, nu ni hoɔ, loo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ tswaa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ kɛ helai baa trukaa eyɛ mli akɛ shishijee dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ moŋ.

english: Why is it risky to buy crop seeds from any random seller in the market instead of a certified source?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ ooohe dumɔwui kɛjɛ mɛi ni hɔ̃ɔ dumɔwui yɛ jara nɔ lɛ adɛŋ moŋ fe hei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ?

english: Seeds from unverified sources may already carry hidden diseases or contamination from the parent plant. Certified seed sources ensure you plant disease-free seeds that give your crop a healthy start.
ga: Ekolɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ loo muji ni jɛ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ yɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ hei ni akwɛɛɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli momo. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ he odaseyeli lɛ haa onaa nɔmimaa akɛ oodu dumɔwui ni helai bɛ mli ni baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if the seed materials I want to plant are already infected with disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ dumɔwui ni misumɔɔ ni madu lɛ yɛ hela momo?

english: Infected planting materials might show subtle spots, discoloration, or rotting, though some carry hidden diseases inside. Sourcing seeds from certified dealers is the best way to ensure your planting material is clean.
ga: Tso mli nibii ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ baanyɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ bibii, amɛhe su, loo amɛfite. Eyɛ mli akɛ kooloi srɔtoi komɛi yɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ yɛ amɛmli moŋ. Dumɔwui ni ooona kɛjɛ jarayelɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ dɛŋ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ ona nɔmimaa akɛ nɔ ni okɛduɔ nii lɛ he tse.

english: Can treating my seeds with chemicals before planting actually harm or contaminate my crops if done wrong?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ dani aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye midumɔwui lɛ awui loo efite lɛ diɛŋtsɛ kɛji akɛ afee lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ?

english: Yes, using unapproved chemicals or applying the wrong amounts during pre-planting treatment can damage the seeds or contaminate the soil, hindering crop growth instead of protecting it.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo abɔ ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii dani aduɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afite dumɔwui lɛ loo efite shikpɔŋ lɛ. Enɛ tsiɔ tsei adalɛ naa moŋ fe ni eeebu amɛhe.

english: What can I do to protect my farm if a plant disease is blowing through the air in our area?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mabu miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛji tso hela ko tswa kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ wɔ akutso lɛ mli?

english: You can plant windbreaks like tall trees around your field to block airborne disease spores, maintain proper plant spacing for airflow, and apply recommended protective sprays.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu kɔɔyɔɔŋ tsɔnei tamɔ tsei kakadaji ni obɔle he. Oshia lɛ koni obu ohe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe Ha tsei lɛ ahi he ko ni sa koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli. ni okɛ tsofa ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ atsu nii.

english: Does leaving too much standing water around my crops make them rot faster?
ga: Nu lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ani miŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baaha egbo oya?

english: Yes, excessive water creates damp, wet conditions around the roots and stems, making it much easier for rot and fungal diseases to settle in and destroy the plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu babaoo haa ŋmɔtɔ baa tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baahi tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛgbe lɛ.

english: Should I add anything to my seeds right before planting to prevent them from getting sick?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ nɔ ko afata midumɔwui lɛ ahe amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani madu koni hela akamɔ amɛ?

english: Applying recommended seed dressings or treatments before planting protects young seeds from soil-borne fungi and insects, ensuring safe germination and healthy growth.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui ahe nɔ loo tsofa ko ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ tsu nii dani adu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu dumɔwui bibii ahe kɛjɛ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ shweshweeshwe ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and dying before the corn is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil or isn't getting enough water. Adding compost or manure early in the growing stage helps the leaves stay green and feed the growing corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli mra Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa baa lɛ ni ehiɔ shi eŋɔli ni ehaa niyenii kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ.

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or lack of nutrients. Keeping the soil moist and adding mulch around the stems helps the flowers stay on and turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛmiihao amɛ, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ Tso lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni ehiɔ shi ni etsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Leaf curling is a natural self-defense mechanism where the plant rolls its leaves to reduce water loss and protect itself from intense sun and heat.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mɔ he. He ni tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. ni obu ohe kɛjɛ hulu ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he.

english: Why are my crops growing much slower now compared to how they grew years ago on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo kwraa fe nɔ ni midu afii ni eho lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting crops on the same piece of land year after year drains the essential plant food from the soil. Without giving the soil a rest or adding organic matter, crops will grow slower and produce smaller yields.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ blɛoo ni amɛbaawo yibii babaoo ni amɛhaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe loo ekɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he.

english: Why do my plantain fruits take so much longer to grow big in drier areas compared to the forest regions?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛdaraa yɛ hei ni nu bɛ lɛ kɛ akɛto koo mli hei ahe lɛ?

english: Plantains require high humidity and consistent moisture to grow fast. In drier soil and weather, the plant slows down its growth to save energy and survive.
ga: Plantains he miihia ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ ahi shi koni ekwɛ̃ oya. Yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli lɛ Tsei haa amɛdalɛ baa shi koni amɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my okra plants grow very tall with many leaves but produce very few okra pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi okra ŋmeii fioo pɛ ewoɔ lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes okra to spend all its energy growing leaves and stems instead of producing flowers and seed pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa okra lɛ kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛkwɛ̃ɔ baai kɛ tsei lɛ tsuɔ nii. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwuhi.

english: Why did my cassava roots turn out tiny and hard this harvest season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe wa yɛ kpamɔɔ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots fail to expand when the soil is packed too hard, lacks nutrients, or experiences long dry spells during the initial months after planting.
ga: Cassava shishifãi nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli, loo hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ ni adu lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines wither and dry up early before the yam tubers are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ miiho ni amɛmiigbi oya dani sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Early drying of yam vines is often caused by heat stress, water shortages, or soil pests attacking the root system, which cuts off water to the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ he haomɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbiɔ oya. nu ni faaa loo kooloi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni tutuaa shishifãi lɛ. ni baafo nu kɛya baai lɛ anɔ

english: Why does my maize crop fail when I plant right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ midu yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rains of the season are often followed by hot, dry weeks that dry up the soil. If the young seedlings do not get continuous moisture, they burn and die before establishing deep roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ otsi ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gbiɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji tso bibioo lɛ enine shɛɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ daa Amɛbaashã ni amɛgboi dani amɛwo shishifãi.

english: Why are my stored cowpea seeds turning into dust and developing small holes after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ mli eyi kɛ sũ ni buji bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ? kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ

english: Small insects called weevils lay eggs inside the seeds around harvest time. As they hatch, the young insects eat the grain from the inside unless the seeds are treated or kept in airtight containers.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Beni amɛfɔɔ lɛ, kooloi bibii yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli. Ja atsu dumɔwui lɛ ahe nii loo akɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli.

english: Why are my cocoa trees producing fewer pods now compared to when my parents planted them years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo fe beni mifɔlɔi du lɛ afii komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees have a peak production age, usually between 10 and 25 years. As trees get older, their yield naturally declines due to aging branches, depleted soil nutrients, and accumulated pest or disease damage over time.
ga: Cocoa tsei ji tsei ni yeɔ wala be babaoo fe fɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ yaa nɔ yɛ afii 10 kɛyashi 25 teŋ. Beni tso lɛ daa lɛ, Eyibii lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ niji ni eda lɛ ahewɔ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ni abua naa lɛ fiteɔ nii yɛ be kɛ bei amli.

english: How do I know if my cocoa farm's soil is exhausted and needs fertilizer to boost yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli ewo muji ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Exhausted soil usually shows through yellowing leaves, slow tree growth, small pod sizes, and a steady drop in yield even when weather conditions and rainfall are good.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ jieɔ ehe kpo kɛtsɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ nɔ. Tso lɛ daa fiofio. Pods lɛ ji bibii. Ni nibii ni afeɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ebaa shi eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ hi moŋ.

english: Why do cocoa trees planted too close together yield smaller pods than those planted further apart?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii fe cacao tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ lɛ?

english: When trees are planted too closely, their roots compete fiercely for the same soil nutrients and water, while their upper leaves block sunlight from each other, resulting in smaller pods and lower total yield per tree.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tso shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ anɔ baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni tso kome baa lɛ baa shi.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in overly wet and shady conditions. Lack of air circulation and high humidity allow fungal spores to destroy the pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ fe nine kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo lɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before the tiny pods can even start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii bibii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ? Ebaabɔi shweremɔ po.

english: Flower drop occurs when the tree experiences stress from poor soil nutrients, prolonged dry spells, or sudden weather changes. The tree sheds its flowers to conserve energy for its own survival.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei na haomɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ mli. Nuu be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. aloo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi trukaa Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to cut off extra shoots and sucker branches from healthy cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔfolɔ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ayitsei kɛ amɛniji ni shwieɔ nu lɛ?

english: Sucker branches, or chupons, consume water and nutrients that should go toward growing pods. Pruning them redirects the tree's energy to pod production and improves airflow to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Sucker niji, loo chupons lɛ, heɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni esa akɛ eya ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli. Tso lɛ he ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ yaa pod feemɔ mli ekoŋŋ ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: How do weeds growing under my cocoa trees reduce the number of pods my trees produce?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kookoo tsei ashishi lɛ haa ŋmeii ni tso lɛ woɔ lɛ baa shi?

english: Weeds act as silent thieves that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from the roots of your cocoa trees. This weakens the cocoa trees, leading to fewer flowers and smaller harvests.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ julɔi ni efee dioo, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ cacao tso lɛ shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kookoo tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fɔfɔii fioo kɛ yibiiwoo fioo.

english: Young cocoa plants naturally thrive in filtered shade. Harsh, direct sunlight causes young leaves to lose water faster than their roots can absorb it, causing heat stress and severe wilting.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Ekɛ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ ni naa wa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees yield heavily during one part of the year and very little during other months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ afi lɛ fã ko mli, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ yɛ nyɔji krokomɛi amli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally cycle based on rainfall patterns. The onset of rains triggers heavy flowering and pod growth, creating the main harvest season, while dry periods cause the trees to rest and conserve energy.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ tsɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni fɔfɔi baa lɛ jeɔ shishi ekɛ fɔfɔi babaoo kɛ pod dalɛ baa. ni kɛ kpamɔ be titri lɛ baa Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, be ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ haa tsei lɛ jɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he.

english: Why do bugs like akate (mirids) attack young cocoa shoots and make the leaves look burned?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ Agate (Mirid) lɛ tutuaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛhaa baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã lɛ?

english: Mirids pierce young shoots and pods to feed on sap, injecting saliva that destroys plant tissue. This stops new growth, weakens the tree, and directly cuts down your pod yield if untreated.
ga: Mirids lɛ tswaa ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii koni amɛye ŋmeii lɛ amli nu lɛ. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ tsei amli fãji lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baatsi dalɛ hee naa. ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa pod yibii lɛ baa shi tɛ̃ɛ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, which plants need to build strong leaves. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen-based fertilizer will help feed the plant so it can stay green and yield well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni tsei he hiaa koni amɛfee baai ni mli wa Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛwo yibii.

english: How do I know if my farmland soil is healthy enough for planting crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, crumbles easily in your hand, holds moisture well, and contains earthworms. If your soil feels hard, pale, or sandy, mixing in decomposed plant waste or animal manure will rebuild its fertility.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii hu yɛ. Kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo eyɛ ŋã lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni egboi ni afolɔ ashwie shi loo kooloi ashishifãi futu mli lɛ, ebaaha eshikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when excess water stays trapped around them for too long. Planting your cassava cuttings on raised soil ridges or mounds allows rainwater to drain away, keeping the roots safe from rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kasava niji ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni etsĩɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite

english: Why are the bottom ends of my pepper and tomato fruits turning black and soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers kɛ tomatoi lɛ ashishigbɛ naagbeei lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifee blɛoo lɛ?

english: This soft black spot is called blossom-end rot, caused by uneven watering or a lack of calcium in the soil. Keeping your watering schedule steady and mulching the soil around the plants helps prevent it.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ he diŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ daa loo calcium ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ amɛnaa.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves get covered in a white powdery substance during humid weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ tsɔɔ powda yɛŋ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ?

english: This white film is a fungal growth called powdery mildew that thrives when plants are crowded together in moist air. Giving your plants enough spacing allows wind to blow through and dry the leaves naturally.
ga: Nɛkɛ sini yɛŋ nɛɛ ji ŋmei ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. Edaa kɛji akɛ tsei ebɔ he babaoo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ mli. Shi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli ni eha baai lɛ agbi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have wide leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa seedlings the soft shade and cool moisture they need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ náa su ni mli tse kɛ fɛ̃i ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why must I stake my yam plants with tall sticks instead of letting the vines spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji adu mi sweet potato tsei lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha wain tsei lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up to catch direct sunlight, which gives the plant energy to build larger tubers below ground. It also keeps leaves off wet ground where soil diseases can easily attack them.
ga: Staking Wo sweet potato baa lɛ nɔ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ ohe tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebaatsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni ekahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ baanyɛ atutua amɛ oya lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience extreme heat or dry soil stress. Covering the soil around the base with dry grass keeps the root zone cool and moist so the flowers stay on to produce peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ he. Mulching around Jwɛi ni egbi shishi haa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ ji koni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi koni amɛwo ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Too many suckers growing around one stem will fight each other for water and soil nutrients, leading to tiny fruit bunches. Removing excess suckers ensures the main plant gets all the food it needs to yield heavy bunches.
ga: ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he Tsobii babaoo tsɔ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ehaa aduawai lɛ feɔ tso bibioo ko. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Why is a strange weed with pink flowers causing my maize to remain short and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɛkɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ni fɔfɔii yɔɔ mli lɛ haa mi-ŋmei lɛ feɔ kuku ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: That weed is Striga, a parasitic weed that attaches to maize roots and steals its food and water. Rotating your field with legumes like cowpea or groundnuts stops Striga seeds from growing and cleans your soil over time.
ga: Nakai jwɛi lɛ ji Striga, ni ji jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni shwieɔ ŋmãa shishifãi anɔ ni ejuɔ niyenii kɛ nu. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake nibii ni odu lɛ. Ehaa Striga dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ ni ehaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli tseɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because their leaves scorch easily under harsh, direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains around them keeps the soil moist and protects the young trees until they grow stronger.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, yɛ amɛhe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ amɛhe waa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is a vital food for growth found in soil or fertilizer. It can also happen if heavy rains flood the farm and drown the roots, preventing them from feeding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ ni anaa yɛ shikpɔŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha ŋmɔ ko mli nu ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ shwie nu mli, ni eha anyɛɛɛ aye niyenii.

english: How do I know which direction the cassava stem stick should face when I push it into the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole beni otsiɔ ŋmei tso lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, gbɛ ni esa akɛ ekwɛ nɔ?

english: Look closely at the stem for small raised bumps called buds or eyes where old leaves grew. These buds must point upwards toward the sky so that new shoots can easily grow up while roots grow down into the soil.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tso lɛ shishi jogbaŋŋ koni ona ŋmeii bibii. Atsɛɔ enɛɛmɛi akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai momoi anɔ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii heei akwɛ̃ oya be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: What is making small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaving little dark dirt in the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mibi lɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni eshiɔ muji bibii ni tsuɔ waa. Okɛwo tso lɛ teŋ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the central funnel of the maize plant during the daytime to eat tender leaves and leave behind their waste.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye baai bibii ni amɛshi jwɛi.

english: Why should I cut off some of the small plantain shoots growing around my main plant stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ plantain tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Mitso titri lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: If too many small shoots (suckers) grow at once, they steal food, water, and sunlight from the mother plant. Leaving only two or three strong suckers allows the main plant to produce much larger, heavier bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ he kome lɛ Ejuɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni dara ni tsii babaoo.

english: Why do some farmers cover the dirt around their crop stems with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves (called mulching) blocks the harsh sun, keeping the soil cool and holding in rain moisture longer so your plants do not dry out quickly between rains.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching.) Etsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni ehaa nugbɔshiimɔ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha otsei lɛ akagbi oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli.

english: Why do I need to clear the grass and put long wooden poles next to my growing yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi lɛ ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama emasɛi lɛ? Ani aduɔ sweet potato wain tsei?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves off the ground to catch sunlight to feed the growing tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off damp ground, preventing diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni amɛkɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Staking hu haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: Maize eats up specific soil nutrients every season; planting it continuously in the same place drains the soil completely and leads to smaller harvests. Swapping maize with groundnuts or beans helps restore food back into the earth.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be fɛɛ mli. Kɛ́ oya nɔ odu nii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu atsɔ mli ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii bibii aba. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Early morning is best because the cool soil can drink up the water before the hot sun evaporates it away. Watering during a hot afternoon can shock the plant roots and waste water through evaporation.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ lɛ baanyɛ anu nu dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ atsɔ mli. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei shishifãi kɛ nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ afee evaporation shock.

english: Why shouldn't I apply dry fertilizer on my crops when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi tsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so plant roots can drink it in safely. Applying fertilizer to dry soil in scorching weather can burn the plant roots and ruin your crop instead of feeding it.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu amɛ shweshweeshwe. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni egbe ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ moŋ fe ni eeeha amɛ niyenii.

english: Can farm tools carry sickness from my neighbor's farm to my own crops?
ga: Ani ŋmɔ mli nibii baanyɛ ajie helai kɛjɛ mikutsoŋnyo ŋmɔ mli kɛya miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Yes, cutlasses, pruners, and hoes can easily transfer plant viruses and fungi from sick plants to healthy ones through contaminated plant sap. Washing your tools with clean water and soap or rubbing alcohol after working in infected areas stops disease from spreading.
ga: Hɛɛ, dade, tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ tsei. Ni hoe tsei baanyɛ ajie tsei amli helai kɛ ŋmeii kɛjɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ kɛtsɔ tsei amli nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ nɔ. Nu ni mli tse kɛ samla ni akɛbaatsu nii loo dãa ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ hei ni hela lɛ yɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ Ebaakpa hela gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: If I see one cocoa tree with swollen branches on my farm, should I cut it down or leave it?
ga: Kɛji mina kookoo tso ko ni eniji efuu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Ani esa akɛ mafo loo mashi?

english: You should cut it down and destroy it immediately. Swollen branch symptoms usually indicate Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, which is spread rapidly by tiny insects called mealybugs. Removing infected trees stops the disease from wiping out your entire cocoa farm.
ga: Esa akɛ afolɔ amɛ ni akpata amɛhiɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, tsei niji ni efuu lɛ tsɔɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ ojie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaha hela lɛ akafite o-kookoo ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Can I bring and plant fresh cassava cuttings from a distant town into my village?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmei hee aba kɛjɛ maŋ ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ mli koni mikɛdu yɛ mi akrowa lɛ mli?

english: It is very risky because those stem cuttings might carry hidden pests or diseases like Cassava Mosaic Disease that are not yet in your village. It is safer to get inspected, disease-free cuttings from your local agricultural extension officer.
ga: Enɛ yɛ oshara waa ejaakɛ ekolɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ, tamɔ ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ yɛ nakai ŋmeii lɛ amli. ni bɛ okrowa lɛ mli lolo lɛ Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oooha okpokpaa lɛ nɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ akwɛ ŋmeii ni hela bɛ mli lɛ.

english: Weeds act as breeding grounds and hiding spots for insect pests and plant diseases. Clearing weeds allows sunlight and air to reach your crops, which lowers humidity and stops fungal diseases from multiplying.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai fɔɔ yɛ kɛ he ni amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ onibii ahe. Enɛ haa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: This leaf curling is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects moving from plant to plant. The disease reduces the leaf's ability to capture sunlight, which stops the underground tubers from growing big.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ. Whiteflies bibii ni fãa kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Hela nɛɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni baai lɛ yɔɔ ni amɛkɛmɔɔ hulu la lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ daraaa.

english: How does a plant disease spread across my whole field so quickly?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa miŋmɔji lɛ amli oya nɛkɛ?

english: Crop diseases spread fast through wind, splashing rainwater, crawling insects, and human contact. Once a single plant is infected, wind can carry microscopic fungal spores or insects can fly to surrounding crops within a few days.
ga: Tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ. Nugbɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi, kooloi bibii ni shwereɔ, kɛ gbɔmɛi ni kɛ amɛhe kpaa gbee. Kɛji tso kome pɛ ná hela lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ aŋɔ fungal spores bibii waa. Aloo kooloi bibii baanyɛ afã kɛya tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli.

english: Why do my tomato plants rot near the soil and die after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ masɛi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains splash fungal spores living in the topsoil up onto the leaves and stems of the tomato plants. Placing dry straw or grass mulch on the soil around the base prevents mud splashing and protects the plants from soil-borne fungi.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ tomato tsei lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Ni akɛ jwɛi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ baawo shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ. Shishitoo lɛ tsiɔ muji ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa, ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up and turn black before the yam tubers are ready for harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ egbi ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: This is caused by Yam Anthracnose, a fungal disease that attacks stems and leaves during wet conditions. Removing infected leaves early and planting disease-resistant yam varieties stops the fungus from destroying your harvest.
ga: Anthracnose ni jɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni tutuaa tsei ashishifãi kɛ baai yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ mli. Kɛ́ ojie baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra Ni odu ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ baaha ŋmeii akafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are tiny green caterpillars eating holes into the leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, an invasive pest that attacks the growing heart of maize plants. Checking your farm early and applying recommended natural or chemical sprays protects the plant before it is destroyed.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni tutuaa ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ tsui lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu tsei lɛ ahe dani amɛfite.

english: Why is it better to buy certified seeds instead of using seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni makɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Certified seeds are laboratory-tested to ensure they are free of seed-borne diseases and pests before you plant them. Using saved seeds from sick crops can carry diseases directly into your soil and lower your yield.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ amli yɛ laboratori mli koni ana akɛ helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui bɛ mli dani odu amɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui ni ato kɛjɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ hela aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni eha onibii ni onáa lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do older farmers advise me to plant plantains on the same farm with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa ko wo ŋaa akɛ madu plantains yɛ ŋmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli ni miduɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under strong sunlight. Fast-growing plantains produce large leaves that create a protective umbrella, keeping the soil cool and providing the young cocoa with necessary shade until it gets established.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei bibii ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo ni he hiaa waa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni etswaa shi.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for growth. Feeding the soil with compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the plants recover their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛ su ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What makes my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpaa?

english: Cassava roots rot when water pools around them in heavy or poorly drained soil, encouraging fungal diseases. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps rainwater drain away and keeps the tubers healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ ashi nu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. ni haa ŋmeii helai baa Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋmeii anɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa he kroko ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato plants often drop their flowers when they experience stress from intense heat, dry soil, or a lack of soil nutrients. Regular watering and mulching around the roots help keep the plant cool so it can hold onto its blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ amɛna nɔnyɛɛ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔni afee ni amɛmɔmɔ fɔfɔii lɛ.

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their strength in the second generation, leading to uneven growth and lower yields. Purchasing fresh certified hybrid seeds each season ensures strong plants and high production.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa kɛ yibiiwoo baa shi. Dumɔwui heei ni akɛ he woɔ mli ni aheɔ daa afi lɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni woɔ yibii babaoo baa.

english: How does spreading dry grass around my vegetables help them grow during dry periods?
ga: Te jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni mi-veggies lɛ adara yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves—a practice called mulching—blocks direct sunlight from drying out the earth. This traps soil moisture longer and keeps crop roots cool.
ga: Mulching kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ atsĩ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni eye ebua ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my land after harvesting a heavy crop like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa sɛɛ?

english: Maize removes a lot of nutrients from the soil. Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally restoring land fertility for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains get eaten by tiny insects even when I put them in closed sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛwoɔ kotokui ni atsĩ naa mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Insects or hidden moisture often come with the maize straight from the field. If grains are not dried thoroughly until they are hard before storage, remaining moisture allows weevils to multiply quickly inside the sacks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi loo ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ baa kɛ ŋmãa ni jɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa ni amɛhe waaa dani akɛto. Fɛ̃i ni eshwɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ aya hiɛ oya yɛ kotoku lɛ mli.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my cassava cuttings too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded, their stems compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to form large, thick tubers underground.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛtsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni mli tse.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops after the rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally adapted to the local soil and climate, making them fast at grabbing available water and food. Clearing weeds early stops them from stealing sunlight and soil nutrients from your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa jwɛi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaju hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ otsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my crops fail to grow properly after I spray chemicals to clear weeds on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ beni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: If you plant your seeds too soon after spraying weed chemicals, the poison left in the soil can damage the young plant roots and prevent them from absorbing nutrients, leading to poor growth and low yield.
ga: Kɛji odu dumɔwui mra tsɔ beni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ efɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Toxins ni eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afite tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi ni eha shishifãi lɛ akaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haaa ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ, ni yibiiwoo hu faaa.

english: How long should I wait after spraying weedkiller before I plant my crops?
ga: Kɛ́ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwie shi lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Most weedkillers stay active in the soil for some time. Waiting two to four weeks allows the chemical to break down fully so it clears the weeds without harming your new crop seedlings.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ ateŋ babaoo hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be ko. Otsii enyɔ kɛyashi ejwɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha tsofai lɛ akumɔ kwraa koni egbe jwɛi ni eyeee tsei ahe dumɔwui heei lɛ awui.

english: Is it better to clear my land with a cutlass or with chemical spray before planting?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ tsɔne loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu nii?

english: Clearing with a cutlass leaves no chemical residue in the soil so you can plant immediately, while using chemical spray saves time and labor but requires careful waiting time before planting so your crops do not die.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsɔne shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tsofa ko kwraa eshwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, no hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ, ehaa be kɛ nitsumɔ baa shi. Shi eheɔ be ni akɛmɛɔ jogbaŋŋ dani otso lɛ baagbo.

english: Why are the leaves of my young crops turning yellow after I sprayed weeds around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mikɛ jwɛi lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When you spray weedkiller too close to your crops or on a windy day, the chemical mist can drift onto the crop leaves and weaken or poison the plant.
ga: Beni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ he ni bɛŋkɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tsɔ loo yɛ gbii ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa lɛ anɔ. Tsofai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ tso lɛ baai anɔ ni eha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ loo ekɛ tsofa fɔŋ aba.

english: How do I know if a chemical from the agricultural officer is for clearing land or for spraying around growing crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofai ni jɛ okwaayeli he onukpai adɛŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛjieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo akɛshwieɔ hei ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ anɔ?

english: Non-selective weedkillers kill all greenery and should only be used on bare land before planting, while selective weedkillers are designed to kill specific weeds without hurting particular growing crops.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni halaaa lɛ baagbe hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ fɛɛ. ni esa akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ pɛ dani adu. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, afee tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni ahala lɛ koni egbe jwɛi pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni eyeee ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ni miida lɛ awui.

english: Why do weeds grow back quickly even after I spray the chemical given to me by agricultural officers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛkɛ yɛ tsofai ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ shwieɔ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds can survive if the chemical was mixed with too much water, if heavy rain washed it away right after spraying, or if the weeds had already grown too old and strong for the chemical to destroy their roots.
ga: Jwɛi baanyɛ ahi shi kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofai babaoo futu nu mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji akɛ ashwie nɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ jwɛi lɛ egbɔ ni ehe wa tsɔ ni tsofai lɛ nyɛŋ afite shishifãi lɛ.

english: Can using strong weed chemicals damage my soil and prevent future crops from producing food?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni mli wa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ afite mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni etsi wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii?

english: Yes, using too much chemical or the wrong type can kill beneficial living things in the soil like earthworms and good bacteria, making the soil weak and reducing crop yields over time.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofa ni akɛtsuɔ nii babaoo loo nɔ ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ agbe nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai kpakpai. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout after I treat the soil with weedkiller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ etsu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii sɛɛ?

english: Certain weedkillers prevent seeds from germinating by stopping their root development underground, which happens when seeds absorb soil water containing active chemical residues.
ga: Tsofai komɛi ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ tsiɔ dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ kɛtsɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ni amɛkpaa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛji dumɔwui gbala nu ni yɔɔ sũ ni tsofai ni eshwɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli.

english: Does spraying chemical on the field before planting affect how much yield my maize will produce?
ga: Ani tsofai ni mikɛshwieɔ ŋmɔ mli dani miduɔ lɛ baaná mi-ŋma lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: If you use the right chemical and wait for it to break down before planting, your yield will not be affected; but if the crop absorbs chemical residue, it will produce smaller ears or fail to grain properly.
ga: Kɛ okɛ tsofai ni sa tsu nii ni omɛ ni amɛfite dani odu lɛ, enaŋ Onitsumɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ. Shi kɛji tso lɛ ŋɔ tsofa ni eshwɛ lɛ, ebaaha toi lɛ afee bibii loo dumɔwui lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ fitsofitso.

english: What should I do if my crops are not producing good yield after I used chemicals to prepare the land?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni mikɛ tsofai esaa shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should check with your agricultural extension officer to confirm if the correct chemical dosage was used, check if your soil needs organic manure to recover, and ensure you follow proper waiting times before the next planting season.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ akwɛ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ akɛ tsofa ni sa tsu nii. Kwɛmɔ kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia organic fertilizer koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ. Ni kwɛmɔ ni okɛ mɛmɔ be ni sa lɛ atsu nii dani be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba.

english: Why should I leave big wild trees like Wawa and Onyina on my cocoa farm instead of clearing them all away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi koo mli tsei wuji tamɔ Wawa kɛ Onina yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsi tsei lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ?

english: Large forest trees provide crucial canopy shade that shields young cocoa from harsh sunlight, keeps the soil cool, and creates a humid environment where cocoa trees thrive.
ga: Koo mli tsei wuji lɛ haa hɔɔŋ ni he hiaa ni buɔ kokoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni cacao tsei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Do large forest trees growing on my farm take away all the nutrients and water from my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani koo mli tsei wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ amli?

english: While big trees use soil resources, their deep roots pull up nutrients from far underground and bring them to the surface through fallen leaves, which actually fertilizes the topsoil for your cocoa.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei wuji kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii tsuɔ nii moŋ Shi shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ ni amɛkɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai ni egbee shi lɛ anɔ, he ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nii diɛŋtsɛ kɛhaa o-cocoa lɛ.

english: How does having shade trees on my land protect my crops during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Shade trees reduce heat intensity, lower ground temperatures, and slow down water evaporation from the soil, preventing your crop leaves from burning and keeping the ground moist.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ baa shi. ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli latsaa lɛ aba shi ni oha nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afee mlɛo Etsiɔ otso lɛ baai lɛ anaa koni ekashã ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What causes the soil on my cocoa farm to lose its natural richness over time?
ga: Mɛni haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli?

english: Soil loses its fertility when crops continually pull out nutrients to grow pods, but no organic matter like rotting leaves, compost, or fertilizer is added back to replenish the earth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ be mli ni tso lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa eshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ. Shi akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ baai ni egboi, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fataaa he ekoŋŋ koni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: How do fallen leaves from non-cocoa trees on my farm help my crop soil stay healthy?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai ni egbee shi kɛjɛ tsei ni jeee kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa koni miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Fallen leaves act as natural mulch that rots into organic matter, returning vital food to the topsoil where cocoa's feeding roots can easily pick it up.
