ga: Baai ni egbee shi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni etsɔɔ wala yibii. Okɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abaanyɛ ajie shishifãi ni haa kookoo lɛ niyenii lɛ oya.

english: How can I tell if the soil on my farm has enough food for my crops to produce well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Healthy, fertile soil is dark, moist, crumbles easily in your hands, has lots of earthworms, and keeps crops deep green even during dry spells.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli edɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ni efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli po.

english: Will growing my cocoa trees in full direct sunlight produce more pods than growing them under shade?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ baaha ŋmeii babaoo aba fe bɔ ni akwɛɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Full sunlight makes cocoa yield high in the early years with heavy fertilizer, but it wears out the tree and soil quickly, whereas shaded cocoa lives longer and produces steadily for decades.
ga: Hulu la babaoo haa kookoo babaoo baa yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli. kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa Shi tsei kɛ shikpɔŋ fiteɔ oya. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kookoo ni akɛwoɔ shĩa mli lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ, ni afeɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be afii nyɔŋmai abɔ.

english: How do I know if the heavy trees on my farm are giving too much shade to my cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha kookoo ŋmɔlɔ babaoo?

english: If cocoa trees grow very tall and skinny with pale leaves and produce very few flowers, the shade canopy is too thick and needs to be pruned back to let light through.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ da ni ekwɛ waa ni efee mlɛo Eyɛ baai ni mli tse ni fɔfɔi fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hulutsoo lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni ehe miihia ni afolɔ mli ekoŋŋ koni la atsɔ mli.

english: Why do older farms planted decades ago yield fewer pods than when they were young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔji momoi ni adu afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: As trees age, their vascular systems become less efficient at moving water and nutrients, and long-term farming drains the topsoil unless organic matter and nutrients are continuously restored.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ eda lɛ Amɛ lá fãji lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ mli. Ni okwaayeli ni heɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ afite. ja aku sɛɛ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛi lɛ baa ekoŋŋ be fɛɛ be

english: Should I clear out all other plant species from my land to give my main crop full space?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie tsei krokomɛi fɛɛ ni adu lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni mitsei titrii lɛ aŋɔ he ko?

english: Completely clearing non-crop plants leaves the land exposed to erosion, severe sun, and wind damage, while keeping select beneficial plants creates a balanced farm that protects your main crop.
ga: Nibii ni jeee tsei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ, hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fiteɔ nii baa. yɛ be mli ni abuɔ tsei ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahe. Ebaaha ŋmɔ ni ja ni buɔ onibii titrii lɛ ahe lɛ aba.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains on the farm before or at the same time as my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantains yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani loo kɛfata kookoo dumɔwui heei ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive and easily get scorched by strong direct sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa trees need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa ni amɛshãa oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do many of the flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often drop off when the tree lacks water, is missing nutrients in the soil, or is being attacked by tiny pests like mirids (capsids). Ensuring adequate shade, proper pruning, and pest control helps more flowers turn into healthy pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu bɛ tso lɛ nɔ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ mirids (capsids) ni tutuaa lɛ, kwɛmɔ ni akɛha hulutsoo ni sa ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa Ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ baaye abua fɔfɔi babaoo ni amɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is essential plant food, or the soil has too much water that is choking the roots. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps restore the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni no haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my rice plants produce white, empty heads that have no grains inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã tsei lɛ ekomɛi woɔ yitsei yɛŋ ni dumɔwui bɛ mli lɛ?

english: White, empty heads in rice are usually caused by stem borer insects that burrow inside the plant stem and cut off food and water from reaching the growing grains. Controlling these pests early in the growing season prevents empty heads.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛfoɔ niyenii kɛ nu koni ekashɛ dumɔwui ni miida lɛ ahe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii yitsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ mra yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ, ebaatsi bulb lɛ naa koni amɛkafee efolo.

english: Why do I need to clear the grass and place tall wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi lɛ ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji ama shi koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need plenty of sunlight on their leaves to make food for building large tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot ground, prevents rots, and allows maximum sunlight exposure.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la babaoo koni eshɛ amɛbaai lɛ ahe koni ekɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ fitemɔ naa ni enine shɛɔ hulu la ni fe fɛɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell when my cassava is mature enough to be dug out of the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava lɛ da bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is generally ready for harvest between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell it is ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baai lɛ efee klalo beni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny insects like whiteflies, thrips, or mites that suck juices from the leaves or spread viruses. Sprinkling or spraying neem oil or recommended organic treatments helps control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies, thrips, loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu loo helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛbaatsu nii lɛ shwie nɔ loo akɛshwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn black and rot before they can even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot, and it happens when the tomato plant cannot get enough calcium, often due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil moisture consistent and adding compost or lime to the soil prevents the fruit bottoms from rotting.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa kɛji akɛ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi be fɛɛ be ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ baatsi aduawai ashishi lɛ anaa koni ekafite.

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and carry very heavy bunches of fruit, making them top-heavy. Supporting the plants with strong wooden poles or bamboo forks placed against the main stem prevents them from falling over.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛwoɔ aduawai babaoo, ni no haa amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni mli wa loo ŋmei ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Why is it helpful to plant cowpea or beans on the same land where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the ground, while cowpeas and beans put valuable nitrogen back into the soil through their roots naturally. Rotating these crops improves soil fertility without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Cowpeas kɛ beans kɛ nitrogen ni jara wa lɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nibii nɛɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ ni tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I remove all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct harsh sunlight. Shade trees protect them from sunburn and keep moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees mature.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he, ni amɛhaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daraa.

english: Planting seeds too close causes competition for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, forcing the plants to stretch upward for light instead of developing thick stems and large cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ kɛ akaŋshii baa kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tso lɛ akpã ehe koni enine ashɛ la nɔ. Mohu ɔ, e ngɛ tso nɛ mi wa kɛ tso agbo.

english: Yam vines need to catch maximum sunlight to produce food for growing big tubers underground, and keeping the leaves off the damp ground prevents leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Ni kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ebaatsi baa helai anaa.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow plenty of deep green leaves but produce very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa shi ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Using fertilizers with too much nitrogen causes the plant to spend all its energy growing leaves instead of producing flowers and fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛkwɛ baai lɛ atsu nii. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yiblii.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my land better for the next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni efee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, which naturally enriches the soil with nutrients for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni enáa niyenii ni haa tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baa lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes in the exact same bed where I just harvested garden eggs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato yɛ saatso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ ni mifo abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes and garden eggs belong to the same plant family and share the same soil pests and diseases. Replanting them in the same spot allows those pests to accumulate in the soil.
ga: Tomato kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii yɛ tsei aweku kome mli ni amɛ fɛɛ amɛyeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai kome. Kɛ́ adu tsei heei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha nakai tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants curl up and turn yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants curl or shed leaves to save water and protect themselves when hot weather and dry-season pests like green mites attack them.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ loo amɛshwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ tutuaa amɛ.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry stretch. Seeds planted too early will germinate and then dry up before the main rainy season settles.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaagbi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aba.

english: Why are small caterpillars hiding inside the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This is typically the Fall Armyworm. The moth lays eggs inside the central funnel of the plant so the caterpillars can feed on tender leaves while staying safe from heat and predators.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ titri nɔ lɛ, enɛ ji Fall Armyworm. Moth lɛ woɔ ewui yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli. Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ aye baai bibii lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do weeds growing near my crops cause my crop yields to drop so drastically?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayibii baa shi kwraa lɛ?

english: Weeds compete aggressively with your crops for water, root space, sunlight, and soil nutrients, effectively starving your crops of what they need to produce fruit.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ waa kɛha nu, shishifãi, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii lɛ yɛ yibiiwoo mli.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to direct heat and sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantain or shade trees alongside them creates a cooler environment and holds moisture in the soil, protecting the cocoa leaves from scorching while the trees are young.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ni yɔɔ amɛmasɛi lɛ adumɔ. Ehaa shihilɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ebuɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ.

english: If too many suckers grow around the main plantain stem, they steal nutrients, water, and sunlight from the main plant. Pruning away weaker suckers and keeping only two or three allows the main plant to produce larger, heavier bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ ehe main plantain trunk Ejuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui titrii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ofolɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ni okɛ enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ahi shi lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds as close together as possible so I can get more harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe bɔ ni manyɛ koni maná ŋmaa babaoo?

english: Planting maize seeds too close together forces the plants to compete with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow strong stems and produce large, fully filled ears of corn.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni wa baakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ ŋmãa toi agboi ni eyi obɔ lɛ baa.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and yellow dust inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Abɛi baai bibii kɛ sũ ŋmɔŋ yɛ tsei lɛ amli.

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds on the growing point of young maize plants. Detecting them early allows you to use appropriate pest control methods before they destroy the growing tip and reduce your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni daraa yɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. mra mli nibii ni ana Ebaaye ebua bo ni okɛ gbɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ atsu nii. dani amɛbaakpãtã ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahiɛ ni amɛha onibii ni owoɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and fall off, the main stem turns woody, and the ground around the base of the plant begins to crack as the tubers expand below the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso titri lɛ tsɔɔ tso. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishitoo lɛ he lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Does my yam crop really need wooden stakes to climb, or can the vines just spread on the ground?
ga: Ani mi-sweet potato dumɔ lɛ biɔ ni akwɔ tsei diɛŋtsɛ loo wain tsei lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make the food that grows big tubers under the ground. Staking lifts the vines off the damp soil, exposing leaves to sunlight while preventing fungal diseases that spread easily on ground-level foliage.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛ́ amɛmiikwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la he ni etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn dark brown and rotten before they even get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, which happens when the tomato plant cannot get enough calcium or water while the fruit is growing. Regular watering and proper soil management help the plant move calcium smoothly to the developing tomatoes.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhaa calcium lɛ yaa tomato ni miiya hiɛ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it better to place fertilizer in a small ring around my crop stem instead of scattering it everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaawo fɔmɔ kotokui bibii amli lɛ? Mi tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ he Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshwa he fɛɛ he

english: Placing fertilizer near the root zone ensures that your crop roots absorb the nutrients directly. Broadening or scattering it across the whole field wastes fertilizer, feeds nearby weeds, and risks getting washed away by heavy rains.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Gbɛɛmɔ loo gbɛɛmɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Ehaa jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ niyenii. ni amɛyɛ oshara mli akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baajie amɛ kɛya

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil every year and allows specific pests and diseases to build up in the field. Rotating with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. ni eha kooloi kɛ helai komɛi abua amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nibii ni akɛtsakeɔ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why is it so critical to clear weeds during the first few weeks after my crops germinate?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa waa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings are delicate and cannot outgrow fast-growing weeds. Clearing weeds early removes competition for light, water, and soil nutrients, allowing the crops to establish strong roots and grow rapidly.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛda fe jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ejieɔ akaŋshii ni kɔɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he lɛ kɛyaa. Ehaa tsei náa shishifãi ni wa ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce energy for growing tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground, giving them maximum sunlight exposure and preventing leaves from rotting on damp, hot soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni miida lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ awó amɛhe nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Na hulu la babaoo ni etsĩɔ baai anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my cassava sticks too close to each other on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ mihe tsɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are too close, their roots and leaves fight over light, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing them properly allows the roots enough room to expand into large, thick tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmeii wuji ni mli tse.

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the ground. Crops like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally restoring soil fertility for your next planting season.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha okwɛ̃mɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Apply fertilizer when the plants are young and actively growing—first when plants are about two weeks old, and again at four to five weeks. Always apply fertilizer when the soil is moist so roots can soak it up.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo ni eedara lɛ. Akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ haa beni tso lɛ eye aaafee otsi enyɔ. kɛ agbɛnɛ hu yɛ otsii ejwɛ kɛyashi enumɔ mli. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Why are small worms eating holes into the leaves and central whorl of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai kɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the plant canopy where they eat leaves, but catching them early and applying approved pest control can protect your yield.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ashishi he ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ yɛ lɛ. Shi kɛ́ omɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why are my cassava leaves turning yellow and curling up into small twisted shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ bibii lɛ?

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whiteflies or infected stem cuttings. You can prevent this disease by planting certified disease-resistant cassava varieties.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni hiɛɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ afolɔ Obaanyɛ otsi hela nɛɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa tree leaves turn yellow and fall off during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees suffer from heat stress and dry air without proper cover. Providing shade trees across your cocoa farm helps retain soil moisture and shields cocoa leaves from burning in extreme heat.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni bɛ nɔ ko ni sa ni akɛhaa amɛhe lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo ha yɛ o-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi, ni ebuɔ cocoa baai lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã yɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa mli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any tomatoes when the days get very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni tomato ko bɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and erratic soil moisture cause tomato flowers to dry up before they can form fruit. Watering consistently in the morning and mulching around plants keeps the soil cool and stops flower drop.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shiŋŋ lɛ haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani aduawai lɛ woɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa leebi kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ he ni ebɔle he lɛ. Tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do the hybrid maize seeds I buy from the agricultural shop grow better than seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni mihe yɛ okwaayeli shwapo lɛ mli lɛ kwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni mikpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred in labs for high yields and uniform growth in their first generation. Saving and replanting those seeds breaks that vigor, leading to weaker plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli yɛ laboratori lɛ mli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni enyɛ ená yibii babaoo kɛ dalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛto he ni adu ekoŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha hewalɛ aba shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do weeds reduce my maize crop yield so quickly if I do not clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi-abele ni miwoɔ lɛ baa shi oya kɛji mijieee amɛ mra lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and steal essential groundwater, sunlight, and soil fertilizer before your maize roots can establish themselves.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni he hiaa, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii dani o-corn shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ama shi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning pale yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants use to build green leaves. Applying fertilizer or compost early gives the crop the energy it needs to grow strong and green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii baafata he mra Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔji.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or beans makes the soil richer for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans have tiny root nodules that capture nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the soil, creating natural plant food that future crops can use.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi bibii. No mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli tsei niyenii ni wɔsɛɛ tsei baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: The very first rain is often followed by a long dry stretch that bakes the ground. If you sow too early, the young seeds will germinate and then dry up; it is safer to wait until the rainy season becomes regular.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui bibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaagbi. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baafee nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa.

english: Why do I need to cover the ground with dry grass around my vegetable beds in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo muji yɛ mi-vegetables saatsoi lɛ ahe yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves or grass (mulching) acts like a blanket. It stops the sun from drying out the earth too fast, keeps the soil cool, and saves water so your crops do not dry up.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Ehaa hulu lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ekɛ nu baa Koni onibii akagbi

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground when there is too much rain on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ miinɛ waa tsɔ yɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain causes water to sit on the land without draining, the roots drown, rot, and attract soil fungal diseases.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu ta shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu bɛ mli lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛgboɔ ni egbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees burn and turn brown when they are planted in open sunlight without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse ni hulutsoo bɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that cannot handle full sunlight. Plantain plants or shade trees act like natural sun umbrellas to protect young cocoa until its stem and leaves become mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli parasols ni buɔ kookoo bibioo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ baadara.

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which love to hide inside the central growing point (the whorl) of maize plants to eat young leaves. Applying targeted treatment inside the leaves early prevents them from destroying the growing stem.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋgbɛ he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ (ring) koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Tsamɔi ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii mra yɛ baa lɛ mli. Enɛ baatsi enaa koni ekafite tsei ni miida lɛ.

english: Why should I cut away extra small shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tso lɛ shishi.

english: Extra shoots (suckers) steal water and food away from the main fruiting tree. Keeping only one or two healthy shoots ensures the main tree produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso ni fa fe nine (tso) juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso titri ni woɔ yibii lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hi shi lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii babaoo ni tsii.

english: Why does planting my cassava bushes too close to my maize stop the maize from producing good cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmãa tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmãa tsɔ lɛ haaa ŋmãa lɛ awo ŋmãa kpakpai lɛ?

english: Cassava grows large stems and deep roots that take over the space, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Spacing crops properly prevents one from overshadowing and starving the other.
ga: Cassava yɛ tsei wuji kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni heɔ he ko, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa baatsi tso kome naa koni ekaha ekroko nɔ tsɔ ni hɔmɔ akaye lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil minerals, causing the plant to drop its flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa ni baa shwane mli lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo minerals ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Gbalamɔ tomato tsei lɛ koni okɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Maize leaves curl up to reduce the leaf area exposed to the sun and heat, which helps the plant conserve water and prevent moisture from evaporating too quickly during dry spells.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛba he ni hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ shɛɔ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he, ni ehaa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ.

english: How does supplying water directly to the crop roots help plants grow better than pouring water over their leaves?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ fe nu ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Delivering water right at the root zone ensures moisture goes straight where the plant absorbs it, while keeping leaves dry prevents leaf burning from direct sun and reduces the risk of fungal diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ yaa he ni tso lɛ shwieɔ lɛ yɛ lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni agbiɔ baai lɛ, ebaatsi amɛnaa koni amɛkashã kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. ni ebaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ shi

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and dry out when rains stop for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Plantains have broad leaves that lose water very quickly in dry air, so when soil moisture drops, the plant naturally sheds its older leaves to conserve remaining water and survive.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ ba shi lɛ, Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai momo lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu nu ni eshwɛ lɛ he ni amɛhi shi.

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when they suffer from high heat or inconsistent moisture, dropping flowers to save energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ kɛ́ amɛna dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hulutsoo ni bɛ shiŋŋ. Kɛtsɔ fɔfɔii ni ashwieɔ shi koni akɛto hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my cassava grow tall and full of green leaves but produce very small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai eŋɔli shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or excess water, cassava spends all its energy developing lush stems and leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the roots.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen loo nu babaoo Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei kɛ ŋmei baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and weak root systems that scorch easily under full sun, requiring partial shade from temporary companion crops like plantains to retain leaf moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Enɛ biɔ hulutsoo ko kɛjɛ tsei ni fata he ni yeɔ be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni eha baai lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why do my tomatoes split open on the vine right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ miikwɛ̃ yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: Fruit cracking occurs when a plant receives a sudden surge of water after a dry period, causing the fruit inside to expand faster than the skin can stretch.
ga: Yibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ ná nu ni yaa hiɛ trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa aduawai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my tomato plants turning pale yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: When nutrients like nitrogen are low in the soil, the plant moves what little nutrient it has from the older lower leaves to feed the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Kɛji niyenii mli nibii tamɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii mli nibii fioo pɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my maize crops grow thin and fall over when I plant many seeds in a single hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbeeɔ shi beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Seeds planted too close together fight for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak, spindly stems that easily break in high winds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la ni faaa, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ, efoɔ oya.

english: Why do weeds stay green and healthy in my farm while my vegetable crops are wilting from heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni mi-aduawai lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ latsaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive, deep root systems designed to extract moisture from deep underground, whereas cultivated vegetables often have shallow roots that dry out quickly.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni afee koni ejie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, aduawai ni bei pii lɛ aduɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛgbiɔ oya.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn quickly in harsh, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain alongside cocoa protects the young saplings from extreme heat until they are strong enough to withstand direct sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya kɛji hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Leaves usually turn yellow due to a lack of nitrogen in the soil or damage from pests like Fall Armyworms. Checking under the leaves for small caterpillars or applying nitrogen fertilizer can help restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nitrogen ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworms lɛ fiteɔ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi kɛji ŋmeii bibii komɛi yɛ mli loo ni akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha ŋmeii lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay small and woody even when the green leafy stems grow very tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ bibii ni amɛji tsei eyɛ mli akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai eŋɔli lɛ amli lɛ kɛlɛ waa moŋ?

english: High leaf growth with small roots often means the soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium or phosphorus. Soil that is too hard and compacted also stops tubers from swelling, so loosening the soil before planting helps cassava roots grow big.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni kɛlɛ kɛ shishifãi bibii tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo tsɔ, ni potassium loo phosphorus ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni wa tsɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baatsi bulb lɛ naa koni ekafu. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ dani adu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ adara.

english: It is best to wait until the soil receives a deep soaking from two or three steady rains, rather than sowing after the very first light shower. Seeds planted in dry or barely damp soil can rot or fail to germinate properly.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ waa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo nɔ ni mli edɔɔɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbo loo amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nutrients like nitrogen. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot strips the soil bare and attracts specific pests, whereas rotating with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally puts nitrogen back into the soil.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen. Kɛ́ adu lɛ shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbala tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn moldy and get eaten by insects even after I dry them in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ mli ewo muji ni kooloi yeɔ amɛ eyɛ mli akɛ migbiɔ amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Grains often retain hidden moisture deep inside the kernel. If bagged before being thoroughly sun-dried on mats until they snap cleanly between your teeth, that trapped moisture allows mold to grow and attracts grain-weevils.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmaa mli lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ okɛwo baagi mli dani ogbi lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ tsɔne nɔ kɛyashi ebaashɛ onyanyɔji ateŋ. Fɛ̃i ni emɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ daa ni egbalaa ŋmaa mli ŋmeii.

english: Why do my vegetable crops droop during the afternoon heat even when I water them early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: Crops lose moisture faster through their leaves under direct midday sun than their roots can drink from the soil. Mulching around the base of the plant with dry grass helps keep the soil cool and holds moisture throughout the day.
ga: Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why should I purchase certified seeds instead of saving seeds from my previous harvest to plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu?

english: Saved seeds from hybrid crops lose their vigor over time, leading to uneven growth, weaker pest resistance, and smaller yields. Certified seeds are specially bred to grow uniformly and yield much bigger harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ baaje mli yɛ be ni sa mli. Ekɛ dalɛ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee baa He ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baa shi kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛdara pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly even when I apply fertilizer to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ fiofio kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii miiwo ŋmɔji amli po lɛ?

english: Weeds steal fertilizer, soil moisture, and sunlight directly from your crops. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks of planting ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to grow strong and produce well.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ sũ mli nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ onibii anɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni okɛdu lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni otsei lɛ náa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Extreme heat, dry air, or irregular watering causes stress in tomato plants, making them shed their blossoms to save energy. Consistent watering and light shade during extremely hot periods help flowers turn into healthy tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. Enɛ haa tomato shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ tomato ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when there are no bigger trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Without shade from larger trees or plantains, the harsh sun scorches their tender leaves, causing them to turn yellow, dry up, and eventually die.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ tsei wuji loo plantains lɛ ahe hulutsoo be bɛ lɛ Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã ebaai bibii lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛgbiɔ, ni naagbee lɛ amɛgboiɔ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in cool, wet, and humid weather. Excess water sitting on the pods creates the ideal condition for the fungus to grow and destroy the crop.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni ŋmeii lɛ adara ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why is it bad to let my cocoa trees grow too tall with many bushy branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mahã mi-kokoo tso lɛ aya hiɛ tsɔ ni ehiɛ niji babaoo lɛ?

english: Overgrown trees waste energy growing useless leaves instead of cocoa pods. Bushy leaves also trap moisture and block sunlight, creating a damp environment where diseases like black pod thrive.
ga: Tsei ni ekpɔtɔ lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛduɔ baai ni he ehiaaa yɛ kookoo ŋmeii najiaŋ. Baai ni yɔɔ jwɛi lɛ hu mɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la naa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do many of the small flowers on my cocoa trees drop off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ji No hewɔ lɛ, mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ fã ni fa lɛ gbeeɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can feed. Also, if tiny beneficial insects called midges are not around to pollinate the flowers, the unpollinated flowers will simply fall off.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. Kɛfata he lɛ, kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ Midge lɛ bɛ jɛmɛ. Enɛ ji koni akɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli pollen. Fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ pollen lɛ baagbee shi.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is missing the food my cocoa trees need to produce well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa mi-cacao tsei lɛ koni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Signs of hungry soil include pale or yellowish leaves, slow growth, and trees that yield very few or small pods. Applying the right crop fertilizer restores essential nutrients like nitrogen and potassium to the soil.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ miiye hɔmɔ lɛ ahe ji baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ, ni edaa blɛoo, kɛ tsei ni woɔ ŋmeii fioo loo bibii waa. Kɛ́ akɛ tso mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ potassium lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is there a green bushy plant growing directly out of my cocoa tree branches, and is it harming my trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi eŋɔlii ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-kookoo niji lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ? Ni ani eyeɔ mi tsei lɛ awui?

english: That green plant is mistletoe, a parasite. It drives its roots into your cocoa tree's branch to steal water and food, which weakens the tree and significantly lowers your cocoa yield if you do not cut it off.
ga: Nakai tso eŋɔli lɛ ji mistletoe. ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela Ewoɔ shishifãi yɛ kookoo tso lɛ niji amli koni eju nu kɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa kookoo ni anáa lɛ baa shi waa kɛji ofolɔɔɔ tso lɛ he.

english: What causes the dark patches and sunken spots on my green cocoa pods and young shoots?
ga: Mɛni kɛ okadii ni tsuɔ diŋ kɛ hei ni ebote mi-cocoa ŋmɔji kɛ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by mirids (capsids), small sap-sucking insects. As they feed on young pods and shoots, their saliva poisons the plant tissue, leaving dead, dark spots that stunt crop growth.
ga: Mirids (capsids), ni ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. be mli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii Amɛ ŋmeii lɛ ji tsofa fɔŋ kɛha tsei ahe fãji. Baai ni egboi, ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ ni tsiɔ tsei adalɛ naa.

english: Why should I clear weeds regularly from around the roots of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Ani oduɔ shishifãi daa?

english: Weeds steal vital water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops. They also act as hiding places for harmful pests and rodents that can destroy your yield.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni he hiaa waa, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Amɛtsuɔ nii hu akɛ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ oshara ni baanyɛ afite nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ teɔ shi yɛ.

english: What happens if I plant my cocoa seedlings too close to each other in the farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu kookoo dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting seedlings too close forces them to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in tall, thin, weak trees that yield fewer pods and allow plant diseases to spread rapidly between them.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei ni kwɔlɔ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ, ni ehaa tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa amɛteŋ oya.

english: Why should I harvest my cocoa pods as soon as they turn yellow instead of leaving them on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makpãtã kookoo ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛji amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ pɛ moŋ fe ni mashi amɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Harvesting pods when they turn yellow or orange ensures the beans inside are perfectly ripe. If left on the tree too long, the beans will begin to germinate inside the pod or rot, spoiling their sale quality.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii lɛ beni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Beans lɛ baaje shishi ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli loo ebaagbo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nibii ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ hilɛ fiteɔ.

english: Hybrid cocoa varieties usually start bearing fruit within 2 to 3 years after planting, while traditional varieties can take 4 to 5 years. Proper weeding, watering, and soil care help seedlings mature faster.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo henɔi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 4 kɛyashi 5. Jwɛi shwiemɔ, nu shwiemɔ, kɛ sũ nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛ daraa oya.

english: Can I plant food crops like plantain or cassava on the same farm with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Yes, planting crops like plantain alongside young cocoa is very good because the plantains provide temporary shade to protect young cocoa leaves from direct sunlight while giving you food and quick income.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ hi waa. Ejaakɛ plantains haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko baa koni ebu kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha niyenii ni oná shika oya.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to leave specific spacing between cocoa trees instead of planting them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ato he ko moŋ fe ni wɔɔdu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Planting cocoa too close together makes the trees fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, which results in smaller yields and allows plant diseases to spread easily from tree to tree.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli, ni haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ahe helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ oya.

english: During prolonged dry weather, cocoa trees drop their leaves to conserve water and protect themselves from drying out. Planting shade trees and keeping organic mulch on the soil helps retain moisture during dry spells.
ga: Yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni hulutsoo be lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce so many flowers, but only a few turn into real pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny beneficial insects like midges to pollinate them before they can form pods. If there are no pollinators, or if heavy rain or chemical sprays drive them away, many flowers will drop off without forming pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii, koni amɛwo amɛmli dani amɛfee ŋmeii. Kɛji akɛ kooloi ni feɔ pollin lɛ bɛ Aloo kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa loo ekɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛshwieɔ amɛ. Fɔfɔi babaoo baagbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do small cocoa pods sometimes turn shriveled and black before they fully mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ bei komɛi lɛ amɛgboɔ ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is often caused by 'pod wilt', where the tree naturally sheds pods it cannot feed due to lack of nutrients or water stress, or it can be caused by early pest and disease attacks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ‘Pod wilt’ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa, ni tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni nyɛɛɛ amɛye nii yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo nu mli haomɔ hewɔ Aloo ekolɛ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yɔɔ shishijee fãi lɛ amli lɛ kɛbaa.

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy to allow fresh air and sunlight to reach the lower trunk, which prevents humidity from building up and stops fungal diseases like Black Pod from multiplying.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli lɛ, egbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la ashɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ akabua ehe naa, ni ehaaa ŋmɔtɔ helai tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ji black pods lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do cocoa pods turn completely black and rot while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ kwraa ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet, dark conditions. Removing infected pods immediately and keeping the farm well-weeded stops the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ duŋ mli. Ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya ni akwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi jogbaŋŋ Enɛ baatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: How do shade trees help my cocoa farm during very hot seasons?
ga: Te tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Shade trees lower the temperature on your farm, shield fragile leaves from harsh sunshine, and drop dead leaves that break down into natural soil fertilizer.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ebuɔ baai ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he. ni ehaa baai ni egboi lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: How does adding fertilizer help an older cocoa farm produce more cocoa pods again?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo ŋmɔ momo ko ni ewoɔ kookoo ŋmeii ekoŋŋ?

english: As cocoa trees grow and produce pods over many years, they pull nutrients out of the earth. Fertilizer restores those missing minerals, helping older trees recover their strength and produce larger harvests.
ga: Beni cacao tso lɛ daa ni ewoɔ ŋmeii afii babaoo lɛ. Amɛjieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Fertilizer yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ minerals ni elaaje lɛ baa ekoŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni edara lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my plantains so they do not ripen too fast?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa plantains lɛ koni amɛkakwɛ oya tsɔ?

english: Harvest plantains when the fruits are full, plump, and still completely green. Waiting until they show yellow spots on the tree means they will ripen and spoil very quickly after cutting.
ga: Kpaa plantains be mli ni aduawai lɛ eyi obɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo. Ni aaamɛ kɛyashi ŋmɔtɔ baaje tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaafite oya waa yɛ be mli ni afolɔ amɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my plantains turn black and soft shortly after I cut them from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni efee blɛoo beni afolɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once harvested, plantains breathe and produce a natural ripening gas called ethylene. Bruising them during cutting or transport speeds up this gas production, causing them to soften and rot quickly.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akpa Plantains lɛ, emuɔ ni ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene lɛ baa. Kɛ́ mɔ ko fã yɛ be mli ni efoɔ loo ekɛyaa he kroko lɛ, ebaaha gas nɛɛ afee oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, efeɔ bɔdɔɔ ni egboɔ oya.

english: Can I leave my cut plantains under the open sun on the farm while waiting for a vehicle?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi plantains ni afo lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni mimɛɔ bɔs lɛ?

english: No, direct heat from the sun bakes the fruits, causing rapid water loss and triggering quick ripening. Always stack harvested plantains under deep shade.
ga: Dabi, la ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã aduawai lɛ. Enɛ haa nu fiteɔ amɛ oya, ni ehaa amɛshwereɔ oya. Esa akɛ akɛ plantains ni akpa lɛ awo hulutsoo be mli be fɛɛ be.

english: What kind of room should I keep my fresh green plantains in before selling or using them?
ga: Mɛɛ tsu mli esa akɛ mikɛ mi-plantains eŋɔli lɛ ato dani mahɔ̃ɔ loo mikɛtsu nii?

english: Keep your plantains in a cool, shaded, and well-ventilated space off the bare floor. Proper airflow slows down heat buildup and delays ripening.
ga: Too plantains lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ, ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko bɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa dɔlɛ baa shi ni ehaa nihoomɔ baa shi.

english: How can I store green plantains to keep them fresh for a few extra days?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ plantains eŋɔli lɛ ato koni amɛhi shi gbii fioo krokomɛi?

english: Store them in a cool shade, detached into small bunches, and keep them away from already ripe fruits like bananas or tomatoes which release gas that forces green plantains to ripen.
ga: Okɛto he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Ajara mli awo tsei bibii amli Ni ajie lɛ kɛjɛ aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ tamɔ banana loo tomato he. Enɛ jieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni nyɛɔ dumɔwui eŋɔli lɛ anɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why is it bad to pile plantains in large heaps after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ abaabua plantains anaa yɛ ŋtayaai wuji amli yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Large heaps trap heat and moisture in the middle of the pile, which cooks the fruits from inside and causes rapid mold growth and rotting.
ga: Pile agbo ko mɔ̃ɔ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ pile lɛ teŋgbɛ. ni hoɔ aduawai lɛ kɛjɛɔ emli ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ shwereɔ ni efiteɔ oya.

english: Which state of plantain is best for processing into plantain chips?
ga: Mɛɛ maŋ mli plantains hi fe fɛɛ kɛha plantain ŋmɔtɔi?

english: Firm, green, completely unripe plantains are best for chips because they are high in starch and low in sugar, giving you crisp chips that do not burn easily.
ga: Plantains eŋɔli ni mli wa ni eshɛko lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha friji ejaakɛ starch babaoo yɛ mli, ni sugar hu faaa. Ehaa friji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eshãaa oya.

english: What happens if I try to make plantain chips with fruits that have started turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mibɔ mɔdɛŋ akɛ mikɛ aduawai ni miije shishi etsɔ ŋmɔŋ fee plantain chips?

english: As plantains turn yellow, starch turns into sugar and moisture increases. Frying yellow plantains makes soft, oily chips that burn quickly instead of becoming crunchy.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ Starch lɛ tsakeɔ efeɔ sugar ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ. Kɛ́ ashã plantains ni ji yellow lɛ, ebaaha ashã lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ kɛ fɔ. ni shãa oya yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why should a farmer consider processing plantains into chips instead of selling them raw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ okwaafoi asusu plantain tsei ahe nitsumɔ he moŋ fe ni amɛaahɔ̃ɔ amɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Raw plantains spoil quickly and force you to sell at low prices during bumper harvests. Converting them to chips preserves the harvest, reduces waste, and allows you to earn more money.
ga: Plantains ni ahoo lɛ fiteɔ oya ni enyɛɔ onɔ ni ohɔ̃ɔ amɛ yɛ jara ni baa shi nɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ babaoo be mli. Kɛ́ otsake amɛ ofee french fries lɛ, ehaa nibii ni anáa lɛ hiɔ shi, ehaa nibii ni afiteɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa onine shɛɔ shika babaoo nɔ.

english: Why do some plantain bunches last longer after harvest than other bunches from the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains komɛi hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ kpamɔ sɛɛ fe ekrokomɛi lɛ? kɛjɛ ŋmɔ kome mli

english: Bunches harvested from strong, well-watered, and properly fertilized plants have thicker skins and healthier fruit tissues, allowing them to resist quick ripening and damage longer.
ga: Bunches ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni nu yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ, ni awo amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli lɛ baaná hewolo ni mli wa kɛ aduawai amli fãji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ shweremɔ oya kɛ fitemɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Most farmers in my village only plant plantains, so why should I consider growing cassava instead?
ga: Okwaafoi ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ mɛi babaoo duɔ plantains pɛ. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu ŋmei dumɔ he moŋ?

english: Cassava is extremely reliable because it tolerates poor soil and dry spells better than plantain. It provides a steady harvest and market income even during harsh weather when plantain yields might drop.
ga: Anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ ŋmei nɔ waa ejaakɛ eŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei ahe gbɛ jogbaŋŋ fe plantain. Ehaa ŋmaakpamɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛ jarayeli shika yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ehiii amli po be mli ni plantain nibii ni anáa lɛ baanyɛ aba shi lɛ.

english: Can I grow cassava on the same piece of land where I already have my plantain trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miyɛ dumɔwui momo lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, you can intercrop cassava with young plantains. While plantains take time to establish and shade the ground, cassava grows quickly in the open space, helping you get two harvests from the same farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ plantains bibii adu ŋmei. Eyɛ mli akɛ plantains heɔ be dani etswaa shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ moŋ, shi yucca daa oya yɛ hei ni gbɛ yɔɔ. Ehaa okpaa nibii ni anáa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ shii enyɔ.

english: Will cassava give me a good harvest even if I don't buy expensive chemical fertilizers?
ga: Ani ŋmei baawo yibii kpakpai kɛji akɛ aheee tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei mli ni jara wa po?

english: Cassava is known for producing decent yields even in low-fertility soils where other crops fail, making it low-cost to grow, though adding compost or manure will produce much larger tubers.
ga: Ale ŋmei akɛ ewoɔ yibii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔji ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi nyɛɛɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ po anɔ. ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shika ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ baa shi Eyɛ mli akɛ kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha bulbs ni dara babaoo aba moŋ.

english: Is cassava farming too exhausting and labor-heavy for a small family to manage?
ga: Ani ŋmei okwaayeli haa mɔ nijiaŋ jeɔ wui tsɔ ni ebiɔ nibii babaoo ni weku bibioo ko nyɛŋ atsu he nii?

english: Main labor is only needed at the beginning for land preparation and planting stems. Once cassava develops a full canopy of leaves, it naturally blocks weeds, making it much easier to maintain than many other crops.
ga: Nitsumɔ titri he miihia yɛ shishijee mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ kɛ tsei lɛ adumɔ pɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ yɛ ŋmei ni eyi obɔ kɛ baai Ebaatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa ekwɛmɔ feɔ mlɛo fe tsei krokomɛi.

english: Is cassava care simple enough for my family members to help manage when I am busy?
ga: Ani ŋmei nɔkwɛmɔ waaa bɔ ni sa ni miweku lɛ mli bii lɛ baaye abua mi kɛkwɛ nɔ kɛ́ mibɛ deka?

english: Yes, once cassava stem cuttings are planted properly, the crop requires simple care like light weeding during the first three months, which makes it easy for family members to look after.
ga: Hɛɛ, beni adu ŋmei ŋmɔji lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Tsei lɛ biɔ ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ, tamɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli fioo, yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa weku lɛ mli bii lɛ akɛ amɛaakwɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava plants are healthy and growing well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛmiida?

english: Healthy cassava plants develop deep green leaves, sturdy main stems, and lush canopy growth without yellowing or curling leaves, which shows the plant is storing energy for large roots.
ga: Cassava tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. tso titri ni mli wa kɛ ŋwɛitsu ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ni shwieɔ shi bɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miito hewalɛ kɛha eshishifãi wuji lɛ.

english: What will happen to my cassava crop if we experience a long period without rainfall?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Cassava protects itself during dry weather by dropping its leaves to save moisture. When the rains return, the plant quickly revives and sprouts fresh leaves without losing its underground tubers.
ga: Yucca buɔ ehe yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ kɛtsɔ ebaai ni ekɛshwieɔ shi koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he lɛ nɔ. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba wala mli oya ni ebaakwɛ baai heei ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ elaajeee.

english: Why do some cassava plants produce big foliage but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei henɔi komɛi yɛ baai wuji shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: If soil has too much nitrogen or if plants are spaced too closely, the crop puts all its energy into leaf growth instead of building thick roots. Proper spacing ensures energy goes down into the tubers.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo kɛji tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai ni miida lɛ mli moŋ fe ni amɛaama shishifãi ni mli tse. He ni jɛkɛmɔ ni sa lɛ haa hewalɛ baa shi kɛyaa yitso lɛ nɔ.

english: How long does cassava take in the soil before it is ready for harvesting?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei lɛ shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani eshɛɔ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Depending on the variety, cassava takes between 8 to 12 months to fully mature. You know it is ready when lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the ground around the stem base begins to crack.
ga: Kɛjɛ bɔ ni ŋmei lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ nɔ lɛ, ŋmei lɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 dani eshɛɔ ŋmei lɛ he. O le kaa e pee klaalo ke tsohi nɛ a ngɛ sisi ɔ ba pee ŋmɔŋ nɛ e je kpo ngɛ adebɔ mi. kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishi shishi jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my neighbor's cassava field so much bushier and greener than mine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ fe minɔ lɛ?

english: Bushy green growth happens when cassava stems are planted at the right depth in loose soil with good moisture and basic organic nutrients, allowing the roots to absorb water easily.
ga: Bushy green growth baa kɛji akɛ adu cassava tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa kɛ shishijee niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmuɔ nu mlɛo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize plant is starving for nitrogen or the soil is too waterlogged. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea when the soil is moist will help the leaves turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do extension officers advise planting groundnuts or beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ adu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. This natural process feeds the soil and reduces the need for expensive chemical fertilizers for your maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa hewalɛ ni ehaa tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he hiamɔ baa shi.

english: Why is it bad for me to apply chemical fertilizer on my farm when the ground is dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baafata miŋmɔ lɛ he beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need moisture to dissolve so that plant roots can absorb them. If applied to bone-dry soil, the concentrated chemical fertilizer can burn and destroy the plant's root system.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe miihia ni nu atsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛ akɛtsu nii kɛ sũ ni egbi ni wui Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite tsei lɛ ashishifãi.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in cool, damp, and overly shady conditions. Pruning excess tree branches to let in sunlight and airflow helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ fe nine. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ aba lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating small holes into the central leaves of my growing maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ daraaa lɛ? Koni aye bu bibioo ko Nɛgbɛ ji mi ŋmãa ni miida lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a destructive pest that hides in the center funnel of young maize plants. Detecting them early and spraying targeted biological treatments or neem oil into the funnel prevents them from destroying the crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ ona amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo neem fɔ afɔ tsɔnei lɛ amli lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the plant sap and spreading viruses. Controlling these insects early with recommended sprays keeps the leaves flat and productive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛtsɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ nɔ lɛ ebaaye ebua ni eha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long because the roots drown from a lack of air. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows water to drain away easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ mli oya.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off without producing any actual tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho ni tomato diɛŋtsɛ ko kwraa bɛ ni miida lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of insect pollinators. Regular watering at the root level and maintaining soil moisture helps flowers convert into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ daa loo kooloi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ falɛ faaa Nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ daa yɛ shishifã lɛ he kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni etsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why do I need to clear away some of the small shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Mi-trunk titri lɛ eje kpo.

english: If too many shoots grow together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to tiny bunches. Keeping only the main stem, one medium shoot, and one small shoot ensures large, healthy fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo ni miida yɛ he kome lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni kɛ tso yibii bibii baa Kɛ́ akpa tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ pɛ, tso lɛ yibii bibii kome, kɛ tso yibii bibii kome pɛ lɛ, ebaaha aduawai agbo ni mli wa aba.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight to manufacture food. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot ground and away from soil diseases, leading to much larger tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ, ni ekɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ hu akashɛ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ feɔ wuji babaoo.

english: When the lower leaves turn yellow starting from the tip down the middle, your maize is starving for nitrogen. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and build big cobs, so if the soil lacks nutrients, the plant pulls food from its older leaves to feed the new growth.
ga: Kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛyitseiaŋ kɛtee teŋgbɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni efee ŋmeii wuji. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts on my land will make my corn grow better next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha miŋmei lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are special crops that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in tiny nodules on their roots. When the plants harvest and decay, that stored nitrogen remains in the soil, acting as free natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi bibii amli kɛ́ akpa tsei lɛ ni amɛfite. Nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yam leaves act like solar panels that catch sunlight to make food, which is then stored underground to form the tuber. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they get maximum sunlight and stay clean from soil diseases, leading to much bigger yams.
ga: Sweet potato baai tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulu la, emɔɔ hulu la ni ekɛfeɔ niyenii. Akɛ enɛɛmɛi toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni efee ŋmeii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hetsemɔ kɛjɛ helai ahe Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ bafee wuji babaoo.

english: Why does my plantain farm produce tiny bunches when I leave many young shoots growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbalaa kɛyaa kui bibii amli lɛ? Beni mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii babaoo yɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he lɛ.

english: Too many young shoots, or suckers, compete directly with the mother plant for nutrients, water, and sunlight. Pruning extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, allowing the main plant to focus all its energy on growing a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii loo tsei bibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ fɔlɔ tso lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ afo tsei bibii krokomɛi amli lɛ, ebaaha tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ aba ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha tso titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama tsei wuji ni tsii ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do weeds stop my crops from growing well even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miitsi miŋmɔshi nibii anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster and have aggressive roots that steal water and fertilizer before your crops can absorb them. They also shade your crops from sunlight, effectively starving your crops of the energy they need to grow.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Amɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii hu feɔ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náaa hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees scorch and drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under full, direct sunlight and harsh winds. They need shade from fast-growing plants like plantains or shade trees to protect them and keep the moisture in the air until their root systems mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Koni abu kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ he ni ekwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baadara.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when the soil stays soaked after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ? Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in the soil for too long without draining, oxygen is cut off, allowing harmful soil fungi to attack and rot the tubers. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ. Afoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji oxygen lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa amɛ ni amɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off before turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from sudden heat stress or a lack of water. High temperatures dry out the pollen inside the flower, causing the plant to shed the blossom because it can no longer produce seeds or fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na piŋmɔ trukaa yɛ latsaa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. He ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa fɔfɔii amli fɔfɔii lɛ agbiɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ejaakɛ enyɛɛɛ ewo dumɔwui loo aduawai dɔŋŋ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in the leaves of my young maize plants with tiny dark specks inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ yɛ bu ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii diji yɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides deep inside the center shoot of the maize plant during the day and feeds on the soft leaves. The dark specks you see are the waste left behind by the pest as it eats.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii diji ni onaa lɛ ji jwɛi ni kooloi ni yeɔ nii lɛ shiɔ yɛ amɛsɛɛ beni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ.
