english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the sap under the leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. As these insects drain the plant's fluids, the leaves contract and curl, which stunts overall growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Enɛ ji akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ. Kɛkɛ lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa dalɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do farmers in my area plant crops twice in the same year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ yɛ afi kome mli lɛ?

english: In Ghana, we have two distinct rainy periods in a year—the major rainy season and the minor rainy season. Planting twice allows you to take advantage of both rainfall cycles so you can harvest crops twice a year instead of just once.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, wɔyɛ nugbɔshiimɔi srɔtoi enyɔ yɛ afi mli: nugbɔshiimɔ be klɛŋklɛŋ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni ji enyɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ shii enyɔ lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ nugbɔshiimɔi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okpa onibii lɛ shii enyɔ yɛ afi mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaakpa nii shikome pɛ

english: How do I know the exact right time to plant my seeds when the rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: You should wait until the ground receives a few steady, heavy rains so the soil gets wet deep down. Planting too early after just one light shower can cause your seeds to dry up and die if the rain stops for several days afterward.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa fioo be fɛɛ be koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Saramɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii babaoo yɛ no sɛɛ.

english: Should I use the same seed variety for both the first and second planting seasons?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kɛ nɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ mli?

english: Not always. The first rainy season is usually longer, so seeds that take longer to mature grow well. The second rainy season is shorter, so it is better to plant fast-maturing or drought-tolerant seeds so they finish growing before the rains end.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Nugbɔshiimɔ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ yɛ kuku, no hewɔ lɛ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya loo ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa koni amɛkwɛ̃ dani nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ aba naagbee.

english: Will planting crops twice every year make my land weak and tired?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ shii enyɔ yɛ afi mli lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ agbɔjɔ ni etɔ lɛ?

english: Growing crops twice a year uses up soil nutrients quickly. You can keep your soil healthy by rotating your crops with beans or groundnuts, which naturally feed the soil, or by adding compost and fertilizer between planting seasons.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ shii enyɔ yɛ afi mli lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Obaanyɛ oha oshikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni okɛbaatsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ. ni ji adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like tubes when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ kanei ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ kɛ́ edɔ fe nine lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up to protect themselves from heat and conserve water. By rolling up, less leaf area is exposed to the hot sun, helping the plant save moisture until the next rain comes.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni amɛbu nu he. Kɛtsɔ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɛɛ he ni baai lɛ yɔɔ lɛ he tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baa.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow when there is too much rain on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains can flood the soil and choke the plant roots, preventing them from breathing oxygen. Without oxygen and with plant food being washed away by excess water, the leaves naturally turn yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu afua ni eha tsei shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, amɛnyɛɛɛ amɛmu kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji oxygen lɛ. Kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ ni akɛ nu ni fa fe nine tsuɔ tsei aniyenii ahe nii. Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do the flowers drop off my crops before turning into fruits when the dry spell starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shiɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli dani amɛbatsɔmɔɔ aduawai kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: When crops do not get enough water, they drop their flowers to save energy and keep themselves alive. Without adequate soil moisture, the plant cannot support the heavy task of producing pods or fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ Amɛbaashwie fɔfɔi hu koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛha amɛhi wala mli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ atsu nitsumɔ ni tsii ni ji ŋmɔtɔ loo aduawai afeemɔ lɛ he nii kɛkɛ.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant them too close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe tsɔ koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with thin, weak plants that produce very small yields compared to properly spaced crops.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oná tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛ akɛto tsei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: Wild weeds are naturally tougher than cultivated crops, and their seeds sit hidden in the soil ready to sprout immediately at the first drop of water. Clearing weeds early gives your main crop a fair chance to grow strong.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli jwɛi lɛ wa fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Ni amɛdumɔwui lɛ etee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛji nu klɛŋklɛŋ gbee lɛ shwie shi pɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha otso titri lɛ aná hegbɛ ni eda waa.

english: Is it bad to harvest my mature crops while it is still raining heavily?
ga: Ani ehiii akɛ aaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni eda yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lolo lɛ?

english: Harvesting in heavy rain makes produce damp, which leads to rotting, mold, and spoiling quickly. It is best to wait for a dry, sunny period to harvest so your produce dries properly and stays fresh during storage.
ga: Nikpamɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ kɛ fitemɔ oya, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ fitemɔ baa. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi dani okpa nii. Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ ni ehi shi ehee yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize farm turning yellow and curling up when it doesn't rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during dry spells to reduce the leaf surface exposed to the sun. This helps the plant trap moisture inside and slows down water evaporation so it can survive without rain.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni hulu la ni baa amɛnɔ lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are dying from the heat or if they will recover when rain falls?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbo yɛ latsaa lɛ hewɔ loo ebaatsake kɛji nugbɔ nɛ?

english: If your crops wilt during the hot afternoon but stand upright again early in the morning, they are just conserving water. If they remain droopy and dry in the cool morning, they are under severe water stress and need help.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwie shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli shi edamɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ leebi. Nu he kwɛmɔ kɛkɛ ni. Kɛji amɛyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lolo ni amɛgbi yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛyɛ nu he haomɔ ni naa wa shishi, ni yelikɛbuamɔ he miihia amɛ.

english: Why does my cassava lose almost all its leaves during a long dry period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fite yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves on purpose when water is scarce to stop water from evaporating through the foliage. The plant goes into a survival sleep and will sprout fresh leaves once moisture returns.
ga: Akɛ yiŋtoo shwieɔ cassava baai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ni baatsi nu naa koni ekatsɔ baai lɛ amli kɛho. Tso lɛ wɔɔ koni ehi shi ni ebaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Is it good to water my crops in the middle of the afternoon when the sun is very hot?
ga: Okɛ nu awo tsei lɛ amli yɛ shwane mli. Ani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi?

english: No, watering in the hot afternoon causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before reaching the roots. It is best to water early in the morning or late in the evening when the soil can absorb it properly.
ga: Dabi, nu ni oooha yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Esa akɛ afɔ nu lɛ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I use water from a nearby stream to water my vegetable farm during a drought?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛ faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ awo mi-aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, but stream water can carry plant diseases or excess salt. Apply the water directly to the soil near the plant roots rather than spraying it on the leaves to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi faa mli nu baanyɛ aŋɔ tsei ahe helai loo ŋoo ni fa fe nine. Okɛ nu awo shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Mohu ɔ, mo ngɔ tso ɔ kɛ pue baai ɔmɛ a nɔ konɛ fungal hiɔ ko nɛ ba nɔ.

english: Will covering the ground around my crops with dry grass help keep the soil wet?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ehà shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Yes, this is called mulching. Placing dry grass, leaves, or palm fronds around the base of your plants shields the soil from direct sunlight, keeping it cool and trapping water for much longer.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching. Jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo ŋmei tsei ni akɛbaabɔle Tso lɛ shishi lɛ baaye abua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers when the weather stays hot and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and lack of moisture stress tomato plants, forcing them to drop their flowers to conserve energy and keep the main plant alive instead of spending resources on growing fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni tso lɛ ahi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baatsu nii kɛdu aduawai

english: Why do young cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up during extended dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Without enough water, cocoa trees cannot move vital nutrients to developing pods. The tree naturally aborts the young pods to protect its main trunk and root system from dying.
ga: Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Cacao tso lɛ nyɛŋ ajie niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛya pod ni miiya hiɛ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ shwieɔ eshishifãi bibii lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ebu eshishifã titri lɛ kɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe koni amɛkagboi.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up completely above the ground when a drought starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ egbi kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Yam vines dry up above ground as a defense mechanism, shifting all remaining energy and water into the underground tuber so it can stay preserved until the rainy season comes back.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ egbi yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ akɛ hebuu gbɛ. Amɛjieɔ hewalɛ kɛ nu ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii amli koni anyɛ akɛto kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: How do shade trees help my crops survive long weeks without rainfall?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhi shi otsii babaoo ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: Shade trees lower the soil temperature, block harsh sunlight, and break dry winds. This protects your main crops from heat burn and keeps moisture in the soil around them for a longer period.
ga: Tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i baa shi. Etsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa ni efiteɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ Enɛ baabu onibii titri lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa ni shãa lɛ he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. kɛha be kakadaŋŋ

english: My crops have just sprouted out of the ground, so what are the main things I should look out for on my farm right now?
ga: Miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, mɛni ji nibii titrii ni esa akɛ makwɛ mihe nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli bianɛ?

english: When crops first sprout, you should check for even growth across the field, look closely under tender leaves for insect damage, and make sure early weeds aren't choking the young seedlings.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ Esa akɛ okwɛ kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii miida yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Kwɛmɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi jogbaŋŋ koni ona kɛji kooloi efite. Ni kwɛmɔ ni jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra lɛ akatsi dumɔwui bibii lɛ anaa.

english: Why is it better for me to get seeds from official bodies like the Seed Council instead of keeping seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ maná dumɔwui kɛjɛ maŋ nitsumɔhei tamɔ Seed Council lɛ adɛŋ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, mo ngɔ dumɔwuhi nɛ a je kpa kpami nɛ be ɔ mi ɔ kɛ yi wami.

english: Certified seeds from official bodies are specially tested and bred to fight off local diseases, grow uniformly, and give you a much higher harvest compared to seeds saved from older crops.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni maŋ lɛ eŋmɛ gbɛ lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni akwɛ koni akɛwu ashi maŋ lɛ mli helai. kwɛ̃ɔ daa ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo kwraa kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛjɛ tsei ni etsɛ amli lɛ ahe.

english: Who can I report to if I notice unusual pests or strange leaf diseases starting to spread across my field?
ga: Namɔ manyɛ mahã lɛ amaniɛ? Ni kɛji akɛ mina tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ loo baa helai ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ hu? Eje shishi egbɛ eshwa miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: You can inform your local agricultural extension officer or representatives from the Plant Protection and Regulatory Services Directorate (PPRS), who can identify the specific problem and give you safe treatment options.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha okpokpaa lɛ nɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ loo najiaŋdamɔlɔ ko ni jɛ Plant Protection and Regulatory Services (PPRS) ni baanyɛ ana naagba pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛ tsofafeemɔ gbɛ̀i ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe aha bo lɛ ale.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up so fast when exposed to direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very delicate roots and thin leaves that lose moisture rapidly in hot sun, which is why temporary shade plants like plantains are grown alongside them to protect them.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa kɛ baai bibii, ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli fɛ̃i lɛ fiteɔ oya. Enɛ hewɔ ni aduɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains yɛ amɛmasɛi koni ebu amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why do some of the flowers on my cocoa trees drop off without turning into full cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi komɛi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee cacao ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Trees drop flowers when they experience stress from lack of rain, poor soil nutrition, extreme heat, or pest damage, as the plant tries to save its energy to survive.
ga: Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɛɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi.

english: How can I tell by looking at my growing crops that the soil needs more fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male beni mikwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: If lower leaves start turning pale yellow while the rest of the plant looks weak and stunted, it is a clear sign your crops are missing vital soil nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni eshwɛ lɛ Tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ ni egbɔjɔ. No ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ otsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why does clearing weeds around my young crops make them grow so much faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ midumɔwui lɛ haa amɛdaraa oya kwraa.

english: Weeds actively steal food, water, and sunlight away from your crops; clearing them ensures all the goodness in the soil goes straight into growing your main crop.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Amɛhe ni ooofɔ lɛ haa nibii kpakpai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yaa oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: What will happen to my newly planted seeds if heavy rain floods my field for days?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui heei ni midu lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha ŋmɔji lɛ amli nu eyi gbii babaoo?

english: Too much standing water cuts off air supply to the soil, which can rot seeds before they sprout or drown young roots that need oxygen to survive.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ kpata kɔɔyɔɔ ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa. Enɛ baanyɛ afite dumɔwui dani amɛkwɛ̃ loo amɛwo shishifãi bibii ni he hiaa kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛhi shi lɛ amli.

english: What standards do officers from the Cocoa Board look for when checking the quality of my cocoa beans?
ga: Mɛɛ shishitoo mlai Cocoa Board onukpai lɛ taoɔ yɛ bɔ ni mi-cocoa ŋmeii lɛ hi ha lɛ mli?

english: Officers check to ensure beans are well-fermented, thoroughly sun-dried to correct moisture levels, uniform in size, and completely free of mould or insect infestation.
ga: Nitsulɔi lɛ kwɛɔ koni amɛkwɛ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ. Gbimɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu lɛ mli koni ekɛsaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, elɛɛmɔ afee ekome ni ŋmɔtɔ loo kooloi akabote mli kwraa.

english: Why is it important for me to cut away extra side branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ aniji ni fa fe nine lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the canopy so sunlight and air can flow through, which lowers dampness inside the tree and stops pod diseases like black pod from developing.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ gbeleɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ naa koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Enɛ haa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa helai ni jɛɔ pod mli kɛbaa tamɔ pod diji lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why does my harvested rice spoil so quickly when I store it inside bags in my house?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ akɛwo kotokui amli yɛ shia lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested rice grain contains hidden moisture. If you bag and store it before sun-drying it properly, the trapped moisture creates heat and mould, which causes the grain to rot and attract storage pests.
ga: Omɔ ŋmaa ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. Kɛji akɛ okɛwo baagi mli ni okɛto jogbaŋŋ dani okɛwo hulu lɛ mli lɛ, Trapped moisture haa dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ haa ŋmaa lɛ fiteɔ ni egbalaa kooloi ni yɔɔ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: How can I keep my harvested maize safe from insects in storage without buying expensive chemicals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ akafee nɔ ko ni kooloi ni akɛtoɔ lɛ akabote mli ni miheee tsofai ni jara wa?

english: You can store thoroughly dried maize grains in airtight containers or specialized triple-layer plastic bags (PICS bags). These bags cut off oxygen, which naturally suffocates insect pests without needing chemical powders.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmãa ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ awo tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo plastic kotokui krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ fãi etɛ (PICS kotokui) amli. Nɛkɛ kotokui nɛɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ tsuuu nii.

english: Why do my yams start rotting from the inside after I keep them in my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ kɛmiijɛ mli beni mikɛto mi-shĩa lɛ mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Internal rot usually starts from small cuts or bruises made during harvesting. Fungi enter through these wounds and break down the tuber, especially if the barn is hot and lacks fresh air circulation.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mligbɛ gangrene lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛ fã bibioo ko ni afo. loo fãji ni baa yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli lɛ Fuji lɛ boteɔ mli kɛtsɔɔ pilamɔi amli ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli.

english: When cassava stems are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in many small, thin tubers instead of big, healthy ones.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take much longer to produce fruit when weeds grow around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal water and soil nutrients away from your plantain. Without enough food, the plantain plant grows slowly and delays producing a heavy fruit bunch.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ plantain lɛ mli. Kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Plantains lɛ daa blɛoo ni ehaa yibiiwoo lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ kui amli.

english: Why does rice require so much standing water in the field to grow well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo he hiaa ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ mli koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: While rice plants naturally love water, standing water acts as a natural barrier that prevents weeds from growing and drowning out your young rice plants.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei sumɔɔ nu yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ni tsiɔ jwɛi naa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkawo o-rice tsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: What will happen to my land if I plant maize on the exact same spot every single year?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that crop loves from the soil, while allowing soil pests and diseases that attack maize to build up over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ lɛ jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that your maize is missing nitrogen, which is the main food leaves need to stay green and healthy. It can also happen if heavy rains waterlog the soil and choke the roots.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa baa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni efo shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do high-yielding crop seeds need more fertilizer than the local seeds I usually use?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fe maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni mifɔɔ nitsumɔ lɛ?

english: Improved crop seeds are bred to grow faster and produce much bigger yields, but to build all those extra grains or tubers, they require much more plant food than traditional varieties.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Shi koni akɛfee nakai dumɔwui loo bulbs krokomɛi lɛ. Amɛbiɔ tsei niyenii babaoo fe blema niyenii srɔtoi lɛ.

english: Your rice is ready for harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the grain heads across the field turn a golden-yellow color and the grains feel hard when you bite one.
ga: O-rice lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni aaafee ŋmaa yitsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 batsɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ lɛ. Ni dumɔwui lɛ baanu he akɛ amɛhe wa kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo mli.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight. Large shade trees or food crops like plantains protect young cocoa seedlings from sunburn and help keep moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and spoil during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cold, overly wet, and humid conditions. Pruning excess tree branches allows sunlight and breeze into your farm to dry off the pods and slow down the fungus.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli Too Wet and Moist Pruning niji ni fa fe nine lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa kɛboteɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni eha ŋmei lɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient for growth. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore green foliage and boosts plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass (mulching) acts like a blanket. It traps moisture in the earth so your crops do not dry out quickly, keeps the soil cool, and stops weeds from sprouting.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbiɛɛ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: Why do weeds always grow faster than my planted crops after the rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya be fɛɛ be fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild local plants that naturally adapt to survive on very few resources. They quickly absorb available water and soil food before your planted crops can, which is why early weeding is necessary.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi kɛtsɔ nibii fioo ko pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya dani tsei ni oduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from the same plot?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food to grow strong and yield larger crops.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoot stems growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, drain food and water away from the main plantain plant. Cutting off extra shoots leaves only one or two strong suckers, which directs energy to produce larger plantain bunches.
ga: Tsoi loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni kudɔɔ hewalɛ koni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji aba.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground if I leave them in the earth too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Once cassava tubers reach full maturity, waterlogging from rain or soil organisms can penetrate the roots, causing fungal decay and rotting if they are not harvested in time.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eda kwraa Nu ni jɛɔ nugbɔ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ abote shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ akpaaa amɛ yɛ be naa.

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to make energy for building big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves high in the light and off damp soil where diseases easily spread.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi tsɔnei wuji. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi yɛ la ni tsoɔ waa mli, ni ejɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ he ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato plants shed flowers when exposed to extreme heat or irregular watering. Providing consistent moisture and shade during very hot weather helps the flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Fɛ̃i kɛ shade ni akɛhaa daa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛhiɛɔ ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Can I grow Prekese on my farmland, or does it only survive in the natural forest?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ Prekese yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ? Aloo ebaahi shi yɛ koo lɛ mli pɛ?

english: Prekese is naturally a large forest tree, meaning it thrives best in rich, moist soil and environments that mimic forest conditions, though it can be cultivated on farms.
ga: Prekese ji koo mli tso agbo ko yɛ adebɔɔ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ. kɛ shihilɛ ni kaseɔ koo mli shihilɛi Eyɛ mli akɛ abaanyɛ adu yɛ ŋmɔji amli moŋ.

english: How much space should I leave around a Prekese tree when planting it?
ga: He enyiɛ esa akɛ mashi yɛ mi Prekese tso lɛ he kɛji midu?

english: Because Prekese grows into a very large tree, it requires significant space so its wide roots and large canopy do not crowd out nearby crops.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, Prekese daa ni etsɔɔ tsei wuji waa. No hewɔ lɛ ebiɔ he ko babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, eshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ kɛ eshishifãi wuji lɛ eboteee ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: Does Prekese need a lot of rainfall to grow and produce fruit properly?
ga: Ani nugbɔ babaoo he miihia Prekese koni ekwɛ̃ ni ewo yibii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Since Prekese is naturally found in forest environments, it relies on good soil moisture and regular rainfall to reach full maturity and yield fruits.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, anaa Prekese yɛ kooi amli shihilɛi amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, edamɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ nɔ koni enyɛ ená dalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni yeɔ emuu.

english: What parts of the Prekese tree can I actually use or sell?
ga: Mɛɛ Prekese tso lɛ fãi manyɛ mikɛtsu nii loo mahɔ̃ɔ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Prekese is a multi-purpose tree; you can harvest and sell its edible fruits, which are used as food and medicine, or harvest its wood for strong timber.
ga: Prekese ji tso ni tsuɔ nibii babaoo he nii. Obaanyɛ okpa aduawai ni ayeɔ, ni akɛtsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛ tsofa lɛ ni ohɔ̃ɔ. Aloo akpa tsei lɛ koni akɛtsu nii akɛ tso ni wa.

english: How is the Prekese fruit used as food?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ akɛ Prekese aduawai tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii?

english: The fruit of the Prekese tree is fully edible and is commonly dried and used as a fragrant spice to flavor soups, stews, and local dishes.
ga: Prekese tso lɛ yibii lɛ ji nɔ ni ayeɔ kwraa, ni bei pii lɛ, agbiɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii akɛ tsofa ni ŋɔɔ ni akɛwoɔ shwiili, shwiili mli niyenii, kɛ maŋ lɛ mli niyenii amli.

english: Can I use Prekese fruit for medicinal purposes on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ Prekese aduawai lɛ atsu nii kɛtsa hela yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, Prekese fruit is widely valued for its natural health properties and is frequently prepared as traditional medicine to treat various ailments.
ga: Hɛɛ, abuɔ Prekese aduawai lɛ akɛ nɔ ko ni jara wa waa yɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ hewalɛnamɔ lɛ hewɔ. Ni bei pii lɛ, asaa lɛ akɛ blema tsofa ni akɛtsaa helai srɔtoi.

english: Why would I choose to plant Prekese instead of just ordinary timber trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mihala akɛ madu Prekese yɛ tso ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Prekese provides double value: while the tree grows big enough to yield quality wood for timber, it continuously produces edible and medicinal fruits year after year.
ga: Prekese haa sɛɛnamɔ ni ji shii enyɔ: Kɛ́ tso lɛ da bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfoɔ tsei baa lɛ po lɛ, Tso lɛ baaya nɔ ewo yibii ni ayeɔ kɛ tsofa afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Will a large Prekese tree block sunlight and spoil my lower-growing crops?
ga: Ani Prekese tsei wuji baatsi hulu lɛ naa ni amɛbaafite miŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ fioo lɛ?

english: As a large forest tree, Prekese forms a wide canopy that creates heavy shade, so lower-growing crops that need direct sunlight should not be planted directly under it.
ga: Ákɛ koo mli tso agbo lɛ, Prekese feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli kwɔ ni haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli wa baa. No hewɔ lɛ, esaaa akɛ aduɔ tsei ni shwereɔ fioo ni biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ lɛ yɛ tsei ashishi tɛ̃ɛ.

english: If I cut down my Prekese tree for timber, will it affect my fruit harvest?
ga: Kɛ mifo Prekese tso ko kɛha tso lɛ, ani ebaana mi yibii ni mikpaa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, because the fruit grows on the mature branches of the tree, cutting down the tree for timber completely stops any future fruit production from that tree.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ yibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ niji ni edara lɛ anɔ. Tso ni afoɔ koni akɛfee tso lɛ haa wɔsɛɛ be mli yibii ni jɛɔ nakai tso lɛ mli baa lɛ kpaa kwraa.

english: How do I know when the Prekese tree is old enough to start giving fruit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi Prekese tso lɛ eda bɔ ni sa ni ebɔi yibiiwoo?

english: Like most large forest trees, Prekese takes several years to establish its trunk and canopy before it begins consistently bearing fruit pods.
ga: Taakɛ tsei babaoo ni yɔɔ kooi wuji amli lɛ ji lɛ, Prekese heɔ afii babaoo dani ekɛ etsitsi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ toɔ shi dani eyaa nɔ ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ cacao tsei fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct heat and strong sunlight. Leaving shade trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects the young leaves from burning and helps the soil stay moist while the cocoa establishes root systems.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei ni ashiɔ loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ buɔ baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ maa eshishifãi lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen, a major food crop plants need to stay green and grow strong. Applying well-timed fertilizer or decomposed manure helps restore the green color and improves yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Ehe miihia ni niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off before setting any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant is stressed by irregular watering, extreme heat, or an excess of nitrogen fertilizer which causes the plant to put energy into leaf growth rather than fruit production.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ haoɔ amɛ. Enɛ haa tsei kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ baai fe bɔ ni amɛkɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Curled and pale leaves on cassava are often caused by whiteflies spreading a plant virus (Cassava Mosaic Disease). Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties helps prevent this problem and keeps plants healthy.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Bei pii lɛ, whiteflies ni gbɛɔ tsei amli helai lɛ kɛbaa. (Cassava mosaic disease) Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni akwɛɔ lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa ni eye ebua ni tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant beans or groundnuts in the same field where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, which naturally feeds and improves the soil for heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛ shikpɔŋ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛha niyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: How does adding dried animal dung or compost help my crops during dry spells?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Organic materials like compost act like a sponge in the soil, holding onto moisture much longer so roots have access to water even when it does not rain for a few days.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ No sɛɛ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ náa nu kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ gbii fioo komɛi po.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly when there are lots of weeds in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ miida blɛoo be mli ni jwɛi babaoo yɛ miŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. When weeds are present, they steal essential food away from your crops, slowing their growth.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni jwɛi yɛ lɛ Ebaaju niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛ onibii amli. haa dalɛ baa shi

english: Yam tubers grow underground and need soft, deep soil to expand. High mounds create loose soil for tubers to grow big and straight while preventing water from logging around the roots.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ehe hiaa shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee mlɛo bɔni afee ni bulb lɛ adara ni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ nu naa koni ekafo tsei ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay thin and light even when the main stem grows very tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ kɛlɛ waa moŋ?

english: When cassava cuttings are planted too close together, plants compete for light and soil food, causing them to grow tall stems to reach the sun instead of storing energy in large root tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ la kɛ shikpɔŋ he akaŋshii mli kɛha niyenii. Amɛkwɛɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ koni amɛha hulu la aba mli moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baato shishifãi wuji amli.

english: It is best to wait until the rains become steady and the ground stays moist for a few days, ensuring the newly germinated seeds do not dry out and die during a sudden dry patch.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ ba shi ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbii fioo komɛi. Enɛ haa dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ akagbi ni amɛgboi yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔi baa trukaa lɛ.

english: I planted my pepper seeds in the nursery bed two weeks ago and nothing has sprouted yet—how long should I wait?
ga: Midu pepper dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli otsii enyɔ ni eho nɛ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko ekwɛko lolo. Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ?

english: Pepper seeds usually take between 7 to 14 days to sprout, but cold or dry soil can delay them up to 3 weeks. Keep the topsoil lightly watered every morning so the seeds stay warm and moist enough to break open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ dumɔwui lɛ heɔ gbii 7 kɛyashi 14 dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ, shi shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ asɛɛ afo kɛyashi otsii etɛ. Okɛ nu awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fioo. daa leebi koni dumɔwui lɛ adɔ ni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like sticks during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ tsei niji yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll inward during intense heat to trap moisture and stop water from evaporating too fast. It is a natural defence mechanism, and the leaves will open up again once the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Abele baa lɛ shwieɔ mli yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni ekɛmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekɛtsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo. Ni baai lɛ gbeleɔ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ gbɛkɛ mli jɔ.

english: My tomato seedlings in the seedbed now have four small leaves—what is the next step to move them into my main farm?
ga: Amrɔ nɛɛ mi-tomato dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ baai bibii ejwɛ. Mɛni ji nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni esa akɛ mafee koni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Once seedlings show 3 to 4 true leaves, they are ready for transplanting. Water the seedbed well so roots lift easily without breaking, and move them to the field late in the afternoon so the hot sun does not dry them out.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ ná baai diɛŋtsɛ 3-4 lɛ, no lɛ amɛfee klalo akɛ abaawo amɛ. Okɛ nu awo dumɔwui lɛ ashishi jogbaŋŋ koni shishifãi lɛ adara oya ni amɛkakumɔ. Ni okɛya ŋmɔ lɛ mli shwane mli koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akagbi shishifãi lɛ.

english: Is it safe to burn cleared brush on my farm before planting, or will the heat damage my soil?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mashã tsei bibii ni ajie yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dani madu? Aloo latsaa lɛ baafite mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Burning clears land quickly, but intense heat kills useful soil organisms and burns off natural organic matter. Leaving cleared weeds to rot naturally as mulch keeps the soil cool, fertile, and moist.
ga: La ni ashãa lɛ baajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Shi dɔlɛ ni naa wa gbeɔ nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ, ni eshãa adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Ha jwɛi ni ajie lɛ lɛ afite yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe be mli ni sũ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the flowers on my cowpea plants falling off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant experiences heat stress, lack of water, or attack from small pests like thrips. Ensuring steady soil moisture and checking for tiny insects will help the flowers set pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ, nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips tutua amɛ. Ehe miihia ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni okwɛ kɛji kooloi bibii yɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛto ŋmeii lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves mean the soil is low in nitrogen, or the plant is shedding old leaves to conserve water during dry periods. Adding compost or manure around the base helps keep the leaves healthy.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo tsei miiho baai momoi koni amɛkɛbu nu he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli yɛ Shishitoo lɛ he yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ mli waa.

english: Why are my yam vines growing very bushy and green, but the tubers underneath remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ miida ni eyɛ ŋmɔji waa lɛ? Shi yitso ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ji bibioo kwraa lolo.

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes the plant focus all its energy on leaves instead of root tubers. Using balanced fertilizer and providing stable stakes for vines allows energy to move down into growing big tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ baai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja tsu nii ni akɛ tsei ni wa wo wain tsei lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni hewalɛ lɛ yaa shi kɛyaa ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: I see tiny white flies swarming under my cassava leaves—will these insects spoil my farm?
ga: Mina ŋmei bibioo ko yɛŋ. Eyi mi-cassava baai lɛ ashishi Ani nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ baafite miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, whiteflies suck nutrients from the leaves and spread the cassava mosaic virus, which stunts plant growth. Spraying a light solution of soapy water or neem oil under the leaves helps control them.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ nuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli ni amɛgbɛɔ cassava mosaic hela lɛ amɛshwãa. ni haa tsei nyɛɛɛ ada Nu ni akɛ samla loo neem fɔ shwieɔ baai lɛ ashishi fioo lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ lɛ.

english: How can I tell that my plantain bunch is fully mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-plantain tso lɛ edara jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: A plantain bunch is ready when the individual fingers lose their sharp green corners and become full and rounded, and the dried flower tips at the ends easily rub off.
ga: Plantains kuu ko efee klalo beni nineshi nine fɛɛ nineshi ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni fɔfɔii ni egbi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain suckers beside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantain ŋmeii yɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa the shade and cool soil moisture it needs to survive its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha kookoo lɛ hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and getting small holes in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni bu bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves with holes are usually a sign of Fall Armyworm attack or a lack of nutrients like nitrogen in the soil. Fall armyworms eat the leaves from the inside before the plant fully grows, while a lack of nitrogen weakens the plant and turns leaves light green or yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni bu yɔɔ mli lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm etutua amɛ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen, bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Fall cutworms yeɔ baai kɛjɛɔ mli dani tsei lɛ daraa kwraa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nitrogen ni bɛ lɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ.

english: Black Pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, shaded conditions. When rain splashes fungal spores from the soil onto the cocoa pods, it rots the fruit. Clearing thick weeds and pruning tree branches lets sunlight in to dry out the farm and prevent this.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni shade yɔɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, ŋmeii ni jɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Yibii baanyɛ agbo. Jwɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la lɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaa naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle strong, direct sunlight and heavy heat. Tall shade trees or fast-growing food crops like plantains act as natural umbrellas, protecting young cocoa plants from sun scorch and keeping the soil moist until the cocoa stems grow mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo loo niyenii tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why is it important for me to stake my yam vines with tall wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ atswa mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally want to climb toward sunlight. By staking them, you help the leaves spread out to catch maximum sunlight, which provides energy to the plant so it can grow larger tubers under the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato wain tsei lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛkwɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli. Staking haa baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ bɔni afee ni enyɛ ekwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I put fertilizer in a circle around my crop instead of dumping it right against the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe yɛ kooyigbɛ moŋ fe ni mashɛrɛ ashwie tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the stem can burn the plant's skin and kill it. Placing it in a ring a few inches away targets the tiny feeder roots underground, allowing the crop to safely absorb the nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ hewolo lɛ ashã ni egbo. Kɛ́ okɛwo ŋwɛi ŋta ni kɛ jɛmɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko lɛ, ebaatswa shikpɔŋ shishi niyenii bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ. Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow huge green leaves but produce very tiny tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi bulbs bibii yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or grows in soil that has too much leaf-growing manure, it spends all its energy developing big branches above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers underground.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmei babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei niji agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why will my harvest be smaller if I plant my maize seeds very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ faaa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni amɛhi mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ babaoo lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for water and soil nutrients, and their leaves block sunlight from neighboring plants. Proper spacing ensures each crop gets enough food and light to grow big ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni dumɔwui lɛ ahe baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni jɛɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ amli lɛ naa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmãa toi wuji.

english: Weed seeds naturally live in the soil and are adapted to survive tough conditions. They wake up instantly with the first rain and pull nutrients faster than planted crops, which is why clearing weeds early gives your crops a fair chance to grow.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛteɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ni amɛjieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii oya fe tsei ni etswa amɛhe shi lɛ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa hegbɛ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do the seeds I saved from last year's harvest produce a smaller yield than the packaged seeds I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ wo yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni akɛwo kotoku mli ni mihe lɛ?

english: Packaged hybrid seeds are specially bred for strong yields and disease resistance in their first planting. When you save seeds from that crop to plant again, those strong traits weaken, resulting in smaller harvests.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛwo adeka mli lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni eha yibiiwoo babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ helai yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔ mli. Beni obua dumɔwui anaa kɛjɛɔ nakai tso lɛ mli ni oduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ. Nakai sui ni mli wa lɛ baagbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kpamɔ fioo.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before setting any fruit when the weather becomes too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi dani ewoɔ yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extremely high temperatures cause heat stress in pepper plants. To protect themselves from losing too much moisture, the plants drop their blossoms instead of spending energy to produce pepper fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ waa lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ haomɔ baa pepper tsei amli. Koni okɛbu ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛfee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and burning up in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiishã yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, strong sunlight. Without shade trees or plantain crops planted nearby to protect them, the harsh sun burns their tender leaves and dries out the surrounding soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei bibii ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ koni akɛbu tsei lɛ ahe lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa tsei lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli gĩɔ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing them properly allows each plant enough room to grow strong and yield larger cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ eda ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I wait for the first heavy rains before planting my crop seeds instead of planting in dry dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ dani madu dumɔwui moŋ fe ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds need continuous moisture to germinate and establish roots. Planting in dry soil leaves the seeds vulnerable to drying out, dying, or being eaten by birds and ants before the rain arrives.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ kɛ oshara baa akɛ amɛbaagbi, amɛbaagboi, loo okpoi kɛ ŋmeii baaye amɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ aba.

english: Yellowing leaves usually indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen, a essential nutrient for green growth. Adding organic manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps bring back the green color and healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava tubers rot when water collects and stays around the roots for too long during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away and protects the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa ni ehiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli ni ebu ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: How does planting beans or groundnuts together with my corn help my soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa fata he ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like beans and groundnuts naturally pull nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil. This enriches the ground and helps neighboring crops like corn grow better without relying heavily on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ anɔ babaoo.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up tightly and stop the plant from growing fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe shi shiŋŋ ni amɛtsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekawo yibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or aphids that spread a plant virus while feeding on leaf sap. Managing these insects early prevents the leaf curl disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni gbɛɔ tsei amli helai eshwaa be mli ni amɛyeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa leaf curl hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are there small holes in my maize leaves and green droppings inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baai kɛ mifɔmɔ nii lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? yɛ teŋgbɛ tso lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar pest that feeds inside the growing funnel of maize plants. Controlling them early with recommended organic or chemical sprays preserves the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni yeɔ ŋmei tsei ni daraa lɛ amli lɛ. Amɛ nɔyeli mra Kɛtsɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ anɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite.

english: Why do flowers drop off my tomato plants without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shiɔ mi tomato tso lɛ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps the plants retain their flowers and produce tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaaa amɛ daa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ tomato.

english: Why do seeds I saved from my last harvest give me a smaller yield than certified seeds bought from a store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Saved seeds can lose vigor over time and carry diseases from previous seasons. Certified seeds are specially selected and tested to ensure high germination rates, disease resistance, and higher fruit yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baanyɛ afite hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli ni ekɛ helai ni jɛ nyɛsɛɛ be lɛ mli lɛ aba. Ahalaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ koni ana akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ babaoo, helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe, ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees burning brown and drying up during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft, tender leaves that cannot withstand direct sun. Without larger shade plants like plantains or shade trees above them, the intense sunlight scorches the leaves and dries out the water the seedling needs to stay alive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa nu ni he hiaa kɛha wala lɛ gĩɔ.

english: Why should I cut away the extra small shoot plants growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Mi plantain tsei titri lɛ ahe lɛ etee.

english: When too many shoots grow around one plantain stem, they steal food and water from each other. Removing the extra shoots leaves only one or two strong ones, ensuring the main tree gets full nourishment to produce large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ ni ebɔle ehe Plantain kome Amɛbaaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ niji kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ewo dumɔwui wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning pale yellow while the top leaves stay light green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the key plant food responsible for dark green growth. The plant starves itself at the bottom to feed new growth at the top, showing it needs compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji tso niyenii titri ni haa ŋmɔŋ ni tsuɔ waa lɛ daa. Hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ koni amɛha shweremɔ hee ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii he miihia bo.

english: Why do my cassava plants have tall stems with plenty of green leaves but tiny tubers under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛlɛ lɛ? Baai eŋɔlii babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: If the soil has too much nitrogen relative to other plant nutrients, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing big leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below. Balancing soil nutrients helps the plant build bigger roots.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo kɛ akɛto tsei amli niyenii krokomɛi ahe Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ŋmei baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, etsɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ gbɛ kɛyaa baai wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi wuji.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts on my plot make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas directly from the air and store it in tiny knots on their roots. When the plants finish growing and rot in the soil, they release this natural fertilizer for future crops like maize to feed on.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ koni amɛkɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines to climb up tall wooden sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔse ŋmei tso ko koni enyɛ ekwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch maximum sunlight, which the plant uses to make food to feed the growing tubers underneath. Keeping leaves off the warm dirt also prevents diseases caused by damp soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. ni tso lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii ni ekɛhaa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ eshishi lɛ Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ muji ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ helai ni shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when temperatures get too high or when the plant gets dry suddenly. Extreme heat prevents the flowers from pollinating properly, so the plant drops them to conserve its energy and water until conditions improve.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ egbi trukaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shiɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Curled, twisted pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or thrips feeding on the undersides of the leaves. As they suck out the plant juices, they cause damage and spread viruses that stunt leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mites loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa ni etse ehe lɛ baa. be mli ni ejieɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ Efiteɔ ni egbɛɔ helai ni tsiɔ baa lɛ naa lɛ eshwaa.

english: Why should I spread dry cut grass or leaves over the bare dirt around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ashwã shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering bare ground with dry grass acts like a protective blanket. It keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, stops moisture from evaporating too fast, suppresses weeds, and turns into rich organic soil food as it decays.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa hei ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ. tsiɔ jwɛi anaa ni ebafeɔ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii amli kɛji efite.

english: The first rain after a long dry season is often followed by a short dry spell that bakes the ground. If seeds sprout during that single wet day, the scorching dry dirt that follows can easily kill the young seedlings before regular rains begin.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ be kuku nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ gbi ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ nɔ Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni shãa ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ baanyɛ agbe tsei bibii dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ aba.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I plant them directly under full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot withstand harsh direct sun. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or bananas alongside them acts like a natural umbrella, keeping the seedlings cool and soil moist until the cocoa plants grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains loo banana, ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta Ha dumɔwui lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ baadara jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do I need to make high mounds of soil before planting my seed yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, deep, and well-drained soil to stretch out and grow big tubers. High mounds prevent water from clogging the roots and make it easier for the tubers to expand underground.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ haa nu tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa, ni ehaa ewaaa akɛ bulb lɛ baagbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my crops yield smaller fruits when I plant them very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Planting crops too close together forces them to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to weak stalks and smaller yields overall.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi yɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Should I start planting my seeds immediately after the very first rainy day of the season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui akwɛmɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to wait until the rainy season fully sets in after two or three good rains. The very first rain is often followed by a long dry spell that can dry out and destroy newly germinated seeds.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baashɛ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni baanyɛ agbi ni efite dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen or is holding too much water. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or improving soil drainage helps restore the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ehiɛɔ nu babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea tsu nii loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it beneficial to plant crops like cowpeas or beans alongside my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for your main crops while also covering the soil to block weed growth.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa otsei titrii lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, akwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni jwɛi akakwɛ̃.

english: Why are there small holes in my young maize leaves with powdery waste inside the center whorl?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ashikiŋsha bibii yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central funnel of the maize plant during the day, so applying approved control treatments early in the morning or late evening reaches them best.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, nibii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe fɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and shrinking in size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from young leaves, or a virus spread by these insects. Controlling these insects early prevents the damage from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni nɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ akagbɛ eshwa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress or uneven watering. Consistent soil moisture and protecting the soil with mulch help keep the soil cool so flowers can turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛbuɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔii lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: How can I tell if my cassava roots are mature enough to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is generally ready for harvest between 9 to 12 months after planting, which is usually indicated by the bottom leaves turning yellow and dropping off and cracks appearing in the ground around the main stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha nikpamɔ yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai lɛ ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kadiɔ enɛ. Ni ŋmeii je kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso wulu lɛ he lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient for leaf growth. When nitrogen is low, the plant starves its older bottom leaves to move available nutrients to the new growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baa lɛ dalɛ Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ yɛ shishigbɛ, baa ni egbɔ lɛ koni ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ aya baa heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my land make the soil richer for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family. They have natural microbes in their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans fata legume weku lɛ he. Amɛyɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi amli. ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food that feeds the underground tuber. Staking spreads the leaves out into the sun and off the damp soil, resulting in much larger tubers and fewer foliage diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Staking gbɛɔ baai lɛ eshwaa koni egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa yitsei lɛ feɔ wuji, ni helai ni jɛɔ tso lɛ mli baa lɛ hu faaa.

english: Why should I cut off most of the small suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Mitso titri lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Extra suckers steal food, water, and sunlight from the main plant. Pruning away all but one strong sucker directs energy back to the main stem so it can produce a bigger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Suckers ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Nine ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni afolɔ mli lɛ kudɔɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa tso lɛ tso titri lɛ nɔ, ja tso kome pɛ. Bɔni afee ni afee dumɔwui wuji ni tsii.

english: Why should I plant my cassava stem cuttings at a slant instead of pushing them straight down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi yucca tsei lɛ aniji lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni madu shi tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Planting cassava stems at a 45-degree angle encourages tubers to develop evenly along one side close to the soil surface, making them grow bigger and easier to harvest without breaking.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei tsei lɛ yɛ 45 degree angle mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdara pɛpɛɛpɛ. ekomefeemɔ yɛ fa kome ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaakpa ni akumɔɔɔ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains next to my newly planted young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense heat and direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees produce broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ haa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without producing fruit during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat dries up pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing proper pollination. When a flower fails to pollinate, the plant sheds it to save water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ agbi. Enɛ haaa amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee pollination jogbaŋŋ. Beni fɔfɔii lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee pollin lɛ Tsei lɛ baajie nu koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why does swamp rice grow well in standing water while my maize crop dies if water covers the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ swamp rice lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli shi wɔ ŋmãa lɛ gboɔ kɛji nu ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have tiny internal air channels inside their stems that carry oxygen down from the air to their roots under water. Maize lacks these channels, so its roots suffocate and rot in standing water.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii yɛ amɛmli. Eyɛ tso lɛ mli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. Abɛi bɛ gbɛi nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, eshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli.

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding on leaf sap, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early prevents leaf damage and fruit loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ kɛ aduawai lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting inside the ground if heavy rain floods the farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When water covers the roots for extended periods, air is cut off, causing root cells to die and allowing rot fungi in the water to destroy the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ nu ha shishifãi lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baafo. ehaa shishifãi lɛ gboiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nu lɛ mli koni efite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Officer, how is it possible for one single grain of maize to turn into a full cob with hundreds of grains later?
ga: Ofisa Te ebaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmãa ŋmãa kome pɛ atsɔ ŋmãa ŋmãa ni eyi obɔ? Ni sɛɛ mli lɛ, dumɔwui ohai abɔ ba?

english: One maize grain grows into a full plant with green leaves that act like food factories powered by sunlight. The plant flowers, gets pollinated by wind, and uses soil nutrients and water to multiply that original single grain into hundreds of new grains on the cob.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwu kome pɛ daa ni etsɔɔ tso ni yeɔ emuu ni baai eŋɔli yɔɔ mli ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii afeemɔ he ko ni hulu la haa hewalɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ haa tso lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ mli muji. ni ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛhaa shishijee dumɔwu kome lɛ shwereɔ ni etsɔɔ dumɔwui heei ohai abɔ yɛ ŋmei lɛ nɔ.

english: How can a small cassava stem cutting produce such huge and heavy tubers under the ground?
ga: Kasava tsei bibii ni afoɔ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni yitso agbo ni tsii tamɔ nɛkɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: The leaves of the cassava plant make extra food from sunlight and air during the growing season. The plant sends this food down to store in its root system, causing the underground roots to swell up into big, heavy tubers.
ga: Kasava baai lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ krokomɛi ni jɛɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Tso lɛ tsuɔ niyenii nɛɛ kɛyaa shi ni ekɛtoɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Officer, why does a single cocoa pod contain so many beans packed inside it?
ga: Ofisa Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ kome hiɛ kɔfi ŋmɔtɔi babaoo yɛ mli lɛ?
