english: Nature designs the cocoa pod as a protective shell that holds 30 to 50 seeds surrounded by sweet white pulp. The pod distributes water and nutrients evenly to all the seeds inside until they are fully grown and ready for harvest.
ga: Adebɔɔ fee kookoo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ koni efee ŋmɔtɔ ni buɔ mɔ he ni dumɔwui 30 kɛyashi 50 yɔɔ mli, ni loo yɛŋ ni ŋɔɔ ebɔle he. Pod lɛ jaa nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ehaa dumɔwui fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ daraa kwraa ni amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: How can a papaya plant with such a slender trunk hold dozens of heavy fruits without breaking?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni papaya tso ni eshishifã lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ nɛkɛ lɛ aaakpa aduawai nyɔŋmai abɔ ni ekuuu lɛ?

english: Papaya trunks are made of strong, flexible plant fibers designed to absorb and balance heavy weight. As long as the tree gets enough nutrients and water, its flexible trunk can safely support many heavy fruits stacked along it.
ga: Akɛ tsei ahe tsɔi ni mli wa ni nyɛɔ etsakeɔ lɛ feɔ papaya tsei lɛ. Afee amɛ koni amɛŋɔ muji ni tsii ni amɛto he gbɛjianɔ. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ baaná niyenii kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, Tso lɛ shishifã ni nyɛɔ efoɔ lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ aduawai babaoo ni tsii ni ato amɛhe lɛ anɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: If I put four or five maize seeds into one planting hole, will I get more harvest from my field?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii ejwɛ loo enumɔ wo dumɔ bu kome mli lɛ, Ani maná ŋmãa babaoo?

english: No, putting too many seeds in one hole causes the plants to fight each other for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Just like sharing a small bowl of food among too many people, each plant stays weak and produces very small cobs.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ he akaŋ, tamɔ bɔ ni niyenii ni akɛwoɔ tsɛnsi bibioo mli lɛ jaa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. kɛ gbɔmɛi babaoo fata he Tsei aŋkroaŋkroi bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: Why do many flowers drop off my tomato plants before turning into actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi dani ebafeɔ anɔkwa yibii lɛ?

english: A plant knows how much weight and fruit it can support based on available food and water. When weather is too hot or soil is dry, the plant drops excess flowers to save energy so it can focus on maturing only the few fruits it can handle.
ga: Tsei leɔ bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua kɛ amɛyibii babaoo yɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lɛ Tso lɛ baajie fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama aduawai fioo komɛi pɛ ni abaanyɛ akwɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Will planting my crops very close together help keep water trapped in the soil during dry times?
ga: Ani tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ baaye abua ni nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: No, crowded crops actually drain water from the soil much faster because too many roots are drinking from the same spot at once. Proper spacing ensures each plant has enough reserved moisture in its own soil area to survive dry spells.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu oya kwraa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi babaoo ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ he kome shikome lɛ yɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Officer, how can just a few tiny insects on my crop leaves suddenly turn into thousands within a few days?
ga: Ofisa, kooloi bibii fioo komɛi pɛ ni yɔɔ mi tsei lɛ ahe baa lɛ baatsɔ akpei abɔ. Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli?

english: Many small crop insects, like aphids, reproduce very quickly in warm weather and can give birth without waiting a long time to mature. A single female can produce dozens of young rapidly, leading to a huge population explosion in a short time.
ga: Tso mli kooloi bibii babaoo, tamɔ aphids lɛ fɔɔ oya waa yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ lɛ. ni ebaanyɛ efɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni emɛ be kakadaŋŋ dani eda Yoo kome pɛ baanyɛ afɔ́ bii babaoo oya. Enɛ haa gbɔmɛi babaoo ni fa babaoo lɛ shwereɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: Why do crops like cassava survive long dry spells while crops like maize dry up and die quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei tamɔ ŋmei hiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya.

english: Crops like cassava have deep root systems that act like deep underground water tanks, drawing moisture from far below the surface. Maize has shallower roots, so when the topsoil dries out, it cannot reach deeper water.
ga: Tsei tamɔ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ŋtayaai ni mli kwɔ. Egbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ shishi shɔŋŋ. Abɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã lɛ mli egbi No hewɔ lɛ enyɛŋ eshɛ nu ni mli kwɔ he.

english: How do I know if I am giving my vegetable crops enough water during the heat?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa miiha mitsei lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: You can check by digging a small hole about a finger's depth near your plant. If the soil at that depth feels damp and sticks together when squeezed, your plant has enough water in its root zone.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ kɛtsɔ bu bibioo ko ni oootse lɛ nɔ. Aaafee inchi kome ni bɛŋkɛ otso lɛ he. Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nakai mli lɛ nuɔ he akɛ edɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ he kɛji akɛ ashɛre lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do experienced farmers recommend planting plantain suckers next to my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ mi kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly and produce broad leaves that create living shade to protect tender cocoa seedlings from the heat, while also giving you food and extra income while waiting for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ latsaa he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika kroko yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with tiny cobs when I put four or five seeds into a single planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni mikɛ dumɔwui ejwɛ loo enumɔ woɔ dumɔ bu kome mli lɛ

english: When too many seeds are planted together, the roots compete aggressively for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Planting only one or two seeds per hole with proper spacing allows each maize stalk to get enough nutrients to grow strong and produce large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ he kome lɛ Shishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli. Dumɔwu kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni aduɔ yɛ bu kome mli ni gbɛ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmãa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ewo ŋmãa wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do small holes appear on my young maize leaves with small caterpillars hiding inside the center leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni Ehiɛ amɛhe yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on the growing tip of young maize plants. Detecting them early and applying appropriate control methods—such as neem extract or recommended sprays—prevents them from destroying your yield.
ga: Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni miida lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. mra ni akɛ gbɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ he tamɔ neem mli nu loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii. Ebaaye ebua ni akafite nibii ni oduɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn completely black and dry up on the branches during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ kwraa ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in cold, damp, and shaded conditions. Clearing weeds, pruning extra tree branches to let in sunlight, and removing infected pods quickly helps prevent the disease from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni edɔ, kɛ hulutsoo. weeding Nibii krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi koni hulu la lɛ abote mli Ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ haaa hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants curling upwards and shrinking into small clusters?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii bibii lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or mites feeding on the leaf sap. Spraying early with a light neem oil mixture or recommended insecticide gets rid of the insects and allows healthy new leaves to unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ baagbe kooloi lɛ ni eye ebua ni baai heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do I need to erect tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mato tso kakadaŋŋ ko kɛha mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ koni makwɔ nɔ beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food for the underground tubers. Lifting the leaves off the ground with stakes increases sunlight exposure, improves air circulation, prevents soil-borne fungal diseases, and results in much larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ wo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ. ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ Tsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa Ni nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bafee wuji babaoo.

english: Why are the bright yellow flowers on my tomato plants dropping off without making any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when watering is uneven, or when there is excessive nitrogen in the soil. Maintaining consistent moisture in the soil and avoiding high-nitrogen fertilizers during flowering helps the blossoms stay attached and form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ejaaa loo kɛji nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛmaa shi yɛ tomato mli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow and dropping off during the dry period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally sheds its lower leaves during dry conditions to reduce water loss and conserve energy for its underground roots. Adding organic matter or compost to the soil helps hold moisture longer and keeps the foliage healthier.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ eshishi baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛba nu ni fiteɔ lɛ shi ni ekɛ hewalɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata sũ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ, ni ebaaha baai lɛ aná hewalɛ kpakpa.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my vegetable plants with dry grass or dry cocoa leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Aduawai ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo kookoo baai ni egbi ewo mli.

english: Covering the soil with organic material is called mulching. It keeps the ground cool under hot sun, traps moisture so you water less often, stops weed seeds from sprouting, and slowly rots to feed the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli fioo Etsiɔ jwɛi dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛfite fiofio koni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become soft and rot inside the ground when the farm stays flooded with rainwater?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nu ho ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When water sits on the field for days, the roots drown and rot; growing cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away and keeps the tubers safe.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ nu lɛ hi ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbaagboi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Should I throw away small seed yams or can I plant them in my farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ ashwie? Aloo esa akɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You do not need to look down on small seed yams. The size of the seed yam at planting time does not determine your final yield; what matters most is the internal strength and health of the seed.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa ni okwɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ akɛ nɔ ko ni he ehiaaa. Bɔ ni o-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ dara ha yɛ be mli ni oduɔ lɛ etsɔɔɔ naagbee yibiiwoo ni obaaná. Nɔ ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ ji dumɔwu lɛ hewalɛ kɛ emli hewalɛnamɔ lɛ.

english: Does planting a small seed yam mean my harvest will also be small?
ga: Ani dumɔwui bibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hu baafee bibioo?

english: No, a small seed yam will not automatically produce a small tuber. If the seed is healthy and comes from strong parent stock, it can grow into a large, heavy yam at harvest.
ga: Dabi, sweet potatoes ni ji dumɔwui bibii lɛ efeŋ ŋmeii bibii amɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛlɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmeii agboi ni tsii kɛji akpa amɛ.

english: Is it necessary to buy very large yams to use as seed for a good yield?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni ahe ŋmeii ni dara waa ni akɛtsu nii akɛ dumɔwui koni aná yibii kpakpai?

english: No, you do not need big yams for seed. Huge tubers are not required because smaller ones carry the same genetic strength needed to produce a good crop, saving you cost and planting material.
ga: Dabi, sweet potato agbo he ehiaaa bo kɛha dumɔwui. Bulb agbo he ehiaaa ejaakɛ bulb bibii lɛ yɛ hewalɛ fe tsutsu lɛ. ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai afeemɔ Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akɛ shika kɛ nibii ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ toɔ.

english: How can I tell if a seed yam is good if I cannot judge it by its size?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ hi loo ehiii? Kɛji minyɛɛɛ makojo kɛtsɔ elɛɛmɔ nɔ

english: Instead of judging by size, look at the health of the seed yam. A good seed yam comes from a vigorous plant line that has been consistently harvested and replanted without internal rot or disease.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni wɔɔkojo kɛtsɔ dalɛ nɔ lɛ Ha wɔkwɛ bɔ ni sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ ahewalɛ yɔɔ ha. Sweet potato dumɔwui kpakpai jɛɔ tsei srɔtoi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akpaa amɛ be fɛɛ be ni aduɔ amɛ ekoŋŋ ni mligbɛ fitemɔ loo hela bɛ mli lɛ amli.

english: If my seed yam has a disease inside it, can I cure it before planting?
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hela Ani abaanyɛ atsa lɛ dani adu?

english: It is very difficult to cure or remove a disease once it is inside the crop material. It is better to avoid planting infected seed yams altogether because the disease will persist in the new plant.
ga: Ewa waa akɛ abaatsa hela lɛ loo ajie lɛ kɛji ebote dumɔwui lɛ amli pɛ. Esa akɛ ajie ŋmeii ni dumɔwui ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ adumɔ yɛ be kome mli ejaakɛ hela lɛ baakã he ahi tsei heei anɔ.

english: Why do my yams keep getting the same disease season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potatoes lɛ náa hela kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Diseases often remain hidden inside the seed yams you save from previous harvests. When you replant infected tubers year after year, you carry the disease directly into your new farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai kɛ amɛhe woɔ sweet potato dumɔwui ni okɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ amli. Kɛji odu bulbs ni hela emɔ amɛ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, Okɛ hela baaba oŋmɔ hee lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Does harvesting yams and replanting them every year make the crop weaker over time?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa ni aduɔ ehee daa afi lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbɔjɔ yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: No, the continuous cycle of carefully harvesting with your tools and replanting healthy stock year after year actually helps maintain and build the crop's growing vigor.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ odɛŋdadei tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni okɛduɔ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa diɛŋtsɛ ni ekwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ ni etswaa amɛhe hewalɛ.

english: Where does a yam crop get its strength to grow well year after year?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni sweet potato tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi?

english: A yam's strength builds over time through a continuous cycle of good care—harvesting healthy tubers and replanting them season after season maintains the crop's vitality.
ga: Bɔ ni sweet potatoes lɛ wa ha lɛ maa shi yɛ be kɛ bei amli kɛtsɔ kwɛmɔ kpakpa ni yaa nɔ lɛ nɔ. Bulbs ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akpaa kɛ eheei ni aduɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I keep saving seed yams from my own harvest to replant next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ sweet potato dumɔwui ni jɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, you can continuously harvest and replant your own seed stock. As long as you select clean, disease-free tubers, this repeated planting cycle keeps your crop line performing well.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okpa bo diɛŋtsɛ odumɔwui lɛ ni okɛdu ekoŋŋ be fɛɛ be. Shii abɔ ni obaahala ŋmeii ni he tse ni hela bɛ mli lɛ. sɛɛkuu ni aduɔ shii abɔ Enɛ baaye abua ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can using iron tools during harvest damage the quality of my seed yams for next year?
ga: Ani dade nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ afite afi ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Using tools to harvest is standard practice, but you must take care not to cut or wound the seed yams, as injuries make it easier for diseases to enter and destroy the inner strength of the tuber.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛkpaa nii lɛ ji nifeemɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ. Shi esa akɛ okwɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okafo loo okapila sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, pilamɔ haa hela boteɔ mli oya ni efiteɔ sweet potato tuber lɛ mli hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow roots that dry out easily under direct sunlight. Planting shade trees or plantains nearby creates a cooler canopy that protects the young seedlings until they grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛgbiɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa ŋwɛi ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ dumɔwui bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient for healthy growth. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help the leaves turn green and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ kpakpa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ni eha dalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Can I use decayed animal manure instead of buying chemical fertilizer from the town?
ga: Ani obaanyɛ okɛ kooloi ashishifãi ni egbo atsu nii moŋ fe ni ooohe tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, well-rotted animal manure adds valuable nutrients to the soil and helps it hold water better during dry periods. Unlike raw chemical fertilizers, proper manure feeds the soil over a longer time without burning crop roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Esoro ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe yɛ gbɛ ni ji akɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii be kakadaŋŋ ni eshãaa tsei shishifãi.

english: What causes small holes in my maize leaves and stops the plants from growing well?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai anɔ ni ehaa ŋmãa tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the leaves and growing points. Checking your field early and using approved treatments or organic neem extracts can stop them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ Fall Armyworm tsɛŋemɔ helai, ni yeɔ nii yɛ baai amli kɛ hei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo neem mli nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ amɛnaa dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my tomatoes develop black spots at the bottom and rot before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔlɔi diji ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, which happens when the plants do not get enough calcium or when soil moisture fluctuates too much. Keeping the soil consistently moist and adding organic matter or lime helps prevent it.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ tsɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ daa ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo lime fata he lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Select mature, healthy stems from plants that show no signs of disease or pest damage. Cut pieces from the middle portion of the stem rather than the soft top or woody base, as middle cuttings sprout stronger roots.
ga: Halamɔ tso ni eda, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ tso ko ni ejieee hela loo tsɛŋemɔ hela he okadi kpo lɛ mli. Kpɔ̃ɔ mli bibii kɛjɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofolɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ashishi Ejaakɛ tso nine ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: Yams need soft, loose earth to expand easily into big, smooth tubers. Heaping the soil into mounds also improves water drainage so the buried seed yams do not rot during heavy rains.
ga: Sweet potatoes hia shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni ekwɛ̃ oya ni etsɔ bulbs agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akɛaawo gɔji amli lɛ hu haa nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ni afu lɛ fiteee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Which plantain sucker is best for me to plant in my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ plantain sucker hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ makwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Sword suckers—which have narrow, spear-like leaves and a broad base—are the best choice because they have strong energy reserves, grow quickly, and yield large, healthy bunches.
ga: Klante ni akɛmuɔ nii ni ŋmeii lɛ mli tse ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ, ni eshishigbɛ lɛ mli kwɔ. Eji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni fa babaoo ni eyɔɔ lɛ hewɔ. shwere oya ni eha kuu lɛ afee agbo ni ehe wa

english: How do I know it is the right time to plant my seeds when the rains begin?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eji be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: It is best to wait until the ground stays consistently wet for a few days after rain begins, rather than planting after the very first shower. Planting too early in dry soil can scorch the seeds if the rains pause.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbii fioo komɛi yɛ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Mohu ɔ, mo du lɛ ngɛ kekleekle nu ɔ se. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ oya tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ ashã kɛji akɛ akpa nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo ko.

english: Weeds grow fast and steal water, sunlight, and soil food away from young crop plants. Removing weeds early allows your crops to establish strong roots and leaves without fighting for survival.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni jɛɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ye obua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛná shishifãi kɛ baai ni mli wa ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛwuu koni amɛhi shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves. It can also happen when too much rain stays in the soil and chokes the roots, preventing them from feeding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ nɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha shishifãi lɛ shwie shi. tsi niyenii ni ayeɔ lɛ naa

english: Tomatoes shed their flowers when they get too stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering. When the plant feels thirsty or overheated, it drops flowers to save energy to survive.
ga: Tomatoi baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ miihao amɛ tsɔ. Kɛ tso lɛ nu kumai he loo edɔ tsɔ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛhi shi lɛ ato.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting just two days after I dig them out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ bɔi fitemɔ beni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Unlike Yams, fresh cassava roots do not have a protective outer skin once harvested. Air and tiny microbes enter the root immediately through small cracks, causing fast spoilage if not processed or eaten quickly.
ga: Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ sweet potato lɛ, cassava shishifãi heei bɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni buɔ amɛhe kɛji akpa. Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli Eboteɔ shishifãi lɛ amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli. Enɛ haa efiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii loo ayeee oya.

english: What is eating holes into the middle leaves of my maize overnight?
ga: Mɛni ye bu ko ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide deep inside the center of the maize stem during the hot day and come out at night to eat the tender leaf leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni amɛje kpo amɛbaye baai bibii gbɛkɛ

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips hiding underneath the leaves and sucking out the juices, or by a virus carried into the plant by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii, tamɔ aphids loo thrips, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ nu lɛ kɛbaa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛyaa tsei amli lɛ nɔ

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds around my young crops early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji ni bɔle mitsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are very aggressive and grow faster than crops. They steal the fertilizer, soil water, and sunlight that your young crops need to grow big and strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ feɔ basabasa ni amɛdaraa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii. Amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei bibii lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe awa lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch maximum sunshine. Keeping leaves lifted off the damp ground prevents leaf diseases and helps the plant send more energy down to make large tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ baai helai anaa, ni ehaa tso lɛ kudɔɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛfee ŋmɔtɔi wuji babaoo.

english: Why shouldn't I spread fertilizer on my field right before a heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall will wash the fertilizer off your field into drains and streams before your crop roots can absorb it, wasting your money and leaving crops hungry.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔji amli lɛ amli kɛyaa nu tsɔji kɛ faai amli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Efiteɔ shika ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ hɔmɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small bunches when I leave many shoots growing around one plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ fãa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni mishiɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ tso kome he lɛ.

english: All the small shoots (suckers) compete with the mother plant for food and water in the soil. Cutting away extra suckers leaves all the food for the main stem to produce a heavy bunch.
ga: Tso bibii lɛ fɛɛ (tso lɛ) kɛ tso nyɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ niyenii fɛɛ kɛhaa tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ koni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Young cocoa plants are delicate and burn under direct sunlight. They need shade from larger trees or plantains to protect them from heat until their roots grow deep enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo plantains amli koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli baawo shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: What basic costs should I expect when starting a new crop farm for the first time?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee shika esa akɛ makpa gbɛ beni mijeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii hee shishi klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: When starting a new farm, your main establishment costs will include clearing and preparing the land, buying seeds or suckers, purchasing initial fertilizers, and paying for labor to plant everything properly.
ga: Kɛji oje ŋmɔ hee shishi Oshishitoo he nyɔmɔwoo titri lɛ baafee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajieɔ kɛ ehe saamɔ. Tso dumɔwui loo tsei ashishifãi ahemɔ Shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii ahemɔ kɛ nyɔmɔwoo ni sa kɛha nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Why do I need to keep spending money on my farm every week after planting is already done?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafite shika yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa otsi beni midu nii sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops need continuous care throughout their growing cycle to stay healthy and yield well. Ongoing maintenance costs cover weeding, applying protective spray against pests, adding top-dressing fertilizers, and paying workers to manage the farm.
ga: Tsei biɔ ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be yɛ amɛdalɛ be fɛɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ kpakpa ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai. Saamɔ he nyɔmɔwoo ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa jwɛi akudɔmɔ. Nibii ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii Akɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni akɛsaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ mli ni awoɔ nitsulɔi nyɔmɔ koni amɛkwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I test a small piece of land with a new crop before planting my whole farm with it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka he bibioo ko makwɛ? Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei dani adu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ hu?

english: Running a small trial plot helps you see how well the crop grows in your specific soil and local climate. It allows you to learn the maintenance demands and true costs without risking all your money at once.
ga: Kaa he gbɛjianɔtoo bibioo ko ni ooofee Ebaaye ebua bo ni ona bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ oshikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ kɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okaseɔ anɔkwa nibii ni he hiaa kɛha tsɔne lɛ saamɔ kɛ shika ni he hiaa bo ni okɛ oshika fɛɛ wooo oshara mli shikome.

english: How long does a crop cycle usually take from planting day until harvest time?
ga: Be enyiɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aheɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔ mli kɛyashiɔ ŋmaakpamɔ mli?

english: Every crop has its own unique lifespan; quick crops like maize take 3 to 4 months, while semi-perennials like plantains or cassava take between 9 to 12 months to complete their full cycle and yield harvestable food.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fɛɛ yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala be ni yɔɔ srɔto. Nibii ni aduɔ oya tamɔ abele heɔ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4, yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ afii fã tamɔ plantains loo cassava. Eheɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani egbeɔ sɛɛkuu lɛ naa ni ehaa niyenii ni abaanyɛ akpa.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my seeds when the rainy season begins in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ aje dumɔwui ashishi beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: You should wait until the rains are steady and the soil is moist several inches deep for about two weeks, rather than planting after the very first light shower which might dry up quickly.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ aba shi ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛyashɛ inchii babaoo aaafee otsii enyɔ. Mohu ɔ, du ngɛ kekleekle nugbɔ nɛ ma nyɛ maa gbi oya ɔ se.

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil, or the ground is flooded with excess rain water, which stops the roots from breathing and absorbing food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. aloo nugbɔ nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii.

english: Why do flowers drop off my pepper plants without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers usually drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, prolonged dry soil conditions, or a lack of beneficial insects like bees to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi be kakadaŋŋ. aloo kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii ni baaha fɔfɔii lɛ afee ŋmeii lɛ ni bɛ

english: Why do weeds make my main crops grow slowly and look weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mitso titri lɛ daa blɛoo ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal essential plant food, water, and sunlight directly from your crops. Because weeds grow aggressively, they starve your crops of the nourishment needed for strong growth.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ tsei aniyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ daa oya No hewɔ lɛ Amɛjieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa bo koni ekwɛ̃ waa lɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has enough plant food to support a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ tsei ahe nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmaa kpakpa?

english: Fertile soil is usually dark in color, holds moisture well without staying muddy, soft to dig, and rich in decomposing plant matter, whereas dry, compact, or very sandy soil usually needs added compost or fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ su feɔ ediŋŋ. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ muji efeee. Tsɔɔmɔ blɛoo ni tsei ni fiteɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi Bei pii lɛ, hei ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋã lɛ biɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he.

english: Can I plant two different crops together in the same field, or will they fight each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ tsei enyɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli? Aloo amɛbaawuu yɛ amɛteŋ?

english: You can plant certain crops together if they complement each other, like planting legumes with maize. Legumes trap nitrogen in the soil, which actually feeds and supports the neighboring grain crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi afee ekome kɛji tsei enyɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛhe, tamɔ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ. Legumes lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni no diɛŋtsɛ haa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow green leaves. Adding fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help restore the green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha amɛdaramɔ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my crops yield less every year even though I keep planting on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same plot every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil. Rotating your crop with beans or groundnuts helps put nutrients back into the dirt and lets the soil recover.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehaa ehe feɔ fɛo.

english: How does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass help them grow during the dry season?
ga: Te jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Dry grass acts like a protective blanket called mulch. It keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, prevents water from evaporating quickly from the roots, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Hay tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekajɛ shishifãi lɛ amli oya. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I plant my seeds very close to each other?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa?

english: No, planting seeds too close together forces the plants to fight with each other for light, water, and food from the soil. Spacing them out properly allows each plant to grow tall, strong, and produce a larger yield.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso daa, ewaa ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Leaving too many small shoots forces the main plantain tree to share its food with all of them. Keeping only one or two strong suckers ensures the mother tree leaves enough strength to produce a huge plantain bunch.
ga: ŋmeii bibii ni ajieɔ lɛ babaoo lɛ baaha dumɔwu titri lɛ aja niyenii yɛ amɛ fɛɛ ateŋ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hi shi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee plantains akui wuji.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when there is too much sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under full sun. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees above them to protect them until their roots grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantain loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei ni buɔ amɛhe kɛyashiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Weeds are fast growers that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your main crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to grow well.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii titrii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is eating the center leaves of my young maize plants and leaving small holes everywhere?
ga: Mɛni ji mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ni ayeɔ ni ashiɔ bu bibii? Ani eyi he fɛɛ he?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the fall armyworm that hide inside the growing whorl of the plant. Spraying approved insecticides or applying neem leaves mixture early can control them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ cutworms ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tsei ni miida lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra loo neem baa ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Abaanyɛ akudɔ lɛ dani efite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are mature and ready to be dug up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakumɔ?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil right around the main stem starts to swell and crack open from the growing tubers underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso titri lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ ni efoɔ kɛjɛɔ bulb ni miida yɛ eshishi lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato stems turn black and the fruits rot when heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni aduawai lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Too much dampness from heavy rain encourages fungal diseases to spread on tomato plants. Making raised soil beds for good water drainage and pruning lower leaves helps air circulate and keeps the plants healthy.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tomato tsei lɛ anɔ. Saa ni awo nɔ ni afee koni nu atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to build green leaves and grow big cobs. Adding well-rotted animal manure or NPK fertilizer gives the soil the boost it needs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ ŋmeii wuji. Koolooi amli ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo NPK ŋmeii ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ taoɔ nibii babaoo.

english: Why does my farm soil dry out and crack so quickly during the sun season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egbɛɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses water fast when direct heat hits it. Covering the soil around your crops with dried grass or leftover crop leaves (mulching) acts like a blanket, keeping the ground cool and trapping moisture.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ fiteɔ nu oya kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ mli. Mulching ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo tso baai ni eshwɛ (mulching) baabɔle Oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Cassava roots rot when too much water sits around them in heavy soil. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo ebɔle amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: What causes my yams to grow thin and crooked instead of large and smooth?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ebɔleɔ ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee agbo ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Yam tubers grow crooked when the soil underneath them is packed too hard or full of rocks. Making soft, deep soil mounds without stones gives the yam tuber space to expand easily.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baakɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ. Kɛ́ afee gɔŋ ko ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni tɛi bɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo.

english: Curled leaves on tomatoes are usually caused by a virus spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. Controlling these insects using organic neem oil sprays or recommended treatments keeps the leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii yɛŋ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Kɛ́ akɛ organic neem oil spray loo tsofai krokomɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ tsu nii kɛye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do tiny insects eat holes in my cowpea pods while they are still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-cowpea ŋmɔji lɛ amli be mli ni amɛdaraa lolo lɛ?

english: Pod-boring insects target tender, sweet young pods to feed their young. Spraying your crop with natural neem extract or approved pesticides right when flowering starts keeps the insects from destroying the pods.
ga: Kplukai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ kwɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋɔɔ lɛ nɔ koni amɛha amɛbii lɛ niyenii. Okɛ adebɔɔ mli neem mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ afɔ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji amɛje fɔfɔii afeemɔ shishi pɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni kooloi akafite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so fast even after I clear my field completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya nɛkɛ beni mijie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ po lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit deep in the dirt and sprout the moment rain and direct sunlight hit them. Planting cover crops like cowpea or using mulch blocks sunlight from reaching the dirt, which stops weed seeds from growing.
ga: Afuɔ jwɛi dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ ni hulu la tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ loo ŋmei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baatsi hulu la naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baatsi jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from harsh heat, lack of water, or attacks from sap-sucking insects like capsids. Providing shade trees and protecting the flowers from bugs helps the tree set pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ capsids lɛ tutua amɛ. Kɛ́ afee fɔfɔi lɛ ahe hulutsoo ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ eshishifãi lɛ toɔ.

english: Plantain roots do not grow very deep, so heavy bunches make the tree top-heavy. Supporting the trunk with sturdy bamboo or wooden poles (staking) prevents the wind from pushing the tree over.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ni tsii waa lɛ baaha tso lɛ yiteŋ afee shwiili. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tsei ni wa (tsei) fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ akatsi tso lɛ shi.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they get too hot without enough water, or if they receive too much leaf-growing fertilizer. Water them regularly during dry spells to help the flowers turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji edɔ tsɔ ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Aloo kɛji onine shɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ kɛha baai ni miida lɛ. Okɛ nu awo mli daa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the center outward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ kɛmiiya kponɔgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow leaves. Adding organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛbaakwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans on a plot after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmei?

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil, but crops like beans and groundnuts take plant food from the air and put it back into the earth. Planting them after maize naturally refreshes the soil for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, shi nakai nɔŋŋ eji yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei hu he. Gbalamɔ niyenii kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ amli ni okɛku sɛɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni ooodu yɛ abele sɛɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does covering the bare dirt around my crops with dry grass help them grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mikɛ jwɛi duɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara lɛ.

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves or grass acts like a blanket that keeps the hot sun from drying out the earth, holding moisture in the soil longer so your crops don't get thirsty quickly.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛhaa hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kumai yeee oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ oya tamɔ bɔ ni eji lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow small and weak when I plant seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too tightly together, the growing plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water underground. Spacing them correctly gives each plant enough space and food to grow big.
ga: Beni adu dumɔwui lɛ babaoo tsɔ lɛ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu mli. Kɛ́ akɛto he ni sa lɛ, ebaaha tso fɛɛ tso aná he ko kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni etsɔ agbo.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my seeds after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: You should wait to plant until the soil has received two or three good, heavy rains that soak deep into the earth, ensuring the soil stays moist enough for the seeds to sprout without drying up.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ ni odu nii kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔshiimɔi kpakpai enyɔ loo etɛ ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kwɛmɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees die if I clear away all the big trees on my farm land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are delicate and burn easily under the harsh direct sun. Keeping big trees gives them the soft shade and cool air they need to survive their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni eda lɛ akwɛmɔ haa amɛnáa hulutsoo ni mli jɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy, and when rainwater sits around them without draining, the roots drown and rot. Planting cassava on top of raised mounds helps excess water flow away.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ kpakpa. Ni kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ebɔle shishifãi ahe ni nu shwieee lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwie nu mli ni amɛgboi. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce fewer and smaller fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo yibii fioo ni amɛmiifee bibii lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal food, water, and sunlight away from your main crops. Clearing weeds early ensures all the goodness in the soil goes directly into your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa nibii kpakpai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes through the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu kɛmiitsɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These insects feed on tender young leaves to grow fast, which damages the plant's ability to catch sunlight. Checking your field early and putting ash or safe organic remedies into the leaf centers can stop them.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ baai bibii koni amɛdara oya. ni fiteɔ nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛnáa hulu la lɛ He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni sũ loo nibii krokomɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ baanyɛ akpa amɛ.

english: Why is it beneficial to pinch off some of the tiny side branches on my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ aaamɔ tsei niji bibii lɛ? Ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ tomato tsei anɔ.

english: Removing extra side branches prevents the tomato plant from wasting its energy on useless leaves, forcing the plant to direct its water and nutrients into making bigger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ afã lɛ ni ooojie lɛ baatsi o-tomato tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tomato tsei lɛ akudɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of the plant usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to grow green and strong. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore the soil nutrients so the leaves stay healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba koni baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops yield less when I plant the exact same crop on the same land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that crop needs and allows targeted pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Alternating your crop with beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility and breaks the pest cycle.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ehiɛ fɔɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni ebua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni ebaaku tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ amli.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops sunlight from drying out the ground too quickly, keeps the soil cool, prevents weeds from taking over, and slowly turns into organic plant food as it rots.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi hulu lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni ekaye nɔ ni fiofio lɛ etsɔɔ tsei aniyenii ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli be mli ni egboɔ lɛ.

english: Why are worms eating into the stalks of my maize and making the leaves look ragged?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii miiye mi ŋmãa toi lɛ ni amɛmiiha baai lɛ miifee tamɔ nɔ ni etse lɛ?

english: These are stem borer caterpillars, which hatch from eggs laid by moths inside the plant. Clearing away old crop leaves after harvest and applying neem leaf extract or appropriate pest controls early in the season prevents them from multiplying.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji stem borers ni fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii woɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ amli. Ni ajieɔ tso baai momoi lɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Ni akɛ neem baa mli nu loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni sa baatsu nii yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ baaye abua ni akafee babaoo.

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck the juice from leaves and pass along viruses. Spraying plants early with mild soapy water or neem oil deters these insects and keeps the leaves expanding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai amli ni ekɛ helai baa tsei anɔ kɛ nu ni mli ejɔ loo neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa ni eha baai lɛ mli alɛɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot and smell bad inside the ground before harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani akpaa?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil retains too much water for a long time, causing fungal diseases to attack the tubers. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows extra rainfall to drain away, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo be kakadaŋŋ. Ehaa fungal hela tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo. Ha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate roots and cannot survive intense direct sunlight and heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain or cassava beside them creates shade and holds soil moisture to protect them until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains loo cassava lɛ yɛ amɛhe lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo baa ni ehaa sũ mli nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ koni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their blossoms without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when they suffer from sudden heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of phosphorus in the soil. Maintaining steady moisture and shielding young plants from harsh weather encourages the flowers to set fruit.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna trukaa hulutsoo he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo fɔsfɔs ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Fɛ̃i ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ tsei bibii ahebuu kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai ahe lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛwo yibii.

english: What will happen if I plant my maize seeds very close to one another?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in tall, weak stems and very small cobs. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow large cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmeii bibii waa yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji baakwɛ̃.

english: Why do some of my planted yam setts fail to sprout and instead decay in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni midu lɛ ekomɛi edaaa ni amɛgbooo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Yam setts fail to sprout if they are infected by soil fungi or attacked by beetles before growing, or if the soil is too hot and dry. Treating the cut seed pieces with wood ash or protective powders before planting shields them until shoots form.
ga: Set sweet potatoes nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ emɔ amɛ loo ladybugs tutua amɛ dani adu. aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni egbi Kɛ́ akɛ tso sũ loo powda ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ tsu dumɔwui ni afo lɛ ahe nii dani adu lɛ, ebaaha nɔ ko abu he kɛyashi ŋmeii baaje shishi.

english: What is the difference between growing my vegetables under a net structure and growing them out in the open field?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ mi-aduawai ni miduɔ yɛ ŋtayaa shishi kɛ ŋmɔ mli ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ teŋ?

english: A net structure acts as a shield against hot sun, heavy rain, and pests, keeping the air around the plants cooler and more humid so vegetables stay healthy, grow faster, and produce better yields than in the open field.
ga: Mesh lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni tsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle he lɛ akaboteɔ mli. Tsei lɛ amli ejɔ ni amɛhe hu edɔ waa. Bɔni afee ni aduawai aná hewalɛ kpakpa lɛ, amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai fe ŋmɔji amli.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings dry out and die so quickly during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young plants have shallow roots and tender leaves that lose water rapidly under intense direct sunlight; shade coverings or nets help reduce heat stress and keep soil moisture from evaporating too fast.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Shading loo netting haa dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning pale green and yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed to build green leaves and grow strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hia koni afee baai eŋɔli ni akwɛ̃ tsei ni wa.

english: How can I tell if my tomato plants are getting too much water or not enough water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo amɛmiiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: Plants needing water will wilt, dry up, and turn brittle, while plants getting too much water will turn yellow, feel soft and limp, and drop their leaves because their roots are drowning in soggy soil.
ga: Tsei ni nu he hiaa amɛ lɛ baagboi, amɛbaagbi, ni amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, yɛ be mli ni tsei ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo ni egbɔjɔ ni baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ afu shishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cabbage plants stretch out long with loose leaves instead of forming a hard, tight head?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai ni etsilɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ yitso ni wa ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cabbages react to extreme heat by trying to flower quickly, causing them to grow tall and leafy rather than wrapping their leaves into a tight head as they do in cooler conditions.
ga: Cabbage tsuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he nii kɛtsɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ebɔɔ koni efɔ̃ oya lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa cabbage lɛ daa ni ehiɛɔ baai, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekɛ baai lɛ abɔ he shiŋŋ tamɔ yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli ejɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why do tiny insects cause my pepper plant leaves to curl up and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii haa mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Small insects like aphids suck the vital sap from young leaves and introduce plant viruses, causing leaves to twist, stunt, and lose their ability to make food for the plant.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ aphids lɛ nuɔ nu ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ baai bibii amli ni amɛhiɛɔ tso mli helai, ni no haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee niyenii amɛha tso lɛ dɔŋŋ.

english: How does covering my crop nursery with a fine mesh netting protect seedlings without using chemicals?
ga: Te ŋshɔŋloo kpakpa ni akɛhaa mi-nursery lɛ baanyɛ abu midumɔwui lɛ ahe ni akɛ tsofai tsuuu nii lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Fine mesh netting creates a physical barrier that prevents pests from landing on plants to feed or lay eggs, blocking insect damage naturally without needing spray chemicals.
ga: Mesh netting ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ feɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii ko ni tsiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafata tso lɛ he koni amɛye niyenii loo amɛwo ŋmeii. Adebɔɔ mli hebuu kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ahe ni tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: What will happen to my crop yield if I plant my seeds very close together to fit more in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni amɛbote he ni miyɔɔ lɛ mli babaoo?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete for limited sunlight, air, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in thin, weak plants that produce smaller fruits and spread diseases easily.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. kɛ nu fioo Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii bibii ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ baa.

english: Why do my garden egg plants grow tall and thin with very few fruits when planted under shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛji akɛ akwɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Fruiting crops need full, direct sunlight to produce the energy required for heavy flowering and fruiting; deep shade forces them to grow tall towards the light instead of producing fruits.
ga: Tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa kɛha fɔfɔi kɛ yibii babaoo. Shade ni mli kwɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛdara kɛyashɛ la lɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do big buyers and hotels pay higher prices for tomatoes that are smooth and uniform in size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nihɔɔlɔi wuji kɛ gbɔiatoohei woɔ tomato ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni dalɛ tamɔ amɛhe lɛ jara babaoo lɛ?

english: Commercial buyers pay top prices for clean, uniform produce because it reduces food waste, lasts longer in storage, looks attractive to customers, and is easier to process in large kitchens.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jarayeli mli lɛ woɔ jara babaoo kɛha nibii ni he tse, ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ. Ejaakɛ ehaa niyenii ni afiteɔ lɛ baa shi Ha ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ Ehaa mɛi ni baahe nii lɛ nyaa he, ni eyɛ mlɛo akɛ aaatsu he nii yɛ shĩa agbo mli

english: Should I plant my maize right after the very first rain of the season or wait a bit?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ loo esa akɛ mamɛ?

english: It is safer to wait for two or three steady rains so the soil holds enough moisture. Planting after just one early rain can cause seeds to sprout and then die if the rains stop for a few weeks.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ kpa otsii fioo komɛi.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I plant my crops closer together so I can fit more plants on my land?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe bɔni afee ni manyɛ makwɛ tsei babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting too close makes crops compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to feed and produce larger, healthier fruit or grains.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ niyenii ni ewoɔ aduawai loo ŋmaa ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving the young cocoa shade and keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha kookoo ŋmɔlɔ ni mli tse ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When you plant maize in that same soil later, it uses that stored nitrogen as free plant food to grow stronger.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ sɛɛ mli lɛ odu ŋmãa yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa kɛ nitrogen ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ tso niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko koni ekwɛ̃ waa.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Lifting the vines on stakes helps the leaves catch more sun and protects the plant from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo. ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛbaa lɛ ahe

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the bottom leaves start turning yellow and dropping off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant is short on nitrogen. The maize plant takes nitrogen from its older leaves at the bottom and sends it to the growing leaves and corn ears at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Abɛi tsei lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli ni amɛkɛyaa abɛi baai kɛ toi ni miida ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ amli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil switches suddenly from very dry to very wet, which stresses the plant and prevents flower pollination.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually a sign that tiny sap-sucking pests like aphids or thrips are hiding on the underside of the leaves, or that a virus has infected the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ aphids loo thrips, kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi. aloo hela ko ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli

english: Why do weeds slow down my crops' growth even if the crops are much taller than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ fioo lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ kwɔ kwraa fe jwɛi lɛ moŋ.

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems under the ground that steal water and fertilizer before your crop's roots can reach them, starving your crop even if it looks taller.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛkwɔ moŋ.

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape starting from the tip, the plant is signaling that it lacks nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen feeds leaf growth, so when soil nutrients are low, the plant pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new top leaves.
ga: Beni ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ eshishigbɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni haa baa lɛ daa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ amli koni amɛkɛya ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ amli.

english: Why are many of my harvested groundnut shells empty inside without nuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ ateŋ babaoo efee efolo ni ŋmeii bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut pods, often called 'pops,' happen when the soil lacks calcium while the pods are developing underground. Without enough calcium, the shell grows, but the nut inside fails to form properly.
ga: Peanut ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ nɔ ko, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ 'pops' lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ miiya hiɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛji calcium faaa lɛ, ŋshɔŋloo lɛ baakwɛ̃. Shi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee amɛhe mfoniri lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot underground when the soil stays too wet and heavy with excess water. Waterlogged soil prevents oxygen from reaching the roots, causing them to suffocate and decay before maturity.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni etsii tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni ji oxygen lɛ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Efoɔ ni efiteɔ dani edaa kwraa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees drop all their flowers without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ fɛɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they suffer from stress caused by high temperatures, direct sunlight, or lack of water. Young cocoa needs shade trees and steady moisture to retain flowers long enough for pods to form.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ hulutsoo be ni mli wa, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ, loo nu ni bɛ lɛ mli baa lɛ hewɔ. Cocoa bibioo he miihia tsei ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa koni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Plantain plants have very shallow root systems holding up heavy leaves and heavy fruit bunches. If pests weaken the roots or the soil becomes soft from rain, the weight of the bunch easily pulls the plant out of the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ waa. Mɔmɔ baai ni tsii kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii. Kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ loo shikpɔŋ ni efee blɛoo yɛ nugbɔ hewɔ lɛ baa. Tso lɛ niji lɛ amli tsiimɔ lɛ gbalaa tso lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mlɛo.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die during the dry afternoon, even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shwane be mli ni nu bɛ lɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: This sudden wilting in moist soil is usually caused by bacterial wilt, a soil-borne disease that blocks the internal water tubes inside the tomato stem. Even though water is in the soil, the plant cannot pull it up to its leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni shikpɔŋ ni tsiɔ nu paipii ni yɔɔ tomato tsei amli lɛ naa lɛ kɛbaa. Eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ agbala lɛ kɛyashɛ baa lɛ nɔ.

english: Curling and wrinkled leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites that suck sap from young leaves, or by plant viruses carried by insects that disrupt normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo tsei amli helai ni jɛɔ kooloi amli ni tsiɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ naa.

english: Why do my cowpea plants flower heavily but fail to produce bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi amɛwooo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants often shed their blossoms without forming pods because tiny insect pests, like flower thrips or pod borers, feed on the delicate parts inside the flower before pollination can happen.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cowpea tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo ŋmeii. Enɛ jɛɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ fɔfɔii a-thrips loo pod borers lɛ ahewɔ. Amɛyeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli hei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ dani amɛfeɔ pollination.

english: Why do my stored yams start growing shoots even when kept in the shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii akwɛ̃mɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛtoɔ shĩa mli moŋ?

english: Yams naturally break their dormancy period after a few months in storage as temperature and humidity change. The tuber is a living organism that uses stored energy to sprout shoots so it can grow a new plant.
ga: Sweet potatoes baafo amɛ adebɔɔ mli wɔɔhe be lɛ mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni akɛto lɛ sɛɛ yɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo tsakemɔi ahewɔ. Tubers ji nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni kɛ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ koni amɛtsɔ tsei heei.

english: Why does my lowland rice grow slowly and turn pale when the water in the field dries up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishishi ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli egbi lɛ?

english: Lowland rice varieties depend on shallow standing water to absorb soil nutrients easily and suppress weeds. When the field dries out, the roots struggle to take up fertilizer and weeds compete heavily for nutrition.
ga: Omɔ henɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ damɔ nu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ nɔ koni enyɛ eŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mlɛo ni egbe jwɛi lɛ. Kɛ ŋmɔji lɛ mli egbi lɛ Shishifãi wuɔ koni amɛná ŋmɔshi nibii ni jwɛi lɛ yeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná niyenii kpakpai.

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape from the tip inward, it usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient it needs from the soil to grow strong and stay green.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baa ko shishigbɛ fã lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni efee V su kɛjɛ enaagbɛ kɛtee mligbɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa amɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from young leaves, or by a virus carried by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast with wide leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing necessary shade and holding soil moisture for cocoa during its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa sũ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi kɛha kookoo yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very tall with lots of leaves, but yields very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa?

english: If soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or too much shade, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and tall stems on top instead of sending energy down to build big roots.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo hulutsoo be babaoo lɛ, Cassava tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii kakadaji yɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaatsu hewalɛ kɛba shi koni amɛma shishifãi wuji.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch as much sunlight as possible. Exposure to light helps the leaves produce food, which is sent down into the ground to make large yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. La ni tsoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii. ni akɛmajeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni efee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji

english: What happens to my maize yield if I plant the seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi ŋmãa yibiiwoo lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, plants must fight each other for sunlight, soil water, and plant nutrients, resulting in thin stalks and very small or missing ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Esa akɛ tsei lɛ atswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu, kɛ tsei lɛ amli niyenii. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmãa toi bibii waa loo ni bɛ mli baa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when water is inconsistent, or when there are no insects or wind around to help shake pollen within the flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ mli ejɔɔɔ Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ he fɛɛ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ewosoɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ koni aduawai aba.

english: Why are small caterpillars suddenly eating holes inside the center funnel of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu ko ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tso lɛ teŋ trukaa lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that targets the soft inner leaves of young maize. They feed inside the central whorl where it is moist and protected.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni tswaa ŋmei bibii amli baai lɛ. Amɛtaoɔ niyenii yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli, ni ŋta lɛ mli edɔ ni abuɔ he.
