english: Why does covering the soil around my vegetables with dry grass help them stay alive during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mi-vegetables lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the dirt with dry grass, known as mulching, stops the hot sun from evaporating moisture out of the ground, keeps the soil cool, and prevents weeds from stealing water.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaatsi hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekajie ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akaju nu

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans help improve my farm's soil for future crops?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans work with beneficial tiny organisms in their roots to capture nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the dirt, acting as a free natural fertilizer for the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans kɛ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ feɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii. Ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli koni emɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Why should I plant my maize seeds in straight rows instead of scattering them across my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi-abɛi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja moŋ fe ni magbɛ amɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting maize in straight, properly spaced rows ensures that each plant receives enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without competing with its neighbors, making weeding and harvesting much easier.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja, ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ yeee akaŋ. Enɛ haa jwɛi lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need maximum sunlight to manufacture food for the growing tuber underground. Staking keeps the leaves exposed to light and off the damp ground where diseases spread easily.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii amɛha tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa tso lɛ yibii lɛ shɛɔ la he, ni ejɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with many leaves but producing tiny tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is packed too tightly, cassava plants put all their energy into growing top leaves instead of expanding their roots into large tubers below ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ebaa lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shishifãi lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do I need to remove some of the shoots growing around the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie ŋmeii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishitoo lɛ

english: Extra shoots suck water and nutrients away from the main fruiting stem. Keeping only one or two strong suckers allows the parent plant to produce a much larger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ yibiiwoo tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ ŋmei kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hi shi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ awo ŋmei ni dara ni tsii kwraa.

english: Flowers drop when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or poor soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist during hot spells helps flowers set fruit properly.
ga: Fɔfɔi baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas alongside my main crops help make my soil stronger?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni mikɛ miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, which enriches the soil with free nutrients for nearby crops like maize or cassava.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmli ni amɛmɔɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii kpakpai ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ abele loo ŋmãa.

english: Why does fertilizer wash away when I apply it right before heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi kɛ́ akɛwo mli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains sweep loose fertilizer off the dry surface before root systems can soak it in. Fertilizer works best when buried shallowly near the base of plants in already moist soil.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ afu amɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Ebɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ momo mli.

english: What makes the new improved seed varieties better than the seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa dumɔwui heei ni asaa amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hi fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved seeds are specifically bred to withstand local dry spells, resist common field pests, and mature faster, yielding a much bigger harvest than older seeds that lose strength over time.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ maŋ lɛ mli hɔmɔ shihilɛi lɛ anaa. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ oya Enɛ haa yibiiwoo babaoo baa fe dumɔwui momo ni hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ.

english: Why should I prune off yellow or spotted leaves from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow or spotted leaves are often infected with fungus or disease. Removing them prevents sickness from spreading across the rest of the plant and allows energy to focus on healthy fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela loo hela yeɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ehaaa helai agbɛ ashwã tso lɛ fãi krokomɛi anɔ, ni ehaa hewalɛ lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my young cocoa seedlings burn and curl up in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛkpãa amɛhe yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that cannot handle direct, intense heat. They need temporary shade from crops like plantains to keep cooler and hold moisture until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ adamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ naa tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛjɛ tsei tamɔ plantains adɛŋ koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential for green growth. This happens when soil nutrients are low or washed away by heavy rains, and it can be fixed by applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ Enɛ baa mli kɛji shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ni abaanyɛ asaa enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains on the same field with my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu kookoo tsei heei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and dry out easily under harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing necessary shade and preserving soil moisture for the cocoa until it matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni okwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha kookoo kɛyashi ebaakwɛ̃.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium and phosphorus, cassava puts most of its energy into producing tall stems and green leaves above ground rather than swelling its tubers below ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛtoɔ potassium kɛ fɔsfɔs he lɛ. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ tsei kakadaji kɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, e yi ɔ fĩɔ ngɛ zugba a sisi.

english: How can I tell if the caterpillar eating my maize leaves is Fall Armyworm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei ni yeɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ baa lɛ ji Fall Armyworm?

english: Check the caterpillar's face for a distinct white inverted 'Y' pattern and look for four dark spots arranged in a square on the top of its tail segment; these features distinguish Fall Armyworm from common stalk borers.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmei lɛ hiɛ mli koni ona ‘Y’ ni atsake lɛ yɛŋ ni mli tse. Ni otao hei ejwɛ ni yɔɔ ediŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Nibii nɛɛ haa Fall Armyworm jeɔ kpo yɛ tsei krokomɛi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ahe.

english: Can I save seeds from my harvested hybrid maize to plant next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: It is not recommended because hybrid seeds are bred for high yield in the first generation only; seeds saved from that harvest will result in weaker plants and significantly lower yields in the next season.
ga: Akɛ enɛ haaa ejaakɛ afɔɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Dumɔwui ni ato kɛjɛ kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ baaha tso lɛ afee nɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kwraa yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot or when soil moisture fluctuates drastically, which causes heat stress and prevents successful pollination.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsakeɔ waa lɛ. Enɛ haa hulutsoo haomɔ baa ni etsĩɔ pollination naa.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help my soil before I plant maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ dani aduɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts capture nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots, naturally enriching the land with free fertilizer for nutrient-hungry crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha tsei ni he hiaa niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot so quickly when stored in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yam rot is caused by fungi and bacteria entering through small cuts or bruises made during harvest, especially if the storage barn is warm, damp, and lacks proper air flow.
ga: Fungi kɛ bacteria kɛ sweet potato ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni afoɔ lɛ anɔ. loo fãji ni baa yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli edɔ, edɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli.

english: Why is the pink-flowered Striga weed so difficult to get rid of on my cereal field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa waa akɛ abaajie Striga jwɛi ni fɔfɔii yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛjɛ miŋmaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Striga (witchweed) is a parasite that attaches directly to the roots of host crops underground to steal water and food, and a single plant can shed thousands of tiny seeds that stay alive in the soil for over ten years.
ga: Striga (witchweed) ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ashishifãi ahe tɛ̃ɛ koni eju nu kɛ niyenii. Ni tso kome pɛ baanyɛ ajie dumɔwui bibii. Dumɔwui akpei abɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nɔ ni fe afii nyɔŋma.

english: Why is it important to prune the extra branches off my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ niji ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ tomato tsei amli lɛ?

english: Pruning excess branches and lower leaves improves sunlight exposure and airflow through the plant, reducing humidity that causes fungal diseases and redirecting energy toward growing larger fruits.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. Ha hulutsoo ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa lɛ aba shi. ni okɛ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aya aduawai wuji ni akwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in high humidity and damp shade. Pruning excess tree branches to let in sunlight and air helps prevent the fungus from taking over.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ jɛɔ ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baa. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aaafolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ aŋɔ he fɛɛ he.

english: This is usually Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties and removing infected plants early helps protect your field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa Aduɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ adumɔ kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he.

english: Is it really necessary for me to put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Ani ehe miihia diɛŋtsɛ ni mikɛ tso ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yes, staking lifts the leaves toward the sun so the plant can make more food. Without stakes, leaves get shaded and diseased on the damp ground, leading to much smaller yam tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, staking haa baai lɛ kɛ hulu lɛ hiɛ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ awo niyenii babaoo. Kɛji akɛ tso ko bɛ ni fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ Baai lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni hela baamɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, sweet potato lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ faaa kwraa.

english: How far apart should I space my seeds when planting maize?
ga: Te esa akɛ makɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ashɛ he tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa?

english: Planting maize about 25 to 30 centimeters apart in rows spaced 75 centimeters apart ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, soil nutrients, and water to grow big ears of corn.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ aaafee sɛntimita 25 kɛyashi 30 yɛ ŋmãa ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimita 75 lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa baaná hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmãa toi wuji akwɛ̃.

english: When is the right time for me to apply fertilizer to my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mawo abifao ŋmãa?

english: Apply your first round of NPK fertilizer about 10 to 14 days after the seeds germinate, and a second round of urea when the plants are knee-high to boost stalk strength and cob formation.
ga: Okɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji klɛŋklɛŋ fã lɛ awo mli aaafee gbii 10 kɛyashi 14 beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Ni okɛ urea ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ lɛ awo mli beni tsei lɛ shɛɔ amɛnaji ahe lɛ koni eha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ cob lɛ feemɔ aya hiɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress or lack water. Giving your plants consistent moisture during hot dry spells stops the flowers from dropping.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo latsaa loo nu ni bɛ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ mli fũu daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔi lɛ akagbee shi.

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, often due to irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture steady allows roots to absorb calcium continuously.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛjieɔ calcium.

english: Legumes like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. When the plant decomposes, it leaves behind natural plant food for crops planted after it.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ tsei fite Ebaashi adebɔɔ mli tsei niyenii aha tsei ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ no sɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly when I delay clearing weeds from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ beni mikɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds aggressively steal water, soil nutrients, and sunlight from your crops. Clearing weeds within the first three to four weeks of planting gives your young crops the best start.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ ni okɛdu lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha otsei bibii lɛ aje shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops each year even when rain falls well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop in the same soil every season exhausts specific nutrients. Practicing crop rotation or adding organic manure restores soil nutrients so crops can yield well again.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei komekomei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ, ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ afite. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni akɛaawo mli lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ koni tsei lɛ anyɛ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which helps plants stay green and grow strong. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients out of the soil or when the ground stays too wet for too long.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa waa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Groundnuts and beans capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the crop is harvested and the roots rot, that stored nitrogen stays in the ground to act as natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ egbo. Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the young plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. This struggle results in tall, thin stalks with very small cobs.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ nɛkɛ nɔmɔ nɛɛ mli baa ji tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: Why do some farmers plant cassava along the edges of their farms instead of mixing it inside with other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmei yɛ amɛŋmɔji lɛ ahe yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi baafutu lɛ?

english: Cassava grows very tall with thick leaves that block sunlight from shorter plants. Planting it along farm edges keeps it from shading out crops like groundnuts or maize while still producing tubers and marking field boundaries.
ga: Yucca daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ waa ni baai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni jɛɔ tsei kukuji lɛ amli lɛ naa. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ tsiɔ hulutsoo naa koni ekafee ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei. yɛ be mli ni ejieɔ yitsei lolo ni ekadiɔ kpokpaa lɛ husui lɛ.

english: Why should I clear my farmland without burning the dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mikɛshãaa jwɛi kɛ baai ni egboi lɛ?

english: Burning destroys organic material that feeds your soil and kills helpful soil creatures like earthworms. Leaving dry weeds and leaves to break down naturally adds nutrients back into the soil and helps retain moisture during dry periods.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni haa sũ lɛ hewalɛ, ni egbeɔ sũ mli nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ jwɛi kɛ baai ni egboi lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why is it so important to clear weeds during the first month after planting my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa waa akɛ ajie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni adu nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings are delicate and need sunlight, water, and soil nutrients to get established. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing these essential resources while your main crop is still small and vulnerable.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni ehe hiaa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛdara. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nibii ni he hiaa nɛɛ yɛ be mli ni oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe waaa lolo lɛ.

english: Why do caterpillars attack my maize plants mostly inside the central funnel where new leaves grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ babaoo yɛ gbɛjegbɛ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ he ni baai heei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: The young leaves inside the center funnel of the maize plant are soft, tender, and full of water, making them the easiest food for pests like Fall Armyworm to eat while hiding from sunlight and predators.
ga: Baai bibii ni yɔɔ abele tso lɛ teŋ lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, bɔdɔɔ, ni nu eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛha kooloi tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni amɛyeɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ hulu la kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Continuous rain and high humidity create damp conditions that allow fungal spores to grow and spread across cocoa pods. This causes Black Pod disease, which rots the pod if air cannot flow through the farm to dry the trees.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo lɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji fungal spores lɛ daa ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ lɛ baa. Ekɛ black pod hela baa, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni eha tsei lɛ agbi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any fruit when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Very high temperatures damage the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing fruit from forming. When it gets too hot, the plant drops its blossoms to save water and energy until cooler weather returns.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli wa waa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaa aduawai lɛ efeee Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots get woody and hard to boil if I leave them in the ground for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ tsei ni ewa akɛ abaahoo kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: As a cassava plant grows older, its roots naturally develop tough, woody fibers to support the plant's weight above ground and store energy through long dry spells, making the tubers hard to cook.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ eda lɛ Shishifãi lɛ feɔ tso mli tsɔi ni wa yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛfi tso lɛ muji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ ato kɛtsɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛgbiɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ aaahoo ŋmei shishifãi lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate foliage and dries out the topsoil too quickly. Keeping taller shade trees creates a cooler microclimate and preserves soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ, ni ehaa sũ ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ gĩɔ oya tsɔ. Tso lɛ ni akɛaaha he ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ haa kɔɔyɔŋ mli jɔɔ fioo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hulutsoo be muu lɛ fɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce very small bunches when I allow all the young shoots to grow around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii nɛkɛ beni mihaa tsei bibii lɛ fɛɛ daraa yɛ tso lɛ tso wulu lɛ he lɛ?

english: When too many young shoots grow around one plantain stem, they compete for the same food, water, and sunlight in the soil. Cutting back excess shoots leaves more energy for the main plant to produce a thick trunk and a larger fruit bunch.
ga: Beni ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni miida yɛ plantain kome he lɛ Amɛbaatswa niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hu. Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛwoɔ tsei ni mli tse kɛ aduawai akui wuji.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to grow green leaves. When nitrogen runs low, the plant pulls it from older leaves at the bottom to nourish new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ baai eŋɔlii Beni nitrogen lɛ faaa Tso lɛ gbalaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Beans and cowpeas are part of a plant family that extracts nitrogen gas from the air and stores it in their roots. When the plants die and decay, that nitrogen stays in the soil, working like a natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas fata tsei aweku ko ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ tsei gboi ni amɛfite Nakai nitrogen lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny, hard-to-see insects like mites or thrips sucking sap from the undersides of leaves. This sap-sucking damages leaf tissue and can spread plant viruses that distort growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii kɛ baai lɛ shwiemɔ baa. ni ewa akɛ aaana, tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips Emuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi Nu nɛɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ tsei amli helai ni fiteɔ amɛdalɛ lɛ eshwã.

english: Why do insect pests get worse on my land if I plant maize on the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ feɔ basabasa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously gives crop-specific insects a steady food supply, allowing their populations and eggs to build up in the soil and surrounding brush over time. Rotating crops starves these pests out.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa tso pɔtɛɛ ko mli kooloi lɛ náa niyenii ni amɛyeɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kooloi bibii kɛ amɛwuji buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the plants instead of turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat stress or erratic watering. To survive the heat and conserve moisture, the plant sheds its blossoms rather than spending energy growing fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni ejaaa ha amɛ. Bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ latsaa be lɛ mli ni ekwɛ koni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi. No hewɔ lɛ tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the sunlight to capture light and produce energy through their leaves. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases and helping the vine build larger underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia ni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe waa koni amɛmɔ la ni amɛfee hewalɛ kɛtsɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Tsiɔ fungal helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa wain tso lɛ ni efeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the ground if I do not harvest them before heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ akpaaa amɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains waterlog the soil and cut off air to the root system. When cassava roots sit in airless, wet soil for too long, naturally occurring fungi and bacteria attack the roots, causing rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni boteɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ mli. Beni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Fungi kɛ bacteria ni jɛɔ adebɔɔ mli baa lɛ tutuaa shishifãi lɛ, ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow short and weak even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ kuku ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal essential soil nutrients and minerals faster than your crops can take them in. Even with plenty of water, crops become stunted because they are starving for soil nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ minerals kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni otsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nu babaoo yɛ moŋ shi Dumɔwui lɛ egbɔjɔ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot mainly when planted in soil that holds too much water without proper drainage, or when delayed harvesting allows soil fungi to enter and breakdown the tubers.
ga: Nɔ ni he hiaa ji akɛ, ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu babaoo yɔɔ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo kɛ́ akpa sɛɛ mli lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baabote mli ni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ amli agbala.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with lots of green leaves but give me very small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are planted too close together or receive too much nitrogen, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of feeding the tubers below.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo enine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baafite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni eeeha ŋmei ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ niyenii.

english: Yellowing on lower leaves is a sign of nitrogen deficiency; the plant naturally moves its limited nitrogen nutrients to the newest leaves at the top to survive.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen niyenii ni faaa lɛ kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi fe fɛɛ lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers before any fruit can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or damage from microscopic pests like thrips feeding on flower stalks.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nibii bibii ni fiteɔ nii tamɔ thrips ni yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up tight and turning small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is commonly caused by a virus spread by tiny whiteflies that suck plant juices, causing leaves to distort and stopping normal fruit growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii yɛŋ bibii ni nuɔ tsei amli nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni no haa baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekpaa aduawai lɛ adalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why did the weed spray I used kill my young cassava plants together with the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ gbeɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ kɛ jwɛi lɛ?

english: Herbicides come in two main types: selective sprays that only target broadleaf weeds, and non-selective sprays that destroy any green plant material they touch.
ga: Tsofai titrii enyɔ yɔɔ ni gbeɔ jwɛi: Tsofai pɔtɛɛ ni akɛshwieɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ baai babaoo lɛ pɛ anɔ. kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni jeee nɔ pɔtɛɛ ni fiteɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛkɛkpeɔ lɛ.

english: If I add double the recommended fertilizer to my crop, will it give me double the yield?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛwo mli lɛ toi enyɔ fata miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe. Ani ebaaha minitsumɔ lɛ aya hiɛ shii enyɔ?

english: Too much fertilizer burns plant roots by pulling moisture out of them, which can stunt crop growth or kill the plant completely.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ shãa tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tsei adalɛ naa loo eha tsei lɛ agbo.

english: Why do my crops dry up quickly during a short rain break while my neighbor's crops stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi kukuji amli lɛ? yɛ be mli ni akutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔji lolo lɛ

english: Covering bare soil around crops with dry grass or leaves (mulching) traps moisture in the ground and shields plant roots from hot sunshine.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi aha ŋmɔshi nibii ahe (mulching) lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebu tsei shishifãi ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous maize crop perform worse than the sealed seed packets from the store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mi tsutsu ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni atsĩ naa kɛjɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Store-bought hybrid seeds are specifically bred for high performance in their first season, but seeds saved from that harvest lose their high yield traits in the next generation.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ koni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ mli. Shi dumɔwui ni ahere amɛ kɛjɛ kpamɔ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ su ni haa amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why is a yellow thread-like vine wrapping around my crops and causing them to dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wain tsei ni tamɔ kpãa ŋmɔŋ lɛ bɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni ehaa amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: This is a parasitic plant that has no roots of its own; it pierces your crop's stem to steal food and water, so it must be stripped off completely and destroyed.
ga: Enɛ ji tso ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni bɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eshishifãi. Efoɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli koni eju niyenii kɛ nu. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ajie kɛya kwraa ni akpata hiɛ.

english: Why is it important to clear my land properly before planting new seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo mihe jogbaŋŋ dani madu dumɔwui heei lɛ?

english: Proper land clearing removes weeds and brush that steal water and plant food from young seedlings, while also reducing hidden pests and making it easier to line up your crops evenly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaato ŋmɔshi nibii ahe gbɛjianɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: How deep should I dig the holes when planting young crop seedlings on my farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafo bu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ beni miduɔ dumɔwui bibii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: You should dig holes slightly deeper and wider than the seedling container so the young roots have soft soil to spread into without bending upward, which prevents stunted growth.
ga: Esa akɛ otsa bu lɛ mli fioo ni elɛɛmɔ fe nɔ ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi bibii lɛ aná shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ Ha egbɛ eshwa ni ekɛ ehe akabɔle ehe. Enɛ baaye abua ni akafee nɔ ni yaa hiɛ.

english: Why should I buy nursery-raised cocoa seedlings instead of just planting seeds directly into my field soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe kookoo dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu dumɔwui lɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Nursery seedlings are protected and nurtured during their weakest early stage, developing strong roots and leaves that give them a much higher chance of surviving field conditions.
ga: Abuɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe ni akwɛɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ amɛshishijee bei ni yɔɔ oshara fe fɛɛ lɛ amli. Kɛtsɔ shishifãi kɛ baai ni mli wa ni anáa lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa hegbɛ babaoo ni akɛhiɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi amli.

english: How do I care for young seedlings when moving them from the nursery to my main farm so they do not die?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ dumɔwui bibii lɛ anɔ kɛ́ mijie amɛ kɛjɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe lɛ kɛmiiya miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli? Koni dumɔwui lɛ akagboi

english: You should shade them from direct wind and burning sun during transport, keep their soil moist, and carry them by the bottom of their bags rather than pulling their stems.
ga: Esa akɛ obu amɛhe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he beni okɛ amɛ yaa gbɛfaa mli lɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni omɔ amɛ yɛ kotoku lɛ shishi moŋ fe ni ooogbala tsɔne lɛ nɔ.

english: If some of my cocoa trees die, can I plant new seedlings in those empty spots without clearing the whole farm?
ga: Kɛji mi-kooko tsei lɛ ekomɛi gboi Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui heei yɛ nakai hei ni nɔ ko bɛ lɛ ni mikɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ efoŋ?

english: Yes, this is called replacement planting or gap filling, and it helps you keep your farm at full capacity to maximize your yield without starting from scratch.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ dumɔwui ekoŋŋ loo ŋmeii ni awoɔ mli. ni ehaa okwɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni oná nibii babaoo ni ehe ehiaaa ni oje shishi kɛjɛ shishijee.

english: How do I know whether my old farm needs total replanting or just replacement of individual dead trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ehe miihia ni adu miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli kwraa loo atsake tsei ni egboi lɛ kɛkɛ?

english: If only a few scattered trees have died, simple replacement planting works best; but if most trees are old, diseased, and yield very few pods, the entire farm needs clearing and replanting.
ga: Kɛ tsei fioo komɛi pɛ gboi lɛ Tsei ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Shi kɛji akɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ babaoo egbɔ, ni helai emɔ amɛ, ni amɛwooo yibii fioo pɛ lɛ, no lɛ ehe miihia ni ajie ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli ni adu ekoŋŋ.

english: What is the benefit of getting seedlings from official research centers like the Cocoa Research Institute?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni anáa kɛjɛɔ niiamlitaomɔ he ko ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ dɛŋ tamɔ Cocoa Research Institute lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Seedlings from research centers come from high-quality mother plants that are specifically bred to resist local diseases, grow faster, and produce more pods than random seeds from a market.
ga: Dumɔwui ni jɛ niiamlitaomɔ he lɛ jɛɔ nyɛ tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni atsɔse amɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli. shwereɔ oya ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ jara nɔ lɛ.

english: When is the best time of the year to move my nursery seedlings into the main field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ ajie dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mi-nsɛri lɛ mli lɛ kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: It is best to transplant at the beginning of the main rainy season so the abundant rainfall helps the roots settle deeply before the hot dry season arrives.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli bɔni afee ni nugbɔ babaoo anɛ ni eha shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shɔŋŋ dani hulutsoo be lɛ aba.

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings wither or turn yellow when they get full sunlight after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and small roots that dry out easily under strong sun, which is why they need shade trees above them until they grow older.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii. ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi lɛ Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ amɛyiteŋ kɛyashi amɛbaadara lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my newly transplanted seedlings in a cleared field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe dumɔwui heei ni adu yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive wild plants adapted to capture sunlight and nutrients quickly from open soil, so you must clear around your seedlings frequently until they grow tall enough to shade out weeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ basabasa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛmɔmɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okɛ jwɛi afɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe shii abɔ kɛyashi amɛbaakwɛ jwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. They need temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava planted alongside them to block intense heat and retain soil moisture while the seedlings get established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo yucca ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Enɛ ji koni akafee dɔlɛ ni fe nine ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛshwereɔ lɛ.

english: Plantains have large leaves that lose water rapidly in hot weather. When soil moisture drops, the plant naturally sheds lower leaves to conserve water and protect its main stalk until the rains return.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai wuji ni nu fiteɔ oya kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ba shi lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛshishi baai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛbu tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ he kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: If I plant twice as many crop seeds on the same piece of land, will I get double the harvest?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui ni fa fe nakai lɛ shii enyɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, Ani maná yibiiwoo lɛ shii enyɔ?

english: Planting too closely causes crops to fight over sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Overcrowded plants grow thin and weak, which often leads to smaller yields and higher chances of disease spreading.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ hulu la lɛ abɔ mɔdɛŋ waa. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ baatsɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbɔjɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi, ni helai hu baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: How far apart should I space my maize seeds when planting a large field?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ abɔ he tɛŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ mihe wo ŋmɔ agbo mli?

english: Spacing maize about 75 centimeters between rows and 40 centimeters between plants ensures each stalk receives enough air, light, and nutrients to produce strong, heavy cobs.
ga: Gbɛ ni kã ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji aaafee sɛntimitai 75 kɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ aaafee sɛntimitai 40, ni ehaa tso fɛɛ tso kɔɔyɔɔ, la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmãa ni mli wa ni tsii.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants turning light green and stunt growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiida lɛ?

english: Light green leaves usually indicate that the soil is running low on essential nutrients like nitrogen. Applying well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer restores green leaf color and encourages leafy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaha baai lɛ adara.

english: Why is it risky to plant new crops immediately on land where old trees were just cut down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu tsei heei trukaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni afo tsei momoi yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Old tree stumps and decaying roots can carry fungal diseases and root rot in the soil. Clearing old debris and allowing the soil to rest prevents these hidden pests from attacking your new crop roots.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni egbɔ kɛ shishifãi ni egboi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shishifãi ni egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi momo ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkatutua otsei heei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ.

english: Extreme heat, irregular watering, or insect attacks can cause tomato plants to stress and drop their flowers. Keeping soil moisture consistent and protecting plants from sap-sucking insects helps flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be Loo kooloi ni baa amɛnɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ ni eha amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa kɛ tsei ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: What causes white spots on my cassava leaves, and does it stop tubers from growing?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa nɔ? Ni ani ebaanyɛ ekpa ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ?

english: White spots or powdery patches are caused by fungal infections or insect damage. Sick leaves cannot produce food for the plant properly, which reduces the size and weight of the cassava tubers under the ground.
ga: Fungal helai loo koolooi ni fiteɔ nii kɛ helai yɛŋ loo powder patches baa. Baai ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ aha tso lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei shishifãi lɛ adalɛ kɛ amɛtsiimɔ ba shi.

english: Why does letting weeds grow around my crop plants slow down their growth so much?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ oŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mitso lɛ dalɛ yaa hiɛ fioo?

english: Weeds grow faster than main crops and steal essential water, sunlight, and fertilizer from the soil. Clearing weeds regularly ensures your crop gets all the nutrients it needs to grow quickly.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ nu ni he hia, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya.

english: How do I know when my yam crop is fully mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yam plants signal maturity when their leaves and vines stop growing green, turn yellow, and begin to dry up naturally, showing that the plant has finished storing energy in the tuber below.
ga: Sweet potato tsei tsɔɔ dalɛ kɛji baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ kpa eŋɔlifeemɔ. tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔi ŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛtoɔ eshishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: If the rain is late this year, should I still plant my seeds at the usual time or wait for the rain?
ga: Kɛji afi nɛɛ nugbɔ lɛ ba sɛɛ Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui bɔ ni sa loo mamɛ nugbɔ?

english: It is better to wait until the rain actually starts and moistens the soil. Planting in dry soil during a rain delay can cause your seeds to dry out, get eaten by insects, or spoil before they get the water they need to sprout.
ga: Ehi akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaje shishi ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi. ni kooloi yeɔ loo egboi dani enine shɛɔ nu ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ

english: Why does it rain on my neighbor's farm nearby, but my own farm stays completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ miinɛ yɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Shi mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli egbi kwraa?

english: At the start of the rainy season, clouds often release rain in small, isolated patches rather than across large areas. Rain will eventually reach your field as the main storm systems move across the region.
ga: Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ Atatui lɛ shwieɔ nugbɔ yɛ hei bibii ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ, moŋ fe ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã hei wuji. Yɛ naagbee lɛ, nugbɔ baashɛ oyale mli beni ahum wulu ko nyiɛɔ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: What happens to my seeds if it rains once after I plant them, but then stops raining for two weeks?
ga: Mɛni baa midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ shikome beni midu amɛ sɛɛ? Shi no sɛɛ lɛ, nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛmɔ otsii enyɔ?

english: The first rain tricks the seed into sprouting, but without follow-up water, the young root will dry up underground and the seedling will die. This is why it is safer to wait until the rains are steady before planting.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃. Shi kɛji nu bɛ ni nyiɛɔ Young shishifãi lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, amɛbaagbi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni dumɔwu lɛ baagbo. Yɛ yiŋtoo nɛɛ hewɔ lɛ, eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ aba shi dani odu.

english: Is it still okay for me to plant my maize in June if the rainy season usually begins in May?
ga: Ani ehi lolo akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ June mli? Kɛji akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ May mli?

english: Yes, you can still plant in June, but you should choose fast-growing seed varieties that mature quickly so they can harvest before the rains stop later in the year.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu amɛ lolo yɛ June mli. Shi esa akɛ ohala dumɔwui srɔtoi ni daa oya ni daa oya bɔni afee ni akpa amɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ akpa yɛ afi lɛ naagbee.

english: How can I keep water in my soil for my crops when the sun is hot and rains are few?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ akɛ nu ato shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii? Kɛ́ hulu lɛ edɔ ni nugbɔ fioo pɛ enɛɔ?

english: You can cover the ground around your crops with dry leaves or crop residues. This practice, called mulching, blocks the sun from drying out the earth and keeps the soil moist for a longer time.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ okɛ baai ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ adu onibii lɛ. Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsĩ hulu lɛ naa ni ebaatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ

english: How do I choose the right seeds to buy when I do not know if the rainy season will be long or short?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ahala dumɔwui ni ahe? Be mli ni oleee kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baafee kakadaŋŋ loo kuku?

english: You should ask for drought-tolerant or short-duration seeds. These varieties are bred to grow faster and require less water, making them safer to plant during unpredictable rainy seasons.
ga: Esa akɛ obi dumɔwui ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa loo ehiɔ shi be kukuoo. Afɔ nɛkɛ tsei srɔtoi nɛɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛkɛ nu fioo pɛ atsu nii. Enɛ haa efeɔ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my crops curling up during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is the plant's natural way of protecting itself. By rolling its leaves, the crop exposes less surface area to the hot sun, which helps it save water inside its leaves until the weather cools down.
ga: Baai ni abɔleɔ he lɛ ji gbɛ ni tso ko tsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe he. Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ bɛ he ko ni ekɛbaatsu nii yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ baai lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Will my seeds rot if I put them in the dry ground before the first rain comes?
ga: Ani midumɔwui lɛ baagbo kɛji mikɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ?

english: Seeds usually do not rot in completely dry soil, but hot ground can damage them, and pests like ants and birds might eat them before the rain finally arrives to help them grow.
ga: Dumɔwui fɔɔ fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kwraa nɔ. Shi hei ni hulu tsoɔ yɛ lɛ baanyɛ akpata dumɔwui lɛ ahiɛ. Ni kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ okpoi baanyɛ aye dumɔwui lɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ aba koni eye ebua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛdara.

english: When is the best time for me to put fertilizer on my crops if the weather is hot and dry?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ?

english: Only apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist or when rain is expected soon. Fertilizer needs water to dissolve into the soil; if applied during dry heat, it can burn your crops' roots.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli pɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo loo kɛji akɛ nugbɔ baanɛ etsɛŋ. Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ hulutsoo be mli Tso shishifãi baanyɛ ashã.

english: Should I clear and clear my land before the rainy season starts or wait until the ground is wet?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba loo mamɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ?

english: It is best to clear the bushes before the rain starts, but wait for the first light rain to soften the hard soil before plowing or making ridges, as wet earth is much easier to dig.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi jwɛi lɛ amli dani nugbɔ lɛ aje shishi anɛ. Shi mɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ anɛ klɛŋklɛŋ koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ afee blɛoo dani otsu nii loo ofee ŋmeii. Akɛni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efɔ hewɔ lɛ, etsamɔ waaa kwraa.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them on freshly cleared land without any bigger trees nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ hee ni agbele naa ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that dry out easily under direct sunlight. Planting them under fast-growing shade crops like plantains or under mature forest trees protects them from burning sun and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei nɛɛ yɛ tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo koo mli tsei ni eda lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaabu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly even after I burn the bush to clear my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mishã jwɛi lɛ koni mikɛjie ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Burning heat clears the weeds on top, but it does not destroy weed seeds buried deep in the soil. In fact, the ash acts like quick food for those buried seeds, causing them to sprout fast as soon as the rains begin.
ga: Shãa lɛ mli la lɛ gbeɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Shi efiteee jwɛi dumɔwui ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ. Yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ, sũ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni ayeɔ oya kɛhaa dumɔwui ni afu. Ha ekwɛ oya kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ pɛ.

english: If I plant my cassava sticks very close together, will I get a bigger harvest from my farm?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe waa Ani maná nibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too closely causes crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of growing large tubers, cassava plants planted too close together will grow tall and thin with small, skinny tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ wuɔ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ bulbs wuji lɛ, Cassava tsei ni adu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛyitsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: My plantain stool has many small suckers growing around the main stalk, should I remove them or leave them all to grow?
ga: Mi plantain shwiili lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. Mɛi babaoo miida yɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ he. Ani esa akɛ majie amɛ loo maha amɛ fɛɛ amɛdara?

english: Leaving all the suckers causes them to steal water and food from the main mother plant. You should trim away most suckers and leave only one or two strong ones so the mother plant can produce a heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ ashɛrɛ ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ ashwie lɛ, ebaaha amɛju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Esa akɛ ofolɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ babaoo ni oshi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ koni tso nyɛ lɛ anyɛ awo plantains babaoo.

english: Why does cassava give me big tubers on new forest land but very small ones on land I have used for three years straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ yitsei wuji kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kooi heei amli lɛ? Shi ŋmeii lɛ faaa kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛtsu nii afii etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Crops remove nutrients from the soil every time they grow. Fresh forest land is full of natural food for crops, but planting every year without resting the soil or adding manure starves the land, resulting in poor yields.
ga: Tsei gbalaa niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni adu amɛ. Kooi amli hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ eyi kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Shi kɛ́ odu lɛ daa afi ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ejɔɔɔ ehe loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye shikpɔŋ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nitsumɔ ni ehiii

english: Is it good for my land if I plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa du tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Yes, leguminous crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the ground, they feed the soil and help heavy-feeding crops like maize grow better.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni tsii ni yeɔ niyenii, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies hiding under the leaves. They suck the juices out of the leaves and spread plant viruses, which stunts the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Amɛmuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai amli ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei amli helai amɛshwãa. Enɛ baaha tsei nyɛŋ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of yellow flowers, but then the flowers drop off without making tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi no sɛɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the air gets extremely hot and dry, or if the soil lacks uniform moisture. Extreme heat prevents the flowers from pollinating themselves, so the plant drops them to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa. aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ tsiɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔtɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of young maize is a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen helps plants stay green and leafy, so when the soil lacks it, the plant moves what little nitrogen it has to its newer top leaves.
ga: Abɛi bibii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni ale waa ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛnáa baai. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fioo ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I tell if my crop needs manure instead of just waiting for rain to make it grow?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ he miihia amɛ moŋ fe ni mamɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ?

english: Rain provides water, but water alone cannot feed a hungry crop. If your plants are watered by rain but still look pale, grow very slowly, or have thin stems, it means the soil is exhausted and needs manure or compost to feed the roots.
ga: Nugbɔ haa nu, shi nu pɛ nyɛŋ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ niyenii. Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ewo otso lɛ nɔ nu shi etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lolo, edaa blɛoo waa, loo eyɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ ni ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ aha shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them directly under the full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from harsh sunlight and strong winds while their roots develop. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby keeps the soil cool and humid so the cocoa can survive its first two years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulu ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ he hulutsoo be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ ji koni kookoo lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know it is the right time to sow my maize seeds after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eji be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first rain, as it might be a false start. Wait until the rains become regular and the soil is moist at least finger-deep, ensuring seeds do not dry out in the ground.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ejaakɛ ekolɛ ebaafee amale shishijee. Mɛɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ eba ekoŋŋ ni kɛ hoo lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ inchi kome koni dumɔwui lɛ akagbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: What simple things can I put into my soil to make my crops grow better without buying chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo awo mli Mɛni manyɛ mikɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni mahe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Adding decomposed animal manure, dry leaves, and leftover crop waste builds soil compost. This natural matter acts like a sponge to store nutrients and moisture, feeding your plants throughout the season.
ga: Kooloo ŋmei, baai ni egbi, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmei feɔ ŋmei. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nii nɛɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji koni ekɛhiɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛtsɔ niyenii ni akɛhaa tsei yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is the main food they need to build leaf energy. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or farmyard compost will help the leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkɛfee hewalɛ kɛjɛ amɛbaai lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Does tying my yam vines up onto tall wooden stakes actually make the yam underground grow bigger?
ga: Ani mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ni mikɛbaafi tso kakadaŋŋ ko he lɛ baaha amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Yes, lifting yam leaves toward the sun using stakes helps them absorb maximum sunlight to produce energy. That extra energy travels down to build larger and healthier yam tubers under the ground.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛtee hulu lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛjieɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Nakai hewalɛ kroko lɛ yaa shi koni ekɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants dry up and fall off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi dani amɛmiiwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop when temperatures get extremely high or when the soil gets too dry. Watering your plants regularly at their base and mulching the soil keeps them cool enough to hold their flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ shishi daa ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ mli ajɔ bɔ ni sa ni eha efɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes right in the center funnel of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-babi corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common crop pest. They hide inside the growing center of the plant to feed, but putting clean sand or neem leaf extract into the central leaf funnel can help stop them.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ koni amɛye niyenii. Shi kɛ́ akɛ ŋã ni mli tse loo neem baa mli nu fata baa lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ekpa amɛ.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the sap under the leaves. Spraying the leaves with a mild soapy water solution or neem oil helps keep these insects away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ latex ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper leaf curl baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli ejɔ loo neem fɔ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akabote mli.

english: How do I choose the best cassava stems to cut and plant for a good yield?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ahala ŋmei tso ni hi fe fɛɛ ni afolɔ ni adu koni ená yibii kpakpai?

english: Select stems from healthy, mature plants that are 8 to 12 months old and free from disease spots. Take cuttings from the thick middle section of the stem with at least 4 to 6 raised nodes.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni eda ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 ni helai ahe tsɔi bɛ amɛhe lɛ ashishifãi. Kpɔ̃ɔ kɛjɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ fã ni mli tse lɛ mli ni kɛ hoo lɛ, ŋmeii 4 kɛyashi 6 awo nɔ.

english: Can I plant beans or cowpeas in the same farm rows as my maize plants?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmeii akuu kome mli kɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ?

english: Yes, intercropping maize with cowpeas is helpful because cowpeas cover the ground to block weeds, and their roots naturally put nitrogen back into the soil, which nourishes the maize.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ tsina ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he ejaakɛ ŋmãa haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ebu he kɛjɛ jwɛi ahe. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛhaa nitrogen kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ hewalɛ

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing lets every plant get enough food and light to grow strong and produce a good harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen or the soil is too full of water, which chokes the roots. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or manure helps the leaves turn healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo, ni no miitsi shishifãi lɛ anaa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before any peppers appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani pepper lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they get stressed by high heat, too little water, or lack of nutrients. Covering the soil with dried leaves or straw helps keep the soil moist and cool so the flowers stay on.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. nu fioo tsɔ loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ Ni akɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ anyɛɔ ahiɔ shi.

english: Why should I not bury my seeds very deep when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mifuɔ midumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu lɛ?

english: If seeds are planted too deep, they run out of stored energy before reaching the surface and die under the dirt. Planting seeds shallow—about two finger-joints deep—helps them shoot out into the sunlight quickly.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ amli tsɔ Hewalɛ ni ato lɛ baaho dani eshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ (aaafee inchi 2) lɛ haa amɛtswaa oya kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli.

english: Will adding a double portion of fertilizer make my crops grow twice as fast?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ shii enyɔ baaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara oya shii enyɔ?

english: No, putting too much fertilizer burns crop roots and can kill the plant, just like taking too much medicine makes a person sick. It is always best to apply only the recommended amount at the right time.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo shãa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ, ni ebaanyɛ egbe tso lɛ. Taakɛ tsofai babaoo ni anuɔ lɛ haa hela mɔɔ mɛi lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛhaa lɛ pɛ baatsu nii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: What brings small green caterpillars to chew holes in my cabbage leaves?
ga: Mɛni ha ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ shwie bu yɛ mi-cabbage baai lɛ amli?

english: Those green caterpillars come from eggs laid by small butterflies visiting your farm. They eat leaves to grow big, but spraying approved organic neem leaf water early stops them before they ruin the cabbage.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii eŋɔlii lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni baa oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ awui amli. Amɛyeɔ baai koni amɛdara. Shi organic neem tso lɛ mli nu ni akpɛlɛ nɔ momo lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ haa amɛkpaa dani akpãtãa kaabii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why do weeds always grow faster than my crops when the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii be fɛɛ be kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally tough and know how to steal water and food from the soil very fast. Clearing weeds early prevents them from starving your main crops of rainfall and nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni le bɔ ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye hɔmɔ kɛjɛ nugbɔ kɛ oniyenii titrii lɛ amli.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to crack open as the tubers expand underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds instead of saving seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato?

english: Saved seeds from previous harvests lose their strength over time, producing smaller crops and weak plants. Certified seeds are specially bred to resist diseases and give you a much higher yield.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baafite hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do farmers uproot young rice plants from one nursery bed just to plant them again in the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi jieɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome pɛ mli koni amɛdu eheei yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Transplanting rice allows seedlings to grow strong and protected in a small nursery first. When transplanted, they grow faster and can easily outgrow weeds compared to seeds sown directly into the main field.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ awoɔ he kroko lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ daraa waa ni abuɔ he yɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe bibioo ko mli klɛŋklɛŋ. Be ni esa akɛ adu amɛ Amɛdaraa oya ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsɔ jwɛi lɛ anɔ oya kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni adu yɛ saatso wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do crop seedlings look wilted or weak right after I move them from the nursery to the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi loo amɛgbɔjɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe lɛ kɛtee ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is called transplant shock. Uprooting damages the tiny root hairs that take up water, so the plant needs a few days in moist soil to grow new root hairs and stand upright again.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Shishifãi ni ajieɔ lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi ahe yitsɔi bibii ni shwieɔ nu lɛ, no hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni tso lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ gbii fioo komɛi dani shishifãi ahe yitsɔi heei akwɛ̃ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: What happens if I leave my crop seedlings in the nursery bed for too long before transplanting them?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi midumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani mikɛwo he kroko?

english: If seedlings stay in the nursery too long, their roots become crowded and weak. Moving them late makes them take longer to recover in the field, leading to smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ otsi amɛ blɛoo lɛ, ebaahe be babaoo dani amɛhe ajɔ amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baafee bibioo.

english: If I clear my farm land today, why do some weeds and crop stalks start growing back after just two weeks?
ga: Kɛji mijie ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɛnɛ Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kɛ tsei ahe ŋmeii jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ otsii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ?

english: Many weeds and plants store energy in roots hidden under the ground. Even when you cut the top part off, those living roots quickly push up new green shoots as soon as they get sunlight and rain.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei babaoo kɛ hewalɛ toɔ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli. Kɛji ofo ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ po lɛ, shishifãi ni hiɛ ka lɛ tsiɔ ŋmeii heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ oya kɛji amɛshɛ hulu la kɛ nugbɔ he pɛ.

english: Why do weeds always seem to grow much faster than my young crops after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ beni midu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that naturally suit the local soil and weather. They sprout quickly and spread aggressively to steal light, water, and nutrients from your gentle crop seedlings.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni kɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kpãa gbee. Amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa oya koni amɛju la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛ otso dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ amli.

english: Why is it important to spend a full month or more continuously weeding my farm after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maŋɔ nyɔŋ muu fɛɛ loo nɔ ni fe nakai kɛjie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni midu nii be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Crops are most vulnerable during their first few weeks of growth. Keeping the farm clean during this critical stage ensures the young plants get all the soil nutrients and light they need to produce a good yield.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ oshara mli fe fɛɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni amɛdaraa lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tse yɛ haomɔ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui lɛ naa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Can rice stalks grow back on their own after being cut down, or must I always plant new seeds?
ga: Ani ŋmãa toi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ loo esa akɛ adu amɛ ekoŋŋ be fɛɛ be?

english: Rice stalks can sprout new shoots from the root stubble (called ratooning), but planting fresh, healthy seedlings usually gives a stronger crop and a much higher yield than letting old stalks regrow.
ga: Omɔ tsei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. (Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ stubble rooting.) Shi dumɔwui heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa yibiiwoo ni mli wa, ni fa babaoo fe ni ashiɔ tsei momoi koni akɛdu eheei.

english: How long should I wait after clearing weeds before I start planting my crops?
ga: Kɛ́ mijie jwɛi lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: Waiting about one to two weeks gives cleared weeds time to dry out and die completely. This prevents them from sprouting back quickly and choking your new seedlings right after planting.
ga: Kɛ́ omɛ otsi kome kɛyashi enyɔ lɛ, ebaaha jwɛi ni ajie lɛ lɛ agbi kwraa ni amɛgboi. Enɛ haaa amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛdara oya ni amɛmiimɔ odumɔwui heei lɛ amli beni odu lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ.

english: Why do extension officers advise gathering a group of people to help during rice transplanting day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ abua gbɔmɛi akuu ko naa koni amɛye amɛbua yɛ ŋmãa dumɔ gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Once rice seedlings are uprooted from the nursery, their roots dry out quickly in the heat. Having a large team ensures all seedlings are replanted into wet soil as fast as possible on the same day.
ga: Kɛji ajieɔ dumɔwui kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Shishifãi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji akɛ amɛwo la mli. Kuu agbo ko ni yɔɔ lɛ haa aduɔ dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ awoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ oya bɔ ni aaanyɛ yɛ gbi kome nɔ.

english: Why must my field be completely cleared of old growth before I transplant my young crop seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni miŋmɔ lɛ mli akafee nɔ ni egbɔ dani manyɛ madu dumɔwui bibii lɛ?

english: Clearing all old vegetation gives young crop transplants direct sunlight and removes competing root networks that would otherwise steal fertilizer and water from your new crop.
ga: Tsei momoi fɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha tsei bibii lɛ aná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. ni ojie shishifãi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ ni baanyɛ aju ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu kɛjɛ onibii heei lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plant turn yellow and fall off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry periods to save water. It is a natural survival trick to prevent water loss, and the plant will sprout fresh green leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Eji adebɔɔ mli wala yibiiwoo he ŋaa ni akɛtsiɔ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ naa. Ni tsei lɛ baakwɛ baai heei eŋɔli kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their small flowers before they turn into full pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Mɛi enyiɛ dani ebatsɔ pod ni eyi obɔ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers but can only support a small percentage of them to full growth. The tree drops excess flowers so it can direct its energy to growing strong, healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi fã bibioo ko pɛ abaanyɛ adu. No dani ebaada kwraa. Tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine lɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ awo fɔfɔi ni mli wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key plant food. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or adding well-rotted animal manure will turn the leaves green again.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmã nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji tso lɛ niyenii titri. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits crack open at the bottom right before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ miitswa yɛ shishigbɛ tɔ̃ɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato fruits crack when there is a sudden heavy watering or rainfall after a dry period. The inside of the fruit grows faster than the skin can stretch, causing the skin to split open.
ga: Tomato aduawai lɛ tswaa kɛ́ akɛ nu wo mli loo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa trukaa yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋshɔŋloo lɛ fãa.

english: Yes, planting cassava and maize together works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested in about three months, leaving plenty of space and time for the cassava to expand later.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ aaafee nyɔji etɛ mli. Enɛ haa gbɛ kɛ be babaoo baaha ŋmei lɛ agbɛ ashwã sɛɛ mli.

english: If I plant my corn seeds very close together, will I get a bigger harvest?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani manyɛ makpa babaoo?
