english: No, planting too closely causes the corn stalks to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in tall, weak plants with very small cobs. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to yield larger cobs.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei kakadaji ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmeii bibii waa yɔɔ mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why shouldn't I apply my fertilizer right before a heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains will wash away the fertilizer into gutters and nearby streams before your crop roots have a chance to soak it up, wasting your hard-earned money.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa nubui kɛ faai ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli. dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baaná hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔ lɛ Ehaa ofiteɔ oshika ni okɛtsu nii waa lɛ.

english: Why do weeds always seem to grow faster and stronger than my planted crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that are naturally adapted to compete aggressively for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Planted crops are softer and need active protection from weeds to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Tsei lɛ yɛ mlɛo fe tsutsu lɛ ni ehe miihia ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ jwɛi ahe koni amɛshwere.

english: Why shouldn't I just save corn seeds from my harvest to plant again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni jɛ kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid corn crops lose their strength and vigor in the second generation, leading to lower yields and weaker plants. Buying fresh hybrid seeds each season guarantees higher yields and disease resistance.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa mli lɛ baafite hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Dumɔwui heei ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he lɛ ni aheɔ daa afi lɛ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ yibiiwoo babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ helai.

english: What causes tiny holes in the leaves of my cabbage crop?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Mi-kaabeji lɛ baai lɛ anɔ

english: Tiny holes in cabbage leaves are usually caused by small caterpillars like the diamondback moth larvae, which feed on the leaves after hatching from eggs laid by small moths. Using proper organic or targeted sprays helps keep them away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii, tamɔ diamondback moth lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ kaabii baai amli lɛ baa. ni yeɔ baai lɛ beni ejɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ afɔfɔi amli lɛ sɛɛ Kɛ akɛ tsofa ni sa loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ he lɛ tsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ he.

english: Why do my crops struggle to grow when I plant them late around September instead of the main rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ beni midu amɛ yɛ September naagbee gbɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Late planting means your crops miss the steady rains needed to establish strong roots. As the dry season approaches, soil moisture drops quickly, leaving young plants without enough water to absorb essential nutrients.
ga: Dumɔ ni ooodu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. Kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ba lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ baa shi oya. Enɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛnu niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: Should I plant my entire farm at the same time, or is it better to plant in different phases?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ shikome loo madu yɛ bei srɔtoi amli?

english: Planting in phases, or staggered planting, spreads out your risk against unpredictable weather or pest outbreaks. It also ensures you harvest at different times, giving you a continuous food supply and steady market income.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli loo dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yaa hiɛ nɔ lɛ gbɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ he oshara lɛ eshwaa. Ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa nii yɛ bei srɔtoi amli hu. Ehaa onáa niyenii ni yaa nɔ kɛ jarayeli shika ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ.

english: Does the size of the stem cutting or sucker I plant affect how fast the crop grows?
ga: Ani bɔ ni tso lɛ shishifã loo sucker ni miduɔ lɛ da ha lɛ saa bɔ ni tso lɛ daa oya lɛ he?

english: Yes, larger stems or suckers store more energy and nutrients, which allows them to sprout and establish roots much faster than smaller ones during the initial weeks.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ashishifãi loo tsei ashishifãi wuji lɛ kɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii babaoo toɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi oya fe tsei bibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do traditional crop varieties behave differently from the new hybrid seeds I buy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ blema tsei srɔtoi lɛ feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee hybrid ni miheɔ lɛ?

english: Traditional varieties are naturally adapted to local conditions and can handle poor soils or dry spells better, but they often grow slower. Hybrid seeds are bred for fast growth and high yields, though they require more water and fertilizer.
ga: Kusum nifeemɔi srɔtoi lɛ ji nɔ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe kɛyaa he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shihilɛi anɔ. ni ebaanyɛ etsu shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo nugbɔshiimɔ bei ahe nii jogbaŋŋ Shi amɛfɔɔ dalɛ blɛoo. Akwɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee hybrid koni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Eyɛ mli akɛ nakai dumɔwui lɛ biɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo moŋ.

english: Why is it beneficial to plant plantains alongside my young cocoa or coffee trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ makwɛ plantains yɛ mi cacao loo kɔfi tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young tree crops have sensitive leaves that burn in direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with broad leaves that provide natural shade and hold moisture in the soil, helping the young trees survive.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism. Plants roll their leaves during peak heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, which helps prevent water from evaporating out of the plant.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tsei lɛ baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ baaye abua ni nu akajɛ tso lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava and yam plants produce large green leaves but very small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava kɛ sweet potato lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ shi amɛmli ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: This usually happens when the soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium or phosphorus. Excessive nitrogen pushes the plant to grow leaves and stems instead of storing energy in the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium loo phosphorus ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ tsirɛɔ tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ

english: What happens if I plant my seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: When crops are crowded, their roots and leaves compete directly for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This causes the plants to grow tall, thin, and weak, resulting in smaller yields.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe waaa ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Why do weeds always seem to grow faster and stronger than the food crops I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe niyenii tsei ni miduɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that have adapted over centuries to survive in tough soils with minimal water. Their aggressive roots absorb nutrients faster than cultivated crops, allowing them to shoot up quickly.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ kɛ nu fioo pɛ mli. Amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei lɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa oya.

english: Why do some of my seeds rot in the soil without sprouting after a heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛkwɛɛɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need oxygen as well as water to germinate. When heavy rain leaves the soil completely waterlogged, air gets trapped out of the ground, causing the seeds to drown and rot before they can sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ nu koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu yiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa. Aheɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves start turning yellow and dropping off during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants dislike too much water sitting around their roots and on leaves. Excessive moisture creates high humidity that encourages fungal diseases like blight, which turns leaves yellow and rots the plant.
ga: Tomato tsei sumɔɔɔ nu babaoo ni bɔleɔ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ ahe. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine lɛ haa fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo baa ni woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ blight he hewalɛ, ni no haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehaa tso lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my growing tomatoes turning black and soft before they even turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni midu lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani efeɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the tomato plant cannot absorb enough calcium from the soil or experiences irregular watering while the fruit is developing.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa beni tomato tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo amɛna nu ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ.

english: How do I know when my onions are fully grown and ready to be harvested from the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-onions lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Onion plants signal they are mature when their green tops naturally fall over and start turning brown. When about half the plants in your field have flopped over, the bulbs under the ground have finished growing and are ready to harvest.
ga: Onion tsei lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛdara beni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛbɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Beni tsei ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aaafee fã eba shi lɛ. Amrɔ nɛɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ edara kwraa, ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa.

english: Why do my onions stay as small as marbles instead of swelling up big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-onions lɛ dalɛ tamɔ marble yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni efuu ni efuu lɛ?

english: Onions need space and soft, loose soil to expand. If you plant them too close together or in hard, packed soil, their roots and bulbs cannot push outward to grow large.
ga: Onions he miihia he ko kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni egbɛ eshwa koni egbɛ eshwa. Kɛji odu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ, Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛhe ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ atsi kɛya kponɔgbɛ koni amɛdara.

english: Why is my maize plant growing very tall with dark green leaves, but the cobs remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ daraa babaoo ni amɛyɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa lɛ? Shi ŋmei lɛ ji bibioo kwraa lolo.

english: This usually happens when maize gets too much nitrogen from fertilizer or manure but lacks phosphorus. Nitrogen makes the leaves and stalk grow big, but phosphorus is needed to develop strong, full cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ ŋmãa nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ kɛjɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa mli shi ebɛ phosphorus. Nitrogen haa baai kɛ tsei ashishifãi kwɛ̃ɔ. Shi fɔsfɔs he miihia koni ŋmeii ni he wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Does my maize crop need full sunlight all day, or can I plant it under big shady trees?
ga: Mi ŋmãa lɛ he miihia hulutsoo gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ loo abaanyɛ adu yɛ tso agbo ko ni yɔɔ hulutsoo shishi.

english: Maize requires direct, full sunlight for at least six to eight hours a day to produce food and grow cobs. Planting maize under heavy shade makes the stalks tall and weak, resulting in very low yields.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he miihia ŋmãa ŋmɛlɛtswai enumɔ kɛyashi kpaanyɔ daa gbi koni enyɛ ená niyenii ni ekɛ ŋmãa lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ adu ŋmã yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa shishi lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee shɔŋŋ ni amɛgbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dark powder inside the center leaf funnel?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ mi-abele baai bibii lɛ amli ni eshi powda ni tsuɔ yɛ baa lɛ mli ŋmei lɛ mli yɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central funnel of young maize plants during the day, feeding on tender leaves and leaving behind droppings.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ni amɛshiɔ ŋmeii lɛ amɛshwieɔ amɛsɛɛ.

english: What is the best time of the year to plant maize in Ghana to get a good harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ Ghana koni ená yibiiwoo kpakpa?

english: Maize performs best when planted right at the start of the major rainy season (usually around April in southern Ghana) or at the start of the minor rainy season (around September) so the crops receive enough water throughout their growth.
ga: Abɛi tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli. (bei pii lɛ, aaafee April yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ) loo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be fioo lɛ shishijee mli. (aaafee September mli) koni tsei lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛdalɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Can I plant tomatoes and onions together on the same plot of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tomato kɛ sabolai yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, tomatoes and onions grow very well together. The strong scent of onion plants acts as a natural deterrent against many insect pests that normally attack tomato plants.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tomato kɛ onion feɔ ekome kɛkwɛɔ jogbaŋŋ waa. Sabala mli ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni tsiɔ kooloi babaoo ni fɔɔ tomato tsei lɛ atutua lɛ anaa.

english: How can I improve my soil so my vegetable crops grow well without spending lots of money on commercial fertilizers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ bɔni afee ni mi-vegetables lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni mikɛ shika babaoo akawo jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: You can enrich your soil naturally by adding decomposed animal manure or plant compost, and by rotating your vegetables with legumes like cowpeas, which put vital nitrogen nutrients back into the dirt.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha oshikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ kooloi ashishifã loo tsei ashishifã ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. Ni kɛtsɔ o-vegetables lɛ ni okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ cowpeas, ni kɛ nitrogen nibii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle too much direct sunlight and heat during the Harmattan or dry season. Without enough shade from nurse crops like plantains or shade trees, the heat dries out the leaves, causing them to turn yellow and fall.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ fe nine kɛ dɔlɛ nɔ yɛ harmattan loo hulutsoo be mli. Kɛji hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ nurse tsei tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli lɛ Dɔlɛ baaha baai lɛ agbi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: Why is my maize crop turning yellow from the bottom leaves upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ baai lɛ ashishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing from the bottom leaves upward is usually a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a key nutrient for crop growth. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or Urea around the root zone helps bring back the green color and increase yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo urea ni akɛbaafata he Shishifã lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do agricultural officers encourage me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ woɔ mi hewalɛ koni madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-ŋmei lɛ duɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil and feeds your maize crop, reducing the need for expensive chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ehaa o-corn tsei lɛ niyenii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: How does covering my soil with dry leaves or grass help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baa loo jwɛi ni egboi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Covering soil with organic matter, called mulching, prevents the hot sun from drying out ground moisture, keeps the roots cool, stops weeds from growing, and decomposes into rich plant food over time.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛfiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ tsei niyenii babaoo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long, especially in flat land or heavy soil during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows water to drain away, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu shwie shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Titri lɛ, yɛ hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ wa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for their growing tubers underground. Staking lifts the foliage off the hot ground, allows maximum light exposure, prevents leaf diseases, and leads to bigger yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni anáa la babaoo. Tsi baa helai anaa ni ekɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji baa

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat holes in the central leaves of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworms, a common pest that lays eggs inside the whorl of young maize plants. Controlling them early using recommended pesticides or local remedies like neem extracts prevents them from destroying the growing shoot.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ. Ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo maŋ lɛ mli tsofai tamɔ neem mli nu lɛ atsu nii kɛye amɛnɔ mra. Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips, mites, or aphids that damage leaves and spread plant viruses. Spraying the plants with neem oil or targeted insecticides keeps these insects away and keeps leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, mites loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Enɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ ni egbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ko ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ amɛhe, ni ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when soil moisture fluctuates too much or when daytime temperatures get extremely hot. Keeping the soil evenly watered and providing light shade during extreme heat helps flowers stay on and develop into fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake fe nine loo kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ mli edɔ waa. Kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu daa ni aha lɛ hulutsoo yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why should I prune or cut off extra shoots growing around my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ loo mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Extra suckers steal water, soil food, and sunlight from the main plantain tree. Leaving only one main tree, one medium follower, and one small shoot ensures the plant directs its energy into producing large, heavy bunches.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Tso titri kome pɛ ni eshiɔ Kɛ sɛɛnyiɛlɔ kome ni dalɛ ji mlɛbo kɛ tso bibioo kome lɛ, tso lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands of flowers, but natural insects like midges can only pollinate a small fraction of them. If a flower is not properly pollinated, it dies and drops off the tree naturally within a day or two.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi adebɔɔ mli kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii baanyɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ mɛi fioo ko pɛ kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Fɔfɔi lɛ baagboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛbaagbee shi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ mli.

english: Hand pollination is when you manually transfer pollen from one flower to another using a small brush or tool. This guarantees that more flowers get fertilized compared to relying on insects alone, resulting in far more pods on each tree.
ga: Nine ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ ji be mli ni okɛ onine shwieɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ kɛtsɔ brɔsh loo dɛŋdade bibioo ko nɔ. Enɛ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ abaawo fɔfɔi babaoo kɛ akɛto kooloi bibii pɛ ni akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso fɛɛ tso yɛ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when exposed to direct heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that dry out very quickly under harsh sunlight. They need shade crops like plantain or shade trees to cover them and keep the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya waa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei koni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: If I cut off surplus branches from my mature cocoa trees, will that lower my total harvest?
ga: Kɛji mifo niji ni fa fe nine ni jɛ kookoo tso ko ni eda lɛ mli lɛ, Ani enɛ baaha mi nibii fɛɛ ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ aba shi?

english: No, regular pruning actually increases your yield. Removing extra or weak branches allows the tree to send its water and nutrients directly to pod growth, while also improving airflow to stop diseases.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni oookpa daa lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni owoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Niji ni fa fe nine loo ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ tsɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ koni helai akpa.

english: This rot is caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads quickly when cold rainwater sits on pods in dense, shady farms. Reducing farm humidity through pruning helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nu ni mli ejɔ ba shi yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ amli. Nibii ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ tsei ni afoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn yellow and droop during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When water in the soil becomes scarce, cocoa trees naturally drop or yellow their leaves to protect themselves. This reduces water loss through the leaves so the main stem and roots can survive until the next rain.
ga: Kɛ nu faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe. Enɛ haa nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi titri lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ ni baa lɛ.

english: Why should I avoid planting my cocoa trees very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ adumɔ he koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When trees are planted too close, their roots fight over the same soil nutrients and water, while their tops block sunlight from reaching lower branches. This leaves you with weak trees that produce fewer pods overall.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tso shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ yiteŋgbɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa onáa tso ko ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ miinɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing root systems that steal food and fertilizer from the soil before your main crop can absorb it, leaving your crops starved of essential nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli dani oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa otsei lɛ bɛ.

english: A pod is fully mature when its outer shell changes completely from green to yellow (or from red to orange-yellow). Picking pods before this color change means the beans will be underdeveloped, while leaving them too long causes beans to germinate inside.
ga: Akɛ ŋmeii lɛ daraa kwraa kɛ́ kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ batsɔ eŋɔli kwraa kɛtee ŋmɔŋ. (loo kɛjɛ red kɛtee yellow-orange) Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛtsake amɛhe lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ eshɛko he lolo. Yɛ be mli ni ashiɔ lɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ mli.

english: Why do some cocoa trees yield heavy pods every year while others on the same farm give very little?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei komɛi woɔ ŋmeii ni tsii daa afi lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ?

english: Trees produce differently based on their age, genetic variety, access to sunlight, and soil fertility. Older or diseased trees produce less, while younger, well-fed, and pollinated trees yield the heaviest pods.
ga: Tsei lɛ ayibii sɔrɔtoi yɛ afii ni amɛye lɛ naa. genetic diversity nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii Tsei ni egbɔ loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ baawo yibii fioo. yɛ be mli ni tsei bibii lɛ yeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ Ni pollination baaha ŋmeii ni tsii fe fɛɛ lɛ aba.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn green and healthy soon after I apply plant medicines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ tso tsofa tsu nii lɛ?

english: Agrochemicals often contain nutrients like nitrogen or specific active ingredients that kill hidden pests and diseases, allowing the plant to absorb food easily and produce chlorophyll, which makes the leaves look bright and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, niyenii mli nibii tamɔ nitrogen loo nibii pɔtɛɛ ni tsuɔ nii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni egbeɔ kooloi kɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ yɛ agrochemicals mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛheɔ niyenii oya ni amɛfeɔ klorofil. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell if a plant medicine sold in the market is safe and real for my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsei ahe tsofai ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni amɛji anɔkwale kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Authentic plant medicines have official registration numbers from regulatory bodies on the label, clear usage instructions, factory-sealed caps, and are sold by licensed agricultural dealers.
ga: Tsofai ni jɛ tsei amli diɛŋtsɛ lɛ yɛ nɔmba ni jɛ nitsumɔhe ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ yɛ nɔ ni aŋmala nɔ lɛ nɔ. Gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni kɔɔ bɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii ahaa Akɛ tsɔne lɛ naa kɛjɛ nitsumɔhe lɛ. ni okwaayeli mli jarayelɔi ni aha amɛ hegbɛ lɛ hɔ̃ɔ

english: Is it safe for me to use one type of plant medicine for every disease on my farm?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tso tsofa kome baatsu nii kɛha hela fɛɛ hela ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: No, different plant medicines are formulated for specific issues—fungicides target fungi, insecticides kill insects, and herbicides clear weeds—so using the wrong one can damage your crops or waste your money.
ga: Dabi, afee tsei ahe tsofai babaoo kɛha naagbai pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni gbeɔ ŋmeii. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ gbeɔ kooloi. Ni tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ gbeɔ jwɛi, no hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛtsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite onibii loo efite oshika.

english: Why are my crops struggling to yield as much food now compared to previous years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miitao ni amɛná niyenii babaoo tamɔ afii ni eho lɛ?

english: Continuous farming on the same land drains essential soil nutrients over time, and shifts in weather patterns create heat and water stress that reduce overall crop productivity unless the soil is restored.
ga: Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. ni tsakemɔi ni baa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi amli lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ kɛ nu he haomɔ baa. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ aba shi. ja aku sɛɛ atsake shikpɔŋ lɛ

english: Why do my crop leaves curl up during the hot afternoon even when the soil has some moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ?

english: When the sun is very hot, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it, so they curl their leaves to reduce exposure to the sun and conserve water.
ga: Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu nu he.

english: Why does heavy rain cause the roots of my crops to rot and turn dark?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air in the soil to breathe; when heavy rain floods the land for days, it pushes out all the air, suffocating the roots and allowing water-loving fungi to cause rot.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu gbii babaoo lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baatswa kwraa. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni sumɔɔ nu lɛ fiteɔ

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow when weeds grow close to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jwɛi bɛŋkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital nutrients like nitrogen, sunlight, and water directly from the soil surrounding your maize, leaving the maize starving and unable to stay dark green.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, hulu la, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle o-ŋmã lɛ he lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ ni enyɛɛɛ ehiɛ eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in cool, damp, and overly shaded conditions, spreading quickly when rain water drops linger on the pods for too long.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ hulutsoo babaoo. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nu lɛ hi ŋmeii lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Why should I change the type of crop I plant on my piece of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ daa afi lɛ?

english: Rotating different crops breaks the life cycles of pests and soil diseases while helping to balance soil nutrients, keeping the land fertile and preventing severe pest outbreaks.
ga: Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ fiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ashihilɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔshi nii ni etsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni naa wa ni baa lɛ anaa

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before producing fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or lack of insect pollinators, as the plant conserves energy to survive rather than make fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo kooloi ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ faaa Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tomato tsei lɛ buɔ hewalɛ koni amɛhi shi moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from direct sunlight and harsh winds. Without shade plants like plantain or shade trees nearby, the hot sun burns the delicate young leaves and dries out the moisture in the plant.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ. Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ shãa baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni egbiɔ nu ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning pale yellow starting from the tips, even though rain is falling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛyitseiaŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize relies on to grow green and strong. Water alone cannot make the plant grow well if the soil nutrients have been exhausted.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ŋmãa damɔɔ nɔ koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehe wa Nu pɛ nyɛŋ aha tsei akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my land help my next crop grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, creating natural plant food for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli tsei niyenii baa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Too much rain fills up air spaces in the soil with water, which starves the roots of oxygen and promotes fungal growth, causing the mature cassava roots to rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yiɔ kɛ nu. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daa. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi ni eda kwraa lɛ baagboi.

english: Why do my plantain plants keep falling over when the fruit bunches grow large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miigbee shi be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Plantain roots do not grow very deep into the ground. When the heavy fruit bundle develops, the weight pulls the shallow root system out of soft, moist soil unless the stem is supported with a wooden pole.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛ aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ, Muji lɛ gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ anɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ ni edɔ. ja tso ko fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to make energy and produce big tubers underground. Staking raises the leaves off the damp ground toward the sun and protects them from ground diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking baatsɔɔ baai lɛ gbɛ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛya hulu la lɛ he, ni ebaabu amɛhe kɛjɛ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper and tomato plants drop off without forming fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Extremely high heat or sudden dry spells stress the plants, causing the pollen to dry up so the flowers cannot form fruit and simply drop off.
ga: Dɔlɛ babaoo loo ŋmɔlɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa pollen ni egbi lɛ baa. No hewɔ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ wooo yibii ni amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow thin and weak even when I use good seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui kpakpai tsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients from the soil before your crop roots can absorb them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites feeding on the leaf juices and spreading plant viruses that stunt leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ amli nu kɛ tsei amli helai ni tsiɔ baai lɛ anaa lɛ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why should I not apply chemical fertilizer when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ efataaa he beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve so plant roots can absorb it. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn the crop's roots and waste the input.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni eha nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ afite.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive direct, harsh sunlight when they are small. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees to shelter them and keep the moisture in the soil until their roots become strong.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ beni amɛji bibii lɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo. Koni ekɛ wɔɔhe aha ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baawa.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry periods to save water and prevent themselves from drying out completely. Once the rainy season starts, the plant will sprout new leaves and continue growing.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛkagbi kwraa. Kɛji akɛ ebote nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the main food plants use to build green leaves, so adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will help restore their green color.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why is it harmful to burn all the cut bushes and weeds on my land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mashã tsei kɛ jwɛi fɛɛ ni afo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the organic material that feeds the soil and kills beneficial insects and micro-organisms. Leaving cleared grass to decompose naturally enriches the soil and retains moisture for your crops.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni haa sũ lɛ hewalɛ, ni egbeɔ kooloi bibii kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ oha jwɛi lɛ fite yɛ ehe diɛŋtsɛ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha ŋmɔlɔ ahi shi kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas in the same field alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli yɛ ŋmei masɛi?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas capture natural nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil. This enriches the ground and provides extra nutrients for your maize without requiring as much store-bought fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa niyenii krokomɛi fataa o-ŋmãa lɛ he ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ŋmɔlɔ babaoo ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ awo mli.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn black and soft when I flood the garden with water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato aduawai lɛ ashishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Irregular or excessive watering damages root health and prevents the plant from absorbing calcium from the soil. This nutrient shortage causes the bottom of the tomato fruit to rot before it ripens.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ be fɛɛ be loo ni akɛhaa fe nine lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ ahewalɛ, ni ehaaa tsei lɛ aná calcium ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ nɛɛ haa tomato shishi lɛ fiteɔ dani ekwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking lifts the leaves into the air and sunlight while keeping them safe from pests and ground rot.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ aya ŋwɛi kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛya hulu la lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha ehi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ahe.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the inside leaves of my young corn stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ daraaa lɛ? Koni maye mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ amli baai lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the soft growing center of corn plants. Treating them early with approved remedies prevents them from destroying the plant before it can grow leaves and ears.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni tsɔɔ hei ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ. Amɛtsamɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsamɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, atsĩɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite tsei dani amɛkwɛ baai kɛ toi.

english: Why do crops grown from saved hybrid seeds yield far less grain than the original seed packet I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ mli lɛ woɔ dumɔwui fioo kwraa fe shishijee dumɔwui akui ni mihe lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to give a high yield only in their first generation. Seeds saved from that harvest lose those special traits, resulting in smaller crops and weaker plants the following season.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ baa yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Too many suckers compete with the main stem for food, water, and sunlight. Removing extra suckers leaves only the strongest shoots, ensuring the main plant grows large and produces heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Suckers babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la. Suckers ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ eshwɛɔ. Enɛ ji koni tso titri lɛ adara ni ewo dumɔwui babaoo.

english: Why are many of my young crop seedlings dying in the field just a few days after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ ateŋ babaoo miigboi yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni midu amɛ lɛ?

english: Young seedlings often suffer from transplant shock or attack by soil fungi and pests if they are planted too abruptly. Hardening them in partial shade first, keeping the soil moist, and planting during cool hours help them survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei bibii lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ be mli ni amɛduɔ amɛhe lɛ hewɔ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa amɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ trukaa tsɔ. Amɛhe ni oooha amɛwa yɛ hulutsoo be mli klɛŋklɛŋ Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Ni dumɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: Why do I need to remove some healthy seedlings and space them out instead of letting them all grow together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ni mikɛ amɛ abɔ he lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha amɛfee ekome kɛdara lɛ

english: When crops grow too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, making all of them small and weak. Spacing them out allows each plant enough room and food to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ. Gbɛ ni kã tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa tsei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: How can I move some of my crop plants to another part of the field without killing them in the process?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ majie miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi kɛya ŋmɔ lɛ fã kroko ni migbeee amɛ yɛ nifeemɔ lɛ mli?

english: To safely relocate plants, dig around the roots to keep the surrounding ball of soil intact, move them during the cool late afternoon, and water them immediately after replanting to protect the roots from drying out.
ga: Bɔni afee ni okɛ tso lɛ aya he kroko shweshweeshwe lɛ, gbee shishifãi lɛ ahe koni muji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ akafite. Tsi amɛ yɛ shwane mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ni okɛ nu awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni okɛ amɛ ewo mli ekoŋŋ lɛ koni shishifãi lɛ akagbi.

english: How can I tell if my crops are dying from a disease or if they are just hungry for soil nutrients?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ helai miigbe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ loo hɔmɔ miiye amɛ kɛkɛ akɛ amɛmiitao niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Nutrient deficiency usually causes uniform yellowing across older leaves, whereas diseases typically cause dark spots, powdery patches, slimy rot, or sudden wilting on specific parts of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ haa baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tamɔ amɛhe. Yɛ be mli ni helai srɔtoi Bei pii lɛ ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Eji he ko ni tamɔ powder, ni egbo, loo ni egbo trukaa yɛ tso lɛ fã pɔtɛɛ ko nɔ.

english: If my crops are already infected and drying up, will spraying medicine bring them back to life?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ etsɔ hela momo ni amɛmiigbi hu? Ani tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei aná wala?

english: Most crop medicines protect healthy plants or stop early infections, but once a plant's internal tissues are destroyed by severe sickness, medicine cannot bring it back to life. Dead or heavily infected plants should be removed so they do not infect others.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛ tsofai tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ ateŋ babaoo buɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe loo amɛkpaa hela ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ eshishijee mli. Shi beni tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ fiteɔ yɛ hela ni naa wa hewɔ lɛ. Tsofai nyɛŋ aha tsei aba wala mli ekoŋŋ. Esa akɛ ajie tsei ni egboi loo ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ waa lɛ koni akagbɛ hela lɛ ashwã mɛi krokomɛi anɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow while the leaves at the top stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baa lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves mean the plant lacks nitrogen. Maize plants move nitrogen from their older lower leaves up to feed the new growing leaves at the top when the soil does not have enough fertilizer.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen. Abɛi tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up during the hot afternoon even when the soil has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Plants roll or curl their leaves in intense afternoon heat to reduce surface exposure and prevent water from evaporating too quickly from their leaves. It is a natural protection mechanism against high heat.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ loo amɛfoɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ shwane mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni baa lɛ aba shi ni nu akajɛ baa lɛ mli oya tsɔ. Eji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hulutsoo ni fe nine naa.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of specific nutrients like calcium and boron, causing the plant to save its energy rather than produce fruit.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli daa loo niyenii pɔtɛɛ tamɔ calcium kɛ boron ni bɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ buɔ hewalɛ he yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Planting the same crop continuously exhausts specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and soil-borne diseases that attack that crop to multiply in the soil over time.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni amɛshwere yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why should I prune or cut off extra side shoots from my crops instead of letting them grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo loo majie sɛɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha etsɔ agbo lɛ

english: Cutting off extra non-fruiting branches focuses the plant's energy and food into growing bigger leaves, flowers, and fruits rather than wasting energy on useless growth.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine ni yibii bɛ mli lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii lɛ yaa baai, fɔfɔii, kɛ aduawai ni daraa lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ dalɛ ni he ehiaaa lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: How many years can my cocoa tree keep producing pods before it becomes too old?
ga: Afii enyiɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ baanyɛ awo ŋmɔtɔ dani egbɔ tsɔ?

english: A cocoa tree usually starts bearing pods around 2 to 3 years after planting and can remain productive for 30 to 40 years if you take good care of it through proper pruning and soil management.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 yɛ be mli ni adu amɛ lɛ sɛɛ, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo yibii afii 30 kɛyashi 40 kɛji okwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni oookpa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ.

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during dry periods to conserve water. Yellowing happens when the plant lacks enough moisture or sunlight protection, so providing shade trees helps keep them green and hydrated.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Yellowing baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo hulu hebuu ni sa. No hewɔ lɛ, hulutsoo ni oooha lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does my cocoa tree produce many tiny flowers, but only a few turn into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo, shi amɛteŋ fioo pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ cocoa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Many flowers drop off naturally if they are not pollinated by tiny insects called midges, or if the tree lacks water and nutrients. Reducing harsh chemical spraying during flowering helps insects pollinate more pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. aloo kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ Tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛshwieɔ shi yɛ fɔfɔii amli lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kooloi bibii babaoo feɔ fɔfɔii lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need big shade trees to grow well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso agbo he hiaa mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to harsh, direct sunlight. Shade trees act like umbrellas, keeping the ground cool and moist while protecting young leaves from burning.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ ni ebuɔ baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he.

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava or plantain together with my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni akɛ kookoo tsei ewo mli?

english: Yes, planting plantains or food crops alongside young cocoa provides helpful shade and early food for your family, but keep food crops at a reasonable distance so they do not fight with cocoa roots for soil food.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains loo niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ niyenii mra. kɛha oweku lɛ Shi ha niyenii tsei lɛ ahi he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ sa bɔni afee ni kookoo shishifãi akatswa niyenii he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot whenever heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Excess rain creates high humidity, which causes Black Pod fungus to spread quickly. Pruning overcrowded branches allows sunlight and air flow into the farm to dry off the pods and keep them healthy.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, blackpod tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Kɛ́ afo jwɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni eha amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are tiny shoots and extra branches growing at the base of my cocoa tree trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei bibii kɛ tsei niji kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi cacao tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: These shoots are called suckers. The tree grows them naturally, but they steal water and nutrients away from the main trunk, so cutting them off helps the main tree produce bigger pods.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akɛ suckers. tsei daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe Shi amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ afo amɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni eda lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: When trees are planted too close, their leaves block sunlight from each other and their roots compete for soil nutrients, resulting in tall, thin trees with lower pod yields.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Ni tsei shishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ pod yibii ni baa shi lɛ baa.

english: How do I know if the soil on my farm is missing nutrients for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa miduɔ nii?

english: If your crops grow slowly, have pale yellow leaves, or produce small fruits, the soil is low on nutrients. Adding compost or recommended fertilizers restores soil health.
ga: Kɛji otsei lɛ daraa blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. loo ewoɔ aduawai bibii Tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛwo mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How will taking part in agricultural training sessions improve what happens on my farm?
ga: Te okwaayeli he tsɔsemɔ mli ni mɔ ko kɛ ehe woɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha nɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Farmer training teaches simple modern methods—like proper tree spacing, timely pruning, and pest management—that prevent crop failure and help you harvest more pods from the same land.
ga: Okwaafoi atsɔsemɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ gbɛi ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ tsei ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ be naa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ Enɛ tsiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ naa ni ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛjɛɔ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ.

english: Can spraying strong weed killers on my farm affect my health or my ability to have children?
ga: Ani tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni tsii ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aná mihewalɛ loo nyɛmɔ ni miyɔɔ akɛ mafɔ bii lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, certain powerful farm chemicals contain toxic compounds that enter the body through skin contact or inhalation. Over time, exposure without proper protective gear can harm male reproductive organs, cause dizziness, and lead to serious long-term health problems.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai komɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ nibii ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni boteɔ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ hewolo nɔ loo mumɔ mli. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, Kɛ́ mɔ ko kɛ ehe wo mli ni ekɛ nibii ni sa ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ bɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye nuu fɔmɔ nii lɛ awui. ni kɛ tsitsi ni tsɔɔ mɔ he shoo baa ni ekɛ helai ni mli wa ni heɔ be kakadaŋŋ baa.

english: Why do I get dizzy and short of breath whenever I mix liquid farm chemicals in a bucket?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minuɔ he akɛ mihe feɔ mi shoo ni mihe feɔ mi gas be fɛɛ be ni mikɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai ni ji nu baafutu tanki lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Strong liquid pesticides and weedicides give off chemical fumes. Breathing in these vapors directly sends toxins into your lungs and bloodstream, which causes dizziness, headaches, and chest tightness.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi kɛ jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ jieɔ tsofa lasu. Kɛ́ mɔ ko mu nɛkɛ lasu nɛɛ mli lɛ, ekɛ tsofai fɔji tsuɔ nii kɛyaa fɛ̃i kɛ lá mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa mɔ tsui fãa, eyitso fãa ni etsitsi shwieɔ shi.

english: How can I store leftover liquid pest medicines safely around my home?
ga: Mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni ji nu ni eshwɛ lɛ toɔ he fɛɛ he. Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ahi shia shweshweeshwe?

english: Always keep liquid chemicals in their original containers with clear labels inside a locked shed or box, far away from children, animal feed, and domestic water sources to avoid accidental poisoning.
ga: Kɛ tsofai ni ji nu lɛ ato amɛ shishijee tsinsii lɛ amli ni aŋmala nɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ greenhouse loo adeka ni aŋã mli. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ gbekɛbii, kooloi aniyenii kɛ nu jɛɛhei ni yɔɔ shia lɛ ahe koni oshara akaye bo.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves curl up and burn after I apply liquid weedicide around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshãa beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ ebɔle kookoo baai lɛ ahe lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves have delicate tissues. If a strong liquid weedicide drifts onto them or if the mixture is too strong, the plant absorbs too much harsh chemical at once, causing leaf burn and stunted growth.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ fãji ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Kɛji tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛboteɔ mli loo kɛji akɛ nɔ ni akɛfutu lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Tsei lɛ shwieɔ tsofai ni mli wa babaoo shikome. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛdaraaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers right after I spray them for bugs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shwie shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ?

english: Spraying high concentrations of liquid chemical spray, especially during the hottest part of the day, shocks the delicate flowers and causes the plant to shed them before fruit can form.
ga: Tsofai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi Titri lɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Ebaaha fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ akpokpo ni eha tso lɛ agbo dani ewo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow after I applied liquid fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mikɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Applying too much liquid fertilizer or spraying it directly on leaves during bright sunshine causes chemical scorching, which pulls moisture out of the leaves and leaves yellow or dry patches.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni mli tse babaoo wo baai lɛ anɔ loo okɛshwie baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsofa ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ aba. Enɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli ni ehaa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ loo amɛgbiɔ.

english: Is it safe to use milder, natural sprays made from neem leaves instead of heavy chemical pesticides?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni akɛ neem baai fee lɛ baatsu nii yɛ tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni mli ewo muji lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Yes, milder botanical sprays like neem act gently on crops by repelling pests slowly without leaving toxic chemical residues on your soil, burning delicate leaves, or threatening human health.
ga: Yes, stronger botanical sprays like neem act gently on crops by slowly repelling pests. without leaving toxic chemical residue on the soil Burn the delicate leaves. loo ewoɔ adesai ahewalɛ he gbeyei

english: Why does liquid spray fail to work when heavy rain falls shortly after I finish spraying my cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ tsuuu nii beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa beni ashwie ŋmei lɛ nɔ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Liquid medicines need several hours of dry weather to sink into plant leaves or pests. Rain washes the chemical off into the soil before it has time to work.
ga: Tsofa ni ji nu lɛ heɔ ŋmɛlɛtswai babaoo yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli dani eboteɔ tsei ahe baai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai amli. Nugbɔ lɛ hoɔ tsofai kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani enáa be ni ekɛtsu nii.

english: How do I know if the liquid medicine I bought is too concentrated for my crop seedlings?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu ni miheɔ lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ mitso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ tsɔ?

english: If seedlings show dark spots, rapid wilting, or yellowing tips within 24 to 48 hours of spraying, the solution was too strong and needs to be diluted with more clean water.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hei ni tsuɔ, amɛgboiɔ oya, loo amɛyitsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 24 kɛyashi 48 mli beni afɔ amɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsofa lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ nu tsɔ ni ehe miihia ni akɛ nu ni mli tse babaoo awo mli.

english: Can I use the same knapsack sprayer for both weed killer and insect spray on my crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ sɛɛgbɛ tsɔne kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii kɛha tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi kɛ kooloi bibii fɛɛ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: It is risky because small traces of weed killer left inside the tank can kill or damage cash crops when you later spray them for insects. Always wash the sprayer thoroughly with soap and clean water multiple times before switching chemicals.
ga: Eyɛ oshara ejaakɛ tsofa bibii ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni eshwɛ yɛ tanki lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ agbe loo efite shika ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji okɛshwie nɔ sɛɛ mli. Esa akɛ akɛ samla kɛ nu afɔ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ kɛha nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Be ni akɛtsakeɔ tsofai lɛ

english: Cocoa trees shed leaves during the dry Harmattan to conserve moisture and protect themselves from severe water loss. Leaving shade trees on your farm and spreading dry leaves around the base of the cocoa trees helps hold water in the soil and reduces heat stress.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ Harmattan hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ waa lɛ he. Shi tsei ni haa hulutsoo yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni okɛ baai ni egbi ashwã he fɛɛ he. Cocoa ŋmeii yeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa shi.

english: When too many suckers grow around one plantain stem, they compete with the main plant for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Pruning down to leaving just two or three healthy suckers allows the main plant to grow strong and produce heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ plantain kome he lɛ Amɛkɛ tsei ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso titri lɛ ni edara waa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni tsii aba.

english: What is causing small green worms to eat the leaves inside the central funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Nɔ ni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest in Ghana that targets young maize plants. Inspecting your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or chemical sprays directly into the funnels early in the morning or late evening will control them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ anɔ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ baakudɔ enɛɛmɛi.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies, which can also pass viruses to the plant. Spraying the plants with neem leaf extract or appropriate insecticide keeps these pests away and lets new leaves grow healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies kɛ chili baa baa. ni baanyɛ agbɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ashwã tsei amli Kɛ́ akɛ neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ akabote tsei amli ni eye ebua baa heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the ground, this naturally enriches the soil with nitrogen, which helps your maize grow greener and stronger without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ baaha nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa o-corn lɛ ni ekwɛɔ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofa babaoo awo mli tamɔ nɛkɛ.

english: How does leaving dry leaves and crop stems on top of my field help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai ni egbi kɛ tsei ashishifãi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with crop residues acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, slows down water evaporation, and prevents heavy rain from washing away the topsoil. As the leaves rot, they turn into organic fertilizer.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. ni etsĩ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ baai lɛ fite lɛ, ebafeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when it rains continuously for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe, but waterlogged soil starves the roots of oxygen and encourages fungal rots. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Shi shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ náa lɛ, ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahe hewalɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce a lot of flowers, but the flowers fall off without growing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the air gets too hot, when the plant lacks sufficient water, or when the soil lacks key nutrients like phosphorus. Keeping the soil consistently moist and applying well-balanced fertilizer encourages flowers to turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii titrii tamɔ fɔsfɔs bɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds and put long wooden stakes next to my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ kɛjɛ mihe lɛ? ni ekɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko ma sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi.

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs sunlight on its leaves to manufacture food for building big tubers underground. Staking raises the leaves off the hot ground, increases sunlight exposure, and prevents leaf diseases caused by damp soil.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni shwereɔ ni he hiaa hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni amɛkɛma shikpɔŋ shishi tsɔnei wuji. Staking baajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ, ebaaha hulu la aya hiɛ, ni ebaatsi baai helai ni shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛbaa lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my young pepper and tomato seedlings wilt and die right after I move them from the nursery bed to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seedlings experience transplant shock when moved directly into hot sunshine. Moving seedlings late in the afternoon or on a cloudy day, keeping root soil intact, and watering them immediately helps them survive the transition smoothly.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ transplant shock mli kɛji ajie amɛ kɛtee hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shwane mli loo yɛ atatu gbi nɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ koni shishifãi lɛ akafite Ni nu ni akɛwoɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsakemɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava crops take so many months before I can harvest and sell them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ heɔ nyɔji babaoo dani akpaa ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava plants need time to store energy down in their roots. In the first few months, the plant uses all its energy to grow leaves and stems, and only later does it send nutrients down to swell the tubers into large, sellable roots.
ga: Be he miihia cassava tsei koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii. Ni no sɛɛ lɛ, atsuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛyaa shi koni eha ŋmeii lɛ adara ni amɛtsɔ shishifãi wuji ni abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: How can I tell if my maize is suffering from too much heat or lack of water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-abele lɛ mli edɔ fe nine loo nu efo mli?

english: When maize gets stressed by heat and drought, its leaves will roll inward like small tubes during the hot afternoon to save moisture, and the lower leaves will turn yellow and dry up early.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo kɛ hɔmɔ miigba ŋmãa naa lɛ Ebaai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli tamɔ ŋmãa bibii. Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Bɔni afee ni eye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi lɛ Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaagbi oya.

english: Should I plant fast-growing vegetables or long-term cash crops like cocoa if I need quick income?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu aduawai ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya loo shika ni anáa be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ kookoo kɛji akɛ shika he miihia mi oya?

english: Vegetables like tomatoes and pepper mature in three to four months, giving you quick cash to pay immediate bills, while cocoa takes three to five years to produce but provides a steady income for many decades once established.
ga: Aduawai tamɔ tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwereɔ yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Ehaa onáa shika oya ni okɛwoɔ nyɔmɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, eheɔ afii etɛ kɛyashi enumɔ dani anáa kookoo. Shi ekɛ shika ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ eha afii nyɔŋmai abɔ kɛjɛ be mli ni ato shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my crops look small and pale even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe tseee eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops need food from the soil, not just water. Pale and stunted crops are usually starving for nutrients like nitrogen, which you can fix by adding decomposed animal manure or proper fertilizer to the soil.
ga: Tsei hia niyenii ni jɛ sũ lɛ mli. Jeee nu pɛ Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ ahe niyenii tamɔ nitrogen, ni obaanyɛ okɛtsu nii kɛtsɔ kooloi ashishifãi ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni okɛaawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are weeds so harmful to my growing crops if there is enough land for all of them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui kɛji miyɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ amɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive thieves. They grow faster than crops and steal the sunlight, water, and soil nutrients that your crops need to grow strong and produce big yields.
ga: Jwɛi ji julɔi ni yɔɔ basabasa. Amɛdaraa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara waa ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants turn yellow and spotty during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rain creates damp conditions where tiny fungal germs multiply quickly. Water splashing off the soil lands on the lower leaves, carrying these germs that cause spots and leaf decay.
ga: Nugbɔ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii baa. baagbɛ eshwa oya Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ gbeeɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Abuɔ lɛ akɛ eji nɔ ni kɛ helai nɛɛ ni kɛ baa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ baa.

english: Why didn't all the seeds I planted in my field sprout into healthy young plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui fɛɛ ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ edaaa ni amɛfeɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: Seeds need the right soil moisture, warmth, and planting depth to wake up. Old seeds, seeds buried too deep, or seeds planted in dry soil will fail to sprout or produce weak seedlings.
ga: Dumɔwui hia shikpɔŋ nu ni sa, dɔlɛ kɛ dumɔ mlibotemɔ koni amɛte shi. Dumɔwui momo, dumɔwui ni afu amɛ tsɔ. Aloo dumɔwui ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ ekwɛŋ loo ewoŋ dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Will planting my maize seeds very close together give me more harvest from my small land?
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui ni madu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baaye abua mi ni makpa babaoo kɛjɛ he bibioo ko. mi nɔ loo daabi

english: No, planting too close causes crops to fight each other for sunlight and soil food. This results in tall, thin plants with tiny or empty cobs instead of strong plants with big cobs.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ awu yɛ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei lɛ kwɔlɔ ni amɛhe tseee ni amɛhe tsei bibii. loo efolo Moŋ lɛ eji tso ni he wa ni ŋmei agbo yɔɔ mli.

english: Why do older farmers advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts alongside my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa ko woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts are natural soil helpers. Their roots pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps neighboring crops grow stronger without extra fertilizer costs.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo. Amɛshishifãi lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ daraa waa ni amɛheee ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: Why do my harvested grains spoil or get eaten by insects so quickly in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔi lɛ fiteɔ loo kooloi yeɔ amɛ oya yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Grains spoil when they are stored while still holding moisture, which causes mold to grow, or when storage bags are not airtight, allowing insects to enter and feed on the dry seeds.
ga: Nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ akɛto ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lolo. ni haa ŋmeii shwereɔ loo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ Enɛ haa ŋmeii baa ni amɛyeɔ dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ.

english: How do I know if the seeds I want to buy will give me a good harvest on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni misumɔɔ ni mahe lɛ baawo yibii kpakpai yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Certified seeds from registered agro-dealers are tested for high germination rates and disease resistance. Seeds saved from market food crops often produce weak plants or unpredictable yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ odaseyeli ni jɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ mli koni ana kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛnɔ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ loo amɛwoɔ yibii ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba.

english: It is best to wait until two or three heavy rains have soaked deep into the ground. Planting after the very first light rain risks the seeds drying out if a brief dry spell follows.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ asɛɛ lɛ woɔ dumɔwui lɛ agbimɔ he oshara mli kɛji akɛ be kukuoo ko ba.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my crops too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants with small fruits or ears.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai bibii loo toi lɛ baa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to grow leaves, or that heavy rain has flooded the roots and stopped them from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehe hiaa ni tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ baai Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyiɔ shishifãi lɛ amli ni ehaa amɛmuɔ.

english: Extreme heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer can stress tomato plants, causing them to drop their flowers to save energy rather than grow fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ni fa babaoo baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tomato tsei lɛ ajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and stop the plant from growing tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies feeding on the leaves and spreading plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper mli lɛ baa.

english: Cassava roots rot when planted in heavy clay soils that hold excess water during rainy seasons, encouraging fungal and bacterial diseases to attack the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli kɛ bacteria mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves off the wet ground towards sunlight, allowing the leaves to make maximum food and send energy down to grow large underground tubers.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ ni amɛtsuɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the trees before they are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tsei anɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cold, humid weather and overly shaded farms where air cannot flow freely.
ga: Fɛ̃i ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni mli edɔ waa lɛ kɛ black pod hela baa. kɛ ŋmɔji ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ atsɔ mli oya

english: Why do my maize plants fall over when a strong wind blows across the field?
