ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa kɛfo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize falls over when its root system is shallow, damaged by soil pests, or planted too close to the surface, making the stalk top-heavy.
ga: Abɛi baagbee baai lɛ kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ efite loo adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ tsɔ Ehaa tso lɛ shishi tsiimɔ waa

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plant turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Leaves usually turn yellow when the crop is hungry for nutrients like nitrogen or when there is too much water sitting around the roots. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer helps the plant make healthy green leaves again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ baai tsakeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji tsei lɛ he miihia niyenii, tamɔ nitrogen, loo kɛji nu babaoo bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant feels stressed by extreme hot weather or irregular watering. Giving the plants consistent water during hot dry spells helps the flowers stay on and turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo nu ni akɛhaaa lɛ ni ejaaa lɛ ha tsei lɛ hao. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting under the soil before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays too wet for a long time. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaves, or by viruses spread by these insects. Checking under the leaves early and using safe insect sprays can protect your plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛjɛ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi mra. Ni kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ ebu otsei lɛ ahe.

english: When plants are crowded, they compete against each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Spacing them properly gives each plant enough space and light to grow strong and produce good fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ eda ni ewo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my vegetable plants droop in the hot afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In the hot afternoon sun, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it up. They droop to protect themselves from drying out, and they usually stand back up as the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Amɛkotoɔ shi koni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. ni bei pii lɛ, eteɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, shields the ground from the hot sun so water does not evaporate quickly. This keeps the soil moist and cool for your plants' roots.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Bɔni afee ni nu akatsɔ oya Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eha otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my crops give smaller harvests when I plant the exact same crop on the same farm every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii babaoo fe be mli ni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil repeatedly and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up. Switching crops, especially planting beans or groundnuts, restores the soil.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ daa be lɛ baajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shii abɔ. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi aba. ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ Titri lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why should I remove the small side shoots and bottom leaves from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? kɛ shishigbɛ baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tomato tso lɛ mli lɛ

english: Removing small extra stems and bottom leaves prevents the plant from wasting food on useless foliage. It directs energy into growing bigger fruits and allows air to flow, which prevents leaf diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ shishifãi ni fa fe nine kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ, no haaa efite niyenii yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ. Kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛdu aduawai wuji lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli ni baanyɛ atsĩ baa helai anaa

english: Why did the leaves on my crops turn brown and dry up after I put fertilizer around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ebɔle amɛhe lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Applying too much chemical fertilizer or putting it directly against the stem burns the plant roots and leaves. Fertilizer should always be applied a small distance away from the plant stem and in recommended amounts.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ tsu nii babaoo loo okɛ tsofa wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaashã tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ fioo, ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli bɔ ni sa.

english: Why can't I just sow my crop seeds directly into the main farm field instead of keeping them in a nursery first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduuu dumɔwui tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ŋmɔji wuji lɛ amli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha amɛhi gbekɛbii akwɛmɔhe lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: A nursery acts like a nursery for human babies, keeping tender young seeds safe from harsh weather, heavy rains, and pests until they develop strong enough roots to survive out in the open field.
ga: Gbekɛbii akwɛmɔhe lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ gbekɛbii akwɛmɔhe. Amɛhaa dumɔwui bibii lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi gbohii, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi ni wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli.

english: Why do some tree seedlings need to stay in the nursery for as long as six months or a year before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni dumɔwui komɛi ahi ŋmɔ mli nyɔji enumɔ loo afi dani adu amɛ lɛ?

english: Certain crops grow slowly at first and need many months to build strong stems and deep root systems in a controlled environment so they do not die when exposed to dry weather on the main farm.
ga: Tsei komɛi daaa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni eheɔ nyɔji babaoo dani amɛnáa shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ yɛ he ko ni akudɔɔ. Enɛ ji koni tsei akagbo kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: Why do extension officers recommend putting young seedlings into individual plastic polybags in the nursery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ dumɔwui bibii awo plastic kotokui babaoo amli yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plastic polybags separate each plant's roots so they do not tangle with others, allowing you to move the plant to the main farm without breaking its fragile roots.
ga: Polybags gbalaa tso fɛɛ tso shishifãi amli koni amɛkafee ekome. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ tsei yaa oŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli ni ofiteee shishifãi ni waaa lɛ.

english: How can I tell by looking at my young plant that it is ready to be moved from the nursery to the field?
ga: Kɛ mikwɛ mi dumɔwui lɛ Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tso bibioo ko efee klalo akɛ ebaashi ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛya ŋmɔ mli?

english: Seedlings show they are ready when they develop a specific number of fully formed leaves—often three or four leaves—and reach a height where their stem feels firm rather than soft and bendy.
ga: Dumɔwui tsɔɔ akɛ amɛfee klalo kɛ́ amɛfee baai ni ebɔle amɛhe kwraa lɛ ayibɔ pɔtɛɛ ko—bei pii lɛ, etɛ loo ejwɛ—ni amɛshɛ he ko ni amɛshishifãi lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛhe wa moŋ fe bɔ ni amɛbaafee blɛoo ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my young seedlings turn yellow and wither if I leave them in full, direct sunlight all day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young seedling leaves are delicate and lack the thick outer layer that older plants have, causing them to burn and lose water faster than their small roots can absorb it.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛbɛ kponɔgbɛ fã ni mli tse tamɔ tsei bibii lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛshãa ni amɛfiteɔ nu oya fe shishifãi bibii lɛ. Abaanyɛ aŋɔ awo mli.

english: Why do baby seedlings grow so slowly above the ground during their first few months in the nursery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo ni yɔɔ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the early months, the seedling spends most of its energy building a invisible root network underground before it starts pushing out big leaves and tall stems above ground.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji lɛ amli lɛ, Seedlings kɛ amɛhewalɛ babaoo maa shishifãi ni anaaa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. dani ebɔi baai agboi kɛ tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwiemɔ

english: Why do my seedlings look weak and droopy right after I move them into the main farm soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is called transplant shock, which happens because the plant's fine root hairs get disturbed during the move, making it temporarily hard for the plant to suck up water.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Enɛ baa mli yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe yitsɔi bibii lɛ ahewɔ. ni tsei ni haoɔ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni aduɔ amɛ lɛ Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei lɛ akɛ amɛaaŋɔ nu yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: Why do small nursery seedlings need to be watered every day while big trees on my farm survive without daily rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni awo dumɔwui bibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ anɔ nu daa gbi yɛ be mli ni tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ daa gbi lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have short, shallow roots that can only reach water in the top inch of soil, while mature crops have long roots that go deep into the ground to find hidden moisture.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shɛɔ nu he yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ naagbee pɛ. Beni tso lɛ daa lɛ, ewoɔ shishifãi kakadaji ni yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛyatao ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ.

english: What special care do seeds need from me during the first few days after they sprout out of the dirt?
ga: Mɛɛ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ he hiaa dumɔwui kɛjɛ midɛŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbii fioo ni amɛje kpo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Freshly sprouted seeds need gentle shade to protect them from heat, light moisture so their tiny roots do not dry out, and protection from crawling insects that like to eat soft leaves.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ hia hulutsoo blɛoo koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Fɛ̃i fioo ko ni baaha shishifãi bibii lɛ ahi shi. Egbiii. ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi bibii ni shwereɔ ni sumɔɔ ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ahe

english: Why is it important to remove all weeds around my young crop plants as soon as they appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ehe miihia ni madu mi dumɔwui lɛ kɛji amɛje kpo pɛ.

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and will quickly steal all the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients before the baby plant's roots can get to them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya kwraa fe tsei bibii ni amɛbaaju nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya dani tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ashɛ amɛhe.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because their leaves burn easily under full sun. Leaving tall shade trees or planting fast-growing plantains next to young cocoa creates a protective leafy canopy that shelters them until they are mature enough to handle full sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ni ashiɔ loo dumɔwui ni daa oya ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni akɛ baai eha nɔ lɛ feɔ shweshweeshwe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ daa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: What will happen to my maize crop if I plant the seeds very close together so I can fit more on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni anyɛ adu babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, soil water, and nutrients. Instead of getting more harvest, you will end up with thin, weak stalks and very small ears of corn.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookpa babaoo lɛ Obaagbe naa kɛ tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa toi bibii waa.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with lots of leaves but producing small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants get plenty of rain early on, the cassava focuses its energy on growing top leaves instead of storing energy underground. Proper spacing and balanced soil nutrients encourage the plant to send strength into expanding its tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ tso lɛ babaoo mra. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei baato hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ eŋwɛi baai lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ he nii. Gbɛ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛgbala bulbs lɛ amli.

english: Why does my maize grow much better when I plant it on a plot where I previously harvested cowpeas or groundnuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ mikpaa tsina loo ŋmãa yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have roots that naturally capture nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the soil. When you harvest them, that trapped nitrogen stays behind in the soil to act as free plant food for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni okpa amɛ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsu nii akɛ tsei niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to plant my seeds when the early rains start coming?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: It is best to wait until the ground gets enough continuous rain to moisten the soil deep down, rather than planting after the very first light rain. Planting too early can cause seeds to sprout and then dry up if a hot week follows without rain.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be bɔ ni sa ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, kɛ́ odu mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbi kɛji otsi ko ni mli edɔ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants full of small ragged holes and looking chewed overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ani atse ni aye nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: This pattern of damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which hide in the central funnel of the plant during the hot day and eat the tender inner leaves. Catching them early by inspecting the leaf funnels helps save the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ jɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ amli. ni amɛye mligbɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ Mɔmɔ amɛ mra Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ agbɛi lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ ahere ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala.

english: How does planting fast-growing groundnuts between my wide cassava rows help keep weeds away?
ga: Peanut ni adu lɛ daa oya yɛ cassava ŋmɔji ni mli kwɔ lɛ ateŋ. Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eshwie jwɛi?

english: Groundnuts spread low across the ground, forming a living green carpet. This dense cover blocks sunlight from reaching the bare soil between rows, preventing weed seeds from getting the light they need to sprout and grow.
ga: Peanuts gbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ. Ebafeɔ kapɛti eŋɔli ni hiɛ kã. Nɛkɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa nɔ ni mli eyi obɔ nɛɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ aná la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdara.

english: Why are my tomato plants wilting and dying even though the soil around them has plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When a plant wilts in moist soil, it usually means tiny soil diseases have infected the stem base or roots. These germs block the inner tubes that carry water up from the soil to the leaves, causing the top of the plant to thirst even when water is present.
ga: Kɛ tsei gbo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ Bei pii lɛ enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ hela bibioo ko emɔ tso lɛ shishi loo shishifãi lɛ. Nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ tsiɔ mligbɛ tsɔnei ni kɛ nu jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛyaa baai lɛ amli lɛ anaa. Ehaa kumai yeɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ kɛji nu yɛ po.

english: Is it safe for me to let my farm animals eat fresh cassava leaves right after I harvest the tubers?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ maha ŋmɔ mli kooloi aye ŋmei baai heei amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Fresh cassava leaves and peels contain natural plant compounds that can make animals sick if eaten raw immediately after harvest. Letting the leaves dry out in the sun for a day or two breaks down these compounds, making them safe for animals to eat.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni baanyɛ aha kooloi aná hela kɛji aye amɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ yɛ cassava baai heei kɛ amɛhewolo lɛ mli. Beni akpa ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ Kɛ́ aŋmɛ baai lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ lɛ, ebaaha nɛkɛ nibii ni akɛfee nibii nɛɛ agbá. Enɛ haa efeɔ shweshweeshwe kɛhaa kooloi ni amɛyeɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience sudden stress, such as extreme heat, very dry soil, or sudden heavy rains. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch helps the plant stay stable and turn its flowers into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe trukaa nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa, loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ, ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ tsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth. Adding animal manure or a nitrogen-based fertilizer helps the plant turn green and produce healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛtsɔ eŋɔli ni eha toi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop is harvested and the roots rot, that nitrogen stays in the ground to feed the next crop, like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. When the crops are harvested and the roots rot That nitrogen remains in the soil to feed next crops, such as corn.

english: Why shouldn't I put chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ woɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Putting chemical fertilizer directly against the stem can burn the delicate skin of the plant and its tender roots. It is safer to place it in a small ring or line a few inches away from the plant.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ hewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oookɛwo ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo ko mli. Aloo okɛto he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells to save water and survive the heat. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout new leaves and continue growing its tubers underground.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi shi yɛ latsaa be lɛ mli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when temperatures get too high or when the plant doesn't get enough water. Keeping the soil consistently moist with watering and mulch helps the flowers stay on and produce tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ anine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛwo tomato.

english: Why is it better for me to water my vegetables early in the morning instead of late at night?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ nu shwieɔ mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ leebi moŋ fe gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Morning watering gives plants the water they need before the hot sun comes up. Watering at night leaves moisture on the leaves all night long, which can cause fungal diseases to spread.
ga: Nu ni oooha otsei lɛ leebi lɛ haa amɛnáa nu ni he hiaa amɛ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli gbɛkɛ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ gbɛkɛ muu lɛ fɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsɛŋemɔ helai agbɛ ashwã.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that scorch easily in full sunlight. Shading them with plantains or shade trees protects them from harsh sun and heat until they grow strong enough to withstand direct light.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he. Kɛyashi tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ekpɛlɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to build tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matswa tso kakadaŋŋ ko koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to reach sunlight so the leaves can feed the plant. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, which prevents leaf diseases and helps the plant grow larger tubers.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni baai lɛ anyɛ aye abua tso lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ foliar helai anaa ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ bulbs wuji.

english: If too many shoots grow around one plantain stem, they steal food, water, and light from each other. Pruning extra shoots leaves one or two strong stems that will yield bigger, heavier bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ ehe Plantain kome Amɛjuɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha tso kome loo enyɔ ni wa aba, ni no baaha tsei niji ni dara ni tsii lɛ aba.

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on the central leaves of young corn. Checking plants early and applying approved pest treatments inside the central funnel of the plant stops them from destroying the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ. Tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ mra ni akɛ gbɛ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atsu nii yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ akafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How do I know when it is the right time to start clearing and preparing my land for the new season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ kɛ ehe saamɔ kɛha be hee lɛ?

english: Land preparation should begin just before the main rains arrive so the soil is ready to absorb water. Clearing early allows you to plant at the very first rainfall, giving your crops the full length of the season to grow strong.
ga: Esa akɛ aje shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ shishi dani nugbɔ lɛ aba koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee klalo akɛ ebaaŋɔ nu. He ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Haa oduɔ nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ mli. Ha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ waa yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How does putting dry leaves or grass around the base of my crops help them grow?
ga: Baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mi tso lɛ shishitoo yeɔ ebuaa mi tso lɛ ni edaa tɛŋŋ?

english: This practice is called mulching. It acts like a blanket over the ground, keeping the soil cool, trapping moisture during dry spells, and stopping weeds from growing around your main crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ naa. Oŋmɔshi nibii titri

english: Why is regular weeding so important if I want my crops to produce a big harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ he hiaa waa kɛji miisumɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds act like food thieves on your farm; they steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops. When you keep the land clear of weeds, all the soil food goes directly into helping your crops yield more fruit.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Beni ohaa jwɛi bɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ Nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yaa tɛ̃ɛ koni eye ebua oŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Is spending time and money on farm maintenance really going to increase my income at the end of the season?
ga: Ani be kɛ shika ni mifiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli saamɔ mli lɛ haa shika ni mináa lɛ yaa hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ naagbee lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, regular maintenance prevents crop loss from pests and diseases and can double or triple your harvest. The extra money you make from selling a much larger crop far outweighs the cost of maintaining the land.
ga: Hɛɛ, saamɔ ni afeɔ daa lɛ baatsi ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai baafite lɛ anaa. Ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ nibii ni ofeɔ lɛ afee enyɔ loo etɛ. Shika kroko ni onáa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni da babaoo ni ohɔ̃ɔ lɛ mli lɛ fa kwraa fe shika ni okɛbaakwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do people say I should cut off some of the healthy branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ niji ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Pruning extra branches opens up the tree so sunlight and fresh air can pass through. This keeps damp diseases away and forces the tree to spend its energy growing big cocoa pods instead of extra leaves.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei krokomɛi ni abaakpa lɛ baagbele tso lɛ naa koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ mli. Enɛ tsiɔ helai ni jɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli baa lɛ anaa, ni enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi wuji moŋ fe ni ekɛ baai krokomɛi baafata he.

english: Flowers drop when the cocoa tree is under stress from drought, poor soil nutrients, or pest attacks. Protecting your trees with light shade, mulching the roots, and feeding the soil helps the tree hold onto its flowers until they mature into pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kookoo tso lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ shishi. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ehiii loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be fioo ko bu tso lɛ he, akɛha shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni akɛ niyenii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa ni etsɔɔ ŋmeii.

english: Do cocoa trees grow better under direct sun or under big shade trees?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo yɛ hulutsoo be wulu shishi?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade from plants like plantains so their soft leaves do not burn. Mature cocoa trees like light, filtered shade—too much direct sun scorches the leaves, but too much heavy shade creates damp conditions that bring fungal diseases.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei tamɔ plantains adɛŋ koni baai bibii lɛ akashã. Kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ sumɔɔ la ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo lɛ baaha baai lɛ ashã. Shi hulutsoo ni fa fe nine lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa lɛ baa.

english: What causes cocoa pods to turn completely black and dry out on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ kwraa ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: This is usually Black Pod disease, which thrives in wet, overcrowded, and shady conditions. Pruning dense branches to let air flow through, clearing weeds, and removing infected pods quickly will stop it from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji black pod hela. Eshwereɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni gbɔmɛi eyi mli obɔ, kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi. Kpãa tsei niji ni mli ewo muji lɛ ahe koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ, ni ojie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya. lɛ baatsi gbɛfaŋnɔ lɛ naa

english: How do I tell if my crops need extra food or fertilizer to yield better?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi he miihia miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai?

english: If your crop leaves turn pale yellow, the stems stay thin, or the plant grows very slowly even when there is rain, the soil lacks nutrients. Adding fertilizer or well-rotted manure feeds the roots so the crop can grow strong and bear heavy fruit.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ, tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli etse lolo. Aloo tsei daa blɛoo waa kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po. tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ adara ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: If I start taking proper care of my cocoa farm today, how long will it take before I see a bigger harvest?
ga: Kɛji mibɔi mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ ŋmɛnɛ. Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani ana nitsumɔ ni yaa hiɛ?

english: You will usually see noticeable results within about six months. Proper pruning and soil care encourage the tree to produce more healthy flowers in the next blooming cycle, leading to a much larger pod harvest later in the year.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, obaana nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ni kadiɔ mɔ yɛ aaafee nyɔji enumɔ mli. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo yɛ fɔfɔi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ ha akpa pod babaoo kwraa yɛ nakai afi lɛ naagbee gbɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps the leaves turn green and produce strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛná ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa.

english: Why do many of the flowers on my cocoa trees drop off before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo miiho dani amɛbatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers but can only support a small percentage as pods. Flowers drop if there are not enough midge insects to pollinate them, during dry spells, or when the tree reduces its load to feed only a few healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi ebaanyɛ eŋɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ. Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ midge ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee amɛ pollination lɛ bɛ. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Aloo be mli ni tso ko baa ejatsu lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ŋmeii fioo komɛi pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃.

english: How can I tell which end of a cassava stem cutting should face up when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male mi-cassava tso lɛ naagbee ni esa akɛ ekwɛ hiɛ beni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Look closely at the small buds or 'eyes' above each leaf scar along the stem—these buds should point upward toward the sky. Planting cassava stem cuttings upside down causes delayed sprouting, twisted root growth, and lower yields.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ‘ŋmei’ ni yɔɔ baa lɛ he ŋmeii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko nɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kasava tsei ni aduɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ baaha amɛkwɛ̃mɔ asɛɛ afo, shishifãi ni etsilɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking sap from the underside of leaves, or by a viral disease spread by insects. Using protective nets or spraying neem oil early helps stop the curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Okɛ tsɔne ni buɔ mɔ he loo neem fɔ ni okɛshwieɔ nɔ mra lɛ baaye abua ni ekpa oyitsɔi lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt during hot afternoons even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In intense sun, tomato leaves lose water through evaporation faster than the roots can pull water from the soil. The plant temporary wilts to shrink its leaf area and save moisture, usually bouncing back once the temperature cools in the evening.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, tomato baai lɛ laajeɔ nu yɛ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni efo baa lɛ mli ni ekɛ nu ahi shi. Bei pii lɛ, efoɔ ehe kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli ba shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to put fertilizer on my crops right before a big rain comes?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli dani nugbɔ anɛ waa?

english: No, heavy rainfall will wash the fertilizer away from your farm into streams before your crop roots have time to take it in. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after rain, or when only light rain is expected.
ga: Dabi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baajie ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛya faai amli dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aná be ni amɛkɛbaaŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. aloo be mli ni akpaa gbɛ akɛ nugbɔ fioo pɛ baanɛ

english: Why should I not save seeds from my hybrid maize harvest to plant again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn harvest lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are created by crossing specific parent plants to produce high yields only in the first generation. If you save and replant those seeds, the second generation loses that strength, resulting in uneven growth and much lower yields.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ feɔ kɛtsɔ fɔlɔi tsei pɔtɛɛ ni akɛfoɔ mli koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ pɛ mli. Kɛji obua nakai dumɔwui lɛ anaa ni odu ekoŋŋ lɛ Yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahewalɛ baaje amɛdɛŋ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa kɛ yibiiwoo baa shi kwraa.

english: Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which takes nitrogen gas from the air and converts it into natural fertilizer in the soil. The nearby maize roots feed on this extra nitrogen, improving crop growth without adding extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas ji legume weku lɛ mlinyo, ni ejieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Abɛi shishifãi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ yeɔ nitrogen ni fa fe nine nɛɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daa ni akɛ tsofai krokomɛi fataaa he.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over right when the fruit bunches grow large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛji aduawai akui lɛ dara pɛ?

english: Plantain plants do not have deep woody roots, so when heavy bunches develop, the weight makes the plant top-heavy. Prop up the stem using a strong wooden Y-stick placed under the bunch to support the weight until harvest.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni tamɔ tsei. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ fɔfɔi lɛ mli tsɔi lɛ, Muji lɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ babaoo. Kɛ tso ni wa ni tamɔ Y ni akɛwo tso lɛ shishi lɛ afi tso lɛ sɛɛ koni ekɛfi etsitsinɔnii lɛ sɛɛ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds always sprout and grow faster than my crops after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are already present in large numbers in the soil and are adapted to germinate instantly at the first sign of water. Clearing weeds early in the first few weeks prevents them from stealing sunlight and soil nutrients from young crop seedlings.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ momo. ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ nu klɛŋklɛŋ okadi lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ baatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaju hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni jɛɔ dumɔwui bibii amli lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under the hot sun. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act like umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa plants need to survive their first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why does my cassava produce smaller tubers when I plant it on the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ hiɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing cassava on the same land repeatedly drains the soil of essential nutrients without giving it time to recover, which leaves the plants with fewer resources to grow large tubers.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shii abɔ. ni ekɛ be haaa ni ekɛtsa ehe Enɛ haa tso lɛ bɛ nibii babaoo ni ekɛbaakwɛ bulbs wuji.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Maize leaves usually turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or when the soil stays waterlogged for too long, preventing the roots from taking in nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo kɛ́ nu ehi sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ anine shɛɛɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves off the ground toward the sunlight so they can make enough food to produce big tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la lɛ. Enɛ ji koni amɛná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, sudden dry spells, or a lack of water, causing the plant to save its energy to stay alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Gbimɔ ni baa trukaa, loo nu ni bɛ lɛ haa tsei toɔ hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛhi wala mli.

english: What causes the white powdery dust on the leaves of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ sũ yɛŋ ni yɔɔ tomato tsei ahe baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa?

english: That white dust is a fungal disease called powdery mildew, which spreads in warm, humid conditions when air cannot flow freely between crowded plants.
ga: Muji yɛŋ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ Be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ ateŋ oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my cowpea plants curling up and feeling sticky?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curling, sticky leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids that suck the sap from the leaves and leave behind a sugary substance called honeydew.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli ni amɛshiɔ nɔ ko ni ŋɔɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ honeydew lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni wa lɛ baa.

english: Why is it better for me to water my vegetable garden early in the morning instead of at midday?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ nu woɔ mi-aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli leebi moŋ fe gbi lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning allows the plants to drink water before the sun gets too hot, whereas midday watering causes most of the water to evaporate quickly into the air.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni enuɔ nu dani hulu lɛ mli woɔ la tsɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni ashwieɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ oya kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my main maize crop when the rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu mainstay maize kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: It is best to wait until the soil gets a few consistent heavy rains so there is enough moisture deep in the ground to nourish the seeds through their early growth.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa daa koni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná niyenii yɛ amɛdalɛ mra be mli.

english: Why should I dry my harvested maize grains thoroughly before putting them into storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbi mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ dani mikɛwo nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Drying maize completely removes dampness that attracts destructive weevils and stops mold from growing and rotting your stored crop.
ga: Abɛi ni agbiɔ lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni gbalaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ kɛbaa lɛ kwraa. ni etsĩ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato lɛ akafite.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow very fast and have large leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa plants need during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa, ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo tsei bibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Yellow lower leaves mean your maize plant lacks nitrogen. When nitrogen is low in the soil, the plant moves what little it has from its older lower leaves up to feed the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tso lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni eda ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: When cassava is mature, the plant's main stalk turns woody, lower leaves fall off leaving leaves mostly at the top, and the ground surrounding the base of the stem begins to crack as the roots swell underneath.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ eda kwraa lɛ, tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ tsɔɔ tso. Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni amɛshiɔ ŋwɛigbɛi lɛ babaoo. kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishigbɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars hiding inside the center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This pest is the Fall Armyworm. It prefers to feed inside the central whorl of young maize leaves because it is dark, moist, and safe from heat and predators while it eats the tender growing tissue.
ga: Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela nɛɛ, ni ji Fall Armyworm lɛ sumɔɔ ni eye niyenii yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋtayaai lɛ amli ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ duŋ, amɛmli edɔ, ni amɛhe bɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ ahe beni amɛyeɔ ŋmãa ni miida blɛoo lɛ.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden stakes next to my yam vines when they start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ masɛi beni ebɔi kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb toward sunlight. Staking exposes more leaves to direct sun, which allows the plant to produce more energy to grow large, healthy tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Staking haa baai lɛ naa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why does planting beans or groundnuts in my field help my maize crop grow better later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni miŋmei lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in small nodules on their roots. When the roots decay, they leave nitrogen in the soil, acts like natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ, amɛshiɔ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus on leaf growth instead of producing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai ni ebaawo lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize immediately after the very first rain of the major season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a brief dry spell. If seeds germinate right away, the soil may dry out before the regular rains return, causing the young seedlings to wither and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ agbi dani nugbɔ lɛ aku esɛɛ aba bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ. Ehaa tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why is my tomato crop growing very tall with big green leaves but no fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomatoi lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? Ani oyɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi obɛ yibii?

english: Using too much nitrogen-based fertilizer encourages leafy growth while delaying flowers and fruit. Tomato plants need more phosphorus and potassium once they mature to stimulate flowering.
ga: Nitrogen ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa baai lɛ daraa yɛ be mli ni ehaa fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Tomato tsei lɛ he miihia phosphorus kɛ potassium babaoo beni amɛdaraa lɛ koni amɛha amɛwo fɔfɔi.

english: Why does spear grass keep growing back so quickly even after I cut it down to the soil level?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ spear jwɛi lɛ daa oya nɛkɛ beni mifo lɛ kɛyashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po lɛ?

english: Spear grass has deep underground stems called rhizomes that store energy. Simply cutting the leaves on top leaves the roots alive, allowing the weed to push up fresh green leaves within days.
ga: Spear jwɛi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ ni atsɛɔ amɛ rhizomes ni kɛ hewalɛ toɔ. Kɛ́ afolɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kɛkɛ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ baa wala mli. Ha jwɛi lɛ ashɛre baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli.

english: Why does my land grow better crops after I leave it untouched for a few years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni mishi nɔ afii fioo komɛi ni mifeee nɔ ko lɛ?

english: Leaving land to rest (fallowing) allows natural wild plants to grow, drop leaves, and decay. This naturally restores essential nutrients and organic matter back into the soil, making it rich and fertile again for future crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ejɔɔ ehe (tillage) lɛ baaha koo mli tsei ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ akwɛ̃, amɛbaaji lɛ baaje mli, ni amɛgboi. Enɛ baaha niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa nii ni ehaa wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow bigger when I plant groundnuts on a field before planting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani midu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. This leaves natural soil food behind, which feeds and strengthens the maize crop planted in the next season.
ga: Peanut tsei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmãa tsei ni adu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aná hewalɛ ni ewo amɛ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under strong sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad leaf shade, keeping the young cocoa cool and moist until it grows strong enough to survive full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ baaha hulutsoo kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ. Ha kookoo bibioo lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi ebaada waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Why should I plant my cassava sticks slanted in the soil instead of standing them straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei ni mikɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mikɛwo ŋwɛi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava sticks at a slant keeps the growing points near the top surface of the soil, where nutrients and rainwater collect. This encourages the plant to produce wide, heavy tuber roots easily.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ baaha he ni edaa yɛ lɛ abɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋgbɛ. Biɛ ji he ni niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nugbɔ nu buaa ehe naa yɛ. Enɛ woɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni efee shishifãi ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsii oya.

english: Why does spread dry grass around my vegetables help them stay healthy during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) acts like a blanket that blocks the direct heat of the sun. It prevents moisture from evaporating quickly out of the dirt, keeping root zones damp and cool.
ga: Mulching ni egbi (mulching) tsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni tsiɔ hulutsoo ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekajɛ muji mli oya. Ha shishifã lɛ he lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which gives plants their rich green color. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen deep into the soil where young root systems cannot reach it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni tsuɔ waa. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms before turning into actual fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔlɔ dani amɛwoɔ aduawai diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme midday heat, irregular watering, or a lack of plant nutrients needed to nourish developing fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ tsei kɛ haomɔi, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kpe yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha aduawai lɛ adalɛ ni bɛ

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt and die when rain water sits on the field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɔ gbii babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When excess water sits around the roots without draining away, it suffocates them, causing the roots to decay and the plant to wilt.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ kpɛtɛ shishifãi ahe ni efooo lɛ Ebaagbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn thin and produce very little yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee mlɛo ni amɛmiiwo yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for the same soil food, water, and sunlight. Because weeds grow quickly, they steal these resources before your crops can absorb them to build fruit or seed.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya. No sɛɛ lɛ, amɛjuɔ nibii nɛɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ koni amɛkɛfee aduawai loo dumɔwui.

english: Why do armyworms specifically target the inside of the young maize leaf funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhiɛ fɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: The inner funnel (whorl) of a young maize plant contains the softest, most tender growing leaves rich in plant sap, making it the easiest and most nutritious feeding spot for young caterpillars.
ga: Abele tsei bibii lɛ amli gbɛjegbɛi (rings) lɛ ji baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo fe fɛɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ, ni tsei amli nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ ni ŋmei bibii lɛ yeɔ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the specific nutrients maize needs and allows pests and soil diseases that target maize to build up in the soil, leading to smaller yields over time.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abɛi lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli ni tsɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ koni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa nibii ni afeɔ lɛ faaa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts makes the soil richer for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots, acting as natural fertilizer that helps feed whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: Cocoa plants thrive under partial shade; removing big trees exposes them to direct heat and sunlight, which stresses the cocoa plants and dries out the soil moisture they need to form healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Tsei wuji ni ajieɔ lɛ haa amɛnáa dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa kookoo tso lɛ he feɔ shoo. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni he hiaa koni efee ŋmeii ni wa lɛ agbi.

english: Why should I cut away some of the extra young shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi tsɔne titri lɛ eje kpo.

english: Too many shoots, or suckers, steal water and plant food from the main stem, resulting in smaller plantain bunches and weaker stems that easily fall over in high winds.
ga: Suckers loo shoots babaoo juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ baa.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves usually indicate that the maize is starving for nitrogen in the soil, suffering from lack of rain, or being attacked at the base by pests like fall armyworms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔleɔ ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli, nugbɔ enɛɛɛ, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ miitutua lɛ yɛ shishigbɛ.

english: How do I know the soil is moist enough to plant my maize seeds at the start of the rainy season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: You should wait until rain has soaked the ground deep enough—about the length of your hand—for two or three days in a row so the seeds don't sprout and then dry up during short dry spells.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ ehà shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa—aaafee onine lɛ kɛlɛ—kɛyashi gbii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui lɛ akakwɛ̃ ni amɛkagbi yɛ be kukuoo ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of leaves, but the roots underground stay tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or green manure, cassava puts all its energy into growing leafy stems above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers underneath.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsɔ lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ niye ní toɔ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Staking allows the yam leaves to catch full sunlight and stay off the wet ground, which prevents fungal diseases and helps the plant produce larger tubers.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ naa hulutsoo be fɛɛ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ahe. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ bulbs wuji.

english: Why are my tomato fruits rotting at the bottom while they are still growing on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato yibii lɛ miifite yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit, usually triggered when watering is irregular or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet.
ga: Enɛ ji fɔfɔii lɛ anaagbee fitemɔ he okadi. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni faaa. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛ́ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ.

english: Why are the blossoms falling off my pepper plants without turning into any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant gets stressed by extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or a lack of phosphorus and potassium nutrients in the soil.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ hao tso lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Why is it bad to burn my farmland after clearing it for planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mashã miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ beni ajie nɔ ni mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Burning destroys beneficial insects and bacteria in the ground, burns away organic matter, and dries out soil moisture, leaving your crops with less natural food to grow well.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ kooloi bibii kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Shã nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni oha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ agbi Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaná adebɔɔ mli niyenii fioo ni baaha amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts naturally take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. This restores the plant food that maize used up, so your next crop grows stronger without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Gbɛ nɛɛ baaha tso niyenii ni ŋmãa lɛ efite lɛ aku sɛɛ aba. No hewɔ lɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa awo mli.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your plants are starving for nitrogen food in the soil, or that too much rain water is standing in your field and choking the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ yɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Aloo nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ miitsi amɛhe.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the stems before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi dani etsɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Extreme afternoon heat, unbalanced watering, or a lack of friendly insects to move flower pollen around can cause tomato plants to drop their flowers as a defense against stress.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa yɛ shwane mli nu ni ejaaa Aloo kooloi bibii ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo ni baatsi pollen kɛyaa he fɛɛ he lɛ ni bɛ. Ebaanyɛ eha tomato tsei lɛ afɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛtsi haomɔ naa.

english: Why do my sweet potato vines grow big leaves but give me very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ baai wuji shi bulbs bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen, the plant uses all its energy to grow leaves and branches above ground instead of sending food down to build heavy tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ baai kɛ tsei niji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, moŋ fe ni amɛaatsu niyenii kɛya shi koni amɛfee bulbs ni tsii.

english: Black Pod is caused by a tiny fungal organism that spreads quickly when the air is damp and trees are crowded. Trimming extra branches lets sunlight and air in to keep pods dry and healthy.
ga: Fungi bibii kɛ pods diji baa. No gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni tsei lɛ hu eyi obɔ. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots develop dark streaks and turn soft inside the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ yɛ fãji ni tsuɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Root rot happens when water gathers around cassava roots in heavy soil without good drainage, or when farmers cut planting sticks from stems that were already sick.
ga: Shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ ehe. Cassava shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu kpakpa hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Aloo beni okwaafoi shwieɔ tsei niji ni ekwɛ̃ kɛjɛ tsei akutsei ni hela emɔ amɛ momo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my young plantain stems fall over easily when the wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa amɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots do not go very deep into the ground. Tiny microscopic worms (nematodes) in the soil can also eat the roots, making the plant weak and easy to push over.
ga: Plantain shishifãi eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. ŋmeii bibii (Nematodes) ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hu baanyɛ aye shishifãi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ewaaa akɛ aaatsi.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings wither and die right after I put chemical fertilizer around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ gboɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ewo mli lɛ?

english: Putting too much dry fertilizer too close to a stem sucks water out of the plant roots and burns them. Fertilizer should always be applied a short distance away from the stem when the soil is wet.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi babaoo fata tso lɛ he tsɔ lɛ, ebaaŋɔ nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli ni eshã shishifãi lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ fioo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ.

english: Why do pepper plants droop during the hot afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: On very hot days, pepper leaves lose water into the hot air faster than the roots can drink it up. If the plant stands tall again when the sun goes down, it is just resting from heat stress.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa nɔ lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu yɛ hulutsoo be mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Kɛji tsei lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ Eji hejɔɔmɔ kɛkɛ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ mli.

english: How can I tell if the seeds from my crops are properly mature and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midumɔwui lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Mature seeds turn a deep, firm, natural color characteristic of the plant (such as dark brown or hard golden) and dry out slightly. If they feel soft, look pale white, or drop prematurely, they were harvested too early or lacked proper nutrients from the main plant.
ga: Dumɔwui ni eda lɛ yɛ su ni mli kwɔ, ni mli tse, tamɔ tso su (tamɔ asasu diŋŋ loo shika tsuru ni wa) ni egbi fioo. Kɛji enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo, etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo egbee shi mra Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ akpa lɛ mra tsɔ loo niyenii ni sa bɛ mli kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ amli.

english: Is it normal for my crop's fruits or seeds to turn bright yellow very quickly before they reach full size?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ mi yibii loo dumɔwui lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse oya dani amɛshɛ amɛdalɛ he?

english: No, sudden yellowing before full growth is usually a sign of plant stress, insect damage, or disease rather than natural ripening. Healthy crops change color gradually as they mature.
ga: Dabi, bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ trukaa dani amɛdaraa lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao, kooloi ni fiteɔ nii, loo hela moŋ fe bɔ ni tso lɛ shwereɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baatsake amɛhe su fiofio kɛji amɛdara kwraa

english: Why do some seeds I harvest look powdery or discolored like pigment instead of healthy seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikpaa lɛ ekomɛi feɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo amɛsu tsakeɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Powdery or oddly discolored seeds are often caused by fungal infections or a severe lack of minerals like potassium and phosphorus in the soil while the plant was forming its seeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ dumɔwui ni etsɔ powda loo amɛhe su tsakeɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko loo minerals tamɔ potassium kɛ phosphorus ni faaa waa yɛ sũ lɛ mli be mli ni tso lɛ miiwo dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Does the health of the parent crop affect how well its seeds will sprout in the next season?
ga: Ani tsei ni ji fɔlɔi lɛ ahewalɛ saa dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ he yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, seeds collected from a weak or unhealthy parent plant carry fewer stored nutrients, making them much more likely to produce weak, discolored, or poor-yielding seedlings.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni bɛ hewalɛ mli lɛ baaná niyenii mli hewalɛ fioo ni ato. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ewoɔ dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni ehiɛ su loo ni wooo yibii fioo.

english: Why are the leaves and developing seeds on my crops turning a pale white color instead of rich green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibaai kɛ midumɔwui lɛ miifee futafuta yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Pale white or yellowish leaves and seeds usually mean the plant is suffering from a lack of nitrogen in the soil, poor sunlight, or root damage from standing water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai kɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ futafuta loo ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli, hulu la ni tsoɔ jogbaŋŋ, loo nu ni damɔ shi lɛ efite shishifãi lɛ.

english: Can the type of soil I plant in change the color and quality of my crops?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsake miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe su kɛ bɔ ni amɛhi ha?

english: Yes, poor soil that lacks essential nutrients prevents crops from producing their natural vibrant colors, often leaving the leaves and seeds looking sickly, pale, or yellowish.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ehiii ni niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anaa koni amɛkafee amɛ adebɔɔ mli sui ni yɔɔ miishɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ ehaa baai kɛ dumɔwui lɛ feɔ tamɔ helatsɛ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo eyɛ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do young tree crop seedlings need shade from larger trees before they can bear good fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni tsei wuji lɛ aná hulutsoo dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Young tree seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Shade trees protect them from heat stress and retain soil moisture so the young trees can develop strong roots and mature properly.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni yɔɔ shade lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ aná shishifãi ni wa ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do seeds bought from the market sometimes grow differently from seeds I save from my own farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ daa yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe dumɔwui ni mibuaa naa yɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Market seeds may come from hybrid varieties or different growing regions that behave differently in your local soil. Saved seeds from your own healthy crops are already adapted to your farm's weather and soil conditions.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajɛ dumɔwui sɔrɔtoi ni akɛfee ekome loo hei ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli. Amrɔ nɛɛ, dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli lɛ etsake kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Are local traditional seeds better for my farm than new improved seeds from town?
ga: Ani maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ blema lɛ hi kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ fe dumɔwui ni atsake ni jɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Local traditional seeds are often tougher against local heat and pests, while new improved seeds can give higher yields but usually require more fertilizer, regular watering, and extra care to thrive.
ga: Kusum dumɔwui ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli latsaa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni atsake lɛ baaha yibiiwoo babaoo. Shi bei pii lɛ, ebiɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo awo mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ koni ekwɛ koni eda

english: Why do some of the seeds I plant fail to sprout at all after I put them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ekomɛi nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they were stored in damp or overly hot conditions, harvested before full maturity, or planted in soil that is too dry or too hard for roots to push through.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni hulutsoo loo edɔ tsɔ. Kpamɔ dani amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. loo adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ loo ni wa tsɔ ni shishifãi nyɛŋ atsɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellowing on the lower maize leaves usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, which is a major food source plants need to stay green and grow strong. Applying a nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure near the roots will fix this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii mli hewalɛ jɛɛhe titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yields of maize every year when I plant it on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same soil every season drains specific plant foods from the soil faster than nature can replace them. Rotating maize with legume crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores vital nutrients like nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ jieɔ tsei niyenii komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni adebɔɔ baanyɛ atsake amɛ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crops immediately after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native plants that are naturally tougher and faster at absorbing water and nutrients than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early within the first three to four weeks of planting keeps them from stealing light, water, and food from your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei ni shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ ni akɛduɔ lɛ mli Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaju la, nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: What is causing tiny caterpillars to eat holes through the growing center of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ko kɛtsɔɔ mi-ŋmei tsei lɛ adalɛ mli?

english: These holes are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the central leaves (the funnel) of maize. Catching them early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts directly into the funnel stops them before they destroy the whole stalk.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ baai (cones) lɛ amli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ amɔmɔ amɛ mra lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua. ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ awo tsɔne lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Tsĩ amɛnaa dani amɛfite tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants curling upward and twisting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or mites that suck the plant's juices from underneath the leaves. Controlling these insects early with insecticidal soap or neem oil prevents leaf distortion and keeps the plant producing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛ́ akɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite, ni ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo yibii.

english: Cassava roots rot mainly because water pools in heavy, poorly drained soil, which smothers the roots and allows fungal diseases to attack. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away and protects the tubers from decay.
ga: Nɔ titri ni kɛ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ji nu ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baatutuaa amɛ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa, ni ebuɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings struggle to survive when I clear all the big trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛhi shi beni mijieɔ tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under harsh, direct sunlight. Leaving taller trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains provides shade and keeps the air humid, giving the young cocoa the protection it needs to establish its roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni ashiɔ Aloo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ koni ekɛha hulutsoo ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hebuu ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛfee eshishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do the blossom flowers on my tomato plants drop off without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when daytime temperatures get extremely hot, or when the plant doesn't get enough water while flowering. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulching helps the plant hold onto its flowers and turn them into fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ waa. Aloo kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔii ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with tall sticks instead of letting them spread on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu sweet potato wain tsei ni tsei kakadaji yɔɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves high up to catch as much sunlight as possible, which allows the plant to manufacture more food for a larger tuber. It also keeps the leaves dry and off the wet ground, preventing fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato lɛ baai lɛ teɔ shi koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo kɛhaa ŋmeii wuji lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebaa lɛ haa egbiɔ ni ehiɛɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Tsi baa helai ni jɛɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ naa

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when heavy winds and rain hit my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and top-heavy fruit bunches, making them unstable in wet soil during storms. Supporting the fruiting trees by propping them up with sturdy bamboo or wooden poles prevents them from snapping or uprooting.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii. Efiteɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ yɛ ahum mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo tsei ni wa fiɔ aduawai tsei asɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkakumɔ loo amɛkajie amɛshishi.

english: Why do my cassava roots stop getting bigger after a certain time, even if I leave them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ yɛ be fioo ko sɛɛ lɛ? Kɛji mishi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ po

english: Cassava plants reach their maximum root weight and starch content around 12 to 18 months. Once they hit this stage, the plant stops storing food in the roots, and leaving them in the ground only risks rot or woodiness, wasting your effort and land.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shɛɔ amɛshishifãi ni tsii fe fɛɛ kɛ starch ni yɔɔ mli lɛ he aaafee nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 18 sɛɛ beni amɛshɛ nɛkɛ fã nɛɛ he lɛ. Tso lɛ kpaɔ niyenii ni ekɛtoɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. ni oshi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebaanyɛ egbo loo etsɔ tso. Ehaa ofiteɔ hewalɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ.

english: Why does my pepper plant stop growing taller once it starts bringing out fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ kɛji ebɔi yibiiwoo pɛ?

english: Once a crop starts flowering and fruiting, it shifts all its energy from building stem and leaf growth into feeding the fruits. Continuing to give it extra food to make it grow taller won't work because the plant has reached its vegetative limit.
ga: Kɛ tsei bɔi fɔfɔii ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ Etsakeɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ adalɛ mli lɛ ewoɔ yibii niyenii mli. Niyenii ni akɛfataa he koni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsuuu nii ejaakɛ tso lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ eda lɛ he momo.

english: Why do my yams start losing weight if I leave them in the ground long after the vines have dried?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɔjɔɔ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ mli beni wain tsei lɛ egbi lɛ?

english: When the yam vine dies, the tuber has finished growing. Leaving it in hot soil causes it to lose water or start sprouting, which uses up its stored food and reduces its size and market value.
ga: Kɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ gbo lɛ Yitso lɛ fɛɛ ekwɛ̃. Kɛ́ oshi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, nu lɛ baaje amɛmli loo amɛbaabɔi shweremɔ. Enɛ baaha niyenii ni ato lɛ afite. ni eha elɛɛmɔ kɛ jarayeli jara lɛ aba shi.

english: How do I know when my watermelons have reached their maximum size so I stop watering them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni watermelon eshɛ he ni eshɛɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ, ni no sɛɛ lɛ makpa nu ni ekɛhaa lɛ?

english: Watermelons stop growing when the small curly tendril on the stem closest to the fruit turns brown and dry. Continuing to water them after this point can cause the fruit to burst or rot, wasting water and labor.
