ga: Watermelons kpaɔ dalɛ kɛji ŋmeii bibii dara. Tso lɛ tso ni bɛŋkɛ aduawai lɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ feɔ blɔfo ni egbiɔ. Kɛ́ oya nɔ okɛ nu wo mli yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha aduawai lɛ amli agbala loo egbo. Efiteɔ nu kɛ nitsumɔ

english: If I put double the amount of fertilizer on my maize field, will I get double the harvest?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ toi enyɔ Ani mafee miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ toi enyɔ?

english: No, crops can only absorb a specific amount of nutrients. Beyond that limit, extra fertilizer will not increase your yield and can burn the roots, meaning you are spending money on inputs that lead to financial losses.
ga: Dabi, tsei baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ. Kɛho nakai husu lɛ he lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haaa onibii lɛ aya hiɛ ni ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oofite shika yɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni kɛ shika fitemɔ baa lɛ ahe.

english: If I plant my okra seeds very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from the same plot?
ga: Kɛji midu okra yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe waa lɛ Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: When crops are too crowded, they fight for sun, water, and soil food. This makes the plants weak and reduces the total weight of okra you harvest, so planting extra seed yields less crop overall.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa okra ni okpaa lɛ fɛɛ tsiimɔ baa shi. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui krokomɛi ni aduɔ lɛ baaha yibiiwoo lɛ fɛɛ aba shi.

english: Is it good to leave my ripe maize on the stalk in the farm for weeks to harvest later when market prices go up?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaashi ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ otsii babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni akpa sɛɛ mli beni jara nɔ jara wa lɛ?

english: Leaving dry maize in the field exposes it to rain, insects, birds, and mold. The crop stops gaining weight once dry, so keeping it in the field causes damage that lowers your final profit.
ga: Abele ni egbi ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ kɛ nugbɔ, kooloi, okpoi kɛ ŋmeii baa. Nibii ni adu lɛ kpaɔ shwiili kɛji egbi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ amɛ to ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa nɔ ni fiteɔ nii baa ni ehaa naagbee sɛɛnamɔi ni onáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why shouldn't I wait for all my tomatoes to turn deep red on the plant before picking them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mimɛɔ ni mi-tomato lɛ fɛɛ afee tɔrɔmɔɔ ni mli edɔ dani mikɛ amɛ atsu nii?

english: Leaving fully ripe tomatoes on the vine slows down the growth of new fruits and increases the risk of pests and rot. Harvesting at the breaker stage (when color just starts changing) allows the plant to send food to younger tomatoes.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tomato ni ekwɛ̃ kwraa yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha aduawai heei lɛ akwɛ̃ fioo. ni ehaa oshara ni yɔɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe lɛ yaa hiɛ. Nikpamɔ yɛ breaker stage (Be mli ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe kɛkɛ) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tomato tsei lɛ ni amɛkɛ niyenii majeɔ tomato bibii lɛ.

english: Why should I prune the extra suckers from my plantain tree if they are all growing healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ midumɔwui lɛ amli kɛji amɛmiida jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Too many suckers compete with the main plant for nutrients. If you leave all of them, the main tree will not get enough energy to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kpakpai. Kɛji oshi fɛɛ lɛ Tso titri lɛ naaa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo plantains wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are my cabbages growing tall stalks and flowers instead of forming tight heads?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kakadaji kɛ fɔfɔi yɛ yitsei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cabbages do this when they get too old or face high heat. Once they start flowering, they stop forming heads and become bitter, so any water or care given after this point is wasted.
ga: Cabbage feɔ enɛ kɛ́ egbɔ tsɔ loo ekɛ ehe wo la ni mli edɔ waa mli. Kɛ ebɔi fɔmɔ Amɛkpaa bulbs feemɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, nu loo kwɛmɔ fɛɛ kwɛmɔ Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni anáa yɛ nɛkɛ sane nɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ afiteɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build strong, green leaves. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea helps restore their green color so they can grow bigger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller harvests every year even when I plant on time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ nii yɛ be naa moŋ lɛ?

english: Planting the exact same crop on the same plot every year drains specific nutrients from the soil. Rotating your crops—such as planting groundnuts or cowpeas after maize—helps replenish nutrients naturally and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Akɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ, ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa sɛɛ. Ebaaha adebɔɔ mli niyenii mli hewalɛi aba ekoŋŋ, ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are there ragged holes and dark dirt inside the upper leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ yiteŋ baai lɛ yɛ bu ni etse kɛ muji ni tsuɔ waa lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides in the central leaf tube of the corn plant and eats the tender leaves. Inspecting your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract can stop them before they destroy the yield.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ amɛnaa dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips feeding on the sap and spreading plant viruses. Spraying the plants early with soapy water or neem oil kills these pests and protects the new leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Ni akɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo neem fɔ baashwie tsei anɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni egbe nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ni ebu baai heei ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry out and die during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have shallow roots and delicate leaves that cannot handle full, harsh sunlight and hot dry winds. Planting shade trees or plantains alongside new cocoa gives them shade and traps moisture to help them survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ kwraa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo dumɔwui yɛ kookoo hee lɛ masɛi lɛ, ebaaha amɛná hulutsoo ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why shouldn't I allow all the shoots growing around my plantain stem to keep growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa ŋmeii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ shwereɔ lɛ? Mi plantain tsei lɛ yaa nɔ amɛdaraa.

english: Allowing too many shoots (suckers) to grow forces them to compete with the main plant for food, sunlight, and water, resulting in smaller plantain bunches. Pruning away extra suckers so only one or two remain ensures the main plant produces large, heavy fruit.
ga: Ni aŋmɛɔ suckers (tsoji) babaoo gbɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii, hulu la kɛ nu, ni no haa amɛnáa plantains bibii. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ amli koni eshwɛ ekome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ woɔ yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Will planting cowpeas or beans between my main crops steal food from them?
ga: Ani tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baaju niyenii kɛjɛ amɛdɛŋ?

english: No, leguminous crops like cowpeas and beans actually help your main crops. They pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, acts as a ground cover to stop weeds, and improves soil moisture for neighboring crops.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yeɔ ebuaa diɛŋtsɛ yɛ onibii titrii lɛ amli. Amɛjieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji nitrogen lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nɔ ko ni akɛkpaa jwɛi. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ aya hiɛ kɛha tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when plants experience extreme heat, dry soil, or lack of pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and giving the plants adequate water during hot dry spells prevents flower drop.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ shɛ latsaa ni naa wa he, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo pollination bɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni okɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ha tsei lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the cooler temperatures allow the soil and roots to absorb the moisture deep down before the sun causes it to evaporate, saving water and keeping plants hydrated all day.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu ni mli kwɔ dani hulu lɛ shwieɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa nu sɛɛ foɔ, ni ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Most cassava varieties mature between 8 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off. You can check maturity by carefully digging around one stem base to inspect the root size before harvesting the whole field.
ga: Cassava henɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo daa yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 mli beni adu amɛ sɛɛ. Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛbaagbee shi. Obaanyɛ okwɛ kɛji eyɛ hewalɛ kɛtsɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni ooofo jogbaŋŋ koni okwɛ bɔ ni shishifã lɛ da ha dani okpa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my rice plants turn yellow when water sits in my field for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When standing water remains completely still for too long, oxygen cannot reach the crop's roots, causing them to suffocate and preventing the plant from absorbing green-making nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Kɛ́ nu lɛ tee nɔ ehi shi dioo kwraa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Oxygen nyɛŋ ashɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa amɛmuɔ ni haaa tsei lɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ tamɔ nitrogen.

english: How do I know if my land stays wet enough to grow a good rice harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ ŋmãa kpakpa nɔ?

english: Good rice soil feels heavy and sticky like clay, holds water on the surface without letting it drain away instantly, and stays muddy even a few days after the rain stops.
ga: Omɔ shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ tsii ni ekpɛɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ. Ehiɛɔ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ ni eho amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ni ehiɔ shi akɛ muji yɛ gbii fioo komɛi po sɛɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ.

english: Why do my crops yield smaller harvests after growing on the same plot for a few years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii babaoo yɛ afii fioo komɛi ni mikɛdu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Crops pull essential nutrients out of the soil every season to grow, so without adding organic manure or fertilizer, the soil becomes depleted and cannot feed new plants properly.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be koni amɛshwere. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ekwɛ tsei heei anɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will burning the cleared weeds on my farm help my soil become richer for planting?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni ajie yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ashãa lɛ baaye abua ni eha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha dumɔ?

english: Burning gives a quick burst of ash nutrients, but it destroys healthy organic matter and kills beneficial earthworms, making the soil dry, hard, and poor over time.
ga: Shãa lɛ jieɔ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ oya. Shi ekpãtãa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahiɛ ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ, ewaa, ni efiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Curled pale leaves are usually a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, a sickness spread by tiny whiteflies that suck sap from plant leaves and pass the virus along.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni mli tse ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji cassava mosaic hela he okadi. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies ni nuɔ tsei ahe baai amli nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa, ni amɛkɛ hela lɛ shwieɔ mɔ nɔ.

english: How can I keep tiny insects from destroying my harvested maize stored in bags?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa? Te aaafee tɛŋŋ akpata ŋmãa ni akpa ni akɛto kotokui amli lɛ hiɛ?

english: Drying maize thoroughly in the sun until the grains are very hard before storing them in airtight, sealed bags starves insects of the moisture and air they need to survive.
ga: Abɛi ni agbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ mli wa waa dani akɛwoɔ kotokui ni akɛ vacuum tsiɔ mli lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha koolooi anine shɛɛɛ fɛ̃i kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my maize crop dry up so quickly when the rains stop for just two weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya nɛkɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa otsii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize has shallow roots near the surface of the soil, meaning it cannot reach deep underground water and quickly runs out of moisture when the top layer dries up.
ga: Abɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ enyɛŋ eshɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he. Ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ laajeɔ oya kɛ́ ŋwɛi fã lɛ gĩ.

english: How do shade trees protect my young cash crops during heavy downpours?
ga: Te tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu miŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ ahe yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Shade tree leaves break the fall of heavy raindrops so they do not wash away topsoil, while their deep roots hold the land firm against severe erosion.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ baa lɛ fiteɔ nugbɔshiimɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ akajo foi. yɛ be mli ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ koni ekafite shikpɔŋ lɛ waa.

english: Why is it harmful to plant the exact same crop on the same field every single year?
ga: Mɛni he je nɛ e ngɛ oslaa kaa a maa du ní kake ngɛ ngmɔ kake mi daa jeha a?

english: Planting the same crop continuously allows specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil year after year while completely draining the ground of specific nutrients.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwraa.

english: Perennial crops like cocoa must spend their first few years growing a strong trunk, deep roots, and broad leaves to gather enough energy to support heavy fruit production later on.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ kookoo he miihia klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ shishifãi ni mli wa, shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ koni amɛbua hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua yibii ni tsii ni baa lɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: I am thinking of starting a tree crop farm in Ghana; between rubber and oil palm, which one gives better profit?
ga: Mimiisusu he akɛ mabɔi tsei ahe ŋmɔ yɛ Ghana. rɔbɔt kɛ ŋmei fɔ teŋ Te nɔ ni haa sɛɛnamɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ?

english: Rubber is generally more profitable than oil palm over time because raw latex commands higher market prices compared to oil palm fresh fruit bunches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, rɔba bafeɔ nɔ ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he fe mu tso yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, latex ni afeee lɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ jara wa waa kɛ akɛto mu tsei heei ahe.

english: Is rubber farming as physically demanding and stressful as oil palm farming?
ga: Ani rɔbɔt ŋmɔshi nitsumɔ biɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛ babaoo ni ehaa mɔ haoɔ tamɔ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei mli lɛ feɔ lɛ?

english: No, rubber farming requires less heavy physical work once established. Tapping rubber trees for liquid latex is much easier on the body than harvesting heavy oil palm fruit bunches.
ga: Dabi, rɔbɔt ŋmɔ shishijee biɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ babaoo kɛji ato shishi pɛ. Rɔba tsei ni akɛtswaa koni akɛfee latɛs ni ji nu lɛ waaa yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ he fe mu tsei ni tsii ni akpaa.

english: Why are some established oil palm farmers in my area switching their land over to rubber?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ oil palm okwaafoi komɛi ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ miitsake amɛshikpɔŋ lɛ koni amɛdu rɔbɔt lɛ?

english: Farmers are making the switch because rubber brings in higher overall earnings and requires less exhausting physical labor compared to managing oil palm.
ga: Okwaafoi miitsake gbɛtsɔɔmɔi yɛ be mli ni rɔba kɛ shika ni fa babaoo baa lɛ. Ni ebiɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ nitsumɔ ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe fioo kɛ akɛto mu tso he nitsumɔ he.

english: What kind of daily work is actually involved in harvesting rubber from the trees?
ga: Mɛɛ daa gbi nitsumɔ fata he diɛŋtsɛ yɛ tsei amli nu ni akpaa lɛ mli?

english: Harvesting rubber involves making light, controlled cuts on the tree bark using a special tapping knife so latex can drip into a cup, which takes soft skill rather than heavy lifting.
ga: Nɔ ni fata nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ni akpaa lɛ he ji ni akɛ tsɔne krɛdɛɛ ko ni akɛtswaa nu lɛ atswa tso lɛ yibii lɛ fioo ni akudɔ koni nu lɛ atsɔ kɔɔpoo lɛ mli. Enɛ biɔ ŋaa ni yɔɔ blɛoo fe nibii ni tsii ni awoɔ.

english: How does harvesting oil palm compare to harvesting rubber in terms of physical effort?
ga: Te ŋmei fɔ ni akpaa lɛ kɛ rɔba ni akpaa lɛ yeɔ egbɔ ehaa tɛŋŋ yɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ gbɛfaŋ?

english: Oil palm requires cutting down heavy, prickly fruit clusters high up in the trees and carrying them, while rubber only requires walking from tree to tree to make light cuts on the bark and collect liquid sap.
ga: Mu tso biɔ ni afo tso yibii ni tsii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii akui amli yɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni awo amɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nɔ pɛ ni he hiaa ji akɛ Yang anyiɛ kɛjɛ tso kome nɔ kɛya tso kroko nɔ koni efolɔ tso lɛ yibii lɛ blɛoo ni ekɛ nu ni mli ewo nu lɛ abua naa.

english: Will I need to hire a large team of heavy laborers if I plant a rubber farm?
ga: Kɛ midu rɔbɔt ŋmɔ lɛ, ani ehe baahia ni maŋɔ nitsulɔi akuu agbo ko ni tsii?

english: Not necessarily. Because rubber tapping relies on steady, careful work rather than heavy lifting, a smaller workforce or family members can easily manage daily collection compared to oil palm.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tai ni akɛtswaa lɛ biɔ nitsumɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ fe nibii ni tsii ni awoɔ nɔ. Eyɛ mlɛo kɛha nitsulɔi loo weku mli bii bibii lɛ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ daa gbi nibii ni abua naa lɛ nɔ kɛ akɛto mu tso he.

english: If I already have an active crop like oil palm, does it make sense for me to move to rubber farming?
ga: Kɛji miyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei fɔ momo Ani shishinumɔ baafee nɔ ni yɔɔ mli akɛ mafã kɛya rɔbɔt ŋmɔji amli?

english: Yes, if your current crop yields lower profit or causes too much physical strain, transitioning parts of your land to rubber can provide better income with less physical exhaustion.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ sɛɛnamɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ onibii ni oduɔ amrɔ nɛɛ ahe loo ekɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ nɔnyɛɛ babaoo baa. Shikpɔŋ komɛi ni aaatsake awo rɔba mli lɛ baanyɛ aha aná shika kpakpa ni gbɔmɔtsoŋ tɔlɛ fioo pɛ aba.

english: How do rubber trees behave and produce yield once they are planted?
ga: Te rɔbɔt tsei feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii kɛji adu amɛ pɛ?

english: Once rubber trees mature, they consistently produce a milk-like sap called latex from their bark for over 25 years when tapped properly.
ga: Kɛji akɛ rɔbɔt tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ mliki ni atsɛɔ lɛ bark sap lɛ be fɛɛ be nɔ ni fe afii 25 kɛji akɛ atswa lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Does a full-grown rubber farm require a lot of clearing and weeding work?
ga: Ani rɔbɔt ŋmɔ ni eda lɛ biɔ ni ajie jwɛi babaoo kɛjɛ mli?

english: No, once rubber trees mature, their dense leafy branches create a thick shade that naturally stops many weeds from growing, reducing field maintenance work.
ga: Dabi, beni rɔbɔt tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Niji ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ hulutsoo ni mli wa koni jwɛi babaoo akakwɛ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔ mli saamɔ nitsumɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Is rubber a good cash crop for long-term financial security in Ghana?
ga: Ani rɔba ji shika helɛtemɔ kpakpa kɛha shika helɛtemɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ Ghana?

english: Yes, rubber is highly valued for international manufacturing, giving farmers a reliable, long-term stream of income that usually exceeds profits from traditional palm oil.
ga: Hɛɛ, rɔbɔt yɛ sɛɛnamɔ babaoo kɛha majimaji ateŋ nitsumɔ. Enɛ haa okwaafoi lɛ náa shika ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ feɔ sɛɛnamɔi ni anáa kɛjɛɔ blema tsofa-kɛ-ŋma mli.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away my crops when I plant them on a hillside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii kɛ midu yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: When rain falls on sloped land, water gathers speed and cuts pathways through the ground, carrying away fertile topsoil and young seeds. Planting across the slope or creating ridges slows down the water, allowing it to soak into the soil safely instead of destroying your farm.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ he ko ni jɛkɛ Nu lɛ baabua oyaiyeli naa ni ebaafo gbɛ ko kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ kɛ dumɔwui bibii lɛ anɔ. Dumɔ yɛ gɔŋji lɛ anɔ loo ŋmeii ni afee lɛ baaha nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Ha nu lɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shweshweeshwe. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite oŋmɔ lɛ

english: How do I know if my maize crop is getting too much water or too little water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele lɛ miihe nu babaoo loo miiye fioo tsɔ?

english: When maize lacks water, its leaves roll up tightly like paper during the hottest part of the day to save moisture. If it receives too much water, the soil gets waterlogged and starves the roots of air, turning the leaves pale yellow.
ga: Beni nu bɛ ŋmãa lɛ Akɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ wolo yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli koni eye ebua ni ŋmãa lɛ ahi shi. Kɛji onine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebaaha ŋwɛi shishifãi lɛ amli nu lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛkɛ lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees turning brown and dying in the bright sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains beside them creates a canopy that shields the young trees from extreme heat and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ lateral plantains lɛ adumɔ Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ baa. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot under the ground when rainwater collects on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava needs soil that drains easily. When water sits around the roots for too long, it suffocates them and creates conditions where rot diseases thrive, causing the tubers to decay before harvest.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ oya lɛ he miihia cassava. Kɛ nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli ewo muji baa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ dani akpaa.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my vegetables with dried leaves or straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dried plant materials acts like a protective blanket. It blocks hot sunshine from drying out the earth, traps moisture in the soil, and stops heavy rain from washing away the dirt around crop roots.
ga: Tsei ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Etsĩɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ muji ni bɔle tsei shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crops too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Crops planted too closely compete with each other for water and nutrients hidden in the soil. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to spread its roots, collect moisture, and grow big and healthy.
ga: Tsei ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ teŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛgbɛɔ eshishifãi lɛ eshwaa, ehiɛɔ nu mli, ni edaa ni ewaa.

english: How can I prevent rainwater from cutting deep gullies through the middle of my land?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ atsĩ nugbɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekafo faa ko ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Rainwater naturally finds paths and cuts deeper into the earth as it flows downhill. Planting deep-rooted grass barriers or digging small shallow trenches along water paths slows down the flow and guides water safely off your land.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ naa adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni efoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ beni ejɛɔ gɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ. Jwɛi ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ ni ooodu loo ŋshɔkei bibii ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ ni ooofo yɛ nu gbɛi lɛ ahe lɛ baaha nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni ebaajie nu kɛjɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does planting right after the first rain help my seeds sprout better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa midumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first main rains soften the dry earth and fill the upper soil with moisture. Planting into wet soil ensures the seeds absorb the water they need to break open and germinate quickly before pests can eat them.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ titri lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛmuɔ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya dani kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ yeɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my crops look weak even after I put fertilizer right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛbɛ hewalɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo amɛmli dani ahum ni naa wa ko baa lɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rainwater flows quickly over the ground and washes away topically applied fertilizer before the crops can absorb it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is damp, but not during heavy downpours.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops dry up faster when rain stops for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gĩɔ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Weeds often have wild, strong roots that drink up underground moisture much faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds leaves all the stored soil water strictly for your crops to survive dry periods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ baajie shikpɔŋ nɔ nu fɛɛ ni ato lɛ kpo kwraa koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct, strong sunlight damages their soft leaves. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides a protective canopy while the cocoa builds a strong root system.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fiteɔ amɛbaai bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋwɛitsu lɛ he. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kookoo haa shishifãi ni mli wa baa.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow starting from the tips down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛyitseiaŋ kɛmiiya amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing that forms a 'V' shape from the leaf tip inward usually means your maize lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main food crop plants use to stay green and build leaves, so applying a nitrogen fertilizer like urea helps restore health.
ga: Yellow ni feɔ ‘V’ su kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ naagbee kɛyaa mli lɛ fɔɔ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo baai. No hewɔ lɛ, nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni mɔ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them because the roots need air to stay alive. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets extra water drain away so the roots remain healthy during wet seasons.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia shishifãi lɛ koni amɛhi shi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu kroko ni fa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they experience extreme heat or inconsistent watering. When the plant gets stressed by drought or hot weather, it sheds flowers to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Tomato tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he. Kɛji hɔmɔ loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ hao tsei lɛ Eshwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛto hewalɛ he kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: Yam vines need to climb high into the air so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight. When the leaves get full sunlight, they make more energy that flows underground to grow larger, heavier yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa lɛ Ebaaha hewalɛ babaoo ni hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aba koni eha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ afee wuji ni amɛtsii.

english: What causes small ragged holes in my maize leaves and dirt inside the central funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ muji ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ

english: This damage is caused by the fall armyworm caterpillar, which hides in the central funnel of the maize plant and eats young leaves. Spraying early with approved insecticides or natural remedies like neem water can control them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji cutworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Loo adebɔɔ mli tsofai tamɔ neem nu lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the extra sucker shoots growing around my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi dumɔwui lɛ etee.

english: When too many shoots grow around a plantain stalk, they compete with the main plant for soil nutrients and water. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, which results in larger plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ plantain tso ko he lɛ, amɛkɛ tso ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ jwɛi wuji.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips sucking sap from the plant or transmitting a leaf-curl virus. Controlling these small insects helps keep the plant leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ loo chili baa mli hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. kooloi bibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ Enɛɛmɛi yeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in tiny nodules on their roots. When the plant roots decay after harvest, that nitrogen stays in the soil as free fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ lɛ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ bibii bibii beni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Heavy rain washes fertilizer away from the soil surface before the plant roots have time to soak it in. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist or when light rain is expected so it dissolves gently into the root zone.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛbaaŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo loo kɛji akɛ akpaa gbɛ akɛ nugbɔ baanɛ fioo. koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ shishifãi lɛ amli fiofio

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when there are no tall trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei kakadaji komɛi bɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Planting taller shade trees or plantains nearby creates a canopy that shields young cocoa leaves from scorching heat and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo dumɔwui kakadaji ni aduɔ Yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my corn turning yellow before the ears are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani toi lɛ eda kwraa lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an important food for corn. The plant takes nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young growing corn ears above.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji ŋmãa niyenii ni he hiaa waa Tsei kɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛha ŋmãa toi ni miida lolo yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my field produce smaller corn harvests every time I plant corn on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting corn continuously drains the specific nutrients corn needs from the soil and lets corn pests multiply. Rotating corn with crops like beans or groundnuts gives the soil time to rebuild its strength.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni abɛi he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa mli ŋmeii ni amɛgbɛɔ eshwaa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtswaa ehewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weevils destroy my harvested maize inside sealed sacks even when I dried the corn first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fiteɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa yɛ kotokui ni akɛwo mli lɛ amli eyɛ mli akɛ migbiɔ ŋmãa lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ moŋ?

english: Weevils often lay tiny, invisible eggs inside the corn kernels while the ears are still on the stalk in the farm. If the grain is not completely dry or treated before storage, those hidden eggs hatch inside the bags.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii fɔɔ wɔji bibii. Anaaa ŋmãa lɛ mli be mli ni toi lɛ kã ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lolo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa loo atsuuu he nii dani akɛtoɔ. Nakai ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ baafɔ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains leave standing water around the plants, the roots drown and soil fungi cause them to rot, which is why planting on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu bua tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ hewɔ ni dumɔwui yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb high on wooden poles to give me big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei anɔ shɔɔŋ koni amɛná bulbs wuji lɛ?

english: Yam leaves use sunlight to manufacture the food that builds large tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines off the muddy ground so every leaf gets plenty of light and fresh air without catching leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ niyenii ni feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni baa fɛɛ baa aná la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baa helai akamɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small shoots growing at the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? No kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwu titri lɛ shishi.

english: Too many young shoots steal water and nutrients away from the main mother plant. Leaving only two or three strong suckers allows the main tree to grow a much larger and heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii babaoo juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ akwɛ tsei babaoo ni dara ni tsii.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off onto the ground before turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ dani amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from hot weather, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Regular watering during dry spells helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hao amɛ. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up and growing slowly during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraa blɛoo yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by heat stress or tiny sucking insects like whiteflies spreading a plant virus. Shielding young plants and controlling insects early stops the virus from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo loo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli lɛ baa. Dumɔwui ahebuu mra kɛ kooloi akwɛmɔ Ebaakpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: How does planting groundnuts help make my soil richer for the crop I plant next season?
ga: Te ŋmeii ni miduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni efee nii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has special roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil as natural fertilizer, leaving the land richer for future crops.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni eyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which acts as food for green growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the leaves turn green and strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my farm yield less maize if I plant maize on the exact same land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo kɛji miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year. Rotating maize with crops like groundnuts or beans naturally restores nitrogen and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the sap from the leaves. Spraying the plants with neem oil or appropriate pest control stops these insects from damaging the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofai krokomɛi ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akafite baai lɛ.

english: Why do tiny insects attack my cowpea farm mostly when the plants start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-cowpea ŋmɔ lɛ mli babaoo beni tsei lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi lɛ?

english: Insects are naturally attracted to the sweet nectar in cowpea flowers and soft young pods. Spraying at early flowering protects the buds so they can develop into full pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni jɛɔ tsina fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ gbalaa kooloi. Kɛ́ afɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔii lɛ ashishijee be mli lɛ, ebaabu ŋmeii lɛ ahe koni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli kwraa.

english: What causes the bottom of my tomatoes to turn black and rot before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egbo dani ekwɛ̃?

english: This black spot is caused by a lack of calcium and irregular watering while the fruit is growing. Keeping the soil evenly moist and adding lime helps prevent the fruit from rotting.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ nɛɛ baa ji calcium ni faaa kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa ni okɛ lime fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aduawai lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground before I am ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long without draining. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater flow away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do I need to put stakes for my yam vines to climb as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei ama mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛkwɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking spreads the leaves out toward the sun so the plant can make bigger yams.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking gbɛɔ baai lɛ eshwaa kɛyaa hulu lɛ he bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ awo sweet potatoes wuji.

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers fall off without growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the tree is stressed by dry conditions or attacked by pests like mirids. Keeping shade trees nearby and protecting the tree from sucking pests helps flowers turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao tso lɛ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ pollen lɛ tutua lɛ. Kɛ́ hulutsoo be bɛŋkɛ ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ nu lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit bunches, making them top-heavy. Supporting the stems with strong wooden props or bamboo forks prevents them from blowing over.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ aduawai akui ni tsii. kɛ muji babaoo baa Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni wa loo ŋmei fɔk fiɔ tsɔne lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekatswa.

english: How do weeds growing close to my crops slow down how fast my crops grow?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ oya?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crop roots. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to grow fast and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni otsei lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crops are lacking key nutrients like nitrogen or iron in the soil. Adding compost or fertilizer feeds the soil so your plants can regain their green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii tamɔ nitrogen loo dade yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛdara hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Do my crop plants need fertilizer, or is regular rainwater enough for them to produce well?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nii lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii? Aloo ani nugbɔnɛmɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔ nii kpakpai aba?

english: Rainwater provides hydration, but crops also need nutrients to feed on. Giving your plants fertilizer or manure supplies essential nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and iron, helping them yield larger and healthier harvests.
ga: Nugbɔ nu haa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Shi niyenii mli hewalɛ hu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ha tsei lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, kɛ iron, ni ehaa amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Why should I clear away weeds and rotting crop waste from around my vegetable beds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egboi ni eshwɛ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ? Mi aduawai shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds and decaying plants act as breeding grounds for pests and fungal diseases. Maintaining clean field hygiene prevents these germs from multiplying and attacking your healthy crops.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei ni fiteɔ lɛ ji hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai fɔɔ yɛ. Okwaafoi amli hetsemɔ ni mli tse lɛ tsiɔ nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkafa babaoo ni amɛtutuaa onibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it important to pick off and remove diseased pods from my cocoa trees immediately?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie cacao tsei amli ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya ni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaving infected pods on the tree allows fungal diseases like black pod to spread to healthy pods via rain droplets and insects. Promptly removing sick pods stops the disease from wiping out your farm yield.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii helai, tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi kɛ kooloi bibii anɔ. Kɛ́ ojie ŋmeii ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, no haaa hela lɛ afite oŋmɔ mli nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin when I plant many seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo beni midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space allows it to grow sturdy and produce well.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni eda waa ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under hot sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide living shade to protect the cocoa seedlings from harsh heat while keeping the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ haa hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ.

english: Why does spreading dry grass on the soil around my crops help them during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbɛ jwɛi ni egbi ashwã shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, ani miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, traps moisture in the soil, keeps the root area cool during sunny days, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ gbii ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: How can I keep my farm soil fertile for my crops without buying expensive fertilizers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni miheee ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa?

english: You can feed your soil by mixing in animal manure, decaying plant compost, and rotating crops with nitrogen-fixing plants like cowpeas or groundnuts to naturally restore soil richness.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛfutuɔ mli lɛ nɔ. ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa nitrogen hiɔ shi tamɔ cowpeas loo peanuts lɛ atsake ŋmɔshi nibii. Koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ

english: How can I get my pepper plants to keep bearing fresh peppers for a longer time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Plucking mature peppers off the plant regularly triggers the crop to produce new flowers and fruit continuously, extending your harvest period.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie ŋmeii ni eda lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli daa lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni eya nɔ ewo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai heei. Enɛ baaye abua ni okpaa nii lɛ asɛɛ atsɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow big leaves above the ground but small roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baa agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shishi?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to spend all their energy growing leaves instead of roots. Using balanced nutrients and keeping the soil loose helps tubers swell larger.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ ebaa lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe eshishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni sa tsu nii ni aha sũ lɛ mli tse lɛ, ebaaye ebua bulb lɛ ni edara.

english: Why do my young cocoa flowers keep falling off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often drop off when the plant experiences heat stress, dry spells, or damage from insects like mirids. Ensuring your cocoa farm has enough shade trees and controlling pests during the flowering period helps flowers turn into healthy pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. shihilɛi ni mli egbi loo nɔ ni kooloi bibii tamɔ pollen fiteɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ koni o-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ aná tsei ni haa hulutsoo be ni sa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves forming a V-shape from the leaf tips usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK at the right growth stage will turn the leaves green again and increase your grain yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe yɔɔ tamɔ V lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Kɛ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo NPK tsu nii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Cassava root rot happens when water stays trapped around the roots for too long, allowing fungal diseases to attack. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges improves water drainage and keeps the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fitemɔ baa kɛji nu ŋmɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai aba. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ aya hiɛ, ni ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need tall stakes so their leaves can reach maximum sunlight to make food for the growing tubers below. Letting vines crawl on hot ground burns the leaves and leads to smaller tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni baaha amɛbaa lɛ aná hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ ni ekɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ ashi wain tsei lɛ ni amɛmiikplekeshi yɛ he ko ni mli edɔ lɛ, ebaashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha ŋmeii bibii aba.

english: Extra suckers compete with the mother plant for nutrients, water, and sunlight. Pruning away excess suckers leaves only the main plant and one strong follower, resulting in much bigger and heavier bunches of plantain.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi lɛ kɛ fɔlɔ tso lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, tso titri lɛ kɛ sɛɛnyiɛlɔ kome ni he wa pɛ eshwɛɔ. Enɛ haa anáa plantains akuu ko ni da ni tsii kwraa.

english: Why are caterpillars eating holes inside the central leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that feeds on the soft inner whorl of young maize. Spraying approved insecticides or bio-pesticides early in the morning or late evening reaches the worms when they come out to feed.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahe nibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo bio-insecticide ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaha kooloi lɛ ajie amɛhe kpo koni amɛbaye nii.

english: Why are my maturing cocoa pods turning black and hard while still on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni ewaa be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Black, hardened pods are caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly during damp, wet seasons. Pruning lower cocoa branches to let in air and sunlight helps keep the environment dry and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ pod diji ni wa baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ kookoo niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la aba lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shihilɛ lɛ mli egbiɔ, ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: When is the right time to apply chemical fertilizer to my field during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo ŋmɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist, but not directly before or during heavy downpours. Applying it right before heavy rain causes the rain to wash the fertilizer away before plant roots can absorb it.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Shi esaaa akɛ akɛwoɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa loo yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛwo mli dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ lɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts fix natural nitrogen from the air into the soil through their roots. This enriches the soil naturally, feeding your main crop without requiring as much artificial fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ tsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛhaa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ha otsei titrii lɛ niyenii ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsuuu nii.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die even when I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting in moist soil is typically caused by Bacterial Wilt, a soil-borne disease that blocks the plant's water pipes. Rotating your tomato crop with maize or cassava helps break the disease cycle in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni jɛɔ sũ mli ni tsiɔ tso ko nu paipii anaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli edɔ trukaa lɛ baa. Tomato ni akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekpaa helai ni yaa nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I burn all the cleared bush and grass on my land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji mishã tsei bibii kɛ jwɛi fɛɛ ni ajie yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani midu nii lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the rich organic layer on top of the soil and kills beneficial insects and earthworms that keep the land fertile. Instead of burning, clearing and leaving weeds to rot into compost feeds your soil naturally.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. ni amɛgbe kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaashã, amɛjie jwɛi lɛ, ni amɛha amɛgboi akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Ebaaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do people advise me to plant plantains next to my young cocoa seedlings on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu kookoo tsei yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Kokoo tsei bibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily dry out and burn in direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and develop wide leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the temporary shade and moisture cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni gbɛ́ɔ oya ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni amɛnáa baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ haa.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, will I harvest more maize from my land?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani makpa ŋmãa babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, planting too closely causes crops to fight over sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. When crowded, maize plants grow tall and thin with small or empty ears. Giving each plant proper space results in bigger, healthier yields.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ awuu koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Beni gbɔmɛi babaoo yɔɔ lɛ Abɛi tsei lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛtoi bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, an essential plant food, or that the ground is flooded with too much water. Adding nitrogen rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore their green color and growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni amɛdara ekoŋŋ.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips hiding underneath the leaves. Spraying with soapy water or appropriate neem-based remedies can clear these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo tsofai ni akɛ neem fee lɛ shwie nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ejie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛya.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting under the soil before I even dig them up for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani manyɛ mafolɔ amɛ po ni makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rot underground mainly when the soil stays waterlogged for too long or gets infected by soil-borne fungi. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps drain excess rain water away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ mli. Kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajie kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: My tomato plants have a lot of yellow flowers, so why are they dropping off without forming tomatoes?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ amɛgbee shi ni amɛfeee tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off without fruiting when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there are no bees to pollinate them. Regular watering during hot spells helps keep the blossoms on the plant.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni yibii bɛ mli kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni ŋmeii bɛ ni baaha tso lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ baaye abua ni eya nɔ ekwɛ fɔfɔi.

english: How long does a plantain shoot take from the day I plant it until I can harvest the fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani akpaa plantain dumɔwui lɛ?

english: A plantain sucker usually takes between 12 to 15 months to produce a mature bunch ready for harvest, depending on soil fertility, water supply, and weather conditions.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantain suckers lɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 15 dani amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni eda ni esa akɛ akpa. Edamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu ni yɔɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi anɔ.

english: Should I start planting my maize immediately after the very first rain of the year falls?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ afi lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become consistent. The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell, which can dry out and kill newly germinated seeds in the ground.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa. Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do small black insects ruin my harvested maize even after I dry it and tie it in sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii diji miifite mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ migbi ni mikɛfi kotokui amli moŋ?

english: Those insects are grain weevils, which often lay microscopic eggs in the maize cob while it is still in the field. Drying maize thoroughly until it is hard, and using airtight storage or treated sacks, prevents them from hatching and multiplying.
ga: Kplukai lɛ ji ŋmãa ŋmeii, ni bei pii lɛ amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii amli be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. Abɛi ni agbiɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewaa Ni okɛ vacuum ni akɛtoɔ kotokui loo kotokui amli lɛ atsu nii koni ŋmeii lɛ akafɔ ni amɛkafee babaoo.

english: Black Pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in wet, shady conditions, causing the pods to decay rapidly. Removing affected pods immediately and applying recommended fungal treatment stops the disease from spreading across your entire crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni shade yɔɔ, ni haa pods lɛ fiteɔ oya. Jiemɔ ŋmeii ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ atsu nii koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã onibii fɛɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomatoes keep rotting on the vine even after I pluck off the damaged ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ miifite yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mijie nɔ ni efite lɛ moŋ?

english: Fungal spores that cause rot remain on nearby leaves and in the soil even after visible rotten fruits are removed. You need to apply proper plant fungicide directly to the leaves and clean up fallen fruits to stop the cycle.
ga: Spores ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ baakã baai ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ kɛ sũ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni ajie ŋmɔtɔ ni anaa lɛ po sɛɛ. Esa akɛ okɛ tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ tso mli ŋmeii lɛ awo baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni otsumɔ aduawai ni egbee shi lɛ ahe koni ekpa ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and rot at the base during heavy rain seasons in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egboɔ yɛ shishigbɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ Ghana lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess moisture creates an ideal environment for soil fungi while preventing roots from getting oxygen. Proper drainage channels and timely spray treatments protect your crop from rotting during wet periods.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Nu ni hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ kɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ buɔ onibii ahe koni amɛkafite yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: What causes the bottom stem of my pepper plants to turn soft and collapse?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ tsei lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛkuɔ shi?

english: This is stem or collar rot caused by soil fungi, often triggered when water pools around the stem base or when the stem gets injured during weeding. Planting on raised mounds helps prevent this decay.
ga: Enɛ ji stem loo neck rot ni ŋmei ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ tso lɛ shishi loo kɛ́ tso lɛ pila yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: What happens to my cassava plants if I accidentally cut or damage their stems while weeding?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava tso lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ oshara fo loo mifite tso lɛ shishifã lɛ beni mikɛ jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Cuts on plant stems act like open wounds on human skin, letting fungal and bacterial diseases enter easily and cause decay. Making clean cuts and avoiding trunk damage keeps the plant healthy.
ga: Tsei ashishifãi ni afo lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ pilamɔi ni agbele yɛ gbɔmɔ hewolo nɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ bacteria helai baabote mli ni amɛkɛ fitemɔ baa. Jwɛi ni afoɔ ni he tseɔ kɛ tso lɛ shishifãmɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do my trees protect themselves after I prune unwanted branches?
ga: Te mitso lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ ebu ehe he beni mifo niji ni ataooo lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Plants gradually seal off cut surfaces with protective bark tissue, but while the cut is open, it is vulnerable to pests and rot. Pruning correctly during dry weather helps wounds dry and heal quickly.
ga: Tso lɛ haa he ni afo lɛ he fiofio kɛ fãji ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ. Shi yɛ be mli ni afo lɛ mli lɛ Eyɛ oshara mli akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ fitemɔ baajɛ mli aba. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa pilamɔ lɛ ni egbiɔ ni etsaa oya.

english: Can insects feeding on my crops cause the stems to rot?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii ni yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ yibii lɛ afite?

english: Yes, when insects bite or bore into plant stems, they create wounds that allow rot-causing fungi and bacteria to enter, leading to internal decay.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ kooloi bibii ŋmɔ loo amɛfo tso shishifãi amli. Amɛfeɔ pilamɔi ni haa ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni fiteɔ lɛ boteɔ mli. kɛ mligbɛ fitemɔ baa

english: Why is it important to spray treatment directly on the diseased parts of my crop instead of just on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsofa afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ?

english: Plant medicine works best when applied directly to the affected leaves or pods where the infection is active, just like putting medicine directly on a cut to heal it.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tsei amli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ akɛwo baai loo ŋmeii ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ he ni hela lɛ yɔɔ lɛ. Etamɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ pilamɔ ko nɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni etsa lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I leave rotten leaves and infected fruits on the ground in my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishiɔ baai ni egboi kɛ aduawai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Rotten plant parts carry live fungi and bacteria that spread through wind and rain to healthy crops. Clearing and burning or burying infected debris breaks the infection cycle.
ga: Tso lɛ fãi ni fiteɔ lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni wala yɔɔ mli ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ mli kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ. Nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ashãa loo afuɔ lɛ fiteɔ hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I wait until my whole farm shows rot before I start applying chemical treatment?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mimɛɔ kɛyashiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli baafite dani mibɔi tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛtsaa helai lɛ kɛ nitsumɔ?

english: Treating crop diseases early at the first sign of damage acts like immediate first aid, saving your yield. Once rot spreads throughout the field, treatments become much less effective and far more expensive.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ahe tsamɔ mra Kɛji ana klɛŋklɛŋ okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ efite lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yelikɛbuamɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ohaa onitsumɔ lɛ yaa nɔ. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ gbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ Tsamɔ lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ ni ejara hu baahe babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow from the center going outwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-corn lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ kɛmiijɛ kpo lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. Applying fertilizers like Urea or NPK, or adding well-rotted animal manure to the soil, will help the leaves turn green and restore healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo NPK tsu nii loo akɛ kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni eha amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the soil if I do not harvest them before the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ akpaaa amɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Excessive rain traps water in heavy soil and cuts off air to the roots, causing the tubers to suffocate and fungal diseases to set in. Harvesting your cassava on time or planting on raised mounds helps water drain away safely.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii mli ni efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni enáa tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmei yɛ be naa loo adu yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ mli shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping their flowers without developing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the tree lacks water or nutrients, or when tiny beneficial insects called midges are missing to pollinate them. Providing light shade and avoiding harsh chemical sprays during peak flowering helps pods form successfully.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii kpakpai. Aloo beni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ bɛ kɛha pollination. Kɛ́ aha ŋmeii lɛ ahe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ajie tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔii amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛmaa shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmãa duɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull natural nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. This enriches your land naturally so your maize can feed on those nutrients without relying entirely on bought fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, o-abele lɛ baanyɛ aye nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ohe afɔ̃ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ahe lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and flat before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani eshɛ po lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit, usually because the soil moisture keeps changing from very wet to very dry. Water your tomatoes regularly to ensure a steady supply of moisture and nutrients.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. ni calcium ni faaa lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ nɔ ni efɔ waa kɛyaa nɔ ni egbi waa nɔ. Okɛ nu awo o-tomato lɛ mli daa koni ená ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do I need to support my yam vines with tall stakes instead of letting them trail on the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ fiɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ asɛɛ moŋ fe ni mahã amɛnyiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines onto stakes allows the leaves to catch maximum sunlight needed to grow large underground tubers, while keeping the leaves off the damp ground prevents leaf spot diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hela akamɔ bo.

english: What is eating small holes into the leaves of my young maize plants and leaving tiny black specks inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni miiye yɛ bu bibioo lɛ mli? Yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ Ni eshiɔ ŋmeii diji bibii yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central funnel of the plant during the day. Applying approved pest treatments or botanical sprays like neem early in the morning into the plant's heart helps clear them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ tamɔ neem wo tso lɛ tsui mli leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛhe afee faŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the extra suckers growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishi lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Leaving too many suckers creates competition for soil nutrients and water, resulting in smaller plantain bunches. Keeping only the main stem, one medium sucker, and one small shoot gives you the best yield.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ekɛ akaŋshii baa kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii. Kɛ́ akpa tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ pɛ, tso lɛ yibii ni dalɛ ji teŋgbɛ, kɛ tso lɛ yibii bibii kome pɛ lɛ, ebaaha yibiiwoo ni hi fe fɛɛ aba.

english: How does covering the bare soil around my pepper plants with dry bush grass help them grow?
ga: Bɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi woɔ pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass creates a protective layer that traps moisture, keeps the soil cool during hot days, and prevents weeds from popping up to steal plant food.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni ŋmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekaje kpo ni eju niyenii kɛjɛ tsei lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper bushes curling upward and looking stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper bush lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee tamɔ mɛi ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that transmit viruses and drain plant sap. Controlling these insects early with insecticidal soap or recommended sprays protects the new leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa ni ekɛ nu ni jɛɔ tsei amli lɛ shwieɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛ akɛ samla loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai heei ahe.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize plant is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure early in the crop's growth helps keep the leaves green so the cobs can grow big.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tso lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he mra yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi ŋmɔŋ bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ adara.

english: Why is it helpful for me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ manyɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. Planting them alongside maize naturally enriches the soil, helps the maize grow better, and gives you two different harvests from the same field.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele ni aduɔ yɛ abele masɛi lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni amɛfee nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ ni jɛ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot on the branch before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ dani amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp conditions. Pruning heavy shade tree branches to let sunlight in and clearing off infected pods right away helps keep the rest of your harvest safe.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo waa lɛ amli koni hulu la babaoo aba mli, ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni oŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up with bright yellow patches on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kpɛɔ lɛ?

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried between plants by tiny whiteflies. The best solution is to obtain and plant disease-resistant cassava stems provided by agricultural extension officers.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. he ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ tsɔɔ tsei ateŋ Nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ ofee ji ni otao ni odu ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛhaa lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over during windstorms before the fruit matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbee shi yɛ ahum ko mli dani aduawai lɛ kwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can easily be weakened by underground pests like nematodes or banana weevils. Supporting the fruiting trees with sturdy wooden poles and planting clean suckers prevents them from falling.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ nematodes loo banana ŋmeii baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa fiɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ asɛɛ, ni aduɔ ŋmeii ni he tse lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the sunlight to make food for growing big tubers under the ground. Staking also keeps the leaves off the damp soil, which protects the plant from fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulb agbo ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Tomato flowers often drop without fruiting when the weather gets extremely hot or when the soil dries out suddenly. Keeping the soil regularly watered and providing light shade during extreme heat helps the flowers turn into fruit.
