ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi trukaa. Kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu daa ni aha lɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why do the bottoms of my pepper fruits turn black and squishy while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper aduawai lɛ shishi batsɔ ediŋŋ ni efee blɛoo beni edaa lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a shortage of calcium in the growing fruit, often triggered by irregular watering. Watering your pepper plants consistently helps the roots absorb calcium steadily from the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ afɔ pepper tsei anɔ nu daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛshishifãi lɛ ni amɛjieɔ calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa.

english: Healthy soil is usually dark brown or black, feels crumbly when squeezed, drains excess water easily, and contains natural organisms like earthworms. Adding animal manure or compost helps build up poor soil over time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa ji ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ. Enuɔ he akɛ egbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ ashɛre lɛ Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ mlɛo Ni adebɔɔ mli nibii tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ama shikpɔŋ ni ehiii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my vegetable crops look weak and wilted even when it rains every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgboi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa gbi po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Too much standing water can drown plant roots by removing oxygen from the soil, causing roots to rot and leaves to wilt. Creating raised garden beds or drainage furrows helps excess rainwater flow away from root systems.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei ashishifãi atsɔ oxygen ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni baai lɛ hu gbɔjɔɔ. Abɔɔ mli saatsoi ni awó nɔ loo nu homɔ ŋshɔi ni afee lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: What is Cocoa Swollen Shoot Disease, and why is it dangerous for my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji Kokoo Bud Swolɛ Hela? Ni mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa Swollen Shoot Disease is a serious viral infection spread by tiny insects that damages cocoa trees, lowers crop yields, and eventually kills the trees if not handled quickly.
ga: Cocoa tip fuumɔ ji hela ko ni hiɛdɔɔ yɔɔ mli ni koolooi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa. ni haa kokoo tsei lɛ fiteɔ Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ agbo kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii oya.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa tree has swollen shoot disease just by looking at the leaves and stems?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ kookoo tso ko eshishifãi efu kɛtsɔ baai kɛ eshishifãi lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ?

english: You can spot swollen shoot disease by looking for swollen branches or stems, red lines along leaf veins, yellow mottled patterns on leaves, and unusually small cocoa pods.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona bud hela ni efuu kɛtsɔ niji loo tsei ni efuu lɛ ataomɔ nɔ. Linei tsuji ni yɔɔ baa lɛ fãji lɛ ahe Hei ŋmɔŋ yɛ baa lɛ nɔ kɛ kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ

english: Why are my cocoa pods growing much smaller and rounder than normal?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ daraaa kwraa ni eyɛ kokroo fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ?

english: Small, rounded, or deformed cocoa pods are a major sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Disease, which prevents nutrients from properly reaching and developing the fruit.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ bibii, ni yɔɔ kokroo, loo ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji okadii ni he hiaa ni tsɔɔ akɛ cocoa lɛ mli efu. Enɛ haaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ashɛ aduawai lɛ ahe ni ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers cut down cocoa trees infected with swollen shoot instead of giving me spray medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ shwieɔ kookoo tsei ni amɛshishifãi efuu lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ tsofa baashwie nɔ lɛ?

english: Swollen shoot is caused by a virus inside the tree's sap system, so chemical sprays cannot cure it. Cutting down infected trees is the only proven way to stop the virus from spreading to surrounding healthy trees.
ga: Virus ko ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nu mli lɛ kɛ tsei ashishifãi ni efuu baa. No hewɔ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nyɛŋ atsa lɛ. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni ana he odaseyeli ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli.

english: How does swollen shoot disease move from an infected cocoa tree to healthy ones nearby?
ga: Te bud swollen hela lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ kɛjɛɔ cacao tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ?

english: The disease is spread by tiny mealybug insects that feed on infected sap and crawl to healthy trees, often carried across the farm by ants or blowing in the wind.
ga: Hela nɛɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni ji mealybugs lɛ amli. No yeɔ nu ni hela emɔ lɛ ni efoɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii woɔ enɛɛmɛi yɛ ŋmɔji amli loo kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa amɛ kɛyaa.

english: Can I plant new cocoa seedlings immediately in the same spot where diseased trees were cut down?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui heei amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ he ni afo tso ni hela emɔ lɛ yɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: No, you should wait and allow all remaining roots and mealybug populations to die out completely, while planting shade crops like plantains first to prepare the soil.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ omɛ ni oha shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ agboi kwraa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, dumɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, koni okɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees get scorched easily by harsh sun. Fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that act as natural umbrellas to shade and cool the young cocoa trees during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta, ni ehaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning yellow and dropping early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves that fall off early can be caused by nutrient shortages in the soil, lack of water during dry spells, or sap-sucking viral diseases weakening the tree.
ga: Niyenii nibii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ mra. Nu ni bɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli Loo hela ni haa tso lɛ nuɔ nu lɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: How can the Cocoa Health and Extension Division help me keep my farm healthy?
ga: Te Cocoa Hewalɛ kɛ Nɔyaa Nitsumɔhe lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni miŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Extension officers provide expert advice on recognizing diseases early, offer training on crop care, and help farmers manage diseased trees properly to protect their income.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ hiɛyaa mli lɛ haa ŋaawoo ni he esa yɛ hela lɛ ni ayɔseɔ mra lɛ he. Ha tsɔsemɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ kɛ yelikɛbuamɔ ni akɛhaa okwaafoi ni amɛkwɛɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛbu amɛshika he.

english: Does dry or rainy weather change how cocoa diseases spread across my farm?
ga: Ani kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ tsakeɔ bɔ ni kookoo hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, warm dry weather encourages pests like mealybugs to multiply and move around, while rainy and humid weather helps fungal diseases spread quickly among dense foliage.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mealybugs lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛfɔ ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛya he fɛɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi yeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ tsei ahe tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to grow green and healthy. When nitrogen is low, the plant pulls it from older bottom leaves to feed new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ nitrogen lɛ faaa Tso lɛ gbalaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves and shallow roots that cannot handle direct sun. They need shade crops, like plantain or cassava, planted next to them to block excess heat and keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo cassava. planted next to Enɛ baatsi dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ naa ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil. Rotating your crops with beans or groundnuts helps put natural nutrients back into the land so future crops grow larger.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Extreme hot weather or uneven watering causes tomato plants to stress. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save water and energy for its own survival.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Plantain roots do not grow deep into the ground. When the fruit bunch grows heavy, the tree becomes top-heavy and needs wooden prop poles to stay upright during strong winds.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji aduawai akuu lɛ batsɔ tsii lɛ Tsei lɛ baaná muji yɛ amɛyiteŋ ni esa akɛ akɛ tsei afi amɛhe koni amɛhi shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot inside the ground during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When water sits in the soil for too long without draining, it prevents air from reaching the roots, causing underground fungal infections that rot the cassava tubers.
ga: Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Enɛ baatsi kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni enyɛ eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsɛŋemɔ hela ko baa ni haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden sticks next to my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers. Staking the vines holds the leaves up off the hot soil and spreads them out to catch more sunlight, which helps the underground tubers grow much bigger.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ gɔŋ. Wein tso lɛ ni akɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ jeɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa koni hulu la babaoo aba. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ daraa babaoo.

english: Why are small caterpillars hiding inside the center leaves of my growing corn stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These pests, known as Fall Armyworms, hide inside the tender center leaves because that is the softest and most nutritious part of the maize plant to eat.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ, ni atsɛɔ amɛ Fall Armyworms lɛ, kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli ejaakɛ no ji ŋmei tso lɛ fã ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni niyenii yɔɔ mli fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ aye.

english: Weed seeds naturally survive in the soil for years and are adapted to sprout immediately with the first drop of rain, using up the soil's nutrients before crops get a chance to grow.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo. ni atsake lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ lɛ nɛ. Ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii dani ŋmɔshi nibii náa hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: How can I keep my harvested pepper crop from spoiling quickly when I cannot sell it right away?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni mi-pepper tsei ni mikpa lɛ akafite oya nɛkɛ? Akɛni minyɛɛɛ mahɔ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ hewɔ lɛ?

english: Harvested peppers continue to breathe and lose water. Storing them in cool, shaded spaces away from direct sunlight or drying them preserves them until you can take them to market.
ga: Peppers ni akpa lɛ yaa nɔ emuɔ ni nu lɛ hu sɛɛ foɔ. Akɛtoɔ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. He ni hulu la shɛɛɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo egbiɔ lɛ, abaato he gbɛjianɔ kɛyashi obaanyɛ okɛya jara nɔ.

english: Why do plantains produce large bunches in places like Agogo while my plantains stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kui wuji amli yɛ hei tamɔ Agogo lɛ? Be mli ni mi plantains lɛ ji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Plantain plants need deep, rich soil with plenty of natural compost and consistent moisture to grow heavy bunches. Areas with high plantain yields usually have forest soils rich in organic matter and good rainfall that allow the shallow roots to feed continuously.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii lɛ he miihia plantains. kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa koni akɛkwɛ jwɛi wuji. Bei pii lɛ, hei ni plantain shwereɔ babaoo yɛ lɛ yɛ koo mli shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli, ni nugbɔ nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni no haa shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ yeɔ nii daa.

english: Why do my green plantains ripen and spoil quickly when transported in large quantities to long-distance markets?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains eŋɔli lɛ shwereɔ ni egboɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛ babaoo tee jarayeli hei ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Harvested plantains naturally release an invisible gas that speeds up their ripening, especially when stacked closely in warm, unventilated trucks. Keeping plantains shaded, cool, and well-ventilated during transport helps them stay green and firm for longer journeys.
ga: Plantains ni akpa lɛ jieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni anaaa ni haa ekwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ akɛto lɔle ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, ni jɛmɛ ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli yɛ be mli ni akɛ amɛ yaa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhi shi shiŋŋ kɛha gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why does my plantain tree stop producing fruit after I harvest the main bunch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ kpaɔ yibiiwoo beni mikpa tso titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A plantain stalk is designed by nature to produce only one bunch of fruit in its lifetime. Once that bunch matures, the main stem naturally dies so its nutrients can feed the new young shoots sprouting around its base.
ga: Adebɔɔ ji nɔ ni fee plantain tsei lɛ koni amɛwo yibii akuu kome pɛ yɛ amɛwala be fɛɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ kuu lɛ eda kwraa lɛ, tso titri lɛ baagbo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aha ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ eshishigbɛ lɛ.

english: How do new plantain shoots grow around the main stem, and which ones should I replant?
ga: Tsofɔi heei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe. Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tso lɛ wulu lɛ Ni mɛɛ tsei esa akɛ madu?

english: Plantain trees spread underground by forming new shoots called suckers. The best suckers to replant are 'sword suckers,' which have narrow, blade-like leaves and a thick base, as they grow into strong plants with bigger bunches than broad-leafed shoots.
ga: Dumɔwui gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ shishi kɛtsɔ ŋmeii heei ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfeɔ lɛ nɔ. Sucker ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha dumɔ ekoŋŋ ji ‘sword sucker’, ni yɔɔ baai ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni tamɔ baai. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ tsei ni he wa, ni amɛyɛ fɔfɔii wuji fe tsei ni yɔɔ baai babaoo lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during strong rains right when the bunches get heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli ni jwɛi lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots rather than deep taproots, making it difficult for the plant to balance a heavy bunch during strong winds or wet soil. Supporting the main stem with a sturdy wooden prop or bamboo pole prevents the plant from uprooting before harvest.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ moŋ fe shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa tsei lɛ akɛ amɛaakwɛ amɛhe nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kui ni tsii amli yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso loo ŋmei tso ni wa fi tso lɛ shishi tso titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekaje shishi dani akpa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my plantain tree turning yellow before the bunch is ready to pick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmɔ lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate that the plant is short on soil nutrients like nitrogen, lacks water, or is affected by leaf spot diseases. Clearing dead leaves and adding manure or compost around the base keeps the leaves green and productive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa, tamɔ nitrogen, nu bɛ mli, loo baa mli ŋmɔtɔ hela miigba enaa. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooojie baai ni egboi lɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo tso lɛ he. Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni ekɛ yibii kpakpai aba.

english: How long does a young plantain sucker take from planting until the fruit is ready to harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani plantain tsei bibii lɛ daraa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛyibii lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: A plantain plant typically takes between 12 to 15 months from planting to harvest. The tree flowers around 9 to 12 months, and the bunch then needs about 3 to 4 months to fill out completely before it is ready to cut.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui heɔ aaafee nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 15 kɛjɛ be mli ni aduɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni akpaa. Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli, ni ehe hiaa aaafee nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 dani tsei akui lɛ afɔ̃ fɔfɔi kwraa dani amɛfee klalo akɛ abaafolɔ amɛ.

english: Plantains have broad leaves that need sunlight and wide root systems that search for food and water. Planting them too close causes them to block each other's light and compete for nutrients, resulting in thinner stems and smaller bunches.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni biɔ hulu la kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni akɛtaoɔ niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee amɛhe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kpakpai. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni kui lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why am I finding dark holes inside my plantain stems that make the leaves wilt and break?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii diji yɛ tsei lɛ amli ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkuɔ lɛ?

english: Tunnels inside the stem are usually caused by plantain stem borers or weevils whose larvae burrow into the trunk and roots. Using clean planting suckers and keeping the base of the plants weed-free stops these pests from multiplying.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantain trunk borers loo weevils, ni amɛmli ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baa. Sucker ni he tse ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ tso lɛ shishi ni jwɛi akafee lɛ Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ akafa babaoo.

english: Why do plantain leaves roll up or split along the sides during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛgbalaa amɛhe yɛ sɛɛgbɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves roll or split naturally during hot, dry weather to reduce water loss from sunlight and wind. Covering the soil around the plant with dry grass or leaves helps trap soil moisture and protects the roots during hot months.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛgbalaa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Koni nu ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Mulching around Dumɔ ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ nyɔji ni mli edɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why does my maize crop take several months to grow before I can harvest it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ heɔ nyɔji babaoo dani anyɛɔ akpaa lɛ?

english: Maize does not mature overnight; it goes through essential stages—sprouting, leaf growth, flowering, and kernel filling. Each stage takes time and proper nourishment to yield healthy cobs.
ga: Abɛi shwereee nyɔɔŋ kome mli. Etsɔɔ gbɛi ni he hiaa tamɔ shweremɔ, baa dalɛ, fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui ni eyimɔ mli. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni afeɔ lɛ biɔ be kɛ saamɔ ni sa koni aná ŋmei ni mli wa.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and grow very slowly early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiida blɛoo waa yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Maize requires heavy nutrients, especially nitrogen, to build strong green leaves. Slow growth and yellow leaves mean the plants are starving for soil nutrients or being choked by weeds.
ga: Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni tsii he miihia ŋmãa. titri lɛ nitrogen Koni afee baai eŋɔli ni mli wa Baai ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo kɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miiye shikpɔŋ lɛ hɔmɔ loo jwɛi miigbe lɛ.

english: What happens to my maize crop if rain stops just when the flowers and tassels start showing?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-abele lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa be mli ni fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛjeɔ kpo lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: Flowering is the most critical time for maize. Without enough water during tasseling, the plants cannot form seeds properly, leading to empty or poorly filled cobs.
ga: Be ni fɔfɔi fɔɔ lɛ ji be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ kɛha ŋmãa. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ tsɔne lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ awo dumɔwui jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ efolo loo amɛwooo amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How will using machines like tractors or shellers help my maize farm compared to doing everything by hand?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔnei tamɔ trakta loo sheller ni mikɛaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ? Kɛ akɛto nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni akɛ niji feɔ lɛ he

english: Farm machines speed up land preparation, planting, and processing, allowing you to cultivate larger acres with less physical effort and harvest your crop before it spoils.
ga: Okwaayeli mli tsɔnei haa shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ, dumɔwui, kɛ nitsumɔ yaa oya, ni ehaa onyɛɔ otsuɔ ŋmɔji wuji ni okɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ fioo pɛ tsuɔ nii. ni okpa onibii lɛ dani amɛgboi.

english: Are there government programs or machine services available to help small-scale maize farmers like me expand?
ga: Ani nɔyeli gbɛjianɔtoi loo tsɔnei ahe nitsumɔi komɛi yɛ ni baaye abua ŋmãa okwaafoi bibii tamɔ mi ni amɛgbɛ amɛ nitsumɔ lɛ amɛshwã?

english: Yes, governments and agricultural initiatives often supply processing machinery, mechanized services, and subsidized inputs to help local farmers increase production and profitability.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, nɔyelii kɛ okwaayeli he gbɛjianɔtoi kɛ tsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa. tsɔnei ahe nitsumɔi kɛ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni nine shɛɔ yelikɛbuamɔ nɔ Koni eye ebua maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi ni amɛha nibii ni amɛfeɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ni amɛná sɛɛnamɔi.

english: Why is it dangerous to leave weeds in my young maize farm during the first month?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mashi jwɛi yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young maize plants grow slowly at first and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds, which steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight your crop needs to thrive.
ga: Abɛi tsei bibii lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ, ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛshwere lɛ.

english: Why should I avoid planting my maize seeds too close together in the same line?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmãa kome mli lɛ he?

english: When planted too closely, maize stalks fight each other for root space and sunlight, resulting in weak, thin plants that produce very small cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, Abɛi tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ shishifãi kɛ hulu la he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: How can I encourage young people in my community to join me in maize farming?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mawo oblahii kɛ oblayei ni yɔɔ mi akutso lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛfata mihe yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Youth are attracted to commercial farming when modern machinery and business tools are introduced, turning labor-intensive hand farming into a profitable, modern enterprise.
ga: Oblahii kɛ oblayei baasumɔ jarayeli okwaayeli beni akɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsɔnei kɛ jarayeli nibii baa lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, okwaayeli ni akɛ niji tsuɔ ni heɔ nitsumɔ babaoo lɛ ebatsɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ nitsumɔ ko ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he.

english: How does investing extra effort and modern tools into maize farming increase my income?
ga: Te mɔdɛŋbɔɔ babaoo kɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ nibii ni mikɛwoɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shika ni mináa lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Using modern tools and careful field management increases your total yield per acre, reduces crop loss during harvest, and provides a larger volume of high-quality grain to sell.
ga: Kɛ okɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha onibii fɛɛ ni obaaná yɛ acre kome mli lɛ aya hiɛ. Ha ŋmɔshi nibii ni laajeɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ aba shi. ni eha dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni abaahɔ̃ɔ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do I need to dry my harvested maize thoroughly before putting it into storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni magbi mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ kwraa dani mikɛwo kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii amli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Wet or moist maize attracts mold and destructive insects like weevils, whereas drying grains properly ensures your harvest stays fresh for months so you can sell at higher market prices.
ga: Abɛi ni mli efɔ loo ni mli efɔ lɛ gbalaa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ nii tamɔ ŋmeii, yɛ be mli ni kɛ́ ogbi oŋmaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni onibii lɛ ahiɔ shi nyɔji babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and curling up in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe yɛ hulu la lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves curl and yellow when exposed to excessive heat and direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides a natural canopy that keeps the young trees cool and retains soil moisture.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ la ni mli edɔ waa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ cocoa masɛi lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi lɛ baa.

english: Why do my maize leaves look like someone shot tiny holes all through them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni mɔ ko tu bu bibii kɛtsɔ mli lɛ?

english: Tiny holes in leaves are usually caused by stemborer or fall armyworm caterpillars feeding on the central leaf shoot. As the leaf unfurls and grows, those feeding spots spread out into visible lines of holes across the leaf blade.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, stem borers loo cutworms ni egbee shi ni eye baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Beni baai lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛdaraa lɛ, nakai niyeli hei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ buji ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni abaanyɛ ana yɛ baa lɛ he fɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Maize benefits most from fertilizer applied in two stages: first at 10 to 14 days after planting to build strong roots, and second when the plant reaches knee height to support growing thick stalks and big cobs.
ga: Abɛi náa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he sɛɛ fe fɛɛ yɛ gbɛi enyɔ nɔ: Klɛŋklɛŋ gbɛ lɛ ji gbii 10 kɛyashi 14 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ koni shishifãi ni wa aba. kɛ fã ni ji enyɔ lɛ beni tso lɛ shɛɔ enaji ahe koni ekɛfi tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji lɛ adalɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots soft-rot under the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when water sits in the soil for too long after heavy rains. Too much stagnant water cuts off air to the roots, allowing soil fungi to infect and break down the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsɛŋeɔ ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ.

english: Why should I cut down extra shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi plantain tso titri lɛ

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water, light, and soil nutrients from the mother plant. Leaving only one strong follower shoot ensures the main plant gets enough energy to produce heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ nu, la kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie sɛɛnyiɛlɔ tso kome pɛ ni he wa lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo plantains babaoo.

english: Why do I need to put up tall sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madamɔ shi shiŋŋ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need maximum sunlight to make food for underground tuber growth. Staking lifts leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to light and protecting them from soil rot diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii kɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tuber lɛ dalɛ. Elevator ni akɛ staking woɔ mli lɛ baashi he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Okɛ amɛ awo la mli ni obu amɛhe kɛjɛ sũ ni fiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when temperatures get too high or water is inconsistent. Extreme heat stresses the plant and prevents pollen from setting fruit, causing the flower stem to dry up and snap off.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ehaaa pollen lɛ akawo yibii lɛ amli. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ ahe tsei lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛkuɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants shrinking and twisting into tiny cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiitsɔ kɔɔpoi bibii amli lɛ?

english: Wrinkled and cupped pepper leaves are caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids. As they feed on the juices inside young leaves, the uneven leaf damage makes the leaves distort and curl.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni egbɔjɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Beni amɛnuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ Baai lɛ ni efiteɔ ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ haa baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my field make my corn grow better afterwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas pull nitrogen gas out of the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots decompose in the soil after harvest, they leave behind rich nitrogen that feeds the next corn crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni tso shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Tso shishifãi shĩɔ nitrogen babaoo yɛ amɛsɛɛ koni ekɛha ŋmãa tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Leaf rolling is a survival trick plants use to save water. By curling their leaves inward, plants reduce the surface area exposed to harsh sunlight and dry wind, stopping moisture from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Baai ni atsiɔ lɛ ji wala yiwalaheremɔ ŋaa ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ awo mli lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa egbiɔ lɛ baa shi. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ.

english: Why do I need to build large soil mounds before planting my yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa gɔŋ agbo dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, loose, deep soil to swell into large tubers. Mounds make it easy for roots to expand without hitting hard ground, while also letting heavy rainwater drain away so the tubers do not rot.
ga: Sweet potato he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ koni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Gɔji haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ shishifãi lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛnáaa shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha nugbɔ nu ni naa wa lɛ atsɔ mli koni tsɔnei lɛ akafite.

english: How can I tell if a cassava stem cutting is healthy enough to sprout well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tso lɛ mli tsei ni afo lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Choose firm, mature stems from disease-free plants. A healthy cutting should bleed milky sap quickly when clipped, have nodes placed close together, and show no tiny holes from stem borers or dark spots from disease.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni eda kɛjɛ tsei ni helai bɛ mli lɛ amli. Esa akɛ lá ajɛ he ni afo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ oya kɛji afo. Ayɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwo amɛhe ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe. Ni buji bibii komɛi hu bɛ jɛmɛ. kɛjɛ tso shishi botemɔ mli loo hei ni yɔɔ duŋ ni jɛɔ hela mli baa lɛ mli

english: If I burn the dry bush on my land before planting, does it ruin the soil?
ga: Kɛ mishã tsei ni egbi yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani midu Ani ebaafite shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: While burning clears the land fast and leaves temporary ash, it destroys organic matter, kills good organisms like earthworms, and dries out the soil. Clearing land without burning leaves nutrients in the ground for longer crop health.
ga: Beni la ni tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he oya ni eshiɔ sũ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ. Shi ebaakpãtã nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ahiɛ. Egbeɔ nibii kpakpai tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gĩɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ashãaa lɛ haa niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Yellow lower leaves mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato plants shed flowers when they face stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil followed by heavy watering, or a lack of phosphorus in the soil. Maintaining steady soil moisture helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni nu babaoo nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. loo fɔsfɔs ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids, mites, or thrips hiding under the leaves. Sprays made from neem seed oil or soap solution can help clear these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, mites loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. Nibii ni akɛ neem dumɔwui amli fɔ loo samla fee lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ejie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily burn under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast with wide leaves that provide living shade, keeping the cocoa plants cool and moist during their first few years.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa cacao tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: What advantage do I get if I plant groundnuts or cowpeas in the same plot as my maize?
ga: Mɛɛ sɛɛnamɔ maná kɛji midu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmei?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When they grow beside maize, they naturally feed the soil and boost your maize harvest without extra cost.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi Amɛbaahã shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛha ŋmãa ni okpaa lɛ aya hiɛ ni okɛ shika kroko fataaa he.

english: How do I know if the first rain after the dry season is enough to start planting my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni mikɛje dumɔwui adumɔ shishi?

english: The very first rain can be misleading and leave soil dry underneath. It is safest to wait until you get two or three steady rains over a week so the ground holds enough deep moisture to keep germinated seeds alive.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ baanyɛ alaka mɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ agbi. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ be fɛɛ be shii 2-3 yɛ otsi mli. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ ahi nu ni mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: How should I apply chemical fertilizer so the heavy rain does not wash it all away?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ afata he koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie fɛɛ?

english: Do not scatter fertilizer on top of the soil right before a downpour. Dig a small hole or shallow ring a few inches away from the plant stem, place the fertilizer inside, and cover it back up with soil.
ga: Kaagbɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ anɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ bu bibioo ko loo ring ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Inchi enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ awo mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ sũ aha nɔ

english: Is there any difference between how I take care of local crops and agric crops on my farm?
ga: Ani srɔtofeemɔ ko yɛ bɔ ni mikwɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ okwaayeli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ teŋ?

english: Yes, agric or improved varieties are specially bred for high yields and often require specific fertilizers, pruning, and spray schedules, while local varieties are naturally tougher and can survive with minimal care, though proper care will still boost their harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, akwɛɔ okwaayeli loo ŋmeii srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛná yibii babaoo ni bei pii lɛ, ehe bahiaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli. ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ bei pɔtɛɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei srɔtoi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe wa yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi kɛji akwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Eyɛ mli akɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa baanyɛ aye abua lolo ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ moŋ.

english: Why do agric crop varieties produce bigger harvests than our traditional local varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli mli ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe wɔ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Agric varieties are bred by scientists to direct most of their energy into making large, abundant fruits, whereas traditional local varieties use a lot of their energy just to survive harsh weather and wild conditions.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi fɔɔ okwaayeli koni ekɛ ehewalɛ babaoo atsu nii ni ekɛwo aduawai wuji ni fa babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, akutseiaŋ okwaayeli henɔi ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ blema lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa kɛ kooi amli shihilɛi amli kɛkɛ.

english: Why do local trees seem to handle diseases better than the agric varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni maŋ tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛkpeɔ helai anaa jogbaŋŋ fe okwaayeli tsei srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Local varieties have adapted to the local environment and pests over many generations, giving them strong natural resistance, while agric varieties trade some of that natural toughness for higher yield and faster growth.
ga: Kuu lɛ mli tsei srɔtoi lɛ etsɔ amɛhe amɛwo akutso lɛ mli shihilɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ amli yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Enɛ haa amɛnáa adebɔɔ mli shitee-kɛ-woo ni mli wa. yɛ be mli ni okwaayeli henɔi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ lɛ ekomɛi koni amɛná yibii babaoo kɛ amɛdalɛ oya.

english: Can I plant local crop varieties and agric varieties together in the exact same field?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ maŋ lɛ mli kɛ okwaayeli mli tsei srɔtoi lɛ ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: It is usually better to separate them because agric crops require specific spacing, fertilizer routines, and pest management that local varieties might disrupt or compete with for sunlight and nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi amɛhe kɛjɛ amɛhe ejaakɛ okwaayeli tsei biɔ he pɔtɛɛ ko ni amɛyɔɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akwɛmɔ yɛ he ni kooloi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ loo amɛye akaŋ kɛha hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Do wild fruit trees that grew naturally on my land need any fertilizer or spray, or should I just leave them alone?
ga: Ani koo mli aduawai tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ awo mli? Aloo esa akɛ mashi lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: While wild trees can survive on their own, giving them basic care like clearing weeds around their trunk, light pruning, and adding fertilizer will help them produce much bigger and sweeter fruit than normal.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ koo mli tsei baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe moŋ, shi shishijee kwɛmɔ tamɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle tso lɛ he lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi fioo. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ewo yibii ni da kwraa ni ŋɔɔ fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ.

english: Is it necessary to prune local wild trees, or is pruning only meant for agric crops?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni afolɔ koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Aloo okwaayeli tsei pɛ ji nɔ ni akɛfoɔ tsei ahe?

english: Pruning benefits both types. It removes dead or sick branches and lets sunlight reach the inner leaves, but agric crops depend on regular pruning much more to control tree size and maximize fruit output.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo hela mɔ amɛ lɛ, ni ehaa hulu la shɛɔ baai lɛ amli. Shi okwaayeli mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ damɔ tsei ni afoɔ daa lɛ nɔ koni akɛkudɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ ni amɛha yibii babaoo aba.

english: Do I need to leave more space between agric trees when planting compared to local ones?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ, ani esa akɛ gbɛ ni kã okwaayeli tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni da fe tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Yes, agric varieties often need precise spacing to ensure every tree gets enough sunlight, air flow, and soil nutrients to produce heavy yields without spreading diseases to each other.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, okwaayeli henɔi lɛ biɔ gbɛ pɔtɛɛ ni amɛaatsɔ nɔ amɛkwɛ akɛ tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni ekɛ nibii babaoo aba ni helai egbɛɛɛ eshwaaa amɛhe.

english: Does a crop that yields big fruits need more fertilizer than one that yields small local fruits?
ga: Ani tsei ni woɔ yibii wuji lɛ biɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fe tsei ni woɔ yibii bibii yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, producing larger fruits requires more food and nutrients from the soil, so big-yielding agric crops generally need more fertilizer than smaller local varieties.
ga: Hɛɛ, aduawai wuji ni abaawo lɛ biɔ niyenii kɛ niyenii kpakpai babaoo kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, okwaayeli mli nibii ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ biɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fe maŋbii bibii lɛ.

english: Should I use the same pest spray for my big fruit trees and my small local fruit trees?
ga: Esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii yɛ aduawai tsei wuji kɛ aduawai tsei bibii anɔ. Kuu lɛ mli loo jeee nakai

english: Not always. While the chemical depends on the specific pest, larger trees and high-yielding agric varieties usually require higher spray volumes and more careful timing than smaller, hardy local trees.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be, eyɛ mli akɛ tsofai lɛ damɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi anɔ moŋ. Bei pii lɛ, tsei wuji kɛ okwaayeli mli tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ biɔ ni afɔ amɛ tsofa babaoo kɛ be ni akɛkwɛɔ jogbaŋŋ fe tsei bibii ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli ni wa lɛ.

english: Do agric crop varieties need more watering during the dry season than local crops?
ga: Ani okwaayeli tsei srɔtoi lɛ biɔ nu babaoo yɛ fɛ̃i be mli fe maŋbii tsei?

english: Yes, because agric varieties grow faster and carry more leaves and fruit, they consume more water and will suffer more quickly during dry spells if not watered.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ okwaayeli mli tsei srɔtoi lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ baai kɛ aduawai babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ amɛyeɔ nu babaoo ni amɛbaana amanehulu oya yɛ hɔmɔ be mli kɛji akɛ ahaaa amɛ nu.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and scorched during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight when they are small. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside them acts as a living shelter, keeping the soil moist and protecting tender leaves from burning.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ beni amɛdarako lɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Etsu nii akɛ shĩa Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni otsi baai bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkashã.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, which maize relies on to grow strong green leaves and develop healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ biɔ ni ŋmãa lɛ akwɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli wa ni ená ŋmãa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I place chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ midumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer contains strong salts that can burn and kill young roots and stems if placed in direct contact. It should be applied in a small ring or side pocket a few inches away from the plant.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ashã ni egbe shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Esa akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai bibii amli. loo sɛɛ kotokui ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ.

english: Leaf curl is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaves, or by a viral infection spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni shwieɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli

english: Tomato plants often shed their blossoms without growing fruit when temperatures get too high or when there is sudden dry weather, as a defense mechanism to conserve water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shihilɛi lɛ mli egbi trukaa. akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ nu ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ naa

english: Why do my cassava tubers start turning dark and spoiling inside if I leave them in the ground too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Once cassava tubers reach full maturity, holding them in the wet ground too long forces them to absorb excessive moisture, causing the core to ferment and rot.
ga: Beni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ edara kwraa lɛ Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii lɛ wo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛŋɔ nu babaoo. Enɛ haa ŋshɔ lɛ mli fã lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efiteɔ.

english: Yam plants store energy in tubers through sunlight absorbed by leaves. Staking lifts the foliage off the ground so leaves catch full sunlight while preventing soil-borne fungal diseases from touching the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ hewalɛ toɔ amɛ bulbs lɛ amli kɛtsɔɔ hulu la ni baai lɛ gbalaa lɛ nɔ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la lɛ fɛɛ ashɛ baai lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni etsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ hu naa koni amɛkashɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that prefer that crop to build up in the ground over time.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tsei ni sumɔɔ tsei lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why does covering the soil around my garden crops with dry grass help them grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo mibɔɔ mli tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves keeps the soil cool under direct sun, retains soil water longer after rain, and suppresses weed growth.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa

english: The first rain usually leaves the soil dry just below the surface; heat trapped deep in the warm earth can dry out fragile germinating seeds before regular rains set in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Dɔlɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli baanyɛ agbi dumɔwui ni waaa, ni ekwɛ̃ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ daa aba.

english: Planting maize too close together causes plants to fight for sunlight and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stalks and small cobs. Spacing them about 75 cm between rows and 25 to 30 cm between seeds gives each plant enough room to feed and yield large cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa. Aaafee 75 cm yɛ ŋmeii ateŋ kɛ 25 kɛyashi 30 cm yɛ dumɔwui ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ nii ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Which type of plantain sucker is best for me to plant on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ plantain sucker hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ makwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Sword suckers—the ones with narrow, blade-like leaves and a heavy base—are best because they have strong energy reserves, establish roots quickly, and grow into healthier, high-yielding plantain trees compared to broad-leafed water suckers.
ga: Sword suckers—ni ji nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tamɔ klante kɛ shishitoo ni tsii lɛ—hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛyɛ hewalɛ ni mli wa ni amɛkɛtoɔ. Bɔɔ shishifãi oya ni odara ni otsɔ plantain tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo. Kɛ akɛto nu mli ŋmeii ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ ahe

english: Why are the leaves on my young cassava plants curling up and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellowing in cassava is usually caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by extension officers is the best way to keep your farm healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baa ni ebɔle ehe ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Oŋmɔŋ henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ oha oŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Ragged holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the central leaf funnel. Checking your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or spraying early in the morning when caterpillars are active helps control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii amli lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu nii lɛ atsu nii. Aloo kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ leebi be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ miitsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off before any fruits appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai baa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulching helps the plant hold onto its flowers and produce fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Should I plant my crops right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu tsei yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ afi lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become steady, usually after two or three continuous heavy rains. The first rain is often followed by a dry spell that can scorch and destroy young germinating seeds.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi. Bei pii lɛ, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ ni baanyɛ ashã ni efite dumɔwui bibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why is it bad to plant maize on the exact same piece of land season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil nitrogen and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Ehaa nitrogen lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: When is the most critical time to weed my farm after planting?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni adu nii agbe naa lɛ?

english: The first 4 to 6 weeks after planting is the most critical period for weeding because young crop seedlings are too weak to compete with fast-growing weeds for water, fertilizer, and sunlight.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 4 kɛyashi 6 ni nyiɛɔ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ ji be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ kɛha jwɛi lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ darako tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha nu, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hulu la.

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting when the bottom leaves naturally dry up and fall, and the soil around the root base begins to swell and crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ. Beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishitoo lɛ he lɛ bɔi shwiemɔ ni egbɛ eshwa.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are just stressed from the sun or actually catching a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kokoo tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ hulu lɛ mli loo hela yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Sun stress usually causes leaves across the whole farm to droop or dry out evenly, while diseases usually start on just a few trees, showing early signs like small yellow spots, swollen stems, or unusual leaf patterns.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo be mli haomɔ haa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛgbiɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Yɛ be mli ni helai srɔtoi Bei pii lɛ, ejeɔ shishi yɛ tsei fioo komɛi pɛ anɔ. Amɛ jieɔ mra be mli okadii tamɔ ŋmɔŋ bibii, tsei ni efuu, loo baai henɔi ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ.

english: Why is it so important for me to treat cocoa diseases as soon as I notice the first tiny symptoms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsa cocoa syndrome lɛ kɛji mina klɛŋklɛŋ okadii bibii lɛ pɛ?

english: Catching a disease when it first appears stops it from spreading to your entire farm. Treating a few sick trees early saves you from the huge financial burden of trying to rescue a dying farm later.
ga: Helai ni ooomɔ beni amɛjeɔ kpo klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ haaa amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli. Tsa tsei fioo komɛi ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Ehereɔ bo kɛjɛɔ shika he jatsu kpele ni ji mɔdɛŋ ni obɔɔ koni ohere ŋmɔ ko ni miigbo lɛ yiwala yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: What causes the leaves on my cocoa trees to show small yellow patches before turning brown?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibii? dani etsɔ blɔfo

english: Yellow patches are early warning signs of stress or infection, such as swollen shoot virus or fungal attacks, indicating that the tree is trying to fight off an illness inside its system.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ji mra be mli kɔkɔbɔɔ okadi ni tsɔɔ haomɔ loo hela, tamɔ hela, tsei ni efuu loo tsɛŋemɔ hela tutuamɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miitao ni ekɛ hela ni yɔɔ egbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli lɛ awuu.

english: Can a cocoa tree fully recover after a disease makes most of its leaves fall off?
ga: Ani cacao tso ko baanyɛ aná hewalɛ kwraa beni hela eha ebaai lɛ ateŋ babaoo egbee shi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, cocoa trees are hardy and can endure severe stress, but they need help to recover. Pruning dead wood, reducing weed competition, and providing light shade will help the tree build up strength to grow new leaves.
ga: Hɛɛ, cacao tsei lɛ wa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ nɔnyɛɛ ni naa wa naa. Shi yelikɛbuamɔ he miihia amɛ koni amɛhe awa amɛ. Niji ni egboi lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ Haa jwɛi akaŋshii baa shi Ni hulutsoo ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enáa hewalɛ koni baai heei anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do some of my cocoa trees seem to survive dry spells much better than others on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ekomɛi hiɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ fe kookoo tsei krokomɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Trees with deeper root systems, better soil around them, or protection from shade trees can hold onto water longer, allowing them to endure heat and drought better than weaker trees.
ga: Tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe loo tsei ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he lɛ baanyɛ ahi nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa amɛŋmɛɔ amɛtsui shi yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ mli fe tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛheɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ.

english: What low-cost steps can I take to protect my farm if I do not have money to buy chemicals?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii ni he ehiaaa tsɔ manyɛ mafee koni mikɛbu miŋmɔ lɛ he? Kɛji obɛ shika ni okɛbaahe tsofai

english: You can protect your farm for free by regularly weeding, pruning dead or overcrowded branches for good airflow, and physically cutting out infected pods or diseased stems before sickness spreads.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔ lɛ he yaka kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ooojie daa lɛ nɔ. Niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ mli. kɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ dani hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why does cutting down one diseased cocoa tree help save the rest of my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tso kome ni hela emɔ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ hereɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ yiwala lɛ?

english: Diseases like cocoa swollen shoot spread easily from tree to tree through insects. Removing one sick tree acts like a barrier, protecting your healthy trees and saving you money in the long run.
ga: Helai tamɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ kɛtsɔɔ kooloi bibii anɔ oya. Tso kome ni hela mɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baatsu nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ mɔ he. Buu otsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe ni okɛ shika ato yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why does shade help my cocoa trees stay healthy when disease or dry weather hits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hulutsoo yeɔ ebuaa mi-cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ hela loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi ba lɛ?

english: Shade trees lower the temperature, shield delicate cocoa leaves from burning in harsh sun, and help the soil keep moisture, giving your cocoa trees the strength to endure weather stress and sickness.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi. Ebuɔ kookoo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe koni hulu la ni naa wa akashã amɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli Enɛ haa o-cacao tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe haomɔi kɛ helai.

english: Why do fungal diseases like black pod spread so fast on my cocoa farm during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ black pod fungal hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Fungal spores love cool, wet conditions. Raindrops bounce off infected pods and splash the fungus onto healthy pods nearby, causing the disease to spread rapidly if pods are not harvested quickly.
ga: Fungal spores sumɔɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ, ni edɔ. Nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ ni amɛshwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ amɛshwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛji akɛ akpaaa ŋmeii lɛ oya.

english: How does clear-weeding around my cocoa trees help them fight off diseases?
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni ajieɔ Bɔ ni Mi-Cacao Tsei lɛ Yeɔ Ebuaa Cacao Tsei lɛ ni Amɛwuɔ Helai

english: Weeds steal water, nutrients, and sunlight from your cocoa trees, making them weak. Removing weeds leaves more food and water for the cocoa tree, giving it the energy to endure and resist diseases.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ kookoo tsei amli. ehaa kookoo tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha kookoo tsei lɛ aná niyenii kɛ nu babaoo. Enɛ haa kookoo tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni ekɛŋmɛɔ etsui shi ni ekɛteɔ shi ewoɔ helai srɔtoi.

english: How should I prepare my plantain suckers before putting them in the ground?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ masaa banana ŋmeii dani mawo shikpɔŋ?

english: Treating young plantain suckers when they start sprouting kills hidden pests like stem borers, ensuring that your newly planted crops grow healthily without early damage.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii ni akwɛɔ amɛ beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ baagbe kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ tamɔ stem borers lɛ. Enɛ baaha tsei ni odu ehee lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfiteee mra.

english: When is the right time to apply pest treatment to my young plantain shoots?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ baatsu nii yɛ mi plantain tsei bibii lɛ anɔ?

english: The best time to apply protective treatment is when the suckers are just beginning to sprout, right before planting, so pests cannot attack the vulnerable young shoots.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ hebuu atsu nii ji be mli ni ŋmeii bibii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛkɛ dani aduɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kooloi bibii nyɛŋ atutua ŋmeii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: Why do Extension Officers recommend treating plantain suckers even if they look healthy to my eyes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ atsa plantain tsei lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni amɛhi jogbaŋŋ yɛ mihiŋmɛii ahiɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Tiny insect eggs and microscopic pests often hide inside the tissue of suckers. Treating them before planting prevents these pests from multiplying and damaging the plant later.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii kɛ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ teɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ amli. Kɛ́ atsa amɛ dani adu lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkafa babaoo ni amɛkafite tso lɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain plants keep falling over or dying soon after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi loo egboɔ beni midu lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pests often attack untreated plantain suckers at the root and stem level. Protecting the planting shoots prevents pest damage, giving the plant strong roots to stay standing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa plantain tsei ni atsako amɛ lɛ yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ abu ŋmeii ni adu lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii akafite amɛ. Ehaa tso shishifãi lɛ waa ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛdamɔ shi.

english: How does protecting young plantain shoots from insects help them grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii bibii ni abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ?

english: When young suckers are protected from pests, they can direct all their energy toward building strong stems and leaves instead of fighting off damage, leading to faster and healthier growth.
ga: Kɛ́ abifao lɛ miinu nu lɛ, abuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. Amɛ baanyɛ amɛkɛ amɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ afee tsei kɛ baai ni wa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewu eshi fitemɔ lɛ Ekɛ oyaiyeli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: What causes some plantain crops to grow much faster and stronger than others in the same community?
ga: Mɛni haa plantains komɛi daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe ekrokomɛi? Yɛ akutso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Plantains started from properly treated shoots suffer less stress from pests, allowing them to absorb nutrients efficiently and grow much stronger than untreated crops.
ga: Plantains ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai haŋ amɛhao babaoo. Enɛ haa amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ nii jogbaŋŋ, ni amɛdaraa waa fe tsei ni atsako amɛ.

english: Why are my plantains struggling to grow properly even when my land has good soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ miitao ni eda jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa moŋ lɛ?

english: Good soil cannot save crops if the suckers carried pests into the field. Clean, treated planting shoots allow the crop to make full use of fertile land.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ba ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni he tse ni atsa amɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I make my plantain farm remain productive for many years without replanting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-plantain ŋmɔ lɛ awo yibii afii babaoo ni ehe ehiaaa ni madu ekoŋŋ?

english: Starting with pest-free, treated suckers keeps the plant roots healthy over time, allowing your plantain farm to yield fruit continuously and remain productive on your land for longer.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ sucker ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli lɛ je shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛhi shi shiŋŋ yɛ be ni sa mli. Ye obua o-plantain ŋmɔ lɛ ni eya nɔ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehi shi yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be babaoo.

english: Will spending money to treat my suckers before planting actually save me money later?
ga: Ani shika ni akɛbaatsa ŋmeii dani adu lɛ baaha shika aba sɛɛ mli?

english: Yes, treating suckers at the start prevents major crop loss from pests and extends the life of your plantation, saving you from the cost of early replanting.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛjɛ shishijee lɛ baaye abua ni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛjɛ ŋmeii amli. ni oha obɔɔ lɛ wala aya hiɛ Enɛ hereɔ bo kɛjɛɔ shika ni okɛbaatsu nii kɛdu ekoŋŋ mra lɛ he.

english: Why do some plantain farms die out after just one harvest while others last for many seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain ŋmɔji komɛi gboiɔ yɛ kpamɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔji komɛi hiɔ shi be babaoo lɛ?

english: Farms that last for many seasons are usually started with pest-protected suckers. Healthy roots prevent diseases and structural weaknesses that cause crops to die after the first harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔji ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ bei babaoo mli lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛ tsei niji ni abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ buɔ he kɛjɛɔ helai kɛ bɔjɔmɔi ni gbeɔ tso lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the key food crops need to grow green and strong. Adding compost or proper fertilizer gives them the nourishment needed to regain their green color and produce large ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii titrii ni esa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛkwɛ̃ toi wuji.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of leaves but only produce tiny roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ? Shikpɔŋ shishi pɛ

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or too much water, the plant gets confused and spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in the tubers below.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen loo nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ futuɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ahi tuber lɛ mli yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants dry up and fall off without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or lack of water in the soil. Without enough moisture, the plant cannot support developing fruits and drops its flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Kɛji hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ aye abua aduawai lɛ ni amɛjie fɔfɔii koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly even though I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikwɛɛɛ amɛ moŋ? Ni mikɛ nu haa daa gbi?

english: Plants need more than just water to grow; they also need loose soil containing organic food like decayed plant matter or animal manure so their roots can breathe and absorb nutrients easily.
ga: Nɔ ni fe nu he miihia tsei dani amɛdara. Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli yɔɔ mli, tamɔ tsei ni egboi loo kooloi afɔfɔi hu he miihia amɛ. Enɛ ji koni amɛshishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are like human babies and burn easily under the strong sun. They need shade trees or plantain plants above them to block the harsh heat and keep the surrounding air cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao tsei loo kooyigbɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ naa koni amɛha kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Why do caterpillars and worms attack my crop leaves more during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii babaoo tutuaa mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The rainy season brings fresh, tender leaf growth, which provides soft and nutritious food for young insects, causing parent pests to lay more eggs on your crops during wet weather.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ haa baai bibii kɛ ehee kwɛ̃ɔ. Ehaa kooloi bibii lɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni hewalɛ yɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii yei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: Weeds are native wild plants that have adapted over hundreds of years to survive in harsh soil, making them much faster at stealing water, sunlight, and soil food than domesticated crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔji ni mli wa nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni dumɔwui feɔ yɛ shĩa mli.

english: Why do I need to clear away extra small stems growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛjɛ mihe lɛ? Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ ahe krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: Those extra small stems, called suckers, act like extra mouths to feed. They steal water and nutrients from the main mother plant, causing her to produce much smaller bunches of plantain.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai tsei bibii ni fata he lɛ akɛ ŋmeii. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ daaŋ krɛdɛɛ ko ni ekɛ niyenii haa. Amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ewoɔ plantains bibii bibii waa.

english: Yam leaves need direct sun to make food for the tubers underground. Lifting the vines on stakes exposes more leaves to sunlight while keeping them off the damp ground where diseases spread.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni ooowo nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ baaha hulu la babaoo ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ wain tso lɛ naa koni ekahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why does my soil turn hard like cement after a heavy rain, making it tough for seeds to sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tamɔ simenti yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ? Ani ehaa ewaa kɛhaa dumɔwui akɛ amɛakwɛ̃?

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic matter like dry leaves or manure, which normally acts like a soft sponge to keep the soil loose, open, and easy for young shoots to push through.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ekɛjieɔ sũ lɛ, egbeleɔ mli ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ akɛ amɛaatsɔ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field with no shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their leaves burn easily. They need partial shade from nurse crops like plantains or shade trees to protect them from heat and to keep the soil moist while their roots develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be ko kɛjɛ nurse tsei tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he, ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Yellow bottom leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to stay green and grow strong. When nitrogen is low, the maize plant pulls nutrients from its old bottom leaves to feed the newer growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni tsei ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ yɛ. Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa lɛ, Abɛi gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha tsei heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension officer lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi ŋmei lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and lock it into the soil through small nodules on their roots. Planting them alongside maize acts as a natural fertilizer, helping the soil stay rich and nourish the maize.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmãa he lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains cause water to stand in the soil without draining properly, it drowns the roots and creates damp conditions where rot-causing fungi quickly destroy the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. cause humidity Fuji ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ baafite ŋmeii lɛ oya.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during strong winds when they start producing heavy bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛshwereɔ babaoo lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that spread near the top of the soil rather than deep underground. When a heavy bunch grows at the top, the plant becomes heavy, making it easy for strong winds to pull the shallow roots right out of the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Beni kuu lɛ da yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Tso lɛ baafee tsiimɔ. ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ aaajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather temperatures become too high, when watering is irregular, or when there is no wind or insects to shake the flowers and self-pollinate them. When the plant gets stressed, it drops its flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli Aloo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ loo kooloi ni baawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwo amɛhe ŋmɔtɔ bɛ. Kɛ tsei miihao Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: What happens to my yam yield if I leave the vines to crawl on the ground instead of staking them with sticks?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji miha wain tsei lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mikɛ amɛ baawo tsei anɔ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to produce energy for expanding the tubers underground. If vines crawl on the damp ground, leaves shade each other, catch diseases easily from the soil, and produce much smaller yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha ŋmeii ni baa shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ. Kɛji wain tsei shwie hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baaha amɛhe. Helai gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. ni amɛwoɔ sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ bibioo kwraa

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves and dirt that looks like sawdust inside the central funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli buji ni etse kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It crawls inside the central funnel of the maize plant during the day to feed on tender young leaves, leaving behind its waste which looks like wet sawdust.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei ni shwieɔ ŋmei tso lɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ gbi mli koni eye baai bibii lɛ. Kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni tamɔ jwɛi ni efɔ lɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the branches of my cocoa trees getting unusually swollen and the leaves showing strange red or yellow patterns?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tso lɛ niji lɛ efuu yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ, ni baai lɛ hu yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ lɛ?

english: This is a key sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease, which is spread between trees by tiny insects called mealybugs. The virus blocks the flow of food and water inside the tree, causing swollen stems and eventually killing the tree.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ko ni he hiaa waa ni tsɔɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, ni ŋmeii bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei anɔ lɛ. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Virus lɛ tsiɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kuku lɛ fuɔ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ efiteɔ tso lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and looking tiny and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curl on pepper plants is caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips or mites, or a virus spread by whiteflies. As these insects feed on sap from young leaves, the uneven damage causes the leaves to twist, wrinkle, and curl up.
ga: Nibii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa Enɛ ji akɛ, ŋmeii nɛɛ yeɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ. Nɔ ni fiteɔ ni ejaaa lɛ haa baai lɛ tsɔɔ, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in a clear, open field with full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. They need shade crops like plantains planted beside them to act as natural sunshades, protecting their delicate leaves while keeping the soil cool and moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo nɔ Ebuɔ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.
