english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need plenty of sunlight to manufacture food for growing big tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves up toward the sun and keeps them off the damp soil, which prevents leaf decay and boosts tuber size.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni hulu la babaoo he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsɔnei wuji lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ kwɛɔ hulu lɛ hiɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni ekafite ni eha bulb lɛ dalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cassava stem cuttings need to be planted with the buds pointing upwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Cassava stems have small nodes where leaves and roots sprout. If you plant them upside-down, the stem wastes valuable energy trying to curve its new shoots back toward the sun, resulting in weak growth and smaller tubers.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. He ni baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Kɛji odu ohiɛ shi lɛ Tso lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni jara wa ni ekɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ ŋmeii heei aku sɛɛ kɛba hulu lɛ he. Enɛ haa amɛdalɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that the maize plant is lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient it uses to build green leaves and grow tall. It can also happen when heavy rain leaves the soil waterlogged, preventing roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni akɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo nu. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets extremely hot or when the plants do not get consistent water. High heat damages the pollen inside the flower, causing the plant to shed the unpollinated flower.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ kpataa fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɛ. Ehaa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni pollin bɛ mli lɛ.

english: What makes the leaves on my pepper plants curl up and turn crinkled?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efoɔ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites, or viruses spread by whiteflies. As these insects feed on the underside of young leaves, they cause the leaf tissue to twist and distort.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa Enɛ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi. Amɛ haa baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ shoo.

english: Why should I plant sword suckers instead of broad-leaf maiden suckers when planting plantain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu klante tsei yɛ oblayoo tsei ni hiɛ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ najiaŋ beni miduɔ plantains lɛ?

english: Sword suckers have narrow leaves and a strong bulb base with plenty of stored food, allowing them to establish roots quickly and yield large bunches. Broad-leaf suckers are weaker because they grew while competing for light.
ga: Sword shoots lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishitoo ni mli wa ni niyenii babaoo yɔɔ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi oya ni amɛwoɔ aduawai babaoo. Broadleaf suckers lɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ oshara waa ejaakɛ amɛdaraa yɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná la.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my soil better for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts work with beneficial soil bacteria to capture nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food. When the crop season ends, that nitrogen remains in the soil to nourish the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛtsake lɛ amɛfee tsei aniyenii. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Nakai nitrogen lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eya nɔ eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Heavy rain washes fertilizer off the topsoil and carries it away into gutters before the plant's roots can absorb it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already damp or when only light rain is expected.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛwoɔ nubui amli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli pɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo loo kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ fioo pɛ.

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your main crops. Clearing them early ensures your crops get all the food and light they need during their most important growth stage.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli. Ni oootsi ohe mra Ebaaha onibii lɛ niyenii kɛ la fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ amɛdalɛ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the green leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that easily scorch under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to young cocoa provides living shade that protects the plants and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe. Ehaa hulutsoo ni buɔ tsei ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ.

english: What causes small ragged holes in the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-abɛi tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ nɔ

english: These holes are usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing tip of the maize plant. Inspecting fields early and using appropriate organic extracts like neem or recommended treatments prevents severe leaf damage and preserves crop yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ashishifãi amli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mra ni okɛ tsofai ni sa tamɔ neem loo tsofai krokomɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ atsu nii. Ebaatsi baa ni fiteɔ waa lɛ naa ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii ahi shi.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is often caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips, aphids, or mites, or a virus spread by them. Controlling these insects early with insecticidal soap or recommended sprays prevents the foliage from twisting and stunted growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids loo mites, loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛ akɛ samla loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with plenty of leaves but forming very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or plants are spaced too closely together, cassava puts all its energy into growing top leaves instead of storing starch underground. Proper plant spacing and balanced nutrients encourage the plant to swell its root tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ tsɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei kɛ ŋmei baato shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ebaai lɛ anɔ. Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ niyenii ni ja yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa bulbs wuji.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce lots of flowers that drop off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo ni shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off without setting fruit when the air is too hot or when the plant experiences irregular watering during the flowering stage. Keeping moisture levels steady during flowering helps the blossoms develop into healthy fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ náa nu ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ Kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I remove some of the young shoots growing at the base of my plantain stand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow creates heavy competition for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Pruning away excess suckers so only one main stem and one or two replacements remain ensures larger, heavier bunches of plantain.
ga: Ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo shwereɔ lɛ kɛ akaŋshii ni naa wa baa kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ amli bɔni afee ni tso titri kome pɛ ahi shi ni akɛto najiaŋ lɛ, ehaa plantains lɛ feɔ agbo ni etsiiɔ.

english: When is the right time for me to apply chemical fertilizer to my maize field?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ awo ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli?

english: Fertilizer is most effective when applied twice: first about two weeks after seeds germinate when roots start expanding, and second when the plant reaches knee height. Applying fertilizer during heavy downpours washes nutrients away before roots can take them up.
ga: Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli shii enyɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ. Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ ji aaafee otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ beni shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛmli shwereɔ lɛ. kɛ shi ni ji enyɔ lɛ beni tso lɛ shɛɔ enaji ahe lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant maize on the same plot every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and lets plant-specific pests and diseases accumulate in the field. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa sũ mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ. ni aŋmɛ gbɛ ni tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Enɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Lifting yam vines on poles allows the leaves to capture full sunlight and improves air circulation, which reduces leaf fungal diseases. Sunlight helps the leaves manufacture food that feeds and expands the tuber underground.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yibii lɛ naa hulu la ni fa babaoo, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa shi Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni amɛyeɔ ni amɛkwɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii.

english: Why do my crops start wilting after just a few days without rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Soil low in organic matter cannot hold moisture long after rainfall stops. Adding compost, animal manure, or leaving crop residue on top of the soil helps trap moisture deeper where roots can reach it during dry spells.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ faaa yɛ nɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ahi ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ.

english: That is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is caused by a virus. It is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies or by using infected stem cuttings from a previous harvest to plant new fields.
ga: No ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi, ni hela ko ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛbaa lɛ. Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whitefly lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Aloo okɛ tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ kɛjɛ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii ni okɛdu yɛ shikpɔŋ hee nɔ.

english: What simple steps can I take to prevent plant viruses from spreading across my cassava farm?
ga: Ma nyɛ ma nyɛɛ blɔ nya tomi komɛ a nɔ. Mɛni mafee koni tsei ahe helai akagbɛ ashwã mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Always select stem cuttings from healthy-looking plants, immediately pull out and destroy any young plants showing twisted or yellow leaves, and keep weeds down to reduce disease-carrying insects.
ga: Halamɔ tsei niji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ be fɛɛ be. Amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ojie tsei bibii fɛɛ ni baai etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ni okpãtã amɛhiɛ. ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mli koni akɛba kooloi bibii ni kɛ helai baa lɛ shi

english: How can I tell if a cassava stem is healthy enough to use as planting material for next season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akɛtsu nii akɛ dumɔ nii yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Choose mature stems from strong plants that showed no signs of leaf yellowing, dark spots, or stunted growth throughout the growing season to avoid carrying hidden diseases into your new field.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni eda kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ okadi ko ni tsɔɔ akɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ, he ko ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ, loo amɛdalɛ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ amɛdalɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji koni helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ akabote odumɔi heei lɛ amli.

english: Why do my bean plants seem to make the soil better for other crops I plant later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tso lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha tsei krokomɛi ni miduɔ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Beans and other legumes have roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This acts like a natural fertilizer that feeds the next crops you plant in that same plot.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes krokomɛi Eyɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni odu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are small insects attacking my bean pods right before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miitutua mi-bean pods lɛ dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Bean pods attract pests like pod borers because they are rich in moisture and nutrients. You can protect your crop by planting early at the start of the rains or using approved bio-pesticides like neem tree extracts.
ga: Bean pods gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ pod borers, ejaakɛ amɛyɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai babaoo. Obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe kɛtsɔ amɛdumɔ mra nɔ. Yɛ nugbɔ lɛ shishijee mli loo okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni akpɛlɛ nɔ tamɔ neem tso mli nu lɛ atsu nii.

english: Can farm animals walking through my land spread diseases to my beans or other crops?
ga: Ani ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni nyiɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ hela ashwã mi-beans loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi anɔ?

english: Yes, livestock can carry crop disease spores and harmful insect pests on their hooves and bodies from infected fields, and their chewing damages plants, making it easier for infections to enter.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloi baanyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ amɛnaji kɛ amɛgbɔmɔtsei anɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔji ni hela lɛ emɔ mli lɛ amli. Ni amɛ ŋmɔlɔ fiteɔ tsei. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ hela baamɔ mɔ

english: What does it mean when agricultural officers say a new crop variety has been officially released in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛ́ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi kɛɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii hee ko kpo yɛ Ghana yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ?

english: It means crop scientists have thoroughly tested that seed or plant variety in local Ghanaian soils and climate conditions to ensure it produces high yields and resists common local pests before making it available to farmers.
ga: Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nilelɔi kaa dumɔwui loo tsei srɔtoi lɛ amɛkwɛɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana maŋ lɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli koni amɛkwɛ akɛ ebaawo yibii babaoo ni ekɛ maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akpee dani amɛjie amɛha okwaafoi lɛ.

english: Why do some new cassava varieties grow bigger roots faster than the old varieties my parents planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi heei lɛ ekomɛi yɛ shishifãi wuji fe ŋmeii srɔtoi ni etsɛ ni mifɔlɔi du lɛ?

english: Scientists breed improved crop varieties specifically to absorb soil nutrients more efficiently and withstand local diseases, allowing the plant to direct more energy into growing large cassava roots in less time.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi ekwɛ tsei ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ, ni amɛnyɛ amɛye helai ni baa jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ ŋmei shishifãi wuji yɛ be fioo mli.

english: Will a new crop variety released in Ghana grow well in every region of the country?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni ajie lɛ kpo yɛ Ghana lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ maŋ lɛ kpokpai fɛɛ anɔ?

english: Some varieties are developed to perform well nationwide, but others are tailored for specific conditions, such as the wetter forest zones or the drier northern savanna zones, so it is best to check which variety fits your specific location.
ga: Afee tsofai srɔtoi komɛi koni amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Shi henɔi krokomɛi Afee lɛ aha shihilɛi pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ kooi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ mli lɛ loo kooyigbɛ savannah ni mli egbi fe fɛɛ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookwɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni sa kɛha he pɔtɛɛ ni oyɔɔ lɛ.

english: How often should I walk through my field to inspect the health of my crops?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔji amli koni makwɛ bɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ ha?

english: It is best to inspect your field at least once or twice a week so you can catch early signs of insect attacks, soil dryness, or leaf diseases before they spread and harm your overall harvest.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookwɛ he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ shikome loo shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ ona mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi tutua bo, shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo tsei ahe hela dani egbɛ eshwa ni eye oŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ awui.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of young maize usually show that the plant is starving for nitrogen or that too much standing water is drowning the roots and stopping them from taking up plant food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli loo nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɛ mli, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni ehaaa amɛye tso lɛ niyenii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or mites that suck the plant sap and spread viruses, causing the leaves to twist and growth to slow down.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdalɛ hu baa shi.

english: Is it better to burn cleared weeds on my farm or leave them to dry and rot on the field?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã jwɛi ni ajie yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ loo maha amɛgbi ni amɛgboi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Burning cleared weeds gives a quick clean field, but leaving them to rot as mulch keeps the soil cool, holds water during hot dry days, and feeds nutrients back into the land.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajie lɛ ni ashãa lɛ baaha ŋmɔ lɛ mli atse oya. Shi ha amɛgboi ejaakɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Kwɛmɔ nu yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: When crops are planted too closely, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, causing them to stretch tall for light instead of growing strong stems and big cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni ekɛ la lɛ awo mli moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop surplus flowers they cannot support, but extreme heat, lack of tiny pollinating midges, or insect attacks can cause excessive flower drop.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, cacao tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ nɔ lɛ kpo. Shi latsaa lɛ Pollen ŋmeii bibii ni bɛ Loo kooloi ni baatutua amɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ afite fe nine.

english: Why do my ripening tomatoes split open on the sides before I can pick them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ afãi dani manyɛ mafolɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when they suddenly get too much water after a long dry period, making the inside of the fruit expand faster than the skin can stretch.
ga: Tomatoes will suddenly break apart. Ena nu babaoo tsɔ beni eha egbi be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ amli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: How do my groundnut plants produce nuts underground when the flowers grow above the soil?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni mi-peanut tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni fɔfɔi lɛ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated above ground, they grow long stems called pegs that bend down and push into the soil, where the nuts safely form in the dark.
ga: Beni afee ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ pollen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ, Amɛyɛ ŋmeii kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs. ni baabɔle ni ebaatsi kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ afee shweshweeshwe yɛ duŋ mli.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are rotting underground before I dig them up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mafo amɛ?

english: If your cassava leaves start dropping early, the stems wilt during rainy periods, or the soil around the plant smells sour, soft rot is likely destroying the tubers under the ground.
ga: Kɛji o-cassava baai lɛ bɔi gbee oya Tso lɛ gboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli loo shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle tso lɛ he lɛ he ŋmɔlɔ. Nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpata ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why do my stored seed yams start growing sprouts early in the barn before the planting season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ mra lɛ? Yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Seed yams sprout in storage when the air in the barn becomes warm and humid, which tricks the yam into believing it has been planted in wet soil.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ nitoohe lɛ mli kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ. Enɛ haa aheɔ ayeɔ akɛ aduɔ sweet potato lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when the fruit bunch gets large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that struggle to hold up the heavy weight of a maturing bunch, requiring wooden Y-sticks for support against strong wind.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua niji ni eda lɛ ni tsii lɛ. Esa akɛ ekɛ tso ni tamɔ Y atsu nii ni ekɛfi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa sɛɛ.

english: Why do my rice grains break into small pieces when I send them to the mill, and how can I prevent it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ fãa bibii bibii lɛ? Beni atsuɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔ mli Ni te ooofee tɛŋŋ otsĩ naa?

english: Rice grains break during milling mainly if they are harvested too late when already brittle, or dried too fast under scorching direct sun. Slowly drying harvested paddy in well-ventilated shade helps the grains stay strong and stay whole during milling.
ga: Afoɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ ŋmãa lɛ. Nɔ ni he hiaa ji kɛji akɛ akpa lɛ sɛɛ tsɔ shi egbɔjɔ momo. loo egbi oya tsɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Omɔ ni akpa lɛ ni egbiɔ blɛoo He ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Why do buyers in the market offer higher prices for long-grain rice compared to short or broken grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ kɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ haa ŋmãa ni hiɛ ŋmãa kakadaŋŋ fe ŋmãa kuku loo ŋmãa ni ekumɔ lɛ?

english: Consumers prefer long-grain rice because it cooks up light, fluffy, and non-sticky. Because market demand for this specific look and cooking texture is higher, buyers pay farmers more for uniform, long-grain harvests.
ga: Nihɔɔlɔi sumɔɔ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa kakadaŋŋ ewo mli ejaakɛ ehooɔ mlɛo, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛ ŋmãa shwieee shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jarayeli nibii ni ataoɔ yɛ nɛkɛ niyenii homɔ pɔtɛɛ nɛɛ hiɛ su kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ fa babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ okwaafoi nyɔmɔ babaoo yɛ ŋmaa kakadaŋŋ ni amɛkpaa daa lɛ hewɔ.

english: What causes my rice plants to produce light, empty husks instead of full, heavy grains?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-ŋmã tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni waaa ni nɔ ko bɛ mli yɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ ni tsii lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Empty grains usually happen when the plant lacks water or nutrients during the flowering stage, or when intense heat and pests damage the delicate plant flowers before the seed inside can fully form.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni bɛ nɔ ko baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii kpakpai yɛ fɔfɔi be mli. aloo kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kpata fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahiɛ dani dumɔwui ni yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ feɔ kwraa.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my rice crop to get the best quality grains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa koni maná ŋmãa ni hi fe fɛɛ?

english: Rice is ready for harvest when about 80% to 85% of the crop heads turn a golden yellow color. Harvesting too early results in soft, chalky grains, while waiting too long makes grains fall off in the field and break during processing.
ga: Omɔ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni ŋmeii lɛ amli aaafee 80% kɛyashi 85% batsɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ akpa dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ omɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni amɛkumɔ yɛ be mli ni atsuɔ he nii lɛ.

english: Why do my rice plants fall over to the ground before harvest, and does this affect my final yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã tsei lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ dani akpaa lɛ? Ni ani enɛ saa minaagbee nibii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe?

english: Plants fall over (called lodging) when stems grow too weak from excessive nitrogen fertilizer, overly dense planting, or strong winds. When plants fall into mud or water, the grains rot, discolor, and drop in market value.
ga: Tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi (ni atsɛɔ lɛ sheltering) kɛ́ amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔ tsɔ kɛjɛ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli babaoo lɛ mli. Dumɔ ni mli eyi obɔ tsɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛji tsei gbee muji loo nu mli. Dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ, amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe su, ni amɛjara baa shi yɛ jara nɔ.

english: How can I store my harvested grain so that insects do not destroy it before I can sell?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ midumɔwui ni akpa lɛ ato? Koni kooloi bibii akafite lɛ dani amɛhɔ̃ɔ?

english: Ensure the grain is thoroughly dried to a low moisture level before bagging. Storing dried grains in sealed, airtight (hermetic) bags keeps oxygen out, preventing insects from surviving without needing harsh chemicals.
ga: Kwɛmɔ akɛ ŋmaa lɛ egbi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashɛ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ baa shi dani okɛwo kotoku mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmaa ni egbi lɛ wo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli (vacuum) mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa he. Etsiɔ kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkahi shi kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofai ni mli wa tsuuu nii.

english: How does applying fertilizer at the wrong stage affect the size and shape of my grains?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ be ni esaaa mli lɛ saa ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ dalɛ kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: If fertilizer is applied too late in the plant's life, the nutrients go into growing extra leaves instead of feeding the grain head. Applying fertilizer at early growth and flowering stages ensures the plant uses food to develop large, solid seeds.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli sɛɛ tsɔ yɛ tso lɛ wala mli lɛ Nutrients yaa baa ni fa fe nine lɛ mli moŋ fe ni eeeha dumɔwui lɛ niyenii. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa kɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ haa amɛnáa niyenii ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui wuji ni wa.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller, shriveled seeds during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ dumɔwui bibii ni egbɔjɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants need water to transport nutrients from their leaves and roots up into the seed head. When water is scarce during grain development, the plant cannot move enough food to the seeds, leaving them shriveled and lightweight.
ga: Nu he miihia tsei koni amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛya dumɔwui lɛ ayitso nɔ. Beni nu faaa yɛ dumɔwui lɛ akwɛmɔ be mli lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ ajie niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛya dumɔwui lɛ amli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo.

english: Does mixing different grain varieties together in the same field lower the price I get at harvest?
ga: Ani dumɔwui srɔtoi ni mikɛfutuɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ baaha jara ni minine shɛɔ nɔ yɛ kpamɔ be mli lɛ aba shi?

english: Yes, mixing varieties produces seeds that mature at different times and cook unevenly. Traders pay less for mixed grains because consumers want uniform grains that cook at the exact same rate.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Jarayelɔi woɔ ŋmaa ni akɛfutu mli lɛ he nyɔmɔ fioo ejaakɛ mɛi ni heɔ lɛ miitao ŋmaa ni ahoɔ yɛ nyɔmɔwoo kome mli.

english: Why do some rice seed varieties need flooded land while others can grow on dry upland soils?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi he hiaa hei ni nu hoɔ yɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni abaanyɛ adu srɔtoi komɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ hei ni kwɔ waa lɛ?

english: Lowland rice varieties have specialized root structures designed to thrive and absorb nutrients in waterlogged soil, whereas upland varieties are bred with deeper root systems that search for moisture in dry soils.
ga: Omɔ henɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛ ko ni afee koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, afɔɔ ŋmãa henɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni taoɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ yɔɔ mli.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and drop off during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during severe dry weather to save water and protect itself from drought. Once the rains return, the crop uses energy stored in its roots to sprout fresh leaves without dying.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hɔmɔ he. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛwo baai heei ni amɛgbooo.

english: Why are some of my maize cobs missing seeds or only half full at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ ekomɛi amli ŋmeii bɛ mli loo fã pɛ eyi mli obɔ kɛ́ akpa lɛ?

english: Maize cobs need pollen from the tassels at the top of the plant to reach every single silk strand. If extreme heat or dry winds occur while the plant is flowering, the pollen dries up and dies before fertilizing the cob, leaving empty spaces.
ga: Abɛi ŋmeii lɛ ahe miihia pollen ni jɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ amli lɛ koni eshɛ ŋmeii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko he. Kɛji latsaa ni naa wa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ba be mli ni tsei lɛ miifɔ lɛ, Pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egboɔ dani ŋmei lɛ woɔ fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha he ko ahi shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field without tall trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under full, direct sunlight. They require temporary shade crops, like plantain or banana, to shield them and keep the surrounding soil moist until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo banana. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu amɛhe ni aha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my tomatoes split open or turn dark and rotten at the bottom before they are ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ tswaa loo etsɔɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ shishigbɛ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split or develop rot at the bottom when watering is irregular—such as a sudden heavy rain after a hot dry period—or when the plant cannot draw enough calcium from the soil, causing the skin to burst as the fruit expands too fast.
ga: Tomatoi lɛ gbáa loo amɛgboɔ yɛ shishigbɛ kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ nu lɛ be fɛɛ be, tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ. aloo be mli ni tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ mli fãa kɛ́ aduawai lɛ mli gbala oya tsɔ.

english: Plantain trees have weak, shallow roots and become top-heavy as the bunch grows. If you do not clear excess shoots (suckers) or prop up the main stem with strong bamboo or wooden poles, wind can easily tip the tree over.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ be mli ni niji lɛ daraa lɛ. Kɛji ojieee tsei lɛ ahe ŋmeii (ŋmeii) ni fa fe nine lɛ loo okɛ ŋmeii loo tso ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, Kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ atsɔ ŋwɛi oya.

english: Why does my maize grow better when I plant it on a farm where I grew cowpeas or groundnuts last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni midu tsina loo ŋmãa yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in tiny nodules on their roots. When the crop is harvested and its stems rot, that nitrogen stays behind as free, natural food for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi bibii amli kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ egbo. Nitrogen baaya nɔ ahi shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when temperatures get too high or when they suffer from uneven watering. The plant sheds flowers to conserve its energy until growing conditions become cooler and moisture improves.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu lɛ haaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni shihilɛi ni amɛdaraa lɛ mli jɔɔ ni fɛ̃i baaya hiɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow slow and turn pale green when weeds are growing close to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni jwɛi bɛŋkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively steal soil nutrients, water, and sunlight away from your main crops. When weeds stay close to crop roots, your plants starve because they cannot access the food in the soil.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli oya. Beni jwɛi bɛŋkɛ tsei shishifãi Otsei lɛ hɔmɔ baaye amɛ ejaakɛ amɛnaŋ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do yam vines need tall sticks to climb, and what happens if I let them trail on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei ahe hiaa niji ni kwɔlɔ koni amɛkwɔ lɛ? Ni mɛni baa kɛji miha amɛnyiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight to make food, which feeds the underground tuber. Keeping vines off the damp soil also prevents leaves from catching fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ kɛha nihoomɔ. ni ji shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ aniyenii Wein tso lɛ ni akɛaatsi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ he lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii helai akamɔ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does putting chemical fertilizer directly touching a young seedling stem burn and kill the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tsei bibii amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers contain concentrated salts. Placing fertilizer directly against fresh roots or tender stems draws water out of the plant tissue through burning, causing the stem to dry out and the crop to die.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli ŋmei babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shishifãi heei loo tsei bibii amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaajie nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ fãji amli kɛtsɔ shãa ni eshãa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hu gboɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure will help bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Does adding sugar to the soil make crops like watermelon or sugarcane produce sweeter fruits?
ga: Ani kɛ́ akɛ sugar wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ watermelon loo sugarcane woɔ yibii ni ŋɔɔ?

english: No, plants produce their own natural sugars inside the leaves through sunlight and water. Adding refined sugar to the soil does not make fruits sweeter and can actually attract ants and soil pests that damage the roots.
ga: Dabi, tsei feɔ sugar yɛ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛtsɔɔ hulu la kɛ nu nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ sugar yɛŋ wo sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaaa aduawai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ebaanyɛ egbala ŋmeii kɛ sũ mli kooloi krokomɛi ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why does burning my bush before planting make my crops struggle in later seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ashãa dani aduɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii shwereɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli bei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Burning clears the land fast, but it destroys essential organic matter and beneficial insects in the topsoil. Over time, repeated burning starves the soil of natural plant food, causing crops to grow poorly.
ga: Shãa baajie shikpɔŋ lɛ oya. Shi efiteɔ nibii ni he hiaa ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋgbɛ lɛ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, shãa ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná tsei ahe nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei lɛ adalɛ ni ehiii.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop all their leaves during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ fiteɔ yɛ harmatta be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry weather to save water. It is a natural protection mechanism that stops moisture from evaporating through the leaves so the root can survive in the dry ground.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni tsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekatsɔ baai lɛ amli. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ha tso lɛ hao. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Is it better to water my vegetable crops shallowly every day or soak the ground deeply twice a week?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu fioo daa gbi loo mawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli?

english: Deep watering twice a week is better because it forces roots to grow deep into the ground searching for moisture, making your crops stronger and better able to survive hot, dry days.
ga: Nu ni mli kwɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ enyɛɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ koni amɛdara kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛtao ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa onibii ni oduɔ lɛ mli waa ni enyɛɔ ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ mli.

english: Why doesn't flour made from our local rice varieties work well when making soft rice meals like omo tuo?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ashikishaŋ ni akɛ wɔ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa srɔtoi lɛ fee lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ afee ŋmãa ni mli jɔ tamɔ omo tuo lɛ?

english: Local Ghanaian rice varieties often contain different types of starch compared to imported soft rice. Their flour forms a firm, sticky paste when ground instead of the smooth, soft texture needed for traditional rice meals.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Ghana ŋmãa henɔi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli ŋmãa henɔi srɔtoi yɛ mli kɛ akɛto ŋmãa ni mli jɔ ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ he. Amɛ ashikishaŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tamɔ krim kɛji akɛ agbɛlɛ. Mohu ɔ, e ngɛ blɔ nya tomi nɛ ngɛ blɛoo nɛ e he hia kɛ ha blema ngma niye ní.

english: Why do some of my rice seeds float when I put them in a bucket of water before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui komɛi shwieɔ nu nɔ kɛ́ akɛwo nu baagi mli dani adu lɛ?

english: Seeds that float are empty, light, or damaged by pests inside. Good seeds are heavy and sink to the bottom. Removing the floating seeds ensures you only plant strong seeds that will germinate.
ga: Dumɔwui ni hoɔ yɛ nu lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko, amɛkpɛɔ, loo kooloi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ efite amɛ. Dumɔwui kpakpai lɛ tsii ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛyaa shishi. Dumɔwui ni hoɔ yɛ nu hiɛ lɛ ni ooojie lɛ haa onaa nɔmimaa akɛ oduɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ ni baakwɛ̃.

english: Young cocoa seedlings get scorched easily by direct sun. Plantains grow fast and provide broad shade leaves that act as natural umbrellas, keeping the ground cool and moist for the young cocoa.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui shãa oya kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛhaa kookoo tsei bibii.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil fast when I store it right after picking it from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ mikpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli pɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Freshly picked maize still holds a lot of moisture inside the grains. If you store it immediately without drying it well in the sun, mold and insects will quickly grow and ruin the crop.
ga: Abɛi ni ajie ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lolo. Kɛ okɛto amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni okɛ hulu lɛ egbiko lɛ, Fungi kɛ kooloi bibii baanyɛ adara oya ni amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are my crops drying up even though I planted them in the same month I always plant every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ nyɔŋ ni miduɔ daa afi lɛ nɔŋŋ mli moŋ?

english: Rainy seasons in Ghana are changing because of shifts in climate. Planting purely by traditional calendar months can cause crops to fail if the rains come late or stop early, so it is better to wait until the soil has enough moisture before planting.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ miitsake yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ hewɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ kusum kalanda nyɔŋ lɛ naa lɛ pɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite kɛji nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ loo ekpa mra. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa dani odu.

english: How can I tell if the rains have really started for the season so I do not waste my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ jeɔ shishi ebaa diɛŋtsɛ? Bɔni afee ni mikafite dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Do not plant after just the first light rain. Wait until the soil is wet down to a depth of about a hand's length so that young seeds have enough underground moisture to survive if the rain pauses for a few days.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ sɛɛ. Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ kɛyashɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ aaafee onineshi fã kome. Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui bibii lɛ aná shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii fioo komɛi.

english: Should I switch to fast-growing crop varieties because the rainy season seems shorter nowadays?
ga: Ani esa akɛ wɔtsake kɛya tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ anɔ ejaakɛ etamɔ nɔ ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ miifee kuku yɛ nɛkɛ gbii nɛɛ amli?

english: Yes, planting early-maturing or short-duration crop varieties helps ensure your crops mature and yield harvestable food before the unpredictable rainy season ends abruptly.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra loo ni shwereɔ be kukuoo lɛ ni ooodu lɛ haa onibii lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii babaoo dani nugbɔshiimɔ be ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ baa naagbee trukaa.

english: Why do my maize plants start producing flowers too early when there is a long break in the rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miibɔi fɔmɔ oya tsɔ beni nugbɔ enɛ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When maize plants experience water stress from dry spells, they panic and try to produce seeds quickly before dying, which leads to early flowering and smaller cobs.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa tsei na nu he haomɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ hewɔ lɛ Amɛbaashe gbeyei ni amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛwo dumɔwui oya dani amɛgboi. Enɛ haa fɔfɔii lɛ fɔɔ mra ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small even when the leaves look healthy during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava protects itself during dry weather by sending energy to keep its leaves alive instead of expanding its underground roots, which stops root growth until regular rains return.
ga: Yucca buɔ ehe he yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii koni eha baai lɛ ahi shi lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni shishifãi lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ adalɛ kpaɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing fruit when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: High heat combined with irregular rainfall creates stress in tomato plants, making the pollen sterile so the flowers drop off instead of turning into tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ kɛ nɔnyɛɛ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Ehaa fɔfɔi amli pollen lɛ sɛɛ foɔ No sɛɛ lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ tomato.

english: Why do my bean leaves turn yellow and drop off when we get heavy rain followed immediately by strong sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ wɔná nugbɔ ni naa wa ni hulu ni naa wa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains followed by intense heat create high moisture and hot humidity, which stresses the plant roots and encourages fungal diseases that make leaves turn yellow and drop.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni dɔlɛ ni naa wa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni naa wa kɛ hulutsoo ni mli edɔ baa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ shoo ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Is there a simple way I can keep moisture in my soil when the rain stops unexpectedly?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa?

english: You can cover the soil around your crops with dry grass or leaves (mulching). This acts like a blanket that shields the ground from the hot sun and holds moisture in the soil longer.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulch) aha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ, ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ atade ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crops after a short, unexpected rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kuku ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Weeds are wild and naturally tougher than farm crops, so they can absorb small amounts of erratic rain much faster and steal the water from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli kooloi ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ amɛhe wa fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛbaanyɛ amɛjie nugbɔ fioo ni nɛɔ ni ejaaa lɛ oya kwraa ni amɛju nu kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Why does my farmland dry out much faster after rain nowadays compared to years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kwraa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ yɛ nɛkɛ gbii nɛɛ amli lɛ? Kɛ akɛto afii komɛi ni eho lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Hotter temperatures dry out the ground faster, and if your soil lacks organic matter like compost or dead leaves, it loses its ability to hold water like a sponge.
ga: He ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Ni kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo baai ni egboi? Shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛŋ amɔmɔ nu tamɔ sponji dɔŋŋ.

english: How do I know if the fertilizer water I give to my greenhouse crops is too strong or too weak?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛhaa mi-greenhouse tsei lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo ebɛ hewalɛ tsɔ?

english: Fertilization water contains salts that act as plant food. You can use a device called an EC meter to measure the salt strength of the liquid, helping you know if you are giving your crops the right amount of food or risking burning their roots.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔmɔ kotoku mli lɛ mli ŋmeii ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛhaa tso lɛ yɔɔ mli. Obaanyɛ okɛ tsɔne ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ EC mita lɛ asusu bɔ ni nu ko mli ŋoo lɛ mli wa ha lɛ he. Enɛ haa oleɔ kɛji ooha onibii lɛ niyenii ni sa loo okɛ ohe woɔ oshara mli akɛ obaashã eshishifãi lɛ.

english: What is pH, and why should I care about it when watering my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji pH ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ ama nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu miiha mitsei lɛ?

english: pH measures how acidic or sweet your soil or water is. If the pH level is bad, your plants' roots get locked up and cannot absorb nutrients from the fertilizer, even if you feed them heavily.
ga: pH lɛ susuɔ bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ loo onu lɛ ji acidic loo sweet ha lɛ he. Kɛji pH lɛ ehiii lɛ, otsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baatsi amɛhe ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ mli kɛji ooha amɛ niyenii babaoo po.

english: Why do the tips of my plant leaves turn brown or burn after I apply chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibaai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo amɛshãa beni mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ ewo mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizers contain salts. If you apply too much salt at once, it draws water out of the roots instead of feeding them, causing the leaf edges to dry out and burn.
ga: Nu yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Kɛ okɛ ŋmei babaoo fata he shikome lɛ, Egbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii. Ehaa baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa.

english: Why should I collect and check the extra water that drips out from the bottom of my plant pots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabua nu ni fa fe nine ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mitsɛnsi lɛ shishi lɛ naa ni makwɛ?

english: Checking the leftover water shows you what your crops did not consume. If the runoff water has a high salt level, it means your crops are full and you are wasting fertilizer.
ga: Nu ni eshwɛ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ baatsɔɔ bo nɔ ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeee. Kɛji nu ni hoɔ lɛ mli ŋmei fa babaoo Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii eyi obɔ ni oofite ŋmei.

english: What does a tool called an EC meter actually do for my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ sɛɛnamɔ dɛŋdade ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ EC mita lɛ yɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: An EC meter measures the amount of electrical-conducting salts dissolved in water. It acts like a tester that tells you exactly how much chemical fertilizer is in your liquid mix before you give it to your plants.
ga: EC mita susuɔ bɔ ni ŋmei ni tsɔɔ nu mli lɛ fa ha lɛ he. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni kaa mɔ ko ni tsɔɔ bo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ nu ni okɛfutuɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ falɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ dani ekɛhaa otsei lɛ.

english: How do I make sure my crops are actually drinking the fertilizer I put in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miinu ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Crops feed by absorbing nutrients dissolved in water through their roots. By measuring the fertilizer level in the water you give them and comparing it to the water that drains out, you can confirm if the plants took in the nutrients.
ga: Tsei yeɔ nii kɛtsɔ niyenii ni mli ewo nu mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Susumɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ nu ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ he ni okɛto nu ni ajieɔ lɛ he. Obaanyɛ oma nɔ mi kɛji tso lɛ eŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ loo eŋɔko.

english: Can adding too much fertilizer to my pepper crops actually stop them from growing?
ga: Ani mi-pepper tso lɛ ni mikɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ enaa diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, excessive fertilizer creates too much salt around the plant roots. This salt build-up makes it difficult for the plant to drink water, causing stunted growth or crop damage.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ haa ŋmei baa ehe. tsei shishifãi babaoo Nu ni buaa ehe naa nɛɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei akɛ amɛaanu nu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dalɛ baa shi loo tsei lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do crops grown in greenhouse bags need closer watching than crops grown open in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akwɛ tsei ni adu yɛ greenhouse bags amli lɛ jogbaŋŋ fe nɔ ni adu yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Greenhouse plants live in confined bags without open rainfall to wash away built-up fertilizer salts. You must carefully measure both what goes in and what drains out so salts do not trap and choke the roots.
ga: Greenhouse tsei lɛ hiɔ kotokui ni akɛwo mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ mli koni amɛkɛjie ŋmeii ni ebua amɛhe naa lɛ. Esa akɛ osusu nɔ ni boteɔ mli kɛ nɔ ni jeɔ kpo lɛ fɛɛ he jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baatsi ŋoo lɛ naa koni ekamɔ shishifãi lɛ ni ekɛtsi amɛnaa.

english: If I put plenty of fertilizer but my crops still look pale and weak, what could be going wrong?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata he ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ lolo lɛ. Mɛni maa ba?

english: The water or soil might have an unbalanced pH level. When pH is off, the crop cannot swallow the fertilizer salts present in the soil, making the plant look starved.
ga: Nu loo shikpɔŋ baanyɛ aná pH ni ejaaa. Kɛji pH lɛ sɛɛ fo lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii nyɛɛɛ ami ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, etamɔ nɔ ni hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ.

english: What is the difference between checking the water I feed my plants and checking the water that leaks out of the bottom?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ nu ni mikɛhaa tsei lɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ kɛ nu ni miiho kɛmiijɛ shishi lɛ mlikwɛmɔ teŋ?

english: The water you put in shows the food you are offering, while the water that leaks out reveals what the crop rejected. Comparing both tells you if your plants are hungry, satisfied, or overwhelmed with salts.
ga: Nu ni okɛbaafata he lɛ baajie niyenii ni okɛbaahã lɛ kpo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni hoɔ lɛ jie nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpoo lɛ kpo. Kɛ́ okɛ enyɔ lɛ to he lɛ, obaana kɛji hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ, eyi obɔ, loo eyɛ ŋoo.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil or get moldy so quickly when I store it in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ loo ehiɛɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛwo kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Maize spoils quickly if it is bagged while still holding too much moisture. Damp grains create a warm, wet environment where mold and fungi grow rapidly, so maize must be dried thoroughly until the grains are hard before long-term storage.
ga: Abɛi fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ awo kotoku mli ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli. Dumɔwui ni mli efɔ lɛ feɔ shihilɛ ni mli edɔ, ni efɔ lɛ. he ni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii shwereɔ yɛ oya No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ agbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ afee shiŋŋ dani akɛto be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my maize is dry enough to be safely stored without testing machines?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmã lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akɛto shweshweeshwe ni mɔ ko bɛ ni kaa lɛ?

english: A simple way is the salt test or fingernail test: if you press your fingernail into a grain and it dents easily, it is too wet. Dry maize grains should be hard, difficult to dent, and make a sharp, metallic clinking sound when shaken together in a bottle.
ga: Gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ji ŋmei kaa loo ŋmei kaa: kɛji onyɛ oŋmei lɛ nɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli ni efo mlɛo Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmei lɛ mli efɔ tsɔ. Esa akɛ ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ afee nɔ ni wa, ni ewa akɛ aaakpã mli, ni efee dade ni tswaa gbee kɛji akɛ atswa lɛ ekome.

english: What causes small insects like weevils to multiply in my stored grain, and how can I stop them?
ga: Mɛni haa kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ miŋmaa ni mikɛto lɛ mli? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛ naa?

english: Weevils often lay hidden eggs inside the grains while the crop is still in the field. To stop them, store fully dried grain in airtight containers or hermetic bags (like PICS bags), which cut off oxygen and suffocate the insects before they can multiply.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii fɔɔ amɛwui ni akɛtee dumɔwui amli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. Bɔni afee ni okpa amɛ Moŋ lɛ, kɛ dumɔwui ni egbi kwraa lɛ awo tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli (tamɔ PICS kotoku mli), ni no baafo kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ mli ni ebaaha mɔ ko agbɔjɔ dani kooloi lɛ baanyɛ afɔ.

english: Why does maize sell for a very low price right after harvest compared to the minor season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ahɔ̃ɔ ŋmãa lɛ jara ni baa shi nɛkɛ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ kɛ akɛto sɛɛ mli yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ he lɛ?

english: Right after the major harvest, almost all farmers are selling their grain at the same time, creating a high supply that lowers market prices. Later in the year, when supply dries up and grain becomes scarce, buyers pay much higher prices.
ga: Yɛ kpamɔ wulu lɛ sɛɛ Nɔ ni miihe ashɛ okwaafoi fɛɛ hɔ̃ɔ ŋmaa yɛ be kome mli. Enɛ haa nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ fa babaoo, ni no haa jarayeli jara lɛ baa shi. Sɛɛ mli yɛ nakai afi lɛ mli Beni nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ bɔi sɛɛ fomɔ ni ŋmaa bafee nɔ ni faaa lɛ. Ehe baahia ni mɔ ni heɔ lɛ awo nyɔmɔ ni nɔ kwɔ kwraa fe nakai.

english: Is it dangerous to feed corn that has white or green mold on it to my family or farm animals?
ga: Ani eyɛ oshara akɛ maha miweku lɛ loo ŋmɔ mli kooloi lɛ ŋmãa ni mli eyi kɛ ŋmãa yɛŋ loo eŋɔli?

english: Yes, moldy corn contains dangerous poisons called aflatoxins produced by fungi. Washing or cooking does not destroy these toxins, and consuming moldy corn can cause serious liver disease and stunted growth in both humans and livestock.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofa ko ni yɔɔ oshara ni atsɛɔ lɛ aflatoxin ni ŋmei lɛ feɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmei ni mli ewo muji lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afɔ he loo ahoo lɛ, ekpataaa nɛkɛ tsofai fɔji nɛɛ ahiɛ. Ni ŋmãa ni mli ewo muji ni ayeɔ lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ mlɛbo hela ni naa wa aba, ni eha gbɔmɛi kɛ kooloi adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do the leaves of my young maize plants turn yellow and stop growing tall after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain can flood the soil and push out air, starving the roots of oxygen. When roots cannot breathe, they fail to absorb nitrogen from the soil, which causes the leaves to turn yellow and stunts the plant's growth.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu afua ni ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aje kpo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji oxygen lɛ bɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Be ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu Enyɛŋ ejie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni etsĩɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Empty spaces happen when pollination fails, usually caused by severe drought or heat when the plant is flowering. If the silks dry up before receiving pollen from the top tassels, kernels will not form.
ga: He ni nɔ ko bɛ lɛ baa kɛji pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii. Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa yɛ tso lɛ fɔfɔi be mli kɛbaa. Kɛji akɛ siliki tsɔji lɛ gĩ dani amɛná pollen kɛjɛ ŋwɛi tsɔji lɛ amli lɛ, Dumɔwu lɛ baafee nɔ ko.

english: What is causing chewed holes in my maize leaves and small dirt-like powder inside the plant's funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni ashɛreɔ yɛ mi-abele baai lɛ amli kɛ muji bibii ni tamɔ muji baa? yɛ tso lɛ ŋmei lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central growing shoot (the funnel) of the maize plant. Spraying recommended treatments directly into the funnel early in the morning or late in the evening helps control them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishifãi (cones) ni miida lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eye nɔ.

english: Can I save some of the maize grain I harvested this season to plant as seeds next year?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmãa ni mikpaa yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ eko ato koni mikɛdu akɛ dumɔwui yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli?

english: If you planted hybrid seed, saving grain for next season will produce weak plants with smaller cobs and low yields. It is best to buy fresh certified seed every season to guarantee strong, high-yielding crops.
ga: Kɛji odu hybrid dumɔwui Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ kɛha be ni baa lɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ. Cobs lɛ daraaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ daa afi koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo baa.

english: Why do my maize plants grow weak and thin when I plant many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa beni midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting too many seeds in one spot forces the young plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Planting fewer seeds with proper spacing gives each plant enough space and food to grow thick stalks and large cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Dumɔwui fioo ni aduɔ ni gbɛ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: If my crops get ruined mid-season, can I immediately plant maize and beans on the same land to recover my loss?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fite yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ hu? Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni maku nɔ ni elaaje lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, planting quick-maturing crops like maize and beans after a loss is a good strategy. Beans grow quickly and put nitrogen into the soil, which helps the maize grow strong and provides you with food and income in a shorter time.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ oya tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa. Yɛ nɔ ko ni elaaje sɛɛ lɛ ji ŋaa kpakpa. Beans lɛ daa oya ni ekɛ nitrogen woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa ni ehaa bo niyenii kɛ shika yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: Can I plant maize and beans together in the exact same field, or will they steal food from each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ? Aloo amɛbaaju niyenii kɛjɛ amɛhe?

english: You can plant them together safely. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen from the soil to grow tall, while beans take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, making them perfect partners that help each other grow.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ amɛ afee ekome shweshweeshwe. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa anáa tsakpaa ni yeɔ emuu ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛhe ni amɛyaa hiɛ.

english: I have big trees on my farm land; do I need to cut them all down before I can grow my crops well?
ga: Miyɛ tso agbo ko yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ani ehe miihia ni mafolɔ mli kwraa dani manyɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: You do not need to cut every tree down. While sun-loving crops like maize need light, keeping some shade trees helps preserve moisture in the soil, protects crops from harsh sun during dry spells, and prevents soil erosion.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa ni ofo tso fɛɛ tso. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei ni sumɔɔ hulu tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ he miihia la ni tsoɔ waa moŋ, shi Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo ha tsei lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Buu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. ni etsi shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa

english: Why is proper land preparation so important before I put my seeds into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani madu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Preparing the land by clearing weeds and loosening the soil allows young roots to spread easily, retain moisture from rain, and collect plant food, giving your seeds the best chance to grow strong.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni asaa kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Ha nugbɔshiimɔ akafee ŋmɔtɔ ni obua niyenii kɛjɛ tsei amli Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Why do extension officers keep telling us to plant beans when our soil seems weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu beans be mli ni amɛduuu lɛ? Ani wɔshikpɔŋ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ?

english: Beans are natural soil fixers. Their roots contain good bacteria that trap nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil, enriching the earth for future crops without requiring expensive chemical fertilizers.
ga: Nuts ji adebɔɔ mli nibii ni kɛ amɛhe kpaa gbee. Muawai kpakpai ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why do my crops yield less every time I plant maize in the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of specific nutrients from the soil. When you plant it repeatedly in one spot, the soil gets exhausted; rotating maize with legumes like beans restores those nutrients naturally.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ odu shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nakai niyenii mli hewalɛi lɛ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: If my crop gets ruined by pests or disease, is it safe to plant new seeds in that same soil right away?
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai kpata miŋmɔshi nii lɛ Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu dumɔwui heei yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: It can be risky because pests and plant diseases often hide in leftover roots and soil. It is best to clear away the dead plants, let the land rest, or plant a completely different type of crop that those pests do not feed on.
ga: Enɛ baanyɛ afee oshara ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai kɛ amɛhe woɔ shishifãi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni eshwɛ lɛ amli. Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ afeɔ enɛ ji ni ajie tsei ni egboi lɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe. Aloo dumɔ tsei krokomɛi ni nakai kooloi lɛ yeee akɛ niyenii.

english: Which crops grow the fastest if I lose my primary harvest and need food for my family in a short time?
ga: Mɛɛ tso daa oya kɛji akɛ miŋmɔ titri lɛ fite ni niyenii he miihia miweku lɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli?

english: Legumes like cowpeas (beans) and early-maturing maize varieties are ideal emergency crops. Some cowpea varieties can be harvested in as little as 60 days, giving you quick food and income.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas (peas) kɛ ŋmãa henɔi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ ji ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha oyaiyeli. Abaanyɛ akpa tsina ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi yɛ gbii 60 pɛ mli, ni enɛ haa onáa niyenii kɛ shika oya.

english: How do I know the exact right time to start land preparation and planting in my area?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ masaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni madu nii yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: You should wait for the steady onset of rains rather than planting after the very first rain. Preparing land just as the regular rains begin prevents seeds from drying out in hot soil.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ aje shishi moŋ fe ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni asaa he pɛpɛɛpɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ baatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow differently on the piece of land near my house compared to the field near large trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ mishia lɛ nɔ kɛ akɛto ŋmɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsei wuji lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Different areas have different soil quality, sunlight levels, and moisture. Land near houses often has richer soil from household compost, while fields near big trees may get more shade and competition for water.
ga: Hei srɔtoi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su, hulu la, kɛ hulutsoo be srɔtoi. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔji ni bɛŋkɛ shia lɛ yɛ sũ ni jara wa fe shia ŋmɔshi nibii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ tsei wuji lɛ baanyɛ ana hulutsoo babaoo ni amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu he.

english: Why do my vegetable crops rot when water sits still around their roots for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ miifite be mli ni nu ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air to breathe just like people do. When water sits trapped around the stems, it starves the roots of oxygen and invites soil fungi that rot the plant from the base.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni adesai feɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ́ nu tsɔ tso lɛ he lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni efɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nine ni haa tso lɛ fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ he.

english: Is it safe to water my pepper plants with dirty, stagnant water from a quiet pond?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oookɛ nu ni mli ewo muji ni ekã shi kɛjɛ nu bu ni yɔɔ dioo mli lɛ afɔ pepper tsei anɔ?

english: Using dirty, still water introduces harmful bacteria and microscopic fungi directly onto your crops, which causes diseases on leaves and stems that can destroy your harvest.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi ni mli ewo muji ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ baa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ kɛ helai baa baai kɛ tsei lɛ anɔ ni baanyɛ afite onibii.

english: What happens to my maize yield if I leave weeds to grow freely alongside my crops?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji miŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi?

english: Weeds eat the food, light, and water meant for your crops. If you leave them uncontrolled, they quickly overpower your plants and drastically lower your harvest.
ga: Jwɛi yeɔ niyenii, la, kɛ nu ni yɔɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛji oha amɛje amɛhe nɔ lɛ Ebaaye otsei lɛ anɔ oya ni ebaaha yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi waa.

english: Why do my nursery seedlings wither so fast when I miss watering them for just two sunny days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gboɔ oya nɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be mli gbii enyɔ pɛ ni mikɛnuɔ nu lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have very short, tender roots that cannot reach deep moisture. Without daily water in warm weather, their stems collapse and cannot recover.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nu bɛ daa gbi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, tso lɛ gbee shi ni enyɛɛɛ ekɛ ehe awo mli.

english: If I leave spoiled or rotten cocoa pods hanging on my tree, will it ruin the healthy pods?
ga: Kɛ mishi kookoo ŋmeii ni efite loo efite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, Ani ebaafite kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: Rotten pods carry plant diseases that spread quickly through rain drips and insects to neighboring healthy pods, eventually destroying the entire tree's yield.
ga: Pods ni egboi lɛ hiɛɔ tsei ahe helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔ kɛ kooloi anɔ kɛyaa pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ. ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, efiteɔ tsei fɛɛ ni afeɔ lɛ

english: Why do my crops catch plant diseases more easily when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ tsei ahe helai waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Planted too closely, crop leaves trap damp air and block sunlight, creating a moist environment where fungi thrive and spread rapidly from plant to plant.
ga: adu ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tso lɛ baai lɛ mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la naa. ni feɔ shihilɛ ni mli edɔ Fɛ̃i lɛ daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply all my fertilizer to the soil at once at the start of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ fataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ be kome mli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Plants can only absorb nutrients slowly as they grow. Dumping all fertilizer at once means rain washes most of it deep into the ground where roots cannot reach, wasting your effort and money.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ fiofio pɛ beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛ́ ashɛrɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ shikome lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ nugbɔ baawo emli babaoo kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Efiteɔ omɔdɛŋbɔɔ kɛ oshika.

english: Why do my harvests grow smaller every year if I plant cassava on the exact same spot continuously?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji mitee nɔ midu ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Repeatedly growing the same crop on one piece of land drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover, leaving the land tired and weak.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ pɛ ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, etɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why should I prevent free-roaming livestock like goats from walking through my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi kooloi ni nyiɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe tamɔ tooi anaa koni amɛkatsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Animals trample delicate crop stems, pack the soil tight so water cannot enter, and eat green leaves that plants need to make their food.
ga: Koolooi nyiɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anɔ. Kpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni nu akabote mli. ni oye baai eŋɔli ni tsei taoɔ kɛha nihoomɔ.

english: What will happen to my harvested corn if I store it in bags while it is still damp?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛwo kotoku lɛ mli be mli ni edɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Damp corn attracts mold and destructive grain insects, which will multiply quickly and ruin the entire bag of crop within a few weeks.
ga: Abɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ gbalaa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ dumɔwui lɛ. Amɛshwereɔ oya ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or cassava planted around them to protect their leaves from burning and to keep the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiisumɔ ni adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ amɛhe. Bɔni afee ni baai lɛ akashã, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ

english: What causes the black spots on my cocoa pods that spread and turn the whole pod soft and black?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni ehaa ŋmeii muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ blɛoo ni eyɛ diŋ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in cool, overly shaded, and wet environments. Pruning excess tree branches lets sunlight and air flow through to dry the pods and stop the fungus.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Fuŋɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Shade babaoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni etsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa.

english: Yellowing leaves at the bottom usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs in large amounts to grow. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps keep the plant healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji bɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmãa akwɛ̃ babaoo Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo nitrogen ŋmãa fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli ni aduɔ ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why do I need to support my yam vines with wood stakes as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei afi mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ asɛɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need stakes to climb high towards the sunlight. The more sunlight the leaves get, the more energy the plant produces to grow large, healthy tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ni amɛkwɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la. Babaoo ni hulu la ni baa lɛ naa lɛ, Babaoo ni tso lɛ jieɔ hewalɛ babaoo lɛ, babaoo ni esa akɛ ená hewalɛ ni ekɛda koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni he wa lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: How do I choose the best plantain suckers from my field for planting new land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛdu shikpɔŋ hee?

english: Look for maiden suckers that have thick bases and narrow, needle-like leaves. These suckers establish faster, handle strong winds better, and yield larger bunches than suckers with broad leaves.
ga: Taomɔ tsei bibii ni amɛshishigbɛ lɛ mli tse kɛ baai ni mli tse ni tamɔ ŋmeii. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ jeɔ shishi oya. Ebaanyɛ etsu kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he nii jogbaŋŋ ni ewo aduawai akui ni dara fe tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot or when watering is irregular. Keeping the soil consistently moist and covering the ground with dry grass mulch helps protect the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ejaaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking nutrients from the leaves. Spraying early with neem oil mixture helps keep these pests away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Ni akɛ neem fɔ ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ baashwie nɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ he.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot strips the soil of specific nutrients and allows pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai buaa amɛhe naa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is damp, but not right before a heavy rainstorm. Applying it right before heavy rain will wash the nutrients away before the crop's roots can drink them in.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ, shi jeee dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa lɛ wo mli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nuɔ amɛ.

english: Why should I plant plantains on the same farm with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as natural shades, protecting delicate young cocoa trees from harsh sunlight and retaining soil moisture until the cocoa matures.
ga: Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Which food crop is best for me to grow alongside my young cocoa trees to support their growth?
ga: Mɛni ji niyenii tso ni hi fe fɛɛ ni manyɛ makwɛ yɛ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ masɛi koni eye ebua edalɛ?

english: Plantains are ideal because their tall, broad leaves provide immediate canopy shade and help retain soil moisture, creating a cool environment for young cocoa seedlings.
