ga: Plantains hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛbaai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni kɛlɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo amrɔ nɔŋŋ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Feemɔ shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ kɛha kookoo dumɔwui.

english: How close can I safely plant plantain trees next to my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Te manyɛ madu dumɔwui lɛ shweshweeshwe tɛŋŋ mabɛŋkɛ kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe?

english: You can plant plantain as close as one foot away from a young cocoa seedling so that its foliage and roots can directly provide shade and moisture protection to the young plant.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu dumɔwui aaafee ninetalɔi 1 kɛjɛ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe bɔni afee ni cacao tsei lɛ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anyɛ aha tsei bibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛbu amɛhe.

english: What distance should I measure between my cocoa plants when setting up a new farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ masusu bɔ ni kookoo tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ ha lɛ he beni miito ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ?

english: A standard spacing like 10 feet by 10 feet gives each cocoa tree enough room for its roots and branches to spread out properly without overcrowding neighboring trees.
ga: Gbɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ tamɔ 10 x 10 feet lɛ baaha cacao tso fɛɛ tso aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni shishifãi kɛ eniji lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã jogbaŋŋ ni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ehiɛɛɛ mli fe nine.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my cocoa trees too close together without proper spacing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ni gbɛ ni sa bɛ amɛteŋ lɛ?

english: When cocoa trees are planted too close together, they compete heavily for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which can stunt their growth and reduce your overall cocoa yield.
ga: Kɛji adu kookoo yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Cocoa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ dalɛ naa ni eha kookoo yibiiwoo fɛɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up so easily during the sun season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and short roots that cannot handle intense direct heat; without nearby shade crops to retain moisture, the soil and plants dry out quickly.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ bɛŋkɛɛɛ ni baaha hulutsoo be lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ baagbi oya.

english: How does planting plantain near cocoa help keep moisture in the soil for my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ cocoa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves block direct sunlight from hitting the ground around cocoa roots, reducing water evaporation and keeping the soil damp and cool for much longer.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni shɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ kookoo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ naa tɛ̃ɛ, ni no haa nu ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ

english: Can my young cocoa trees survive if I plant them out in the open sun without any shade cover?
ga: Ani mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ baahi shi kɛji midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli?

english: Young cocoa trees struggle to survive under direct sun because strong sunlight burns their leaves, so they require temporary shade crops like plantains during their first few years.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛhi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baaha baai lɛ ashã. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ kookoo tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe afɔ̃ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains lɛ anɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Will planting a plantain tree very close to my cocoa seedling steal nutrients from the cocoa?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ahe lɛ baaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ kookoo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Although plantains take some nutrients from the soil, the moisture and sun protection they provide to young cocoa far outweigh the minimal competition for soil nutrients.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ plantains kɛ niyenii komɛi ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsuɔ nii moŋ, shi ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulu hebuu ni amɛhaa kookoo bibii lɛ feɔ akaŋshii fioo ko ni akɛtaoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do cocoa seedlings seem to grow stronger when they have plantain trees growing nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa waa kɛ́ dumɔwui komɛi miida yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains create a cool, humid climate underneath their leaves that reduces heat stress on young cocoa, allowing the seedlings to direct more energy into healthy root and leaf growth.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ feɔ shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ejɔ yɛ baai lɛ ashishi. Enɛ haa dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni yɔɔ kookoo bibii anɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ tsɔɔ hewalɛ mli kɛyaa shishifãi kɛ baai ni wa ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and die when I clear all the tall shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct harsh sunlight. Tall shade trees act like natural canopy umbrellas, protecting the young leaves from burning and keeping the soil moist so the seedlings can establish strong roots.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta. Buu baai bibii ahe kɛjɛ shãa he ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ afee shishifãi ni wa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left up to the newest leaves at the top to survive, leaving the older bottom leaves to starve and turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baajie nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛya baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni ehi shi. Ha shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start to rot underground when heavy rains flood my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water fills all the air gaps in the ground for too long, the roots drown, rot, and become easy targets for soil fungus.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu eyi kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛgboiɔ ni amɛfeɔ nɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he oya.

english: Why do my maize plants produce tiny cobs when I plant many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ miiwo ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ dumɔwui babaoo Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the crop roots fight each other for water and soil food, while their leaves block sunlight from one another. Giving each plant enough space allows it to get the nutrients needed to produce big cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tso lɛ shishifãi wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe lɛ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni enáa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do elderly farmers tell me to plant groundnuts on my land before planting maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa ko kɛɛ mi akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmei yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the groundnut crop finishes, that natural food remains in the soil to help the next maize crop grow strong without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ agbe ŋmei dumɔ naa Nakai adebɔɔ mli niyenii lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eye ebua ŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmei ni jara wa awo mli.

english: Why am I seeing ragged holes inside the young leaves of my maize funnel with tiny dark droppings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji ni ekpɔtɔ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii bibii ni ŋmeii diji bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The caterpillar crawls inside the growing center of the maize plant where it eats the soft tender leaves and leaves behind its waste.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ dalɛ teŋgbɛ. Eyeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ ni eshiɔ jwɛi yɛ esɛɛ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small shoots growing around the main trunk of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishifã titri lɛ ajie.

english: If too many small shoots (suckers) grow around the main plantain tree, they steal water and nutrients away from the mother plant. Pruning them so only two or three remain ensures the mother plant has enough food to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ, Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ mli lɛ, ehaa tso nyɛ lɛ náa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb up high instead of trailing along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves up high toward sunlight so they can manufacture food efficiently. Lifting the leaves off the damp ground also prevents leaves from catching fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kɛya hulu lɛ he bɔni afee ni amɛná niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ akamɔ amɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants roll upward into tight curls during the dry, hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves up to protect themselves from losing too much water in extreme heat. By rolling the leaves, less leaf surface is exposed to the harsh hot air and sun.
ga: Tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite yɛ hulutsoo be mli. kɛtsɔ baai ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ Ba lɛ hiɛ lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulu la shɛɛɛ he tsɔ.

english: Why is it so important for me to clear weeds during the first three weeks after my crop sprouts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ ni tsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young crop sprouts are weak and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds. Clearing weeds early ensures your young crops get all the sun, water, and soil nutrients during their most critical growth phase.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ aná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ yɛ amɛdalɛ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know when it is the right time in July to start planting my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa yɛ July mli ni esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: In many parts of Ghana, the major rains begin around the second week of July. Planting right as these steady rains start ensures your seeds get enough soil moisture to sprout successfully.
ga: yɛ Ghana hei babaoo Nugbɔ ni naa wa baaje shishi yɛ July otsi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔ ni ooodu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ je shishi pɛ kɛkɛ ni ebaaha odumɔwui lɛ aná shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How many weeks of continuous rain can I expect once the July rainy season starts?
ga: Otsii enyiɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be ni manyɛ makpa gbɛ beni July nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: The July rainy season typically lasts about a month and a half (around six weeks). Knowing this length helps you choose crops that can complete their main growth before the water stops.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baa yɛ July mli lɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji kome kɛ fã. (aaafee otsii enumɔ) Kɛ́ ole bɔ ni elɛɛmɔ ji lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ohala tsei ni baanyɛ ashɛ dalɛ he dani nu lɛ akpa.

english: Should I sow my seeds immediately after the very first light shower in July?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ahum ni tswa yɛ July mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is better to wait until the steady rains begin around the second week of July. A single light shower usually does not provide deep enough soil moisture for seeds to survive.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaya nɔ anɛ yɛ July otsi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, kane ni akɛtsuɔ nii shikome pɛ lɛ haaa sũ lɛ mli atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant them late in July instead of when the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu yɛ July naagbee gbɛ moŋ fe be mli ni nugbɔ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: If you plant late in July, your crops may run out of water before they fully mature because the rainy period only lasts about a month and a half, ending around late August.
ga: Kɛji odu yɛ July naagbee lɛ Ekolɛ nu baaho yɛ onibii amli dani amɛshɛ shweremɔ he ejaakɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji kome kɛ fã pɛ. ni baagbe naa aaafee August naagbee gbɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my fellow farmers in another region already planting while my field is still dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minanemɛi okwaafoi ni yɔɔ kpokpai krokomɛi anɔ lɛ miidu nii yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔji lɛ mli egbi lolo lɛ?

english: Rainfall across Ghana does not start in all places at once. The rains usually begin earlier in about seven specific regions, so planting times vary depending on where your farm is located.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ Ghana fɛɛ lɛ ejeee shishi yɛ he fɛɛ he yɛ be kome mli. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ jeɔ shishi mra yɛ kpokpai aaafee 7 nɔ, no hewɔ lɛ, be ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ srɔtoi yɛ he ni oŋmɔ lɛ yɔɔ lɛ naa.

english: Does every part of Ghana get the exact same rainy season schedule in July?
ga: Ani Ghana hei fɛɛ yɛ July nugbɔshiimɔ be he gbɛjianɔtoo kome?

english: No, rainfall patterns differ across the country. While seven major parts of Ghana experience early rains in July, other areas may see different start dates and rainfall levels.
ga: Dabi, bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ehaa lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ maŋ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ Ghana hei titri kpawo naa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe fɛɛ yɛ July mli moŋ, shi hei krokomɛi Obaanyɛ ona shishijee gbii srɔtoi kɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ehaa.

english: What kind of crop varieties should I select if the rain only lasts for six weeks?
ga: Mɛɛ tso henɔ esa akɛ mahala kɛji nugbɔ nɛɔ otsii enyɔ pɛ?

english: You should choose early-maturing or short-duration crop varieties—like fast-growing maize, cowpeas, or vegetables—that can yield fully within a month and a half.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tsina ŋmãa, loo aduawai, ni baanyɛ ashɛ ŋmãa ni yeɔ emuu yɛ nyɔŋ kome kɛ fã mli.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer to my crops during this short rainy period?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛwo miŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku nɛɛ mli?

english: Fertilizer should be applied early in the six-week rainy window. Crops need water to dissolve and absorb nutrients, so applying fertilizer while the rains are active ensures maximum growth.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ otsii enumɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli. Tsei hia nu koni amɛtsɔ mli ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ adara babaoo.

english: How can I keep my soil moist after the six weeks of rain end in late August?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa otsii enyɔ yɛ August naagbee gbɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You can practice mulching by covering the soil around your crops with dried grass or leaves. This traps the moisture left behind from the six weeks of rain and keeps the soil cool.
ga: Obaanyɛ okase mulching kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ni oookɛwo mli lɛ nɔ. ŋmɔshi nibii ni jwɛi loo baai ni egbi yɔɔ mli Enɛ baamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ otsii enumɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i.

english: How do short rainy periods affect how fast my crops grow?
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be kuku Te enaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ oya lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When rain lasts for only a month and a half, crops grow rapidly during those weeks because soil moisture is high. Once the rain stops, their growth slows down as they shift into producing seeds and fruits.
ga: Beni nugbɔ nɛ nyɔŋ kome kɛ fã pɛ lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ daa oya yɛ nakai otsi lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa babaoo lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ, amɛdalɛ baa shi beni amɛtsakeɔ kɛyaa dumɔwui kɛ aduawai ni amɛwoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is essential for their growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the leaves regain their green color and produce better yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant groundnuts or beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ baadu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans naturally pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them alongside maize improves soil fertility naturally and feeds the maize plants without requiring extra synthetic fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei Ejɛɔ ebɔɔ su mli ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ abele masɛi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni ekɛ niyenii aha ŋmãa tsei ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa krokomɛi afata he

english: Why do my cassava roots soft rot in the ground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil for too long and drowns the roots. Building soil mounds or ridges before planting helps excess rainwater drain away so the cassava tubers remain healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli. Kɛ́ afee gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ dani adu lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. koni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ

english: How does spreading dry grass around my crops help them grow during dry spells?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass (mulching) acts as a protective shield. It prevents the strong sun from evaporating soil moisture, keeps the roots cool, and reduces weed growth.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ jwɛi (mulching) baabɔle Oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ akafee ŋmɔtɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ adalɛ baa shi

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their small young pods before they can fully grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ? Dani ebaada kwraa?

english: Young cocoa pods drop (a condition known as cherelle wilt) when the tree experiences stress from drought, poor soil nutrients, or insect attack. Adequate shade, moisture retention, and pest control help the pods reach full size.
ga: Kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ baagbee shi. (Shihilɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ Cherelle Wilt) baa kɛji tsei kɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ kpe. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi tutuamɔ hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa Fɛ̃i ni ahiɔ mli kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ shɛɔ amɛdalɛ he.

english: Why should I cut down some of the small shoots growing at the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? No kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantain titri lɛ shishi.

english: Leaving too many side shoots (suckers) forces them to compete with the main plant for water and nutrients. Pruning them down to leave only one or two strong suckers ensures the main plantain tree produces a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ sɛɛ ŋmeii (ŋmeii) babaoo tsɔ lɛ, enyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa plantain titri lɛ woɔ tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: What causes small holes in my young maize leaves and leaves powdery waste inside the stalk?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ jwɛi yɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed on the growing tips of maize plants. Checking your crops early and applying recommended pest treatments protects the plant before severe damage occurs.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Okwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii amli mra Ni okɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii kɛgbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe lɛ baaye abua ni abu tsei ahe dani nɔ ko ni yɔɔ hiɛdɔɔ aba.

english: Curled pepper leaves are typically caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites, or a virus spread by them. Spraying the plants with neem oil or appropriate insecticides helps control the insects and allows healthy new leaves to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi lɛ ni ewo tso yibii heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn black and hard before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato aduawai ashishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni ewaa dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: Black, sunken spots on tomato bottoms (blossom end rot) happen when the plant cannot get enough calcium, often due to irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture consistent helps the plant absorb calcium and produce healthy fruit.
ga: He diŋŋ ko ni ebote mli yɛ tomato ko hiɛ. Blossom tip rot (fɔlɔ tip rot) baa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛheɔ calcium ni amɛwoɔ aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: The very first rain is often followed by a heat period and dry days that can scorch germinating seeds. Waiting for the rains to become consistent ensures the soil stays wet enough for your seeds to grow safely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, gbii ni mli edɔ, ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ni baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves during dry spells as a survival trick to conserve water in its stems and roots. Once the rains return, the plant will quickly sprout fresh green leaves and continue growing.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Taakɛ teemɔŋ sane kɛha wala koni akɛbu nu he yɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ oya ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: Why do my maize plants roll up their leaves like tubes when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ jwɛi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants curl their leaves tightly during hot days to expose less surface area to the sun, which stops moisture from escaping too fast through transpiration.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ haaa nu ni hoɔ yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli lɛ aya oya tsɔ.

english: Is it a good idea for me to plant beans together with my maize on the same plot?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ ooodu ŋmeii kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize benefits both crops. Beans capture nitrogen from the air and add it to the soil to feed the maize, while the tall maize stalks give climbing bean plants physical support.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ. Beans mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmãa tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛfiɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ agbɔmɔtso lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why does burning grass off my farm before planting harm my soil over time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni mishãa dani miduɔ lɛ baaye mishikpɔŋ lɛ awui yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ?

english: Burning destroys rich organic matter on top of the soil, kills helpful living insects and bacteria, and leaves the soil open to being washed away by heavy rains.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Egbeɔ kooloi kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. ni eha nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites feeding on the underside of the leaves, or by a viral infection carried by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ amli

english: Why are my tomato stems rotting and turning dark right near the ground level?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miifite ni amɛhe yɛ ediŋ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by damping-off or fungal rot, which happens when the soil stays too wet and heavy around young plant stems with little airflow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni efite. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni eyɛ tsii tsɔ yɛ tsei bibii ni kɔɔyɔɔ fioo pɛ tsɔɔ mli lɛ ahe.

english: When is the best time of day for me to apply chemical fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Apply fertilizer early in the morning or late in the afternoon when temperatures are cool. Applying it under hot mid-day heat can burn the plant leaves and roots.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli leebi loo shwane be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ dɔlɛ wo mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ baai kɛ eshishifãi.

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants with deep roots that absorb water and nutrients faster than farm crops, allowing them to take over quickly if not cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa jwɛi lɛ ni amɛyeɔ nɔ oya kɛji akɛ atsaaa amɛ mra.

english: It is not recommended because seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their strength in the second generation, leading to smaller yields and uneven plant growth.
ga: Akɛ enɛ haaa ejaakɛ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ baafite hewalɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ hu daaa ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee.

english: How do I tell when my yam tubers are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Yams are ready for harvest when the leaves and vines above ground turn yellow and completely dry up, showing that the plant has stored all its energy in the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha nikpamɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi kwraa lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ eto eyitso mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which acts as food for leaf growth, or that the soil is too waterlogged. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure will help restore their green color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii ni haa baa lɛ daa. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔji kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which has the natural ability to take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. This enriches the ground naturally, helping your maize grow better without buying as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua o-ŋmã lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe tsofa-kɛ-ŋma babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I remove all the big trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are fragile and burn under direct, harsh sunlight. Leaving some large shade trees or planting temporary crops like plantains provides living shade that protects young cocoa from heat stress and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ashi tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ loo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli

english: If I pack my crops very close together on my land, will I get a larger harvest?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii to he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe waa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ani maná yibii babaoo?

english: Planting too closely causes your crops to compete against each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Spacing them correctly gives each plant enough space and resources to produce larger, healthier yields.
ga: Tsei ni ooodu kɛbɛŋkɛ ohe tsɔ lɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ to he jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer directly from the roots of your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures all the goodness in the soil goes straight to your crops instead.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ basabasa ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa nibii kpakpai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ moŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when heavy rains start falling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long without draining. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater flow away from the root zone, keeping the tubers safe from rotting.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ efooo Shika ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ha yitso lɛ akafite

english: Why is it necessary to put tall wooden stakes next to my yam plants for the vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso masɛi koni wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to capture sunlight for making food. Staking keeps leaves away from damp soil diseases and allows the plant to direct its energy into growing large underground tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe kɛha nihoomɔ. Staking baabu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ helai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. ni ehaa tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, lack of water, or attacks from tiny insects. Giving your plants consistent water during dry periods and checking for hidden pests helps save the blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, nu bɛ, loo kooloi bibii tutua amɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ nɔ daa yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ, ni okwɛ kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ yɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling tightly and stopping the plant from growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe waa ni etsĩɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekadara lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies that transmit viruses, or by water stress from high temperatures. Protecting crops with insect barriers or organic sprays and maintaining consistent watering helps prevent this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo nu mli haomɔ ni jɛɔ hulutsoo be ni mli wa mli baa Nibii ni abuɔ he kɛtsɔ kooloi bibii loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ kɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: How can I tell the exact time when my maize is fully ready to be harvested from the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ akpa mi-ŋma lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the outer husks turn completely brown and dry, and the grains inside become hard enough that you cannot easily dent them with your fingernail.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kwraa ni egbi lɛ. Ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni ehaaa otsitsii lɛ atsɔ mlɛo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil has run out of nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will feed the soil and turn the leaves green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii kpakpai ni ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops yield less every time I plant the same crop on the same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets pests build up in the ground. Rotating your crops—such as planting cowpeas or peanuts after maize—restores nutrients naturally and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni eha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Oŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaatsake, tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni ooodu yɛ ŋmãa sɛɛ. Ebaaha adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ, ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have tiny nodules on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the earth. When you harvest them, the roots and fallen leaves decompose, leaving natural fertilizer behind for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ amɛshishifãi ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni okpaa Fallen shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ fiteɔ. ni oshi adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves with small green droppings inside the center funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that feeds on the tender growing core of maize plants. Applying neem oil spray or recommended treatments early in the morning directly into the central funnel helps stop them before they destroy the stem.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni yeɔ ŋmei tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛbaatsu nii lɛ wo tsɔnei ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekpaa enɛɛmɛi dani amɛfiteɔ tso lɛ yitso lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is caused by tiny pests like thrips or mites sucking the sap out of young leaves, or by viruses spread by these insects. Keeping your farm clean of weeds and spraying early with organic neem leaf extract stops these insects from attacking.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa ji kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Ha oŋmɔ lɛ mli atse ni jwɛi akafee nɔ ko ni okɛ organic neem baa mli nu lɛ afɔ nɔ mra. Bɔni afee ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akatutua

english: Does leaving weeds around my crops really hurt them, or are the weeds just sharing the space?
ga: Jwɛi ni ashiɔ yɛ Miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ miipila amɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Aloo amɛji jwɛi ni jaa he ko kɛkɛ?

english: Weeds aggressively steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer directly from your crops' roots. Clearing weeds during the first month of planting ensures your crops get all the food and light they need to produce a big harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ ni akɛduɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni onibii lɛ aná niyenii kɛ la ni he hiaa amɛ kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ agbo.

english: How do I stop my cassava roots from rotting under the ground when heavy rains fall?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ aha shishifãi lɛ akafite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in flat soil and suffocates the roots. Planting your cassava stems on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to flow away, keeping the roots safe and dry underneath.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei tsei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajo foi kɛya. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ shishi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open clear field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight and harsh winds in their first years. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside your cocoa creates living umbrellas that shelter the young seedlings until they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ dumɔwui bibii ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: My tomato plants have plenty of flowers, but why are the flowers dropping off without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo. Shi mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets too hot, lacks steady water, or isn't visited by pollinating insects like bees. Mulching the soil with dry grass keeps the roots cool and moist, helping the flowers stay attached and turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shɛ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ he. Nu ni fiteɔ daa loo ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni baaa saramɔ Mulching kɛ jwɛi ni egbi yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots, and heavy fruit bunches make them top-heavy during strong winds. Supporting the main stem with a strong forked wooden prop prevents the tree from bending or snapping before the plantain matures.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Ni aduawai akui ni tsii baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ fi tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakumɔ loo ekakumɔ dani dumɔwui lɛ adara.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants showing small holes and looking chewed up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni etamɔ nɔ ni ashɛre lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by leaf-eating pests like the Fall Armyworm. They hide in the center of young maize plants and eat the leaves, which slows down growth if not treated early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai, tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha edalɛ aya hiɛ fioo kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the sap from the leaves, or by viral diseases spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my crops turning yellow while the new top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low on nitrogen. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has to the newest growth at the top, leaving the older leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baajie nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛya tso hee ni eda fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ nɔ. Ha baai ni egbɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by very high temperatures, lack of water, or a shortage of nutrients like phosphorus and potassium which help flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium ni bɛ lɛ hao tsei lɛ. ni haa fɔfɔi feɔ aduawai

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, their leaves and roots fight for sunlight, water, and soil food. This competition starves the plants, preventing them from growing thick stems and large fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Baai kɛ shishifãi kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei yeɔ hɔmɔ. Tsi tsei ni mli tse kɛ aduawai wuji anaa.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes so their leaves can get maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to make food, which travels down to make the underground yam tuber grow large.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ koni amɛbaji lɛ ajie amɛhe kpo yɛ hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ mli. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my vegetables with dry grass or leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Aduawai ni jwɛi loo baai ni egbi yɔɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating quickly under the harsh sun, keeping moisture near the roots.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shishifãi lɛ ahe

english: Cassava roots need well-drained soil to breathe. When water sits in the field for too long, it cuts off air to the roots, causing fungal and bacterial rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he hiaa cassava shishifãi koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and stronger than the crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants that absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than farm crops. Clearing them quickly prevents them from stealing food from your main crop.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ oya lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛjɛ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when planted in an open field without trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight. They need temporary shade from fast-growing plants like plantains to protect them and trap moisture while they are young.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛbu amɛhe ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli be mli ni amɛji gbekɛbii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. Leaving shade trees or planting plantains beside them creates a canopy that shields the young leaves from heat and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why should I avoid planting my maize seeds very close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ dumɔ he?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stalks and tiny cobs.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves are symptoms of Cassava Mosaic Disease, often spread by tiny insects called whiteflies, which weakens the plant and reduces the size of your tuber harvest.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ nɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ enɛ amɛshwãa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa o-tuber ni okpaa lɛ baa shi.

english: How can I tell if my farmland soil has lost its strength and needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli hewalɛ efo mli ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli?

english: If your crops grow slowly, have pale yellow leaves instead of deep green ones, and produce light yields despite good rainfall, the soil has exhausted its nutrients.
ga: Kɛji onibii lɛ daraa blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ. ni ehaa la kpakpa kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ efo mli.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants before producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ tomato tsei anɔ dani tomato baa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off without forming fruit when the plants experience severe heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of bees and insects to pollinate them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa kpe. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi daa loo ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni baahã ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmeii lɛ ni bɛ

english: Can I save grains from my harvested hybrid maize to plant during the next farming season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmaa ni jɛ hybrid corn mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ okwaayeli be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid maize harvests will grow into weaker plants with unpredictable yields; purchasing fresh certified seeds each season guarantees strong growth and uniform cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akpaa lɛ mli lɛ daa ni etsɔɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli ni aheɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ haa amɛdalɛ ni mli wa kɛ ŋmeii ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ naa nɔmimaa.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants roll up into tight tubes during the sunny afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ shwieɔ shi efeɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants curl their leaves inward to protect themselves from intense heat and slow down the amount of water escaping from their leaves into the air.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni amɛha nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and will quickly steal the water, sunlight, and soil food your young crops need to build strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛbaaju nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei bibii lɛ oya koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that crop loves and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do small insects attack and destroy my dried maize after I put it in storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ beni mikɛwo kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii amli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Insects called grain weevils multiply in stored maize if the grain was not dried completely before bagging or if the bags are not stored in a clean, airtight space.
ga: Kpluka ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ seed moth lɛ fɔɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛwo kotoku mli loo akɛ kotoku lɛ etooo he ko ni he tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli.

english: If I start by planting very small seed yams, will they actually grow to produce big tubers at harvest?
ga: Kɛ mije shishi kɛtsɔ sweet potato dumɔwui bibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ Beni akpa lɛ, ani ebaakwɛ bulbs wuji diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, small seed yams can yield large, healthy tubers. As long as the small seed is healthy and free from diseases, it has all the genetic instructions and energy needed to build a strong plant that produces full-sized yams.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ dumɔwui amli lɛ baanyɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Shii abɔ ni dumɔwui bibii lɛ He wa lolo ni hela bɛ amɛhe lɛ. Ojogbaŋŋ, eyɛ fɔmɔ su mli gbɛtsɔɔmɔi kɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛfee tso ko ni he wa ni woɔ ŋmeii ni dalɛ fa babaoo.

english: Why do yams grown from clean laboratory seeds produce better harvests than seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potatoes ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui amli yɛ laboratori ni he tse mli lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from old harvests often carry hidden diseases and pests accumulated over time. Laboratory-grown seeds start completely free of viruses and rot, allowing the plant to use all its strength to produce a bigger yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni yeɔ wala yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ momo mli lɛ hiɛɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ. Dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ yɛ Lab lɛ jeɔ shishi ni helai kɛ fitemɔ bɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ nibii babaoo mli.

english: Why do agriculture officers keep young yam plants inside a net structure before moving them to the open farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi kɛ sweet potato tsei woɔ trellis mli dani amɛjieɔ amɛ kɛyaa ŋmɔji ni agbele mli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: A net house or screen house protects fragile young plants from harsh direct sunlight, heavy rains, and insects that spread diseases. It creates a safe environment for sprouts to grow strong roots before facing tough field conditions.
ga: Greenhouses loo trellises buɔ dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kooloi ni gbɛɔ helai amɛshwãa lɛ ahe. Feemɔ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe koni dumɔwui lɛ aná shishifãi ni mli wa dani amɛkɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi ni mli wawai akpee.

english: How long do young yam sprouts usually need to stay in a nursery before they are ready for field planting?
ga: Be enyiɛ ehe hiaa ni sweet potato tsei lɛ ahi ŋmɔ mli dani amɛfee klalo akɛ abaadu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Young yam plants typically spend about two months in the nursery. This gives them enough time to form sturdy roots and healthy leaves so they can survive transplanting to the main farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato tsei lɛ hiɔ aaafee nyɔji enyɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛ be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛfee shishifãi ni wa kɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ bɔni afee ni anyɛ atsake amɛ kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: Does strong direct sunlight hurt very young crop sprouts when they first emerge?
ga: Ani hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ saa tsei bibii ahe beni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Yes, intense sunlight can burn tender young leaves and dry out delicate roots. Providing light shade and moisture during the early weeks helps young sprouts establish themselves without getting stressed.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai bibii ni eha shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbi. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli. Ehaa tsei bibii lɛ ŋmɛɔ amɛhe shi ni haomɔ ko bɛ he.

english: What does it mean when agricultural experts talk about tissue culture or lab-grown yams, and are they safe to plant?
ga: Okwaayeli he nilelɔi wieɔ fãji akusum loo atomo ni adu yɛ laboratori lɛ he. Ni mɛni ji nɔ ni shweshweeshwe ni aduɔ lɛ tsɔɔ?

english: Lab-grown yams are produced by taking tiny, clean tissues from a healthy plant and growing them in a sterile environment. They are completely safe and natural, giving you strong plants that are free from common yam diseases.
ga: Akɛ fãji bibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ feɔ sweet potatoes ni akwɛɔ yɛ Lab lɛ. Aduɔ tsei ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ he ko ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ. Amɛyɛ shweshweeshwe kwraa ni amɛji adebɔɔ mli nɔ. Enɛ haa onáa tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni sweet potato helai ni afɔɔ namɔ bɛ mli.

english: How can I produce a large quantity of seed yams if I only have a few good tubers to start with?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafee sweet potatoi babaoo? Be ni miyɛ yitso kpakpa lɛ yitso fioo pɛ

english: You can cut healthy tubers into small pieces called minisetts, treat the cut surfaces to prevent decay, and plant them close together in a nursery bed. This allows you to turn a few tubers into dozens of small, healthy seed yams for the next season.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli bibii bibii. Atsɛɔ lɛ minisɛt. Tsɔɔmɔ he ni afo lɛ koni ekafite. ni odu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ mli saatso ko nɔ Gbɛ nɛɛ haa onyɛɔ otsakeɔ ŋmeii fioo komɛi ofeɔ ŋmeii bibii. Tubers ni yɔɔ hewalɛ srɔtoi kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why do my young plant seedlings sometimes wilt or look weak immediately after I move them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, midumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ ewo shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is known as transplanting shock, which happens because moving the plant disturbs its roots. Planting during cool mornings or evenings and watering immediately helps the plant settle into the soil smoothly.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Enɛ baa mli ejaakɛ tso lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ gbalaa eshishifãi lɛ anaa. Kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ yɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni afɔ amɛ nu oya lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do crop diseases get into my field if I am planting on fresh land?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsei ahe helai abote miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji midu yɛ sũ nɔ?

english: Diseases usually enter fresh land through infected seed materials or tiny insects like aphids that carry viruses from neighboring farms. Starting with certified disease-free seeds prevents these problems from starting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ boteɔ sũ ŋmɔji amli kɛtsɔɔ dumɔwui nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni hiɛ hela lɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui ni ana he odaseyeli akɛ hela bɛ mli lɛ je shishi lɛ, ebaatsi naagbai nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkaje shishi.

english: Why do yam vines seem to focus on growing leaves for months before any big tubers form under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ nyɔji babaoo dani ŋmeii wuji baa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: The plant uses its early months to build a large factory of vines and leaves to capture sunlight. Once the leafy top is fully developed, it uses that energy to feed and swell the tubers underground.
ga: Tsei yeɔ amɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli kɛdaraa. Koni afee wain tsei kɛ baai ahe nitsumɔhe agbo ko ni akɛbaamɔ hulu la lɛ. Kɛji baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ edara kwraa Ekɛ nakai hewalɛ lɛ yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii ni ekwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tip and moving down the middle in a V-shape usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Maize needs plenty of nitrogen to grow strong green leaves, so when it runs out, the plant pulls nutrients from old lower leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ kɛyaa shishi yɛ teŋgbɛ, ni feɔ V su lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. No hewɔ lɛ kɛ́ etee lɛ Tso lɛ baajie niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas or groundnuts helps make the soil better for my maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi ŋmãa lɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have tiny bumps on their roots called nodules. Friendly bacteria living in these nodules capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acts as a natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ ŋmeii bibii. Atsɛɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ akɛ nodules. Muawai ni yɔɔ naanyobɔɔ mli ni hiɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ amli lɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with very small cobs when I plant three or four seeds in one small hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ daa ni efeɔ mlɛo ni eyɛ ŋmei bibioo ko kwraa beni midu dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ yɛ bu bibioo kome mli lɛ?

english: Planted too closely together, crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Placing only one or two seeds per hole at the recommended distance gives each plant enough space and food to grow thick stems and large cobs.
ga: ni adu yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui kome loo enyɔ pɛ wo bu kome mli yɛ he ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛto lɛ, ebaaha tso fɛɛ tso aná he ko kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain suckers to shade my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui koni mikɛwo mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe shade lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that dry out easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad shade leaves to shield the young cocoa plants while keeping the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ.

english: Why do some of my cassava stem cuttings fail to grow leaves after I plant them upside down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ ekomɛi ewooo baai beni mikɛ amɛ ewo shishi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cassava stems have small buds or 'eyes' where shoots and roots grow. The buds must point upwards toward the sky so water and plant nutrients flow in the right direction to sprout new leaves.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ‘ŋmeii’, ni ji hei ni ŋmeii kɛ shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ. Ehe miihia ni fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ atsɔ gbɛ ni ja nɔ koni baai heei akwɛ̃.

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when temperatures get too high, when the soil gets too dry, or when bees are not visiting to pollinate the blooms. Consistent watering and light shade during extreme heat can help flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato baafɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii baaa koni amɛbawo fɔfɔii amli ŋmeii. Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up into tight cups and looking wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ efolɔ amɛhe ewo kɔɔpoi ni mli wa mli ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids, mites, or whiteflies feeding on sap under the leaves, or transmitting a virus. These pests weaken the leaf structure as it grows.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids, mites, loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli latex loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ haa baai lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ gbɔjɔɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch maximum sunlight. Lifting the leaves away from wet soil also prevents fungal leaf diseases and allows the plant to produce larger tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ baa helai ni ji fungal lɛ anaa, ni ehaa tso lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily before the fruit bunches are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya dani aduawai akutsei lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Plantains fall over because they have shallow root systems that get weakened by microscopic worms called nematodes or plantain root weevils. Supporting heavy bunches with bamboo props prevents the trees from snapping in strong winds.
ga: Plantains gbeeɔ shi ejaakɛ amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo plantain shishifãi ŋmeii lɛ egbɔjɔ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni akɛfiɔ jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ asɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa amɛkumɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why do my crops dry up and die even when I plant right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ moŋ?

english: The first rain after a long dry season is often a false start, followed by hot dry weather before the main rainy season truly begins. Seeds sprout from the initial moisture but burn up when soil moisture disappears in the hot sun.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ ji amale shishijee. Nɔ ni nyiɛɔ enɛ sɛɛ ji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi diɛŋtsɛ. Dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ shishijee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli. Shi ebaashã kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ laaje kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ enɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning pale yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: When the lower leaves turn yellow in a V-shape from the tips, it usually means your maize is lacking nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow tall, so adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted manure around the roots will fix this.
ga: Kɛji akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛjɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata Roots he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in my field help my next season's maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni miŋmei lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes, which means they have tiny natural factories on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. When you harvest groundnut, that extra nitrogen stays in the earth, acting as free fertilizer for the crop you plant next.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛyɛ adebɔɔ mli nitsumɔhei bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛsaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni okpaa ŋmeii Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Curled leaves with yellowish patches are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. The best solution is to pull up severely infected plants and use disease-resistant cassava stem cuttings for your next planting.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmei bibioo lɛ ji nɔ ni hiɛɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ Tsabaa ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ waa lɛ. Ni okɛ ŋmei niji ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ atsu nii kɛha dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Early drying of yam vines is often caused by underground pests like yam beetles or microscopic nematodes damaging the roots, or fungal leaf spots. Keeping the field clear of weeds and using clean, undamaged seed yams at planting keeps the foliage healthy longer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ sweet potato ŋmeii loo nematodes bibii ni kɛ shishifãi fiteɔ loo fungal leaf spots baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbiɔ oya. Kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ jɛmɛ ni okɛ ŋmeii ni he tse ni efiteee tsu nii beni aduɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my sweet pepper leaves droop in the hot afternoon even when the soil has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bell pepper lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: On very hot days, pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than the roots can pull it up from the ground, causing them to wilt to protect themselves. As long as the soil stays moist and the leaves perk back up by evening or early morning, the crop is fine.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa nɔ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgbiɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafee ŋmɔtɔ ni baai lɛ baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ loo leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees lose their leaves and dry up when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ baa lɛ miiho ni amɛmiigbi yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have thin leaves and shallow roots that cannot tolerate strong direct sunlight or hot dry winds. Planting shade crops like plantains or shade trees alongside young cocoa protects them from harsh heat until their root systems grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baatswa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing very leafy and tall, but not producing many flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa lɛ? Shi jeee fɔfɔi babaoo?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes tomato plants focus all their energy on growing stems and leafy foliage instead of blossoms. To get more tomatoes, feed the crop with fertilizers higher in phosphorus and potassium, which trigger flowering and fruit setting.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmeii kɛ baai ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi. Bɔni afee ni oná tomato babaoo Ha tso lɛ niyenii ni phosphorus kɛ potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli. ni baaha fɔfɔi kɛ yibii aba

english: Why are the small fruits on my watermelon vines rotting at the tips and falling off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ mi watermelon tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miifite yɛ eshishigbɛ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Watermelon fruits rot at the tips if bees haven't properly pollinated the flowers or if the plant lacks calcium and steady water. Ensuring good drainage and allowing bees to visit the yellow flowers will help the tiny melons grow big and healthy.
ga: Watermelon yibii lɛ baafite yɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ ehiɛɛɛ ŋmeii lɛ jogbaŋŋ loo kɛji tso lɛ bɛ calcium kɛ nu ni baa daa. Kɛ́ akwɛ koni nu ho jogbaŋŋ ni aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii ayasara fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua melon bibii lɛ ni amɛdara. tsɔ agbo ni ehe wa

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers if they are attacked by sap-sucking insects like mirids or if the tree is experiencing water stress. Protecting the farm from insect pests and keeping sufficient shade keeps the humidity right for flowers to turn into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii, tamɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi, loo kɛji tso lɛ miina nu he haomɔ. Kɛ́ abu ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe, ni anáa hulutsoo ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo ni sa hiɔ shi koni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why are my plantain bunches taking a very long time to fill out and mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani eyiɔ ni edara lɛ?

english: Plantain bunches take longer to fill out when the soil lacks potassium or when the plant doesn't get enough water during the fruiting stage. Adding compost or ash rich in potassium around the base and keeping old leaves pruned helps the plant send energy straight into the bunch.
ga: Plantain ŋmeii lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ kɛ́ potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii lɛ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo sũ ni potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ afata he. Kɛ́ tso lɛ shishifãi shwie shi ni efolɔ baa lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ aya ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if my land is suitable for growing cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha kookoo tsei akwɛmɔ?

english: Good cocoa land needs deep, rich soil that drains excess water easily while keeping enough moisture for the roots. It should also be in an area that gets reliable rainfall and has taller trees around to provide shade for young cocoa plants.
ga: Kookoo shikpɔŋ kpakpa biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii ni haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya yɛ be mli ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ hiɔ shi. Esa akɛ ehi he ko ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa, ni tsei kakadaji ebɔle he. Koni ekɛ hulutsoo aha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when I plant them in a low swampy area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ adu yɛ hei ni ŋmeii yɔɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Maize roots need air in the soil to breathe. In swampy or waterlogged areas, water fills all the space in the soil and smothers the roots, preventing them from taking up nutrients, which causes the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Abɛi shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Yɛ hei ni ŋmeii loo nu ni damɔ shi yɔɔ lɛ. Nu baayi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli obɔ ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ akumɔ. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Planting cassava on the same soil every year removes the same nutrients repeatedly without giving the soil time to recover. It also allows soil diseases and pests that attack cassava to build up and ruin future harvests.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni aduɔ daa afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ. ni ekɛ be haaa koni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ Ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ helai kɛ kooloi ni tutuaa ŋmei lɛ hu feɔ wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before any peppers actually grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani pepper lɛ eda diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants usually drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as very high heat during the day, irregular watering, or a lack of key nutrients in the soil needed to support fruit development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Nu ni ashwieɔ shi daa loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha aduawai adalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and thin but yield very little fruit when planted close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds or suckers are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight. The plants put all their energy into stretching upwards to reach the sun instead of developing thick stems and heavy fruit.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui loo ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ tsohi nɛ a mi wa kɛ yiblii nɛ mi wa.

english: Why do plantain suckers take so much longer to bear fruit when grown under dense bush shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Plantains require full sunlight to manufacture food efficiently. When shaded heavily, their leaves cannot make enough food, which slows down growth and delays flowering and fruiting.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia plantains koni enyɛ efee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ eyɛ hulutsoo waa lɛ Ebaai lɛ nyɛŋ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa edalɛ baa shi ni ehaa fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: How can I tell if my wilting tomato crop is sick from a disease or just needs water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela emɔ mi-tomato ni egbo lɛ loo nu kɛkɛ he miihia amɛ?

english: A thirsty tomato plant will revive quickly in the evening or after you water it. A diseased tomato plant will remain wilted even with plenty of soil moisture and may show brown spots or yellowing stems.
ga: Tomato tsei ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa wala mli oya gbɛkɛ loo beni okɛ nu ha amɛ sɛɛ. Tomato tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ baaya nɔ agbi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo po. ni ebaanyɛ ejie ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ kpo.

english: Why is it harmful to apply liquid farm medicine or chemicals on crops during hot sunny afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ akɛ tsofai ni ji nu loo ŋmɔ mli tsofai baatsu nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Spraying chemicals in direct, hot sunlight causes the liquid to evaporate too fast before the plant absorbs it. The intense sun combined with the chemical can also burn the crop leaves.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ dani tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Hulu la ni naa wa ni akɛ tsofai fata he lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei ahe baai.

english: Yam tubers rot underground when soil stays too wet for long periods, creating an environment for soil fungi and bacteria to enter the tuber through tiny wounds or cracks.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ baanyɛ abote bulb lɛ mli kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni egbɛ eshwa lɛ anɔ.

english: Curled cassava leaves with yellow patterns are caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus. Small white insects called whiteflies spread this sickness by feeding on healthy leaves after biting diseased plants.
ga: Kasava baai ni atsɔ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kasava mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kplukai bibii yɛŋ ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa kɛtsɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛyeɔ beni amɛye tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crops are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient found in fertilizer that helps plants build green leaves and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni anaa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Will applying too much fertilizer at once hurt my crops?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni mikɛwoɔ mli shikome lɛ baaye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui?

english: Yes, putting too much fertilizer close to plant roots can burn them and pull water out of the plant, causing the crops to wither and die instead of growing bigger.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo tso shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã lɛ ni ejie nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ he. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaadara.

english: Why do my crops dry up faster during dry spells when I use chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ fɛ̃i be mli kɛ́ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need water to dissolve properly into the soil; without enough moisture, concentrated fertilizer salts can trap water away from plant roots.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ faaa lɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ahi nu ni jɛ tsei shishifãi amli lɛ mli.

english: Why should I buy certified improved seeds instead of saving seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ? Mohu ɔ, mo ngɔ dumɔwuhi nɛ je ngma kpami nɛ be ɔ mi ɔ kɛ to.

english: Improved seeds are specially bred to resist local pests, tolerate drought better, and give higher yields compared to old saved seeds that lose their strength over time.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Hɔmɔ he tsuishitoo ni hi kɛ yibiiwoo ni fa kɛ akɛto dumɔwui momo ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do some of my seeds fail to sprout after I plant them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are planted too deep, if the soil lacks sufficient moisture, or if soil insects eat the seed before it sprouts.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ye dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller cobs or fruits when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii loo aduawai kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving less energy for the plant to produce big cobs or fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ aná hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji loo aduawai.

english: How does weed growth affect how well my crops use fertilizer?
ga: Te jwɛi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ saa bɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii ahaa lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?
