english: Weeds grow aggressively and will steal the applied fertilizer from the soil before your crops' roots have a chance to absorb it.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛbaaju ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔ.

english: Why are fall armyworms attacking my young maize plants so heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall worms lɛ tutuaa mi-baby corn tsei lɛ waa nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms target tender young leaves because they are soft and easy to eat, and the pests multiply rapidly during warm weather if not treated early.
ga: Fall armyworms lɛ kwɛɔ baai bibii lɛ anɔ ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛyeɔ mlɛo. Ni tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yaa hiɛ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ atsaaa amɛ mra.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants start to curl up and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips that feed on sap and spread plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni yeɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tsei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my crops look weak and pale even when it rains heavily every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa daa gbi lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains can wash essential plant nutrients deep into the soil below root level or flood the roots so they cannot breathe and absorb food.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ tso lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛya sũ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ashishi loo ekɛ nu abɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛyashɛ he ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli niyenii lɛ.

english: What is the best way to water my mango trees so that all the branches get enough moisture?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ afɔ mango tso nɔ nu koni tso nine fɛɛ nine aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: Using an overhead sprinkler system is very effective for mango trees. It sprays water widely across the entire tree, reaching all the upper leaves and branches, which helps the tree stay healthy and produce better fruit.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ yiteŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa kɛhaa mango tsei. Okɛ nu afɔ tso lɛ he fɛɛ yɛ kooyigbɛ. kɛyashi ŋwɛi baai kɛ niji fɛɛ Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enáa hewalɛ ni ewoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Is it better to pour water directly at the root of my fruit tree or use a sprinkler system?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofɔ nu yɛ aduawai tso lɛ shishi loo oookɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ atsu nii?

english: While pouring water at the roots keeps the soil wet, using a sprinkler sprays water over the whole tree canopy. This cools down the leaves in hot weather, washes off dust, and ensures moisture reaches all branches evenly.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni okɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ afɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ fɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli, etsuɔ ​​sũ he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ niji fɛɛ ahe pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: How do I know if my fruit trees are getting enough water during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli?

english: If leaves begin to curl, turn yellow, or drop early, the tree is lacking moisture. Using sprinklers to evenly coat the branches and foliage with water helps the tree resist the dry winds and maintain its health.
ga: Kɛji baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Etsɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo egbeeɔ shi oya, ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nu. Kɛ́ akɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ tsu nii ni akɛ nu shwie tsei aniji kɛ baai anɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi mli ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ mli.

english: Why do my mango trees drop their flowers before the fruits even start to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Trees often shed flowers when they suffer from heat stress or irregular watering. Providing consistent water that reaches both the roots and the upper leaves helps the tree keep its flowers until fruit sets.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ fɛɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why are some branches inside my mango tree canopy not producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji komɛi ni yɔɔ mango tso lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii lɛ?

english: Inner branches often miss out on sunlight and direct water when watered only from below. Ensuring light and water reach all parts of the tree canopy encourages all branches to flower and bear fruit.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ mli lɛ sumɔɔ ni hulu la kɛ nu akashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ kɛji akɛ nu jɛ shishi pɛ. Kɛ́ akwɛ koni la kɛ nu ashɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ hei fɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa niji fɛɛ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Does spraying water on the leaves of my fruit tree help protect it from heat?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛshwieɔ aduawai tsei ahe baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni abu he kɛjɛ latsaa he?

english: Yes, spraying water over the foliage lowers the leaves' temperature during extreme hot days, preventing sun scorch and helping the tree hold onto its growing fruits.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baaye abua ni eha amɛhe dɔlɛ aba shi yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Ebuɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ eyibii ni miida lɛ mli.

english: How can I make my mango trees produce bigger and sweeter fruits every season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi mango tso lɛ awo yibii wuji ni ŋɔɔ daa be mli?

english: Getting a good harvest of sweet fruits requires balanced watering across all branches during dry periods, good exposure to sunlight, and proper care while the green fruits are developing on the tree.
ga: Bɔni afee ni aná aduawai ni ŋɔɔ lɛ akpamɔ kpakpa lɛ biɔ ni akɛ nu awo tsei lɛ aniji fɛɛ amli yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Hulu la kpakpa ni anáa kɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni aduawai eŋɔlii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Should I continue watering my mango trees when green fruits start appearing on the branches?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo mi mango tso lɛ nɔ nu beni aduawai eŋɔli jeɔ shishi ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, fruit trees need steady moisture while the fruits are expanding to ensure they become plump and juicy. However, reduce excessive watering right before full harvest to allow sugars to concentrate.
ga: Hɛɛ, aduawai tsei lɛ he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be be mli ni aduawai lɛ miigbɛ amɛshwã koni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔtɔ, shi kɛlɛ, tsi nu ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ shi fe nine dani akpa amɛ nii lɛ fɛɛ koni sugars lɛ afee ekome.

english: How does adopting better irrigation tools like sprinklers help my family's income?
ga: Te nu shwiemɔ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ tamɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miweku lɛ ni amɛná shika aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Proper irrigation increases your overall yield and fruit quality. Selling higher volumes of healthy fruit at the market brings in better profits, improving your home's financial stability and livelihood.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha onibii kɛ aduawai lɛ fɛɛ aya hiɛ. Kɛ́ ahɔ̃ɔ tso yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ babaoo yɛ jara nɔ lɛ, ebaaha aná sɛɛnamɔ kpakpa. Ha shika helɛtemɔ kɛ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ oshia lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my neighbor's fruit trees yield more uniform crops than mine during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ woɔ yibii ni yaa nɔ daa fe mi nɔ lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Uniform crops usually result from even water distribution across the whole farm. Methods like sprinkler irrigation ensure every tree—and every branch on each tree—gets equal water and grows at the same pace.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni jɛɔ nu ni ajaa pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ. Gbɛi tamɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso—kɛ tso nine fɛɛ nine ni yɔɔ tso fɛɛ tso nɔ lɛ—náa nu abɔ ni sa ni edaa yɛ oyaiyeli ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ mli.

english: How do I choose a crop that will guarantee I find buyers as soon as I finish harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ akɛ ebaana mɔ ni baahe kɛji akpa lɛ pɛ?

english: To ensure quick sales, focus on high-demand staple crops like maize, cassava, or popular vegetables like tomatoes and peppers that market traders buy daily. Checking local market demand and securing interest from buyers before planting helps turn your harvest into cash quickly.
ga: bɔni afee ni ahɔ̃ɔ oya Kɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama nibii ni ataoɔ waa tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo aduawai ni ehe gbɛi tamɔ tomato kɛ ŋmãa nɔ. ni jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ heɔ daa gbi Kɛ́ okwɛ nibii ni jarayelɔi lɛ taoɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli ni oná mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ ahe miishɛɛ dani odu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni otsɔ onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ anɔ oya.

english: Why do some crops sell very fast at the local market while others sit on the display bench and rot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ahɔ̃ɔ oya yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayeli hei lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi taraa nibii ni ajieɔ atsɔɔ lɛ anɔ ni amɛgboɔ lɛ?

english: Crops like tomatoes or onions are used in everyday Ghanaian cooking, so demand is constant. Crops with low daily demand or poor shelf life take longer to sell. Understanding what consumers use daily helps you pick crops that clear out quickly.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ tomato loo sabolai Akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ Ghana daa gbi niyenii homɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, nibii ni abiɔ lɛ yaa nɔ daa. Nibii ni aduɔ ni ataoɔ daa gbi loo ni sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ baahe be babaoo dani ahɔ̃ɔ. Kɛ́ onu nɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii daa gbi lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ohala ŋmɔshi nibii ni obaajie lɛ oya.

english: Why do my tomatoes all ripen at the exact same time, making it hard to sell them all to market buyers before they spoil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ miikwɛ̃ yɛ be kome mli lɛ? Ani ehaa ewaa akɛ aaahɔɔ tomato muu aha mɛi ni heɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ dani amɛfite?

english: Tomato plants produce a natural gas called ethylene that triggers ripening across the whole crop at once. To avoid losing your harvest, plant your seeds in small batches a few weeks apart so the tomatoes mature in stages rather than all at once.
ga: Tomato tsei jieɔ adebɔɔ mli la ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene ni haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ shwereɔ shikome. Bɔni afee ni nibii ni anáa lɛ akafite lɛ Dumɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ kui bibii amli otsii 2-3 kɛjɛ amɛhe koni eha tomatoi lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ fãi srɔtoi amli moŋ fe fɛɛ shikome.

english: If I keep my harvested maize for a few months to wait for better market prices, why do insects destroy it in storage?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ mi-ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ to nyɔji fioo komɛi koni mamɛ jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ lɛ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Harvested maize still contains moisture that attracts pests like weevils. If the grain isn't dried completely under the sun before storage, insects easily breed inside. Thoroughly drying the grain and using airtight storage bags stops pests from ruining your stock.
ga: Abɛi ni akpa lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni gbalaa kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛtoɔ. Kplukai baanyɛ afɔ yɛ mli mlɛo. Kɛ́ ogbala oŋmaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ vacuum storage bags tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akafite oŋmaa lɛ.

english: Why do my leafy green vegetables wilt so quickly after I pick them to take to the market buyer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-green lɛ shwieɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mifolɔ koni mikɛyaha mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Leafy vegetables lose water rapidly through their leaves once cut from the root, especially in hot weather. Harvesting early in the morning when it is cool and keeping the produce covered in a cool, shaded area preserves their freshness for buyers.
ga: Aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji ajie amɛ kɛjɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli pɛ. Titri lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Nikpamɔ leebi be mli ni hulu lɛ miitso ni okɛ onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ ato he ko ni hulu lɛ miitso ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ baaye abua ni efee ehee aha mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why do some of my cassava plants grow huge roots for the market while others only grow tall stems and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ekomɛi yɛ shishifãi babaoo kɛha jara lɛ? yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu kwɛ̃ɔ tsei kɛ baai kakadaji pɛ.

english: Cassava plants direct their energy into leaves and stems if there is too much nitrogen in the soil or if they are planted too close together. Spacing the plants properly and ensuring good soil drainage encourages the plant to store its energy underground in thick tubers.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ baatsɔɔ hewalɛ kɛya amɛbaai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli kɛji akɛ nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei lɛ to he ko jogbaŋŋ ni ana koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse amli.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop producing new peppers after I harvest a few for my family?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ pepper heei feemɔ beni mikpa pepper komɛi miha miweku lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants need extra water and nutrients to keep forming new flowers after a pick. If the soil lacks moisture or food, the plant enters a resting phase. Giving the plant organic manure and regular water keeps it producing fruit throughout the season.
ga: Nu kɛ niyenii krokomɛi he miihia pepper tsei koni amɛwo fɔfɔi heei beni ajie amɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo niyenii bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baabote wɔɔhe be mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ nu ha otsei lɛ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why does growing only one single crop in my field attract more pests than when I mix different crops together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso henɔ kome ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui babaoo fe be mli ni mikɛ tsei babaoo futuɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: A single crop over a large area creates an easy, endless food source for specific insects, allowing them to multiply fast. Planting different crops side-by-side confuses pests and breaks their feeding cycles, keeping your market crop safer.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ wulu nɔ lɛ haa kooloi komɛi náa niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni bɛ naagbee. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛfɔɔ oya. Tsei srɔtoi ni aduɔ Side by side lɛ baaha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ afutu ni ebaafite amɛ niyenii yeli gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ojarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafee shweshweeshwe.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest plantains so they stay firm until I can transport them to buyers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa plantains lɛ koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi be mli ni manyɛ mikɛ amɛ aya mɛi ni heɔ lɛ aŋɔɔ?

english: Plantains should be harvested when the individual fruits are plump and full, but still fully green. Harvesting at this green stage gives you a few days to transport and sell them to market buyers before they naturally soften and turn yellow.
ga: Esa akɛ akpa plantains beni aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko egbɔ shi eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ amli lɛ baaha oná gbii fioo komɛi ni okɛya ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ. dani efee blɛoo ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Why do my yam tubers start rotting underground if I leave them in the soil too long after the leaves die back?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni baai lɛ egbo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When yam leaves turn yellow and dry up, the plant stops growing and goes dormant. Leaving tubers in damp soil after this stage exposes them to soil fungi and excess wetness, which causes them to rot. Harvesting as soon as the vine dies protects the tuber.
ga: Kɛji sweet potato baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi lɛ Tso lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ ni eyaa wɔɔhe. Kɛ́ ashi bulbs lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ yɛ nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ mli ŋmeii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine aba amɛnɔ. ni haa amɛgboiɔ Nikpamɔ kɛji wain tso lɛ gbo pɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow instead of dark green even after I clear new land to plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ? Beni mijie he hee ko ni mikɛbaadu nii lɛ sɛɛ po.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil. Even fresh land can be missing key nutrients, so adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the maize leaves turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ po baanyɛ afee nɔ ni niyenii mli nibii titrii bɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, kooloi ashishifãi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with many leaves but small roots when I plant them under big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ baai babaoo shi shishifãi bibii yɔɔ mli kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko ni yɔɔ hulutsoo shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava needs full sunlight to produce energy and store food in its roots. Under heavy shade, the plant uses all its energy stretching upwards toward the light instead of building tubers underground.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia cassava koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba ni ekɛ niyenii ato eshishifãi lɛ amli. yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ shishi Tsei yeɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛtsɔ ŋwɛi ni amɛkpãa kɛyaa la he lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii

english: Why does my farm give me fewer sacks of maize every year when I plant on the exact same plot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ haaa mi ŋmãa fioo daa afi be mli ni miduɔ ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil each season. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts refills nitrogen in the soil and restores crop yields.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be fɛɛ mli. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Ebaaye ebua ni akɛ nitrogen afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up right on the branch during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives and spreads in cool, damp shade. Pruning excess tree branches to let in sunlight and clearing infected pods helps stop the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ejɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la aba ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni akpa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why do my cabbage leaves get full of tiny holes shortly after I transplant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Beni mikɛ mihe wo mli lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ?

english: Tiny holes are made by small caterpillars or beetles feeding on young leaves. Checking under the leaves regularly and applying diluted neem seed oil acts as a natural spray to protect the leaves.
ga: Buji bibii lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ amli. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi daa ni kɛ okɛ neem dumɔwui amli fɔ ni ajie lɛ awo mli lɛ baatsu nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants lose their flowers without growing any tomatoes when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛduuu tomato ko kwraa kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains can knock off delicate blossoms or create high humidity that causes flower rot. Staking tomato plants and planting on raised beds improves air movement and protects the flowers.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ afee mlɛo loo eha hulutsoo ni fa babaoo aba ni eha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo. Tomato tsei ni akɛwoɔ tso mli ni aduɔ yɛ saatsoi ni awo nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ebuɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my pepper plants while they are small instead of waiting until they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Pepper tsei be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ kɛyashi ebaada?

english: Weeds compete directly with young crop roots for water, fertilizer, and sunlight. Clearing weeds early ensures your pepper plants get all the nutrients they need to produce abundant fruit.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii shishifãi yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hulu la. Enɛ baaha o-pepper tsei lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that produce food through leaves exposed to sunlight. Staking keeps leaves spread out toward the sun and off the damp ground, reducing leaf rot and boosting tuber size.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii kɛtsɔɔ baai ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Staking haa baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa hulu lɛ mli kɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ asɛɛ. Ehaa baai ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi ni ehaa yitso lɛ dalɛ yaa hiɛ

english: Why do my crop seedlings wither and die when I water them in the middle of a hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo amɛmli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Watering under intense sun causes water to evaporate rapidly before reaching deep roots and can shock hot roots. Watering early in the morning or late afternoon allows soil to soak up moisture safely.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya dani eshɛɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ ahe, ni ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi ni mli edɔ lɛ akpokpo. Kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu leebi loo shwane mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do some plantain suckers take over a year to bear fruit while others produce much faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei komɛi aheɔ nɔ ni fe afi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni henɔi komɛi woɔ yibii oya kwraa lɛ?

english: Using old, diseased, or oversized suckers slows down establishment. Selecting healthy, medium-sized 'maiden' suckers with vibrant roots helps plantains establish fast and bear fruit sooner.
ga: Suckers ni egbɔ, ni hela emɔ amɛ, loo ni da fe nine ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha shishitoo lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. ‘Gbekɛ yoo’ tsei ni dalɛ ji mlɛbo, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ wala mli lɛ halamɔ yeɔ ebuaa plantains ni etswaa shi oya ni ewoɔ yibii oya.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive roots and cannot handle direct sunlight or hot dry winds. Planting shade crops like plantain alongside them shields the young cocoa leaves from scorching and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa roots grow deep enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ, ebaabu kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi kookoo shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa.

english: If I plant oil palm on my land this year, how long will I wait before I start harvesting the fruits?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu mu tso yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi nɛɛ Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani mabɔi ŋmaakpamɔ?

english: Improved varieties of oil palm usually take about 3 to 4 years after field planting to produce their first harvestable fruit bunches. After that initial growth period, the trees will continue producing fruits for over 25 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mu tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 yɛ be mli ni adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ dani amɛnáa amɛklɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaa. Yɛ shishijee dalɛ be lɛ sɛɛ Tso lɛ baaya nɔ awo yibii nɔ ni fe afii 25.

english: The very first rain of the season is often followed by a heatwave or a sudden dry break. If seeds germinate during this dry gap, the tender shoots will dry up and die due to lack of steady soil moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ loo nugbɔshiimɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni bɛ daa lɛ hewɔ.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize is a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil or excessive waterlogging that stops roots from breathing. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea helps the plant regain its green color and growth strength.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo ni miiha shishifãi lɛ miigbɔjɔ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa amɛhe su eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off without turning into small peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper bibii lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plants face stress such as extreme heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently moist during flowering helps the blossoms stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ kɛ haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ kpe. loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fũɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do you advise me to cut off some of the extra suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okɛɔ akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ ekomɛi? Mi plantain baai titri lɛ.

english: When too many suckers grow around one plantain stem, they fight with the main plant for water and nutrients, resulting in small bunches. Leaving only two or three strong suckers ensures large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ ehe Plantain kome Amɛkɛ tsei ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kui bibii lɛ amligbalamɔ. Kɛ́ ashi tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha plantain lɛ afee agbo ni etsii.

english: Yam plants use their leaves to catch sunlight and produce food that gets stored in the underground tuber. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they get maximum sunlight, leading to larger and heavier yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛbaai lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛhe hulu la ni amɛfee niyenii ni akɛtoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaha baai lɛ akaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves of the plant naturally turn yellow and drop off, the base of the stem thickens, and small cracks appear in the soil around the plant stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ shishigbɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛ Ejeɔ kpo yɛ sũ ni bɔle tsei ahe lɛ mli.

english: Why does planting cowpea or groundnuts together with my main crop improve my soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ duɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpea and groundnuts have beneficial bacteria in their roots that take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which acts as a natural fertilizer for other crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa tsei krokomɛi.

english: Weeds grow much faster than domestic crops and aggressively steal the added fertilizer, water, and sunlight before your crops can absorb them, leaving your main plants weak and hungry.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi, nu kɛ hulu la dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, otsei titrii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni hɔmɔ baaye amɛ.

english: Officer, is it really necessary for me to level my farmland before planting, or can I just plant on uneven ground?
ga: Officer Ani ehe miihia ni afee he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ dani adu nii? Aloo abaanyɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ etseee nɔ?

english: Leveling uneven ground helps rainwater spread balanced across your farm so water does not gather in low spots to rot your crop roots while leaving crops on high ground thirsty.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ooofee lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. No hewɔ lɛ nu lɛ ebuaaa ehe naa yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ koni efite otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ be mli ni eshiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kɛ kumai.

english: Why does heavy rain keep washing away my topsoil and sweeping away my young seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ mi tsei bibii lɛ tee lɛ?

english: Sloped or bare soil allows rainwater to rush downhill quickly. Planting across slopes or leaving cover crops slows down water runoff and keeps soil nutrients where your crop roots can reach them.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ loo nɔ ko bɛ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya kɛyaa gɔŋ lɛ shishi. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ ni ashiɔ lɛ baaha nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. ni akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ ato shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ hei ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ ayashɛ he lɛ

english: Why do some farmers put dried coconut husks around the base of their young tree crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni egbi fɔ̃ɔ tsei bibii ashishi lɛ?

english: Coconut husks act as natural mulch around tree bases. They trap water in the soil during dry spells and slowly decay over time to feed nutrients directly to the roots.
ga: Kokooŋ tso lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi. Amɛmɔɔ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli ni amɛjieɔ lɛ fiofio. Efiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli koni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ abote shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why does the soil around my crop bases crack open during the dry season, and does it hurt my plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ mli fãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ? Ni ani eeye mi tsei lɛ awui?

english: Clay soils shrink and split into cracks when moisture dries up. These cracks let hot air reach deeper roots and dry them out, but adding organic mulch helps keep the ground cool and moist.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ lɛ. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ ni ehaa amɛgbiɔ. Shi kɛ akɛ organic mulch fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: How can I tell if a piece of land will allow my crops to do well before I start planting on it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ bibioo ko baaye abua ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ dani mibɔi dumɔwui?

english: Good farming land has dark, loose soil that crumbles easily in your hand and drains excess rainwater smoothly without becoming waterlogged for days.
ga: Okwaayeli shikpɔŋ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni shwieɔ shi oya yɛ oniji amli. ni ejieɔ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ehaaa nu lɛ ahi shi gbii babaoo.

english: Officer, why do I see a round ball-like swelling at the base of some nursery tree seedlings?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ minaa bɔɔlu ko ni tamɔ bɔɔlu yɛ dumɔwui komɛi ashishi lɛ?

english: That swelling is usually a graft union where a high-yielding stem was joined onto a hardy root stock. It is a normal sign of an improved variety bred to grow strong and fruit earlier.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ fuumɔ baa ji tso ni akɛ tso ni woɔ yibii babaoo ewo shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ naa yɛ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛdara waa ni amɛwo yibii oya lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the top roots of my young tree crops showing above the ground at the trunk base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ jieɔ amɛhe kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Heavy rains can wash away topsoil or the plant was set too shallow in the ground. Covering exposed root bases with soil and organic mulch protects them from sun damage and keeps the plant stable.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ nɔ loo edu tsei ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ha shishitoo nibii ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ ahe lɛ, ebuɔ shishitoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni efiteɔ lɛ he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do crops growing near rotting plant leaves look greener and grow faster than crops on bare soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ baai ni miifite lɛ ahe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdaraa oya fe tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: decaying plant material acts like a natural sponge that holds moisture in the dirt while releasing rich food into the soil for crop roots to absorb easily.
ga: Tso mli nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli sponji, ni ehiɛɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni ejieɔ niyenii kpakpai babaoo kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ oya.

english: What will happen to my crops if I plant them too close to one another without leaving space between them?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ni mishieee gbɛ ko yɛ amɛteŋ?

english: Overcrowded crops compete against each other for sunlight, soil water, and plant food. Their leaves get tangled, stems grow thin, and overall yields drop.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ tsei niyenii kɛjɛ amɛhe. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɔjɔɔ. ni nibii fɛɛ ni afee lɛ ba shi

english: Why do my young seedlings fail to grow well when I leave the farm completely open with no shade or protective border?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ beni mishiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mibɛ ŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmeii ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ?

english: Young crops are delicate and easily damaged by harsh overhead sun, strong winds, and stray farm animals. Providing shade plants or field boundaries gives young crops the protected environment they need to settle in.
ga: Nibii bibii ni aduɔ lɛ waaa ni hulu la ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni elaaje lɛ fiteɔ amɛ oya. Tsei ni akɛwoɔ hulutsoo mli loo ŋmɔ mli husui haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ naa shihilɛ ni abuɔ he ni he hiaa amɛ kɛha shihilɛ.

english: Why should I draw a plan for my farm layout instead of just planting seeds wherever I find space?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafee gbɛjianɔtoo kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui yɛ he fɛɛ he ni gbɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Planning your farm layout ensures that every crop gets enough sunlight, air, and room for roots to expand. Placing crops strategically prevents overcrowding, reduces competition for nutrients, and makes caring for and harvesting your crops much easier.
ga: Oŋmɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo he gbɛjianɔtoo haa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ he ni sa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ adara. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa gbɔmɛi ayi obɔ fe nine. Tsɔɔmɔ akaŋshii ni kɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ he lɛ shi Ni ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ kɛ amɛkpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: How can using simple farming technologies or designs help my crops produce more food?
ga: Kɛtsɔ okwaayeli he ŋaa loo gbɛjianɔtoo ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛná niyenii babaoo?

english: Modern farm designs help you arrange crops and manage land efficiently. By organizing how water flows and where crops are placed, plants waste less energy fighting for resources and can put all their strength into growing bigger fruits and grains.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmɔ mli gbɛjianɔtoo haa onyɛɔ osaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni okwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛtsɔ bɔ ni nu hoɔ kɛ he ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo nɔ Tsei fiteee hewalɛ babaoo ni amɛkɛwuɔ amɛhaa nibii ni he hiaa lɛ. Ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ awo aduawai kɛ ŋmaa wuji ni amɛduɔ lɛ mli.

english: How do water boards or earthen ridges help keep my crops healthy during heavy rains?
ga: Te nu ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Earthen ridges and water boards slow down fast-moving rain water across your farm. This stops the top layer of rich soil from washing away and holds enough moisture in the ground for crop roots to drink slowly.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi kɛ nu ŋmeii haa nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ oya kɛtsɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu lɛ fiofio.

english: Why do the leaves on my crop plants turn yellow and rot when water stays trapped on my land for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ beni nu hiɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like people do. When water settles on the farm for too long, it chokes the roots, preventing them from absorbing food from the soil, which turns the leaves yellow and kills the plant.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni adesai feɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ Etsiɔ enaa koni ekaŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni efite tso lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in an open field without other crops around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and short roots that easily dry out under direct heat. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains beside them creates a cool canopy that protects the seedlings from the intense heat while they settle.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo la mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛgbiɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli ni aduɔ, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he beni aduɔ lɛ.

english: Can I grow cassava and maize together on the same piece of land without them damaging each other?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni amɛfiteee amɛhe?

english: Yes, planting them together works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested early, while cassava grows slowly at first. Once the maize is harvested, the cassava spreads out and uses the remaining space without competing.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa lɛ mra. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei baakwɛ̃ fiofio yɛ shishijee mli lɛ. Kɛji akpa ŋmãa lɛ agbe naa lɛ, Cassava baagbɛ eshwa ni ekɛ he ni eshwɛ lɛ atsu nii ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Will planting my maize seeds very close to each other give me a larger harvest?
ga: Ani ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛduɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ baaha maná ŋmaa babaoo?

english: No, planting seeds too close forces plants to steal food, water, and sunlight from one another. This results in thin, weak stalks with very small cobs. Giving each plant proper space yields bigger, healthier ears of corn.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aju niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa baa. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa toi lɛ adara ni ehi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some crops grow tall and strong while others right beside them stay weak and stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi daa ni amɛhe wa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ kã he amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Crops stay weak when their roots cannot reach enough nutrients or water due to hard soil, shade from bigger plants, or competition from weeds. Proper spacing and soil preparation give all plants an equal chance to thrive.
ga: Tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa hewɔ. Shade ni jɛɔ tsei wuji amli loo akaŋshii ni jɛɔ jwɛi amli Gbɛ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ he saamɔ haa tsei fɛɛ hegbɛ ni tamɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwereɔ.

english: Why do I need to dig deep mounds or raised beds before planting yam tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akumɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ loo awo saatso lɛ nɔ dani adu sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yams expand underground and need soft soil to grow large. High, soft mounds allow the tuber roots to push downward and swell without struggling against hard, packed ground.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia koni etsɔ agbo. Pile ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ haa bulb lɛ shishifãi lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans after harvesting maize make my next crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Maize draws heavy nutrients out of the ground, while leguminous crops like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and return natural fertilizer to the soil through their roots, making the earth rich again for the next crop.
ga: Abele gbalaa niyenii ni tsii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I clear my land without burning the dry bushes before planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mikɛshãaa jwɛi ni egbi lɛ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Burning destroys rich organic matter and micro-organisms in the soil that feed your plants. Clearing without burning leaves a natural mulch layer that traps moisture, suppresses weeds, and preserves soil fertility for a strong root system.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ nibii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ ni haa otsei lɛ niyenii lɛ. Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ashãaa lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. tsiɔ jwɛi anaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do I need to build high soil mounds or ridges before planting my yam tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee gɔŋ loo ŋshɔ dani madu sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose soil to expand and grow deep underground. Making big mounds loosens hard earth, improves drainage so roots do not rot, and gives the tubers space to grow long and thick.
ga: Sweet potato tubers he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛdara yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Gɔji wuji ni aaafee lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ No hewɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteee. ni ehaa yitso lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why is it better to space my maize seeds evenly instead of planting several seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaaja ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ amli pɛpɛɛpɛ moŋ fe ni aaadu babaoo lɛ? Dumɔwui ni abua naa yɛ bu kome mli.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight for sunlight, water, and soil food. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough nutrients and room to grow strong, resulting in bigger cobs and better yield.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ he ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight and heat. Fast-growing plantains provide big leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving the young cocoa plants the shade and cool soil moisture they need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: How do I choose the best cassava stems to cut for planting my new field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mafo koni mikɛdu yɛ shikpɔŋ hee nɔ?

english: Select mature, thick, and healthy stems from plants that are 8 to 18 months old and free of diseases. Thin or very young stems lack stored food energy, making it hard for them to sprout strong roots and leaves.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 18 ni hela bɛ mli lɛ ashishifãi ni eda, ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Tsoi ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa loo ni yɔɔ blɛoo waa lɛ bɛ niyenii hewalɛ ni ato. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ shishifãi kɛ baai ni wa baakwɛ̃.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow even though we are getting enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ wɔnine eshɛ nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for green growth. Applying fertilizer like NPK or well-decomposed manure early gives the plant the food foundation it needs to thrive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ ana niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when the soil lacks moisture, when temperatures get extremely hot, or when the soil lacks essential minerals like calcium. Regular watering and applying compost help the plant retain its blossoms and produce fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ Aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why should I not plant maize on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil and stops pests from settling in.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ bii. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsake ŋmeii lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ebaatsi ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds lower my crop yield even if I apply fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops. Removing weeds during the early weeks ensures your crops get all the nutrients to establish a good foundation.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ana niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛma shishitoo kpakpa.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the inner leaves of my growing maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ amli baai lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that targets the soft growing centers of young maize plants. Catching them early with recommended neem treatments or biological pesticides prevents them from destroying the growing tip.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni gbeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ adalɛ hei lɛ. Amɔmɔ amɛ mra Kɛtsɔ neem tsofafeemɔ loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ nɔ lɛ ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when there are no big trees or plantains around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni tsei ni eda loo plantains bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under full, direct sunlight. Plantains or shade trees act as living umbrellas, providing the cool shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ haa.

english: Maize plants curl their leaves to protect themselves from losing water. By rolling the leaf inward, less leaf surface is exposed to the hot sun, which helps the plant hold onto moisture until the day cools down.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni nu akafite. Kɛ́ okɛ baai lɛ shwie mli lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ anɔ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashɛ shi lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edɔɔ.

english: Why does my cassava plant drop almost all of its leaves during the long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells to stop water from evaporating through the foliage. The plant goes into a resting state, surviving on the food stored in its underground roots until the rain returns.
ga: Akɛ ŋmei baa shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni nu akatsɔ baai lɛ amli kɛho. Tso lɛ baabote shihilɛ ko ni bɛ mli mli. Ekɛ ehe fɔɔ niyenii ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and greener than my crops even when I haven't added any fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? Ni mikɛ fɔmɔ wooo mli kwraa?

english: Wild weeds are naturally adapted to local conditions and have very aggressive root systems. They quickly drink up water and steal soil nutrients before your planted crops can take root and grow.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli, ni amɛyɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei waa. Amɛnuɔ nu oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani otso lɛ baanyɛ atswa shishifãi ni eda.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing plenty of bright yellow flowers, but the flowers just dry up and fall off without making tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when it gets too hot or when water supply changes suddenly. If temperature levels are too high or insects are not visiting to transfer pollen, the plant sheds the unfertilized flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tsake trukaa. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kooloi baaa koni amɛbabua fɔfɔi lɛ anaa lɛ, Tso lɛ baajie fɔfɔi ni afɔɔɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my maize crops produce very small cobs when I plant the seeds close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Because no single plant gets enough food, they all end up weak with small cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. No hewɔ lɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in cold, very wet, and shaded environments. Raindrops splash the tiny fungus spores from infected pods or soil onto healthy pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ waa, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ fungal spores bibii anɔ. kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛtee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants shrinking, curling upward, and looking twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbɔjɔ, amɛmiibɔle amɛhe, ni amɛmiifee tamɔ mɛi ni efite lɛ?

english: Curled and twisted leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from young shoots. This sap loss distorts leaf growth as the plant develops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ nu ni laajeɔ nɛɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ beni tso lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to manufacture food for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground where they get good sun exposure and stay free from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ tsei ahe tsei kɛjɛɔ he ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ bɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans make the soil better for the maize I plant in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans belong to the legume family, which works with beneficial soil bacteria to trap nitrogen from the air into the ground. This leaves natural fertilizer in the soil that feeds the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛkɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛmɔmɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii lɛ nɔ.

english: What is causing small holes in my maize leaves and sawdust-like dirt inside the stalks?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ mli?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which eats young maize leaves and stems. Detecting them early and using safe insecticides or recommended natural remedies like neem leaf extracts can save your farm yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooona amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni ajieɔ yi tamɔ neem baa mli nu lɛ atsu nii. Obaanyɛ okɛ oŋmɔ mli nibii lɛ ato.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and stopping the fruits from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa aduawai lɛ adalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites, or a virus they transmit. Controlling these insects early with insecticidal soap or recommended sprays prevents the virus from spreading and damaging your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛji akɛ okɛ samla loo spray ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ni efite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How can I prevent small insects from turning my harvested maize into powder during storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkatsɔ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ nɔ amɛfee powda yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Insects like grain weevils attack maize if it is stored with moisture. Make sure your maize is fully dried in the sun before storing, and keep it in airtight bags (like PICS bags) or clean containers to suffocate any pests.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmaa ŋmeii baatutua ŋmãa kɛji akɛ aha ehiɛ edɔ. Kwɛmɔ akɛ o-corn lɛ egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani okɛto. Ni okɛto kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli (tamɔ PICS kotoku) loo nɔ ko ni mli tse mli koni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akamu.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and getting scorched?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiitso lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that burn easily under full sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains beside young cocoa acts like a living umbrella, protecting them from heat while their roots develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ kookoo tsei bibii ni aduɔ lɛ, tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni hiɛ ka. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Is it really necessary for me to put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mikɛ tso ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yes, staking lifts yam leaves off the ground so they get full sunlight. Sunlight helps the leaves manufacture food, which travels down to grow bigger and healthier tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, staking baajie sweet potatoes lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulutsoo be fɛɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii. ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi koni eha yitso lɛ afee agbo ni ehiɛ hewalɛ

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets extremely hot or when the soil dries out completely. Covering the soil around the plant with dry leaves or straw (mulching) keeps the roots cool and retains water.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Mulching around Kɛ akɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi (mulch) ha tsei ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa nu hiɔ shi.

english: If too many suckers grow together, they fight for nutrients and water, resulting in smaller bunches. Leaving only one main plant and one strong sucker ensures your plantain bunch grows big and heavy.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo efee ekome Amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ bibioo Kɛ́ oshi tso titri kome pɛ kɛ sucker ni mli wa kome pɛ lɛ, ebaaha o-plantain kuu lɛ adara ni etsii.

english: When is the right time for me to apply fertilizer to my maize farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mawo mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Maize needs fertilizer at two main stages: first when the plants are about two weeks old to help roots and leaves grow, and again when the plants reach knee height to support large ear formation.
ga: Abɛi he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛi titrii enyɔ nɔ. Nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni esa akɛ afee ji be mli ni tsei lɛ eye aaafee otsii enyɔ koni eye ebua shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ ni amɛdara. kɛ agbɛnɛ hu beni tsei lɛ shɛɔ amɛnaji ahe koni amɛye amɛbua toi wuji afeemɔ lɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my soil better for the next season?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ aha be ni baa lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots rot after harvest, they release natural fertilizer into the soil for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tso shishifãi fite yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha odumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground if I leave them in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain creates waterlogged soil, which cuts off oxygen to the cassava roots and causes rot. Harvesting mature cassava before the peak of heavy rains protects your tubers from spoiling.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ. Kɛ́ okpa ŋmei ni eda dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu oŋmeii lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn under direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides temporary canopy shelter and preserves soil moisture, protecting young seedlings until they grow stronger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ cocoa masɛi lɛ, ebaaha ŋwɛitsu lɛ ahi shi yɛ be kukuoo mli, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko. Buu dumɔwui bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa.

english: Yellowing in a V-shape starting from leaf tips indicates a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize requires high amounts of nitrogen to grow green leaves, which can be corrected by applying nitrogen-rich fertilizers like Urea or NPK early in the plant's growth.
ga: Yellow ni yɔɔ V su mli ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ naa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ebaakwɛ̃. Abaanyɛ atsake enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo NPK ni akɛbaafata he yɛ tsei lɛ adalɛ shishijee bei amli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become watery and woody if I leave them in the soil for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu kɛ tsei kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava stays in the ground past maturity or after heavy rains, the plant converts stored starch back into water and plant fiber to grow new leaves, making the roots hard, stringy, and unpleasant to eat.
ga: Beni ŋmei yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa kwraa loo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ. Tso lɛ tsakeɔ starch ni ato lɛ ekoŋŋ ewoɔ nu mli kɛ tso lɛ mli tsɔji ni ekɛfeɔ baai heei, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo, amɛhe wa ni amɛhiɛ kpaaa nɔ.

english: Should I cut off the small shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ he Ani ajie mi plantain shishifãi lɛ?

english: Yes, leaving too many young shoots (suckers) creates competition for water and nutrients. Keeping only one main plant and one strong sucker per stand ensures the plant gets enough nourishment to produce large plantain bunches.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) babaoo ni ajieɔ lɛ kɛ akaŋshii baa kɛha nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Tso titri kome pɛ kɛ sucker ni mli wa kome pɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ shidaamɔhe fɛɛ shidaamɔhe lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo plantains wuji.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of calcium and phosphorus. Keeping the soil consistently moist and applying mulch helps moderate soil temperature and keep flowers attached.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo calcium kɛ phosphorus ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli latsaa lɛ afee nɔ ni sa ni eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ he.

english: Upward curling in pepper leaves is typically caused by tiny insects like thrips, mites, or aphids feeding on the sap and spreading viruses. Controlling these pests early with suitable treatments stops the leaves from contorting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, mites, loo aphids ni yeɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛji akɛ atsa amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa baa lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly in high humidity and cool shade. Pruning excess branches to improve airflow and regularly harvesting infected pods prevents the fungus from spreading across the farm.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya mli jogbaŋŋ, ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves into the sunlight so they can make food for underground tuber growth, while keeping the leaves off damp soil where fungal diseases easily infect and weaken the vine.
ga: Akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ woɔ tso mli koni amɛgbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni akɛfee niyenii kɛha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ adalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ, he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baanyɛ atswa wain tso lɛ oya ni eha egbɔjɔ lɛ.

english: What is eating small ragged holes into the leaves at the center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ni ayeɔ lɛ he?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that burrow into the central funnel of maize plants. Applying targeted biopesticides or recommended treatments directly into the center whorl early in the morning destroys the pests.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni akwɛɔ nɔ loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ wo jɛmɛ tɛ̃ɛ leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaakpata kooloi lɛ ahiɛ.

english: How can I store my cassava stems after harvesting so they stay fresh for planting?
ga: Kɛ́ okpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, te ooofee tɛŋŋ okɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ato koni amɛhi shi ehee kɛha dumɔ?

english: Cassava stems should be stored upright in a cool, heavily shaded area with their lower ends resting on moist soil. This keeps the stems alive and prevents them from drying out until you cut and plant them.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ cassava tsei lɛ ato shi shiŋŋ yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni shade yɔɔ. ni shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ kã shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ, ni ebaaha amɛkagbi kɛyashi obaafolɔ amɛ ni odu amɛ.

english: People say plants make their own food, but I feed them fertilizer. How do my crops actually feed themselves?
ga: Mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsei feɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii. Shi mikɛ amɛ woɔ fɔmɔ kotoku mli. Te miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛhe amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Plants use sunlight like a cooking fire to mix water from the soil and air around their leaves to produce their own food (sugars). Fertilizer is not the main food itself, but acts like essential provisions or vitamins that help the crop build strong leaves and roots to make that food easily.
ga: Tsei kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii tamɔ la ni akɛhooɔ nii kɛfutuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Baai koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfee niyenii (sugar). Fertilizer jeee niyenii ni he hiaa waa. Mohu ɔ, e tsuɔ ní kaa niye ní nɛ he hia loo vitamin nɛ yeɔ bua tsehi nɛ a peeɔ baai kɛ sisi nɛ mi wa konɛ a pee niye ní mlɛo.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and dull when the weather stays cloudy and dark for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ewo atatu ni ewo atatu gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves need direct sunlight to manufacture their food and maintain their rich green color. When it stays cloudy for a long time, the plant cannot cook enough food for itself, causing the leaves to lose their dark green shade.
ga: Hulu la he miihia cassava baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni amɛhiɛ amɛ su eŋɔli ni yeɔ emuu lɛ mli. Kɛji atatu eba be kakadaŋŋ lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ ahoo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Ehaa baai lɛ ahe su ni ji eŋɔli ni tsuɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin when I plant them too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa beni miduɔ amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When maize plants are crowded, they fight for sunlight to make their food. Each plant stretches upward as fast as it can to reach the light above its neighbors, which results in tall, weak stems instead of thick, sturdy ones.
ga: Beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛyeɔ hulu la he akaŋ koni amɛfee niyenii. Tso fɛɛ tso shwieɔ ehe kɛyaa ŋwɛi oya bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ená hegbɛ ni ekɛ ehe awo ekutsoŋbii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ baa yɛ tsei ni mli tse ni wa lɛ najiaŋ.

english: What happens inside the soil when I add animal manure to my vegetable beds?
ga: Mɛni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ mikɛ kooloi ashishifã fata mi aduawai aŋmɔ lɛ he?

english: Manure breaks down into essential provisions like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. These nutrients mix into the soil, creating a rich meal that plant roots can absorb to support healthy crop growth.
ga: Ajaraa ŋmɔshi nibii amli awoɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ naitrɔjin, fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium mli. Akɛ niyenii mli nibii nɛɛ futuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa niyenii babaoo ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ aŋɔ koni eye ebua tsei lɛ adalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: Why do my crops stop growing well even when I give them plenty of water every single day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekpaa shweremɔ jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu babaoo daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Water carries nutrients through the plant, but water alone is not food. If the soil lacks minerals and nutrients, the plant is drinking on an empty stomach and cannot build new leaves, branches, or fruit.
ga: Nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa kɛtsɔɔ tsei anɔ. Shi nu pɛ jeee niyenii. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ minerals kɛ nutrients Tsei lɛ nuɔ nu kɛ musu ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo baai, niji, loo aduawai heei.

english: In extreme afternoon heat, pepper leaves lose water faster than the roots can drink it. Curling up reduces the leaf surface exposed to the sun to save water, and the plant usually recovers once the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Ni aaawo nɔ lɛ haa hulu la ni baa baa lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi koni ekɛbu nu he. Ni tsei lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ gbɛkɛ mli fɛ̃i ba.

english: Why do my yam vines automatically wrap around and climb up any stick or tree nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ ebɔle mihe lɛ? ni ekwɔɔ tsei niji loo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ

english: Yam vines naturally climb upward to reach higher places where there is more sun. By spreading their leaves high on a stake, they catch maximum light to cook food, which is then stored underground to make large tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛyashɛ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ ni hulu la babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ tso ko nɔ lɛ nɔ Amɛheɔ la ni fe fɛɛ kɛji amɛmiihoo nii. ni no sɛɛ lɛ akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni efee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without making any tomatoes when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When temperatures get extremely high, the heat damages the flower pollen and stresses the plant. To save its energy and survive, the tomato plant lets the flowers fall off until the weather cools down to safer conditions.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, hulutsoo be lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni ehaa tso lɛ haoɔ. Bɔni afee ni Tomato tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi lɛ, no lɛ amɛhaa amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ kɛyaa shihilɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees shed many of their leaves right when the dry Harmattan season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ baai babaoo yɛ harmattan be ni hɔmɔ baa lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: During the Harmattan, water becomes very scarce in the soil and air. Cocoa trees drop some of their leaves on purpose to reduce water loss, helping the tree survive the dry period until the rains return.
ga: Yɛ harmattan beaŋ Nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ baafee nɔ ni faaa kwraa. Cacao tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ekomɛi ashwieɔ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds always seem to grow faster and greener than the main crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ fe ŋmɔshi nibii titri ni miduɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with aggressive roots that quickly grab water, sun, and soil provisions before your crops can. Because they steal these inputs early, they grow faster unless you clear them out.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ oya dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Ejaakɛ amɛjuɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli nɛɛ mra. No hewɔ lɛ amɛdaraa oya ja ojie amɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow while the top leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow strong. The plant moves nitrogen from its older leaves to nourish the newer leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in a field clear of trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni midu yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under full sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains to act as natural umbrellas to keep them cool and retain soil moisture during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains koni amɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo koni amɛha tsei lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Cassava tubers rot when water settles around the roots for too long due to heavy rain and poor soil drainage. Waterlogged soil prevents the roots from breathing, causing fungi to break down the tubers underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become excessively hot or when the plant experiences drought stress. Without sufficient water and mild temperatures, the flowers cannot convert into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ na hɔmɔ he haomɔ. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ hulutsoo be ni esaaa lɛ bɛ lɛ, anyɛɛɛ atsake fɔfɔi lɛ afee aduawai.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to feed the tubers growing below ground. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet soil, catching more sunlight and preventing leaves from rotting on the damp earth.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ ajɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Egbalaa hulu la babaoo ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is typically caused by tiny pests like thrips or aphids hiding under the leaves. They suck out the plant's juices, causing the young leaves to distort and stop growing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Amɛmuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei amli. Enɛ haa baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaaa amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the branch during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in cold, wet, and dark conditions. Heavy rain sprays the fungus spores onto the pods, which causes them to rot quickly if trees are not pruned to let sunlight through.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ duŋ shihilɛi amli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii amli ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha amɛgboi oya kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ tsei lɛ anɔ koni hulu la atsɔ mli.

english: Why do my groundnut plants push their flowers back down into the dirt after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ tsiɔ efɔfɔi lɛ ekoŋŋ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni ewo fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Groundnuts naturally develop their pods underground. Once the flower is pollinated above ground, the stalk grows downward into the soil where the nut can safely form into a hard shell away from hot sun and surface pests.
ga: Peanuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔii lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ shishifã lɛ baakwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nuts lɛ baanyɛ afee ŋmei ni wa shweshweeshwe. Ekɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛ ŋwɛi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akabɔ he.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over so easily when the fruit bunch gets big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Plantains do not have deep taproots to anchor them securely in the ground. The heavy weight of a growing fruit bunch makes the plant top-heavy, causing wind or loose soil to pull the shallow roots out of the dirt.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni baaha amɛfi shikpɔŋ lɛ shi shiŋŋ. Yibii akui ni miida lɛ amli tsiimɔ ni tsii lɛ haa tso lɛ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni etse ehe lɛ gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize plants stay small and thin when I sow many seeds in one small hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu bibioo kome mli lɛ?

english: When too many seeds grow close together, their roots fight over the limited water, fertilizer, and sunlight in that single spot. Spacing seeds out ensures each plant gets enough food to grow thick and tall.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la fioo ni yɔɔ nakai he kome lɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and drop their flowers when the afternoon sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ shwane hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants, causing water to evaporate faster than the roots can pull it from the soil. This heat stress forces the plant to drop its blossoms to save energy and protect itself.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ nɛɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn brown and look burnt during long dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni etamɔ nɔ ni eshã yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: When the sun is intense and water is scarce, crop leaves lose moisture rapidly. Without enough ground water to cool the plant down, leaf edges dry out and scorch under direct sunlight.
ga: Beni hulu lɛ mli wa ni nu babaoo bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ. Tso baai lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya. Kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tsei lɛ afee fɛ̃i lɛ bɛ lɛ, Baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa kɛji akɛ hulu la lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the base of my crops protect them from heat?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mi tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, acts as a blanket that blocks direct sunlight, keeps the soil cool, and stops soil water from evaporating quickly.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni tsiɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya

english: Why do my crop roots rot when heavy rains flood the field for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ashishifãi fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eyi ŋmɔji amli gbii babaoo lɛ?
