english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When standing water fills all the small air spaces in the soil for too long, the roots suffocate and rot.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ eyi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaagboi.

english: Why do my young seedlings wash away or break during heavy downpours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ hoɔ loo amɛkuɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have shallow roots and weak stems that cannot withstand the physical force of heavy rain droplets and flowing surface water, which easily unearths them.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni eshishifã lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛɛɛ adamɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi ni tsii kɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni anyɛɔ atsaa oya lɛ naa.

english: Why is growing tomatoes much harder and more risky than growing cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato dumɔ wa waa ni eyɛ oshara fe ŋmei dumɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes are delicate crops that react quickly to pest attacks, bad weather, and diseases, whereas cassava is a hardy root crop that can endure poor soil and dry conditions with less care.
ga: Tomato ji tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutua amɛ lɛ, amɛtsuɔ nii oya. kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa kɛ helai, yɛ be mli ni ŋmei ji tso ko ni shishifãi ni wa yɔɔ mli ni baanyɛ aŋmɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my harvested vegetables spoil so fast if I leave them in the sun at the farm gate?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ shinaa lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Once harvested, vegetables can no longer draw water from the soil. Direct sun heat speeds up their internal breakdown and causes rapid water loss, leading to soft, spoiled produce.
ga: Kɛji akpa Aduawai lɛ nyɛŋ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔŋŋ. Dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa mligbɛ fitemɔ yaa oya ni ehaa nu lɛ fiteɔ oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nibii ni aduɔ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni egboɔ.

english: How can I use my mobile phone to know the best time to plant my seeds before the rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ mi-mobail foŋ lɛ atsu nii koni male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ madu dumɔwui dani nugbɔ anɛ?

english: You can sign up for agricultural SMS or voice message services that send daily local weather forecasts and expert planting alerts directly to your phone.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ohe awo okwaayeli he SMS loo gbee mli nitsumɔ ni kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he adafitswaa ni kɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli daa gbi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nilelɔi ahe kɔkɔbɔɔ majeɔ otɛlifoŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli.

english: How can sending photos of my sick crops through a phone help me treat them?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ahe mfonirii ni mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ tɛlifoŋ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni mahere amɛyiwala?

english: Extension officers can look at clear photos of damaged leaves or stems on their phones to quickly identify the specific pest or disease and text you the right treatment.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ nitsumɔhe lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ baai loo tsei ni efite lɛ ahe mfonirii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ yɛ amɛfoni nɔ. Koni oyoo tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai pɔtɛɛ komɛi oya ni okɛ shɛɛ sane ko amaje bo yɛ tsofafeemɔ ni ja lɛ he.

english: When crops get too much nitrogen from soil or fertilizer, they put all their energy into growing stems and leaves instead of developing strong flowers and fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Mohu ɔ, a peeɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yiblii nɛ ngɛ he wami.

english: Why should I carefully space my maize seeds in rows instead of just scattering them in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-abɛi lɛ ato ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: When seeds are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants with tiny cobs. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow strong and produce big, healthy ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ewo ŋmãa toi wuji ni mli wa.

english: Yam vines naturally want to reach up toward the sun to get light for making food. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, which prevents leaf rot diseases and helps the plant direct its energy into growing large tubers underground.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, sweet potato wain tsei lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛshɛ ŋwɛi kɛya hulu lɛ he koni amɛná la kɛha amɛ nihoomɔ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaatsiɔ baai lɛ anaa, ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast with broad leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa trees need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why is it important for me to trim off some of the extra branches on my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine yɛ kookoo tso nɔ lɛ?

english: Cutting away unnecessary or dead branches allows sunlight and air to flow through the tree canopy. This keeps dampness away, which stops black pod disease from spreading and encourages the tree to produce more pods.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa loo ni egboi ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko. Enɛ haa black pod hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ kpaa, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ pods babaoo awo.

english: Covering the soil with dried leaves or grass (mulching) keeps the hot sun from drying out the earth too quickly. It holds water in the soil longer and prevents weeds from popping up and stealing food from your plants.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkaje kpo ni amɛju niyenii kɛjɛ otsei lɛ amli.

english: Dropping leaves is a normal defense trick cassava uses to save water when rain is scarce. By shedding leaves, the plant loses less water through evaporation, keeping its underground roots alive until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni yucca kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛbu nu he kɛ́ nugbɔ faaa. Kɛji baai lɛ gbee shi lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu fioo kɛyaa hulutsoo be mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why do my crops grow much stronger when I mix chicken manure into the dirt before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli wa waa nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani midu lɛ?

english: Chicken manure acts as natural food for the soil, rich in nutrients like nitrogen that plants need to build strong stems and green leaves. It also helps the soil hold on to moisture much better.
ga: Kooloo ŋmei tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Niyenii nibii babaoo yɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hu ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell me to plant beans together in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ afee ekome kɛdu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special plants that pull natural fertilizer directly from the air and store it in their roots. Planting them near maize feeds the soil naturally, making the maize grow better without buying as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli.

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which lay eggs on young maize leaves because the soft inner shoot is easy for young worms to eat. Spotting them early allows you to use simple remedies like ash or safe sprays before they destroy the whole stalk.
ga: Ekolɛ Fall Armyworms ji enɛɛmɛi, ni amɛwoɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii anɔ ejaakɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ yeɔ amɛ mlɛo. Amɛtaomɔ mra Enɛ baaha okɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ sũ loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe atsu nii. Dani amɛbaakpãtã tso lɛ shishi muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ

english: Why do my garden eggs and pepper plants rot at the roots when there is heavy rain for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii tsei lɛ fiteɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: When heavy rain stays pooled around the roots without draining away, the plant roots drown because they cannot breathe. Too much trapped water causes fungi in the dirt to attack and rot the roots.
ga: Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa buaa ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni nu ejeee kpo lɛ. Tsei shishifãi lɛ baagbo ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu. Nu ni emɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when I leave them in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mishi amɛ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very delicate leaves that burn easily under direct heat. They need artificial shade or shade trees above them to keep the leaves cool and conserve soil moisture while their roots are still developing.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni shãa oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo loo hulutsoo tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ koni amɛha tsei lɛ ahe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do my older cocoa trees stop producing as many pods after twenty or thirty years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei ni edara lɛ kpaɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ afii nyɔŋmai enyɔ loo nyɔŋmai etɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age, their root systems become less efficient at taking up nutrients from the soil, and the wood becomes more vulnerable to diseases, causing pod yields to naturally decline unless pruned and fertilized regularly.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ eda lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ hu baafee nɔ ni esaaa akɛ amɛheɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni helai baanyɛ aba tso lɛ nɔ babaoo. Enɛ haa pod yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ja akwɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa ni awoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do the leaves of my plantain trees curl up tightly during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves curl up during hot, dry weather to reduce the leaf surface exposed to the sun. This is a natural behavior that helps the plant conserve internal moisture until water becomes available again.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni egbi lɛ mli koni eha hulu la ni baa baa lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli subaŋ ko ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nu baa ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know when my yam tubers are fully mature and ready to be harvested from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-sweet potato tubers lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yams are mature when the leaves and vines above ground naturally turn yellow and dry up, which signals that the plant has finished transferring its energy down into the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning light green or yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow or pale leaves usually mean your maize plants are missing nitrogen, a crucial nutrient in the soil that helps the plant make food and grow strong green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ni etsake lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tso lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii ni amɛhaa amɛbaai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli kɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my pepper plants without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or lack of water in the soil, causing the plant to abort fruit production to survive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei kpaɔ yibiiwoo bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why does spear grass keep coming back on my farm even after I clear it completely with my cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akpɔlɔ jwɛi lɛ yaa nɔ ekuɔ esɛɛ ebaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛ mikɛ dade jie fɛɛ po?

english: Spear grass stores energy in strong stem roots hidden deep underground, so cutting the visible leaves leaves the underground roots alive and ready to grow new shoots immediately.
ga: Spear jwɛi lɛ toɔ hewalɛ yɛ eshishifãi ni wa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ afo baai ni anaa lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: How can I make sure my cassava plants grow large tubers that will bring good money at the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni mi-cassava tsei lɛ aná ŋmeii wuji ni baaha maná shika kpakpa yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Cassava plants need loose, well-drained soil so the roots can expand easily, along with regular weeding during the first three months so the crop doesn't have to fight for nutrients.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo Agbɛnɛ hu, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ daa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ lɛ amli. Bɔni afee ni ehe akahia ni tsei lɛ awuu kɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Planting maize too close forces the stalks to fight for sunlight, water, and nutrients, resulting in thin stalks with tiny or empty cobs instead of healthy, heavy yields.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. loo efolo Moŋ lɛ, eji nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni tsii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes on the exact same piece of land where I harvested tomatoes last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa yɛ nɔ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting tomatoes in the same soil year after year allows tomato-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground, which will attack your new plants much earlier and harder.
ga: Tomato ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ baaha tomato he kooloi bibii kɛ helai babaoo aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baatswa otsei heei lɛ oya ni etswa waa.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with very few roots when I plant them under large shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni ebɛ shishifãi fioo pɛ kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava plants need direct sunlight to perform photosynthesis and send energy down into their underground roots. When shaded by tall trees, the plant spends all its energy stretching upwards toward the light, leaving very little energy to produce thick tuberous roots.
ga: Cassava tsei he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee fotosintɛsis ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ amaje amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Beni eyɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko shishi lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛ ehe afɔ ŋwɛi kɛya la lɛ he. Hewalɛ fioo pɛ eshwɛɔ koni ekɛfee shishifãi ni mli tse.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up and droop during hot afternoons even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: During intense afternoon heat, pepper leaves lose water through evaporation faster than their roots can suck it up from the ground. Curling their leaves reduces the surface area exposed to the sun to conserve moisture until the evening cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi koni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edɔɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on young maize usually indicates a nitrogen deficiency in the soil or poor water absorption. Nitrogen gives leaves their green color, and when soil lacks this nutrient, the plant moves what little nitrogen it has to its newer top leaves, causing the bottom ones to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ. Nitrogen haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli. kɛ be mli ni niyenii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why does my farm produce smaller harvests every year even though I plant the exact same crop on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Kɛji akɛ midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ po.

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to replenish. Rotating your crops with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores vital nutrients like nitrogen back into the soil and breaks crop disease cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛwo mli ekoŋŋ. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. ni eha tsei ahe helai ni yaa nɔ lɛ aba shi

english: How do I know if the soil on my open piece of land is suitable for growing vegetable crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mihe ni migbele lɛ nɔ lɛ hi kɛha aduawai adumɔ?

english: Good vegetable soil should feel dark, soft, and moist when squeezed, crumbling easily in your hands without turning into hard clay or running like loose sand. If the soil is too hard or dry, mixing in organic material like decomposed animal manure will improve its ability to feed crops.
ga: Esa akɛ tso shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ afee ediŋŋ, bɔdɔɔ, ni edɔ kɛji akɛ ashɛre. Efoɔ oya yɛ nine mli ni etsɔɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ehoɔ tamɔ ŋã ni etse ehe. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo egbi Ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ kooloi aŋmei ni egbo futu mli lɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni akɛyeɔ abuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant maize seeds too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Planting seeds too closely causes crop plants to compete aggressively with one another for space, sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition results in thin, weak stalks and very small or empty cobs because no single plant gets enough food to develop properly.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ he tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko, hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster and stronger than my young crop seedlings after a rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants with deep root systems adapted to absorb water and nutrients immediately after rain. Young crops have smaller, tender roots that take longer to absorb food, making early and regular weeding essential so weeds do not choke out your crop.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji tso ko ni yɔɔ koo mli ni wa ni eshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ etsake amɛhe koni amɛnyɛ amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ. Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni heɔ be babaoo dani amɛmuɔ niyenii. Ha efee nɔ ni abaanyɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ mra. Ni nɔ ni afeɔ daa lɛ he miihia. Bɔni afee ni jwɛi akafite onibii.

english: Excessively high temperatures damage the pollen inside tomato blossoms, preventing proper fertilization. When flowers fail to fertilize, the plant naturally drops them to save energy rather than attempting to grow fruit without seeds.
ga: Kɛ́ latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ lɛ, ebaafite pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haaa aná fɔmɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Beni anyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔi ko fɔ lɛ Tsei baajie fɔfɔi kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni okwɛ aduawai ni dumɔwui bɛ mli lɛ

english: Which crops can I plant on my available land that will mature quickly so I can harvest food within a few months?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ ni miyɔɔ nɔ momo lɛ nɔ ni baakwɛ̃ oya bɔ ni abaanyɛ akpa niyenii yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli?

english: Short-duration vegetable crops such as okro, garden eggs, leafy greens, and cowpeas mature in 60 to 90 days. These fast crops allow you to harvest food and generate quick income while you prepare the land for longer-term crops like cassava or plantain.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ okra, abɔɔ mli ŋmeii, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai kɛ tsina ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ gbii 60 kɛyashi 90 mli. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ oya nɛɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa niyenii kɛ shika oya yɛ be mli ni osaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei.

english: Why do some cassava varieties rot in wet soil during heavy rains while other varieties survive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli, ni ekrokomɛi hu hiɔ shi lɛ?

english: Different crop varieties have different levels of resistance to waterlogging and root fungal diseases. Improved disease-resistant cassava varieties have stronger root structures that prevent water-loving fungi from attacking and rotting the tuber underground during heavy rainy seasons.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi lɛ yɛ bɔ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛ ŋmeii shishifãi helai lɛ srɔtoi. Cassava henɔi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni nyɛɔ helai anaa lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa waa ni baatsi ŋmeii ni sumɔɔ nu lɛ anaa koni amɛkatutua shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfite yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa beaŋ.

english: Why is burning my bush clearings bad for crop growth if the ash makes my maize sprout fast at first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hei ni agbele yɛ mi ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ ni ashãa lɛ ehiii kɛha tsei adalɛ lɛ? Kɛji akɛ sũ lɛ ha mi-abele lɛ kwɛ̃ oya yɛ shishijee mli

english: While ash gives a quick dose of nutrients, the heat from burning kills the helpful organisms in the dirt and destroys organic matter, leaving your soil weak and unable to hold water for future crops.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ sũ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ oya moŋ, shi Dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ shãa mli lɛ gbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ni efiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ehiɛ nu kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ wɔsɛɛ.

english: How can I protect my maize farm from bushfires during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ koo mli la he yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: You can create a firebreak by clearing a wide, weed-free strip of bare soil around your farm boundary, or by planting fire-resistant green barrier crops like cassava and plantain to block flames.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee la he ko kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni jwɛi bɛ nɔ lɛ ni oootsi kɛbɔle he lɛ nɔ. Oŋmɔ lɛ husui loo kɛtsɔ tsei eŋɔlii ni la nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ni ooodu koni okɛbu ohe kɛjɛ la he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I clear and burn my farmland late in the dry season right before rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mijieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ ni mishãa lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ naagbee, dani nugbɔ anɛ?

english: Late burning leaves the soil completely exposed and baked hard by the sun, so when the rain finally falls, it washes away topsoil instead of soaking in to feed your seeds.
ga: La ni ashãa fiofio lɛ haa hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ haa sũ lɛ mli waɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ naagbee lɛ Efoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekɛwo nu mli koni ekɛha dumɔwui lɛ niyenii.

english: How do cover crops like mucuna control weeds without me needing to burn my field?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ tamɔ mucilage lɛ akudɔ jwɛi ni eshãaa miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Cover crops grow fast and form a thick leafy carpet over your field, blocking sunlight so weed seeds cannot sprout while naturally adding nutrients into the soil.
ga: Nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ baai ni mli edɔ yɛ oŋmɔji lɛ anɔ, ni amɛtsiɔ hulu lɛ naa koni jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ akakwɛ̃ yɛ be mli ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛkɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry periods on purpose to save water; the plant stays alive underground in the roots and will sprout fresh leaves once rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Tso lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ eshishifãi amli, ni ebaawo baai heei kɛji nugbɔ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to shrivel and turn black during intense heat spells?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and lack of water put heavy stress on cocoa trees, causing young pods to dry out and die early because the tree cannot get enough moisture from the dry ground.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ kɛ haomɔ kpele baa cacao tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya ejaakɛ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines wither and die back when the hot dry winds start blowing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ tswa lɛ?

english: Hot winds pull moisture out of yam leaves faster than the roots can drink from dry soil; mulching the ground around the yam mound keeps roots cool and retains soil moisture.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ sweet potato baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ sweet potatoes ni ato lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why are my maize leaves rolling up tight into tubes during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl inward during hot afternoons to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, helping the plant conserve water until the air cools down.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do wild forest animals keep coming onto my farm to destroy my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋa nɔ lɛ miiba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ koni amɛbafite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: When nearby forests lose their natural food sources due to dry season fires or land clearing, wild animals move into crop fields searching for water and food like cassava and maize.
ga: Beni kooi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ laajeɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii yɛ la ni tsoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ lɛ hewɔ. Koolooi ni yɔɔ ŋa nɔ lɛ fãa kɛyaa ŋmɔji amli koni amɛyatao nu kɛ niyenii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei.

english: How do shade trees help my young crops survive hot weather and dry spells?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo kɛ hɔmɔ mli?

english: Shade trees keep the soil beneath them cool, trap moisture in the air, and shield sensitive young crops from direct scorching sunlight and hot drying winds.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ he.

english: Is it normal for a few seedlings on my farm to die even if most of them look healthy?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ dumɔwui komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baagboi eyɛ mli akɛ amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo tamɔ mɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Yes, losing a small percentage of seedlings is normal due to natural factors like weak seeds, minor insect damage, or transplanting shock. As long as the vast majority of your field is thriving and sickness is very low, losing one or two plants here and there is expected.
ga: Hɛɛ, eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ dumɔwui fioo komɛi baafite yɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii tamɔ dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ hewɔ. Kpluka lɛ fite nɔ ko fioo. loo shoofeemɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ mli Bei abɔ ni okpokpaa lɛ mli hei babaoo miiya hiɛ ni helai faaa kwraa lɛ. Elaaje tso kome loo enyɔ yɛ biɛ kɛ biɛ, ni no ji nɔ ni esa akɛ akpa gbɛ.

english: Leaf curling and yellow patches on cassava are usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems from the agricultural office is the best way to prevent this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmei nɔ lɛ baa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ enɛ naa.

english: Why are my maize plants light green or yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ji eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ moŋ fe eŋɔli ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowish leaves on maize are a common sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen is the nutrient that gives plants their dark green color and energy to grow, so adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure will help.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ namɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni haa tsei feɔ eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛdaraa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua.

english: Why should I leave proper space between my crops instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ ni sa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded together, their roots compete for the same soil food and water, and their leaves block sunlight from each other. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room, air, and nutrients to grow big and produce a heavy harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua tsei anaa yɛ kui amli lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. ni amɛbaai lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni etsɔ agbo ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the plant lacks sufficient water, or if there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Keeping the soil consistently moist and shading young plants can help protect the flowers so they turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo kɛji nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo aha tsei bibii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛtsɔmɔ aduawai.

english: Why do small young pods on my cocoa tree turn black and dry up before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛdaraa.

english: This can happen either from natural pod wilt, where the tree naturally discards excess pods it cannot feed, or from Black Pod disease caused by excess moisture. Pruning extra branches to let in sunshine and air helps reduce pod loss.
ga: Enɛ baanyɛ aba kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli pod wilting nɔ fɛɛ. Biɛ ji he ni tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aye niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. aloo kɛjɛ black pod hela ni hulutsoo ni fa fe nine kɛbaa lɛ mli Nibii krokomɛi ni afolɔ koni akɛha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ haa pod ni laajeɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves wilt during the hot afternoon even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: During the hottest part of the day, plants lose water from their leaves faster than their roots can drink it up from the ground. If the leaves stand back up in the cooler evening, it is just heat stress, which is normal for hot afternoons.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ te shi yɛ gbɛkɛ ni mli ejɔ lɛ mli lɛ Eji dɔlɛ he haomɔ kɛkɛ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam vines start drying up early before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔ oya dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Yam vines drying up too early is often caused by a fungal disease called anthracnose or damage to the roots by yam beetles. Keeping the field clear of weeds and using healthy seed yams helps the vines stay green until full maturity.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ni tsɛŋemɔ hela ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya tsɔ baa. Kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ ŋmɔji amli ni akɛ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua wain tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: How do I know if my crop is suffering from an insect attack or a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi loo helai etutua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Insects usually leave physical signs like holes eaten into leaves, damaged stems, or visible bugs. Plant diseases usually cause color changes like brown spots, white powder on leaves, rotting roots, or complete wilting without any bite marks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii shiɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii, tamɔ bu ni baai yeɔ, tsei ni efite, loo kooloi bibii ni anaa. Bei pii lɛ, tsei ahe helai haa amɛhe su tsakeɔ, tamɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, powda yɛŋ ni yɔɔ baai anɔ, kɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ. loo egbo kwraa ni ŋmei ko bɛ he.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops if I do not clear them early?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji mijieee amɛ mra?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal sunlight, water, and soil fertilizers meant for your crops. They also act as homes for insect pests and crop diseases that can spread and destroy your harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii. ni ekɛ ekãa juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ. Amɛtsuɔ nii hu akɛ shia kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ tsei ahe helai ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni efite onibii.

english: How long does it usually take for a newly planted orange tree to start producing fruit?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Grafted orange trees usually start producing fruit within 3 to 4 years after planting, whereas trees grown directly from seeds can take up to 7 to 10 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, citrus tsei ni akɛwo mli lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli beni adu amɛ sɛɛ. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni jɛɔ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 7 kɛyashi 10.

english: Why do some farmers cut off the small side branches from their fruit trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi shwieɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? Shi aduawai tso lɛ?

english: Cutting off weak or extra branches, known as pruning, allows the tree to direct its energy, water, and soil nutrients into growing bigger and healthier fruit.
ga: Niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ niji ni afolɔ. Ehaa tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛwo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell if my orange trees are being damaged by insects or diseases?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmeii loo helai efite mi-citrus tso lɛ?

english: Common signs of pest or disease damage include leaves curling up, dark spots on the skin of the fruit, yellowing leaves, or fruit falling off before it is fully ripe.
ga: Nɔ ni afɔɔ naa yɛ okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai efite lɛ ekomɛi ji baai ni ebɔle ehe, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ yɛ aduawai lɛ anɔ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, loo aduawai ni shwieɔ shi dani eshɛɔ kwraa.

english: What is a planter machine, and how can it help me on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji dumɔ nii? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua mi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: A planter machine is an equipment that drops seeds into the ground at equal distances and correct depths automatically, saving you time and labor compared to planting manually with a hoe.
ga: Dumɔwui ji tsɔne ko ni duɔ dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ yeɔ egbɔ, ni ekɛ ehe saa bɔ ni mli kwɔ ha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Ekɛ be kɛ nitsumɔ baa shi kɛ akɛto nine ni akɛ ŋmei duɔ lɛ he.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stems and a poor harvest.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni akpaaa nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Maize leaves usually turn yellow when the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or when the roots are getting too much or too little water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ ná nu babaoo loo fioo pɛ.

english: Why do flowers drop off my pepper plants before they turn into actual pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛmiitsɔ pepper aduawai diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off prematurely when the plant experiences stress, which is often caused by extreme heat, irregular watering, or attacks from small insects.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ haomɔ kpe. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi bibii ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ

english: Why is it necessary for me to clear all weeds from my land before sowing seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu nii lɛ?

english: Weeds grow very fast and steal moisture, fertilizer, and sunlight away from young seedlings, so clearing them early gives your seeds the best environment to grow.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, mra be mli ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná shihilɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How often should I water my crop seedlings during the dry season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo mi tso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Young crop seedlings need light watering twice a day—early in the morning and late in the afternoon—to keep the topsoil moist without drowning the delicate roots.
ga: Ehe miihia ni afɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ anɔ nu fioo shii enyɔ daa gbi. Leebi kɛ shwane Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ shwieee nu mli.

english: Fertilizer is best applied a few weeks after seeds sprout when the roots are strong enough to absorb nutrients, and again right before the plants start producing flowers.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli otsii 2-3 yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ beni shishifãi lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ekoŋŋ dani tsei lɛ aje fɔfɔi abɔi.

english: Yellow, curling leaves on maize usually mean the plants are lacking nitrogen in the soil or are being attacked by pests like armyworms or aphids that suck vital nutrients directly from the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ cutworms loo aphids ni shwieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ emɔ tso lɛ.

english: Is it good for me to plant cassava and cowpeas together on the same land?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaadu ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with cassava helps your farm because cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, which feeds the soil naturally while protecting the ground from drying out.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmei duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua oŋmɔ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsina ŋmei lɛ kɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to strong, direct sunlight; without shade crops like plantains or large trees to block the intense heat, their leaves dry up and their root systems fail.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo tsei wuji bɛ ni baatsi hulutsoo ni naa wa lɛ naa lɛ. Baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii.

english: How can I tell if my farm land is tired and needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ bɛ shihilɛ kpakpa mli ni ehe miihia ni awo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If your crops are growing slowly, look weak, have light green or pale leaves, or yield smaller harvests than in previous seasons, your soil has run out of essential nutrients.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo, etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ, eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo yibiiwoo ni baa shi fe nyɛsɛɛ be lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets too hot or receives irregular watering, causing the plant to enter stress mode and shed flowers to conserve its energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ adɔ tsei lɛ fe nine loo awo amɛ nu be fɛɛ be. Enɛ haa tsei yaa stress mode mli ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: What will happen if I plant my maize seeds very close together in a row?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: If seeds are planted too close, the growing crops will compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in tall, weak plants that produce tiny or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui bibii bibii. loo dumɔwui ni nɔ ko bɛ mli

english: Why do weeds make my crops suffer so badly even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii awui eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal the water, fertilizer, and soil nutrients right out from under your crops, starving your plants regardless of rain.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ ekɔɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting so quickly in my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ oya yɛ mi-shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they are cut or bruised during harvest, or if they are stored in a hot place without proper ventilation, allowing mold and fungi to grow.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ afolɔ loo atswa yɛ kpamɔ be mli. aloo kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwereɔ.

english: Why should I cut off some of the leaves and extra shoots from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni eshwɛ yɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Removing non-essential leaves and side shoots allows the plant to send its energy directly into growing larger tomatoes while improving airflow to prevent leaf diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ baai kɛ sɛɛ ŋmeii ni he ehiaaa lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa tomatoi wuji ni miida lɛ amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ koni akafoli helai aba.

english: Why should I buy fresh certified seeds instead of saving seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato?

english: Saved seeds lose their strength and disease resistance over time, whereas certified seeds are specifically bred to resist local pests and produce higher yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ hewalɛ kɛ helai ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds from around my oil palm trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mu tsei ni akwɛɔ daa lɛ he hiaa mi.

english: Weeds compete directly with your palm trees for groundwater, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds away ensures your young trees get all the nourishment they need to grow strong and produce good fruit.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ o-palm tsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Jwɛi ni ooojie lɛ haa otsei bibii lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Does keeping my farm clear of tall weeds help prevent insect attacks on my palm trees?
ga: Ani jwɛi kakadaji ni mikɛhaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi bibii baatutuaa mi-palm tsei lɛ?

english: Yes, tall weeds and bushes serve as hiding spots and breeding grounds for harmful insects. Keeping your farm neatly weeded destroys their homes and makes it harder for pests to multiply and attack your trees.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi kakadaji kɛ tsei bibii tsuɔ nii akɛ he ni kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ teɔ shi amɛwoɔ amɛhe kɛ amɛfɔmɔhei. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaakpata amɛshia lɛ hiɛ. Ni ehaa ewaa kɛhaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akɛ amɛbaafɔ ni amɛtutua otsei lɛ.

english: What signs should I look for when walking around my farm to know if pests are eating my palm trees?
ga: Mɛɛ okadii esa akɛ makwɛ kɛ́ miiya he fɛɛ he? ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mana kɛji kooloi komɛi miiye mi-palm tsei lɛ.

english: Look for chewed or ragged leaf edges, holes in the fronds, sawdust-like powder near the base of the leaves, or yellowing foliage, which all indicate that insects are feeding on your tree.
ga: Taomɔ baai lɛ ahe ni atsɔ mli loo egbɛ eshwa, bu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli, sũ ni tamɔ ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ baai lɛ ashishi, loo baai ni efee ŋmɔŋ, ni enɛɛmɛi fɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii eye otso lɛ.

english: How often should I inspect my palm trees for insect damage?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ makwɛ mi-palm tso lɛ mli koni mana kɛji kooloi efite?

english: You should check your trees frequently, especially while doing routine tasks like weeding. Inspecting them regularly allows you to catch insect damage early before pests destroy the leaves or spread to other trees.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ otsei lɛ amli shii abɔ. Titri lɛ, yɛ be mli ni otsuɔ nitsumɔi ni afeɔ daa tamɔ jwɛi shwiemɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okwɛ amɛ daa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona nɔ ni kooloi bibii efite lɛ mra. Dani tsɛŋemɔ helai baafite baai lɛ loo amɛbaagbɛ amɛshwã tsei krokomɛi anɔ lɛ,.

english: How does using an insecticide spray like 'spirit' help protect my palm trees from insects?
ga: Te ‘Mumɔ’ ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu mi-palm tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Insecticide sprays act as a defense against harmful bugs by either killing them on contact or leaving a protective coat on the leaves that drives them away and stops them from eating the tree.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni tsiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa kɛtsɔ amɛgbemɔ nɔ kɛji amɛshɛ amɛhe loo kɛtsɔ atade ni buɔ mɔ he ni ashiɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ koni eshwie amɛ ni ekpa amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye tso lɛ nɔ.

english: What should I do immediately if I spot pests eating the leaves of my palm trees?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji mina kooloi ni yeɔ mi-palm lɛ baai lɛ?

english: Once you spot harmful insects, you should identify the affected trees and apply a recommended insecticide spray targeted at those pests to stop the damage before it spreads across your entire farm.
ga: Kɛji ona kooloo ko ni yɔɔ oshara Esa akɛ oyɔse tsei ni ena hela lɛ. Ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi bibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nakai kooloi bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ atsu nii ni okɛkpa nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ dani egbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my palm tree leaves turn pale or yellow, and how can fertilizer fix it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, te abaafee tɛŋŋ asaa ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Pale or yellow leaves usually mean your tree is starving for key nutrients in the soil. Adding fertilizer restores those essential food elements, helping the leaves turn dark green again so the tree can produce heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ nakai niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aba ekoŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ awo yibii ni tsii.

english: What is the correct way to apply fertilizer around my palm trees so it works effectively?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmei tsei ahe koni ená yibii kpakpai?

english: Clear a ring around the base of the tree beneath the leaf canopy, spread the fertilizer evenly in that cleared circle, and mix it light into the topsoil so the roots can absorb it easily when rain falls.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni bɔle Tso lɛ shishi lɛ he yɛ baai ashishi Gbalamɔ ŋtayaa lɛ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni agbele lɛ mli. Ni okɛfutu shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli fioo koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ mlɛo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ.

english: How can I enroll in local fertilizer support programs to get fertilizer for my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maŋma migbɛi awo maŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe yelikɛbuamɔ gbɛjianɔtoo ko mli koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: You can visit your local district agricultural office or join a registered farmers' group. Extension officers register smallholder farmers into support programs that provide access to subsidized fertilizers and training.
ga: Obaanyɛ oyasara kpokpaa nɔ okwaayeli nitsumɔhe ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ loo oyafata okwaafoi akuu ko ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo mli lɛ he. Extension officers lɛ kɛ okwaafoi bibii woɔ yelikɛbuamɔ gbɛjianɔtoi ni haa amɛnáa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛyeɔ abuaa kɛ tsɔsemɔ lɛ amli.

english: Where can a small-scale farmer like me get expert guidance when my crops are struggling?
ga: Nɛgbɛ okwaafoi bibii tamɔ mi baanyɛ ana ŋaawoo ni he esa yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: You can reach out to local agricultural extension officers who offer free farm visits, practical training, and advice on pest control, crop health, and government support schemes.
ga: Obaanyɛ oyana okpokpaa lɛ nɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ni haa ŋmɔ mli saramɔi ni aheee nɔ ko lɛ. Tsɔsemɔ ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii kɛ ŋaawoo yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ahewalɛ, kɛ maŋ yelikɛbuamɔ gbɛjianɔtoi.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny pests like thrips, mites, or whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves and spread viruses. Keeping weeds down and spraying recommended neem or insecticidal solutions early prevents this damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, mites, loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni shwieɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni egbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa Akɛ ŋaawoo ha akɛ akwɛ jwɛi lɛ anɔ mra ni akɛ neem solution loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ nɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when the heavy rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because roots need air to survive and water traps stop them from breathing. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the root zone.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia shishifãi lɛ koni amɛhi shi. kɛ nu mli tsɔnei haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe Kɛ́ aduɔ ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Giving plants consistent moisture and light shade during extremely hot days helps flowers stay attached and form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ tomatoi lɛ ahe ni amɛmaa shi.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my maize turn yellow in a V-shape before the corn is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize is a clear signal that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant stay green and develop full cobs.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ ŋmei lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does spreading dry leaves around the base of my crops help them during the dry heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbɛ baai ni egbi ashwã he fɛɛ he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mitsei lɛ ashishi yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket that traps moisture in the soil, lowers ground temperature, and keeps crop roots cool and hydrated.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni ŋmɛɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔlɛ aba shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why should I apply fertilizer to my farm after it rains instead of when the soil is dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ moŋ fe be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi lɛ?

english: Fertilizer must dissolve in soil moisture for plant roots to absorb it. Putting chemical fertilizer on bone-dry soil can burn roots or sit unused until it gets blown away.
ga: Esa akɛ atsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli awo sũ mli nu mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni fãji yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ ashã loo amɛfee nɔ ni tsuuu nii kɛyashi amɛbaafã kɛya.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when planted in an open field without tall trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni tsei kakadaji bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight and need partial shade to grow safely. Planting temporary shade crops like plantain or cassava alongside young cocoa creates living umbrellas that protect them during their first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he tɛ̃ɛ. Ni ehe miihia ni ená hulutsoo ko koni ekwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ. Kɛfata kookoo ni mli tse lɛ he lɛ Ehaa ŋmɔlɔ ni buɔ tsei nɛɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy rains before the bunches are ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli dani jwɛi lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, and keeping too many suckers attached to one stem weakens the mother plant's grip in the soil. Removing extra suckers so only two or three remain, and mounting soil around the base, keeps the plant sturdy.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii babaoo fĩ tso lɛ tso kome he lɛ, ebaaha fɔlɔ tso lɛ nine ni shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ afee mlɛo. Ajieɔ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ koni enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ eshwɛ. Ni sũ ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why does planting cowpea or beans together with my maize make the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ du tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa edaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. As these roots break down, they release natural fertilizer into the soil, feeding the neighboring maize plants.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ shishifãi nɛɛ gbee shi lɛ Amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛkɛye ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops give me smaller harvests even if I water the field regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo yibii fioo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa miŋmɔji lɛ amli daa moŋ?

english: Weeds are strong competitors that steal valuable soil nutrients, light, and root space directly from your main crops. Removing weeds within the first few weeks of growth leaves all the soil nutrients for your crop to produce a heavy yield.
ga: Jwɛi ji akaŋshilɔi ni he wa ni juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni jara wa, la kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni amɛdara lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii fɛɛ ni haa onibii lɛ aná yibii babaoo lɛ aba.

english: What makes a piece of farmland fertile enough for crops to grow well?
ga: Mɛni haa okwaayeli shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa nii bɔ ni sa koni ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Fertile soil is rich in nutrients, holds moisture well, and has good structure from decayed plant leaves and organic matter, which allows crop roots to breathe and absorb food easily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ eyi mli obɔ lɛ Haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni eyɛ gbɛjianɔtoo kpakpa kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai kɛ nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ amli Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaamu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii.

english: Why do crops grow very well on my neighbor's land but struggle on my farm nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ akutsoŋnyo ko shikpɔŋ nɔ shi amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Soil quality can change even over short distances due to differences in soil depth, water drainage, past crop history, or organic matter content.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su baanyɛ atsake yɛ gbɛ kukuji po amli. Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ, nu ni hoɔ, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ he yinɔsane ni eho lɛ hewɔ. loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ayibɔ srɔtoi

english: How do I know which crops are best suited for my piece of land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: You can tell by observing how well the soil holds water, checking its texture (sandy, clay, or loam), and seeing which crops naturally grow healthy in your local area.
ga: Obaanyɛ ole kɛtsɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ nu jogbaŋŋ ehaa lɛ nɔ. Kwɛmɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha (ŋã, shikpɔŋ loo sũ) ni okwɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why do some crops like cassava grow almost anywhere while crops like cocoa need rich forest land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi, tamɔ ŋmei, kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ he fɛɛ he, yɛ be mli ni tsei tamɔ kookoo biɔ koo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ yɔɔ fɛo lɛ?

english: Cassava is a hardy crop with deep roots that can search for water and nutrients in poor soils, whereas cocoa trees require deep, rich, nutrient-heavy soil with steady moisture to produce pods.
ga: Cassava ji tso ni wa ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni baanyɛ ana nu kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ he miihia kookoo tsei koni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with big leaves but yield very small roots underwater?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛ baa wuji shi ewoɔ shishifãi bibii yɛ nu shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes plants focus all their energy on growing upper leaves and stems instead of storing food in the underground tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ tsei ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ ahe nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii amli lɛ,.

english: Why do my crop leaves start turning yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen, or the soil is waterlogged, which prevents the roots from taking up nutrients.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu eyi sũ lɛ mli obɔ. ni tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii mli hewalɛ

english: What will happen to my land if I grow maize on the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi?

english: Repeatedly planting the same crop wears out specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I plant different types of crops together on the same farmland without harming them?
ga: Mibaanyɛ makwɛ tsei srɔtoi. Ani amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee ekome kɛtsu nii yɛ okwaayeli he kome ni amɛyeee nɔ ko nɔ ko?

english: Yes, mixing crops with different feeding habits—like pairing maize with beans—helps protect the soil because legumes add nitrogen back into the earth while maize uses it.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ niyenii sɔrɔtoi futuɔ mli, tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli. Ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he ejaakɛ ŋmeii kɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii kɛtsuɔ nii.

english: Why does my soil become dry and hard like concrete during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi ni ewa tamɔ kɔnkrit yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic matter like compost or dried leaves, which act like sponges to trap moisture and keep the earth loose and soft.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo baai ni egboi bɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni ekɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni efeɔ bɔdɔɔ.

english: How can I improve my land so that it can support different kinds of crops successfully?
ga: Mafee mishikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni manyɛ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi anɔ. Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ eye omanye?

english: Adding animal manure, compost, and practice mulching enriches the soil structure, making it balanced enough for a wide variety of crops to feed and thrive.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ afee ekome bɔ ni sa koni ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi anyɛ aye niyenii ni amɛshwere.

english: Young cocoa plants are very delicate and burn easily under full, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantain alongside cocoa protects the young seedlings from heat and keeps moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he, ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi kookoo tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking essential nutrients, especially nitrogen, or that the soil is waterlogged. Adding compost, animal manure, or a balanced nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy green foliage.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmã nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa. titri lɛ nitrogen loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why does my soil become very hard and dry up quickly during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa waa ni egbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Soil dries out fast when it lacks organic matter and is left exposed to direct sunlight. Leaving crop residues or spreading mulch like dried grass over the farm bed traps moisture and stops the sun from baking the soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ oya kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli, ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shɛɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ loo ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔ mli saatso nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ aba mli ni ebaatsi hulu lɛ naa koni ekashã shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in cool, overly shaded, and wet conditions. Pruning excess canopy leaves lets air and sunshine into the farm, which keeps the environment dry enough to prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ lɛ Shade babaoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ mli feɔ ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa koni ŋmɔtɔ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do small worms bore holes into my green pepper fruits before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miifo mi chili aduawai eŋɔli lɛ mli dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: These are pests like fruit borers that lay eggs on the flowers or young fruits. Using natural neem leaf extracts or recommended organic sprays early in the flowering stage stops the pests from laying eggs on your crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fruit borers ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ fɔfɔi loo aduawai bibii anɔ. Akɛ neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii mra yɛ fɔfɔii lɛ amli. Ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shwieɔ onibii anɔ.

english: Tomato plants often drop their flowers when the afternoon heat is too high or when they experience sudden water stress. Regular watering early in the morning keeps the plant cool and helps flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji shwane mli latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo kɛ́ ena nu he haomɔ trukaa Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing small and twisted instead of big and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni egbɛ eshwa moŋ fe ni eeefee agbo ni eja lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose earth to expand smoothly. If the soil is hard, stony, or the planting mounds are too small, the roots struggle to grow deep, resulting in small or deformed yams.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, tɛi yɔɔ mli, loo dumɔwu lɛ gɔŋ lɛ ji bibioo tsɔ lɛ, Shishifãi lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛdara kɛya shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni efite lɛ baa.

english: Insects called grain weevils eat the inside of the maize if the grains were not dried properly before storage. Drying your maize until the seeds are very hard prevents insect larvae from feeding inside.
ga: Kooloo ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dumɔwui ŋmei lɛ baaye ŋmãa mli kɛji akɛ agbiko dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani akɛto. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ aahu kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, ehaa kooloi bibii lɛ akayeɔ nii yɛ mli.

english: Why do the seeds I saved from last year's maize harvest yield less crop this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmãa kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Many modern farm seeds are hybrids designed to give high yield only in their first planting generation. Reusing saved hybrid seeds causes the next crop to grow unevenly and yield less, so buying fresh certified seeds gives better results.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei dumɔwui babaoo ji tsei ni afee amɛ ekome ni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ mli. Hybrid dumɔwui ni akɛto lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii ekoŋŋ lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ akwɛ̃ ni ekɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi aba. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahemɔ haa yibii kpakpai baa.

english: Why do my cassava stems rot in the ground when I plant them during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei tsei lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings rot when planted in flooded or poorly drained soil because excess water suffocates the stem tissues before roots can form. Planting on raised soil ridges allows extra water to drain away freely.
ga: Kasava tsei ni afo lɛ baafite kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tso lɛ shishi fãji lɛ shwieɔ shi dani shishifãi lɛ daa. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ ni aduɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why do some seed packs contain small seeds, and will they produce as much yield as larger seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui akui komɛi yɛ dumɔwui bibii lɛ? Ni ani ebaawo yibii babaoo tamɔ dumɔwui wuji lɛ?

english: Seed size does not determine yield potential. Foundation seeds carry pure, strong genetics, which gives them high growing power to produce excellent harvests even if the seeds themselves look small.
ga: Dumɔwu lɛ dalɛ etsɔɔɔ bɔ ni ebaanyɛ ewo yibii. Shishitoo dumɔwui lɛ yɛ fɔmɔ nii ni he tse ni mli wa. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛdaraa waa ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Eyɛ mli akɛ dumɔwui lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛji bibii moŋ

english: What is the main difference between foundation seeds and the seeds I save from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ shishitoo dumɔwui kɛ dumɔwui ni mibuaa naa kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ mli lɛ ateŋ?

english: Saved seeds gradually lose their strength and yield capacity over time, whereas foundation seeds are high-purity seeds bred under strict agricultural supervision to give maximum yield and strong plant growth.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ baafite fiofio hewalɛ kɛ nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛbaawo yibii yɛ be mli ni shishitoo dumɔwui lɛ ji dumɔwui ni he tse waa ni afɔɔ yɛ okwaayeli nɔkwɛmɔ ni mli wa shishi koni amɛwo yibii babaoo kɛ tsei adalɛ ni mli wa.

english: Why does a small quantity of certified seed cost more than buying a large bag of seed from the local market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui fioo ko ni awo he odase lɛ jara wa fe dumɔwui kotoku agbo ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ?

english: Certified seeds have high genetic purity and natural strength. Even a small quantity of these seeds will produce much higher yields and healthier crops than a large quantity of uncertified market seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ fɔmɔ su mli hetsemɔ ni nɔ kwɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ. Dumɔwui nɛɛ amli fioo po woɔ yibii babaoo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe jara nɔ dumɔwui babaoo ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Will planting a small amount of foundation seed yield enough crop to feed my household and sell?
ga: Ani shishijee dumɔwui fioo ko ni aduɔ lɛ baaha aná ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛyeɔ weku ko ni ahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Yes, foundation seed has strong germination power and yield capacity, so even a small amount planted correctly will produce a bountiful harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, shishitoo dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shweremɔ hewalɛ ni nɔ kwɔ kɛ yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, aduɔ fioo po jogbaŋŋ ni abaanyɛ ana ŋmaa babaoo.

english: How can I be sure that the crop seeds I am buying in the market are approved by the Ministry of Agriculture?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ kpɛlɛɔ nɔ?

english: You should buy from registered seed growers or official seed sellers. Genuine seeds come in sealed, officially labeled packages that show they have been tested and certified by agricultural authorities.
ga: Esa akɛ ohe kɛjɛ dumɔwui akwɛlɔi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ loo dumɔwui ahɔ̃ɔlɔi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ adɛŋ. Dumɔwui diɛŋtsɛ baa yɛ kotokui ni atsĩ naa mli ni amɛyɛ wolo ni aŋmala nɔ nii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ okwaayeli nitsumɔhe ko eka lɛ ekwɛ ni ekɛ odaseyeli ha.

english: Can I buy certified seeds directly from local seed farmers, or do I have to go to government offices?
ga: Ani manyɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui okwaafoi lɛ adɛŋ tɛ̃ɛ? Aloo esa akɛ maya nɔyeli lɛ nitsumɔhe ko?

english: You can buy directly from registered seed producers in your community. Because they are official seed growers authorized by the Ministry of Agriculture, they are legally permitted to sell certified seeds directly to farmers.
ga: Obaanyɛ ohe tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛ dumɔwui ahe nitsulɔi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ yɛ akutso lɛ mli lɛ adɛŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛji dumɔwui akwɛlɔi ni Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ eha amɛ hegbɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, mla eŋmɛ amɛ gbɛ ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ amɛha okwaafoi tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Who is a registered seed grower, and why should I trust their seed quality?
ga: Namɛi ji dumɔwui akwɛlɔi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mihe afɔ̃ amɛdumɔwui su lɛ nɔ?

english: A registered seed grower is a trained farmer monitored by the Ministry of Agriculture to produce clean, disease-free, high-yielding seeds that meet official national standards.
ga: Dumɔwui akwɛlɔi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ ji okwaafoi ni atsɔse amɛ ni Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ ekwɛ amɛ koni amɛwo dumɔwui ni he tse, ni hela bɛ mli, ni woɔ yibii babaoo. ni kɛ maŋ lɛ shishitoo mlai ni amralo lɛ kɛhaa lɛ kpãa gbee.

english: Do high-quality foundation seeds require special chemical treatments or soaking before I plant them?
ga: Ani shishitoo dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ biɔ ni akɛ tsofa krɛdɛɛ ko atsu he nii loo akɛwo nu mli dani adu?

english: No, certified foundation seeds are naturally strong and do not require extra chemical treatments before planting; they are ready to put straight into the soil.
ga: Dabi, shishitoo dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ji nɔ ni wa yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai krokomɛi afata he dani adu. Efee klalo akɛ ebaagbee shikpɔŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ

english: Why do certified seeds sprout faster and stronger in the field than seeds I collect from my neighbors?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛhe wa fe dumɔwui ni mibuaa naa kɛjɛɔ mikutsoŋbii lɛ adɛŋ lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are carefully selected for high germination vigor, giving them the natural strength to sprout quickly and grow steadily without needing extra chemical stimulants.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa enáa adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni ekɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya ni edaa be fɛɛ be ni tsofai krokomɛi ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Is it safe to plant certified seeds directly into my cleared field once the rainy season starts?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ awo miŋmɔ ni mli tse lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Yes, certified seeds are tough and designed for direct planting. As long as the soil has basic moisture, the seeds will sprout successfully without needing complex preparation.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ wa ni afee koni adu tɛ̃ɛ. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ shishijee ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji asaa he ni mli wa bɛ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants keep falling over whenever heavy rain and strong wind come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baa lɛ?

english: When maize plants fall over, it is called lodging. This usually happens when seeds are planted too shallowly, plants are spaced too close together, or the soil around the base is too soft to support tall stems.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmãa tso ko gbee shi lɛ, atsɛɔ lɛ shĩa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ. Okɛ tsei lɛ abɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Aloo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ efi tso lɛ tso kakadaŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to heap soil around the bottom of my maize stems as they grow tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mabua sũ naa yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Heaping soil around the base of the plant covers the lower roots that sprout above the ground. This gives the maize extra anchorage in the soil so it can stand firm against heavy storms.
ga: heaping dirt around Tso lɛ shishigbɛ shishifãi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ enyɛɔ edamɔ ahum ni naa wa naa.

english: Yam plants are vines that need physical support to lift their leaves up toward the sun. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground to prevent diseases and helps the stem stay upright to produce larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni he hiaa gbɔmɔtsoŋ yelikɛbuamɔ koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛyashɛ hulu la lɛ he. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni helai akabote mli, ni eye ebua ni eha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ koni amɛwo bulbs wuji.

english: How can I stop my cassava plants from snapping near the ground during strong winds?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ atsĩ ŋmei tsei anaa koni amɛkakumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ masɛi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli?

english: Planting your cassava cuttings at a slight angle deep within well-tilled soil encourages strong, spreading roots that hold the stem firmly in the ground as the top grows heavy.
ga: Dumɔ ŋmei niji yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ fioo kɛya shikpɔŋ ni atsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ awa ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni tsii.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over right when the fruit bunch becomes big and heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi trukaa be mli ni aduawai akui lɛ dara ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that struggle to carry the weight of heavy fruit bunches. Supporting the main stem with a sturdy branched wooden pole prevents the tree from tipping over before harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ agbɔjɔmɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni akɛ niji ni mli wa fiɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ akagbee shi dani akpa tso lɛ.

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings wither or fall over if I do not plant plantains next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi kɛji miduuu dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender stems and roots that burn and weaken in full sun. Planting fast-growing plantains alongside them provides shade and moisture, helping the cocoa stems grow thick and sturdy.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ tsei kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni shãa ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Kookoo tsei ni daa oya lɛ ni ooodu yɛ he kome lɛ baaha hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i aba. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my tomato plants bend over and touch the dirt once the fruits start appearing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛ́ aduawai lɛ je shishi amɛje kpo lɛ?

english: Tomato stems are naturally flexible and become top-heavy as fruit develops. Tying the stems gently to vertical wooden stakes holds the plant upright, keeping the fruit clean and free from soil rot.
