ga: Tomato tsei lɛ amli tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ be mli ni aduawai lɛ daraa lɛ. Akɛ tso ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ ni baaye abua ni emɔ tso lɛ shi shiŋŋ lɛ akpɛtɛ tso lɛ shishi blɛoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni aduawai lɛ ahe tseɔ ni sũ ni egbo bɛ nɔ.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete for light and stretch upward too fast. This makes their stems thin and weak, causing them to bend or break easily.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tso lɛ baatswa la he akaŋ ni ekɛ ehe baawo mli oya tsɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa amɛkotoɔ loo amɛkuɔ oya.

english: Why should I plant a line of tall trees along the edge of my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsei kakadaji ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Trees planted along farm borders act as windbreaks. They slow down strong winds before they enter your field, protecting fragile crops like plantain and cocoa from snapping or uprooting.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ husu lɛ he lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔŋ tsɔnei. Amɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ baa shi dani etswaa oŋmɔji lɛ. Buu ŋmɔshi nibii ni waaa tamɔ plantains kɛ cocoa he koni akakumɔ loo akajie amɛ.

english: Why do my crops have shallow roots that easily pull out of the ground during rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Roots stay near the surface if the hard layer of soil beneath them was not broken up before planting. Loose, deeply tilled soil allows roots to penetrate deep into the ground to anchor the plant securely.
ga: Shishifãi lɛ baahi shi ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ ajieee shikpɔŋ ni wa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli dani adu. Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni ekɛtswa tso lɛ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees are like human babies and burn easily under harsh sunlight. Shade trees act like living umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa plants from heat and drying out until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ ambrela ni hiɛ ka. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he ni ogbi amɛ kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhe hulu la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants roll up and droop during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves to protect themselves from losing water through heat. When the sun is hot, the plant closes up to conserve moisture and usually opens back up once the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ mli baa lɛ he. Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ Aŋmɛɔ tsei lɛ koni hulutsoo akahi shi. Ni bei pii lɛ, etsuɔ ​​ekoŋŋ kɛ́ hulu lɛ enyɔ shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that the plant is hungry for nitrogen, a key food in the soil that keeps leaves green. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji niyenii titri ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛ ŋmɔji lɛ amli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do officers advise me not to plant pepper on the exact same bed where I harvested pepper last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mikadu ŋmeii yɛ saatso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ yɛ he ni mifo yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same spot exhausts specific soil nutrients and allows pests and diseases that love that crop to build up in the soil. Changing to a crop like beans or maize helps clean the soil and restore nutrients.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa sũ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi baa shi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ tsei lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tseɔ ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller cobs when I plant maize seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. Giving each plant proper space allows its roots and leaves to get enough nourishment to form big, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ kɛ baai lɛ náa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso agbo ni mli wa akwɛ̃.

english: Why does my plantain take so long to fruit if I leave all the young shoots growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii kɛji mishi ŋmeii bibii ni bɔle tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: The extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and food from the main mother plant. Cutting away extra suckers leaves only the strongest shoot to direct all food into producing big fruit bunches fast.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ ashiɔ koni eye niyenii muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ koni ewo yibii wuji oya.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the leaves inside the center funnel of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ funnel lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars, known as Fall Armyworms, feed on the newest and softest green leaves inside the maize funnel. Checking your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides directly into the funnel protects the main growing point of the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ni ale amɛ akɛ Fall Armyworms lɛ yeɔ baai eŋɔli heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii amli lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaye abua ni abu hei titri ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa yɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do weeds cause my vegetable crops to grow weak and thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha mi-aduawai lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients. Keeping your field weed-free ensures all available food in the ground goes directly into your vegetables.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kpakpai waa. Kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aya o-vegetables lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How do I know that my cassava roots are mature and ready for harvest under the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava shows it is ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and shed off, leaving a bare stem near the ground, typically between 9 to 12 months after planting depending on the variety.
ga: Akɛɛ akɛ, kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi lɛ, efee klalo. ni ashiɔ tso ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ masɛi Bei pii lɛ Enɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Edamɔ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ

english: Why does trimming extra side branches off my tomato plants give me bigger fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ afo tomato tso lɛ niji krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ, ewoɔ yibii wuji lɛ?

english: Trimming unnecessary side branches stops the tomato plant from wasting energy on growing excess leaves. The plant then redirects all its energy and nutrients into growing larger, healthier fruits.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaha o-tomato tso lɛ akafite hewalɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ baai krokomɛi lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ tsɔɔ ehewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ kɛyaa aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when planted out in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sun and lose moisture quickly. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides shade and keeps the surrounding soil humid while the young trees establish roots.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa, ni amɛmli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu nurse tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains yɛ cocoa masɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Lifting yam leaves into the sunlight helps the plant capture more light to feed its underground tuber. Keeping the foliage off damp ground also reduces fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ owó sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ koni amɛgbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni emɔɔ la babaoo ni ekɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai helai ni ji fungal lɛ baa shi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate a nitrogen deficiency. The maize plant takes nitrogen from its older lower leaves and moves it up to feed the newer growth at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. Abɛi tsei lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is my cassava growing tall with thick green leaves, but producing very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi eyɛ yitso bibioo ko kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil encourages cassava to spend its energy building stems and foliage above ground rather than storing nutrients in the roots.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmei hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ

english: Why does covering the soil around my crop roots with dry grass help them survive during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Mulching with dry grass shades the soil from intense sun, slowing down water evaporation, keeping root temperatures cool, and preventing weed competition.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Ha shishifã lɛ mli latsaa lɛ afee fɛ̃i. ni atsĩ jwɛi akaŋshii naa

english: Why should I prune off extra suckers around my plantain stand instead of letting all of them grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Plank damɔ shi lɛ jeɔ kpo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha amɛ fɛɛ amɛdara

english: Multiple suckers compete for the same food and water in the soil. Removing weaker suckers allows the main plant to focus its energy on producing large, healthy bunches.
ga: Suckers babaoo kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ tsei bibii lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa tsei wuji ni he wa lɛ afeemɔ nɔ.

english: Why is it harmful to weed aggressively around my groundnut plants once they start showing flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mikɛ yiwalɛ baagbe mi-peanut tsei lɛ ahe jwɛi be mli ni amɛjeɔ fɔfɔi shishi pɛ kɛkɛ?

english: After flowering, groundnut plants send flower stalks down into the soil to grow nuts underground. Digging or weeding near the plant during flowering snaps these stalks and stops nuts from forming.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmei tsei wo fɔfɔi sɛɛ lɛ, amɛtsuɔ fɔfɔi ahe ŋmeii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛdu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ atsa loo ajie jwɛi yɛ tsei lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, ebaaku nɛkɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi nɛɛ amli ni ebaatsi ŋmeii ni baa lɛ anaa.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without forming any small fruits during hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho ni amɛwooo yibii bibii lɛ? Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Extreme heat and water stress cause tomato plants to abort their blossoms to save energy and protect the main plant from drying out.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu he haomɔ haa tomato tsei lɛ kpaɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu tso lɛ he koni ekagbi.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants twisting upward and curling into tight cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miitsi amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee kɔɔpoi ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids, or viruses transmitted by these pests while feeding on young leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids kɛ chili baa baa. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa beni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea pods look flat and empty even though the plants produced plenty of green leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea ŋmɔji lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nɔ ko bɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Flat pods usually occur when sap-sucking insects or pod borers attack the young pods and feed on the developing seeds inside, preventing them from swelling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baa kɛji kooloi ni nuɔ nu loo pod borers lɛ tutua ŋmeii bibii ni amɛyeɔ dumɔwui ni miiya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ. Koni akafee fuumɔ

english: How can I estimate how much crop yield and money I will get from my farm before harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masusu miŋmɔshi nibii ni mawo lɛ he akɔntaa kɛ shika enyiɛ mana kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani akpa nii?

english: Your final yield depends on crop variety, soil quality, rainfall, and farm care. By knowing the standard yield per acre for your specific seed variety and keeping track of your input costs, you can project your expected harvest quantity and market earnings.
ga: Onaagbee yibiiwoo damɔ tsei srɔtoi lɛ anɔ, sũ lɛ mlihilɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ, kɛ ŋmɔ mli saamɔ nɔ. Lemɔ yibiiwoo ni sa yɛ acre kome mli kɛha odumɔwui srɔtoi pɔtɛɛ ni okwɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe nyɔmɔwoo. Obaanyɛ otsɔɔ ŋmaa lɛ falɛ ni akpaa gbɛ kɛ jara nɔ nyɔmɔwoo.

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, a vital soil nutrient needed for leaves to make plant food. Yellowing can also happen when heavy rains make the soil waterlogged, preventing the roots from taking up nutrients.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Eji shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ kɛtsu nii akɛ tsei aniyenii. Yellowing hu baanyɛ aba kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ nu. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii mli hewalɛ

english: Why do my cassava plants lose their leaves when the weather gets dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava plants naturally drop leaves during dry spells to save water and keep from drying out. Once rain returns, the plant uses saved energy from its roots to sprout fresh green leaves and continue growing.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛkagbi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ Tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni ehere kɛjɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyaa nɔ edaa.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when plants experience heat stress or irregular watering. Extremely hot daytime temperatures or dry soil cause the flowers to dry out and fall before fruit can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Gbi mli latsaa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why is my farm producing fewer bags of crops each year even when I use the same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ kotokui amli lɛ faaa daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: Every crop takes nutrients out of the earth as it grows. Planting the same crop on the same ground continuously drains the soil's natural food supply, resulting in smaller harvests unless you add manure, fertilizer, or rotate crops.
ga: Nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni afee lɛ fioo. Ja okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsake lɛ fata he.

english: Why is it better to make mounds or ridges instead of planting directly on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaafee gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ moŋ fe ni ooodu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Mounds and ridges create soft, aerated soil that makes it easier for root crops like cassava and yams to expand. They also channel heavy rain away from roots to prevent root rot.
ga: Gɔji kɛ ŋshɔkei feɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ni ŋɔɔ lɛ akɛ amɛbaagbɛ amɛshwã. Amɛjieɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli hu koni shishifãi lɛ akafite.

english: Why are small worms eating the inside leaves of my young maize plants during the cool morning hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ?

english: These are fall armyworms, a common pest that feeds on tender maize leaves inside the central whorl of the plant. They hide from the strong daytime sun and come out in the cooler morning or evening hours to feed.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji fall asraafoi. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋtayaa lɛ mli lɛ. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni amɛje kpo amɛbatao niyenii leebi loo gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why do crops planted during the minor rain season often fail compared to the major rain season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli lɛ fɔɔ shweremɔ kɛ akɛto nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he lɛ?

english: The minor rain season in Ghana has shorter and unpredictable rainfall patterns. Soil dries out quickly before young crops can fully establish deep root systems to survive to full harvest maturity.
ga: Nugbɔ be ni nɛɔ fioo yɛ Ghana lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kuku ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba. Shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya dani tsei bibii lɛ baanyɛ ato shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kwraa koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi amɛdara.

english: Why do you advise me not to plant my crops too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ owoɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mikadu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stems and small harvest yields.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ amli tsei bibii kɛ ŋmaa ni baa shi.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil and rot inside my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ miifite ni miifite yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize rots in storage if it is stored before being thoroughly dried in the sun, or if damp air enters the storage container. Moisture encourages mold and insects to grow rapidly inside stored grain.
ga: Abɛi fiteɔ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ akɛto dani agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. aloo kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ bote nibii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli Fɛ̃i woɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ amli lɛ adalɛ oya lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Is there a specialized tool or device I can use to put medicine directly into a diseased plantain tree?
ga: Ani dɛŋdade loo nibii krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ ni manyɛ mikɛ tsofa awo plantains ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yes, stem injection devices allow you to inject treatments directly into the trunk of a plantain or banana plant. This delivers medication straight into the plant's system to fight internal diseases without wasting chemical sprays on the leaves.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ tsofafeemɔ nibii woɔ plantains loo banana tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Koni ekɛ tsofai awo tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛwu eshi helai ni yɔɔ emli lɛ ni ekɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ efiteee.

english: Why are my plantain leaves turning yellow and dying before the fruit bunch is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi dani aduawai lɛ baa lɛ?

english: This is often caused by fungal diseases like Black Sigatoka or Panama disease, which attack the leaves and roots. These fungi prevent the plant from taking up water and sunlight, causing the leaves to rot early and leaving the fruit bunch small and unripened.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Black Sigatoka hela loo Panama hela kɛbaa. ni tutuaa baai kɛ shishifãi Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná nu kɛ hulu la. Enɛ haa baai lɛ fiteɔ oya ni ehaa aduawai akui lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛshɛɛɛ.

english: Can diseases spread from a sick plantain tree to a healthy one through my cutlass?
ga: Ani hela baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛjɛ plantain ni hela mɔ lɛ mli kɛya nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ mi-dagger lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, fungal spores and bacteria stick to your tools when you cut diseased plants. If you cut a healthy plantain tree with that same cutlass without washing or sterilizing it with bleach or fire, you will transfer the disease directly into the healthy tree.
ga: Hɛɛ, fungal kɛ bacteria spores lɛ kpɛtɛɔ odɛŋdadei lɛ ahe kɛ́ ofo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ tsɔne kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ŋmɔ dumɔwu ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni okɛ bleach loo la tsuuu he loo okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ helai lɛ efɔɔɔ he. Obaagbɛ hela lɛ oshwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: What causes tiny holes near the roots of my plantain tree that make the plant snap during strong winds?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Ebɛŋkɛ mi plantain lɛ shishi ni haa tso lɛ fãa yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ.

english: This damage is caused by banana stem weevils or root nematodes. Their larvae tunnel into the plant stem and roots to feed, destroying the plant's underground anchor and making it snap at the base under heavy weather.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji banana ŋmeii loo shishifãi amli ŋmeii. Larvae tsɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli koni amɛye nii. Efiteɔ tso lɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ. ni ehaa efoɔ yɛ shishigbɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa shishi.

english: Why do farmers in my area plant plantains in the middle of their young cocoa farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ duɔ plantains yɛ amɛ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow much faster and produce broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the temporary shade and cooler soil young cocoa seedlings need to survive.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya kwraa ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa kookoo dumɔwui bibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ haa.

english: How do I choose healthy plantain suckers from an old farm so I do not bring sick plants to my new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ momo ko mli? Bɔni afee ni mikɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ akaba miŋmɔ hee lɛ mli.

english: Look for 'sword suckers'—young shoots with narrow, spear-shaped leaves and thick bases. Avoid shoots with broad leaves or any dark brown holes and rot around their roots, as those carry pests and diseases.
ga: Taomɔ ‘sword shoot’, ni ji tso bibioo ko ni baai lɛ mli tseee, ni tamɔ lance, ni eshishigbɛ lɛ mli tse. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni baai lɛ mli kwɔlɔ loo buji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ahe. kɛ fitemɔ ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe akɛni amɛji helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe nibii

english: How many months does it take for a plantain plant from planting until the fruit bunch is ready to harvest?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ eheɔ dani plantain tso ko daa kɛjɛɔ dumɔ mli kɛyaa aduawai akui ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: In good Ghanaian soil with adequate rain, a plantain plant usually flowers around 8 to 11 months after planting, and the fruit takes another 3 to 4 months to fully mature for harvest, making the total cycle around 11 to 15 months.
ga: Yɛ Ghana shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ fɔɔ fɔmɔ aaafee nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 11 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Ni aduawai lɛ baahe nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 krokomɛi dani amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛha kpamɔ. Ehaa sɛɛkuu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ aaafee nyɔji 11 kɛyashi 15.

english: Why does my plantain tree produce small bunches even though I planted it in rich black soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miifɔ yɛ kui bibii amli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ midu yɛ shikpɔŋ diŋ ni mli wa nɔ moŋ.

english: Plantains need huge amounts of water and potassium to make large bunches. Even in good soil, if the plant faces dry spells or has too many competing suckers growing around its base, the food gets divided and the fruit bunch stays small.
ga: Nu kɛ potassium babaoo he miihia plantains koni efee ŋmeii wuji. Yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa nɔ po Kɛji tso lɛ na be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi loo eyɛ ŋmeii babaoo ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ ni miida yɛ eshishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, ajaa niyenii mli ni aduawai akuu lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ bibioo.

english: Should I cut off dead plantain leaves and leave them on the ground or burn them?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ plantain baai ni egboi lɛ ni mashɛ shikpɔŋ loo mashã amɛ?

english: If the leaves died of natural old age, chopping them up to cover the soil (mulching) keeps the soil moist and adds organic manure. However, if the leaves died from a contagious disease, you should remove and destroy them away from healthy plants.
ga: Kɛji baai lɛ gboi yɛ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ hewɔ lɛ baai ni afolɔ koni akɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni akɛ organic fertilizer afata he. Shi, kɛji akɛ baai lɛ gboi yɛ hela ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ hewɔ lɛ, Esa akɛ Ojie nakai baai lɛ ni okpãtã amɛhiɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe.

english: How can I tell if my plantain leaves are turning yellow from lack of fertilizer or from a plant disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ loo tso hela hewɔ?

english: When a plant lacks nutrients like nitrogen or potassium, the outer edge or lower old leaves turn a smooth yellow evenly. When it is a disease, you will see dark brown spots, black streaks, or sudden drying across young leaves as well.
ga: Kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium lɛ Baai ni egbɔ lɛ asɛɛgbɛ loo amɛshishi baatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ po. Kɛji akɛ hela lɛ mɔ lɛ, abaana ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmeii diji loo ŋmeii ni egbi trukaa lɛ hu yɛ baai bibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why should I nurse my seeds in a small nursery first instead of planting them directly on the big farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli klɛŋklɛŋ moŋ fe ni madu yɛ ŋmɔ agbo mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Nursing seeds gives delicate young sprouts a protected environment with shade and careful watering, helping them grow strong roots before facing harsher weather and pests in the main field.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui bibii lɛ naa he ko ni abuɔ he ni amɛnáa hulutsoo kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni mli wa dani amɛshɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my tomato seedlings droop and wilt immediately after I move them to the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Moving seedlings damages their tiny water-absorbing root hairs, causing transplant shock. Moving them during the hot sun makes them lose water faster than their weak roots can draw it up.
ga: Dumɔwui ni tsiɔ amɛhe lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe yitsɔi bibii ni shwieɔ nu lɛ, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ baa. Kɛ́ otsi amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ afite oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu lɛ.

english: What causes the leaves on my green crops to turn light yellow during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant lacks nitrogen or that the soil is waterlogged, which suffocates the roots and prevents them from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa amɛye nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it helpful to cover the soil around my young crops with dry grass or palm leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmei baai baawo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle midumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil, known as mulching, keeps the ground cool, reduces water evaporation during hot days, and prevents weeds from popping up and stealing plant food.
ga: Mulching, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ha nu ni hoɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ aba shi. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekaje kpo ni eju niyenii kɛjɛ tsei lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and produce smaller cobs when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving less energy to form full cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ fioo pɛ feɔ cob ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients, forcing the plant to shed flowers to save energy.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni esaaa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei ajie amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to erect wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe hiaa mi kɛha mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni makwɔ nɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves in full sunlight. The leaves use sunlight to make food, which is sent down to grow large tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Baai kɛ hulu la feɔ niyenii. Kɛtsɔ amɛ ni amɛtsuɔ kɛyaa shi koni amɛyadu bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings scorch and die if I clear away all the large shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn under direct sunlight. Shade trees act like umbrellas, providing shade and keeping the air humid so the seedlings can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha hulutsoo ni oha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee fɛ̃i koni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: How does planting cassava together with groundnuts on the same field benefit my land?
ga: Te ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aná he sɛɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts naturally capture nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the soil, which feeds the cassava plant and keeps the soil fertile.
ga: Peanuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii kɛha ŋmei tsei lɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Why do wild weeds seem to grow much faster than my cultivated crops after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants naturally adapted to the local soil and weather, allowing them to absorb rainwater and soil nutrients far quicker than farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛjieɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei.

english: How do I know if my soil is suitable for starting a new cocoa farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ hee shishijee?

english: Cocoa trees need deep, fertile, and well-draining soil rich in organic material. Avoid clay-heavy lands that hold too much water or rocky soils where roots cannot easily penetrate.
ga: Cacao tsei biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni baa nii, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni shikpɔŋ yɔɔ nɔ ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli loo shikpɔŋ ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ ni shishifãi nyɛŋ abote mli mlɛo lɛ he.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to plant cocoa trees in straight lines with specific spacing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ akɛ adu cocoa tsei yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ ni gbɛ pɔtɛɛ ko yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines ensures every tree gets equal access to sunlight and soil nutrients, while also making farm activities like weeding, spraying, and harvesting much easier.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔi tamɔ jwɛi shwiemɔ, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: How many years will I have to wait before my newly planted cocoa tree starts producing pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani cacao tso ni adu ehee lɛ aje shishi ewo ŋmeii?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties typically start producing pods within 2 to 3 years, whereas older traditional varieties take about 4 to 5 years under good care.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ ŋmɔtɔ shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 5 yɛ kwɛmɔ kpakpa shishi.

english: Why do the yellow flowers on my cocoa tree fall off without growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the tree is stressed by dry weather, lacks proper nutrients, or is attacked by insects like mirids. Ensuring proper shade and pest control helps flowers mature into pods.
ga: Fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa. Niyenii ni sa ni bɛ loo kooloi bibii tamɔ pollen ni baatutua lɛ. Shade ni sa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii.

english: Is it safe for me to cut off branches from my cocoa tree, or will it damage the plant?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafolɔ mi-kookoo niji lɛ? Aloo ebaafite tso lɛ loo efiteee?

english: Pruning dead or excess branches is beneficial because it allows sunlight and air to reach all parts of the tree, which prevents diseases and encourages higher pod production.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔi yɛ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aaafo lɛ he ejaakɛ ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ helai anaa ni ewoɔ pod ni fa babaoo lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds regularly when my cocoa trees are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ daa lɛ? Kookoo tso lɛ yɛ bibioo lolo.

english: Young cocoa plants have small roots and easily lose the fight against weeds for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, which can stunt their growth or kill them.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwu amɛshi jwɛi lɛ mlɛo koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ amɛdalɛ naa loo egbe amɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in humid, overgrown farms. Pruning trees to let air in and harvesting ripe pods promptly prevents it.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli ewo fɔ ni efee basabasa lɛ amli. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli koni kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli, ni akpa tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ, ebaaha abu he amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: How do I protect my cocoa seedlings from dying during the hot dry harmattan season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-kokoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe koni amɛkagboi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli?

english: Provide permanent shade trees around the farm, cover the soil around the seedling base with dry leaves (mulching) to trap moisture, and build firebelts around the land boundaries.
ga: Ha tsei ni baaha ŋmɔ lɛ he afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ daa. Okɛ baai ni egbi (mulch) awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle dumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ he koni ekɛmɔ ŋmɔtɔ. ni amɛma la tsɔne amɛbɔle shikpɔŋ lɛ he fɛɛ he.

english: Apply fertilizer early in the rainy season when the soil is moist so the roots can absorb the nutrients efficiently without getting burned by dry heat.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ ni la ni mli egbi lɛ akashã amɛ.

english: Why do I need to cover my harvested cocoa beans with plantain leaves for a few days before drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ plantain baai haa mi-kookoo ni mikpa lɛ nɔ gbii fioo komɛi dani migbiɔ lɛ?

english: This process is called fermentation; it develops the rich chocolate flavor and dark brown color inside the beans, making them high quality for the market.
ga: Atsɛɔ gbɛ nɛɛ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Ehaa tsokolate ni ŋɔɔ waa kɛ su ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa kɔfi yibii lɛ amli. Ha efee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha jarayeli.

english: How can I tell if a batch of seeds is good enough to give me a strong crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui akuu ko hi bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba?

english: Good seeds are clean, dry, full-sized, and free from insect holes or mold. You can test them by putting a handful in water; healthy seeds usually sink to the bottom, while weak or damaged seeds float to the top.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔwui kpakpai ahe atse, amɛgbi, amɛdalɛ fɛɛ afee nɔ ni kooloi bu loo ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli. Obaanyɛ oka enɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui kpakpai fɔɔ gbee kɛyaa shishi. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ loo efite lɛ baafo kɛya ŋwɛi.

english: Does planting a bigger seed mean I will get a bigger crop at harvest time?
ga: Ani dumɔwui wuji ni miduɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: A bigger seed usually contains more stored food energy, giving the young sprout a stronger start in its first few weeks. However, the final harvest size depends mainly on how well you water, feed, and protect the plant as it matures.
ga: Dumɔwui wuji lɛ fɔɔ niyenii hewalɛ babaoo ni ato. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛnáa hewalɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli, shi kɛlɛ naagbee ŋmaa lɛ dalɛ damɔ bɔ ni okɛ nu haa tsei lɛ, ohaa amɛ niyenii ni obuɔ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ beni amɛdaraa lɛ nɔ.

english: How deep should I put my seeds into the soil so they can sprout easily?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛya shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya?

english: A simple rule is to plant a seed at a depth equal to two or three times its thickness. If you plant a seed too deep, it wastes all its energy trying to push through the dirt and dies before reaching the surface.
ga: Mla kpakpa ni esa akɛ akwɛ nɔ ji ni adu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ ni ekɛ amɛmli ŋtayaa lɛ toi enyɔ loo etɛ yeɔ egbɔ. Kɛji odu dumɔwui lɛ mli tsɔ Ebaafite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni egbo dani eshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can a small sprout manage to break through dry, hard soil after planting?
ga: Ani dumɔwui bibii baanyɛ abote shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wa mli beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Sprouting seeds are strong, but if the topsoil forms a hard, dry crust, the delicate shoot can get trapped underneath and bend or rot. Keeping the soil moist and breaking up hard dirt clumps helps the sprout push through safely.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ mli wa. Shi kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ bafee nɔ ni wa ni egbi. Tsobii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baanyɛ akpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo amɛgboi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni akumɔ ŋmeii ni wa lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ tsɔɔ mli shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my seeds sprout nicely at first, but then suddenly fall over and die a few days later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishijee mli, shi trukaa lɛ amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by a soil fungus that thrives in overly wet or crowded conditions. It attacks the tender stem right at the soil level, causing the seedling to weaken, collapse, and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sũ mli ŋmeii ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ loo hei ni gbɔmɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Etutuaa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, amɛkuɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: What happens if I plant my seeds too close to each other in the same row?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta kome mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight underground for water and soil nutrients, while their leaves block each other from getting sunlight. This leaves you with thin, weak plants that produce small yields.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Enɛ baaha oná tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo pɛ.

english: Why is it better to plant my crops in neat lines rather than scattering seeds everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu dumɔwui yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines gives every crop enough room to grow, makes it easier for you to weed and apply fertilizer, and ensures sunlight reaches all parts of your field evenly.
ga: Kɛ́ akwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei fɛɛ náa hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa bo akɛ obaajie jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. ni ehaa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli hei fɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ

english: Why do my crop stems start bending and falling over on the ground as they get taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfoɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shikpɔŋ beni amɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Stems fall over when they grow too tall and thin due to shade, heavy rains, strong winds, or having too many plants crowded together. Giving plants proper spacing and mounding soil around their bases helps keep them upright.
ga: Tso lɛ baagbee shi kɛji etsɔ ŋwɛi tsɔ ni efee mlɛo yɛ hulutsoo, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, loo tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ hewɔ. Ni akɛ he ni sa kɛ muji ni abua naa ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ baaha tsei lɛ. Shishitoo lɛ haa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my crops spread long vines along the ground instead of growing upright like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi shwereɔ wain tsei kakadaji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ ja tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Crops like sweet potatoes, watermelons, and groundnuts naturally grow as creeping vines. Spreading along the ground allows them to cover the soil, conserve moisture, and stay safe from strong winds.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ sweet potatoes, watermelon, kɛ peanuts kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe tamɔ wain tsei ni shwereɔ. Kɛ́ egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kwɛmɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he

english: Why do all the plants on the side of my field lean towards one direction?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ etsi amɛhe kɛmiiya he kome lɛ?

english: Plants naturally lean and grow toward sunlight to make food. If taller trees or structures are shading one side of your field, the crops will stretch towards the open areas where the light is brightest.
ga: Tsei ji epiphytes ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa hulu la mli koni amɛfee niyenii. Kɛji tsei loo tsũi ni kwɔlɔ tsi ŋmɔ lɛ fã kome naa lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baagbɛ ashwã hei ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni la yɔɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Rice plants fall over, known as lodging, when their stems are too weak to support the heavy weight of mature grain heads. This usually happens if plants receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, are planted too close together, or face heavy winds and standing water late in the season.
ga: Ale ŋmãa tsei ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ hu akɛ shĩai. Beni tso lɛ shishifã lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ dumɔwu yitso ni eda kwraa lɛ nɔ muji ni tsii lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ Aloo okɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kpeɔ yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ?

english: Why are my corn plants growing extremely tall and thin without producing strong stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛbɛ ŋmeii ni wa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants compete for limited sunlight. They stretch rapidly upward to catch light instead of developing thick, sturdy stems that can support heavy ears of corn.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa. Amɛshwereɔ oya koni amɛhe la lɛ, ni moŋ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa ni baanyɛ akwɛ ŋmãa toi ni tsii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does some farm rice cook up firm and separate, while other rice turns soft and sticky?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbalaa amɛhe kɛ́ amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa henɔi komɛi yɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ?

english: The cooking behavior of rice depends on the type of starch stored inside the grain. Varieties high in a starch called amylose stay firm and fluffy after cooking, while low-amylose varieties absorb more water and cling together.
ga: Omɔ homɔ su damɔ starch henɔ ni abua naa yɛ omɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni starch babaoo yɔɔ mli, ni atsɛɔ amɛ amylose lɛ baahi shi shiŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ ahoo. yɛ be mli ni amylose henɔi ni faaa lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo ni amɛbua amɛhe naa.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots sometimes turn out watery instead of heavy and full of starch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ nu yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsii najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava plants convert sunlight and soil nutrients into starch stored in their roots. If the soil lacks potassium, if the crop gets harvested too early, or if there is excessive nitrogen, the plant puts energy into leafy green growth instead of packing starch into the roots.
ga: Cassava tsei tsakeɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amɛfeɔ starch ni akɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ potassium Kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mra tsɔ loo nitrogen fa tsɔ Tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ starch baawo amɛshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to let my harvested grains sit out to dry thoroughly before storing them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maŋmɛ gbɛ ni midumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ agbi kwraa dani mikɛto?

english: Freshly harvested grain contains moisture that allows mold to grow and attracts grain-boring insects. Drying the grain until it is hard lowers the moisture level so it can sit safely in storage without spoiling.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ nu ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii ni amɛdaraa ni egbalaa koolooi ni shwieɔ dumɔwui lɛ. Kɛji akɛ agbi ŋmaa lɛ mli kɛyashi ewa lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baa shi bɔni afee ni anyɛ akɛto shweshweeshwe ni efiteee.

english: Why is it important to cure my harvested yams in a cool area for a few days before sending them to market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ ato he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ gbii fioo komɛi dani akɛmaje jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Allowing yams to rest or cure in a shaded, well-ventilated space allows skin abrasions from harvesting to heal and thicken. This protective skin barrier keeps moisture inside and prevents rot organisms from entering.
ga: Aŋmɛɔ sweet potato gbɛ ni ejɔɔ ehe loo etsa yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ. Ebaaha hewolo ni shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ mli lɛ atsa ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nɛkɛ hewolo nɔ tsɔne nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ mli, ni ehaaa nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ abote mli.

english: How can I make sure my stored grains last for years without getting destroyed by insects?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ miŋmaa ni mikɛto lɛ baahi shi afii babaoo ni kooloi bibii efiteee lɛ?

english: To store grains long-term, ensure they are dried to below 13% moisture and kept in clean, airtight containers or hermetic bags. Sealing the container blocks oxygen, which stops insect eggs from hatching and keeps the grain preserved.
ga: Bɔni afee ni akɛ ŋmaa ato be kakadaŋŋ Kwɛmɔ ni ŋmaa lɛ agbi kɛyashɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi fe 13% ni akɛto tsɛnsi ni mli tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo vacuum bag mli. Kɛ́ atsĩ tsɛnsi lɛ naa lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa lɛ naa. Enɛ haaa kooloi bibii lɛ awui lɛ afɔ, ni ehaa ŋmaa lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Can I save seed grains from this season's harvest and expect them to sprout well if I plant them three years later?
ga: Ani manyɛ mahere dumɔwui ni jɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato ni makpa gbɛ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ afii etɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seed viability drops over time as living tissues inside the seed gradually age. While well-dried seeds stored in airtight, cool conditions can survive a few seasons, older seeds generally sprout weakly or fail to germinate entirely compared to fresh seed.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ anyɛmifeemɔ baa shi yɛ be mli ni fãji ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ daraa fiofio lɛ, kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ to he ko ni nɔ ko bɛ mli po. Shi yɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ehi shi bei fioo komɛi. Shi yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni egbɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ fioo loo amɛkwɛ̃ŋ kwraa kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ahe.

english: Why does my rice crop need standing water during early growth but needs the field drained before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni yɔɔ kpoo he hiaa mi-ŋmãa tso lɛ yɛ be mli ni edaa mra lɛ? Shi ani ehe miihia ni nu atsɔ mli yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani akpa nii?

english: Water prevents weeds from growing and helps rice plants absorb soil nutrients during early growth. Draining the field a few weeks before harvest prompts the plant to finish ripening its seeds uniformly and makes the soil dry enough for harvesting.
ga: Nu tsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ ni amɛheɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa mra lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie nu kɛjɛ ŋmɔji amli otsii fioo komɛi dani akpa lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ adumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ agbi bɔ ni sa kɛha kpamɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I wait until my seedlings are established before applying fertilizer instead of putting it all down on the day I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ atswa shi shiŋŋ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli moŋ fe ni mawo ŋmɔshi nii kwraa yɛ gbi ni midu lɛ nɔ?

english: Young seedlings have very small root systems that cannot absorb large amounts of nutrients. Applying heavy fertilizer too early can burn tiny roots or get washed away by rain before the plant is big enough to use it.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii waa ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii wo mli oya lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi bibii akwɛ̃. Eshãa loo nugbɔ shwieɔ lɛ dani tsei lɛ daraa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛtsu nii.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has lost its strength and needs treatment?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ egbɔjɔ ni ehe miihia ni atsa lɛ?

english: When soil loses its strength, your crops will look pale or stunted, weeds might grow faster than your crops, and the ground dries out quickly. You can restore it by adding animal manure, planting nitrogen-fixing crops like beans, or letting the land rest.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ he wa lɛ sɛɛ fo lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafee tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ loo egbɔjɔ. Jwɛi baanyɛ adara oya fe oŋmɔshi nibii. ni shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya Obaanyɛ okɛ kooloi ashishifãi awo mli ekoŋŋ. Dumɔ nibii ni haa nitrogen hiɔ shi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe.

english: How long does it take for tired soil to regain its strength after I add manure?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii efata he lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Organic manure releases its strength gradually. You will usually see a boost in crop growth within 2 to 4 weeks after rain falls on the treated soil, and the manure continues to nourish the soil for several seasons.
ga: Organic fertilizer baajie ohewalɛ lɛ kpo fiofio Bei pii lɛ obaana tsei lɛ adalɛ ni yaa hiɛ yɛ otsii 2 kɛyashi 4 mli beni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni atsa nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa nɔ ehaa sũ lɛ hewalɛ yɛ bei babaoo mli.

english: Can I mix animal manure with chemical fertilizer to get a better yield on my maize farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ kooloi ashishifãi afutu tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ koni maná yibii kpakpai yɛ mi-abele ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, combining organic manure with chemical fertilizer gives excellent results. Manure improves the soil's ability to hold water and nutrients, while chemical fertilizer provides a fast, powerful boost for immediate crop growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ futu ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ, ebaaha oná yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Muji haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa oya ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: What is the difference in strength between NPK fertilizer and Urea, and how do I choose between them?
ga: Mɛni ji hewalɛ srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ NPK kɛ urea ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala amɛteŋ?

english: NPK is a balanced fertilizer containing three main foods for roots, stems, and fruits. Urea is a single high-potency nitrogen fertilizer mainly used to give crops a quick boost to grow big, green leaves during their early stage.
ga: NPK ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni niyenii titrii etɛ yɔɔ mli kɛha shishifãi, ŋmeii kɛ aduawai. Urea ji nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii titri koni akɛwo tsei adalɛ oya kɛha baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji yɛ shishijee mli.

english: Is it safe to mix weed killer with my crop fertilizer in the sprayer to save time?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ baafutu ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ jwɛi nɔ lɛ mli koni akɛ be akafite?

english: No, you should never mix weed killers directly with fertilizers in a spray tank. The chemicals can react badly, reducing the potency of both or burning your crops. They must be applied separately.
ga: Dabi, esaaa akɛ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii futuɔ jwɛi shwiemɔ tsɔne lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Tsofai baanyɛ afee nɔ ko ni ehiii kwraa. Amɛhaa nibii enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ loo amɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii shãa. esa akɛ akɛtsu nii srɔtoi

english: Why do farmers mix groundnuts and cassava together on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi futuɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts extract nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps the cassava grow larger roots. Meanwhile, groundnut plants cover the ground to reduce weed growth and keep the soil cool.
ga: Peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa shishifãi wuji. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ashɛreɔ Peanut tsei lɛ hu koni jwɛi lɛ akakwɛ̃ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Will my crops grow well if I plant two different varieties of maize seeds right next to each other?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji midu ŋmãa sɔrɔtoi enyɔ dumɔwui yɛ amɛhe?

english: Planting different maize varieties right next to each other causes cross-pollination. This can result in mixed, lower-quality cobs with irregular grains, so it is better to space different varieties apart.
ga: Abele henɔi srɔtoi ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ kɛ cross-pollination baa. Enɛ baanyɛ aha cob mixes ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmaa ni ejaaa aba. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ato srɔtoi srɔtoi lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ.

english: If I mix two different pest medicines together, will it make a stronger mix to kill caterpillars?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ahe nibii enyɔ futu mli lɛ, Ani akɛ tsofa ko ni mli wa fe no baafutu mli koni ekɛgbe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ?

english: Not necessarily. Mixing random pest medicines can cause chemical reactions that destroy their potency, harm your plants, or create dangerous fumes. It is safer to use the correct dosage of one effective product.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛfutuɔ amɛhe trukaa lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofa ko ni fiteɔ tsofa lɛ hewalɛ lɛ aba. Eyeɔ tsei awui loo ekɛ lasu ni yɔɔ oshara baa. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛ tsofa ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ falɛ ni sa pɛ baatsu nii.

english: How do I know if the pest medicine I am spraying is too strong or too weak for my young crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mikɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo ebɛ hewalɛ tsɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ?

english: If the medicine is too weak, pests will continue damaging your crops. If it is too strong, you will notice burnt brown patches on the leaves. Always follow the exact mixing ratios recommended on the package.
ga: Kɛji tsofa lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ baaya nɔ amɛfite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ni kɛji amɛhe wa tsɔ lɛ, obaana shãa he okadii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, nyiɛmɔ bɔ ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni atsɔɔ yɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: My pepper plants look weak and yellow; how do I know if they lack food or need medicine for disease?
ga: Mi pepper tsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ. Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ amɛyeee niyenii kpakpa loo tsofa he miihia amɛ?

english: Yellow leaves spread evenly across the plant usually mean a lack of nitrogen fertilizer or water. Yellow leaves with dark spots, leaf curling, or sticky residue indicate a pest or disease attack that requires specific crop medicine.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ gbɛ eshwa tso lɛ he fɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo nu bɛ. Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, baai ni ebɔle, loo nɔ ni eshwɛ ni kpɛtɛɔ he. Etsɔɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko loo hela ko ni biɔ tso tsofa pɔtɛɛ ko.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when I cut down all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight and intense heat. Leaving shade trees protects young cocoa from getting scorched, keeps the soil cool, and retains the moisture the roots need to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ ashi tsei lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo yibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ anáa ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa koni amɛhi shi lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off some of the young suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: When too many suckers grow together, they steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from the main tree. Removing extra suckers leaves only two or three strong ones, allowing the main tree to grow big, heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ he kome lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni jɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 2-3 pɛ ahi shi, ni no baaha tso titri lɛ adara ni etsɔ ŋmeii akuu agbo ko ni tsii.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize turning yellow even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or the soil is too waterlogged for the roots to breathe. Nitrogen is the main food element that keeps crop leaves deep green and growing well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu eyi sũ lɛ mli tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eha shishifãi lɛ amu. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni haa tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my pepper plants wilting and dying during the hot afternoon even though the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ?

english: This sudden wilting is often caused by soil-borne diseases like bacterial wilt or root rot. The disease damages the internal water pipes of the plant so it can no longer draw water up to its leaves, making it wilt despite wet soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli baa, tamɔ bacteria wilt loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ baa. Hela nɛɛ fiteɔ tsei amli nu paipii lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, anyɛɛɛ agbala nu kɛya baai lɛ anɔ dɔŋŋ. ni haa egbɔjɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ eji shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ

english: Why are my tomato plants growing many big green leaves but not producing any flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi fɔfɔi bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Applying too much nitrogen fertilizer makes tomato plants spend all their energy growing leaves instead of flowers. Tomatoes need balanced nutrients, particularly phosphorus and potassium, to produce flowers and fruit.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ baai moŋ fe fɔfɔi. Niyenii ni ja he miihia tomato. titri lɛ, fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium ni akɛfeɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the ground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava root rot happens when water gathers in the soil without proper drainage, creating conditions for fungi to attack the tubers. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni ŋmei lɛ baanyɛ atutua ŋmeii lɛ baa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: What causes tiny holes in my maize leaves and small worms hiding inside the stem?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni Akɛtee yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ anɔ?

english: These holes and worms are caused by stem borers or fall armyworms. The adult moths lay eggs on the leaves, and when the caterpillars hatch, they chew through the leaves and tunnel into the stalk to feed.
ga: Nɛkɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji nɔ ni stem borers loo fall armyworms kɛbaa. Akpɔlɔi ni eda lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ baai anɔ. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ Ekɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii amli koni ena niyenii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop all their flowers without producing any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ fɛɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ ko lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers if the flowers are not pollinated by beneficial tiny insects, or if the tree is stressed by severe dry weather, poor soil fertility, or pest attacks like mirids.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii efɔɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ loo kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi waa, shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ pollen lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up toward the sun so they can make food efficiently. It also keeps the leaves off damp soil, which prevents fungal diseases and leads to larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la bɔni afee ni amɛhoo nii jogbaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Enɛ baatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ anaa, ni ebaaha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ adara yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my crops with dry grass during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo he ni ebɔle he lɛ mli lɛ? Nibii ni akɛ jwɛi woɔ mli yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation so moisture stays longer in the ground, and stops weeds from growing and taking nutrients from your crop.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Maize needs a lot of food to build strong stalks, so when nitrogen is low, the plant pulls nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Niyenii babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛfee ŋmãa ni mli wa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ nitrogen lɛ faaa Tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi ŋtayaa hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up and roll inward during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ mli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in hot weather is the plant's natural shield against losing too much water. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun to conserve moisture inside its stems.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ nu babaoo ni efiteɔ lɛ he. Tsei haa hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi tso lɛ mli

english: Why does my yam crop produce huge vines and thick green leaves, but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ yɛ wain tsei wuji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen fertilizer early on, they spend all their energy growing tall leaves and vines instead of storing energy in the roots. Yams need potassium and phosphorus to expand their tubers underground.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ mra Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ baai kakadaji kɛ wain tsei moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baato amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Potassium kɛ phosphorus he miihia ŋmeii koni amɛkwɛ̃ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How can I tell if my cassava plant is starting to form roots underground or just growing leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava tso lɛ shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi loo ebɔi baai kwɛ̃mɔ kɛkɛ?

english: During the first three months, cassava focuses mainly on leaf and stem growth. Once the main stem starts branching out into a canopy shape, the plant shifts its energy down into storing starch in the root system.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ lɛ mli lɛ, Cassava kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ nɔ titri. Kɛji tso lɛ shishifã lɛ je shishi efo ni etsɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ Tsei tsakeɔ hewalɛ amɛwoɔ ŋmei ni akɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ mli.

english: Can I plant beans together with my maize on the same piece of land, or will they steal food from each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ? Aloo amɛbaaju niyenii kɛjɛ amɛhe?

english: Beans and maize actually help each other. Beans take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food in the soil, which feeds the maize, while the tall maize stalks give the bean vines something to climb on.
ga: Beans kɛ corn yeɔ ebuaa amɛhe diɛŋtsɛ. Beans jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji niyenii kɛha ŋmãa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmãa tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ naa nɔ ko ni amɛkwɔɔ.

english: What will happen to my tomato plants if I plant them very close to each other to save space?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni he akafite?

english: If tomato plants are crowded together, their leaves block sunlight from reaching each other, and air cannot blow through the plants. Moisture gets trapped on the leaves, which causes fungal diseases and yields fewer tomatoes.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tomato tsei lɛ efee ekome yɛ kuu mli lɛ Baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ tomato tsei lɛ amli. Fɛ̃i ni kpɛtɛɔ baai lɛ ahe lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa ni ehaa tomato yibii lɛ baa shi.

english: Which food crops can I plant that will produce a harvest quickly if I only have land for a few months?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu ni baawo yibii oya kɛji akɛ miyɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɔji fioo pɛ?

english: Short-season vegetables like okra, spinach (gboma), cucumber, and hot peppers mature within two to three months. These short-cycle crops allow you to harvest and sell quickly compared to long-term crops like cassava or plantain.
ga: Aduawai ni yeɔ be kuku tamɔ okra, spinach (boma), kukumba, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ nyɔji enyɔ loo etɛ mli. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nɛɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ni ohɔ̃ɔ oya kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo plantain he.

english: Why do my cowpea plants shed their flowers before the pod pods even start to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii lɛ po jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas drop their flowers when the plant experiences heavy heat stress, lack of water, or attack by tiny pests called thrips. Without enough moisture or protection from flower-eating insects, the plant drops flowers to save its strength.
ga: Cowpeas shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii amli. Atsɛɔ nakai feemɔ akɛ thrips hela. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo hebuu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe lɛ, Tso lɛ baashwie efɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni ehiɛ hewalɛ mli.

english: Why do large holes appear on my cabbage leaves overnight even though I do not see any insects on them during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bulɛi wuji je kpo yɛ mi-cabbage baai lɛ anɔ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ minaaa kooloi bibii komɛi yɛ kaabe baa lɛ nɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Cabbage caterpillars and armyworms are nocturnal feeders. They hide under the soil or deep inside the cabbage leaves during the hot daytime to avoid the sun and emerge at night to eat the fresh leaves.
ga: Kaabeji ŋmeii kɛ asraafoi ŋmeii ji ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii gbɛkɛ. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi loo amɛyaa shɔŋŋ yɛ kaaba baai amli yɛ gbii ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli koni hulu lɛ akashɛ amɛnɔ. ni amɛje kpo amɛbaye baai heei gbɛkɛ

english: Why do my plantain suckers take over a year to fruit while my neighbor's plantains flower much faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu lɛ heɔ nɔ ni fe afi dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ dumɔwui lɛ fɔɔ oya kwraa lɛ?

english: Plantain speed depends on the initial size and health of the sucker you plant, as well as soil organic matter. Choosing strong 'sword suckers' with narrow leaves and keeping the base mulched helps the plant establish roots faster and flower sooner.
ga: Bɔ ni ooodu oya lɛ damɔ shishijee ŋmeii ni oduɔ lɛ adalɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ nɔ. Okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ohala ‘klante sucker’ ni wa ni baai lɛ mli tseee, ni okwɛ shishitoo ni akɛ muji ewo nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni etswa shishifãi oya ni ewo fɔfɔi mra.

english: Why is it important to press the soil firmly around a seedling or cassava stem when I plant it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-cassava dumɔwui loo ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ ama shi shiŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Pressing the soil firmly removes air pockets around the stem and roots. This ensures the plant stays securely upright and allows the roots to easily absorb soil moisture so the seedling does not dry out and die.
ga: Kɛ́ onyɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi kɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ni ebaaha tso lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛjieɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mlɛo Koni dumɔwui lɛ akagbi ni amɛgboi.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in tall, thin, weak stems and small cobs with very few grains.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni dumɔwui fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ baa.

english: Does it matter which direction the buds are facing when I plant cassava stems in the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu ŋmei tso yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ fɔfɔi lɛ baakwɛ?

english: Yes, cassava stem buds must point upwards toward the sky so the shoots can grow straight up easily. Planting them upside down forces the sprouts to grow sideways or downwards, which stresses the plant and reduces your root yield.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ ŋmei lɛ shishifã lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ akwɛ ŋwɛi tɛ̃ɛ mlɛo. Kɛ́ adu lɛ kɛtee shishi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ kɛya afã loo kɛya shi. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ mli awa ni ebaaha shishifãi ni baa lɛ aba shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen nutrient or the field is waterlogged. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or improving drainage helps the leaves get their healthy green color back to make food for the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli loo nu eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea ni akɛaawo mli loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba koni ekɛha tso lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my tomato plants turning brown and dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Lower leaves turning brown and falling off is often caused by fungal diseases from rain or irrigation water splashing soil onto the leaves. Clearing the lowest leaves and mulching the base helps keep the plant healthy.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi, bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ nugbɔ loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni shwieɔ sũ nɔ baa lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ ajie baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ ni aha shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I clear weeds from around my crops while they are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Miŋmɔshi nibii be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients before your crop can reach them, which starves your young plants during their most critical growing stage.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ odumɔwui lɛ yɛ amɛdalɛ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my crop is getting too much water from the rain or irrigation?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu babaoo kɛmiijɛ nugbɔ loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ mli?

english: When crops get too much water, their leaves often turn pale green or yellow, soft rot can develop near the base, and the roots turn dark and slimy because they cannot breathe in wet soil.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nu babaoo lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. Ebaanyɛ egbo yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he. Ni shishifãi lɛ yɛ ediŋŋ ni amɛhe tse ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ.

english: When is the best time of day for me to apply water or liquid fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ nu loo nu ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: It is best to water or feed crops early in the morning or late in the afternoon when it is cool. This allows the roots to drink before the hot sun evaporates the water away.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha onibii lɛ nu loo oha amɛ niyenii leebi loo shwane be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ feɔ lasu.

english: Planting the same crop in the same spot every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the dirt, leading to poorer harvests over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when the crops are still very young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tso lɛ ji gbekɛ fioo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which acts as essential food for the crop, or that excessive rainfall is drowning the plant's roots.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmãa lɛ. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli.

english: Should I apply chemical fertilizer directly on seeds when I put them in the soil?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ awo dumɔwui lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛ́ mikɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: No, putting fertilizer directly on seeds can burn and ruin them. It is best to wait until the seeds sprout and form roots before applying fertilizer nearby.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo dumɔwui lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha amɛshã ni efite amɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛwo shishifãi dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: I sprayed pesticide on my crops, but the insects are still eating the leaves. Why is it not working?
ga: Mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ. Shi ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ baai lɛ lolo. Mɛni hewɔ etsuuu nii?

english: Pest treatments fail if they are sprayed at the wrong time of day, mixed incorrectly with water, washed away by sudden rain, or if the chemical is not meant for that specific insect.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsaa tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ baafee nɔ ni ehiii kɛji akɛ afɔse amɛ yɛ be ni esaaa mli. Nu ni nugbɔ lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa lɛ futumɔ ni ejaaa loo kɛji akɛ afeee nakai kooloo pɔtɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my stored dried maize grains get full of small holes and turn into dust after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni etsɔɔ sũ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: This destruction is caused by tiny insects called grain weevils. To stop them, store fully dried grains in sealed airtight bags or treat them with safe grain-protecting storage dust.
ga: Kooloi bibii ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ hiɛkpatamɔ nɛɛ baa. Atsɛɔ nakai dumɔwui lɛ. Bɔni afee ni akpa amɛ Okɛ dumɔwui ni egbi kwraa lɛ ato kotoku ko ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli lɛ mli. Aloo okɛ sũ ni abua naa lɛ atsu nii ni okɛbu dumɔwui lɛ ahe shweshweeshwe.

english: Young cocoa seedlings dry out and die under full hot sun. Plantains grow rapidly with big leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and moist soil for the cocoa seedlings.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha kookoo dumɔwui lɛ hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ.

english: Can I plant cassava and groundnuts together in the same field?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, groundnuts put natural nitrogen back into the soil which nourishes the land, while cassava grows taller, allowing both crops to share space effectively.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii kɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli, ni no haa sũ lɛ hewalɛ. be mli ni ŋmei daa lɛ Enɛ haa tsei enyɔ lɛ jaa he ko jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting maize when the rains begin in Ghana?
