ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mije ŋmãa dumɔ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ yɛ Ghana?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first rain. Wait until the rain becomes steady and thoroughly wets the soil deep down so the seeds do not dry out during a sudden hot spell.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ anɛ fiofio ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ akagbi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ.

english: Dropping leaves is a natural survival trick. Cassava sheds its leaves during hot and dry weather to save water inside its roots and protect the plant from drying out completely.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ teemɔŋ sane ni haa mɔ hiɔ shi. Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ ni egbi koni nu ahi shishifãi lɛ amli ni ebu tso lɛ he koni ekagbi.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high, when the soil drops below required moisture levels, or when the plant gets too much leafy fertilizer instead of fruit-producing nutrients.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ baa shi kɛyashɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ataoɔ lɛ shishi Aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ naa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaana niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ aduawai lɛ amli.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than the food crops I planted after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe niyenii ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants that are naturally tough and well-adapted to local soil, allowing them to absorb water and soil food faster than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji tso ko ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni eyɛ shiŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa amɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni amɛ duɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight when they are small. Without shade trees or plantains growing nearby to block the intense sun, their delicate leaves scorch and turn yellow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ beni amɛdarako lɛ. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei bibii ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ koni amɛtsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa lɛ bɛ lɛ, Amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ hu shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why is my maize growing tall with light yellow leaves instead of dark green ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ miida ni ekwɛ̃ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Light yellow leaves on maize are usually a sign that the soil is low in nitrogen. Nitrogen is the key nutrient plants use to build strong green leaves and fuel healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛha amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is causing my cocoa pods to turn black and rot before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, dark environments. Clearing weeds and pruning extra branches helps air and sunlight dry out the pods to keep them healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni duŋ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛjieɔ jwɛi kɛ tsei ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la haa tsei lɛ agbiɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ kpakpa.

english: Why do small caterpillars keep chewing holes in the leaves and ears of my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii sumɔɔ ni amɛye bu yɛ mi baai kɛ mi ŋmãa toi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, pests that hide inside the central leaves of maize plants during the day and feed aggressively on the leaves and young grains at night.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai amli yɛ gbi mli, ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii kɛ dumɔwui gbɛkɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot or when they do not get enough water. Heat stress stops the flowers from pollinating successfully to form fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo ahaaa amɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Dɔlɛ tsiɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are my cassava roots growing so thin even though the tops look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ nɛkɛ lɛ? Yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ?

english: When cassava plants are planted too close together, their underground roots compete for soil space, water, and food, which prevents the tubers from expanding properly.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko, shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ niyenii he akaŋshii mli, ni no haaa ŋmei lɛ mli alɛɛ kɛyashɛ bɔ ni sa lɛ he.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop during the afternoon sun even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In extreme afternoon heat, pepper leaves lose water faster than the roots can drink it from the wet soil. The plant wilts temporarily to protect itself and recovers once the sun sets.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe he ni ehiɛ aba ehe nɔ kɛji hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Why did seeds saved from my last maize harvest yield smaller cobs than the original store-bought seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli lɛ wo ŋmãa bibioo fe shishijee dumɔwui ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ?

english: Store-bought hybrid seeds are specially bred from two strong parents to give high yields, but the seeds produced from that harvest lose those special traits and produce weaker plants in the next generation.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ fɔɔ fɔlɔi enyɔ ni he wa lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Shi dumɔwui ni jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my yam vines turning dark and dying early before the tubers grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ feɔ duŋ ni egboɔ oya dani bulbs lɛ daa lɛ?

english: This is often caused by a fungal disease called anthracnose that attacks yam vines. When the leaves die early, the plant stops making the food it needs to enlarge the underground tuber.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose ni tutuaa ŋmei wain tsei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ́ baai lɛ gboi oya Tso lɛ kpaɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ feemɔ koni ekɛkwɛ̃ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so fast in my field right after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mijie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds can lie dormant buried under the soil for years. When you clear the land, sunlight and rain reach the bare soil, triggering those dormant seeds to sprout immediately.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ awɔ. Afu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi afii babaoo. Kɛji ojie jɛmɛ lɛ Hulu kɛ nugbɔ baashɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, dumɔwui ni ekã shi lɛ kwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and shriveling up in the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. They need shade plants like plantains planted alongside them to act as natural umbrellas until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ adamɔ hulu muu lɛ fɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my maize crops turn pale yellow when there is continuous heavy rain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa be fɛɛ be yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive rain floods the soil and suffocates plant roots by cutting off air. When roots cannot breathe, they are unable to take up essential nitrogen nutrients from the soil, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Beni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu Amɛnyɛŋ amɛjie nitrogen niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: How can I test if the seed maize I bought will sprout before I plant my whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ dani madu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: You can do a simple germination test by putting 10 seeds inside a damp piece of cloth for a few days. If at least 8 seeds sprout roots, your seeds are good quality and ready for full planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee shweremɔ he kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Obaanyɛ ofee enɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni okɛaawo mama ni mli efɔ mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɛ hoo lɛ, dumɔwui 8 kwɛ̃ lɛ, no lɛ odumɔwui lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ni ofee klalo akɛ obaadu yɛ jɛmɛ fɛɛ.

english: Leaf curling and yellow patches are signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whiteflies or passed on through infected stem cuttings used during planting.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ woɔ loo amɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be mli ni aduɔ nii lɛ amli lɛ mli.

english: Crops feed on nutrients in the soil every growing season. Without adding poultry manure, compost, or fertilizers, or rotating crops like beans and groundnuts, the soil becomes depleted and exhausted.
ga: Tsei yeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ daa be mli ni amɛdaraa. Ni akɛ kooloi ashishifã, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii fataaa he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaagbɔjɔ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight, leading to thin stalks and very small or empty maize cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa nu he akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii waa loo amɛfeɔ efolo.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures get too hot, when the soil dries out completely during flowering, or when there is too much chemical nitrogen fertilizer in the soil.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli loo be mli ni nitrogen babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and stronger than my crops right after the first rains arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ nɛɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with deep root systems designed to quickly absorb moisture and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops, which is why early weeding is necessary.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni afee koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ.

english: How can I tell that my yam tubers under the ground are mature enough to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Yams are ready for harvesting when the leaves and stems above the ground naturally turn yellow and dry up at the end of the rainy season.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛ́ baai kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee.

english: Why are small insects creating holes and powder inside my stored dried maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii feɔ bu kɛ sũ yɛ mi-ŋmãa ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Grain weevils attack stored maize if the grains were not dried completely to a hard state before storage, or if the storage barn was not properly cleaned of old pests.
ga: Dumɔwui amli ŋmeii tutuaa ŋmãa ni ato lɛ kɛji akɛ agbiko dumɔwui lɛ kwraa kɛyashi amɛhe wa dani akɛto. Aloo kɛji akɛ ajieee tsɛŋemɔ helai momoi ni yɔɔ tsũ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do my crops consume fertilizer, and why is it called crop food?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli? Ni mɛni hewɔ atsɛɔ lɛ tsei aniyenii lɛ?

english: Crops absorb dissolved nutrients from the soil through their root systems, using them to build stems, leaves, and fruits just like humans use food to grow strong. Fertilizer supplies essential nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium that soil naturally loses over time.
ga: Tsei tsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛjieɔ niyenii ni mli ewo muji kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Akɛtsuɔ nii kɛmaa tsei ashishifãi, baai, kɛ aduawai, taakɛ bɔ ni adesai kɛ niyenii tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ naitrɔjin, fɔsfɔs, kɛ potasium. ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be ni sa mli

english: How do I know if my crops are hungry or lacking nutrients?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ loo niyenii ni esaaa amɛyeɔ?

english: Crops show hunger signs through their leaves and overall growth. Yellowing leaves usually mean a lack of nitrogen, stunted stems point to low phosphorus, and dried or burnt leaf edges indicate a shortage of potassium.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ hɔmɔ he okadii kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai kɛ amɛdalɛ fɛɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. Tso lɛ mli tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs faaa. Ni baai lɛ ahe ni egbi loo eshã lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ potassium faaa.

english: What is the benefit of placing fertilizer directly near the root base instead of scattering it all over the farm?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shishitoo lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe ni aaagbɛ ashwã ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Placing fertilizer near the roots ensures your target crop absorbs the nutrients directly before weeds can take them or heavy rains wash them away, saving you money and fertilizer.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa tso ni ataoɔ lɛ lɛ nyɛɔ eŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ dani jwɛi lɛ boteɔ mli loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ amɛ. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okɛ shika kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii toɔ.

english: Can farm animal manure work as food for my crops the same way chemical fertilizer does?
ga: Ani ŋmɔ mli kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ aye nii tamɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, organic manure feeds your crops by slowly releasing nutrients into the soil while also improving the soil's ability to hold moisture and stay healthy during dry periods.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ haa onibii lɛ niyenii kɛtsɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ejieɔ fiofio kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: What is the benefit of planting food crops like plantain or cassava alongside my young cash crops?
ga: Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ Kɛfata mi shika ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ahe lɛ, mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni jɛɔ mli baa?

english: Intercropping provides you with immediate food and income while your cash crop matures. Tall food crops like plantains also provide essential shade to shield delicate young cash crops like cocoa from strong sunlight.
ga: Intercropping haa onáa niyenii kɛ shika amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ be mli ni oshika ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ. Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛlɛ tamɔ plantains lɛ hu haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni akɛbu shika ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ kookoo he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he.

english: Why do extension officers advise us not to plant the same crop on the exact same plot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔkadu ŋmɔshi nibii komekomei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting different crops each season breaks pest and disease cycles that build up in the soil and prevents the ground from losing all of its specific nutrients.
ga: Nibii srɔtoi ni aduɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. ni etsĩ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekafite niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ.

english: When is the right time to give food or fertilizer to my crops during their growth?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Apply fertilizer when crops are actively growing—usually a few weeks after germination or transplanting and again during flowering—so the plants can use the extra energy to produce high yields.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ—bei pii lɛ, yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ loo amɛdu amɛhe lɛ sɛɛ. kɛ agbɛnɛ hu yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ kroko atsu nii ni amɛkɛfee yibii babaoo.

english: What basic safety rules should I follow to protect my own health when applying agrochemicals on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ shweshweeshwefeemɔ he mlai titrii esa akɛ makwɛ nɔ koni mabu mihewalɛ he kɛ́ mikɛ agrochemicals miitsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Always wear personal protective equipment like rubber boots, long sleeves, gloves, and a nose mask when spraying to prevent toxic chemicals from absorbing into your skin or being inhaled.
ga: Womɔ nibii ni buɔ ohe tamɔ rɔbɔt atadei, nine kakadaŋŋ agboi, glɔvs kɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa hiɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛji ooshwie tsofa lɛ. Enɛ ji koni tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei akabote hewolo lɛ mli loo akamu.

english: How do cover crops help protect my land and main crops?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni abu mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cover crops act like a protective blanket over the ground, suppressing weed growth, keeping the soil cool and moist, and preventing heavy rains from washing away fertile topsoil.
ga: Tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Tsi jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. ni etsĩ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Where should I store unused farm chemicals to protect my family and livestock at home?
ga: Nɛgbɛ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai ni akɛtsuuu nii lɛ ato koni mikɛbu miweku kɛ kooloi ahe yɛ shia?

english: Store chemicals in their original locked containers inside a well-ventilated shed or wooden box, far away from children, farm animals, stored food, and drinking water sources.
ga: Kɛ tsofai lɛ ato shishijee tsɛnsi ni aŋã mli lɛ mli yɛ tsũ loo adeka ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli mli, ni okɛ gbekɛbii kɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi akabɔ he. niyenii kɛ nu ni anuɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ

english: Why do experienced farmers advise me to plant plantains alongside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu plantains yɛ mi-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct heat. Plantains grow fast and produce broad leaves that shade the young cocoa plants from harsh sunlight while keeping the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shãa oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on instead of just spreading across the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to make food for tuber growth. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground to capture light while preventing fungal diseases caused by damp soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii kɛha tuber lɛ dalɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ tsei ahe tsei kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni enyɛ emɔ la kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the rest of the plant stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni baai ni eshwɛ lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign of nitrogen shortage in the soil. The plant moves nitrogen from older leaves to feed newer leaves at the top to stay alive.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni amɛha baai heei ahi nɔ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow lots of green leaves but very few pods when I give them strong fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ wo mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas naturally capture their own nitrogen from the air. Adding extra nitrogen fertilizer tricks the plant into putting all its energy into growing foliage instead of producing flowers and beans.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ afite ehewalɛ fɛɛ yɛ baai ni miida lɛ ahe. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ngma.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long heat spell before regular rains start. Sprouted seeds will dry up and die in the hot soil if sustained rains do not follow immediately.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ jeɔ shishi. Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ eyaaa nɔ enɛɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground when heavy rains flood my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eyi miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. Excess standing water chokes the roots and creates an ideal environment for water molds and bacteria to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nu ni ekã shi fe nine lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yɔɔ nu mli lɛ koni amɛtutua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfite.

english: What causes the leaves of my pepper plants to curl upward and turn small and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on leaf sap and spreading viruses. The plant's leaves wrinkle as a reaction to insect damage and viral infection.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ amli nu kɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ akɛ nɔ ni jɛɔ kooloo mli nibii ni fiteɔ kɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ amli baa.

english: Why do weeds on my farm grow faster and stronger than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to local soil. They steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients much more aggressively than domesticated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa fe tsei ni yɔɔ shia lɛ.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when temperatures become extremely hot or when water supply drops suddenly. The plant sheds flowers to conserve moisture and protect itself from stress.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ba shi trukaa. Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ haomɔ he.

english: Why do I need to raise my vegetable beds above ground level before planting garden eggs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo mi-vegetables tsei lɛ anɔ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmeii yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Mounded or raised beds improve soil drainage, keeping plant roots out of standing water while making it easier for young roots to spread out into loose, warm soil.
ga: Saji ni ama nɔ loo awo nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa tsei shishifãi ehiɛɛɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa shishifãi bibii lɛ akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni etse ehe nɔ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck the plant's sap, or by a virus carried by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaves from curling and stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa ni ekɛ helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in humid, shady conditions during the heavy rainy season. Clearing weeds and pruning shade trees to let sunlight into the farm helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Tsei ni ajieɔ jwɛi kɛ amɛhe ni afoɔ koni hulu la abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ amli jwɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes my tomato fruits to turn black at the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-tomato lɛ miifee ediŋŋ yɛ shishigbɛ dani ekwɛ̃?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant lacks calcium or receives uneven watering, which prevents the crop from absorbing necessary nutrients from the soil while the fruit is developing.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ calcium loo akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the maize crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is essential for leafy green growth, so applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea can restore the green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he hiaa waa kɛha baa eŋɔli lɛ dalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How do I know if my farmland needs chemical fertilizer or if animal manure is enough?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia tsofa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: If your soil is sandy or heavily farmed without rest, it loses nutrients quickly. Animal manure improves soil structure over time, while chemical fertilizers give quick nutrients; using both together usually yields the best results.
ga: Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ ji ŋã loo okwaayeli babaoo ni hejɔɔmɔ bɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ laajeɔ oya. Koolooi ashishifãi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii yaa hiɛ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ tsu nii ekome lɛ, nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ baa.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over easily when strong winds blow during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that struggle to hold heavy bunches in soft, wet soil. Staking the plants with strong wooden poles or planting them deeper in loose soil prevents them from toppling over during storms.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛmɔ panicles ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni wa ŋmɛ tso lɛ loo okɛdu shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekagbee shi yɛ ahum be mli.

english: Why do my cowpea crops grow plenty of green leaves but yield very few beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmei fioo pɛ ewoɔ lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes leguminous plants like cowpeas focus on growing leafy stems instead of flowers and seeds. Cowpeas naturally make their own nitrogen, so high-nitrogen fertilizers should be avoided.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui. Cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ adebɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my okra plants before turning into okra pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ okra tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛtsɔɔ okra ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flower drop occurs when the plant is stressed by extreme dry heat, irregular watering, or attacks from pests like thrips. Ensuring steady soil moisture and protecting the flowers from insects helps the pods form properly.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa ni haa tsei lɛ gbiɔ lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ thrips ni tutuaa amɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ kooloi bibii ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin even after many months in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa yɛ be mli ni mikɛ nyɔji babaoo ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots remain small if planted in hard, compacted soil or during long dry spells without adequate rain, as the plant cannot store starch efficiently when under severe heat or drought stress.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ nɔ loo yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei nyɛŋ ato starch jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ he haomɔ mli.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up early before the yam tubers are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ miiho oya dani ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Premature drying of yam vines is often caused by leaf spot diseases or attacks from tiny root worms called nematodes. Protecting the leaves early and using clean seed yams ensures the tuber has time to mature fully underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa mli hela loo shishifãi bibii ni tutuaa amɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbimɔ baa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes Abuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ amɛgbekɛbiiashi Ni akɛ yams ni he tse tsuɔ nii haa bulbs lɛ be ni amɛdaraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: What is the main difference between the 'aggreko' oil palm and the local palm trees I see around?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ ‘aggreko’ mu tso lɛ kɛ maŋ lɛ mli tsei ni minaa yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ ateŋ?

english: Aggreko' is an improved palm variety bred specifically to yield much more oil with a thinner shell, whereas local varieties grow very tall, take longer to fruit, and produce far less oil per bunch.
ga: Aggreko’ ji tso ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ palm tso ko ni atsɔse lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni ekɛ mu babaoo ni eshishifã lɛ mli tseee lɛ aba. yɛ be mli ni maŋ lɛ mli henɔi lɛ daraa waa. Eheɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii. ni amɛjieɔ mu fioo kwraa yɛ kuu kome mli

english: Why do buyers at the market pay higher prices for some oil palm harvests than others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmei fɔ komɛi ahe nyɔmɔ babaoo fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Buyers pay higher prices for high-yielding varieties like 'aggreko' because oil processors extract much more oil from their fruit bunches compared to local or mixed palm varieties.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo tamɔ ‘aggreko’ lɛ nyɔmɔ babaoo ejaakɛ mɛi ni feɔ mu lɛ jieɔ mu babaoo kɛjɛɔ aduawai akui lɛ amli kɛ akɛtoɔ maŋ lɛ mli loo tsofai ni akɛfee mu lɛ ahe.

english: Is it a good idea for me to plant a mix of local and improved palm seeds together on my farm?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ mafee ekome kɛdu maŋ lɛ mli ŋmei dumɔwui kɛ ŋmei dumɔwui ni asaa amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting a mix of seeds leads to unequal fruit growth and lower overall crop value, as buyers usually offer a lower flat price for mixed harvests rather than paying premium rates for pure high-quality varieties.
ga: Dumɔwui ni efutu ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ aduawai daalɛ ni ejaaa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ jara baa shi baa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛkɛ jara ni ato ni baa shi aha kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfutuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooowo nyɔmɔ ni fe fɛɛ kɛha purebreds ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How can I be sure I am buying high-yielding crop varieties before planting them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ miheɔ tsei srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo dani miduɔ?

english: Young crop seedlings look very similar, so you should buy certified seedlings directly from approved agricultural nurseries rather than picking wild seeds or unverified local varieties.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ tamɔ amɛhe waa. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ohe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ kɛjɛ okwaayeli hei ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Mohu ɔ, hlami koo mi loo ma a mi dumɔwui nɛ a hyɛ we mi saminya.

english: Do improved crop varieties like 'aggreko' palm take less time to produce fruit than local ones?
ga: Ani tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ, tamɔ ‘aggreko’ tso lɛ heɔ be fioo dani amɛwoɔ yibii fe tsei srɔtoi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, improved varieties are developed to reach maturity faster, often bearing fruit in about three years, whereas traditional local varieties can take up to seven years to yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, afee tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. Bei pii lɛ, amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ aaafee afii etɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni maŋbii akutseiaŋ tsofai srɔtoi lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii kpawo dani amɛwo yibii.

english: Why should I spend more money to buy improved crop seeds if local seeds are free?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafite shika babaoo kɛhe dumɔwui ni asaa amɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui yɛ?

english: While local seeds cost nothing upfront, improved seeds produce bigger yields and higher-quality crops that earn significantly more money at harvest, easily covering the initial seed cost.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, shika ko bɛ kɛha maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ. Shi dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shika babaoo baa kɛji akpa. ni ekɛ shishijee dumɔwui ahe nyɔmɔwoo lɛ haa mlɛo.

english: Why do my local palm trees get so tall that harvesting becomes dangerous?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mimaŋ lɛ mli ŋmei tsei lɛ kɛlɛ waa akɛ amɛkpamɔ ji oshara lɛ?

english: Local palm trees naturally put most of their energy into growing tall trunks, while improved varieties remain shorter for many years, making fruit harvesting much safer and easier.
ga: Akutso lɛ mli tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ. yɛ be mli ni henɔi ni atsake amɛ lɛ baahi shi kuku afii babaoo. Enɛ haa aduawai akpamɔ feɔ shweshweeshwe kwraa ni efeɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do palm oil mill owners prefer processing 'aggreko' fruit over local palm fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni yɔɔ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma ŋmɔ mli lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛtsu ‘aggreko’ aduawai ahe nii fe maŋ lɛ mli tsofa-kɛ-ŋma aduawai lɛ?

english: Oil mills prefer 'aggreko' fruit because it has a thick, fleshy pulp with high oil content and a very thin shell, which means less waste and more oil during extraction.
ga: Mu tsei sumɔɔ ‘aggreko’ aduawai yɛ amɛloo ni mli tse kɛ mu ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ mli kɛ amɛhewolo ni mli tse waa lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, jwɛi fioo pɛ kɛ mu babaoo yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ lɛ.

english: Do high-yielding crop varieties need extra fertilizer compared to local crops?
ga: Ani tsei srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ biɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi awo mli kɛ akɛto maŋ lɛ mli tsei ahe?

english: Yes, because high-yielding varieties produce many more fruits, they draw more nutrients from the soil and need regular feeding with fertilizer to maintain high production.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ tsei srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aha amɛ daa koni amɛná yibii babaoo.

english: Should I separate my crop harvest by variety before selling it to buyers?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majara miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli yɛ srɔtoi lɛ anaa dani mahɔ̃ɔ maha mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ?

english: Yes, sorting your harvest allows you to sell premium varieties like 'aggreko' separately for a top-tier price, instead of letting lower-quality local crops drag down the price of the whole load.
ga: Hɛɛ, onibii ni okɛbaa lɛ mligbalamɔ haa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ nibii srɔtoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ tamɔ ‘aggreko’ srɔtoi kɛha jara ni nɔ kwɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha maŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehiii lɛ agbala ŋmɔshi nii lɛ fɛɛ jara shi lɛ,

english: Officer, what is a greenhouse, and how can it help my crops grow better than planting directly in the open field?
ga: Ofisa Mɛni ji ŋmɔ mli nibii? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ fe ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: A greenhouse is a plastic or glass house that protects plants from heavy rains, harsh sunlight, and pests, creating a controlled environment where crops can grow safely all year round.
ga: Greenhouses ji plastic greenhouses loo greenhouses ni buɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe, ni ehaa shihilɛ ko ni akudɔɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe afi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Will putting my crops inside a plastic greenhouse make them too hot during the afternoon sun?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ plastic greenhouse mli lɛ baaha amɛdɔ fe nine yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli?

english: Greenhouses can trap heat, but good greenhouses are designed with side vents, netting, or shade cloths to let air flow through, keeping the temperature comfortable for crops.
ga: Greenhouses baanyɛ ato dɔlɛ. Shi afee greenhouse kpakpa ni akɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai, ŋtayaai, loo mama ni akɛwoɔ ŋtayaai amli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ mli. Ha tsei lɛ ahi he ko ni hulutsoo be lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops dry up and stop growing during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During high heat, plants lose water faster through their leaves than their roots can drink from the dry soil, causing them to wilt and pause their growth to survive.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekpaa dalɛ be kukuoo ko bɔni afee ni ehi shi.

english: Can crop seeds brought from cooler countries survive in our hot weather here in Ghana?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni akɛbaajɛ maji ni mli ejɔ lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ wɔ Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Some foreign crops struggle with local heat and rain, but they can succeed if you shade them, water them regularly, or grow them inside a greenhouse to protect them from extreme weather.
ga: Esa akɛ maŋsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi kɛ maŋ lɛ mli latsaa kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ akpe. Shi tsei nɛɛ baanyɛ aye omanye kɛji okɛ hulutsoo ha amɛhe. Nu daa Aloo akwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli koni akɛbu tsei ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai ahe.

english: Why do the leaves on my plants turn yellow and drop off after a heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Too much rainwater fills all the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the plant roots so they cannot absorb food, which turns the leaves yellow and causes them to drop.
ga: Nugbɔ nu ni fa babaoo lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyashɛɔ he ko ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: What should I check first if my crops are not growing well even though I planted them properly?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ makwɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni midu amɛ jogbaŋŋ po sɛɛ?

english: Check your water supply, soil nutrients, and signs of pests or diseases, as any problem with these three things will slow down crop growth immediately.
ga: Kwɛmɔ nu jɛɛhe lɛ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ahe okadii. Ejaakɛ naagbai ni kɔɔ nibii etɛ nɛɛ ahe lɛ baaha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: If my crop harvest fails this season, does it mean I should stop planting that crop entirely?
ga: Kɛji mikpamɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii yɛ be nɛɛ mli Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ makpa nakai tso lɛ dumɔ kwraa?

english: No, crop failure usually means something went wrong with the weather, water, or planting method, which can be fixed next season by adjusting how and when you plant.
ga: Dabi, bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehiii lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nɔ ko etɔ̃ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ, nu loo gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii lɛ mli. Abaanyɛ atsake enɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli kɛtsɔ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii kɛ be ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ nɔ.

english: How can I know if my crops are struggling because of the soil quality in my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miipiŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ?

english: If crops have pale leaves, thin stems, or slow growth despite getting enough rain and sunlight, it means the soil lacks the proper nutrients they need to grow.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, eshishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ, loo edaa blɛoo yɛ nugbɔ kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni sa ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Do all crops need strong direct sunlight all day long to produce a good harvest?
ga: Ani tsei fɛɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai?

english: No, while some crops love full sun, delicate crops like tomatoes and young seedlings prefer light shade during the hottest parts of the day to avoid leaf damage.
ga: Dabi, eyɛ mli akɛ tsei komɛi sumɔɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa moŋ. Shi tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ tomato kɛ tsei bibii sumɔɔ hulutsoo yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkafite baai lɛ.

english: Is it better for me to water my crops early in the morning or during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mitsei lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo shwane be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: It is best to water early in the morning so the plants can drink before the sun heats up, preventing quick evaporation and protecting leaves from heat stress.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha tso lɛ nu leebi koni enu dani hulu lɛ adɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ la ni hoɔ oya lɛ naa ni ebuɔ baai ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: How do I know if the stool land given to me by my local chief is good for planting crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni maŋ onukpa ko kɛha mi lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: Good farming land usually has dark, rich topsoil that holds moisture well without staying flooded after heavy rain. You can test your land by digging a small hole to see if the soil is loose and dark, which means it has good organic nutrients for young plant roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni akɛtsuɔ okwaayeli he nii yɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni mli edɔ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni nu shwieee nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ oka shikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ bu bibioo ko ni oootse lɛ nɔ. Koni ana kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etse ni edɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsei bibii ashishifãi.

english: Will using a tractor to plow my land harm my crops or help them grow better?
ga: Ani trakta ni mikɛbaatsu nii kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui loo ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Plowing breaks up hard soil so plant roots can easily spread out and absorb water and fertilizer. However, if done too deeply or too often, it can destroy the natural structure of the soil, so tractor work must be done carefully based on your soil type.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ gbálaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya ni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Shi, kɛji akɛ afee lɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ loo shii abɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, traktɔ nitsumɔ biɔ hiɛdɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ henɔ naa.

english: Planting in straight rows makes it much easier to walk through your field, control weeds, apply fertilizer, and use equipment. Scattering seeds leads to crowded plants that fight each other for food and light, making field care very difficult.
ga: Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ aaatsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli, akudɔ jwɛi, awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii, ni akɛ nibii atsu nii. Dumɔwui ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ haa tsei akui ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii kɛ la baa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔ mli kwɛmɔ feɔ nɔ ni wa waa.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and yield small fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: Plants need space, sunlight, water, and soil nutrients to feed themselves. When they are planted too close together, they shade each other out and fight over the same soil nutrients, causing weak growth and poor yields.
ga: He ko he hiaa tsei, hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ amɛhe. Kɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛhaa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛyeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kome lɛ nɔŋŋ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi baa.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my seeds after clearing my bush?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ maje dumɔwui ashishi beni ajie jwɛi lɛ amli sɛɛ?

english: Seeds need reliable soil moisture to germinate and establish strong roots. In Ghana, it is best to plant right after the first major rains of the season start, when the soil stays moist enough to support early growth without drying out.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa. Yɛ Ghana lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔi wuji ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ je shishi pɛ, beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua mra be mli dalɛ ni egbiŋ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops, and how does that affect my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ? Ni te no saa mikpamɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that naturally adapted to survive and take over land quickly. If left unchecked, weeds steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight from your crops, which starves the crops and significantly reduces your harvest.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi ni amɛye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ, ni ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi waa.

english: How can I tell if my crops are hungry and need extra fertilizer during their growth?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: When crops lack nutrients, their leaves often lose their deep green color, turn pale yellow, or grow very slowly. Applying fertilizer at the right growth stage restores their health so they can produce strong leaves and big fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ebaa lɛ baaje amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli ni tsuɔ waa lɛ mli. tsakeɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo edaa blɛoo waa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni eha baai ni wa kɛ aduawai wuji aba.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops curling up and turning brown before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and browning are common signs that pests are sucking sap from the leaves or a disease is spreading due to humidity. Catching these signs early allows you to treat the affected plants before the entire field damaged.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ji okadii ni afɔɔ namɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ miinu nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ loo akɛ hela miigbɛ eshwa yɛ ŋmɔtɔ hewɔ. Okadii nɛɛ ni ooomɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otsaa tsei ni ena hela lɛ dani jɛmɛ fɛɛ fiteɔ.

english: How can I tell the exact time my crops are mature enough to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Crops give visual signs when mature, such as leaves drying naturally, grains hardening, or skin colors changing from green to yellow or red. Harvesting too early results in underdeveloped crops, while harvesting too late causes rotting or pest damage.
ga: Tsei baaha okadii ni anaa beni amɛdaraa lɛ, tamɔ baai ni egbiɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Dumɔwui lɛ wa. aloo hewolo lɛ su tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli nɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo etsuru nɔ. Nikpamɔ mra tsɔ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyaaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ baa. yɛ be mli ni ŋmaakpamɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ lɛ kɛ fitemɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai fiteɔ nii baa.

english: Why do my crops spoil or rot so quickly right after I harvest them from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ fiteɔ loo efiteɔ oya beni mikpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested crops spoil fast if they are bruised during harvesting, left lying in the direct sun, or packed into hot bags while wet. Storing harvested produce gently in a cool, shaded, and well-ventilated space helps them stay fresh.
ga: Nibii ni akpa ehee lɛ baafite oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔ be mli. Shi ni hulu la lɛ ashɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. loo akɛwoɔ kotoku ni mli edɔ lɛ mli be mli ni edɔ Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni akpa lɛ to he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hu yɔɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehaa ehe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Will planting my maize seeds very close together give me more harvest from my small piece of land?
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui ni madu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baaye abua mi ni makpa babaoo kɛjɛ he bibioo ko. mi nɔ loo daabi

english: Planting maize too close together causes the plants to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in thin, weak stalks and tiny or empty cobs, which actually reduces your total harvest compared to proper spacing.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. loo efolo Enɛ haa okpamɔ fɛɛ baa shi kɛ akɛto gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ he.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to produce fruit after I transplant them to my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii beni mikɛ amɛ tee miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers delay fruiting if the planting hole is too small, if weeds steal nutrients from their shallow roots, or if old roots were not properly trimmed before planting to encourage new growth.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baaha amɛwo yibii sɛɛ kɛji akɛ bu ni adu lɛ mli lɛ faaa tsɔ. Kɛji jwɛi ju niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ amɛshishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ amli loo kɛji akɛ afolɔɔɔ shishifãi momo lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani aduɔ koni ewo shweremɔ hee he hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil or poor root health from excess water. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps restore their dark green color and growth energy.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kpakpa yɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni mli kwɔ kɛ hewalɛ ni haa edaa lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava roots small and woody even though the stems and leaves look very big and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛji tsei eyɛ mli akɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛji ŋmɔji moŋ lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or excess shade, the cassava plant puts all its energy into leaf and stem growth instead of storing starch in the tubers below the ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ hulutsoo. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai kɛ tsei ni miida lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ ashikishaŋ lɛ baato ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ,.

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they experience stress from dry weather, hot sun, poor soil nutrients, or damage from insects like mirids. Providing shade trees and adequate moisture helps the tree retain its flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ ahe haomɔ mli. hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ haaa sũ mli niyenii kpakpai loo nibii ni kooloi bibii tamɔ atatui kɛ afua fiteɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni fa bɔ ni sa ha tso lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if my tomato plant leaves are curling because of hot sun or because of a disease?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa loo hela hewɔ ni tomato baai lɛ miihoso lɛ?

english: Leaves that curl inward during the hottest part of the day to conserve water will usually uncurl when it cools down. If the leaves stay tightly curled, turn yellow, or look stunted, it is caused by a virus usually spread by whiteflies.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni ekɛbu nu he lɛ fɔɔ shwiemɔ be mli ni amɛhe jɔɔ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa Etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo etamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ. Virus ko ni bei pii lɛ whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their leaves suddenly after a period of heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Sudden leaf drop after heavy rain is often caused by waterlogged soil that suffocates the roots, leading to root rot or fungal infections that force the plant to shed leaves to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni fiteɔ trukaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ baa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni haa tso lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ koni ehi shi.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot inside the soil before it is even time to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani be po shɛɔ ni abaakpa lɛ?

english: Yam rot in the soil is caused by water pooling around the tuber in poorly drained soil, which allows fungi and tiny microscopic worms called nematodes to attack and decay the tuber.
ga: Nu ni buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato fitemɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ tutuaa ni amɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cabbage plants full of small holes every rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii daa nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are usually made by diamondback moth caterpillars feeding on the tender foliage. Intercropping with strong-smelling herbs or spraying natural neem oil early can keep them away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, diamondback ŋmeii ni yeɔ baa bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ kaabe baa mli lɛ baa. Dumɔ tsofai ni he yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ waa loo okɛ adebɔɔ mli neem fɔ afɔ nɔ mra. Ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni tsofai nɛɛ akashɛ he.

english: Why do my orange trees produce sour fruit even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso lɛ woɔ yibii ni mli edɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Citrus sweetness comes from adequate sunlight and soil nutrients like potassium. Watering too heavily close to harvest time can also dilute the natural sugars inside the oranges, making them taste sour.
ga: Hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ potassium lɛ ji nɔ ni haa akutu mli ŋɔɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine yɛ be ni bɛŋkɛ kpamɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha adebɔɔ mli sugar ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ afee mlɛo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔlɔ ni mli edɔ

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow very quickly and produce broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and cool soil moisture it needs to survive its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop during the hot afternoon but wake up again in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane latsaa be mli shi amɛteɔ shi ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the afternoon heat is too strong, plants lose water quickly through their leaves. They intentionally curl or droop to reduce their exposure to the hot sun and conserve water, then bounce back when the sun goes down and temperatures drop.
ga: Kɛ shwane lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Akɛ yiŋtoo ko fɔ̃ɔ amɛnɔ loo amɛfoɔ amɛhe koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akashɛ amɛhe ni amɛbu nu he. Kɛkɛ ni efoɔ ehe ekoŋŋ beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize turning yellow while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ kã he eji ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of a maize stalk usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is its main food for growing green leaves. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left to the top young leaves to keep growing, leaving the bottom leaves hungry.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni akɛhaa baai eŋɔlii ni kwɛɔ Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni eya nɔ ekwɛ baai lɛ. kɛtsɔ shishigbɛ baai lɛ ni eshiɔ hɔmɔ lɛ nɔ

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans on my land after harvesting my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil. Legume crops like groundnuts and beans have special roots that take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground, naturally feeding the soil so your next crops grow strong.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does spreading dried manure or compost help my cassava grow better than just leaving the soil alone?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi fata he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-cassava lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ashiɔ lɛ pɛ?

english: Animal manure and compost act like long-lasting food and a sponge for your soil. They feed the soil with rich nutrients and help the ground hold onto rainwater much longer, allowing crop roots to grow deep and strong.
ga: Manɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ kɛ sponji kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii kpakpai babaoo ni amɛyeɔ amɛbua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do weeds reduce my farm yield even when there is plenty of rain falling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa nibii ni anáa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that fight your crops for food, soil space, and sunlight. Even with plenty of rain, weeds will steal the natural nutrients out of the earth before your main crops have a chance to feed on them.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii, shikpɔŋ kɛ hulu la, kɛji nugbɔ enɛ babaoo po. Jwɛi hu baaju adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ aná hegbɛ ni eye amɛ.

english: What causes small holes and sawdust-like dirt inside the center leaves of my growing corn?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ni miida lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ amli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The caterpillar hides deep inside the growing whorl of the corn plant during the day to feed on the tender leaf tissue away from the hot sun.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ teɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ahe fãji ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why do farmers cover the ground around their tomato stems with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi haa he ni tomato tsei lɛ yɔɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) protects the bare earth from direct hot sunlight. It keeps the soil cool, stops rainwater from evaporating quickly, and prevents weed seeds from sprouting around your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ oya. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why is it important for me to prune off some branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ cacao tso ni eda lɛ niji komɛi?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches so fresh air and light can pass through the tree canopy. Good airflow reduces dampness that causes black pod disease and encourages the tree to produce more pods instead of unnecessary leaves.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ la boteɔ tsei lɛ ayiteŋ. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ baa shi, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ baatsu nii.

english: Why will my cassava tubers stay small if I plant the stems too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛji akɛ adu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii lɛ?

english: Cassava needs room underground to expand its roots into thick tubers. When planted too close, the roots tangle together and struggle against each other for soil nutrients and moisture, resulting in small, thin roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi he ko he miihia cassava koni shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse. Kɛ adu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛyeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe tseee.

english: Why are my young corn leaves turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your corn plants are starving for nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient found in manure or fertilizers, or that too much water is choking the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni anaa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli Loo nu babaoo baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my corn plants grow thin and weak without big cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛbɛ ŋmeii wuji beni mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close to each other, the crops compete with one another for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving no single plant with enough strength to grow large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei komɛi bɛ ni baanyɛ akwɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: How do I know if my soil has enough food to grow healthy maize without buying expensive fertilizers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha makwɛ ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni miheee ŋmãa ni jara wa?

english: Healthy, fertile soil is usually dark in color, crumbly to touch, holds moisture well, and has earthworms; you can feed poor soil naturally by adding decayed animal manure or compost.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Efoɔ kɛji akɛ ata he. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni eyɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii Obaanyɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo loo kooloi ŋmɔtɔ ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ.

english: Leaves curl or droop in high heat to protect themselves from losing too much water into the hot air, acting like a natural shield until temperatures cool down.
ga: Ha ni ebɔle ehe loo egbee shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni obu ohe koni nu babaoo akafite yɛ latsaa be mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsɔne ni buɔ mɔ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: What happens to my crops when heavy rainfall leaves standing water on my farm for several days?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu lɛ ŋmɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo?

english: Standing water drowns plant roots by blocking air from reaching them, causing the roots to rot and preventing the plant from drinking up nutrients from the soil.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ shwieɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni etsĩɔ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do worms like to eat the tender center leaves of my young corn plants before the cobs show?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii sumɔɔ ni amɛye mi-ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Pests like Fall Armyworms target the soft inner funnel of young corn because those newest leaves are the tenderest and most nutritious part of the growing plant.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworms lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli gbɛi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Enɛ ji akɛ, baai heei lɛ ji tso ni miida lɛ fã ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni niyenii yɔɔ mli fe fɛɛ.

english: Weeds have strong roots that steal the fertilizer and water from the soil much faster than your main crops can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni otso titri lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Beans pull nitrogen food out of the air and put it back into the soil, helping to naturally feed the maize plants growing next to them.
ga: Beans gbalaa niyenii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. koni eye ebua ŋmãa tso ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ Atsɔse lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before growing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme heat during the day, lack of regular water, or a shortage of essential plant food.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Nu ni faaa yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli daa loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni jɛɔ tsei amli lɛ bɛ

english: Why do seeds bought from the agro-dealer produce better corn than the seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ahe kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa ni hi fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Store-bought certified seeds are specifically bred for high vigor and disease resistance, while seeds saved generation after generation gradually lose their strength and produce smaller cobs.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni ahe yɛ shwapoi amli ni awo he odase lɛ mli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ babaoo ni amɛnyɛ amɛshi helai. Yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ yinɔi kɛ yinɔi amli lɛ baafite hewalɛ fiofio ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die during the hot sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and cannot tolerate full direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby shields them from extreme heat and helps retain moisture in the soil.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛŋmɛɛɛ hulu la gbɛ kwraa. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why do flowers on my cocoa trees drop off without turning into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers due to dry weather, nutrient stress, or lack of small pollinating insects like midges. Proper soil nutrients and retaining shade help maintain humidity so flowers can set into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi hewɔ. niyenii mli haomɔ loo ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni bɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa kɛ hulutsoo yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet and humid conditions. Regular harvesting, weeding, and pruning help increase airflow and reduce excessive moisture where the fungus thrives.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. harvest weeding Ni ŋmeii ni afoɔ daa lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ni ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ hei ni ŋmeii shwereɔ yɛ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do some cocoa farms start bearing pods in two years while others take over four years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji komɛi jeɔ pods feemɔ shishi yɛ afii enyɔ mli lɛ? yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu heɔ nɔ ni fe afii ejwɛ?

english: The time to first harvest depends on the cocoa variety. Hybrid cocoa varieties are bred to produce pods in two to three years, whereas older traditional varieties naturally take four to five years to mature.
ga: Be ni akɛkpaa klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaa lɛ damɔ kookoo henɔ lɛ nɔ. Afɔ Hybrid cocoa henɔi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ afii 2-3 mli, yɛ be mli ni blema cocoa henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ afii 4-5 dani amɛdaraa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why should I cut off the fresh shoots growing from the base of my mature cocoa tree trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ cacao tso ni eda lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: These fresh shoots, called chupons or suckers, steal water and nutrients from the main trunk. Removing them directs all the tree's energy back into growing healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii heei nɛɛ, ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons loo ŋmeii lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni miida lɛ amli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa branches turning yellow and developing tiny burn patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa nine lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiitsɔɔ shãa he okadii bibii lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves with damaged patches are often caused by sap-sucking insects like mirids (capsids) or indicate a lack of essential soil nutrients like nitrogen and potassium.
ga: Baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii. Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mirids (capsids) lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa loo etsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ potassium bɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it bad to harvest green cocoa pods before they turn fully yellow or orange?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ abaakpa kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ dani amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Unripe green cocoa pods contain flat beans with low sugar content. Harvesting only fully ripe yellow or orange pods ensures high-quality beans that ferment properly.
ga: Cocoa pods eŋɔli ni ahoko lɛ ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni sugar fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii ni ji ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ pɛ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ ŋmeii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant cocoa trees very close to each other to fit more trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni anyɛ adu tsei babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting cocoa trees too closely causes them to compete for sunlight and soil nutrients, resulting in tall, thin trees with fewer pods and a higher risk of fungal diseases due to poor airflow.
ga: Kɛ́ adu kokoo tsei kɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa cacao tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. Ni oshara ni yɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa mɔ nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii ni hoɔ lɛ hewɔ lɛ fa babaoo.

english: Why must I heap my wet cocoa beans under plantain leaves for several days before drying them in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ toɔ plantain baai ashishi gbii babaoo dani mikɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Covering the beans creates natural heat and starts fermentation, which stops the seed from germinating, removes bitterness, and creates the chocolate flavor buyers look for.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛha kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ baa ni ebɔi ŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haaa dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃, ejieɔ ŋmɔlɔ, ni ehaa tsokolate lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ taoɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do food crops like cassava stop yielding well once my cocoa trees grow big and form a thick leafy cover?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niyenii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei lɛ kpaɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai beni mi-cacao tsei lɛ daraa ni baai ni mli tse eha amɛhe lɛ?

english: Food crops need direct sunlight to produce tubers and grain. As mature cocoa trees grow and shade the ground completely, light cannot reach the food crops beneath them.
ga: Niyenii tsei he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛwo ŋmeii kɛ dumɔwui. Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ eda kwraa ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kwraa lɛ, La nyɛŋ ashɛ niyenii tsei ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ahe.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is lacking nitrogen, an essential plant food. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer like urea helps restore the green color and supports healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: When cassava plants are spaced too closely, their roots compete fiercely for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives the roots enough room to expand and produce large tubers instead of many tiny ones.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ baatswa akaŋ waa koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji. Yɛ yitsei bibii babaoo najiaŋ

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or cowpeas helps improve my soil for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When you harvest them, that natural fertilizer remains in the soil to nourish your next crop, like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Kɛji okpa amɛ Adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Covering the ground with dry organic material, called mulching, blocks the harsh sun from drying out the soil. It traps moisture, stops weeds from growing, and slowly rots down into rich manure.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni egbi ni akɛhaa lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsĩ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ akagbi. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep drying up and dying during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigboi yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive strong direct sunlight and heat. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains or cassava alongside them creates a living canopy that keeps the soil cool and protects the seedlings.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ yɛ he kome. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni ebuɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food that builds the underground tuber. Staking lifts the leaves into the air and sunlight while keeping them off damp ground where diseases easily spread.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii ni feɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ aya ŋwɛi kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛya hulu la lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha ekɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ akabɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I save and plant seeds from my hybrid maize harvest for the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni miduɔ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to produce high yields only for their first planting. Seeds saved from that harvest lose their strength, resulting in weaker plants, uneven growth, and much smaller cobs.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo pɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni egbɔjɔ. shweremɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee ni cob lɛ ji bibioo kwraa

english: Why is it better to water my tomato plants early in the morning rather than in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ oooha tomato tsei lɛ nu leebi fe shwane lɛ?

english: Watering under the hot afternoon sun causes most of the water to evaporate before the roots can drink it. Morning watering lets the plant absorb moisture before the heat of the day sets in.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani shishifãi lɛ anu. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ yeɔ nɔ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot on the tree during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a tiny fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet weather. Pruning overcrowded tree branches lets sunlight and fresh air flow through to keep the pods dry.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Fungi bibii ni kɛbaa Ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ. Tso niji ni mli eyi obɔ fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ mli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi.

english: Why are insects eating big holes in my pepper leaves, and how can I stop them naturally?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiye buji wuji ni yɔɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ amli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa amɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa?

english: Insects chew young leaves because they are tender and full of juices. Spraying a homemade mixture made from crushed neem leaves and water drives away many pests without harming your soil or crops.
ga: Kplukai ŋmɔɔ baai bibii ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛyi obɔ kɛ nu. Kɛ́ okɛ neem baai ni atswa kɛ nu ni akɛfutu nii ni akɛfee shia lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai srɔtoi babaoo akashɛ he ni eyeee oshikpɔŋ loo oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui.

english: Lower leaves turning yellow usually means your maize is short on nitrogen, an essential nutrient the plant needs to build green tissue and produce healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa waa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛma fãji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛwo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl upward during the hot afternoon sun?
