ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl in intense heat to reduce water loss through transpiration; while it is a natural defense, persistent curling indicates the plant is stressed for soil moisture.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli koni nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ latsaa mli lɛ aba shi. Eyɛ mli akɛ eji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he moŋ. Shi ŋmɔlɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ he miihia tso lɛ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas in the same field as my cassava crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu cowpea yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ mi-cassava tso lɛ?

english: Cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which enriches the land for your cassava while helping shade out weeds.
ga: Cowpeas mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa he babaoo ni okɛbaahã o-cassava lɛ yaa hiɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What will happen to my maize if I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting maize too close causes the stalks to compete for sunlight, water, and ground nutrients, resulting in weak plants with thin stems and tiny cobs.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants becoming sticky and covered in white powder?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ nɔ lɛ mli wa ni powda yɛŋ ehà nɔ lɛ?

english: This sticky white layer is caused by small sap-sucking insects like mealybugs or whiteflies, which weaken the plant and reduce cassava root formation.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mealybugs loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ni ŋmɔɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmei shishifãi ni feɔ ŋmei lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are my young cocoa pods turning dark brown and shriveling on the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigboi yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a water-loving fungus that spreads rapidly during heavy rain and high humidity in dark, shaded cocoa farms.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji hydrophilic fungus ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji ni mli ewo duŋ, ni shade yɔɔ mli lɛ amli.

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when stressed by severe dry weather, extreme heat, or excessive fertilizer, which causes them to focus on leafy growth rather than fruiting.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi waa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hao amɛ. Enɛ haa amɛsusuɔ baai lɛ adalɛ he moŋ fe aduawai ni amɛbaawo lɛ.

english: How does heavy rain during tassels formation affect my maize yield?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ tassel be mli lɛ saa mi-ŋmãa yibiiwoo lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy rainfall during flowering can wash away pollen from the maize tassels before it reaches the silks, leading to cobs with missing or scattered kernels.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ afɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ahe dani amɛyashɛ siliki lɛ he. Enɛ haa cobs ni dumɔwui elaaje loo egbɛ eshwã lɛ baa.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow thin and twisted instead of big and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ mli tse ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee agbo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, deeply tilled soil to expand freely; hard or compacted soil creates physical resistance that distorts the shape and restricts the size of the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni enyɛ egbɛ eshwa. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ shitee-kɛ-woo ni fiteɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ baa ni ehaa bulb lɛ dalɛ baa shi.

english: Why are my plantain suckers growing very slowly in land that holds standing water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ miida blɛoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu damɔ shi yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Standing water drowns plantain roots by cutting off oxygen, leading to root rot which prevents the crop from absorbing nutrients needed for healthy growth.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ shwieɔ plantain shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ, ni no haaa tso lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do crops grown in the Tamale area behave differently from those grown in southern Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ Tamale kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe tsei ni aduɔ yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ?

english: Ghana has distinct climate zones. Northern areas like Tamale experience a single rainfall season and higher temperatures, which causes crops to mature faster and require more drought-tolerant traits compared to the double-rainfall forest zones in the south.
ga: Ghana yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ hei srɔtoi. Kooyigbɛ hei tamɔ Tamale lɛ naa nugbɔshiimɔ be kome pɛ kɛ hulutsoo be ni yaa hiɛ waa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii daa oya ni ebiɔ sui ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa babaoo kɛ akɛto nugbɔshiimɔ kooi ni yɔɔ anaigbɛ lɛ amli shii enyɔ he.

english: How do I know what crops my land is capable of growing successfully?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male nibii ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ adu yɛ omanyeyeli mli?

english: Different crops require specific soil textures, drainage levels, and nutrient contents. Observing how water settles on your land after rain and having an extension officer test your soil will tell you whether your ground is better suited for grains, roots, or legumes.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ eko fɛɛ eko biɔ shikpɔŋ srɔtoi. drainage level kɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ falɛ Kwɛmɔ bɔ ni nu shwieɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. Ni ha mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ aka oshikpɔŋ lɛ amɛkwɛ. Ebaatsɔɔ bo kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmaa, shishifãi, loo ŋmeii.

english: Is there a specific reliable phone service or helpline I can contact from anywhere in Ghana to get crop advice?
ga: Ani tɛlifoŋ nitsumɔhe loo hotline ko ni ajɔɔ nɔ aha ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ ni manyɛ matswa kɛjɛ he fɛɛ he yɛ Ghana koni maná ŋaawoo yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: Yes, there are national agricultural extension helplines and mobile advisory services in Ghana that allow farmers in any region to call or text experts for real-time guidance on pest outbreaks, weather forecasts, and crop care.
ga: Hɛɛ, maŋ okwaafoi anitsumɔ he yelikɛbuamɔ nitsumɔhe ko kɛ ŋaawoo ni akɛyaa he fɛɛ he lɛ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni yɔɔ kpokpaa fɛɛ kpokpaa nɔ lɛ. Tswaa loo ŋmaa mɔ ko ni le nii jogbaŋŋ koni ená ŋaawoo yɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ he. kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he adafitswaa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ

english: Why should I use certified seeds from an agent instead of saving seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni jɛ najiaŋdamɔlɔ ko ŋɔɔ lɛ atsu nii? Mohu ɔ, mo ngɔ dumɔwuhi nɛ je ngma kpami nɛ be ɔ mi ɔ kɛ to.

english: Certified seeds are professionally selected and treated to resist local pests and diseases, giving them a higher germination rate and predictable crop behavior compared to saved seeds which lose their strength over time.
ga: Akɛ ŋaalɔi halaa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ni atsaa amɛ koni amɛkaye helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ɔ babaoo ni anyɛɔ atsɔɔ tsei lɛ asui amli jogbaŋŋ. Akɛ enɛ toɔ dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ ahe.

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism. Crops roll their leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to the hot sun, which conserves water inside the plant during dry or high-heat conditions.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tsei lɛ baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni ekɛba he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ baaye abua ni nu ahi tso lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be loo hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow tall very quickly but fail to produce big fruits or grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida oya shi ewooo aduawai loo dumɔwui wuji lɛ?

english: Rapid leaf and stem growth usually means the plant has plenty of nitrogen, but producing strong grains or fruits requires phosphorus and potassium. Without a balanced soil diet, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves instead of crop yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai kɛ ŋmeii ni daa oya lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa. Shi koni dumɔwui loo aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba lɛ, ehe miihia ni phosphorus kɛ potassium aba. Kɛji niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ja bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ baai moŋ fe ni amɛaafee tsei amli nibii.

english: Why are insect pests attacking my crops more heavily this season than last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be nɛɛ mli fe afi ni eho lɛ?

english: Pest populations change based on weather patterns, rainfall timing, and crop rotation. If temperatures stay warm or if the same crop is planted year after year on the same land, pests multiply much faster.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ tsakeɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi, nugbɔnɛmɔ bei, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsakemɔ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ tee nɔ ehi shi loo odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baafa oya kwraa.

english: The first rain is often followed by a heat spell that can dry out the topsoil and kill newly germinated seedlings. It is safer to wait until the rains become steady so the soil holds constant moisture for the young roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ aba daa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛha shishifãi bibii lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why does my soil produce lower yields every year even though I use the same farming methods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo afi fɛɛ afi lɛ? Ni mikɛ okwaayeli gbɛi lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii?

english: Growing the same crop continuously removes the same specific nutrients from the soil without giving the land time to recover. Rotating your main crop with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts helps restore soil fertility naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. ni okɛ be haaa ni okɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ Tsɔɔmɔ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ kɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Does plowing my land deeply always help crop roots grow better?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Deep plowing breaks up compacted dirt so roots can penetrate easily, but over-plowing in dry areas can strip the topsoil of organic matter and cause it to dry out quickly, which can stress young crops.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoo ni mli kwɔ lɛ gbálaa muji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ abote mli mlɛo. Shi kɛ́ atsu nii babaoo yɛ hei ni egbi lɛ, ebaanyɛ ejie nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ ni eha egbi oya. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ aná haomɔ.

english: How can I tell if a specific spot on my land is good enough for growing crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji he pɔtɛɛ ko yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: Good soil is usually dark, soft to break apart, and holds moisture well. If you see wild plants growing very tall and green in a specific spot, it means the soil there has plenty of natural nutrients for your crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli edɔ, eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, egbɛ eshwa, ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji ona koo mli tsei ni miida ni amɛfee ŋmɔji yɛ he ko. No tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii babaoo kɛha onibii.

english: Should I clear out every plant when preparing a home farm for new crops?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie tso fɛɛ tso kɛji misaa mishia ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛha tsei heei?

english: Clearing weeds is necessary, but saving healthy wild seedlings or useful shade trees can save you money and protect your soil from drying out under the hot sun.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ he miihia. Shi koo mli dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ loo tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni oookwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha okɛ shika akafite, ni ebu oshikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Is it good to dig up wild seedlings growing on my land and replant them in my farm?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafo koo mli dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni madu amɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Transplanting wild seedlings is a cheap way to add crops to your farm, but these naturally sprouted plants often grow unevenly and produce smaller harvests than carefully raised nursery plants.
ga: Koo mli dumɔwui ni ooodu lɛ ji gbɛ ni shika helɛtemɔ bɛ he ni oootsɔ nɔ oha ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Shi bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa nɛɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ, ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo tamɔ tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ.

english: Why do seeds bought from agriculture officers yield more food than seedlings I collect from the bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mihe kɛjɛ okwaayeli he onukpai adɛŋ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mifo kɛjɛ jwɛi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Improved or certified seeds are specially selected and bred to resist diseases and produce high yields, while wild bush seedlings come from random plants and carry unpredictable growth traits.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ loo ni awo amɛ he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ ni akwɛɔ amɛ koni helai akamɔ amɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Yɛ be mli ni koo mli koo mli tsei bibii lɛ jɛɔ tsei ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko amli ni amɛyɛ dalɛ sui ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ.

english: What happens if I mix wild plant shoots with improved nursery seedlings on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ koo mli tsei ashishifãi futu ŋmɔ kome mli dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli?

english: Your farm will produce food, but the crops will mature at different times and produce different amounts, making harvesting harder because wild plants will yield much less than the improved ones.
ga: Oŋmɔ lɛ baawo niyenii. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii shwereɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Enɛ haa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ nɔ ni wa waa ejaakɛ koo mli tsei wooo yibii babaoo fe tsei ni atsake amɛ.

english: What is the best way for me to move a young shoot from one part of my land to another without killing it?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ majie ŋmeii bibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛya shikpɔŋ kroko nɔ ni migbeee amɛ?

english: You should dig a deep circle around the shoot so the roots remain covered in a ball of soil, then move it early in the morning or late evening so the sun does not dry out the exposed roots.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ kooloo ni mli kwɔ abɔle he. ŋmeii koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli No sɛɛ lɛ, shwiemɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ koni hulu lɛ akagbi shishifãi ni miiba lɛ.

english: Why do my young seedlings dry up and die shortly after I move them to a new spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ amɛ tee he ko hee sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: This happens due to root shock. When root hairs break during digging or get exposed to hot sun, the plant loses its ability to drink water until it settles into its new home.
ga: Enɛ baa mli yɛ shishifãi ni tswaa lɛ hewɔ. Beni shishifãi lɛ ahe yitsɔi lɛ fãa yɛ be mli ni akuɔ shikpɔŋ loo hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ. Tso lɛ nyɛŋ anu nu kɛyashi ebaahi eshia hee lɛ mli.

english: Can I use extra young shoots to expand my farm size without buying new seeds?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmeii bibii ni fa lɛ atsu nii koni mikɛgbala miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni mahe dumɔwui heei?

english: Yes, using existing shoots is a simple way to extend your farm boundary and get extra harvest without spending money, though the extra yield might be modest.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ momo lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ji tsabaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Koni okɛgbala oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni oná nibii babaoo ni okɛ shika tsuuu nii. Eyɛ mli akɛ yibiiwoo ni fata he lɛ baanyɛ afee bibioo moŋ.

english: Why are some plants on my farm growing bigger while others remain small even though I planted them at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ bibii eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ amɛ yɛ be kome mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Crop growth depends heavily on the soil quality in that exact spot, sunlight exposure, and the genetic strength of the individual seedling you planted.
ga: Tso lɛ dalɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ, hulu la kɛ dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu ni oduɔ lɛ mli hewalɛ nɔ.

english: How can I increase the food I get from my small home farm without buying expensive land?
ga: Mikɛ niyenii ni minine shɛɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji bibii amli lɛ baafata he. yɛ shia ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe shikpɔŋ ni jara wa?

english: You can get a bigger harvest by feeding your soil with compost or manure, placing your plants with proper spacing, and gradually replacing wild seedlings with high-yielding nursery plants.
ga: Obaanyɛ oná ŋmaa babaoo kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaafata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Okɛ tsei awo he ni sa ni okɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo awo koo mli dumɔwui lɛ anajiaŋ fiofio.

english: When maize leaves turn yellow starting from the tip and moving down the center in a V-shape, it means the crop is starving for nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main nutrient that gives crops their healthy green color and strong growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛyitseiaŋ ni eyaa shi kɛyaa teŋgbɛ yɛ V su mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli, amɛhe wa ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my soil dry out and crack so quickly after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egbɛɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil cracks and loses moisture quickly when it lacks organic matter. Adding compost, animal manure, or dry leaves helps the soil act like a sponge, holding onto water much longer for your crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gbalaa ni efiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo baai ni egbi fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni etsu nii tamɔ sponji. Too nu kɛha onibii lɛ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil and allows pests to multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yaa hiɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa tsake lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to leave holes and sawdust-like dirt inside my corn leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shiɔ bu kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ mi-ŋmãa baai lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm. These caterpillars hide inside the central leaves (the funnel) of the maize plant during the day and eat the tender inner leaves, which weakens the whole crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ateŋ baai (cones) lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni oye mligbɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking leaf sap, or by a viral disease spread by whiteflies. Removing infected plants early prevents it from spreading to healthy ones.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Ebaatsi enaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when planted in open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily in harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains provides shade and keeps the air humid, giving young cocoa plants time to establish strong roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni naa wa shɛ amɛnɔ. Nurse tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo baa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Enɛ haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ náa be koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do my maize crops grow tall and thin with very small cobs when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Spacing them properly ensures each plant gets enough resources to form large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso fɛɛ tso to he ko jogbaŋŋ lɛ, enáa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmei agbo ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds around my young cassava stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Kasava tso bibioo?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal soil nutrients, water, and sunlight from young cassava plants. Keeping the field clear for the first three months allows cassava roots to bulk up properly.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, nu kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ ŋmei tsei bibii amli lɛ. Kɛ́ oha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli tse yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ afee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper flowers drop off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they suffer from stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or having too much nitrogen fertilizer which causes the plant to grow leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni haa tso lɛ baa lɛ shwereɔ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the air to catch maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to make food, which is then stored underground to form big yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. No sɛɛ lɛ, akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni efee sweet potato ŋmeii agboi.

english: Why do seed packages have specific numbers or codes on them instead of just the standard crop name?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ kotokui amli lɛ yɛ yibɔ loo kood krɛdɛɛ ko lɛ? Yɛ tso lɛ gbɛi ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ lɛ pɛ najiaŋ

english: Seed codes or numbers represent specific improved crop varieties that have been scientifically tested to yield higher, resist local pests, or mature faster than traditional farm seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ahe koodi loo yibɔ lɛ tsɔɔ tso henɔ ni afee lɛ pɔtɛɛ. ni aka lɛ akwɛ yɛ jeŋ nilee mli koni ewo yibii babaoo Eteɔ shi ewoɔ maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ loo edaa oya fe dumɔwui ni yɔɔ blema ŋmɔji amli lɛ

english: How do I know if a new variety of maize will grow well in my region of Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmãa henɔ hee ko baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mikpokpaa ni ji Ghana lɛ nɔ?

english: Different crop varieties are bred for specific soil types and rainfall zones across Ghana, so matching the variety number to your district's weather pattern ensures a good harvest.
ga: Akwɛ tsei srɔtoi yɛ shikpɔŋ henɔ kɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ yɛ Ghana fɛɛ lɛ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tsofai srɔtoi lɛ ayibɔ lɛ to okpokpaa lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he lɛ, ehaa wɔnáa ŋmaa kpakpa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cassava plants turning yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves during dry spells mean the plant is under water stress or lacking nitrogen, causing it to shed older leaves to conserve moisture for survival.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ nu mli haomɔ shishi loo nitrogen bɛ ehe. Ha ejie ebaa momo lɛ koni ekɛto ŋmɔtɔ he koni ehi shi.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without forming fruits when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa he lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses the plant and dries up pollen, preventing fertilization and causing the tomato plant to drop blossoms to protect its energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa amɛmli ŋmeii lɛ gĩɔ. Tsi fɔmɔ nii ni oha tomato tsei lɛ afɔlɔ koni ebu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my pepper seeds take much longer to sprout out of the ground than my maize seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛjeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe mi-corn dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Different crops have different seed coats and growth cycles; small vegetable seeds like pepper naturally require more consistent moisture and time to break open.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi yɛ dumɔwui ahe tsɔi kɛ amɛdalɛ bei srɔtoi. Aduawai bibii tamɔ ŋmeii, yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, amɛbiɔ nu babaoo ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why is it important to leave a specific measured distance between my crops instead of planting them closely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mashi gbɛ pɔtɛɛ ko ni anyɛɔ asusuɔ he yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures each crop gets enough sunlight, airflow, and root space to feed on soil nutrients without competing with neighboring plants.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛ shishifãi ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ akaŋ akaŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight, so fast-growing plantain leaves act as living umbrellas to provide shade and hold soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, plantain tso lɛ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo koni ekɛ hulutsoo aha ni eha sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why do armyworms attack my crop leaves so aggressively right after the early rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The start of the rainy season creates warm, moist conditions that cause insect eggs to hatch all at once, leading young caterpillars to feed heavily on fresh green leaves.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee kɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ fɛ̃i baa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kooloo lɛ wui lɛ fɛɛ fɔɔ shikome. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ aye baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo.

english: How does trimming or pruning older leaves help my crop produce larger fruits?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai momoi ni afoɔ loo afoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni ewo yibii wuji?

english: Removing weak or old leaves redirects the plant's food and nutrients directly into developing bigger, healthier fruits rather than wasting energy on useless foliage.
ga: Baai ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni egbɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ niyenii kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛi lɛ yaa tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeefite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does applying fertilizer at the wrong time cause my crops to burn instead of growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be ni esaaa mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shãa moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer contains concentrated salts; applying it when the soil is too dry or placing it too close to roots draws water out of the plant, causing foliage to dry up and burn.
ga: Fertilizer lɛ yɛ ŋoo babaoo. Ni akɛbaafata he beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo ebɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe tsɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni ejie nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa.

english: Can I plant cassava or other food crops inside my mature cocoa farm to get extra food?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei loo niyenii krokomɛi? yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ ni eda lɛ mli koni maná niyenii krokomɛi?

english: When you plant food crops too close to mature cocoa trees, they compete directly for water and soil nutrients. This can weaken your cocoa trees and reduce your cocoa yields because the other crops absorb the nutrients your cocoa needs.
ga: Kɛji odu niyenii yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ tsɔ lɛ, Amɛyeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha cacao tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni eha cacao ni afeɔ lɛ aba shi, ejaakɛ tsei krokomɛi shwieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa o-cacao lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when there are too many other plants growing near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɛ be mli ni tsei krokomɛi babaoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Too many plants growing in the same space fight over the same soil nutrients and sunlight. When cocoa trees have to share their food with nearby plants, they do not get enough strength to produce healthy, heavy pods.
ga: Tsei babaoo ni akwɛɔ yɛ he kome lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ hulu la lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Beni esa akɛ cacao tsei lɛ kɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ aja niyenii. Kakao tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii ni mli wa ni tsii.

english: How far away from my cocoa trees should I plant other crops if I want to intercrop?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu tsei krokomɛi kɛjɛ kookoo tso lɛ he tɛŋŋ kɛji miisumɔ ni madu amɛ yɛ teŋ?

english: You should keep companion crops outside the root zone of the cocoa trees—usually a few meters away—so that each plant has its own soil area to feed from without stealing fertilizer from the cocoa.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tsei ni fata he lɛ ahi kookoo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ asɛɛ. Akɛ amɛ toɔ (bei pii lɛ, mitai fioo pɛ kɛjɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ) bɔni afee ni tso fɛɛ tso aná lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eshikpɔŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni eju ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ kookoo lɛ mli.

english: How do I make sure the fertilizer I buy actually reaches my cocoa roots?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miheɔ lɛ shɛɔ mi-kokoo shishifãi lɛ ahe diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Clear away weeds and unwanted plants around the base of the cocoa tree before applying fertilizer directly under the tree's leaves canopy, where its feeding roots are spread out.
ga: Jiemɔ jwɛi kɛ tsei ni ataooo ni ebɔle ohe lɛ kɛjɛ ohe. Kookoo tso lɛ shishi dani ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Biɛ ji he ni cacao tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ gbɛ eshwã.

english: Is it a waste of money to put fertilizer on a farm that has a lot of weeds?
ga: Ani eji shikafitemɔ akɛ aaawo ŋmɔ ko ni jwɛi babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, because weeds often grow faster than cocoa trees and will absorb most of the fertilizer first, wasting your money and feeding the weeds instead of your crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ fɔɔ daa oya fe cacao tsei lɛ, ni amɛbaaŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ babaoo klɛŋklɛŋ. Kɛtsɔ shika ni ofiteɔ kɛ jwɛi ni oooye yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ najiaŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What happens to the soil if too many different plants are feeding from it at the same time?
ga: Mɛni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ aha tsei babaoo niyenii yɛ be kome mli?

english: The soil loses its natural fertility very quickly because multiple crops draw out essential nutrients simultaneously, leading to weak crop growth and smaller harvests.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ laajeɔ ebɔɔ su mli fɔmɔ oya ejaakɛ tsei babaoo jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli yɛ be kome mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraaa jogbaŋŋ, ni ŋmaa lɛ hu baa shi fioo.

english: Why do weeds harm my cocoa trees even if I apply fertilizer regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiye mi-cacao tsei lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ amɛmli daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have broad, aggressive root systems that rapidly soak up soil nutrients and water before your cocoa tree roots can reach them, leaving your cocoa tree hungry.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei. Enɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ oya dani kookoo shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, hɔmɔ yeɔ kookoo tsei lɛ.

english: Why should I clear out old or wild plants growing near my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei momo loo koo mli tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi cacao tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Removing unwanted plants removes obstacles that steal soil food and block sunlight, allowing your cocoa trees to get 100% of the natural nutrients and fertilizer available.
ga: Tsei ni ataooo lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ gbɛtsii nii ni juɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni tsiɔ hulu la naa lɛ kɛyaa. Enɛ haa kookoo tso lɛ naa adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii 100%.

english: What does it mean to rehabilitate an overgrown cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni ji kookoo ŋmɔji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni aku sɛɛ akɛba lɛ tsɔɔ?

english: Rehabilitating an overgrown farm means clearing out unwanted plants, cutting back heavy shade, and removing obstacles so soil nutrients and light go directly to feeding your cocoa trees.
ga: Okwaafoi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni aku sɛɛ akɛba lɛ tsɔɔ tsei ni ataooo lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli. Kpɔ̃ɔ shade ni mli tse lɛ. ni ajie gbɛtsii nibii koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kɛ la aha cacao tsei lɛ niyenii tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Do different crops draw nutrients from the exact same depth in the soil?
ga: Ani tsei srɔtoi gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ kome mli?

english: Some crops have shallow roots while others have deep roots. If two crops feed at the exact same soil depth, they will fight constantly for the same food and fertilizer.
ga: Tsei komɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Kɛji tsei enyɔ yeɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ, Amɛbaawuu be fɛɛ be koni amɛná niyenii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds when the rains are so unpredictable?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui? Be ni nugbɔ baanɛ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba?

english: Planting immediately after the very first rain of the year is risky because a dry spell might follow. It is best to wait until the soil receives steady, deep moisture over several days so the young seeds have enough water to germinate and grow strong roots.
ga: Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyɛ oshara ejaakɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be baanyɛ aba. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbii babaoo. Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui bibii lɛ ana nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: What happens to my crops if a dry spell hits right after I sow my seeds?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji hɔmɔ ba beni midu dumɔwui lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Seeds need continuous moisture to sprout properly. If a dry spell occurs immediately after sowing, the seeds may dry up in the hot soil before sprouting, or the young seedlings will wilt and die, forcing you to replant.
ga: Dumɔwui he hiaa nu daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ba yɛ dumɔwui ni adu lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ Dumɔwui baanyɛ agbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃. Aloo tsobi lɛ baagbi ni ebaagbo. ni haa okɛ ohe woɔ mli ekoŋŋ

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants roll up tightly during the heat of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the plant's natural defense mechanism to survive heat and drought. By rolling its leaves into tight tubes, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun, which stops water from evaporating out of its leaves too quickly.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ mli. Tsei haa he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ nɔ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛshwieɔ amɛwoɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ akajɛ baai lɛ amli oya tsɔ.

english: Why are the flowers dropping off my pepper plants without producing any fruit during hot, dry weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ otsii ni mli edɔ ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: When plants face extreme heat and dry soil, they get stressed and try to save water to keep themselves alive. Shedding their flowers helps them conserve energy and moisture that would otherwise go into growing fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe wo latsaa ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ Amɛhaoɔ amɛhe ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu nu he koni amɛhi wala mli. Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa amɛnáa hewalɛ kɛ fɛ̃i ni abaanyɛ akɛtsu nii kɛkwɛ aduawai lɛ.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my crops turn yellow and fall off during a short drought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: When there is not enough water in the soil, plants cannot pull up nutrients like nitrogen. To protect new growth at the top, the plant sacrifices its older bottom leaves, drawing out their remaining food and letting them drop.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ nitrogen. koni ebu shweremɔ hee ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ he Tso lɛ kɛ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ baashã afɔle. koni ejie niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ ni eha egbee shi

english: Why does my cassava crop stay alive during long dry spells while my maize dies?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ hi shi yɛ hɔmɔ ni heɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ gbo lɛ?

english: Cassava has deep taproots that reach water stored deep in the earth, and it can shed its leaves to stop losing moisture. Maize has shallow roots and large leaves, making it much more vulnerable to dry soil.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni shɛɔ nu ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he, ni ebaanyɛ ejie amɛbaai lɛ koni ekɛkpa ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ. Abɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai wuji. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ mlɛo

english: How does covering my crop fields with dry grass or cocoa pods help during dry spells?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi loo kookoo ŋmeii ni mikɛhaa miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil (mulching) acts like an umbrella that shades the dirt from direct sun. It keeps the soil cool, stops moisture from evaporating into the air, and gives your crops water to draw from during dry breaks in the rain.
ga: Mulching (mulching) tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni buɔ muji he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa otsei lɛ ni amɛnáa nu yɛ amɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ.

english: Should I apply chemical fertilizer to my crops if a dry spell is expected soon?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ atsu nii kɛji akɛ etsɛŋ ni hɔmɔ baaba?

english: No, you should avoid applying dry fertilizer before a dry spell. Without enough rainfall to dissolve the fertilizer into the soil, the high concentration of salts can burn your crop's roots and damage the plants.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ okpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni okɛbaafata he lɛ he dani hulutsoo be lɛ aba. Kɛji nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ. Nu ni fa babaoo lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni efite tsei lɛ.

english: What can I do to keep my young vegetable seedlings alive if the rain stops for two weeks?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛmɔ otsii enyɔ?

english: You can protect your seedlings by providing temporary shade using palm fronds, placing mulch around the stems to trap soil moisture, and watering them very early in the morning or late in the evening when the heat is lowest.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo ni okɛ ŋmei baai baatsu nii lɛ nɔ. Mulch bɔle tso lɛ he koni ekɛmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Ni okɛ nu awo mli leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ faaa kwraa lɛ.

english: Which crop varieties should I choose if the weather forecast predicts a short rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ tso esa akɛ mahala kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he adafitswaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku ko baaba?

english: You should choose fast-maturing or early-variety crops that grow and yield within a shorter time frame, allowing them to complete their growth cycle before the rains end abruptly.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya loo tsei srɔtoi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ be kukuoo mli. Enɛ ji koni eha tsei lɛ agbe amɛdalɛ be lɛ naa dani nugbɔ lɛ aba naagbee trukaa.

english: How can I check if the maize seeds I bought from the local market are good quality and pure before planting them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhe tse dani madu?

english: Good quality seeds look uniform in size, clean, and free from cracks or insect holes. You can test seed purity and viability by placing a sample in water—healthy, dense seeds will sink to the bottom, while weak or damaged seeds float and should not be planted.
ga: Dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ dalɛ tamɔ amɛhe, amɛhe tse, ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bu bɛ mli. Obaanyɛ oka bɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ ahe tse ha kɛ bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi amɛha lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ko ni okɛaawo nu mli lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni mli wa ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shishi. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ loo efite lɛ baaho ni esaaa akɛ aduɔ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the main food plants need to build strong, green leaves, so applying well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea will help the crop regain its healthy color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ kooloi amli ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmeii tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su lɛ fɛɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes my cassava leaves to curl up with yellowish spots, and how can I stop it from spreading?
ga: Mɛni haa cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛnáa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ? Ni te aaafee tɛŋŋ atsĩ enaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread by tiny whiteflies. To stop it, uproot and burn infected plants early, and always plant disease-resistant cassava cuttings provided by agricultural officers.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ baa ni ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ woɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ. koni ekpa lɛ Gbalamɔ tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli ni oshã amɛ mra. ni amɛdu ŋmei niji ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi kɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be

english: Why is it necessary to dry my cocoa beans properly on raised mats before selling them to buyers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni magbi mi-kookoo lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsɔji ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ dani mahɔ̃ɔ maha mɛi ni heɔ lɛ?

english: Properly drying cocoa beans on raised mats reduces moisture to safe levels (around 7%), which prevents mold from growing and preserves the bean's rich chocolate flavor. Buyers inspect dryness because high-quality, mold-free beans command the full market price.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni agbiɔ yɛ tsɔji ni awo nɔ lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi kɛyashɛɔ he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe (aaafee 7%), ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ, ni ehaa tsokolate ni mli ŋɔɔ ni yɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ hiɔ shi. Nihɔɔlɔi kwɛɔ bɔ ni egbi lɛ be mli ni kɔfe yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mli bɛ mli lɛ yeɔ jara fɛɛ jara nɔ.

english: If I plant my crops very close together, won't I harvest more food from my field?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani minyɛŋ makpa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔji amli?

english: No, planting too closely forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stems and small yields. Giving crops proper spacing ensures every single plant gets enough resources to produce large, healthy fruits or tubers.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa kã ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo aduawai loo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that easily scorch and dry out under intense sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad living shade and keep the soil moist, acting as protective umbrellas for cocoa during its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: How do I properly weigh and measure my harvested produce to ensure buyers pay me fairly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masusu mikpamɔ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ ni masusu he koni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ awo mi nyɔmɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: You should dry and clean your produce thoroughly before weighing it on a standard scale in kilograms or grams. Knowing the exact weight of your clean produce prevents buyers from underestimating your yield or offering low prices based on guesswork.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ onibii lɛ agbi ni otsumɔ he jogbaŋŋ dani okɛ lɛ asusu yɛ sɛkɛl ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ kilogram loo gram mli. Kɛ́ ole bɔ ni onibii ni he tse lɛ tsiimɔ yɔɔ ha lɛ, ebaatsi mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ anaa koni amɛkabu onibii lɛ akɛ nɔ ko bibioo loo amɛkafee nibii ni baa shi yɛ nɔ ni amɛsusuɔ he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant maize on the same plot of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing maize repeatedly in the same spot drains specific soil nutrients and lets maize-specific pests and diseases multiply in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally recharges soil fertility and breaks pest life cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. kɛ ŋmɛlɛtswaa ni akɛhaa ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ mli kooloi bibii kɛ tsei ahe helai babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Atsake ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni ji ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ ekoŋŋ, ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashihilɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off before developing into actual peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛbatsɔ pepper diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers usually drop off when the plant experiences stress from high temperatures, irregular watering, or a lack of soil phosphorus. Mulching the soil to hold moisture and applying a balanced fertilizer keeps the flowers healthy so they can turn into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo fɔsfɔs ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Mulching koni akɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa bɔ ni sa ni amɛtsɔmɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my young crops so much faster than older crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi tsei bibii lɛ daraa oya fe mi tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Young crops have small, shallow roots and struggle to compete with aggressive weeds for water, sunlight, and fertilizer. Clearing weeds during the first 3 to 6 weeks after planting gives your young crops the head start they need to grow tall and shade out future weeds.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni mli ekɔɔɔ. ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkɛ jwɛi ni mli wa lɛ abɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 3 kɛyashi 6 mli yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ haa odumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa ni etsĩɔ jwɛi ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ anaa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential for leaf growth. The plant starves its older bottom leaves to send remaining nitrogen to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Tsei lɛ hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ yɛ shishigbɛ, baai ni egbɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ amaje koni amɛha tsei heei ni daraa yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium while the fruit is growing. It usually happens when watering is uneven, preventing the plant roots from taking up calcium from the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni ji nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die when I clear all the large trees off my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive under direct, harsh sunlight because their leaves lose moisture faster than their small root systems can absorb water. Planting them near shade crops like plantains protects them until they mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ. Ebaaŋɔ nu. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: What is eating small holes in my corn leaves and leaving behind stuff that looks like brown sawdust inside the plant stem?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ nɔ ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The pest crawls deep inside the center of the plant (the whorl) to eat the tender leaves, leaving behind its waste as it feeds.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shwereɔ kɛboteɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ (ring) lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. ni eshiɔ jwɛi yɛ esɛɛ be mli ni eyeɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my plantain plants turning yellow and growing in a tight, stunted bunch at the top instead of spreading out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi plantain lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiida yɛ ŋmeii ni ebɔle amɛhe yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Banana Bunchy Top Disease, spread by tiny insects called aphids. The virus stunts the plant's growth, causing leaves to stay small, narrow, and bunched together at the tip.
ga: Enɛ ji Banana Bunchy Top hela lɛ he okadi, ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ aphids lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Virus tsiɔ tsei adalɛ naa. Ehaa baa lɛ feɔ bibii, efeɔ mlɛo ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ baa lɛ naa.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden stakes next to my yam vines as soon as they start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahe kɛji amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in the air to catch as much sunlight as possible to produce energy for growing tubers underground. Staking also lifts leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni emɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba kɛha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛmɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Why should I leave wide spaces between my pepper plants instead of planting them close together to get more crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi he ko ni da yɛ pepper tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni amɛwo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When pepper plants are crowded, they fight for soil nutrients and light, resulting in smaller, weaker fruits. Spacing allows air to circulate, drying the leaves faster and reducing fungal disease outbreaks.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ la. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ. He ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. Baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ aba shi

english: Why do my tomato seedlings droop and die right after I move them from the nursery bed into the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Moving seedlings damages delicate root hairs, causing transplant shock because they struggle to absorb water immediately. Moving them late in the afternoon allows plants to recover overnight away from the strong sun.
ga: Dumɔwui ni tsiɔ amɛhe lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi ahe yitsɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Enɛ haa transplant lɛ he feɔ shoo beni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛŋɔ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ yɛ shwane mli lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ nyɔɔŋ kome kɛjɛɔ hulu ni naa wa lɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become soft, watery, and rot underground during heavy rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo, nu yɔɔ mli, ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need oxygen in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits in the field without draining, the roots drown and soil bacteria cause the tubers to rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ efo ŋmɔji ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ amli. Shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni helatsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaha bulb lɛ agbo.

english: Watering early in the morning gives plants time to soak up moisture before the heat of the day. Watering in the hot afternoon leads to fast evaporation and can scorch heated leaves.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ leebi lɛ haa amɛnáa be ni amɛkɛbaaŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli adɔ tsɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ aba oya, ni ebaanyɛ eshã baai ni mli edɔ fe nine lɛ.

english: How long does a newly planted cocoa tree take before it starts bearing fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ yibii?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually start producing pods within 2 to 3 years, while older traditional cocoa trees take about 4 to 5 years to give their first yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo tsei ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo tsei ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛwoɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How do I know when my cocoa pods are mature enough to pick from the tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: Ripe cocoa pods change color from green or deep red to a clear bright yellow or orange, and they make a hollow sound when tapped gently with your knuckles.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni egbɔ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo akutu ni mli tse. ni efeɔ gbɛɛmɔ ko ni mli ewo muji kɛ́ okɛ onine tswa lɛ fioo.

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop leaves during severe dry periods to save water and protect themselves from drought, helping the tree survive until the rainy season returns.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛtsi hɔmɔ naa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ be lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without fruiting when the air is too hot, the soil is too dry, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer causing the plant to produce leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. aloo kɛ́ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ Ha tsei awo baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: What makes my cocoa pods turn black and dry up while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection triggered by excess water, heavy shade, and cold damp conditions during rainy months.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Nu ni fa fe nine, hulutsoo be ni mli wa, kɛ shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ejɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ nyɔji lɛ amli lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa.

english: Leaf curling in cassava is usually caused by the cassava mosaic virus, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects feeding on the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Flɔfoi yɛŋ bibii ni yeɔ baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwãa.

english: Why do I see tiny insects clustering under my cocoa tree leaves and young shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa kooloi bibii lɛ? Abua naa yɛ mi cacao baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ashishi.

english: These insects are usually capsids or aphids, which suck sap from young stems and leaves, causing shoots to die back and reducing pod yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji ŋmeii loo ŋmeii. ni shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii kɛ baai amli lɛ Ehaa tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ ni ehaa pod yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Why is it important to trim or prune the extra branches off my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ loo afolɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei amli lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy to let in air and sunlight, which reduces humidity that causes fungal diseases and encourages the tree to grow more pods.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli lɛ, egbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli. Enɛ haa hulutsoo ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa lɛ baa shi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enáa ŋmeii babaoo

english: Why should I plant crops like cowpeas or beans on my field before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani madu ŋmãa?

english: Beans and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that feeds the next maize crop.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ tsinabii amɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa niyenii haa ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How does heavy rainfall affect my maize seeds right after planting them?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ saa mi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ beni midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall can wash away seeds, compact the soil so seeds cannot sprout, or fill the ground with excess water that rots the seeds before they germinate.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo dumɔwui lɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni dumɔwui lɛ akakwɛ̃. Aloo okɛ nu babaoo awo sũ lɛ mli, ni no baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbo dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to build strong stems and leafy foliage. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their rich green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná ŋmeii kɛ baai ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it good for my land if I plant groundnuts after I harvest my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmei beni mikpa ŋmei sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the earth, but groundnuts are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, acting like a natural restorer for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava stems curling up and turning yellowish-green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ-ŋɔli lɛ?

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, carried by tiny whiteflies. It prevents the cassava plant from making food efficiently, which keeps the tuberous roots from growing big beneath the ground.
ga: Hela nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ akɛ mɛi ni hiɛɔ, ni no tsiɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ anaa jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkahoo. Enɛ haaa tuberous shishifãi lɛ adara yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark black and rot during the damp rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that grows quickly in warm, wet shade. Pruning extra shade tree branches lets air and sunlight into the farm to keep the pods dry.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni daa oya yɛ shĩa mli hei ni edɔ, ni efɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Niji ni afoɔ koni aná hulutsoo babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ŋmeii lɛ akagbi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds right after the very first small rainfall of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔi fioo ni nɛɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first light rain often wets only the top surface, and a long dry dry spell can follow. If you plant too early, the heat will dry out and destroy the newly sprouted seeds before full rains return.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ haa ŋwɛigbɛ pɛ fɔ̃ɔ. Ni hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ baanyɛ anyiɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dɔlɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni efiteɔ dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any tomatoes during hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high and water is low, tomato plants drop their blossoms as a defense mechanism to conserve energy and survive the stress.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni nu lɛ hu faaa lɛ Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he ni amɛyeɔ nɔnyɛɛ mli.

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, water, and soil food. When weeds take over, your crops do not get enough nourishment to grow strong leaves or heavy fruit.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni jwɛi lɛ yeɔ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha baai ni wa loo aduawai ni tsii aba.

english: Why should I trim off some of the bottom branches on my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-tomato tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Trimming lower branches keeps leaves from touching wet soil where fungal diseases hide, and it forces the plant to send its energy into making bigger, healthy fruit.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni aaafo lɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkashɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ he he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ lɛ. ni ebaanyɛ tsei anɔ koni amɛtsu hewalɛ koni amɛwo yibii wuji ni mli wa

english: Why do saved seeds from last year's harvested maize yield less grain when I replant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui ni mikɛwo nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ woɔ dumɔwui fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds lose their special vigor and uniformity after the first generation. Replanting saved seeds yields weaker plants with smaller ears compared to fresh certified seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛ nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ baaha tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni toi bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ aba kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow very fast and have wide leaves that act like umbrellas, providing shade and trapping soil moisture to help the cocoa survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha hulutsoo ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eye ebua kookoo ni ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do I have to build high soil mounds before planting my seed yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔma gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ dani wɔdu ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow large underground and need soft, loose earth to expand easily. Building mounds keeps the soil loose and prevents water from pooling around the tubers, which would cause them to rot.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daraa wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛbiɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli edɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya. Kɛ́ afee gɔŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi, ni ehaaa nu akabɔle bulb lɛ he, ni no haa sũ lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Beans and groundnuts have special roots that trap air from the atmosphere and feed it into the soil as natural fertilizer. This makes the soil richer and helps crops like maize grow bigger and healthier without buying extra chemical fertilizers.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nii babaoo ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ni amɛdaraa ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛhe tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli.

english: Why should I cover the bare ground around my crops with dry leaves and grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi aha he ni miŋmɔ lɛ yɔɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with organic material, called mulching, blocks the hot sun from drying out the earth. It keeps the soil cool, holds water longer so plants do not dry up, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛhaa lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsĩ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa ni ebaatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Ehaa nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ Koni tsei lɛ akagbi. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why are the leaf tips of my young maize plants getting tiny holes and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ? ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ?

english: Tiny caterpillars, often called fall armyworms, hide inside the center leaves of the maize plant and eat them from the inside out. The leaf damage stops the plant from making food properly, causing it to turn yellow.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ amɛ fall caterpillars lɛ, kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛmli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Baai ni fiteɔ lɛ haaa tso lɛ afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. ni haa efeɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly droop and dry up even when the ground is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni amɛgbiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by tiny soil organisms or bacteria that enter the roots and block the tubes that carry water inside the stem. Even if there is water in the soil, the plant cannot drink it, causing it to wilt.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ kɛbaa. yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni boteɔ shishifãi lɛ amli ni etsiɔ paipii ni kɛ nu yaa yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa Eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ sũ lɛ mli moŋ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ anu nu. ha egbi

english: Why do young green oranges fall off my trees before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tangerine bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tsei anɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Trees drop young fruits when they do not have enough water, nutrients, or strength to support all of them to maturity. It can also happen if insects bite the flower base or tiny fruits early in the season.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ aduawai bibii kɛji nu, niyenii, loo hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua aduawai bibii muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛyashi be mli ni eshɛɔ dalɛ he lɛ bɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ kooloi ŋmɔ fɔfɔi loo aduawai bibii ashishi yɛ be lɛ mli mra.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers underground are ready to harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving bare stems, and the base of the main stem begins to swell and crack the soil surface.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi, ni amɛshi tso lɛ shishi, ni tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know if the earth is wet enough to plant my seeds after the major rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu midumɔwui yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ?

english: Scoop up a handful of soil from a hand-length deep and squeeze it into a ball. If it holds its shape without dripping excess water and breaks apart easily when pressed, the soil is ready for planting.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ sũ fioo ko kɛjɛ tso ko mli ni okɛmimɔ mli ni efee bɔɔlu. Kɛji ehiɛ egbɛhe lɛ mli ni nu ni fa fe nine shwieee shi ni efoɔ oya kɛji akɛ anyɛ nɔ. Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ eshɛ he kɛha dumɔ.

english: Why am I told not to let chemical fertilizer touch the stem or leaves of my crops when applying it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛɛ mi akɛ mikaha tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ akashɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi loo baai ahe beni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains concentrated salts that pull water out of the plant tissue. If it touches leaves or stems directly, it chemically burns the plant and can kill it.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmei ni mli wa ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe fãji amli. Kɛji akɛ ekɛ baai loo shishifãi lɛ kpe tɛ̃ɛ Tso lɛ baatsɔ tsofa nɔ esha ni enɛ baanyɛ agbe lɛ.

english: Sir, why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which acts as essential food for the crop, or the soil has too much water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure will help bring back their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ atsɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very tall with many leaves but gives me very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or chemical fertilizer, the cassava puts all its energy into growing top stems and leaves instead of roots. Cassava needs balanced nutrients and good sunlight to store energy underground into big roots.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ babaoo lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishifãi kɛ baai anɔ moŋ fe shishifãi. Niyenii ni ja kɛ hulu la kpakpa he miihia cassava koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi ni eda ni etsɔ shishifãi wuji.

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first rain because the soil underneath is still dry and warm. Wait until you get two or three heavy rains so the soil is wet deep down, giving seeds enough water to sprout safely.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi ni edɔ lolo. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ nɛ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni okɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Sir, why should I buy certified seeds from the shop instead of using seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ kɛjɛ shwapo ko mli moŋ fe ni mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Saved seeds from hybrid crops lose their yield strength and disease resistance in the second generation. Certified seeds are specially produced to sprout evenly, resist common pests, and give you much higher harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ baafite yibiiwoo hewalɛ kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Afeɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ, ni ehaa yibii babaoo baa

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant maize and cassava together in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize grows quickly and is ready to harvest in three months, while cassava grows slowly over a full year. Planting them together lets you harvest maize first without disturbing the cassava, giving you two crops from the same land and labor.
ga: Abɛi daa oya, ni nyɔji etɛ mli lɛ, esa akɛ akpa. Cassava kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Hefatalɔi dumɔ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmãa lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ni ogbalaaa ŋmãa lɛ naa. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ nitsumɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die if I clear all the large forest trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under full sunlight and dry winds. Leaving tall shade trees creates a cool shelter that keeps the air humid and protects the young cocoa leaves until the plants grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi shishi. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ ni ekwɛ ŋwɛi ni eyɛ hulutsoo lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ daa waa.

english: Why do tomato fruits develop black rotten spots at the bottom before they can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato aduawai lɛ yɛ ŋmeii diji ni fiteɔ yɛ amɛshishi dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: This rot happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium or water while the tomatoes are forming. Irrigating your farm regularly and adding lime or wood ash to the soil prevents this damage.
ga: Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa beni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana calcium loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni tomato lɛ miifee lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu shwie oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ daa ni okɛ lime loo tso sũ fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ akafite.

english: Sir, why do armyworms destroy my young maize plants so fast without me seeing them early?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ kpata mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahiɛ oya ni minaaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Armyworm caterpillars crawl deep inside the center growing funnel of the maize stalk during the day to hide from heat and spraying. They eat the tender internal leaves secretly before emerging in large numbers.
ga: Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmeii ni miida yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛtee amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ahe. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ teemɔŋ dani amɛjeɔ kpo babaoo.

english: Why is it good for me to trim some of the branches off my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mafolɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ aniji komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Removing excess lower branches and leaves opens up the plant to sunlight and air flow, stopping diseases and directing the plant's food into growing bigger peppers instead of useless leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ niji kɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ aná tso lɛ. Ehaa helai kpaa ni ekɛ tso lɛ yeɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ najiaŋ.

english: How does planting cover crops like velvet beans keep my soil wet during dry days?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ tamɔ velvet bean ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli?

english: Cover crops spread across the ground like a thick carpet. This carpet shades the earth, blocking the sun from drying out the dirt and keeping water locked in the soil for your main crops.
ga: Egbɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ kapɛti ni mli wa. Kapɛti nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ shade, ni ehaa hulu la lɛ shɛɛɛ he, ni ehaaa muji akagbi. ni okɛ nu ato shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha onibii titrii lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth, or that heavy rains have washed the nutrients too deep into the soil. Adding a nitrogen-based fertilizer like Urea or NPK when the soil is moist helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Aloo, nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo NPK fata he beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting beans or groundnuts on my farmland help my soil for the next crop season?
ga: Te ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Beans and groundnuts are legumes that gather nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants die, they leave this nitrogen in the soil, which acts as a natural fertilizer for your next crop, such as maize or cassava.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, eshiɔ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce big tall stems with leaves, but tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai kakadaji lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or the plants get too much shade, the cassava puts all its energy into growing tall leaves above ground rather than storing food below. cassava needs full sunlight and balanced soil to send energy down into building thick tubers.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo tso lɛ ná hulutsoo babaoo lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaai lɛ amli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔɔŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni Yucca baato niyenii yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ, hulu ni eyi obɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ja he miihia lɛ koni ekɛ ehewalɛ awo ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ afeemɔ mli.

english: Is it necessary to put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb, or can I let them spread on the bare ground?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni makɛ tso ko ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ? Aloo obaanyɛ oshi lɛ kɛkɛ ni egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ ko bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes so their leaves can catch direct sunlight to make food for growing large tubers. Letting them trail on the ground exposes leaves to soil diseases and shade, leading to much smaller yields.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ koni amɛha amɛbaai lɛ aya hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulb agboi ni miida lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ aná hela yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ebaaha hulutsoo aba. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ faaa kwraa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant suffers from sudden dry conditions. High heat stresses the plant and prevents proper pollination, so the plant drops its flowers to save water and energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi trukaa lɛ tso lɛ naa amanehulu. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ ni etsĩɔ pollination ni sa naa. Bɔni afee ni tsei akafite nu kɛ hewalɛ, amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies hiding under the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by these insects. Spraying early with neem oil or appropriate farm insecticides protects new growth from twisting.
