ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper leaf curl baa. aloo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Neem fɔ loo tsofai ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli mra. Enɛ baatsi dalɛ hee naa koni ekatsɔ.

english: It is best to water early in the morning because the soil can absorb water before the sun evaporates it. Watering in the hot afternoon sun causes quick evaporation and can stress hot leaves, while watering late at night leaves foliage damp, which invites fungal rot.
ga: Esa akɛ afee nu leebi maŋkpa ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu dani hulu la lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baaha hulu lɛ atsɔ oya ni ebaanyɛ eha baai ni tsoɔ waa lɛ afee nɔ ni haoɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni oooha amɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋmei lɛ agbo.

english: What makes my plantain trees fall over easily just when the fruit bundle gets big?
ga: Mɛni haa mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi mlɛo nɛkɛ kɛ́ amɛfee kui wuji?

english: Plantain trees fall over because tiny microscopic worms called nematodes or stem borers attack and weaken the root system under the ground. Staking heavy plantain trees with bamboo poles and keeping soil clean around roots prevents them from toppling in strong winds.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ tutuaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni tsii wo dumɔwui lɛ ahe, ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ he tse yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, dark, and cool conditions. Pruning extra shade branches to let sunlight reach the trunk helps dry out the pods and stops the fungus from multiplying.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ, duŋ, ni mli ejɔ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji krokomɛi ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ amli koni hulu la ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafa babaoo.

english: Why should I wait for the main rains to fully start before planting my seeds instead of planting after the first early rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ aje shishi dani madu dumɔwui moŋ fe ni madu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rainfall often trickles away quickly and is followed by a dry hot spell. If seeds sprout after the first rain and no follow-up rain falls, the fragile young shoots will dry up and die in the hot soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ hoɔ oya. ni ahum ni mli edɔ ni egbi nyiɛɔ sɛɛ Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ bɛ. Tsofɔi bibii ni waaa lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know when my maize is completely ready to be harvested from the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Maize is fully mature and ready to harvest when the leaves and husks turn brown and dry, and the kernels become hard so that your fingernail cannot easily dent them.
ga: Abele lɛ eda ni esa akɛ akpa kɛji baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi. Ni dumɔwui lɛ mli wa waa akɛ amɛbaafee nɔ ni shwieɔ otsitsi nɔ mlɛo.

english: What is the best way to store my harvested maize so it does not spoil?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni aaatsɔ nɔ aha ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ akafite?

english: Dry the harvested maize thoroughly under the sun until the grains are very hard, then store them in clean, airtight bags (PICS bags) or raised granaries kept off the ground to prevent moisture, mold, and insects.
ga: Gbimɔ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu lɛ shishi kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛto vacuum bag ni he tse (PICS bag) loo ŋmɔ mli ni awo nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi bibii ahe.

english: What should I do if armyworms attack my corn right when it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ ŋmeii tutua mi-ŋmãa lɛ yɛ kpamɔ be lɛ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: If the corn is mature, harvest it as quickly as possible to save the crop from further damage, and avoid spraying chemical pesticides right before harvesting so the grain remains safe to eat.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Kpamɔ oya bɔ ni ooonyɛ koni ohere ŋmãa lɛ yiwala kɛjɛ fitemɔ kroko mli. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni oooshwie nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani okpa. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe ni aye.

english: Can I put my freshly harvested corn directly into storage bags right after picking it?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ni akpa ehee lɛ afata he. Ani abaanyɛ akɛwo kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ beni akɛto sɛɛ?

english: No, fresh corn contains moisture that causes heat, mold, and rot if bagged immediately. You must dry the corn well in the sun until the grain moisture is very low before bagging it.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔtɔ ni baanyɛ aha hulutsoo, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba kɛji akɛ awo kotoku mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmãa hee mli. Ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmãa lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ baa shi waa ni okɛwo baagi mli.

english: What happens if I am forced to leave mature corn on the field for a few weeks without harvesting it?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ anyɛ minɔ koni mashi ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ mli otsii fioo komɛi ni mikpaaa hu?

english: Leaving mature corn in the field exposes it to rain, field pests like armyworms or weevils, birds, and rodents, which will cause the cobs to rot and reduce your overall yield.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi ŋmãa ni egbɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ anɛ. Gbɛjegbɛ nɔ kooloi tamɔ armyworms loo ŋmeii, okpoi kɛ ŋmeii. Enɛ baaha ŋmei lɛ agbo ni ebaaha yibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ aba shi.

english: Why is sun-drying my corn so important before taking it to the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa waa akɛ magbi mi-ŋma lɛ dani mikɛya ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Sun-drying removes water from inside the kernels. Lower water content prevents dangerous mold from growing and makes the grains too hard for pests to bore into easily.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ni agbiɔ yɛ hulu la mli lɛ jieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli. Nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni eba shi lɛ tsiɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni ekakwɛ̃. ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ mlɛo tsɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai nyɛŋ abote mli mlɛo.

english: How can I protect my stored corn from weevils without using dangerous chemicals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-abele ni mikɛto lɛ he kɛjɛ ŋmeii ahe ni mikɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara tsuuu nii?

english: You can use airtight triple-layer hermetic storage bags which suffocate any insects inside, or mix safe organic preservatives like neem leaf powder or ash with dry grains.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ vacuum storage bag ni yɔɔ fãi etɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli ni baanyɛ ajie kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ atsu nii. Aloo okɛ nɔ ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛbuɔ nii ahe tamɔ neem baa powda loo sũ afutu dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ.

english: Is it good to harvest my corn early if caterpillars start eating the farm?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaakpa ŋmãa mra? Kɛji ŋmeii lɛ bɔi ŋmɔ lɛ yeli?

english: If the maize grains have already formed and hardened, harvesting early can save the crop from total destruction, but you must make sure to dry the cobs thoroughly off the field.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ efee ni ewa Nikpamɔ mra baanyɛ ahere ŋmãa lɛ yiwala kɛjɛ hiɛkpatamɔ nɔ kwraa. Shi ehe miihia ni okwɛ koni ŋmei lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ kponɔ.

english: Can I store corn cobs that were partially eaten by insects together with healthy corn?
ga: Ani manyɛ mabua ŋmãa ni ayeɔ fã ko lɛ naa kɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: No, you should separate insect-damaged cobs from good ones. Damaged cobs collect moisture and attract pests quickly, which will spread and ruin the rest of your healthy stored corn.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ ogbala ŋmeii ni kooloi efite lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ateŋ. Cobs ni efite lɛ buaa ŋmɔtɔ naa oya ni egbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ. Enɛ baagbɛ abele fɛɛ ni eshwɛ ni ato jogbaŋŋ lɛ ashwã ni efite.

english: Why do armyworms suddenly appear in large numbers on my maize field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cutworms lɛ miije kpo trukaa babaoo yɛ mi-ŋma ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Armyworm moths travel long distances on the wind and lay hundreds of eggs on healthy green crops. Warm weather causes these eggs to hatch all at once into large groups of hungry caterpillars.
ga: Caterpillar moth lɛ fãa gbɛ kakadaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ewoɔ wuji ohai abɔ yɛ tsei eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii akui wuji ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ shikome.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow instead of green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient in the soil. It can also happen when heavy rain washes away soil nutrients or when weeds steal the plant's food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ loo kɛji jwɛi ju tsei aniyenii.

english: How do I know the exact right time to plant my seeds after the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ hɔmɔ sɛɛ?

english: You should wait until the rainy season settles and the soil stays moist for a few consecutive days, usually after two or three good rains, so the seeds have enough moisture to sprout without drying up in the soil.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba shi ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbii fioo komɛi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii 2-3 sɛɛ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ akagbi.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting if I leave them in the ground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Too much standing water in the soil drowns the roots by cutting off air. Excess soil water encourages rot-causing fungi and bacteria to attack and spoil the cassava underground.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ babaoo lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebaafo mli lɛ nɔ. Nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfite amɛ.

english: Maize drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every season. Planting it repeatedly exhausts the soil completely and allows pests that feed on maize to multiply in that spot.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Nibii ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ faa yɛ nakai he lɛ.

english: This is caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which thrives in cool, dark, and excessively wet conditions. Pruning heavy foliage to let in sunlight and fresh air helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Fungi hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpod kɛ enɛ baa. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, duŋ, kɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ fe nine. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni tsii lɛ amli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa aba lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ amli tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow weak and thin when I plant too many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough root and leaf room to absorb what it needs to grow thick and strong.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛyeɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa shishifãi kɛ baai ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aŋɔ nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee hewalɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when weather gets extremely hot or when the soil dries out completely. High temperatures interfere with pollination, causing the plant to drop its flowers to protect itself.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ tsiɔ pollination naa. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe.

english: Why shouldn't I pour dry fertilizer directly against the stem of my young plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi woɔ tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer contains concentrated salts that can burn and kill the tender stem and roots of young crops. Place fertilizer a few inches away in a ring or groove so the roots can draw it in safely.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ashã ni efite tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo ŋwɛi ŋta loo ŋtayaa mli inchii fioo komɛi koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbala kɛbote mli shweshweeshwe.

english: Weeds are naturally wild and tough, so they react quickly to open sunlight and moist soil. They absorb available soil food and water faster than delicate crop seedlings, which is why early weed clearing is necessary.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji adebɔɔ nɔ, adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wa. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛfeɔ amɛnii oya kɛji amɛgbele hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ. Amɛheɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ oya fe tsei dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ.

english: How long will it take for my new oil palm seedlings to start bearing fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani mi-palm dumɔwui heei lɛ baaje yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Oil palm seedlings usually take about 3 to 4 years after planting to produce their first harvestable fruit bunches when given proper care and fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mu tso dumɔwui lɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ dani amɛwoɔ aduawai akui ni abaanyɛ akpa klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa kɛji akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni awo amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How far apart should I plant my oil palm seedlings in the field?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu oil palm dumɔwui yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Oil palm trees should be planted about 9 meters apart in a triangular pattern so their large fronds do not block sunlight from each other as they grow.
ga: Esa akɛ adu mu tsei ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 9 yɛ gbɛ ni tamɔ koŋ etɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni baai wuji lɛ akatsi hulu la lɛ naa yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Yes, intercropping cassava or maize between young palm trees during the first 2 to 3 years is good, as long as you keep the food crops a few meters away from the palm stem to avoid competition for nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii ateŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 lɛ hi. Shii abɔ ni okɛ niyenii tsei lɛ toɔ he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji ninetalɔi fioo komɛi koni akaye niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋshii lɛ,.

english: Yellowing leaves often mean the plant is lacking nitrogen or water. Adding balanced fertilizer or compost and maintaining moisture will help the leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen loo nu bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my oil palm flowers dry up and fall off without producing fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei fɔfɔi komɛi gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Palm flowers fall off when trees experience stress from lack of water, poor soil nutrients, or insufficient pollination by beneficial palm insects.
ga: Palm fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ mli. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ehiii loo ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ni haaa ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa

english: Why do the leaves on my palm trees droop downwards during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Palm trees naturally bend their lower fronds downward during hot, dry weather to conserve water and protect the central growing trunk from severe heat.
ga: Palm tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛshishi baai lɛ anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Koni akɛbu nu he ni abu tso lɛ teŋgbɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he.

english: Why are the fruit bunches on my oil palm trees becoming smaller each year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai akui ni yɔɔ mi-oil palm tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee bibii daa afi lɛ?

english: Smaller fruit bunches usually mean the nutrients in the soil have been exhausted by previous harvests. Applying recommended fertilizers will restore fruit size and yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai bibii ni abua naa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ efo kɛjɛ ŋmaa ni akpa tsutsu lɛ mli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ baaye abua ni aduawai lɛ adalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: How do I know when an oil palm fruit bunch is ripe and ready to harvest?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei yibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: A palm bunch is ready for harvest when a few bright reddish-orange fruits loosen and fall to the ground naturally, showing high oil content inside.
ga: Palm tsei akui lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni aduawai fioo komɛi ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ gbee shikpɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Ejie lɛ kpo akɛ mu babaoo yɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to prune the lower fronds from my oil palm tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mu tso ko shishi baai lɛ?

english: Pruning dead or old lower leaves makes it easier to inspect and harvest fruit bunches while allowing the tree to direct its energy toward growing new leaves and fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egboi loo ni egbɔ lɛ, ebaaha efee mlɛo akɛ aaakwɛ aduawai akui lɛ amli ni akpa amɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ kɛyaa baai kɛ aduawai heei adalɛ mli.

english: What causes a black soot-like coating to appear on my oil palm leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-oil palm lɛ baai lɛ feɔ diŋ ni tamɔ sũ?

english: Black soot is caused by a fungus growing on sugary waste left by insect pests like mealybugs; clearing the insects will stop the fungus from blocking sunlight on the leaves.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ sũ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ sũ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ sugar ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ mealybugs lɛ shiɔ lɛ nɔ; Kɛ́ atsa kooloi bibii lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni ekatsi hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ naa.

english: How do I check if the piece of land I want to rent or use is actually suitable for growing cabbages?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni misumɔɔ ni maha loo mikɛtsu nii lɛ sa diɛŋtsɛ kɛha kaabii adumɔ?

english: Good land for cabbage should have loose, dark topsoil that drains water easily after rain. Cabbages need soil that holds moisture without staying waterlogged, as wet roots will rot.
ga: Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni akɛduɔ kaabe lɛ aná shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ediŋ ni nu hoɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni nu bɛ mli lɛ he miihia Kaabaji. Ejaakɛ shishifãi ni efɔ lɛ baagboi.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow soon after I plant them on newly cleared land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ trukaa beni midu yɛ he ko ni ajie ehee lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plants are starving for nitrogen. When you clear fresh bush, the decaying plant material in the soil temporarily traps nitrogen, leaving little available for your new crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Kɛji ojie jwɛi heei Tsei ni fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen lɛ be kukuoo ko. Enɛ ha eshwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why are my cabbage plants producing large green leaves but not forming a hard head in the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ewaaa yɛ eyitso teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to head when they get too much nitrogen fertilizer, face irregular watering, or experience extreme heat during the stage when the head is supposed to close.
ga: Kaabage nyɛŋ ajie eyitso kɛji enine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa bo daa loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa kpeɔ yɛ be mli ni esa akɛ aŋmɛ yitso lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in the afternoon heat is a plant's natural way of protecting itself to reduce water loss. If the leaves uncurl when the sun goes down, your plant is normal; if they stay curled, the crop needs water or is under attack by tiny pests like aphids.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe he koni nu ni efiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Kɛji baai lɛ shwie shi beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ ji nɔ ni sa. Kɛji amɛkoto Dumɔwui lɛ he miihia nu loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ ŋmeii tutuaa amɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable crop flowers fall off before any fruit or vegetable actually grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai loo aduawai lɛ daa diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off when plants face severe stress, such as sudden hot spells, prolonged dry soil, or a shortage of essential nutrients like phosphorus and calcium.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa kpe, tamɔ ahum ni mli edɔ trukaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi be kakadaŋŋ. aloo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs kɛ kalsium ni bɛ

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings suddenly fall over and die right at the base of the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ miigboi yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: This is a common condition called 'damping-off' caused by soil fungus. It happens when seedbeds are kept too wet, planted too densely, or lack proper sunlight and airflow.
ga: Enɛ ji shihilɛ ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘Damping’ ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa Ebaa kɛji he ni dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. adu babaoo tsɔ loo hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ bɛ mli.

english: How does heavy rainfall in Ghana affect my young cabbage crop?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ Ghana lɛ saa mi-cabbage tsei bibii lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy downpours can wash away important topsoil nutrients, damage young leaves physically, and soak the soil so much that roots choke from a lack of air, inviting fungal diseases.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kpãtãa baai bibii lɛ ahiɛ yɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ ni ekɛ sũ lɛ ewo nu mli aahu akɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ hewɔ lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa.

english: Why do some of my vegetables stay stunted and grow slowly even though I water them every morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ ekomɛi egbɔjɔ ni amɛdaraa oya eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: Watering alone is not enough; crops need soil nutrients to grow. Overwatering can also drown root systems, preventing them from taking up the food they need from the ground.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ pɛ faaa. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia tsei koni amɛdara. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Enɛ haaa anyɛ ajie niyenii ni otaoɔ lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are small worms eating holes right through the leaves of my cabbage plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu kɛmiitsɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are caterpillars, often the Diamondback moth larvae, which feed heavily on green leaves. They lay eggs on the undersides of leaves and can completely ruin a cabbage crop if not managed early.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii. Bei pii lɛ, enɛɛmɛi ji Diamondback ŋmei ni yeɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo lɛ ŋmeii. Amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ baai lɛ ashishi, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite kaabe tsei lɛ kwraa kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii mra.

english: Why should I avoid planting cabbage on the exact same piece of land season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ kaabii dumɔ he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously allows pests and soil diseases that feed on that specific crop to build up in the ground. Rotating cabbage with crops like maize or beans breaks this disease cycle and helps keep the soil healthy.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake kaabeji. Ebaakpa hela nɛɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ, ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in an open field without any trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that cannot withstand harsh direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain or shade trees protects the young cocoa from heat, retains soil moisture, and creates a cool environment for roots to settle.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo shade tsei ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ latsaa he. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ofee shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi.

english: Yellowing of bottom leaves is a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the plant moves its limited nutrients from older bottom leaves up to the newer top leaves so it can keep growing.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen faaa Tsei lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni fa fioo kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei amli koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Why do my cassava plants shed all their leaves during the long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ shwie shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves to conserve water and survive extreme heat. Shedding foliage stops moisture from evaporating through the leaves, allowing the plant to remain alive underground until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa. Baai ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ haa nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ kpaa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize stalks roll up tightly like needles during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a defense mechanism maize uses to reduce the leaf area exposed to the sun. This slows down water loss through transpiration when soil moisture is low or temperatures are very high.
ga: Baai ni atsiɔ lɛ ji hebuu gbɛ ni ŋmãa kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛba he ni baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la lɛ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ haa nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baa shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ faaa loo hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa.

english: Why do my yam vines need to be staked with tall sticks instead of trailing along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ awo tsei kakadaji anɔ moŋ fe ni aaagbala shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up to catch direct sunlight and improves air movement around the plant. Better access to sunlight allows leaves to make more food, which results in larger, healthier tubers underground.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ bɔleɔ amɛhe. Nitsumɔhe lɛ etee hiɛ Hulu la ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii babaoo. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites, or viruses spread by whiteflies. These pests feed on sap from young leaves, causing stunted and deformed growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ yeɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ. Enɛ haa dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why are the dark bottom tips of my green tomatoes turning soft and black before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ najiaŋ feɔ ediŋŋ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit. It usually happens when watering is irregular, which prevents the roots from taking up calcium consistently from the soil.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ji blossom end rot, ni calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my plantain plants produce small, thin bunches when I leave all the young suckers growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Bei komɛi kɛ́ mishi ŋmeii bibii yɛ Nakai tsei lɛ ahe

english: Multiple suckers compete with the main plant for nutrients, water, and sunlight. Pruning excess shoots—leaving only one main stem and one or two followers—concentrates nutrients into growing larger, heavier bunches.
ga: Suckers babaoo kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la. Kpãa tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ amli, ni oshi tso titri kome kɛ sɛɛnyiɛlɔi kome loo enyɔ pɛ. Enɛ baaha niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ afee ekome koni eha ŋmeii lɛ afee wuji ni amɛtsii.

english: Why do groundnut flowers drop down and push themselves into the dirt after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants form their pods underground. Once the flower is pollinated above ground, the stalk bends down and grows into the soil (a process called pegging), where the groundnut pod safely matures.
ga: Peanut tsei feɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔii lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shishifã lɛ baabɔle ni eda kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does growing cowpeas or beans on my field make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have beneficial root bacteria that convert nitrogen gas from the air into usable soil nutrients. When the legume crop finishes, this natural nitrogen stays in the soil and feeds the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi amli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni tsakeɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ewoɔ niyenii ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ adu legume lɛ agbe naa Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains rot quickly when I store them in my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛto mitsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Harvested maize rots quickly if it is not dried properly before storage. Extra moisture inside the grain attracts mold and insects, so drying them in the sun until they are hard prevents spoilage.
ga: Abele ni akpa lɛ baafite oya kɛji akɛ agbiko lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani akɛto. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ gbalaa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaawa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni efiteɔ.

english: Can I use small machines to clear and weed my farm instead of using just a cutlass?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsɔne bibioo ko atsu nii ni mikɛjie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mikɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi lɛ baatsu nii kɛkɛ?

english: Yes, using small motorized tools like brush cutters or light tillers can save time and reduce body strain, allowing you to manage your farm faster and clear land with less effort.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ akɛ nibii bibii ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi loo tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ be akafite ni eha nɔnyɛɛ ni baa gbɔmɔtso lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okwɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ oya ni ojieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ fioo ko pɛ.

english: How do I know the best time to harvest my tomatoes so they don't spoil before I sell them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa tomato? Enɛ ji koni tomato lɛ akafite dani ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: Harvest tomatoes when they just start showing a pinkish or reddish color at the bottom. Picking them at this stage allows them to ripen safely during transport without rotting on the farm.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ tomato kɛji ebɔi pinki loo red yɛ shishigbɛ. Nɛkɛ gbɛ ni akɛtoɔ he nɛɛ haa amɛshwereɔ shweshweeshwe yɛ be mli ni akɛ amɛ yaa lɛ mli ni amɛgbooo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside them acts like a shelter, protecting the cocoa leaves from burning until the trees mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Etsuɔ nii akɛ shĩa Buu kookoo baai ahe koni amɛkashã kɛyashi tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to create food for the tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves up towards the sun while keeping them off the damp ground where diseases can attack them.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ kwɛɔ hulu lɛ hiɛ, ni ehaa amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ ahe. baanyɛ atutua

english: Why does my cassava produce huge green leaves above ground but very small tubers under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or gets excess rain early in the season, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing top leaves instead of storing food in the tubers underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo nugbɔ enɛ babaoo yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ebaai lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii amli lɛ,.

english: Yellowing in a V-shape starting at the leaf tips means your corn lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to stay green and grow strong stalks.
ga: Yellow ni yɔɔ V su mli ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ anaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛ ŋmɔji lɛ amli ni amɛkwɛ̃ amɛshishifãi ni wa.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer to my crops when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo miŋmɔshi nibii amli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so plant roots can absorb it safely. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn the roots and waste the fertilizer.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite.

english: Planting seeds too close causes the crops to compete with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak, thin stalks that produce small or empty cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni feɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ baa. loo dumɔwui ni nɔ ko bɛ mli

english: Why are there holes in my young maize leaves with tiny dark droppings inside the center shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ? Eyɛ teŋgbɛ tso lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central shoot of young maize plants and eats the tender growing leaves before the cobs form.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli lɛ. ni oye baai bibii lɛ dani ŋmei lɛ afee.

english: What causes my cassava leaves to turn yellow and curl up, and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni haa cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ? Ni te aaafee tɛŋŋ akpa?

english: Leaf curling and yellowing in cassava is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. You can protect your farm by planting disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by agricultural officers and removing infected plants right away.
ga: Kasava lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela kɛbaa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛtsɔ ŋmei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ ni ooodu kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooojie oya lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning pale green and growing very slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiida blɛoo waa lɛ?

english: Pale green leaves and slow growth usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to grow green and strong. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea will help the maize regain its dark green color and grow faster.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ amɛdalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eda oya.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun and can die in dry weather. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that provide living shade, keeping the young cocoa seedlings cool and moist until they are strong enough to handle full sunlight.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo. Ha cacao tsei bibii lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhe hulu la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why should I alternate planting groundnuts with maize on the same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake mihe kɛdu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil, while legumes like groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the earth. Rotating these crops keeps your soil fertile naturally without relying only on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii nɛɛ ni oootsake lɛ yeɔ ebuaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni okɛ ohe fɔ̃ɔɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ pɛ nɔ.

english: How far apart should I space my maize seeds when planting during the rainy season?
ga: Beni aduɔ nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ Te esa akɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ ajɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Spacing maize about 75 centimeters between rows and 25 centimeters between plants gives each plant enough light, soil nutrients, and water to grow big cobs without crowding and competing with each other.
ga: Gbɛ ni kã ŋmãa lɛ teŋ lɛ ji aaafee sɛntimita 75, ni tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji aaafee sɛntimita 25, ni no haa tsei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko kpɛɔ waa. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃ ni amɛfeee ekome ni amɛkɛ amɛhe akaŋ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves wilt in the hot afternoon even when the soil is not completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbiko kwraa?

english: During intense midday heat, pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the soil. Mulching the ground around the stems with dry grass keeps the roots cool and reduces water loss.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Pepper tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mulching ni akɛwo Dry stems lɛ ahe lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni ebaaha nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when the plant experiences stress from extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Giving the plants consistent water at the base and adding balanced nutrients helps the blossoms stay on and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa kɛ niyenii ni ja ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How do I know that my maize is completely ready to harvest from the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the leaves turn brown and dry, the husks turn papery, and a small black spot appears at the base of the grain kernel. Harvesting at this time prevents rot and keeps field insects from damaging the grain.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi. Kpoji lɛ tsɔɔ wolo. Ni ŋmeii bibii diji yɛ jɛmɛ. Ejeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii ashishi Nibii ni akpaa yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ dumɔwui lɛ.

english: How can I stop weevils from destroying my harvested beans in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ŋmeii ni akpa yɛ nitoohe lɛ?

english: Weevils thrive on moisture and air in stored grains. Sun-dry your beans until they are completely hard before storing them in clean, airtight bags or sealed containers to suffocate any pests and keep the beans fresh.
ga: Weevils lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ amli. Gbimɔ ŋmeii lɛ aahu kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kwraa dani okɛwo kotokui ni he tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo nibii krokomɛi ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli koni ekɛshwie ŋmeii lɛ ni eha ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What is the best time of the day to water my vegetable garden?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ aduawai abɔɔ mli nu?

english: The best times to water vegetables are early morning or late afternoon. Watering during these cooler times allows the roots to absorb the moisture deeply before the hot sun evaporates the water.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ aduawai anɔ nu ji leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli. Nu ni akɛhaa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ nu ni mli kwɔ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ nɔ.

english: Do I really need to put fertilizer on my yam farm, or will the yam grow fine on its own?
ga: Ehe miihia waa ni mawo mi sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Aloo ani ŋmeii baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe?

english: While yams can grow without added plant food in very rich soil, using the right fertilizer gives the tubers extra nutrients to grow much larger, healthier, and give you a better harvest overall.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ abaanyɛ adu sweet potatoes ni akɛ tsei niyenii fataaa he yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii waa nɔ moŋ, Shi kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha bulbs lɛ aná niyenii babaoo ni baaye abua amɛ ni amɛdara. Na hewalɛ kpakpa ni okɛ nitsumɔ fɛɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ aha

english: Is it safe for me to mix my fertilizer together with weed-killing chemicals before applying them to my crops?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi baafutu dani mikɛwo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: No, you should not mix fertilizers and plant protection chemicals together unless explicitly instructed, as combining them can burn your crops or make the chemicals stop working properly.
ga: Dabi, esaaa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsofai ni buɔ tsei ahe lɛ futuɔ amɛhe. ja atsɔɔ lɛ faŋŋ Enɛ ji akɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsofai nɛɛ futu mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmɔshi nibii ashã loo eha tsofai lɛ akpa nitsumɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: If my farmland is already very rich, do I still need to clear weeds around my growing yams?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ baa nii waa lɛ, ehe miihia ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ lolo. Ani aduɔ ŋmeii yɛ jɛmɛ?

english: Yes, because weeds grow fast and steal water, sunlight, and underground nutrients away from your crops, which will reduce your tuber size even in fertile soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ baaha o-tuber lɛ dalɛ aba shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ po nɔ.

english: What makes some yam tubers grow very large and fat while others stay small?
ga: Mɛni haa sweet potato ŋmeii komɛi daraa ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ waa? Yɛ be mli ni kooloi srɔtoi lɛ ekomɛi ji bibii

english: Yam tubers grow large when the soil is loose enough for them to expand, and when the leaves get plenty of sunlight, steady rain, and good nutrients during their growing stage.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etse bɔ ni sa ni egbɛ eshwa. Ni kɛ́ baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa kɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the tuber underground. Staking lifts the vines off the damp ground so leaves catch maximum sunlight and stay free from rot and diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. koni baa lɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ, ni ŋmeii kɛ helai akafite amɛ.

english: How do I know if my crop is naturally healthy or if it is suffering from a lack of food in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: A healthy crop has deep green, vibrant leaves and sturdy vines, while a crop lacking nutrients will often show yellowish leaves, slow vine growth, or thin stems.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ baai ni kpɛɔ, ni ji eŋɔli kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ tsei ni niyenii eshɛɛɛ amɛhe lɛ baa yɛ ŋmɔŋ, wain tsei ni daa blɛoo, loo amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo.

english: How do I know the right time to spray chemicals on my crops to protect them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni mikɛbu amɛhe?

english: Chemicals should be sprayed early in the morning or late afternoon when pests are active and the sun is not too hot, and only when you start seeing early signs of insect damage or disease.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔ tsofai lɛ anɔ leebi loo shwane mli. Be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ miitsu nii ni hulu la lɛ edɔɔɔ tsɔ. Ni kɛ́ oje shishi ona mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi efite loo hela eba lɛ pɛ.

english: What will happen to my crop if I use extra chemicals to try and kill pests faster?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsofai krɛdɛɛi tsu nii koni mikɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni majie tsɛŋemɔ helai oya?

english: Using too much chemical can burn your crop's leaves, damage the soil, leave harmful residues on your harvest, and cost you unnecessary money without fixing the pest problem.
ga: Tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ baai ashã. ni kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ Eshiɔ nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ kpamɔɔ be lɛ mli. Ni efiteɔ bo shika ni he ehiaaa kɛtsɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe naagba lɛ ni osaaa lɛ nɔ.

english: How can using a mobile technology app actually help me get a better yield on my farm?
ga: Te mobile tɛknɔlɔji apps ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ ni maná yibii kpakpai yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Mobile technology gives you quick access to accurate rain forecasts, proper planting dates, pest detection advice, and current market prices right on your phone so you can plan better.
ga: Mobile tɛknɔlɔji haa onyɛɔ ona nugbɔshiimɔ he saji ni ja. Be ni sa ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ Ŋaawoi ni akɛtaoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ jarayeli jara ni yɔɔ amrɔ nɛɛ yɛ otɛlifoŋ nɔ yɛ hiŋmɛi kome nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ oto gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can mobile technology tell me the best time to start planting my yam seed pieces?
ga: Ani mobile tɛknɔlɔji baanyɛ atsɔɔ bo be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni obaanyɛ oje sweet potato dumɔwui adumɔ shishi?

english: Yes, mobile farming tools track seasonal weather patterns and send alerts when the rains have stabilized enough for planting so your seeds do not dry up in hot soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, okwaayeli dɛŋdade ni akɛyaa he fɛɛ he lɛ kwɛɔ be mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ekɛ kɔkɔbɔɔ majeɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, odumɔwui lɛ gĩii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up like tight tubes during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the sun gets very hot, maize plants roll their leaves inward to shade themselves and stop water from evaporating too fast. It is the crop's natural way of surviving high heat and dry air.
ga: Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ, Abɛi tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛha hulutsoo ni amɛtsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ. Eji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow big green leaves but fail to yield any flowers or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi enyɛɛɛ ewo fɔfɔi loo aduawai lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, the plant uses all its energy to grow leaves instead of flowers. Balancing the soil with phosphorus and potassium encourages the plant to form flowers and fruit.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ baai yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium to shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my young cabbage plants look limp and dead in the afternoon but stand up straight again by morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage tsei bibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Shi te shi jaŋŋ ekoŋŋ leebi.

english: In intense sunlight, cabbage leaves lose water faster than the roots can pull it from the ground. Once the sun sets and temperatures drop, the roots catch up and refill the leaves with water.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baafo kɛya ŋwɛi ni amɛkɛ nu baafata baai lɛ ahe.

english: Cassava deliberately drops its outer leaves during extended dry periods to save water and stay alive. Once the rains come back, the plant will push out fresh green leaves.
ga: Yucca jwɛŋɔ ni ekɛ esɛɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi wala mli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baatsi baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni kpɛɔ lɛ.

english: Groundnut roots have tiny swellings that take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the dirt. When the groundnut crop is harvested, that trapped nitrogen stays behind as natural fertilizer for maize.
ga: Peanut shishifãi lɛ baaná ŋmɔlɔ bibioo ko. No gbalaa nitrogen gas lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmei kɛha ŋmei.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers without producing any young pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni ekɛ ŋmeii bibii komɛi baaa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they do not get enough water, lack essential soil nutrients, or when there are not enough tiny insects around to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ bɛ.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my tomato plants turn yellow while the top leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tso shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants move nutrients from older bottom leaves to feed new top leaves when nitrogen in the soil is running low or when excess water damages the bottom roots.
ga: Tomato tsei jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen lɛ faaa. aloo be mli ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes go soft and rot quickly when left under a shed after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya kɛ́ ashi yɛ tsũ lɛ shishi beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes are still alive after harvest and generate heat. Keeping them in warm, still air speeds up their breakdown and lets rot organisms spread through the fruit much faster.
ga: Tomatoi yɛ wala mli lolo yɛ be mli ni akpa amɛ ni amɛhaa dɔlɛ baa lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo he ko ni mli edɔ ni amɛhiɛ ekã shi lɛ, ebaaha amɛfite oya, ni ebaaha nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ agbɛ ashwã aduawai lɛ amli fɛɛ oya kwraa.

english: Why do my stored yams start growing green shoots even when I keep them inside a dry barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛtoɔ ŋmɔ ko ni egbi mli moŋ.

english: Yam tubers naturally wake up from dormancy after resting for a few months. They use the energy and water saved inside the tuber to start sprouting new foliage.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ wɔɔhe mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe lɛ sɛɛ. Akɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu ni ato yɛ bulb lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛjeɔ baai heei shishi.

english: Why do tiny beetles appear inside my stored maize even though I kept the bags tied shut?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miije kpo yɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛwo kotoku mli moŋ?

english: Weevil insects often lay microscopic eggs inside the maize grains while the crop is still in the field. If the grain is not dried very well before storage, those eggs hatch inside the tied bags.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ woɔ amɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli yɛ ŋmeii amli be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbiko dani akɛto Nakai ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ yɛ kotoku ko ni akɛ kpãa ebɔ he lɛ mli.

english: Why is my neighbor's corn growing so much better than mine when we both received the same amount of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmãa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe mi nɔ lɛ? akɛ wɔyi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ wɔnine shɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ

english: Different crop varieties react differently to weather conditions. Your neighbor might be using an improved or drought-tolerant seed variety that handles changing rainfall patterns better than traditional or late-maturing seeds.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi tsuɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe nii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ. Ekolɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ kɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ loo ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa ni baanyɛ atsu nugbɔshiimɔi ni tsakeɔ lɛ ahe nii jogbaŋŋ fe blema dumɔwui loo dumɔwui ni shwereɔ sɛɛ lɛ miitsu nii.

english: Does it really matter what type of maize seed I buy if I am planting at the start of the rainy season?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli Mɛɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui esa akɛ mahe?

english: Yes, seed variety matters a lot. Fast-growing seeds mature in about two months and suit short or uncertain rains, while long-season varieties need steady, full rain throughout three to four months to yield well.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui srɔtoi ahe miihia waa. Dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ daa yɛ aaafee nyɔji enyɔ mli, ni amɛhi jogbaŋŋ kɛha bei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa loo anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ he miihia ni nugbɔ anɛ be fɛɛ be ni eshɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: What is the difference between early-maturing and late-maturing corn seeds?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni shwereɔ mra kɛ ŋmãa ni shwereɔ sɛɛ mli lɛ teŋ?

english: Early-maturing corn reaches harvest quickly—often in about two months—and requires less total rainfall, while late-maturing corn takes longer to grow but can produce higher yields if rain falls continuously throughout the season.
ga: Akpaa ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra lɛ oya—bei pii lɛ yɛ aaafee nyɔji enyɔ mli—ni ehe ehiaaa ni nugbɔ nɛɔ kwraa. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛɔ shi ebaanyɛ ewo yibii babaoo kɛji nugbɔ tee nɔ nɛ yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to plant two different varieties of maize on my farm at the same time?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makwɛ ŋmãa henɔi enyɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, planting different varieties helps protect you against losses. If the rains stop earlier than expected, the fast-maturing variety will still produce a harvest even if the longer-season variety fails.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ni aduɔ srɔtoi srɔtoi. Ebaabu ohe kɛjɛ nɔ ni elaaje lɛ he. Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra fe bɔ ni akpaa gbɛ lɛ Early maturing henɔi lɛ baaya nɔ awo yibii kɛji henɔi ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo yibii po.

english: Why does early rainfall cause some crops to produce a good harvest while others perform poorly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu wooo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Early rains can be unpredictable. Crops planted with fast-maturing or drought-resistant seed varieties can take advantage of short early rains, whereas varieties that need continuous heavy water will suffer if the rain stops suddenly.
ga: Anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra. Tsei ni adu kɛ dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra loo ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ baanyɛ aná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, ni baa mra lɛ he sɛɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kooloi srɔtoi ni biɔ nu be fɛɛ be lɛ kɛ naagbai baakpe kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛmɔ trukaa.

english: What happens to my crops if the rainy season ends earlier than expected?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ba naagbee mra fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ lɛ?

english: If rains stop before a crop completes its growth cycle, plants dry out before producing full grains. Using short-duration seed varieties helps ensure your crops mature before the rain stops.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ kwraa Tso lɛ gĩɔ dani ewoɔ dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ. Dumɔwui srɔtoi ni yeɔ be kukuoo lɛ ni okɛaatsu nii lɛ haa onibii lɛ shwereɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ kpaa.

english: Why do my young crops dry up and fail even after starting off strong during the first few weeks of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiifee nɔ ko yɛ shishijee ni mli wa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: First rains can sometimes be a false start followed by dry weather. If your seed variety needs continuous water and doesn't get it, the young plants will wilt and die before maturing.
ga: Bei komɛi lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee amale shishijee ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ nu he miihia odumɔwui lɛ daa ni amɛnáaa. Tsei bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi dani amɛshɛ shweremɔ he.

english: How does the timing of rain affect when my corn will mature?
ga: Te be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ saa be ni mi-abele lɛ baakwɛ̃ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Crops need water at critical stages like germinating and flowering. If rain arrives at the right stage for your specific seed variety, it will grow smoothly; if rain comes too late or inconsistently, growth slows down or fails.
ga: Nu he miihia tsei yɛ bei ni he hiaa waa tamɔ amɛkwɛ̃mɔ kɛ fɔfɔii amli. Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ eba yɛ be ni sa kɛha odumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ nɛ blɛoo tsɔ loo ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee lɛ Dalɛ baafee blɛoo loo ebaafee nɔ ni sɛɛ efooo.

english: How can I choose the right maize seed if I am not sure when the main rains will fully arrive?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmãa dumɔwui ni sa? Ani oleee be ni nugbɔ titri lɛ baashɛ?

english: When rain start times are uncertain, choosing short-duration or drought-tolerant seed varieties reduces your risk, as they require less water overall and reach harvest in a shorter time.
ga: Be ni nugbɔ lɛ baaje shishi lɛ bɛ faŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni hiɔ shi be kukuoo loo ni nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli lɛ ni ooohala lɛ baaha oshara ni yɔɔ ohe lɛ aba shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu fioo pɛ he hiaa yɛ fɛɛ mli, ni abaanyɛ akpa ŋmaa lɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: Why do plants in different sections of the same farm sometimes grow at different speeds after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli hei srɔtoi lɛ daa oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: In addition to seed variety, differences in soil water retention across your field mean some areas hold moisture longer, allowing those specific plants to absorb water and nutrients faster.
ga: Kɛfata dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ ahe lɛ Srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni ahiɛɔ yɛ oŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ hu baanyɛ aha hei komɛi ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa nakai tsei pɔtɛɛi lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because strong sunlight burns their tender leaves. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide shade and keep the soil cool until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand the full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hulutsoo be muu lɛ naa.

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the stems compete for sunlight, water, and plant food in the soil. Giving them proper space allows the roots to spread out and grow into large, heavy cassava tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ tsei aniyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmei shishifãi wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of a maize stalk usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the leaves back their green color and helps the maize grow big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmei loo kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni eye ebua ŋmei lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmei wuji.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts on my farm after I harvest maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the soil. Groundnuts and beans are special because they trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, naturally fertilizing the land for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii ji ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi ejaakɛ amɛheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How do I tell if my cassava is suffering from disease or just lacks water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela emɔ mi-cassava lɛ loo nu efo mli?

english: If cassava lacks water, the leaves droop during the hot afternoon but stand back up in the cool evening. If it is diseased, leaves will show permanent yellow spots, curled edges, or white powdery spots that stay even after rain.
ga: Kɛji nu efo ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli shi ekuɔ esɛɛ ebaa yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ hela lɛ mɔ lɛ, baai lɛ baajie ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi ni hiɔ shi daa, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi ni ebɔle amɛhe, loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi yɛŋ ni shwɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ po.

english: Why are the leaves on my yam vines drying up and turning brown before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ egbi ni efee ŋmɔtɔ dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Early drying of yam leaves is often caused by leaf spot fungal disease, which spreads when weeds trap too much damp air around the vine. Clearing weeds around the base allows fresh air to keep the leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fungal leaf spot hela ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato baai lɛ gbimɔ oya baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛ́ jwɛi lɛ mɔmɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ babaoo ni ebɔle wain tso lɛ he. Koni lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni etsuɔ ​​kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ he ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my garden eggs drop their flowers without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Garden egg plants drop flowers when the soil gets too dry or during sudden periods of intense heat. Keeping the soil consistently moist and covering the ground around the roots with dry grass helps save the flowers.
ga: Egg tsei ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be ni mli wa baa trukaa lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: Watering in the hot afternoon causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before the roots can drink it. Morning watering lets the soil stay moist so roots can absorb water before the heat sets in.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ nu lɛ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ anu. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu dani latsaa lɛ aba.

english: Why do insects get into my stored maize bags even when I close them tightly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii boteɔ mi-abele kotoku ni mikɛto lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛwo mli jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Insects like weevils often lay invisible eggs inside the grain while it is still drying on the field. Drying your maize completely on a clean sheet under the sun and using airtight bags kills these eggs and prevents damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii fɔɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa amɛ yɛ ŋmaa mli be mli ni egbi lolo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ yɛ saatso ni he tse nɔ yɛ hulu shishi ni akɛ vacuum bag tsu nii lɛ, ebaagbe ŋmãa nɛɛ ni ebaatsi nɔ ni efite lɛ naa.

english: Why does the soil around my tomato plants become hard like rock after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ mli wa tamɔ tɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains compact bare soil and wash away organic matter. Adding dry grass, leaves, or compost around your tomato plants protects the soil from hard raindrops and keeps it soft so roots can breathe.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi. Jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa Tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔi ni mli wa lɛ ahe. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to strong sunlight. If they get too much direct sun without shade plants around them, their leaves burn, turn yellow, and dry up.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji amɛná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo ni tsei komɛi ebɔle amɛhe ni baaha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, Baai lɛ baashã. Tsɔmɔmɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbi

english: How does shade from bigger trees affect how many cocoa pods my farm produces?
ga: Te hulutsoo ni jɛɔ tsei wuji amli lɛ saa kookoo ŋmeii ayibɔ ni miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Young cocoa trees need heavy shade to protect their leaves, but mature cocoa trees need balanced sunlight to produce plenty of flowers and pods. Too much shade on old trees lowers pod yield and encourages fungal diseases.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ni mli wa koni ebu baai lɛ ahe. Shi cacao tso ni eda lɛ he miihia hulu la ni sa koni enyɛ ewo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be babaoo ha tsei ni edara lɛ, ehaa pod lɛ baa shi ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ.

english: How do I know if the soil on my land is good enough to plant cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu kookoo?

english: Good cocoa soil should be deep, dark, rich in decayed leaves, and able to hold moisture without staying flooded after heavy rains.
ga: Esa akɛ kookoo shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ afee nɔ ni mli kwɔ, ni ehiɛ edɔ, ni baai ni egboi babaoo yɔɔ mli. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ato ni nu shwieee nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ.

english: Why does the soil on my farm produce smaller crops now than it did years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ miiwo ŋmɔshi nibii bibii fe afii ni eho lɛ?

english: Crops pull nutrients out of the earth every season. If you continuously farm the same land without adding compost, manure, or fertilizer, the soil becomes exhausted.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Kɛji akɛ oya nɔ otsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite.

english: Why do my green cocoa pods turn black and rot before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, overly shaded farms. Clearing weeds and pruning thick branches helps sunlight dry out moisture and stop the rot.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei niji ni mli tse lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ekpaa ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do mistletoe plants grow on my cocoa branches, and should I remove them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso ni ji mistletoe lɛ miida yɛ mi-kokoo nine lɛ nɔ lɛ? Ni ani esa akɛ majie kɛjɛ mihe?

english: Mistletoe is a parasitic plant that steals water and food directly from your cocoa tree. You should cut mistletoe off completely because it slowly weakens the tree and reduces cocoa yield.
ga: Mistletoe ji tso ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ cacao tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Esa akɛ ofo mistletoe fɛɛ mli beni ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ fiofio lɛ. ni eha kookoo ni afeɔ lɛ aba shi

english: Cocoa flowers drop if they are not pollinated by tiny insects called midges, or if the tree is stressed by severe dry weather and lack of nutrients.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. Aloo kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi waa kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over easily during strong winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and heavy fruit bunches, making them top-heavy. Staking them with sturdy wooden poles helps keep them standing during high winds.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii. kɛ muji babaoo baa Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa fĩ amɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdamɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds from around the roots of my crops regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi daa lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital nutrients, water, and sunlight from your crops, while also creating hiding spots for harmful pests.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ náa he ko ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants curl their leaves to save water during hot dry spells, but leaf curling can also be a sign of viral diseases spread by whiteflies.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Shi baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ afee hela ko ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an important food for growth. The plant takes the remaining nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Tso lɛ jieɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ, ni egbɔ lɛ amli ni ekɛhaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply my chemical fertilizer right before a heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa?

english: Heavy rain will wash away the fertilizer from the topsoil before the crop's roots can absorb it, wasting your money and potentially damaging nearby water sources.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ shika, ni ebaanyɛ efite nu jɛɛhei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Why does burning my bush to clear my land make the soil poor after a few years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ashãa koni akɛjie mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ afii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: While burning clears the land quickly, it destroys organic matter, kills beneficial soil organisms, and leaves the soil exposed to erosion, which degrades soil fertility over time.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, la ni ashãa lɛ haa sũ lɛ mli tseɔ oya. Shi efiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ hu. Ekpãtãa shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahiɛ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: What is making small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving brown powder inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ powda ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tsei lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. The brown powder is their waste, and treating them early with approved insecticides or neem extracts protects your yield.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Powda ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ji jwɛi. ni kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling upwards and turning small and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites transmitting a virus. Controlling these insects early prevents the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai akagbɛ amɛshwã

english: Why do my tomato plants grow plenty of flowers, but the flowers fall off without growing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi efoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer causes tomato plants to drop flowers instead of setting fruit. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ awo yibii yɛ yibii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ najiaŋ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ tomatoi.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn watery and rot in the ground when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ náa nu ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need well-drained soil. Excess water in flat or heavy clay soil starves the roots of air, leading to root rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nu babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni tsii mli lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbo.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant plantain trees beside my newly planted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn under intense sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide necessary temporary shade and keep the soil cool while the cocoa grows strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni shwereɔ oya lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa yɛ be kukuoo mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ baa lɛ.

english: Why is it bad for my farm if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eyeɔ miŋmɔ lɛ awui kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas restores nitrogen naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen baa ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know when my underground yams are fully mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potatoes ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yams are ready for full harvest when the leaves and vines on top stop growing, turn yellow, and dry up naturally, showing that energy has moved completely into the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes efee klalo kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ ni yeɔ emuu beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ kpa shweremɔ. tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbi yɛ adebɔɔ naa Etsɔɔ akɛ hewalɛ lɛ efã kɛtee yitso lɛ mli kwraa.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of a maize plant mean it is hungry for nitrogen. When the soil runs low on food, the plant moves what little nitrogen it has from older bottom leaves up to the young top leaves to keep growing.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia lɛ. Kɛ niyenii fioo pɛ eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fioo ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ amli koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with thick green leaves but produce only tiny roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ kɛlɛ waa ni eyɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli tse shi shishifãi bibii yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen food from the soil, it spends all its energy growing leaves and stalks above ground instead of storing starch in the tubers below ground.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ niyenii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ ashikishaŋ lɛ baato ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ,.

english: Why are my okra plants staying stunted and small even though I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛji bibii eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Hard, compacted soil stops okra roots from spreading out to suck up food, while sour (acidic) soil locks up nutrients so the roots cannot feed, keeping the plant tiny.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ baatsi okra shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã koni amɛye niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ (acidic) lɛ hiɛɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii haa tsei feɔ bibii

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up tightly during the hot afternoon sun but open up again in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, shi amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves in intense afternoon heat as a self-defense trick to reduce their surface area, which keeps water from evaporating out of the plant too fast.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane mli dɔlɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni amɛha amɛhiɛ aba shi. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ akajɛ tso lɛ mli oya tsɔ.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants falling off before any small fruits appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai bibii jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Extreme heat or sudden dry spells cause tomato plants to panic and drop their flowers to save water and stay alive, rather than spending energy growing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ feɔ gbeyei ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi wala mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii kɛdu aduawai

english: When maize experiences strong heat or drought early in its life, it rushes to flower early as a survival instinct so it can produce seeds before it dies of dry weather.
