ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa shɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ he yɛ eshihilɛ shishijee mli lɛ, Ebaafɔ̃ oya kɛjɛ wala mlihilɛ su mli. Enɛ ji koni enyɛ ewo dumɔwui dani egboi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear away all the large trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ? Ashɛrɛ nakai tso lɛ ashwie?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and shallow roots that burn under full direct sun; they need shade trees above them to shield them from high heat until they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo koni amɛkadɔ fe nine kɛyashi amɛhe baawa.

english: Why does my plantain tree give me small, weak fruit bunches when I leave all the young suckers growing around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ haa mi yibii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ beni mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ?

english: The young sucker shoots constantly steal food, water, and sunlight from the mother plantain tree, leaving it with less energy to build a big fruit bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei bibii juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Enɛ haa hewalɛ fioo pɛ ni akɛfeɔ aduawai akuu agbo ko.

english: Why do weeds growing around my cassava lower the amount of crop I harvest at the end of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mihe lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mi-cassava lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ baa shi?

english: Weeds are fast growers that fight your cassava for sunlight above ground and steal fertilizers and groundwater below ground, starving your crop.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji tso ko ni daa oya ni ekɛ yucca wuɔ koni ená hulu la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni ajuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii.

english: Cowpeas are legumes that take nitrogen gas out of the air and put it back into the soil through their roots, naturally feeding the maize plants growing alongside them.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmei tso ko ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ náa adebɔɔ mli niyenii.

english: Should I wait for my coconuts to drop from the tree naturally before I collect them?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mamɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ ajɛ tso lɛ nɔ amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe dani mafolɔ amɛ?

english: No, you should harvest mature coconuts directly from the tree before they drop. Waiting for them to fall on the ground can cause the shell to crack, allow bacteria inside, or lead to rot, which ruins the flesh used for making oil.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ okpa ŋmeii ni eda lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ dani amɛgbee shi. Kɛ́ oomɛ ni amɛgbee shikpɔŋ lɛ, ekolɛ ebaaha ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli agbá. Muawai yɛ mli. aloo ekɛ fitemɔ ni fiteɔ he ni akɛfeɔ mu lɛ baa

english: How do I know if a coconut on my tree is ripe enough to make oil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ ekwɛ̃ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo fɔ?

english: A coconut is ready for oil processing when its outer husk turns brown and you hear water sloshing loudly inside when shaken. Green coconuts contain mostly water and thin flesh, which is good for drinking but bad for oil.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha mu ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛji amɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ batsɔ ŋmeii. Ni obaanu gbee ni naa wa ni shwieɔ shi yɛ mli beni okpokpoɔ lɛ. Nu ji nɔ ni feɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ babaoo, ni amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nɔ ni hi kɛha ninumɔ shi ehiii kɛha fɔ.

english: What happens to mature coconuts if I leave them lying on the ground under the tree for a long time?
ga: Mɛni baaba ŋmei ni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ ni ekã tso lɛ shishi be kakadaŋŋ?

english: If left on the ground, coconuts absorb moisture from the dirt and begin to sprout roots or rot inside. This makes the coconut meat taste sour and unfit for producing quality cooking oil.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ŋmei lɛ baaŋɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ebɔi shishifãi loo fitemɔ yɛ emli. Enɛ haa ŋmei loo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni esaaa akɛ afeɔ fɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛhooɔ nii.

english: Is it better to sell my fresh coconuts whole or process them into coconut oil first?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaahɔɔ ŋmeii muu heei loo afee amɛ ŋmeii fɔ klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Processing your coconuts into oil adds extra value to your crop. While whole fresh coconuts sell for low prices and spoil quickly, coconut oil lasts longer, is easy to store, and sells for a much higher price in local food markets.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ ni ooofee lɛ fɔ lɛ kɛ sɛɛnamɔ kroko baa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ahɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii muu ni afee ehee lɛ yɛ jara ni baa shi nɔ ni efiteɔ oya moŋ, shi ŋmeii fɔ lɛ baahi shi be kakadaŋŋ. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ abaato ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ kwraa nɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli niyenii ajarayelihe lɛ.

english: Is coconut oil safe and healthy to use for cooking regular household food like rice?
ga: Ani ŋmei fɔ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛbaatsu nii kɛhoo shia niyenii ni afɔɔ feemɔ tamɔ ŋmãa?

english: Yes, coconut oil is a high-quality cooking oil that withstands heat well without burning. It provides essential fats, adds a rich natural flavor to food like rice, and stores safely for long periods without going bad.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei fɔ ji fɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛhooɔ nii ni hulutsoo nyɛɔ eshɛɔ he, ni eshãaa. Ehaa fɔ ni he hiaa Ekɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ baa niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa nɔ ni abaanyɛ akɛto shweshweeshwe be kakadaŋŋ ni efiteee.

english: Can I use the solid coconut waste left behind after squeezing out the oil for anything on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmei ni eshwɛ yɛ mu ni ajie lɛ sɛɛ lɛ atsu nii kɛfee nɔ ko yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, the leftover pressed coconut fiber and meal is full of protein and fiber. You can feed it to farm animals like pigs and poultry or mix it into your soil as organic manure.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei ni agbɛlɛ ni eshwɛ kɛ niyenii lɛ eyi kɛ protein kɛ fiber. Obaanyɛ oha ŋmɔ mli kooloi tamɔ tsinai kɛ kooloi niyenii. Aloo obaanyɛ okɛfutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli.

english: Why do mature coconuts fall off the palm tree by themselves if they are not plucked?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii momoi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji okɛ amɛ shwieee lɛ?

english: When a coconut reaches full maturity, the stalk connecting it to the tree naturally dries up and dies so the tree can release its seed to grow a new palm. Harvesting early prevents this natural drop.
ga: Kɛji ŋmei lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Tso lɛ shishifãi ni kɛ tso lɛ kpãa gbee lɛ baagbi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛbaagboi. Enɛ ji koni tso lɛ ajie edumɔwui lɛ ni ekɛfee ŋmei tsei heei. mra kpamɔ Abaatsi nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli gbee nɛɛ naa.

english: Will plucking coconuts directly off the palm damage the tree or reduce my future harvests?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni mijieɔ kɛjɛɔ midɛŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baafite tso lɛ loo ebaaha miwɔsɛɛ yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi?

english: No, carefully plucking mature coconuts directly from the crown does not hurt the palm. In fact, regularly removing mature fruit bunches helps the tree focus its nutrients on developing new young flowers and fruits.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ gbala ŋmei ni egbɔ kɛjɛ ŋwɛi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, efiteee ŋmei lɛ. Yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ, aduawai akui ni eda lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔi heei kɛ aduawai bibii ni ebaawo lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are some of my young green coconuts falling off the tree before they get fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ miigbee shi kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara kwraa lɛ?

english: Immature fruit drop is usually caused by environmental stress, such as prolonged dry weather, lack of nutrients in the soil, or insect attacks. Giving the tree enough water and fertilizer helps it hold onto its fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shihilɛ mli haomɔi, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ aduawai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo kooloi ni baatutua lɛ Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ aduawai amli.

english: How long can I keep harvested dry coconuts before I have to grate them and process them into oil?
ga: Be enyiɛ ŋmei ni egbi lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi dani ehe baahia ni atsɔ mli ni afee lɛ fɔ?

english: If kept whole inside their dry brown husks in a cool, ventilated place off the ground, harvested mature coconuts can be stored safely for several weeks without spoiling before you process them.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akɛto muu lɛ fɛɛ, yɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ni egbi mli yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kponɔ. Abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ ato shweshweeshwe otsii babaoo ni efiteee dani atsu he nii.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when heat gets too intense or when water supply drops suddenly. When stressed, the plant drops its blossoms to conserve water and energy rather than growing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ la lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu lɛ ba shi trukaa. Kɛ́ haomɔ ba Yɛ yibii ni tsei baakwɛ̃ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ, tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: What causes the bottom of my tomatoes to turn black and rot before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egbo dani ekwɛ̃?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot. It happens when the growing plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering or dry spells.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei ni miida lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni eyaaa nɔ loo hulutsoo be lɛ kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my tomato plants turning yellow and dying off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually indicates a lack of nitrogen in the soil or a soil-borne fungal infection that enters through the roots as the plant matures.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni sũ ni tsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛboteɔ mli beni tso lɛ miida lɛ kɛbaa.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt during the hot afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: During intense afternoon heat, leaves evaporate water faster than roots can draw it up from the soil. It can also mean soil pests or fungal diseases have damaged the root system.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Baai lɛ shwieɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ hu akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko efite shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why does my mango tree produce plenty of flowers but very few actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: High humidity or heavy rains during flowering can wash away pollen and promote fungal diseases like anthracnose, which destroys the delicate flowers before small mangoes can set.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni mli wa loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ ajie fɔfɔii lɛ amli fɔfɔii lɛ ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ anthracnose, ni gbeɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ dani mango bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why does my mango tree produce a huge harvest one year and almost nothing the following year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ afi kome mli shi afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ewooo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: This is called alternate bearing. Producing a massive crop exhausts the tree's stored energy and nutrients, forcing it to take a year to rebuild its strength before fruiting heavily again.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ sɛɛkuu bearing. Nibii babaoo ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni tsei lɛ eto lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, eheɔ tso lɛ afi dani enáa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ dani ewoɔ yibii ni tsii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do dark, sticky patches appear on my young mangoes while they are still on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango ni tsuɔ ni wa lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi yibii lɛ anɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This often happens when sap leaks from stem injuries or when small insects like aphids produce sticky honeydew on the fruit, which then grows black mold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ pilamɔ ko mli kɛyaa tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii jieɔ wuo ni shwieɔ shi yɛ aduawai anɔ, ni no haa ŋmeii diji baa.

english: Can liquids or treatments sprayed around the stem base of my crop actually reach inside the fruit?
ga: Nu loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi kɛbɔleɔ Ani tso lɛ shishigbɛ baanyɛ ashɛ aduawai lɛ amli?

english: Yes, plants draw up water and soluble compounds from the soil around their base through their root systems, transporting those substances up the stem into the leaves and developing fruits.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei gbalaa nu kɛ nibii ni shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli. Tso lɛ shishigbɛ tsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Okɛ nakai nibii lɛ aya tso lɛ yibii lɛ anɔ kɛya baai lɛ anɔ ni oha aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How do my crops take in food and water from the ground around their stems?
ga: Miŋmɔshi nii lɛ heɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle mi lɛ nɔ. Te ebaafee tɛŋŋ ni trunk lɛ

english: Crops have fine feeder roots near the surface around their base. These roots soak up moisture and dissolved nutrients from the soil and carry them up to feed the whole plant.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ shishifãi kpakpai ni yeɔ niyenii ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni bɔleɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he. Nɛkɛ shishifãi nɛɛ gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii ni mli edɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli ni amɛhaa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ niyenii.

english: Why do weeds growing right next to the base of my crop slow down its growth so much?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ miiha amɛdalɛ miiba shi waa lɛ?

english: Weeds near the stem compete directly with your crop's main roots for soil moisture, nutrients, and space, effectively starving the plant during its critical growth stage.
ga: Jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ otso lɛ shishifãi titrii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ he ko, ni ehaa tso lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni edaa waa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen, which acts as the main food for leaf growth, or that excessive water is choking the roots. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their deep green color and vigor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baai lɛ daa. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ mli ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ su ni mli kwɔ kɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it safe for my soil if I plant cassava and maize together on the same plot of land?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa fee ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting cassava and maize together is a smart practice. Maize grows rapidly and is harvested early within a few months, leaving the slow-growing cassava to take over the space and soil nutrients later in the season.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ ji nilee nifeemɔ. Abɛi daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Ha ni ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ aŋɔ he ko kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop when weather temperatures become excessively high, when soil moisture fluctuates too drastically, or when tiny insect pests damage the stems. Keeping the soil consistently moist and planting shade crops nearby can help prevent flower loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsakeɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii fite tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni aaakwɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the tall trees from my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei kakadaji lɛ? Mashi miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very tender and cannot handle direct, intense heat from the sun. Tall shade trees act as a canopy that shelters the young cocoa from sunburn and keeps humidity high around the crop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni jɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ naa. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he, ni ehaa hulutsoo be babaoo hiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my pepper leaves droop in the hot afternoon even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛji He ni esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: During intense afternoon heat, pepper leaves lose water into the air faster than roots can draw it up from the ground, causing them to wilt temporarily. As long as the soil is moist, the leaves will perk back up when the temperature cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are mature enough to dig up without destroying the plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa ni efiteee tso lɛ?

english: Cassava is typically ready for harvest when its lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to crack due to the swelling roots beneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni eshishi baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ yɛ shishifãi ni efuu yɛ shishi lɛ ahewɔ.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and nutrients away from the main plantain tree. Removing most of them and leaving only one strong sucker ensures that the main stem produces large, heavy bunches of fruit.
ga: Tsoi loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie mɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ashi ŋmɔtɔ kome pɛ ni mli wa lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ woɔ yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help improve my farmland for future crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha miŋmɔ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural plant food in the soil. When the crop is harvested, this leftover nitrogen fertilizes the soil for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nitrogen ni eshwɛ nɛɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb up high to expose their leaves to direct sunlight. The leaves use sunlight to manufacture energy, which is then directed down into the ground to build bigger and healthier yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Baai kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ hewalɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, ekɛ eyitso shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do black spots spread faster across my crops when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ black spot lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli oya fe be mli ni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Planting crops too tightly together prevents fresh air from circulating between the leaves, keeping humidity high and leaves wet. Fungal diseases thrive in damp, dark environments and easily jump from leaf to touching leaf.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa akabote baai lɛ ateŋ. Enɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Fungal helai yaa hiɛ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni duŋ ewo mli. Ni otu kɛjɛ baa kome nɔ kɛya ekroko nɔ kɛ mlɛoyeli.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tight like tubes during sunny afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ paipii yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: When maize plants do not get enough water, they curl their leaves to shrink the surface area exposed to the hot sun, which helps them save moisture until the weather cools down.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ Ebaatsɔ ebaa lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋwɛi ŋta ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ afee bibioo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: At what stage does my corn farm need water the most to grow big cobs?
ga: Mɛɛ be mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ he hiaa nu fe fɛɛ koni ekɛdu ŋmãa wuji?

english: Maize needs the most water when it starts showing tassels and silks, because this is the critical time when the plant is forming the kernels inside the cobs.
ga: Nu he hiaa ŋmãa fe fɛɛ kɛ́ ebɔi ŋmãa kɛ siliki feemɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eji be ni he hiaa waa beni tsei lɛ miiwo dumɔwui yɛ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Can leaving standing water in my maize farm spoil the crop roots?
ga: Ani nu ni mahã edamɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite tsei shishifãi?

english: Yes, maize roots need air to breathe just like they need water. Flooded soil chokes the roots, causing them to rot and turning the leaves yellow.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmãa shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni nu he hiaa amɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Is natural rainwater better for growing my corn than river water?
ga: Ani adebɔɔ mli nugbɔ nu ni akɛduɔ ŋmãa lɛ hi fe faa mli nu?

english: Rainwater is naturally soft and absorbs small amounts of nitrogen from the air, which gives corn a quick greening boost, although clean river water is also good during dry spells.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli ni ejieɔ nitrogen fioo ko kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli oya. Eyɛ mli akɛ faa mli nu ni mli tse lɛ hi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli moŋ.

english: How do destructive pests like armyworms find my corn field even when my farm is far from town?
ga: Nibii ni fiteɔ nii tamɔ cutworms Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ kɛ maŋ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ moŋ.

english: Many adult crop pests are moths that travel long distances on strong wind currents across regions to search for fresh, green maize fields to lay their eggs.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni eda lɛ ateŋ babaoo ji ŋmeii ni fãa gbɛ kakadaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli kɛtsɔɔ hei srɔtoi. koni amɛtao ŋmɔji ni ŋmãa yɔɔ mli ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii

english: Why should I clear the bushy grass around the borders of my maize farm before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi ni yɔɔ brɔshi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Abɛi ŋmɔ lɛ naa dani adu?

english: Clearing border bushes destroys hiding spots and breeding grounds for insects and diseases, preventing them from easily jumping into your main field.
ga: Husu lɛ naa jwɛi lɛ amli saamɔ fiteɔ hei ni kooloi bibii kɛ helai kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli kɛ hei ni amɛfɔɔ yɛ lɛ. Tsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkatu kɛbote oŋmɔ titri lɛ mli mlɛo.

english: What simple measures can I put along the edge of my field to stop insects from invading my crop?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ gbɛjianɔtoi komɛi ni yɔɔ mlɛo awo shi. Mɛni manyɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ naa koni kooloi akabote miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Planting a few boundary rows of trap crops like sorghum or sprinkling wood ash along the farm borders creates a natural barrier that slows down crawling and flying insects.
ga: Trap ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ tamɔ ŋmãa loo tso ashwishwɛ ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ naa. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni haa kooloi bibii shwieɔ shi ni amɛfoɔ oya lɛ baa.

english: Why does my maize grow tall and green in one season but remain short and yellow in another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ daa ni ekwɛɔ be ko lɛ? Shi loloolo lɛ, eyɛ kuku ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be kroko mli.

english: Yellow and stunted maize usually lacks plant food like nitrogen, which happens when heavy rains wash nutrients deep into the soil beyond the roots' reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni ji ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmãa ni egbɔjɔ lɛ bɛ tsei amli niyenii tamɔ nitrogen, ni baa kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛ waa ha niyenii mli hewalɛ ho kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why do my corn plants grow thin and weak when I plant them close to big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Maize needs full sunlight to make its food. When planted under large trees, the crop stretches tall and weak while trying to reach the light, resulting in small cobs.
ga: Abɛi he miihia hulu ni fa bɔni afee ni ehoo. Kɛ adu tso agbo ko shishi Tso lɛ baafee kakadaŋŋ ni egbɔjɔ be mli ni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ la aha lɛ. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmei bibioo ko.

english: Why does harvested corn turn hard and dry so quickly when stored in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni egbiɔ oya kɛ akɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Once corn is cut from the living plant, it stops taking in water and naturally releases its internal moisture into the air, causing the grains to shrink and harden for long-term storage.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afo ŋmãa kɛjɛ tso ni hiɛ ka mli lɛ Ebaakpa nu hemɔ ni ebaajie ŋmãa ni yɔɔ emli lɛ kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwaa koni akɛto be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How do I know which side of a sprouted seed goes down into the dirt when I am planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male dumɔwu ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ fã ni yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ midu lɛ?

english: The small root part that sprouts out first should point downwards into the soil, while the part where the green leaves will grow must point upwards toward the sky.
ga: Esa akɛ shishifãi bibii ni jeɔ kpo klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ atsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Esa akɛ fã ni baai eŋɔli lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi.

english: What happens if I accidentally plant my sprouting seed upside down in the soil?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ oshara du dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: If planted upside down, the root has to waste precious energy turning itself downward while the shoot turns upward, which delays growth and can even cause the seedling to die.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Esa akɛ shishifãi lɛ afite hewalɛ ni jara wa kɛtsɔ shishigbɛ ni amɛaatsɔ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ shishifã lɛ kwɛɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha dalɛ asɛɛ afo ni ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwu lɛ agbo.

english: Which part of a germinated seed actually turns into the roots of my crop?
ga: Mɛɛ dumɔwu ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ fã baafee miŋmɔshi nii lɛ shishifã diɛŋtsɛ?

english: The small white sprout pointing downward, known as the radicle, is the part that grows deep into the earth to become the roots of your crop.
ga: tso bibioo yɛŋ Nɔ ni tsɔɔ shi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ radicle lɛ ji fã ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni ebatsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shishifã.

english: Which part of the seedling grows to become the leaves and stem above the ground?
ga: Mɛɛ dumɔwu lɛ fã daa ni etsɔɔ baai kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: The upper part of the sprout, called the plumule, points upward and naturally grows out of the soil to form the stem and leaves.
ga: Atsɛɔ tso bibioo lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ fã lɛ akɛ plumule. Amɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛi ni amɛdaraa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai.

english: Why do my young shoots sometimes take too long to come out of the ground after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ heɔ be babaoo tsɔ dani amɛjeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: This often happens if the seed was planted upside down or buried too deep, forcing the young shoot to spend extra energy finding its way upward to the light.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ ashwie shi loo afu amɛ tsɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛna gbɛ kɛya ŋwɛi kɛya la lɛ he.

english: Why is it important for me to press the soil down around my seed after putting it in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ sũ ni bɔle midumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ atswa beni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pressing the soil down firmly removes air gaps and ensures the seed makes full contact with the soil so it can easily absorb water and nutrients to grow.
ga: Kɛ́ anyɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kwraa. No hewɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ oya.

english: Will loose dirt around my newly planted crop affect how well it grows?
ga: Ani muji ni ebɔle miŋmɔshi nibii ni midu ehee lɛ he lɛ baaná edalɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, loose dirt leaves large air pockets around the roots, making it hard for the young plant to pull water from the ground, which can cause it to dry up.
ga: Hɛɛ, muji ni etse ehe lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui wuji bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haa ewaa ahaa tso bibioo lɛ akɛ ebaajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ agbi.

english: How can I make sure my new seedlings get a strong grip in the dirt right after planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ dumɔwui heei baanyɛ amɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ?

english: You can ensure a strong grip by putting the root side pointing downward into the hole and gently pressing the soil down around the base of the plant.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ ama shi kɛtsɔ shishifã lɛ fã ni okɛaawo shi yɛ bu lɛ mli lɛ nɔ ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ashɛ shi blɛoo ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ he.

english: How deep should I place a sprouted seed when putting it into my farm field?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ midumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ awo mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Place the sprouted seed so the root portion points straight down into the moist soil while the leafy shoot tip faces upward near the soil surface before pressing the soil around it.
ga: Okɛ dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ baai lɛ kwɛɔ ŋwɛi ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ dani amɛmiimii shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is solid contact between the dirt and the seed so important when I am planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ lɛ he hiaa waa kɛ́ midu nii lɛ?

english: Solid contact allows moisture in the ground to transfer directly into the seed and young roots, giving the plant the water connection it needs to start growing immediately.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaa gbee waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa tsei kɛ nu tsaa koni amɛjeɔ dalɛ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and delicate root systems that burn easily in direct sun. They need shade trees to protect them from harsh sunlight and to keep the soil moist while they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How many years will I wait after planting cocoa before I can start harvesting the pods?
ga: Kɛ́ odu kookoo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani obɔi ŋmeii lɛ akpamɔ?

english: If you plant the improved hybrid cocoa varieties, you can expect your first harvest in about 2 to 3 years, whereas traditional cocoa varieties take around 5 years to start fruiting.
ga: Kɛji odu cocoa hybrids ni atsake lɛ Obaanyɛ okpa klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaa lɛ gbɛ yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni blema cocoa henɔi lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 5 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi.

english: Is it a good idea for me to cut down old, unproductive cocoa trees to plant new ones?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tsei ni egbɔ ni wooo yibii lɛ koni madu ehee?

english: Yes, replacing old, non-bearing trees is necessary for long-term farm yield, but you should replant in stages or maintain shade crops so the exposed soil does not dry out.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni egbɔ ni wooo yibii lɛ najiaŋdamɔlɔ he miihia waa kɛha okwaayeli nitsumɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Shi esa akɛ okɛwo mli ekoŋŋ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Aloo ha tso lɛ ahi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ lɛ akagbi.

english: Why is it important for me to weed around the base of my crops every few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ majie jwɛi ni bɔle ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ shishi lɛ? Otsii fioo komɛi?

english: Weeds steal vital water, fertilizer, and sunlight from your crops, and they also hide harmful pests and diseases that can damage your farm.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Ekɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara kɛ helai ni baanyɛ afite oŋmɔ lɛ hu teeɔ.

english: That rot is caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads rapidly when the farm is too wet, dark, and crowded with overgrown branches that block airflow.
ga: Hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpod kɛ fitemɔ baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ ŋmɔji lɛ amli edɔ tsɔ, amɛhe ewo duŋ ni tsei niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine ni tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa lɛ eyi mli obɔ.

english: What causes small white insects that look like cotton to gather under my plant leaves?
ga: Nɔ ni feɔ kooloi bibii yɛŋ Nɔ ni tamɔ kotoku ni abua naa yɛ mitsei lɛ baai ashishi lɛ.

english: Those insects are mealybugs. They suck energy out of your crops and spread serious diseases like the Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus from farm to farm.
ga: Nakai kooloi lɛ ji mealybugs. Amɛmuɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus lɛ amɛshwãa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔ mli.

english: Why do thousands of small flowers drop off my cocoa trees without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, fɔfɔi akpei abɔ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can support. Only flowers pollinated by tiny insects will form pods, and the tree drops the rest to save energy for the pods that survive.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. Fɔfɔi ni kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ pɛ feɔ pods. Ni tso lɛ shwieɔ nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and drop off during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is a survival mechanism. Crops shed leaves during dry weather to stop losing water through evaporation so they can keep their stems and roots alive until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi koni nu ni shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ akpa. Bɔni afee ni anyɛ akwɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my crops grow larger and greener near riverbanks than on hilltops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji yɛ faai ahe fe gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Soil near riverbanks stays moist longer and collects rich topsoil washed down from higher areas, while hilltop soil dries out quickly and loses its nutrients to erosion.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ faa lɛ naa lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni ebuaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya, ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ hewɔ.

english: What makes my crops grow plenty of heavy green leaves but fail to produce fruit?
ga: Mɛni miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa shi amɛwooo yibii?

english: This usually happens when the soil has too much nitrogen (which builds leaves) but lacks phosphorus and potassium, which are the main nutrients plants need to produce flowers and fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ. (ni woɔ baai) shi ebɛ phosphorus kɛ potassium ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow so tall and thin that they fall over when the wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe efee mlɛo bɔ ni kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa amɛ lɛ, amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ?

english: Maize plants get weak and fall over when they lack essential nutrients in the soil like potassium and nitrogen. Applying balanced fertilizer helps build thick, strong stems that can withstand strong winds and carry heavy ears of corn.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛgbee shi kɛji amɛbɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ potassium kɛ nitrogen. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ama tsei ni mli tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baanyɛ adamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa ni ewo ŋmãa toi ni tsii.

english: How does fertilizer actually make my crops stronger and healthier?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ?

english: Fertilizer acts like nutritious food for plants. It provides essential nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium that soil loses over time, helping crops build sturdy stems, deep roots, and green leaves.
ga: Fertilizer tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni hewalɛ yɔɔ mli kɛhaa tsei. Ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ naitrɔjin, fɔsfɔs, kɛ potasium. ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baaje mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa, shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji.

english: Why do my crops look weak and pale even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Water alone is not enough for plants to grow well; soil needs nutrients to feed the crop. In fact, heavy rain can wash away existing soil nutrients, so crops still need fertilizer to stay green and strong.
ga: Nu pɛ kɛkɛ faaa koni tsei akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ he miihia niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii. Yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie sũ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ momo lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia lolo koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: How do I know if my farmland soil needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If your crops grow slowly, have pale or yellow leaves, develop thin stems, or give you smaller harvests than in past years, these are clear signs that the soil nutrients are exhausted and need fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji otsei lɛ daraa blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ, eyɛ tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo, loo ewoɔ yibii ni faaa fe nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Enɛɛmɛi ji okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ efo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What kind of fertilizer is best for tall grain crops like maize or sorghum?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii hi fe fɛɛ kɛha ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛlɛ tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Nitrogen-rich fertilizers, such as NPK blends or Urea, are best for tall grain crops because nitrogen encourages strong leaf growth and sturdy stalks during the early and mid-growing stages.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ NPK blends loo urea lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsei ni dumɔwui shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nitrogen haa baai lɛ daraa waa, ni ehaa tsei lɛ hu feɔ hewalɛ yɛ shishijee kɛ teŋgbɛ fãi lɛ amli.

english: Can applying fertilizer prevent my crops from catching diseases?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ ŋmɔshi nibii anaa koni hela akamɔ amɛ?

english: Yes, well-fed crops build a natural resistance to sickness. Just like healthy human bodies fight off illness better, crops nourished with fertilizer can resist common plant diseases and pests much better than starving plants.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei ni ayeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ maa adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni teɔ shi ewoɔ helai. Taakɛ adesa gbɔmɔtso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ wuɔ helai jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Tsei ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo mli lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ tsei ahe helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ anɔ kwraa fe tsei ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ.

english: The best time is usually when the soil is moist after a rainy morning or evening, shortly after planting or during the early growth stage. This allows the roots to absorb the nutrients easily without burning.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni enɛɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ sɛɛ. Beni adu lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ loo yɛ be mli ni edara oya lɛ Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛshãaa amɛ.

english: Can I pour fertilizer directly on the leaves and stems of my plants?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tsei lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: No, placing dry fertilizer directly on stems or leaves can burn the plant. Fertilizer should be placed in the soil near the root zone where the plant can safely drink it in through its roots.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo tso lɛ shishi loo ebaa lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ shishifã lɛ he ni tso lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ shweshweeshwe kɛtsɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my tall crops turn yellow and dry up before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei kakadaji lɛ ashishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: This usually happens when plants run out of nitrogen in the soil, forcing them to pull food from older bottom leaves to feed new top growth. Adding fertilizer early prevents this leaf loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni egbala niyenii kɛjɛ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha tso hee ni eda yɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii. Ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli mra Ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ baa nɛɛ akafite.

english: Why are my plants growing very tall without producing big fruits or grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ daa ni ewooo aduawai loo dumɔwui wuji lɛ?

english: Plants that grow tall without producing good harvest usually have too much nitrogen but lack phosphorus and potassium. A balanced fertilizer gives the plant what it needs to form healthy fruits and seeds, not just tall stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛwooo yibii kpakpai lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo tsɔ shi amɛbɛ phosphorus kɛ potassium. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni ja lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii kɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Jeee tsei kakadaji kɛkɛ ni.

english: How many years does it take for a newly planted tree crop to fully establish itself in the soil?
ga: Afii enyiɛ ebaahe ni tso ni adu ehee lɛ atswa shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Most long-term tree crops require at least six years to build a deep root network and firmly establish themselves in the soil for sustainable production.
ga: Tsoi ni aduɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ateŋ babaoo biɔ kɛ hoo lɛ afii enumɔ dani amɛto shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛma shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná nibii ni yaa nɔ daa.

english: I planted tree crops on my farm three years ago; is it time to cut them down or clear the field yet?
ga: Midu tsei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli afii etɛ ni eho nɛ. Ani be eshɛ ni esa akɛ afo amɛ loo ajie ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, three years is too early. Perennial crops need at least six years in the ground to become firmly established before you consider clearing or replacing them.
ga: Dabi, afii etɛ etsɛ tsɔ. Kɛ hoo lɛ, ehe miihia ni tsei ni yeɔ afii enumɔ lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii enumɔ dani obaanyɛ osusu amɛhe ni oootsi loo okɛ amɛ atsake lɛ he.

english: Why shouldn't I uproot my cash crop trees after only three years of growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mijieɔ shika ni aduɔ yɛ afii etɛ pɛ ni midara lɛ sɛɛ?

english: At three years, a tree is still developing its root system. Uprooting it early cuts its growth short right before it reaches full strength at six years.
ga: Beni eye afii etɛ lɛ Tso lɛ miiya shishifãi lɛ amli lolo. Ajieɔ shishifãi lɛ mra Ebaaha edalɛ afee kuku dani eshɛ dalɛ ni yeɔ emuu he beni eye afii enumɔ.

english: What is the minimum number of years I should leave a tree crop in the field for it to grow strong?
ga: Afii enyiɛ esa akɛ mashi mitso lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli koni ekwɛ̃ waa?

english: You should leave tree crops in the field for a minimum of six years to ensure their roots and branches are firmly established.
ga: Esa akɛ oshi otso lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛ hoo lɛ afii enumɔ koni eshishifãi kɛ eniji lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: What happens if I remove a crop from my land before it completes six years?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mijie ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani afii enumɔ lɛ ho?

english: Removing a crop before six years means taking it out before it has firmly established, which leads to lost effort, lower yields, and wasted investment.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ dani afii enumɔ baashɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ajieɔ amɛ dani amɛma shi. Enɛ haa mɔdɛŋbɔɔ ni afiteɔ, nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi, kɛ shika ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni afiteɔ.

english: My farm trees are three years old now—are their roots already strong enough to survive harsh weather?
ga: Amrɔ nɛɛ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ eye afii etɛ. Ani amɛshishifãi lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli?

english: At three years, roots are still growing. Trees usually need up to six years for their root systems to become fully established and resistant to severe conditions.
ga: Beni eye afii etɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ miida lolo. Bei pii lɛ, ehe bahiaa ni tsei aye afii enumɔ dani amɛshishifãi lɛ adara ni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ shihilɛi ni mli wawai anaa.

english: Why do extension officers recommend keeping long-term crops in place for at least six years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ato be kakadaŋŋ kɛyashi afii enumɔ lɛ?

english: Six years gives plants enough time to anchor deeply in the soil, develop firm main stems, and produce steady harvests for many seasons to come.
ga: Afii enumɔ haa tsei lɛ be ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkɛ amɛhe awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Feemɔ tsɔne titri ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ. ni ekɛ nibii ni anáa lɛ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ aha kɛha bei babaoo ni baa lɛ.

english: Can I replace my shade trees or cover crops after three years of planting?
ga: Ani manyɛ matsake tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo maha ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ afii etɛ sɛɛ beni midu amɛ lɛ?

english: It is best to leave shade or cover crops for at least six years so they can fully establish, improve soil structure, and protect main crops properly.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo oooha nɔ kɛ hoo lɛ afii enumɔ koni eŋmɛ gbɛ ni etswa shi. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ kwraa. ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii titrii ahe yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ.

english: How do I know when my perennial crop has stayed long enough to be considered mature?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni abu amɛ akɛ amɛdara?

english: A perennial crop is generally considered firmly established after it has been allowed to grow uninterrupted for at least six full years.
ga: Abuɔ tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ akɛ amɛhi shi shiŋŋ yɛ be mli ni aŋmɛ amɛ gbɛ ni amɛdara daa kɛ hoo lɛ afii enumɔ kɛ sɛɛ.

english: Is there any benefit to letting my tree crop stay in the farm past three years?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔi komɛi yɛ he akɛ mashi mitsei lɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli nɔ ni fe afii etɛ?

english: Yes, allowing your crop to grow past three years until it reaches at least six years ensures the plant moves from early growth to full, firmly established production.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ oha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dara yɛ afii etɛ kɛyashi kɛ hoo lɛ afii enumɔ mli lɛ, ehaa ejɛɔ mra be mli dalɛ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ emuu ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and weak roots that burn easily under intense heat. Planting shade crops like plantains around them creates a protective canopy that lowers temperatures and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni shãa oya yɛ la ni naa wa waa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ ehe lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which plants need to make food. Applying compost, animal manure, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the maize regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni tsei taoɔ kɛha niyenii lɛ bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee eŋɔli ni ekwɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Growing cassava continuously in the same soil drains all the nutrients and allows soil pests to build up. Rotating your cassava with leguminous crops like cowpeas restores nutrients naturally.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hoɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsake o-cassava lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do black spots appear on my cocoa pods whenever the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ ŋmɔji diji yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Black spots are caused by a fungal infection called Black Pod Disease, which spreads quickly in wet and humid weather. Pruning heavy branches lets sunshine and air into the farm to keep the pods dry.
ga: Fungi hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi waa lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi.

english: Why are small pests gathering on the undersides of my pepper leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ mi-pepper baai lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Pests like aphids gather underneath leaves to hide from direct sunlight and heavy rains while feeding on plant sap. Checking under leaves allows you to spot them early and treat them with local mixtures or neem oil.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ aphids buaa amɛhe naa yɛ baai ashishi koni amɛtee amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he be mli ni amɛyeɔ tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona amɛ mra. ni okɛ maŋ lɛ mli nibii loo neem fɔ atsu he nii.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow tall with lots of green leaves but yield very few tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ? Baai eŋɔlii babaoo shi tomato aduawai fioo ko pɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil causes plants to focus on leaf growth rather than flowers. To produce heavy fruit, tomatoes need balanced soil nutrients rich in phosphorus and potassium.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei kɛ baai lɛ adalɛ yeɔ hiɛ fe fɔfɔii. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja ni phosphorus kɛ potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ he miihia tomato koni ewo yibii ni tsii.

english: Planting seeds too closely forces the crops to compete for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to develop big, full cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee ŋmei agbo ni eyi obɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water sits around them for too long and suffocates the root system. Planting on raised ridges or mounds allows excess water to drain away easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. Etsɛ tsɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl as a natural reaction to reduce the surface area exposed to heat, preventing excessive water loss. As temperatures drop in the evening, the leaves uncurl again.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni baaha ŋwɛi ni hulutsoo baa lɛ aba shi. Etsiɔ nu ni hoɔ fe nine lɛ naa. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi gbɛkɛ lɛ Baai lɛ baagbala ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell the right time to harvest my yam tubers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yams are mature and ready for harvest when the vines and leaves naturally turn yellow and dry up. Harvesting before this stage leaves you with small tubers that spoil quickly.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ eda ni amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni wain tsei lɛ kɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Nikpamɔ dani nɛkɛ be nɛɛ baashɛ lɛ baaha oná bulb bibii ni fiteɔ oya.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I cut down all the large trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because intense sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries up the surface soil moisture around their young, shallow roots before they can establish.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ ni bɔle tsei bibii kɛ tsei ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ ahe lɛ mli lɛ agbi dani amɛbaaje kpo.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in dark, very wet conditions when rain droplets splash fungal spores from the soil onto low-hanging pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ waa. Kɛji nugbɔshiimɔi shwie fungal spores kɛjɛ sũ lɛ nɔ kɛtee pods ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ,

english: Why does my cassava produce huge green leaves above ground but very tiny tubers under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Adding too much nitrogen fertilizer causes cassava plants to spend all their energy growing thick leaves and stems instead of storing starch in the root tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo baai kɛ ŋmeii ni mli ewo muji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans alongside my maize help my soil grow better crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil and sharing nutrients with neighboring maize plants.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ekɛ ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ jaa niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: What causes small ragged holes in the leaves of my young maize plants early in the season?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli.

english: Small holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by fall armyworm caterpillars, which feed on the growing tissue inside the leaf whorl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni egbee shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii baai amli lɛ baa. ni yeɔ fãji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ

english: Why do the lower leaves of my tomato plants start yellowing and curling during hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl and turn yellow when the plant experiences extreme heat or irregular watering, as a way to conserve moisture and protect itself from stress.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni esaaa. Koni okɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni obu ohe kɛjɛ haomɔ he.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close to each other in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋmãa kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the plants to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stalks and very small ears of corn.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii toi bibii waa baa.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up and turn brown late in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally die back at the end of their growth cycle to signal that the plant has stopped growing leaves and transferred all its energy into the tuber below ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gboiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ amɛdalɛ be lɛ naagbee, ni no tsɔɔ tso lɛ akɛ ekpa baai lɛ akwɛmɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ aya ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster than my food crops immediately after the first rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have deep root systems and seeds that stay dormant in dry soil, allowing them to absorb the first rains and sprout faster than newly planted domestic crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ wɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa jwɛi lɛ ni amɛmuɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya fe shia tsei ahe dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ.

english: Why does my harvested maize get moldy and filled with insects when I store it in sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli ewo ŋmɔtɔ ni eyi obɔ kɛ kooloi kɛ akɛto kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Stored maize develops mold and attracts pests if the grain is not dried thoroughly in the sun before bagging, as trapped moisture creates an ideal environment for fungi and beetles.
ga: Abɛi ni ato lɛ haa ŋmeii baa ni egbalaa ŋmeii kɛji akɛ agbiko ŋmaa lɛ yɛ hulu mli dani awo lɛ kotoku mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow in a V-shape?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves in a V-pattern usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. Applying NPK or urea fertilizer around the roots early in the season fixes this issue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tamɔ V lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa lɛ. NPK ŋmɔshi nibii loo urea ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ Roots he yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ baaye abua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up and becoming small and yellowish?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii ni amɛji ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is a disease carried by tiny whiteflies that suck sap from the plant. Protecting young seedlings with insect nets or spraying with neem oil early on stops whiteflies from spreading the disease.
ga: Leaf curl ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ kɛbaa. Buu tsei bibii ahe kɛtsɔ kooloi bibii ahe loo okɛ neem fɔ afɔ nɔ mra. Koni whiteflies lɛ akagbɛ helai amɛshwã

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up to catch maximum sunlight, which the plant turns into food to grow large tubers underground. Unstaked yam leaves stay on the ground and are easily damaged by heat and diseases.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ koni ená hulu la babaoo. Tsei lɛ bafeɔ niyenii ni akɛduɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Sweet potato baai ni shishifãi bɛ amɛhe lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni dɔlɛ kɛ helai fiteɔ amɛ oya.

english: Why should I cut away some of the shoots growing around my plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi plantain tsei lɛ ekomɛi etee.

english: Extra shoots steal water and nutrients from the main stem, resulting in small plantain bunches. Keeping only the main stem and two healthy suckers ensures you get big, heavy bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso lɛ mli. Efeɔ plantain tsei bibii. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ kɛ tso lɛ yibii enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ to lɛ, ebaaha oná tsei niji wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the soil before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long or when fungal diseases in wet soil attack them. Planting on raised soil ridges helps rain drain away and keeps the tubers healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ loo kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tutua amɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ ni aduɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni bulb lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Weeds steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight away from your crops like unwanted guests. Clearing weeds early leaves all the nutrients for your crops so they can grow big and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tamɔ gbɔi ni ataooo amɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaashi niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ kɛha otsei lɛ. Bɔni afee ni amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they lack water or when tiny insects like mirids attack the delicate buds. Providing good shade trees and treating insect pests during the flowering season protects the pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ nu efo amɛmli loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ mirages tutua ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ waa lɛ. Kɛ́ aha hulutsoo kpakpa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ fɔfɔi be lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when the plant lacks nutrients. Watering regularly and mulching the base keeps the root zone cool so fruit can form.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni aduawai aba.

english: Planting maize repeatedly drains the same nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts rebuilds soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ Ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni etswaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ emaa shi ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why shouldn't I sow my crop seeds right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rain is often followed by a long hot dry patch that can scorch young sprouting seeds. Waiting for two or three steady rains ensures the soil stays wet enough for seedlings to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ hei ni egbi ni mli edɔ waa ni baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui ni ekwɛko lɛ sɛɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why should I plant my seeds as soon as the very first rain of the season falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ pɛ?

english: Planting with the first rain allows seeds to absorb deep soil moisture and natural nutrients released after the dry period, helping crops grow quickly and establish strong roots early.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni mli kwɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni jeɔ kpo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi ni wa mra.

english: Why do crops planted right after the early rains seem to grow faster than those planted weeks later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni tsei ni adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni nɛ mra lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ daa oya fe nɔ ni adu yɛ otsii komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: The early rains cause a sudden release of nitrogen and other nutrients trapped in the dry soil, giving early-planted seeds a natural boost of fertility that promotes rapid growth.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ haa nitrogen kɛ niyenii krokomɛi jeɔ kpo. ŋmɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi trukaa lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni adu mra lɛ woɔ yibii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ehaa amɛdaraa oya.

english: What happens to my seeds if the rain stops completely shortly after I plant with the first rain?
ga: Mɛni baa midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ du lɛ sɛɛ?

english: If a dry spell follows early planting, young sprouts may wither due to lack of moisture, which is why it is important to ensure the soil is deeply wet before sowing.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ ba mra yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ Tsei bibii baanyɛ agbi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ana akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa dani adu dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Which crop varieties should I plant if I need to harvest food within three months?
ga: Mɛɛ tso esa akɛ madu kɛji miisumɔ ni makpa niyenii yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli?

english: Short-duration crop varieties, such as three-month early maize, cowpeas, and quick vegetables, are specifically bred to reach maturity quickly so you can harvest in a short timeframe.
ga: Akwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kukuoo tamɔ nyɔji etɛ ŋmãa, tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ koni eshɛ ŋmãa ni eda lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okpa nii yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: Is it better for me to plant short-duration crops or long-duration crops during the main rainy season?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ be kukuoo loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli?

english: Planting both is ideal; short-duration crops provide quick food while you wait, while long-duration crops usually produce larger yields for long-term storage and major sales.
ga: Enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni ooodu lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ baaha oná niyenii oya be mli ni omɛɛɔ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo kɛha be kakadaŋŋ ni akɛtoɔ kɛ jarayeli ni he hiaa.

english: How can planting quick-maturing crops help protect my household from hunger during the lean season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni miduɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu miweku lɛ he kɛjɛ hɔmɔ he yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Quick-maturing crops produce food early before main crops are ready, filling the hunger gap when food reserves from the previous year have run out.
ga: Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ woɔ niyenii oya dani ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ feɔ klalo. Tsɔɔmɔ hɔmɔ ni yeɔ lɛ mli beni niyenii ni ato yɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ fite lɛ.

english: What financial benefit do I get if I harvest my crops before the main harvest season begins in my village?
ga: Mɛɛ shika he sɛɛ maná kɛji mikpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ dani kpamɔ be titri lɛ je shishi yɛ mi akrowa lɛ mli?

english: Harvesting early allows you to sell food at the market when local supply is low, enabling you to get higher market prices before the flood of the main harvest lowers crop prices.
ga: mra be mli nikpamɔ Ehaa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ niyenii yɛ jarayeli hei be mli ni niyenii ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa. Enɛ haa onáa jara ni nɔ kwɔ dani nu afua ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmaa titri lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe jara baa shi.

english: How can I plan my farm so I don't run out of food between my first quick harvest and my main harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mato miŋmɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni niyenii akaho yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaa oya kɛ ŋmaa titri lɛ teŋ?

english: You can stagger your planting dates or grow a mix of fast-yielding crops alongside main season crops to ensure a steady supply of food throughout the year.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsake gbii ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ loo odu ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii mra lɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be mli lɛ ahe koni niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ahi shi yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How do I know if the soil conditions are right for my quick-maturing seeds to sprout successfully?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ lɛ hi kɛha midumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ?

english: Soil is ready for seed germination when it is moist down to a few inches, soft enough for root penetration, and warm from sunlight without being baked dry.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔwui akwɛ̃mɔ beni ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko pɛ eshwɛ. Eyɛ blɛoo bɔ ni sa ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ abote mli. ni hulu lɛ mli edɔ ni egbiɛɛ

english: Do crops planted early in the rainy season face fewer pest problems than those planted later?
ga: Ani tsei ni adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli mra lɛ baaná tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe naagbai fioo fe tsei ni adu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Early-planted crops often mature before insect and pest populations build up to dangerous levels later in the season, reducing pest damage to your yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni aduɔ mra lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he dani kooloi bibii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ yaa hiɛ kɛyashɛɔ he ko ni yɔɔ oshara yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ. Enɛ baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ onibii lɛ aba shi.

english: What does it actually mean to farm organically, and how will it help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ shishi? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Organic farming means using natural materials like animal manure, compost, and plant wastes instead of bought chemical fertilizers and sprays. It builds up the soil so it stays soft, rich, and holds rain water longer, making your crops stronger over time.
ga: Organic okwaayeli tsɔɔ akɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ tsei amli nibii ni efite lɛ baatsu nii moŋ fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ahemɔ. Etswaa shikpɔŋ lɛ emaa shi koni efee blɛoo, ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni enyɛ ehiɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli waa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my crops keep struggling even when I use chemical fertilizer every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ waa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii daa afi moŋ?

english: Using only chemical fertilizer year after year can burn out the soil and make it hard and sour. Adding organic manure or compost improves the soil structure so your crops can actually take up the nutrients they need.
ga: Tsofai pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii afi fɛɛ afi lɛ baanyɛ ashã shikpɔŋ lɛ ni eha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ ana niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Is it good practice to plant pawpaw trees on the same farm with my food crops like maize?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ aaadu pawpaw tsei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa?

english: Yes, planting pawpaw trees with crops like maize is beneficial. Pawpaw roots dig deep into the ground to pull up nutrients without competing heavily with shallow-rooted crops, and the trees provide mild shade and wind protection.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ pawpaw tsei ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ he. Pawpaw shishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛjie niyenii mli hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ he eko lɛ akaŋ waa. ni tsei lɛ haa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛbu he kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he

english: Why do some of my pawpaw trees flower heavily but never produce any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mipapaya tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewooo yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Pawpaw plants have male, female, and mixed flowers. Male trees produce lots of flowers on long stems but cannot bear fruit; you need mostly female or mixed plants on your farm, keeping just one male for every ten females for pollination.
ga: Pawpaw tsei yɛ fɔfɔi ni ji hii, yei, kɛ fɔfɔi ni efutu. Tsei ni ji hii lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ tsei kakadaji anɔ shi amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii. Esa akɛ oná tsei ni ji yei loo tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ ateŋ babaoo yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ nuu 1 pɛ ni akɛhaa yɛ yei 10 mli kɛha pollination lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning light yellow while they are still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse be mli ni amɛdaraa lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on growing maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which gives plants their green color and strength. You can fix this by adding manure or growing crops like beans alongside the maize.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Obaanyɛ osaa enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmei loo ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei ni ooodu yɛ ŋmei masɛi lɛ nɔ.

english: Will planting different crops together on one plot make them fight for nutrients?
ga: Ani tsei babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ awuu koni amɛná niyenii kpakpai?

english: Not if you mix the right crops. For instance, planting legumes like beans or groundnuts with maize actually helps because the legumes feed nitrogen into the soil, which the maize then uses to grow taller and produce larger cobs.
ga: Dabi kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa futu mli. Akɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa woɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa diɛŋtsɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii kɛ nitrogen woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Akɛ abele tsuɔ nii koni ekwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: How can I stop pests from eating my crops without spending money on expensive chemical sprays?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkaye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni mikɛ shika tsuuu nii yɛ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ahe?

english: You can make natural pest repellents by soaking crushed neem leaves, pepper, or garlic in water with a little soap and spraying it on your plants. Planting strong-smelling crops around your farm also keeps harmful insects away.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee adebɔɔ mli tsofa ko ni gbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛtsɔ neem baai ni atswa, ŋmɔtɔ, loo galiki ni okɛ samla fioo baawo nu mli ni okɛshwie otsei lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni ŋmɔlɔ waa yɔɔ mli ni ooodu yɛ Oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Why does the soil around my crop roots dry out so fast during the dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Bare soil loses water quickly through sun heat. Covering the ground around the base of your crops with dry grass, corn stalks, or leaves—known as mulching—keeps the soil cool and locks in moisture for your plants.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ nu fiteɔ oya kɛji hulu la ha edɔ. Nɔ ni akɛhaa he ni ebɔle he lɛ Akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, ŋmãa, loo baai haa tsei lɛ ashishi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ebaaha otsei lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why is my farm yielding less harvest even though I plant the exact same crop every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi moŋ?

english: Planting one crop repeatedly sucks out the same specific nutrients from the ground and allows pests that love that crop to multiply in the soil. Rotating your crops every season breaks pest cycles and gives the soil time to recover.
ga: Tso kome ni akwɛɔ lɛ baajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shii abɔ. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni sumɔɔ tsei lɛ koni amɛshwere yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ otsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa be lɛ, efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛbaatsake ehe.

english: How do I know which crops will leave my soil richer after harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei ni baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: Crops in the bean and pea family, such as cowpeas, groundnuts, and Bambara beans, take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant leaves and roots rot after harvest, they leave rich food behind for the next crop.
ga: Legumes kɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii, ŋmeii, kɛ bambara ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji baai kɛ shishifãi fite yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Amɛbaashi niyenii ni jara wa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How do I calculate the right distance to leave between my maize plants when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu gbɛ ni sa ni kã ŋmãa tsei ateŋ lɛ he akɔntaa kɛ́ midu?

english: Spacing plants properly ensures each crop gets enough sunlight, soil nutrients, and water to grow strong. If planted too close together, crops fight for resources and produce smaller yield.
ga: Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha shweremɔ kpakpa Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa akaŋ yɛ nibii ni he hiaa lɛ ahe ni amɛbaawo yibii fioo.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very leafy and tall but give me small root tubers at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baa ni kɛlɛ waa ni kɛlɛ shi ewoɔ bulbs ni shishifãi bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ akpa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing big leaves above ground instead of expanding its root tubers underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ bɛ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeegbɛ eshishifãi lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings turning brown and drying up after I cut down all the big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mifo tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to harsh, direct sunlight and dry winds. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them provides living shade and holds soil moisture until the cocoa matures.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he waa. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he kome. Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná hulutsoo, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Does burning the dry leaves and weeds on my plot help my crops grow better?
ga: Ani baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi ni ashãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: While burning gives a fast dose of ash nutrients, it kills beneficial organisms in the soil and burns off organic matter that holds water during dry weather, damaging soil fertility over time.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ la ni ashãa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli oya moŋ, shi efiteɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ni eshãa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni hiɛɔ nu lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Enɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves turn yellow and drop off when heavy rains fall for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper roots cannot breathe in waterlogged soil. Excess water drowns the root system, preventing the plant from taking up food and causing leaves to turn yellow and fall off.
ga: Pepper shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ shishi. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upwards and stopping the plants from fruiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa amɛ yibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by sap-sucking insects like whiteflies that transmit plant viruses, or by extreme heat stress as the plant tries to conserve water.
