ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies ni hiɛ helai ni baa tsei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa mli beni tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu nu he lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after the rainy season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants with deep roots that absorb water and nutrients faster than cultivated crop seeds, allowing them to sprout and dominate the farm quickly.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii oya fe dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ. Ha amɛdara ni amɛye ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ oya.

english: Why does planting the exact same crop on the same piece of land every year reduce my yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Growing one crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and lets crop-specific pests and diseases multiply in the soil year after year.
ga: Nibii kome ni aduɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ehaa sũ mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ. ni eha tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo aya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my maize before insects destroy it on the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa dani kooloi bibii aba miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the outer husks turn brown and dry, and the kernels become hard and glossy, showing a dark mark where they connect to the cob.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi. ni dumɔwui lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa ni amɛkpɛɔ Okadi diŋ ko yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛɔ ŋmei lɛ.

english: How long does it usually take to properly clear and prepare one acre of bush land for planting?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ajieɔ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ acre kome mli lɛ ni asaa he kɛha dumɔwui?

english: Preparing an acre depends on the land type and tools used; manual clearing usually takes a week or two, followed by stumping and land conditioning before planting can start.
ga: Shikpɔŋ he saamɔ damɔ shikpɔŋ henɔ kɛ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ anɔ. Bei pii lɛ, nine ni ajieɔ lɛ heɔ aaafee otsi kome loo enyɔ. Nɔ ni nyiɛɔ enɛ sɛɛ ji tsei ashishifãi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani ajeɔ dumɔ shishi.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomatoes turning black and rotting while the rest of the plant looks fine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant lacks calcium or receives irregular watering while fruits are growing. It is a nutritional and moisture problem, not a disease that spreads from plant to plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji blossom end rot, ni baa kɛji tso lɛ bɛ calcium loo akɛ nu haa lɛ be fɛɛ be be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ. Eji niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he naagba. Ejeee hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko mli.

english: What causes my tomato fruits to crack or split open before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi tomato yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Cracking happens when a dry plant suddenly gets a lot of water, like after heavy rain or sudden overwatering. The inside of the tomato grows faster than the skin can stretch, causing the skin to burst.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei ni egbi lɛ bote nu babaoo mli trukaa, tamɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ loo nu ni awo amɛ fe nine trukaa lɛ, fãmɔ baa. Tomato lɛ mli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: What happens to my tomato plants if the soil does not have enough calcium?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: Calcium gives strength to plant cells. Without enough calcium, the developing ends of your tomatoes cannot grow properly, causing the tissues at the bottom of the fruit to collapse and turn into black, flattened spots.
ga: Calcium haa tso mli wala yibii lɛ hewalɛ. Kɛji akɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ bɛ Tomato lɛ fãi ni miiya hiɛ lɛ nyɛŋ adara jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa fãji ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔ he ko diŋŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Can my crops look sick even if there is no pest or disease attack on my farm?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafee tamɔ nɔ ni hela mɔ amɛ eyɛ mli akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ni tutuaa miŋmɔ lɛ bɛ moŋ?

english: Yes, crops can show signs of weakness or damage from non-living causes such as too much sun, poor soil nutrients, incorrect watering, or extreme heat. These conditions stress the plant even when pests and diseases are absent.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ ajie bɔjɔmɔ loo nɔ ni efite kɛjɛ nibii ni wala bɛ mli, tamɔ hulu la ni fa babaoo lɛ ahe okadii akpo. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni ejaaa loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa Shihilɛi nɛɛ haa tsei haoɔ eyɛ mli akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai bɛ amɛhe moŋ.

english: How can I tell the difference between hot sun damage and a crop disease on my fruits?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ hulu ni fiteɔ nii waa kɛ tsei ahela ni yɔɔ mi yibii lɛ anɔ lɛ teŋ?

english: Sunburn usually creates dry, light-colored or papery patches only on the side of the fruit facing the direct sunlight. Diseases, on the other hand, usually cause dark, watery spots or mold that can appear anywhere on the plant regardless of sun exposure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulu ni tsoɔ lɛ haa aduawai lɛ afã ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ pɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, helai kɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni baanyɛ ajie ehe kpo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ he fɛɛ he baa, ni hulu la lɛ kɔɔɔ he eko.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt and droop during the hot afternoon even when the ground is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In the hot afternoon sun, plants lose water through their leaves faster than the roots can suck it out of the ground. The leaves wilt temporarily to save moisture, and they usually stand back up once the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ gboɔ be kukuoo ko koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. ni bei pii lɛ, eteɔ shi beni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi sɛɛ

english: Why do crops grown inside a greenhouse or shade house still develop rotten spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli loo ŋmɔji amli lɛ yɛ hei ni egboi lɛ?

english: Greenhouses keep pests away, but they do not automatically fix soil nutrients or air movement. If the air inside gets too hot or the crops lack proper nutrients like calcium, the fruits can still develop physiological spots and rot.
ga: Greenhouse ni kooloi nyɛŋ abote mli Shi etsakeee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo niyenii ni sa, tamɔ calcium bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ, aduawai lɛ baanyɛ aná gbɔmɔtsoŋ hei ni efite.

english: What basic signs should I look for on my crop leaves and fruits to check if they are healthy?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee okadii esa akɛ makwɛ yɛ tso ko baai kɛ eyibii anɔ koni mana kɛji eyɛ hewalɛ?

english: Healthy crops have bright, firm leaves without dry patches or yellowing, sturdy stems, and smooth fruits without dark spots, soft rotting areas, or strange cracks at the tips.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ baai ni kpɛɔ, ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni nɔ ko bɛ he ni egbi loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. tso lɛ mli wa ni aduawai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ŋmeii diji bɛ he He lɛ egbo blɛoo. Aloo ŋmei ko ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ yɛ naagbee.

english: Why is it harmful to give my tomato plants too much nitrogen fertilizer during the fruiting stage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaawo tomato tsei lɛ nitrogen babaoo yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen forces the plant to grow thick stems and leafy green leaves instead of strong fruits. It can also make it harder for the roots to take up calcium, leading to black spots on the fruits.
ga: Nitrogen babaoo baaha tsei lɛ aná ŋmeii ni mli edɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji yɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ. Ehaa ewaa ahaa shishifãi lɛ hu akɛ amɛbaaŋɔ calcium. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ diji baa aduawai lɛ anɔ

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with poor fruits when they do not get enough sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida ni amɛmiiya shɔŋŋ kɛ yibii gbohii lɛ? Beni onine shɛɛɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ?

english: Plants rely on sunlight to manufacture their own food. When kept in deep shade, they stretch upward searching for light, leaving them weak, fragile, and unable to support good fruit growth.
ga: Tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔɔ hulu la nɔ koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii. Kɛ akɛto he ko ni hulutsoo be mli kwɔ lɛ, ekpãa ehe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni etao la, ni no haa egbɔjɔɔ, egbɔjɔ ni enyɛɛɛ eye ebua aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds instead of just saving seeds from my maize harvest like my father used to do?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui baato tamɔ bɔ ni mitsɛ feɔ tsutsu lɛ,.

english: Certified seeds are specifically bred to resist diseases, grow uniformly, and give higher yields. While saving seeds from your old harvest is cheaper, those seeds lose their strength over generations, leading to smaller harvests and weaker plants.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai. shweremɔ ni yaa nɔ daa ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo Eyɛ mli akɛ ejara waaa akɛ abaajie dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ momo lɛ mli moŋ, Shi nakai dumɔwui lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why do my corn plants sometimes form ears with missing kernels or empty patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni bɛ mli loo ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ?

english: Empty patches on corn ears usually mean the plant was not fully pollinated. Maize relies on wind to carry dust-like pollen from the tassels at the top to the silks on the ear; if it is too hot, dry, or windy during flowering, pollination fails and kernels do not grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hei ni nɔ ko bɛ ŋmãa toi anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ eshɛko ŋmãa lɛ he kwraa. Abɛi kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ koni ekɛ ŋmeii ni tamɔ sũ kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ kɛya siliki ni yɔɔ toi lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ yɛ fɔfɔii akwɛmɔ be mli lɛ, edɔ, edɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa lɛ, pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii ni dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ.

english: Are insects like bees good or bad for my vegetable farm?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii hi loo ehiii kɛha mi aduawai ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Bees and other insects are essential helpers on your farm because they carry pollen from flower to flower, enabling crops like peppers, garden eggs, and legumes to form healthy fruits and yield good seeds.
ga: Wuo kɛ kooloi krokomɛi Eji yelikɛbualɔ ni he hiaa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Akɛni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔi amli muji kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi amli kɛyaa ekroko mli hewɔ lɛ, amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, abɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni woɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui kpakpai.

english: What does it mean to give my crops a good foundation, and how do I prepare my soil for it?
ga: Mɛni ji shishitoo kpakpa ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsɔɔ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: A good foundation means giving your crops rich soil full of organic matter and proper nutrients right from the start. You can achieve this by adding manure or compost and clearing weeds early so root systems can grow deep and strong.
ga: Shishitoo kpakpa tsɔɔ akɛ obaakwɛ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni sa yɔɔ mli kɛjɛ shishijee. Obaanyɛ onine ashɛ enɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaafata he kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why does my land produce less food today than it did twenty years ago, even though I plant the same crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo ŋmɛnɛ fe afii nyɔŋmai enyɔ ni eho lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ miidu moŋ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously removes the same nutrients from the soil year after year and allows soil pests to build up. Without resting the land, adding organic fertilizer, or rotating crops, the soil becomes exhausted.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa Kɛji sũ lɛ ejɔɔɔ ehe Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli afata he loo otsake ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, sũ lɛ mli baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Where do new crop varieties come from, and do scientists use local crops to make them?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni ŋmɔshi nibii heei jɛɔ? Ni ani jeŋ nilelɔi kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ lɛ?

english: Scientists create new varieties by working directly with traditional crops saved by local farmers. They take the best qualities of local plants—like resistance to local diseases or dry spells—and cross-pollinate them to produce stronger, higher-yielding varieties.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi feɔ tsei srɔtoi heei Kɛtsɔ blema ŋmɔshi nibii ni maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi hereɔ lɛ ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Akɛ sui ni hi fe fɛɛ ni tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii, tamɔ bɔ ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛshiɔ helai ni baa jɛmɛ lɛ loo baai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ. kɛ cross-pollinate koni ekɛfee ŋmeii srɔtoi ni he wa ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do some crop varieties perform well in the forest zone of Ghana but grow poorly in my village in the north?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana kooi lɛ amli lɛ? Shi ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mi akrowa ni yɔɔ kooyigbɛ lɛ mli.

english: Crop varieties are adapted to specific climate conditions, rainfall amounts, and soil types. A variety bred for cool, rainy forest areas will struggle in warmer, drier regions with shorter rainy seasons.
ga: Atsakeɔ tsei srɔtoi lɛ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi pɔtɛɛ komɛi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ henɔi anɔ. Hei srɔtoi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha kooi ni mli ejɔ, ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ mli lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ waa yɛ hei ni mli edɔ, ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ.

english: Why is proper spacing important when planting crops instead of planting as many seeds as possible in one place?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ he ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ he hiaa beni aduɔ tsei moŋ fe ni aaadu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, soil nutrients, and moisture to thrive. When crops are overcrowded, they fight each other for resources, resulting in tall, weak stalks with very small fruits.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dalɛ Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔi tsɔ Amɛbaatswa amɛhe adafi yɛ nibii ni he hiaa lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛlɛɔ, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ aduawai bibii waa.

english: How do crops like cocoa or cassava know when it is time to start flowering and producing fruit?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo loo ŋmei leɔ be ni esa akɛ amɛje fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Crops sense environmental signals like changes in rainfall, temperature, and sunlight hours. For example, a short dry spell followed by the start of heavy rains signals to the plant that it has water to support new flowers and set fruit.
ga: Tsei nuɔ shihilɛ mli okadii tamɔ nugbɔshiimɔ tsakemɔi, dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo ŋmɛlɛtswai, nɔkwɛmɔnɔ be kukuoo ni nugbɔ nɛɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛ waa nyiɛ sɛɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ tso lɛ koni ená nu ni baaye abua fɔfɔi kɛ yibii heei.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow during periods of heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves during heavy rains usually mean the soil is waterlogged, which prevents the roots from breathing properly, or that excess rainwater has washed away important nutrients like nitrogen from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu jogbaŋŋ. Aloo, nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ efo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves roll up and droop during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves during the hottest part of the day to protect themselves from losing too much water. As long as the soil has moisture and the leaves perk back up by evening, it is just the plant's natural way of conserving water under high heat.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite amɛ. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni baai lɛ baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ, Eji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ nu he yɛ latsaa ni naa wa shishi kɛkɛ.

english: Why do people cover the soil around the base of young plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi haa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket. It keeps the soil cool under strong sunshine and stops moisture from evaporating quickly, helping root systems stay hydrated.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi, ni ehaa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why do my cassava leaves fold down when the afternoon heat becomes intense?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants temporarily lower or fold their leaves during extreme midday heat to reduce the amount of leaf surface exposed to direct sunlight. This helps the plant retain body moisture until the temperature cools down.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ baa amɛbaai lɛ shi loo amɛfoɔ amɛhe be kukuoo ko yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni ajie baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: How often should I water my young vegetable crops during the dry season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo tsei bibii lɛ nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Young vegetable seedlings need water at least twice a day during the dry season—once early in the morning before the sun gets strong, and once late in the afternoon. This gives the soil enough moisture to keep the roots cool and hydrated throughout the heat of the day.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, nu he hiaa aduawai bibii lɛ shii enyɔ daa gbi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Shikome leebi dani hulu lɛ naa wa. Ni agbɛnɛ hu yɛ shwane mli Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Is it bad to water my crops during the middle of the day when it is very hot?
ga: Ani ehiii akɛ oooha ŋmɔshi nibii nu yɛ gbi teŋgbɛ ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, watering in hot midday heat causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before the roots can absorb it. Cold water on sun-heated leaves can also cause stress to the plant.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu ni afɔɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa be mli lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋɔɔ. Nu ni mli ejɔ ni yɔɔ baai ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ.

english: Can I use dirty water collected from washing or household chores to water my vegetables?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni mli ewo muji ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ atadei ahe loo shia nitsumɔi amli lɛ awo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu?

english: Water containing soap, detergents, or chemicals can damage plant roots and ruin the soil. However, water containing plain mud or organic dirt is safe. Clean, fresh water is always best to prevent spreading plant diseases.
ga: Nu ni samla, tsofa ni akɛjieɔ muji, loo tsofai yɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ afite tsei shishifãi ni efite shikpɔŋ lɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, nu ni sũ folo loo muji ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛkɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe. Nu ni mli tse ni mli tse ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ tsei ahelai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ naa be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when planted in direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that cannot handle strong, direct sun exposure. They need shade crops like plantains or bananas planted next to them to act as living umbrellas until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛdu tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantain loo banana yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni etsu nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka kɛyashi cacao tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when water sits on the farm field after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ ashi nu yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When water stands in the field without draining away, soil air gets blocked. Without air, the roots suffocate, stop taking up food, and cause the leaves to turn yellow from lack of nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ nu ho yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni ajieee kɛjɛɛɛ mli lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baatsi. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛkpaa niyenii ni amɛyeɔ ni amɛhaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: How do I know if my crop is wilting from lack of water or from a plant disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu ni bɛ loo tsei ahe hela hewɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho lɛ?

english: If a plant is just thirsty from heat, its leaves will bounce back after you water it or after the sun goes down. If the plant stays wilted even when the soil is wet, it is likely suffering from a disease or root damage.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ he kumai miiye lɛ Baai lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba kɛji okɛ nu ha amɛ loo beni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi sɛɛ. Kɛji tso lɛ tee nɔ egbo eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ Etamɔ nɔ ni hela loo shishifãi lɛ efite.

english: When seeds are planted too closely together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. As a result, the plants grow tall and weak with small yields because none of them get enough resources.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei daa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwooo yibii fioo ejaakɛ tso ko bɛ ni naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellowing on lower leaves usually means your crop is lacking nitrogen, which is essential for healthy plant greenness. The plant moves nitrogen from old leaves to fuel new top growth, showing that the soil needs a nutrient boost.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni he hiaa koni tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ afee eŋɔli Tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni ekɛwo ŋmeii heei adalɛ mli hewalɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii babaoo he miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why are my maize stalks staying short and thin even though we are getting good rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ yɔɔ kuku ni amɛhe ejɔ lolo lɛ? Nɛgbɛ nugbɔ miinɛ yɛ?

english: Rainwater provides moisture, but crops also need nutrients like phosphorus in the soil to build deep roots and strong stems. If the soil lacks key nutrients, the plant stays small regardless of water.
ga: Nugbɔ nu haa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii hu he miihia niyenii tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛfee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tsei ni wa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii lɛ Tsei lɛ baahi shi bibii ni nu kɔɔɔ he eko.

english: Why does my cassava grow big bushy leaves above ground but produces very small tubers under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi eyɛ yitso bibioo ko kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen and lacks potassium, the plant focuses all its energy on growing leaves instead of roots. Adding potassium encourages the plant to send energy downward to expand the tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo ni potassium bɛ mli lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni miida lɛ he nii moŋ fe shishifãi. Potassium ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ yaa shi koni ekɛ bulbs lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up early before the yam tubers are fully mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ miiho oya dani ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines dry prematurely when plants lack balanced nutrients to withstand pest pressure or dry spells. Providing adequate nutrients early in the season keeps the vines green longer so tubers can reach full size.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni sa ni baanyɛ adamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo hulutsoo be lɛ naa. Niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ baaye abua ni wain tsei lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ. koni yitso lɛ anyɛ ashɛ egbɔmɔtso lɛ he

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they undergo nutrient stress or severe heat. Supplying nutrients like phosphorus and keeping shade trees helps the cocoa plant hold onto its flowers so they turn into healthy pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji niyenii mli hewalɛ loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Niyenii tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni akɛhaa tso lɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa cacao tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni efeɔ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cashew trees turning light brown and dry along the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi yɛ eshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Dry brown leaf edges are often a sign of potassium deficiency or soil salt stress. Supplying the right mix of plant nutrients strengthens leaf tissue and helps young tree crops withstand hot weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ potassium faaa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmei haomɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei amli niyenii ni sa ha lɛ, ebaawaje baai lɛ amli fãji lɛ, ni eye ebua tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ naa.

english: This condition is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit during growth. Ensuring balanced soil nutrition and regular watering prevents the fruit tips from turning black.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ji fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ hi shi jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ nu wo mli daa lɛ, ebaatsi aduawai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ ediŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato seedlings droop and look weak immediately after I transplant them from the nursery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni adu amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Transplanting disturbs the tender roots, causing 'transplant shock' where the plant temporarily loses water. Transplanting in the cool late afternoon and giving plants balanced root-building nutrients helps them recover quickly.
ga: Tso ni akɛwoɔ tso kroko mli lɛ gbalaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anaa, ni ekɛ ‘tso ni akɛwoɔ tso kroko mli lɛ he gbeyeishemɔ’ baa ni tso lɛ mli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli, ni akɛ niyenii ni sa ni haa shishifãi lɛ maa shi lɛ haa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ shi oya.

english: Why do my tall crops fall over so easily whenever a moderate wind blows across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli wa tswa kɛfo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops lodge or fall over when their root systems are shallow and stems are weak. Potassium helps plants build thick stalk walls and deep roots, keeping them anchored against wind.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ feɔ ais loo amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Potassium yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛ naa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ amɛ nyɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster on my farm than my actual crops do?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to pull food and water aggressively from poor soil. Feeding your crops the specific nutrients they need helps them grow fast and thick enough to shade out and suppress weeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ ajie niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ. Niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ ni akɛhaa amɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni amɛha jwɛi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ he.

english: How does drying my harvested peppers help them stay good for long-distance buyers?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mikpamɔ lɛ ni mikɛgbiɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa mikpamɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Removing moisture stops bacteria, mold, and insects from spoiling your peppers. Dry produce can be packaged, stored, and transported long distances—even shipped overseas—without rotting.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, ebaatsi bacteria, fungus, kɛ kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ o-peppers lɛ anaa. Abaanyɛ akɛ nibii ni egbi lɛ awo kotoku mli, akɛto ni akɛya he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ akɛmaje maŋsɛɛ ni efiteee po

english: Why do my harvested root crops rot so quickly when I store them while they are still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikɛto be mli ni amɛhe ejɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Moisture trapped on harvested crops creates the perfect environment for mold and fungi to grow. Drying your produce in a shaded, well-ventilated space before storing keeps it healthy and fresh longer.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni kpɛtɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ ahe lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni shwereɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ gĩ yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ dani okɛto lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehi shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I clear all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboi ni amɛgbi beni mijie tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive strong direct sunlight. They need partial shade from taller crops like plantains or shade trees to keep their delicate leaves from burning while their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo fã ko kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Enɛ haaa ebai bibii lɛ ashã yɛ be mli ni eshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my cabbage leaves curl inward tightly during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kaabe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism. The plant reduces the amount of leaf area exposed to the sun so it doesn't lose too much water through evaporation during hot weather.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tsei haa hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi. No hewɔ lɛ, nu babaoo laajeee kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers end up small and twisted when I plant them in hard soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose earth to expand smoothly underground. When soil is hard and packed, the tuber struggles to push outward, resulting in stunted and misshapen roots.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tubers baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni etsi ehe kɛya kponɔgbɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛhe bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow even though it rains every week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa otsi moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the food plants use to stay green and grow strong. Rain provides water, but water alone cannot nourish the crop if the soil nutrients are exhausted.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Nugbɔ haa nu, shi nu pɛ nyɛŋ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ahi shi kɛji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa.

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots compete for the same nutrients and water, and their leaves block sunlight from each other. This results in thin, weak stalks with very small cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. ni baai lɛ baatsi hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛ amɛhe Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: Extreme heat or inconsistent watering stresses the tomato plant, causing it to drop its blossoms to save energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ ajie fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni akɛ hewalɛ akafite kɛyashi shihilɛi ni yaa nɔ yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does one sick cassava plant in my farm quickly cause the surrounding plants to show leaf spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ miihe hela lɛ? Baai lɛ ahe tsɔi jeɔ kpo oya.

english: Diseases spread easily between nearby crops through tiny sap-sucking insects or shared farm tools. When insects feed on a sick plant, they carry the infection directly to healthy neighbor plants.
ga: Hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ateŋ oya kɛtsɔɔ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ anɔ. loo ŋmɔ mli nibii ni ajaa Kɛji kooloi ye tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ Amɛbaatswa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my harvested papayas ripen so much faster when I stack them all together in one basket?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mipapaya ni mikpaa lɛ shwereɔ oya kwraa kɛ́ mikɛ fɛɛ to tsɛnsi kome mli lɛ?

english: As fruits begin to ripen, they release an invisible natural gas that triggers ripening in nearby fruits. Stacking them traps this gas, causing all the papayas in the basket to ripen together rapidly.
ga: Kɛ́ aduawai lɛ bɔi shweremɔ Amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni anaaa ni haa aduawai ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ shwereɔ lɛ kpo. Amɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ mɔ̃ɔ gas nɛɛ. Oya oya ni okɛ papayai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ tsɛnsi lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii yɛ be kome mli.

english: Why do agricultural officers cut down cocoa trees when they get sick instead of just spraying them with medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ shwieɔ kookoo tsei kɛji hela mɔ amɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo amɛ tsofa kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Certain diseases, like the Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, live inside the sap system of the tree. Chemical sprays only kill insects on the outside, but they cannot cure the virus inside. Cutting down infected trees is the only proven way to stop the virus from spreading to nearby healthy trees.
ga: Helai komɛi, tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ mli. Tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ kpo nɔ pɛ lɛ. Shi enyɛŋ etsa hela ni yɔɔ emli lɛ. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni aaafo lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni ana he odaseyeli ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees have swollen shoot disease before the trees die completely?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cacao tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe dani tsei lɛ gboi kwraa?

english: Early signs include red vein patterns on young leaves, yellow or mottled patches on mature leaves, and unusual swellings on the twigs or stems. Inspecting your trees' leaves and stems regularly helps you catch the disease early.
ga: Nɔ ni fata mra be mli okadii lɛ ahe ji ŋmɔlɔ tsuru ni yɔɔ baai bibii lɛ anɔ. Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi ni yɔɔ baai ni eda lɛ anɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni bɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni yɔɔ tsei niji loo tsei akutsei anɔ Kɛ́ okwɛ otso lɛ baai kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli daa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni oná hela oya.

english: If my neighbor has sick cocoa trees on his farm, will the disease spread to my farm?
ga: Kɛji mikutsoŋnyo lɛ yɛ kookoo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ yɛ eŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ani hela lɛ baagbɛ eshwa miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, many crop diseases are spread by tiny insects like mealybugs, or carried by wind and shared farm tools. Keeping a clean boundary strip between farms and cleaning your tools helps protect your crops from nearby infections.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai babaoo jɛɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs mli. aloo kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa bo ni okɛ okwaayeli nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ tsuɔ nii Husui ni he tse ni ka ŋmɔji kɛ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛjieɔ muji lɛ ateŋ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ helai ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ ahe.

english: If sick trees are removed from my land, how long do I have to wait before planting new cocoa seedlings in that spot?
ga: Kɛji ajie tso ko ni hela mɔ lɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani madu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ nakai he lɛ?

english: It is best to wait a few months until all roots of the diseased trees are completely dead and insects carrying the disease have died off. Replanting too quickly in the same spot can infect the new seedlings.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi kɛyashi tso ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ baagboi, ni kooloi ni kɛ hela lɛ baa lɛ hu baagboi. Kɛ́ adu tsei heei mra tsɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ hela aba dumɔwui heei anɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees have shallow root systems and delicate leaves that burn easily under intense heat. Without enough moisture in the ground and shade overhead, direct sunlight scorches their leaves and weakens the plant.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛbaai lɛ hu yɛ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ la ni naa wa waa shishi. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni hulutsoo bɛ yiteŋ lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni eha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Should I leave dead or fallen cocoa trees on the ground, or must I clear them away from my farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashi kookoo tsei ni egboi loo egbee shi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ? Aloo esa akɛ majie kookoo tsei kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: If the tree died from a disease, you must clear and burn it so pests and fungi do not continue living inside the dead wood. However, healthy trees that fall can be cut up and left to decay slowly, which returns valuable nutrients to the soil.
ga: Kɛji hela gbe tso lɛ Esa akɛ Ojie lɛ ni oshã. Enɛ ji koni kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii akahi tso ni egbo lɛ mli. Shi kɛlɛ, abaanyɛ afolɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni egbee shi lɛ amli ni ashi amɛ ni amɛgboi fiofio. Enɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some big shade trees need to be left standing inside my cocoa farm instead of cutting them all down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mafo amɛ fɛɛ?

english: Big shade trees protect young cocoa from harsh sunlight, keep the soil cool and moist, and reduce wind damage. They create a gentle forest environment that cocoa trees naturally prefer.
ga: Tsei wuji haa hɔɔŋ koni ebu kookoo yibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni fiteɔ nii lɛ baa shi Amɛfeɔ koo mli shihilɛ ni mli jɔ ni kookoo tsei lɛ sumɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees are planted too close to each other?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ebɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: If the branches of neighboring trees overlap heavily, blocking sunlight from reaching the lower leaves and soil, the trees will fight for space and nutrients. This competition leads to low pod yields and encourages fungal diseases due to poor airflow.
ga: Kɛji tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ aniji lɛ tsɔ amɛhe kɛyashɛ he ko ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ baai lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he. Tsei baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná he ko kɛ niyenii. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa pod yibiiwoo baa shi ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii mli baa lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell when a cocoa tree is too old to produce good pods anymore?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ cacao tso ko egbɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ ewo ŋmeii kpakpai dɔŋŋ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 25 to 30 years, their bark hardens, trunk rot may set in, and pod production drops significantly despite good care. Replacing old trees gradually with high-yielding seedlings restores farm productivity.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso lɛ ye afii 25 kɛyashi 30 lɛ, ehewolo lɛ mli waɔ. Stem rot baanyɛ abote mli. Ni pod ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi waa kɛji akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ po. Tsei ni egbɔ ni akɛ dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo baatsake lɛ fiofio lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: How does feeding the soil with fertilizer help my trees fight off diseases on their own?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi tsei lɛ ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwu amɛshi helai?

english: Fertilizers provide essential nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium that make roots grow deep and stems grow thick. A well-nourished tree develops strong natural defenses, making it harder for diseases to overcome it.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ naitrɔjin, fɔsfɔs, kɛ potasium. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni tsei lɛ ahe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tsei ni ayeɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli hebuu nibii ni mli wa. kɛ helai srɔtoi baa Ewa akɛ aye nɔ kunim

english: Why are my young vegetable seedlings dying during sudden cold and rainy spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui bibii lɛ gboiɔ yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tender young seedlings have delicate root systems that cannot handle cold temperatures or waterlogged soil. Cold weather slows root growth and creates ideal conditions for fungal diseases that rot young stems at ground level.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ fɛ̃i loo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ naa. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ haa shishifãi lɛ adalɛ baa shi ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa tsei bibii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to cover my nursery seedbeds with palm fronds when the sun is very harsh?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmei tsei haa midumɔwui ashishi lɛ nɔ be mli ni hulu lɛ mli wa waa lɛ?

english: Direct scorching sun dries out the soil moisture quickly and burns delicate emerging shoots. Covering the seedbeds provides shade, keeping soil temperatures lower and preserving moisture until the seedlings are strong enough to handle full sunlight.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa sũ mli nu lɛ gĩɔ oya ni eshãa tsei bibii ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ atsu lɛ nɔ ni oooha lɛ baaha hulutsoo aba. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli latsaa lɛ aba shi ni oha ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: What will happen if I plant my sweet corn right next to standard yellow field maize?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmãa ni ji yellow ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ masɛi?

english: Wind carries pollen between neighboring maize plants during flowering, which acts like mating. If pollen from field maize fertilizes your sweet corn, the harvested cobs will lose their sweet flavor and become tough.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ pollen yaa ŋmã tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ateŋ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ fɔmɔ Kɛji akɛ pollen ni jɛɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmãa mli lɛ haa oŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ lɛ yeɔ emuu Akpa ŋmãa lɛ laajeɔ amɛ ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ lɛ ni ewaa.

english: Why should I immediately dig up and remove a plant that shows spots or wilting from the rest of my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ni egboi kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fã kroko lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni majie lɛ?

english: Infected plants can rapidly pass fungal, bacterial, or viral diseases to nearby healthy crops through wind, rain splash, or insects. Isolating or destroying the sick plant prevents the disease from spreading across your entire farm.
ga: Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ fungal, bacteria, loo virus helai ashwã ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli oya kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, loo kooloi bibii anɔ. Tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni oootsi amɛhe loo ofite lɛ baaye abua ni hela akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off without producing fruit when it gets extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ he lɛ?

english: High heat stresses the crop and sterilizes pollen, preventing fertilization. When a plant experiences heat shock during its reproductive stage, it drops its flowers to save water and energy to stay alive.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni egbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa Kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he gbeyeishemɔ yɛ fɔmɔ be lɛ mli. Ebaashɛ fɔfɔii ashwie shi koni ekɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ ato koni ehi shi.

english: Can cold Harmattan nights damage my newly sprouted cassava cuttings?
ga: Ani Harmattan gbɛkɛ ni mli ejɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpata mi yucca tsei niji ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ ahiɛ?

english: Yes, dry and cold Harmattan winds chill the soil and draw out moisture rapidly, shocking young shoots. Keeping organic mulch around the base of the cuttings retains warmth and ground humidity.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni egbi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahe feɔ amɛ yaa. Organic mulch ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is planting my tomatoes too close together dangerous for their growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomatoi ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ yeɔ amɛdalɛ awui lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded together, humidity gets trapped between them and air cannot circulate well. This damp environment causes foliage diseases to spread very fast, which can destroy all your plants quickly.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ, nu shwieɔ tsei nɛɛ ateŋ. ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ abɔle he jogbaŋŋ Nɛkɛ shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ nɛɛ haa tsei amli helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya waa. ni baanyɛ akpata tsei muu fɛɛ ahiɛ oya

english: Why should I keep my newly germinated nursery sprouts far away from mature crop fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni eda lɛ ahe?

english: Older plants often carry insect pests and diseases that do not kill them, but these pests will quickly move onto soft, young shoots nearby and destroy them before they can mature.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni egbɔ lɛ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni nyɛŋ agbe amɛ. Shi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yaa oya kɛyaa tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ. ni okpata amɛhiɛ dani amɛdara.

english: Why do my maize leaves begin to turn brown and dry out right after pollination finishes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni pollination lɛ egbe naa lɛ?

english: Once flowering and pollination occur, the plant redirects almost all its nutrients and energy into growing the ear of corn, causing the rest of the plant to naturally age and wither.
ga: Kɛ fɔfɔii lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni pollination ba lɛ Tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ mli kɛyaa ŋmãa toi lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ daa ni egboɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my yam seed tubers rot underground if the soil stays cold and wet after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo ni edɔ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam seeds need warm, well-drained soil to break dormancy and sprout. Cold, oversaturated soil starves the seed tuber of oxygen, causing anaerobic rot before shoots can emerge.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkumɔ shi ni amɛkwɛ̃. Shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni eyi obɔ lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baaye dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ. Enɛ haa anaerobic rot baa dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops use to build strong green leaves. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted poultry manure early in their growth helps them recover their rich green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo kooloi aŋmɔŋ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo amɛmli yɛ amɛdalɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛná su ni mli kwɔ.

english: Why are the blossoms falling off my tomato plants before any fruit starts to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat or stress from irregular watering. When it gets too hot or dry, the plant drops its flowers to conserve energy and save itself rather than spending energy producing fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo haomɔ ni jɛɔ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli baa. Kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛtsa amɛhe. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo yibii

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up tightly like little cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies hiding on the undersides of the leaves to suck out plant juices, or by viruses transmitted by these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛnu tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Excess rain and high humidity encourage a fungal disease called Black Pod to spread rapidly. Pruning excess branches lets sunshine and fresh air flow through the farm, drying out the pods and stopping the rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo woɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ oya lɛ he hewalɛ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaaa amɛfite.

english: Why are my cassava stems growing very tall with plenty of leaves, but the tubers underground remain tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or is planted too close to other crops, it puts all its energy into growing tall leaves above ground to fight for sunlight instead of storing food in the tubers below.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsei krokomɛi tsɔ lɛ, Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaai lɛ amli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔɔŋ, ni ekɛ hulu la lɛ yeɔ akaŋ, moŋ fe ni eeekɛ niyenii ato bulb ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily whenever a heavy rain or wind comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that do not go deep into the earth. When the plant carries a heavy bunch of fruit, the top becomes heavy and easily pulls the roots out of soft, wet soil unless supported by wooden props.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Beni tso lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo Tso lɛ yiteŋ tsii ni ejieɔ shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ oya. ja tsei ni akɛfiɔ sɛɛ lɛ fiɔ sɛɛ

english: Why do my vegetable crops wilt in the hot afternoon sun even when the soil is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ?

english: In the hot afternoon sun, water evaporates from the leaves faster than the roots can suck water out of the soil. The temporary wilting is just the plant's defense mechanism to reduce leaf surface area and preserve moisture until temperatures cool down.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa Nu lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Be kukuoo mli shwiemɔ ji tso ko hebuu gbɛ kɛkɛ ni ekɛbaa baa lɛ nɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why does my maize grow much better when I plant it on a farm where I harvested groundnuts last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ midu yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which can draw nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest groundnuts, that trapped nitrogen stays behind in the earth to feed your next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa ŋmeii Nakai nitrogen ni emɔ lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do some patches of maize in my farm remain short and weak while plants just a few feet away grow tall and strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi yɛ kuku lolo ni amɛhe waaa lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni kɛ jɛmɛ jɛkɛmɔ ji ninetalɔi fioo pɛ lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Patchy growth can happen because soil nutrients are not spread evenly across the field, or because parasitic weeds like Striga are hiding underground and stealing water and nutrients directly from the roots of the weaker maize plants.
ga: Patchy growth Enɛ baanyɛ aba ejaakɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ejaraaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Aloo akɛni jwɛi ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ tamɔ Striga lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ oshara fe fɛɛ lɛ ashishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ hewɔ.

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes allows leaves to catch maximum sunlight for making food, while keeping them off the damp ground prevents leaf spot diseases and rot caused by soil-dwelling fungi.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ kɛha nihoomɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ ajie sweet potato wain tsei kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ebaatsi baai lɛ ahe ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: Why can't I use the exact same planting schedule in Tamale as someone farming down south in Accra?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ahe gbɛjianɔtoo ni yɔɔ Tamale lɛ atsu nii tamɔ mɛi ni tsuɔ okwaayeli yɛ anaigbɛ yɛ Accra lɛ?

english: Northern Ghana (like Tamale) has a single rainy season, whereas Southern Ghana (like Accra) experiences two rainy seasons. Because rainfall patterns, temperature, and soil moisture differ between regions, planting schedules and crop varieties must be adjusted to match the local climate.
ga: Ghana Kooyigbɛ (tamɔ Tamale) yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kome, yɛ be mli ni Ghana wuoyigbɛ (tamɔ Accra) yɛ enyɔ. Enɛ ji akɛ, bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ehaa, dɔlɛ, kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i yɛ srɔtoi yɛ kpokpaa fɛɛ kpokpaa nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ atsake be ni akɛduɔ nii kɛ tsei srɔtoi lɛ koni ekɛ he ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi yɔɔ lɛ akpo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep drying up when I plant them in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct heat and burn easily under strong sunlight. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantain alongside cocoa provides living shade and retains moisture until the young cocoa trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ, ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Nurse tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantain ni aaadu yɛ kookoo masɛi Ebaaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi kookoo tsei bibii lɛ baadara.

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become steady. The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell, which can cause newly sprouted seeds to dry out and die in the hot ground before the next rain comes.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for leaf growth. Adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the maize regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara waa.

english: During intense midday heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can absorb it. Drooping is a temporary self-defense reaction to reduce surface area and limit water loss until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Drooping ji nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he yɛ be kukuoo mli koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi ni ekɛtsi nu ni fiteɔ lɛ naa kɛyashi gbɛkɛ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and lets pests build up. Rotating cassava with legumes like cowpea puts nutrients back into the soil and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni eha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ abua amɛhe naa Kasava ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ cowpea tsakeɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ kpaa.

english: Planting crops too closely makes them compete with each other for light, soil nutrients, and water. This results in thin, weak plants and a smaller overall harvest than properly spaced plants would yield.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná la. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa ni wooo yibii babaoo kɛ sɛɛ ni sa.

english: Tomato plants often drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat or water stress. The plant sheds flowers to conserve energy and survive the stress rather than spending energy producing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛji amɛyashɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu he haomɔ he. Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi yɛ nɔnyɛɛ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo yibii

english: Why do my crops grow so much faster after I clear the weeds around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa oya waa beni mijie jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. When you clear weeds, all those resources become fully available for your crops to grow faster and healthier.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji ojie jwɛi lɛ Nibii nɛɛ fɛɛ baafee nɔ ni yɔɔ kwraa koni eha onibii lɛ akwɛ̃ oya ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to give high yields only in their first generation. If you plant saved hybrid seeds, the resulting crop will produce uneven, much lower yields compared to buying fresh certified seeds.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ Nibii ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baafee nɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee ni yibiiwoo lɛ baafee nɔ ni baa shi kwraa fe be mli ni oheɔ dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves, so when it runs out, the plant pulls nutrients from older leaves to feed newer growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ etee Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni amɛkɛha shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does planting beans in my field before maize make the maize grow stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ midu ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani midu ŋmãa lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ mli waa lɛ?

english: Beans and other legumes have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and leave it in the soil. When you plant maize afterward, the maize feeds on this leftover natural fertilizer and grows much better.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes krokomɛi Amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛshiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ ŋmãa lɛ baaye adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa ni eshwɛ lɛ ni ebaada jogbaŋŋ kwraa.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up and die before I dig up the yam tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ gbo dani mifo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: When yam vines dry up at the end of the season, it is a natural sign that the plant has finished sending all its energy into the ground to mature the tuber, showing that the yam is fully ready for harvest.
ga: Beni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ egbi yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ. Eji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛwo bulb lɛ mli kɛyashɛ shweremɔ he. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ he kwraa kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees drop many of their small pods before they can grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiho ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ? Babaoo dani eda?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed small pods (a process called cherelle wilt) when the tree is stressed by dry weather, lacks enough soil nutrients, or carries more pods than its roots can support.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii (nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ cherelle wilt) kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao tso lɛ. Niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo ŋmeii babaoo yɛ fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my newly transplanted plantain suckers take so long to start growing new leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso ni midu ehee lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ebɔi baai heei kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ?

english: Transplanted plantain suckers suffer from root shock and must focus on establishing a new root system under the ground first before they have enough strength to push out new green leaves above.
ga: Suckers ni atsake amɛ lɛ naa shishifãi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ he amanehulu ni esa akɛ amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama shishifãi heei ni amɛaama yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ nɔ dani amɛná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛtsi baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and turning pale yellow during the dry period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl to protect the plant from losing moisture in extreme heat, but if paired with yellowing, it is often caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies that feed on the leaves.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ebu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ he. Shi kɛji akɛ akɛ yellow card fata he Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa.

english: Excess rain fills up all the small air spaces in heavy soil, effectively drowning the cassava roots. Without air, fungal diseases quickly attack the roots and cause them to rot inside the wet soil.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ boteɔ nu lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Fungal hela lɛ tutuaa shishifãi lɛ oya ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from high heat, insufficient water, or when there are not enough insects around to transfer pollen from flower to flower.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe hulutsoo ni naa wa waa he. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ebɔle he lɛ Eshɛɛɛ ni ajieɔ pollen kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko mli.

english: Why do tiny holes appear in my stored cowpea seeds a few weeks after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Eje kpo yɛ mi-cowpea dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ amli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Tiny holes in stored beans are caused by cowpea weevils, small insects that lay hidden eggs on the seeds in the field that hatch and eat their way out of the grain during storage.
ga: Buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni ato lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni cowpea ŋmeii lɛ kɛbaa. Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi bibii ni woɔ amɛwui ni amɛkɛtee dumɔwui anɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli he ni amɛfɔɔ yɛ lɛ ni amɛyeɔ amɛ gbɛ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants with aggressive roots that absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than domestic crops, allowing them to germinate and spread quickly before crops can compete.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe shia tsei. Enɛ haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa oya dani tsei nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ akaŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wilt and die when I clear all the large trees off my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive to harsh, direct sunlight. Large shade trees shield them from sunburn and keep the soil moist and cool until the cocoa trees grow old enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he waa. Tsei ni eda lɛ haa hulutsoo, ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni edɔɔɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ hulutsoo tɛ̃ɛ he.

english: Yellowing leaves usually indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key food maize needs to build healthy green leaves, or that heavy rains have washed the nutrients too deep for the roots to reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ aba. Aloo, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ amli kɛtee shɔŋŋ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with leafy branches, but yield very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ niji ni yɔɔ baai lɛ? Shi kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen compared to potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy developing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛtoɔ potassium he lɛ. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without producing any fruit during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni yibii bɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry soil cause stress to pepper plants. To protect themselves from drying out and dying, the plants drop their blossoms so they do not spend scarce water on growing fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa pepper tsei anɔ. Koni okɛbu ohe he koni okagbi ni ogbo. Tsei baa amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi bɔni afee ni amɛkɛ nu ni anaaa lɛ akatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo yibii.

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow around one plantain stool creates heavy competition for water and soil nutrients. Keeping only two or three strong stems ensures the main plant produces large, heavy bunches.
ga: Ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Plantain kome he Enɛ kɛ akaŋshii ni naa wa baa kɛha nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. Tso lɛ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ haa tso titri lɛ woɔ tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. Planting them restores the soil's fertility so the next crop can grow better.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii nɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the seeds I saved from last year's hybrid maize harvest give me smaller cobs when I replant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ woɔ dumɔwui bibii kɛ́ midu ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred from two distinct parent plants to produce a high yield for only one generation. Replanting the harvested seeds loses that special hybrid strength, resulting in weaker plants and smaller cobs.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔɔ tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ yinɔ kome pɛ mli. Dumɔwui heei ni akpa lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ ahewalɛ aba shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ hu feɔ bibii.

english: Why are small ragged holes appearing in the young funnel leaves of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-ŋmei tsei lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Ragged holes inside the center funnel are a classic sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide deep inside the growing tip during the day and chew on the tender leaves before they open.
ga: Bu ko ni etse ehe yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ahe okadi ni ale waa, ni amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni okɛ baai bibii lɛ atsu nii dani ogbele amɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close to each other, the growing crops fight for the same limited sunlight, soil nutrients, and root space, leaving all the plants undernourished.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛná hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ husu lɛ nɔŋŋ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso muu lɛ fɛɛ bɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I place chemical fertilizer a few centimeters away from the plant stem instead of touching it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimitai fioo komɛi moŋ fe ni mata he lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers contain concentrated salts that can burn delicate plant stems and roots if applied directly against them. Placing it slightly away allows the roots to safely draw in dissolved nutrients from the moist soil.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ashã tsei ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ waa lɛ yɔɔ mli kɛji akɛ akɛwo mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ akɛto he ko ni kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ fioo lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛjieɔ niyenii ni mli ewo muji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ mli lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains spoil and get moldy so quickly when I store them in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ ni ehiɛɔ oya kɛji mikɛto ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize rots and grows mold if it is not dried properly before storage. Damp grains trap moisture inside the storage container, creating an environment where fungi and insects multiply fast, so drying them thoroughly under the sun until they are hard prevents spoilage.
ga: Abɛi fiteɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛji akɛ agbiko lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani akɛto. Dumɔwui ni mli efɔ lɛ baamɔmɔ nu yɛ nɔ ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ko baa ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii babaoo baa oya. No hewɔ lɛ, ha amɛgbi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la shishi kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni amɛkafite.

english: Why do my stored yams start sprouting and becoming soft after just a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miije shishi amɛmiikwɛ̃ ni amɛmiifee blɛoo yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that continue to breathe after harvest. Warmth and humidity signal to the yam that it is time to grow new shoots, which consumes the energy stored inside and leaves the tuber soft and dry.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i tsɔɔ sweet potato lɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ adu tsei heei. Enɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do my stored cowpea beans end up with tiny holes in them after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: Tiny insects called weevils lay invisible eggs on the beans while they are still in the field or during drying. Once in storage, the eggs hatch into larvae that eat their way out of the bean, leaving small holes.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa amɛ lɛ anɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo loo be mli ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Kɛ akɛto he ko ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ aahu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛshiɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why do local crop varieties seem to store better than some imported seeds I buy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni tsei srɔtoi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ toɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ ni miheɔ lɛ?

english: Local crop varieties have naturally adapted over many generations to Ghana's climate, soil, and local pests, giving them tougher skins and natural resistance that help them last longer after harvest compared to seeds bred for colder climates.
ga: Kuu mli tsei srɔtoi lɛ etsake amɛhe kɛjɛ yinɔi babaoo mli kɛtee Ghana akutsoŋ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ, shikpɔŋ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa amɛhewolo nɔ waa kɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Akɛ enɛ toɔ dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli ejɔ waa lɛ ahe.

english: How can I tell when my peppers are fully mature so they do not rot on the long journey to the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-peppers lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni amɛkafite yɛ gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ ni mikɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ mli?

english: Peppers are ready to pick when they reach their full color and feel firm to the touch. Picking them when they are firm ensures they can withstand the movement and heat during transport without getting crushed or rotting quickly.
ga: Chili peppers lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji amɛhe efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛnuɔ he akɛ amɛhe wa kɛji akɛ amɛta he. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ beni amɛyɔɔ shihilɛ ni mli wa mli lɛ, ehaa amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ nyiɛmɔ kɛ dɔlɛ mli yɛ be mli ni akɛ amɛ majeɔ lɛ, ni amɛkumɔɔɔ loo amɛfiteee oya.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize crops turn yellow and dry up when rain stops for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Water carries essential food and nutrients from the soil up into the plant's leaves. When the soil dries out, the plant cannot feed itself, so it sacrifices its lower leaves by turning them yellow to conserve what little water remains.
ga: Nu woɔ niyenii kɛ niyenii ni he hia kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛyaa tsei ahe baai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ gbi lɛ, tsei nyɛɛɛ amɛye amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, ekɛ eshishigbɛ baai lɛ shaa afɔle kɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni etsɔɔ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛbu nu fioo ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their flowers without producing any fruit during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat destroys the pollen inside tomato blossoms, making it impossible for the flowers to become fertilized. When fertilization fails, the plant drops the useless flowers to save energy for survival.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ. Ehaa fɔfɔii nyɛɛɛ afɔ. Kɛji fɔmɔ nyɛɛɛ aba lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why do my young plantain suckers wither when I plant them in open fields under full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ?

english: Young plantain suckers have broad leaves that lose water rapidly in direct heat, but their new roots are not strong enough yet to draw up groundwater fast enough, causing the plant to dry out and wither.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Shi shishifãi heei lɛ ahe waaa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi oya bɔ ni sa. Ehaa tso lɛ gĩɔ ni egboɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the soil before I even dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mifolɔ amɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water settles in heavy or poorly drained soil for too long, the roots drown, rot, and get infected by water-loving bacteria.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, amɛgboiɔ ni helatsɛmɛi ni sumɔɔ nu lɛ yeɔ amɛhe.

english: How does clearing and tilling the soil heavily affect the roots of my crops?
ga: Te shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ saa mi tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe waa ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Tilling breaks up hard ground so crop roots can easily push deep to find water and nutrients, but over-tilling can expose the soil to hot sun, drying out beneficial microbes that feed the crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni atsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ gbálaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛre kɛya shɔŋŋ oya koni amɛna nu kɛ niyenii. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsuɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither when there are no big trees nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he ko lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from larger trees or plantain plants because direct sunlight burns their tender leaves and rapidly dries out the soil moisture they need to survive.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo plantains adɛŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ agbi oya.

english: What happens if I plant too many maize seeds together in one small hole?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo fee ekome yɛ bu bibioo kome mli?

english: Planting too many seeds together forces the maize plants to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak, thin stalks with small or empty cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ nyɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ dumɔwui bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Excess water in poorly drained soil starves the roots of oxygen, creating conditions that allow fungal diseases to attack and decay the cassava tubers.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ko ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ tutuaa ni ehaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ baa.

english: Why does swamp rice perform better when there is shallow standing water in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Standing water smothers competing weeds and keeps the soil temperature stable, which rice plants need to build strong stems and produce full grains.
