ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni egbeɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔlɛ yaa hiɛ. Ehe miihia ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ ama ŋmeii ni wa ni amɛwo dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves at the bottom of the plant mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is a key nutrient maize needs to produce green leaves and healthy food.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa aba.

english: How does planting cowpeas on my land help the maize I plant in the next season?
ga: Te tsina ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ŋmãa ni midu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and store it in tiny nodules on their roots, leaving natural fertilizer in the soil when the plant roots break down after harvest.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi bibii amli, ni eshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fite yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and growing smaller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii lɛ?

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on leaf sap and spreading plant viruses that stunt growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ tso mli helai ni tsiɔ dalɛ naa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off before any fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani aduawai jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when extreme heat or irregular watering stresses the plant, preventing proper pollination and forcing the plant to shed its blooms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni eyaaa nɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ. Etsiɔ pollination ni sa naa ni enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi.

english: Why is it necessary to tie my yam vines to tall wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akɛ sweet potato wain tsei akpɛtɛ tsei kakadaji ahe?

english: Staking holds the leaves high off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight, which gives the vine energy to develop bigger tubers underground.
ga: Staking haa baai lɛ yaa shɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Enɛ haa wain tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I remove the small extra shoot stems growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Removing extra shoot stems, called suckers, stops them from stealing water and nutrients from the main trunk, allowing the plantain to bear a larger, heavier bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, ehaaa amɛju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi titri lɛ mli. Enɛ haa plantain lɛ nyɛɔ ewoɔ ŋmeii ni dara ni tsii.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil has run out of nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost around the base will help the plant regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛsu eŋɔli lɛ mli Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ afata tso lɛ he. Kɔnii lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni eku esɛɛ eba eŋɔli lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni eda waa.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small even when the plants grow tall and full of leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyi kɛ baai moŋ?

english: Cassava plants put all their energy into leaves instead of roots if there is too much nitrogen in the soil or if they are planted too close together. Spacing your cassava hills properly and avoiding excess fertilizer ensures energy goes into swelling the roots.
ga: Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai lɛ amli moŋ fe shishifãi lɛ. Kɛji akɛ nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ ŋmei gɔji lɛ ateŋ kɛ ŋmei ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ baaha hewalɛ aba ni eha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing necessary shade and preserving soil moisture for cocoa trees during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ kɛha kookoo tsei lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Plantain roots are shallow and stay close to the top soil, making heavy fruit bunches top-heavy. Proping up the trees with sturdy wooden poles and mounding extra soil around the base helps anchor them against strong winds.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ. Ha aduawai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nɔ. Okɛ tso ni akɛ tsei ni wa awo mli lɛ awo mli ni okɛ muji krokomɛi ato he. Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni emɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he.

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly during cool, damp rainy seasons. Clearing weeds and pruning tall shade tree branches allows sun and airflow into the farm, which dries out the pods and stops the fungus.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni mli ejɔ ni edɔɔ lɛ mli. Tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo nɔ lɛ ahe jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ amɛhe ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ yaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ŋmeii lɛ akpa.

english: Why do the leaves on my okra plants get covered in a sticky white powder?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni powda yɛŋ ni shwieɔ shi ehà mi gumbo tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: That white powder is a fungal infection called powdery mildew, which happens when air cannot circulate between crowded plants. Removing infected leaves and planting rows slightly farther apart stops it from spreading.
ga: Nakai powda yɛŋ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ tsei ni gbɔmɛi babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ateŋ. Kɛ́ ajie baai ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ, ni adu ŋmeii ni yɔɔ amɛhe fioo lɛ, ebaaha hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves end up full of small holes during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Insects like beetles and caterpillars feed heavily on cowpea leaves when other green plants dry up. Spraying your field early in the morning with neem water or safe extension-recommended insect treatments protects the leaves.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yeɔ tsina ŋmeii babaoo kɛji tsei krokomɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ egbi. Kɛ́ okɛ neem nu loo tsofa ko ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ shwieɔ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the soil gets too dry or when the air becomes extremely hot. Giving your plants consistent water during dry spells helps them hold onto their flowers until peppers form.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ nu ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop dark, rotten spots right at the bottom end?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: This problem, called blossom-end rot, happens when tomato roots cannot get enough calcium because watering is irregular. Keeping the soil evenly damp helps the plant draw calcium from the soil into the developing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tomato shishifãi lɛ enine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ calcium jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa aduawai ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Yam tubers crack when heavy rains arrive suddenly after a long dry spell, causing the inside of the tuber to grow faster than the outer skin. Keeping your yam mounds mulched with dry grass helps keep soil moisture even and prevents cracking.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ tswaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Ehaa yitso lɛ mligbɛ lɛ daa oya fe kponɔgbɛ lɛ. Kɛ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi ha sweet potatoes ni abua naa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i be fɛɛ be ni ebaatsi mligbalamɔ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither when I clear all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi beni mijie tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to survive because direct sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries out soil moisture. Leaving taller trees or planting plantains around them protects them from harsh heat until they are strong enough.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo koni amɛhi shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ agbi. tsei kakadaji loo tsei bibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ Enɛ baabu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he kɛyashi tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the maize regain its deep green color and produce bigger ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii waa ni amɛná toi wuji.

english: Why is it good for my soil when I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ́ midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts naturally pull nitrogen out of the air and put it back into the soil through their roots. This feeds the soil naturally and helps heavy-feeding crops like maize grow better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua tsei ni yeɔ niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when heavy rains last for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers need well-drained soil to breathe. When water sits in the soil for too long, it drowns the roots and creates the right environment for fungi to grow, causing the tubers to rot before harvest.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he hiaa cassava tsei lɛ koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. ni efee shihilɛ ni sa kɛha ŋmeii adalɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ dani akpaa.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and twisting tightly together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe shi shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in peppers is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck the sap from under the leaves, or by a virus carried by these insects. Controlling these small pests early stops the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ hiɛɔ lɛ nɔ Mra be mli ni akudɔ kooloi bibii nɛɛ akwɛmɔ Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when the weather becomes too hot, when watering is irregular, or when insects fail to visit and pollinate the flowers. Keeping moisture steady helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ ayasara ni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ Kɛ́ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for their growing tubers. Lifting the leaves off the ground on wooden stakes increases sunshine exposure and prevents wet ground rot from attacking the foliage.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha amɛ bulbs ni miida lɛ. Kɛ́ awó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa baai lɛ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Ajieɔ plantain tsei titrii lɛ.

english: Leaving too many suckers around one plantain plant forces them to fight for food and water, resulting in tiny bunches. Cutting away extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Ni aaashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ dumɔwu kome he Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ awuu kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji jwɛi bibioo ko Kɛ́ afo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ tsei 1 loo 2 pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha jwɛi agbo ko ni tsii.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly when I leave weeds in my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛ́ mishi jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are strong competitors that steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight away from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to grow fast and produce a good yield.
ga: Jwɛi ji akaŋshilɔi ni he wa ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why should I cover the dirt around my crop stems with dried leaves or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi awo tsei ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool, traps moisture during hot dry spells, and stops weeds from sprouting around your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ waa lɛ, ni ehaaa jwɛi akakwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the primary nutrient crops need to build healthy green leaves. Applying an appropriate fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure will supply nitrogen and turn the leaves green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa, tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen afata he ni ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Alternating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts helps restore soil fertility naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsakeɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe and grow. When heavy rains leave water standing in the soil for days, the roots drown from lack of oxygen, allowing fungal decay to set in and rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu hiɔ sũ lɛ mli gbii babaoo. Shishifãi lɛ baagboi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Ha ŋmei lɛ ahi shi ni egbo.

english: Why does covering the soil with dry grass around my vegetable beds help them survive the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo he ni ebɔle he lɛ? Mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛjoɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa foi.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a protective blanket. It shades the soil from direct sunlight, stops moisture from evaporating quickly, and keeps the crop roots cool during dry spells.
ga: Mulching ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kooko dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn and dry out quickly under harsh, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a living canopy that shelters the young cocoa until it is strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ he kroko. Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe waɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are there ragged holes and dark waste inside the central leaves of my growing corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji ni etse kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ su diŋ yɛ mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which crawls deep into the central funnel of the maize plant to feed on fresh, soft leaves. Catching them early with recommended sprays or neem extracts prevents them from destroying the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Amɔmɔ amɛ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi lɛ nɔ lɛ ebaaye ebua ni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips, mites, or whiteflies feeding on the leaf sap, or by a virus transmitted by these insects. Controlling sucking insects early keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, mites, loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms before turning into actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔlɔ dani amɛwoɔ aduawai diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme midday heat, sudden changes from dry to very wet soil, or lack of pollination. Keeping soil moisture consistent and planting suitable heat-tolerant varieties prevents flower drop.
ga: Tomato baashwie efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ ekɛ nɔnyɛɛ ko kpe, tamɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Tsakemɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni efɔ waa nɔ. loo pollination ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ tsei sɔrɔtoi ni sa ni nyɛɔ dɔlɛ mli lɛ adumɔ baatsi fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ anaa.

english: Too many suckers compete directly with the main mother tree for food, water, and sunlight. Pruning away excess shoots so that only one or two strong suckers remain allows the main plant to produce a much larger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la. Kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aaafo koni ashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso titri lɛ baanyɛ awo ŋmeii ni dara ni tsii babaoo.

english: Why do weeds cause my crop plants to remain small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are fast-growing competitors that steal fertilizer, soil moisture, and sunlight away from your crops. When weeds surround your farm, your crops cannot get enough nutrients to grow to their full potential.
ga: Jwɛi ji akaŋshilɔi ni yaa hiɛ oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ yaa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Beni jwɛi ebɔle oŋmɔ lɛ he Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ enaaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛdara kɛyashɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ he.

english: Your maize plants need a nutrient called nitrogen to stay healthy. When the soil lacks enough food, the plant pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new leaves growing at the top, which makes the bottom leaves turn yellow and wither.
ga: O ŋmãa tsei lɛ he miihia niyenii ni atsɛɔ lɛ nitrogen koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ, ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Enɛ haa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that capture natural food from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them with maize naturally enriches the land with nitrogen, helping your maize grow strong without wearing out the soil.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele ni akɛ abele duɔ lɛ haa nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua o-abele lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni efiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear away all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tender young cocoa trees burn easily under intense, direct sunlight. Plantains or shade trees act like living umbrellas, keeping the air cool and moist around the seedlings until they grow big enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi. Dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni ooofee lɛ nɔ Ha dumɔwui lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb up wooden stakes instead of spreading out on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ tsei anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves work like solar panels that catch sunlight to build big underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves into the light and fresh air, which prevents diseases from the damp soil and allows the vine to make larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato baai tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulu la, emɔɔ hulu la ni ekɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji. Staking haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ he ni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ lɛ. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ baaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa wain tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I cut off extra small suckers growing around the base of my main plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Too many suckers growing around the main plantain tree compete for the same food, water, and sunlight in the soil. Removing extra shoots leaves full strength for the main plant to produce heavy, high-quality bunches.
ga: Ayɛ tsei babaoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ ebɔle ehe. Dumɔwui titrii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ shɛɔ hewalɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ he ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni tsii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my mango trees produce so many flowers, but most of them drop off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi amɛteŋ babaoo gboɔ dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Mango trees naturally produce thousands of flowers, but they drop extra ones if they lack enough water, nutrients, or proper insect pollination. The tree drops what it cannot support so it can focus its energy on growing a smaller number of full-sized fruits.
ga: Mango tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi ebaawo fɔfɔi babaoo kɛji akɛ ebɛ nu ni sa, niyenii mli hewalɛ loo kooloi bibii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ baa lɛ. Tsei shiiɔ nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ mli lɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama aduawai ni dalɛ yeɔ emuu fioo ni amɛduɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why am I finding ragged holes and dark dirt inside the center funnel of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji ni etse kɛ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Ragged holes and dark powdery dirt inside the center stalk are caused by caterpillars like Fall Armyworms feeding on the tender inner leaves. These worms hide inside the stalk during the day to feed undisturbed.
ga: Buji ni mli edɔ kɛ muji ni mli edɔ ni tamɔ powder ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworms ni yeɔ mligbɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ kɛbaa. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli bɔni afee ni niyenii akagbala amɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into small bunches and stopping the plant from growing fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho amɛhe amɛmiifee jwɛi bibii ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekawo yibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips sucking juice from the leaves and spreading plant viruses. The damaged leaves lose their ability to capture sunlight, causing the plant to stunt and stop producing peppers.
ga: Kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Baai ni efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ hulu la lɛ dɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa ŋmeii feemɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when rainwater stays on my farm field for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ? He ni nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Cassava roots need air pockets in the dirt to breathe. When water sits on the field without draining away, it drowns the roots, creating conditions where harmful fungi grow and cause the tubers to rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ni ajieee kɛjɛɛɛ mli Nu baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ shishi. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ daa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do the bottom ends of my green tomatoes turn dark and rotten before they can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ naagbeei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: Dark, sunken bottoms on green tomatoes occur when the plant cannot absorb enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering. Water moves calcium through the plant, so uneven soil moisture starves the growing tip of the fruit.
ga: Tomato eŋɔli ni buji yɔɔ mli lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nu tsiɔ calcium lɛ kɛyaa tso lɛ mli fɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni bɛ ekome lɛ haa aduawai lɛ ashishifãi ni miida lɛ laajeɔ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which results in thin, weak stems and very small cobs.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ dumɔwui bibii waa baa.

english: How should I position cassava stem cuttings in the soil when planting?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu lɛ, te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ ŋmeii lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava stems should be sloped at an angle or planted horizontally just beneath the soil surface, making sure the small growth buds on the stem are facing upwards so shoots can sprout easily.
ga: Esa akɛ atsɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ anɔ atsɔ ŋwɛigbɛ loo adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. kɛtsɔ hiŋmɛii bibii ni akɛhaa Yɛ tso lɛ shishi ni kwɛɔ ŋwɛi koni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ mlɛo lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle strong, direct sunlight. Without shade trees or plantain plants nearby to protect them, intense heat dries out the soil and scorches their leaves.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ ni baabu he lɛ bɛ lɛ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni ebaashã baai lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt in the afternoon heat even when I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ leebi moŋ?

english: Under intense afternoon heat, pepper leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can draw water from the soil, causing temporary wilting until temperatures drop in the evening.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa ni baa shwane mli lɛ shishi lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Egboɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ.

english: What causes small green worms to eat the leaves inside the center of my maize stalks?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These worms are Fall Armyworms, pests that hatch from eggs laid by moths inside the tender central leaves of young maize plants where they feed and damage growth.
ga: Woji lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ amli lɛ amli, he ni amɛyeɔ nii ni amɛfiteɔ amɛdalɛ lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves from the bottom of the plant usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is an essential nutrient needed for plants to make green leaves and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa koni tsei awo baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do agricultural officers encourage planting cowpeas or groundnuts before planting maize on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ hewalɛ akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii dani adu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, naturally fertilizing the ground for future crops like maize.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Tomato plants shed flowers when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of phosphorus in the soil, preventing proper pollination and fruit development.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji latsaa ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo fɔsfɔs ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Etsiɔ pollination kɛ aduawai ni yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ naa.

english: Why do some of my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves but have tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ ekomɛi daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ waa, ni amɛyɛ baai babaoo, shi amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to spend all their energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing food in roots underground.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli lɛ

english: Why do my stored cowpea seeds get tiny holes in them after a few months in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Beni akɛto nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: Storage insects called weevils lay eggs on the seeds before or after harvest. The larvae hatch, eat the inside of the seed, and chew their way out leaving small holes.
ga: Picker kooloi ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ dumɔwui anɔ dani akpaa loo yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Lala lɛ baafɔ. ye dumɔwu lɛ mli No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ fɛɛ atsu nii kɛyashi ŋmei bibioo ko baashwɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize is starving for nitrogen, an essential plant food. When soil nutrients run low, the plant takes food from its older bottom leaves and sends it up to keep the new top leaves growing, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye ŋmãa lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa Kɛji niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi amli ni amɛtsuɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ŋwɛi baa heei akwɛ̃. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves roll up into tight cups during the hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi ni mli wa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl up as a self-defense reaction to protect themselves from losing too much water during extreme heat, or because tiny pests like thrips and aphids are hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant juices.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ nɔ ko ni akɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Aloo akɛni kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips kɛ aphids teɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop and look dead during the hot afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gboɔ ni etamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Hot midday sun causes water to evaporate from leaves faster than the roots can drink it up, making the plant temporarily wilt. However, if the plant stays wilted even at night, root rot or stem fungal diseases may have damaged the roots so severely that they can no longer absorb water.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko. Shi, kɛji tso lɛ tee nɔ egbo gbɛkɛ po lɛ, Root rot loo stem fungus baanyɛ afite shishifãi lɛ waa aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ nu dɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the branches without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they get stressed by high temperatures, poor soil moisture, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. When the plant feels stressed, it drops its flowers to save energy for its own survival rather than producing fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa hao amɛ. shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehiii loo nitrogen ni fa fe nine Kɛ tsei nu he akɛ amɛmiifee haomɔ Ebaashi fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii

english: Why is my cassava crop growing very tall with bushy leaves but producing tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium, the plant spends all its energy making lush leaves and stems above ground. Potassium is needed to feed and swell the underground roots, so without enough potassium, tubers remain small.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛtoɔ potassium he lɛ. Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ fɛo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Potassium he miihia koni akɛye nii ni aha shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ bɛ lɛ Yitso lɛ ji bibioo lolo.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees drop their tiny green pods before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiho ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Dani ebaada kwraa?

english: This natural drop is called cherelle wilt. The cocoa tree automatically reduces the number of pods it is carrying if it does not have enough water, shade, or soil nutrients to support all of them to maturity.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nu ni shwieɔ shi nɛɛ akɛ cherelle wilt. Cacao tsei lɛ haa ŋmeii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ baa shi kɛji nu, hulutsoo loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my young maize leaves have small holes and ragged edges inside the center funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni etse amɛhe yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Ragged holes inside the funnel are a clear sign of caterpillars like Fall Armyworms. The parent moth lays eggs on the leaves, and the hatched caterpillars crawl deep into the leaf funnel where it is soft and sheltered to chew through tender young leaves.
ga: Buji ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ baai anɔ lɛ he okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ. Ni ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ shwereɔ kɛboteɔ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain suckers beside my newly transplanted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantain dumɔwui yɛ emasɛi lɛ? Newly planted cocoa seedlings

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense tropical sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have large leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the temporary shade and cool soil moisture young cocoa trees need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa lɛ shishi. Plantain ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to support my yam vines with tall wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji afi mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ asɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food that feeds the growing tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground into the sun, which maximizes leaf growth and prevents wet soil diseases from rotting the leaves.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii. Staking baaye abua ni ewó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ adara babaoo ni ebaatsi helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite baai lɛ.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every year when I plant maize in the exact same field without resting the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ejɔɔɔ mihe lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season without giving the earth time to recover. It also allows specialized pests and soil diseases that feed on maize to build up in high numbers in that field.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ baaya nɔ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ hu buaa amɛhe naa babaoo yɛ nakai he lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen or that the soil is waterlogged, which suffocates the roots. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives them the nutrient boost they need to grow green and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha ená niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ ni ehiɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow tall, skinny stems with very few beans when I grow them under big trees?
ga: Why is my cowpea plant growing so tall? Tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli tse ni ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli beni mikɛdu tso agbo ko shishi lɛ.

english: Cowpeas need direct sunlight to produce energy for flowering and making pods. Under dense shade, the plant wastes all its energy stretching high to find light, leaving no energy to produce good yields.
ga: Cowpeas he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba kɛha fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afeemɔ. Yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ shishi lɛ Tsei fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkpãa kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛna la. ni hewalɛ ko bɛ ni eshwɛ ni ekɛbaafee nɔ ni hi ni jɛɔ mli baa

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their tiny flowers before they can grow into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Before it grows into a cocoa pod?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they suffer from water stress, extreme heat, or lack of soil nutrients. Providing shade trees and keeping the soil moist helps the tree retain its flowers so tiny insects can pollinate them into healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji nu he haomɔ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔlɔ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli, no hewɔ lɛ, kooloi bibii baanyɛ afee fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce small, hard fruits or stop flowering completely during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii ni wa loo ekpaa fɔfɔi kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hot, dry weather causes pepper plants to drop flowers to save water. Watering them regularly and spreading dry grass or leaves around the base keeps the roots cool and moist, encouraging continuous flowering.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ, ni no haa chili tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu nu he. Okɛ nu awo mli daa ni okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi afɔ he. Konii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi daa.

english: Why do my crops give smaller yields when I plant many seeds close together in one small area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ he bibioo kome lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants compete against each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. Spacing them properly ensures each plant gets enough resources to produce big, healthy crops.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛto he ko ni sa lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What causes my yam setts to rot inside the soil mound before they can sprout?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato lɛ fiteɔ yɛ muji lɛ mli dani ekwɛ̃ɔ?

english: Yam setts rot when planted in soil that traps too much water or when the cut surfaces of the sett are left exposed to bacteria. Drying the cut setts in the shade and coating them with wood ash before planting protects them from soil germs.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu babaoo hiɛɔ mli lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛ́ ashi jwɛi ni afo lɛ hiɛ ni helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ yɔɔ mli. Niji ni afolɔ ni agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni akɛ tso sũ ha amɛhe dani adu lɛ baaye abua ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my cassava so the roots do not spoil underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? To keep the roots from rotting underground?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, typically between 9 and 12 months after planting. Leaving roots in wet soil for too long makes them woody, watery, or rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ ashi shishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛtsɔ tsei. Nu loo egbo

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl upward during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in the afternoon is the tomato plant's defense mechanism to reduce water loss under intense sun and heat. Mulching the soil and maintaining consistent morning watering keeps the leaves relaxed and healthy.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni buɔ tomato tsei ahe koni nu ni fiteɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ shishi lɛ aba shi. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ ahe jɔɔ amɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Weeds are wild plants with deep roots adapted to store energy and absorb water faster than cultivated crops. Weeding early prevents them from stealing nutrients and water away from your young seedlings.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni nyɛɔ amɛtoɔ hewalɛ ni amɛmɔɔ nu oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: How does burning the bush on my land before planting affect the long-term growth of my crops?
ga: Te jwɛi ni ashãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani aduɔ lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: While burning clears the land quickly and provides quick ash nutrients, it destroys organic matter and beneficial organisms in the soil. Over time, this makes the soil hard, dry, and less fertile for future crops.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, la ni ashãa lɛ haa sũ lɛ mli tseɔ oya ni ehaa sũ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ baa oya. Shi efiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hu. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa, ni egbiɔ ni ehiii kwraa kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, an essential nutrient they need to grow, or that the soil is too wet, which prevents the roots from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye niyenii.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop flat black spots at the bottom before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ? yɛ shishigbɛ dani efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: This is known as blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium, often caused by irregular watering where the soil gets too dry between waterings.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee yɛ he ni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ tsɔ yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field without taller plants nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni cacao tsei kakadaji bɛŋkɛɛɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily in direct sunshine; they require shade from trees or plantains to retain moisture and protect their leaves during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei loo plantains adɛŋ koni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛbu baai lɛ ahe yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves fold up and look sleepy during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni ewɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas fold their leaves in strong heat to reduce the amount of surface area exposed to the sun, helping the plant save water so it does not dry out.
ga: Cowpea kɛ la ni naa wa tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfoɔ ebaai lɛ amli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he koni amɛkagbi.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my crops when the soil is completely dry or after it rains?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist after rain, as water is required to dissolve the fertilizer so the plant roots can absorb it without getting burned.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ehe miihia ni nu atsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ ni amɛshãaa.

english: Why is it harmful to plant cassava in the exact same field season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ?

english: Growing cassava repeatedly in the same field drains the specific nutrients that cassava needs from the soil and allows cassava diseases to build up in the dirt.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ, niyenii ni he hiaa cassava lɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni abaajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmei helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What happens to my crop if I plant my cassava stems too close together?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When cassava plants are spaced too closely, they compete with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients, leading to tall, thin stems with small underground roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shishifãi bibii yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce lots of flowers but the flowers drop off without forming peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeee pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the weather gets extremely hot, when the plant receives too little water, or when tiny insects attack the blossoms.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Kɛ́ tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ nu fioo tsɔ nɔ Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tutua fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and stronger than my crops after the rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive with deep roots and fast seed sprouting, allowing them to steal rainwater and soil nutrients before your crops can react.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani otsei lɛ feɔ nɔ ko.

english: How can I tell that my groundnuts are mature and ready for harvest under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Groundnuts are usually ready when the leaves start turning yellow and dry up; you can test by pulling up one plant to check if the inside of the pods has turned dark brown with visible veins.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ baai lɛ je shishi amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi. Obaanyɛ oka enɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ tso kome ni ooogbala kɛya ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ koni ona kɛji ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyɛ fãji ni anaa.

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to direct sunlight and heat. Without enough shade from companion crops like plantain or shade trees, intense sunlight burns their leaves and dries out the moisture in the stem.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ tsei ni fata he, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ahe lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha nu ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ agbi.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or that the roots are waterlogged from heavy rain. Adding manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the leaves regain their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eha shishifãi lɛ eyi mli obɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Does it matter which way I stick my cassava stems into the dirt when planting?
ga: Ani bɔ ni mikɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ miduɔ lɛ he hiaa mi?

english: Yes, cassava stem cuttings have small buds that point upward. If you plant the stem upside down, the plant spends too much energy trying to turn its shoots right-side up, leading to fewer and smaller tubers underground.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei ni afo lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ odu tso lɛ shishi lɛ, Tso lɛ baafite hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni etsɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii fioo komɛi kɛ bibii baa.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes for my yam leaves to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matswa tso ko ni sweet potato baa lɛ akwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up to catch maximum sunlight for growing big tubers underground. Keeping the leaves off the damp soil also protects the foliage from rot and soil insect damage.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la babaoo kɛha bulb agboi ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ hu, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe fitemɔ kɛ fitemɔ he.

english: When too many shoots grow around one plantain stem, they fight over water and soil nutrients. Leaving only one or two strong shoots allows the main stem to produce a much bigger, healthier bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ plantain kome he lɛ Tsobii kɛ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ baatswa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow weaker when I plant maize on the exact same patch of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests that target that crop to multiply. Rotating with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ekɛmamɔ ehiɛ lɛ koni amɛshwere. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsake lɛ, no baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my planted seeds fail to come up even after receiving one heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ekwɛɛɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shikome pɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds require steady moisture over several days to swell, sprout, and establish roots. A single rain starts the sprouting process, but if followed by dry sunshine, the delicate new shoots dry out under the dirt.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu ni mli edɔ daa gbii babaoo koni amɛfuu, amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi. Nugbɔshiimɔ fioo ko pɛ jeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi. Shi kɛji akɛ hulu la ni egbi nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ, tsei heei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baagbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot, when the plant lacks water, or when insects fail to pollinate the blossoms. Keeping the soil moist and maintaining balanced nutrients helps flowers turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ nu loo be mli ni kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni sa lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akwɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why does fresh chicken manure burn my crops if I put it on the stems right away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmɔtɔ hee shãa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛji mikɛwo tso lɛ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Fresh chicken manure contains strong raw ammonia and generates high heat as it decomposes, which scorches young roots. Allowing the manure to dry out and rot into compost first makes it safe and highly rich for crops.
ga: Ammonia ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ fa babaoo yɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ mli. ni ekɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa baa be mli ni efiteɔ Enɛ baaha shishifãi bibii lɛ ashã. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbi ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ shweshweeshwe ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii baa.

english: Why do my tomato fruits touch the dirt and start rotting before I can pick them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ miitswa muji ni ebɔi fitemɔ dani abaanyɛ ajie lɛ?

english: When tomato fruits lie directly on moist soil, bacteria and fungi present in the dirt easily infect the fruit skin. Tying the tomato branches up to wooden stakes keeps the fruits off the ground, clean, and healthy.
ga: Kɛ akɛ tomato aduawai lɛ fɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, helai kɛ ŋmeii ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ aduawai lɛ anɔ helai oya. Tomato niji ni akɛfiɔ tsei ahe lɛ baaye abua ni aduawai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ, amɛhe atse ni amɛhiɛ ahi amɛhe nɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and easily get scorched under full sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly and produce broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the vital shade and soil moisture cocoa trees need to survive their first two years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo tso lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that your maize lacks nitrogen, a crucial nutrient for leaf growth. This often happens when the soil lacks organic matter or when heavy rains wash away nutrients from the root zone.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ he.

english: Cassava plants naturally curl their leaves to save water during extreme heat, but persistent curling and pale patches are often caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu nu he yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Shi bei pii lɛ, yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yaa nɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni tsakeɔ lɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when exposed to stress, such as sudden hot weather, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. The plant drops its blooms to save energy so it can keep itself alive.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛkɛ nɔnyɛɛ kpe, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ trukaa. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my ripe tomato fruits split open while they are still hanging on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ miijara be mli ni ekã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Tomatoes crack when heavy rain or sudden heavy watering follows a dry period. The inside of the fruit absorbs water quickly and grows faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the skin to burst.
ga: Tomatoi gbáa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo nu ni hoɔ trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Yibii lɛ amligbɛ lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni edaa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow small and twisted even when the leaves above ground look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ bibii ni amɛtsake eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need loose, soft soil to expand properly. If the soil is hard, compact, or stony, the tubers cannot push through easily, resulting in stunted or crooked shapes. Making tall, loose mounds solves this problem.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo eyɛ tɛi lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ mli mlɛo. Enɛ haa mɔ he feɔ shoo loo egbɔjɔ. Pile kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni aaafee lɛ baatsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is rich and healthy enough for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa kɛha okwaayeli?

english: Healthy soil is dark in color, crumbles easily in your hands, stays moist without staying waterlogged, and contains earthworms, which show that the soil is rich in organic plant food.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni nu ehiɛɛɛ mli ni eyɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ tsei aniyenii ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli.

english: Why is it bad practice to plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ ji nifeemɔ gbonyo lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot exhausts specific nutrients from the soil, especially nitrogen. It also allows maize-specific pests and soil diseases to build up and ruin future harvests.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baafite. titri lɛ nitrogen Ehaa ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai hu feɔ wɔsɛɛ ŋmãa ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why should I space out my cowpea seeds instead of planting them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbala cowpea dumɔwui amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When cowpea seeds are planted too close, the crowded plants compete for sunlight, water, and soil food. Proper spacing lets air circulate to prevent fungal diseases and encourages the plants to produce more pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu cowpea dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dense plants lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni ewoɔ tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo.

english: How do I know when my cassava crop is fully ready for harvest without digging it all up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa ni mikɛ amɛ fɛɛ efoŋ?

english: Cassava is usually mature when its lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, the stem becomes thick and woody, and the ground around the base of the stem begins to crack as the swollen roots push upward.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yuccas lɛ daa kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ tsei. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shishifãi ni efuu lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why are my crops turning yellow and dying even though I give them plenty of water every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ? Ni mikɛ nu babaoo haa daa gbi?

english: Giving crops too much water can drown their roots because soil needs air for roots to breathe. Excess water causes root rot, which prevents the plant from taking up nutrients, causing it to turn yellow and die.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo onibii amli fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ shishi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu. Nu babaoo haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. ni tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii mli hewalɛ Enɛ haa efeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egboɔ.

english: Can my crops die if they don't get enough water during the dry season?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ agboi kɛji amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, crops need water to carry essential nutrients from the soil up to their leaves. Without enough water, plants wilt, dry out, and eventually die.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu he miihia tsei koni amɛkɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛya amɛbaai lɛ amli. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baagbi, ebaagbi ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaagbo.

english: Is it true that different crops need different amounts of water to survive?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ tsei sɔrɔtoi biɔ nu babaoo dani amɛnyɛ amɛhi shi?

english: Yes, every crop type has unique water requirements. Some plants are sensitive to even a little extra water, while others will die quickly if the soil gets slightly too dry.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ yɛ nu he hiamɔ nii sɔrɔtoi. Tsei komɛi nuɔ nu fioo ni akɛfataa he lɛ he waa. yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi baagboi oya kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi fioo fe nine.

english: What happens to the roots of my plants when the soil stays completely soaked for days?
ga: Mɛni baa mi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo nu gbii babaoo?

english: When soil remains soaked, air cannot reach the roots, causing them to rot under the ground. Healthy roots turn mushy and bad, which kills the plant from the bottom up.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. ha egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baafee ŋmɔtɔ ni ehiii. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbo kɛjɛ shishi kɛya ŋwɛi.

english: Why do my crops wilt during the afternoon heat even when I watered them a few days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu wo mli gbii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ moŋ.

english: In hot sunshine, plants lose water quickly through their leaves. If they do not receive a steady and balanced supply of water in the soil, they dry out faster than they can absorb moisture, causing them to wilt.
ga: Yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Kɛji amɛnáaa nu ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa lɛ, Ebaagbi oya tsɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baatsu nii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do some crops on one side of my farm grow big while the ones on the other side stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daraa wuji yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ fa kroko lɛ nɔ lɛ faaa lɛ?

english: Uneven growth usually happens when water is not distributed equally across your field. Plants that receive too little or too much water will struggle, while plants getting the right balanced amount will grow healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dalɛ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee lɛ baa kɛji akɛ ajaaa nu lɛ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Tsei ni nu fioo pɛ amɛnáa loo babaoo lɛ baaná naagbai. Yɛ be mli ni tsei ni nine shɛɔ nɔ ni sa lɛ nɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ waa.

english: What is drip irrigation and how can it help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni ji nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Drip irrigation is a watering system using thin pipes that drip water slowly right at the base of each plant. It ensures that every crop gets an equal, balanced amount of water directly at its roots without wasting water or flooding the soil.
ga: Drip irrigation ji nu ni akɛ paipii bibioo ko tsuɔ nii kɛshwieɔ nɔ. koni nu ashwie shi fiofio Yɛ tso fɛɛ tso shishi Ekwɛɔ koni ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ aná nu ni sa ni yeɔ egbɔ kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. ni nu fiteee loo ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ewo nu mli

english: How can I make sure every single plant on my farm gets the exact same amount of water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ tso fɛɛ tso ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa nu abɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: You can use controlled watering methods like drip irrigation, which delivers measured drops of water evenly to every crop so no plant gets flooded while another goes thirsty.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ nu ni akudɔɔ tamɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ atsu nii. Enɛ haa nu ni asusuɔ yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ lɛ baa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ mli. Enɛ ji koni nu akatsɔ tso kome nɔ yɛ be mli ni kumai miiye ekroko lɛ.

english: Why is pouring heavy buckets of water directly on young crops bad for them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baagi ni tsii ni afɔɔ ashwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ náa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii lɛ?

english: Pouring heavy water from buckets can flood the roots of some plants while missing others entirely. It creates uneven moisture in the field and can easily drown delicate young roots.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ muji ni jɛɔ tanki lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsei komɛi ashishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu, yɛ be mli ni ekpãtãa ekrokomɛi ahiɛ kwraa. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni ejaaa baa ŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ awo nu mli mlɛo.

english: How does balanced watering help me get a better harvest at the end of the season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni akɛhaa mi yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ni minine shɛɔ ŋmaa kpakpa nɔ yɛ be lɛ naagbee?

english: Balanced watering prevents both crop drowning and crop drying. When every plant in your field gets just the right amount of water consistently, your entire crop grows uniformly and produces a higher yield.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsiɔ tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ anaa koni amɛkabote nu mli, ni amɛkagbi hu. Beni tso fɛɛ tso ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nine shɛɔ nu ni sa nɔ daa lɛ. Oŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ baakwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛbaawo yibii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which helps them make green food, or that the soil is waterlogged. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea helps the leaves regain their deep green color so the plant can grow properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi yɛ ŋmɔŋ mli koni tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: What actually happens to my crops after I apply fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli sɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer acts like food for your plants by feeding the soil key nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. The plant roots absorb these dissolved nutrients from the dirt to build stronger stems, larger leaves, and heavier yields.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛhaa otsei lɛ kɛtsɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, kɛ potassium ni ekɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tse shishifãi gbalaa nɛkɛ niyenii ni egbɛ eshwa nɛɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli koni ekɛfee tsei ashishifãi ni wa, baai wuji, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii.

english: Animal manure feeds the soil with natural nutrients and organic matter. It acts like a sponge, helping the soil hold onto moisture longer during hot dry spells while slowly feeding your crops.
ga: Koolooi aŋmɔshi nibii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, fiofio lɛ, Ha onibii lɛ niyenii

english: Why do my cassava leaves droop and curl up during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants naturally rest and fold their leaves during the hottest hours to protect themselves from losing too much water. As long as the leaves bounce back in the cooler morning or evening, it is a healthy protective behavior.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ jɔɔ amɛhe yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛfoɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni amɛfiteɔ fe nine lɛ he. Shii abɔ ni baai lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ lɛ. Eji subaŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni buɔ mɔ he.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers before any tomatoes grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani tomato lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off without making fruit when the weather becomes too hot or when the soil dries out suddenly. Keeping the soil moisture steady helps the plant hold onto its flowers until fruit forms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi trukaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my vegetables grow much faster after heavy rain compared to when I water them by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ daa oya kwraa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ? Kɛ akɛto nu ni akɛ niji shwieɔ nɔ lɛ he?

english: Rainwater contains natural nitrogen absorbed from the air, which gives plants an instant boost. Rain also washes dust off the leaves so they can catch more sunlight and breathe better.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Nugbɔ hu tsuɔ sũ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ahe lɛ he koni amɛná hulu la babaoo ni amɛmu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites hiding under the leaves. Spraying an appropriate organic or chemical treatment removes these pests so new leaves can grow flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni sa loo tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ. Enɛ haa baai heei daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow smaller and weaker if I leave them in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thief plants that aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsei ni juɔ, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in a clear field with full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily in full sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides a cool umbrella that shields them until they grow mature and strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe. Ebaaha amɛná hulutsoo ni baabu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛbaadara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my crops give me smaller harvests when I plant many seeds very close together in one spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for the limited water and nutrients in that small patch of soil. Giving each plant proper spacing allows the roots to spread and feed fully.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni fa fioo ni yɔɔ nakai shikpɔŋ bibioo lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni amɛyeɔ nii.

english: How can I get my maize plants to produce more than one good ear of corn on a single stalk?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-abele tsei lɛ awo abele kpakpa ni fe ekome yɛ tso kome nɔ?

english: Giving your maize enough space when planting and applying manure or fertilizer at the right time ensures the plant has enough energy and nutrients to develop multiple healthy ears.
ga: Kɛ́ aha ŋmãa lɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛdu ni okɛ ŋmãa wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ená toi ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are some of the pods on my cocoa tree dying and turning black before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ekomɛi egboi ni amɛfee ediŋŋ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, which thrives in wet and dark conditions. Pruning extra tree branches allows sunlight and airflow in, which protects the pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela, ni yaa hiɛ yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ duŋ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Tso niji krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. ni buɔ pod lɛ he lɛ

english: Does cutting off extra branches from my fruit trees really make the fruits grow bigger?
ga: Ani niji ni fa fe nine ni mifoɔ yɛ mi tso lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha tso lɛ yibii lɛ agbo diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, pruning removes weak or extra branches so the tree focuses all its water and food on developing fewer, much bigger, and healthier fruits.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni fa fe nine lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ fɛɛ maa enu kɛ niyenii fɛɛ nɔ koni ekɛwo yibii bibii, wuji, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What simple tricks can I use to scare birds away from eating my ripening crops?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ ŋaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo atsu nii. Mɛni obaanyɛ ofee ni okɛwo okpoi ahe gbeyei koni amɛkaye ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃?

english: Hanging shiny reflective items, old CDs, or noisy empty cans on sticks around your field creates light flashes and sounds that trick birds into thinking danger is near.
ga: Nibii ni kpɛɔ, CD momoi, loo tsɛnsii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni feɔ dede ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ tsei anɔ yɛ shia lɛ he lɛ haa kanei ni kpɛɔ kɛ gbɛɛmɔi ni lakaa okpoi ni amɛsusuɔ akɛ oshara miiba lɛ baa.

english: How do I protect my tender vegetable seedlings from being destroyed by heavy rainfall?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-vegetable dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ahe koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akafite amɛ?

english: Building a simple shade shelter above your nursery beds using palm fronds breaks the force of heavy rain drops and keeps the soil from washing away from young roots.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tsei fee shĩa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ o-nursery saatso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he hewalɛ baa shi, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi bibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do many farmers plant cassava together with maize on the same farm plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo duɔ ŋmãa kɛfataa ŋmãa he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava and maize together makes good use of land because maize grows quickly and is harvested early, while cassava grows slowly underneath and is harvested later.
ga: Cassava kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ekomefeemɔ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, abele daa oya, ni akpaa lɛ mra. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo yɛ shishi ni sɛɛ mli lɛ akpaa.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant is stressed by severe heat or lack of water. Water your plants regularly and provide light shade during hot spells to help fruit form.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni faaa yɛ emli lɛ mli. Ha tso lɛ nu daa ni oha lɛ hulutsoo yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ koni eye ebua lɛ ni ewo yibii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant lacks soil nutrients like nitrogen, or is getting improper watering. Adding animal manure or compost around the base restores leaf health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo awo lɛ nu yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shishi lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni eha baai lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my soil has enough moisture for planting after the first rain falls?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Squeeze a handful of topsoil into a ball; if it holds its shape together but easily crumbles when gently poked, the moisture level is safe for seeds to germinate without rotting.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ fioo ko ni okɛfee bɔɔlu. Kɛji akɛ ehiɛ egbɛhe lɛ mli shi egbeeɔ shi oya kɛji akɛ atswa lɛ fioo. He ni hulutsoo be lɛ yɔɔ lɛ baafee shweshweeshwe koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛfiteee.
