english: How do I keep insects from destroying my harvested maize while it is stored in the barn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite mi-ŋmãa lɛ be mli ni mikɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Thoroughly dry your maize before storing it, clean the barn well, and store the grains in airtight bags or elevated cribs to keep insects out.
ga: Gbimɔ ŋmãa lɛ dani okɛto. Tsumɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Ni okɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo vacuum bags loo hammocks ni nɔ kwɔlɔ amli koni kooloi akabote mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is a key nutrient plants need to stay green and grow tall. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the leaves regain their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii waa ekoŋŋ.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by dry conditions, lack nutrients, or suffer from insect attacks like mirids. Maintaining reasonable shade and keeping the soil moist helps the flowers set into healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Cacao tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi, niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ pollen ni tutuaa amɛ lɛ haoɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ aha fɔfɔi lɛ hulutsoo ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtoɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in wet and dark conditions. Pruning heavy foliage to let air and sunlight reach the pods helps prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ duŋ mli. Baai ni mli tse lɛ ni afolɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni eshɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my land before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you plant maize on that same land later, it feeds on that natural fertilizer and grows much stronger.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji odu ŋmãa yɛ nakai he lɛ nɔŋŋ sɛɛ mli lɛ Ebaaye nakai adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa lɛ ni eda waa babaoo.

english: Why shouldn't I place chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Putting chemical fertilizer right against the stem can burn the tender plant tissue and roots. It is best to place it a small distance away in a circle or ring so the roots can safely draw in the food when watered.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ fata he ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ mli fãji kɛ shishifãi lɛ ashã. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ amɛ awo kooyigbɛ loo ring mli ni okɛ niyenii lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ fioo. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛboteɔ niyenii lɛ mli shweshweeshwe kɛ́ amɛmiiwo amɛ nu.

english: Why do small caterpillars hide and eat inside the funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ teeɔ amɛhe ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ a-funnel lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These are usually Fall Armyworms, which crawl inside the leaf funnel to stay safe from sunlight and predators while feeding on soft leaves. Checking the funnels early helps you treat them before they destroy the growing point of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni shwereɔ kɛboteɔ baai lɛ amli koni amɛná shweshweeshwe shihilɛ kɛjɛ hulu la kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahe be mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ. Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli mra Enɛ baaha onyɛ otsa amɛ dani amɛfite hei ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why does weedkiller chemical fail to work if it rains right after I spray it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ tsuuu nii kɛji nugbɔ nɛ beni mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Rain washes the chemical off the weed leaves before the plant has time to soak it in. Weedkillers usually need a few dry hours after spraying so the leaves can absorb the liquid and kill the weeds properly.
ga: Nugbɔ shwieɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ jwɛi baai amli lɛ ahe dani tsei lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛwoɔ nu mli. Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ biɔ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi dani amɛgbi beni afɔ amɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji koni baai lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛgbe jwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up into cups during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi etsɔɔ kɔɔpoi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves in hot sun to shade themselves and cut down on water loss. If the leaves open back up in the evening when it cools down, the plant is simply protecting itself from the heat.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛha hulutsoo be lɛ aba shi ni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Kɛji baai lɛ gbele ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ beni edɔ lɛ Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miibu ehe kɛmiijɛ latsaa lɛ he kɛkɛ.

english: Why do some of my cassava tubers grow big and thick while others remain small like sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmeii lɛ ekomɛi dara ni amɛhe wa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu ji bibii tamɔ tsei lɛ?

english: Cassava needs loose soil, room to spread, and sunlight to swell its roots into big tubers. If the stems are planted too close together or in hard, unworked soil, the roots struggle to expand.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse he miihia cassava. Ehe miihia he ko ni egbɛ eshwa kɛ hulu la ni baaha eshishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni amɛfee bulbs agboi. Kɛji akɛ adu tsei lɛ ahe tsɔ loo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni akɛtsuuu nii lɛ nɔ lɛ, Ebaawa akɛ shishifãi lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: How deep should I push maize seeds into the ground when planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ matsi mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashɛ he ni miishɛ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Maize seeds should go about a finger-joint deep (around 3 to 5 centimeters). Planting too shallow lets birds eat the seed or sun dry it out, while planting too deep causes the seed to tire out before reaching the surface.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ mli afee tamɔ ŋmãa (aaafee sɛntimitai 3 kɛyashi 5). Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha okpoi aye dumɔwui lɛ loo amɛgbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ adumɔ ni mli kwɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agboi dani amɛshɛ nu lɛ hiɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade because direct sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries up soil moisture quickly. Planting companion crops like plantains or shade trees provides living umbrellas that protect the young cocoa until it is strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii biɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai bibii lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi oya. Hefatalɔi tsei tamɔ plantains loo shade tsei ni aduɔ lɛ haa shade ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ amɛhe waa.

english: Flower drop usually happens when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of balanced nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and applying the right fertilizer helps the plant hold its flowers and turn them into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni sa ni bɛ Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewo yibii.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape starting from the leaf tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli, ni amɛjeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves in a V-shape from the tips usually mean the maize plant is starving for nitrogen. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and healthy, so applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea at the right time fixes this.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni feɔ V su kɛjɛɔ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ fɔɔ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea tsu nii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge green leaves above ground but tiny cassava tubers below?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ŋmei shishifã bibioo ko yɛ shishigbɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing leafy stems instead of roots. Reducing nitrogen and making sure the soil has enough potassium encourages the plant to grow thick, healthy tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ najiaŋ. Nitrogen ni abaaba shi kɛ potassium ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ aná bulbs ni mli wa ni mli wa.

english: Why do farmers say planting groundnuts or cowpeas together with maize helps the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa du ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have natural roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Nearby crops like maize feed on this extra soil nitrogen, making them grow greener and stronger without extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ adebɔɔ mli shishifãi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa yeɔ sũ mli nitrogen ni fa fe nine nɛɛ. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai krokomɛi awo mli.

english: Why do the bottom tips of my green tomatoes turn dark brown and rotten before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ naagbee lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit. Irregular watering often prevents the roots from absorbing calcium from the soil, so watering your plants consistently prevents this rotting.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni faaa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli be fɛɛ be lɛ haaa amɛná calcium ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekafite.

english: Why do yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on to give me big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ? Kwɔ ni okɛ yitso agbo aha mi?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up toward the sun so they can capture maximum sunlight and produce energy. The plant stores this energy underground, which causes the yam tubers to expand and grow much larger.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he koni amɛnyɛ amɛmɔmɔ hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ ni amɛjie hewalɛ kpo. Tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ nɛɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni amɛfeɔ agboi babaoo.

english: Why should I remove the extra sucker shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: If too many sucker shoots grow at the base, they steal food, water, and light from the main plantain stem. Removing extra suckers leaves just one or two shoots, ensuring the main plant gets enough strength to grow huge plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo miida yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ Ejuɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ plantain tsei wuji lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ koni ekwɛ akɛ tso titri lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do seeds I harvest and save from hybrid crops produce weaker plants than new certified seeds bought from the store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikpaa ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ woɔ tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ hela fe dumɔwui heei ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred for one generation of high yield. The seeds collected from those harvested crops lose their special parent qualities, leading to mixed growth, weaker disease resistance, and lower yields in the next season.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni ekɛ yibii babaoo aba yinɔ kome. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nakai tsei ni akpaa lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ sui krɛdɛɛi ni amɛfɔlɔi yɔɔ lɛ. ni kɛ dalɛ ni futuɔ baa Helai ahewalɛ ni baa shi kɛ nibii ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli

english: How do I know if a specific crop variety will grow well in my local area before I spend money planting it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso pɔtɛɛ ko baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ? dani efite shika yɛ ekwɛmɔ nɔ

english: Crop varieties are developed for specific weather patterns, soil types, and regional diseases. Checking certified seed labels or asking local agricultural extension officers will confirm if a variety is suited for your district's climate.
ga: Akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi, shikpɔŋ henɔi, kɛ helai ni yɔɔ hei pɔtɛɛ komɛi lɛ feɔ tsei srɔtoi. Dumɔwui ahe woji ni aŋmala nɔ odaseyeli lɛ ni oookwɛ loo obi okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ni yɔɔ oakutso lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ona nɔmimaa akɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni yɔɔ lɛ. Ani ehi kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ?

english: If I get new improved seeds from a government farming project, do I still need to spray them for pests?
ga: Kɛji minine shɛ dumɔwui ni atsake nɔ kɛjɛ nɔyeli okwaayeli gbɛjianɔtoo ko mli lɛ Ani ehe miihia ni mafɔ tsofa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai lolo?

english: Yes, even improved seeds from agricultural projects can still get attacked by pests and diseases. Improved seeds are often bred to produce high yields or tolerate specific conditions, but they are rarely completely immune to all insects and rots.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai baanyɛ atutua dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ kɛjɛ okwaayeli nitsumɔi amli lɛ po. Bei pii lɛ, afɔɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo loo koni amɛdamɔ shihilɛi pɔtɛɛ komɛi anaa. Shi nɛkɛ dumɔwui nɛɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛye amɛhe kwraa kɛjɛ kooloi kɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi fɛɛ ahe.

english: Why do my neighbour's project crops get eaten by insects when we were told the crop variety is strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii miiye ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ nitsumɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Akɛɛ wɔ akɛ tsei srɔtoi lɛ ahe wa?

english: When experts say a crop variety is strong, it usually means it resists specific environmental stresses or a particular illness. Insects will still feed on any healthy plant, so routine pest checks and control are still necessary.
ga: Kɛji nilelɔi kɛɛ tsei srɔtoi lɛ ahe wa Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ enyɛɔ eshiɔ shihilɛ mli haomɔi loo helai komɛi. Kplukai baaya nɔ aye tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni akwɛ mli daa ni akudɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ.

english: Is it possible for a new crop variety to look healthy outside while carrying a hidden disease?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii hee ko baafee tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ yɛ kponɔgbɛ yɛ be mli ni helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ yɔɔ mli?

english: Yes, some plant sicknesses start inside the roots or stem before any signs show on the leaves. You should always inspect your farm regularly, even if your new crops look green and healthy at first.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai komɛi jeɔ shishi yɛ amɛshishifãi loo amɛshishifãi lɛ amli dani okadi ko jeɔ kpo yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Esa akɛ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa. Kɛji akɛ onibii heei lɛ tamɔ eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ shishijee mli po lɛ,

english: How can a small pest problem on my farm cause me to lose all the money I spent on planting?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsɛŋemɔ hela bibioo ko ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shika fɛɛ ni mifite yɛ okwaayeli mli lɛ afite mi?

english: Pests multiply very fast in warm weather. If you ignore a few insects early in the season, they can quickly destroy your entire harvest, leaving you with nothing to sell to cover your seed and fertilizer costs.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ oya waa yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ lɛ. Kɛji oku ohiɛ ofɔ̃ kooloi komɛi anɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, Amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite onibii fɛɛ oya. Enɛ haaa oná nɔ ko ni okɛbaahɔɔ ni okɛwo dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nyɔmɔwoo he nyɔmɔ.

english: What should I do first when I notice strange spots spreading on my crop leaves?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee klɛŋklɛŋ kɛ́ mina hei ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ni egbɛ eshwã mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Remove a few affected leaves, put them in a clear plastic bag, and show them to an extension officer immediately. Catching leaf diseases early stops the sickness from spreading across your entire field.
ga: Jiemɔ baai ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ekomɛi. Okɛwo plastic kotoku ni mli tse mli No sɛɛ lɛ otsɔɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ nitsumɔ nɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Baa helai ni ooomɔ mra Ebaatsi hela naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa oŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops keep getting the same disease every time I replant in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa hela kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ be fɛɛ be ni madu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Disease organisms and pest eggs remain alive in the soil long after harvest. If you keep planting the exact same crop without rotating it with a different crop type, the soil sickness builds up and attacks every new planting.
ga: Helai kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni okɛ tsei srɔtoi tsakeee lɛ, Shikpɔŋ nɔ helai buaa amɛhe naa ni amɛtutuaa tso hee fɛɛ tso hee.

english: Why should I clear my field and replant new crops right after harvesting instead of leaving the land empty?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni madu tsei heei amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji akpa ŋmɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi he ni eyɔɔ lɛ efolo

english: Replanting right after harvest makes full use of remaining soil moisture and the current rainy season. However, you must add manure or fertilizer so the continuous planting does not exhaust the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ekoŋŋ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni yɔɔ amrɔ nɛɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he bɔni afee ni dumɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ akafite shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: If I harvest a very good yield this season, can I save those seeds to plant again next season?
ga: Kɛji minine shɛ kpamɔ kpakpa diɛŋtsɛ nɔ yɛ be nɛɛ mli. Ani manyɛ makɛ nakai dumɔwui lɛ ato koni madu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: It depends on the seed type. Many modern high-yielding hybrid seeds lose their strength in the next generation, resulting in smaller harvests and weaker plants if you replant seeds saved from your harvest.
ga: Edamɔ dumɔwu henɔ lɛ nɔ Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ babaoo he waaa yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi fioo ni tsei lɛ baa shi kɛji okɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ okpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ du ekoŋŋ.

english: If I want to plant more crops to make more money, why shouldn't I just pack the seeds close together?
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ ni odu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo koni oná shika. Mɛni hewɔ okɛ dumɔwui lɛ ebɛŋkɛɛɛ amɛhe?

english: Planting seeds too close forces them to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin plants. Dense planting also traps moisture, creating a perfect environment for fungal diseases to spread.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ feɔ mlɛo. Dumɔ ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ hu mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow even though I gave them enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil or damage to the roots caused by hidden pests or rot, which prevents the plant from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo shishifãi lɛ ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ loo ŋmeii efite. ni tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaye niyenii

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that easily get scorched by direct heat. They require shade trees or fast-growing companion crops like plantain to block harsh sunlight and keep the surrounding soil moist until the cocoa bushes mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo tsei ni fata amɛhe ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains koni amɛná ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ hulu ni naa wa lɛ nɔ ni amɛha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: How can I tell if I am planting my cassava stem cuttings in the correct direction?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ mi-cassava ŋmɔji lɛ miidu yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ?

english: Look closely at the small leaf buds along the stem stick; these buds must point upwards toward the sky. If you plant cassava stems upside down, the tubers will struggle to form properly and your harvest will be very low.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu ŋmei tso ni okɛ ohiɛ fɔ shi lɛ ŋmei lɛ baaná naagba yɛ efeemɔ he jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmaa lɛ baafee bibioo kwraa.

english: Why is it necessary for me to put high bamboo sticks next to my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ ŋmei tso kakadaŋŋ ama ŋmei tso ko masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch as much sunlight as possible. Staking keeps the leaves dry and helps the plant send more energy down into growing large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ agbi ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo aya ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my young maize leaves have ragged holes in them with tiny green drops inside the central funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar eating the growing heart of the maize plant. The green drops are its droppings; spraying early in the morning with biological control options or recommended pesticides can save your crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ tsui ni miida lɛ. Blob eŋɔli lɛ ji efɔfɔi. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofa ko ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ leebi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ehere onibii lɛ ayiwala.

english: Can I prepare a natural insect spray using leaves from the local neem tree for my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ kɛtsɔ neem tso ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baai anɔ?

english: Yes, crushing neem leaves in water and letting them steep produces a natural bitter spray that drives away many leaf-eating insects from vegetable crops without costing money or harming useful soil life.
ga: Hɛɛ, neem baai ni akumɔ awo nu mli ni aha amɛ shwie shi lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli tsofa ko ni mli edɔ ni shwieɔ kooloi bibii babaoo ni yeɔ baai lɛ kɛjɛɔ aduawai amli ni efiteee shika loo eyeee shikpɔŋ nɔ wala ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ awui.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my growing maize crop turning pale yellow from the tips inward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni miida lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛjɛ emligbɛ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting at the lower leaf tips indicates a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to stay green and full; applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure solves this.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why is it good for my soil if I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my farm after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are leguminous crops that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in roots underground. Rotating them with maize naturally restores fertility into the dirt for your next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli. Kɛ okɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa ni akɛtsakeɔ ŋmãa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmãa ekoŋŋ kɛha onibii ni baa lɛ.

english: Plantain roots are shallow and easily destroyed by tiny underground pests called nematodes or weevils. When heavy fruit bunches grow, weak roots break under the weight; supporting the stems with sturdy wooden props prevents them from snapping.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ amɛ awui oya. Kɛ aduawai akuu lɛ da lɛ, shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ baafo yɛ muji lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni wa fiɔ tsɔne lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa ekumɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants get black patches on leaves and rot during the main rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ baa lɛ nɔ tsɔi diji ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess rain and humidity encourage fungal diseases like late blight to grow on wet leaves. Spacing plants further apart lets air flow through to dry the leaves, and tying vines to wooden stakes keeps fruit off damp ground.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine kɛ hulutsoo woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ late blight hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ ajie tsei lɛ kɛjɛ amɛhe lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ mli koni eha baai lɛ agbi. Ni kɛ́ akɛ wain tsei lɛ fĩ tsei ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aduawai lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize plants usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, which the crop needs to build strong, green leaves. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii awo baai ni wa, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they are stressed by hot dry weather, uneven watering, or poor soil nutrients. Keeping the soil damp with mulch and watering regularly helps the flowers stay on the plant to form fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ, shihilɛi ni mli egbi hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli fũu kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi tso lɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when planted in an open field without big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under full direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains around them creates a cool canopy that protects the young seedlings until they grow strong enough to withstand direct sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ amɛhe lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni buɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves high into the air to catch sunlight for growing big tubers under the ground. Staking also keeps the leaves off damp ground, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la lɛ bɔni afee ni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Koni akɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Giving each plant proper space allows it to grow thick stalks and full, heavy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli wa kɛ ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and bigger than my planted crops after clearing the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛdaraa fe tsei ni midu beni mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds naturally adapt to sprout fast and steal water and nutrients from the soil before young crops can establish roots. Clearing weeds early gives your planted crops full access to the soil's food.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ shishifãi. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha otsei lɛ aná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Curled and yellow-spotted cassava leaves are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by small white insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems helps stop this from spreading.
ga: Kasava baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni kooloi bibii yɛŋ ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ. Kasava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why are small worms eating holes in the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These worms are Fall Armyworms that target the soft central leaves of young maize. Inspecting fields early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem leaf extracts will protect the crop from damage.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms ni kwɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ anɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem baa ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ fitemɔ he.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my seeds after the first rain of the season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the rain penetrates deep into the soil—about a hand's depth—before planting seeds. Planting after just a small rain can dry out seeds if the sun returns quickly.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ—aaafee tso ko ni mli kwɔ—dani odu dumɔwui. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi kɛji hulu lɛ ku esɛɛ eba oya.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn soft and moldy in the storage room after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nitoohe lɛ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize rots in storage if there is still water trapped inside the kernels when they are stored. Drying the maize cobs thoroughly in the sun until the grains are hard prevents mold and insects from destroying them.
ga: Abɛi fiteɔ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛji nu hiɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli beni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa ŋmeii yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii akafite amɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field without any tall trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni midu yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil. Planting shade crops like plantains or leaving natural canopy trees provides shelter and keeps the soil moist while the young cocoa plants mature.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui biɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ, tamɔ dumɔwui bibii loo adebɔɔ mli cacao tsei ni ashiɔ lɛ haa mɔ náa he ko ni eyɔɔ fɛo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni cacao tsei bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: I noticed flowers growing directly on the trunk of my cocoa tree instead of the leaves; is this normal or a disease?
ga: Miyɔse fɔfɔi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ cacao tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ baai najiaŋ. Ani enɛ ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ loo hela ko?

english: This is completely normal and healthy. Cocoa trees naturally produce flowers and pods directly on their main trunk and thick branches, a trait called cauliflory, which allows the tree to support heavy cocoa pods as they grow.
ga: Enɛ ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kwraa ni ehi jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii yɛ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ kɛ eniji ni mli tse lɛ anɔ. ni atsɛɔ lɛ cauliflower Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛfiɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Won't cutting off branches from my growing cocoa trees weaken them and lower my harvest?
ga: Ani niji ni mifoɔ yɛ mi cacao tso ni miida lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha mi yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi?

english: No, pruning actually strengthens the tree by removing weak, overcrowded, or diseased branches. This lets sunlight and fresh air reach the inside of the tree and directs nutrients straight into making healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Dabi, tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ haa ewaa kɛtsɔ niji ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni eyi obɔ kɛ niji, loo ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ mli ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ baa tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning black and rotting right on the tree during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in dark, humid, and overly wet environments. Keeping your farm weeded and pruning trees to let air pass through helps pods stay dry and resist the infection.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni duŋ yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ fe nine lɛ. Jwɛi ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ tsei ni afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ helai.

english: Why are the leaves on my young crop turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the crop lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that the roots are sitting in waterlogged soil. Adding manure or appropriate fertilizer helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ shishifãi lɛ eta sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do weeds harm my crops if there is plenty of space in the field?
ga: Te jwɛi baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji akɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Weeds grow quickly and aggressively steal water, soil nutrients, and sunlight away from your main crops. They also act as hiding spots for insects and diseases that can attack your plants.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛjuɔ nu. niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ hulu la ni kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ Amɛtsuɔ nii hu akɛ he ni kooloi bibii kɛ helai kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli. ni baanyɛ atutua otsei lɛ

english: Can I plant leguminous crops like groundnuts together with my main crops without ruining the soil?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ni mifiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yes, intercropping with legumes like groundnuts or beans actually improves the soil. Legumes capture nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for surrounding crops.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii. Ebaaye ebua diɛŋtsɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ. Legumes mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa tsei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ.

english: When is the best time for me to plant my seeds so they do not dry up or wash away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ madu dumɔwui koni amɛkagbi loo amɛkaho?

english: The best time to plant is at the very start of the major rainy season when the soil is moist enough for seeds to germinate, but before heavy downpours begin that could wash away seeds or flood young sprouts.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ji nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ shishijee. Enɛ ji be mli ni sũ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃. Shi dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaje shishi. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ laaje loo nu atsɔ tsei bibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to measure specific distances between plants instead of planting closely to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ masusu bɔ ni tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ ha lɛ he moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures each plant gets its own fair share of soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. When plants are packed too closely, they compete for resources, resulting in thinner crops and lower total yields.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la ni sa lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ tsei lɛ ebɔ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ amɛhe shi yɛ nibii ni he hiaa lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why should I loosen and till the soil before planting instead of just digging small holes in hard ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ agbɔjɔ dani odu nii lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofo bu bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Loosening the soil creates air spaces and softens the earth, making it easy for young roots to spread deep, absorb water, and establish a strong foundation for the plant.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui baa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shɔŋŋ oya, amɛmɔɔ nu, ni amɛfeɔ shishitoo ni wa kɛha tsei.

english: Why do weeds grow back so fast and choke my crops if I stop clearing the farm for even a short time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni efiteɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ? Kɛji mikpa miŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii ahe nitsumɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli po?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants that absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. If left unchecked, they quickly take over the field, stealing light and food from your crops until the crops weaken and fail.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Amɛbaaye jɛmɛ oya. Ejuɔ la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why are tiny worms eating the leaves of my maize and making them turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ aahu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Pests like Fall Armyworms feed on the tender green tissue of maize leaves. When the leaves get destroyed, the plant cannot use sunlight to make food for itself, causing the leaves to turn yellow and halting crop growth.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworms lɛ yeɔ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ fite lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ amɛkɛ hulu la afee amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa tsei lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die when planted in an open field under full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni hulu lɛ eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily in direct sun. They need shade crops like plantains or nursery trees above them to trap moisture and block harsh heat while their root systems develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei ni akɛkwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo ni fe nine lɛ he yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves dry out and split into strips during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ gĩɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Harmattan dry winds pull moisture out of broad plantain leaves much faster than the dry roots can pull water from the soil. The leaves split naturally as a defense mechanism to reduce surface area and cut down water loss.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ jieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ plantain baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi ni egbi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa akɛ gbɛ ni akɛbuɔ he koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi ni ekɛba nu ni fiteɔ lɛ shi.

english: Why do my cassava plants have lush, tall green leaves but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: If the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or lacks key nutrients like potassium, the plant directs all its energy into growing big stems and leaves above ground instead of sending food down to expand the tubers.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium bɛ mli lɛ, tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baawo tsei agboi kɛ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsu niyenii kɛba shi koni ekɛgbala yitso lɛ mli

english: Why do my yam tubers grow short, crooked, and hard to sell instead of straight and long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ kukuji, amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛhɔ̃ɔmɔ wa, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee tɛ̃ɛ ni kɛlɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow by pushing down into soft soil. If the land is compacted or full of heavy clay, the growing tuber cannot push downwards smoothly and gets forced into bent or stunted shapes.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli jɔ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ loo shikpɔŋ eyi mli obɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ Tsofai ni miida lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛtsi amɛhe kɛya shi jogbaŋŋ ni anyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛku amɛsɛɛ loo amɛfee shwiili.

english: Why do extension agents recommend planting cowpeas or beans in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu cowpeas loo beans yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-corn lɛ?

english: Beans and peas are legumes that draw nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to grow, so planting them together helps feed the maize naturally.
ga: Beans kɛ peas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Bɔni afee ni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Abele he miihia nitrogen babaoo dani ekwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni eyeɔ kooloi niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How does using a tractor to plow my land help my crops grow better than just clearing the bush with a cutlass?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ trakta ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe jwɛi ni mikɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ nii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Plowing turns over deep soil, loosens hard ground, and buries old grass to decay into organic matter. Soft soil lets crop roots spread deep and easily drink water and nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efuɔ jwɛi momo koni egbo ni etsɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛnuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ mlɛo.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when stressed by intense heat, uneven watering, or a lack of insect pollinators. Without fertilization or proper water balance, the plant saves energy by shedding the flower.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni naa wa waa he. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni feɔ pollinating lɛ faaa Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nu ni sa bɛ. Tsei buɔ hewalɛ he kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛjieɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plant stems turn soft and rot at ground level during continuous heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When heavy rain floods the land, standing water squeezes air out of the soil. Without oxygen, the roots suffocated and fungal diseases easily attack the wet stem bases, causing root rot.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baatutua tso lɛ shishi ni efɔ lɛ oya. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do some tomato varieties produce firm fruits that local market women prefer to buy, while others spoil quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato henɔi komɛi woɔ yibii ni mli wa ni yɔɔ loo ni maŋ lɛ mli jarayeli yei sumɔɔ ni amɛhe lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tomato komɛi fiteɔ oya lɛ.

english: Different crop varieties are bred for specific uses. Varieties with thicker skins and firmer flesh are developed for long storage and transport to distant markets, whereas softer varieties are meant for fast local consumption immediately after harvest.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi kɛha nitsumɔi pɔtɛɛ komɛi. Afee srɔtoi ni hewolo lɛ mli wa kɛ loo ni mli wa koni akɛto be kakadaŋŋ ni akɛya jarayeli hei ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni afee srɔtoi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ koni akɛye yɛ maŋ lɛ mli oya yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape and dying early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli ni amɛgboi oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize is a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency. The plant starves for food and automatically pulls nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to keep the young top leaves growing.
ga: Abele baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Hɔmɔ yeɔ tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni eha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ adara.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in full sunlight without shade crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are extremely sensitive to intense tropical heat and direct sunlight. Fast-growing shade plants like plantains act as natural shade umbrellas, protecting young cocoa leaves from drying out while keeping the root soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulutsoo be kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade. Ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe koni amɛkagbi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why is my cassava producing flowers above ground, and does that mean the underground tubers are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ miifɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Ni ani no tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ edara kwraa?

english: Flowering is simply how the cassava plant reproduces above ground, but it does not directly show if tubers are ready. Tuber size depends on the age of the crop variety and soil nutrients, not the presence of flowers.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni baa lɛ ji gbɛ kɛkɛ ni yucca tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛfɔɔ bii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi etsɔɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo loo amɛfeee klalo. Tubers lɛ dalɛ damɔ tso lɛ afii kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Jeee akɛ esa akɛ mɔ ko aná fɔfɔii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and stopping the flowers from setting fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo yibii lɛ?

english: Upward curling in pepper leaves is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids, or a viral infection they spread. These pests drain nutrients from the leaves, preventing the plant from holding onto its flowers and growing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni jɛɔ helai amli ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa Nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni miida.

english: Yam plants need their leaves elevated high to catch maximum sunlight for producing starch. Staking also keeps the leaves off the damp soil, preventing fungal diseases and leaf rot.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato tsei lɛ baai lɛ afee shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛfee starch. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa baai lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why can paddy rice survive in flooded farmland, but my maize crop dies if water stands around its roots for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa hiɔ shi yɛ okwaayeli hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ? Shi ani mi-ŋma lɛ baagbo kɛji nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe gbii babaoo?

english: Rice plants have specialized internal air passages in their stems and roots that allow them to transport oxygen underwater. Maize roots lack these air tubes, so flooded soil suffocates and rots maize roots.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ pɛ amli. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lɛ yaa nu shishi. Abɛi shishifãi bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu lɛ eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do the blossom flowers on my garden egg plants fall off during very dry, hot weather without forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni fɔ̃ɔ yɛ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ waa ni egbiɔ ni ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Excessive heat and dry weather stress the plant and dry out the pollen needed for fertilization. When temperatures are too high, the plant drops its blossoms to conserve energy and water for survival.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine kɛ shihilɛ ni mli egbi lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo fɔmɔ lɛ agbi. Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why does planting groundnut or cowpea before maize make the soil richer for the next farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei dani adu ŋmei lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmei shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas form partnerships with helpful soil bacteria that live in their roots. These bacteria take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil, creating natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni hiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ yɛ wekukpaa ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli. Muawai nɛɛ heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ lɛ amɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli. koni akɛfee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Why do my peppers change color from dark green to red or yellow as they stay longer on the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers lɛ su tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ kɛyaa etsuru loo ŋmɔŋ be mli ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: As pepper fruits reach full maturity, green chlorophyll breaks down and natural pigments turn the skin red, orange, or yellow. This color change signals that the seeds inside are fully formed and sugar levels are at their highest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ yibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ, Green chlorophyll lɛ fiteɔ ni adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, loo ŋmɔtɔ. Nɛkɛ su tsakemɔ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ebɔi feemɔ kwraa ni eshɛ sugar ni fa fe fɛɛ he.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen, a key plant food. The plant moves nitrogen from old leaves to feed new top growth, causing lower leaves to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni ji tso lɛ niyenii titri lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni ekɛha ŋmeii heei. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same plot where I planted maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension officer lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ madu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. Planting them after maize naturally restores nutrients to the soil so your next crop grows stronger without needing as much expensive chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele ni aduɔ yɛ abele ni adu sɛɛ lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ adara waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ tsofai ni jara wa atsu nii.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and yield smaller cobs when I plant three seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ mli tseee ni ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ beni midu dumɔwui etɛ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for the same limited water, food, and sunlight in the soil. Giving each seed its own space allows roots to expand and grow bigger, healthier ears.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aha dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy and feed the growing yam underground. Staking holds the leaves off the ground and spreads them out to catch maximum sunlight while protecting them from rot.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛha sweet potato ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ be mli ni ehaaa amɛfite hu.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing lots of big green leaves but not producing any flowers or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi fɔfɔii loo aduawai bɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen fertilizer causes them to put all their energy into leafy foliage instead of flowers. Tomatoes need phosphorus and potassium to encourage flower blooms and fruit development.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tsei lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ afite ehewalɛ fɛɛ yɛ baai anɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔi. Tomato he miihia phosphorus kɛ potassium koni ewo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ahe hewalɛ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my crops with dry leaves or straw during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he sũ? Aduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baai egbi loo jwɛi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli?

english: Covering the soil with organic mulch acts like a blanket that shields the ground from hot sun. It keeps water from evaporating quickly, keeps soil roots cool, and prevents unwanted weeds from growing.
ga: Organic mulch tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ akafo oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Curled, yellow-mottled cassava leaves are usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insect flies (whiteflies). The disease weakens the plant and stops root tubers from growing properly.
ga: Cassava baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe Bei pii lɛ, cassava mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. ni ŋmeii bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa (Whitefly) Hela nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa amɛshishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do small caterpillars suddenly appear inside the central leaf funnel of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii eba trukaa yɛ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms. Moths lay eggs inside the dark, protected central whorl (funnel) of the plant where hatching larvae can safely eat young tender leaves away from direct heat and rain.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ŋmeii ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ hei ni duŋ yɔɔ. Ebuɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋwɛi ŋta (cone) lɛ he, he ni ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye baai bibii lɛ shweshweeshwe lɛ. Ekɛ dɔlɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when there is too much sun, but older ones survive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la fa babaoo lɛ? Shi ani kookoo tsei ni egbɔ lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn easily and lose water quickly under full sun. They need shade crops like plantains to shelter them until their root systems grow deep enough to handle heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa oya ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains koni amɛha amɛhe nɔ aahu kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli baawo mli bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsu hulutsoo lɛ he nii.

english: Why do my pepper leaves wilt and drop down in the middle of the afternoon even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu ha amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can draw water up from the soil. The plant temporarily wilts to close leaf pores and save water, usually bouncing back once the sun cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛgbala baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ ni ekɛ nu ato he. Bei pii lɛ, efoɔ ehe kɛji hulu lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow before the crop matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ eda lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, an essential plant food found in fertilizer or animal manure, or that excess water around the roots is choking the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa ni anaa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii amli loo nu ni fa fe nine yɛ Shishifãi ni tsiɔ tso lɛ he lɛ he.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when the soil dries out quickly, or when pests attack the blossoms, preventing the plant from setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ oya loo kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tutua fɔfɔi lɛ ni haa tso lɛ wooo yibii.

english: Why do my pepper plants curl their leaves and stop growing taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miifo amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛdaraaa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking sap from under the leaves, or by a virus carried by insects that stunts the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni haa tsei lɛ daraaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans in the same farm where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ ŋmã yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Legumes like cowpeas capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, which feeds your maize naturally and improves soil fertility for the next season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: How does burning the bush before planting affect my crops?
ga: Te mi jwɛi ni mishãa dani miduɔ lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: While burning clears land quickly, the intense heat destroys beneficial living organisms in the soil and burns away natural organic matter, making crops weaker in the long run.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, la ni ashãa lɛ haa jɛmɛ tseɔ oya. Shi dɔlɛ ni naa wa gbeɔ nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ, ni eshãa adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii baa shi yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Yams need loose soil to expand; if the ground is hard, un-ploughed, or full of rocks, the growing tuber cannot push down easily and becomes bent or stunted.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse he miihia sweet potato koni egbɛ eshwa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, atsu nii, loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ Anyɛɛɛ ashɛ yitsei ni eda lɛ shi mlɛo ni amɛbaakumɔ loo amɛbaakumɔ.

english: Why do cassava roots rot inside the ground when there is heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water staying in heavy soil starves cassava roots of air, creating a damp environment where soil fungi and bacteria quickly rot the tubers.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ akafee ŋmei shishifãi lɛ. ni feɔ shihilɛ ni mli edɔ Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ baafite ŋmeii lɛ oya.

english: What makes cocoa pods turn black and dry up while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet, humid weather when water drops carry disease spores from pod to pod.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ́ nu mli nu bibii lɛ kɛ hela mli nibii bibii lɛ jɛ pod kome mli kɛtee ekroko mli lɛ,

english: Plantains have shallow roots that struggle to support heavy bunches, especially if microscopic worms in the soil have damaged the root system underneath.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi tsei niji ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fite shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do crop seeds fail to sprout even after I plant them in wet soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ po lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are buried too deep, if the seeds are old or damaged, or if insects and soil fungi attack them before they can push through the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ tsɔ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbɔ loo amɛfite loo kɛji kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutua dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsɔ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop excess flowers when they are stressed by drought, poor soil nutrients, or heavy shade, as the tree only keeps the number of pods it can successfully feed.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine kɛji hɔmɔ hao amɛ. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo eyɛ hulutsoo ni mli wa Enɛ ji akɛ, tso lɛ baakwɛ ŋmeii ayibɔ ni ebaanyɛ ekɛye omanye lɛ pɛ nɔ.

english: How long does a newly planted cocoa seedling take before it starts giving me pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties in Ghana start producing pods in about 2 to 3 years, while older traditional varieties take around 4 to 5 years to bear fruit.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfutuɔ nii yɛ Ghana lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and dry up during the dry harmattan period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni agbiɔ harmattan lɛ?

english: Dry harmattan winds strip water from the leaves faster than the roots can drink, so the cocoa tree drops leaves to protect itself and conserve moisture.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Bɔni afee ni kookoo tsei abu amɛhe ni amɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi lɛ, amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly during wet, rainy weather when water collects on pods and daylight cannot dry them out.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ. Nu buaa ehe naa yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ aha amɛgbi.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest a pod from my cocoa tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa cacao tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: A cocoa pod is ripe and ready for harvesting when its color changes completely from green to yellow, or from dark reddish-purple to bright orange.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji amɛhe su tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli nɔ kɛtee ŋmɔŋ kwraa. aloo kɛjɛ magenta ni mli kwɔ nɔ kɛyashi ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse nɔ.

english: What will happen to my cocoa tree if I do not cut off excess shoots and mistletoe branches?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mifolɔɔɔ mistletoe tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ eniji ni fa fe nine lɛ?

english: Unwanted shoots and parasitic weeds steal water and food from the main tree, causing fewer flowers to bloom and smaller pods to grow.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni ataooo kɛ jwɛi ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso wulu lɛ mli. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi fioo pɛ shwereɔ ni ŋmeii bibii hu shwereɔ.

english: What happens to my yield if I plant my cocoa trees too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Trees planted too close together fight for ground water and sunlight, leading to thin stems, fewer pods, and easy spread of fungal diseases between overlapping leaves.
ga: Tsei ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ hulu la miitswa akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛ ŋmeii helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa baai ni feɔ ekome lɛ ateŋ oya.

english: Why does my cocoa farm produce a big harvest at one time of year and a smaller one later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoe ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ afi lɛ mli be pɔtɛɛ ko mli, ni ewoɔ yibii fioo yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees follow weather cycles; the main harvest comes after the heavy rainy season, while the smaller mid-crop harvest comes after minor rains.
ga: Cacao tsei nyiɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi asɛɛ. Nikpamɔ titri lɛ baa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa sɛɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni aduɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ akpãa lɛ yaa nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ.

english: Why must I heap my harvested cocoa beans and cover them with plantain leaves before drying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibuaa kookoo yibii ni akpa lɛ anaa ni mikɛ plantain baai haa nɔ dani migbiɔ lɛ?

english: Covering beans under plantain leaves allows natural sweating and fermentation to occur, which develops the rich brown color and chocolate flavor buyers look for.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ ha plantain baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaha adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii aba. Enɛ haa efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli kɛ tsokolate ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ.

english: What care should I give to my cocoa trees right after I finish harvesting all the pods for the year?
ga: Te esa akɛ makwɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ aha tɛŋŋ beni akpa ŋmeii lɛ afi kome sɛɛ?

english: After harvest, cleaning the farm by removing diseased pods, clearing weeds, and light pruning allows the trees to rest and build strength for the next season's flowering.
ga: ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Okwaafoi lɛ amli saamɔ kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ nɔ Ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ fioo lɛ haa tso lɛ jɔɔ ehe ni enáa hewalɛ kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli fɔfɔii lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plant is starving for nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to make green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rain leaves too much standing water in the field, preventing roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha nu babaoo tsɔ ŋmɔ ko mli. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Why are my cassava roots small and hard like wood even though the plant leaves look healthy and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe wa tamɔ tso lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ?

english: If soil has too much nitrogen, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below. Harvesting during a long dry season can also cause the roots to dry out and turn hard.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ ebaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baatoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli. Nikpamɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbi ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why do I have to train my yam vines onto tall wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔse mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves toward the sun. The more direct sunlight the leaves catch, the more food the plant produces to grow big, heavy tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Babaoo ni baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, babaoo ni tso lɛ baajie niyenii babaoo koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni dara ni tsii lɛ adara.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off the plant without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the afternoon air gets too hot, dry, or when the soil goes too long without water. Without steady moisture and moderate temperatures, the flowers cannot form fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ shwane mli kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ, egbi, loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etse be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu bɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni tamɔ ekome kɛ hulutsoo be ni sa bɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii.

english: Why are my young oil palm trees growing lots of leaves but not producing any fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu lɛ yɛ baai babaoo shi ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Oil palms take about three to four years to mature before they can bear fruit. If they lack sufficient water or nutrients during these early years, the tree will prioritize growing leaves to stay alive rather than making fruit.
ga: Mu tsei aheɔ aaafee afii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ dani amɛwoɔ yibii. Kɛji nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni amɛkwɛɔ koni amɛhi wala mli lɛ nɔ babaoo fe yibii ni amɛwoɔ.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny pests like mites or aphids sucking the juice out of young leaves, or by viruses spread by those insects. Extremely hot weather can also cause leaves to curl inward to conserve water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ atsɔ mli koni ekɛbu nu he.

english: Why do extension officers tell me that planting cowpeas will improve my soil for next season's crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ, kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmeii lɛ, ebaaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli dumɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which pulls nitrogen food straight out of the air and traps it in tiny bumps on their roots. When the cowpea plant dies, that trapped nitrogen stays in the earth to fertilize the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji legume weku lɛ mlinyo, ni egbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ kui bibii amli. Kɛji cowpea tso lɛ gbo lɛ, Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: If too many shoots grow around one main plantain trunk, they steal water and nutrients from each other. Leaving only one or two strong shoots ensures the main plant gets enough food to produce big plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ, Plantain titri kome Amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo plantains agboi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant four or five maize seeds together in the exact same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ejwɛ loo enumɔ feɔ ekome yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with thin, weak stalks and tiny corn cobs instead of strong plants with full ears.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oná tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibii. Mohu ɔ, e ji tso nɛ he wa nɛ e tue hyi.

english: How do I know if a piece of land is good for planting before I clear it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha dumɔ nii dani majie nɔ?

english: Before clearing land, look at the soil color and the wild plants growing there. Dark, rich soil with healthy green weeds usually means the land is fertile and ready for crops like maize or cassava.
ga: Dani obaajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ su kɛ koo mli tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ, ni jwɛi eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɔɔ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa nii ni efee klalo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: Why is it important for me to inspect my soil a few days before I plant my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii fioo komɛi dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Checking your soil a few days ahead lets you see if it holds enough moisture and is loose enough for seeds to sprout easily, helping you avoid planting in dry or rocky soil.
ga: Kɛ́ okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii fioo komɛi kɛtsɔ hiɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona kɛji eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa. ni eyɛ mlɛo bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ mlɛo. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa dumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo tɛsaa nɔ.

english: Why do weeds come up so much faster than my planted crops after clearing the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are naturally strong and adapted to grow quickly whenever land is disturbed and exposed to sunlight. Clearing the bush gives weed seeds direct rain and sun to sprout fast.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsuɔ nii waa yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya be fɛɛ be ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baahao ni hulu la bashɛ enɔ lɛ. Jwɛi lɛ mli ni ajieɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulu la ni jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya.

english: Why should I leave some big trees standing on my farm instead of clearing everything?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi tsei wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni majie nɔ fɛɛ nɔ kɛjɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certain large trees provide shade that protects young crops like cocoa from harsh sunlight, while their deep roots hold moisture in the soil and protect the land from wind damage.
ga: Tsei wuji komɛi haa hulutsoo ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii tamɔ kookoo he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he, yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ haa sũ lɛ mli fũuɔ ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni kɔɔyɔɔ akafite lɛ.

english: How can I tell if a young cocoa seedling is healthy before I plant it on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ dani madu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: A healthy seedling should have deep green leaves without spots, a strong upright stem, and fresh roots that are not yellowing, rotting, or bound tightly in a coil.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ aná baai eŋɔli ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli. Tso lɛ damɔ shi ni eyɛ hewalɛ. kɛ shishifãi heei ni jeee ŋmɔŋ, ni egbo, loo ni ebɔle amɛhe shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes the leaves on my young cassava plants to turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni miiha baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is lacking key nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or that the ground has become waterlogged and the roots are suffocating.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: What will happen to my crops if I plant the seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting too close causes crops to fight with each other for water, sunlight, and food in the soil, resulting in tall, weak stems and very low yields.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ yɛ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ, tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi waa baa.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting after the first rains arrive?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the ground has received a few heavy rains so the soil is thoroughly soaked, ensuring seeds do not dry out if there is a short break in the rain.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni naa wa fioo dani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ egbiɛɛ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ be kukuoo ko.

english: How can I divide farm work among my household members during the planting season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ aja ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ yɛ mishiabii lɛ ateŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ amli?

english: Assign clear, simple roles to each family member—such as land clearing, row digging, seed dropping, and weeding—so that work gets done quickly without overloading anyone.
ga: Ha weku lɛ mlinyo fɛɛ weku mlinyo nitsumɔi ni mli ka shi faŋŋ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, tamɔ shikpɔŋ tsemɔ, ŋtayaai atsamɔ, loo dumɔwui afɔmɔ. kɛ jwɛi nɔkwɛmɔ Koni atsu nitsumɔ lɛ oya ni ahaaa mɔ ko mɔ ko atsu nii fe nine

english: How often should I walk through my field to check on my growing crops?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔji amli koni mayakwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ?

english: You should walk through your field at least twice a week to inspect the leaves and stems so you can spot insects or diseases early before they spread to the whole farm.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ otsɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli koni oyakwɛ baai kɛ tsei lɛ ahe. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ ona kooloi bibii loo helai mra. dani egbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to protect their delicate leaves from harsh sunlight and conserve soil moisture. Leaving some large shade trees or planting temporary crops like plantain creates a cooler climate that allows young cocoa to establish strong roots.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo be fioo ko koni ebu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni ashiɔ loo aduɔ be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains lɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ baa ni eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo bibii lɛ ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize turning yellow from the tips down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛshishigbɛ kɛmiiba shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is an essential nutrient for leaf growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure early in the growing season can help restore healthy green leaves.
