ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli yɛ baa lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava tubers rot underground mainly when the soil holds too much water due to poor drainage or waterlogging during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi titri lɛ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat or water stress during flowering. Regular watering at the base of the plant and covering the soil with dry grass helps keep root temperatures stable so fruit can set properly.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu he haomɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ daa kɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ mli dɔlɛ yaa nɔ daa koni eha aduawai lɛ ama shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it good to plant cowpeas or beans together in the same field with my maize?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ ooodu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas or beans alongside maize is beneficial because leguminous plants naturally capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps the maize grow better without exhausting the land.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa he lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteee.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make energy for growing large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off damp ground into the sunlight, which prevents leaves from rotting and increases harvest size.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni ekɛfee hewalɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ewó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli. Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the sap from the leaves and spreading viruses. Controlling these insects early with neem oil spray helps keep the leaves expanding normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ eshwaa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why does clearing weeds while my crops are still small matter so much?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji sane bibioo ko akɛ majie jwɛi lɛ yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops have small roots that easily lose the battle for water, light, and soil nutrients against fast-growing weeds. Weeding early ensures your crops get all the food they need to build a strong foundation.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii. ni nyɛŋ awuu ashi jwɛi ni daa oya ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli mlɛo Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ana niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkɛma shishitoo ni wa.

english: Leaving too many shoots around a single plantain tree forces all of them to compete for water and food, resulting in smaller bunches. Pruning down to one main stem and one strong replacement sucker yields larger, healthier fruit bunches.
ga: Shimɔ ŋmeii ni ebɔle Dumɔwu kome he lɛ fa tsɔ. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ abɔi nu kɛ niyenii he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei niji lɛ feɔ bibii. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli koni ashi tso lɛ yitso titri kome kɛ sucker kome ni he wa ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ lɛ, ebaaha aduawai akuu ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Why shouldn't I pour chemical fertilizer on dry soil when there has been no rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ afɔseɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve so crop roots can absorb it safely. Applying fertilizer on dry soil can burn plant roots and waste nutrients into the air before the rain comes.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe miihia ni nu atsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ shweshweeshwe. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ awo kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani nugbɔ aba.

english: The very first rain is often followed by a hot dry spell that can scorch young seedlings. It is safer to wait until the rains become steady so your seeds get consistent moisture to sprout and grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni naa wa ni baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui bibii lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ daa koni eha dumɔwui lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdara.

english: Use the hard, mature middle section of a healthy cassava stem. Cut pieces about 20 to 30 centimeters long with at least 4 to 6 nodes or buds, as these sprout strongest.
ga: Kɛ ŋmei tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ teŋgbɛ ni wa, ni eda lɛ atsu nii. Kpɔ̃ɔ mli bibii ni kɛlɛ ji aaafee sɛntimita 20 kɛyashi 30 ni kɛ hoo lɛ, nodes loo ŋmeii 4 kɛyashi 6 yɔɔ mli, ejaakɛ enɛɛmɛi ji nɔ ni wa fe fɛɛ.

english: Early morning is best because plants can absorb the moisture before the sun gets too hot. Evening watering leaves foliage wet overnight, which encourages fungal diseases to grow.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ tsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu lɛ adɔ tsɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli gbɛkɛ lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ nyɔɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ. ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa

english: Why do my cocoa tree leaves turn yellow and fall off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop leaves during severe heat to reduce water loss. Providing shade trees like plantains and mulching around the roots retains soil moisture and stops severe leaf shedding.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Tsei tamɔ plantains ni akɛwoɔ hulutsoo mli kɛ mulching ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni ebaakpa baai ni fiteɔ waa lɛ.

english: I see small holes in my maize leaves and tiny caterpillars inside the leaves. What is happening to my crop?
ga: Mi naa bu bibioo ko Yɛ ŋmãa baa lɛ nɔ ni ŋmeii bibii yɛ jɛmɛ. yɛ baa lɛ mli Mɛni ba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. They feed on young maize leaves and central shoots, so spraying early with approved insecticides or applying neem extract helps protect your harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm lɛ. Amɛyeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, atsɔɔ akɛ afɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ mra. Aloo kɛ okɛ neem mli nu tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by uneven soil moisture and calcium deficiency. Keeping water levels steady and adding compost or wood ash to the soil prevents this rot.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ejaaa kɛ calcium ni faaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Nu lɛ ni aaakwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tso sũ ni akɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni akafite nɛkɛ sũ nɛɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over before the bunches are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miigbee shi dani ŋmeii lɛ dara kwraa lɛ?

english: Heavy plantain bunches easily tip trees over in strong winds or when stem borers weaken the roots. Using strong wooden props to support heavy stalks keeps the plant standing until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni tsii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli loo kɛ́ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa tsu nii koni akɛfi tsei ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdamɔɔ shi kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to put tall sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsei kakadaji ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam plants need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves high above weeds and exposed to the sun.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ jwɛi lɛ anɔ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ.

english: Can I plant beans together with my maize on the same farm plot?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting beans alongside maize is very beneficial. Beans absorb nitrogen from the air and feed the soil, which helps your maize grow stronger while naturally blocking weeds.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ahe lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Beans shwieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa o-corn lɛ ni edaraa waa yɛ be mli ni etsĩɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Signs of weak soil include crops with pale or yellowing leaves, stunted growth, and lower yields compared to previous years. Adding organic manure or crop residues restores lost nutrients.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ lɛ he ji tsei ni baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔŋ. shweremɔ ni egbɔjɔ kɛ nibii ni afee lɛ ba shi kɛ akɛto afi ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni elaaje lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: How do I know if my land is suitable for growing mango trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha mango ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Mangoes need deep soil where water drains away easily after heavy rain. If your land stays flooded or soggy for days, the roots will rot, but if the water drains well and the soil is deep enough for roots to push down, your land is suitable.
ga: Mango he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ. Kɛji nu eyi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo edɔ gbii babaoo lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baagboi, shi kɛji nu lɛ ho jogbaŋŋ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni baaha shishifãi lɛ ashɛ shi pɛ. Oshikpɔŋ lɛ sa.

english: Can I plant a mango farm on rocky or stony ground?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu mango abɔɔ yɛ tɛsaa loo tɛsaa shikpɔŋ nɔ?

english: It is best to avoid very rocky ground because mango trees develop long, strong taproots that must go deep into the earth to anchor the tree and find water. Hard rocks block root growth and cause weak trees that can easily fall during strong winds.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi ohe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ waa lɛ he ejaakɛ mango tsei yɛ shishifãi kakadaji ni mli wa ni esa akɛ amɛfo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛha tso lɛ ama shi ni amɛna nu. Tɛi ni wa tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ adalɛ naa ni ehaa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbee shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: How far apart should I space my mango trees when planting them?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashi gbɛ ko yɛ mango tsei lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ?

english: You should plant mango trees at least 10 meters apart from each other. Mango trees grow very large spread-out branches, so good spacing ensures they do not block sunshine from each other or fight for soil nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ adu mango tsei kɛ hoo lɛ mitai 10 kɛjɛ amɛhe. Mango tsei yɛ niji wuji waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaaa amɛtsi hulu la naa kɛjɛ amɛhe loo amɛkaye akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How big should I dig the hole before placing my new mango seedling in the soil?
ga: Te esa akɛ atsa bu lɛ dalɛ aha tɛŋŋ dani akɛ mango dumɔwui heei awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Dig a hole about 2 feet wide and 2 feet deep. Digging a big hole loosens the hard soil around the seedling and allows you to mix in rich topsoil or manure, giving the young roots a smooth start to spread out.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ bu ko ni kɛlɛ ji aaafee ninetalɔi enyɔ ni elɛɛmɔ ji ninetalɔi enyɔ. Bu agbo ni atsa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli awa. Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi Ni ehaa okɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi bibii lɛ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it better to plant grafted mango seedlings or plant the seeds directly from the fruit?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooodu mango dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ loo ooodu dumɔwui kɛjɛ aduawai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Grafted seedlings are much better because they produce sweet, high-quality fruit in just 3 to 4 years. Planting directly from seeds takes over 7 years to bear fruit, and the fruit may not taste as good as the original fruit you ate.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛwoɔ yibii ni ŋɔɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni adu tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baahe nɔ ni fe afii 7 dani ewo yibii. Ni ekolɛ aduawai lɛ ŋɔɔŋ tamɔ shishijee aduawai ni oyeɔ lɛ.

english: Do young mango trees need full sunshine or shade to grow properly?
ga: Ani hulu loo hulutsoo be babaoo he miihia mango tso bibioo ko koni enyɛ eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: Mango trees need full, open sunshine throughout the day. Unlike crops like cocoa that need shade when young, mangoes thrive in direct sunlight, which helps them build strong stems and produce plenty of flowers later on.
ga: Mango tsei lɛ he miihia hulu ni fa yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli. Mango tamɔɔɔ tsei tamɔ kookoo ni biɔ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛdara lɛ. Mango daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ ahe wa ni ehaa fɔfɔii babaoo baa sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my young mango seedlings turn yellow and die when water collects around them after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egboɔ kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Mango roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When standing water collects around the stem without draining away, it suffocates the roots and causes root rot, which makes the leaves turn yellow and eventually kills the plant.
ga: Mango shishifãi hia kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ bua ehe naa yɛ tso lɛ he ni efooo Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni eha amɛgboi. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ gbo.

english: Can I plant crops like maize or beans between my young mango trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ mi mango tsei lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, you can plant short crops like maize, groundnuts, or beans between young mango trees during their first two years. This helps you get food while the mangoes grow, as long as the temporary crops do not shade or overcrowd the young mango trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii kukuji tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ mango tsei bibii ateŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua bo ni oná niyenii yɛ be mli ni mango lɛ miida lɛ. Shii abɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ haaa mango tsei lɛ afee duŋ loo eyimɔ obɔbɔ lɛ,.

english: How many years will I have to wait before my mango trees start bearing fruit?
ga: Afii enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani mango tso awo yibii?

english: If you plant well-cared-for grafted mango seedlings, they will start producing their first fruits in about 3 to 4 years. By the fifth or sixth year, the harvest will become much bigger.
ga: Kɛji odu mango dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Mango dumɔwui lɛ baabɔi amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii lɛ womɔ yɛ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli. Beni shɛɔ afi ni ji enumɔ loo ekpaa lɛ, Nikpamɔ lɛ baafee babaoo kwraa.

english: Why should I trim or prune the branches of my young mango trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ loo mafolɔ mi mango bibii lɛ?

english: Trimming off weak or low-hanging branches allows sunlight and air to move freely through the tree canopy. This keeps fungal diseases away, helps the tree grow a sturdy trunk, and results in cleaner, larger fruits.
ga: Niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ni aaafolɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa tsei ni wa. ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yibii ni dara ni he tse.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees need tall shade trees growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa tsei kakadaji ni haa hulutsoo baa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees easily get stressed and burnt under direct heat from the sun. Tall shade trees act as natural umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and moist while protecting the tender cocoa leaves from scorching heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ haoɔ amɛhe ni amɛshãa oya kɛ́ hulu lɛ mli dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ kookoo baai ni mli tse lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes through my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu kɛmiitsɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the center whorl of the maize plant during the day and feed on the leaves at night. Catching them early with organic sprays or recommended crop protection products prevents them from destroying your harvest.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋtayaai amli yɛ gbi mli, ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ gbɛkɛ. Amɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ organic spray loo tsofa ni abuɔ tsei ahe ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ nɔ lɛ obaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava turn yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that water is trapped around the roots causing root rot. Rain provides water, but plants still need balanced nutrients in the soil to stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo nu ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haa amɛgboiɔ. Nugbɔ haa nu, shi tsei hu hia niyenii ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience high heat stress, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. When the plant gets too hot or stressed, it conserves energy by shedding blossoms instead of setting fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe hulutsoo ni naa wa waa he. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo Beni tsei lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo amɛhaoɔ Tsei lɛ buɔ hewalɛ he kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow very tall and thin with few peppers when planted close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni pepper fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ, kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they compete aggressively for sunlight, air, and nutrients. Instead of spreading wide to produce flowers and fruit, the plants stretch upward to reach light, resulting in weak stems and low yield.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Mohu ɔ, e gbɛɔ kɛ woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yiblii mohu. Mohu ɔ, tsei ɔmɛ pee jã konɛ la ɔ nɛ ba mi. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: Yam rot in the soil is caused by microscopic pests called nematodes or fungal infection from waterlogged ground. Using healthy seed yams and planting in well-drained soil prevents moisture from trapping rot organisms around the tubers.
ga: Nibii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato sũ ni fiteɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ sweet potato dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ tsu nii ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekamɔ nibii ni fiteɔ ni bɔleɔ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: Saving seeds from hybrid crops usually results in lower yields and uneven plant sizes the next season. Hybrid seeds are specifically bred for one generation of high production, so buying fresh certified seeds each season guarantees the best crop performance.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ adalɛ hu feɔ ekome yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɔtɛɛ kɛha yinɔ kome ni woɔ yibii babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui heei ni awo he hewalɛ ni aheɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my plantain trees curl up and turn brown during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have large leaves that lose water rapidly in dry heat. Leaf curling is the plant's natural survival mechanism to reduce leaf area exposed to the sun, but prolonged drought without mulching or watering causes the edges to dry out and brown.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai agboi ni nu fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni mli egbi mli. Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛhaa baa lɛ he ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Shi hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii loo nu bɛ mli lɛ baaha baai lɛ ashishigbɛ agbi ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why is it beneficial to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the field where I harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔji ni mikpaa ŋmeii yɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the soil. Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas fix natural nitrogen back into the soil through their roots, restoring soil fertility naturally for the next planting season.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei tsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛhaa nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does spear grass keep coming back so quickly even after I cut it down completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akpɔlɔ jwɛi lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa oya nɛkɛ beni mifo fɛɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Spear grass has deep underground stems called rhizomes that store energy and survive cutting or burning. To get rid of it permanently, you must dig up the underground roots or use systemic weedkillers that travel down to destroy the roots.
ga: Spear jwɛi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ ni atsɛɔ amɛ rhizomes ni kɛ hewalɛ toɔ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛji afo loo ashã amɛ. Bɔni afee ni ojie lɛ kɛya naanɔ Esa akɛ Otsa shishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi loo okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ gbɛjianɔtoo mli ni baafã gbɛ kɛba shi ni efite shishifãi lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and burning when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under direct heat. They need shade crops like plantains to act as natural umbrellas, protecting them from full sunlight until they are mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni shãa oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains koni amɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Buu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he kɛyashi amɛbaadara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava crop drop almost all of its leaves during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fiteɔ yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava sheds leaves in the dry season to protect itself from losing water. The plant is not dead; it goes dormant to save energy while storing water and starch inside the tubers underground.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni nu akafite. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Ehiɔ shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato be mli ni ekɛ nu kɛ starch toɔ tuber lɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the heat is too severe or when watering is irregular. Extreme temperatures or water stress cause the plant to drop blossoms to save its own strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ amɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa mli loo kɛ́ awo amɛ nu be fɛɛ be. Dɔlɛ ni mli wa loo nu mli haomɔ haa tsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ hiɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhewalɛ mli.

english: Groundnuts flower above ground, but after pollination, the plant grows pegs that push into the dirt. The groundnut pods actually form and mature under the dark, moist soil.
ga: Peanuts fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi yɛ pollination sɛɛ lɛ Tso lɛ daa kɛjɛɔ ŋtayaa ko ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Bean pods lɛ feɔ ni amɛdaraa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni edɔ shishi.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow starting from the tips along the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Yellowing along the main vein of maize leaves is a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the maize regain its deep green color and produce good cobs.
ga: Yellowing ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai wuji lɛ ahe lɛ ji okadi ni ale jogbaŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai aba.

english: Why does my farm produce smaller maize cobs when I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa bibii beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific soil nutrients and allows pests to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil and restores fertility.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Ekɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I cover my dry soil with cut grass and dry leaves instead of leaving the dirt completely clear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni afolɔ kɛ baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi muji lɛ he tse kwraa lɛ.

english: Covering the soil with organic matter, called mulching, keeps the ground cool, traps moisture so you water less, and slowly breaks down into rich food for your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli woɔ mli lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Eŋmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu fioo pɛ awo mli ni egbala mli fiofio ni efee niyenii ni jara wa kɛha onibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into tight, wrinkled shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites, or a virus spread by them. Spraying early with neem oil or safe bio-insecticides protects new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ Ni akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ baashwie nɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ebaatsi baai heei adalɛ naa.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to capture maximum sunlight for their leaves. Sunlight allows the leaves to make food, which travels down to swell the underground yam tubers into large sizes.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ kɛyashɛɔ agbo.

english: Why do some of my new plantain shoots grow very weak while others grow into strong, heavy-yielding trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui heei lɛ ekomɛi bɛ hewalɛ waa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi daraa ni amɛfeɔ tsei ni he wa ni woɔ yibii ni tsii lɛ?

english: Broad-leafed shoots called sword suckers carry more energy from the mother plant and build strong roots quickly, whereas thin, water-suckers lack reserves and produce weak stems with small bunches.
ga: Baai ni mli kwɔlɔ, ni atsɛɔ amɛ sword shoots lɛ, heɔ hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli ni amɛtswaa shishifãi ni wa oya. be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ nu fioo Ebaafee nɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni ebaafee ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why are some of the seeds I planted sprouting quickly while others in the same field haven't grown after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ekomɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔɔ lolo yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds do not always sprout at the exact same time. Differences in seed depth, soil moisture, and the natural characteristics of individual seeds mean some will sprout early while others need a few extra weeks to grow.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ be kome mli. Dumɔwui lɛ amlibotemɔ mli srɔtofeemɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko adebɔɔ mli sui Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui komɛi baakwɛ̃ oya. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui komɛi he hiaa otsii fioo komɛi ni fata he koni amɛdara.

english: Is it normal for some seeds to stay in the soil for up to four weeks before showing any growth above the ground?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni ja akɛ dumɔwui komɛi baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi otsii ejwɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, for certain crop varieties, taking three to four weeks to break through the soil is completely normal because their natural characteristics slow down initial sprouting.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ tsei komɛi ahe lɛ Otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ ni akɛfoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kwraa. Yɛ bɔ ni amɛji lɛ hewɔ lɛ, amɛbaaha shishijee shweremɔ lɛ asɛɛ afo.

english: If my crops sprout later than my neighbor's crops planted on the same day, does it mean my farm has a problem?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ midumɔ nii lɛ kwɛ̃ sɛɛ fe mikutsoŋnyo lɛ dumɔ nii ni adu yɛ nakai gbi lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ hu? Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ naagba?

english: Not necessarily. If you planted a different seed variety, your crops may simply have a naturally longer germination time due to their internal traits, even if planted under the same conditions on the same day.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Kɛji odu dumɔwui srɔtoi Onibii lɛ baanyɛ ahe be babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa dani amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ amɛmli sui lɛ ahewɔ. Kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ yɛ shihilɛ kome mli yɛ gbi kome nɔ po.

english: What does it mean when agriculture officers talk about a crop's 'variety'?
ga: Kɛ okwaayeli he onukpai wieɔ Mɛni ji ŋmɔshi nibii ‘srɔtofeemɔ’ tsɔɔ?

english: A crop variety is a specific subgroup of a plant type that shares special inherited traits, such as how quickly it sprouts, how long it takes to yield, or how well it handles dry weather.
ga: Tso henɔ ji tsei akuu pɔtɛɛ ko ni yɔɔ gboshinii sui, tamɔ bɔ ni amɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya. Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ baa? loo bɔ ni amɛtsuɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi lɛ ahe nii jogbaŋŋ amɛhaa lɛ

english: Does the specific variety of seed I buy affect how long it takes to sprout out of the ground?
ga: Ani dumɔwui srɔtoi ni miheɔ lɛ baaná be ni amɛheɔ dani amɛjeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, every seed variety has its own natural growth speed built into its genetics. Some varieties are bred to sprout very quickly, while others naturally take much longer.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, dumɔwui srɔtoi fɛɛ yɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa oya amɛhaa. Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi komɛi koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya waa. Yɛ be mli ni adebɔɔ mli henɔi komɛi heɔ be babaoo lɛ.

english: Why do two seeds of the same crop that look identical end up sprouting at completely different times?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui enyɔ ni tamɔ amɛhe kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ bei sɔrɔtoi amli kwraa lɛ?

english: Even if seeds look the same on the outside, they may belong to different varieties with different genetic characters that dictate how fast the seed absorbs water and starts growing.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe yɛ ekome moŋ, shi ekolɛ amɛji kooloi srɔtoi hu, ni amɛyɛ fɔmɔ sui srɔtoi ni tsɔɔ bɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: What causes one crop type to naturally take longer to germinate than another?
ga: Mɛni haa tso kome heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe ekroko?

english: This difference comes down to genetic characters. Nature gives each plant variety its own internal clock that determines how many days or weeks its seeds must spend in the soil before opening.
ga: Srɔtofeemɔ nɛɛ damɔ fɔmɔ sui anɔ. Adebɔɔ eha tso fɛɛ tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ emli ŋmɛlɛtswaa ni ekɛtsɔɔ gbii loo otsii enyiɛ esa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛgbele.

english: How long should I wait before deciding that a planted seed has failed to sprout and needs replanting?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani makpɛ miyiŋ akɛ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ekwɛɛɛ ni ehe miihia ni adu ekoŋŋ?

english: Before digging up your field, check the expected germination duration for that specific variety. Some varieties naturally take four weeks or more to sprout, so waiting for their natural timeframe avoids wasting seeds.
ga: Dani obaatsa shikpɔŋ lɛ Kwɛmɔ be ni akpaa gbɛ akɛ nakai tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ lɛ. Henɔi komɛi heɔ aaafee otsii ejwɛ loo nɔ ni fe nakai dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. No hewɔ lɛ, adebɔɔ mli be lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaye abua ni dumɔwui lɛ akafite.

english: What key information should I ask about a seed variety before I buy and plant it on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ saji ni he hiaa esa akɛ mabi yɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ko he dani mahe ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You should always ask about the variety's germination time and growth nature so you know in advance whether it sprouts early or takes several weeks to emerge from the soil.
ga: Esa akɛ obi nɛkɛ tso nɛɛ kwɛ̃mɔ be kɛ bɔ ni edaraa ehaa lɛ he sane be fɛɛ be. Enɛ ji koni ale kɛtsɔ hiɛ kɛji tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya loo ebaahe otsii babaoo dani eje kpo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I make sure that all the crops on my field sprout fast and around the same time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ be kome too mli?

english: To get uniform sprouting, purchase certified seeds of a single known variety with fast germination traits, and ensure all seeds are planted at an even depth in moist soil.
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ ni okwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ Hemɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni ji nɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ oyaiyeli sui lɛ. Ni kwɛmɔ akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ yɛ he kome.

english: Why did the leaves on my crops turn brown and dry after I sprayed them with crop medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mikɛ tsei ahe hela efɔ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: When crop medicine or pesticide is mixed too strong or used incorrectly, it acts like a poison that burns the plant leaves. Always follow the correct water-to-chemical ratio so the mixture protects your crop instead of damaging its green leaves.
ga: Kɛji akɛ aafutu tsei ahe tsofai loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mli wa tsɔ loo akɛtsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsofa ni shãa tso lɛ baai lɛ. Nyiɛmɔ nu kɛ tsofa ni sa lɛ sɛɛ be fɛɛ be. koni nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ aye abua ni ebu onibii ahe moŋ fe ni eeefite baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ.

english: Can I mix two different types of farm chemicals together in the same knapsack sprayer to save time?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai srɔtoi enyɔ afutu tsɔne kome ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli koni mikɛ be akafite?

english: Mixing different farm chemicals without expert guidance can create a strong reaction that destroys their effectiveness or turns the combination toxic to your crops. It is safest to apply chemicals separately unless the product label explicitly states they can be mixed.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ ŋmɔji srɔtoi amli Kɛji ŋaalɔi akudɔɔɔ amɛ lɛ ebaanyɛ ekɛ nibii ni naa wa aba ni baafite tsofai lɛ anitsumɔ loo eha tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ nii nɛɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ akɛ akɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ srɔtoi baatsu nii. Ja nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ abaanyɛ akɛfutu amɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow strong. When nitrogen is low, the plant moves the remaining nutrients to its newest upper leaves, causing the older lower leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my field help my next maize crop grow better?
ga: Te ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni mikɛduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special root nodules that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the legume crop is harvested, that trapped nitrogen stays in the earth, acting as natural fertilizer for your next maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural defense mechanism against extreme heat and drought. By rolling its leaves inward, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun, helping it conserve water inside its stems.
ga: Baai ni etsilɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ he. Tsei haa he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai ni amɛfoɔ mli kɛyaa mli lɛ nɔ. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ tso lɛ mli

english: Why do my cocoa trees shed so many of their flowers without forming any cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miifɔlɔ babaoo ni amɛjieee cocoa ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they experience stress from lack of water, shade, or proper soil nutrients. Protecting young trees from harsh direct sunlight and ensuring adequate moisture helps the flowers remain attached long enough to form pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ amɛna haomɔ ni jɛɔ nu, hulutsoo, loo niyenii ni sa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli baa. Kɛ́ abu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ he, ni aha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy and breathe. When heavy rainfall causes water to puddle and stay in the ground, the roots suffocate and drown, leading to fungal rot underground.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia cassava shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu kpɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaagboi yɛ nu mli. Ehaa ŋmeii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin but produce small harvests if I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete aggressively for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Instead of using energy to grow big fruit or tubers, the plants stretch upward rapidly just to reach the sunlight.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni naa wa Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛdu aduawai loo bulbs lɛ Tsei lɛ baatsɔ oya koni amɛmɔ hulu la lɛ kɛkɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear away all the big shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni mijie cacao tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily under intense, direct sunlight. Leaving large trees or planting plantains nearby creates a shaded umbrella that keeps the air humid and protects the young plants while they develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei wuji ni ajieɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Enɛ haa hulutsoo ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why should I pinch off the extra small shoots growing on my tomato stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ajie nɔ ni yaa hiɛ babaoo yɛ mi tomato tso lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Extra side shoots, often called suckers, take away valuable water and soil food from the main fruit-bearing branches. Removing these extra shoots directs the plant's food supply toward growing larger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Ekstra lateral shoots, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ suckers lɛ, gbalaa nu ni jara wa kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei niji titri ni woɔ yibii lɛ ahe. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine nɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ niyenii lɛ yaa tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are getting sick before the whole farm gets infected?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cacao tsei lɛ hela mɔ amɛ dani ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli hela lɛ emɔ amɛ?

english: Look out for early warning signs like yellowing leaves, dark brown spots on young pods, unusual swelling on branches, or white powdery growth. Catching these signs early allows you to prune off infected parts before the sickness spreads to neighboring trees.
ga: Taomɔ kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii mra, tamɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ anɔ. niji ni efuu yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo edalɛ ni etsɔ powda yɛŋ Okadii nɛɛ ni ooomɔ mli mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ofoɔ hei ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ dani hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in damp, wet conditions. Pruning overgrown branches to allow sunlight and airflow into your farm helps keep the trees dry and prevents the fungus from destroying your harvest.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni oookpa koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ agbi ni ebaaha ŋmeii akafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: What is causing the branches on my cocoa trees to swell up and the leaves to turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni haa niji ni yɔɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ?

english: This is a sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, which is spread by tiny insects called mealybugs. Once a tree gets this virus, it cannot be cured with chemical sprays, so the infected tree must be cut down to protect the healthy ones around it.
ga: Enɛ ji Cocoa Swollen Shoot Hela lɛ he okadi, ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Beni tso lɛ ená nɛkɛ hela nɛɛ Anyɛɛɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ atsa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ afolɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ koni akɛbu tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ahe.

english: Why are there dark, dry patches appearing on my young cocoa pods and shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ ni egbi jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii kɛ mi-kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: These patches are usually caused by mirids (capsids), which are tiny sap-sucking insects that bite young pods and shoots. Spraying recommended insecticides during their peak season in August and September helps control them and saves your yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mirids (capsids), ni ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baa. ni shwieɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni akɛwoɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni mɛi fa babaoo yɛ August kɛ September mli lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to trim off extra branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ kookoo tso ni eda lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or non-producing branches so the tree can send all its energy and nutrients directly into growing healthy pods. It also opens up the tree canopy to let in light, which reduces disease risk.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwieɔ shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni edaaa lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ. Egbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi hu koni la abote mli, ni no haa helai baa shi.

english: Is it better for my cocoa trees to grow under shade trees or in full sunlight?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mi-cocoa tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need heavy shade from plants like plantains so they do not dry out. Mature cocoa trees produce best under light shade, which protects them from harsh heat while giving them enough sunlight to make plenty of pods.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei tamɔ plantains adɛŋ koni amɛkagbi. Kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ woɔ yibii fe fɛɛ yɛ hulutsoo shishi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ cacao tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha efee ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why are weeds under my cocoa trees dangerous to my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei ashishi lɛ ji oshara kɛha mikpamɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital water, fertilizer, and soil nutrients away from your cocoa roots. They also create a damp hiding place for pests and diseases that can jump onto your crops.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ okkoo shishifãi lɛ amli. Amɛfeɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ hu kɛhaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baanyɛ atsɔ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ.

english: Can I plant plantains on the same land with my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu plantains yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni miduɔ mi-kokoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ?

english: Yes, planting plantains with young cocoa is very beneficial. The plantains grow quickly and provide essential shade to protect the delicate young cocoa plants from burning in the sun, while providing you with food and income early on.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛ kookoo bibii duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni akɛbu kookoo tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika mra.

english: How do I know if my farm soil needs fertilizer to help my crops grow better?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: If your cocoa leaves look pale green or yellowish instead of deep green, or if mature trees stop producing many pods despite getting good rain, your soil lacks essential nutrients and needs cocoa-specific fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cocoa baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Aloo kɛji tsei ni eda lɛ kpa ŋmeii babaoo ni amɛwoɔ lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ko awo kookoo mli.

english: Leaving ripe pods on the tree causes the beans inside to sprout or rot, destroying their quality. It also attracts pests and diseases that can easily spread from overripe pods to healthy green ones on the tree.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akwɛ̃ loo amɛgboi. ni fiteɔ su kpakpa lɛ Egbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ amli kɛya ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ hu.

english: Sir, why should I plant cassava or plantain on the same land where I am planting my young cocoa trees?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo plantain yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmei tsei bibii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing crops like cassava and plantain provide vital living shade to protect the cocoa, while also giving you food and cash flow while waiting for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ cassava kɛ plantain haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni buɔ kookoo he. Be nɛɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ, ekɛ niyenii kɛ shika haa bo yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans help make my soil better for my next crop of maize?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots decay, they leave this nitrogen in the ground as natural fertilizer for your next maize crop.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tso shishifãi fite Amɛshiɔ nitrogen nɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my young maize plants turn yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually means your soil is low in nitrogen. The plant moves whatever little nitrogen it has to its newer top leaves to survive, leaving the bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen fioo ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi. Kɛtsɔ shishigbɛ baai lɛ ni oooŋmɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it bad to plant groundnuts in the exact same spot on my farm every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ he kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting groundnuts in the same place every season depletes specific soil nutrients and allows soil-borne pests and diseases that target groundnuts to multiply and ruin future yields.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ he kome daa be lɛ, ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. ni eye ebua tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni tsɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ ni amɛshwere ni amɛfite wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Tomato flowers fall off due to stress, usually caused by extremely hot weather, irregular watering, or a lack of essential nutrients like phosphorus in the soil.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔnyɛɛ hewɔ. Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nu ni afɔɔɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the tree during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cool, overly shaded, and wet conditions. Clearing weeds and trimming shade trees helps air circulate and prevents it.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ lɛ Shade babaoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo nɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ yaa hiɛ ni ebuɔ mɔ he.

english: Why do my yams grow much bigger when I plant them in high mounds instead of flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ daraa babaoo waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: High soil mounds create loose, warm earth that allows yam tubers to expand easily without fighting hard soil, while also protecting the roots from sitting in stagnant water that causes rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni kwɔ lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni mli edɔɔ ni haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa akawu. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe koni amɛkatara nu ni ekã shi ni haa amɛgboɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do I get smaller maize ears when I plant three or four seeds in one single hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmãa toi bibii anɔ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa ŋmãa etɛ loo ejwɛ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight against each other for soil food, water, and light, leaving all of them weak and producing small cobs.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ la mli lɛ, ni no haa dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui bibii.

english: Why should I cut off the side branches and suckers from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ aniji kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ?

english: Pruning extra branches prevents the plant from wasting energy on foliage, directing water and nutrients into growing larger and healthier fruits instead.
ga: Kpojiemɔ kroko ni akɛfataa he lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ nu kɛ níhi nɛ haa nɔ he wami tsuɔ ní kɛ woɔ yiblii nguahi nɛ a ngɛ he wami.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster in open fields compared to under a mature cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli tse mli kɛ akɛto kookoo ŋmɔji ni eda lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Weeds require direct sunlight to sprout and grow. A dense canopy of mature trees blocks light from reaching the ground, naturally suppressing weed growth.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdara. Tsei wuji ni etse amɛhe banee lɛ tsiɔ la gbɛ koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ. ni tsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ

english: If crops are thirsty, their leaves will droop, turn yellow, or curl inward during the sunniest part of the day, showing that the soil moisture is dangerously low.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kumai miiye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Baai lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔŋ loo amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ faaa yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ oshara nɔ.

english: Is it better to water my crop field early in the morning or in the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafɔ miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning gives plants time to absorb moisture before the sun heats up, preventing water from evaporating into the air before the roots can reach it.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu leebi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ náa be ni ekɛnuɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu lɛ haa edɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haaa nu lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why do my young plantain leaves dry up when exposed to heavy sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ ahe baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Young plantain leaves have a large surface area that loses water quickly under direct heat, so they need steady soil moisture or temporary shade to stay green and healthy.
ga: Plantain baai bibii lɛ yɛ he ko ni da ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛbiɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa loo hulutsoo be kukuoo ko koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do extra suckers sprout around my plantain plant, and should I leave them all to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii krokomɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? mi plantain Ni ani esa akɛ maha amɛ fɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Plantains naturally grow suckers to reproduce, but leaving too many attached causes them to steal food from each other, resulting in much smaller fruit bunches.
ga: Plantains lɛ kwɛɔ ŋmeii koni amɛfɔ bii yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Shi kɛ́ amɛshi babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛjɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa aduawai bibii babaoo baa.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow before the fruit bunch is fully mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani aduawai akui lɛ dara kwraa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves during fruit development usually mean the plant lacks water or key soil nutrients like nitrogen, forcing it to sacrifice older leaves to feed the growing bunch.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, ni no nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ shaa afɔle koni ekɛha tso lɛ kuu ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my land yield fewer crops now than it did when I first started farming it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo fe be mli ni mibɔi okwaayeli lɛ?

english: Harvesting crops continuously without replacing nutrients drains the natural fertility of the soil over time, requiring crop rotation, compost, or fertilizers to restore crop yields.
ga: Nibii ni akpaa daa ni akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ tsakeee lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ biɔ ni atsake ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away topsoil on my farm, and how does that harm my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Ni te no saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy rain strips away topsoil because it holds most of the organic food plants need, leaving behind hard earth where roots struggle to grow and absorb nutrients.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ laajeɔ. Ejaakɛ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli tsei babaoo biɔ Enɛ shĩɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛdara ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Planting too close makes crops fight each other for sunlight, air, and underground food, causing stems to grow tall and thin with very low yield.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni yibiiwoo ni baa shi waa.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally hardier and rapidly absorb water and nutrients from the soil, stealing the vital food your planted crops need to produce food.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ ni ejieɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Kɛtsɔ niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii ahe hiaa koni amɛná niyenii lɛ ni amɛjuɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crop stems bend and snap easily when a strong wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkuɔ oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Weak stems occur when crops do not get enough balanced nutrients or sunlight, preventing the stalks from developing strong, thick walls to support the plant.
ga: Tsoi ni bɛ hewalɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ niyenii loo hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Etsiɔ tso lɛ shishi koni ekafee gbogboi ni mli wa ni baaye abua tso lɛ.

english: Why should I plant my pepper and tomatoes in low-lying land instead of on higher ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tomato yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ moŋ fe hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Low-lying land naturally holds water and moisture longer, giving vegetables like pepper and tomatoes the steady water supply they need to grow strong and produce good fruit.
ga: Hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ haa nu kɛ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa aduawai tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tomato nu ni he hiaa amɛ daa koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Where on my farm land is the best place to start planting at the beginning of the rainy season?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji miŋmɔ lɛ he ni hi fe fɛɛ ni manyɛ maje nugbɔshiimɔ be mli dumɔ shishi yɛ?

english: Starting in the lower areas of your farm is best because rainwater collects there first, giving your young crops immediate moisture to sprout even before the heavy rains fully establish.
ga: Kɛ́ oje shishi kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ shishi lɛ, no hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ buaa ehe naa yɛ jɛmɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Ha oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ akwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aje shishi kwraa.

english: Why do my vegetable crops perform better when planted in moist lowland areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akwɛ amɛ yɛ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Vegetables like pepper, tomato, and okra have shallow root systems and high water needs, so lowlands provide consistent soil moisture that prevents them from wilting during short dry spells.
ga: Aduawai tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, tomato, kɛ okra yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nu babaoo he miihia amɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be koni ekɛtsi aduawai anaa koni amɛkagbo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo lɛ mli.

english: How can I keep my tomato roots from rotting when planting in wet lowland soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi tomato shishifãi anaa koni amɛkafite kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ?

english: Creating raised soil mounds or ridges in low-lying areas keeps tomato roots slightly elevated above standing water while still letting them reach the deep ground moisture they need.
ga: Gɔji loo ŋmeii ni afee yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tomato shishifãi ni amɛyaa ŋwɛi fioo yɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha tomato shishifãi lɛ aná shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni mli kwɔ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: How does frequent rainfall affect how fast my okra crops grow?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii abɔ lɛ saa okra tsei lɛ adalɛ oya lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Okra thrives on steady moisture; frequent rainfall helps the seeds germinate quickly and encourages rapid leaf and pod growth, leading to an earlier harvest.
ga: Okra shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii abɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya ni ehaa baa kɛ pod lɛ daa oya. Enɛ haa anáa nikpamɔ mra.

english: Why do my tomato leaves turn yellow when there is too much continuous rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Heavy rain can wash away essential plant nutrients like nitrogen from the topsoil, and waterlogged soil prevents roots from breathing properly, causing leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie tsei amli niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How does wet weather affect how pepper plants flower and produce fruits?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ saa pepper tsei lɛ afɔfɔi kɛ amɛyibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Constant rain provides the moisture needed for strong plant growth, but extremely heavy rains can knock off open flower blossoms, which reduces the number of pepper fruits that form.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa koni tsei lɛ adara lɛ aba. Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo. Enɛ baaha pepper aduawai ni baa lɛ ayibɔ aba shi.

english: Why do some traditional land preparation methods take so much longer before I can plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ blema gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani aduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Manual clearing and soil preparation take time because working the soil carefully by hand preserves the nutrient-rich topsoil from washing away when early heavy rains fall.
ga: Nine ni akɛjieɔ sũ lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ heɔ be ejaakɛ nine ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni niyenii mli nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ hiɔ shi koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ akashwie nɔ.

english: Is it good to plant okra in soil that stays wet for a long time?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu okra yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ nɔ?

english: Okra grows well in moist soil because it uses large amounts of water to develop fresh pods, but the land must still drain well enough so the roots do not sit in stagnant water.
ga: Okra kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ ejaakɛ ebiɔ nu babaoo dani ekɛ ŋmeii heei aba. Shi esa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hu atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa. koni shishifãi lɛ akahi nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli

english: Why do I need to control weeds early in farm areas that receive frequent rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akudɔ jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ? Yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni nugbɔ nɛɔ shii abɔ lɛ mli?

english: Frequent rain makes weeds grow aggressively, and if they are not cleared early, they will quickly outgrow your crop seedlings and steal vital soil nutrients.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii abɔ lɛ haa jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya. Ni kɛji akɛ ojieee jwɛi lɛ dani be ni ato lɛ shɛ lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ hu baakwɛ̃ oya fe dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛbaaju niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape starting from the tip, the plant is telling you it lacks nitrogen food in the soil. The plant steals nitrogen from its older, bottom leaves to feed the new leaves at the top.
ga: Beni ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ eshishigbɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ he waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet too quickly. The heat stresses the plant, so it drops flowers to save its own energy.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ he ni egbi waa kɛtee he ni edɔ oya tsɔ. Dɔlɛ haa tsei haoɔ No hewɔ lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛhere amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhewalɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves roll up during the hottest part of the afternoon even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Rolling leaves is the plant's way of protecting itself from losing too much water in extreme sun. By curling up, the leaves expose less surface to the hot air, acting like a sunshade until the temperature drops.
ga: Baai ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni tso ko tsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ nu babaoo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ he. Curling baai lɛ baa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛɛɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines on high sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu sweet potato wain tso yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves are like mini solar panels that feed the seed tuber underground. Staking raises the vines into the air so every leaf gets full sunlight without shadowing other leaves, helping the tuber grow much larger.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ tamɔ hulutsoo be mli tsɔnei bibii ni haa dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking haa wain tso lɛ yaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli bɔni afee ni baa fɛɛ baa aná hulu la ni fa ni etsĩii baa krokomɛi anaa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa yitso lɛ feɔ agbo babaoo.

english: Why does planting cassava on the exact same piece of land three years in a row give me smaller tubers each time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Cassava roots draw specific nutrients out of the soil every season. Planting it repeatedly on the same plot drains the soil bank without giving it time to rest or refill, resulting in smaller harvests.
ga: Cassava shishifãi gbalaa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛ́ adu nii shii abɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ŋshɔi lɛ atsɔ nu ni ehe ehiaaa ni ajɔɔ amɛhe loo awo mli ekoŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kpamɔ fioo.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground if heavy rains stay too long at harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ kpamɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water fills all the soil gaps for many days, oxygen cannot reach the roots, causing fungal rot organisms to multiply and decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli gbii babaoo Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ feɔ babaoo ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why are the new leaves on my pepper plant tightly curled, wrinkled, and stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe, ebɔle ehe, ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Curled, wrinkled leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips under the leaf. They suck the plant's sap and spread viruses that interrupt normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Amɛmuɔ tsei amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni tsiɔ baai lɛ adalɛ naa lɛ amɛshwãa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry out and die when I cut down all the large shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mifoɔ cacao tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees do not have strong roots yet and cannot handle direct sunlight all day. Shade trees break the harsh sunlight and keep the air humid, keeping young cocoa plants alive until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni wa lolo, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ. Tsei ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa ni amɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Enɛ haa kookoo tso bibioo lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ edaa kwraa.

english: Why does my plantain tree easily fall down when the heavy fruit bunch starts to mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ bɔi shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots grow shallow in the soil, and microscopic worms called nematodes or stem borers can weaken them. As the top gets heavy with fruit, the weak roots cannot hold the weight against wind.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ. Beni ŋmeii lɛ woɔ yibii ni tsii Shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ nyɛŋ adamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa.

english: Why do the maize seeds I saved from my last harvest yield far fewer cobs than the certified hybrid seeds I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ wo ŋmãa fioo kwraa fe ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli ni mihe lɛ ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred from two strong parent plants to yield high in the first generation. Seeds saved from that harvest lose that special vigor, leading to mixed and lower yields in the next season.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔ̃ɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɔ nyɛ tsei enyɔ ni he wa mli koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ hewalɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ baafee srɔtoi ni ebaa shi yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees burn and turn yellow when exposed to direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that cannot tolerate intense heat. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside young cocoa creates a living canopy that provides shade and traps moisture needed for the seedling's survival.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni haa hulutsoo ni emɔɔ nu ni he hiaa koni dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi lɛ baa.

english: How can I tell if my rubber trees are ready for me to start tapping them for latex?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ rɔbɔt tso lɛ efee klalo akɛ mabɔi tswaa?

english: A rubber tree is ready for tapping when the trunk's circumference reaches about 50 centimeters at a height of one meter from the ground, which normally takes between five to seven years of growth.
ga: Rɔba tsei efee klalo kɛha gbee kɛji tso lɛ shishigbɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ feɔ aaafee sɛntimita 50 yɛ mita 1 kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ aaafee afii 5-7 dani edaa.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very bushy with many green leaves, but producing small underground tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni eyɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo lɛ? Shi ani eyɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei bibioo ko?

english: When soil has high nitrogen content but lacks potassium, the plant spends most of its energy expanding foliage above ground instead of storing nutrients below ground to form large tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa babaoo shi potassium bɛ mli lɛ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niyenii kpakpahi kɛ toɔ zugba a sisi konɛ a pee ngmɔkɔ nguahi.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to grow instead of trailing on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ lɛ? Koni adu nii moŋ fe ni aaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ mli?

english: Yam vines need sunlight to generate energy for tuber growth. Raising the vines on stakes exposes more leaf surface to sunlight while keeping the leaves off damp ground where soil-borne fungal diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha tuber dalɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ haa hulu la babaoo shɛɔ baa lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why do my young maize leaves have ragged holes and small green dropping spots inside the center funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu ni ekpɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ? yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: This pattern of damage is caused by pests such as the Fall Armyworm, which feed on the tender leaf tissues inside the growing whorl of the maize plant during the cooler hours of the day.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants produce plenty of flowers but drop them all before any bean pods form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ekɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi dani enáa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers drop off prematurely when small insects like flower thrips feed on the soft buds, or when the crop experiences extreme heat stress during the flowering phase.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ fɔfɔi thrips lɛ ye fɔfɔi bibii lɛ. aloo be mli ni hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ haa tsei haoɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over easily during strong rains once heavy bunches start to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli ni jwɛi babaoo yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow, fibrous root systems rather than a deep taproot. When heavy fruit bunches develop, the plant becomes top-heavy, making it easy for wet, softened soil to lose its grip on the roots during windy storms.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyɛ fibrous fe shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Kɛ́ aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni efɔ kɛ bɔdɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛjɛɔ shishifãi ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ he lɛ anɔ yɛ ahum ni naa wa mli.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by sap-sucking pests like thrips or aphids damaging young leaves, or by a viral infection spread by whiteflies that distorts healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni tutuaa baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli. ni fiteɔ dalɛ kpakpa

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn dark and rotten before the fruit ripens?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: This issue, known as blossom-end rot, occurs when the tomato plant cannot absorb enough calcium or experiences irregular water supply while the fruit is expanding rapidly.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. loo enine shɛɔ nu nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ mli miilɛɛ oya lɛ

english: Why do the roots of my crops get exposed and washed away whenever heavy rain falls on my sloped farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ lɛ, nu lɛ hoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: When sloped land is left bare, running rainwater strips away the loose topsoil layer. Planting crops along soil ridges or mounds across the slope slows down rainwater movement and anchors the topsoil around the roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ ni nɔ ko bɛ nɔ lɛ Nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛboteɔ mli lɛ baagbala shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni etsilɛ lɛ kɛya. Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ŋmeii loo gɔŋji ni tsɔɔ gɔŋji lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ fioo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ŋmɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn easily and lose water quickly under full sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains around them provides living shade and traps soil moisture to help them survive their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaha amɛná hulutsoo ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why are the pods on my cocoa tree turning black before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ dani amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Black pods are caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod Disease, which thrives in overly shady, wet, and humid farm conditions. Pruning excess branches to allow sunlight inside and removing infected pods early helps stop the disease from spreading.
ga: Hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ pods diji baa. Eshwereɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi ni shade yɔɔ mli, nu, kɛ nu ni mli edɔ fe nine. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la aba mli ni ojie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni akpa helai gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Leaf curling and yellow spots are signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny flying insects called whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava stem varieties is the best way to prevent this infection.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kooloi bibii ni foɔ ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela nɛɛ naa.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my cassava so the roots do not spoil in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? Koni shishifãi lɛ akafite yɛ sũ lɛ mli?

english: Most cassava varieties mature between 9 to 12 months after planting, when lower leaves begin to turn yellow and drop off. Leaving tubers in the ground for too long past maturity makes them woody, hard, and unusable.
ga: Cassava henɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi yitso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha efee tso, ewa ni anyɛɛɛ akɛtsu nii.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the center leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a destructive pest that feeds rapidly on young corn leaves and growing tips. Regularly scouting your farm early in the season and applying approved treatments at the first sign of leaf damage protects your yield.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii ni yeɔ ŋmeii baai bibii kɛ amɛ ŋmeii ni daa oya lɛ. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli. Ni tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ baa lɛ efite lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.
