english: Why are the leaves of my corn plants turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves indicate a lack of nitrogen, an essential nutrient maize needs to grow strong and green. Adding well-decomposed animal manure or applying nitrogen fertilizers like Urea at the right growth stage will restore greenness and boost cob size.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ hewalɛ ni efee ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he loo akɛ nitrogen fertilizers tamɔ urea tsu nii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants rot at the base and die during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ fiteɔ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants suffer from root rot when water collects around their roots for too long without proper drainage. Planting on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely, keeping roots healthy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa. Shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ kɛji nu bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe. Ha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms without setting any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when temperatures are extremely high or when plants experience erratic watering. Providing consistent soil moisture and using organic mulch around the stem base keeps the roots cool and helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be fɛɛ be ni okɛ organic mulch abɔle he. Shishitoo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when they start producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛji ebɔi yibii womɔ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems and heavy fruit bunches, making them top-heavy and vulnerable to strong winds. Supporting the fruiting stems with strong wooden or bamboo props prevents the trees from snapping or uprooting.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii. Enɛ haa efeɔ tsiimɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ atswa lɛ oya. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei loo ŋmeii ni wa fi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakumɔ loo eshishifãi.

english: Why does my land yield less crop when I plant the same crop on it every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific plant nutrients from the soil and allows specialized pests to multiply. Rotating different crop types, such as switching between maize and legumes like cowpeas, restores soil fertility and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa tso pɔtɛɛ ko mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai krɛdɛɛi babaoo yaa hiɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi ni atsakeɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa teŋ tsakemɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Maize leaves roll up during extreme heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun. This helps the crop slow down water loss and protect itself from drying out until the cool evening.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa be mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhaa nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ebuɔ amɛhe koni amɛkagbi yɛ fɛ̃i mli.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without forming pods during hot, dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and lack of water cause cocoa trees severe stress. To survive, the tree drops its flowers to conserve energy and moisture rather than spending resources on developing new pods.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa cacao tsei lɛ anɔ. koni ehi shi Tso lɛ baashwie efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ nibii baatsu nii kɛfee pods heei

english: How do green crops cool themselves down when the midday sun gets extremely hot?
ga: Te tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛhaa amɛhe jɔɔ beni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Crops cool themselves through a process called transpiration. They draw water up from their roots and release it as vapor through tiny pores in their leaves, which functions just like human sweating.
ga: Tsei haa amɛhe jɔɔ kɛtsɔɔ gbɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ transpiration nɔ. Amɛgbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi ni amɛjieɔ lɛ kpo akɛ lasu kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ amli, ni no tsuɔ nii tamɔ adesa latsaa.

english: Will using too much heat to dry my seed grains kill them before I can plant them next season?
ga: Ani la ni mli edɔ babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii beni agbiɔ midumɔwui lɛ baagbe amɛ dani adu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, excessive heat can destroy the tiny living embryo inside the seed. To ensure seeds remain viable for planting, they should be dried with gentle warmth and good airflow rather than extreme heat.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, dɔlɛ babaoo baanyɛ akpata fɔmɔ kotokui bibii ni hiɛ ka lɛ ahiɛ. yɛ dumɔwu lɛ mli Enɛ haa anyɛɔ aduɔ dumɔwui lɛ lolo. Esa akɛ agbi amɛ kɛ hulutsoo blɛoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni tsɔɔ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine baatsu nii

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout when I plant them in soil that has been baking under strong sunshine all day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛji mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ ni ashã nɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Overheated soil can bake delicate seeds and kill the tender shoots before they break through the surface. Planting early in the morning or after a rain ensures the soil is cool enough for seed germination.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni efite ŋmeii bibii lɛ dani amɛfo mli. Kɛ́ adu nii leebi loo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: How does exposing harvested grain to hot sunshine kill the insects hidden inside without using chemicals?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ awo hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni egbe kooloi bibii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo mli lɛ ni akɛ tsofai tsuuu nii?

english: Insects, larvae, and eggs cannot regulate their body temperature. High heat dehydrates and kills them completely inside the grain, making heat a natural and safe way to clear pests from stored crops.
ga: Kplukai, ŋmeii, kɛ ŋmeii nyɛɛɛ amɛkwɛ amɛgbɔmɔtso lɛ mli dɔlɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa nu sɛɛ foɔ ni egbeɔ amɛ kwraa yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Enɛ haa dɔlɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato lɛ amli.

english: Why does my harvested cassava or maize spoil so quickly if I store it without drying it first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava loo ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mikɛto ni migbiko lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested crops contain high moisture levels that allow mold and bacteria to thrive. Drying crops uses heat to remove this moisture, creating an environment where fungi cannot survive.
ga: Tsei ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ hulutsoo babaoo, ni no haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helatsɛmɛi akwɛ̃ɔ. Nibii ni agbiɔ lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛjieɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ko baa ni ŋmei lɛ nyɛɛɛ ahi mli.

english: Is using a covered solar dryer better for preserving my crops than spreading them out on the bare ground?
ga: Ani hulutsoo tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ ŋwɛitsu nɔ ni akɛbuɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ hi fe ni mikɛbaagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ?

english: Solar dryers trap heat to raise temperatures safely and evenly, drying crops faster while keeping them protected from dust, rain, insects, and animals compared to bare ground drying.
ga: Solar dryers lɛ mɔ̃ɔ dɔlɛ koni ekɛha dɔlɛ aya hiɛ shweshweeshwe ni efee ekome. Ehaa tsei gbɛ́ɔ oya Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ sũ, nugbɔ, kooloi bibii, kɛ kooloi ahe. Kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni egbiɔ lɛ he

english: How does spreading dry grass on top of the soil keep my young crops from dying in hot weather?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aha mi tsei bibii lɛ akagboi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Dry grass acts as mulch, forming a protective barrier that prevents direct sunlight from overheating the soil. This keeps crop roots cool and preserves soil moisture.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch. Etsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni tsiɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli adɔ fe nine. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi.

english: Does setting fire to my bush plot before planting kill the bad weed seeds in the ground?
ga: Ani la ni ashãa ŋmɔ mli dani aduɔ lɛ baagbe jwɛi fɔji dumɔwui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The intense heat from burning destroys weed seeds resting on the surface, but it can also destroy beneficial soil nutrients and organic matter that your crops need to stay healthy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni jɛɔ la ni ashãa lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ jwɛi dumɔwui ni kpɛtɛɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Shi ebaanyɛ efite sũ mli niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ hu.

english: Yam leaves need sunlight to make food that grows big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves high off the hot ground where they can catch maximum sunlight and fresh air, leading to larger yams and preventing leaf rot.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛ́ amɛmiikwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi kɛjɛɔ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa babaoo yɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ agboi ni ehaa baa lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my yams start turning soft and rotting while they are still inside the mound?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egboɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ mli lolo lɛ?

english: Underground rotting happens when heavy rains soak the soil without proper drainage, or when tiny insects bite the growing tuber and open pathways for waterborne rot to destroy the crop.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi fitemɔ baa kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fũuɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii ŋmɔ bulb ni miida lɛ ni amɛgbele gbɛ kɛha nu ni fiteɔ koni efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Curled, yellow leaves are usually a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. This sickness stops the plant from feeding properly, causing small and woody cassava roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Hela nɛɛ haaa tsei aye niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛfee tamɔ tsei.

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize plants and leaving dirt in the leaves?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli ni mishiɔ muji yɛ baai lɛ amli?

english: That is the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides inside the central leaf funnel during the hot part of the day to eat soft young leaves, weakening the plant before it can grow maize cobs.
ga: No ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ. Ekɛ ehe teeɔ baai lɛ ateŋ ŋshɔi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa be lɛ mli koni eye baai bibii. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ dani ŋmãa lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning light yellow from the tip downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛjɛɔ amɛshishi kɛyaa shishi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom indicate that your soil is low in Nitrogen, which is the food crops need to stay green. Adding animal manure or rich organic fertilizer helps restore leaf color and plant strength.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii tso ni esa akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Kooloo ŋmei loo ŋmei ni mli ewo muji ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ ahe su kɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the young cocoa pods on my trees turning black and shriveling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads in cold, overly shaded, or damp environments. Pruning excess tree branches and clearing weeds allows sunlight and wind to dry out the farm and protect pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Fɔ̃ɔ ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Shade loo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli gĩɔ ni ebuɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or poor pollination. Spreading dry grass around the base of the plant retains moisture and keeps roots cool so flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛyashɛ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo pollination ni ehiii nɔ. Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shishitoo lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. koni fɔfɔii lɛ afee aduawai

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can be weakened by soil pests or strong winds once heavy fruit forms. Supporting the trunk with a sturdy branched wooden stick holds the weight of the bunch until harvest.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ kɛji yibiiwoo ni tsii ba. Kɛ tso ni niji ni wa yɔɔ mli lɛ fi tso lɛ sɛɛ. Efiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tsiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why does my farmland yield fewer crops each year even when the rains are good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops pull food out of the ground during every harvest. Planting the same crop on the same plot every season drains the soil; alternating with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts puts vital nutrients back into the earth.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be fɛɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu atsɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii wo mli lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings wither and die immediately after I move them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young plants suffer from transplant shock when moved into hot, dry soil under full sun. Planting late in the afternoon and watering right away allows seedlings to adjust coolly overnight without losing moisture.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ naa hela ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe kɛji akɛ ajie amɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ shwane mli ni awo amɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi nyɔɔŋ kome mli ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing necessary shade and conserving soil moisture during the cocoa trees' early years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ kookoo tso lɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do we raise big earth mounds to plant yam instead of planting directly into flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔkɛ muji agbo ko duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii moŋ fe ni wɔbaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ kplanaa lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose soil so they can easily expand and grow deep into the ground. Mounds also allow water to drain away easily, which prevents the tubers from sitting in soaked soil and rotting.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse bɔni afee ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛdara kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Gɔji hu yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hoɔ oya. Enɛ baatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkamɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ ni amɛkafite.

english: Check the tiny growth buds or nodes along the cassava stem and make sure they are pointing upward toward the sky. Planting stems upside down causes delayed growth and significantly reduces tuber yields.
ga: Kwɛmɔ kɛji ŋmeii bibii loo nodes yɛ. Yɛ ŋmei tso lɛ shishi Ni okwɛ koni amɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ haa amɛdalɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii ni anáa lɛ baa shi waa.

english: The first rainfall of the season is often followed by a long dry spell that can dry out the soil and kill young seedlings. It is safer to wait until the rains become steady and consistent before planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni ebaanyɛ egbe tso bibioo lɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa, ni ehiɛɛɛ shi dani odu.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize stalks usually indicate that the plant lacks nitrogen, which is essential for healthy green growth. It can also happen when soil stays waterlogged, preventing roots from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ tso lɛ mli. ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu be mli ni nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my land improve the soil for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to the legume family, which takes nitrogen gas from the air and fixes it into the soil. When the plants decompose, they leave this natural fertilizer behind for future crops.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas fata legume weku lɛ he, ni amɛjieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ tsei fite Amɛbaashi adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are there small holes and caterpillar droppings inside the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmeii afɔfɔi?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the central funnel of maize leaves to feed. Early detection and treatment are necessary to stop them from destroying the growing point of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye nii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ehe miihia ni ana ni atsa lɛ mra. Bɔni afee ni akafite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark brown and black during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ediŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly in damp, dark, and humid conditions. Pruning excess branches and clearing weeds helps air circulate through the farm to reduce the humidity that the fungus needs.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni edɔ, kɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛba ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa ŋmei lɛ shi.

english: Leaf curling and yellow patches are key symptoms of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies and infected planting stems. Using disease-resistant cassava varieties helps prevent this issue.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi titri. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Kɛ akɛ ŋmei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when plants suffer from extreme heat or irregular watering. Maintaining steady soil moisture and ensuring the soil has proper nutrients helps the flowers successfully set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaaa lɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ nɔmimaa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive and burn easily in direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow fast and provide big leaves that shield the young cocoa from harsh sun and heat while keeping the soil moist during their early years.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ nuɔ he waa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: How do I know which direction to stick my cassava stems into the soil when planting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole he ni esa akɛ okɛ o-cassava tso lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look at the small raised bumps (nodes or buds) on the stem where old leaves grew. These buds must point upward toward the sky so the plant can easily sprout branches upward and send healthy tubers into the ground.
ga: Taomɔ ŋmeii bibii (nodes loo buds) yɛ baai ni edara lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ atswa niji kɛya ŋwɛi mlɛo. ni etsuɔ ​​ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ.

english: Why is it important for me to erect wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mato tsei kɛha sweet potato wain tsei koni amɛkwɔ?

english: Yam plants need their leaves lifted high off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight. When leaves get full sunlight, the plant produces more food, which goes straight into making larger and heavier yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa lɛ Tsei lɛ baawo niyenii babaoo. Enɛ kɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ afeemɔ baa tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a key plant food, or that heavy rainfall has washed nutrients too deep into the soil where roots cannot reach them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Aloo, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I pour fertilizer directly against the main stem of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ tso titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the stem can burn the sensitive outer bark and roots due to high chemical concentration. It is safer to place fertilizer in a small ring a short distance away from the stem where fine feeding roots can safely absorb it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã eshishifãi ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kɛ eshishifãi lɛ. Ejaakɛ tsofai babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oookɛ fɔmɔ nii awo ŋmeii bibii amli. ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ fioo ni shishifãi ni niyenii kpakpai yɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do people say that growing groundnuts on my farm will help my next crop of maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that work with good bacteria in the soil to capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When groundnuts finish growing, they leave this free fertilizer behind for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ bacteria kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛto sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Amɛshiɔ ŋmeii nɛɛ ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in cold, wet, and humid weather. Water droplets spread the tiny fungal spores from infected leaves or soil onto healthy pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ fɛ̃i, fɛ̃i, kɛ fɛ̃i shihilɛi amli. Nu mli nu bibii lɛ gbɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii eshwaa. kɛjɛ baai loo shikpɔŋ ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ

english: What is causing ragged holes in my maize leaves and small worms hidden inside the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa? Akɛtee tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar pest that crawls into the central shoot (funnel) of young maize plants to feed on new leaves before they unfold.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmãa (cone) lɛ mli koni eye baai heei dani amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets extremely hot or when plants experience severe dry spells, which prevents proper pollination and causes the plant to shed its blossoms to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ ni naa wa waa. ni tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa lɛ. ni eha tsei afɔlɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my vegetable plants with dry grass or dry leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Tsoi ni jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egboi yɔɔ mli

english: Covering soil with dry organic material, called mulching, blocks the hot sun from drying out the soil, keeps roots cool, prevents weed growth, and holds moisture in the ground longer.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to protect their soft leaves from intense heat and direct sunlight. Leaving large shade trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantain keeps the soil moist and prevents the young plants from drying out.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo fioo ko koni ebu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Kɛ́ oshi tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo odu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaatsi tsei bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why do the lower leaves on my maize turn yellow while the crop is still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tso lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season helps the corn produce full, healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua o-ŋmei lɛ ni ewo toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When planted alongside maize, they naturally feed the soil and help the maize crop grow better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa fata he lɛ Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow weak and produce very small yields if I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough food and light to produce large fruits or grains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo yibii loo ŋmaa wuji.

english: Leaving too many shoots around one plantain stem forces the mother plant to share its nutrients with all of them, resulting in small bunches. Keeping only one or two strong suckers allows the plant to direct its energy into growing a large, heavy plantain bunch.
ga: Ni ashiɔ ŋmeii babaoo ni ebɔleɔ Tso kome pɛ nyɛɔ tso nyɛ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ plantain lɛ fɛɛ aja niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei akui bibii Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ tso lɛ tso lɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei agboi ni tsii, ni yɔɔ fãji lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when rain stays on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When water sits on the field for too long, it chokes the roots, causing them to rot underground. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nu hi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi fiteɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food that builds big tubers under the ground. Staking lifts the vines off the damp soil so the leaves get maximum sunlight and avoid diseases that live on the ground.
ga: Sweet potato baai biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ koni ekɛha tso lɛ baai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ he, ni ekwa helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants drop off without turning into tomatoes during hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat dries up tomato pollen, preventing flowers from producing fruits. When the plant gets too stressed by heat or lack of water, it naturally sheds its flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baaha tomato pollen lɛ agbi. Tsi fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkawo yibii Beni tsei lɛ haoɔ amɛhe tsɔ kɛjɛɔ latsaa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do small caterpillars hide inside the central heart of my maize leaves instead of staying on the outside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abele baai lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe kponɔgbɛ lɛ?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm hide in the central rolled leaves because the leaves are soft, tender, and protected from birds and hot sunlight. This is why chemical or natural sprays must be directed straight into the funnel of the plant to reach them.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli ejaakɛ baai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe jɔ ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ okpoi kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ahe. Enɛ hewɔ ni esa akɛ afɔse tsofai loo adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ koni eshɛ amɛhe lɛ.

english: Planting the same crop on the same field every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil continuously and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating with different crops allows the soil to recover and breaks the cycle of diseases.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ehe feɔ fɛo ni efoɔ helai ni baa lɛ amli.

english: Is there any medicine or chemical I can spray on my cocoa trees to cure Swollen Shoot disease without cutting them down?
ga: Ani tsofai loo tsofai komɛi yɛ ni manyɛ makɛshwie cacao tso lɛ nɔ koni mikɛtsa ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ ni mikɛfolɔ cacao tso lɛ shi?

english: Currently, there is no chemical spray or cure for the Cocoa Swollen Shoot virus. The only proven way to stop the disease from spreading to healthy trees across your farm is to completely uproot and destroy infected trees.
ga: Amrɔ nɛɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus nɔ loo tsofai ni akɛtsaa Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus lɛ bɛ. Gbɛ pɛ ni ana he odaseyeli ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ ji ni otsi tsei fɛɛ ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ashishi ni okpãtã amɛhiɛ.

english: Why do I have to uproot my whole cocoa tree if only a few leaves are showing signs of disease?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo cacao tso muu lɛ fɛɛ mli yɛ be mli ni baai fioo komɛi pɛ ena he sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Diseases like Cocoa Swollen Shoot spread through the entire living system of the tree, including the roots. Cutting off just a few leaves or branches leaves the virus alive inside the trunk, allowing it to keep spreading to nearby healthy trees.
ga: Helai tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot lɛ gbɛ eshwa tso lɛ wala gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli fɛɛ. Shishifãi lɛ fata he Kɛ́ afo baai loo niji fioo komɛi pɛ lɛ, ebaaha hela lɛ ahi shi yɛ tso lɛ mli. Ha egbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: How long should I wait to plant new cocoa trees after uprooting infected ones from my farm?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani madu cacao tsei heei beni mijie cacao tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: After uprooting diseased cocoa trees, it is best to clear the land of leftover roots and plant fast-growing shade crops like plantains first. This gives time for disease-carrying pests like mealybugs to die off before you introduce new cocoa seedlings.
ga: Beni ajie kookoo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ abaajie shishifãi ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ jɛmɛ ni adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ haa be ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa, tamɔ mealybugs lɛ gboiɔ dani oduɔ kookoo dumɔwui heei.

english: What is Cocoa Swollen Shoot disease and how does it affect my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni ji kookoo hela? Ni te enáa mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Cocoa Swollen Shoot is a serious viral disease spread by tiny insects called mealybugs. It causes stems and roots to swell, turns leaves yellow or red along the veins, shrinks cocoa pods, and eventually kills the tree within a few years.
ga: Cocoa Swollen Shoot ji hela ko ni naa wa ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ fuɔ. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo etsuru yɛ fãji lɛ ahe. Cocoa pod shrinks Ni yɛ naagbee lɛ tso lɛ gboɔ yɛ afii fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: Why are the stems of my young cocoa trees swelling up and turning weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ efuu ni amɛgbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Swollen stems are a main symptom of the Cocoa Swollen Shoot virus. The virus disrupts how food and water move through the tree, causing swollen shoots, leaf discoloration, and a drop in pod production.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni efuu lɛ ji Cocoa Swollen Shoot hela lɛ he okadi titri. Virus lɛ tsiɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe fũuɔ, baai lɛ ahe su tsakeɔ ni pod lɛ feemɔ baa shi.

english: How can I tell if a crop disease has just arrived in my district or has been around for a long time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso hela ko eba he ni miyɔɔ lɛ pɛŋ loo ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ?

english: When a disease is new to a district, only isolated farms show sudden leaf yellowing or branch dieback. If it has been present for a long time, large areas of older farms will show widespread tree loss, stunted growth, and chronic stem swellings.
ga: Beni hela hee ko ba nɛkɛ he nɛɛ Okwaafoi ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ pɛ jieɔ baai ni miifee ŋmɔŋ loo tsei niji ni egboi lɛ ahe okadi kpo. Kɛji ejie ehe kpo be kakadaŋŋ Yinɔsane ŋmɔji amli hei wuji lɛ baatsɔɔ tsei ni elaaje babaoo. shweremɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛ tsei ni efuu be fɛɛ be

english: Can cocoa diseases move from neighboring farms into my cocoa farm?
ga: Ani kookoo helai baanyɛ ajɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ amli kɛba mi kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, cocoa diseases easily move across farm boundaries. Insects like mealybugs carry viruses from infected trees nearby, and wind, shared farm tools, or carrying infected plant materials can bring the disease onto your land.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo hela gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ husui anɔ. Kplukai tamɔ mealybugs hiɛɔ hela lɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ okwaayeli nibii ni ajaa lɛ amli. Aloo tsei ahe nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni okɛyaa lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ hela aba oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: If I uproot my diseased cocoa trees and plant fresh seedlings, will the new trees get sick too?
ga: Kɛ mijie kookoo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni midu dumɔwui heei lɛ, Ani tso hee lɛ hu baaná hela?

english: New seedlings can stay healthy if all diseased trees in the immediate area are completely removed, proper shade is established early, and you regularly check your farm to control pests that spread viruses.
ga: Abaanyɛ aha dumɔwui heei ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛji ajie tsei fɛɛ ni hela emɔ amɛ ni yɔɔ hei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ. Ato hulutsoo be ni sa he gbɛjianɔ mra. Ni okwɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa koni okwɛ kooloi ni gbeɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ anɔ.

english: Should I replant my farm with local cocoa seeds or look for new hybrid varieties after a disease outbreak?
ga: Ani esa akɛ makwɛ cocoa ŋmeii yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ moŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli loo matao ŋmeii heei ni akɛfee ekome yɛ hela lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is better to plant recommended hybrid cocoa varieties provided by agricultural officers because these varieties grow faster, produce more pods, and tolerate environmental stress better than older local seeds.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu hybrid cocoa henɔi ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ tsei srɔtoi nɛɛ daa oya. Ehaa pods babaoo ni enyɛɔ ekɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi kpeɔ fe maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni etsɛ.

english: Why do cocoa trees in some farming districts die off quickly while trees in other areas stay productive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ okwaayeli hei komɛi lɛ gboiɔ oya yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yɔɔ hei krokomɛi lɛ woɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tree survival depends heavily on soil conditions, proper shade, weather, and whether severe viral diseases like Swollen Shoot have entered the district without being promptly cut out.
ga: Tso lɛ wala shihilɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shihilɛ nɔ. He ni sa, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi, kɛji helai ni naa wa ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa, tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ baanyɛ abote jɛmɛ ni afolɔɔɔ amɛ oya.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them directly in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under intense tropical sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain or cassava nearby creates a living canopy that protects young cocoa trees until they are mature enough to handle direct sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa bɔ ni sa ni hulu la baashɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my crops with dry leaves or cut grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo he ni ebɔle he lɛ mli lɛ? Nibii ni aduɔ ni baai egbi loo jwɛi ni afo?

english: Covering the soil with organic material, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground during hot days, keeps the root zone cool, and stops weeds from growing and taking nutrients away from your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛhaa lɛ akɛ mulching. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: What is eating the central leaves inside my young maize plant and leaving brown powder behind?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ni eshiɔ powda ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ sɛɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that burrows into the center whorl of young maize plants to feed on soft leaves. Catching them early with recommended insecticides or organic treatments keeps your maize stalks growing healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni shwieɔ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli koni eye baai bibii lɛ. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli tsuɔ nii yɛ mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ lɛ, o-abele tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or mites. As these pests feed on leaf juices, they cause leaves to deform and can spread viral diseases to the rest of the farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi, ejaakɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli kɛba ŋmɔ lɛ mli hei krokomɛi.

english: Why do I need to cut away some of the small shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishigbɛ ni ajie lɛ

english: When too many suckers grow around a plantain tree, they fight with the main stem for food and water. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, which leads to bigger, heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwu ko he lɛ, amɛkɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛwuɔ koni amɛtao niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha plantain tso lɛ afee agbo ni etsii.

english: Yams are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves up toward sunlight to generate energy for tuber growth. Staking also keeps the foliage off the wet ground, which prevents leaves from rotting and catching soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu la mli koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha bulb lɛ dalɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa ni helai akabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tip usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, a vital nutrient for plant growth. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen away, so top-dressing with a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea restores healthy green leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni eha baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Should I put fertilizer in the planting hole at the same time I drop my seeds into the ground?
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo bu lɛ mli yɛ be kome too mli. Kɛ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo daabi?

english: Placing chemical fertilizer directly against fresh seeds can burn and destroy the tender roots as they emerge. It is better to wait 1 to 2 weeks after germination and apply fertilizer a few centimeters away from the base of the seedling.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwui heei amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni egbe shishifãi bibii lɛ kɛji amɛje kpo pɛ. Mɛɛ otsi 1 kɛyashi 2 beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he sɛntimita fioo ko pɛ kɛjɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashishi.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plant without making any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the air is extremely hot and dry or when the soil lacks consistent water. High heat disrupts flower pollination, so keeping the soil steadily moist and using shade netting can encourage healthy fruit formation.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa. aloo be mli ni nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa Dɔlɛ ni naa wa tsiɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa ni akɛ shade netting tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ ewo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni baa lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are ready to harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves naturally dry up and fall off, and the soil at the base of the stem begins to crack open due to the expanding tubers growing underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees producing fewer pods now than they did ten years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiwo ŋmɔtɔ fioo fe afii nyɔŋma ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Over many years of harvest, cocoa trees draw out natural nutrients from the soil. Without replacing these nutrients, the land becomes exhausted, causing the trees to produce fewer and smaller pods over time.
ga: yɛ afii babaoo ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ mli fɛɛ Cacao tso lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ́ akɛ niyenii mli nibii nɛɛ tsakeee lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi, ni no haa tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ. Beni be hoɔ lɛ

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has become exhausted?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efo?

english: Exhausted soil usually shows signs like weak crop growth, yellowing leaves, small cocoa pods, and trees that easily suffer or drop leaves even during the rainy season.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ jieɔ okadii tamɔ tsei ni edaaa jogbaŋŋ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ, kɛ kookoo ŋmeii bibii kpo. kɛ tsei ni baanyɛ adamɔ hɔmɔ naa loo amɛgbee shi oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli po

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings struggle to grow on land that has been farmed for a very long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Old farmland has lost most of its natural plant food and rich topsoil through years of farming. Young seedlings need high levels of soil nutrients to build strong roots, which exhausted land can no longer supply on its own.
ga: Okwaayeli shikpɔŋ momo lɛ efite tsei adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ babaoo yɛ afii babaoo ni akɛtsu nii yɛ okwaayeli mli lɛ mli. Tsei bibii biɔ niyenii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ekwɛ ehe dɔŋŋ.

english: Why was cocoa farming easier for our elders years ago than it is for us today?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ afii babaoo ni eho nɛ lɛ, afii babaoo ni eho nɛ lɛ, kookoo dumɔ fee mlɛo fe bɔ ni eji kɛha wɔ ŋmɛnɛ lɛ?

english: In the past, farms were planted on fresh virgin forest land packed with natural nutrients. Decades of continuous farming without feeding the soil back have cleared those nutrients, making farming harder today without extra soil care.
ga: Be ko ni eho lɛ, aduɔ ŋmɔji yɛ kooi ni eyi kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kpakpai amli. Okwaayeli ni aya nɔ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni ahaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ekoŋŋ lɛ eha nakai niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ efo mli. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ aaafee okwaayeli ŋmɛnɛ kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn yellow even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves during good rains usually mean your crops are hungry. While rain provides water, exhausted soil lacks essential food like nitrogen, causing the leaves to lose their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ kpakpa be mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye onibii. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ lɛ haa nu moŋ Shi shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, ni no haa baai lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ fɛo.

english: Why do I need to put fertilizer on my land if plants grow naturally in dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe?

english: Every time you harvest cocoa pods, you carry away nutrients that came from the dirt. Fertilizer works like food for the land, putting back what was removed so your crops can keep feeding well.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa kookoo ŋmɔtɔ Obaajie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ. Ejieɔ nɔ ni ajie lɛ ekoŋŋ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aye nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: What does a fertilizer like 'Oye Asaase Yie' actually do for tired land?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ‘Oil Asa Ia’ baanyɛ aye abua shikpɔŋ ni etse ehe lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Oye Asaase Yie' replaces specific missing nutrients in worn-out soil, restoring the land's strength so cocoa trees can grow deeper roots and bear healthy fruit again.
ga: Oye Asaase Yie’ yeɔ niyenii ni elaaje yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ najiaŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ Bɔni afee ni kookoo tso lɛ anyɛ atswa shishifãi babaoo ni ewo yibii kpakpai ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it really possible to fix soil that has been farmed on for more than twenty years?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ esaa shikpɔŋ ni atsu nɔ fe afii 20 lɛ jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, tired soil can be restored. By applying proper fertilizers, adding organic matter, and practicing good farm care, you can bring old farmland back to high productivity.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ asaa shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ ekoŋŋ. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ lɛ, okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli afata he ni okwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Obaanyɛ okɛ okwaayeli shikpɔŋ momo lɛ aku sɛɛ aba nibii ni woɔ yibii babaoo mli.

english: Will fertilizer still help my crops if the farm ground is already completely worn out?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii baaye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ lolo kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efite kwraa?

english: Yes, fertilizer is designed to revive exhausted soil. However, adding organic matter like dead leaves or mulch alongside fertilizer helps the worn-out ground hold onto the food much better.
ga: Hɛɛ, afee ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ. Shi, kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egboi loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ niyenii lɛ he jogbaŋŋ.

english: How long will it take for my cocoa farm to recover after I start feeding the exhausted soil?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe ni mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ aya hiɛ beni mibɔi shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ nɔ niyenii yeli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Trees usually start looking healthier with greener leaves within a few weeks after feeding the soil, but significant improvements in pod harvest typically show during the next major yield season.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli kɛjɛ be mli ni ayeɔ amɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Shi bei pii lɛ, hiɛyaa ni sa kadimɔ yɛ pod kpamɔ mli lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ nibii afeemɔ be titri ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I give my young crop seedlings a large amount of fertilizer as soon as they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛji amɛje kpo pɛ?

english: Young crop plants have small, tender roots that cannot handle heavy feeding. Applying too much fertilizer early on can burn the roots and kill the plant; starting with a small amount allows the roots to absorb nutrients safely as they grow.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aye niyenii ni tsii. Ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ ni egbe tso lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ fioo ko je shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ shweshweeshwe beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry periods to conserve moisture and protect themselves from heat. Once the rains return, the plant naturally recovers and shoots new green leaves.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ Tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ebaakwɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, dark conditions. Keeping the field pruned lets in sunlight and fresh air, which prevents the moisture that fungus needs to destroy your crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni duŋ yɔɔ. O jwɛi lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ koni onine ashɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa nɔ Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ baafite onibii lɛ anaa.

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or thrips sucking the sap from young leaves. Treating the plants early stops the insects and helps the fresh shoots grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Tsei ahe nitsumɔ mra Ehaa ŋmeii kpaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii heei ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms instead of producing tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔlɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛwoɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed flowers when exposed to extreme heat or irregular watering. Providing steady moisture and shade during hot afternoons helps the plant retain flowers so fruit can develop.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ mli fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni ewo yibii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings get burned easily under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that provide temporary shade and retain moisture, giving young cocoa trees protection during their early years.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa cacao tsei bibii lɛ oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe bulɛ yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: When maize plants grow too close together, their roots and leaves fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough food and space to grow thick stalks and large corn cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmãa tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ he ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji baakwɛ̃.

english: Yam plants naturally climb to reach sunlight. Training the vines up wooden stakes spreads out the leaves, allowing them to capture sunlight and convert it into energy to swell the yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛná hulu la. Kɛ́ atsɔse wain tso lɛ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ebaa lɛ agbɛ ashwã. Enɛ haa amɛnáa hulu la ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ hewalɛ ni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow plenty of leafy foliage but very few beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ baa babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas produce too much foliage and few pods when given fertilizers rich in nitrogen. Cowpeas naturally make their own nitrogen from the soil, so excessive feeding encourages leaf growth over bean production.
ga: Cowpea woɔ baai babaoo tsɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo komɛi kɛji akɛ akɛ nitrogen ni fa babaoo wo mli. Cowpeas lɛ feɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, niyenii ni ayeɔ fe nine lɛ haa baa lɛ daa fe bɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees fall over easily during heavy rains and wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni eda lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain roots grow shallowly near the top of the soil and struggle to hold heavy fruit bunches in strong winds. Supporting heavy fruit bunches with wooden props helps prevent the trees from uprooting.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛmɔmɔ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ amli. yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli Tso yibii akui ni tsii ni akɛ tsei ni akɛfiɔ shi lɛ fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why are extension officers advising me to cut down some of my cocoa trees even when they still look green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ekomɛi lɛ? Ani tso lɛ tamɔ eŋɔli lolo?

english: Even if a cocoa tree looks green, it might be infected with Swollen Shoot Disease, which spreads secretly to surrounding healthy trees. Cutting affected trees immediately stops the disease from destroying your entire farm.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ kookoo tso lɛ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ moŋ, Shi amɛbaanyɛ amɛná bud swollen hela hu, ni teemɔŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anɔ. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooofo lɛ haa hela lɛ kpataaa oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ shikome.

english: What causes my young cocoa pods to turn black and rot before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa?

english: Black pod rot is caused by a fungal disease that thrives in wet and humid conditions. Keeping weeds low and pruning crowded branches allows sunshine and air to reach the pods, reducing moisture and preventing rot.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛ black pod rot baa. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi lɛ shi ni afolɔ mli waa lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ jwɛi lɛ ahe. Ehaa hulutsoo baa shi ni ehaaa efite.

english: How far apart should I plant my cocoa seedlings when setting up a new farm?
ga: Beni atoɔ ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ Te esa akɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni kɛ mi teŋ jɛkɛ ha tɛŋŋ?

english: Spacing cocoa seedlings about 3 meters (10 feet) apart in rows gives each tree enough room for its roots to feed and its branches to grow without overcrowding and fighting for sunlight.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ to he ko aaafee mitai 3 (naji 10) yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aye nii ni amɛniji lɛ hu akwɛ ni amɛhiɛɛɛ amɛhe tsɔ ni amɛyeee akaŋ kɛha hulu la.

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava or yam together with my young cocoa plants?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ akwɛ niyenii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei?

english: You can grow plantains or cocoyams to provide temporary shade for young cocoa, but avoid growing cassava close to young cocoa because cassava roots draw too much water and food away from the soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu plantain loo cocoa tsei koni eha cocoa tsei bibii lɛ aná hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli. Shi tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmei dumɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ejaakɛ ŋmei shishifãi gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Should I completely burn all the cleared bush when preparing my land for planting cocoa?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashã jwɛi ni ajie lɛ fɛɛ beni miisaa shikpɔŋ kɛha kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: It is better not to burn the cleared vegetation completely because burning destroys essential soil nutrients. Clearing and allowing the plant material to decay naturally enriches the soil for your young plants.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshã tsei ni eshã lɛ kwraa ejaakɛ shãa fiteɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ otsi tso lɛ mli nibii lɛ ahe ni oha amɛfite yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo kɛha otsei bibii lɛ.

english: Why should I leave some large forest trees standing inside my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi koo mli tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Large forest shade trees protect mature cocoa from harsh heat, keep the soil cool and moist during dry seasons, and help your cocoa trees live and produce pods for many more years.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ koo agbo lɛ mli lɛ buɔ kookoo ni eda lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni o-cacao tsei lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii afii babaoo ni baa lɛ.

english: Removing extra branches and unwanted water shoots (chupons) helps the tree direct all its energy and nutrients into growing big, healthy cocoa pods instead of wasting energy on useless leaves.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine kɛ nu mli ŋmeii ni ataooo (chupon) ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni etsɔɔ ehewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ kɛyaa kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa ni miida lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: What is the best month of the year for me to plant my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni ji nyɔŋ ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli ni abaanyɛ adu kookoo dumɔwui heei?

english: The best time to plant cocoa seedlings is at the start of the major rainy season, around May or June, so the young plants receive enough rain to build strong roots before the dry season arrives.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu kookoo dumɔwui ji nugbɔ be ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shishijee. Aaafee May loo June No hewɔ lɛ, tsei bibii lɛ baaná nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba.

english: It is natural for cocoa trees to drop extra flowers because a tree can only carry a limited number of pods, but heavy flower loss can also happen due to dry weather, insect pests, or lack of soil nutrients.
ga: Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ cacao tsei baawo fɔfɔi krokomɛi ejaakɛ tso lɛ baanyɛ awo fɔfɔi fioo ko pɛ. Shi fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aba yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: How can I tell if the soil on my cocoa farm needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If your cocoa leaves start turning pale yellow, look weak, or fail to produce good pod yields even after adequate rainfall, it is usually a sign that the soil has run out of nutrients and requires fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cocoa baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ, loo ewooo ŋmeii kpakpai yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehe miihia ni awo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is fertile and healthy without using expensive tools?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ hewalɛ ni mikɛ nibii ni jara wa tsuuu nii?

english: Healthy soil usually has a dark color, feels soft when moist, smells like fresh earth, and contains earthworms or insects. If wild plants and grass grow thick and deep green on the land naturally, the soil has good nutrients for your crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo kɛji edɔ Ehe ŋmɔlɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ hee. Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo kooloi bibii hu yɛ. Kɛji akɛ koo mli tsei kɛ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná niyenii kpakpai kɛha onibii.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant the same crop on the same plot of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same soil nutrients year after year. It also gives pests and soil diseases a permanent home and food supply, causing your yields to drop over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite daa afi. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ hu naa shia kɛ niyenii ni amɛyeɔ daa. Enɛ haa nitsumɔ ni otsuɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during hot, dry weather as a survival trick to save water. As long as the stems stay green and alive, the tubers underground remain safe and will sprout fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ ni egbiɔ lɛ. Taakɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔ kɛha wala koni akɛhere nu yiwala. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ yitso lɛ baafee eŋɔli ni ehiɛ kã lɛ Shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ baahi shi shweshweeshwe ni amɛbaakwɛ baai heei kɛji nugbɔ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when they feel stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Giving them steady water and light shade during midday heat helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa ha amɛhao. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ hulutsoo yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither and die when I cut down all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ gbo ni egbo beni mifo tsei ni eda ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants naturally thrive in the cool shade of forest trees. Strong direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and bakes the soil dry, so keeping taller shade trees protects them until they are mature.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ ashishi. Hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã ebaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ aha tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ hɔɔŋ lɛ, ebaabu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot underground when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Yam roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in the ground for too long without draining, it chokes the soil and creates ideal conditions for fungal diseases to multiply and rot the tubers.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa sweet potato shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ aya hiɛ ni efite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Plantain roots are shallow and stay close to the top of the soil rather than going deep. Digging deeper planting holes, mounding extra soil around the stem base, and using wooden stakes to support heavy bunches stops them from falling.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ moŋ fe ni amɛmli kwɔ. Dumɔ bu lɛ mli ni aaawo mli jogbaŋŋ Okɛ shikpɔŋ krokomɛi abɔle tso lɛ shishi ni okɛ tsei ni akɛfiɔ jwɛi ni tsii lɛ sɛɛ koni tso lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Why are my groundnut shells empty inside even though the plant grew leaves very well above ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut ŋmɔji lɛ amli efee efolo lɛ? Mɛɛ tsei yɔɔ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Empty groundnut pods happen when the soil lacks calcium, which the plant absorbs through its underground pods to fill the nuts. Adding wood ash or lime to the soil gives the plant the nutrient it needs to produce solid seeds.
ga: Peanut ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji akɛ calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tso lɛ shwieɔ kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii amli koni ekɛwo ŋmeii lɛ amli ekoŋŋ Kɛ́ akɛ tso sũ loo ŋmeii fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo dumɔwui ni wa.

english: How can I protect my stored maize seeds from insects without using dangerous chemicals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu ŋmãa ni ato lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ahe ni mikɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara tsuuu nii?

english: Drying your maize completely in the sun and mixing the seeds with clean wood ash or crushed neem leaf powder creates a natural barrier that chokes tiny insects like weevils without harming the seed.
ga: Abɛi ni hulu lɛ haa egbiɔ ni akɛ tso sũ ni he tse loo neem baa ni atswa lɛ futuɔ dumɔwui lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni mɔɔ kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii, ni eyeee dumɔwui lɛ awui.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes spoil so quickly after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomatoi ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mikpa lɛ?

english: Tomatoes rot quickly if they are picked while wet from dew, bruised during handling, or stored in hot, sealed containers. Picking them gently when they start showing a reddish tint and keeping them in cool, ventilated places extends their shelf life.
ga: Tomatoi fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Epila yɛ be mli ni ekɛtsuɔ nii Aloo akɛto tsɛnsi ko ni mli edɔ ni aŋã mli jogbaŋŋ mli. Tsɔɔmɔ blɛoo beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ lɛ ni okɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ koni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen or your plants are not getting enough water. Nitrogen acts like food that keeps plants green and growing strong; without it, the plant pulls nutrients from its older leaves to save the new ones.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo otso lɛ naaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Nitrogen tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ ebɛ lɛ, tsei gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni amɛkwɛ eheei lɛ anɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to heat and dry out very quickly under full sun. They need fast-growing shade crops like plantain or cassava planted nearby to shield them and keep the soil moist while they are young.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ he waa ni amɛgbiɔ oya waa yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo yucca ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ koni ebu amɛhe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ.

english: Is it good for my soil if I plant cowpeas in the same field as my maize?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmãa?

english: Yes, cowpeas and other legumes pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. This acts like free natural fertilizer, which enriches the soil and helps your maize grow stronger and yield more.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa o-abele lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: If one of my cassava plants gets brown spots on its leaves, why does it spread to the rest of my farm so fast?
ga: Kɛji mi-cassava tsei lɛ eko yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ Mɛni hewɔ egbɛ eshwa miŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ mli oya nɛkɛ?

english: Leaf spots are caused by fungal or bacterial diseases that travel easily through wind, rain splashes, or on your hands and farm tools. Removing and destroying infected leaves early stops the sickness from spreading to healthy crops.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni tsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, loo yɛ niji kɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii anɔ lɛ. Baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra kɛ amɛhiɛkpatamɔ Enɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Cassava rot is usually caused by heavy rain leaving water standing in the soil for too long, or by soil fungi. Too much water prevents the roots from breathing, creating soggy conditions where rot organisms quickly multiply and ruin the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, ni haa nu hiɔ sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ, loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ cassava fitemɔ baa. Nu babaoo baatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkamu. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ baa ni nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ feɔ babaoo oya ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are there ragged holes in the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn plant lɛ yɛ bu yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Ragged holes in maize leaves are a major sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the growing core of the plant and eat the leaves. Catching them early with appropriate controls prevents them from destroying the whole crop.
ga: Buji ni ekumɔ yɛ ŋmãa baai amli lɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ahe okadi titri, ni amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli ni miida lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ. Amɔmɔ mra Kɛji akɛ akudɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, atsĩɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii muu fɛɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves to shrink their surface area and reduce water loss during intense heat. It acts like closing a window to save water, though if they remain curled in the cool morning, it means they desperately need irrigation.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi ni ekɛha nu ni fiteɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Efeɔ enii tamɔ samflɛ ni aŋaa koni akɛbu nu he. Kɛji amɛfo amɛhe yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be mli po lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu he miihia amɛ waa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when water supply is irregular, or when there are no bees or wind to pollinate them. Consistent watering and keeping the soil cool with mulch helps the plant hold onto its flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii loo kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmeii. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell that my yam tubers are mature and ready to harvest underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato tubers lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Yams are ready for harvest when the green vines and leaves turn yellow and dry up naturally. This signals that the plant has stopped growing above ground and has transferred all its food energy into the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔɔ beni wain tsei lɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dalɛ ni ekɛ eniyenii hewalɛ fɛɛ etee ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow short and weak if I don't clear them quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ kɛji mijieee amɛ oya lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food and light they need to grow tall and produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ naa niyenii kɛ la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed to make green leaves and build strong stalks. It can also happen when the soil stays too waterlogged and the roots cannot breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii ni he hiaa waa koni akɛfee baai eŋɔli kɛ tsei ni wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: What causes small round holes to appear all over my cabbage leaves overnight?
ga: Mɛni haa buji lɛ feɔ bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ kaabe baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ nyɔɔŋ kome mli.

english: Small holes in cabbage leaves are typically caused by caterpillars or beetles that feed under the cover of darkness. Inspecting the undersides of leaves and using appropriate crop protection sprays early will prevent them from destroying your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ duŋ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ kaaba baa mli lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni okɛ tsofai ni sa ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ atsu nii mra. Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of essential soil nutrients like calcium. Keeping the moisture steady around the roots helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, tamɔ calcium. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and hard even after staying in the ground for over a year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛhe wa eyɛ mli akɛ amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nɔ ni fe afi moŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots cannot expand if the ground is packed too hard or lacks potassium. Loosening the soil properly before planting and using healthy stem cuttings allows the roots to swell and store food easily.
ga: Kasava shishifãi nyɛŋ alɛɛ mli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo potassium bɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani adu ni akɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛbuaa niyenii anaa oya.

english: If tomatoes get too little water, their leaves will curl upward and feel dry or crisp. If they get too much water, the leaves will turn yellow and look limp while the surrounding ground stays constantly soggy.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tomatoi lɛ ná nu fioo tsɔ lɛ Ebaai lɛ baabɔle amɛhe ni amɛnu he akɛ amɛgbi loo amɛhe ejɔ. Kɛji onine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli ewo ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why does grass grow back so quickly after I cut it down on my farm with a cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya nɛkɛ beni mikɛ dade ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When you only chop grass off at ground level, the roots remain alive under the soil and quickly send up fresh green shoots using stored energy. Removing the root systems or using suitable weed management treatments prevents them from coming right back.
ga: Ofoɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ. Shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa ŋwɛi oya. Kɛ́ ajie shishifã lɛ loo akɛ gbɛi ni sa ni akɛkwɛɔ jwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi shishifã lɛ naa koni ekaku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the small cocoa pods on my trees turning black and dry instead of growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Ani mi tsei lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ agbo lɛ?

english: Small cocoa pods turn black and shrivel when affected by Black Pod disease, which is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet weather. Trimming excess branches lets sunlight and air into the canopy to keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛji ŋmeii diji hela lɛ ye amɛnɔ. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ tsei lɛ amli koni eha tsei lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and slender with small cobs when I plant many seeds together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ Dumɔwui babaoo yɛ be kome mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They stretch upward to reach light instead of building strong stalks and large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛsɛɛ tsɛɔ koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he, ni moŋ amɛfeɔ tsei ni wa kɛ tsei wuji ni eyi obɔ.
