english: Why do my harvested beans end up with tiny holes and turn to powder after a few months in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kɔfi ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni etsɔɔ powda yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni akɛtoɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Tiny holes in stored beans are caused by bean weevils, which are tiny insects that lay eggs on the seeds. Storing clean, dry beans in airtight bags or treating them safely before storage kills the pests and protects your grain.
ga: Bean weevils, ni ji kooloi bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni ato lɛ amli lɛ baa. ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ dumɔwui anɔ Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii ni he tse ni egbi lɛ wo vacuum kotokui amli loo okwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ dani okɛto lɛ, ebaagbe ŋmeii ni baabu odumɔwui lɛ ahe.

english: Why does my yam crop grow plenty of thick green leaves above ground but produces very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli tse babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When a yam plant receives too much nitrogen fertilizer, it spends all its energy producing heavy leafy vines on top rather than directing energy down to develop large tubers in the soil.
ga: Kɛji sweet potato tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛfee wain tso ni baai ni tsii yɔɔ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ he wami tsuɔ ní konɛ e pee bulb nguahi ngɛ zugba a mi.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain or shade trees alongside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantains loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are delicate and burn easily in direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains acts like an umbrella, protecting the cocoa from intense heat and keeping moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ hu tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Buu kookoo he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa

english: What is the difference between traditional cocoa trees and the hybrid cocoa varieties?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ blema kookoo tsei kɛ kookoo henɔi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ ateŋ?

english: Hybrid cocoa trees are bred to produce pods much faster—often within 2 to 3 years instead of 5 years—and they produce higher yields while standing up better against common pests and dry weather.
ga: Akwɛ cacao tsei ni akɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi ebɔ he lɛ koni amɛwo ŋmeii oya kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, amɛhiɔ shi afii 2 kɛyashi 3 yɛ afii 5 najiaŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ.

english: Why are the pods on my cocoa trees turning black and rotting before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet and overly shaded conditions. Trimming excess branches to let air and sunlight in, along with applying approved fungicides, stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la abote mli Kɛfata tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ he. Ebaaye ebua ni akpa helai gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why are the stems on my cocoa trees swelling and the leaves turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ashishifãi lɛ efu ni baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Swollen stems and yellow patterned leaves are symptoms of the Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease. Because it is spread by tiny insects called mealybugs and has no cure, affected trees must be safely removed to stop it from infecting healthy trees nearby.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni efuu kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji kookoo hela ni efuu lɛ he okadii. Ejaakɛ kooloi bibii ji mɛi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa. Atsɛɔ nakai tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akɛ mealybugs ni tsamɔ ko bɛ kɛha amɛ. No hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe koni tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why should I cut off the small vertical shoots growing out of my cocoa tree stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ mli lɛ

english: Those shoots, called chupons, steal water and nutrients from the main tree without producing many pods. Cutting them off forces the tree to send its energy into making healthy flowers and heavy pods.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli ni ekɛ ŋmeii babaoo baaa. Kɛ́ afo amɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ anyɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo fɔfɔi ni mli wa kɛ ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Weeds should be cleared regularly, especially during the rainy season, because they steal fertilizer and water from the soil and create damp hiding places for dangerous pests.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ daa. Titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ be mli Enɛ ji akɛ, jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni amɛfee hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ kɛha kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ.

english: If your cocoa leaves are turning pale, growth has slowed down, or your pods remain small despite good rainfall, the soil lacks nutrients. Applying specialized cocoa fertilizer at the start of the rains helps restore soil strength.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cocoa baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, amɛdaraa blɛoo Aloo ŋmeii lɛ daraaa bibii lolo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ. tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛ ko fata he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed extra flowers they cannot support, but heavy flower loss usually means the tree lacks water, fertilizer, or tiny pollinating insects like midges to fertilize the blooms.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, kookoo tso lɛ baawo fɔfɔi babaoo kɛyashi be mli ni anyɛŋ akɛto he. Shi bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi babaoo ni laajeɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ aná ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Can I grow root crops like cassava inside my mature cocoa farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ ni eda lɛ mli?

english: Growing cassava in a mature cocoa farm is not recommended because cassava roots spread aggressively, competing with cocoa for nutrients and disturbing cocoa roots when harvested.
ga: Akɛ ŋaawoo haaa akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji ni eda lɛ amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa waa. Akɛ kookoo akaŋ kɛha niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ogbala kookoo shishifãi lɛ amli kɛji akpa

english: What happens if I leave ripe cocoa pods on the trees for too long before harvesting?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani mikpa?

english: Leaving ripe pods on the tree causes the beans inside to germinate or rot, which ruins their quality and attracts disease that can quickly spread to the rest of your crop.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ loo amɛgboi. Enɛ haa nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa shi ni egbalaa helai ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ amli oya.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is an essential food plants need to grow strong. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves regain their green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni eha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomatoes turning black and soft before the fruit even ripens?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ bɔdɔɔ dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant or irregular soil moisture. Keeping the soil consistently watered and adding agricultural lime or compost can help fix this problem.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ tsei amli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ejaaa. Kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu daa ni akɛ lime loo okwaayeli mli ŋmeii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily in direct sunshine. Planting food crops like plantains beside young cocoa provides living shade and traps soil moisture, protecting the cocoa until it gets older and stronger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ Young cocoa tsei lɛ ahe lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná hulutsoo ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Buu kookoo lɛ he kɛyashi ebaada ni ená hewalɛ.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to produce energy to grow big tubers under the ground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp soil, exposing them to more light and preventing leaf fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwo bulbs wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enáa la babaoo ni etsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: What is causing the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up tightly and stop growing leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekpaa baai lɛ adalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the sap, or a virus spread by these insects. Spraying neem oil extract or recommended pesticides can control the insects and protect new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. loo helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Akɛ neem mu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ kooloi lɛ ni etsĩ shweremɔ hee naa.

english: Why are small holes appearing inside my harvested maize grains after storing them for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Eje kpo yɛ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ amli beni mikɛto otsii fioo komɛi sɛɛ.

english: Small holes in stored grain are caused by maize weevils that hatch inside the grain and eat their way out. Drying your maize until it is very hard and storing it in airtight bags or sealed containers prevents these pests from surviving.
ga: Buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmaa ni ato lɛ mli lɛ jɛɔ ŋmãa mli ŋmeii ni shwereɔ yɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ejeɔ kpo lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa kɛyashi ebaawa waa ni okɛwo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo nɔ ko ni atsĩ naa mli lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkajo foi.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and store it naturally in the soil. When you plant maize afterwards, the maize feeds on this stored soil nitrogen, giving you a better crop yield.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ ŋmãa baaye nitrogen ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa onine shɛɔ nitsumɔ kpakpa nɔ.

english: Weeds act like extra hungry plants that steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight away from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your main crop gets all the nutrients it needs to grow big.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsei ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ waa, ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why should I spread dry grass or leaves on top of the soil around my garden vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle mihe lɛ nɔ lɛ? aduawai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass is called mulching. It keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, prevents water from drying out quickly, stops weeds from growing, and rots into free plant food.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekagbi oya Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkafite ni amɛtsɔ tsei aniyenii

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are mature enough to be dug up for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mafo mli koni akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety. You will notice the lower leaves turning yellow and dropping off, and the soil around the base of the stem cracking as the underground tubers grow big.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Edamɔ henɔi lɛ anɔ Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli gbalaa kɛ́ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei lɛ da.

english: How do I choose the best seeds for planting corn so that I get a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala dumɔwui ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii koni maná yibii kpakpai?

english: To get a good corn yield, buy certified seeds from accredited dealers or choose well-matured, fully dried seeds from healthy, high-yielding crops. Avoid using small, cracked, or insect-damaged seeds.
ga: Bɔni afee ni oná ŋmãa kpakpa Be fɛɛ be lɛ, hemɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ jarayelɔi ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ adɛŋ. Aloo halamɔ dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni egbi kwraa kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ amli. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ dumɔwui bibii, ni egbɛ eshwa, loo ni kooloi efite lɛ ahe.

english: How can I save good quality pepper seeds from my harvest to plant next season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ pepper dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ mikpamɔ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Select fully ripe, healthy pepper fruits from your best plants, extract the seeds, clean them, and dry them thoroughly in a shaded area. Store them in airtight containers with ash or drying agents to keep pests away.
ga: Halamɔ pepper aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ kwraa, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ otsei ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ amli. Jiemɔ dumɔwui lɛ, otsumɔ amɛhe, ni ogbi yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli ni sũ loo nɔ ko ni haa egbiɔ lɛ awo mli koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote mli.

english: What should I do to my land before planting pepper seeds so they sprout properly?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee mishikpɔŋ lɛ dani madu pepper dumɔwui koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Clear the bush, remove weeds, and till the soil to break up hard earth. Mix in decomposed manure or compost to make the soil soft and rich in nutrients before sowing seeds.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ jwɛi lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ, ni otsu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii koni ekɛgbala shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afutu mli koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo aba mli dani odu dumɔwui.

english: Why is it important to follow proper row spacing when planting corn on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ato ŋmãa lɛ he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting in organized rows with proper spacing ensures every corn plant gets enough sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, while making weeding and harvesting much easier.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo ni gbɛ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa naa hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: What kind of soil condition gives the best results for crops like corn and pepper?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ shihilɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ?

english: Crops thrive best in well-drained, dark, loamy soil rich in organic matter. Soil that holds moisture without getting waterlogged helps roots grow deep and strong.
ga: Tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni mli edɔ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni nu bɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do some of my corn stalks produce big cobs while others right next to them stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ekomɛi woɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ ji bibii waa lɛ?

english: Uneven plant size is usually caused by planting seeds at uneven depths, unequal fertilizer application, or weed competition early in the plant's growth stage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei lɛ adalɛi ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ jɛɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ hei srɔtoi ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli baa. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ fɔmɔ kotoku mli lɛ kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee. aloo akaŋshii kɛha jwɛi yɛ tsei lɛ adalɛ shishijee mli

english: Why are my pepper plants flowering but taking a long time to show small fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi shi eheɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii bibii lɛ?

english: Delayed fruiting can happen due to high temperatures, lack of consistent watering, or insufficient soil nutrients like potassium and phosphorus needed during the flowering stage.
ga: Yibiiwoo ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ baanyɛ aba yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa tamɔ potassium kɛ phosphorus bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli.

english: How can I protect my newly planted seeds from pests in the soil before they grow?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu midumɔwui heei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe dani amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Treating seeds with approved seed dressings before planting or mulching the soil lightly can protect seeds from insects, birds, and fungal infections.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui ahe ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii dani odu loo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli tseee. Ebaanyɛ ebu dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛ kooloi, okpoi kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Where can I watch or learn proper modern farming methods if I cannot travel to demonstration farms?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ makwɛ loo makase ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli gbɛi ni sa? Kɛji akɛ onyɛɛɛ oya nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Many agricultural extension initiatives broadcast step-by-step practical farming guides on local television channels like UTV, as well as community radio stations.
ga: Okwaayeli mlilɛɛmɔ gbɛjianɔtoi babaoo jieɔ okwaayeli he gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii fiofio kpo yɛ maŋ lɛ mli tɛlivishiŋ nɔ tamɔ UTV kɛ agbɛnɛ akutso lɛ mli redio nitsumɔhei.

english: When is the right time for an extension worker to come check my farm work?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni sɛɛgbɛ nitsulɔ ko baakwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: It is best for extension officers to visit during land preparation, early planting, and flowering stages so they can spot issues early and advise you on proper field maintenance.
ga: Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni aha maŋ onukpa ko abasara bo yɛ be mli ni asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ, dumɔ mra, kɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛbaanyɛ amɛyoo naagbai mra. ni ekɛ ŋaawoo aha yɛ ŋmɔ mli saamɔ ni sa he.

english: Why shouldn't I plant three or four maize seeds right next to each other in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yibii etɛ loo ejwɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants compete with each other for space, sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This overcrowding results in thin, weak stems and very small ears of corn.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko, hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa toi bibii waa.

english: The small shoots, called suckers, draw water and food away from the main plantain tree. Removing most of them leaves only one or two strong suckers, allowing the main tree to produce large, healthy bunches of plantains.
ga: Tsobii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ he. Kɛ́ ajie emli babaoo lɛ, ebaashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha tso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of a maize plant usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer helps the plant stay green and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why should I mix animal manure or decomposed leaves into my soil before planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ kooloi ashishifãi loo baai ni egboi afutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Adding organic materials like manure or compost improves the soil's ability to hold moisture during dry periods and slowly feeds essential nutrients to your crops as they grow.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli, ni fiofio lɛ, ebaaha onibii ni he hiaa lɛ aya hiɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant maize on the exact same spot on my farm every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ he kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows specific pests and diseases to build up, leading to poorer yields over time.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on the sap under the leaves, or by a virus carried by these insects. Clearing weeds and managing pests early prevents this spread.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ latex ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ hiɛɔ lɛ nɔ Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe nitsumɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ nɛkɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, irregular watering, or lack of pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist and planting in suitable conditions helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. Nu ni ashwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni adu yɛ shihilɛ ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Weeds grow fast and steal nutrients, water, and sunlight directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your planted crops get all the field's resources for themselves.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛnii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I plant them in full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and sensitive to intense direct heat. They require shade crops, such as plantains, to shield them from excessive sunlight and keep the surrounding air humid during their early growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛnuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he tɛ̃ɛ he. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe jɔɔ, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo he. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ shishijee be mli ni edara lɛ

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when there is too much rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When water collects in the soil without draining away, it starves the roots of air and allows harmful fungi to attack the cassava tubers, causing them to rot under waterlogged conditions.
ga: Beni nu buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Enɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni ebaaha ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atutua ŋmeii lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfiteɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli.

english: Can I use leftover soybean husks on my farm instead of throwing them away?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ soybean ŋmeii ni eshwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii moŋ fe ni mashɛrɛ ashwie?

english: Yes, soybean husks are rich in organic matter and nitrogen. Spreading them over your field or digging them into the soil helps feed your crops as they rot down and helps the ground hold onto water during dry spells.
ga: Hɛɛ, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ nitrogen babaoo yɛ soybean ŋmeii amli. Kɛ́ ogbɛ amɛ oshwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli loo okɛ amɛ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛgboi, ni ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ nu mli yɛ hɔmɔ be mli.

english: Why do crops grow much taller and greener in spots where farm waste was previously dumped?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii miiya hiɛ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔji yɛ he ni tsutsu lɛ ŋmɔ mli jwɛi yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Decaying plant waste, like bean shells and crop stalks, breaks down into natural food for the dirt called organic matter. It releases trapped nutrients back into the ground, acting like natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Tsei amli jwɛi ni fiteɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsei ahe ŋmeii Efoɔ mli ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha muji ni atsɛɔ lɛ organic matter. Ebaajie niyenii mli nibii ni emɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Is it safe to mix cooked or boiled crop residues back into my soil before planting?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛ tso ni ahoo loo ahoo lɛ mli nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ baafutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ dani adu?

english: Yes, cooked or processed plant residues are safe and actually break down faster in the soil than raw residues. As long as no salt or toxic chemicals were added during processing, they will enrich your soil with nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni ahoo loo atsu he nii lɛ ahe nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni amɛfiteɔ oya yɛ sũ lɛ mli fe nibii ni eshwɛ ni ahoo lɛ. Shii abɔ ni akɛ ŋoo loo tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei fataaa he yɛ be mli ni atsuɔ he nii lɛ. Enɛɛmɛi baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii babaoo.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and healthy. Rain helps plants take up water, but it cannot feed them if the nutrients are missing from the dirt.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Nugbɔ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmɔɔ nu. Shi anyɛɛɛ aha tsei niyenii kɛji niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ.

english: Why do my soybean plants produce plenty of green leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi soybean tso lɛ miiwo baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ ewoɔ lɛ?

english: This happens when there is too much nitrogen in the soil relative to phosphorus. Too much nitrogen causes the plant to spend all its energy growing leaves and stems instead of making flowers and bean pods.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛ akɛto phosphorus he. Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tsei kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii

english: Why do the leaves of my young crops droop and wilt during the afternoon hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibaai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: In the heat of the day, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can soak it up from dry soil. The plant wilts to save water, which is a sign your soil needs a layer of mulch to stay cool and moist.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Trees do not want to save water. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔtɔ koni eha edɔ ni edɔ.

english: What can I put on my soil to stop the hot sun from drying out my crop roots?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mikɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akagbi mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ?

english: You can cover the ground around your crops with dry crop leftovers like soybean husks, dry grass, or maize stalks. This organic cover, called mulch, shades the dirt, keeps it cool, and locks moisture in the root zone.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni eshwɛ tamɔ soybean ŋmɔshi nibii, jwɛi loo abele ŋmɔji atsu nii. Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛhaa nɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulch. It will help cover dirt. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shishifã lɛ he

english: Why do extension officers tell us to plant beans or groundnuts before planting maize on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mɛi akɛ amɛdu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii dani amɛdu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like beans and groundnuts have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. When you plant maize afterward, the maize eats the leftover nitrogen and grows much better without needing as much expensive chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ ŋmãa baaye nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ kwraa ni tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: How can I tell if my yellowing crops are suffering from pests or from poor soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi safron tsei lɛ miipiŋ kɛmiijɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli loo amɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ?

english: Insect attacks usually leave visible signs like chewed holes, webbing, or bugs under the leaves. Poor soil nutrition affects whole leaves or whole rows evenly, turning them pale green or yellow without physical leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ haa okadii ni anaa, tamɔ bu ni atsɔ mli, tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli, loo kooloi ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ saa baa loo ŋta muu lɛ fɛɛ he pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni ehaa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni efiteee baa lɛ.

english: Why are holes appearing in my bean leaves right after the plants start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-bean baai lɛ anɔ beni tso lɛ jeɔ fɔmɔ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Flowering attracts beetles and caterpillars because the plant becomes sweet and tender. These insects feed on leaves during this growth stage, so applying early organic repellents like wood ash or neem extract can keep them away.
ga: Efɔfɔi lɛ gbalaa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ejaakɛ tso lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni ŋɔɔ, ni ebɛ mlɛo. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ baai yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ helai tamɔ tso mli sũ loo neem mli nu tsu nii mra lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsĩ amɛnaa.

english: How do I know when my oil palm fresh fruit bunches are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni FFB lɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaakpa?

english: You know an oil palm bunch is ripe when a few loose fruits naturally drop off the bunch to the ground. The individual fruits will also change color from a dark blackish-purple to a bright orange-red.
ga: Ekolɛ ole akɛ mu tsei akui lɛ ekwɛ̃ kɛ́ aduawai lɛ gbee shikpɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Yibii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko tsakeɔ su kɛjɛɔ purple-black ni mli kwɔ mli kɛyaa orange-red ni mli tse nɔ.

english: Why does my young oil palm tree produce flowers that dry up without growing any palm nuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ni egboi ni ehe ehiaaa ni madu tso lɛ kwraa lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees produce separate male and female flowers on the same tree. Young or stressed trees often produce only male flowers first to supply pollen, which do not form fruits themselves.
ga: Mu tsei woɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi yɛ tso kome nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, tsei bibii loo tsei ni haoɔ amɛhe lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi hii pɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii akɛ pollen. ni kɛ nɔ ko ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ baaa yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ emli

english: Young cocoa leaves are sensitive and lose moisture faster than small root systems can drink from the soil. They need shade trees like plantain or cassava around them to block harsh direct sunlight while they establish.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛfiteɔ nu oya fe shishifãi bibii lɛ. ni abaanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo yucca ni ebɔle amɛhe. Koni ekɛtsi hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ naa be mli ni edaa lɛ.

english: Why do the small cocoa pods on my tree turn black and shrivel before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is often caused by a fungal infection called black pod disease, which spreads quickly in damp, shady conditions, or by the tree shedding excess pods it cannot support with water and nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela kɛbaa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ loo kɛ́ tsei shwie ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with bushy leaves but give me very small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or water, cassava puts all its energy into growing green leaves above ground instead of storing food down in the root tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen loo nu babaoo lɛ Yucca kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baawo baai eŋɔli ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds away from my yam vines and give them wooden stakes to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mijie jwɛi kakadaji ni yɔɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ amli lɛ ni mikɛ tsei ma shi koni amɛkwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines climb stakes so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight. Sunlit leaves produce food that travels down to make big tubers, while weeds steal soil food and block sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Baai ni hulu lɛ ewo mli lɛ woɔ niyenii ni tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi ni efeɔ bulbs agboi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, jwɛi juɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la naa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow starting from the middle vein?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts at the leaf tips and moves down the central vein is a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen is necessary for plants to stay green and produce strong leaves.
ga: Yellowing ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baa lɛ naagbee ni eyaa shishi kɛyaa shishigbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni ale waa ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia koni tsei ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Cowpea roots work with natural soil organisms to pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acting as a natural green fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Cowpea shishifãi kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: The extra shoots, called suckers, fight with the main parent plant for nutrients and water. Removing extra suckers leaves enough food for the main stem to produce a larger, heavier bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ kɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajieɔ tsei ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha tso lɛ yitso lɛ koni efee kuu agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl upwards and look twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni efite lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites feeding on the sap underneath tender leaves, or by a virus carried by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ latex ni yɔɔ baai bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ hiɛ lɛ nɔ

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight and wind. Plantains grow fast with broad leaves that shade the young cocoa, keeping the soil cool and moist so the seedlings can establish strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Plantain lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa kookoo bibioo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ afee shishifãi ni wa.

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that thrives in wet, overly shady conditions. Pruning extra tree branches lets sunshine and air in, which keeps the pods dry and reduces the disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ tsɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Niji krokomɛi ni afoɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa helai baa shi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to grow leaves. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer near the base gives the crop the food it needs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni baai lɛ akwɛ̃ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo nitrogen ŋmãa fata he ni bɛŋkɛ shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know when my maize is fully ripe and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Maize is ready when the outer husks turn brown and dry, and the silk at the top becomes dark brown. If you press a grain with your fingernail and no milky liquid comes out, the corn is dry and mature.
ga: Abɛi lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi. ni siliki ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ. Kɛ okɛ onineshi tsɔne nyɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ ni nu ko ni tamɔ mliki ejeee kpo lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbi ni edɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay small and thin instead of swelling up big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo moŋ fe ni amɛaafee wuji ni amɛfuu lɛ?

english: Cassava roots struggle to grow in hard, packed soil. Loosening the earth deeply before planting creates soft ground that allows the roots to expand freely into thick tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ dani adu lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ blɛoo ni haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛshwereɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse.

english: How do I tell if my yam crop is ready for harvesting under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yam tubers are ready when the leaves and vines above the ground dry up and turn yellow. This tells you the plant has finished putting energy into growing the tuber beneath the soil.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ egbi ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ bo akɛ tso lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛduɔ e-bulbs lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ naa.

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from under the leaves. Spraying the plants with mild soapy water or neem oil helps clear the pests so the leaves can grow straight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Kɛ okɛ nu ni mli ejɔ loo neem fɔ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie tsɛŋemɔ helai koni baai lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too hot or when the plant gets irregular water. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and giving the plants steady water helps flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ nu daa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni okɛ nu ha tso lɛ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni ehiɛ fɔfɔi kɛ eyibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops wilt during the hottest part of the afternoon even when the soil isn't completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbiko kwraa po?

english: In intense sun, crops lose water from their leaves faster than roots can draw it from the soil. Placing dry grass or straw around the base of the crop retains moisture and protects root stems from excessive heat.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ nu kɛjɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi loo jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ shishifã lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine he.

english: Why do my plantain plants easily fall over when strong winds and rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ miinɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit bunches at the top, making them unbalanced. Supporting the main stalk with a sturdy wooden or bamboo pole prevents the plant from snapping or uprooting.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akuu ni tsii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. unbalance Kɛ́ okɛ tso loo ŋmei tso ni wa fi tso titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakumɔ loo eshishijee.

english: Why are my crops not growing big and green even though I weed my farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraaa ni eyɛ ŋmɔji eyɛ mli akɛ mifoɔ jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa moŋ?

english: Just like humans need food to grow strong, crops need extra nutrients from the soil to thrive. Over time, soil loses its natural food, so adding fertilizer is necessary to feed the plants and help them produce a good yield.
ga: Taakɛ niyenii he hiaa adesai koni amɛdara lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Niyenii nibii krokomɛi hu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he miihia koni eha tsei lɛ niyenii ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: What is the main difference between animal manure and store-bought chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ kooloi aŋmeii kɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ ateŋ?

english: Animal manure improves the soil structure slowly over a long period, while factory-made chemical fertilizers provide a concentrated, fast-acting boost of nutrients directly to the plant when it needs immediate food.
ga: Koolooi ashishifãi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ feɔ fɛo fiofio. yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ nitsumɔhei lɛ haa tsei lɛ niyenii ni mli wa ni tsuɔ nii oya lɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ́ niyenii he miihia amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers insist that I measure chemical fertilizer with a specific cup instead of just sprinkling it by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ mikɛ kɔɔpoo pɔtɛɛ ko asusu tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he moŋ fe ni mikɛ minine baagbɛ eshwã lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer is very powerful and concentrated. Using a specific cup ensures you give the plant the exact amount it needs; using too little won't help it grow, while using too much can burn and kill the roots.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ. Kɔɔpoo pɔtɛɛ ko ni okɛaatsu nii lɛ haa onáa nɔmimaa akɛ okɛ nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ haa otso lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nɔ ko fioo pɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeee ebuaaa lɛ ni eda. Shi kɛ akɛtsu nii fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ shishifãi lɛ ashã ni egbo.

english: Where exactly around my plant should I place the fertilizer so it works best?
ga: Nɛgbɛ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mitso lɛ he koni nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ aba?

english: Fertilizer should be placed a few centimeters away from the plant stem near the root zone, usually in a small hole or ring, so the roots can drink it safely without the concentrated chemical touching and damaging the main stem.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimitai 2-3, ni ebɛŋkɛ shishifã lɛ he. Bei pii lɛ, amɛyɔɔ bu bibii loo ŋwɛi ŋtayaai amli. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anu nu shweshweeshwe ni tsofai ni mli ewo wu lɛ akabɔ ni amɛkafite tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ.

english: What will happen to my maize if I put too much fertilizer on a single plant?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa babaoo wo tso kome mli?

english: Applying too much fertilizer causes 'fertilizer burn' by pulling moisture out of the plant roots, which causes the leaves to turn yellow or brown and can dry out the plant completely.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo lɛ haa ‘ŋmei lɛ shãa’ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo asarasu. ni ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ agbi kwraa

english: Is it better to apply fertilizer when the soil is dry or right after it rains?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after rain because water is needed to dissolve the fertilizer so the plant roots can drink the nutrients.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ ejaakɛ eheɔ nu ni ekɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow even when there is enough rainfall on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves are often a sign that the plant is starving for key soil nutrients like nitrogen, which means the crop needs fertilizer to regain its healthy green color and continue growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ ni eda.

english: How long does it usually take to see changes in my crops after applying factory-made fertilizer?
ga: Be enyiɛ bei pii lɛ eheɔ dani minaa tsakemɔi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli beni mikɛ tsofa ewo tso lɛ mli sɛɛ?

english: Because chemical fertilizers dissolve quickly in moist soil, you can usually see greener leaves and stronger growth within one to two weeks after proper application.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya. Bei pii lɛ, obaana baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kɛ dalɛ ni mli wa yɛ otsi kome kɛyashi enyɔ mli kɛji akɛ okɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can using chemical fertilizer every season ruin my farmland over time?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa afi lɛ baanyɛ afite nibii ni midu lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: If you use chemical fertilizer continuously without adding organic matter like compost or crop remains, the soil can become hard and acidic over time, so mixing both methods keeps the soil healthy long-term.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsu nii be fɛɛ be ni okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni wa ni efee acidic yɛ be ni sa mli. No hewɔ lɛ, gbɛi enyɔ lɛ ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why do cassava and maize need different kinds of care and fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa biɔ kwɛmɔ kɛ ŋmãa sɔrɔtoi lɛ?

english: Different crops feed differently; leaf crops like maize need high nitrogen to grow tall and produce grain, while root crops like cassava need potassium to swell and form big tubers under the ground.
ga: Akɛ niyenii srɔtoi haa ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi. Nibii ni yɔɔ baai, tamɔ ŋmãa, biɔ nitrogen babaoo koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛwo dumɔwui. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi, tamɔ ŋmei lɛ, potassium he miihia amɛ koni amɛfu ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: How can I tell if a mango tree growing on my farm is a local variety or a hybrid one?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mango tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji maŋbii loo tsei ni akɛfee tsofai krokomɛi?

english: Local mango trees usually grow very tall, take many years to fruit, and produce smaller, fibrous fruits. Hybrid varieties are generally shorter, bear larger and smoother fruits much earlier, and often have distinct leaves when young.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, maŋ lɛ mli mango tsei lɛ daraa waa. Eheɔ afii babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii. ni amɛwoɔ aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ fiber Hybrid henɔi lɛ fɔɔ kuku. Ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli babaoo ni ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli. Ni bei pii lɛ, amɛyɛ baai srɔtoi beni amɛdarako lolo lɛ.

english: What is the difference between planting traditional local seeds and buying improved hybrid seeds for my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli kusum dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni aheɔ kɛhaa miŋmɔ lɛ teŋ?

english: Local seeds come from crops already growing in your region and are very tough, but they take longer to produce and yield less fruit. Hybrid seeds are specially bred to grow faster, resist diseases, and give you a much bigger harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ jɛɔ tsei ni miida momo yɛ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ amli, ni amɛhe wa waa. Shi eheɔ be babaoo dani anyɛɔ afeɔ, ni etsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛdara oya, amɛte shi amɛwo helai, ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do cocoa trees grow better under the shade of big forest trees instead of in full sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ koo mli tsei wuji ashishi moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ̃ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa naturally comes from forest environments where bigger trees block intense heat. Young cocoa trees have sensitive leaves that scorch easily in direct sun, so forest shade keeps them cool and retains soil moisture.
ga: Cocoa jɛɔ koo mli shihilɛ ni tsei wuji tsiɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa lɛ naa lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. No hewɔ lɛ, koo lɛ mli hɔnɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo tsei lɛ amli jɔɔ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi.

english: Do young mango trees need shade from bigger forest trees when they are small, just like cocoa does?
ga: Ani mango tso bibioo ko he miihia ni ená hulutsoo kɛjɛ koo mli tso agbo ko mli beni eji bibioo lolo tamɔ kookoo lɛ?

english: Unlike cocoa, mango trees naturally love full sunlight and build deep roots to handle heat. While tiny seedlings benefit from temporary shade during harsh dry weather, mango trees need direct sun to grow strong and bear plenty of fruit.
ga: Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ kookoo tsei lɛ, yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, mango tsei sumɔɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛkpee hulutsoo be lɛ naa. Eyɛ mli akɛ eji dumɔwu bibioo moŋ Enáa be kukuoo mli hulutsoo be mli hulutsoo be mli he sɛɛ. Shi hulu la he miihia mango tsei tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do some fruit trees take almost ten years to bear fruit while others start fruiting in just two or three years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni woɔ yibii lɛ heɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ afii nyɔŋma dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ekomɛi jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Trees grown straight from seeds spend years growing deep roots and trunks before they are mature enough to fruit. Grafted or hybrid trees come from branches of already mature trees, allowing them to skip that long waiting period.
ga: Tsei ni jɛ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ baa dani amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛwoɔ yibii. Tsei ni akɛwo mli loo ni akɛwo mli lɛ jɛɔ tsei ni eda lɛ aniji amli. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ otsi nakai mɛmɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ naa.

english: Why do local wild trees survive the long dry season better than the new high-yielding crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli fe tsei heei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Local trees have spent generations adapting to the local climate, growing deep taproots that find water far underground. High-yielding varieties focus more energy on producing heavy fruits, which makes them need more water and care.
ga: Ehe yinɔi babaoo dani jɛmɛ tsei lɛ nyɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo jɛmɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ taproot ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Henɔi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa hewalɛ babaoo nɔ yɛ yibii ni tsii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ehe hiaa ni ana nu babaoo kɛ ekwɛmɔ.

english: Can I plant different varieties of mango trees together on the same piece of land without them spoiling each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu mango tsei srɔtoi yɛ he kome ni mifiteee amɛhe?

english: Yes, planting different mango varieties together will not spoil the fruit on your trees. However, if you collect seeds from those fruits to plant new trees later, the new trees will be a natural mixture of both varieties.
ga: Hɛɛ, mango henɔi srɔtoi ni ooodu yɛ he kome lɛ efiteŋ yibii ni yɔɔ otso lɛ nɔ lɛ. Shi, kɛji obua dumɔwui anaa kɛjɛ nakai aduawai lɛ amli koni okɛdu tsei heei yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ, Tso hee lɛ baafee adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni akɛ tsofai enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ efutu.

english: How can I know which crop variety is best suited for the soil and rainfall in my part of Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei srɔtoi ni sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha shikpɔŋ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: You can look at which traditional trees thrive naturally in your area's forests and consult local extension officers, who test which improved varieties are bred specifically for your region's rain patterns and soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona nɔ ni ji maŋ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kooi ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ amli lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni obi he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ. Ekaa tsei srɔtoi ni atsɔse amɛ pɔtɛɛ kɛha nugbɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ ekwɛɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young trees look so soft and broad compared to the tough leaves on older trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo waa ni egbɛ eshwa kɛ akɛto baai ni wa ni yɔɔ mi tsei wuji lɛ anɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Young plants grow soft, broad leaves to catch as much sunlight as possible while growing fast. As the tree matures, its new leaves become thicker and tougher to conserve water and protect against hot winds.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ kwɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni mli kwɔ koni amɛmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa oya lɛ. Kɛ tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Baai heei lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ewa akɛ amɛaahiɛ nu mli ni amɛtsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why does my farmland produce very tall trees with very few fruits compared to my neighbor's shorter, heavily fruiting trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ waa ni woɔ yibii fioo kɛ akɛto mikutsoŋbii lɛ tsei kukuji ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Trees that grow very tall with little fruit are usually unpruned local varieties or are stretching upward to compete for sunlight. Shorter, heavy-fruiting trees are typically grafted hybrids designed to spend energy on making fruit rather than growing tall stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ waa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo lɛ ji shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei ni afolɔɔɔ amɛhe loo ashɛɛɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akaŋ. Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ kuku ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ ji tsei ni akɛ amɛhe ewo mli ni afee koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ awo yibii moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ̃ tsei ni kɛlɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I plant them in an open field without trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under full sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or large trees around them to act as natural sunshades and keep the soil moist while the cocoa roots mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei wuji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize crop lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. Adding compost or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore the green color and improves grain production.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha dumɔwui lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Curled leaves with patches of yellow indicate Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava stems for planting helps prevent this problem from ruining your harvest.
ga: Baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ. Nɔ ni tsɔɔ cassava mosaic hela ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kɛ́ okɛ cassava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ tsu nii yɛ odumɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni naagba nɛɛ akafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Can I plant groundnuts or beans in the same field alongside my maize crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ ŋmei masɛi?

english: Yes, planting legumes like groundnuts alongside maize is very beneficial because legumes naturally pull nitrogen from the air into the soil, which helps feed the maize and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni akɛfataa ŋmeii ahe lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into fruit during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and lack of water cause stress to tomato plants, making them drop their flowers to conserve energy. Regular watering at the root level and applying mulch around the plants keeps the soil cool and helps fruit form.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa tomato shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa yɛ shishifã lɛ he kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle he lɛ. Tsei yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Should I save seeds from my current hybrid maize harvest to plant again next season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akpaa lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: It is better to buy fresh certified hybrid seeds each season. Seeds saved from a hybrid harvest lose their vigor, resulting in uneven growth and much lower crop yields in the second generation.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni akɛwo mli ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ daa afi. Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ hybrid ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ hewalɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi kwraa yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds from my crop field early while the plants are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔji amli mra? Yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ ji bibioo lolo lɛ, ehe miihia

english: Weeds grow fast and steal vital soil nutrients, sunlight, and water from young crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your main crops get everything they need to grow strong root systems.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, hulu la, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ehaa tso ni hereɔ lɛ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Why shouldn't I build my yam mounds very close to one another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ matswaa ŋmeii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need ample room underground to expand. If mounds are too close, the roots compete for space, water, and nutrients, resulting in smaller tubers at harvest time.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Kɛji gɔŋ lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa ŋmeii bibii baa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are ready to be dug up from the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is typically mature when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and cracks begin to appear in the soil around the base of the main stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ daa kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. Ni ŋmeii bɔi baa yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to loosen the soil before planting my vegetable seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani madu aduawai dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Loosening hard soil allows air and rainwater to sink deeper into the ground, making it much easier for fragile young plant roots to push through and draw up food.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ nu boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa tsei bibii ni shishifãi ni waaa lɛ akɛ amɛaatsɔ mli ni amɛjie niyenii.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and dying when the sun is very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby creates a living umbrella that shields young cocoa plants from heat and keeps the soil moist while they establish roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Does it matter which direction I point cassava stems when I stick them in the soil?
ga: Beni aduɔ ŋmei tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ Ani ehe miihia ni atsɔɔ he ko?

english: Yes, cassava stems have small buds or 'eyes' that must point upwards toward the sky. Planting stems upside down forces the new shoots to grow downward first, which weakens the plant and leads to very low crop yields.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ‘hiŋmɛii’ ni esa akɛ amɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ yitso lɛ hiɛ shi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii heei akwɛ̃ shi klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: Why do I need to clear my field and tie wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo ŋmɔji lɛ amli ni mafi tsei ahe tsɔi koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy for growing tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves elevated off the damp ground, preventing leaf diseases and maximizing sunlight exposure so tubers grow big and healthy.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking haa baai lɛ teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Tsi foliar helai anaa ni oha hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo. Koni yitso lɛ adara ni ehiɛ hewalɛ

english: Is it better for me to water my tomato plants in the early morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ nu leebi maŋkpa loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning allows the soil to absorb moisture before the sun gets too hot. Watering during the hot afternoon causes water to evaporate rapidly before roots can take it in, and can stress the plant.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani hulu lɛ mli woɔ la tsɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ haomɔ aba tso lɛ nɔ

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the corn is ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, which is essential for green leafy growth. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores this nutrient so the maize can form full, healthy cobs.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha niyenii nɛɛ aku sɛɛ aba koni ekɛ ŋmei ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ mikɛ mi-corn lɛ adu cowpeas loo beans lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans naturally pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them with maize works like free fertilizer, enriching the soil for your maize without costing extra money.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans Ejɛɔ ebɔɔ su mli ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni akɛ ŋmãa haa lɛ yaka. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ sɛɛnamɔ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmãa ni afiteee shika kroko.

english: Why should I let cleared weeds rot on my farm instead of burning them with fire?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maha jwɛi ni ajie lɛ lɛ agbo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mashã amɛ yɛ la mli lɛ?

english: Burning weeds destroys rich organic matter and kills helpful organisms living in the soil. Allowing weeds to rot creates natural mulch that holds moisture, cools the ground, and decomposes into rich food for your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo lɛ, ni egbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni hiɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ jwɛi lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi lɛ baa. shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ niyenii ni jara wa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What is making ragged holes in the middle whorl of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworms, which feed deep inside the central leaf funnel of young maize. Applying recommended organic treatments or targeted sprays early in the morning into the funnel stops them before they ruin the whole plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ nii kɛyaa ŋmãa bibii lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee loo tsofa ko ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ leebi lɛ wo ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ, ebaatsi amɛnaa dani amɛbaakpãtã tso muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ.

english: How do I select the best shoot from an old plantain bush to start a new crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ plantain tso momo ko mli koni mikɛje tso hee shishi?

english: Look for 'sword suckers' that have narrow, sword-like leaves and a thick base. Avoid suckers with broad, flat leaves because they carry less energy from the parent plant and take much longer to produce fruit.
ga: Taomɔ ‘klante ŋmei’ ni baai lɛ mli tse ni tamɔ klante kɛ shishigbɛ ni mli tse. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ahe ejaakɛ amɛheɔ hewalɛ fioo kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli, ni amɛheɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves roll up tightly into a ball during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni efeɔ bɔɔlu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling in pepper plants is often caused by tiny insects like mites or whiteflies sucking the juices from under the leaves, or by extreme water stress. Keeping the plant roots mulched and using insecticidal soap helps protect the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛŋ ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ nu mli haomɔ ni naa wa mli Kɛ́ ooha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ ni okɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ atsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe.

english: When heavy machines clear my land before I plant, does it affect how my crops will grow in that soil?
ga: Beni tsɔnei ni tsii tsuɔ nii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛduɔ tsei lɛ Ani ebaana ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ adalɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Heavy machinery can pack the soil down tightly, making it difficult for crop roots to breathe and absorb water. Loosening the soil after clearing helps roots spread easily and grow strong.
ga: Tsɔnei ni tsii baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei shishifãi akɛ amɛaamu ni amɛŋɔ nu. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo yɛ be mli ni ajie lɛ sɛɛ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: If I clear all vegetation off my land completely every season, will my crops keep yielding well?
ga: Kɛji mijie tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ daa be. Ani midumɔ nii lɛ baawo yibii kpakpai lolo?

english: Clearing all plant material continuously strips the soil of its natural nutrients. Leaving healthy crop residues or planting cover crops helps restore fertility to the land.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie tsei amli nibii fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. Nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ashiɔ loo nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees stop growing and need to be cut down after producing just one bunch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ ni ehe hiaa ni afolɔ amɛ beni amɛwo ŋmeii kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A plantain stem naturally produces fruit only once in its lifecycle. Cutting down or uprooting the main stem after harvest directs water and nutrients to the young suckers at the base so they can grow into new fruiting plants.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli plantain tso lɛ shishifã lɛ woɔ yibii shikome pɛ yɛ ewala be mli. Afo loo ajieɔ tso titri lɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. koni eha amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ tsei heei ni woɔ yibii

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and scorching in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hulu lɛ shãa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants get burnt under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa protects the tender leaves until the trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ baashã kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi tsei lɛ baadara.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop during the hot afternoon even when the soil is slightly moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo moŋ?

english: In intense heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the ground. Drooping is the plant's natural defense mechanism to reduce water loss until temperatures cool down.
ga: Yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Drooping ji tso adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe koni ekɛba nu ni efiteɔ lɛ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli baa shi.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings wilt and die shortly after I transplant them from the nursery to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Moving seedlings causes transplant shock because root hairs get damaged. Watering seedlings before moving them, transplanting during cool late afternoons, and providing temporary shade helps them survive.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajieɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ baa ejaakɛ shishifãi ahe yitsɔi lɛ efite. Nu ni awoɔ dumɔwui amli dani aduɔ Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shwane mli ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli Ni hulutsoo be kukuoo mli hulutsoo ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my crops so I do not uproot them too early?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ? Bɔni afee ni mikajie oya tsɔ?

english: Crops give visual signals when mature, such as leaves turning yellow, stems drying out, or fruit changing color. Uprooting crops before these signs appear results in lower yields and poorer quality.
ga: Tsei haa okadii ni anaa beni amɛdaraa lɛ, tamɔ baai ni tsakeɔ ŋmɔŋ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni gbɛ́ɔ, loo aduawai ni tsakeɔ amɛhe su. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ dani okadii nɛɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi, ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ hu ehiii kwraa.

english: How can I stop my yam tubers from rotting underground before harvest time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpa?

english: Yam tubers rot when standing water settles around them in the soil. Planting yams on raised mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away, keeping the tubers safe.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni ekã shi lɛ ba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Sweet potato ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ babaoo. ni oha yitso lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe

english: Is it good to plant cassava and maize together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaadu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping maize and cassava works well because maize grows fast and is harvested early, leaving plenty of room, light, and nutrients for the slower-growing cassava to develop.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya ni akpaa lɛ mra. Enɛ haa gbɛ, la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How do weeds actually harm my food crops if there is plenty of space on the farm?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye miniyenii ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji miyɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Weeds aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crop roots. Clearing weeds early ensures your food crops get all the nourishment they need to produce a good yield.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaha oniyenii tsei lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key food in the soil. When there is not enough food in the dirt, the plant pulls nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii titri ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa Tsei gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Yam tubers grow long and deep underground, so loose, soft soil in a high mound makes it easy for the tuber to expand freely without pushing against hard, compacted ground.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ amɛhe ni amɛtsiii shikpɔŋ ni wa ni edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees get burnt leaves when I clear all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shã beni mijie cacao tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight all day. Big trees act like natural umbrellas that shade the farm, cool the air, and keep the soil moist so the young cocoa leaves do not scorch.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ. Tsei wuji lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni haa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ. ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔɔ ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni kookoo baai bibii lɛ akashã.

english: Does it matter which way up I stick my cassava stems into the ground when planting?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ, ani abaadu ŋmei tsei lɛ yɛ gbɛ ko nɔ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, it matters a lot. Cassava stems have tiny growth buds that must point upwards toward the sky because that is where the branches sprout; planting them upside down makes it very hard for the plant to grow.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehe miihia waa. The cassava stem has tiny buds. Esa akɛ etsɔɔ ŋwɛi ejaakɛ jɛmɛ ji he ni tsei niji lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ da ni etsɔ hiɛ lɛ, ebaaha ewa waa kɛha tso lɛ akɛ ebaada.

english: If too many small shoots grow around one plantain, they all fight for the same soil food and water, leaving you with small bunches. Keeping only two or three healthy shoots ensures the main stem gets enough food to grow heavy plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso kome he lɛ, Amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. This leaves you with a small branch. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha tsei wuji ni akwɛɔ lɛ.

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant's juices. Removing affected leaves or spraying mild soapy water helps protect the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ajieɔ baai ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ loo akɛ samla ni mli ejɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ. It will help protect the trees.

english: Tomato flowers often drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. High stress causes the plant to drop its flowers to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Haomɔ ni mli wa haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my watermelons rot on the bottom side where they touch the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ miifite yɛ fã ni taa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Watermelons rot when they lie directly on wet soil because moisture, bugs, and damp dirt decay the skin. Placing dry grass or straw under each growing melon keeps it dry and protected.
ga: Watermelon lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Ejaakɛ hulutsoo, kooloi bibii, kɛ muji haa hewolo lɛ fiteɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo jwɛi wo melon fɛɛ melon shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehi shi ni ebu ehe.

english: Why do my groundnut plants push their stems into the soil after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ tsiɔ eshishifã lɛ ewoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni ewo fɔfɔi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut flowers open above ground so bees can pollinate them, but the nuts themselves only grow underground. Once pollinated, the flower stem bends down and buries itself in the dirt to form the groundnut pods.
ga: Peanut fɔfɔii lɛ gbeleɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ afee amɛ ŋmeii. Shi ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi pɛ. Kɛji akɛ pollination wo mli lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why does swamp rice grow so well standing in water while my other crops die if flooded?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ marsh rice lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu mli shi mi tsei krokomɛi lɛ gboiɔ kɛji nu shwie shi lɛ?
