english: Swamp rice plants have special hollow air tubes inside their stems that act like snorkels, carrying air from above the water surface down to their roots so they do not drown.
ga: Swamp rice tsei lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛmli ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ mumɔ tsɔnei. Kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ nu lɛ hiɛ ni ekɛbaa shi kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkabote nu lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: How many times can I plant and harvest crops on my land in a single year?
ga: Nibii enyiɛ manyɛ madu ni makpa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ afi kome mli?

english: In many parts of Ghana, crops are grown once a year during the main rainy season. However, in regions with two rainy seasons or where farmers use irrigation, you can plant and harvest twice in a single year.
ga: yɛ Ghana hei babaoo lɛ, aduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii shikome yɛ afi mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli. Shi, yɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ shii enyɔ loo hei ni okwaafoi kɛ nu shwieɔ shi lɛ, Obaanyɛ odu ni okpa nii shii enyɔ yɛ afi kome mli.

english: How do I know the right time of year to start planting my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male afi lɛ mli be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi tsei akwɛmɔ?

english: The best planting time depends on your local rainfall pattern. Planting usually begins after the first steady rains start, ensuring the soil remains moist enough for seeds to germinate and survive.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ damɔ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔ jeɔ shishi beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ eje shishi sɛɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Can I plant crops a second time in the same year if the rains come back?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ, ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ yɛ afi lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Yes, if your area experiences a second rainy season or if you choose quick-maturing crops, you can plant a second cycle to get another harvest within the same year.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ shii enyɔ nɔ loo kɛji akɛ ohala tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya. Obaanyɛ odu fã ni ji enyɔ lɛ koni okpa ekoŋŋ yɛ nakai afi lɛ nɔŋŋ mli.

english: Why do my crops suffer so much when the rains stop falling on time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ awui waa kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa yɛ be naa lɛ?

english: Crops need water to dissolve nutrients in the soil and transport them to their roots. Without timely rain, crops cannot feed themselves, leading to stunted growth or crop failure.
ga: Tsei hia nu koni eha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ atsɔ mli ni ekɛ amɛ aya amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ yɛ be mli lɛ Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraaa loo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ.

english: What happens to my planted seeds if a long dry spell hits right after planting?
ga: Mɛni baaba dumɔwui ni midu lɛ anɔ kɛji hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ba yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ?

english: Seeds need continuous moisture to sprout and establish strong roots. An unexpected dry spell right after planting can cause seeds to dry out in the soil or kill young seedlings.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa. Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ egbi amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo eha tsei bibii lɛ agboi.

english: How can I keep my crops growing when there is no rain falling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha minibii lɛ akwɛ̃ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: You can use basic irrigation techniques, such as collecting rainwater, fetching water from nearby streams, or using simple pumps to deliver water directly to your crops during dry periods.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ shishijee nu shwiemɔ gbɛi tamɔ nugbɔ nu ni ooobua naa, nu ni ooojie kɛjɛ faai ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ atsu nii. Aloo okɛ pɔmp ni yɔɔ mlɛo atsu nii ni okɛ nu aya onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Is there a way to help my soil hold water longer during hot days?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni aaatsɔ nɔ aye abua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli?

english: Adding compost or spreading dried leaves and grass around the base of your plants (mulching) helps block the sun, keeping the soil cool and locking in moisture longer.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he loo okɛ baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi shwie tso lɛ shishi (mulching) lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hulu lɛ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is it risky to start planting as soon as the very first rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaaje dumɔ shishi kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ pɛ?

english: The first rain can sometimes be a false start followed by weeks of sunshine. If you plant immediately, the dry period that follows will dry out the soil and kill your sprouts.
ga: Bei komɛi lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee amale shishijee. Hulu ni tsoɔ waa otsii komɛi nyiɛ enɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ Be ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni ebaanyɛ egbe tso bibioo lɛ.

english: Why do farmers in northern Ghana farm differently from farmers in the south?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ wuoyigbɛ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Northern Ghana has a different climate with a single, shorter rainy season compared to parts of the south. This means northern farmers must pick crops that mature quickly or survive with less water.
ga: Ghana Kooyigbɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ faaa kwraa kɛ akɛto kooyigbɛ hei lɛ ahe. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ kooyigbɛ lɛ ahala ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya loo ni baanyɛ ahi shi kɛ nu fioo.

english: What kinds of crops are best to plant if my area gets very little rain?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu kɛji nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛɔ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Drought-tolerant crops like millet, sorghum, groundnuts, and cowpeas are ideal for drier areas because they require much less water to grow compared to crops like maize or cocoa.
ga: Nibii ni nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, ŋmei, kɛ tsina ŋmei hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha hei ni nu egbi ejaakɛ amɛhe ehiaaa nu babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ fe ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo kookoo.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow and grow very thin when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ waa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, they compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition starves the plants, causing their leaves to turn yellow from nutrient lack and forcing them to grow tall and thin as they fight for light.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋshii mli. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ, akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei yeɔ hɔmɔ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. kɛ tsei ni anyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛkwɛ ni amɛfee mlɛo yɛ be mli ni amɛwuɔ amɛhaa la lɛ.

english: Early light rains can cause seeds to germinate, but if a dry spell immediately follows, the tender young seedlings will dry up and die. Waiting for consistent, heavy rains ensures the soil holds enough deep moisture to support root development.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo mra lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui akwɛ̃. Shi kɛji hɔmɔ ba ni nyiɛ Tender sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ji Tender lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni baa be fɛɛ be lɛ mɛmɔ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua shishifãi lɛ akwɛmɔ.

english: Why does my cassava grow big green leaves above ground but produces very small tubers under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes cassava plants to put all their energy into growing leaves and stems above ground. To get large underground tubers, the plant needs balanced nutrients like potassium, which encourages energy storage in the roots.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa ŋmei tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. koni anyɛ ana shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji Tsei lɛ he miihia ni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ja, tamɔ potassium, ni haa hewalɛ ni akɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do the leaves and vines of my yam plants die and dry up before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ egboi ni amɛgbi dani akpa lɛ?

english: When yam vines turn brown and dry up at the end of the season, it is a natural process showing that the plant has finished moving all its energy down into the root. This is the crop's natural signal that the yam tubers are fully mature and ready to dig up.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ Eji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ejie ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛba shi kɛtee shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ atsa.

english: Why do the small flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without forming cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee cacao ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa flowers fall off when the tree is stressed by excessive heat, long dry spells, or pest attacks from insects like mirids. Keeping adequate shade trees around cocoa plants helps lower temperature and retain moisture so flowers can turn into pods.
ga: Kookoo fɔfɔi bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ pollen Haa hulutsoo be ni ebɔle Cacao tso lɛ haa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ yaa nɔ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to produce a bunch when I leave weeds growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii beni mishiɔ jwɛi yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing shallow roots that steal water and soil nutrients meant for the plantain. Clearing a wide circle around the base of each sucker stops this competition, allowing the plantain to grow faster and fruit earlier.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni amɛdaraa oya ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha plantain lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie kooloo ko ni da ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ fɛɛ he lɛ, ebaakpa akaŋshii nɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa plantains lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii oya.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants wilt in the afternoon heat even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, pepper leaves lose moisture through evaporation faster than their roots can drink water from the soil. The temporary wilting is the plant's self-defense to reduce water loss, and the leaves usually bounce back when temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ fiteɔ nu yɛ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Be kukuoo mli ni egboɔ lɛ ji tso lɛ hebuu koni ekɛba nu ni elaajeɔ lɛ shi. Ni baai lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: What causes my tomato plant leaves to curl upward and turn light green or yellow?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi tomato tsei lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is commonly caused by the Leaf Curl Virus, which is carried and spread from plant to plant by tiny insects called whiteflies. Controlling these insects early prevents the virus from spreading across your garden.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Leaf Curl Virus, ni ji kooloo bibioo ko lɛ kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaatsi helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa obɔɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my stored cowpeas get full of small holes and turn into dust after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii ni ato lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ebaatsɔ sũ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: The holes are caused by cowpea weevils, small insects that lay eggs inside the seeds during or after harvest. The insect larvae eat the inside of the beans as they grow, which can be prevented by thoroughly drying the seeds and storing them in airtight containers.
ga: The holes are caused by cowpea weevils. Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi bibii ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ dumɔwui amli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli loo yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Lala lɛ yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Abaanyɛ atsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni agbiɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtoɔ tsinsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are insect pests attacking my cabbage crop more during the dry season than in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa mi-cabbage tsei lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Many crop pests, like diamondback moths, thrive and reproduce much faster in warm, dry conditions. Heavy rains also naturally wash small insects and their eggs off crop leaves, so dry weather allows pest populations to build up quickly.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui srɔtoi babaoo, tamɔ daimond ŋmei lɛ Daa ni efɔɔ oya waa yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ ni jɛmɛ egbi. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu haa kooloi bibii kɛ amɛwuji lɛ shwieɔ tsei ahe baai anɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. No hewɔ lɛ, shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ yaa hiɛ oya.

english: Seeds need moisture and warm soil to wake up. If planted too deep or in dry soil, the seed lacks the energy to push through the ground, causing slow or failed germination.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia ŋmɔtɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ koni amɛte shi. Kɛji akɛ adu shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ tsɔ loo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛtsi shikpɔŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them directly in the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby creates a living umbrella that protects the cocoa while its roots establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ emaa shi lɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a cry for food. It means the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen, or the plant is getting too much or too little water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji niyenii he foomɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ tsei lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo fioo tsɔ.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by stress from intense heat and lack of water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni faaa lɛ mli baa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize plants stay short and weak even when I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛhe waaa eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Water helps plants survive, but nutrients give them strength. Short, weak stalks mean the soil has run out of nutrients like nitrogen, which maize needs in large amounts to grow tall.
ga: Nu yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi. Shi niyenii mli hewalɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ. Tsoi kukuji ni bɛ hewalɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen, ni ŋmã he hiaa lɛ babaoo koni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why does my farmland soil become dry and hard like concrete during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli egbi ni ewa tamɔ kɔnkrit yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic matter. Adding compost or leaving dead leaves and crop residues on the ground protects the soil from drying out and keeps it soft.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he loo ashi baai ni egboi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi ni eha efee blɛoo.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has lost its nutrients before I plant my next crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ efo mli dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: If your previous harvest was smaller than usual, or if wild weeds growing on the plot look pale and stunted, the soil is exhausted and needs manure or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okpamɔ ni okpa tsutsu lɛ faaa fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ Aloo kɛji akɛ koo mli jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɔjɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my tomato plants without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when stressed by severe heat, erratic watering, or when there are no bees around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ loo be mli ni ŋmeii bɛ ni baawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii

english: Why are my yam tubers growing small and twisted instead of long and large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe yɛ be kakadaŋŋ kɛ agbo najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, deep soil to expand easily. If the soil is hard, compact, or filled with rocks, the tuber cannot force its way down and becomes deformed.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ, Shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shi kɛyashi ebaafite.

english: Why do my cabbage heads stay loose and fluffy instead of forming hard balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni wa lɛ?

english: Cabbage heads fail to firm up if the weather is too hot or if the soil lacks sufficient nutrients like phosphorus and nitrogen during the heading stage.
ga: Kaabaji yitsei nyɛŋ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛji akɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa, tamɔ fɔsfɔs kɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ be mli ni aduɔ nii lɛ

english: Officer, why is it necessary for me to trim or cut old leaves off my crops?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ loo mafolɔ baai momoi ni jɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Trimming old or overgrown leaves removes dead and diseased parts, allowing the plant to redirect its energy and water into producing bigger, healthier fruits and leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ ofolɔ baai ni egbɔ loo ni eda fe nine lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ajie fãi ni egboi kɛ helai ni yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei tsakeɔ hewalɛ kɛ nu amɛfeɔ nibii ni da, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ baai.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and soil nutrients from the main tree. Removing the unnecessary ones ensures the main tree gets full nourishment to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tso krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ juɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ tso wulu lɛ mli lɛ. Nibii ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo tso agbo ni tsii.

english: What happens to my crops if I delay harvesting them past their normal ripe time?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ sɛɛ fo fe be ni sa akɛ amɛkpaa nii lɛ?

english: Leaving mature crops on the field too long causes them to overripe, lose their attractive color, and become tough or rotten. It also exposes them to field pests that ruin crop quality.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni edara lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛkwɛ̃ fe nine. efiteɔ su fɛfɛo ni ewaa loo egboɔ Ehaa amɛyaa ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hu anɔ.

english: Why do my peppers and tomatoes lose their firmness and attractive color if left on the farm too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper kɛ mi-tomato lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ fɛo lɛ sɛɛ foɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Once fruits reach full maturity, the plant stops sending fresh nutrients to them. Over time, heat and age break down the fruit's skin and flesh, reducing its appearance, market appeal, and value.
ga: Kɛji aduawai lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ Tso lɛ baakpa niyenii heei ni ekɛhaa lɛ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, Dɔlɛ kɛ afii fiteɔ aduawai lɛ ahewolo kɛ loo. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji hiɛ ni jarayeli lɛ gbalaa mɔ kɛyaa kɛbaa lɛ, ni jara lɛ ba shi

english: Can leaving old plant stems and leaves to decay on my field actually benefit my soil?
ga: Ani tsei ashishifãi kɛ baai momo ni mashi koni amɛgboi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aná he sɛɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, as dead leaves and plant parts rot on the field, they break down into organic matter that enriches the soil with natural nutrients and helps store ground moisture for future crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ baai ni egboi kɛ tsei lɛ ahe nibii ni fiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, amɛgbalaa amɛhe amɛfeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni haa sũ lɛ feɔ niyenii kpakpai yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: When crops are overcrowded, they fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, causing all of them to grow weak, stunted, and less productive.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii eyi mli obɔ lɛ Amɛwuɔ koni hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná fioo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei fɛɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔ, amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: How do weeds growing close to my young crops slow down their growth?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛdalɛ aba shi?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that quickly absorb fertilizer, water, and sunlight before your young crops can reach them, essentially starving your crops of vital growing resources.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu kɛ hulu la oya dani ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ nibii ni he hiaa ni baaha amɛdara.

english: Yellowing leaves are a clear sign that the plant is suffering from nutrient deficiencies, water stress, or disease, which weakens the plant and reduces the size of your yield.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he naagba hewɔ. Nu mli haomɔ loo hela, ni haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: Officer, why should I quickly remove and destroy a sick plant showing leaf spots?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ ni baai lɛ amli ewo muji lɛ oya ni makpãtã amɛhiɛ?

english: Diseased plants easily spread fungi, bacteria, or viruses to neighbouring healthy crops through wind or rain drop splashes, which can destroy your entire farm yield.
ga: Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ gbɛɔ fungi, bacteria, loo virus kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ loo nugbɔshiimɔi anɔ. ni baanyɛ afite oŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii fɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops require full sunlight instead of growing under dense forest shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa he hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛakwɛ̃ yɛ koo ni mli ewo wu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to make their own food through photosynthesis. Without sufficient light, crops grow tall and spindly but fail to flower or produce healthy fruits.
ga: Tsei taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfee amɛ niyenii kɛtsɔ fotosintɛsis nɔ. Kɛji la ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ daa ni amɛhe wa shi amɛwooo fɔfɔi loo amɛwoɔ yibii ni hi.

english: How do I know the right month to harvest my crops after planting them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male nyɔŋ ni sa ni esa akɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ?

english: Most crops have specific maturity periods—for example, main-season maize usually takes 90 to 120 days. By tracking your planting date and watching for physical signs like dry leaves or firm grains, you can predict your harvest time accurately.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ pii yɛ be pɔtɛɛ ko ni amɛdaraa. Ákɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, ŋmãa be titri lɛ heɔ gbii 90 kɛyashi 120. Kɛtsɔ gbii ni aduɔ nii lɛ asɛɛdii kɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii tamɔ baai ni egbi loo ŋmaa ni wa lɛ taomɔ nɔ lɛ, Obaanyɛ otsɔɔ kpamɔɔ be lɛ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow faster when I plant right at the start of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ daa oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Early rains supply steady soil moisture and release natural nitrogen trapped in the dry soil, giving young seedlings the strong start they need to grow quickly before dry spells hit.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ni emɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ kpo. Enɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ jeɔ shishi waa ni amɛdaraa oya dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baashɛ.

english: What should I do to make sure my farm produces extra crops beyond what my family eats?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni miŋmɔ lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi kɛfata nɔ ni miweku lɛ yeɔ lɛ he?

english: To get a surplus harvest, focus on using healthy certified seeds, spacing your plants correctly so they do not fight for nutrients, and clearing weeds early so the crops get all the soil food.
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ ni okpa nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ Okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama dumɔwui ni atsɔɔ akɛ amɛhe wa lɛ anɔ. Space tsei jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkaye niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. ni ojie jwɛi lɛ mra. koni tsei lɛ anine ashɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ

english: How can I store my harvested maize so that insects do not destroy it before I sell it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ato koni kooloi akafite lɛ dani mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: After drying your grains thoroughly in the sun, store them in airtight PICS (Picot-layer) bags or clean drums in a dry room. Removing oxygen prevents head caterpillars and weevils from surviving.
ga: Kɛji oŋmaa lɛ egbi yɛ hulu lɛ mli lɛ, Too yɛ PICS kotoku ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli (picot layer) loo baagi ni akɛjieɔ muji mli yɛ tsu ko ni mli egbi mli. Oxygen ni ajieɔ lɛ haaa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ahi shi.

english: How often should I walk through my farm to check on how my crops are doing?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni makwɛ bɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ ha?

english: It is best to inspect your farm at least twice a week. Regular visits help you spot early pest attacks, plant diseases, or water stress before they cause severe damage to your crop yield.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli. Saramɔi ni afeɔ daa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni ona tsɛŋemɔ helai, tsei ahe helai, loo nu mli haomɔ mra. dani ekɛ naagbai ni mli wa aba onibii ni oduɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Is it better to divide my farmland into portions for different crops or plant only one crop on the whole land?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ majara miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli awo fãi amli? kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi Aloo adu tso henɔ kome yɛ shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Dividing your land to plant different crops (intercropping or crop rotation) protects you from total loss if one crop fails, improves soil fertility, and helps suppress pest outbreaks.
ga: Shikpɔŋ mlijaa koni akɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi Adumɔ (ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ) buɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ fitemɔ kwraa he kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii kome fite. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ aya hiɛ ni eye ebua ni akpa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil, poor drainage holding too much water around the roots, or damage from sap-sucking insects underneath the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa nu babaoo hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. loo nɔ ni kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ fiteɔ yɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight for water and soil nutrients, and their leaves block sunlight from each other, resulting in thin, weak plants with small yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni amɛbaai lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ faaa.

english: Why is it helpful for me to keep track of the exact days I plant and apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eyeɔ ebuaa mi akɛ makwɛ gbii pɔtɛɛ ni miduɔ nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ?

english: Keeping simple record dates helps you time your farm activities correctly, ensures you do not waste fertilizer by applying it too late, and helps you estimate your crop harvest date accurately.
ga: Gbi ni atoɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo Eyeɔ ebua bo ni otoɔ ŋmɔ mli nifeemɔi ahe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kwɛmɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akafite kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaatsu nii blɛoo tsɔ lɛ nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebua bo ni osusuɔ gbi ni obaakpa onibii lɛ ahe lɛ he akɔntaa pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: What causes crops to look healthy at first but produce very small fruits or grains at harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa tso ko feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ yɛ shishijee mli, shi ewoɔ aduawai loo ŋmaa bibii kwraa yɛ kpamɔ be mli?

english: Crops often lack key nutrients like phosphorus and potassium during their flowering stage, or they suffer from water shortage when the fruits and seeds are forming.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ phosphorus kɛ potassium yɛ fɔfɔi be mli. aloo nu ni faaa beni aduawai kɛ dumɔwui miifee lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth, or that heavy rain has waterlogged the soil and prevented the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaaa shishifãi lɛ amu.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help improve my soil for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts have beneficial microbes on their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, leaving behind natural fertilizer for future crops like maize.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Will I harvest more food if I plant my seeds very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Ani makpa niyenii babaoo kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni amɛhi mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ babaoo?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak plants that produce much smaller harvests overall.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ baa, ni no haa yibiiwoo fɛɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: Growing cassava repeatedly on the same land drains all the specific nutrients it needs from the soil and allows pests and soil diseases that target cassava to build up and ruin future harvests.
ga: Cassava ni aduɔ shii abɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ hoɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi ni he hiaa lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni kwɛɔ ŋmei nɔ lɛ feɔ wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni abaadu lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ.

english: Why do people recommend planting plantains next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu plantains yɛ mi kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily in direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves, acting as living umbrellas to shade and protect the cocoa seedlings during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai wuji. Etsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo ni ebuɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why are my tomato flowers and small fruits falling off before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai bibii ji lɛ? Ani minɔ lɛ gbee shi dani eda?

english: Tomato flowers and young fruits fall off mainly due to extreme heat, uneven watering, or a lack of calcium in the soil, which stresses the plant and causes it to drop its flowers to survive.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai bibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa fe fɛɛ ji dɔlɛ ni naa wa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa efɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni ehi shi.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt in the afternoon heat even when the soil is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ lɛ?

english: During peak hot sun, pepper leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can pull it up from the wet soil, causing temporary wilting to protect themselves until the temperature cools down.
ga: Yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Egboɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli koni ebu ehe he kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why do yam vines need to climb tall sticks or trees to give a good yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei akwɔ tsei niji loo tsei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ koni amɛkpa nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch as much sunlight as possible, which allows the plant to produce the energy needed to expand its tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ enáa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛkwɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if there is enough space in the field?
ga: Te jwɛi baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji akɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal water, soil fertilizer, and sunlight from your plants, while also acting as hiding places for insects and diseases.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii hu akɛ he ko ni kooloi bibii kɛ helai nyɛɔ amɛbuɔ he.

english: Why should I cut off the extra small shoots growing on my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Extra ni miida yɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Extra side shoots waste the plant's energy on growing useless leaves instead of fruit, so removing them directs all the plant's food into making bigger and healthier tomatoes.
ga: Lateral shoots krokomɛi fiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ baai ni he ehiaaa yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni shwieɔ nu lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ niyenii muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ tomato agbo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Can I just buy fresh coconuts from the roadside market seller to plant on my new farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mahe ŋmeii heei kɛjɛ gbɛjegbɛ nɔ jarayelɔi adɛŋ koni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ hee lɛ mli?

english: No, eating coconuts sold on the roadside are often uncertified, may carry hidden diseases, or may have lost their vitality from sitting in the heat too long, leading to poor growth or dead crops.
ga: Dabi, bei pii lɛ, aŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ ni ayeɔ ŋmeii ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ he lɛ. Ekolɛ hela ko ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ yɛ jɛmɛ. Aloo ekolɛ amɛhewalɛ baaje amɛdɛŋ yɛ hulu lɛ nɔ ni amɛtara be kakadaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii gboiɔ.

english: Does it matter how long a coconut fruit has been sitting on a pile before I plant it?
ga: Be enyiɛ ŋmeii baahi ŋmeii lɛ anɔ dani amɛdu?

english: Yes, coconuts left sitting out for too long dry up internally and lose their energy, which causes them to sprout weakly or fail entirely once planted in the soil.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii ni ashi amɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ baagbi yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli ni amɛhewalɛ baaje mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ fioo loo amɛgboɔ kwraa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ.

english: Where should a farmer go to get proper coconut seeds that are safe for planting?
ga: Nɛgbɛ esa akɛ okwaafoi aya koni amɛyatao ŋmei dumɔwui ni sa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni amɛduɔ?

english: You should get planting materials from certified agricultural officers or trusted government nurseries that specifically breed disease-free and strong seed nuts.
ga: Esa akɛ ohe nibii ni akɛduɔ nii kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ loo nɔyeli lɛ akwɛmɔhei ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ amɛnɔ ni fɔɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni hela bɛ mli lɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ adɛŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I just use old coconuts from my own harvest as seeds for my next farm expansion?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii momo ni mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ dumɔwui kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Harvested coconuts from ordinary trees might carry diseases from the parent plant or lack resistance to local sicknesses, putting your whole future farm at risk.
ga: Ekolɛ helai ni jɛ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ yɛ mli lɛ amli loo amɛbɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ helai anɔ yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, owɔsɛɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ yɛ oshara mli.

english: Why do some coconut farms in my area dry up and die while others stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei ŋmɔji komɛi ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigboi lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni hei komɛi yɛ ŋmɔji lolo lɛ?

english: Some coconut varieties have natural strength built into them to fight off deadly crop diseases, while non-resistant varieties easily catch the sickness and die.
ga: Ajɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi yɛ hewalɛ yɛ tsei ahe helai ni woɔ mɔ wala he gbeyei lɛ ahe tawuu mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni nyɛɛɛ amɛye hela lɛ anɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ helai oya ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: How can I protect my new coconut farm from catching deadly tree diseases in the future?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-kokoo ŋmɔ hee lɛ he kɛjɛ tsei ahe helai ni naa wa he wɔsɛɛ?

english: The most effective protection starts at planting by choosing certified, disease-resistant coconut seedling varieties recommended by agricultural extension officers.
ga: Hebuu ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe fɛɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛ dumɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ amɛhe esa ni amɛjieɔ yi lɛ nɔ.

english: What happens if I plant coconut trees that do not have strong resistance to disease?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmei tso ni helai nyɛɔ eshiɔ lɛ babaoo?

english: The trees may grow fine for a while, but as soon as a coconut disease spreads through your area, your entire farm can be wiped out before you get a good harvest.
ga: Tso lɛ baanyɛ ada jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi be ko. Shi kɛji akɛ ŋmei hela gbɛ eshwa he ni oyɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ pɛ kɛkɛ ni abaakpata Oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ dani obaanyɛ oná ŋmaa kpakpa.

english: Why do agricultural officers say that coconut farming requires more care in seed selection than crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmeii akwɛmɔ biɔ hiɛdɔɔ babaoo yɛ dumɔwui ahalamɔ mli fe ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei lɛ?

english: Coconuts take many years to grow and bear fruit, so planting poor seeds wastes years of money, land, and hard work before you realize the trees are bad.
ga: Kokoo heɔ afii babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ ni ewoɔ yibii. No hewɔ lɛ dumɔwui gbohii ni ooodu lɛ baafite shika, shikpɔŋ, kɛ afii babaoo ni okɛtsu nii waa dani ole akɛ tso lɛ ehiii.

english: Why do my young coconut sprouts fail to grow even after I give them good soil and rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmei tso bibioo lɛ edaaa eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa lɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛ nugbɔ moŋ?

english: If the original seed nut was old, sick, or taken from a weak parent tree, the seedling will remain weak and fail to grow well regardless of water or soil.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shishijee ŋmeii lɛ egbɔ tsɔ, hela mɔ amɛ, loo ajie kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso ko ni egbɔjɔ mli lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ baakã he ahi shi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛdara jogbaŋŋ kɛji amɛyɛ nu mli loo shikpɔŋ nɔ.

english: Is it worth paying more money for certified coconut seeds instead of using free ones?
ga: Ani ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ akɛ ooowo nyɔmɔ babaoo kɛha ŋmei dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ moŋ fe ni awoɔ yaka?

english: Yes, paying for certified seeds guarantees disease-resistant, high-yielding trees that protect your income for decades, whereas free uncertified seeds often lead to farm failure.
ga: Yes, paying for certified seeds will guarantee that the plants are disease-resistant and high-yielding. Enɛ baabu shika ni onáa lɛ he afii nyɔŋmai abɔ. Meanwhile, uncertified seeds given out for free often lead to farm failure.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh, direct sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains nearby to block the heavy heat, the sun dries out the soft leaves, causing them to burn, turn yellow, and curl to protect themselves from water loss.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. If there are no shade trees or saplings nearby to block the intense heat Sunlight will dry out the young leaves. Resulting in leaf burn turn yellow and curled to prevent water loss

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. The maize plants stretch upward to catch light instead of building thick stems and food for big cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ niyenii aha ŋmeii wuji lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛmɔ la lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow plenty of green leaves but very small tubers underneath the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Excessive leafy growth often happens when the soil has too much nitrogen and lacks potassium. The plant puts all its energy into growing leaves on top instead of storing food in the root tubers underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni daa fe nine lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛ potassium hu faaa. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ baai yɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli lɛ

english: Why do my crops grow faster and greener when I mix dried chicken manure into the soil before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji kɛ́ mikɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani midu lɛ?

english: Animal manure acts as a natural food store for the soil. As it breaks down, it slowly releases essential nutrients that feed plant roots and helps the soil hold onto water longer.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Beni efiteɔ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa tsei shishifãi lɛ hewalɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ fiofio.

english: Why is it bad for me to water my tomato plants in the middle of the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afɔ tomato tsei anɔ nu shwane mli lɛ? Ani ehiii kɛha mi?

english: Watering under the hot sun causes water droplets on the leaves to act like small glass lenses, which can scorch the leaves. Most of the water also evaporates into the air before the roots can drink it.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ haa nu ni hoɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ tamɔ glase ŋmɛlɛtswai bibii. ni baanyɛ ashã baai Nu lɛ babaoo shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ nuɔ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce very small yields even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo po lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer away from your crops. Even with good rain, your crops go hungry because the weeds absorb most of the soil nutrients first.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii lɛ lolo ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii lɛ babaoo klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Flower drop usually happens when the plant experiences stress from high heat, lack of water, or attacks from tiny insects. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to conserve energy for its own survival.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo kooloi bibii ni tutuaa amɛ lɛ mli. Kɛji haomɔ ba lɛ Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Continuous planting of the same crop drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows plant diseases and insects that like maize to build up in the field year after year.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe helai kɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmãa buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔji amli afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why do my cowpea seeds fail to come up out of the dirt when I bury them deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui lɛ ejeee kpo kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds carry only a limited amount of stored energy. If planted too deep, the young shoot exhausts all its energy trying to push through the heavy soil and dies before reaching the surface light.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ni ato. Kɛji akɛ adu mli tsɔ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ nijiaŋ jeɔ wui ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ mli ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛshɛɔ la ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ he.

english: Why do farmers recommend planting beans in the same farm as my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ duɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and leguminous crops have special root nodules that pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, which naturally fertilizes and strengthens nearby crops like maize.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii baa ni ewoɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow before the cobs even form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmeii lɛ po feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the main food crop plants need to stay green and produce big, healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛwo toi wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow so many green leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or manure, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves instead of flowering and producing pods.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmeii babaoo Tsei kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ baai lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔi ni ekɛ pods baa lɛ

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat or dry soil stress, causing the plant to shed flowers to save water and stay alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ kpe. Enɛ haa tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi bɔni afee ni ekɛ nu akafite ni ehi shi.

english: Young cocoa leaves will look scorched, brown at the edges, or pale yellow because bright sunlight burns their tender leaves before they build a strong canopy.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ baafee tamɔ nɔ ni ashã. Eyɛ blɔfo yɛ eshishigbɛ. Aloo amɛji ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ dani amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni mli wa.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt in the afternoon heat even when the soil is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: In intense sun, tomatoes lose water through their leaves faster than roots can pull it from the soil, causing temporary wilting until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Tomatoi shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ tomato lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kukuoo ko kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in poorly drained soil during heavy rains, creating conditions where soil fungus can attack the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu shwie shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ atutua ŋmeii lɛ baa.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to yield fruit after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii beni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains are heavy feeders that require rich organic matter and consistent moisture; dry spells or poor soil slow down their growth and delay fruiting.
ga: Plantains ji niyenii ni tsii ni biɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ baaha dalɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni ebaaha aduawai lɛ aba sɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my yam vines curling up and turning dark brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curling and brown spots on yam leaves are typically caused by fungal infections like anthracnose, which spread fast during warm, humid rainy seasons.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ anthracnose, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do my green cowpea pods have small holes in them right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea ŋmɔtɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? dani akpa kpamɔ

english: Small holes in pods are caused by pod borer caterpillars that hatch on the plant and chew into the pods to feed on the developing beans inside.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baa ji ŋmeii ni fɔ̃ɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛye ŋmeii ni shwereɔ yɛ mli lɛ.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, will I harvest more cobs?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani manyɛ makpa ŋmãa babaoo?

english: Planting too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, which results in thin stalks and smaller or empty cobs.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ atswa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Leaves turn yellow mainly when the plant is missing important food from the soil, especially nitrogen. It can also happen when too much rain fills the soil with water and prevents the roots from breathing.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ titri lɛ kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛmu.

english: Why does planting maize on the exact same plot of land every year result in a smaller harvest each time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ haa yibiiwoo fioo baa be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Every crop eats specific nutrients from the ground. Planting the same crop repeatedly drains those exact nutrients completely and allows soil pests that love maize to multiply in that spot.
ga: Tsei fɛɛ yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni ooodu shii abɔ Enɛ baaha niyenii ni yeɔ emuu aba ni eye ebua shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ ni amɛshwere yɛ nakai he lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in a field with no shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily in direct sunshine. They need shade trees or plantain plants above them to block strong heat and hold moisture until their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo kooyigbɛ tsei koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa lɛ naa ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli baawa.

english: Rolling leaves is the plant's clever way of defending itself against heat. By curling up, the leaves expose less surface to the hot sun, which helps the plant hold onto its water during dry hours.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji ŋaa gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɛɛ baai lɛ ahe tsɔ. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɔ amɛhiɛɔ nu mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Why does covering the soil with dry grass around my tomato plants keep them green longer in dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-tomato lɛ ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts like a blanket over the dirt. It stops the sun from drying out the soil, keeps the ground cool, and traps moisture so the plant roots stay hydrated longer.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ

english: Yam leaves are solar panels that need sunlight to build big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground toward the sun and prevents fungal diseases caused by wet soil.
ga: Sweet potato baai ji hulutsoo be mli nibii ni biɔ hulu la koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la mli ni etsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: How can I tell that my cassava tubers are big and ready for harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ dara ni esa akɛ akpa ni okɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ efooo?

english: You can tell cassava is ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil right around the stem begins to swell and crack open from the growing roots below.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle tso lɛ he lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ ni efoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do fall armyworm caterpillars hide deep inside the center of my maize plants during the daytime?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ teɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Armyworms have soft bodies that dry out quickly in hot sunlight. They hide deep inside the funnel of the maize plant where it is cool and moist, coming out to feed heavily when temperatures drop at night or early morning.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yɛ gbɔmɔtsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni kɛ́ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ, amɛgbiɔ oya. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ ni edɔ lɛ. Amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛyatao niyenii waa kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi gbɛkɛ loo leebi maŋkpa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling downwards and becoming crinkly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle shi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or thrips hiding underneath the leaf. As they suck the plant's sap, they cause the leaf to grow twisted and unhealthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mites loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. be mli ni ekɛ tsei amli nu lɛ shwieɔ Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air gets too hot, or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Extreme heat stops pollination from happening inside the flower, so the plant drops it.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haaa pollination aba yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli. Therefore, the plant falls off.

english: Leaf curling in the afternoon heat is a natural defence mechanism. The plant rolls its leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, helping it conserve water and stay alive during hot periods.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛha he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi ni ehiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing lots of flowers but no actual tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi tomato diɛŋtsɛ bɛ lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high or water is inconsistent, tomato plants drop their blossoms to survive. Giving them consistent water at the base and adding mulch helps keep the root area cool so fruit can set.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu lɛ ejaaa lɛ Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni aduawai lɛ anyɛ atswa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the maize is running out of nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves the remaining nutrients up to support new growth, which means it is time to apply fertilizer or compost.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eye ebua dalɛ hee. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he.

english: Cassava roots cannot expand well if the soil underneath is too hard and compacted. Loosening the soil deeply during planting creates space for the tubers to swell easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi nyɛŋ alɛɛ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwie shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ dumɔ be mli lɛ, ebaaha efee mlɛo aha bulb lɛ akɛ ebaakwɛ̃.

english: Why do weeds come back so much faster than my crops after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds have hardy wild seeds that lie dormant in the ground and sprout immediately when sunlight hits the bare earth. Covering the bare soil with mulch or planting cover crops blocks sunlight and slows weed growth.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ koo mli dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni wɔɔ shi. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni edaa kɛji hulu la lɛ shɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ tsei ni miida lɛ ha shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi hulu la naa ni ebaaha jwɛi lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants wilting and dropping when the ground is full of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ lɛ?

english: When soil stays waterlogged, the roots suffocate because they cannot get oxygen, causing them to rot. Building raised beds or mounds allows excess water to drain away so roots can breathe.
ga: Kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Saa ni awo nɔ loo gɔji ni afee lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu.

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings scorch and die when I plant them in direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive tender leaves that burn easily under full sun. Planting fast-growing food crops like plantains next to them provides living shade and moisture while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni nuɔ he waa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ baaha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo aba yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ maa ehe shi lɛ.

english: Why does my maize produce very thin stalks when I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ shishi tsei bibii waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crowded crops fight each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and sunlight to build a thick, strong stalk.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni mli wa lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ hulu la koni ekɛwo tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli tse ni mli wa.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell that can dry out and kill newly sprouted seeds. It is safer to wait until the rains become steady so the soil maintains constant moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni baanyɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ daa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do seeds saved from last year's harvest produce smaller yields than certified seeds bought from the agro-dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni ahe kɛjɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds from hybrid crops lose their strength, vigor, and disease resistance over time. Certified seeds are specially produced to ensure uniform growth, pest resistance, and high yield every season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ, hewalɛ, kɛ helai ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Afeɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛkwɛ koni amɛdara daa. Pest ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo daa be mli

english: What happens to my crops when it does not rain at all after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: When rain does not fall after planting, seeds struggle to germinate and young roots cannot find water to grow. Without water, crops dry out, wither, and can die because they need moisture to transport nutrients from the soil.
ga: Be ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ Dumɔwui lɛ naa wa akɛ amɛakwɛ̃ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana nu ni amɛkɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ nu bɛ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii gbɛ́ɔ, amɛgboiɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi ejaakɛ amɛhe miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛkɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aya.

english: How can I keep my crops alive during a long dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli?

english: You can protect your crops during dry spells by spreading dry grass or leaves around their stems as mulch. Mulch traps moisture in the soil, keeps the ground cool, and reduces the amount of water lost to heat.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli kɛtsɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni okɛbaabɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ. The trunk is a mulch material. Mulch mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa nu ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ mli baa lɛ baa shi

english: Which crops are safest for me to grow if I am worried about a dry year?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei yɔɔ shweshweeshwe akɛ makwɛ kɛji afi ni nu bɛ lɛ he miihao?

english: Crops like cassava, millet, sorghum, and cowpeas naturally survive with very little water. They have deep roots or tough leaves that allow them to produce yields even when rainfall is very low.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, ŋmei, kɛ tsina ŋmei baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli. Amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo baai ni wa ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo po.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize crops curl up during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Curling leaves are a crop's natural way of protecting itself. By rolling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun, helping it conserve water until the heat reduces.
ga: Baai ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni tso ko tsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe he. Tsei haa hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nu toɔ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni la ni tsoɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and stunt when it rains too much?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Too much rain fills all the small air spaces in the soil with water, literally suffocating the roots. Without oxygen, roots cannot breathe or feed the plant, causing the leaves to turn yellow and growth to stop.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yiɔ kɛ nu. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛji oxygen bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu loo amɛhaŋ tso lɛ niyenii. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ.

english: How does heavy rain damage the good soil on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy downpours wash away the soft topsoil where all the essential plant nutrients sit. Planting crops across slopes or keeping cover crops on the land stops rainwater from carrying away your rich soil.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ nɔ, ni no haa tsei lɛ anáa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ. Tsei ni ooodu yɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni oooha nɔ ko nɔ lɛ baatsi nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ oshikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ lɛ naa.

english: Can my crops recover if standing water stays on my farm for a few days?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ kɛji nu lɛ tee nɔ ehi miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi?

english: Most crops can survive in flooded water for up to 24 to 48 hours. However, if the water sits longer than that, root rot usually sets in, making full recovery very difficult for crops like maize or vegetables.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ nu afua mli kɛyashi ŋmɛlɛtswai 24 kɛyashi 48. Shi, kɛji nu lɛ hi shi be kakadaŋŋ fe nakai lɛ, bei pii lɛ Root rot boteɔ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai lɛ naa hewalɛ kwraa.

english: How do I know it is the right time to plant after the first rainfall?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eji be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best not to plant after the very first light shower, as it can be a false start to the season. Wait until the rain falls steadily 2 to 3 times and the soil stays moist deep down before putting seeds in the ground.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ahum lɛ sɛɛ. Ejaakɛ ebaanyɛ efee amale shishijee kɛha be lɛ. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ shii 2 kɛyashi 3 be fɛɛ be ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa lolo dani odu dumɔwui.

english: Why does the soil on my land crack open when it gets very dry, and does it hurt my plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli fãa kɛji edɔ waa lɛ, ni ani eyeɔ mitsei lɛ awui?

english: Clay soils shrink and crack when intense heat dries out all moisture. These cracks stretch and break small crop roots underground, making it harder for plants to stand firm and absorb food.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ ha ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli egbi. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfoɔ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli, ni no haa ewaa kɛhaa tso lɛ akɛ ebaadamɔ shi shiŋŋ ni eŋɔ niyenii.

english: Is it safe for me to use water from a nearby river to water my crops during dry periods?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛɔ faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ baashwie ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, using river water is a great way to save crops during a dry spell. Just make sure the river water is not polluted with trash or chemicals from washing, which could harm your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, faa mli nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ji gbɛ kpakpa ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Kwɛmɔ kɛkɛ akɛ jwɛi loo tsofai ni jɛɔ tsɔne ni akɛfɔɔ nu mli lɛ mli lɛ efiteee faa lɛ mli nu lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aye onibii lɛ awui.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which acts as essential food for leaf growth. Heavy rains can wash this nutrient out of the topsoil, causing the plant leaves to pale.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ he kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tso baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act as temporary umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and cool air it needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ be kukuoo mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to produce food for the underground tuber. Staking keeps leaves off the damp soil, improving air flow and preventing fungal rot.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkajɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ ni etsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni atsĩ ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ naa

english: Why does my cassava produce big tall bushes with lots of leaves but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ jwɛi agbo kɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: If cassava receives too much nitrogen or water early on, it spends all its energy growing branches and leaves instead of storing energy underground in the tuber roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen loo nu babaoo nɔ mra lɛ, Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo tsei niji kɛ baai amli. Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, akɛ hewalɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ tuber lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Extra suckers compete with the main plant for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Removing them ensures the main stem gets enough energy to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Suckers ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ plantains agboi ni tsii.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and sucking out plant sap, or by a virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my maize stalks falling over and breaking near the root when the wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ tswa lɛ?

english: Maize stalks fall over easily when pests like stem borers tunnel inside to weaken the stem, or when the plant roots are too shallow to anchor the heavy cob load.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii shwie tsei lɛ amli yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni amɛha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ. aloo be mli ni tso shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ cob jatsu ni tsii nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when weather gets too hot or when soil moisture swings suddenly from dry to wet. Excessive heat dries out the flower pollen so fruit cannot form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ mli. Dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ baaha pollen lɛ agbi kɛyashɛ he ni aduawai nyɛŋ afee.

english: Why do my cabbage leaves look soft and droopy in the hot afternoon even though I watered them early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kaabɛji baai lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu leebi maŋkpa?

english: In intense midday heat, leaves release water vapor faster than roots can draw it up from the soil. The plant wilts temporarily to conserve water and usually recovers by evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Baai lɛ jieɔ nu lasu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tsei baagbi be kukuoo ko koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni bei pii lɛ, amɛhe baajɔ amɛ gbɛkɛ.

english: How does planting groundnuts on my farm help my next crop of maize grow better?
ga: Te ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnut roots work with friendly soil bacteria to trap nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the soil. When groundnuts are harvested, this natural fertilizer remains in the soil for the next crop.
ga: Peanut shishifãi kɛ sũ mli helai ni ji naanyobɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmei nɛɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. They need shade from plants like plantains or forest trees to keep them cool and hold moisture in the soil while they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei tamɔ plantains loo koo mli tsei adɛŋ koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be mli ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their small flowers before any pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Dani pods lɛ baakwɛ̃?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they lack water, when pests attack the blossoms, or when the soil lacks food. Ensuring proper shade, adequate moisture, and protecting the flowers from bugs helps the pods develop.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ nu faaa. Beni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutua fɔfɔi lɛ loo be mli ni niyenii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shade ni sa ni haa hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa Kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: This rot is caused by a fungus that grows quickly in wet, shaded conditions. Pruning extra branches allows sunlight and air to dry out the leaves and pods, preventing the fungus from taking over.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni daa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ. Prevent fungus from taking over.

english: Why should I cut off extra stems and branches from my cocoa tree if I want more yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-kokoo tso lɛ mli tsei kɛ tsei niji krokomɛi kɛji miitao yibiiwoo babaoo?

english: Removing dead or extra branches helps the tree save its food and energy. Instead of feeding unnecessary leaves, the tree can direct its strength into growing bigger and healthier pods.
ga: Niji ni egboi loo ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ toɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaha foliar niyenii ni he ehiaaa lɛ, Tsei baanyɛ atsake amɛhewalɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛdara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots go soft and rot in the ground during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long without draining. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets excess rainwater flow away so the tubers stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ efooo Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Koni yitso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Yam plants grow as climbing vines that need to reach up toward the sun. Lifting the leaves off the ground helps the plant capture sunlight to feed the growing tubers underneath the soil.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ daa tamɔ wain tso ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ eshɛ ŋwɛi kɛya hulu lɛ he. Kɛ́ tso lɛ wo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɔ enáa hulu la ni ekɛhaa bulb ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are there holes in my maize leaves and small worms eating the inside of the stalk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ye nii yɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm. They feed on the tender young leaves inside the stem, which stops the maize plant from growing well unless treated early.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ja atsa lɛ oya.

english: Why does my maize crop grow better when I plant cowpeas alongside it in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans pull natural goodness called nitrogen out of the air and put it into the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer that helps neighboring maize plants grow taller and greener.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans gbalaa adebɔɔ mli kpakpa ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhaa shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ feɔ ekome.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt in the afternoon heat even when I gave them water in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: On hot days, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it up. Covering the soil around the plant stem with dry grass keeps the soil cool and stops the water from evaporating.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie tso lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i, ni ebaatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho.

english: Why should I wait until the soil is wet before spreading fertilizer on my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ dani mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Fertilizer must dissolve in water before plant roots can drink it in. Putting fertilizer on dry soil can burn the plant roots and waste your money because the crop cannot use it dry.
ga: Esa akɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awo nu mli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ anu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni efite shika ejaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nyɛŋ amɛkɛtsu nii ni amɛkɛgbi.

english: Why does my maize crop dry up and fail whenever the rains stop for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni efiteɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ lɛ baakpa otsii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Maize needs a steady supply of water to transport soil nutrients throughout the plant. Without enough moisture, the leaves dry up and the plant cannot form full cobs, leading to poor yields or total crop failure.
ga: Nu ni yaa nɔ daa he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aya tso lɛ mli fɛɛ. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ faaa lɛ Baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee ŋmei ni eyi obɔ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo ni ehiii loo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ kwraa.

english: Why are the leaves of my corn plants curling up during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is the corn plant's natural way of protecting itself from losing too much water in extreme heat. It is a clear warning sign that the soil is too dry and the plant is suffering from water stress.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji ŋmãa tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ nu babaoo ni efiteɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ he. Eji kɔkɔbɔɔ okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni tso lɛ miina nu he haomɔ.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my corn plants turn yellow when there is no rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?
