english: When water is scarce, corn plants cannot absorb nitrogen from the dry soil. To survive, the plant steals nitrogen from its lower leaves to feed the young growth at the top, turning the bottom leaves yellow.
ga: Beni nu faaa lɛ Abɛi tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. koni amɛhi shi Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: At what stage of growth does my corn plant need water the most?
ga: Mɛɛ dalɛ mli mi ŋmãa tso lɛ he hiaa nu fe fɛɛ yɛ dalɛ mli?

english: Corn needs water most during the flowering stage, when it is producing silks and tassels to form the ears. Drought stress during this short window can destroy the harvest even if rain comes later.
ga: Nu he hiaa abele fe fɛɛ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Enɛ ji be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ miifee siliki kɛ ŋmeii ni ekɛfee toi. Haomɔ ni jɛɔ hɔmɔ be kukuoo mli baa. Enɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ yɛ sɛɛ mli po.

english: How does supplying water to my maize farm during dry periods help my crops produce better yield?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni mikɛhaa mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai?

english: Providing a steady water source keeps the plant growing without stress, allowing it to continuously absorb nutrients and fill out large, heavy cobs regardless of whether rainfall is reliable.
ga: Nu jɛɛhe ni akɛhaa daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa ni haomɔ ko bɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, ni ehaa ŋmeii wuji ni tsii lɛ woɔ mli ekoŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nugbɔ lɛ nɔ loo anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ

english: Can I plant my corn during the dry season if I have a reliable stream or well nearby?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli? Kɛji miyɛ nu jɛɛhe ko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ loo he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi.

english: Yes, with a reliable water source, you can farm corn year-round. Dry season corn often commands higher prices in the market because fewer farmers are harvesting at that time.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ nu jɛɛhe ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ. Obaanyɛ odu ŋmãa afi muu lɛ fɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni baa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ haa jara ni yaa hiɛ lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ jara nɔ ejaakɛ okwaafoi fioo ko pɛ kpaɔ ŋmãa yɛ nakai beaŋ.

english: If I have access to a good water source, can giving my maize farm too much water harm the crop?
ga: Kɛji miyɛ nu jɛɛhe kpakpa Ani nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔ mli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aye ŋmãa lɛ awui?

english: Yes, overwatering drowns the plant roots by removing air from the soil. This causes root rot, yellowing leaves, and poor growth, so water should be applied steadily in balanced amounts.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli fe nine lɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdaraaa jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ nu atsu nii daa yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ.

english: What is the simplest way for me to get water directly to my corn roots without wasting it?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ mikɛ nu aya ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni mifiteee nɔ ko?

english: Using simple drip pipes or watering directly at the base of each plant delivers water straight to the roots where it is needed, preventing loss through sun evaporation.
ga: Kɛtsɔ drip hose ni yɔɔ mlɛo nɔ loo nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishi tɛ̃ɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nu kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ he ni ehe hiaa yɛ lɛ. Tsi hulu la ni hoɔ lɛ ni elaajeɔ lɛ naa.

english: What simple practice can I use on my farm to keep water in the soil longer when it does not rain?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ nifeemɔi komɛi ni yɔɔ mlɛo atsu nii. yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni nu ahi sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ.

english: Covering the bare soil around your crops with dry grass, leaves, or crop stalks (mulching) blocks hot sunlight, keeps the soil cool, and prevents water from evaporating quickly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ni okɛbaabɔle ohe lɛ Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai loo tsei ahe tsei ahe (mulching) baaye abua ni atsĩ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya.

english: Why does sandy soil lose moisture much faster after rainfall compared to clay soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya kwraa yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ fe shikpɔŋ ni shikpɔŋ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Sandy soil has large, coarse particles with wide gaps that let water drain straight down, while clay soil has fine, tightly packed particles that hold onto water like a sponge.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni mli kwɔlɔ ni nu lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛba shi. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nibii bibii bibii ni ekpɛtɛ nu he tamɔ sponji.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure will help bring back their green color and improve yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need taller crops like plantains growing next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with lots of leaf foliage but producing very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to put all their energy into growing leaves instead of roots. Avoiding excessive nitrogen fertilizers encourages the plant to store its energy underground in big tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai yɛ shishifãi najiaŋ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ ŋmɔji wuji amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and showing yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread plant viruses, or by stress from extreme heat and dry conditions. Controlling sap-sucking insects early helps protect your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli baa lɛ mli. Kplukai ni nuɔ nu lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why do my crops yield much less grain when I plant many seeds very close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ dumɔwui fioo kwraa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and food to produce full, healthy grains.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni adu lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they get stressed by high temperatures, sudden dry spells, or overwatering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and avoiding water stress helps flowers stay on and form peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa hao amɛ. trukaa ŋmɔlɔ loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine Sũ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ nu he haomɔ he lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Weeds are wild plants that naturally adapted to quickly steal water, sunlight, and food from the soil. Clearing weeds early in the season stops them from choking your crops while they are young.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛju nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni jwɛi lɛ akatsi onibii amli be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ.

english: Why do small insects eat up my harvested maize grains after I put them in storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yeɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ beni mikɛwo nitoo kotoku lɛ mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Storage insects like weevils thrive when grain is stored with too much moisture inside. Drying your harvested maize thoroughly in the sun until it is hard prevents weevils from damaging your stored grain.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ mli tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ yaa hiɛ waa kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui ni mli edɔ babaoo to mli. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaawa lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkafite ŋmãa ni ato lɛ.

english: Why does putting dry grass or leaves around the roots of my vegetables help them grow better during dry dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni akɛfataa he lɛ ji nɔ ni ebɔle he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ mishishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, blocks the hot sun from evaporating soil water, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from coming up.
ga: Mulching kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsĩ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa ni etsi nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekaho. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃.

english: Why should I cut off small, weak branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? Baai ni bɛ hewalɛ ni jɛ kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ amli?

english: Removing weak branches—called pruning—allows light and air to move freely through the tree. This prevents fungal diseases like black pod and directs the tree's energy into producing bigger, healthier pods.
ga: niji bibii ni afolɔ Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsei niji ni afoɔ. Enɛ haa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli oya. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji anaa, ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and burning during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight scorches their delicate leaves and dries out the soil moisture. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them protects them from heat until they grow strong.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, ni ooodu yɛ masɛi Enɛ baabu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ latsaa he kɛyashi ebaada waa.

english: Why do my maize plants stay short and turn purple instead of growing tall and dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛfeɔ purple yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Purple leaves and stunted growth usually mean the soil lacks phosphorus. This nutrient helps crops grow deep roots and strong stems, so feeding the soil with phosphorus fertilizer will help the maize mature properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ amɛdalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ shishifãi ni wa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ fɔsfɔs ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the crop experiences heat stress or uneven watering. When the heat is too high or the ground dries out suddenly, the plant sheds its flowers to save energy to survive.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ekɛhaaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ trukaa lɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Beans are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This natural nitrogen feeds the nearby maize, acting like a free soil boost.
ga: Beans ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen nɛɛ haa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ niyenii. Etsuɔ nii akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni fata he ni yɔɔ ehe.

english: Why do my crops perform better when I cover the soil around them with dry leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ sũ wo amɛhe lɛ? kɛ baai ni egbi

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves creates mulch. Mulch traps moisture in the dirt so plants do not dry out quickly, keeps the roots cool, and turns into rich natural food as it rots.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii baa. Mulch mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ akagbi oya Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ ni ebafeɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛji egbo.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn out thin and woody instead of big and plump?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ tsei moŋ fe ni amɛaafee wuji ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava needs loose, well-tilled soil and proper spacing to expand. If the stems are planted too close together or in hard, unworked ground, the roots cannot swell to store starch.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni gbɛ ni sa yɔɔ nɔ koni egbɛ eshwa lɛ he miihia Cassava. Kɛji akɛ adu tsei lɛ abɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni akɛtsuuu nii nɔ lɛ, Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɔjɔ ni amɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ato.

english: Why shouldn't I spread fertilizer on dry ground when the rain has not fallen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ? Nugbɔ enɛko lolo?

english: Fertilizer needs water to melt into the soil where plant roots can drink it up. If applied to dry dirt under hot sun, the fertilizer can evaporate into the air or burn the plant's stems.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli he ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ anu lɛ yɛ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, Fɛ̃i baanyɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli loo eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi.

english: Why do my tomato plants rot from the bottom of the fruit before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifite kɛmiijɛ shishi dani amɛmiikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Bottom rot in tomatoes happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium, usually caused by irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the fruit develop evenly without spoiling.
ga: Tomato shishigbɛ fitemɔ baa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i lɛ, ebaaye ebua aduawai lɛ ni amɛdara pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛfiteee.

english: Why do the new seed varieties from the agriculture office produce food faster than the seeds I saved from last year's harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui heei ni jɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ woɔ niyenii oya fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved seeds are specifically bred to grow quickly and withstand dry spells. This allows them to complete their life cycle and produce food before the rainy season ends prematurely.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛdamɔ hɔmɔ shihilɛi anaa. Enɛ haa amɛgbeɔ amɛwala shihilɛ naa ni amɛwoɔ niyenii dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baa naagbee mra.

english: Why do I see tiny holes appearing in the young leaves of my corn field every morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli baai bibii lɛ anɔ daa leebi.

english: Small holes on young corn leaves are caused by pests like fall armyworms that feed inside the soft leaf whorls at night. Checking the center of the plants early allows you to treat them before they damage the growing point.
ga: Buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ jɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ armyworms ni egbee shi ni yeɔ baa bibii ahe ŋtayaai gbɛkɛ lɛ amli. Kwɛmɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otsaa amɛ dani amɛfiteɔ hei ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that easily burn under full, direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide big leaves that shade the young cocoa plants and keep the soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantains ni shwereɔ oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: When maize plants grow too close to one another, their roots and leaves compete heavily for the same sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving no single plant with enough food to grow large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei dara ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei komɛi bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. This naturally adds fertilizer to the soil, helping the next crop grow stronger.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Gbɛ nɛɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii afata he yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Help the next crop grow stronger.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that the maize plant is running out of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is essential for keeping leaves green and helping the plant build food for the growing cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he hiaa koni eha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni efee niyenii eha ŋmei ni miida lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and growing tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by very small sucking pests like aphids or mites, or a plant virus spread by insects, which damages the leaf tissue and stops normal growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo tso mli helai ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Enɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji ni ehaa amɛdalɛ ni sa lɛ kpaa.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to create food for the tubers growing underground. Lifting the leaves off the wet soil exposes them to more sun and prevents diseases from infecting the damp leaves on the ground.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Kɛ́ awó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la babaoo shɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ, ni ehaaa hela aba baai ni edɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the plant experiences water stress from drying out. Extreme heat causes the plant to drop its flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ kɛjɛ egbimɔ mli. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tsei shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains flood the farm and water sits in the soil without draining away, the roots suffocate and rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ ni nu lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ baafo ni amɛbaagboi.

english: Why do my orange trees drop many of their small fruits before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii babaoo dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Citrus trees drop excess fruit if they do not have enough water or nutrients to feed all of them. Dropping some young fruit allows the tree to focus its energy on growing the remaining ones.
ga: Citrus tsei lɛ baashwie aduawai ni fa fe nine kɛji amɛbɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua amɛ fɛɛ. Yibii bibii ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa yibii ni eshwɛ lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ nɔ.

english: Too many extra shoots, called suckers, will steal water and nutrients away from the main plantain tree, resulting in smaller bunches of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, plantains lɛ baaná panicles bibii.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn yellow and dry up during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. They require temporary shade crops, like plantains, planted nearby to act as living umbrellas and keep the soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots taste bitter and become tough when I harvest them during a long drought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ mli edɔ ni amɛhe wa kɛ́ akpa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When cassava suffers from lack of rain, the plant builds up natural protective compounds as a survival mechanism against water stress. These compounds make the tuber bitter and fibrous until steady rains return.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ ni bɛ lɛ naa amanehulu lɛ Tsei lɛ feɔ nibii ni buɔ mɔ he akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi kɛjɛɔ nu mli haomɔ he. Nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ yaa nɔ enɛɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and weak with small cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ Dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crowded roots and leaves fight over light, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing seeds properly ensures each stalk gets full sunlight and nourishment to develop strong stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shishifãi ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifã lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa hulu la kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni haa tso lɛ shishifãi ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on instead of spreading across the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines on tall stakes exposes more leaves to sunlight, which allows the plant to make more energy to feed the underground tubers. It also keeps leaves away from wet soil where fungal diseases breed.
ga: Kɛ́ owó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la babaoo ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛhaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Etsiɔ baa hu naa koni amɛkashɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ he, ni ji he ni ŋmeii fɔɔ yɛ.

english: Why should I cut off the small extra shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishi.

english: Extra shoots suck water and food away from the main mother plant. Removing all but one or two strong suckers directs the soil nutrients into the main plant so it can produce a larger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ he. Ajieɔ ŋmeii fɛɛ ja ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Akɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yaa tso titri lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni afee dumɔwui wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are there small ragged holes and green dust inside the central leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni sũ eŋɔli hu yɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar eating the growing heart of the plant, and the dust is its waste. Treating the center of the plant early kills the worm before it destroys the shoot.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ tsui ni miida lɛ. Ni sũ ji jwɛi. Tsɔɔmɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ mra. Enɛ baagbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛkpãtã ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling tightly upward and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ waa lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by microscopic insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap out of leaves and passing along plant viruses. Controlling these tiny pests stops the leaves from curling and dying.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Emuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni ekɛ helai ni baa tso lɛ mli lɛ yaa. Nibii bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ Enɛɛmɛi baaye abua ni baai lɛ akabɔle amɛhe ni amɛgboi.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my field help my next crop of maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni mikɛduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have beneficial bacteria on their roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, leaving free natural fertilizer behind for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ helatsɛmɛi ahe nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashiɔ ahaa dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I wait for rain before putting granular fertilizer around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ dani mikɛ granular fertilizer awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Plants can only drink nutrients that are dissolved in water. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn the plant's roots and waste your money because the crop cannot absorb dry chemicals.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ anu niyenii ni mli ewo nu mli pɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni efite shika ejaakɛ tsei nyɛŋ aŋɔ tsofai ni egbi lɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn dark, soft, and rotten before they can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ, eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit, usually triggered by inconsistent watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist prevents the plant from getting stressed and allows calcium to reach the growing fruit.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji calcium ni shɛɛɛ aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ ni faaa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ tsiɔ nɔnyɛɛ ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ naa, ni ehaa calcium lɛ shɛɔ aduawai ni miida lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and turn yellow when there is too much sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ hulu la fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and small roots, so direct sunlight burns them easily and dries out their soil. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains nearby creates natural shade that protects young cocoa trees while they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii. No hewɔ lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛdaraa waa lɛ baa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the top is still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil has run out of nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to stay green and grow tall. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the plant regain its strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛdara ni amɛhe wa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or if there are no insects around to carry pollen between flowers. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing light shade during extreme heat helps fruits form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. When the soil is completely dry or if there are no insects blowing pollen between the flowers Keeping the soil evenly moist and shaded during periods of extreme heat will help fruit formation.

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or grows under heavy shade, it spends all its energy building stems and leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the roots underground.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo edaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ. It will use all its energy to build stems and leaves above ground. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: Why do my yam seeds take so long to sprout after I plant them in the mound?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni mikɛ amɛ ewo gɔŋ ko mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers enter a natural resting phase called dormancy after harvest. They will not shoot up sprouts until this resting period ends naturally and the soil gets enough warmth and moisture from the early rains.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ boteɔ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Amɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛyashi be nɛɛ baagbe naa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upward into tight cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee kɔɔpoi ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking sap from the undersides of young leaves, which distorts their growth as they expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni fiteɔ dalɛ beni egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ

english: When plantains are planted too close, their large leaves block sunlight from each other and their roots fight for the same water and soil nutrients, leaving less energy for big fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantains ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Baai wuji lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni yɔɔ kɛha aduawai wuji lɛ faaa.

english: Why do my corn seeds rot in the soil instead of sprouting after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: If you plant after the very first light rain and the weather turns dry and hot again, the seeds get trapped in warm, wet soil without enough continuous water to complete sprouting, allowing soil fungi to rot them.
ga: Kɛji akɛ odu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ fioo lɛ sɛɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni edɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni edɔ nɔ ni nu ni yaa nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak even when the soil has plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than cultivated crops and steal essential plant nutrients, root space, and sunlight from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food in the soil.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni aduɔ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ tsei lɛ amli niyenii ni he hiaa, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ana niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How do I know that my groundnuts are ready for harvesting since the pods are under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-peanuts lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa ejaakɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Groundnuts show they are mature when the leaves turn yellowish and start dropping, and when you pull up a test plant, the inside lining of the pod shells has turned dark brown instead of white.
ga: Peanuts tsɔɔ akɛ amɛdara kɛji baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbɔi shwiemɔ. Ni kɛ́ ogbala kaa tso lɛ kɛtee ŋwɛi lɛ, pod lɛ mli gbogboi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is a key plant food, or that heavy water is drowning the roots so they cannot eat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Aloo tsiimɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyashɛɔ he ko ni anyɛɛɛ aye.

english: Planting the same crop every season sucks out specific nutrients from the soil without giving the ground time to recover, causing the land to get tired.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa afi lɛ shwieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ. ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ agbɔjɔ

english: How does planting cowpeas alongside my main crops help the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas have special roots that trap natural plant food from the air and store it in the ground, acting like a natural fertilizer for other crops.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni jɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmli lɛ, amɛmɔɔ tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa tsei krokomɛi.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely tender and lose water quickly under full heat, which is why they need shade trees to protect them until their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ mli tse waa ni kɛ́ edɔ amɛ kwraa lɛ, nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ koni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli baa lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb up tall wooden stakes to give me big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei kakadaji anɔ koni amɛná ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in the sunshine to manufacture the energy required to grow big tubers underground, and climbing keeps them safe from heat on the soil.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã hulu la lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Ni kɛ́ amɛkwɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava sticks too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛɔ he tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded, their stems and roots fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin plants with tiny tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Etso kɛ eshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei lɛ yɛ bibii ni amɛyitsei bibii.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when they suffer heat stress or irregular watering, as the plant sacrifices flowers to save water and stay alive.
ga: Tomato baashwie efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo hulutsoo loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei kɛ fɔfɔi ashã afɔle koni amɛhere nu ni amɛhi shi.

english: How do weeds in my pepper farm reduce the size of my harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha mikpamɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi?

english: Weeds act like thief plants that steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight intended for your peppers, leaving your crop weak and unproductive.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ tsei ni juɔ, ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha o-peppers lɛ. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwooo yibii.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn brown and fold down even during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfoɔ amɛhe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Browning leaves in the rainy season are usually caused by tiny worms or fungus in the soil that block the plant's roots from drinking water properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii kɛ baa ni tsuɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ baa. yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsiɔ tsei shishifãi anaa koni amɛkanu nu jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli

english: Why do my harvested grains spoil quickly in storage if I pick them right after a rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmaa ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ nitoohe kɛji mijie amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Grains harvested while wet retain trapped moisture inside, which encourages mold to grow and attracts grain-eating bugs inside your storage bags.
ga: Nibii ni akpa beni edɔ lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi emli. Enɛ woɔ ŋmeii hewalɛ ni amɛdara ni egbalaa ŋmeii ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛbaa onitoo kotokui lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which is a key nutrient they need to grow strong and green. It can also happen if the field stays flooded for too long and the roots cannot get enough air.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nu eyi ŋmɔ ko mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my cassava so the tubers don't spoil or get woody?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? Koni ŋmeii lɛ akafite loo amɛkatsɔ tso?

english: Most cassava varieties are ready for harvest between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell it is time when the bottom leaves start turning yellow and dropping off, and the ground around the stem base begins to crack.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ole be ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce a lot of flowers, but the flowers drop off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets extremely hot, when there is irregular watering, or when the plant lacks essential nutrients like phosphorus. Ensuring steady watering and proper shade during hot periods helps fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa Aloo kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be ni sa yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: Why are there small ragged holes in my young maize leaves with powdery dust inside the shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni egbɛ eshwa ni sũ yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central leaf shoot and feeds on the plant. Applying recommended biological treatments or neem oil early in the morning helps control them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni wala yɔɔ mli loo neem fɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ lɛ dani efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like aphids, thrips, or mites, or a virus transmitted by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early using insecticidal soaps or neem sprays helps keep the leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips loo mites, loo helai ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛ akɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem spray tsuɔ nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Plantain trees fall over because their roots are shallow and can be weakened by tiny soil worms called nematodes. Supporting the main stem with a bamboo or wooden prop as the fruit grows prevents the plant from snapping under the heavy weight.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni sũ mli ŋmeii bibii baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ. ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes Akɛ ŋmei loo tsei ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ daa lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ akakumɔ yɛ muji ni tsii shishi.

english: How often should I water my vegetable garden during the dry season to prevent the crops from drying out?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akagbi?

english: Vegetables need consistent moisture, so watering them deeply once a day early in the morning or late in the afternoon is best. Applying dry grass or leaves as mulch around the plants also keeps the soil damp for longer.
ga: Aduawai he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni afɔɔ nɔ shikome daa gbi leebi loo shwane lɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ha otsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is it recommended that I plant cowpeas or beans on the same land where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmã yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans capture nitrogen gas from the air and put it back into the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil, making it more fertile for heavy-feeding crops like maize in the next season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans mɔɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kooloi aniyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa, yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa trees need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds around my yam mounds when the vines start climbing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Pile sweet potatoes beni wain tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɔɔ lɛ?

english: Tall weeds steal light, water, and soil food from your yam plants. Clearing weeds ensures the climbing yam vines get full sunlight and the roots under the mound can expand without competition.
ga: Jwɛi kakadaji juɔ la, nu, kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ sweet potato tsei amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa sweet potato wain tsei ni kwɔɔ lɛ naa hulutsoo be fɛɛ. And the roots under the mound can grow larger without competition.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants turn yellow and dry up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have shallow roots and delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight and hot Harmattan winds. Without temporary shade trees like plantains to protect them and keep the soil cool, the heat evaporates moisture faster than the roots can drink it.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni jɛɔ Harmattan lɛ. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko bɛ, tamɔ plantains, ni baabu shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i. Dɔlɛ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ.

english: How do I choose good cassava stem cuttings that will grow well on my fresh farmland?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei niji kpakpai ni baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mi-sod ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Look for mature, healthy stems from plants that are 8 to 18 months old, avoiding stems that are too thin, soft, or damaged by pests. Good cuttings should be firm, about finger-thickness, and have clear, raised buds along the stem.
ga: Taomɔ tsei ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 18 lɛ amli tsei ni eda ni amɛhe wa. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo tsɔ, ni darako tsɔ, loo ni tsɛŋemɔ helai efite lɛ ahe. Esa akɛ tso nine kpakpa lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni eyɛ fɔfɔii ni mli tse yɛ tso lɛ he fɛɛ

english: Why should I not plant my maize seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for water and soil nutrients, while their leaves fight for sunlight. This competition leaves you with tall, skinny plants that produce tiny cobs or no cobs at all.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la he akaŋ Akaŋshii nɛɛ haa onáa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii. loo cob ko bɛ kwraa

english: Why do yam vines need long wooden stakes to climb on to give me big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ tsei kakadaŋŋ agboi lɛ? Ni kɛ́ okwɔ koni onine ashɛ yitso agbo nɔ lɛ hu?

english: Yam plants make food in their leaves using sunlight to feed the growing tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they can catch maximum sunlight without rotting or catching fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛbaai lɛ feɔ niyenii, ni amɛkɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛhaa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking woɔ tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ ni amɛkafite loo amɛkaná tsɛŋemɔ hela.

english: Why do the leaves on my fresh plantain suckers dry up after I transplant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi plantain tsei heei lɛ anɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Transplanting causes temporary shock because the root system gets disturbed and cannot supply water immediately. Cut off most of the outer leaves before planting so the sucker does not lose too much water while building new roots.
ga: Kɛ́ atsake tso lɛ, tsɔne lɛ tswaa be kukuoo ko ejaakɛ shishifã lɛ mli gbala ni anyɛɛɛ aha nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Kpɔ̃ɔ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo dani okɛdu. Enɛ ji koni nu ni nuɔ nu lɛ akafite tsɔ yɛ be mli ni ebɔɔ shishifãi heei lɛ.

english: Why do pepper leaves curl up when the sun gets very hot during the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl inward during intense sun to reduce their surface area and save moisture. However, if they stay curled all the time, it is usually a sign of sucking pests like thrips or mites feeding under the leaves.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ mli yɛ hulu be mli koni eha nɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi ni eha fɛ̃i ahi shi. Shi, kɛji akɛ amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, Bei pii lɛ eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ thrips loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ.

english: How do planting beans or cowpeas make my farmland better for the next crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha miŋmɔ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas have special bacteria in their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil. When the plant dies, this trapped nitrogen acts as natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas yɛ helai krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nɛkɛ nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Fertilizers are strong salts that need soil water to dissolve so plant roots can drink them safely. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can concentrate the salts around the roots and burn or kill the crop.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ ni biɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni etsɔ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu amɛ shweshweeshwe. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmei abɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe ni eshã loo efite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when temperatures get too high or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Extreme heat makes the pollen dry out and die before it can fertilize the flower to form a fruit.
ga: Tomatoi shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after the first major rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are already adapted to local soils and rest in the ground waiting for water to burst into growth. Crop seeds take longer to settle, while native wild weeds naturally sprout fast to grab early nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ etsɔ amɛhe amɛwo jɛmɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli momo ni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛmɛɔ ni nu lɛ akwɛ̃. Dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛhiɔ shi. Yɛ be mli ni adebɔɔ mli jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya koni amɛmɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ mra.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I plant different types of vegetables together in the same field instead of just one?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu aduawai srɔtoi yɛ he kome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ fe nɔ ni miduɔ eko pɛ lɛ?

english: Mixing different crop species helps protect your soil and manage pests naturally. Some crops put vital nutrients like nitrogen back into the ground while others feed on them, creating a balanced farm where plants support each other.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi ni afɔɔ amɛ lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni ekwɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Tsei komɛi kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ kuɔ sɛɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi yeɔ niyenii nɛɛ Enɛ haa ŋmɔ ni ja baa ni tsei yeɔ amɛbuaa amɛhe.

english: Why do weeds always seem to grow much faster than the food crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that are adapted to quickly steal sunlight, water, and soil food from your farm crops. Early and regular clearing gives your young crops the space and nutrients they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni atsake amɛ koni amɛju hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Mra be mli ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli Ni ehaa otsei bibii lɛ hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ daa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for maize, or that heavy rainfall has flooded the soil and is choking the plant roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmãa Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How does adding dried farm animal manure help my soil and crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmeii ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Animal manure acts as a natural soil food that slowly releases essential nutrients to plants and helps the soil hold on to water much longer during warm weather.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni yaa hiɛ fiofio. Ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ kpo fiofio kɛyaa tsei lɛ anɔ. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be babaoo yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: How can I protect my cassava leaves from insects without buying expensive chemical sprays?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ abu ŋmeii ahe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ahe ni aheee tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmeii anɔ ni jara wa?

english: You can make safe and affordable sprays at home using local materials like extracts from neem tree leaves, wood ash, or mild soapy water to repel leaf-eating insects.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ maŋ lɛ mli nibii tamɔ neem baa mli nu, tso mli sũ, loo nu ni mli ejɔ ni akɛ saamɔ ewo mli lɛ afee tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni jara waaa yɛ shia. Koni akɛshwie kooloi ni yeɔ baai lɛ

english: Pepper flowers usually drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme afternoon heat, lack of water, or a shortage of plant nutrients needed to form fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo tsei lɛ amli niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛwo yibii lɛ haaa tsei lɛ aná haomɔ.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable farm early in the morning or in the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning gives roots plenty of time to drink the water before the hot afternoon sun evaporates moisture from the top layer of soil.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa shishifãi lɛ leebi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛnuɔ nu dani shwane hulu lɛ shwieɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I trim or remove some of the extra side branches on my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo loo majie niji ni fa fe nine yɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning unnecessary branches allows the tomato plant to send its food directly to growing big, healthy tomatoes rather than wasting energy on surplus leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni he ehiaaa lɛ, ehaa tomato tso lɛ kɛ niyenii majeɔ tomato ni miida ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: How can I test if the dried seeds I saved from last year's harvest are good enough to plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji dumɔwui ni egbi ni mibua naa kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu?

english: Place a sample of your seeds in a bowl of clean water; seeds that sink to the bottom are solid and healthy enough to sprout, while seeds that float are empty or insect-damaged.
ga: Okɛ odumɔwui lɛ ahe nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ awo nu ni mli tse mli. Dumɔwui ni shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shishi lɛ wa ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃. Dumɔwui ni hoɔ lɛ baafee efolo loo kooloi bibii baafite amɛ.

english: How can I store my harvested yams in the barn so they do not rot quickly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ ato ŋmɔ mli koni amɛkafite oya?

english: Store your yams off the ground in a cool, well-ventilated barn and separate bruised or damaged tubers from the rest, as damaged yams rot fast and spread decay to healthy ones.
ga: Okɛ o-sweet potato lɛ ato shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. ni ajie yitsei ni ekpɔtɔ loo efite lɛ kɛjɛ ekrokomɛi lɛ amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni efite lɛ baagboi oya ni amɛbaatsɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, an essential food they need from the soil to stay healthy, or that too much standing water is choking their roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ ji niyenii ko ni he hiaa ni he hiaa amɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ. Aloo nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ tsiɔ eshishifãi lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my crops grow much stronger when I mix animal manure into the soil before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli wa waa nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani midu lɛ?

english: Animal manure acts as a slow-release natural food for crops and acts like a sponge in the soil, holding onto moisture so your plants stay hydrated during dry days.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni jeɔ kpo blɛoo kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii. ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ sponji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ehiɛɔ nu mli bɔni afee ni otsei lɛ ahi shi yɛ nu mli yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: Leaf curling is a defense trick pepper plants use to shield themselves from intense sun and reduce the amount of water escaping from their leaves during the hottest hours.
ga: Leaf curling ji ŋaa ni buɔ mɔ he ni pepper tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. ni eha nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ aba shi.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the stems before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: When the weather gets too hot or the plants do not get enough water, tomato plants drop their flowers to save energy and protect themselves from dying under stress.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagboi yɛ haomɔ shishi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant multiple maize seeds too close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the young plants end up fighting each other for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, resulting in thin stems and very small cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, nu kɛ hulu la mli, ni no haa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight; fast-growing plantain leaves act like wide umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. The fast-growing plantain leaves act like wide umbrellas. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Lifting yam leaves high up on stakes helps them catch as much sunlight as possible, which allows the plant to produce more energy and grow much bigger underground tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ owó sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ hewalɛ babaoo. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraa babaoo.

english: How do cassava roots grow so big underneath the ground while the stem grows above?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ daraa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ daraa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves catch sunlight to manufacture food, and whatever energy the plant does not use immediately is sent downstairs to be stored in the roots, causing them to swell into thick tubers.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ naa hulu la koni ekɛfee niyenii. Akɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ hewalɛ ni tsei kɛtsuuu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ yaa shishigbɛ koni akɛto shishifãi lɛ amli. ni ehaa amɛfuɔ ni amɛfeɔ yitsei ni mli tse

english: Why do weeds in my field cause my main crops to look thin and sickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ afee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal food, water, and root space directly from your main crops, effectively starving your crops while they grow.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. This will starve your crops while they grow.

english: Why should I wait until after a good rain before spreading fertilizer around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ jogbaŋŋ dani makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so roots can drink it in; applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn plant roots and waste the fertilizer.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite.

english: Why does my harvested cocoa spoil if it stays under cloudy skies without bright sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋwɛi ni atatu ewo mli ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa bɛ mli lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Cocoa beans need direct sunlight to dry quickly and evenly. When the weather stays cloudy, humidity remains high and the wet beans absorb moisture from the air, creating perfect conditions for mold to grow and ruin the batch.
ga: Cocoa yibii lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛgbi oya ni amɛfee ekome. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ewo atatu lɛ Humidity baakã he ahi shi ni kɔfi ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ baajie fɛ̃i kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni ŋmeii lɛ adara ni efite nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I let rain touch my cocoa beans while they are drying on raised mats?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ be mli ni migbiɔ yɛ tsɔne ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Rainwater rehydrates drying beans, causing them to spoil, develop internal mold, and lose the rich flavor required by cocoa buyers.
ga: Nugbɔ nu baaha kookoo yibii lɛ agbi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ. Fungus baa mli ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔ ni ŋɔɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ kookoo lɛ taoɔ lɛ baa shi

english: How often should I turn my cocoa beans while drying them under the sun?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ mi-kookoo lɛ nɔ yɛ hulu lɛ mli?

english: You should turn the beans several times a day so that every side receives equal heat and air, preventing trapped moisture underneath where rot can start.
ga: Esa akɛ otsake kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ shii abɔ yɛ gbi kome mli bɔni afee ni fãi lɛ fɛɛ aná dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekabote he ni ebaanyɛ eje shishi egbo lɛ shishi.

english: Is it bad to spray my cocoa trees when rain is about to fall?
ga: Ani ejaaa akɛ aaashwã kookoo tsei anɔ tsofa kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ?

english: Yes, spraying right before rain washes the chemical off the leaves before the plant can absorb it, wasting your money and leaving crops exposed to pests.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsofai kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli dani tsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Eji oshika ni ofiteɔ ni ehaa onibii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ yeɔ.

english: How do I know if a motorized power sprayer is too big or heavy for my cocoa farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ da loo etsii tsɔ kɛha mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: If a machine is very heavy and hard to carry through closely planted trees, it will tire you out quickly and high-pressure blasts can physically damage young pods and blossoms.
ga: Kɛji tsɔne lɛ tsii ni ewa akɛ oootsɔ tsei ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ amli lɛ Ebaaha ogbɔjɔ oya. Ni tsɔnei ni tswaa ni mli wa waa lɛ baanyɛ afite fɔfɔi kɛ fɔfɔi bibii lɛ yɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to spray chemical treatments on my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔ kookoo tsei anɔ?

english: Early morning or late afternoon is best because the air is cooler, allowing the mist to stick to leaves without evaporating too quickly in the hot sun.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli Ehi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Enɛ haa afua lɛ kpɛtɛɔ baai lɛ ahe ni efoŋ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why is my spray machine leaving large drips on leaves instead of a fine mist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sprayer lɛ shĩɔ nu agboi yɛ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ afua bibii najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Large drips usually mean the spray nozzle is clogged or the pressure is too low, which wastes chemical and can burn the plant leaves instead of covering them evenly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni hoɔ babaoo lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ efo loo nu lɛ mli hewalɛ eba shi tsɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ tsofai ni ekolɛ ebaashã tso lɛ baai lɛ moŋ fe ni eeeha amɛhe pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Continuous rain creates high moisture in the air and on the pods, allowing fungal diseases like Black Pod to grow fast and spread across wet trees.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli kɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ hulutsoo babaoo baa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ahe helai, tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ daa oya ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa tsei ni efɔ lɛ ateŋ.

english: Why do cocoa trees drop their young pods when there is too much rain and no sun for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei shwieɔ amɛbii bibii lɛ ashwieɔ shi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo ni hulu la hu bɛ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Without sunlight, trees cannot produce enough food to support all their pods, so they shed young pods to keep the main tree alive during stressful weather.
ga: Kɛji hulu la bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshwieɔ ŋmeii bibii koni tso titri lɛ ahi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni haa mɔ haoɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why do cocoa leaves turn yellow when floodwater sits on my farm for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nu hi miŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Standing water drowns tree roots by blocking oxygen, preventing the tree from absorbing soil nutrients and causing leaves to yellow and fall off.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ shwieɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekaŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I cut down all the large trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mifo tsei wuji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive direct, intense heat from the sun. Taller trees and food crops like plantains provide necessary shade, keeping the leaves cool and protecting the soil moisture so the roots do not dry out.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ kɛ niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa. Ehaa baai lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ he koni shishifãi lɛ akagbi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow in a V-shape even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves in maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is main plant food. The crop steals nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed new growth at the top when the soil nutrients run out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso lɛ niyenii titri lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋmeii heei ni eda yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii beni sũ lɛ mli niyenii lɛ faaa lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava crop drop all its leaves during the dry season, and does it mean the crop is dead?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ? Ni ani no tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbo?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells as a natural survival trick to prevent water loss. The plant is not dead; it goes dormant and keeps its stored energy underground in the tubers until the rains return.
ga: Akɛ ŋmei baa shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala yibiiwoo gbɛ koni nu akafite. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Ebaajɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ hewalɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ eyitso mli kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on sticks so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight to manufacture food for the tuber. Leaves sitting on hot, damp soil get diseases more easily and produce much smaller yams.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Baai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ helai nyɛɔ emɔ amɛ oya, ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii kwraa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high or when plants face sudden water stress. Extreme heat damages the pollen inside the flower, causing the plant to drop unpollinated flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ trukaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do people advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu tsina loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have roots that suck nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural fertilizer in the soil. Planting them with maize feeds the maize and leaves the soil fertile for the next season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and shrinking into tight knots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee ŋmeii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips feeding on the plant sap and spreading viruses. As they suck nutrients, the leaves warp and stop the plant from growing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni yeɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. be mli ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ Baai lɛ tsɔɔ sɛɛ ni amɛtsiɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ kpakpa naa.

english: Why should I clear away small suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Mi plantain tsei titrii lɛ etee.

english: Leaving too many suckers around one mother plantain causes them to fight for water, space, and food underground. Pruning away excess suckers leaves only one or two shoots, ensuring large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Ni aaashi ŋmeii babaoo ni ebɔle Dumɔwu kome pɛ he lɛ baaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu, ŋwɛi, kɛ niyenii he yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaashi ŋmeii 1 loo 2 pɛ ni ekɛfee plantain panicle agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do my groundnuts rot in the ground if I wait too long after maturity to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mimɛ be kakadaŋŋ dani mikpa lɛ?

english: When groundnuts mature underground, the stalks attaching pods to the plant dry out and break. Leaving mature pods in wet soil attracts soil fungi and insects that cause the shells to soften and the nuts inside to spoil.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii kwɛ̃ kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Tso lɛ tso ni kɛ ŋmeii lɛ kpãa tso lɛ he lɛ baagbi ni ebaagbala. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni eda yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ lɛ, egbalaa sũ mli ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my pepper and tomato roots rot and die when water stays pooled on my farm after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nu ŋmɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Roots need air to breathe just like people do. When water sits on the farm for days, it drowns the roots by cutting off air, causing them to turn black, rot, and stop feeding the plant.
ga: Taakɛ gbɔmɛi ji lɛ, shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo Akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni afoɔ lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ, amɛgboɔ ni amɛkpaa tso lɛ niyenii hamɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a major food source in the soil. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color so they can grow strong cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hewalɛ. Kooloo ŋmei, ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ ŋmei lɛ aku sɛɛ aba koni ŋmei lɛ anyɛ adara waa.

english: Tomato leaves curl up to protect themselves from losing too much water in extreme heat. By rolling their leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun so it does not dry out.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi bɔni afee ni baai lɛ akagbi.

english: Why does leaving weeds around my cassava reduce the size of the tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni Hewɔ Eshiɔ Jwɛi yɛ He No hewɔ lɛ mi-cassava tubers lɛ ji bibii?

english: Weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients away from the young cassava plant. When cassava has to fight weeds for survival, it puts its energy into growing thin roots instead of storing food in thick tubers.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ ŋmei tsei bibii amli. Beni esa akɛ ŋmei kɛ jwɛi awui koni ehi shi lɛ Ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ shishifãi bibii amli yɛ niyenii ni ekɛtoɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ amli lɛ najiaŋ.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet and cool conditions. Pruning extra tree branches to let sunlight and air flow through the farm helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli. Niji krokomɛi ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to sprout if I plant them when the soil is only slightly damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ ni ŋmɔtɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize seeds need a strong, steady supply of water to break open their hard outer shell and start growing. If the soil is too dry, the seed absorbs only a little water, gets stuck, and dies underground.
ga: Nu ni yaa nɔ daa, ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ he miihia ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛgbala amɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni wa lɛ mli ni amɛbɔi dalɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ nu fioo pɛ, amɛkpɛtɛɔ he, ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce smaller fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, their roots tangle and fight for the same limited food and water in the soil. Giving each pepper plant enough space allows its roots to spread wide and support bigger peppers.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ feɔ ekome ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛhiɛ niyenii kɛ nu fioo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli. Kɛ́ aha pepper tso fɛɛ tso he gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni eshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa pepper tso wuji lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on to give me good yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ koni maná sweet potato kpakpai lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves out toward direct sunlight. When the leaves catch plenty of sun, they create more energy, which travels down to swell the yam tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã kɛya hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa Ebaaha hewalɛ babaoo aba. ni tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi ni ehaa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or a sudden lack of water. If the plant feels it doesn't have enough water to nourish fruit, it sheds the flowers to save its own life.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni faaa trukaa lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Kɛji tso lɛ nu he akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ bɛ lɛ Ebaashwie efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala.

english: Why is it good to leave dry crop leaves on top of the soil instead of burning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaashi tsei ahe baai ni egbi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ moŋ fe ni aaashã amɛ lɛ?

english: Leaving dry leaves on the ground acts like a natural blanket that keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating. As the leaves rot, they turn into rich organic food that feeds your next crop.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi baai ni egbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli tsɔne ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi. Beni baai lɛ miifite lɛ Ebaatsɔ niyenii ni jara wa, ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle harsh direct sunlight. They require temporary shade crops, like plantains, to shield them from heat and help the soil retain moisture while their roots develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛtsi dɔlɛ naa ni eye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do older farmers tell me not to plant cassava right next to my cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa ko kɛɛ mi akɛ mikadu ŋmei yɛ mikookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Cassava is a heavy feeder that spreads wide roots underground, stealing nutrients and water away from young cocoa trees and slowing down their early growth.
ga: Cassava ji niyenii ni tsii ni gbɛɔ eshishifãi lɛ eshwaa shikpɔŋ shishi. Ejuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ cacao tsei bibii amli. ni ehaa dalɛ baa shi

english: Why are some of my small green cocoa pods turning black and dry before they can grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ No hewɔ lɛ minɔ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbi dani etsɔ agbo.

english: This is typically caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in cool, wet, and dark conditions, destroying pods before they mature.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni duŋ yɔɔ, ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛdaraa.

english: Why do tiny insects cause the young branches on my cocoa trees to look burnt and die back?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii haa tsei niji bibii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ashã ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: These insects are capsids (mirids) that suck sap from young stems and leaves, injecting toxic saliva that damages the branches and stops the tree from producing fruit.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji capsid kooloi bibii (mirids) ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii kɛ baai amli lɛ. Okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni fiteɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ ashwie shi ni ehaaa tso lɛ awo yibii.

english: Why should I cut off the extra shoots growing out of the main trunk of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ cacao tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ mli lɛ?
