english: These shoots, called chupons, drain nutrients from the main tree without producing good pods. Cutting them off directs energy into pod development and allows airflow to prevent disease.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli ni ekɛ ŋmeii kpakpai baaa. Amɛfolɔ kudɔɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa pod lɛ shweremɔ he ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli koni helai akabote mli.

english: Why are flowers falling off my cocoa trees without turning into any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects like midges for pollination; if the weather is too dry or the tree lacks soil nutrients, it drops flowers to protect itself from exhaustion.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii biɔ kooloi bibii akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛfeɔ pollination. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Amɛbaafɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwie shi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ tɔlɛ he.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees need fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: When cocoa trees lack nutrients, their leaves turn pale green or yellow instead of deep green, and the trees produce fewer, smaller pods than usual.
ga: Kɛji akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ kookoo tso lɛ mli lɛ Ebaai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. ni tso lɛ baawo ŋmeii fioo ni amɛbaawo bibii fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I scrape away all the fallen dead leaves under my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egbee shi yɛ kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Fallen leaves act as a natural blanket that keeps the soil cool and moist, breaking down over time into rich organic plant food for the cocoa roots.
ga: Baai ni egbee shi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ. Yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, egbɛɔ eshwaa ni etsɔɔ tso niyenii ni jara wa waa kɛha kookoo shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees giving fewer pods every year even though I clear the weeds around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso momo lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo daa afi lɛ? Ani ajie jwɛi ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce less fruit as they age past 25 to 30 years, indicating that the old trees need to be gradually pruned back or replaced with newer, high-yielding varieties.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ woɔ yibii fioo yɛ amɛfɔmɔ su naa kɛji amɛye afii 25 kɛyashi 30, ni no tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni tso lɛ adara fiofio. Kpɔ̃ɔ amɛ loo okɛ srɔtoi heei ni woɔ yibii babaoo awo amɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why is it important for all farmers in my community to treat tree diseases at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni okwaafoi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mi akutso lɛ mli lɛ atsa tsei ahe helai yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Diseases and pests easily spread across farm boundaries, so if one neighboring farm leaves an infection untreated, the pests will quickly travel back onto surrounding healthy farms.
ga: Helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ husui lɛ amli fɛɛ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ateŋ ekome shi hela lɛ ni atsaaa lɛ, Pests hu baaku esɛɛ oya kɛya ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli.

english: Will using a machine like a tractor to plow my field help my crop roots grow better than clearing by hand?
ga: Ani tsɔne ko tamɔ trakta ni mikɛaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ fe ni mikɛ nine baakpa amɛ?

english: Machines loosen deep, hardened soil much better than hand tools, making it easier for crop roots to spread deep into the earth to drink water and absorb nutrients.
ga: Tsɔnei shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni wa lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ fe nibii ni akɛ niji tsuɔ nii. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛha tsei shishifãi akɛ amɛ baa gbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛnu nu ni amɛ nu niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Yam tubers twist and bend when they hit hard, unplowed soil underground. Digging deep, loose soil mounds gives the tuber space to push straight downward.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ amɛhe kɛji amɛtswa shikpɔŋ ni wa ni atsuuu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni etse ehe lɛ ni akuɔ lɛ baaha tuber he lɛ ashɛ shi tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field without shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kooko tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that easily scorch under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains protects them from harsh heat while they establish root systems.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ maa eshishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa beni miduɔ amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they compete for sunlight and stretch upward as fast as possible, resulting in tall, weak stems that break easily in strong winds.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ ni amɛbaakpã amɛhe kɛya ŋwɛi oya bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni kɛlɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni fãa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing huge bushy leaves but producing very tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai wuji shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or fresh manure, the cassava plant spends all its energy building leaves above ground instead of storing starch in its root tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii heei babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛmaa baai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my land help my next crop of maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni mikɛduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua mi ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that nitrogen stays in the dirt as natural food for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii aha onibii ni obaakpa yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into fruit during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes tomato flowers to dry out before pollination can happen, so the plant drops the dead flowers to save its remaining water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani anyɛɔ ashɛɔ amɛhe. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni egboi lɛ koni ekɛbu nu ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants turn yellow and drop off when rain floods my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Flooded soil suffocates plant roots by cutting off air. Starved of oxygen, the roots rot and cannot send nutrients up to the leaves, causing them to turn yellow.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ hewɔ No sɛɛ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aya baai lɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why don't my maize seeds sprout when I bury them deep in the ground during planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ be mli ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds buried too deep run out of stored food energy pushing up through the heavy dirt before their green shoots can reach the surface sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui ni afu amɛ tsɔ lɛ baafite niyenii hewalɛ ni ato lɛ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛ gbɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji lɛ nɔ. dani eshishifãi ni eŋɔli lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ he.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look pale and sickly even when rain falls regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni hela mɔ amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing root systems that steal food and water from the soil much faster than your crops can, leaving your crops starving.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ oya fe oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure around the base will help them turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ. Konii lɛ baaye abua amɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant experiences irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and covering the ground around the stem with dry grass mulch helps keep the roots cool.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants feel sticky and curl up tightly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛhe wa ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Sticky, curled leaves are caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that leave a sugary substance behind. Spraying the undersides of the leaves with mild soapy water or recommended organic pesticides can clear them off.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies kɛ baa ni ebɔle ehe, ni wa baa. ni shĩɔ nɔ ko ni mli edɔ yɛ sɛɛ. Ni akɛ nu ni mli ejɔ ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ nɔ. Aloo, tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ bɔɔ nii amli ni ajieɔ yi lɛ baanyɛ ajie amɛ.

english: What is causing small holes in my corn leaves and chewed-up centers in the stems?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ kɛ fãi ni ashɛreɔ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ shishi lɛ anɔ.

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central funnel of the maize plant. Applying recommended crop protection products early in the morning or late in the evening helps control them before they destroy the yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni akɛbuɔ tsei ahe ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa plants the shade and cool soil moisture they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over during windstorms before the fruits mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbee shi yɛ ahum ko mli dani aduawai lɛ kwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit bunches, making them top-heavy. Supporting the main stem with strong wooden poles or bamboos, a practice called propping, prevents the wind from knocking them over.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ aduawai akui ni tsii. kɛ muji babaoo baa Akɛ tsei loo ŋmeii ni wa fiɔ tso wulu lɛ sɛɛ. Nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ bracing. Enɛ baatsi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ naa koni ekatswa amɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long during heavy rains. Planting your cassava stems on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Fertilizer works best when applied into moist soil shortly after planting or during early growth. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn the plant roots, while applying it right before a heavy rainstorm can wash it away completely.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ loo yɛ be mli ni edara mra lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ shishifãi ashã. Shi okɛwo mli dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aho tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ.

english: How do I keep my harvested yams from sprouting and getting soft in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efee blɛoo kɛji akɛ akɛto?

english: Yams sprout and lose water when exposed to excess heat and direct light. Storing tubers on raised wooden racks in a cool, dark, well-ventilated yam barn slows down sprouting and keeps them firm.
ga: Sweet potatoes baakwɛ̃ ni nu baaje mli kɛji akɛ akɛwo la ni mli edɔ fe nine kɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ mli. Kɛ tubers lɛ ato tsei ni awo nɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ sweet potato shĩa ni mli ejɔ, ni yɔɔ duŋ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni ebaaha ehi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than the crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are natural wild plants that adapt very quickly to steal sun, water, and soil food from your farm. Clearing weeds while your crops are still small ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to grow faster than the weeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni jɛɔ adebɔɔ mli ni tsakeɔ amɛhe oya koni amɛju hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi shwie shi yɛ be mli ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako lolo lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya fe jwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms without producing fruit when the afternoon sun gets very intense?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛwooo yibii be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, tomato pollen becomes sticky or sterile, preventing proper pollination. High heat also stresses the plant, causing it to drop flowers to save energy and water rather than producing fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Tomato pollen lɛ shwieɔ shi loo ebɛ fɔmɔ nii. Etsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa hu haa tsei haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu akafite yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: How does growing vegetables inside a covered structure like a greenhouse help them grow better than planting in the open field?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ aduawai ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni tamɔ ŋmɔ ni aha nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ fe ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse mli lɛ?

english: A greenhouse controls the crop's environment by blocking harsh heat, trapping soil moisture, and keeping out common insects and heavy rains. This allows crops to grow continuously, produce higher yields, and suffer fewer diseases.
ga: Greenhouses kudɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛtsɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni tsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi bibii ni afɔɔ namɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ahe Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa be fɛɛ be. Ha nitsumɔ ni nɔ kwɔ kɛ hela ni baa shi

english: Why do my leafy vegetables wilt in the afternoon heat even though I water them every morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa leebi moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, leaves lose water through transpiration faster than the roots can suck it up from the soil. Watering early helps, but under strong tropical heat, plants temporarily wilt to protect themselves until temperatures cool down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ latsaa nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli mra lɛ yeɔ ebuaa, shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, Tso lɛ baagbo yɛ be kukuoo mli koni ebu ehe he kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: This is usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency. Nitrogen moves easily inside the plant, so when soil nutrients are low, the maize plant steals nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nitrogen lɛ nyiɛɔ yɛ tsei amli oya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa lɛ, Abɛi juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛye baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with huge green leaves but produce very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to spend all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in the roots underground. Balanced soil nutrients with adequate potassium are needed for thick tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ja kɛ potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmeii ni mli tse.

english: If I plant my crops very close together, will I harvest more produce from my plot?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani manyɛ makpa babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too closely forces crops to fight over sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak plants with smaller fruits, whereas proper spacing gives each plant enough room and resources to produce maximum yields.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai bibii baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo yibii babaoo.

english: Should I trim off the small side branches growing on my tomato plants or leave them to grow?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei niji bibii lɛ? Jiemɔ fã ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tomato tso lɛ nɔ lɛ loo oha ekwɛ̃?

english: Removing those extra side shoots (called suckers) directs the plant's energy into growing bigger, healthier tomatoes instead of wasting energy on excess leaves. It also improves airflow around the plant, reducing disease.
ga: Ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ŋmeii (ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii) lɛ kudɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ koni ekwɛ tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ he lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa helai ni baa lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why does my field produce smaller harvests every year if I keep planting tomatoes on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo daa afi kɛji mitee nɔ midu tomato yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and soil diseases that target tomatoes to build up. Rotating with crops like beans or maize helps restore the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni tsɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ.

english: Why do white powdery patches cover my cucumber leaves when the weather gets warm and humid?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ haa mi kukumba baai lɛ anɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ?

english: This is powdery mildew, a fungal disease that thrives in warm, humid weather with poor air circulation around plants. It coats the leaves and stops them from absorbing sunlight, weakening the whole plant.
ga: Enɛ ji powder mli ŋmei. Enɛ ji fungal hela ko ni yaa hiɛ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Akɛni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ eyaaa tso lɛ he jogbaŋŋ hewɔ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ ahe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaaa amɛná hulu la lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tso muu lɛ fɛɛ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do wild weeds stay green and healthy during hot dry spells while my planted crops wither?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ be mli ni tsei ni miduɔ lɛ gboɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with deep root systems and natural toughness that allow them to search deep underground for moisture and survive stress much better than domesticated crops, which require extra care and managed water.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛhe wa yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni no haa amɛtaoɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ haomɔi amli jogbaŋŋ fe shia tsei, ni biɔ kwɛmɔ babaoo kɛ nu he nitsumɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen acts as the main building block for leaf growth, and when it is missing, the plant cannot make enough green chlorophyll to feed itself.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ titri ni haa baa lɛ daa. Ni kɛ́ elaaje lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ afee klorofil ni ji eŋɔli ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkwɛ amɛhe.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every season when I plant maize on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ faaa daa be mli ni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop loves without giving the soil time to replenish. It also allows pests and diseases that attack maize to multiply in the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii ni tsei sumɔɔ lɛ pɛ ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ awo mli ekoŋŋ. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ hu feɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce very tiny tubers when I plant the stem cuttings close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ hiɛ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded, their roots compete heavily with each other underground for limited water and food, leaving less energy for the roots to swell into large tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii fioo. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni eshwɛɔ lɛ baa shi koni shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why did my young cocoa seedlings begin to wilt and dry up after I cut down the large shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ miibɔi shwiemɔ ni amɛmiigbi beni mifo hulutsoo tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight. Shade trees act as living shields that cool the soil, retain moisture, and protect young cocoa leaves from burning.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gãimlibi ni hiɛ ka ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi, ni ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe koni amɛkashã.

english: Why do the blossoms on my pepper plants keep falling off before any peppers form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani pepper lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or uneven watering. When it is too hot or dry, the plant sheds its flowers to conserve energy for its own survival.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ekɛhaaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛji edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ tsɔ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why are my plantain bunches smaller and taking much longer to mature during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛheɔ be babaoo dani amɛdaraa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain needs steady water to transport nutrients from the roots up into the fruiting stem. Without adequate water, the plant slows down its fruit development to conserve energy.
ga: Nu ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ he miihia plantains koni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aya kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛya tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ anɔ. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ haa aduawai lɛ daalɛ baa shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: If I save seeds from my high-yielding hybrid maize harvest and plant them next season, why do they grow so poorly?
ga: Kɛji akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ mli lɛ to ni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ amɛkwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ nɛkɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred from two unique parent plants for one generation of high performance. The seeds saved from that harvest lose those special traits and produce weak, uneven yields.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔ̃ɔ fɔlɔi tsei enyɔ ni yɔɔ srɔtoi lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni enyɛ etsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ yinɔ kome mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee.

english: Why do my yam mounds yield very small yams if I plant them late in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato pile lɛ naa sweet potato fioo ko kɛji midu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Yam plants require a long vegetative period under steady rains to grow big leaves that capture sunlight energy to build and expand large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛdara yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ shishi koni amɛkwɛ baai wuji ni ŋmɛɔ hulu la hewalɛ koni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly into tubes during the middle of hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe amɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism. By rolling its leaves up, the tomato plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun, preventing excessive water evaporation.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ baai lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ebaaha tomato tso lɛ hiɛ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi. Tsi nu ni hoɔ fe nine lɛ naa.

english: Why do caterpillars suddenly appear and eat the center leaves of my maize after a short break in the rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baa trukaa koni amɛbaye mi-ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be kukuoo ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pests like Fall Armyworm thrive in warm, dry spells following early rain. The hot, dry weather speeds up their hatching cycle, causing sudden attacks on vulnerable plant shoots.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ be ni mli edɔ, ni nugbɔ enɛɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ mli. Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ yaa oya. Ekɛ trukaa tutuamɔ baa tso ni bɛ hewalɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow from the middle instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, a vital food for crop growth. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or rotating your maize with nitrogen-fixing crops like groundnuts helps bring back healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Ni akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmãa ni akɛ nitrogen-fixing ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa woɔ mli lɛ baaye abua tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ ni amɛdara ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant corn on the exact same piece of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ?

english: Planting corn continuously on the same soil drains specific nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up. Rotating corn with crops like beans restores soil fertility and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ lɛ baa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni ehaa helai ni yaa nɔ lɛ kpaa.

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving crops proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to produce large, healthy fruits or tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa kã tsei ateŋ lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ aduawai loo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I choose the right cassava stems to cut for planting on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei ni sa ni mafo koni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Select mature, healthy cassava stems from plants that produced good yields and show no spots or pest damage. Cut pieces from the middle portion of the main stem, ensuring each cutting has at least 3 to 7 raised nodes.
ga: Halamɔ ŋmei tsei ni eda, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli. ni ŋmɔtɔ loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii bɛ mli, ni afolɔ mli bibii bibii kɛjɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ teŋgbɛ. Kwɛmɔ ni kɛ hoo lɛ, fã fɛɛ fã ni afo lɛ aná fãji 3 kɛyashi 7 ni awó nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees burn and dry up when I cut down all the tall trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei kakadaji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains near young cocoa creates living umbrellas that shield them from heat and retain moisture until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Aduɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe. Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa.

english: Yam leaves produce food for the growing tuber underground and need sunlight to do this. Staking lifts leaves off the damp ground where diseases spread, allowing them to catch maximum sunlight for bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ woɔ niyenii kɛhaa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ni hulu la he miihia amɛ koni amɛfee enɛ. Shihilɛhe lɛ holeɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ. Enɛ haa yitsei wuji lɛ naa hulu la babaoo.

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes, called blossom-end rot, are caused by a lack of calcium uptake, usually due to irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the plant draw up the calcium it needs.
ga: Atsɛɔ hei diji ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni anyɛɛɛ ashɛ he. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa calcium ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Consistent watering during hot periods helps flowers remain on the plant to form peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni amɛwo ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Leaving too many suckers causes them to steal food and water from the main plantain stem. Removing extra suckers leaves behind just one or two strong stems, resulting in bigger and heavier bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii babaoo kɛjɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ plantain tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni da ni tsii.

english: How does covering the bare soil with dry grass around my crops help them grow during dry spells?
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi ebɔle he lɛ nɔ. Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, blocks the sun from evaporating soil moisture. It keeps the soil cool, conserves water, and stops weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsĩ hulu la lɛ naa ni ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekaho. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ, ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall and bushy but produce tiny tubers when I plant them too close to my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmɔ mli shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni miduɔ lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ ŋmãa tsɔ?

english: When cassava and maize are planted too closely, they compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. The cassava spends its energy growing upward to reach sunlight instead of directing energy underground to build large, starch-filled tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛdaraa kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛ hulu la lɛ akpee, moŋ fe ni eeetsu lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ shishi koni efee ŋmeii agboi ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii.

english: Why is it good practice to plant cowpeas in the same field where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Cowpeas work together with natural soil bacteria to take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. This naturally fertilizes the land, feeding the hungry maize crop and reducing the need for chemical fertilizers.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ adebɔɔ mli sũ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛsaa lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ha ŋmãa tsei ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ niyenii ni oha tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ ahe hiamɔ aba shi

english: Why do I have to wait several years for my new cocoa trees to bear fruit while maize yields in just a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ afii babaoo dani cacao tso hee awo yibii yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa woɔ yibii yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa is a long-term tree crop that invests its early years into establishing deep roots and a strong trunk to survive for decades. Annual crops like maize grow quick, shallow roots to reproduce fast within a single season.
ga: Cocoa ji tso ko ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛ eshishijee afii lɛ daa. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tsei ni mli wa ahi shi afii nyɔŋmai abɔ lɛ, tsei ni yeɔ daa afi tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni amɛfɔɔ oya yɛ be kome mli.

english: Why does letting my land rest unfarmed for a year make my next tomato harvest much bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ miha mishikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe ni mifeee okwaayeli afi kome lɛ, no haa mi-tomato ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ feɔ babaoo nakai lɛ?

english: Leaving land fallow lets nature restore soil health. Dead leaves decompose into rich organic matter, soil organisms rebuild the structure, and nutrient levels recover naturally, giving future crops a strong foundation.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni ashiɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ. Baai ni egboi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ nibii heei. ni niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baaya hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ shishitoo ni ma shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my growing maize plants turning yellow while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. To protect its new leaves at the top, the maize plant steals nitrogen from its older bottom leaves, causing them to lose green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni abu baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ahe lɛ, Abɛi tsei lɛ juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni etsɛ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ ahe su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do my sweet potato tubers turn out crooked and small when planted in hard, unplowed soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ bibii kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni atsuko nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Sweet potato tubers expand underground by pushing against loose earth. In packed, hard soil, the roots struggle to force their way through, resulting in small, bent, and misshapen roots.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ Shishifãi lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛfo mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ daraaa, ebɔle amɛhe, ni amɛhe bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli.

english: Leaf rolling is a survival mechanism. By curling its leaves inward, the maize plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun, slowing down water loss through evaporation during dry spells.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala. Abɛi haa he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ ebaai ni ekɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Ha nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off during very hot, dry weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ otsi ni mli edɔ ni nu bɛ nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get extreme and water is scarce, pepper plants experience heat stress. They drop their blossoms to save water and energy for basic survival, delaying fruit production until rain returns.
ga: Be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ waa ni nu faaa lɛ. Pepper tsei lɛ baaná dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔii amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛha shishijee wala. Kɛtsɔ aduawai ni anáa lɛ ni akɛbaagbe naa kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my young yam vines look weak and stunted so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi sweet potato tsei lɛ miifee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ oya lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal vital soil nutrients, sunlight, and water before young yam roots can reach them. Starving the vine early on prevents it from building strong stems and healthy foliage.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli, hulu la kɛ nu mli dani sweet potato shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Wein tso lɛ ni ayeɔ hɔmɔ kɛjɛɔ egbekɛbiiashi Ebaatsi enaa koni ekafee ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai ni wa.

english: Why do fall armyworms prefer to chew on young maize shoots rather than mature stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛye ŋmãa bibii lɛ moŋ fe ŋmãa ni eda lɛ?

english: Young maize shoots are soft, tender, and high in water and plant sugars, making them easy for young caterpillars to eat and digest compared to tough, fibrous mature stalks.
ga: Abele bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe yɛ mlɛo ni nu kɛ tsei amli sugars fa yɛ mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ akɛ amɛaaye nii ni amɛye nii, kɛ akɛto ŋmeii ni eda, ni wa, ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa trees need steady moisture and shade. During the dry Harmattan season, hot dry winds and direct sunlight evaporate water from the leaves faster than the young roots can pull it from the soil, causing the leaves to dry up and drop unless protected by shade plants.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be. Yɛ Harmattan be ni mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ, ni mli egbi kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa nu ni jɛɔ baai amli lɛ shwieɔ shi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa baai lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ja tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ ebu he.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt in the hot afternoon sun even though I water them every morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Nu ni oooha daa leebi?

english: In intense midday heat, tomatoes lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can absorb it from the soil. Placing dry grass around the base of the plant (mulching) keeps the soil cool and retains moisture, reducing afternoon stress.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tomatoi shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi (mulch) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nɔnyɛɛ baa shi yɛ shwane mli.

english: Why do my crops grow much taller and greener near where I keep my goats than in the rest of the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji yɛ he ni mikwɛɔ mitooi lɛ yɛ lɛ masɛi fe ŋmɔji krokomɛi amli lɛ?

english: Animal manure contains high amounts of nitrogen and essential nutrients. When added to soil, it acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds the plants, helping them build strong stems and deep green leaves much faster.
ga: Nitrogen kɛ niyenii krokomɛi ni he hiaa waa yɛ ŋmɔ mli. Kɛ akɛfata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ Ebaatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa tsei lɛ hewalɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa oya.

english: Why do I get smaller yams when I plant my seed tubers very close to each other on the mound?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmeii bibii anɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui akui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: When plants are overcrowded, their roots compete with each other for nutrients, soil space, and water. Giving each yam enough space ensures the roots have plenty of room and plant food to expand into large tubers.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa niyenii, shikpɔŋ nɔ he ko, kɛ nu he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha sweet potato fɛɛ sweet potato gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ babaoo kɛ tsei niyenii koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does covering the bare soil around my vegetable crops with dry grass help them grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi haa mi-vegetables lɛ koni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Covering soil with dry grass (mulching) blocks direct sunlight, which prevents water from evaporating quickly, stops weeds from growing, and keeps the soil cool so plant roots stay healthy.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa ni ekaho oya. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ koni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into tight cups and stopping new growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee kɔɔpoi ni mli wa ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ hee lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of leaves. As they suck the sap, they deform the tender leaves and stunt the plant's overall growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ numɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. be mli ni enuɔ mliki Efiteɔ baai bibii ni ehaa tso lɛ dalɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why is my cowpea crop producing plenty of flowers but very few actual bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi pea pods diɛŋtsɛ fioo pɛ?

english: Flowers often fall off without producing pods if insect pests eat the delicate flower parts, or if there is too much nitrogen in the soil, which causes the plant to spend its energy growing leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ye. aloo nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why are the stems of my maize plants falling over easily whenever a strong wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ?

english: Maize stalks fall over (lodge) when root systems are weak, planted too shallow, or weakened by pests. Mounding extra soil around the base of the plant (earthing up) gives the roots stronger support against the wind.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi (ejeɔ kpo) kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Adu yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ loo egbɔjɔ yɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahewɔ Okɛ shikpɔŋ krokomɛi ato tso lɛ shishi (shikpɔŋ nɔ) koni eye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛte shi amɛwo kɔɔyɔɔ hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my cassava roots turn woody and hard to cook instead of remaining soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ekomɛi feɔ tsei ni ehoomɔ wa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahi shi blɛoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots turn woody if they are left in the ground too long past their harvest maturity, or if they suffer through extended periods of drought in poor, hard soil.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ ekɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ kpe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ehiii nɔ.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to sprout when I plant them directly into dry soil before the rain begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ tɛ̃ɛ dani nugbɔ nɛ?

english: Seeds require moisture alongside warmth to activate growth. When planted in completely dry soil, the seeds remain dormant and are vulnerable to being eaten by insects or birds before the rains arrive.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ hia hulutsoo kɛfata he koni eha amɛdara. Kɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kwraa nɔ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baakã he ahi shi. ni oshara ni yɔɔ mli akɛ kooloi bibii loo okpoi baaye lɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ aba

english: Why does it matter which specific variety of seed I choose to plant on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mahala dumɔwui pɔtɛɛ ni mikɛbaadu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Different seed varieties are bred for different conditions—some produce higher yields, some mature faster to survive dry spells, and others resist local pests and diseases better than regular seeds.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi yɛ shihilɛi srɔtoi amli. Henɔi komɛi haa yibii babaoo. Henɔi komɛi shwereɔ oya koni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Ni henɔi komɛi nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ mli kooloi kɛ helai fe dumɔwui krokomɛi.

english: Why are certified seeds from dealers better than seeds saved from my local grain market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ jarayelɔ ko ŋɔɔ lɛ hi fe dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mimaŋ ŋmaa jarayelihe lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are carefully produced and tested to guarantee high germination rates and disease resistance, whereas market grain may sprout poorly or carry diseases into your soil.
ga: Afeɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ koni ana akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni helai nyɛŋ amɛye amɛnɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ekolɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ŋ jogbaŋŋ loo amɛkɛ helai baa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know if a crop seed will actually grow well in my farm's soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Crops have different soil needs; some prefer free-draining sandy soil while others need moisture-retaining clay. Testing soil drainage and texture helps determine if a crop will thrive.
ga: Tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ he hiamɔ nii srɔtoi. Mɛi komɛi sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni mɛi komɛi sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ mli lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ kaa yeɔ ebuaa ni anaa kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii baashwere.

english: How can I test if old seeds saved from my previous harvest are still alive and good for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji dumɔwui momo ni abua naa kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni ehi kɛha dumɔ?

english: You can perform a simple germination test by putting ten seeds in a damp cloth for a few days; if fewer than seven sprout, the seed batch is weak and should be replaced.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee shweremɔ he kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Obaanyɛ ofee enɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni okɛaawo mama ni mli efɔ mli lɛ nɔ. kɛha gbii fioo komɛi Kɛji tsei ni fa fe 7 kwɛ̃ lɛ, no lɛ dumɔwui akuu lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni esa akɛ atsake.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with tiny yields when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to weak stalks and small harvests.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe waaa, ni akpaa nii fioo.

english: Why is it risky to plant my crops late after the main rains have already started?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ oshara yɔɔ akɛ abaadu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Late-planted crops miss the early release of rich soil nutrients triggered by first rains and risk drying out before maturity when the rainy season ends.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie shikpɔŋ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ ni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ kpo mra, ni amɛyɛ oshara mli akɛ amɛbaagbi dani amɛdara yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee.

english: What causes the bottom leaves of my crops to turn yellow while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni haa tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, causing the plant to move nutrients from its older leaves up to feed new top growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eye ebua ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmeii heei anɔ.

english: Why do blossoms on my crops sometimes drop off without producing any fruits or grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii loo dumɔwui ko lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when plants experience stress from intense heat, lack of water, poor soil nutrition, or a lack of pollinating insects like bees.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni faaa lɛ mli. aloo kooloi bibii ni feɔ pollin tamɔ ŋmeii ni bɛ

english: Why is it bad to plant the exact same crop on the same field every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and soil diseases to build up, lowering yields over time.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa sũ mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa tsei pɔtɛɛ anɔ lɛ babaoo. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Can I plant two different crops like maize and cassava together on the same field without them destroying each other?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi enyɔ tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa. Ani amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee ekome kɛtsu nii yɛ yiŋkpɛɛ kome mli ni amɛfiteee amɛhe?

english: Yes, intercropping works when planned well; fast-growing maize is harvested early, leaving sunlight and root space for the slower-growing cassava to expand later.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛji ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ. Akpaa ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ mra. Kɛtsɔ hulu la kɛ shishifãi ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ koni ŋmei lɛ ada blɛoo ni sɛɛ mli lɛ egbɛ eshwa lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings get burnt easily under direct, intense sunlight. Planting plantains next to them creates temporary shade and holds soil moisture, acting as natural protection until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ shãa oya kɛji akɛ amɛ shɛ hulu la nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko baa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning dark brown and rotting during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, wet conditions. Pruning excess tree branches lets sun and air inside to dry out moisture, which stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni efɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ agbi. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves means your soil is low on nitrogen, an essential food for maize. When soil nitrogen is low, the plant moves what little it has from older lower leaves to feed the new top growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmãa Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛye ŋmãa ni eda lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmãa heei anɔ.

english: Why do agricultural officers suggest planting cowpeas before growing maize on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina ŋmãa dani adu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans gather nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small root nodules. When the cowpea plant dies, that stored nitrogen stays in the ground to serve as free, natural fertilizer for your next maize crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans buaa nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ naa ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi bibii amli. Kɛ cowpea tso lɛ gbo Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha o-corn ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava stems twisting up and showing light green patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋwɛi ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Twisted leaves with pale spots are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by small whiteflies. Damaged leaves cannot make enough food, leading to very small tubers at harvest.
ga: Baai ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ woɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ. Baai ni efite lɛ nyɛŋ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii waa baa kɛji akpa.

english: Yam vines need support sticks to lift their leaves up toward sunlight so they can make food. Clearing weeds prevents pests from hiding nearby and stops them from stealing nutrients meant for your yam mounds.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia yelikɛbuamɔ koni amɛwo baai lɛ anɔ kɛyashɛ hulu la lɛ he koni anyɛ akɛtsu nii kɛhoo nii. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi tsi he lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkatee amɛhe yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo. ni etsĩɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha o-sweet potato pile lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture swings quickly from dry to wet. Keeping the soil evenly watered helps the plant hold onto its blossoms until fruit sets.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ sũ lɛ nɔ nu be fɛɛ be lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shwereɔ aahu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do the bottoms of my pepper fruits turn soft, black, and sunken as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper aduawai lɛ shishi feɔ bɔdɔɔ, ediŋŋ, ni efoɔ mli beni edaa lɛ?

english: Soft black spots on pepper bottoms are caused by blossom-end rot. This happens when the crop cannot absorb enough calcium from the soil, usually due to irregular watering while the fruit is forming.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ baa ji fɔfɔi ni egbo lɛ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be be mli ni aduawai lɛ miifee lɛ.

english: Why do my green plantain trees keep falling over even when there is no heavy storm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains eŋɔli lɛ miigbee shi lɛ? He ni ahum ni naa wa bɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees easily fall over when underground pests like root weevils or microscopic worms eat away the roots, leaving the heavy tree without an anchor in the soil.
ga: Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ dumɔwui lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ shishifãi loo ŋmeii bibii ye shishifãi lɛ. Shi tso lɛ ni etsii ni ŋwɛi ŋta ko bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the lower fronds on my young oil palm trees turning brown and hanging down early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiiho oya lɛ?

english: Early browning and drooping of lower palm fronds usually shows that the tree is lacking potassium or water. Without enough potassium, the palm cannot maintain all its leaves and drops the oldest ones.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mra be mli tso lɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ potassium loo nu faaa yɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛji potassium faaa lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ ni ehaa baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How far apart should I space coconut trees when planting them on my farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mafo ŋmeii tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ?

english: Coconut trees need about 7 to 8 meters of space between each tree so their wide roots and large fronds do not compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients.
ga: Kokoo tsei biɔ ni tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji mitai 7 kɛyashi 8, no hewɔ lɛ amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ amɛbaai wuji lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ akaŋ.

english: Can I plant other crops like cassava or maize between my coconut trees while they are still young?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsei krokomɛi tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ be mli ni amɛdarako lɛ?

english: Yes, during the first three to four years before the tree canopy closes, planting short-term crops like cassava, maize, or legumes between rows makes good use of land and provides extra income.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ lɛ mli dani tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ baakpa. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛha kooloi aniyenii Loo ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ ateŋ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ shika kroko aba.

english: How many years will it take for a coconut tree to start giving me fruits after planting?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei tso ko jeɔ shishi ewoɔ yibii beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It depends on the variety you plant. Dwarf coconut varieties usually start bearing fruit in 3 to 4 years, while traditional tall varieties take about 6 to 8 years to yield.
ga: Edamɔ tso srɔtoi ni oduɔ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni ji dwarf lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ blema lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 6 kɛyashi 8 dani amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the young tiny coconuts falling off my tree before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji bibii nɛkɛ? Ni magbee shi kɛjɛ mitso lɛ nɔ dani eda?

english: Early fruit drop happens mainly because of irregular watering, lack of soil nutrients, or insect pests attacking the flowers and young nuts during development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ aduawai ni fiteɔ mra lɛ baa ji nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi ni tutuaa fɔfɔi bibii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: How do I know if a coconut seedling is healthy enough for me to buy and plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ ahe ni adu?

english: A healthy seedling has dark green leaves, a thick stem base, a strong sprout free of spots or holes, and a firm nut attached at the bottom.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni tsuɔ kɛ tso shishi ni mli wa. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ bɛ ŋmeii loo bu. Ni ŋmei ko ni mli wa yɛ shishigbɛ.

english: How can I prevent my coconut seedlings from getting damaged when carrying them to my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmei tsei anaa koni amɛkafite kɛji mikɛ amɛ ba miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Keep the seedlings upright, shade them from harsh sun and strong wind during transit, and avoid snapping the delicate sprout or disturbing the root base.
ga: Okɛ dumɔwui lɛ ama shi shiŋŋ. Buu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he yɛ gbɛfaa mli. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ akumɔ loo shishifãi lɛ ni ooohao lɛ he.

english: Can coconut trees grow well on inland forest soil, or do they only survive near the sea?
ga: Ani ŋmeii tsei yeɔ omanye yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kooi amli shikpɔŋ nɔ loo amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ masɛi pɛ?

english: Coconut trees grow very well on inland forest soils as long as the soil is deep, well-drained, and receives adequate rainfall throughout the year.
ga: Kokoo tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shia koo shikpɔŋ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ. Etsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: Why do the leaves of my young coconut palms turn yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves mean the tree is losing water faster than its roots can pull from dry soil. Placing dry grass or leaves around the base as mulch helps keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miifite nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni akɛwoɔ shishi lɛ he akɛ mulch lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: What causes V-shaped cuts on the leaves of my coconut trees?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-kokoo tso lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni tamɔ V lɛ ba?

english: V-shaped cuts are caused by the Rhinoceros beetle, which burrows into the soft, unopened leaves at the crown of the tree to feed on sap.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fã ni tamɔ V lɛ baa ji rhinoceros ŋmei. Efoɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ baai bibii ni agbeleee lɛ amli koni enu tso lɛ mli nu lɛ.

english: Is it true that putting salt around the roots of coconut trees helps them grow better?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmei tso lɛ ni edaa jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, applying small amounts of common coarse salt supplies chloride, which helps coconut palms retain water, improve leaf health, and increase nut size, especially in inland soils.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ akɛ ŋmei fioo ko ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa chloride lɛ yaa hiɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmei tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli. Ehaa baai lɛ ahewalɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa ŋmei dalɛ yaa hiɛ titri lɛ yɛ shia shikpɔŋ nɔ

english: What is 'nsusua', and why does it start growing on my farm when I didn't plant any seeds for it?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘Tsusua’ ni mɛni hewɔ ebɔi kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Akɛni miduuu dumɔwui ko kwraa hewɔ lɛ?

english: Nsusua' (turkey berry) is a wild plant common across Ghana. Its seeds are often spread across fields by birds or wind and can sleep in the dirt for a long time until you clear the land and expose them to sunlight.
ga: Nsusua’ (turkey tso yibii) ji koo mli tso ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana fɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, okpoi loo kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛɔ edumɔwui lɛ eshwaa ŋmɔji amli. Ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ kɛyashi obaajie he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ni okɛ hulu la lɛ ashɛ nɔ.

english: Why do new plants suddenly sprout up right after I clear and plow my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei heei kwɛ̃ɔ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ ni mitsu he nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: When you plow or clear the land, you flip the soil and expose dormant seeds that were buried deep underground to sunshine and air, which signals them that it is time to wake up and grow.
ga: Kɛji otsu nii loo ojie shikpɔŋ lɛ Obaatsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ojie dumɔwui ni ehiɛ edɔ ni afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ kpo koni onine ashɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ wɔte shi ni wɔda.

english: How do seeds stay alive in the soil for a long time without rotting before they sprout?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni dumɔwu ko ahi sũ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni efiteee dani ekwɛ̃?

english: Many natural plant seeds have a hard outer shell that protects them in a sleeping state called dormancy, allowing them to wait in dry or dark soil until farming activities bring them water and warmth.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli dumɔwui babaoo yɛ kponɔgbɛ fã ko ni wa ni buɔ dumɔwu lɛ he yɛ wɔɔhe shihilɛ mli ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy. Ha dumɔwui lɛ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ nɔ kɛyashi okwaayeli nitsumɔ kɛ nu kɛ hulutsoo baaba.

english: Why do wild plants like 'nsusua' grow so easily without fertilizer while my main crops struggle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli tsei tamɔ ‘nsusua’ lɛ daa oya ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli yɛ be mli ni mi tsei titrii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ waa lɛ?

english: Wild local plants have adapted to Ghana's soil and climate over hundreds of years, making them naturally strong against harsh conditions, poor soil, and local weather compared to cultivated crops.
ga: Koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ etsake amɛhe amɛwo Ghana shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛkpeɔ shihilɛi ni mli wawai, shikpɔŋ ni ehiii, kɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi anaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ akɛto tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Can eating local wild plants like 'nsusua' really help cure a fever or keep me healthy?
ga: Ani maŋ lɛ mli koo mli tsei tamɔ ‘Shingles’ ni ayeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa yɛ atridii mli diɛŋtsɛ loo ehaa gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛnamɔ yaa hiɛ?

english: Yes, plants like 'nsusua' are packed with iron, vitamins, and antioxidants that boost your immune system, helping your body fight off infections like fevers and build up weak blood.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei tamɔ ‘nsusua’ lɛ eyi kɛ dade, vitamini, kɛ nibii ni haa gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli nii ni gbeɔ helai lɛ yaa hiɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa gbɔmɔtso lɛ ni ekɛ helai tamɔ atridii wuɔ, ni ehaa lá ni bɛ hewalɛ buaa ehe naa.

english: How do I know if a wild berry or plant growing on my land is safe for my family to eat?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji koo mli tsei loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha miweku lɛ ni amɛye?

english: You should check if local community members traditionally cook with it, look for well-known local names like 'nsusua', or confirm with an extension officer before consuming unfamiliar wild plants.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ kɛji akutso lɛ mli bii lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii kɛhooɔ niyenii yɛ kusum gbɛ nɔ. Taomɔ maŋ lɛ mli gbɛi ni ale jogbaŋŋ tamɔ ‘nsusua’ loo okɛ extension official ko ama nɔ mi dani oye koo mli tso ko ni oleee.

english: Are traditional plants that grow naturally just as nutritious as modern vegetables I buy at the market?
ga: Kusum tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ hu yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ. kɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ aduawai ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Traditional wild plants are often even more nutritious than commercial crops because they absorb rich minerals directly from natural soil without being weakened by over-farming.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koo mli tsei ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ blema lɛ mli hewalɛ babaoo fe tsei ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ jarayeli mli lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei nɛɛ shwieɔ shika tsuru ni jara wa kɛjɛɔ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni okwaayeli ni fe nine lɛ efiteee amɛ.

english: How can I tell if a plant that pops up on its own is a useful crop or a harmful weed?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ji tso ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ loo jwɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui?

english: A plant is a harmful weed if it chokes your main crop and offers no value, but if it produces edible fruit, medicinal leaves, or market value like 'nsusua', it can be treated as a useful wild crop.
ga: Tso ji jwɛi ni yɔɔ oshara kɛji eyeɔ onibii titri ni oduɔ lɛ ni sɛɛnamɔ ko bɛ he. Shi kɛji ewo yibii ni ayeɔ, tsofafeemɔ baai, loo jarayeli jara, tamɔ ‘nsusua’ lɛ, abaanyɛ abu lɛ akɛ koo mli tso ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Should I destroy wild plants that grow on my land, or can I let them grow alongside my crops?
ga: Ani esa akɛ makpãtã koo mli tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahiɛ? Aloo mihaa ekwɛ̃ɔ kɛfataa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: If wild plants grow too close to your crops, they will steal water and soil food. It is best to dig them up carefully and move them to the edge of your farm so both can grow well.
ga: Kɛji koo mli tsei kwɛ̃ ni bɛŋkɛ onibii lɛ tsɔ Amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsa amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ amɛ aya oŋmɔ lɛ naa koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I collect seeds from wild plants on my land and plant them in neat rows like a regular crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ mabua dumɔwui anaa kɛjɛ koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli ni madu amɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ daa lɛ?

english: Yes, you can harvest ripe berries from wild plants, dry the seeds, and nurse them in seedbeds just like tomatoes or eggplants to create an organized crop field.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okpa tsei ayibii ni ekwɛ̃ kɛjɛ koo mli tsei amli. Gbimɔ dumɔwui lɛ. ni aduɔ yɛ dumɔwui ashishi tamɔ tomato loo eggplant koni ekɛfee he ko ni aduɔ nii yɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow big. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the crop the energy it needs to grow healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔji.

english: Is it better to apply fertilizer to my crops when the ground is dry or after it rains?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist right after a gentle rain. Dry soil can burn the crop's roots when fertilizer touches them, while moist soil dissolves the fertilizer gently so the roots can drink it up safely.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bashɛ amɛhe. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli blɛoo koni efee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnu nu.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and lose leaves during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and shallow roots that cannot survive harsh sunlight and dry winds on their own. Planting food crops like plantains or shade trees alongside them creates shade and traps moisture in the air to protect them through the dry season.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ. Niyenii tsei tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi. Ehaa hulutsoo baa ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli koni ebu tsei ahe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my yam plants need tall wooden sticks for the vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ koni wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally like to climb toward the sky so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight. Staking holding the leaves up allows the plant to produce plenty of food, which travels down to make big, heavy tubers underground.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, sweet potato wain tsei sumɔɔ ni amɛkwɔ kɛya ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ baai lɛ wo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo. Enɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi ni efeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Leaf curling in hot weather is a crop's way of protecting itself from losing too much water. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to direct sun, but ensuring good soil moisture through mulching helps keep the plant cooler.
ga: Baai ni abɔleɔ amɛhe yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite amɛ. Kɛ́ abɔle tso lɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi. Shi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they feel stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients in the ground. When the plant feels it doesn't have enough water or food to support baby peppers, it drops the flowers to save its own life.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ tsei lɛ nu he akɛ amɛbɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaatsɔse amɛ chili bii lɛ, Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: How do I stop small worms from boring holes into my tomato fruits?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmeii bibii ni shwieɔ mi-tomato aduawai lɛ amli lɛ naa?

english: Those worms hatch from tiny eggs laid on the leaves by night-flying moths. Checking under the leaves early in the morning to pick off eggs or young caterpillars, or spraying organic neem leaf water, keeps them from boring into the tomatoes.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii bibii amli. he ni ŋmeii ni foɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ jɔɔ amɛhe yɛ baai anɔ lɛ Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi leebi koni ona ŋmeii loo ŋmeii. Aloo okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu afɔ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkafo tomato lɛ mli.

english: When too many shoots grow around one plantain stem, they all fight for the same water and food in the soil. Leaving only one main stem and one or two small shoots ensures the main stem grows strong and produces a large bunch of plantains.
ga: Be mli ni ŋmeii babaoo ni miida yɛ tso kome he lɛ fa babaoo. Tsoi lɛ fɛɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Tso lɛ yitso titri kome pɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo. Niji kome loo enyɔ baaha tso titri lɛ adara ni ewo plantains babaoo.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn out small and watery instead of big and firm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni nu yɔɔ mli moŋ fe ni amɛaafee wuji ni wa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots become watery if they are harvested too early or grown in hard, waterlogged soil where air cannot reach the roots. Loose, well-drained soil and giving the crop enough months to mature allows the roots to pack full of solid starch.
ga: Cassava shishifãi baanyɛ ahi nu mli kɛji akpa amɛ mra tsɔ loo adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ. he ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa tso lɛ nyɔji babaoo ni ekɛdara lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa.

english: Can I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the same land where my maize is growing?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsina ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, planting legumes like beans or groundnuts alongside maize is very beneficial. Legumes pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which helps feed the maize plant so both crops yield better.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmei duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Legumes jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ niyenii Bɔni afee ni tsei henɔi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ awo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why is it important to mix sand with topsoil when I am preparing soil for my nursery bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akɛ ŋã afutu sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli beni asaa sũ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ kotokui lɛ?

english: Mixing sand with topsoil improves soil drainage and air circulation. Sand prevents the soil from compacting into hard blocks, making it easy for tender young roots to breathe and spread without rotting from excess water.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋã futu sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu hoɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ. Ŋã tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekafee blɔkii ni wa. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ muɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa mlɛo ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ fiteee.

english: Does the height and width of a nursery bag really affect how my young crops grow?
ga: Ani grow bag lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta kɛ elɛɛmɔ baaná mi dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, bag size matters because young plant roots need enough room to grow downwards and outwards. A container that is at least 5 to 7 inches deep gives roots enough space to build a strong foundation before being transplanted to the main farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, kotoku lɛ dalɛ he hiaa ejaakɛ tsei bibii ashishifãi lɛ he miihia he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara yɛ shishi kɛ kponɔgbɛ fɛɛ. Kɛ hoo lɛ, tsɛnsi ni mli kwɔ fe inchi 5 kɛyashi 7 lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛto shishitoo ni wa dani amɛdu kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: How full should I fill my nursery polybags with soil before sowing seeds?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ sũ awo grow bag mli bɔ ni sa dani madu dumɔwui?

english: You should fill nursery bags neatly near to the top, leaving about an inch from the rim. Leaving this small space holds water when you irrigate, allowing it to soak slowly into the root zone instead of washing soil over the edges.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ grow bag lɛ awo mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ. Eshiɔ aaafee 1 inch kɛjɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ naa, ni eshiɔ he bibioo ko. Enɛ haa nu lɛ hiɔ shi kɛ́ okɛ nu shwie nɔ. Ha ni ekɛ ehe awo mli fiofio Ekɛ ehe awo shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛi lɛ anɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my crops grow faster in loose, well-mixed soil compared to heavy clay soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni hi ni mli ewo muji ni akɛfutu mli lɛ nɔ kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni tsii he lɛ?

english: Loose soil allows soft root tips to push through easily in search of water and nutrients. Heavy soil holds back root expansion and traps excess water, which chokes the roots and slows down overall plant growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa shishifãi bibii lɛ akɛ amɛaatsɔ mli koni amɛyatao nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni tsii tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ naa ni ehaa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shi. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tso lɛ fɛɛ dalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do some of my seedlings turn yellow and collapse shortly after sprouting in the nursery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi beni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seedlings often yellow and collapse due to overwatering or poor soil drainage. When soil stays too wet, oxygen cannot reach the roots, leading to root rot and preventing the plant from absorbing basic nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkuɔ shi yɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli fe nine loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ lɛ Oxygen nyɛŋ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaaa tso lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ.

english: Why should I press the soil down gently around my plant when putting it into a nursery container?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ sũ ni bɔle mitsei lɛ ahe lɛ atswa blɛoo beni mikɛwoɔ tsɛnsi ni akɛkwɛɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pressing the soil down gently removes large air pockets around the plant roots. This ensures the roots stay firm and in direct contact with moist soil so they can absorb water immediately.
