ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaashɛ shi blɛoo Enɛ jieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui wuji ni bɔleɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe lɛ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ kpaa gbee tɛ̃ɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, enyɛɔ emɔɔ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if the soil on my farm has too much sand for crop farming?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli eyi kɛ ŋã tsɔ akɛ manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If your soil feels gritty, dries out completely within a few hours after rain, and cannot hold together when you squeeze it in your hand, it has too much sand. Sandy soil loses nutrients quickly and requires organic manure to hold water.
ga: Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eji ŋã lɛ Egbiɔ kwraa yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Ni enyɛŋ ekpɛtɛ ehe kɛji omimɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ onine mli lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋã babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ laajeɔ niyenii mli nibii oya, ni ehe hiaa ni akɛ tsofa ni wala yɔɔ mli awo mli koni nu lɛ ahi mli.

english: Why do my nursery seedlings grow very tall and thin instead of strong and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mi-nursery lɛ mli lɛ miida waa ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ yɛ hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Seedlings grow tall and thin when they are crowded together or kept in too much shade because they stretch upward to find sunlight. Giving them enough space and moderate sunlight builds thicker, stronger stems.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhe ejɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyi obɔ loo akɛ amɛ to he ko ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli ejaakɛ amɛbaagbala amɛhe kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛmɔ hulu la lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ hulu la ni sa ha lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: What happens if I plant my crop seeds too deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ mi aduawai dumɔwui lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Planting seeds too deep forces them to spend all their stored energy trying to push through the soil surface. If they run out of energy before reaching the light, they die underground.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ mli tsɔ lɛ baaha amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛto lɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji hewalɛ lɛ ba naagbee dani eshɛ la lɛ he lɛ Amɛbaagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why is dark topsoil better for starting young plants than the deeper red or light soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni tsuɔ ediŋŋ lɛ hi kɛha tsei bibii ashishijee fe shikpɔŋ tsuru loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Topsoil is rich in broken-down leaves and organic matter, which contain essential plant foods. Deeper subsoil is often hard, contains few nutrients, and makes it difficult for young seedling roots to establish.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ baai ni ekumɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, ni haa tsei lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mli kwɔ lɛ fɔɔ kaa. Niyenii mli hewalɛ fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli. ni ehaa ewaa kɛhaa tsei bibii ashishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛbaafee.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a signal that the plant is starving for nitrogen, a key food crop plants need to stay green. It can also happen when heavy rains wash nutrients away from the soil or when the roots are sitting in waterlogged ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii tso titri ni ehe hiaa ni tsei afee eŋɔli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ ta shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant's sap. This damages the leaves and can also pass diseases to the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper leaf curl baa. Enɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ hela hu eshwa tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or dry, or if the soil lacks sufficient moisture. When the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or dry conditions, it drops its blossoms to save its own energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ waa. aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Beni hulutsoo ni naa wa loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ haa tsei haoɔ Tsei lɛ baagbee shi koni amɛkɛhere amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do I have to stake my yam vines with tall wooden sticks instead of letting them grow on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu sweet potato wain tsei ni tsei kakadaji yɔɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha eda yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high on sticks so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight to manufacture food. Leaving them on the wet ground exposes them to fungal diseases and reduces the size of the underground tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná niyenii. Kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛná tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ baa shi.

english: Plantain suckers compete with the main tree for soil water and food. By leaving only one or two strong suckers, all the plant's energy goes into producing a larger, healthier cluster of plantains.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eshiɔ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ yaa plantain akui wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ afeemɔ mli.

english: Why do my groundnut plants need loose, soft soil around them after they start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ he hiaa shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Beni ebɔi fɔmɔ sɛɛ

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated, they grow little stems called 'pegs' that must push down into the ground to form nuts under the soil. If the ground is hard, these pegs cannot push through, and nuts will not form.
ga: Beni afee ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ pollinating sɛɛ Kɛji enɛ ba lɛ, tsei bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘pegs’ lɛ baafee ni esa akɛ ashɛre awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni afee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wa lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ mli. ni nut lɛ hu efeŋ.

english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning dark brown and rotting on the trees during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal attack known as black pod disease. The fungus thrives in heavy humidity, shade, and excessive wetness, quickly spreading from pod to pod through raindrops.
ga: Fungal tutuamɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela kɛ enɛ baa. Mold yeɔ omanye yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ, hulutsoo, kɛ hulutsoo be ni fa fe nine. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ pod kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi anɔ.

english: Cowpea flowers produce sweet nectar and tender young pods that attract pests like flower thrips and pod borers. The insects feast on these nutritious buds, which can destroy the harvest if not managed early.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔii lɛ woɔ nu kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni gbalaa ŋmeii tamɔ fɔfɔi thrips kɛ pod borers. Kplukai baaye nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ afite yibiiwoo lɛ kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii mra.

english: Cassava roots rot when left in heavy, waterlogged soil for too long during continuous rains. Excess water cuts off air to the roots, causing underground fungi to rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni yaa nɔ lɛ amli. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why does swamp rice need to grow in standing water while crops like maize will die in water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ nu ni mli ejɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni esa akɛ tsei tamɔ ŋmãa agboi yɛ nu mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special tubes in their stems that allow air to reach their submerged roots, surviving comfortably in flooded conditions. Maize roots lack this ability and drown when underwater because they cannot breathe.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ tsɔnei krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ ahe. ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu afua shihilɛi amli Abɛi shishifãi bɛ nyɛmɔ nɛɛ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji amɛyɔɔ nu shishi ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries out the topsoil. Planting shade crops like plantains or leaving canopy trees protects the young cocoa until it is mature enough to handle direct sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ehaa sũ ni yɔɔ amɛteŋ lɛ mli gĩɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ loo ashiɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and turning yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellowing are often caused by water stress or insect pests like whiteflies and mealybugs that suck sap from the leaves. During dry spells, plants curl leaves to save water, but severe damage usually points to pest infestations or viral diseases spread by insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu mli haomɔ loo ŋmeii tamɔ whiteflies kɛ mealybugs ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu nu he. Shi bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni fiteɔ waa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko eba loo hela ko ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela mli baa ni kooloi bibii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why does my maize grow very tall with green leaves, but the corn cobs stay tiny and empty?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ? Shi ŋmãa lɛ ji bibioo lolo ni nɔ ko bɛ mli?

english: This usually happens when you apply too much nitrogen fertilizer without enough phosphorus and potassium. Nitrogen makes the leaves and stems grow leafy and big, but phosphorus and potassium are required for strong roots, flowering, and filling out the corn cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen babaoo wo ŋmɔ mli ni phosphorus kɛ potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Nitrogen haa baai kɛ tsei lɛ feɔ baai ni amɛdaraa. Shi phosphorus kɛ potassium he miihia kɛha shishifãi ni wa, fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is my harvest getting smaller every year even though I plant the exact same crop on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ faaa daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and soil diseases to build up. Rotating your crop with leguminous plants like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil and disrupts pest cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Enɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ni ebaakpa tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants rot at the stem base and fall over right after heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fiteɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains soak the soil and create ideal conditions for fungal diseases like root rot and damping-off. Excess water suffocates roots and allows soil fungi to attack the stem, causing the plant to rot at ground level and collapse.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fũɔ ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ shishifãi ni fiteɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛkuɔ shi.

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when exposed to extreme heat, poor watering, or lack of soil nutrients. When a plant experiences environmental stress, it drops its flowers to save energy for survival rather than fruit production.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛbote la ni naa wa mli. nu ni ehiii loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ tsei kɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi kpe Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛto hewalɛ ni ekɛhi shi lɛ he. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ aduawai

english: Does leaving weeds around my young cassava hurt the plants, or do the weeds help shade the dirt?
ga: Jwɛi ni ashiɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Ani mi yucca gbekɛ lɛ miipila tso lɛ loo jwɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Weeds aggressively compete with young cassava for soil moisture, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients. Keeping the farm clean during the first three months allows the cassava root system to establish without competition, leading to much higher yields.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ ŋmei bibii yeɔ akaŋ waa kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ́ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tse yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi ni akaŋshii bɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ babaoo.

english: Why did my maize seeds fail to sprout after I buried them deep in the dirt to keep birds away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni mikɛtsi okpoi anaa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seeds need a mix of air, moisture, and warmth to germinate properly. Buried too deep, the shoot exhausts all its stored energy trying to push through the heavy soil and dies before reaching sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, fɛ̃i, kɛ dɔlɛ ni akɛfata he koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Tsoi ni afu amɛ ni mli kwɔ tsɔ lɛ fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛto lɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ ni amɛgboi dani amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting long green shoots in the barn before I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ je shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii kakadaŋŋ agboi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani midu amɛ lɛ?

english: Yams have a natural internal clock and break dormancy after a rest period, especially when stored in warm, humid air. The seed tuber uses its stored moisture and carbohydrates to send out green shoots in preparation for the next rainy season.
ga: Sweet potatoes yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɛlɛtswaa ni efoɔ wɔɔhe yɛ hejɔɔmɔ sɛɛ. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ akɛto he ko ni hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ kɛ nu ni ato kɛ carbohydrates tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛtsu ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli koni amɛkɛsaa amɛhe kɛha nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baa lɛ.

english: If I plant my plantain suckers very close together, will I get a bigger harvest from my small piece of land?
ga: Kɛ midu plantain tsei lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. mi nɔ loo daabi

english: Planting suckers too closely creates severe competition for sunlight and root space. Instead of yielding more, the plants grow tall, thin, and weak, producing much smaller, lighter bunches than properly spaced plants.
ga: Tso yibii ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ tsɔ lɛ kɛ akaŋshii ni naa wa baa kɛha hulu la kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo yibii babaoo lɛ Tsei lɛ daraa, amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ, ni no haa amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa fe tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why does my farm soil seem to lose its power after several years of harvesting cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ dɔŋŋ yɛ afii babaoo ni mikɛkpa kookoo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When you harvest cocoa pods, the trees draw essential nutrients out of the ground to grow those fruits. Taking the pods away removes those nutrients from your land, leaving the soil drained over time unless you put nutrients back in.
ga: Kɛ́ okpa kookoo ŋmeii Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛkɛwo nakai aduawai lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii lɛ, ejieɔ nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ atsɔ mli yɛ be ni sa mli. Ja okɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ku sɛɛ awo mli.

english: Why do extension officers say I am taking away substances from my soil when I harvest my cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ akɛ mijieɔ nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpaa kookoo lɛ?

english: Every cocoa pod and bean harvested contains minerals absorbed directly from the ground. When you pick and sell your crop, you are permanently removing those stored minerals from your farm, which exhausts the soil.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii fɛɛ ni akpaa lɛ yɛ minerals ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwie shi ni ohɔ̃ɔ lɛ Ojieɔ nakai shika tsuru ni ato lɛ kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa naanɔ. Enɛ baaha sũ lɛ mli agbɔjɔ.

english: How can I put back the goodness that my cocoa trees have taken out of the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ kpakpa ni cacao tsei lɛ jieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ?

english: You can restore soil nutrients by applying recommended fertilizers, spreading compost, and leaving decayed cocoa pod husks or fallen leaves on the farm floor to break down into rich plant food.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ okɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ashwã ni oshi kookoo ŋmeii ni egboi loo baai ni egbee shi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni egbo ni etsɔ tsei niyenii babaoo.

english: What is nitrogen, and why do my young cocoa trees need it?
ga: Mɛni ji nitrogen? Ni mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa nitrogen lɛ?

english: Nitrogen is a key plant food that builds strong stems and leafy green foliage. Young cocoa trees need nitrogen early on to establish healthy leaves and branches so they can capture sunlight and grow big.
ga: Nitrogen ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa tsei lɛ ahe wa kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nitrogen he miihia kokoo tsei bibii lɛ mra. Koni ekɛfee baai kɛ niji ni mli wa Koni enyɛ emɔ hulu la ni etsɔ agbo.

english: Can I use only one type of fertilizer like nitrogen on my farm every single year?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ henɔ kome, tamɔ nitrogen, atsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi?

english: No. While nitrogen helps trees grow leaves and branches when they are young, mature cocoa trees also need other nutrients like phosphorus and potassium to grow strong flowers, healthy pods, and heavy beans.
ga: Dabi, eyɛ mli akɛ nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbaa kɛ amɛniji kwɛ̃ɔ beni amɛji bibii lɛ moŋ. Shi cacao tso ni eda lɛ hu he miihia niyenii krokomɛi, tamɔ phosphorus kɛ potassium, koni fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃. Pods ni mli wa kɛ ŋmeii ni tsii

english: Why are my cocoa yields dropping even though my trees are around 12 years old and look fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa yibiiwoo lɛ miiba shi eyɛ mli akɛ mitsei lɛ eye aaafee afii 12 ni amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara moŋ?

english: Around 10 to 12 years of age, cocoa trees reach heavy production and pull large amounts of food from the soil. If that food is not replenished, the soil runs empty and the trees yield fewer pods even if they look large.
ga: Cacao tsei hiɔ shi aaafee afii 10 kɛyashi 12, amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo ni amɛjieɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ niyenii eyaaa mli ekoŋŋ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tsei lɛ woɔ yibii fioo, eyɛ mli akɛ amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara moŋ.

english: Why did my cocoa farm give me plenty of pods when it was young without much fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji haa pods babaoo beni miji gbekɛ fioo lɛ? Ani bei pii lɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he?

english: Newly planted soil usually contains natural nutrient reserves accumulated over years. As your young cocoa trees fed on this initial supply for their early harvests, those natural reserves gradually ran out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni adu ehee lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni abua naa yɛ afii babaoo mli. Beni ahaa o-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishijee niyenii kɛha klɛŋklɛŋ kpamɔ lɛ. Nakai adebɔɔ mli hei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ miiho fiofio.

english: What happens to my cocoa trees if the soil completely runs out of nutrients?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ efo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwraa?

english: When soil nutrients are empty, cocoa trees show yellowing leaves, slow growth, flower drop, small or empty pods, and become weaker against pests and diseases.
ga: Kɛji niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ fo lɛ Cocoa tsei lɛ baajie baai ŋmɔŋ kpo. Edaa blɛoo, fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi, pods lɛ ji bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli. ni helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛ oya.

english: Why do my neighbor's cocoa trees stay green and full of pods while mine look tired and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ cacao tso lɛ ji eŋɔli ni eyi kɛ ŋmeii yɛ be mli ni mi cacao tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni etɔ lɛ ni ebɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Trees stay green and produce well when the soil is regularly fed. Tired-looking trees are usually starving because the food taken out during past harvests has not been replaced.
ga: Tsei lɛ baahi shi ni amɛwo yibii kɛji akɛ aha amɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii daa. Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei ni tamɔ nɔ ni etɔ lɛ ejaakɛ atsakeee niyenii ni ajie yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Is animal manure enough to fix old, worn-out soil on my cocoa farm?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛsaa shikpɔŋ momo ni efite ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Manure helps improve soil texture and adds natural organic food, but older farms usually need balanced commercial fertilizers alongside manure to quickly restore specific minerals like nitrogen and potassium.
ga: Manure haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ni ekɛ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataa he yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔji ni etsɛ waa lɛ biɔ ni akɛ jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba oya.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into tubes when the sun gets very hot during the dry period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves to protect themselves from losing moisture. By rolling up, less leaf surface is exposed to the harsh sun and heat, helping the plant conserve water until the heat cools down or rain falls.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ he. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ, hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ shɛɛɛ baa lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni latsaa lɛ baa shi loo nugbɔ baanɛ.

english: Can I still grow fresh vegetables during the long dry season if there is no river near my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu aduawai heei lolo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli? Kɛji faa ko bɛ ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, you can grow vegetables in the dry season by harvesting rainwater in simple underground pits or tanks during the wet season, and using simple drip irrigation buckets that slowly deliver water straight to the crop roots with minimal waste.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu aduawai yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli kɛtsɔ nugbɔ nu ni oookpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi bu loo tanki ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ nɔ. Ni okɛ nu ni hoɔ ni shwieɔ shi ni tsɔɔ nu lɛ gbɛ blɛoo kɛyaa tsei shishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni jwɛi fioo pɛ fiteɔ lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow and falling off during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their lower leaves during drought as a natural survival mechanism. It reduces the amount of water the plant needs, allowing it to keep its underground tubers alive until rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛshishi baai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni eha nu ni he hiaa tsei lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt in the afternoon sun even when I watered the soil earlier?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mra moŋ?

english: During intense midday heat, plants lose water from their leaves faster than their roots can drink it up. They wilt temporarily to protect themselves, but as long as the soil has moisture, they will bounce back when the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛjɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Amɛbaagbo yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe. Shi be fɛɛ be ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ Ebaaku esɛɛ kɛ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any tomatoes during hot sunny spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo tomato yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and dries out the pollen inside the flowers. When it gets too hot, the plant sheds its flowers to conserve energy rather than trying to form fruit it cannot support.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ gĩɔ. Kɛji edɔ tsɔ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni obɔ yibii ni anyɛɛɛ awo he nyɔmɔ lɛ

english: How does intense dry weather affect young cocoa pods on my trees?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi waa lɛ saa kookoo bibii ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Without adequate soil moisture during long dry spells, young cocoa trees cannot feed all their pods, causing many small pods to dry up, turn black, and die—a condition called cherelle wilt.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ, Cacao tsei bibii po nyɛŋ aha niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa aha ŋmeii lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ babaoo gbɛ́ɔ, amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ, ni amɛgboiɔ, ni eji shihilɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ cherel wilting.

english: Why does covering the soil around my crops with dry leaves stop the ground from drying out so fast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mulching ebɔle mihe lɛ miduɔ miŋmɔshi nibii kɛ baai ni egbi, ni no haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tamɔ bɔ ni eji lɛ.

english: Mulching with dry leaves acts like a blanket over the earth. It shades the soil from direct sunlight, lowers soil temperature, and traps moisture beneath so your crops stay hydrated much longer between waterings.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ aba shi ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shishi Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ.

english: Is it better for me to water my farm early in the morning or in the middle of the day?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu leebi loo shwane mli?

english: It is best to water early in the morning because the air and soil are cool, allowing the crop roots to soak up the water before the harsh midday sun causes most of it to evaporate into the air.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔse nu leebi maŋkpa ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ejɔ. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ nu dani hulu la ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ mli babaoo shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why do cowpeas grow better in dry, poor soils than many of my other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni ehiii nɔ fe miŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Cowpeas have deep root systems that reach hidden moisture deep underground, and their roots feature special nodules that make their own fertilizer from the air, allowing them to thrive where other crops starve.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni shɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ he. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi ni feɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ ŋmeii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa amɛshwereɔ yɛ he ni tsei krokomɛi hɔmɔ baaye amɛ lɛ.

english: Why does planting shade trees help my young cocoa and plantain crops survive dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-cacao kɛ mi-plantain lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Shade trees reduce the surrounding temperature, block harsh winds that dry out crops, and prevent the soil from baking under direct sun, creating a cooler environment for delicate crops to grow.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo ni ebɔle he lɛ baa shi. Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii gĩɔ lɛ naa. ni etsĩ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekashã yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ baa kɛha tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, a key plant food. When soil lacks nutrients or heavy rains wash them away, the plant cannot make green leaf pigment, which slows down its growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji tsei aniyenii titri lɛ Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ amɛ, Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ baaha dalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and weak roots that burn under direct hot sun and dry wind. They need temporary shade plants like plantains or shade trees to protect them and keep moisture in the soil until they grow stronger.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni shãa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Koni ebu sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ he ni ehi mli kɛyashi amɛhe wa.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or when they experience water stress. Excessive heat damages the pollen inside the flower, causing the plant to shed the blossom instead of growing a tomato fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ loo kɛ́ amɛna nu he haomɔ. Dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Ha tsei lɛ agbo yɛ tomato ni ooodu lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up tightly and stop expanding?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe shi shiŋŋ ni egbɛɛɛ eshwaaa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaf, or a plant virus they spread. The plant reacts to the feeding damage by curling its leaves to protect itself, which stunts its growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo tsei amli helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ Tsei tsuɔ niyenii ni efiteɔ lɛ he nii kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baatsi dalɛ naa.

english: How do I know when my yam tubers are mature and ready to harvest since they grow underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ edara kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Yam plants signal maturity above ground when the vine leaves stop growing, turn yellow, and dry up completely. This shows that the plant has stopped feeding the tuber underground and the yam is fully ripe.
ga: Sweet potato tsei tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ dalɛ kɛji wain tso lɛ baai lɛ kpa dalɛ. Etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbi kwraa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa ŋmeii lɛ niyenii hamɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: Why do the green pods on my cocoa trees turn black and rot before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in cool, overly wet, and shady conditions. The fungus attacks the pod skin, quickly turning it black and spreading to ruin the beans inside.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Fung ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ ni eyɛ hulutsoo, ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tutuaa pod lɛ hewolo lɛ. Etsɔɔ ediŋŋ oya ni egbɛɔ eshwaa koni efite ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rain sits in soil with poor drainage, water fills all the air spaces, effectively suffocating the roots and causing rot-causing fungi to multiply.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Nu baayi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ feɔ babaoo.

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over easily when strong winds blow during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that spread sideways rather than deep into the earth. When the heavy fruit bunch gets full and the soil becomes soft from rain, strong winds easily tip the tree over unless it is propped up with wooden poles.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa afãi moŋ fe ni amɛaaya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Beni aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ eyi ni shikpɔŋ lɛ efee blɛoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ hewɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ tswaa tsei amɛshwieɔ shi oya, ja akɛ tsei ni akɛtswaa tsei fiɔ amɛsɛɛ.

english: Why do tiny beetles start eating my harvested maize even after I have dried it properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ miibɔi mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ yeli eyɛ mli akɛ migbi lɛ jogbaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Maize weevils often lay invisible eggs inside the grain kernels while the crop is still in the field. Even if the grain feels dry, those eggs hatch inside storage and the larvae eat their way out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ woɔ ŋmãa ni anaaa lɛ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmãa lɛ nuɔ he akɛ egbi moŋ Shi nakai ŋmeii lɛ baafɔ yɛ nitoohe. ni ŋmeii lɛ baaye gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ejeɔ kpo lɛ.

english: Why do my freshly harvested tomatoes soften and spoil so quickly before I can get them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpa ehee lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni efiteɔ oya dani eshɛɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes continue to ripen and breathe after being picked. High temperatures, direct sunlight during transport, and piling them high in deep wooden crates crush the skin, causing rapid breakdown and rot.
ga: Tomato yaa nɔ ekwɛ̃ɔ ni emuɔ beni ajie lɛ sɛɛ, ni ekɛ ehe woɔ hulutsoo be ni mli wa mli kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ mli yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ. Ni kɛji akɛ ato adekai ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli lɛ, ebaakumɔ hewolo lɛ. Enɛ haa fitemɔ kɛ fitemɔ baa oya.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce broad leaves that shade young cocoa seedlings, keeping the soil cool and moist so the cocoa can survive its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen. Nitrogen moves to the newest growth at the top, leaving older bottom leaves yellow; adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea helps fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tso lɛ. Nitrogen lɛ yaa shweremɔ hee ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ nɔ. Shi shishigbɛ fã ni etsɛ lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: You should wait until the soil gets at least two or three steady, deep rains rather than planting after the very first shower. Planting too early in dry soil causes seeds to dry out and die before they can grow properly.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi kɛ hoo lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ daa. Mohu ɔ, mo du lɛ ngɛ kekleekle nu ɔ se. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi dani amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers but fail to grow any actual tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi ekwɛɛɛ tomato diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off without growing fruit when temperatures are extremely hot or when the soil gets too dry. Heavy heat dries out the pollen, preventing insects or wind from pollinating the flowers successfully.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa pollen lɛ gĩɔ. Eyeɔ omanye ni ekɛtsiɔ kooloi bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni amɛkafee fɔfɔii lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Can I save and plant seeds from this season's hybrid maize harvest for next year?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ ato ni madu kɛha afi ni baa lɛ?

english: Saving and planting hybrid seeds results in a much lower yield and weak, unequal plants. Hybrid seeds only pass down their strong, high-yielding traits in the first generation, so new certified seeds must be bought every season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ ni akɛtoɔ ni aduɔ lɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi waa, ni tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ baa. Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jieɔ sui ni mli wa, ni woɔ yibii babaoo pɛ kpo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ daa be mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants have tall bushy stems but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli shi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ daraaa kwraa lɛ?

english: Excessive leafy growth with thin tubers happens when the soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium. Potassium is the key nutrient that pushes plants to store food and expand their roots.
ga: Baai ni yaa hiɛ fe nine ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Potassium ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsirɛɔ tsei koni amɛto niyenii ni amɛwo shishifãi.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts alongside my main crop improve my land?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri ni miduɔ lɛ baadu lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas out of the air and fix it into the soil through their roots, acting as natural fertilizer for neighboring crops while keeping weeds under control.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha tsei ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ kɛ agbɛnɛ hu jwɛi ni yeɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do black spots appear on my pepper leaves and fruits during the wet rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ diji jeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛ aduawai anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Excess moisture and high humidity allow fungal spores to multiply on wet leaves and spread through splashing rain. Spacing plants further apart lets air flow through, drying the leaves and stopping fungal diseases.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine kɛ fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo haa ŋmeii fɔɔ yɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ anɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ agbala tsei lɛ amli babaoo lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ amɛmli. Ehaa baai lɛ gĩɔ ni ekpaa tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: How can I protect my harvested dry maize from weevils without applying chemical powders?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-ŋmãa ni egbi ni mikpa lɛ he kɛjɛ ŋmeii ahe ni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Using hermetic storage bags (such as PICS bags) seals out air completely. Without oxygen inside the bag, weevils and their eggs cannot breathe or multiply, keeping the grain safe for many months.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ vacuum ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe (tamɔ PICS kotoku) tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ akabote mli. Kɛji oxygen bɛ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ amɛwui lɛ nyɛŋ amu loo amɛfɔ bii. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo.

english: Why is it important to stake my yam vines with wood or bamboo poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni okɛ tsei loo ŋmeii awo o-sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need tall stakes to lift their leaves high up toward the sunlight. When leaves capture plenty of sunlight without being shaded on the ground, the plant generates more energy to feed big tubers underneath.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu lɛ nɔ. Beni baai lɛ nine shɛɔ hulu la babaoo nɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsiii amɛnaa lɛ. Tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛhaa ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ niyenii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn and dry out easily under strong sunshine. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains near them creates living shade that protects the cocoa and keeps the soil moist until the trees grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds around the base of my oil palm trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water and nutrients from the soil that the oil palm needs to produce fruits. Clearing the weeds around the tree base ensures the palm gets full food and water to yield heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa mu tsei koni amɛdu nii lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ náa niyenii kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ yibii ni tsii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize plants need to grow dark green and healthy. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores the green color and helps the crop grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa ŋmãa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I drop three or four maize seeds into one single planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ woɔ dumɔ bu kome pɛ mli lɛ?

english: When too many seeds are planted in one hole, the plants crowd each other and fight for light, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing one or two seeds per hole gives each plant enough space to make large maize cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ Tsei lɛ buaa amɛhe naa ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui kome loo enyɔ to bu kome mli lɛ, ebaaha tso fɛɛ tso aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee ŋmãa ŋmãa agbo.

english: Staking yam vines allows the leaves to spread out high and catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight gives the leaves energy to send food down to make large yam tubers underground.
ga: O-sweet potato wain tso lɛ ni oookɛwo tso nɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ ni enine shɛɔ hulu la ni fe fɛɛ nɔ. Hulu la haa baai lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ niyenii tsuɔ nii kɛyaa shi koni amɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when water stands on my field for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water covers the farm and cannot drain away, it drowns the roots and encourages fungi that turn the cassava soft and rotten.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛji nu ha ŋmɔ lɛ he ni anyɛɛɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli lɛ Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli ni eha ŋmeii ni haa ŋmei lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why is it good to plant groundnuts or beans on my field before planting maize the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmei yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans gather natural nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest them, that trapped nitrogen stays in the dirt to naturally feed the next crop like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Buaa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni okpaa amɛ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii aha sɛɛ mli tsei, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Can I put fresh chicken manure directly around my young vegetable plants right after collecting it?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ hee awo he fɛɛ he. Ani manyɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji mikpa amɛ?

english: Fresh poultry manure produces heat and strong chemicals that can burn plant roots. It should be left to dry and decompose in a cool pile for a few weeks before applying it to your farm.
ga: Kooloi afɔfɔi ni afee ehee lɛ jieɔ dɔlɛ kɛ tsofai ni mli wa ni baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi lɛ kpo. Esa akɛ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni egbi ni egbo yɛ ŋtayaa ni mli ejɔ mli otsii fioo komɛi dani akɛtsu nii yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: What is causing small holes in my maize leaves and small worms hiding inside the central shoots?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni Akɛtee yɛ teŋgbɛ gɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They burrow into the central leaves to feed, so early spraying with approved insecticides or neem leaf extracts is necessary to stop them before they destroy the stalk.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛfoɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛtao niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem tso lɛ mli nu ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra lɛ baanyɛ aba mli. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni akpa amɛ dani amɛfite tso lɛ shishifã lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl upward and stop growing during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is often caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies that thrive in dry weather. Removing weeds and protecting young plants from whiteflies early prevents the foliage from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni koolooi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ mli ni obu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ whiteflies ahe mra. Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and burning when they get direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because their leaves are very sensitive to harsh heat. Without shade plants like plantains or temporary shade trees to shield them, the intense sun burns the leaves and dries out the soil, preventing the plant from growing properly.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko bɛ lɛ, Hulu la ni naa wa baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, tsei nyɛŋ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do Extension Officers advise us to cut down some branches from our cocoa trees during pruning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔfolɔ kookoo niji komɛi yɛ be mli ni wɔfoɔ tsei lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches so air and sunlight can reach all parts of the tree. This reduces humidity that breeds diseases and helps the tree direct its nutrients into growing bigger, healthier pods instead of useless leaves.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ashɛ tso lɛ fã fɛɛ fã he. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ hela baa lɛ baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii mli nibii tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ najiaŋ

english: Why do my small cocoa pods turn black and dry up before they are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egbiɔ dani edara lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in damp, overly shaded farms during rainy periods. Keeping the farm clean, weeding regularly, and removing infected pods helps stop it from spreading.
ga: ni bei pii lɛ, black pod hela kɛbaa Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ tsɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ amli. Okwaafoi lɛ Ahe Hetsemɔ Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ daa. Ni ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why do mirid insects attack my cocoa farm mostly when new leaves and pods start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mirid kooloi lɛ tutuaa mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli babaoo beni baai kɛ ŋmeii heei jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Mirids, also known as capsids, feed on young, juicy plant tissue. When rainy weather causes the tree to produce fresh shoots and tender young pods, the insects flock to the farm to feed, sucking the sap and causing the stems to die back.
ga: Mirids, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ capsids lɛ yeɔ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ náa ŋmeii heei kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Kplukai hoɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔji amli koni amɛyatao niyenii. Emuɔ nu lɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ shishi lɛ gboɔ.

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects called midges to carry pollen from flower to flower. If there are no rotting banana stems or leaf litter where these insects live, or if heavy rain washes them away, the flowers drop without turning into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ lɛ midge ni ekɛ pollen woɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko mli. Kɛji akɛ banana tsei loo baai bibii komɛi bɛ he ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ hiɔ lɛ, Aloo kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ amɛ kɛyaa. Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbatsɔŋ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How can I tell the exact right time to pick my cocoa pods so the seeds inside do not ruin?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ? koni ekafite dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ

english: Ripe cocoa pods change color clearly—green pods turn bright yellow, and red pods turn orange-yellow. Picking them green means the beans inside are underdeveloped, while leaving them too long causes the beans to sprout inside the pod.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su yɛ faŋŋ mli. Pods eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. ni ŋmeii tsuji lɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii-ŋmei. Kɛ́ ohala ŋmɔŋ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ afeee kɔfi ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ lolo. Yɛ be mli ni ashiɔ lɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why is it necessary to cover harvested cocoa beans with plantain leaves for several days before drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ plantain baai aha kookoo yibii ni akpa lɛ ahe gbii babaoo dani amɛgbi lɛ?

english: Covering wet beans with plantain leaves allows them to ferment naturally. Fermentation generates heat that kills the seed inside, creates the rich chocolate flavor and color foreign buyers want, and makes the beans easier to dry.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ plantain baai ha ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Fɛ̃i haa dɔlɛ gbeɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Ehaa tsokolate lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ kɛ su ni majimaji ateŋ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ biɔ lɛ baa. ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ baagbi

english: Why must I dry my cocoa beans on raised bamboo mats instead of spreading them on the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ migbiɔ mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni awo nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛshwie shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Drying beans on raised mats allows air to flow underneath them so they dry evenly without molding. Spreading them on the ground exposes them to dirt, stones, animal droppings, and ground moisture, which ruins their quality for export buyers.
ga: Kɛ́ ogbi okɔfi yibii lɛ yɛ tsɔne ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ yɛ amɛshishi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɔfi yibii lɛ gĩɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he. Amɛgbɛfaŋnɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa amɛnaa muji, tɛi, kooloi afɔfɔi kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha mɛi ni heɔ nibii kɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do hybrid cocoa seedlings bear pods much faster than the old cocoa trees my parents planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ woɔ ŋmeii mra kwraa fe kookoo tsei momo ni mifɔlɔi du lɛ?

english: Hybrid cocoa varieties have been developed by plant scientists to grow faster, root deeper, and produce flowers much earlier in their lifespan, allowing them to yield pods in about two to three years instead of five.
ga: Tsei ahe nilelɔi fee kookoo henɔi ni akɛfutu mli koni amɛdara oya. shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi oya kwraa yɛ ewala be mli Enɛ haa amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi yɛ aaafee afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ mli yɛ afii enumɔ najiaŋ.

english: Why does leaving dry leaves on the ground help my crop survive during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mishi baai ni egboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni nu lɛ mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: A layer of dry leaves, called mulch, covers the soil like a blanket. It prevents the hot dry wind and sun from evaporating moisture from the dirt, keeping the roots cool and wet longer through dry spells.
ga: Baai ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi kɛ hulu la naa koni ekajie ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛ muji mli lɛ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i be kakadaŋŋ kɛtsɔ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct heat. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa trees need to survive.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i koni amɛhi shi.

english: When plants are crowded, they fight with each other for light, water, and plant food in the soil. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough resources to produce large, healthy crops.
ga: Kɛ tsei ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná la, nu kɛ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make energy that feeds the tuber underground. Lifting the vines on stakes helps leaves catch maximum sunlight while keeping them off wet ground where diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni haa ŋmeii lɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aba. Wein tso lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu, ni no ji nɔ ni haa helai gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Yellow leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen, which is essential for leaf growth. Heavy rains can wash this nutrient out of the soil, or excess water at the roots can prevent the plant from taking it up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli, ni he hia kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo, nu ni fa fe nine yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tso lɛ naa koni ekaŋɔ.

english: Leaf curling and yellow patches are key symptoms of cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava stems helps prevent this problem.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi titri. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Cassava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my pepper plants suddenly wilt and dry up even when the soil around them is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho trukaa ni egbi eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli edɔ moŋ?

english: Sudden wilting in moist soil is usually caused by soil fungi or bacteria attacking the root system. The damaged roots can no longer carry water up into the stem, causing the plant to dry out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sũ mli ŋmeii loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni tutuaa shishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli efɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Shishifãi ni efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛwo nu kɛya tso lɛ shishi dɔŋŋ, ni no haa tso lɛ gbiɔ.

english: Why are flowers falling off my tomato plants without forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ tomato tsei anɔ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they experience high temperature stress or irregular watering. When stressed, the plant conserves energy by shedding flowers rather than growing fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛna haomɔ ni jɛɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei buɔ hewalɛ he kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yɛ aduawai ni amɛwoɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my garden eggs turning black and soft before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ ashishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani ahoɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Black, rotting bottoms on vegetable fruits are caused by a lack of calcium while the fruit is forming. Irregular watering prevents the plant from moving calcium smoothly from the soil into the fruit.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni fiteɔ yɛ aduawai kɛ aduawai anɔ lɛ jɛɔ calcium ni faaa yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miifee lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa lɛ haaa amɛnyɛ amɛjie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya aduawai lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I avoid spreading fertilizer on my crops right before a heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa aba lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes the fertilizer away from your plants' roots before they can drink it in. It is best to apply fertilizer when the ground is moist but heavy rain is not expected.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ tsei ashishifãi amli dani anuɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi akpaaa nugbɔ ni naa wa gbɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers plant cowpeas or beans on the same land as maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ duɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni amɛduɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, naturally feeding the soil. When grown with maize, they share this essential plant food and keep the soil rich.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa du Amɛjaraa tso niyenii ni he hiaa nɛɛ ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does my harvested cassava turn dark or black after processing instead of staying bright white?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ loo ediŋŋ beni atsu he nii sɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ futafuta

english: Cassava tubers contain natural starches and juices that react quickly with air and heat once harvested. If the tubers are left too long before processing, or if moisture is left inside during milling, oxidation occurs, which turns the resulting flour or fufu dark.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli ŋmei kɛ nu ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ dɔlɛ tsuɔ nii oya kɛji akpa lɛ yɛ ŋmei shishifã lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmeii lɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani atsu he nii loo kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ko eshwɛ yɛ mli yɛ be mli ni aŋmɔɔ lɛ Oxidation reaction baaba. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How does using a processing machine affect the color and texture of my cassava fufu?
ga: Te tsɔne ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ saa mi tapioca ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ su kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: A processing machine grates and grinds cassava rapidly, but if the machine gets too hot or isn't cleaned between uses, remaining juices ferment or scorch, which can darken the flour and make the dough sticky rather than firm.
ga: Mɔ ni tsuɔ nii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ oya ni ekɛshwieɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛji akɛ tsɔne lɛ mli edɔ fe nine loo atsuuuu he yɛ nitsumɔi ateŋ. Nu ni eshwɛ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ebaashã. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ afee ediŋŋ ni eha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What makes some cassava starch bright white while other starch looks dull and gray?
ga: Mɛni haa tapioca ŋmei lɛ feɔ yɛŋ ni kpɛɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmei krokomɛi feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Bright white starch comes from peeling off all outer brown bark completely, washing the tubers immediately in clean water, and drying the starch rapidly away from dust and soil contamination.
ga: Akɛ hewolo ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ ni ji blɔfo lɛ fɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ni kpɛɔ lɛ. Okɛ nu ni mli tse afɔ oyitso he amrɔ nɔŋŋ. ni oha ashikiŋsha lɛ agbi oya He kɛjɛ sũ kɛ sũ ni mli ewo muji mli.

english: Why do some of my cassava tubers turn out watery and soft when boiled, while others are firm and good for fufu?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ekomɛi feɔ nu ni amɛhe yɔɔ blɛoo kɛ́ ahoo lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi komɛi wa ni ehi kɛha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ?

english: Watery cassava happens when tubers are harvested right after heavy rains or too early in their cycle. The plant absorbs excess water, diluting the starch. Firm tubers come from plants harvested during dry periods when starch concentration is high.
ga: Nu mli ŋmei lɛ baa kɛji akɛ akpa ŋmeii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ loo mra tsɔ yɛ ŋmei lɛ mli. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ, ni ehaa starch lɛ mli shwieɔ shi. Tubers ni wa lɛ jɛɔ tsei ni akpaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni starch lɛ fa babaoo yɛ mli lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if my cassava crops are fully ready for harvest without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava tsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mikɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Look at the lower leaves and stems of the plant. As cassava reaches maturity (around 9 to 12 months), the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the lower stem turns thick and woody.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tso lɛ baai kɛ shishigbɛ shishigbɛ fãi lɛ. Beni ŋmei lɛ daa (aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12) lɛ, shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi. ni shishigbɛ tso lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ tso

english: Why do my cocoa trees take so many years to bear fruit while neighboring farms get fruits much faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔ ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ woɔ yibii oya kwraa lɛ?

english: Different varieties grow at different speeds. Older traditional cocoa varieties take up to five years to yield, whereas newer hybrid varieties start bearing pods in two to three years if pruned and shaded correctly.
ga: Srɔtoi srɔtoi daa oya yɛ oyaiyeli srɔtoi amli. Kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ blema lɛ heɔ afii enumɔ dani anyɛɔ afeɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kookoo henɔi heei ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he lɛ baabɔi ŋmeii feemɔ yɛ afii enyɔ loo etɛ mli kɛji akɛ afolɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni awo amɛ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my cassava leaves start curling and drying up during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ ni egbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hot, dry conditions favor sap-sucking pests like spider mites and mealybugs. Without rain to wash them off, these pests multiply quickly on leaf undersides, draining the plant's moisture and causing leaves to curl.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ, ni egbi lɛ sumɔɔ kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmei kɛ mealybugs. Kɛji nugbɔ bɛ ni akɛbaafɔ nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ babaoo oya yɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ. Ehaa tso lɛ mli nu lɛ hoɔ ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow at the bottom when I plant them close to my cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ kɛ́ midu lɛ yɛ ŋmei masɛi lɛ?

english: Cassava has deep, aggressive roots that steal nitrogen nutrients and water from neighboring crops. Maize planted too close gets crowded out and lacks nitrogen, causing its lower leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Yucca yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nitrogen, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli. Abele ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nitrogen bɛ mli. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do cassava cuttings brought from Côte d'Ivoire yield more tubers than my local farm cuttings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni akɛjɛɔ Côte d’Ivoire kɛbaa lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo fe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mimaŋ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved crop varieties developed across the border are often bred specifically for disease resistance and higher starch content, allowing them to produce larger tubers even in poor soils.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afɔɔ tsei srɔtoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni afee yɛ husui lɛ ateŋ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛha helai ni nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛyeɔ kɛ starch ni fa babaoo. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ anáa ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii po nɔ.

english: Why do my groundnut seeds rot in the ground when I plant them right after a big rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut dumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kpeteŋkpele ko sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain compacts soil and fills air pockets with water. Groundnut seeds need oxygen to germinate; soaking them in waterlogged mud suffocates the seeds, causing them to rot before sprouting.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛ nu eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ amli. Oxygen he miihia ŋmei dumɔwui koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui wo muji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key food crops need to build green leaves. Adding compost or manure gives the plants the nutrients they need to grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam tubers need loose, soft soil to expand properly. If the soil is hard, compact, or full of rocks, the tuber struggles to push through and ends up stunted or bent.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ, Tubers baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi ebaatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: When rain saturates the soil without good drainage, it drowns the roots by cutting off oxygen, allowing soil fungi to multiply and decay the cassava roots.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔɔ jogbaŋŋ. Cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faa babaoo ni ehaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves fold up during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants fold their leaves in high heat to reduce the surface area facing the direct sun, which helps them trap moisture inside and prevent water loss.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ kɛ la ni mli wa tsuɔ nii kɛfoɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ kɛkpeɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shi. Enɛ haa amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛtsiɔ nu ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my pepper plants before they turn into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress or prolonged dry soil, shedding flowers to save energy and protect themselves.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi be kakadaŋŋ nɔ. Amɛfɔ̃ɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe.

english: Why do my mature cocoa trees yield fewer pods when covered by big thick forest trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso ni eda lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ beni koo agbo ko ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ehà nɔ lɛ?

english: While young cocoa trees need shade from direct sun, older cocoa trees need sunlight to make food for flowering and pod production. Heavy canopy shade starves them of this essential light.
ga: Nakai beaŋ lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he miihia kookoo tsei bibii lɛ. Kokoo tsei ni egbɔ lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛná niyenii kɛha fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ feemɔ. Kpokpaa lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be lɛ haaa amɛná la ni he hiaa nɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my garden egg plants curling up and twisting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ mli ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that hide under the leaves and feed on the plant's juices, spreading plant sickness.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ekɛ ehe teeɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni eyeɔ tsei amli nu. kɛ tsei ahe helai baa

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and gives crop-specific pests a permanent home to multiply.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsei amli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ naa shia ni amɛhiɔ shi daa ni amɛfɔɔ bii.

english: Why does my plantain sucker wither and die soon after I transplant it to a new field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ ewo shikpɔŋ hee nɔ lɛ?

english: A young sucker dies if its root base is damaged during removal or if it is left in the heat before planting, which prevents it from sucking up water in its new home.
ga: Suckers baagboi kɛji akɛ shishitoo lɛ fite yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ lɛ loo ashi yɛ latsaa mli dani adu. Enɛ baaye abua ni nu akashɛ oshia hee lɛ mli.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster on my farm than the vegetables I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya fe aduawai ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally built to survive harsh local soils and conditions, allowing them to absorb nutrients and water much faster than cultivated farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni abɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔji kɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Enɛ haa amɛnáa niyenii kɛ nu oya fe tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why does it take several years for a new cocoa tree to produce pods when crops like maize produce food in just a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii babaoo dani cacao tso hee ko woɔ ŋmeii, yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa baanyɛ awo niyenii yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa is a perennial tree crop that invests its early years into building deep roots and strong woody stems. Once established, it can bear fruit for over 30 years, unlike seasonal crops like maize that grow quickly but die after a single harvest.
ga: Cocoa ji tso ko ni yeɔ afii babaoo ni ekɛ eshika woɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tso shishifãi ni wa lɛ amli yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli. Kɛ́ adu amɛ pɛ lɛ, amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo yibii fe afii 30, ni amɛtamɔɔɔ be mli nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa ni daa oya shi amɛgboiɔ yɛ ŋmãa kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it necessary to cut down and destroy a cocoa tree if it catches the swollen shoot disease instead of just spraying it with medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ afolɔ kookoo tsei ni akpata amɛhiɛ kɛji akɛ hela ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ emɔ amɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha tsofa ko kɛkɛ?

english: The Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus lives deep inside the tree's sap system where chemical sprays cannot reach. Cutting down and removing infected trees is the only effective way to stop the virus from spreading through insects to the rest of your healthy farm.
ga: Cocoa bud hela lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. ni tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ kooloi bibii anɔ egbɛ eshwa hei krokomɛi. ni ji oŋmɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli

english: If I plant my cocoa trees very close together so I can fit more on my land, will I get a bigger harvest?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ midu kookoo tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa bɔni afee ni maná he ko babaoo hu? Ani maná ŋmaa babaoo fe nakai?

english: Planting cocoa trees too close together causes their leaves to block sunlight from each other and their roots to fight for soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each tree enough sunlight, water, and airflow, which reduces fungal diseases and leads to a better overall harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ adu kokoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ atsĩ hulu la lɛ naa, ni shishifãi lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa.

english: Can young cocoa trees survive if I clear all the big trees from my land so they get direct sunlight?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei bibii lɛ baahi shi kɛji mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn under strong, direct sunlight. Keeping taller shade trees on the farm protects young cocoa from heat stress, helps soil retain moisture, and creates a cool environment where cocoa thrives.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ akwɛmɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. ni efee shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni kookoo shwereɔ yɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce hundreds of small flowers, but most of them drop off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi bibii ohai abɔ, shi amɛteŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can support as full pods to attract pollinating insects. Dropping excess flowers is the tree's natural way of saving energy so it only spends resources maturing the pods it can properly nourish.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe fɔfɔi ni eyi obɔ lɛ koni ekɛgbala fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ. Fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, nibii pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛha pod lɛ aná niyenii kpakpa.

english: Is it safe for me to plant cassava right next to my young cocoa trees to make extra food while waiting for the cocoa to mature?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makwɛ ŋmei yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii ahe koni mafee niyenii krokomɛi yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ŋmei lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Cassava is a heavy feeder that aggressively drains soil moisture and nutrients, and its expanding root tubers can disturb young cocoa roots. Plantain is a safer companion crop because it provides helpful shade without competing as aggressively for root space.
ga: Cassava ji niyenii ni tsii ni jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa. Ni shishifãi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ baanyɛ agbala kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ anaa. Plantains ji nanemɛi tsei ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ejaakɛ amɛhaa hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni amɛkɛ hiɛdɔɔ etswaaa shishifãi ahe akaŋ.

english: How does dry, windy weather during the Harmattan season affect how cocoa trees grow and yield?
ga: Te shihilɛ ni mli egbi ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa yɛ Harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ saa kookoo tsei lɛ adalɛ kɛ amɛyibiiwoo he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Dry Harmattan winds suck moisture out of cocoa leaves, causing trees to drop leaves and young pods (cherelles) to save water. Placing organic mulch around the base of the trees helps retain soil moisture and protects roots during dry spells.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kookoo baai lɛ amli lɛ. Ha tsei lɛ ashwie baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii (cherelles) koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Organic mulch ni akɛwoɔ Tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do some of my tiny young cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up before growing into big pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Young pods often turn black due to fungal infections like black pod disease or natural cherelle wilt caused by excess dampness and shade. Pruning lower branches improves air circulation through the farm, keeping pods dry and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ ŋmeii helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji hela loo adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni fa fe nine kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ. Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. Ha pods lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cocoa farm yield fewer pods each year even though the trees are still alive and standing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoe ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ daa afi be mli ni tsei lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni amɛdamɔ shi lɛ?

english: Over many years, cocoa trees absorb nutrients like potassium and phosphorus out of the soil. Without returning nutrients through organic compost or proper fertilizers, old soil becomes exhausted, causing healthy-looking trees to produce fewer pods.
ga: Afii babaoo ni eho nɛ lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ potassium kɛ phosphorus kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsuuu nii ekoŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ momo lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ.

english: Why do fewer weeds grow on the ground once my cocoa trees grow tall and close together at the top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ faaa yɛ be mli ni mi-cacao tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees mature, their upper branches overlap to form a thick overhead canopy that blocks direct sunlight from reaching the ground. Since weeds need sunlight to grow, the shade created by mature cocoa trees naturally prevents weed growth.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ, ŋwɛi niji lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni tsiɔ hulu la ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Ejaakɛ hulu la he miihia jwɛi dani amɛkwɛ̃. Shade ni kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ haa lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are my cassava plants producing very small tubers this season while my neighbor gets huge ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ miiwo ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ná yitso agbo diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers need loose soil and balanced nutrients like potassium to expand; if the ground is too hard or lacks nutrients, the plant spends its energy growing leaves instead of heavy tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ potassium, he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli lɛ, Tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ bulbs ni tsii baatsu nii.

english: Why do my cocoa pods drop off the tree and die before they are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed young pods if they are stressed by dry spells, poor soil, or insect attacks, but providing adequate shade, water, and fertilizer helps the tree keep its fruit.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbii bibii lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji hɔmɔ, shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo kooloi bibii hao amɛ. Shi kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo, nu, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ha tso lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ eyibii lɛ amli.

english: Why does my garden egg plant produce plenty of flowers, but the flowers just fall off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Flowers fall off without fruiting when the plant suffers from water stress, extreme heat, or a lack of pollinating insects like bees to transfer pollen between blossoms.
