ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ nu mli haomɔ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo nibii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ ŋmeii ni kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ lɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: How do I know if an old orange tree on my farm will produce fruit again or if I should cut it down?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji citrus tsei momo ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baawo yibii ekoŋŋ loo esa akɛ afo amɛ?

english: If a fruit tree continues to produce very low yields for two or three consecutive seasons despite good care and fertilizer, it may be too old or diseased, meaning it is best to replace it with a new seedling.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ tee nɔ amɛwo yibii ni baa shi kwraa yɛ bei enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli yɛ kwɛmɔ kpakpa kɛ fɔmɔ nii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Ekolɛ tso lɛ hu egbɔ tsɔ loo hela emɔ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ eheei atsake dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over when the bunch of plantains gets big and heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ miigbee shi lɛ? Ni plantains akuu lɛ miije shishi eefee agbo ni etsii?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that cannot support heavy fruit bunches on their own, so supporting them with strong wooden props or stakes prevents them from bending or snapping.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛŋ akwɛ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ anɔ. by yourself No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tsei loo tsei ni wa fi dumɔwui lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anaa koni amɛkakumɔ loo amɛkakumɔ.

english: I planted many pepper seeds in my nursery, but only a few sprouted and survived; what went wrong?
ga: Midu pepper dumɔwui babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmɔtɔ dumɔwui fioo komɛi pɛ kwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi. meni ba?

english: Pepper seeds need consistent moisture, loose soil, and proper planting depth; if planted too deep or in dry soil, many seeds fail to germinate or die before breaking through the soil.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui taoɔ nu ni mli edɔ daa, shikpɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ dumɔ mlibotemɔ ni sa. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ tsɔ loo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ Dumɔwui babaoo kwɛŋ loo amɛgboii dani amɛfo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cabbage seedlings suddenly wilt and die just a few days after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young seedlings often die from fungal diseases caused by excessive moisture in the soil, so avoiding overwatering and ensuring good water drainage keeps the tender stems healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei bibii gboiɔ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ fe nine lɛ mli baa lɛ hewɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okpa nu ni fa fe nine ni okwɛ koni nu lɛ aya nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Should I let my maize land rest for a season after a bad harvest, or can I plant again immediately?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maha mi-ŋma ŋmɔ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe be kome yɛ ŋmaa ni ehiii lɛ sɛɛ loo esa akɛ madu ekoŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Giving soil a rest period or planting soil-enriching crops like beans allows the land to rebuild essential nutrients, resulting in much stronger crops during the next planting cycle.
ga: Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ loo adu ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ etswaa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ ekoŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ babaoo yɛ dumɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: How long should I wait after applying fertilizer to see if my yam plants are responding well?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwo mli lɛ sɛɛ koni mana kɛji mi-sweet potato tso lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yam plants usually show greener leaves and faster vine growth within one to two weeks after receiving fertilizer, provided the soil has enough moisture to absorb the nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato tsei lɛ baajie baai eŋɔli kpo ni wain tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya yɛ otsi kome kɛyashi enyɔ mli beni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: If my current tomato seeds keep giving me poor yields every harvest, should I switch to a different type of seed?
ga: Kɛji akɛ mi tomato dumɔwui ni miyɔɔ amrɔ nɛɛ woɔ yibii fioo be fɛɛ be ni makpa amɛ. Ani esa akɛ matsake kɛya dumɔwu kroko nɔ?

english: Yes, switching to high-quality, certified seeds that are resistant to local diseases and suited for your climate will yield far better harvests than re-planting low-performing seeds.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsakemɔ kɛmiiya dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ, ni awo he odaseyeli nɔ. Amɛnyɛŋ amɛye helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ, ni amɛhi kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni oyɔɔ lɛ. Ebaaha yibiiwoo ni hi fe dumɔwui ni tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Can I plant cassava, yams, and cocoyams together on the same plot of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei, ŋmei kɛ kookoo yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, you can plant them together, but you must space them carefully. Cassava takes up a lot of room and draws heavy nutrients from the soil, so if planted too close, it will shade out and starve nearby yams and cocoyams.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ amɛ afee ekome. Shi esa akɛ okɛ ohe akabɔ he jogbaŋŋ. Cassava heɔ he babaoo ni ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni tsii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ Etsiɔ hulu lɛ naa ni ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ sweet potatoes kɛ cocoa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava grow tall with many leaves but give very small tubers when I plant it under my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai kakadaji babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ dumɔwui ashishi lɛ?

english: Cassava needs direct, full sunlight to build energy and store food in its roots. When planted in the deep shade of heavy plantain leaves, the cassava spends all its energy stretching upwards for light instead of growing tubers.
ga: Cassava he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee hewalɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ato eshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ adu yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni plantain baai ni mli tse yɔɔ mli Yɛ bulbs ni eeekwɛ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ, ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛshwieɔ shi koni ekɛmɔ la lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on to produce good tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ koni ená ŋmeii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Yam vines are climbing plants that need stakes to lift their leaves off the ground and expose them to direct sunlight. More leaf surface in the sun means the plant can generate more energy to grow large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛhaa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ waa. Hulu la ni tsoɔ baa lɛ nɔ babaoo lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ baanyɛ afee hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛwo bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce smaller bunches of fruit after a few harvest cycles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii bibii lɛ? Yɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli fãi fioo komɛi asɛɛ

english: Plantain plants feed heavily on soil nutrients and water. Over time, the parent tree creates too many young suckers that steal food from the main plant, so you must prune away extra suckers and add fresh organic manure to keep fruit bunches large.
ga: Dumɔwui yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, tso ni ji nyɛ lɛ baawo ŋmeii bibii babaoo tsɔ ni ebaanyɛ eju niyenii kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni okɛ humus hee afata he koni aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cocoyam leaves dry up faster in the heat compared to my cassava plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ latsaa be mli kɛ akɛto mi-cassava tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Cocoyams have broad leaves and shallow root systems that lose water quickly and require moist soil or mild shade to thrive. Cassava has deeper root systems that store water, making it much more resistant to dry spells.
ga: Cocoyam yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nu fiteɔ oya ni ebiɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo hulutsoo be fioo. kɛha dalɛ Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni kɛ nu toɔ. Enɛ haa enyɛɔ eshiɔ hɔmɔ shihilɛi babaoo.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are mature and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Most local cassava varieties mature between 9 to 12 months after planting, which is usually indicated by lower leaves turning yellow and dropping off. Harvesting too late makes the tubers turn woody or rot in the soil.
ga: Kuu lɛ mli ŋmeii srɔtoi lɛ ateŋ babaoo daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai lɛ ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kadiɔ enɛ. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ tsei loo amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How does growing plantains and cocoyams help if I want to raise snails on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ plantain kɛ cocoa ni ooodu lɛ he kɛji oosumɔ ni okwɛ ŋmeii yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Broad leaves from plantain and cocoyam plants trap moisture and block direct sunlight, creating the cool, humid shade that snails need to stay moist, survive heat, and lay eggs.
ga: Baai ni mli kwɔlɔ kɛjɛ dumɔwui kɛ akooshi tsei amli lɛ mɔɔ nu ni amɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa hulutsoo, ni mli edɔ ni he hiaa ni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi yɛ nu mli lɛ baa. Enyɛɔ dɔlɛ naa ni ewoɔ ŋmeii

english: Why is it best to plant my root crops right at the start of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu ŋmeii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Planting at the beginning of the major rains ensures young crop cuttings and seed tubers get steady water to develop strong root systems before the heat sets in, leading to higher survival rates and better yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shishijee mli lɛ haa dumɔwui kɛ dumɔwui ayitsei lɛ naa nu ni yaa nɔ daa koni amɛná shishifãi ni mli wa dani latsaa lɛ aba.

english: Why do my crops yield less food if I keep planting the exact same crop on the same spot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ naa niyenii fioo kɛji midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from that spot and allows pests and diseases that attack that specific crop to multiply in the soil. Rotating your crops keeps the soil balanced and healthy.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ nakai he lɛ pɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi kɛ helai ni tutuaa nakai tso lɛ koni amɛshwere yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Oŋmɔshi nibii ni oootsake lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does writing down the total harvest of my crops each season help me manage my farm better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni mikɛwoɔ wolo nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi koni makwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Keeping simple records of what you harvest helps you see whether your crop yields are growing or dropping each season. It makes it easier to plan how much produce to sell, how much food to keep for your family, and how much seed or fertilizer to buy for the next planting.
ga: Niŋmaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni kɔɔ nɔ ni okpaa lɛ he lɛ baaye abua bo ni ona kɛji onibii ni okpaa lɛ miiya hiɛ loo ebaa shi yɛ be ko mli. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ oooto nibii ni obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ lɛ ayibɔ he gbɛjianɔ. Niyenii enyiɛ yɔɔ kɛha weku lɛ? Ni dumɔwui loo ŋmɔshi nibii enyiɛ obaanyɛ ohe kɛha odumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when there is strong sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct sunlight because their foliage is soft and fragile. Planting fast-growing crops like plantain beside them provides natural shade and preserves soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe waaa. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ Emasɛi lɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo aba ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize farm turning pale yellow from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ kɛjɛ shishi kɛtee ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the nutrient responsible for green leaf growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will nourish the soil and bring back the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni haa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ daa lɛ Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people recommend planting groundnuts together on the same farm as cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ afee ekome kɛdu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and other legumes trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil naturally. Cassava feeds on this extra nutrient, improving soil fertility and giving you better yields without wearing out the land.
ga: Peanuts kɛ legumes krokomɛi Mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Cassava yeɔ niyenii krɛdɛɛ nɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa yibii kpakpai baa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteee.

english: Yam tubers grow underground and need soft, deep, and loose soil to expand easily into large shapes. High mounds also protect the tubers from soaking in excess water, which prevents root rot during heavy rains.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ehe miihia ni amɛná shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ, ni shwieɔ shi koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ hu buɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ nu ni fa fe nine ni shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ he. Enɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ akafite yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin with small cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ amli tsei ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ Dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots and leaves fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil food. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to build thick stalks and produce full, heavy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni mli tse ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni tsii ni eyi obɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why does my plantain farm produce smaller bunches after two or three years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ afii enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A mature plantain plant sprouts many shoots called suckers around its base. If you do not cut away the extra suckers, they steal water and food from the main plant, resulting in smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Plantain tso ni eda lɛ baawo ŋmeii babaoo ni atsɛɔ amɛ peripapillary ŋmeii. Kɛji ofolɔɔɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, Ebaaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why are small worms eating the inside funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: These pests are likely Fall Armyworms, which feed on the growing centers of maize plants. Checking your crops early and applying approved insecticides or remedies like neem oil helps stop them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii amli mra Ni okɛ tsofai loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ, tamɔ neem fɔ atsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani efite.

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips that suck sap from the leaves and spread viruses. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves flat and healthy so fruit can develop properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baa lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper leaf curl baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa bɔni afee ni aduawai lɛ anyɛ ada jogbaŋŋ.

english: The very first rain is often followed by a long dry spell, which bakes the soil and kills newly sprouted seeds. Waiting for two or three steady rains ensures the ground remains wet enough for young seedlings to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔi ni nɛɔ mra lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ashã ni egbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔwui bibii. koni ehi wala mli

english: Tomato flowers often drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes dry during flowering. Regular watering at the root level and protecting plants from extreme heat keeps the flowers attached so they can turn into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu daa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni obu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔi lɛ akakpɛtɛ aduawai lɛ ahe.

english: How many days should I wait to see my maize seeds sprout after planting them in the soil?
ga: Kɛ́ amɛdu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ, gbii enyiɛ esa akɛ amɛmɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Maize seeds usually germinate and sprout within 4 to 7 days if the soil has enough moisture and warmth. If it takes longer than a week, the soil may be too dry, the seeds were planted too deep, or insects have damaged the seeds underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbii 4 kɛyashi 7 mli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ ni edɔ. Kɛji ehe be fe otsi kome Ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Adu dumɔwui lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. loo kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: What will happen to my corn crop if I leave it in the field for two extra weeks after it is ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli otsii enyɔ krokomɛi beni amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Leaving mature corn in the field too long exposes it to wild birds, insects, and rain. The moisture can cause mold to grow on the cobs and rot the grains, lowering the market value and quality of your harvest.
ga: Abele ni ekwɛ̃ ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ kɛ koo mli okpoi, kooloi bibii kɛ nugbɔ woɔ oshara mli. Fɛ̃i baanyɛ aha ŋmɔtɔ aba tso lɛ nɔ ni eha dumɔwui lɛ agbo. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, jara ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ jara kɛ bɔ ni ehi ha lɛ baa shi.

english: Why is it bad if I delay the first weeding on my maize farm by a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ klɛŋklɛŋ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ sɛɛ otsii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and quickly steal the water, sunlight, and plant food in the soil. If you delay weeding, your young corn plants will become weak, thin, and stunted because the weeds are choking them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Kɛji okɛ jwɛi lɛ shwiemɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ O-ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ, amɛbaagbɔjɔ, ni amɛbaagbɔjɔ ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ miitsi amɛnaa.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a cry for food, specifically nitrogen. When the soil lacks nitrogen or when heavy rain washes it away, the plant cannot make energy, causing its lower leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ji niyenii bolɔmɔ. titri lɛ nitrogen Beni nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Tsei nyɛŋ afee hewalɛ. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Fertilizer is best applied in two stages: the first batch about 10 to 14 days after the seeds sprout to build strong roots, and the second batch at about 4 to 5 weeks when the plant grows tall and prepares to form cobs.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ gbɛi enyɔ nɔ: klɛŋklɛŋ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ aaafee gbii 10 kɛyashi 14 sɛɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ koni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa. Ni fã ni ji enyɔ lɛ heɔ aaafee otsii 4 kɛyashi 5 beni tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛsaa amɛhe koni amɛfee ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do I see small holes in my corn leaves and green dirt inside the stalk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ muji eŋɔli ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: This is damage caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaves of the maize plant and eat the tender growth, which can destroy the stalk if not treated early with proper pest control.
ga: Enɛ ji nɔ ni Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ afite tso lɛ yitso lɛ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra. Kɛtsɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ ni sa nɔ

english: Why shouldn't I plant my corn seeds very close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the adult plants will compete with each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow thin and produce very small cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei ni eda lɛ kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: How do I know if my land is located in a good place for growing maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ he ko ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Good land for maize should get plenty of direct sunlight, have rich dark topsoil, and drain water easily so that the roots do not sit in flooded water after heavy rains.
ga: Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa lɛ aná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa yɛ jɛmɛ. ni nu ni ajieɔ lɛ waaa Enɛ ji koni shishifãi lɛ akabote nu afua mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa sɛɛ.

english: Why do my harvested vegetables spoil quickly when I transport them from my farm to the town market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ?

english: Vegetables spoil quickly if they are harvested in the hot sun, bruised during packing, or stacked tightly in plastic sacks without air holes. Heat and lack of ventilation cause them to sweat and rot quickly during transit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akpa aduawai yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, amɛfiteɔ oya. Atswa lɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ Aloo akɛwo plastic kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ bu bɛ mli lɛ amli. Dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ latsaa kɛ fitemɔ oya baa beni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ.

english: Why does my stored corn turn moldy even though the cobs looked dry when I picked them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmãa lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbi kɛ́ mikɛto lɛ?

english: Corn grains often feel dry on the outside while still holding moisture deep inside. If you store them immediately without thoroughly drying them on a clean mat in the sun, that trapped moisture causes dangerous mold to grow in storage.
ga: Abele ŋmeii lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛhe egbi yɛ kponɔgbɛ shi amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli shɔŋŋ kɛji akɛ okɛto amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛgbiko kwraa yɛ ŋmei ni he tse nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Fɛ̃i ni emɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ oshara aba he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth. It can also happen when the soil is too waterlogged, preventing the roots from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye niyenii.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl up to protect themselves and reduce water loss when the weather is too hot or dry. Adding mulch around the base of the plants keeps the soil moist and reduces heat stress.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe ni amɛha nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ waa. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa hulutsoo he haomɔ baa shi.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, uneven watering, or getting too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently moist during flowering helps the plant hold onto its blooms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ mli. Nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa tsɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni afeɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why do people tell me to plant cassava or plantain together with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko baakɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ adu ŋmei loo ŋmei?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Fast-growing crops like plantains or cassava act as temporary shade partners, keeping the soil cool and moist so the young cocoa can survive its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo cassava tsuɔ nii akɛ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo bibioo lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why does planting cowpeas in my field help my next maize crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni mi-ŋmei srɔtoi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When the cowpea plants decay, they release this free natural fertilizer into the ground for the next crop to feed on.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Beni tsina tsei lɛ miifite lɛ Amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko nɛɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aye.

english: How do I know which direction to push cassava stem cuttings into the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole he ni esa akɛ okɛ ŋmei nine lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava cuttings should be planted with the buds pointing upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down causes the new roots and stems to grow backward, leading to weak growth and very small tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei niji ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ ŋwɛi. Dumɔ ni aduɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ haa shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii heei kwɛ̃ɔ kɛyaa sɛɛ. Enɛ haa amɛdalɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛyitsei lɛ hu feɔ bibii waa.

english: Yam vines naturally climb to catch sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they get maximum sun, stay safe from fungal diseases, and send more energy into growing big underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛná hulu la. Staking baaye abua ni awo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ni ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo majeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin with tiny cobs if I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ amli tsei ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ni kɛji akɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ hu?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients. Giving each seed proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough food to grow thick stalks and full cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, prevents weeds from sprouting, traps moisture in the ground during hot days, and cools down the root area.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni jwɛi akakwɛ̃. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every season and lets crop-specific pests and diseases multiply in the ground. Rotating with different crops keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni eha tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo aya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are green caterpillars eating the center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana. They hide inside the growing tip of young maize plants and chew the leaves, which slows plant growth and reduces crop yields unless managed early.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni miida lɛ ashishifãi amli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi. ja atsu he nii oya

english: This condition is known as Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly during rainy, humid weather. Clearing heavy weeds and removing infected pods early stops the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Atsɛɔ hela nɛɛ akɛ black pod hela. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ latsaa be mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ waa kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra. Enɛ baatsi ŋmei lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or mites that transmit plant viruses. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaf curl from spreading through your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ni hiɛ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baatsi baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn dark and rotten?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ mli edɔ ni egbo lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot, caused by uneven watering and a lack of calcium in the plant during fruit development, rather than an insect or disease attack.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli be fɛɛ be kɛ calcium ni bɛ tsei amli yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ aduawai lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni kooloi loo helai baatutua lɛ

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn pale yellow and drop off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually signal that the soil is low in essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that the plant is suffering from drought or cassava mosaic virus. Adding organic compost or appropriate fertilizer restores health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. loo tsei miikpe hɔmɔ loo ŋmei mosaic hela. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting maize in the same spot continuously drains specific soil nutrients and lets pests and diseases build up in the soil; rotating with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: It is best to wait until the rains become steady for about two consecutive weeks rather than planting right after the first rain, which can dry out seeds if a sudden dry spell follows.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi aaafee otsi enyɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi kɛji hɔmɔ ba trukaa.

english: Why does my crop yield drop when I plant seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ baa shi kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in thin plants and small harvests. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to thrive.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmaa fioo ko baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda.

english: What causes my yam tubers to grow thin and twisted instead of big and smooth?
ga: Mɛni haa mi sweet potato tubers lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni efiteɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee agbo ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Hard, compacted soil makes it difficult for tubers to expand smoothly, while tiny worm-like pests called nematodes in the soil can damage the growing tips of the roots, causing deformed shapes.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa bulb lɛ akɛ ebaagbɛ eshwa. yɛ be mli ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tamɔ ŋmeii bibii Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ soil nematodes lɛ baanyɛ afite shishifãi ni miida lɛ ashishifãi. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ gbɔlɛ aba.

english: How can I stop tiny insects from destroying my stored beans after harvest?
ga: Matsi kooloi bibii lɛ anaa Te aaafee tɛŋŋ atsĩ kɔfi ŋmeii ni ato lɛ anaa koni ekafite yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: Weevils attack dried beans during storage; drying your harvested beans thoroughly under the sun and storing them in sealed, airtight PICS bags cuts off oxygen and kills the pests without using harmful chemicals.
ga: Moths tutuaa ŋmeii ni egbi yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmei ni akpa lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu shishi ni akɛto PICS kotokui ni atsĩ naa lɛ amli lɛ, efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baa shi ni egbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni akɛ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui tsuuu nii.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and dry during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight and dry winds. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby creates a canopy that shields the young cocoa from hot sun until they are mature enough to handle full sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi mli. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ agbo bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do I see small ragged holes in my maize leaves and tiny caterpillars hidden inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni akɛtee baai lɛ amli lɛ anɔ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds on the soft green leaves and growing shoots of maize plants. Early treatment with recommended organic sprays or neem extracts helps protect your crop before the pests ruin the whole stalk.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ahe baai bibii kɛ amɛmli bibii lɛ. Mra be mli tsamɔ Kɛtsɔ organic spray loo neem extract ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebuɔ onibii ahe dani tsɛŋemɔ helai fiteɔ tso lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting under the ground before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when the soil holds too much water or when waterlogging causes root fungal diseases. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away and keeps the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo loo kɛ́ nu afua ba, ni ekɛ fungal shishifãi helai baa. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋmei nɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the plants are still short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ yɔɔ kuku lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves mean your soil is low on nitrogen, which maize plants need to build strong leaves and grow tall. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer early in the planting season will turn the leaves green again and encourage fast growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ akwɛ baai ni wa ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara oya.

english: Why are my plantain bunches getting smaller every year on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibii daa afi yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: When a plantain stool produces too many side shoots or suckers, they all fight for the same soil food and water. Pruning extra suckers so that only two or three strong stems remain per plant leaves enough food for the plant to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Beni plantain stool lɛ yɛ ŋmeii loo afã ŋmeii babaoo tsɔ. Amɛbaatswa niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hu. Afoɔ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ amli bɔni afee ni ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahi tso kome nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni efee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Weeds grow quickly and steal nutrients, water, and sunlight that your crops need to thrive. Removing weeds early in your crop's growth stage removes this competition so your plants can feed well and grow rapidly.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛshwere. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Yɛ tsei adalɛ be mli lɛ ajieɔ akaŋshii nɛɛ kɛyaa. No hewɔ lɛ, otsei lɛ baanyɛ aye nii jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdara oya.

english: Why do the flowers drop off my tomato plants without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the ground gets too dry or when daytime temperatures become extremely high. Keeping the soil moist with regular watering and spreading straw mulch around the base cools the soil and helps flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ waa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i kɛtsɔ nu ni oooha lɛ daa kɛ jwɛi ni okɛbaabɔle shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ, ni no haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need their leaves lifted high to catch direct sunlight, which helps the plant make food to swell the tubers underground. Staking also lifts leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ adara babaoo koni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii haa ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛfuu. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Why should I sort my harvested maize by size and remove insect-damaged kernels before selling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahala mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ yɛ bɔ ni elɛɛmɔ ji lɛ naa, ni majie ŋmeii ni kooloi efite lɛ fɛɛ dani mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Sorting out bad or insect-damaged grains raises the overall quality of your produce, prevents rot from spreading during storage, and attracts buyers who are willing to pay a higher price for clean, uniform grain.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie ŋmaa ni ehiii loo ni kooloi efite lɛ, ebaaha onibii fɛɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ aya hiɛ. Etsiɔ fitemɔ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. ni egbalaa mɛi ni heɔ nii ni sumɔɔ ni amɛwo jara ni nɔ kwɔ kɛha ŋmaa ni he tse ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ.

english: Why does my stored corn turn powdery and smell bad after a few weeks in the crib?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ bafeɔ powder ni eŋɔɔɔ kɛji akɛ ehi ŋmãa lɛ mli otsii fioo komɛi?

english: Stored corn rots and grows mold when it is put away while still holding too much moisture. Thoroughly drying your corn on tarpaulins in the sun until kernels are hard before putting them into bags keeps mold away and keeps the grain safe.
ga: Abɛi ni ato lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛji ajie lɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ yɛ tarpaulin nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa dani awo mli yɛ kotoku mli lɛ, no tsiɔ ŋmãa naa ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and dry up when I plant them in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are like human babies—they burn easily under intense sun. Planting shade crops like plantains or cassava next to them provides living shade and moisture, helping the young cocoa survive its first couple of years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantain loo cassava yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my vegetable crops with dried grass or dry leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass (mulching) acts like a cool blanket. It traps moisture in the ground during hot sunny days, keeps weeds from growing, and stops the soil from becoming too hard for plant roots.
ga: Mulching ni egbi (mulching) tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni mli ejɔ. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni wa tsɔ kɛha tsei shishifãi.

english: Planting too close forces overcrowded maize plants to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks with small or empty cobs, which actually reduces your total harvest compared to proper spacing.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha ŋmãa tsei lɛ ayi obɔ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ tsei bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa. Enɛ haa okpamɔ fɛɛ baa shi kɛ akɛto gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ he.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to plant cassava stem cuttings at an angle into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei niji yɛ he ko ni kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kpãa gbee lɛ?

english: Planting cassava stems at a slight angle ensures the growing buds point upward toward the sun while keeping enough stem buried to sprout strong roots. Planting upside down or incorrectly prevents proper growth and reduces tuber yields.
ga: Kɛ́ adu yucca tso lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ fioo lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni miida lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛya hulu lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi ni wa akwɛ̃. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛi loo yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ tsiɔ dalɛ ni sa naa ni ehaa tuber yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Why is it necessary to put tall wooden sticks next to my yam vines as they start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akɛ tsei kakadaji ama amɛhe lɛ? Mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ beni ebɔi kwɛ̃mɔ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch maximum sunlight so leaves can make food for underground tubers. Staking lifts leaves off the damp ground, preventing leaf diseases and helping the plant produce larger yams.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ afee niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I trim off extra shoots sprouting around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and nutrients away from the main plant. Trimming them off leaves only the strongest shoot, ensuring the mother plant has enough energy to produce large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Afoɔ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo plantains ŋmɔji wuji ni tsii.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas in my farm help make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the plants decay, this stored nitrogen acts as a free natural fertilizer for crops planted afterward.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tsei fite Nitrogen ni ato nɛɛ baatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha tsei ni adu sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when plants experience extreme heat stress, poor soil moisture, or nutrient shortages. Keeping the soil evenly watered and lightly shaded during severe heat encourages flowers to turn into healthy peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehiii loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa Nɔ ni fata shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ he ji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo fioo ni akɛhaa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ewo fɔfɔi lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn black and soft while still growing on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato aduawai lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo yɛ be mli ni edaa yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, often due to irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture consistent allows the roots to absorb calcium steadily.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛjieɔ calcium.

english: Why are the leaves on my young rice plants turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Pale yellow leaves on young rice plants usually mean the crop is lacking essential nitrogen fertilizer or the water in the paddy field is stagnant and suffocating the roots. Adding nitrogen and managing water flow restores green growth.
ga: Baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ omɔ tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa waa. Aloo nu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nitrogen ni akɛbaafata he kɛ nu ni hoɔ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to direct sun and can easily scorch. Plantains grow quickly and produce wide leaves that act as natural sunshades, keeping the soil moist and protecting the young cocoa trees during their early growth.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ nuɔ hulu la he tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshã oya. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa shishijee lɛ.

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen out of the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil with free fertilizer that the maize plants can feed on.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ baanyɛ aye lɛ.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is essential for green leafy growth, and when it is missing, the plant shifts its remaining nitrogen to the upper leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he hiaa waa kɛha baa eŋɔli lɛ dalɛ. Ni kɛ́ etee Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress, such as extremely hot weather, irregular watering, or a lack of essential nutrients like calcium and boron needed for fruit development.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium kɛ boron ni he hiaa koni aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ bɛ.

english: This leaf curling is caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant stem cuttings is the best way to prevent this infection.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwiemɔ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Nibii ni afolɔ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela nɛɛ naa.

english: Why are my pepper plant leaves getting tightly wrinkled and bunched up at the top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe waa ni ebua ehe naa yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ?

english: Wrinkled and stunted leaves on pepper plants are caused by tiny pests like thrips or mites sucking the sap from young leaves, which deforms the growth and reduces your yield.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa ji kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ehiii baa ni ehaa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves and capture maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to create energy, which is sent underground to grow larger yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai ni amɛfeɔ hewalɛ. ni akɛmajeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛkwɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji

english: Why do my mature plantain trees fall over easily during light storms before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains ni eda lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum bibioo ko mli dani kpamɔ baa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can be destroyed by microscopic soil pests called nematodes or stem borers, weakening the tree's base so it cannot support heavy fruit bunches in the wind.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ baanyɛ afite. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, enyɛŋ ekwɛ aduawai akui ni tsii yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable farm in the afternoon heat or early morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ shwane mli loo leebi maŋkpa?

english: It is best to water early in the morning so the moisture reaches the roots before the heat evaporates it. Afternoon watering can scorch wet leaves under intense sunlight.
ga: Esa akɛ afee nu leebi maŋkpa koni ŋmɔtɔ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe dani la ni tsoɔ lɛ atsɔ mli. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ shwane mli lɛ baanyɛ aha baai ni efɔ lɛ ashã yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi.

english: Weeds have strong roots that aggressively steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer from your main crop, leaving your crops hungry and weak despite plenty of rain.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii ni ogbɔjɔ yɛ nugbɔ babaoo ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: How do I know if a piece of land I want to buy is good for growing cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni misumɔɔ ni mahe lɛ hi kɛha kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Cocoa trees need deep, rich soil that holds water well but does not flood. You can test the soil by digging down; if it is dark, soft, full of decomposed leaves, and crumbles easily in your hand, it has the nutrients to support healthy cocoa roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii ni nu yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ shi nu shwieee nɔ lɛ he miihia koko tsei. Obaanyɛ oka shikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ mli ni oootsɔ mli lɛ nɔ.Kɛ́ eyɛ ediŋ, eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, ni baai ni egboi eyi mli obɔ lɛ. ni egbeeɔ mlɛo yɛ nine mli Etsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo shishifãi lɛ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ kookoo ŋmeii amli.

english: Why does land that produced a good harvest of cassava last year yield smaller crops when I plant it again this year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni wo ŋmei kpakpa yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ wooo ŋmei fioo beni miduɔ ekoŋŋ afi nɛɛ?

english: Crops like cassava feed heavily on soil nutrients to form their roots. Planting on the same land repeatedly without giving the soil rest or adding organic manure exhausts the ground, leaving fewer nutrients for the next harvest.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛfee shishifãi. Shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni aduɔ nii shii abɔ Kɛji akɛ ahaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite. Niyenii mli hewalɛ fioo pɛ eshwɛɔ kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does rainwater stand on top of my farm for days, and is this bad for cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ enɛ eyi miŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ? Ni ani enɛ náa kookoo tso lɛ nɔ hewalɛ gbonyo?

english: Water stands on the surface when soil has heavy clay content that prevents water from sinking in. This waterlogging is dangerous for cocoa because cocoa roots need oxygen from the soil; constant standing water causes the roots to rot and kills the tree.
ga: Nu damɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni haaa efo. Nu ni hoɔ nɛɛ yeɔ kookoo awui ejaakɛ kookoo shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nu ni damɔ shi be fɛɛ be lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni efiteɔ tsei.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. Leaving larger shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantain acts as a living umbrella, protecting tender cocoa leaves from sun scorch and keeping the surrounding soil moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni adu koni amɛfee hulutsoo. Ebuɔ kookoo baai ni mli tse lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Can I grow food crops like yam or maize on the same field with my newly planted cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni adu kookoo tsei heei lɛ?

english: Yes, intercropping young cocoa with food crops provides useful shade and weed control while giving your family food and income. Just ensure the food crops are spaced far enough so they do not choke or steal sunlight from the growing cocoa stems.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo bibii ni akɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii baadu lɛ baaha hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ jwɛi akudɔmɔ aba. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha oweku lɛ niyenii kɛ shika. Kwɛmɔ pɛ akɛ niyenii tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ bɔ ni sa bɔni afee ni amɛkatsi amɛhe loo amɛkaju hulu la ni jɛɔ kookoo tsei ni miida lɛ amli lɛ.

english: If I plant my cocoa trees very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting trees too close together forces them to compete with each other for sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients. Giving each tree proper spacing allows branches to spread wide, catch light, and produce larger, healthier pods.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ aniji lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa, amɛmɔɔ la, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I cut off the extra shoots growing out from the lower part of my cocoa trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: These extra shoots, called suckers, steal valuable nutrients and water from the main tree. Removing them directs all the plant's energy into the main trunk to grow strong flowering branches and full pods.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers nɛɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ amɛ lɛ, etsɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ nɔ koni eha niji ni woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ ni ŋmeii lɛ ayi obɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my young crop leaves turn yellow and stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mibaai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee bibii lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-spreading roots that aggressively steal soil nutrients, nitrogen, and moisture meant for your crops. Without enough soil nutrients, crop leaves turn yellow and growth slows down.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni juɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii, nitrogen, kɛ nu ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Kɛji niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni edalɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the small young pods on my cocoa tree turning black and drying up before they grow full size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛdaraa kɛyashɛɔ amɛdalɛ he.

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in dark, damp, and overly humid conditions. Pruning excess branches lets air and sunlight flow through the farm, drying up the moisture that spreads the disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ fe nine. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ni gbɛɔ helai eshwaa lɛ agbi

english: How many years must I wait for a newly planted cocoa tree to start bearing pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Traditional cocoa trees usually take 3 to 5 years to start producing pods. However, newer hybrid cocoa varieties developed in Ghana can start yielding fruit in as little as 2 to 3 years under proper care and regular weeding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blema cacao tsei lɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛjeɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi. Shi kɛlɛ, yinɔ hee ko ni ji cocoa hybrids ni afee yɛ Ghana lɛ baanyɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 pɛ mli yɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ shishi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant is running out of nitrogen in the soil. When the soil lacks nitrogen, the plant moves what little it has from the older bottom leaves up to the younger leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni eda lɛ amli kɛyaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: Planting maize on the same spot repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and allows pests that feed on maize to build up in the dirt. Switching to legumes like groundnuts restores nutrients like nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ ni amɛbuaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide the soft shade and humidity cocoa trees need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo be fioo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Ehe miihia ni cacao tso lɛ ahi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up off the ground to catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight allows the leaves to make energy, which flows down into the ground to build big, healthy yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai ni amɛfeɔ hewalɛ. ni hoɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efeɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too hot or when the plant goes from dry conditions to sudden heavy watering. Extreme stress prevents the flower from pollinating properly, causing the plant to drop the bloom.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo beni tsei tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shihilɛ ni mli egbi mli kɛyaa shihilɛ ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Haomɔ ni naa wa haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ. ni haa tsei lɛ shwereɔ

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground when there is too much rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe and stay healthy. When heavy rains leave standing water in the soil for too long, the roots suffocate and harmful mold attacks them underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi hia kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni amɛmu ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are the leaves on my corn plants filled with ragged holes and small dark droppings in the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ eyi kɛ buji ni etse kɛ ŋmeii diji bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which hide inside the growing tip of the young maize plant and chew through the leaf whorls as they unfold.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni miida lɛ ashishifãi amli lɛ. ni efoɔ baa lɛ mli be mli ni amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo lɛ.

english: Why are the young leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and twisting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips hiding underneath the leaves and sucking out the sap, or by a viral infection spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ hela ko ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow so small and thin when I leave weeds around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni amɛhe waaa beni mishiɔ jwɛi yɛ he lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer directly from your crops. Because weeds grow aggressively, they choke your crops and leave them without enough food to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ daa oya Ehaa egbeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ni ehaa amɛnáaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: It is best to wait until the rain has soaked the soil deeply enough to reach your wrist when you push your hand into the dirt. Planting after small, light rains can cause seeds to sprout and then die if the rain stops for a week.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni eshɛ oniji ahe beni okɛ onine tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsi kome.

english: Why do some yam farmers get a massive harvest while others get very little on the same size of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato okwaafoi komɛi náa yibii babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mɛi komɛi naa nibii fioo pɛ yɛ he ni dalɛ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Different yields come down to farming practices—using clean, disease-free seed yams, proper spacing, staking early, and managing soil fertility can multiply your harvest many times over compared to traditional methods.
ga: Yibiiwoo lɛ srɔtoi yɛ okwaayeli nifeemɔi ahe. Kɛtsɔ sweet potatoes ni he tse ni hela bɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ he jɛkɛmɔ ni sa Shihilɛ mra kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsumɔ Ebaanyɛ eha onitsumɔ lɛ aya hiɛ shii abɔ kɛ akɛto blema gbɛi ahe.

english: How can I dramatically increase my yam yield without buying a larger piece of land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-sweet potato nitsumɔ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ni miheee shikpɔŋ wulu ko?

english: You can increase yields on the same land by using improved seed technology like yam minisetts, enriching your soil with organic manure or fertilizer, and keeping your farm free from weeds and pests.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui ahe ŋaa ni atsake, tamɔ minisette sweet potatoes lɛ atsu nii ni okɛha yibiiwoo aya hiɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ nɔ. Kɛ humus loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ. ni oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli afee nɔ ni jwɛi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui akafee nɔ ko.

english: What makes Ghanaian yams so popular with buyers in overseas markets like Europe and America?
ga: Mɛni haa mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ majimaji ateŋ jarayeli hei tamɔ Europa kɛ Amerika lɛ sumɔɔ Ghana mantis lɛ waa?

english: Ghanaian yams, particularly varieties like Pona, are globally prized because of their excellent taste, rich dry-matter content, fine texture, and good shelf life during transport.
ga: Ghana yams, titri lɛ, henɔi tamɔ Pona, ji nɔ ni jara wa waa yɛ je lɛŋ he fɛɛ he yɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ fɛo waa lɛ hewɔ. Eyɛ nibii ni mli egbi waa. Texture kpakpa kɛ shelf wala kpakpa yɛ gbɛfaa be mli

english: What standards do my crops need to meet before I can sell them to export companies?
ga: Mɛɛ shishitoo mlai esa akɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ashɛ he dani abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ aha nitsumɔhe ko ni kɛ nibii majeɔ maŋsɛɛ?

english: Export buyers look for smooth tubers that are uniform in size and weight, completely free from diseases, cuts, or bruises, and grown without harmful chemical residues.
ga: Majimaji ateŋ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ bulbs ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛdalɛ kɛ amɛtsiimɔ yeɔ egbɔ, ni helai, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bɛ mli, ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui eshwɛɛɛ amɛhe.

english: Which specific yam varieties should I plant if I want to target high-value buyers?
ga: Mɛɛ sweet potato henɔ pɔtɛɛ esa akɛ makwɛ kɛji miisumɔ ni makwɛ mɛi ni heɔ nibii ni jara wa waa lɛ anɔ?

english: Varieties like Pona and Labako are highly demanded for their taste and market value, though you must select healthy seed tubers that resist rot to satisfy premium buyers.
ga: Ataoɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi tamɔ Pona kɛ Labako waa yɛ bɔ ni amɛ ŋɔɔ ha kɛ bɔ ni amɛjara wa ha lɛ hewɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ, ehe miihia ni ohala dumɔwui ayitsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni teɔ shi woɔ fitemɔ koni oha mɛi ni heɔ nibii ni jara wa lɛ atsui anyɔ amɛmli moŋ.

english: Why is it important to make large mounds or ridges when planting yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afee gɔji wuji loo ŋmeii beni aduɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Mounds soften the soil so the tuber can expand freely underground, improve water drainage to prevent rot, and make it much easier to harvest the crop without breaking the tubers.
ga: Gɔji haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Ha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ koni akafite. Ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni akuuu bulb lɛ mli.

english: Will planting my crops closer together give me a bigger harvest in the end?
ga: Ani tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe lɛ baaha maná yibii babaoo yɛ naagbee?

english: No, planting too closely forces the crops to compete for sunlight, water, and nutrients, which results in many small, poor-quality tubers instead of large, healthy ones.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ ehe tsɔ lɛ, enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ehe awo hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa tso lɛ mli tsɔji bibii babaoo ni ehiii lɛ baa. Yɛ yitso agbo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ

english: How does the quality of the seed tuber I plant affect the ultimate size of my harvest?
ga: Te bɔ ni dumɔwui ayitsei ni miduɔ lɛ hi ha lɛ saa bɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ naagbee lɛ dalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: A healthy, disease-free seed tuber gives the plant a strong start with vigorous roots and shoots, leading to much higher yields compared to planting infected or weak seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ayitsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni hela bɛ mli lɛ haa tsei jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ kɛ shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo babaoo baa kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni hela emɔ amɛ loo ni egbɔjɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my harvested yams spoil quickly when I store them in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they are injured during harvest, exposed to intense heat, or stored in poorly ventilated areas where fungal infections can spread easily from one tuber to another.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ amɛpila yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. ni akɛwoɔ la ni mli edɔ waa mli loo akɛto he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ jogbaŋŋ Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela nɛɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛjɛ tuber kome mli kɛya ekroko mli oya.

english: What steps can I take to change my small family farm into a profitable commercial farming business?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni matsake miweku ŋmɔ bibioo lɛ? mi lɛ kɛtee jarayeli ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ ko ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he.

english: To grow into a commercial farm, you need to adopt improved crop varieties, keep farm financial records, practice proper post-harvest handling, and build direct links with larger commercial market buyers.
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ ni oda ni ofee jarayeli ŋmɔ Ehe baahia ni okɛ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ atsu nii. Kɛ ŋmɔ mli shika he saji ato. Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ni sa. ni ekɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jarayeli hei wuji lɛ afee tsakpaa tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive strong, direct sunlight and dry winds. They need shade crops like plantain or taller trees to protect them while their roots and leaves are young and fragile.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo tsei kakadaji kɛha hebuu yɛ be mli ni shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ ji gbekɛbii ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for growth. Applying nitrogen fertilizer early prevents this and stops you from losing your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Ebaatsi enɛ naa ni ebaatsi bo gbɛ koni okafite onitsumɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into tight shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the sap from under the leaves. Spraying or controlling these insects early keeps the plant healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nibii nɛɛ ni akɛshwieɔ loo akudɔɔ amɛ mra lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhe wa

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when the rains become heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped around them in heavy soil without draining away. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain off easily so roots can breathe.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu tsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ mlɛo bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds too deep in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ?

english: If seeds are buried too deep, they waste all their stored energy trying to push through the heavy dirt to find sunlight, causing them to sprout very weak or die under the soil.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwu lɛ mli tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ amɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛto lɛ beni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ he lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ waa loo amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: If I clear weeds late, why does my crop suffer even after the weeds are gone?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa amanehulu eyɛ mli akɛ jwɛi lɛ etee moŋ?

english: Weeds steal fertilizer and water from crops during their early growth stages. Delaying weeding causes permanent damage because crops miss the crucial feeding window, making late efforts far less effective.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa mra lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ kɛ fitemɔ baa daa ejaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ foɔ niyenii be ni he hiaa lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, mɔdɛŋbɔɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kwraa.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu sweet potato wain tsei kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines on poles allows the leaves to catch maximum sunlight and keeps them away from damp ground where diseases live, leading to larger and healthier tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yibii lɛ náa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni etsiɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai yɔɔ lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ feɔ agbo ni eyɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I trim off extra side shoots from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Trimming extra shoots prevents the plant from wasting energy on useless leaves and directs all water and food straight into growing larger, healthier tomato fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, no haaa efite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ. ni okɛ nu kɛ niyenii fɛɛ aya tomatoi wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with very few fruits when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete against each other for sunlight and air. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough sunlight and nutrients to grow strong stems and produce plenty of fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa ni ekɛ ŋmaa babaoo baa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the stem without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when tiny insects attack the flowers before the fruit can start forming.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tutuaa fɔfɔii dani aduawai jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when there are no bigger trees planted around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigboi yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate strong, direct sunlight in their early years. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby creates a protective canopy that keeps the soil cool and shields the young leaves from heat damage.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ebuɔ baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the plants the strength they need to turn green and grow fast.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara oya.

english: Why do my crop leaves scorch and dry up if I place chemical fertilizer right next to the plant stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ wo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers contain strong salts that draw moisture out of the plant stem and roots when in direct contact. Fertilizer should always be applied in a small ring or line a few inches away from the stem so the roots can absorb it safely.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli kɛji akɛ amɛkpe tɛ̃ɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ ŋmeii bibii amli. Aloo be fɛɛ be lɛ, ekɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi 2-3 bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do I get smaller yields when I plant my seeds very close together to fit more on my plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ yibii fioo nɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni amɛhi miŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves compete fiercely for limited soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Giving each plant proper space allows it to grow strong and produce larger fruits or grains.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tse lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, nu kɛ hulu la ni faaa lɛ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni eda ni ewo aduawai loo dumɔwui wuji.

english: How do weeds growing around my crops reduce the size of my harvest?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aye abua ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that quickly steal water, soil nutrients, and sunlight intended for your crops. Removing weeds early prevents them from starving your main crop during its most critical growth stage.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ basabasa ni juɔ nu. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ kɛha onibii oya Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye otsei titrii lɛ hɔmɔ yɛ amɛdalɛ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or pest attacks. Maintaining steady soil moisture and protecting plants from pests helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ tsei ahebuu kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.
