english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is often caused by soil-borne fungal or bacterial diseases that block the plant's internal water tubes. Rotating crops and avoiding overly soggy soil helps keep these diseases from attacking the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ sũ mli ni tsiɔ tso lɛ mli nu paipii lɛ anaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli efɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai nɛɛ akatutua shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why is it risky to plant my maize immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ ji oshara lɛ?

english: The season's first rain is often followed by a dry spell before the main rains settle in. If seeds sprout during that early brief wet period, the young seedlings will wither and die when the dry heat returns.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔi wuji lɛ baa. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ mra yɛ be kukuoo mli ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi beni hulutsoo ni egbi lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when the rainy season lasts unusually long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ?

english: Excess rain fills air spaces in the soil with water, effectively suffocating the roots. Without oxygen, soil fungi and bacteria quickly attack the weakened cassava tubers, causing them to rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa nu yiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii ni egbɔjɔ lɛ oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why does planting maize on the exact same piece of land every year result in a smaller harvest each time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ haa yibiiwoo fioo baa be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop relies on and allows specialized pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas restores soil nutrients naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai pɔtɛɛ komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellowing leaves on young cocoa often mean the plants are getting too much direct sunlight or lack moisture. Young cocoa trees need shade from fast-growing plants like plantains to protect them while their root systems develop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ kookoo bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hulu la miishɛ tso lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ tsɔ loo nu bɛ mli. Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in high humidity and damp conditions. You can reduce it by pruning dense branches to let air flow through and quickly removing infected pods from the field.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ kɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. Obaanyɛ oha enɛ aba shi kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni oookpa koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooojie oya kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it normal for my cocoa tree to shed its leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, cocoa trees drop their older leaves during dry spells to save water and protect themselves. As long as the branches remain flexible and green inside, new leaves will grow back once the rains start.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai momo lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe. Shii abɔ ni tsei lɛ aniji lɛ baahi shi ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ mli lɛ. Baai heei baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ bɔi nɛmɔ.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are fully matured and ready to dig up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ edara kwraa ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil base around the stem begins to swell and crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ bɔi shwiemɔ ni egbɛ eshwa.

english: Why are small white insects gathering under my cassava leaves and turning them twisty?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yɛŋ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ mi-cassava baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: These are whiteflies, which suck sap from the leaves and can spread mosaic virus. Planting resistant cassava varieties provided by agricultural officers is the best way to prevent damage.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii yɛŋ, ni nuɔ baa mli nu lɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ mosaic hela lɛ amɛshwã. Cassava henɔi ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ nibii ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi etsɔɔ mli lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ nibii ni efiteɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Staking exposes yam leaves to sunlight so the plant can make food to build big tubers underground, while keeping the foliage away from damp soil diseases.
ga: Staking haa hulu la shɛɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ afee niyenii ni ekɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ helai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: Why does my maize grow tall stalks but fail to produce big ears of corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmeii kakadaji shi ebɛ toi wuji lɛ?

english: Maize needs nutrients like nitrogen early in its growth to build healthy ears. Tall stems without good corn ears mean the soil lacks nutrients or plants were sown too close together, forcing them to compete for food.
ga: Niyenii nibii tamɔ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa mra yɛ edalɛ mli koni ekɛfee toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Tsoi ni kɛlɛ ni ŋmãa toi kpakpai bɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo adu tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. ni nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛwu amɛha niyenii

english: This is likely the Fall Armyworm, a common pest in Ghana that targets the growing center of maize plants. Catching them early and applying approved pest treatments saves the crop before severe damage occurs.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛ ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni ekɛ ehiɛ fɔ̃ɔ hei ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ anɔ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni ahere ŋmɔshi nibii ayiwala dani nɔ ko ni mli wa aba.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop to the ground without making peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni efiteee pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers fall off when the weather is too hot, soil gets too dry, or there is too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping soil moisture consistent with mulch helps the plant hold its flowers and set fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. aloo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛ mulch tsuɔ nii be fɛɛ be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: What causes my plantain leaves to get dark brown spots and dry up from the edges?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi plantain baai lɛ anɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi ni egbi?

english: This is Black Sigatoka, a leaf leaf-spot disease that lowers plant strength. Cutting off badly infected leaves and keeping weeds down helps air circulate and slows the spread.
ga: Enɛ ji Black Sigatoka, ni ji hela ko ni haa tsei ahewalɛ baa shi. Kɛ́ afo baai ni hela emɔ amɛ waa lɛ amli ni ajie jwɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli ni ebaaha hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã oya.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate harsh, direct sunlight because their young leaves burn easily and lose water quickly. Tall trees act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and cool air young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ebaai bibii lɛ shãa oya, ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I cut off some of the small plantain suckers growing around the main stalk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ plantain tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ tso titri lɛ he lɛ.

english: When too many suckers grow around one stem, they all compete for the same food and water in the soil, resulting in small plantain bunches. Pruning extra suckers allows the parent plant to direct all its energy into growing large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso kome he lɛ, amɛ fɛɛ amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ nu kome ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji plantains bibii bibii. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa tsei wuji ni tsii ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential soil food needed for green growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help the crop regain its rich green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye ŋmãa tso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛsu ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do worms attack the very center funnel of my maize plants instead of the outer leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋgbɛ gbɛi lɛ moŋ fe kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm target the middle funnel because the tissue inside is soft, moist, and tender to eat. Applying approved treatments directly into the funnel kills the pests where they feed.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ kwɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ fã ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ni eyɛ mlɛo akɛ ayeɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ wo tsɔne lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi ni yɔɔ he ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when heavy rains stay for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air inside the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits in the ground without draining away, it chokes the roots, causing them to drown and rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ejɛɛɛ mli. baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ Nu mli gbee kɛ fitemɔ

english: Yam leaves produce food for the underground tuber by catching sunlight. Lifting the vines on stakes exposes more leaves to the sun and keeps them off the damp ground where diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ niyenii kɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ kɛtsɔ hulu la ni shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ awó wein tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, hulu la babaoo shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe, ni ehaaa efee hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop to the ground instead of turning into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or insect attack. Keeping the soil consistently moist and controlling pests prevents the flowers from falling.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi ni shwieɔ amɛ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ haa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: This issue, known as blossom-end rot, happens when tomato plants do not get enough calcium or when watering is irregular. Consistent watering helps the plant absorb calcium smoothly from the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji akɛ tomato tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ loo kɛji akɛ afɔɔ amɛ nu be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekɛ calcium ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my farm make the soil better for next season's crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have natural nodules on their roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, leaving rich nutrients behind for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ adebɔɔ mli shishifãi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass keep them alive during short dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching around lɛ mikɛ jwɛi duɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni eye ebua ni tsei lɛ ahi shi yɛ hulutsoo be kuku lɛ mli.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) acts like a blanket that blocks direct sunlight, keeping the soil cool and preventing moisture from evaporating into the air.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ atade ni tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ, ni ehaaa nu ni hoɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ aya.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. They need protection from shade trees or quick-growing crops like plantains to shelter their delicate leaves while they establish strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Ehe miihia ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ ahe koni abu amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers growing small and hard instead of big and soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ daa bibii ni amɛhe wa yɛ agbo ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots cannot expand properly if the soil is packed too tightly or if they lack sufficient moisture during their early growth stage. Soil needs to be loose and well-tilled for tubers to swell fully.
ga: Cassava shishifãi nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã jogbaŋŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli yɛ shishijee be mli ni edara lɛ. Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni atsu he nii jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni bulb lɛ agbɛ ashwã kwraa.

english: Yam plants make food for their underground tubers through their leaves. Staking lifts the vine off the wet ground so leaves catch maximum sunlight and stay clean from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ feɔ niyenii kɛhaa eshikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ kɛtsɔɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. koni baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ ni eha ehe atse kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves and small caterpillars hiding inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji ŋmeii lɛ? Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ yɛ bu ni akɛtee mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest that eats young maize leaves from the inside out. Spotting them early and applying targeted organic or chemical treatments protects your harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Ni oookwɛ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off before they can grow into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛdara ni amɛbatsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they get too stressed by intense heat, uneven watering, or a lack of soil nutrients like phosphorus, which the plant needs to form fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hao amɛ tsɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ fɔsfɔs, ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo yibii lɛ.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, often due to irregular watering during dry weather.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why do my crops look pale green and weak even after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe waaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall can wash key soil nutrients, especially nitrogen, deep down beyond the reach of short crop roots. Adding compost or fertilizer helps replace these lost nutrients.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Yaa mli shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni tso shishifãi kukuji baanyɛ ashɛ he Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akɛ niyenii ni elaaje nɛɛ ato najiaŋ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crowded plants compete against each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients, resulting in thin stems and very small cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛ tsei bibii bibii waa.

english: Why do weeds sprout back so fast after I clear my plot during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛkɛ beni ajie ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie dormant in the soil surface and germinate immediately when exposed to rain and direct sunlight. Covering the clear soil with dry crop residue or mulching blocks sunlight and slows weed growth.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ jɔɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ kɛ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ ni mli tse nɔ kɛ tsei ni egbi loo mulch koni etsĩ hulu la naa ni eha jwɛi lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my stored dry maize grains turn to white powder after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ batsɔ ŋmãa yɛŋ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tiny insects called grain weevils lay eggs inside stored maize. Drying your maize thoroughly until it is completely hard before sealing it in airtight storage bags prevents weevils from surviving.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ seed moths lɛ fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa lɛ kɛyashi ebaawa kwraa dani okɛwo vacuum kotoku mli lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkajo foi.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is essential food in the soil. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or Urea when the soil is moist will help them regain their green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo urea wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eku esɛɛ eba eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply dry chemical fertilizer to my crops when the soil is completely dry and dusty?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa ni sũ ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Crops cannot absorb dry fertilizer directly; they drink their nutrients dissolved in water through their roots. Putting fertilizer on bone-dry soil can burn and damage the roots, so it is best applied right after a rain when the ground is wet.
ga: Tsei nyɛŋ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛnuɔ niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nu mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wu yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite shishifãi lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ enɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ.

english: Why are my maize plant leaves suddenly filled with small ragged holes and dark powder inside the central whorl?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ahe baai eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? No ji nɔ ni ekumɔ ni powda ni tsuɔ diŋ yɛ teŋgbɛ kooyigbɛ lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds on the growing center of the plant. Applying recommended pest controls early in the morning or late evening when the worms are active will save the plant before it dies.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli he ni edaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni kooloi lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ahere tso lɛ yiwala dani egbo.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up right on the tree branches before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Black pods are caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in dark, humid, and overgrown farms. Pruning extra shade trees to let in sunlight and spraying approved fungicides protects your cocoa pods from rotting.
ga: Black pods hela ji nɔ ni kɛ pods diji baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli ewo duŋ, ni edɔ, ni ŋmɔji ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ofolɔ hulutsoo be kroko mli koni hulu la aba mli ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ afɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu o-cocoa ŋmeii lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tight and turning small and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ bibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Wrinkled and curled leaves on pepper plants are caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that spread leaf-curl viruses. Controlling these insects early using neem oil or soapy water sprays stops the leaves from curling.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ hela ko ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni egbɔjɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Neem fɔ loo nu ni akɛ samla shwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that cannot tolerate harsh direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides a cool canopy that protects the seedlings during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu hulutsoo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when heavy rains fall continuously for weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ ni naa wa yaa nɔ otsii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe, but waterlogged soil suffocates them, creating a perfect environment for fungal rot. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Shi shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ baa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping all their blossoms before any fruit starts to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɛɛ woɔ fɔfɔi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme afternoon heat or erratic watering. Keeping the soil moisture consistent with mulching helps the plant hold onto its flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛna haomɔ ni jɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ ni ejaaa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ mulching ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli koni ewo yibii.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during light storms before the fruit bunch fully matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum be mli dani aduawai akui lɛ daraa kwraa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and often weakened by underground pests called nematodes or banana weevils. Planting healthy, pest-free suckers and mounting rich soil tightly around the base gives the stems stronger support against high winds.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo banana ŋmeii lɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli lɛ, ni akɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni akɛwo shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛdamɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow short, crooked, and branched instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ kukuji, amɛhe ejɔ, ni amɛyɛ niji moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers twist and branch out when the soil underneath is hard, compact, or stony, preventing smooth downward growth. Digging deep, soft mounds or ridges frees the soil so the tubers can grow long and straight.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛjeɔ niji kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo tɛi yɔɔ mli, ni no haaa amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishigbɛ. Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni atsa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ehe bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ adara ni amɛfee tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, an essential plant food. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps the leaves turn deep green so they can feed the plant and form large corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ koni ekɛha tso lɛ niyenii ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii agboi aba.

english: Why does my maize grow much bigger when I plant it on land where I harvested cowpeas or beans last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa waa kɛ́ midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa tsina loo ŋmãa yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans naturally pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you plant maize there afterwards, the maize feeds on that leftover soil food.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Beni oduɔ ŋmãa yɛ jɛmɛ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ baaye niyenii ni eshwɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Yam plants make their food through leaves catching sunlight. Lifting the vines up on wooden stakes spreads the leaves out to capture maximum sun, which sends energy down into the ground to make larger yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ feɔ eniyenii kɛtsɔɔ baai ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ owó wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ebaagbɛ ebaa lɛ eshwa koni ená hulu la ni fa babaoo. Enɛ haa hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the ground when heavy rains flood my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eyi miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in the ground for too long without draining, the roots suffocate and rot. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds allows excess water to drain off easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ baafo ni amɛbaagboi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why do my seeds rot in the soil if I plant them right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a hot dry spell that bakes the dirt. If seeds get wet once and then stay dry in hot soil, they die and rot. It is safer to wait until rains become steady before sowing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shãa lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ edɔ shikome lɛ no lɛ ha amɛgbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ baagboi ni amɛbaagboi. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ aba shi dani odu dumɔwui.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and drop off without turning into small tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato bibii lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their blossoms when exposed to extreme afternoon heat or dry spells. Providing adequate water during dry periods cools the crop so the flowers can complete pollination and grow into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli loo shwane shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ha yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee fɛ̃i. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking sap from the undersides of leaves. Washing the leaves or using targeted organic sprays like neem oil stops the insects from stunting leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ ofɔ baai lɛ ahe loo okɛ tsofa ko ni akɛwoɔ mɔ he, tamɔ neem fɔ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi bibii lɛ akaha baai lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my fruiting plantain trees fall over so easily whenever a strong wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that struggle to support heavy fruit bunches. Placing sturdy wooden or bamboo support poles beneath the fruiting stem prevents the weight of the bunch from pulling the tree down.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso loo ŋmei tso ni wa ni fiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ kuu lɛ muji lɛ naa koni ekagbala tso lɛ kɛba shi.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and choke my crops when I leave wide gaps between my plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni efiteɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mishiɔ gbɛ ni da yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Leaving wide gaps allows direct sunlight to reach empty dirt, giving weed seeds ideal light to sprout quickly. Spacing crops at recommended distances allows their leaves to form a natural roof that shades out weeds.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi gbɛ ni mli kwɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shɛɔ muji ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ he. Ha jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ la ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei lɛ to he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni tsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my crops get black spots and rot even when it has not rained for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji kɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ? Ni nugbɔ enɛko be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Even without rain, high humidity creates damp air that deposits invisible moisture on leaves. Fungi and bacteria thrive in this moisture, causing rots and leaf spots to develop on your crops.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ po lɛ, hulutsoo ni fa babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni haa hulutsoo ni anaaa lɛ baa baai lɛ anɔ. Mold kɛ bacteria shwereɔ yɛ nɛkɛ hulutsoo be nɛɛ mli. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ baai ŋmɔtɔ baa onibii anɔ.

english: What does humidity mean, and how can it harm the crops on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji hulutsoo shishi? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ awui?

english: Humidity is the amount of water vapor or dampness trapped in the air. When the air stays heavy and wet, crop leaves remain damp longer, creating the ideal conditions for plant sicknesses to attack.
ga: Humidity ji nu mli lasu loo ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ falɛ. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli wa lolo ni edɔ Tso lɛ baai lɛ baakã he afee ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsei ahe helai shishijee.

english: Why do my crop leaves stay wet in the morning even when there was no rain overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ mli efɔ lolo leebi lɛ? Ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ nyɔɔŋ kome mli?

english: When humidity is high, moisture in the warm air cools down overnight and settles on leaves as dew. If this dampness stays on the plants without drying quickly, it opens the door for diseases.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ fa lɛ hulutsoo ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli jɔɔ nyɔɔŋ kome ni efeɔ baai lɛ anɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ hi tso lɛ nɔ ni ehaaa egbi oya. Ebaagbele shinaa kɛha helai.

english: What simple steps can I take to protect my farm during periods when the air is very damp?
ga: Ma nyɛ ma nyɛɛ blɔ nya tomi komɛ a nɔ. Mɛni yɔɔ ni baabu miŋmɔ lɛ he yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: You can space your plants properly and trim overgrown branches so that air flows freely through your farm. Good airflow dries damp leaves quickly, making it harder for disease to build up.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ otsei lɛ ato he jogbaŋŋ ni ofolɔ tsei niji ni eda fe nine lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli oya. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ baaha baai ni efɔ lɛ agbi oya. Ehaa ewaa waa akɛ helai baabua amɛhe naa

english: How does hot sunshine help keep my crops healthy from sickness?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ hela mli?

english: Bright sunshine heats up the farm and rapidly evaporates water drops and damp air off crop leaves. Keeping the leaves dry prevents disease spores from germinating and spreading.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli dɔɔ. ni ekɛ nu mli nu ni hoɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ shwieɔ shi oya Baai lɛ ni agbiɔ lɛ haaa helai amli tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do plant sicknesses spread so fast on days when the sun does not shine at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ gbii ni hulu lɛ shɛɛɛ kwraa lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: On cloudy or overcast days without strong sun, moisture stays trapped in the air and on plant leaves for many hours. This continuous damp environment allows mold and sickness to multiply rapidly.
ga: Yɛ gbii ni atatu loo atatu ewo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa bɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli kɛ tsei ahe baai anɔ ŋmɛlɛtswai babaoo. Nɛkɛ shihilɛ ni mli efɔ be fɛɛ be nɛɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Is it safe for me to plant my vegetables directly under big shade trees like a mango tree?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu aduawai yɛ tso agbo ko ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ mango tso shishi?

english: Big trees like mango trees create dark, cool shade that traps damp air and stops sunlight from drying your crops. Crops planted under them stay wet longer and easily catch fungal diseases.
ga: Tsei wuji tamɔ mango tsei lɛ feɔ hulutsoo ni mli ewo duŋ. Ehiɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ mli ni ehaaa hulu lɛ agbi oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Tsei ni adu yɛ amɛshishi lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ, ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ yeɔ amɛ oya.

english: Why do the leaves and flowers on my mango trees turn black during humid weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei ahe baai kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High humidity creates damp conditions under the tree canopy that favor fungal diseases like anthracnose. This mold attacks mango leaves and flowers even if no rain has fallen.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo lɛ haa fɛ̃i baa tsei lɛ ashishi, ni no haa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ anthracnose baa. Nɛkɛ ŋmei nɛɛ tutuaa mango baai kɛ fɔfɔi kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ po.

english: Why should I prune the heavy branches of shade trees growing near my crop field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ masɛi lɛ aniji ni tsii lɛ?

english: Pruning heavy branches lets sunshine filter through and improves wind movement. This helps clear away damp air trapped beneath the trees, keeping nearby crops dry and healthy.
ga: Niji ni tsii ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la tsɔɔ mli ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ajie kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni emɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Ha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does planting my crops too close together lead to leaf sickness on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ sɛɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ hela baa ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Crowded crops block wind from blowing through the field. This traps humid, damp air between the plants, making it easy for diseases to form and move quickly from one plant to the next.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni eyi obɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekafo ŋmɔji lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ lɛ amɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ helai baaje shishi ni amɛya oya kɛjɛ tso kome mli kɛya tso kroko mli.

english: Why does my cassava plant grow big bushy leaves but leaves me with very tiny tubers at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai wuji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛji akpa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen and lacks potassium, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing thick leaves above ground instead of feeding and swelling the roots below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium bɛ mli lɛ Yucca tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛha ebaa ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, moŋ fe ni eeeha shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ niyenii ni amɛfuu.

english: Why do my harvested yams start producing green shoots while sitting in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃mɔ be mli ni mita ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams naturally enter a brief resting period after harvest, but warm temperatures and air moisture trigger the tuber to wake up and start growing a new plant using the food stored inside itself.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potatoes yaa hejɔɔmɔ be kuku mli. kpamɔ sɛɛ Shi hulutsoo be kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ ateshi ni amɛje tsei heei akwɛmɔ shishi kɛtsɔ niyenii ni ato yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers fall off without ever turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers fall off if tiny insects called midges are not present to pollinate them, or if the cocoa tree suffers from water stress and too much direct sunlight.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii bɛ jɛmɛ. Atsɛɔ lɛ midge koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ nu he haomɔ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo lɛ miipiŋ kookoo tso lɛ he.

english: Plantain roots are shallow and spread near the surface. If tiny worms called nematodes damage the root system or if the soil gets too waterlogged, the tree loses its anchor and topples under its heavy bunch.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã nu lɛ hiɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ fite shishifãi lɛ loo kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Tso lɛ laajeɔ eŋmei lɛ ni egbee shi yɛ etsei ni tsii lɛ ashishi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow from the tip inwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa yitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are a sign of nitrogen hunger. The plant moves nitrogen from its older leaves to support new growth, showing that the soil needs organic matter or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji nitrogen hɔmɔ he okadi. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni eye ebua dalɛ hee. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my cowpea plants lose their buds before producing any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ miifite ŋmeii dani ewoɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Tiny insects called flower thrips attack and feed on tender cowpea flower buds before they can open into flowers, causing them to drop off prematurely.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ flower thrips lɛ tutuaa ni amɛyeɔ tsina ŋmeii dani amɛfeɔ fɔfɔii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgbeeɔ shi oya.

english: Why do my maize crops yield better when I plant groundnuts or beans in the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ fe be mli ni miduɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans gather nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots, naturally fertilizing the neighboring maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Buaa nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ naa ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning dark black and soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato eŋɔli lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni eyɛ blɛoo lɛ?

english: This condition is blossom-end rot, caused when the tomato plant cannot absorb enough calcium from the soil, usually due to dry spells or irregular watering.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ji fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ loo nu ni afɔɔɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Leaf curling in pepper is commonly caused by microscopic pests like thrips or whiteflies sucking plant sap, or by hot weather causing leaves to fold to protect themselves from water loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Aloo kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Why does my farm soil turn hard as rock and crack wide open when the sun gets hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa tamɔ tɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ mli egbɛ eshwa kɛji hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ enɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy clay soil loses its water quickly under heat, causing it to shrink and harden. Adding animal manure or dry plant mulch softens the soil structure and helps retain moisture.
ga: Shikpɔji ni mli wa ni shikpɔŋ sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ nu fiteɔ oya yɛ dɔlɛ shishi. ni haa egbɔjɔɔ ni ewaa Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee blɛoo ni eye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli.

english: Why does my chemical fertilizer stop working or ruin my soil if heavy rain washes over it right after I apply it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ekpaa nitsumɔ loo efiteɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa nɛ yɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛwo mli lɛ?

english: When fertilizer gets flooded by heavy rain before it dissolves into the soil properly, the nutrients wash away into nearby streams or get locked deep underground where crop roots cannot reach, resulting in wasted money and lost plant food.
ga: Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tswaa ŋmɔshi nibii dani enyɛɔ efoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shwieɔ faai ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli loo akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shika ni afiteɔ kɛ tsei aniyenii ni afiteɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when water collects and stays on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu bua amɛhe naa ni ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits on the field for too long, it drowns the roots, allowing harmful fungi to attack and cause rotting before harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Ha ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atutua ni amɛgboi dani akpa.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn black and moldy if I pack it into bags while it is still damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛji mikɛwo kotoku mli be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Grains trap moisture when bagged damp. This trapped wetness creates heat and creates the perfect environment for mold and fungi to grow, which ruins the grain and makes it unsafe to eat or sell.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nu kɛji akɛ awo kotokui ni mli ewo nu mli. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ mli nɛɛ haa dɔlɛ baa ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔtɔ baakwɛ̃. Enɛ baafite dumɔwui lɛ ni eha efee nɔ ni esaaa akɛ ayeɔ loo ahɔ̃ɔɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and die when there are no plantains or big trees planted near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui loo tsei wuji bɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive to strong direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing trees like plantains nearby provides crucial shade that shields the delicate cocoa leaves from burning until the crop matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ebaaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni baabu kookoo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he kɛyashi tso lɛ baadara.

english: Rolling up leaves is the maize plant's natural defense mechanism to conserve water. By reducing the leaf surface area exposed to the hot sun, the plant slows down water loss during dry hours.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni abele tsei yɔɔ koni amɛbu nu he. Kɛtsɔ baai ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ anɔ lɛ ni abaajie lɛ shi lɛ nɔ. Tsei haa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Why shouldn't I sow my maize seeds immediately after the very first rain of the major season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: The first rain after a long dry spell can trick seeds into germinating, but if a dry week follows, the fragile young sprouts will dry up and die due to lack of subsoil moisture.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui akwɛ̃. Shi kɛji akɛ otsi ni nu bɛ lɛ nyiɛ sɛɛ hu? Tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my yam plants need tall wooden stakes to climb on instead of just growing on the soil surface?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up toward the sunlight and exposes them to better air circulation, which prevents leaf diseases and allows the plant to produce much bigger tubers underground.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baa lɛ nɔ koni ená hulu la ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa, ni ehaa tso lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni dara babaoo.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas alongside my main crop like cassava or maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ madu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ahe lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which naturally take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, feeding your main crop and improving soil fertility without extra fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii. ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa Koni ekɛ niyenii aha oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he.

english: Why do weeds always sprout and grow much faster than my crop seeds after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe midumɔwui lɛ be fɛɛ be beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are wild, hardy, and already well-adapted to the local soil. They are designed to absorb rain immediately and compete aggressively for sunlight and nutrients before cultivated crops can establish themselves.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui ji adebɔɔ mli nibii, amɛhe wa, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔji lɛ anɔ. Afee amɛ koni amɛŋɔ nugbɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛye akaŋ waa koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii kpakpai dani tsei ni miida lɛ anyɛ ama amɛhe shi.

english: Why do Fall Armyworm caterpillars attack the hidden center funnel of my young maize plants instead of eating the outside leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaaye kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ?

english: The center funnel contains soft, tender young leaf tissue that is easy for young caterpillars to feed on and offers a dark, moist hiding spot safe from the hot sun and predators.
ga: Baai bibii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ŋmeii bibii yeɔ amɛ mlɛo lɛ yɛ funnel lɛ teŋgbɛ. Ni hei ni yɔɔ duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ nyɛŋ amɛhi shi yɛ jɛmɛ yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why does my farmland dry up and turn hard like a savannah when I cut down all the big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi ni ewa tamɔ savannah beni mifo tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: When trees are cut down, there is no leaf canopy left to shade the ground from the hot sun. Without tree roots to hold water in the soil, the land loses moisture quickly, washes away during heavy rain, and hardens into open dry land.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ ashwie shi lɛ, nɔ ko eshwɛɛɛ ni baabu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Kɛji tsei shishifãi ni akɛ nu baato shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ fiteɔ oya. shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa mli ni ehaa ehe waɔ kɛyaa hei ni egbi ni agbele naa.

english: Is it bad for my soil if I completely clear and burn all trees on my land before planting?
ga: Ani ebaaná shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ gbonyo kɛji mijie tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni mishã amɛ dani midu?

english: Yes, complete clearing and burning destroys the nutrient-rich topsoil, kills helpful earthworms and soil insects, and leaves the bare land exposed to hot sun and heavy winds, which dries out the soil very fast.
ga: Hɛɛ, sũ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli kwraa kɛ shãa lɛ fiteɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni niyenii mli hewalɛ eyi mli obɔ lɛ. Egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. ni oshi he ni nɔ ko bɛ lɛ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ ashɛ he Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya waa.

english: What can I do to fix a piece of land that has become bare, dry, and poor for farming?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mikɛsaa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ, ni egbi, ni ehiii lɛ koni matsu nii yɛ nɔ?

english: Planting fast-growing trees and cover crops helps restore bare land. Trees protect the soil from direct sunlight, their roots retain underground water, and their falling leaves decay to rebuild fertile topsoil over time.
ga: Tsei ni daa oya kɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ ni nɔ efee efolo lɛ baa ekoŋŋ. Tsei buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Amɛshishifãi lɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu. Ni baai ni egbee shi lɛ fiteɔ koni ekɛfee shikpɔŋ hee ni woɔ yibii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why are farmers planting teak trees on land where trees were previously cut down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ teak tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni afo tsei yɛ nɔ tsutsu lɛ?

english: Teak trees grow strong and fast, making them great for bringing forest shade back to bare land. They also act as a long-term financial investment because their timber becomes very valuable as they mature over several years.
ga: Teak tsei daa oya ni amɛhe wa. Ekɛ koo mli ŋmɔlɔ baa hei ni nɔ ko bɛ lɛ ekoŋŋ. Amɛtsuɔ nii hu akɛ shika ni akɛwoɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛtsei lɛ jara wa waa beni amɛdaraa yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ.

english: How long does a newly planted mango seedling take before it starts producing fruits?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani mango dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Grafted mango trees usually start bearing fruit within 3 to 4 years, whereas mango trees planted directly from seeds take much longer—around 7 to 10 years—to yield their first harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mango tsei ni akɛwo mli lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni mango tsei ni akwɛɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ heɔ be babaoo, aaafee afii 7 kɛyashi 10, dani amɛwoɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young, newly planted mango tree drying up and turning brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango baai ni midu ehee lɛ mli egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Young mango trees have delicate roots and suffer easily from intense heat. Brown, dry leaves usually mean the young tree is not getting enough water or needs temporary shade to protect it while it settles into the soil.
ga: Mango tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi yɛ mlɛo ni amɛŋmɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he gbɛ oya. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso bibioo lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo ehe miihia ni ená hulutsoo be kukuoo ko koni ebu tso lɛ he be mli ni ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why should I spend time planting non-edible timber trees like teak when I need food crops right now?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ be kɛdu tsei ni ayeee tamɔ teak lɛ? Akɛni niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia mi bianɛ hewɔ lɛ?

english: Timber trees like teak serve as a long-term bank account for farmers. While food crops provide immediate food every season, timber trees protect your land from harsh weather and provide a large income payout when harvested years later.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ tsei amli tamɔ teak tsuɔ nii akɛ shikatoohe akaunti ni heɔ be kakadaŋŋ kɛhaa okwaafoi. Eyɛ mli akɛ niyenii tsei haa niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ daa afi moŋ, shi tsei ni akɛ tsei fee lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai ahe. ni ekɛ shika babaoo baa kɛji akpa yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli

english: Will planting shade trees on my farm help my food crops survive the dry season better?
ga: Ani tsei ni haa hulutsoo be ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua mi niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ koni ehi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, shade trees lower the ground temperature and stop water from evaporating out of the dirt quickly. Their shade keeps the surrounding air moist, which helps nearby crops stay green longer into the dry season.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shade yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli.

english: Can I grow food crops like maize or vegetables on the same plot with young teak trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ teak tso bibioo ko?

english: Yes, when teak trees are young and small, food crops can easily grow between them. However, after 2 to 3 years, the teak leaves will grow large and shade out the ground, so food crops will need to be moved to open land.
ga: Hɛɛ, beni teak tso lɛ ji gbekɛ ni eji bibioo lɛ. Niyenii tsei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ teak tsei lɛ ateŋ mlɛo. Shi, yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 sɛɛ lɛ, teak tsei lɛ baatsɔ agbo ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ajie niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛya he ko ni gbɛ yɔɔ.

english: If I plant big trees near my crops, won't their roots steal all the water from my crops?
ga: Kɛ midu tso agbo ko yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe Ani eshishifãi lɛ ejuŋ nu kɛjɛŋ miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Tree roots go much deeper into the soil than crop roots, pulling water up from deep underground without competing with your crops. As long as trees are spaced properly, their deep roots and top shade actually help keep moisture in the ground for your crops.
ga: Tso shishifãi boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ kwraa fe tsei shishifãi. Egbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ kɛyaa ŋwɛi ni ekɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeee akaŋ. Shii abɔ ni tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa. Shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ hulutsoo baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are some maize plants in the same section of my field growing tall while others nearby stay small and yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei komɛi shwereɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ? yɛ be mli ni tsei krokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ji bibioo ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Crops require uniform access to soil nutrients and moisture. Variations in soil depth, uneven fertilizer application, or root competition from nearby weeds cause some plants to thrive while others become stunted.
ga: Ehe miihia ni tsei lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ ni tsakeɔ Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni ejaaa loo akaŋshii ni akɛtaoɔ shishifãi ni jɛ jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli Enɛ haa tsei komɛi shwereɔ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my crops produce less yield every harvest season even though I use the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo yɛ kpamɔ be fɛɛ kpamɔ be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ lɛ?

english: Soil loses nutrients over time when the same crop is planted repeatedly without rest or soil enrichment. Rotating crops or adding organic manure restores the soil balance so crops can feed properly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ laajeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ. ni hejɔɔmɔ bɛ mli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ jara ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ekome ekoŋŋ koni tsei lɛ anyɛ aye nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and droop during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in high heat is a natural survival response. The plant reduces its leaf surface area to save water from evaporating, helping it survive until temperatures cool down in the late afternoon.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yibiiwoo hetoo. Tsei haa amɛbaai lɛ anɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ baa shi koni nu akatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ shwane mli.

english: If I plant my cassava stems very close together, will I get more yield from my land?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he waa Ani yibiiwoo lɛ baaya hiɛ?

english: Planting too closely causes crops to fight over sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing allows each plant enough root space and light to develop large, healthy tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ hulu la lɛ abɔ mɔdɛŋ waa. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa shishifãi kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛ bulbs agboi ni mli wa aba.

english: How do weeds actually prevent my crops from growing well if there is enough rainfall for all plants?
ga: Te jwɛi baafee tɛŋŋ atsĩ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa kɛha tsei fɛɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive competitors. Even with plenty of water, weed roots spread faster to absorb nutrients, and tall weeds block essential sunlight that your crops need to make their food.
ga: Jwɛi ji akaŋshilɔi ni yɔɔ basabasa. Kɛ nu babaoo po yɛ Jwɛi shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya koni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Ni jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni he hiaa ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ niyenii lɛ naa.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas next to my maize makes the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ Ani mi ŋmãa lɛ haa mi ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have tiny root organisms that capture nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil. This natural fertilizer feeds neighboring crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli. Emɔɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ haa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ tamɔ ŋmãa niyenii.

english: Why do my tomato plants turn yellow and decay when water collects around their roots after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air just like humans do. Waterlogged soil smothers root systems, cutting off oxygen and preventing roots from absorbing nutrients, which causes leaf yellowing and rot.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi hu he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. ni etsĩɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ.

english: Why are flowers dropping off my okra plants before turning into okra pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ okra tsei anɔ dani amɛfeɔ okra ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flower drop occurs when crops experience environmental stress, such as sudden hot spells, irregular watering, or a lack of flowering nutrients like phosphorus.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na shihilɛ mli haomɔi, tamɔ hulutsoo ni fe nine trukaa. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa fɔfɔi baa, tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ

english: Why do pests attack the soft young leaves of my crops instead of the older leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai miitutua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ moŋ fe baai momo lɛ?

english: Young leaves are tender, easy to chew, and rich in plant sugars and water, making them the most nutritious and easy target for insects.
ga: Baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe waaa ni amɛmli tsei amli sugar kɛ nu babaoo. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ ateŋ ekomɛi, ni ewaaa akɛ abaanyɛ atswa amɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams spoil quickly when stored in a warm closed room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ akɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni aŋã mli lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that continue to breathe after harvest. High temperatures and lack of airflow cause them to sweat, creating dampness that invites fungi and bacteria to cause rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. He ni mli edɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni fɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ nine baa, ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Which type of coconut tree should I plant if I want to sell fresh coconut water versus making coconut oil?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmei srɔtoi osumɔɔ ni okwɛ ni okɛ ŋmei nu hee ahɔ̃ɔ moŋ fe ni ooofee ŋmei fɔ?

english: Dwarf or hybrid coconut varieties usually produce sweeter and abundant water earlier, while traditional tall varieties develop thicker meat inside, which yields more oil when processed.
ga: Dwarf loo hybrid akooshi henɔi lɛ feɔ nu ni ŋɔɔ, ni eyi obɔ oya. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kusum mli ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ lɛ mli lɛ mli tse fe tsutsu lɛ. Enɛ baaha mu babaoo aba kɛji akɛ atsu he nii.

english: How many years do I have to wait after planting before my coconut trees start bearing fruit?
ga: Kɛ́ mɔ ko du nii sɛɛ lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ emɛ dani ená ŋmei yibii?

english: Dwarf coconut trees usually start bearing fruit in 3 to 4 years, whereas traditional tall coconut trees take about 6 to 8 years to start producing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni blema ŋmei tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 6 kɛyashi 8 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi.

english: How do I know when my coconuts are ready to harvest for drinking water instead of waiting to make oil?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii kɛha nu ni anuɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaamɛ ni ajie mu lɛ?

english: For drinking water, harvest the coconut when it is bright green and about 7 to 8 months old; for oil, wait until the nut turns completely brown and dry at around 12 months when the flesh inside is thick and hard.
ga: kɛha nu ni anuɔ Kpaa ŋmeii beni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛye aaafee nyɔji 7 kɛyashi 8 lɛ. Kɛha fɔ lɛ, mɛ kɛyashi ŋmeii lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kwraa ni amɛgbi, aaafee nyɔji 12 be mli ni emli lɛ mli edɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the tiny young coconuts falling off my tree before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji bibii nɛkɛ? Koni migbee shi kɛjɛ mitso lɛ nɔ dani etsɔ agbo?

english: Young coconuts fall off mainly due to dry weather, lack of sufficient soil nutrients like potassium, or extreme heat; keeping the root area covered with mulch and well-watered helps the tree hold its fruit.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ titri hewɔ ni ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ potassium, loo latsaa ni naa wa. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ŋmɔtɔ ni awo amɛ nu bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ yibii lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my coconut trees turning yellow and dying from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmeii tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves can be caused by nutrient deficiency or a severe disease like Lethal Yellowing; if the yellowing spreads fast and young flowers die, notify an extension officer immediately to stop it from spreading.
ga: Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ loo hela ko ni naa wa, tamɔ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ. Kɛji akɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ gbɛ eshwa oya ni fɔfɔi bibii lɛ gboi. Ha extension official lɛ ale amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni ekpa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkagbee shi lɛ.

english: What makes some mature coconuts have thick flesh inside for oil while others have very thin flesh?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii komɛi ni edara lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha fɔ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii henɔi komɛi yɛ loo ni mli tse waa lɛ.

english: As a coconut stays longer on the tree, it converts its inner liquid into hard white flesh; trees planted in nutrient-rich soil with good sunlight produce thicker flesh rich in oil.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii hi tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tsɔɔ loo ni wa ni yɛŋ. tsei ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ nɔ ni hulu la kpakpa yɔɔ nɔ lɛ woɔ loo ni mli edɔ ni fɔ eyi mli obɔ.

english: Can coconut trees produce well on my farm far away from the sea, or do they only do well near the coast?
ga: Ani ŋmeii tsei baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔji ni kɛ ŋshɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ loo hei ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa pɛ?

english: Coconuts can produce very well inland as long as your land receives good rainfall, stays moist, gets plenty of sunlight, and has deep, well-draining soil.
ga: Kokooi baanyɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ babaoo, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ hulu la babaoo. ni eyɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yes, during the first 3 to 4 years when coconut trees are small, intercropping with food crops like maize, legumes, or cassava helps maximize your land and keep weeds under control.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ ji bibioo. Nibii ni aduɔ kɛ niyenii nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa. loo cassava Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ohaa ogbɛhe lɛ yaa hiɛ ni eyeɔ jwɛi anɔ.

english: Why does the coconut water from my farm taste sweet during some months and flat or watery during others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei nu ni jɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ŋɔɔ yɛ nyɔji komɛi amli, ni ekrokomɛi amli lɛ efeɔ ŋmei loo nu lɛ?

english: Coconut water is sweetest during dry, sunny months when the tree gets plenty of sunlight and enough soil potassium, whereas heavy rainy periods can dilute the natural sugars in the water.
ga: Kokoo nu lɛ ŋɔɔ fe fɛɛ yɛ nyɔji ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Enɛ ji be mli ni tsei lɛ naa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, adebɔɔ mli sugars ni yɔɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afee mlɛo.

english: How should I dry and store my harvested corn and soybean crops so they don't spoil before being ground into cereal flour?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ magbi mi-ŋmãa kɛ soybeans ni mikpa lɛ ni mikɛto? Bɔni afee ni ekafite dani atsɔ ŋmãa ashikishaŋ nɔ.

english: Grains must be sun-dried until they are hard and completely dry before storing them in clean, airtight bags in a cool, dry place to prevent mold and insect damage.
ga: Esa akɛ agbi ŋmaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaawa kwraa ni egbi dani akɛwo kotokui ni mli tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi koni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii akafite amɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct sunlight overheats them and dries out the moisture in their leaves. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or keeping shade trees protects the cocoa and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa amɛdɔɔ fe nine ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli lɛ mli egbiɔ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ dumɔwui loo shade tsei ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu kookoo lɛ he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: If I plant groundnuts together with my maize on the same plot, will they fight for nutrients?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ ŋmei fata ŋmei he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Ani nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ?

english: Groundnuts and maize complement each other well. Groundnuts naturally take nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, which feeds the maize and keeps the soil healthy without stealing food from the maize.
ga: Peanuts kɛ ŋmãa yaa jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ejuuu niyenii kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is a key nutrient for growth. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen-based fertilizer helps the leaves regain their green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛsu ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: When is the best time for me to put fertilizer on my crop so that rain doesn't wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli koni nugbɔ akashwie amɛ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is damp, but not during heavy rain. Digging a small hole near the plant stem, placing the fertilizer inside, and covering it with soil stops heavy rainwater from washing it away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi tsi ohe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. Tsɔɔmɔ bu bibioo ko ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi, ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ni okɛ sũ aha nɔ koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Planting the same crop every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like beans or cowpeas restores soil nutrients and breaks the pest cycle.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ bii. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: What is causing small holes in my maize leaves and dark powder inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ powda ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that feeds on tender leaf whorls. Checking your field early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts helps keep them under control.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ni yeɔ tsei ahe baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli loo neem mli nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ enɛɛmɛi.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays waterlogged because saturated ground prevents air from reaching the roots. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baagboi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehi shi ni nu eyi mli obɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ ni eyi obɔ kɛ nu lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops stay small even when I water the farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ afee bibioo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa moŋ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for light, water, and soil food. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nourishment to grow big instead of sharing it with weeds.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni okɛ jwɛi lɛ baaja

english: Why do seeds I buy from the agricultural office grow better than seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mihe kɛjɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ kwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mijie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds from agricultural officers are specially selected and tested to resist local diseases, tolerate drought, and produce higher yields, whereas saved seeds weaken over generations.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kpɛlɛɔ nɔ lɛ krɛdɛɛ ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ koni ana kɛji amɛnyɛŋ amɛye maŋ lɛ mli helai anɔ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ hɔmɔ ni ehaa yibii babaoo Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ fɛɛ yinɔ mli.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off extra side branches from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Trimming unnecessary side shoots directs the plant's food and energy into growing larger, healthier fruits rather than wasting energy on extra stems and leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ ŋmeii ni he ehiaaa lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ lɛ daa, ni ewoɔ yibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ fe ni eeefite hewalɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ.

english: Is it safe to use animal manure like cow dung on my crop fields, or will it make my harvested food bad?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ kooloi afɔfɔi, tamɔ tsina afɔfɔi baatsu nii yɛ miŋmɔji amli? Aloo ebaaha niyenii ni akpa lɛ afee nɔ ni ehiii?

english: Properly dried or composted animal manure is safe and rich in nutrients like nitrogen. It feeds the soil and improves crop yields without spoiling or contaminating the harvested food.
ga: Nibii ni agbi loo afee lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni niyenii tamɔ nitrogen babaoo yɛ mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ ni efiteee loo efiteee niyenii ni akpa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil, which is essential for healthy green growth, or that waterlogged soil is preventing the roots from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Aloo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ anine ashɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when stressed by severe heat, erratic watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer, which causes the plant to focus on growing leaves instead of setting fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hao amɛ. nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine Enɛ haa tomato tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why do my cassava roots remain thin and small even after growing for many months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛji bibii lolo yɛ nyɔji babaoo ni mikɛdu lɛ sɛɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots stay small if planted in hard, compacted soil where tubers cannot expand, or if heavy weed growth competes with the plant for sunlight and soil nutrients during early development.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ baafee bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ he ni ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛji jwɛi ni miida waa lɛ kɛ tsei miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii yɛ amɛshweremɔ shishijee fãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems. When heavy fruit bunches make the tree top-heavy and rain softens the soil, strong winds can easily pull the shallow roots out of the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ tsii lɛ, tso lɛ yiteŋ hu feɔ tsii. ni nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ ooojɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow thick foliage but produce very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ baai lɛ mli tse shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas produce excessive leaves and few pods when given too much nitrogen fertilizer or planted in overly rich soil, leading the plant to invest energy in greenery rather than flowering.
ga: Cowpea woɔ baai babaoo tsɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo kɛji akɛ akɛ nitrogen babaoo wo mli loo adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii babaoo nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei kɛ hewalɛ woɔ he ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli moŋ fe ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is typically caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites, or viruses transmitted by them, which stunt leaf development and damage growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ amɛmli Enɛ haa baai lɛ eyaaa hiɛ ni efiteɔ dalɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly in damp, shady conditions when rainwater splashes fungal spores onto the pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔ nu shwie ŋmei mli ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why should I space my maize seeds carefully instead of scattering many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ama shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooogbɛ dumɔwui babaoo ashwã he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ.

english: Proper spacing ensures each maize plant receives sufficient sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without competing with neighboring plants, leading to larger, healthier ears.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ Enɛ haa toi lɛ feɔ agbo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow crooked and irregular in shape under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Yam tubers twist and bend when they encounter rocks, hard clay, or compacted soil. Planting in deep, soft, well-tilled mounds allows tubers to expand freely and grow straight.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baakoto kɛji amɛkɛ tɛ ko kpe. shikpɔŋ ni wa loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ Kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni atsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ amɛhaa amɛhe ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know which crop will perform best on the piece of land given to me?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei ni baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛha mi lɛ nɔ?

english: Different crops prefer different soil types and moisture levels. For example, cassava grows well in poorer, well-drained soils, while maize needs rich, fertile soil that holds water well. Checking the depth and texture of your dirt helps you pick the right crop for success.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi biɔ shikpɔŋ srɔtoi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa babaoo. Akɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa he miihia shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni baa nii ni baanyɛ ahiɛ nu mli jogbaŋŋ.
