Shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ mlipɛimɔ yeɔ ebua bo ni ohalaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛha omanyeyeli.

english: What happens if I plant my seeds too close together on my plot?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: If crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow thin and weak, resulting in smaller yields than if they were given proper spacing.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ baafee bibioo fe kɛji akɛ aha gbɛ ni sa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ aduɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry period before the real rainy season sets in. If seeds sprout during this dry gap, the young seedlings will quickly dry up and die from heat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baa. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ latsaa lɛ hewɔ.

english: How does heavy rainfall affect young crops right after planting?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Excessive rain can wash away small seeds or drown tender roots in waterlogged soil, preventing them from getting the air they need to breathe and grow strong.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ ajie dumɔwui bibii. loo shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni awo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Ehaaa amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛmu ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is starving for key nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil is too wet around the roots. Adding poultry manure or fertilizer helps restore green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii fataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ekoŋŋ.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally built to steal water and food from the soil faster than domestic crops. Clearing them early ensures your crops get all the nourishment.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni abɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ koni amɛye nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he akaŋ oya fe shia tsei. Amɛjiemɔ mra Ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yeɔ emuu.

english: Can I grow beans together with my maize in the same field?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmeii kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is helpful. Beans absorb nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, which feeds the maize and keeps the land fertile.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he. Beans shwieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii kɛha ŋmãa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii

english: Why do my crops grow better when I add animal manure to the soil before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ kooloi ashishifãi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani midu lɛ?

english: Manure acts like food and a sponge for the soil; it supplies slow-release nutrients and helps the dirt hold onto water during dry days.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛ sponji kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni jeɔ kpo blɛoo lɛ baa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni muji lɛ kpɛtɛɔ nu lɛ he yɛ gbii ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ amli.

english: Plants drop flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme hot weather or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the flowers stay on and turn into fruit.
ga: Tsei baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How do I know when underground crops like cassava or yam are ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tso ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei, miida? Ani ofee klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: When tubers are fully grown underground, the plant leaves above ground will naturally begin to yellow and dry up because the plant stops growing new leaves and focuses energy on the roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Shikpɔŋ nɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ baaje shishi amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni tso lɛ kpaɔ baai heei ni ekwɛɔ lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ maa shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning light yellow while the top leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to stay green and grow big. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season feeds the crop and turns the leaves green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii ni ebaaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every year even when I use seeds from my best crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ miiba shi daa afi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ.

english: Every time you harvest crops, they pull nutrients out of the earth. If you plant the same crop on the same plot every season without feeding the soil with manure or compost, the soil becomes exhausted and produces less.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii Ebaajie niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haaa lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaawo yibii babaoo.

english: Why is it good for my land if I plant groundnuts or cowpeas after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have small pods on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the earth. Planting them after maize naturally heals and fertilizes the soil for your next planting season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmeii bibii. Yɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ. Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ abɛi sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods turn dark brown, rot, and dry up right on the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ? Rot kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal sickness that thrives in dark, wet conditions. Pruning excessive shade leaves to let in sunlight and removing diseased pods right away stops the sickness from spreading to healthy cocoa.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni duŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ baai ni yɔɔ shade fe nine koni hulu la aba ni ojie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya. Enɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã kookoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my hot pepper leaves twisting up, wrinkling, and stopping the plant from growing tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-hot pepper baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsĩɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf twisting is caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that transmit plant sicknesses. Spraying your pepper plants with neem water or recommended insecticide early keeps these insects away.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni ji tsei ahe helai ni baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Akɛ neem nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ ohe.

english: Why do small caterpillars eat ragged holes in the middle leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni etse yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Those are Fall Armyworms that hide deep inside the central leaf funnel of the maize plant. Checking your farm frequently and applying neem extract, wood ash, or safe bio-pesticides directly into the leaf funnel destroys them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms ni akɛtee ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mli kwɛmɔ shii abɔ kɛ neem mli nibii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe, tso mli sũ, loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛtsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa baai lɛ amli. baafite amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my heavy plantain trees fall over easily when strong winds and rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni tsii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ miinɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots do not grow deep into the ground, making the plant top-heavy when bearing fruit. Supporting the fruiting stems with strong bamboo poles or wooden forks keeps them upright until harvest.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Ehaa tso lɛ tsiimɔ babaoo kɛ́ ewo yibii. Okɛ ŋmei tsei loo tso ni akɛfee ŋmei ni wa afi aduawai tsei lɛ asɛɛ koni amɛhi shi shiŋŋ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Extreme heat and dry air destroy the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing them from forming fruit. Watering plants regularly at the roots and providing light shade during very hot afternoons helps the flowers stick and set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. make it unproductive Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃.
